The next component of power we require is one born of hatred, fashioned within the Emerald Nightmare. It is known as the Nightmare Lash.

The Nightmare Lash has the power to suffocate all hope... all light... from within a living soul.

The Shade of Xavius himself carries the lash. Defeat him and bring the lash to me!

I will use it to dominate the steeds of the damned!

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: The Nightmare Lash
passages.text: Do you have the Nightmare Lash?

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: The Nightmare Lash
passages.text:
At long last, the Nightmare Lash! Holding it in my hands, I can feel the truth of the legends.

Such power... such darkness... such... anguish!

Yes, this will do nicely.

passages.title: Advancing the War Effort
passages.text:
The quest for the Four Horsemen is of the utmost importance, however we must turn our attention to the warfront.

Our continued success on the field of battle has shaken the Burning Legion and as a result, they have increased the frequency and intensity of their assaults.

We must meet the increased aggression with continued resistance!

Only then will we be able to turn our attention back to the Four Horsemen.

passages.title: Advancing the War Effort
passages.text: How goes the war effort?

passages.title: Advancing the War Effort
passages.text:
The Ebon Blade's success on the battlefield has not gone unnoticed by the Burning Legion.

As we continue the war effort, we must be mindful of increased attention from the forces of Sargeras...

passages.title: Maw of Souls: Maul of the Dead
passages.text:
All of the necessary components have been gathered together. Soon, the unholy steeds of the damned will trample the armies of the Burning Legion.

However, our work is not quite done. One item yet remains beyond our grasp...

Lurking within the depths of Helheim, the fallen queen Helya rules over the dead. In her possession is a maul, infused with the souls of countless fallen warriors.

Bring to me the Maul of the Dead and with it, I will forge barding so impenetrable... no demon shall break it!

passages.title: Maw of Souls: Maul of the Dead
passages.text: Have you brought me the Maul of the Dead?

passages.title: Maw of Souls: Maul of the Dead
passages.text: The legendary Maul of the Dead... it resonates with the hatred and despair of countless anguished souls. As a tool of misery, it is the embodiment of perfection.

passages.title: Regroup at the Refuge
passages.text:
I cannot think clearly in this place.

Even though the moonwell is still pure, the corrupting influence of the Nightmare remains.

Come, we will return to the refuge and gather our wits. Then we will continue the hunt for my husband.

passages.title: Regroup at the Refuge
passages.text: Already my mind is sharper.

passages.title: Maw of Souls: Message to Helya
passages.text:
We cannot fight on two fronts and succeed.

If we're to give ourselves the room we need to fight off the Legion we need to deliver a decisive victory against Helya. Not her armies, not her lieutenants, but the mother of the underworld herself.

Go to the Maw of Souls and defeat Helya, <name>.

passages.title: Maw of Souls: Message to Helya
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Maw of Souls: Message to Helya
passages.text: A glorious victory! It's unfortunate that Helya survived, but she will think twice about moving against us with you leading the armies of Skyhold.

passages.title: To the Deeps
passages.text:
I assure you the legends are true: Sharas'dal, the Scepter of Tides, was forged around living waters of the Well of Eternity. It gave Azshara dominion over life itself. I have sent shaman throughout the world looking for it, but the only one to ever find it has gone missing.

Wavespeaker Adelee said she had tracked the scepter to the Ruins of Vashj'ir, but we haven't heard from her since.

<name>! Come with me to the ocean depths. Let's track down our missing shaman and get that artifact!

passages.title: To the Deeps
passages.text: I can transport us to the depths. Step into the bubble here... It's mostly safe.

passages.title: To the Deeps
passages.text:
Very good!

If you haven't been to this realm before, I have learned a trick or two to give you your "Sea Legs," allowing you to breathe underwater for the duration of our mission here.

Now, let's find out missing <class> and the scepter she was looking for!

passages.title: Lumenstone
passages.text:
To prepare for the battle ahead, we will need armor and weapons.

We have learned of lumenstone, a rare metal that can negate magic... even fel magic.

It is found in small quantities all over the Broken Isles, and many of the native races use it in their own metalcrafting.

We should send our champions to target enemies around the Broken Isles - there should be plenty of lumenstone to be found in their stockpiles.

passages.title: Lumenstone
passages.text: Have you acquired any lumenstone?

passages.title: Lumenstone
passages.text: There's enough lumenstone here to craft armor and weapons for an army. Thank you, Highlord.

passages.title: Defenders of the World
passages.text:
Requests are pouring in from across the Broken Isles for our aid, Highlord.

I know that we are working to aid the priests at Netherlight Temple, but there are many others who need our help.

We cannot turn our backs on those who need our aid.

passages.title: Defenders of the World
passages.text: Thank you, Highlord. Too many dangers abound in these dark times. With heroes like you out there, we are all a little bit safer.

passages.title: The Call of Battle
passages.text:
Once, the mighty titanforged keepers of Ulduar and Odyn acted as one. Ever since Odyn broke off to create the valarjar, not even Odyn's own son Thorim is bound to follow his father's advice.

There is one hope to unite the forces of Skyhold and Ulduar however.

The Gjallarhorn was a gift given to Hymdall before Odyn's departure. The keepers of Ulduar are oathbound to answer the call of the Gjallarhorn were it to be sounded as it would signal that the end times are upon us!

passages.title: The Call of Battle
passages.text: Ah yes, the Gjallarhorn.

passages.title: Down to Business
passages.text:
First things first, <name>: we must set up our camp.

We do not have the time or resources for a prolonged siege. It is not like we can starve them out. No, we must be swift and sure as an arrow, piercing their heart in one strike.

They are drawing up their battle lines within the city, but could attack us while we are setting up our defenses.

Venture forth and show them what the kaldorei have learned from thousands of years of war. Discover their weaknesses so that we may exploit them.

passages.title: Down to Business
passages.text: Any regret I had for these people vanished when they went under that shield.

passages.title: Down to Business
passages.text:
Time to get to business, <name>. We cannot afford to tarry.

While we are not setting up for a prolonged engagement, we must still have a war camp of some sorts. I do not expect the Nightborne to stay patiently in their city while we plant stakes.

They are starting to build their defenses. Go in there and see what we are up against. You will strike them from within while we finalize our preparations.

passages.title: Down to Business
passages.text: Excellent. We will be able to defend our borders for now.

passages.title: Spy vs. Spy
passages.text:
SI:7 is the espionage and intel branch of the Alliance. They are based out of Stormwind City and headed up by Master Mathias Shaw. As of late, they have been acting, shall we say, peculiar.

I would like for you to send some of our people out to assess the situation. It might be nothing, but I am not fond of situations that I do not fully understand.

If we are going to win this war against the Burning Legion, the last thing we need is for something wholly unexpected to occur.

passages.title: Spy vs. Spy
passages.text:
Why is Mathias Shaw stepping up the number of agents that he has in Horde territory?

We must keep a close and watchful eye on this situation.

passages.title: Elixirs of Aid
passages.text:
We can never be too prepared for battle. The Legion will strike at any moment, and we must be ready to deal with a multitude of injuries and afflictions.

Zabra and Yalia have provided me a list of their most potent potions and battle elixirs than can do everything from restore health to blind the enemy.

We have an exhaustive list of ingredients that we'll need in order to craft a respectable supply.

passages.title: Elixirs of Aid
passages.text: You are as dependable as you are resourceful.

passages.title: Convincin' Old Yancey
passages.text:
Avast ye! Th' time be long overdue that we get some more pirate blood into our ranks.

<Crackers gives a sudden squawk in agreement.>

And I know just th' man t' do it.

I'm talkin' about good old Yancey Grillsen, o' course. He's an old salt down Stranglethorn way.

Send some o' your land lovin' scallywags off t' round him up.

passages.title: Convincin' Old Yancey
passages.text:
Arrr! Now that be what I like t' hear.

What do you think, Crackers... will a bunch o' freebooters class up this crow's nest or scuttle th' ship? I say it's a fair toss o' th' bones.

passages.title: Recruiting More Troops
passages.text:
Word of your leadership has spread rather fast. Priests of all sorts have traveled to the temple to lend their aid.

We're lucky enough to have caught the eye of Vicar Eliza. She's quite the leader in her own right, commanding countless devotees that do her bidding without question. 

Speak to her now.

passages.title: Recruiting More Troops
passages.text: It is an honor to serve you, High <class>.

passages.title: Fancy Lads and Buccaneers
passages.text:
Aye, it warms me heart t' know that Yancey's now part o' th' crew.

<Tethys feeds Crackers some cackle fruit from the table.>

Why don't you be a good <lad/lass> and see if he can sponge us up some bilge rats.

passages.title: Fancy Lads and Buccaneers
passages.text:
Are you lookin' t' be shark bait? Where be our new crew of pirates?

<Crackers squawks in agreement.>

passages.title: Fancy Lads and Buccaneers
passages.text:
Now that's more like it. Get them some holystone and put them t' work scrubbin' th' deck.

That and a few black jacks o' rum will put courage in their sails.

passages.title: Steeds of the Damned
passages.text:
Salanar the Horseman has arrived at Ebon Hold from the Realm of Shadows. He alone has the knowledge and power to conjure the steeds of the Four Horsemen.

Salanar has given us the first list of necessary components to create the steeds. I have organized a number of missions to obtain these items.

Use the mission table to assign your chosen champions to the task.

passages.title: Steeds of the Damned
passages.text: Have you completed the necessary missions for Salanar the Horseman?

passages.title: Steeds of the Damned
passages.text: Excellent work, Deathlord. The missions for the Steeds of the Damned were successful. Salanar the Horseman now has the first set of necessary components for conjuring the steeds.

passages.title: Aggregates of Anguish
passages.text:
Our preparations for conjuring the Steeds of the Damned are nearly complete.

Salanar the Horseman has given us a list of the remaining components. The ritual of conjuring requires five unholy essences known as the Aggregates of Anguish.

I have taken it upon myself to organize the necessary missions to obtain these components.

Use the mission table to assign your chosen champions to the task.

passages.title: Aggregates of Anguish
passages.text: With the Aggregates of Anguish procured, our work is nearly complete. Soon, the Steeds of the Damned will rise... and the Burning Legion will fall!

passages.title: A New Path
passages.text:
Highlord <name>, if I could have a moment of your time?

Long have I followed the path of the Light, and for many years I studied under the Priestesses of the Moon. Yet, I have always felt my education incomplete, and a yearning to know more.

When I walked into these halls, I finally felt a spark of what was missing. I believe that a new path lies before me.

I wish to become a paladin of the Silver Hand. Will you allow me to join you?

passages.title: A New Path
passages.text: What do you think?

passages.title: A New Path
passages.text: Thank you, Highlord.

passages.title: A Second Legend
passages.text:
Perhaps it's time to consider improving your flexibility when it comes to powerful artifacts. There are still others that I think are worth pursuing if you are interested.

Let me show you what your options are and you can choose one.

passages.title: A Second Legend
passages.text: Excellent. You can begin as soon as you are ready.

passages.title: Expanding Your Horizons
passages.text:
You are a fast study, <class>t <name>. The elements speak through you - it is rare to have such a connection to the world.

A true shaman must walk many paths. For every role, one must have the right tools at hand. Only the most powerful weapons can lead us to victory against the Legion. Perhaps it is time to seek out another?

Speak with me and let us discuss your options.

passages.title: Expanding Your Horizons
passages.text:
Very well. Your allies have gathered here on the precipice - they will know how best to proceed.

May the winds be ever in your favor, Farseer.

passages.title: More Weapons of Legend
passages.text:
It is wise to carry more than one weapon to war. Sometimes one will be better suited than another. You should choose another weapon of legend to carry with you, especially against foes so deadly.

What say you?

passages.title: More Weapons of Legend
passages.text: A powerful weapon for a powerful champion of the Halls. Let us begin.

passages.title: A Body of Evidence
passages.text:
There is an urgent matter that requires your attention, <name>.

The body of a woman with a knife in her back has turned up in the sewers.

Normally, such a matter would be less than newsworthy... but this isn't your average cutthroat. It's an SI:7 operative!

I've got some of our goons guarding the body, but you had better get over there before the word spreads.

If SI:7 finds out about this... it will be bad for business.

passages.title: A Body of Evidence
passages.text: Did you identify the body? Was it an SI:7 operative?

passages.title: A Body of Evidence
passages.text:
So it's true? An SI:7 agent was assassinated in our own backyard?

If SI:7 links us to the murder, this will be bad for business. We'll need to get to the bottom of this sooner rather than later...

passages.title: Blades of Destiny
passages.text:
I'm glad that weapon you've been carrying around has proven useful. Our ally, the Lich King, has offered to provide you with a lead on another weapon should the one you already have somehow be lacking.

Consider the options carefully and let me know which you would like to seek out.

passages.title: Blades of Destiny
passages.text: Very well.

passages.title: Hired Help
passages.text:
I was fond of Margaux. News of her death weighs heavily on many of us.

<Vanthir shakes his head sadly.>

If we are to carry on, we need to send a strong message. We need those like Durant to know that we are watching, and we will hold them accountable.

I know someone who could help us.

His name is Arluin. To call him a reluctant ally would be generously overstating it. He is cautious, and will not risk himself without compensation.

You can find him in the alleys north of the Evermoon Bazaar.

passages.title: Hired Help
passages.text: Best not to lurk if you aren't doing business.

passages.title: Hired Help
passages.text: I will help you, but first I need you to do something for me.

passages.title: Two Paths, Two Weapons
passages.text:
We've searched through our scrolls and have found new leads on a couple of powerful weapons. They may prove beneficial in our efforts.

Here, let me show you what I've found. If any of these interest you then simply let me know.

passages.title: Two Paths, Two Weapons
passages.text: A wise choice.

passages.title: Another Weapon of Old
passages.text:
You have done well but our foes are powerful and cunning. It would be wise to be prepared for whatever they may unleash upon us. 

You would be wise to consider obtaining another of the weapons of old to aid in our conflict.

Let me know how you'd like to proceed.

passages.title: Another Weapon of Old
passages.text: A sound choice.

passages.title: The Tome Opens Again
passages.text:
You've been doing well, friend, but you would be unstoppable if you had another weapon at your side.

Here, let me show you what options remain in the book. If either of these interest you then simply let me know.

passages.title: The Tome Opens Again
passages.text: Thoughts, friend?

passages.title: The Tome Opens Again
passages.text: Yes, very good choice!

passages.title: Your Fullest Potential
passages.text:
I see that you walk many paths, as a true shaman should.

Two mighty artifacts are already in your possession. To seek a third would not be greed: it would be the fulfillment of your destiny, the completion of a circle.

Speak with me, and together we will unlock your fullest potential.

passages.title: Your Fullest Potential
passages.text: Where are the spirits guiding you, Farseer?

passages.title: Your Fullest Potential
passages.text: The path ahead is clear. Your allies await you on this ledge. May the spirits walk with you, Farseer!

passages.title: Another Worthy Blade
passages.text:
We still have plans prepared to obtain other weapons of incredible power - tools that you may find useful to have on hand as you continue your work.

I would be happy to go over the remaining options with you so that you may make an informed decision.

passages.title: Another Worthy Blade
passages.text:
Yes, I think that will do rather nicely as well.

Good choice.

passages.title: Vote of Confidence
passages.text:
I will endeavor to protect my son until the votes are cast.

Coryn Stelleris is a predator even among the nobility. It does not surprise me that he should stoop to such depths to ensure his own success.

Tell Ly'leth that she has my support. Unequivocally.

You may also choose to tell her that Coryn Stelleris will hurt her, if she gives him a chance.

Be careful.

passages.title: Vote of Confidence
passages.text:
I know of Coryn. We will not underestimate his venom, rest assured.

Thank you for helping Aurore. She is a dear friend of mine.

passages.title: The Bloody Truth
passages.text:
We need to find out who is behind the assassination of Amber Kearnen.

It won't be long before SI:7 realizes that their agent is MIA and comes sniffing around The Hall of Shadows.

Here, take these stylish spy glasses and set them to scan for traces of hemoglobin. I've taken the liberty of calibrating them specifically for Amber Kearnen's blood.

Follow the blood trail back to the culprits, but make sure to stay out of sight!

Report back to us when you've got the information we need.

passages.title: The Bloody Truth
passages.text: Were you able to find out who's behind the assassination attempt?

passages.title: The Bloody Truth
passages.text:
Let me get this straight...

You are saying that Master Mathias Shaw ordered the death of one of his best agents? This is far more serious than I first thought.

We'll need to continue the search for clues...

passages.title: Continuing the Legend
passages.text:
There are still two paths you may walk - two powerful weapons you might yet obtain to aid you in the fight against the Legion.

I will help you recall your remaining options, of course.

passages.title: Continuing the Legend
passages.text: A wise path to follow - may it take you far.

passages.title: And They Will Tremble
passages.text:
There will be consequences for what has transpired this day.

For now, you should return to Thalyssra. Tell her that we have avenged Margaux and that the Dusk Lily has announced itself to all of Suramar.

There will be many more deaths before this is over, rest assured, but this is a death that will teach others like Durant to tread more carefully in the future.

passages.title: And They Will Tremble
passages.text: It is a relief, if a small one. You have done well - rest for now.

passages.title: Friends With Benefits
passages.text:
The Lunastre Attendant, silent as ever, offers you a wax-sealed scroll.

It reads:
"Dearest <name>,

I asked my attendant to catch you, should things go in my favor.

The role of Advisor will keep me away from the estate for some time and I settled on a gift for Thalyssra.

I have sent a detachment of attendants to Shal'Aran with some comfort items. Treat them well- they need someone to wait on and I could think of none better!

Give the others my thanks, and my love,
Advisor Ly'leth Lunastre"

passages.title: Friends With Benefits
passages.text: She certainly is a worthy companion.

passages.title: Bolstering Your Arsenal
passages.text:
Highlord, there are still weapons that you might obtain to help you defeat the Legion. We have kept a close eye on them during your time on the Broken Isles.

I would be happy to review them with you if you wish.

passages.title: Bolstering Your Arsenal
passages.text: Excellent. There's no time to waste.

passages.title: The Missing Admiral
passages.text:
Alright. According to the clues you found, that was Anduin's ship, and Admiral Taylor was the captain. 

And Admiral Taylor's last entry says he was going to fight off the hozen and protect the vessel after the shipwreck.

The locals say these hozen sometimes take prisoners, and I didn't see Taylor's corpse anywhere among the wreckage. So you'll probably find Taylor at the hozen encampment to the northeast.

Get going, we have no time to lose!

passages.title: The Missing Admiral
passages.text: <You found him, but the Admiral is unconscious. He looks on the verge of death.>

passages.title: Hozen Aren't Your Friends, Hozen Are Your Enemies
passages.text:
We've located an Alliance wreck to the south. Unfortunately, the locals have informed us that it's currently being scavenged by a group of creatures called "hozen."

By pillaging our wrecked ships, these creatures have already shown that they aren't friendly. We can't have them taking spoils from our ships, stealing our supplies, and worse, potentially capturing or killing any survivors.

Get down there and take them out! When you're done, meet up with Nodd Codejack, our SI:7 agent in the area.

passages.title: Hozen Aren't Your Friends, Hozen Are Your Enemies
passages.text:
Good work. Dirty creatures trying to kick us when we're down... 

That'll teach 'em to try and salvage an Alliance vessel!

passages.title: The Path of War
passages.text:
I see you want to save your friend. I can help you, if you will help me.

First of all, it should be obvious that the fewer the Slingtail roaming around, the easier it will be to escape.

Kill the hozen guards around us, and we will be one step closer to freedom.

passages.title: The Path of War
passages.text: You fight well, foreigner.

passages.title: The Path of War
passages.text:
Ahahaha! You are brave.

An admirable trait.

passages.title: Freeing Our Brothers
passages.text:
You may be an outsider, but you and I have a common enemy in the hozen.

Many members of my tribe are trapped in cages nearby. I have also seen your... Alliance... soldiers as well.

I cannot leave without freeing my brethren, just as you cannot leave yours.

The Slingtail hold the keys to those cages. Find the keys and free our friends.

passages.title: Freeing Our Brothers
passages.text: Are they freed?

passages.title: Freeing Our Brothers
passages.text:
You have freed my brothers? Good.

We are in your debt.

passages.title: Ancient Power
passages.text:
Hozen skulls are prized tokens among my village.

We use them to perform ceremonial rites, and the older the skull, the more potent its magic.

Luckily for us, the hozen are careless, filthy beasts. They leave the skulls of their dead scattered among their huts and campfires.

Collect these skulls for me, and I will reward you handsomely.

passages.title: Ancient Power
passages.text: The skulls are precious to my tribe. How many have you collected?

passages.title: Ancient Power
passages.text:
It is good to see that you are so resourceful, <name>. It is a trait admired by my people.

The fine specimens you have brought me will produce powerful magic.

passages.title: Jailbreak
passages.text:
Without healing, your friend Taylor will die. My village is just east of here, in the middle of the large lake.

I will take Taylor myself, but the fighting is most dangerous in that direction.

I need you to help clear a path through the hozen, so that I may run safely into my village.

Can you do this?

passages.title: Jailbreak
passages.text: Our conflict with the hozen goes back many generations.

passages.title: Jailbreak
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Because of you, we were able to make it here safely.

passages.title: The Double Hozen Dare
passages.text:
There is a witch in the woods but no one believes me. She turned my friend Shin into jade!

We were all so scared we tried to run back but she sicced her big jade monsters on us. A bunch of my friends tried to get away by climbing trees.

Can you help me save my friends?

passages.title: The Double Hozen Dare
passages.text: Where is Shin? I didn't see Shin.

passages.title: The Double Hozen Dare
passages.text: Oh thank you so much for helping find my friends.  I still don't see Shin though...

passages.title: The Jade Witch
passages.text:
The Jade Witch must still have Shin.

I... I can't do it! I don't want to see the witch. Can you please go talk to her and see if she has Shin?

You're an adult, I don't think she would try to turn you into jade.

passages.title: The Jade Witch
passages.text:
Hurray! Thank you so much! Shin is saved and you beat up the old witch! And the best part is our parents were never told what we were up to. Hurray!

It looks like everybody who came back are trying to get rid of whatever jade they had. Toya's been collecting it for some reason and said you should go chat with him.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Fire From the Sky
passages.text:
Yeah, we found Amber, she's alive, and all that. That's about where the good news stops though.

Let's see if I can pick up where ol' Rell left off...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Fire From the Sky
passages.text: I'm not done with the report yet, <name>. Settle down.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Fire From the Sky
passages.text:
So, now you know why ol' Rell's all beat up.

<You detect a change in Sully's facial expression, and he quickly turns away. Is he... crying?>

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text: I... I can tell you what happened next! We continued north, into the forest...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text:
Luckily, we all made it out alive.

Well... all of us except for Socks...

passages.title: Scouting Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text:
I bet I know your first question: "What the ook happened to Sergeant Gorrok?" Don't worry, don't worry. He's totally alive. Not dead or anything.

<Riko shuffles uncomfortably.>

Well, we THINK he's alive, but he ALSO might be very, very dead.

<Riko looks into your eyes for approval.>

Fine! Let me tell you exactly what happened.

passages.title: Scouting Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text: I'm not ookin' done yet!

passages.title: Scouting Report: Hostile Natives
passages.text: So, as you can see, none of this is Riko's fault.

passages.title: Scouting Report: On the Right Track
passages.text:
MOST of what Riko said is true.

We didn't dare pursue Gorrok - the Horde's numbers here are far too few. Our forces can only sustain so many losses, and frankly, we don't know how powerful that witch really is.

Let me pick up where the hozen left off...

passages.title: Scouting Report: On the Right Track
passages.text: If I may continue, please?

passages.title: Scouting Report: On the Right Track
passages.text:
And that's how we found our Alliance captive.

But that's not all that happened. Not by a long shot...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Lost in the Woods
passages.text:
<Rell coughs heavily before speaking.>

Please, <name>. You need to hear what we've been through.

The whole damned Alliance needs to hear what we've been through. There may not be much time left.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Lost in the Woods
passages.text: <Rell doesn't look too good. He should probably save his energy.>

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Lost in the Woods
passages.text:
...and that's <cough> how we found...

<Rell's speech devolves into heavy coughing. The corner of his mouth produces a trickle of blood.>

passages.title: Kung Din
passages.text:
I hope you are capable of this next task, for our lives depend on it.

There is only one key that will unlock our chains. Unfortunately, the key hangs around the neck of the hozen's pet tiger, Kung Din.

They keep the tiger in the great pit to the north. The only way to retrieve the key will be to kill the beast.

passages.title: Kung Din
passages.text: Did you find him?

passages.title: Kung Din
passages.text:
Yes, with this key I will be able to free our chains.

You have delivered us from this vile place.

passages.title: Forensic Science
passages.text:
These creatures are everywhere - and very hostile! We'll need to deal with them before any more Alliance show up.

This one's taken quite a beating, but I've still made some determinations about its anatomy.

With the proper reagents, I'll be able to fashion a poison that should be quite effective against this species. In fact, I'll just need to modify a bit of the poison I have with me.

Go and find me some viscous chlorophyll down by the water. Any semi-sentient flora should do.

passages.title: Forensic Science
passages.text: I hope you were successful. Our survival here may depend on it.

passages.title: Forensic Science
passages.text: Oh, yes, <name>. This will do nicely.

passages.title: Missed Me By... That Much!
passages.text:
Listen, <pal/toots>.

I sent out a coupla supply drones from the gunship, and they've all been lost or crashed. Almost all, that is.

One of 'em buzzed right through the camp here and crashed out by them waterfalls.

How 'bout you see what you can do about bringin' the contents of that crate back here, hmm?

We're all outta drones, but my rocket boots might yet come in handy... or footy, as the case may be.

Hah! I just kill me...

passages.title: Missed Me By... That Much!
passages.text: This crate should be full of supplies...

passages.title: Scouting Report: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
We weren't only looking for Alliance, you know. We were also looking for those snooked-up, tik-flikklin' jinyu!

Well, we found 'em all right...

passages.title: Scouting Report: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text: Riko wishes you were a bit more patient, <name>.

passages.title: Scouting Report: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
Yeah, I ran away. So blikkin' what? If it weren't for me, Kiryn would be dead. Oh, wait... she's already dead... already...

Go away! Riko's head hurts.

passages.title: Road Rations
passages.text:
We do not have time to wait around for the Admiral to recover.

Sully and I are planning to search for Anduin to the north, but we'll need supplies for our journey.

The lake here is teeming with wildlife, which we have received permission to hunt.

Go and gather some supplies while Sully and I finalize our preparations.

passages.title: Road Rations
passages.text:
Time is short. Each hour we delay, the White Pawn may move further away.

Where are the supplies I asked for?

passages.title: Road Rations
passages.text: This should be plenty, <name>. Thanks.

passages.title: Borrowed Brew
passages.text:
A delicious smell wafts out from the bottle on the table.

A little taste couldn't hurt, right?

passages.title: Borrowed Brew
passages.text:
I heard your people had washed up on our shores, but I did not expect to find one washed up on my very doorstep! What brings you here, stranger?

<You explain about your search for Prince Anduin, and describe the boy to the pandaren.>

Very interesting! And so the Pearlfin sent you to me, did they?

passages.title: Body
passages.text:
A brew's body is an important and often overlooked factor.

To create the perfect consistency, I will need pristine eyes from the Bog Crocolisks to the east.

Take care. The creatures are quite vicious.

passages.title: Body
passages.text: Watch your step in the swamp, my new friend.

passages.title: Body
passages.text: Do you have crocolisks where you are from?

passages.title: Hue
passages.text:
The most distinguishing feature of the Dream Brew is its iridescent, dream-like color.

To the east, you will find Glittering Amberflies. I will need their wings to create the final luminescent color of the brew.

Take this knife and use it to collect 8 wings.

passages.title: Hue
passages.text: Have you collected all the ingredients? It is almost time to make the Dream Brew.

passages.title: Hue
passages.text:
Beautiful color, rare transparency, shimmer but not sparkle...these will do quite well.

I am beginning to see great potential in you, strange one.

passages.title: Rest in Peace
passages.text:
The spirits... the cavedwellers... they howl in agony... 

Trapped... in this world... cannot move... to the next.

I... will go mad... listening... to their cries... 

Please...go...put them to rest.

passages.title: Rest in Peace
passages.text: Thank you... friend. I am... happy... knowing... the spirits... are at peace.

passages.title: Anduin's Decision
passages.text:
You have done all you can for the Prince's friends.

You completed your mission and found the White Pawn - Prince Anduin. Admiral Taylor and the other SI:7 agents will be eager to have the boy safe in their custody.

It is time to return home.

passages.title: Anduin's Decision
passages.text:
He did WHAT?!?!?

He's lucky that I haven't found him yet, because when I do, I just might kill him myself!

Whatever he thinks he's doing... chasing after this Vale... it is not behavior fit for a prince!

If we didn't have more pressing matters at hand, I would send our entire fleet chasing after his heels!

passages.title: Let Them Burn
passages.text:
Advance scouts report that the hozen at the Slingtail Pits are amassing with reinforcements from their tribes to the north.

Our forces are gathered for battle on the ridge to the northwest. They are just waiting for you.

Now is the time to show them what we are made of. Now is the time to destroy them indefinitely.

passages.title: Let Them Burn
passages.text: The waters were right about you, <name>. Because of your efforts, this village has a future. We will not forget the lessons you've taught us, <class>.

passages.title: Carp Diem
passages.text:
Despite the hozen's apparent disarray, there is an order to their chaos. Their leader, Chief Gukgut, is the shrewd mastermind behind their attacks.

He is organizing their movements at the great pit at the hozen camp to the northwest.

Strike now and show him no mercy, <name>, for he will do the same.

passages.title: Carp Diem
passages.text:
Without their leader, these hozen should once again settle into disarray.

Today we rejoice in our victory! <name>, you came to us a stranger, but you depart as a friend.

From henceforth, you are the highest of the high - a valued friend and defender of the Pearlfin tribe.

passages.title: Chen and Li Li
passages.text:
My niece and I are new to Pandaria. Probably like yourself. We're visitors from the Wandering Isle, and, to be honest, we have no idea where we're going.

That farm up ahead looks as fine a place as any to take off our shoes and enjoy a brew. What do you say, Li Li?

<race>? Would you like to share the road with us?

passages.title: Chen and Li Li
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Chen and Li Li
passages.text:
Welcome, welcome, visitors! You've come to sample some of my son's turnips? Perhaps purchase a few pigs?

Please, make yourselves at home. I have plenty of room.

passages.title: Low Turnip Turnout
passages.text:
Your help here is appreciated, <name>. I'd like to give you another job, if you're interested.

My son, Ang, runs the small farm just down this hill. He should have brought me some fruits and vegetables this morning, but I haven't seen him all day.

Would you go down there and see what's going on?

passages.title: Low Turnip Turnout
passages.text:
Wha-? Who the...? My father sent you?

Pshh... he can be so nosy sometimes. I have everything under control here.

passages.title: Back to the Sty
passages.text:
I try to keep an eye on my stock, but every once in a while some of them sneak away. With all the confusion these virmen are causing, I may have let my guard down for a few moments, and some of my pigs escaped.

Care to look for them? I'd start by looking down the hill, to the west.

passages.title: Back to the Sty
passages.text: Have you found them? There should be three missing, I think.

passages.title: Back to the Sty
passages.text:
There they are! Back into the sty with you three, now!

<Liang looks up at you.>

Thank you, neighbor. I'm truly grateful for your assistance.

passages.title: Piercing Talons and Slavering Jaws
passages.text:
First the hawks came. You've probably seen some of them circling up above.

The wolves came shortly after. I think they smelled my weakness.

I'm not nearly as brave as Master Shang thought I was. The master will be quite cross with me if I don't do something about these beasts.

Can... can you help, <sir/ma'am>?

passages.title: Piercing Talons and Slavering Jaws
passages.text: I wish I were brave enough to fight them, but...

passages.title: Piercing Talons and Slavering Jaws
passages.text: They... they're not stopping, but at least we fought back. Right?

passages.title: Lupello
passages.text:
I've been thinking... the wolves might stop attacking if we kill their pack leader.

We call him Lupello, and he patrols the opposite riverbank.

<Francis' concentration is broken by another attack. Perhaps you should go deal with Lupello yourself.>

passages.title: Lupello
passages.text: What will Master Shang say when he finds out?

passages.title: Lupello
passages.text: I know I should be the one fighting them off. Maybe I'm not cut out for shepherding after all.

passages.title: Mann's Man
passages.text:
<For once, the foreman lowers her voice.>

Look, this ain't easy... I got another favor to ask. My idiot husband, Hao, is a shift lead down at the quarry. I told him not to go back, that it was too dangerous, but he's as stubborn as a hozen and twice as stupid. Says the boys need him around for "moral support."

<Mann sneers.>

What about my moral support?! What am I gonna do if that idiot dies?!

Please... keep an eye out for him. Tell him to come home.

<Her eyes soften before she turns away.>

passages.title: Mann's Man
passages.text:
<Hao looks up at you, struggling to pull himself from the rubble.>

No, no. I got it. HNNGHHH!!

Okay, maybe I don't got it.

passages.title: Trapped!
passages.text:
<Hao struggles against the rubble with all his might.>

HNNNGHHH!!

Let me guess: my wife sent you? Imagine that, my delicate little snow lily all worried. Ha ha! She's always frettin' over me. Look--HNNGHH!!!--it'll take more than a little--HNNGGHHH!!--cave-in to keep ol' Hao down.

Some o' the boys, on the other hand, are in trouble. Help 'em out if you find any, will ya? I'll be fine.

Really.

passages.title: Trapped!
passages.text:
<Hao lets out a hearty laugh.>

I seen 'em come runnin' out o' there like ol' Kher Shan himself were givin' chase.

passages.title: Orders are Orders
passages.text:
Hmm, maybe wikket not so bad after all!

Other baldskins not nice to hozen.

Hozen take this from bad wikkets!

All wikket loot goes to Kah Kah - Chief's orders!

Here, wikket. You take it. Kah Kah will want to meet new hozen friend.

His camp south at Grookin Hill.

passages.title: Orders are Orders
passages.text:
Hmm.

Mean wikkets fighting with nice wikkets?

Hozen fight mean wikkets too!

passages.title: Silly Wikket, Slickies are for Hozen
passages.text:
You think hozen crazy, wikket? Wait til you see hozen with no slickies!

Not enough slickies for hozen and wikkets.

Snappers! Hozen hate them ookin' snappers. Wikkets can eat all the snappers!

<Eekle Eekle points to the south.>

passages.title: Silly Wikket, Slickies are for Hozen
passages.text: Wikket grook all them ookin' snappers?

passages.title: Silly Wikket, Slickies are for Hozen
passages.text:
Now everybody got grub! Great hozen wisdom in Eekle Eekle.

Maybe Eekle Eekle become Chieftain someday...

passages.title: The Warren-Mother
passages.text:
We've dealt with the alpha males. Now, the alpha female.

Virmen aren't terribly selective when it comes to breeding, but most broods will still have a dominant mother figure. She's usually bigger, meaner, and tougher than anyone else in the brood.

You know, I wouldn't mind testing my skills against a warren-mother. Mind if I fight alongside you?

passages.title: The Warren-Mother
passages.text:
That should take care of the virmen for a few weeks, at least. Enough time for Mudmug to get out a few good batches of beer, uninterrupted.

And isn't that what's really important?

passages.title: Legacy
passages.text: I'd say we've earned our reward. I can't wait to taste what Mudmug's been brewing.

passages.title: Legacy
passages.text:
I know Uncle Chen's coming back. I'm not worried.

Actually, this is probably my big chance to finally explore Pandaria! No fat uncle tying me down!

passages.title: Green-ish Energy
passages.text:
One word: Methane!

We're going green. Clean burning, high availability, all natural, and will keep the druids off my back when we get back to our neck of the world.

That, and I ran out of blasting powder...

So, I need your help, <name>.

No, no, I wouldn't ask you to do the dirty work - especially not in front of the general. I'll collect these 'deposits' myself.

You gather up some wood for an outhouse - I'm thinking long-term here!

passages.title: Green-ish Energy
passages.text: Gotta watch out for the wet ones...whewee!

passages.title: Green-ish Energy
passages.text: Ah, the smell of progress, and methane.

passages.title: Stemming the Swarm
passages.text:
I'm not from here. I've never even BEEN here before today. But even I can tell you that something's wrong.

That wall over there was built to keep mantid off of pandaren lands. Now, the mantid are sending their winged scouts over the top, as if the wall wasn't even there!

The only reason those spindly scouts aren't dying is because they're attacking farmers, not soldiers. They wouldn't stand a chance against someone like you.

passages.title: Stemming the Swarm
passages.text: If the flying mantid troops have always been able to fly over, why haven't they before now?

passages.title: Stemming the Swarm
passages.text:
Lin asked you to help us out? Rather presumptive of her.

Still, we are short-manned. We won't turn down your help... or the girl's. You have our thanks, <class>.

passages.title: They Will Be Mist
passages.text:
The mist in this forest is a constant nuisance - one which I'm glad to hand off to trainees like you. Strange creatures lurk in the mist between these trees, and they must constantly be pushed back.

Consider this part of your training.

passages.title: They Will Be Mist
passages.text: Living outside of society has its advantages. I can focus all my energies on training, without being shackled to the societal conventions of modesty, politics, and basic personal hygiene. Here in the woods, I am free to be myself.

passages.title: They Will Be Mist
passages.text: You follow directions well, <name>.

passages.title: Find the Boy
passages.text:
Have you seen my son, Lo? He was here a moment ago and I told him we were leaving today.

I'm sure he's off trying to woo that young Syra Goldendraft. That is the very reason we need to leave!

No son of mine is going to run off with a Goldendraft!

I'm going to search around here for them.

I do keep catching those two sneaking off to the Arboretum. Any chance you could head out there and look for them?

passages.title: Find the Boy
passages.text:
You seek two lovers blind to the ambitions of their family names. They were here, seeking a way to hold to their path.

Sadly they did not find their answers among the trees or art.

passages.title: Shrine of the Dawn
passages.text:
The "children" you seek are not actually children but grown pandaren, despite what their elders might claim. Their love will not be held in check by the feuds of their families.

You will find both Syra and Lo at the Shrine of the Dawn, ever seeking an answer to their dilemma amongst the pandriarchs of old.

passages.title: Shrine of the Dawn
passages.text: Oh stranger! Please tell me you can help us. They really hurt my Lo.

passages.title: The Librarian's Quandary
passages.text:
Lorewalker Stonestep is in charge of the entire temple library. Lately, something has been troubling him and his work.

With thousands of ancient tomes to be transcribed, I can't afford to have him distracted.

Would you follow the path south to the library and see what ails him?

passages.title: The Librarian's Quandary
passages.text:
The Elder Sage Rain-Zhu sent you?

Very well. You shall help me.

passages.title: The Rider's Bind
passages.text:
Have you seen the young serpents in the training yard?

The littles ones tend to be mischievous, and some of them ran off to play before the training session.

The Mistress will get angry if she discovers they're missing.

Would you go find them and bring them back to me? I don't want them to get into trouble.

They like to play out in the open, so look for them in courtyards and around the spires.

passages.title: The Rider's Bind
passages.text: I hope they didn't give you too much trouble.

passages.title: The Rider's Bind
passages.text:
You found them and brought them all back!

They've really taken a liking to you.

Thank you so much!

passages.title: The Jade Serpent
passages.text:
You came to deliver a message to the Jade Serpent, right?

<The little girl tilts her head up at you inquisitively.>

I guess it's time you met her.

passages.title: The Jade Serpent
passages.text: Did you deliver your message?

passages.title: Moth-Ridden
passages.text:
Moths have infested the library. Moths!

Any librarian worth his letters knows that moths are the most dangerous threat to paper, second only to bookworms.

As it turns out, my assistants are a useless bunch of insect-fearing cowards.

Please, you MUST help me get rid of the moths immediately! The works of a thousand pandaren storytellers depend on you!

passages.title: Moth-Ridden
passages.text: I can see the moths eating the pages from here!

passages.title: Moth-Ridden
passages.text: Yes, yes, thank you! You've thinned out their numbers wonderfully.

passages.title: Lighting Up the Sky
passages.text:
Do you like fireworks, <sir/miss>?

I love them! In older times we would set them off to frighten away demons, but I just like them because they're pretty!

I think there are still some old launchers lying around the temple.

Would you go set off some big fireworks for me? It would make me so happy!

passages.title: Lighting Up the Sky
passages.text:
Yay! I saw the fireworks all the way from over here!

Thank you so much, <name>.

passages.title: Out of Sprite
passages.text:
Just to be clear, what happened was an accident. What I did, I did for INDUSTRY!

There was no way I could have known that a sprite invasion would happen at any time, or that one of them would try to eat my new "Pan's Miracle Gro" formula.

Now not only do they have a big sprite leading them, but he's one angry beast.

If I pay you, will you take him out?

passages.title: Out of Sprite
passages.text: Oh why? Why did I have to tamper with the natural order of things? All I wanted was to make these grains grow faster and more numerous.

passages.title: Out of Sprite
passages.text:
Now that that's over I have some ideas on how to make a new concoction. We'll see.

Thank you for your help. Here is your reward.

passages.title: Chen's Resolution
passages.text:
You know what? I don't have to take this.

I'll show that Uncle Gao what it means to be a real brewer. I'll brew the best beer he's ever tasted, with ingredients I've never even used before.

I'm Chen Stormstout, and I'm the best brewer alive.

passages.title: Chen's Resolution
passages.text: Let's make some beer.

passages.title: The Chen Taste Test
passages.text:
Uncle Chen is going to love this. Or... he might tell us to find something sweeter. He's kind of dumb like that.

Let's get this grain back to him at Halfhill.

passages.title: The Chen Taste Test
passages.text: Ah! Now these are some beautifully malted grains. The two of you have a good eye and nose.

passages.title: Hop Hunting
passages.text:
With Li Li fetching grain, and Mudmug handling our water, all we need is hops, and some good wood barrels. I'll handle the barrels... but I need you to gather the hops.

I don't know much about the hops from this land, but I'm sure the nearby farmers have something worth brewing with. Go see what you can rustle up.

passages.title: Stormstout's Hops
passages.text: All three farmers have delivered their hops to Halfhill. Perhaps you should check in with Chen to make sure that he received them.

passages.title: Stormstout's Hops
passages.text:
Look at all these hops! This is quality stuff, too.

We're making headway, <name>. Soon we'll have all the ingredients to finally start brewing.

passages.title: The Farmer's Daughter
passages.text:
Brave <class>, you could not have arrived at a better time. My daughter is missing!

I've got a suspicion that the virmen took her down into that stinking little warren of theirs. I'm too old to fight virmen, and my farmhand is already exhausted from fighting them off all morning.

Could you look for her?

passages.title: The Farmer's Daughter
passages.text:
No... no... get back... I don't want...

Wait, you're not a carrot. You're not a virmen either. You're here to save me?

passages.title: No Plan Survives Contact with the Enemy
passages.text:
Quickly and quietly; that's how SI:7 prefers to operate. That was the plan, at least.

Rell Nightwind is already inside Garrosh'ar Point looking for signs of Anduin and Taylor, but it's getting hot in there and he needs support.

Fight yer way through these dogs and find Rell!

passages.title: No Plan Survives Contact with the Enemy
passages.text: This place is crawling with Horde soldiers - we can't advance on their leader with so many at our backs.

passages.title: No Plan Survives Contact with the Enemy
passages.text: Great work! If you ever decide to give up your life of adventure, the SI:7 could use more talent like you...

passages.title: The Emperor
passages.text:
We have everything we need. It's time to start brewing.

Pay attention, <name>... you might learn a thing or two.

passages.title: The Emperor
passages.text: It takes more than three seconds to make beer, <name>. Even when your name is Chen Stormstout.

passages.title: The Emperor
passages.text: Thanks for waiting so long. You are as patient as you are brave.

passages.title: The Fanciest Water
passages.text:
I've heard lots of cockamamie rumors about this here brewery. I thought they were all false... until I saw that giant hozen.

So, it got me thinkin', what if the other rumors are true? I heard this one rumor just the other day about some water sprites that run around inside the brewery, causin' a ruckus and whatnot. Their bodies are actually MADE OF WATER.

I reckon a man could make some mighty fine beer with some fancy water like that. If you find any, could you bring me some?

passages.title: The Fanciest Water
passages.text: This is gonna be great. It'll be just like makin' beer, but instead of water, I'm gonna use water sprite meat.

passages.title: The Fanciest Water
passages.text:
Looks like plain ol' water to me. It's hard to believe it's actually the corpse of a real, honest-to-goodness walkin'-around living thing.

Can't wait to turn it into beer and drink it.

passages.title: Barrels, Man
passages.text:
I can't believe that giant hozen! He's just throwing barrels everywhere!

Barrels, man!

It looks like he managed to get pretty much all the pandaren that were working out in front of the brewery. If I were you, I'd help some of them break out. Put some of those ridiculous muscles to use.

We're headed over to the brewery's rear entrance, to the east. Meet you there!

passages.title: Barrels, Man
passages.text: What is it with monkeys and barrels, anyway?

passages.title: Finding Yi-Mo
passages.text:
My nephew, Yi-Mo, has always been sort of a downer. When this wave of despair hit the town, he took it harder than most. He sat around for days refusing to eat, just staring off into the horizon.

Now he's wandered off toward the cliffs northeast of here, where the thunderbirds nest and hunt.

Please, <class>, will you look for him?

passages.title: Finding Yi-Mo
passages.text: <Yi-Mo lets out a long sigh.>

passages.title: Finding Yi-Mo
passages.text: Let me guess: my aunt sent you?

passages.title: Skitterer Stew
passages.text:
Leza has a fever. No mother in labor should have a fever.

Mama Bramblestaff once told me that Skitterer Stew could heal almost any illness. Let us put this knowledge to the test.

Gather some intact skitterer glands for me while I get the herbs we'll need and I'll whip up a batch.

passages.title: Skitterer Stew
passages.text: Even the jungle air is alive with danger.

passages.title: Skitterer Stew
passages.text:
Excellent! Nothing clears a sickness like Skitterer Stew.

Here, take this. It's a little memento of Mama Bramblestaff.

passages.title: Blind Them!
passages.text:
These sunwalkers are a tiresome lot. I need soldiers with horde blood in their veins and honor in their hearts. Not some pacifist sun spirit filth.

The Alliance are here, adventurer. Followed us no doubt, or somehow tracked the same visions Leza had that led us here. It doesn't matter. I don't want them to know how divided we are at the moment. Go kill their scout south of here before it can report back.

Hellscream's eyes upon you.

passages.title: Blind Them!
passages.text: Well done, <name>. You have performed admirably and bought us some time to fortify our defenses. Now if I can just get Dezco to go on the offensive.

passages.title: The Mogu Agenda
passages.text:
Mogu don't often gather in numbers like this. We should find out what they are up to.

I thought I heard someone shouting orders near the center of the ruins.

We should probably see if he has information.

passages.title: The Mogu Agenda
passages.text:
The mogu once ruled as emperors, subjugating all races they encountered.

It would seem these particular mogu have aspirations of reliving the past.

passages.title: The Mogu Agenda
passages.text:
Wait. This document talks about the Pools of Youth!

The pools exist?!

passages.title: Life
passages.text:
My child is coming. I must help as I may.

Stay nearby, hero. If my wife and child survive, I would have them look on the face of the one who saved them.

passages.title: Life
passages.text: I pray to An'she that my wife and child survive this journey.

passages.title: Life
passages.text:
She... she died. For all the powers the Light has given me, I was unable to save her.

Thanks to your help, however... we saved my sons.

passages.title: For the Tribe
passages.text:
We fell back to the refuge when the mogu attacked but lost a number of our people along the way.

Travel west and north of here and look for any captives you can rescue that could help us in our fight.

Leave any Alliance you find to their fate.

passages.title: For the Tribe
passages.text: Hellscream's eyes upon you.

passages.title: For the Tribe
passages.text: We've already lost so many. I refuse to lose any more.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text:
I tried to save as many of the Stoneplow envoys as I could but these "mantid" dragged many of them off into the jungle.

These are civilians in need of our help.

Please take the herbs you gathered earlier. I've infused them with what gifts of the Light are still granted me. Use them on as many of the Stoneplow envoys as you can.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text: A sunwalker's first duty is to preserve and protect life.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text:
The civilians are trickling in thanks to you. These "mantid" creatures are a serious threat. We will need to rally our forces soon to help.

One of the envoys asked me to give this to you as a token of thanks.

passages.title: The Greater Danger
passages.text:
I apologize for my harsh words earlier. Dezco might have been right to wait and move west with a unified strength.

The mogu hit us hard when we were searching the ruins west of here. They ambushed us using summoning portals and some dark magics. I haven't seen such evil sorcery used since Outland. 

We need a respite. Head west, kill their summoners, cut their supply line.

passages.title: The Greater Danger
passages.text: Did you break their reinforcements?

passages.title: The Greater Danger
passages.text: With their reinforcements severed we can begin to mount an offensive against their Lord Reclaimer.

passages.title: Striking the Rain
passages.text:
Now as for that "striking the rain" part... well, sometimes you have to.

"Hope is the sun behind a stormy sky - ever in the heart, but veiled to the eye."

There seems to be no end to the sha pouring out of the temple. But in order to see beyond the veil of despair, you must carve through it.

With any luck, you'll find a sun behind the clouds...

passages.title: Striking the Rain
passages.text: We shouldn't press further into the temple before clearing out some of the sha presence outside.

passages.title: Striking the Rain
passages.text: You know something, <name>? We make a pretty good team!

passages.title: The Arcanic Oubliette
passages.text:
An Alliance member? Here? Elune be praised.

My team has encountered a snag. We opened a portal to this land using some ancient scrolls we had found that predated Azshara's rule.

Unfortunately, the coordinates provided on the tablets were warded and the portal that meant to take us to our destination landed us in this oubliette.

We have been trapped here for days, and it is slowly leaching our energies to power itself.

Can you find the nearby shackles that bind the oubliette and disable them?

passages.title: The Arcanic Oubliette
passages.text:
Fabulous! Your timing was impeccable. Another day in there and I think we would have wasted away to nothing.

Now we can continue our search for the Pools of Youth!

passages.title: Where are the Pools
passages.text:
Perhaps these mogu know where the pools are.

Our scouts have reported seeing a commander along the southern side of the Ruins of Dojan.

Kill him and take whatever information he is carrying. They should lead you to the pool.

passages.title: Where are the Pools
passages.text:
<You sense the presence of Lorekeeper Vaeldrin, then hear his voice within your mind.>

Hmm. I'm still not sure about these references to "torture" regarding the Pools of Youth.

passages.title: Where are the Pools
passages.text:
Well done, <name>. Hmm, it looks like the mogu are here to collect ancient relics and weapons from their forgotten dynasty. That is a problem we can face later though.

Ah! Here is a reference to the Pools of Youth.

passages.title: Immortality?
passages.text:
Something is... off. The water feels strange.

When we arrived here I felt the presence of the Light, strong and vibrant, far to the north.

I thought it would be the Pools of Youth. But this... this water is tainted somehow. Stained with mogu magics.

I think it best I try only a sip and we see what happens.

passages.title: Immortality?
passages.text: Wha... what happened? The water... it... it only transfers life. It will not make new life.

passages.title: Squirmy Delight
passages.text:
The hidden master may have to wait. Look at these people, adventurer.

They are so THIN! They must be starving.

You know what we need? A big steaming bowl of Squirmy Delight.

If you find yourself near a river, try rounding up some intact skitterer glands and I'll cook up a batch.

passages.title: Squirmy Delight
passages.text: Mama Bramblestaff always said Squirmy Delight will cure any hunger one way or another.

passages.title: Squirmy Delight
passages.text: Ha! With this I can make a stew potent enough to knock these waifish elves on their feet.

passages.title: Lotus Tea
passages.text:
The mogu really like their poisons and curses. Mama Bramblestaff always said lotus tea cures any mogu curse.

I saw some imperial lotus plants in the nearby Ruins of Dojan. We should go gather some of their leaves and keep them on hand just in case the mogu get unruly.

Also, this will give me a chance to introduce my fists to some mogu faces.

passages.title: Lotus Tea
passages.text: I have never seen the mogu this numerous before. They have always been a nuisance but never this bad.

passages.title: Lotus Tea
passages.text: That's it! You pick, I punch!

passages.title: No Sister Left Behind
passages.text:
We were searching the ruins south of here when the mogu fell upon us out of nowhere.

Some of us were able to retreat to this encampment but many others were captured. The mogu have also caught a number of the Horde who happened to be in the area as well.

Please, adventurer, rescue any sentinels that you can.

Leave the Dawnchasers to their fate.

passages.title: No Sister Left Behind
passages.text: There are so few of us, it is a great relief to see such help.

passages.title: Sever Their Supply Line
passages.text:
The mogu reclaimers are using portals to connect to Kun-Lai Summit, bringing in reinforcements and supplies.

What is worse, they are sending their captives through these portals.

Go to the Ruins of Korja and destroy as many of these Korjan Reclaimers as you can find.

passages.title: Sever Their Supply Line
passages.text: You have bought us some much needed breathing room to lick our wounds and prepare a counter-attack.

passages.title: The Lord Reclaimer
passages.text:
They have my daughter! Brojai... that Lord Reclaimer! I can see him clearly through Lyalia's eyes.

That foolish girl must have tried to take him head on.

Please, adventurer! Go to the Ruins of Korja and try to free her.

I'll get Kang and try to draw out Brojai from the ruins with a distraction.

passages.title: The Lord Reclaimer
passages.text: Lyalia is the only family I have left. I had to bury her mother during the war of Ahn'Qiraj.

passages.title: The Lord Reclaimer
passages.text:
Thank you for avenging my daughter. I am not willing to let her stay dead however.

I still have the waters of youth.

passages.title: Going on the Offensive
passages.text:
Ha! So my father just wasted twenty years of our lives on a fool's errand!

I'm taking charge.

When Tyrande sent us here she was very specific that we not come back until we find the source of the Light that she saw in her visions. It's obvious now that the Pools of Youth were not it.

I want you to look for my scout. I sent her to investigate the Crane Temple but she hasn't returned.

Get her report and rendezvous with us at the Sentinel Basecamp further west.

passages.title: Going on the Offensive
passages.text: Did you find the scout?

passages.title: Going on the Offensive
passages.text: <name>, well timed as usual. It turns out the mogu know how to use portals as well.

passages.title: Hope Springs Eternal
passages.text:
The Shado-Pan are likely dealing with similar outbreaks elsewhere in Pandaria.

Seek out Loon Mai, the Shado-Pan Watch Commander in Stoneplow on the western end of the Valley of the Four Winds. Let him know that we have the situation here under control; the Shado-Pan need not send any aid.

Quite the opposite, in fact - I will be sending many of my followers on pilgrimage, to bring a message of hope to those in need.

Thank you again, adventurer. Farewell.

passages.title: Hope Springs Eternal
passages.text:
Finally, some good news. I will send a falcon to Winter's Blossom right away and let them know the Temple of the Red Crane is safe.

Between the sha outbreak and the increasing aggression of the mantid, our forces are being stretched thin.

passages.title: Blind Them!
passages.text:
Horde sunwalkers! We saw one of their scouts patrolling by the oubliette not long before you arrived.

I don't know how he got here but I can guarantee you he isn't alone. They never are.

Kill the sunwalker scout before he reports our position.

passages.title: Blind Them!
passages.text:
Sunwalkers are not to be trusted. They are the most militant branch of the tauren armies within the horde.

Thank you for your help in this, <name>. Please accept this token as a reward.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text:
Leza now walks with the ancestors of this strange land. I must look now to the living.

Kor has led a group of our scouts west deeper into the jungle.

Track him down and lend what aid you can to him. We will join you as quickly as we are able.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text:
<name>! Well timed!

We were laying an ambush for the Alliance in the ruins west of here when the mogu ambushed us. They are using mage portals to call in reinforcements.

passages.title: Going on the Offensive
passages.text:
Ha! So my father just wasted twenty years of our lives on a fool's errand!

I'm taking charge.

When Tyrande sent us here she was very specific that we not come back until we find the source of the Light that she saw in her visions. It's obvious now that the Pools of Youth were not it.

We are pressing westward and could use your help.

Meet us at the Sentinel Basecamp further west when you are ready.

passages.title: Going on the Offensive
passages.text: <name>, well timed as usual. It turns out the mogu know how to use portals as well.

passages.title: Sufficient Motivation
passages.text:
Training these savages has been quite a task, <name>.

Finding ways to motivate them was easy enough; the problem is keeping them motivated.. and focused... and awake.

Now that you're back, you can help me in getting the less disciplined Hozen moving, if you catch my drift. I'll leave the method up to you.

passages.title: Sufficient Motivation
passages.text: Are the Hozen ready to deploy?

passages.title: Sufficient Motivation
passages.text:
Hrmm, I'll be surprised if we can keep these creatures focused enough to employ any tactics at all, <name>.

They'd better not get in my way when blades begin to fly!

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text:
Oh, before I forget, I have something I was asked to deliver to you. A letter from one of your companions, I assume.

I was made to understand that your presence was urgently required, so I took the liberty of arranging your passage.

Speak to Ginsa Arroweye just south of here when you're ready. She has a kite waiting.

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text: Welcome back, <name>. I trust your journey has been insightful, particularly in regards to the layout of the land. There is still much to do before we march into battle.

passages.title: Residual Fallout
passages.text:
Pandaria is a mystical land, traveler.

It bears repeating that some of its secrets remain hidden, even to Lorewalkers.

Sealing those fissures did not mend what has been broken. If the legends are true, it will take much more to release this land from the grasp of the Sha.

The aggression of that battle awakened a host of living negative emotions. What you see here is likely the first of many such manifestations.

For now, we can only try to diminish their presence here.

passages.title: Residual Fallout
passages.text: This, it seems, is only the tip of the iceberg, <name>.

passages.title: Residual Fallout
passages.text:
This is terrible...

We must find a way to undo what has been done here.

passages.title: Jaded Heart
passages.text:
The more powerful remnants of that horrible manifestation may be too much for you to handle on your own, <name>.

I fear I'd be of little help in terms of actual combat, but I can suggest a solution.

The great jade statue was soon to become a living serpent - one of our revered celestials. Its construction imbued it with special powers that may sufficiently weaken these adversaries.

passages.title: Jaded Heart
passages.text: Do you have the jade, <name>?

passages.title: Jaded Heart
passages.text:
<Cho looks at you despondently.>

This jade was meant for... so much more.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your Admiral Taylor has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house across the way.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
<name>, is that you? I can't believe we survived the destruction of the Jade Serpent.

Some of us anyway.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your Admiral Taylor has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
<name>, is that you? I can't believe we survived the destruction of the Jade Serpent.

Some of us anyway.

passages.title: Eastwind Rest
passages.text:
I am injured, but we can't stop here.

The hozen were... unreliable. The pandaren would be much better allies.

You have seen the refugees in this village, and heard of the yaungol invasion, no?

Well, we've heard from the locals that Eastwind Rest, a nearby village, was destroyed by the Yaungol.

Apparently some survivors have gathered along the road out of town.

Go. Take the road west. Gather the survivors. 

We'll help them rebuild. Then, they will see the advantage of joining the Horde!

passages.title: Eastwind Rest
passages.text: I will not rest until our people are returned and this village rebuilt.

passages.title: Eastwind Rest
passages.text:
Well... we are alive, and that is better than we could have hoped for without your help.

But, if this is truly to become a base of operations for you, and if we are to join your Horde, there is one more thing you must do to guarantee our security.

passages.title: Helping the Cause
passages.text:
Welcome back, <name>! It seems the Jinyu have taken to our training even better than I had hoped. We're in the final stages of our preparations now.

I need someone to go check in with Amber, Bold Karasshi, and Mishka. See if they need any help to complete their training.

You'll find Karasshi and Mishka here in Pearlfin Village. Amber is training recruits in Slingtail Pits to the northwest.

passages.title: Helping the Cause
passages.text: Is everyone in order and ready to move?

passages.title: Helping the Cause
passages.text: Impressive work, <name>. We should be ready to move out shortly. With our allies at our side, there is no way we can be defeated.

passages.title: Farmhand Freedom
passages.text:
Those Ordo yaungol are working my farmhands to death! It just ain't right.

Please, <class>, save them before it's too late.

passages.title: Farmhand Freedom
passages.text: Look, mister, I don't mean to be telling you your business, but I can still see a lot of my farmhands still out there.

passages.title: Farmhand Freedom
passages.text:
Now ain't you just the thing?

Though, I guess it's not fair to force these here workers to stay with us, now that we don't have much work for 'em...

passages.title: Blue Dwarf Needs Food Badly
passages.text:
Oi!

We need ta' get us some food, if we're gonna survive here for long!

Ye' may not know it, but I'm somethin' of a cook me'self. Why don'tcha go out there and fetch us some meaty bits. I can cook 'em up and feed us for weeks! Or, days, at least.

passages.title: Blue Dwarf Needs Food Badly
passages.text: Well... ya' got my meat?

passages.title: Blue Dwarf Needs Food Badly
passages.text: Good work! I'm telliin' ye, these Kun-Lai meaty bits are grade A goodness!

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text:
The admiral's asked me to take care of a major problem, but my specialty's in healing, not fighting!

The pandaren in the camp here have told me that something is animating the statues to the northeast at Mogujia.

Will you help me out, <name>? We can't afford to have a fight with an army of statues right now.

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text: Alright! Looks like we won't have a bunch of statues to worry about any more. Good work, <name>!

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text:
I've got much to do here, <name>. I could use your help.

There's a place to the northwest. The pandaren here call it Mogujia. Something's causing the statues there to animate, and our pandaren friends here are pretty spooked about it.

If they're not dealt with soon, we might have a serious problem. We just moved in. It's not like we can afford to fight a war with an army of statues right now.

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text: Weren't you going to destroy all of those mogu statues so that we don't, you know, get overrun by them?

passages.title: Deanimate the Reanimated
passages.text: Oh, you dealt with the statues? Good work. Here's something for your trouble.

passages.title: The Swarm Begins
passages.text:
Without the wall to protect us, we barely stand a chance. If you hadn't gathered so many people to help us, we wouldn't have a prayer.

Check in with Captain Oakenshield - he should be up near the break in the wall. Kill as many mantid as you can on the way there.

If we win, we win. If we lose, we go down fighting. For Pandaria!

passages.title: The Swarm Begins
passages.text: Look at the SIZE of that thing...

passages.title: The Swarm Begins
passages.text: My wall... I spent my life atop that wall...

passages.title: Moving On
passages.text:
Your journey in this land has already proven most eventful, traveler. And mine, it appears, is destined to continue for a time.

A chain of events began when your people arrived here, and while some of those happenings are traumatic to behold, I feel there must be a larger purpose behind your presence.

For now it is wisest that you leave this place and explore Pandaria's other regions.

Speak to me when you are ready to leave.

passages.title: Moving On
passages.text:
Be wise, traveler.

Prove to these inhabitants that there is more to your people than war and destruction.

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Look, I know the Alliance needs recruits, and there's just not enough of us here right now to make a fighting presence of this town.

But I know that the yaungol over at Fire Camp Ordo, to the northwest, have taken many of my people as prisoners. And I also know that if you would be willing to rescue them from their captivity, they'd more than likely be willing to join the Alliance.

What do you say, <name>?

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Well, if it isn't our hero, <name>.

I really wasn't sure we stood a fighting chance out here, you know?

These guys may be a little rough around the edges, but we'll be able to whip 'em into shape. And when we do, we'll have a real fighting chance at holding our own here in Kun-Lai.

Good work.

passages.title: In Tents Channeling
passages.text:
The yaungol of Fire Camp Ordo are a dire threat. I need you to head northwest and take out their leader.

Unfortunately, his four subordinates are maintaining a fire barrier that prevents us from getting to him in the adjoining cave.

Take them out and the shield will come down. You'll find them in their tents, channeling.

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Look, I know the Horde needs recruits, and there's just not enough of us here right now to make a fighting presence of this town.

But I know that the yaungol over at Fire Camp Ordo, to the west, have taken many of my people as prisoners. And I also know that if you would be willing to rescue them from their captivity, they'd more than likely be willing to join the Horde.

What do you say, <name>?

passages.title: Pandaren Prisoners
passages.text:
Well, it looks like we've got ourselves a little army, here, thanks to you.

They may not look like much yet, but a little Horde discipline and we'll have them in fighting shape in no time.

By the way, <name>... good work.

passages.title: In Tents Channeling
passages.text:
The yaungol of Fire Camp Ordo are the worst threat we're facing. I need you to head west and take out their leader.

The coward is hiding in a cave, which is protected by a fire shield cast by his four underlings.

Take them out and the shield will come down. You'll find them in their tents, channeling.

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've taken the shield down at Fire Camp Ordo. Go back there before the shield goes up again.

Time to head into the cave and slay their chief!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text: <name>, what are you doing here? The Ordo Warbringer isn't dead yet!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've done it, <name>! I'm in your debt!

Again!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've taken the shield down at Fire Camp Ordo. Get back over there before they get that shield up again.

Slay the Warbringer of the Ordo!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
Once again you've accomplished what no one else could.

Was there any doubt?

passages.title: The Defense of Shado-Pan Fallback
passages.text:
I sent for reinforcements from the Shado-Pan Monastery, but have heard nothing back. We have already lost the town.

A few lucky villagers may have survived, but we are pinned down here.

We do not have time to entertain strangers. If you can fight, help my men defend this tower. If not, leave, for you will not survive long here.

passages.title: The Defense of Shado-Pan Fallback
passages.text: Have you dealt with the yaungol yet?

passages.title: The Defense of Shado-Pan Fallback
passages.text: You have bought us some time to breathe. We must not despair - instead, we must act.

passages.title: Turnabout
passages.text:
Our true enemies are the sha, not the yaungol.

The sha are emotion manifest. Destructive, yes. But undisciplined. Undisciplined force cannot last. The flood, in dispersion, loses its force. The wildfire burns its fuel.

And, discipline and wisdom can turn their destructive energy against themselves.

Bring me the essences of the sha in the village, and I will explain further.

passages.title: Turnabout
passages.text: Have you harvested their essences?

passages.title: Turnabout
passages.text:
Good. Now you will see how to defeat unbridled rage.

I will craft these into a trap for Kobai, the leader of the yaungol. Though he will be snared, and we will defeat him, he is not our ultimate target...

passages.title: To Winter's Blossom
passages.text:
The battle against the Sha is eternal - we can not leave this place. 

But I am troubled by the absence of reinforcements from the Monastery given that we sent for them days ago. 

You have performed admirably, perhaps you could travel to Winter's Blossom, our base camp on the way to the Shado-Pan Monastery.
