Speak with Lin Silentstrike once you arrive - he should know what is happening. To get there, travel north of the village and follow the road through Shado-Li Basin to Winter's Blossom.

passages.title: To Winter's Blossom
passages.text:
Shado-Master Chong sent you, hmm?

Yes, we received his request for reinforcements.

We are in no position to grant it, however. We've just concluded a battle of our own, and the monastery's been locked up tight. 

We can't even get reinforcements here, and we're just down the hill!

passages.title: Honor, Even in Death
passages.text:
Hmm... If Shado-Master Chong trusted you, perhaps you can help us.

The yaungol are our enemies.

Still, we must prove we are better than they. We will show them honor in death.

As after most battles, the carrion birds have begun gathering. Thin their numbers, so the bodies of our foes will not be desecrated. They've gathered at the battlefield to the west.

passages.title: Honor, Even in Death
passages.text: Killing those birds may not soothe my anger, but at least it proves that we are better than our enemies. They would not do such a thing.

passages.title: Honor, Even in Death
passages.text: Good. After what they have done, I would not show the Yaungol kindness in life. But neither will I allow their bodies to be eaten by the birds.

passages.title: Off the Wall!
passages.text:
The yaungol on the wall here are providing covering fire for the ones below. I don't know what Lao-chen is thinking, but I want you to deal with these archers.

The good news is, up here we've got the spirit of the Ox helping us. When they're weakened, the ox spirit will stun them and you can use it to knock 'em off the wall.

You'll find the archers just out that door.

passages.title: Off the Wall!
passages.text: Come on, come on.

passages.title: Off the Wall!
passages.text: Ha! I could see them flying. Good work.

passages.title: A Terrible Sacrifice
passages.text:
I have an idea, and... am prepared to make a terrible sacrifice.

As much as I know that we need my stout brew, to fortify our defenders for the long-term security of the Ox Gate...

It is too painful to discuss details now, but please - while you are up here defending the wall, gather the barrels of oil they are using to light their arrows. We will need them.

passages.title: A Terrible Sacrifice
passages.text: Do you have the oil?

passages.title: A Terrible Sacrifice
passages.text: Alright. I am off to prepare our next move. Good luck, friend.

passages.title: First Assault
passages.text:
Now that we have had time to assess our enemies' weaknesses, it is time for us to deal the yaungol a direct blow.

Go and confront the Osul Sharphorn up the mesa to the west.

Let them know that we are here, and that we are not scared of their threats.

passages.title: First Assault
passages.text: Well done, <name>. I hope you showed those cretins no mercy.

passages.title: Running Rampant
passages.text:
There is one thing that every army needs, and that is a supply line.

The enemy camp to the west contains a large beast herd, which serves as the yaungol army's main source of food.

Luckily for us, the yaks and mushan beasts of this region are easily scared.

Sneak in, give the beasts a good slap, and watch the results.

passages.title: Running Rampant
passages.text:
Ohohoho! I saw those animals trailing dust from up here.

Those yaungol are probably still wondering what happened.

passages.title: Seeing Red
passages.text:
Ahead of us is the main thrust of the yaungol army.

Here, they prepare their vast army to attack the villages of Kun-Lai.

If we strike at the Osul now, we can cut them at their very core.

Remember, for every of their number that we strike down here, we save one of our own back at home.

passages.title: Seeing Red
passages.text:
That should put a serious dent in their numbers.

I doubt they will be able to recover from such losses.

passages.title: Pitching In
passages.text:
The yaungol's siege weapons - those ballista spearthrowers down there - are tearing apart our defenses both at Longying Oupost and in Kun-Lai Summit.

Those terrible weapons must be destroyed.

Take these explosives. I've covered them in the pitch that you collected.

Toss them at those ballistas, and we'll give the yaungol a little taste of their own medicine.

passages.title: Pitching In
passages.text: Fire is a cruel weapon. Luckily, we are only using it to destroy weapons of war.

passages.title: Pitching In
passages.text:
Good, <class>.

Now that they cannot hide behind their siege weapons, they have no choice but to face us.

passages.title: The Exile
passages.text:
What is there to say, stranger?

I fought Jung Duk and lost. I was the fool to believe he would fight fairly.

Now, my own brothers turned against me, and here I am, speaking to our enemies.

I know you have come for Osul blood.

I only ask that you hunt down the three who betrayed me.

Urang, who poisoned my drink. Ku-Tong, who bent my spear. And Battat, whose dagger slipped into my side as my victory was assured.

Do this, and I can die in peace.

passages.title: The Exile
passages.text:
How could they have betrayed me? They were once my brothers!

Why did they turn on me? WHY?

I hate them! I will slaughter them all!

passages.title: The Exile
passages.text:
It pleases me to know those cowards died at your hands.

Perhaps now, this burning tide in my heart will ebb.

passages.title: In Search of Suna
passages.text:
I have bad news. When I returned, Suna was already gone.

The others say that she took her things and headed down the road to the east, muttering about hunting down the source of the yaungol aggression.

I cannot allow her to venture into dangerous territory alone.

I've already prepared a group of soldiers to push further east.

We are leaving shortly. Hop on the caravan if you wish to travel with the Shado-Pan. You can also meet us there if you wish.

passages.title: In Search of Suna
passages.text: Well, we made it.

passages.title: Dust to Dust
passages.text:
If we are to make camp here, we cannot leave all of these yaungol bodies lying to rot.

Take this torch and set fire to the villagers' corpses.

The incense from the torch should purify the earth and air around them as well.

Even our enemies deserve to be laid to rest.

passages.title: Dust to Dust
passages.text: The stench of death is overpowering.

passages.title: Dust to Dust
passages.text:
Good work, <name>.

Hopefully, their spirits are in a better place.

passages.title: Slaying the Scavengers
passages.text:
The rotting corpses are attracting hyena scavengers.

In addition to spreading diseases from feeding on the dead, the feral creatures will attack us on sight.

Go and eradicate the beasts. It is unfortunate, but ultimately for the best.

passages.title: Slaying the Scavengers
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. It was an unpleasant task, but it had to be done.

passages.title: Totemic Research
passages.text:
As we entered the village, I couldn't help but notice yaungol totems lying around this camp.

I have a suspicion that there are dark forces at work here, and those totems may be the key to drawing them out.

Could you bring me some of these totems for further inspection? I would like to study them.

passages.title: Totemic Research
passages.text: I do believe the totems could be of use to us.

passages.title: Totemic Research
passages.text:
I was right! These totems were once used to store and conduct immense magical energies.

I do believe I can use them once again to do the same.

passages.title: Last Toll of the Yaungol
passages.text:
Ban has asked me to explore the village to determine what happened here.

I noticed smoke rising up from the east, the west, northwest, and the south.

I need someone I trust to watch my back.

What do you say? Want to help me on my first scouting mission?

passages.title: Last Toll of the Yaungol
passages.text: Something terrible must have happened here.

passages.title: Last Toll of the Yaungol
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <name>.

We cannot know exactly what happened here, but it's clear that something caused the yaungol to turn on one another.

What kind of power could do this?

passages.title: Spiteful Spirits
passages.text:
The spirits of the fallen villagers have risen! I can feel the hatred emanating from the spirits.

<name>, if we are to survive here, we must defend ourselves. This is the only way we can put them to rest.

passages.title: Spiteful Spirits
passages.text: The air is thick with their malicious intent.

passages.title: Spiteful Spirits
passages.text: Well done. We cannot bring them retribution, but at least we can end their rage.

passages.title: The Point of No Return
passages.text:
One of our rangers reported seeing Suna up the hill to the northwest.

I am relieved to find her safe. I had feared what she would do in her grief.

Would you go speak to her on my behalf?

Take this totem with you. If you encounter any danger along the way, you may find it useful.

passages.title: The Point of No Return
passages.text:
If I could change the past, I would. If I could take Lin's place, I would.

In a thousand lifetimes, I will never be able to repay Suna's loss, or share even a measure of her grief.

passages.title: The Point of No Return
passages.text:
What? She was possessed by the Sha of Hatred?

No. NO!

Despite our differences, she was one of us. Today, the Shado-Pan has lost a dear sister.

Her death will not be in vain. I will not rest until I have defeated the Sha of Hatred!

Suna, I swear this to you!

passages.title: A Foot in the Door
passages.text:
<Lord Taran immediately pins you down with his steely gaze.>

<class>, you bear the marks of many a past battle.

Good! We need more seasoned people like you to hold back the front.

We've managed to secure a foothold here, but the yaungol are desperate to remove our presence.

If you wish to prove your worth, go down the hill and show the yaungol that we will not back down.

passages.title: A Foot in the Door
passages.text: We are slowly gaining ground.

passages.title: A Foot in the Door
passages.text:
Good. I can see that you are capable.

I hope to rely on your talents for what is to come.

passages.title: Behind the Battlefront
passages.text:
This battlefront has been undermanned and unsupplied for too long during my absence in Kun-Lai. We need to get things back in order here before we can pick up the trail of the Sha of Hatred.

Taoshi is my best. I've sent her north to investigate rumors of mantid that have somehow made it through the battlefront. I need someone I can trust to get out there and work with her to plug any holes in our defenses.

If my reports on you are correct, I can trust you with this, right <class>?

passages.title: Behind the Battlefront
passages.text: You look capable. Taran knows to send me the best. I like that.

passages.title: Unwelcome Intruders
passages.text:
Those are mantid scouts down there. Gao-Ran's Battlefront is meant to keep them out of eastern Townlong Steppes. If we allow them north of the barricade, we may lose our foothold here.

Let's clear them out. I'll be with you.

passages.title: Unwelcome Intruders
passages.text: This is where they're getting through, the eastern pass.

passages.title: Trap Setting
passages.text:
Good to meet you, <class>. We have traps all along the pass to help us catch mantid that might be sneaking through, but their numbers have been so great that most of the traps have already been triggered.

Taoshi said you might be able to reset some of them while you're out there. Can you help?

passages.title: Trap Setting
passages.text: These traps have been very effective, the mantid numbers are just getting out of hand in these past weeks.

passages.title: Trap Setting
passages.text: We could use a few more capable men like you around the camp. Thank you for your help, <class>.

passages.title: Back on Their Feet
passages.text:
<name>, I could use your help. With their long shifts, our warriors down at the southern front of the battlefront are fighting to the point of exhaustion, and many of them have been exposed to the mantid poison.

We need more people to tend to the wounded. I've prepared some bandages with the herbs you brought me, but if you have some healing skills, those might work even better.

Please, <name>, get our men back on their feet so that they can get back here to safety.

passages.title: Back on Their Feet
passages.text:
With the constant mantid attacks, the men are being worked to the bone. We are undermanned on all fronts.

Your help means a lot to us, <name>.

passages.title: Back on Their Feet
passages.text: There are several warriors that owe their lives to you. You have my deepest appreciation, <class>.

passages.title: The Endless Swarm
passages.text: Gao-ran's men need help down on the southern front. If you want to stand by the Shado-Pan, that's where you should do it.

passages.title: The Endless Swarm
passages.text: The men of the battlefront are growing to respect you. You clearly know how to fight.

passages.title: Thieves and Troublemakers
passages.text:
I can't catch the little buggers for the life of me.

Kill any you can get your hands on. And keep a close eye on your valuables, they like to steal anything that isn't tied down.

passages.title: Thieves and Troublemakers
passages.text: I haven't hated plants so much since my job back at Halfhill.

passages.title: Thieves and Troublemakers
passages.text:
I guess you're a bit faster than me. Well, thanks.

I'll try to finish collecting some orbs and get them back to camp while there's still some face to save.

passages.title: Cutting the Swarm
passages.text:
The mantid numbers have been increasing since you left for the cleft. Let's put these orbs you gathered to use.

Get down on the battlefront and man one of the cannons. Let none through.

passages.title: Cutting the Swarm
passages.text: I can't remember the last time they swarmed this thickly. They probably haven't within my lifetime.

passages.title: Cutting the Swarm
passages.text: We're not done yet...

passages.title: Terror of the Dread Wastes
passages.text:
That thing is huge!

The Shado-Pan holding the battlefront were never trained for something like this... let's get down there and take it out ourselves.

passages.title: Terror of the Dread Wastes
passages.text:
You. You're coming with me.

I've never seen someone handle themselves on the battlefield like that. I need a strong <class> like you with me when we face the Sha of Hatred.

passages.title: Along the Southern Front
passages.text:
I'm heading westward with Taoshi to gather the strongest I can find to confront the Sha of Hatred.

I would like you to come with me.

passages.title: Along the Southern Front
passages.text: Let's get this taken care of so we can get down to the bridge.

passages.title: Returning from the Pass
passages.text:
I still have some cleanup to do here in the pass - there are some mantid still making it through. You're a valuable person to have at hand though, and I know Taran wouldn't appreciate me keeping you longer for such basic work.

Taran should still be in the main camp with Gao-Ran. Report back in. I'll catch up with you a bit later.

passages.title: Returning from the Pass
passages.text: Welcome back. I heard about the breaches in the eastern pass. It sounds like I put the right people on the job.

passages.title: The Sha of Hatred
passages.text:
The end of our hunt is upon us. We have gathered the strongest the Shado-Pan have to offer, and with your strength to aid us, we will defeat the Sha of Hatred and choke out its influence on the world.

When we enter the tunnel, stay close, and keep hatred clear from your heart. The fight ahead will put all of us to the test.

Whatever happens, it has been an honor traveling beside you, <name>.

passages.title: The Sha of Hatred
passages.text:
Defeating a Sha... is not an easy thing. It is a miracle that we came out of this unscathed.

Taran still blames himself for letting his hatred get the best of him and setting this beast loose upon the land. It may take some time for him to come to terms with this, but it is important that he does, lest he be vulnerable again.

We accomplished a great thing this day, a thing that will not soon be forgotten.

And neither shall you for your hand in this.  Thank you.

passages.title: Enraged By Hatred
passages.text:
These scorpions are infected with sha. It seems to have driven them out of their hole and into our camp, seething with hatred at invaders in their territory.

We need to clear the scorpions and secure the camp. Kill any you find.

passages.title: Enraged By Hatred
passages.text: The Sha of Hatred's passing did this to them. I doubt this is the only thing that will have been affected by its passing.

passages.title: Enraged By Hatred
passages.text: Good. What's left of the camp will be a bit safer.

passages.title: Taking Stock
passages.text:
I was dispatched back to camp to gather pitch-tipped arrows for our archers at the bridge, and this is what I came to. I trained with most of these pandaren... I wasn't prepared for this.

Still, the archers at the bridge need our help. If you could help gather arrows from the wreckage, then maybe we can salvage something from this horror.

passages.title: Taking Stock
passages.text: The pandaren at the bridge are depending on us...

passages.title: Taking Stock
passages.text: I... you... er, thank you. You didn't have to help, but you did. Thank you.

passages.title: Up In Flames
passages.text:
The mantid coming across the bridge have thick carapaces that shrug off most of our attacks. They have a weakness though: fire.

Lao-Chen's men brought kegs to the battlefield for exactly this purpose. Kick the kegs into groups of mantid, and Lao-Chin's archers will light them up.

They should be easy to finish off from there.

passages.title: Up In Flames
passages.text: Creative solution.  Lao-Chin impresses.

passages.title: Up In Flames
passages.text: We have the added benefit that the mantid will leave with broken morale after watching their brethren burn to death.  Grim, but many lives will be spared if they simply stop pressing our lines.

passages.title: Joining the Hunt
passages.text:
We are one stronger. Your help is invaluable.

Let's move on westward to Rensai's Watchpost to find the last member for our party.

passages.title: Joining the Hunt
passages.text:
We are close. I can feel the unnatural hatred surging.

It's a testament to the training of the Shado-Pan that the forces here have not been consumed by its influence.

passages.title: Grounded Welcome
passages.text:
All of my men are down at Farwatch Overlook to the southwest, holding off mantid that are trying to fly across the chasm. As long as my marksmen have arrows, they'll ground any mantid that clear the chasm.

If you're here to help, I could use some more men clearing the mantid out once they're on the ground. Are you willing, <class>?

passages.title: Grounded Welcome
passages.text: Your efforts are appreciated, <class>. Even a few more moment's breath between attacks are a relief these days.

passages.title: Hostile Skies
passages.text:
We're about to get hit hard... 

Pick up that cannon there and lend a hand, if you would. There will be no shortage of targets.

passages.title: Hostile Skies
passages.text: I could really use you on that cannon...

passages.title: Hostile Skies
passages.text:
Excellent shooting!

I'm pretty sure that big bug survived the fall though...

passages.title: Devastation Below
passages.text: Let's get down there and finish that big bug off, you and I.

passages.title: Devastation Below
passages.text:
Where have you been all my life?!  That was amazing!

I'd be proud to fight beside you any day.

passages.title: Taoshi and Korvexxis
passages.text:
Taoshi is setting up an ambush for one of the mantid leaders on the south side of Sik'vess. She is tasked with retrieving his crystal so that we can use it to open the door.

Two are stronger than one. I want you there to make sure it goes smoothly.

passages.title: Taoshi and Korvexxis
passages.text: Our hunt is nearly over...

passages.title: Taoshi and Korvexxis
passages.text: The first crystal is ours...

passages.title: Finish This!
passages.text:
We've heard back from Suna, on the wall. Something's going on...

It looks like they are preparing for their final push. It's time to finish this, friend.

passages.title: Finish This!
passages.text: Lin is captured... we must break Taran Zhu from his complacence!

passages.title: Finish This!
passages.text:
Well, their lieutenant is dead. I think we have finally pushed them out of Kun-Lai. 

But at what cost? So many dead, Lin captured... I will not allow Taran Zhu to continue to ignore his charge.

passages.title: Psycho Mantid
passages.text:
You aren't going to believe what I saw! Two mantid fighting each other, whipping some serious magic back and forth.

One of them didn't look like any mantid I've ever seen. Completely different color and dress to him, like some kind of... oracle or something. The other one was a total psycho, splashing sha energy around like it was a keg of Stormstout Special.

Look, I gotta get back to my post, but those two are still fighting in the cave behind me and I have a feeling it's a big deal. Check it out?

passages.title: Psycho Mantid
passages.text: The empress... is... misguided.

passages.title: Psycho Mantid
passages.text:
<This mantid is severely wounded. He barely manages to choke forth his words between wheezing gasps for breath.>

Hold, <race>...

We are... not your enemy.

passages.title: Feeding the Beast
passages.text:
I must join the Klaxxi Council and the other paragons immediately, but I am barely strong enough to stand.

I must feed, Wakener.

I sense the beating hearts of creatures on the northern bank of the lake.

Kill them for me, and I shall do the rest.

passages.title: Feeding the Beast
passages.text: I have been sleeping for many thousands of years. I must regain my strength before rejoining the Council.

passages.title: Feeding the Beast
passages.text: I feel the strength returning to my body.

passages.title: Choking the Skies
passages.text:
Nurong wants me to pass out torches for burning the bodies.

The flying mantid are fragile, and won't last long in the hot smoke.

passages.title: Choking the Skies
passages.text: Some of them can make it through the smoke, but in small enough numbers that we can easily pick them off.

passages.title: Choking the Skies
passages.text: Your help is appreciated, stranger.

passages.title: Lao-Chin and Serevex
passages.text:
Lao-Chin is facing off against the leader just above the entrance in the tree, on the north side of Sik'vess. He is to bring back the second crystal that we need to get into the mantid tunnel.

Go there and lend him your aid.

passages.title: Lao-Chin and Serevex
passages.text: We have the second crystal then. Good.

passages.title: Nurong and Rothek
passages.text:
Hawkmaster Nurong has gone ahead to the northwest of Sik'vess to make sure the last mantid leader cannot escape.

Catch up with him and help him kill the mantid leader. Nurong will bring back the final crystal once you've aided him in this.

passages.title: Nurong and Rothek
passages.text: Act swiftly. I do not want the Sha of Hatred to escape our grasp again.

passages.title: Nurong and Rothek
passages.text: The final crystal is ours. We are on the doorstep of our final confrontation.

passages.title: Buried Beneath
passages.text:
Taoshi set up a spyglass on the ridge edge to show me what her scouting uncovered.

Go over and take a look.

passages.title: Buried Beneath
passages.text: Go. Look.

passages.title: Buried Beneath
passages.text: Our tasks lay before us.

passages.title: The Heavens Hum With War
passages.text:
The mantid don't ever make my job easy, but now they've gone too far.

We can fend off the occasional attack from Kor'vess, but now... now they're starting to surround us. What's worse, they're draining the amber from our tree.

This will not stand! We need that amber! To make beer!

They've dug a burrow into the south side of the tree. I'm short-handed here. Could you take care of them for me?

passages.title: The Heavens Hum With War
passages.text: Azzix, his name was. I think. Azzix K'tai.

passages.title: The Heavens Hum With War
passages.text: We're not here to hurt anybody. We just want to make a little bit of brew out of this tree sap. Is that too much to ask?

passages.title: Bound With Wood
passages.text:
<Vu eyes the recipe.>

Hmm... "bound with wood". We don't typically brew with wood. Sap, yes... but not wood.

We have, on rare occasions, infused our drinks with corewood from the treants to the west of here. Most of them have fallen to the mantid... but their remains should suffice for our recipe.

passages.title: Bound With Wood
passages.text:
We don't brew with wood here. It gives the brew a harsh, insipid flavor, not unlike that of wine.

<Vu spits.>

passages.title: Bound With Wood
passages.text:
I'll get these pieces prepared.

We've already gathered quite a few of these ingredients! I'll have to get a pot boiling soon.

passages.title: Wood and Shade
passages.text:
"Rending daggers of the great ones shall be bound with WOOD and SHADE." Hmm.

I've learned a lot about the Kor'thik mantid in my time here. I know that they maintain shrines within their settlement, Kor'vess.

One is a heartroot of the very tree that they inhabit. The other is a dark pillar, connecting them with their queen.

These shrines are the wood and shade. If my predictions are right... the daggers should react in their presence.

passages.title: Wood and Shade
passages.text:
<name>, look! The daggers - they've bound together, into a forked blade.

We are on the right track. I knew this wasn't a beer recipe.

passages.title: Sunset Kings
passages.text:
Olon had a clever idea. He thinks that we should visit the sprites to the west, and ask them if they have any of these ingredients. Some of the elements to this recipe are seeming... strange.

The Rikkitun sprites have a village to the west of Kor'vess. I hope to see you there, <name>.

passages.title: Sunset Kings
passages.text: It's been a while since I brewed on the road.

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text:
Greetings, <race>. I am Chen Stormstout.

I'm looking for my family. I am told that several Stormstouts came across the wall to help face the mantid threat. I mean to find them, and join them.

Have you seen anyone named Stormstout come through here? Would you mind helping me ask around?

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text: You are brave to have come across the wall, <race>.

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text:
<Chen listens intently.>

Big Dan, Han, Evie, and Mama. I understand.

It seems like Dan will be safe here. I will go look for Evie, Han, and Mama Stormstout.

Travel well, <name>, and follow the Wanderer's Way.

passages.title: Han Stormstout
passages.text:
There will be time for mourning later. For now, there are other Stormstouts to be found.

They say that Han Stormstout was last seen exploring Kor'vess. I suspect he headed into that mantid burrow, just across the way.

You should meet me down there, <name>. I don't doubt that I can handle a few mantid by myself... but I'd feel better with you by my side.

passages.title: Han Stormstout
passages.text: I think I see someone over there, but I can't seem to get across these amber beams.

passages.title: Han Stormstout
passages.text:
First Evie, now Han.

I was too late again.

passages.title: Incantations Fae and Primal
passages.text:
I suspect we are going to need the help of these sprites.

We have two enchanted daggers, bound together with wood and shade. Now we need someone to perform ancient "incantations" on our artifact.

Before we ask for favors, let's show the sprites that we mean well. I heard their leader talking about a pair of mistlurkers that kidnapped several of their villagers. If we slay these fog beasts... we may get the "incantation" we need in return.

passages.title: Incantations Fae and Primal
passages.text: I hope we're on the right track...

passages.title: Incantations Fae and Primal
passages.text:
Nice work. I've heard the sprites talking about us.

We're getting their attention.

passages.title: Bind the Glamour
passages.text: It has been a very, very long time since our tribe has been called on to perform this rite. I will do the best I can.

passages.title: Bind the Glamour
passages.text:
The blade is prepared.

Now, only one task remains: you must use it.

passages.title: Citizens of a New Empire
passages.text:
At Shek'zeer's command, the great kypari tree of Kypari Vor was twisted into a totem of horror.

Like those outside of the palace, the clutch nearby is now used to corrupt our swarmborn.

Recover the eggs of the Vor'thik before they are tainted. We shall raise them here. They will be the citizens of a new empire, free from the sha.

passages.title: Citizens of a New Empire
passages.text: Kypari Vor was beautiful once. Rich with amber and surrounded by prime hunting grounds.

passages.title: Citizens of a New Empire
passages.text:
They are large. They will hatch soon.

Good. We may need them.

passages.title: Stay a While, and Listen
passages.text:
Rush rush rush - are your people always in such a hurry?

Sit and have some tea with me a moment, and we will discuss your plight.

<Lorewalker Cho's features settle into a patient smile.>

passages.title: Stay a While, and Listen
passages.text: I hope I didn't bore you, traveler.

passages.title: Stay a While, and Listen
passages.text: I will help you, traveler, but first I would like to learn a little about this Horde of yours...

passages.title: A Mile in My Shoes
passages.text:
Oh, where have my manners gone? Technically, I suppose I am the host here.

Allow me to tell you a little bit about myself and my people before asking questions of you.

passages.title: A Mile in My Shoes
passages.text: I suppose the best way to explain what a Lorewalker is all about is to show you...

passages.title: If These Stones Could Speak
passages.text:
This is a very ancient place, traveler.

Only recently have I pieced together a method of translating the forgotten language carved into these stones.

Oh, the thrill of discovery! This never gets old, I assure you.

Here, you are the guest. You do the honors. I insist.

Use this key to unlock the secrets the stones contain.

passages.title: If These Stones Could Speak
passages.text: Your assistance is most appreciated, traveler.

passages.title: If These Stones Could Speak
passages.text:
That is enough translating for one day, I think.

This experience has been an enlightening one, I hope.

passages.title: Peering Into the Past
passages.text:
Just a moment, now. Allow me to gather my things.

Wouldn't want me to lose these notes now, would we? Especially after you risked life and limb for them!

There, all set. Let us be off, shall we?

I must say, I feel much safer traveling with you after seeing how you handled that saurok!

passages.title: Peering Into the Past
passages.text:
I am most grateful for the knowledge my forebears have passed on to me.

I stand upon their shoulders.

passages.title: Family Tree
passages.text:
So there you have it, traveler, or as much of it as would make for a proper introduction, hmm?

What of you, then? Are your people so much different than mine?

Surely, there must be things we share in common. Let us see...

passages.title: Family Tree
passages.text: A fine day we're having, wouldn't you say?

passages.title: Family Tree
passages.text:
Not so different, you and I.

I believe we can become good friends.

passages.title: Meet the Cap'n
passages.text:
Alright, adventurer, I got another job for ya.

You see that lion seal in the pen over there? Name's Dog. He's been Soggy's pet for years.

Dog's acting up lately - I think he's getting restless in that pen. Why don't you go talk to Soggy and let him know.

I'd say it's about time you meet the cap'n anyway.

passages.title: Meet the Cap'n
passages.text:
New deckhand, eh? We'll see about that.

I run a tight ship - even if she IS at the bottom of the sea.

passages.title: Dog Food
passages.text:
<Dog whines as best as a lion seal can, feebly lifting one flipper toward his massive jaws.

He's hungry.

The Shelf of Mazu is covered in rockshell makrura that should make a fine meal for him.>

passages.title: Dog Food
passages.text: <This has got to be the most pathetic lion seal you've ever seen.>

passages.title: Dog Food
passages.text: <Dog licks his chops happily, looking satisfied.>

passages.title: Reeltime Strategy
passages.text:
I never thought I'd see the day, but for the first time since... well, EVER, Master Angler Ju Lien asked for some help with his lines.

Apparently the sea is going crazy today and he can't keep up. See if you can give him a hand. He's fishing just south of here.

passages.title: Reeltime Strategy
passages.text: Go give Ju Lien a hand, would ya?

passages.title: Reeltime Strategy
passages.text: What happened out there?! I heard a scream and next thing I know these nasty things come rolling in on the next wave!

passages.title: What's in a Name Name?
passages.text:
So, you wanna be a hozen. Huh, wikket?

Hozen defend their lands from enemies, like jinyu.

Kah Kah fought many jinyu fights, and won them all.

Hozen only give name name to good grookers. Go grook jinyu and maybe they call you <name> <name>.

Jinyu creepin' down by the river. Ook 'em in the dooker!

passages.title: What's in a Name Name?
passages.text: Ha ha! Wikket Grooked ookin' Jinyu!

passages.title: Best Meals Anywhere!
passages.text:
Yeah, yeah.

Everyone knows us goblins do tinkering. And explosives. And... well, ya' know, the less reputable stuff.

But what nobody knows is that I'm really a great chef! It's a hobby of mine.

Gather us up some meaty bits from the creatures around here, and I'll cook us up the best meals ANYWHERE!

And I promise, I'll only use three or four percent rocket fuel.

passages.title: Best Meals Anywhere!
passages.text: The meaty bits, <name>? We need 'em!

passages.title: Best Meals Anywhere!
passages.text: You know what they say about cooking - GTL. Garnish, taste... and... laundry?

passages.title: Back to Westwind Rest
passages.text:
Well, far as I figure, we've got quite a lot of rebuildin' to do.

I'm not one for joining any big causes, but my farmhands aren't gonna have much to do 'round here, to be honest. And, since you helped them out, they want to join your "Alliance." So, who am I to stop 'em?

Bring 'em with you, back to Farmhand Bo. I'll miss 'em, but they're better off with you.

passages.title: Back to Westwind Rest
passages.text: You did good, bringing these guys back. We'll have 'em farming you up some food in no time!

passages.title: Back to Eastwind Rest
passages.text:
Well, far as I figure, we've got quite a lot of rebuildin' to do.

I'm not one for joining any big causes, but my farmhands aren't gonna have much to do 'round here, to be honest. And, since you helped them out, they want to join your "Horde". So, who am I to stop 'em?

Bring 'em with you, back to Farmhand Ko. I'll miss 'em, but they're better off with you.

passages.title: Back to Eastwind Rest
passages.text: You did good, bringing these guys back. We'll have 'em farming you up some food in no time!

passages.title: Mazu's Breath
passages.text:
Here to help, are ya? Well, first thing's first.

<Arie rummages through her pockets for a moment before producing a small vial of glowing blue fluid.>

Here it is! "Mazu's Breath." Cap'n's own formula.

What? You thought I'd send you out to sea without a means of breathin'? I need deckhands, not corpses!

Down the hatch with it, green. This'll give you a fighting chance out there on the shelf.

passages.title: Mazu's Breath
passages.text: No, I don't have a "chaser!" Just drink it!

passages.title: Mazu's Breath
passages.text: You'll thank me later.

passages.title: The Seal is Broken
passages.text:
<Cho looks at you in disbelief.>

I... I thought Sha of this immensity were a myth - we all did. Just a story to keep our children from fighting.

No time to talk now. Those fissures - they're feeding it... it grows stronger by the moment!

I must research the scrolls from my family archives. You, take this cannon and ride Mishi.

You must find a way to contain this horror that has been unleashed!

passages.title: The Seal is Broken
passages.text:
I have much research to do in very little time.

The emperor's message only warned of the unique threat war would bring to our land - this... Sha.

Sadly, the time to heed his message has passed. And as for how to bring an end to the crisis, the Emperor's Omen is silent.

passages.title: Emergency Response
passages.text:
Your companions have made themselves at home in our land, and brought with them a dangerous conflict.

The full extent of their destruction here we cannot yet know. Already it is... unspeakable.

Nevertheless, to forsake your friends out of spite would be against our way. Any that yet live are doubtlessly wounded and in desperate need of care.

These fireworks were to celebrate the statue's completion. Use them near your companions to signal Mishi, and she will bear them off to safety.

passages.title: Emergency Response
passages.text:
My thoughts will be with your fallen companions, traveler.

May their wounds mend well.

passages.title: Mazu's Bounty
passages.text:
That was some amazing work you and the captain did out there, adventurer! It's an honor to have you on the crew.

Oh! And Ju Lien survived! He swam ashore just after you started letting the harpoons fly. He was raving about some kind of gigantic egg or something that washed in with Jiao.

Go check up on him, will you? He's probably hauled it out of the water by now.

passages.title: Mazu's Bounty
passages.text:
Hey there!

Oh, I'm fine. I've had worse spills than that after a night at the Chum Bucket.

But would you look at this thing? I spotted it peeking out of the sea floor when I went under - Jiao must have dredged it up while he was thrashing around.

Not really sure what to do with it, but it looks valuable. Seeing as how you pretty much saved all our hides, I think we owe you this catch.

passages.title: The Shado-Pan
passages.text:
Our new recruits have spoken in hushed tones about a group of Pandaren they call the "Shado-Pan". They are apparently very strong, and secretive.

It's clear that, no matter what happens here in Kun-Lai, making an alliance with these Shado-Pan will be critical to our foothold in Pandaria.

That's where you come in. Rumor is they have a base of operations to the southeast, near Firebough Nook.

You will go there, and curry their favor. For the Horde!

passages.title: The Shado-Pan
passages.text: Who are you? Can you fight? If so, we can use your help.

passages.title: Not Fit to Swarm
passages.text:
Newly hatched mantid have only two instincts: kill and feed. They turn on one another, devouring the weak and leaving the strongest to mature.

Those hatched during a swarm - the swarmborn - are turned loose on our enemies instead.

The swarmborn in the Clutches of Shek'zeer have been tainted. They are born into shadows and nightmares. Driven by terror, not hunger.

They are not fit to swarm. They must be purged.

passages.title: Not Fit to Swarm
passages.text: Let me know if you want to be dropped into a sea of swarmborn. It would entertain me greatly.

passages.title: Not Fit to Swarm
passages.text:
Their eggs should have basked in the warmth of the sun and the song of a million wings for ten more years.

The Empress will pay for her crimes.

passages.title: Ancient Vengeance
passages.text:
I can hear them howling in rage... The spirits of the Gurthani mogu I slew so long ago. They wander this ruined terrace, seeking vengeance.

If they find me in this state, I will not have the strength to fend them off. Draw their attention and put them down.

Finish what I started, and I will tell you who I am.

passages.title: Ancient Vengeance
passages.text: The mogu of Clan Gurthan are quilen lords. Do not wake their guardians.

passages.title: Ancient Vengeance
passages.text:
We have a common enemy in the mogu. And perhaps others.

We shall see.

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text:
The Klaxxi'va hear another paragon. His cries are weak and lost in darkness. The signal must be strengthened.

There is a tower in Amberglow Hollow that has been silent for many years. It must sing; The Klaxxi demand it!

This time I will go with you. You will help me repair it.

Take the resonating crystal and meet me in Amberglow.

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text:
It is good you showed up when you did.

The Klaxxi'va sing to the paragon now. Soon they will know where to send you. For now there are other tasks.

passages.title: Crime and Punishment
passages.text:
The Stinging Trail nurtures young Kypari trees. The empress drains the saplings too early, outsider. They must grow before the amber can be taken.

The Klaxxi'va demand punishment for this crime! It will please them if you rain death on the Ik'thik harvesters.

passages.title: Crime and Punishment
passages.text: The Klaxxi are pleased with our work, outsider. You have proven to be more resourceful than we thought.

passages.title: Thinning the Sik'thik
passages.text:
For all our efforts to keep the mantid in the Dread Wastes, some have broken through, seemingly intent on Niuzao Temple. My men have been attempting to extinguish their presence to the west, at Sik'vess, but to no success. If you're half of the <class> Taran paints you to be, maybe you will fare better.

Head west, and kill any Sik'thik mantid you find. And remember, this is no time for mercy. There are lives at the temple depending on us.

passages.title: Thinning the Sik'thik
passages.text:
The mantid are relentless. Fortunately for us, you have a dedication that surpasses even theirs.

It is good to have you walk these roads, <class>.

passages.title: The Search for Restless Leng
passages.text:
One of my best scouts, Restless Leng, went missing during a mission on the other side of Sik'vess. I'm hopeful that he was captured rather than killed, but with the mantid corrupted so heavily by sha, it doesn't seem likely.

Still, can you investigate the cages around Sik'vess? I owe him a more thorough search than even this, but I have no men to spare without allowing our southern lines to break.

Please, <class>, even if there's no life left in him, find him that I might know his fate.

passages.title: The Search for Restless Leng
passages.text: Leng told me of your heroics. He is in your debt, as am I.

passages.title: The Dreadsworn
passages.text:
The Klaxxi see far and hear much. They have shared their insight with me.

The Vor'thik embrace the sha, using its power to fuel their march in this false swarm. Their warriors consume tainted amber and call themselves dreadsworn.

There is no future for them. They are waste which needs disposing.

And YOU will begin that process for us when you reach Kypari Vor.

passages.title: The Dreadsworn
passages.text:
In disciplined hands, the spear is the perfect weapon. Only the weak would augment it with sorcery.

And we have no need for the weak.

passages.title: Welcome Wagons
passages.text:
Did you see the size of those war wagons? They're packing so many explosives, I cannae tell if the Horde is here to take over this continent or just blow it out of the sea!

We need to neutralize those wagons before they leave Garrosh'ar Point.

Here, take me pocket flares. Fire 'em into a wagon and watch the fireworks!

passages.title: Welcome Wagons
passages.text: Did "The Pickle" send you with a mission?

passages.title: Welcome Wagons
passages.text: With those wagons out of commission, we can turn our attention to the commander.

passages.title: Envoy of the Alliance
passages.text:
North of this base is a cherry blossom orchard and a village tucked away behind it. We will need to quarter there and tend to our wounded while we plan our next move.

Head to that village and make contact with the native leader. Agent Mishka and I will rendezvous with you there.

Be courteous, <name>! I am authorizing you to represent the entire Alliance here.

I'm banking that seeing a powerful Alliance hero like you should make a favorable impression.

passages.title: Envoy of the Alliance
passages.text:
When the mist fell, we knew it would only be a matter of time before visitors arrived.

We could not have predicted it would be like this.

passages.title: The Cost of War
passages.text:
This whole place is going up in flames and the Skyfire is reporting that more of those... shadows are crawling up out of the ground. We need to get our people out of here.

Clear a path through the base on your way north and head for the town. I will rendezvous with you there.

passages.title: The Cost of War
passages.text: You have no idea what kind of consequences your actions may have here!

passages.title: The Cost of War
passages.text: I am glad you took responsibility for your actions. Left unchecked, negative emotions can quickly overwhelm an individual here, just as they started to overwhelm the one you call "Rell."

passages.title: Pillaging Peons
passages.text:
How did my village become a battlefield?

To the west, your Horde enemies cut down our precious orchard. Without our apple trees, we will have no harvest, no food, and no livelihood.

If you are truly different than this Horde, show us! Help us protect our grove by killing those who defile the land.

passages.title: Pillaging Peons
passages.text: It is easier to harbor hatred than to make peace.

passages.title: Pillaging Peons
passages.text: Our orchard is one of our village's greatest treasures. For saving our harvest, we are truly grateful.

passages.title: Priorities!
passages.text:
Those "orc" things ransacked the brewery and made off with my family's finest barrels of cider.

I know there is a war out there, but I am not a brewer who will stand idly by while his prized vintage is chugged by undeserving lips.

The "Horde" will likely put up some resistance. Why don't you put that weapon to good use and help me recover my cider?

passages.title: Priorities!
passages.text: Is that my husband with you? Did you recover the cider?

passages.title: Priorities!
passages.text: I see that you two have been busy. Thank you for recovering our kegs.

passages.title: Koukou's Rampage
passages.text:
We have more than just our cellars to worry about.

Koukou, our beloved mushan, has gone crazy! Just look at him!

I've tried cajoling and pleading and yelling and soothing, but nothing has worked.

I'm afraid he is no longer of his own mind. There is only one way to save him, and our brewery.

Strike swift and sure. He will not feel a thing.

passages.title: Koukou's Rampage
passages.text: Things are going crazy around here, and it all started when you arrived, <race>.

passages.title: Koukou's Rampage
passages.text:
You did well to help the Brewers and bring this news to me.

From what you have told me, it sounds as if Koukou was possessed by some dark energy. Could it be...?

No. That is impossible.

passages.title: Twinspire Keep
passages.text:
I do not trust this Horde. They wield foul magic, and their intentions are clearly malevolent. We can no longer stand their presence in Twinspire Keep, so close to Paw'don.

I beg you, visitor: thin their numbers before they do something awful to this village.

passages.title: Twinspire Keep
passages.text: Gol' dang, but there's a bunch of 'em down there...

passages.title: Twinspire Keep
passages.text:
One heck of a bloody mess y'made down there, kid.

Nice work.

passages.title: Fractured Forces
passages.text:
The Horde have made our jobs easier for us. Their infighting and segregation have split their camp in two: orcs in the west, and undead in the east.

The orcs obey their commander Dalgan, while the undead follow Bellandra Felstorm, a powerful warlock. Hopefully, their internal squabbles will be enough of a distraction that you'll be able to sneak in there and kill both of them. Sully has already infiltrated the ruins; find him inside when you are done.

passages.title: Fractured Forces
passages.text: Pretty scary-lookin' characters around here...

passages.title: Fractured Forces
passages.text:
That's some fine and fancy killin', <class>.

Now, with those two all done 'n' taken care of, all that's left is the big fella in the hall behind me.

passages.title: Touching Ground
passages.text:
Nazgrim has taken command of the ground assault and has requested that you be sent to meet up with him immediately.

We have several rappelling ropes setup near the guns. Fastest way down you're going to find, save the one that ends poorly.

passages.title: Touching Ground
passages.text: What?

passages.title: Touching Ground
passages.text:
There you are!

I was starting to worry we'd have to charge in and have all the fun without you.

passages.title: Finish Them!
passages.text:
We've softened them up. Now it's time to finish them off!

That fortress must be cleansed of Alliance, and we've got nowhere to keep any prisoners.

<The hint of a smile crosses Nazgrim's face.>

You know what to do, <name>. The cowards will run if you give them the chance.

See that you don't!

passages.title: Finish Them!
passages.text: Destroy them all!

passages.title: Finish Them!
passages.text: Good work, <class>! We have them on their heels!

passages.title: Fire Is Always the Answer
passages.text:
It's not enough that we destroy their forces. Nothing must be left for them to salvage!

Take this flare-gun and fire it into their munitions stockpiles. Leave them nothing!

passages.title: Fire Is Always the Answer
passages.text: Burn them out!

passages.title: Fire Is Always the Answer
passages.text:
Haha! Good work, <name>.

Leave 'em nothing!

passages.title: The Final Blow!
passages.text:
We've learned that their captain has barricaded himself in above us.

The coward allowed his forces to die while he hid from our fury! Typical Alliance! No matter. He cannot delay his fate any longer.

I will scale the walls with my marines while you lead a frontal assault up the ramps. Use your flare gun on munitions near the barricades to blast your way through.

We will meet you up top and destroy this pathetic excuse for a captain together!

passages.title: The Final Blow!
passages.text:
An air base - they had a hidden airbase here this entire time! Had I known I would've kept more men on the guns, I would've - Uaaghh -

<The color drains from Nazgrim's face, and his body begins to exude a mysterious dark energy.>

passages.title: Face to Face With Consequence
passages.text:
I do not know the history of this war that you fight, and I am not interested. This land responds to negative energy in kind. The hatreds, doubt, and violence you have brought here now ooze out of Pandaria like blood from an open wound.

Your actions have wrought havoc all over these ruins! Clean up after yourself and meet me in the village below - I will do my best to explain what is happening here.

passages.title: Face to Face With Consequence
passages.text: Have you cleansed the ruins?

passages.title: Face to Face With Consequence
passages.text: I am glad you took responsibility for your actions. Left unchecked, negative emotions can quickly overwhelm an individual here, just as they started to overwhelm the one you call "Nazgrim."

passages.title: Prowler Problems
passages.text:
The animals have all gone crazy!

Normally the prowlers steer clear of the village, but now we can't seem to keep them away. I've never seen them act this way before!

The mayor has summoned in the Shado-Pan, but they're not all here yet. Can you take care of those prowlers before they maul one of our farmers?

passages.title: Prowler Problems
passages.text:
Ah, so your conflict at the ruins is beginning to pollute the local wildlife? This is very troubling - I have never seen a reaction so intense.

Thank you for protecting the village, but it is a tragedy that those poor animals had to die.

passages.title: Assault on the Airstrip
passages.text:
I have found their hidden airfield, <name>: the Strongarm Airstrip. It wasn't hard to spot, it's swarming with Alliance.

<Nazgrim spits.>

They think they've wiped us out, but we're Horde! We fight until we're corpses... and sometimes even afterwards. Let them taste our steel!

passages.title: Assault on the Airstrip
passages.text:
The best thing about killing Alliance in Pandaria? It'll be months before they get any reinforcements.

This land will belong to the Horde, <class>. We're nearly finished.

passages.title: The Darkness Within
passages.text:
You didn't see Captain Doren while you were out there, did you?

That sniveling Alliance leader must be in hiding somewhere. If he wasn't in that airbase, he can't be far. Search the perimeter - try searching the cave southwest of the main airfield. I want the Alliance gone from here!

passages.title: The Darkness Within
passages.text: On your way then, <name>.

passages.title: The Darkness Within
passages.text:
The Alliance have been routed. You, Nazgrim, Kiryn, Gorrok, Shokia, and Rivett need a base of operations.

These flags will have to be changed.

For the Horde!

passages.title: Ancient Guardians
passages.text:
Before the mogu overwhelmed our scouting party, we found relics scattered amongst the ruins to the north.

I would like to collect some samples, but the mogu's terracotta watchdogs are too much for us to handle.

If you could clear the area of their presence, we will be able to resume our work.

passages.title: Ancient Guardians
passages.text: I am quite keen to understand the mogu's magic.

passages.title: Ancient Guardians
passages.text: Ah! Well done! With the guardians gone, we should be able to excavate these ruins safely.

passages.title: Dagger in the Dark
passages.text:
Shadow Hunter Vol'jin has joined a group of Kor'kron scouts on an important mission for the warchief.

Of course a proud member of the Horde such as yourself is welcome to go along, but be warned - it could get ugly.

passages.title: Dagger in the Dark
passages.text: Good ta see ya, mon. I be needin' true allies at my side for dis mission.

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text:
We can use the pterrorwing that you found to strike a decisive blow against the mogu. 

Their mining operation is vulnerable to attack from the air, and your pterrorwing is the only beast we have capable of flying out there.

Let me know when you are ready!

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text: It's time to begin your mission!

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text: Incredible work. This presents us with a monumental opportunity.

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text:
Long ago, Lei Shen found a rare clutch of storm dragon eggs. One of these creatures - Nalak - was particularly brutal, and Lei Shen took it for his own.

The Thunder King's servant, Shan Bu, works to resurrect Lei Shen's dragon, Nalak.

We must defeat Shan Bu and, if we are able, prevent him from resurrecting the dragon.

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text: We must defeat Shan Bu while he is exposed!

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Shan Bu's fall will weaken the Mogu and your heroism will surely be remembered.

passages.title: The Horde Is Family
passages.text:
This hearthstone was part of a conversation Vol'jin and I shared a long time ago.

He believes his people are in danger. I don't know what all has transpired in my absence, but I can at least do this for my friend.

Come, adventurer, travel with me to the Echo Isles. We must make sure that the Darkspear are safe.

passages.title: The Horde Is Family
passages.text: Vol'jin has saved my life many times in the past. To see my own Kor'kron used against his people cuts deeper than I can put into words.

passages.title: The Monkey King
passages.text:
Ever since the Horde captured the Divine Bell I have been searching for a means to counter its power.

My research got as far as this tomb. I am going inside. If you follow me, I will share the rest as we go.

If we get separated, meet me back here at the entrance to the tomb. Speak to me when you are ready to proceed.

passages.title: The Monkey King
passages.text:
You come asking for the Monkey King?

Let us see how well you ookin' sing.

Who are you, so tiny and boring?

Your cause is silly! You leave me snoring.

Three riddles I will ask,

These riddles are a task,

Finish each without pause,

And we shall see if I help your cause.

passages.title: Victorious Return
passages.text: The portal by my side will return you safely to Domination Point. I will return behind you; I must clean up our tracks a bit before we leave, so that Proudmoore doesn't discover our involvement.

passages.title: Victorious Return
passages.text:
You found the bell! And Fanlyr teleported it to Silvermoon for study, as instructed? The Horde will put this to good use.

You have done the Horde a great service today. Lok'tar, friend!

passages.title: What's in the Box?
passages.text:
We are trying to uncover the secrets of one of the mogu artifacts Garrosh insisted we investigate. It is proving most difficult, as anyone who probes it magically is greatly affected by raw, negative emotions.

I called in the assistance of Arch-mage Aethas of the Sunreavers in the hopes that he and Rommath could crack this puzzle. They asked for you specifically - apparently you have some relevant experience?

Go to the chamber below Farstrider Square east of here and see if you can assist them.

passages.title: What's in the Box?
passages.text: This reckless use of my people by Garrosh is becoming intolerable. If you had not been here to assist I dread to think what might have happened.

passages.title: The Second Riddle: Fellowship
passages.text:
You want to stop the Divine Bell? We need the mallet first.

You want the mallet? We need to be friends first.

You want to be friends? We need a Metal brew first. 

You want a Metal brew? You need to go to the Shrine of Fellowship first. 

You want to go to the Shrine of Fellowship? Great! It's in the Jade Forest southeast of the Tian Monastery.

Ring the bell and get the Monkey King some brew while there. Oh... you may have to fight for it.

passages.title: The Second Riddle: Fellowship
passages.text: You have the Metal Brew?

passages.title: The Second Riddle: Fellowship
passages.text:
The Metal Brew is strong and lasting, a brew to be shared with friends after a battle.

Emperor Shaohao and his Monkey King had many a round in our day. Many battles, and many good friends.

passages.title: The Third Riddle: Strength
passages.text:
The mallet you seek is not a toy for children,

It calls trouble like the song of a siren.

A test of strength the Monkey King will require,

Before you receive this tool of your desire.

At the Temple of the White Tiger you will find

A challenger to test how well you are resigned

Step through the main door and then turn right down the ramp

Challenge the ook waiting for you there like a champ!

passages.title: The Third Riddle: Strength
passages.text:
Why engage in duelery? Why engage in foolery?

You ask the Monkey King for an artifact of power, I have to make sure when the time comes you will not cower. One tough dooker you think you might ookin be, but against mogu, many will turn and flee.

passages.title: The Greatest Prank
passages.text:
So riddles three you answered me. Good good. The Monkey King is not so old that he tells just anyone his tricks.

It was the greatest prank ever!

You want to hear story of the Mallet and the Monkey? Too bad! No choice!

passages.title: The Greatest Prank
passages.text: What you think?

passages.title: The Greatest Prank
passages.text:
It looks like it is going to take us a few days to track all of these "minions" down.

Thank you for your help, <name>. Meet me in Lion's Landing in a few days and we will embark to track down these objects.

passages.title: A Gathering Storm
passages.text:
If General Nazgrim sent you, then I trust you are capable of discretion.

When I arrived here, I found Garrosh... experimenting... with some ancient power that he found in the mountains to the north.

He believes that this "sha" can strengthen our soldiers.

Unfortunately, so far the results have been quite the opposite.

Our troops are erupting into random violence. Go and interrogate them. If they threaten you, be prepared to defend yourself.

passages.title: A Gathering Storm
passages.text: There is great power here... Why is it that so many fear it?

passages.title: A Gathering Storm
passages.text:
You bested my defenders? Finally, one who can control his hatred and violence!

I need more men like you.

passages.title: Clearing a Path
passages.text:
First thing's first. If we're going to take the leader captive, we'll need to thin the numbers of his agents.

Be careful. These mogu are particularly dangerous - they appear to be manipulating the sha in ways we haven't seen before.

passages.title: Clearing a Path
passages.text: Good. We should be ready to make our move.

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
If the Alliance thought they could steal the Divine Bell from us, they were wrong!

Even now, we have them trapped in the crypts beneath us.

Death will be the price they pay for defying us.

Come, <class>. Let us show them the error of their ways.

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
Darnassus, is it?

The Alliance believes they have won the day. Now, when their arrogance is at its greatest, is our opportunity to pluck the prize from their fingers.

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
Garrosh is right over there, and he's going to ring that bell at any moment.

We don't have time to wait for my father's army. This is our only chance to stop him!

I'll attempt to appeal to his senses before resorting to using the Harmonic Mallet.

Charge in whenever you're ready, <name>. I'll be right behind you.

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
<Anduin looks like a crumpled doll. He lays as still as a stone, and the only movement comes from the frigid air ruffling his fair, golden hair.>

<You sit quietly for a while, until the cold settles into your bones. The bell is destroyed, but the silence is deafening.>

<Out of the corner of your eye, you see the slightest flicker from the boy's hand. You lean in close. He breathes - but just barely! Anduin is alive!>

passages.title: The Situation In Dalaran
passages.text:
The night elves learned that the Divine Bell was stolen. This much we anticipated.

However, they've also found out that the "neutral" Sunreavers of Dalaran were complicit. Now, we've got a situation.

I need you to go to Dalaran. Speak with Kromthar for a ride. You are to rendezvous with Grand Magister Rommath once you arrive.

passages.title: The Situation In Dalaran
passages.text:
Good... you've arrived. It's not a good day to be Horde in Dalaran.

Jaina's called for the exile of all the Sunreavers. You and I are going to save as many as we can - including Archmage Aethas Sunreaver himself - and then get out of here as fast as possible.

passages.title: It Starts in the Sewers
passages.text:
Compared to the rest of the city, this part of the sewers is relatively calm. This is good - we can extract more Sunreavers in peace than we can in war.

Find as many citizens as you can. Tell them that it is not safe here, that they must leave the city at once.

And try to stay clear of the Silver Covenant. We don't want to cause a scene if we can avoid it. Not yet, anyhow.

passages.title: It Starts in the Sewers
passages.text: I think I see a few more Sunreavers over there...

passages.title: It Starts in the Sewers
passages.text: Let's press on.

passages.title: Hand of the Silver Covenant
passages.text:
Every Sunreaver Jaina expels from this city is a new blade that fights for the Horde. For US.

I'm off to gather more strong elves. You've proven your hand in combat thus far - go take care of that creep in the black market.

When you're done, we'll meet at the ramp and prepare to go aboveground.

passages.title: Hand of the Silver Covenant
passages.text:
The first stage of our mission is complete. That was the easy part.

<Rommath takes a deep, measured breath, then continues...>

passages.title: The Silver Covenant's Stronghold
passages.text:
I have it on good authority that Archmage Aethas Sunreaver is being held in the Silver Enclave, home of the Silver Covenant. Arcanist Rathaella holds him in captivity.

Most Covenant agents are out slaughtering Sunreavers right now, which means our chance is ripe. Slay Rathaella, and spring Aethas from his prison.

passages.title: The Silver Covenant's Stronghold
passages.text: We will continue saving Sunreavers for a while longer. Aethas' location may become clearer as we press on.

passages.title: Krasus' Landing
passages.text:
We can rescue as many Sunreavers as we want, but if they can't escape, then there's no point.

The Silver Covenant will certainly be subduing and killing the Sunreavers' dragonhawks. Put a stop to it.

passages.title: Krasus' Landing
passages.text: The depravity of this Silver Covenant sickens me. Attacking innocent creatures!

passages.title: Krasus' Landing
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Well done.

passages.title: Sewer Cleaning
passages.text:
Jaina's doing a good job taking care of Sunreavers above ground, but there's still plenty rooting around in the sewers.

Go find those lying rats and exterminate them!

passages.title: Sewer Cleaning
passages.text: <Vereesa looks out over her city.>

passages.title: Sewer Cleaning
passages.text: It's nice to have those rats out of here for good. Well done, hero.

passages.title: Cashing Out
passages.text:
I just saw one of the Sunreavers - Brasael, I think his name was - running off in the direction of the bank to the north. No doubt he's trying to gather whatever assets he can before he leaves.

Head him off and make sure he doesn't steal any resources from our coffers. He relinquished whatever funds he left in the bank when he and his Sunreaver kind betrayed us.

passages.title: Cashing Out
passages.text:
I suppose it wasn't enough for him to be a coward and a backstabber... he had to be a greedy thief as well.

Hmph. The Horde and the Sunreavers aren't all that different. They deserve one another.

passages.title: Impending Danger
passages.text:
Our scouts have sighted a fel command ship looming on the horizon, Grandmaster. It appears to be headed on a collision course with the Wandering Isle.

We should prepare our troops for the worst case situation - an all out attack.

In the meantime, let us send our champions ahead to try and divert the Legion ship's attention.

passages.title: Impending Danger
passages.text: The command ship appears to be gunning straight for us. We need everyone on alert, now!

passages.title: Impending Danger
passages.text: Our champions defeated the first wave of attackers, but the command ship is nearly upon us!

passages.title: Ties with the Past
passages.text:
While I was in the Vale, I came across an ancient pandaren recipe for Memory Wine. I believe this brew can coax some helpful information out of Shan Kien.

I am needed here, so I have no choice but to ask you to recover the essential ingredient for me. We need the spirit essence of a mogu that lived in the time of the memory we wish to see.

You should be able to find just such a spirit inside the Path of Conquerors, to the northeast.

passages.title: Ties with the Past
passages.text:
You never know what you will find in a book. Especially an ancient pandaren one.

I'm eager to see how this Memory Wine works.

passages.title: Ties with the Past
passages.text: Ah, very good. This is the last thing we needed.

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text:
We have a plan to halt the mogu's weaponmaking capabilities, and it involves the creature you recovered from the Zandalari.

Speak to me when you're ready to learn more.

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text: It's time to begin your mission!

passages.title: To the Skies!
passages.text: Incredible work. This presents us with a monumental opportunity.

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text:
Lei Shen found a clutch of rare storm dragon eggs early in his campaign. One - known as Nalak - was particularly brutal and killed all of its handlers, so he took it for his own.

Now, Shan Bu, one of Lei Shen's most loyal servants, works to resurrect the dragon.

It is time for us to strike against Shan Bu!

Speak to me when you are ready to launch the assault!

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text: The time to defeat Shan Bu is now!

passages.title: The Fall of Shan Bu
passages.text: You've done it, <class>! Shan Bu is dead once and for all, and we've learned that Lor'themar may not be all that he seems.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text:
There is no time to waste, <name>. Every moment we delay here gives the Sunreavers more of a hold on the Isle.

Lady Jaina Proudmoore awaits us. We should not make her wait any longer.

Speak to me when you are ready to depart. I will escort you there myself.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text: The key to our safety lies here, <name>. I feel it to my core that we are meant to be here.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text: You have arrived just in time, <name>. This land needs to be controlled by the Kirin Tor for everyone's safety. This will not be an easy task.

passages.title: Allies in the Shadows
passages.text:
The Shado-Pan arrived here before we did, and they are already at work undermining the Thunder King's forces.

I want you to meet with Taran Zhu, the leader of the Shado-Pan, and offer your services on behalf of the Kirin Tor. I doubt he is truly in need of the aid, but the gesture holds importance in itself.

passages.title: Allies in the Shadows
passages.text: Welcome, <name>.

passages.title: Allies in the Shadows
passages.text:
The Shado-Pan arrived here before we did, and they are already at work undermining the Thunder King's forces.

I want you to meet with Taran Zhu, the leader of the Shado-Pan, and offer your services on behalf of the Sunreavers. I doubt he is truly in need of the aid, but the gesture holds importance in itself.

passages.title: Allies in the Shadows
passages.text: Welcome, <name>.

passages.title: A Timeless Tour
passages.text:
You should first familiarize yourself with the island.

Explore. Investigate anything that catches your interest. Return when you're done, and I'll reward you for whatever information you've gathered about this strange place.

And do be careful! Monstrous beasts and supernatural creatures abound.

passages.title: A Timeless Tour
passages.text:
Bizarre place, is it not?

I do hope you found some adventure along the way.

passages.title: The Last Emperor
passages.text:
From what I have gathered, this place used to be a tournament ground of sorts, where warriors from throughout Pandaria would show their prowess by following in the footsteps of their last emperor, Shaohao.

I have heard that when Shaohao completed his trials, he became one with the land, and enveloped Pandaria in a thick mist, obscuring it from even our abilities to penetrate the passages of time.

That sounds quite interesting, perhaps you should speak with him?

passages.title: The Last Emperor
passages.text: Greetings, I am Shaohao. Are you here to hear the wisdom of the celestials?

passages.title: The Last Emperor
passages.text: In my pride, I sought to keep Pandaria a secret, and once again I have found myself learning great lessons from this land. I am glad to be able to share my stories with my people, once again, in that they may learn as I have, and learn from my mistakes. Perhaps you, too, can still learn a thing or two from the lessons of Pandaria.

passages.title: The Archiereus Of Flame
passages.text:
Your efforts have driven back the Ordon and brought peace to the Celestial Court, but it will not last. It is time to silence the great emissary of Ordos - the Archiereus of Flame.

Speak with Mistweaver Ku and purchase a scroll of challenge, then travel to Three-Breeze Terrace to the north. Issue a challenge at the challenge stone, it will undoubtedly catch the attention of the Ordon, drawing the archiereus out of the Ordon Sanctuary. It is your only chance.

passages.title: The Archiereus Of Flame
passages.text: The emissaries of Ordos are powerful, do not underestimate them.

passages.title: The Archiereus Of Flame
passages.text:
The emissaries of Ordos have been silenced, for a time.

Know that anger, violence, and hatred will never cease. Wherever there is the darkness within one's spirit, you will find these sha awaiting you. They may become manifest in many forms: a warlord hungering for power, a dagger in your back in the night, a young prince following a dark path, and even your own battle against forces not aligned with your own.

Learn from the lessons of these emotions, lest you lose yourself to the darkness.

passages.title: Goblin Escape Pods
passages.text:
<name>, I'm sorry, I thought you were dead!

This is just crazy. We sailed into a fight between the Alliance and Horde!

You know, our brothers and sisters still need to be rescued.

<He points out all of the escape pods in the water around you.>

I think I'm going to sit here a while longer and catch my breath. Can you swim around and let them out? Take my pair of thermohydratic flippers so you can get around faster.

Let Sassy know that I'll swim in shortly.

passages.title: Goblin Escape Pods
passages.text:
Oh, thank heavens that you survived, <name>! I thought for sure that you'd drowned when I saw you go over the side!

Look at all of these folks you saved!

passages.title: Get Our Stuff Back!
passages.text:
Our bombs and tools! Those sneaky monkeys to the east stole them all in the dead of night!

Can you go out there and get them back for us, <name>? Without those tools, we have absolutely no way to get off of this island!

passages.title: Get Our Stuff Back!
passages.text: Bomb-throwing monkeys?! The nerve!!!

passages.title: Get Our Stuff Back!
passages.text:
<Sassy breathes a sigh of relief when she sees all of the tools and bombs that you recovered.>

I thought we were doomed for sure. But now we can start working on a way to get off of this island!

passages.title: Miner Troubles
passages.text:
Smart mining monkeys!

They're all over the inside of the cavern, mining... with picks! It's just not natural and I'm sure it's because of the kaja'mite!

None of my miners have come back out. I don't have many left! You can see my predicament, <name>.

<The foreman lowers his voice.>

These guys are nowhere near as good as my old group of jungle trolls. Ah, those were the days.

Maybe you can escort my last miner here through the cavern and keep those monkeys off of him? We need that kaja'mite!

passages.title: Miner Troubles
passages.text: How did it go? How much kaja'mite were you able to get?

passages.title: Miner Troubles
passages.text:
We've hit the mother lode!!!

Now, what's all this about a pygmy witchdoctor in charge of the monkeys? Is he dead? Because if he's dead, then legally I can stake my claim... not that I wasn't going to do that anyway. By <race> law, all Kaja'mite belongs to us!

passages.title: Lockdown!
passages.text:
What are you still doing here, citizen? Haven't you heard? The city's under complete lockdown.

Go see Lieutenant Walden -- he'll give you further directions for evacuation.

passages.title: Lockdown!
passages.text: Deep claw marks run through the man's corpse.

passages.title: Something's Amiss
passages.text:
The lieutenant appears to have died from severe wounds. The prince might want to hear this news.

You hear the sound of fighting coming from the market.

passages.title: Something's Amiss
passages.text: It's you again.  Looks like you're not one to hide in the face of danger.  Very well, then.

passages.title: All Hell Breaks Loose
passages.text:
Worgen! My father had warned me that Archmage Arugal's creations had run amok.

But where are they coming from?

I suppose it doesn't matter. Help us make quick work of them. We'll show them what we Gilneans are made of!

passages.title: All Hell Breaks Loose
passages.text: Have the <race> been dealt with?

passages.title: All Hell Breaks Loose
passages.text: It's no use, <name>!  They're not letting up.

passages.title: Salvage the Supplies
passages.text:
Listen, <name>. We can't let our supplies get destroyed.

With Gilneas walled off from the outside world, we won't last through winter if we lose much more of our stock.

Please help me salvage what you can.

passages.title: Salvage the Supplies
passages.text: Have you salvaged the supplies, <name>?

passages.title: Salvage the Supplies
passages.text: Excellent!  I'll make sure these get taken to a safe place.

passages.title: Evacuate the Merchant Square
passages.text:
The civilians aren't safe here anymore. Not even inside their homes.

We're doing our best to stop the worgen from getting indoors, but their numbers are too great.

Help us by evacuating the civilian homes. My father's army in the prison district will be able to better protect them.

passages.title: Evacuate the Merchant Square
passages.text: Have you succeeded, <name>?

passages.title: Evacuate the Merchant Square
passages.text: Good job, <name>.  Thanks to you, many Gilneans will live to see another day.

passages.title: Royal Orders
passages.text:
It's time for you to leave, <name>. Go to the Military District with the other civilians.

Check in with Gwen Armstead when you cross the bridge to the southeast... see if everyone's okay.

I will stay here with the guards and cover the civilians' retreat.

Go now. That is an order!

passages.title: Royal Orders
passages.text: We're all fine here.  A little shaken... but alive.

passages.title: By the Skin of His Teeth
passages.text:
One of those mangy fleabags got Dempsey real good. We cannot move him until we stabilize his bleeding.

Give us a hand holding back these mongrels. A couple of minutes is all we need, <brother/sister>!

passages.title: By the Skin of His Teeth
passages.text: Getting there!  Careful or we'll lose him!

passages.title: By the Skin of His Teeth
passages.text: We did it, <name>.  Thanks to you a good man has survived.

passages.title: Old Divisions
passages.text:
Lord Darius Crowley has been called many things. Rebel. Traitor. Terrorist.

Before the civil war I called him... friend.

I never blamed him for leading an insurrection against me. His land and people were separated from Gilneas by a stone wall... but we had no choice.

Regardless... Crowley is exactly the type of person we need now.

Enter Stoneward Prison and ask Captain Broderick about Crowley's whereabouts. I'd send my own men, but there's still bad blood.

passages.title: Old Divisions
passages.text: Greymane wants to save Crowley?  Has he gone mad?

passages.title: The Rebel Lord's Arsenal
passages.text:
The arsenal Crowley speaks of is in the cellar of a building just west of here.

It is unnerving that artillery was smuggled inside the city by my enemies, yet it might end up saving Gilnean lives today.

Find Josiah Avery and requisition the rebel artillery. We will put the weapons to good use.

passages.title: The Rebel Lord's Arsenal
passages.text: Don't look at me!  Leave me alone!
