passages.title: From the Shadows
passages.text:
He turned into one of them... didn't he? How do we even begin to fight an enemy that can do this to us?

My father's arsenal's certainly a good start, I suppose.

Worgen are hiding in the alleys ahead. Take one of my mastiffs to find them more easily.

We're going to need to clear the way ahead if we're going to move these cannons above ground.

passages.title: From the Shadows
passages.text: Is it done yet, <name>?

passages.title: From the Shadows
passages.text: Excellent.  I'll start rounding up some help to get these cannons positioned.

passages.title: Sacrifices
passages.text:
You don't have to do this, <name>. You've done more than enough already.

But if you decide to stay... I'd be a fool to turn you away.

My men have fortified their position inside the cathedral and are ready for what comes next.

I'm about to head there and take as many of these flea-ridden devils with me as I can. You're welcome to come along for the ride.

passages.title: Sacrifices
passages.text: Every <race> we keep inside the city is one less <race> going after our loved ones outside.

passages.title: Sacrifices
passages.text:
Brace yourself, <name>.

Here they come.

passages.title: Message to Greymane
passages.text:
It's time, <name>. We'll take it from here.

Tell King Greymane that my father's arsenal will be at his disposal. There's more than enough firepower here to blow the worgen from here to the north sea.

passages.title: Message to Greymane
passages.text: I knew Crowley would come through.  His weapons will be more than useful to us.

passages.title: By Blood and Ash
passages.text:
The time has come, <name>. If we're going to put a dent in their numbers, the time is now.

We have the position.

We have the firepower.

All that remains to be seen is whether we have the courage... and I sure don't see a coward standing in front of me.

passages.title: By Blood and Ash
passages.text: We must take out as many of them as we can, <name>.

passages.title: By Blood and Ash
passages.text:
You've done well, <name>.  You've done more than could be asked of any Gilnean.

We're running low on ammunition.  It's time to regroup inside now.

passages.title: Never Surrender, Sometimes Retreat
passages.text:
We had enough ammunition to carry on the civil war for another month. Yet the worgen's numbers are such that we're nearly spent.

We don't want to be caught out here in the open when that happens. Fall back inside the cathedral and report to the boss. I'm sure old Crowley will know what to do next.

passages.title: Never Surrender, Sometimes Retreat
passages.text: We've given them everything we have... yet still they come.  Do not worry, <name>.  We'll slay many more before today is over.

passages.title: Last Stand
passages.text:
We've got a good chokepoint here, <name>. Feel free to say a prayer if that's your sort of thing.

Take courage and let's kill these mutts.

passages.title: Last Stand
passages.text: We can do this, <name>.

passages.title: Last Stand
passages.text:
They... they've stopped coming.

No, <name>.  That's not a good thing.

passages.title: Up, Up & Away!
passages.text:
While you were rescuing the Warchief and saving us all from the Alliance, Foreman Dampwick built this rocket sling to shoot us over the shark-infested strait to the bigger island.

Luckily for us, the foreman managed to salvage a Town-In-A-Box from the shipwreck. Once you get it set up, we'll have a town of our own. I can't wait to sleep in a bed again!

Dampwick's down there at the Landing Site, waiting for you. Why don't you take the next rocket over?

passages.title: Up, Up & Away!
passages.text: <name>, I sure am glad you survived the trip... not everyone did!

passages.title: Your Instructor
passages.text:
Most of us made it here alive... but there are worgen on this side of the city as well.

We're going to continue heading south once everyone's accounted for.

That reminds me, someone was asking about you. A fellow by the name of Cleese said you were one of his students and wanted to make sure you were all right.

passages.title: Your Instructor
passages.text:
<name>!  Where have you been?

Anyway... it's great to see you in one piece.

passages.title: Someone's Looking for You
passages.text:
Most of us made it here alive... but there are worgen on this side of the city as well.

We're going to continue heading south once everyone's accounted for.

That reminds me, someone was asking about you. A woman named Loren... she seemed a little disappointed when I told her you were all right.

I think she mentioned she owes you money.

passages.title: Someone's Looking for You
passages.text: Oh, hey!  There you are!

passages.title: Shady Associates
passages.text:
Most of us made it here alive... but there are worgen on this side of the city as well.

We're going to continue heading south once everyone's accounted for.

That reminds me, someone was asking about you. A strange fellow named Vitus... he was really giving me the creeps.

He kept talking about some "forbidden knowledge" he'd uncovered.

passages.title: Shady Associates
passages.text: A darkness has descended over our lands.  And not our kind of darkness, if you know what I mean.

passages.title: Someone's Keeping Track of You
passages.text:
Most of us made it here alive... but there are worgen on this side of the city as well.

We're going to continue heading south once everyone's accounted for.

That reminds me, someone was asking about you. A man named Blake. Said something about a plan to escape into the woods.

passages.title: Someone's Keeping Track of You
passages.text: <name>!  I knew you had to be around here.

passages.title: Arcane Inquiries
passages.text:
Most of us made it here alive... but there are worgen on this side of the city as well.

We're going to continue heading south once everyone's accounted for.

That reminds me, someone was asking about you. It was a mage named Myriam. She mentioned something about you being "ready."

passages.title: Arcane Inquiries
passages.text: A disciple of the arcane always finds a way forward.  I'm glad to see you, <name>.

passages.title: Seek the Sister
passages.text:
Most of us made it here alive... but there are worgen on this side of the city as well.

We're going to continue heading south once everyone's accounted for.

That reminds me, someone was asking about you. A member of the clergy, Sister Almyra, said that you were in great peril and needed the Light's protection.

You should go talk to her. She seemed very concerned.

passages.title: Seek the Sister
passages.text: The Light is with you, <name>.  It's still quite a relief to see you.

passages.title: The Winds Know Your Name... Apparently
passages.text:
Most of us made it here alive... but there are worgen on this side of the city as well.

We're going to continue heading south once everyone's accounted for.

That reminds me, someone was asking about you. It was that harvest-witch, Celestine; she said the winds spoke your name.

You'd best hurry, <name>. We're going to need you to get back to the worgen-smashing once you're done conversing with nature.

passages.title: The Winds Know Your Name... Apparently
passages.text: We have been blessed today!  You are alive and well!

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text:
There's only so much I can teach right now with all these worgen trying to dismember us.

We really should think about heading south with the other survivors. We've been told that King Greymane is there.

If we stick together our chances of survival will increase... especially if you choose someone nutritious-looking to stand next to.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text: You've done well in coming here.  If we Gilneans stick together we might yet defeat this terrible enemy.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text:
I've taught you all that is practical for now.

It is time we joined with the other survivors. The others mentioned that King Greymane and his royal guard are just south of here.

We should go there and seek safety in numbers.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text: You've done well in coming here.  If we Gilneans stick together we might yet defeat this terrible enemy.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text:
I've taught you all that is practical for now.

It is time we joined with the other survivors. The others mentioned that King Greymane and his royal guard are just south of here.

We should go there and seek safety in numbers.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text: You've done well in coming here.  If we Gilneans stick together we might yet defeat this terrible enemy.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text:
There's only so much I can teach right now with all these worgen trying to dismember us.

We really should think about heading south with the other survivors. We've been told that King Greymane is there.

If we stick together our chances of survival will increase... especially if you choose someone nutritious-looking to stand next to.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text: You've done well in coming here.  If we Gilneans stick together we might yet defeat this terrible enemy.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text:
I've taught you all that is practical for now.

It is time we joined with the other survivors. The others mentioned that King Greymane and his royal guard are just south of here.

The others are going to need the aid of the Light in these troubling times.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text: You've done well in coming here.  If we Gilneans stick together we might yet defeat this terrible enemy.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text:
I've taught you all that is practical for now.

It is time we joined with the other survivors. The others mentioned that King Greymane and his royal guard are just south of here.

We should go there and seek safety in numbers.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text: You've done well in coming here.  If we Gilneans stick together we might yet defeat this terrible enemy.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text:
I've taught you all that is practical for now.

It is time we joined with the other survivors. The others mentioned that King Greymane and his royal guard are just south of here.

We should go there and seek safety in numbers.

passages.title: Safety in Numbers
passages.text: You've done well in coming here.  If we Gilneans stick together we might yet defeat this terrible enemy.

passages.title: Save Krennan Aranas
passages.text:
All these years after the war and Crowley was still hiding enough firepower in that cellar to level half of the district.

It might have to come to that, unfortunately.

We can't open fire just yet, there is a civilian trapped on the other side of the prison.

Not just any civilian, either. Krennan Aranas is one of the most brilliant alchemists this world has known.

One of his potions saved my daughter, Tess, from dying soon after being born.

Take my horse and rescue him. Krennan must live.

passages.title: Save Krennan Aranas
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  We'll make sure Krennan makes it out of the city alive.

passages.title: Time to Regroup
passages.text:
We've done all we can here. Let King Greymane know we've bought some time.

I've a feeling it won't be long 'til the worgen are back in force.

We'll need to fall back to Greymane Court to the west, if that's the case. It's the last place we can hold out without being trapped like fish in a barrel.

passages.title: Time to Regroup
passages.text: We're left with very few choices, <name>.  What we do next will be a critical decision.

passages.title: Among Humans Again
passages.text:
So Krennan's potion did not kill you? Well, I suppose that means the human inside of you is in control then.

I guess I won't be shooting you after all. At least not yet.

Go speak to Krennan Aranas and give him the good news. He's in charge of the house where we keep... your kind.

Just remember, <name>. I've got my eye on you. You so much as try anything funny and you'll get a bullet between the eyes.

passages.title: Among Humans Again
passages.text: It worked!  By the Light, it worked!

passages.title: In Need of Ingredients
passages.text:
Ah, yes. The effects of the Curse cannot ever be fully cured as far as we know.

With treatment, however, your mind will remain yours... and not that of a wild animal.

We are fortunate that the treatment worked on you. Normally, I can only treat recent infections.

We'll need to continue your medication if we're to have you reverse the Curse.

I will need mandrake essence to brew another batch of my serum for you. You will find a crate stashed beneath a shed southwest of town.

passages.title: In Need of Ingredients
passages.text: The crate has been smashed and the vials inside of it appear to have been broken.

passages.title: Invasion
passages.text:
<A long knife with a skull ornament on its hilt sticks out of the militiaman's ribs. As you look around for clues, you spot a pair of savage-looking warships at the shore.>

<Gilneas is being invaded. Bring word back to Duskhaven's Mayor, Gwen Armstead.>

passages.title: Invasion
passages.text: Forsaken!  Quick, <name>!  We must mount a defense.

passages.title: Kill or Be Killed
passages.text:
The reefs have always protected us from a coastal attack. The earthquakes must've opened a passage for the Forsaken ships.

Quick, <name>. Slow down the attackers while I get the rest of the militia ready.

I think I can hear the Prince and some of our men engaging the Forsaken even as we speak. Speak to Liam and see how you can be of use.

Oh... and make sure he doesn't get himself killed. I'm afraid he might be a little reckless in his current state.

passages.title: Kill or Be Killed
passages.text:
<name>!!!  You ARE alive!

I thought I was having dreams about the old days when I heard your voice...

passages.title: You Can't Take 'Em Alone
passages.text:
Look here, <name>. The big fat ones -- abominations, they're called -- they don't go down easy, so don't tackle them on your own.

But I have an idea so crazy it might just work. Or it might get you killed, if we're not careful, I suppose.

There's barrels of gunpowder beneath the sheds and by the windmills. Grab them and toss 'em right on the abominations' heads. I'll take care of the rest with this trusty old blunderbuss.

passages.title: You Can't Take 'Em Alone
passages.text: They just keep coming, don't they?

passages.title: You Can't Take 'Em Alone
passages.text:
You and me, <name>.  We make a great team...

It's good to have you back.

passages.title: Holding Steady
passages.text:
We can take it from here, <name>. Check in with Mayor Armstead.

These are only a small part of the Forsaken's forces. If we don't move quickly we're going to have bigger problems on our hands.

See what you can do to engage the Forsaken army at their landing location.

passages.title: Holding Steady
passages.text: Great news, <name>.  I've sent the remaining militia to the shore to meet the Forsaken force head on.

passages.title: Save the Children!
passages.text:
The military will not allow me outside the cellar, but my children are still in my farm! Please, you must go find them.

The Forsaken have no regard for innocent life -- my kids are in great danger!

Their names are Cynthia, Ashley and James. If you find them, bring them back here. I'll be forever in your debt.

passages.title: Save the Children!
passages.text: I... I don't know if I can go on without them.

passages.title: Save the Children!
passages.text: My children are safe!  You've done a wonderful thing, <name>.  I don't know how to thank you!

passages.title: Unleash the Beast
passages.text:
I'm not going to lie, <name>. I don't like the idea of having worgen among our ranks.

Who knows how long 'til Krennan's concoction wears off and you're trying to chomp one of our heads off.

Until that time, however, we can make ample use of your ferocity.

I want you to go out in the battlefield and kill as many of those Forsaken as you can, in as brutal a way as you can.

We're going to put the fear of the worgen in them, <name>.

passages.title: Unleash the Beast
passages.text: Not bad, <name>.  It's a good thing you're on our side.

passages.title: Leader of the Pack
passages.text:
Excellent work so far, <name>. Our scouts have identified the leader of the Forsaken ground assault.

One of Sylvanas' handpicked dark rangers is overseeing the battlefront from the Walden house near the shore. Take this whistle and use it when you're close to her.

I'll have my men let loose our attack mastiffs to take her down. Be careful, <name>. You don't want to engage her alone.

passages.title: Leader of the Pack
passages.text: Is it done yet, <name>?

passages.title: Leader of the Pack
passages.text: You did it, <name>.  That should take the wind out of their sails.

passages.title: Gasping for Breath
passages.text:
<name>! I was on my way when it happened.

No time to waste. A good half of the town watch was in the area that collapsed. Get in there and save as many as you can.

Make sure to get them out of the water and onto shore. I'll make sure they get any aid they need.

passages.title: Gasping for Breath
passages.text: There aren't many of us left, <name>.  We have to look out for those remaining Gilneans.

passages.title: Gasping for Breath
passages.text: You did what you could, <name>.  With any luck a few others will find their way to shore.

passages.title: As the Land Shatters
passages.text:
What in the world was that, <name>?

Those were not cannons or catapults, that is for sure.

Go outside and see what is going on.

passages.title: As the Land Shatters
passages.text: The ocean, <name>.  It swallowed everything... the land... the Forsaken... our men!

passages.title: Evacuation
passages.text:
We've escaped death through dumb luck, <name>. But luck is running out.

The coast is becoming flooded even as we speak. And from the look of it, the landmass beneath us hasn't quite settled yet.

I hate to say this, but we have to leave. Curses, <name>.... I cannot lose my homeland twice in one lifetime. Yet these earthquakes are not an enemy we can defeat.

Tell Gwen Armstead to start the evacuation.

passages.title: Evacuation
passages.text:
Liam is right.  We must get everyone to higher ground.

You must help me spread the word while I manage the logistics of the evacuation.

passages.title: Grandma Wahl
passages.text:
It's not going to be easy to get Grandma Wahl to come with us. You must do whatever you can to convince her, though.

You'll find her at the Wahl Cottage. Please, <name>. Do not lose your patience with her. Her mind is old and she's not entirely lucid.

passages.title: Grandma Wahl
passages.text: A visitor!  Are you staying for tea, sweetheart?

passages.title: Grandma's Lost It Alright
passages.text:
Leave? Now?

Well, if I must, then I must. But will you be a sweetheart and find something for me?

I've lost my favorite book and won't leave without it.

<After you explain the gravity of the situation, Grandma Wahl shakes her head condescendingly.>

Dear, just find the book will you?

passages.title: Grandma's Lost It Alright
passages.text: How goes it, dear?  Will you be staying for tea?

passages.title: Grandma's Lost It Alright
passages.text:
Why thank you, <name>.  I hope you didn't peek!

Where are your manners, dear?

passages.title: I Can't Wear This
passages.text:
What was it you wanted again?

Oh, right. The evacuation orders.

Well I can't be expected to go out in public like this, can I?

Go get me my good clothes. They're on the clothesline right outside.

<You struggle in vain to convince Grandma Wahl that what she's wearing will do.>

You young people truly have no manners. Were you raised by ogres? Now go get my clothes, sweetie.

passages.title: I Can't Wear This
passages.text: Did you find everything okay, dear?

passages.title: I Can't Wear This
passages.text: You're a peach, <name>.  Thanks!

passages.title: Grandma's Cat
passages.text:
Right! About the evacuation, dear.

I just cannot leave without my cat. He's an adorable orange tabby.

Chance's favorite spot to play is a broken down cart near an arbor northeast of here.

Bring him here and we'll be on our way.

passages.title: Grandma's Cat
passages.text: You're such a charming young man, <name>.

passages.title: Grandma's Cat
passages.text:
There he is!  Grandma's special boy!

Thank you so much for finding him.  I hope it wasn't too much trouble.

My... what manner of dirt found its way underneath my fingernails!

passages.title: Ready to Go
passages.text:
I suppose now is as good a time to leave as any.

I have my best outfit, my favorite book and my loving cat.

I hope I'm not forgetting anything.

Tell that mayor of yours that I'll be on my way. I suppose I'll see you in town with the others!

passages.title: Ready to Go
passages.text:
You did the impossible, <name>.  You convinced Grandma Wahl to leave her home.

You are something else, let me tell you.

passages.title: The Hayward Brothers
passages.text:
The Hayward Fishery can be found far to the south. The Hayward brothers have been running it for years.

They don't make it to town very often, except to trade their fish. Send word to them that the evacuation is underway.

passages.title: The Hayward Brothers
passages.text: You here to give us a hand?

passages.title: Not Quite Shipshape
passages.text:
Evacuation, you say? Well, we had that very same idea all on our own after these Forsaken started showing up.

We were thinking the water would be the safest way out of here.

Unfortunately our boats didn't come out from that last earthquake unscathed.

I need some additional supplies to finish my repairs: wood, tar and my tools. Get them for me so that my brothers and I can make it out of here.

passages.title: Not Quite Shipshape
passages.text: Do you have my supplies, <name>?

passages.title: Not Quite Shipshape
passages.text: This is great, <name>.  I should be able to finish the repairs in no time.

passages.title: Escape By Sea
passages.text:
Thanks for your help, <name>. This ship is ready to sail.

Now you go and tell Miss Armstead that we're not going to be part of the land evacuation.

We Haywards have been men of the sea for generations. If we're to leave our home, then we'll do so by sea.

passages.title: Escape By Sea
passages.text: It's just as well, <name>.  Maybe the Haywards will fare better than us.

passages.title: The Crowley Orchard
passages.text:
Of course you remember Lord Darius Crowley's daughter, Lorna.

She never quite recovered after losing her father in Gilneas City. She's basically led the life of a hermit. The only visitor she's allowed into her house has been Krennan... and he won't say a word about the whole thing.

Send word to her about the evacuation.

passages.title: The Crowley Orchard
passages.text:
Stay back! Don't make me...

Is it you?  By the Light!  It's you, <name>!

passages.title: The Hungry Ettin
passages.text:
Listen, <name>. We're not going to make it very far without transportation, are we?

If we just hightail it out of here, the forsaken will catch up to us in no time at all.

Rounding up some horses from the stable grounds southeast of here would normally be a breeze, but there's one snag.

That last quake must've spooked Koroth, the ettin, down from the mountains. If we don't get our horses soon, I fear that he will.

passages.title: The Hungry Ettin
passages.text: You're back, <name>.

passages.title: The Hungry Ettin
passages.text: We've got the horses, I'll make sure Duskhaven gets them.

passages.title: Horses for Duskhaven
passages.text:
Saving the horses might've saved the rest of the town. They have plenty of carriages in Duskhaven, but not enough horses to pull them.

Go tell Mayor Armstead that the horses you saved are at her disposal.

I'll get things ready and join you in a bit.

passages.title: Horses for Duskhaven
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  I think I speak for everyone when I say the sooner we get out of here, the better.

passages.title: To Greymane Manor
passages.text:
It's time for everyone to head to safety. That includes you, <name>. Head to Greymane Manor, the others will be there shortly.

Don't worry about me, I'll make sure that everyone makes it out of here in one piece. Yes, even the few ferals we have in the pens.

Once you get there, speak to Queen Greymane about the gravity of the situation.

passages.title: To Greymane Manor
passages.text:
<name>.  I've heard much about you.

I understand you were crucial in my family's survival during the outbreak in Gilneas City.

passages.title: The King's Observatory
passages.text:
You ought to speak to Genn. He's been locked up in his observatory ever since this ordeal started.

I'm sure he's working on a plan for his people. He's a very stubborn individual.

passages.title: The King's Observatory
passages.text:
There you are, <name>.  I've been expecting you.

I got word of your recovery and... wait -- do you feel that?

passages.title: It's Our Problem Now
passages.text:
Looks like those monkeys will steal anything! Those thieving little monsters have driven the teraptor matriarch into a frenzy by stealing her eggs. Worse yet, the eggs have started to hatch! We've got hungry teraptor hatchlings running around all over the place, looking to make a quick meal out of us!

We didn't start this, but it's our problem now. You'll have to head into the jungle and kill those hungry teraptor hatchlings before they kill us all.

passages.title: It's Our Problem Now
passages.text: Let's just hope we don't have to deal with their mommy later. That would be very bad.

passages.title: Goblin Escape Pods
passages.text:
<name>, I'm sorry, I thought you were dead!

This is just crazy. We sailed into a fight between the Alliance and Horde!

You know, our brothers and sisters still need to be rescued.

<He points out all of the escape pods in the water around you.>

I think I'm going to sit here a while longer and catch my breath. Can you swim around and let them out? Take my pair of thermohydratic flippers so you can get around faster.

Let Sassy know that I'll swim in shortly.

passages.title: Goblin Escape Pods
passages.text:
Oh, thank heavens that you survived, <name>! I thought for sure that you'd drowned when I saw you go over the side!

Look at all of these folks you saved!

passages.title: Exodus
passages.text:
We have no choice, <name>. We must move further inland.

I don't like it one bit, but we're vulnerable here.

Return to the stables below the manor. Let's get everybody on carriages and send them eastbound. I pray it's not too late.

passages.title: Exodus
passages.text:
Thanks for stopping, <name>.  Our carriage got hit pretty bad.

The one in front of us got it worse.

passages.title: Stranded at the Marsh
passages.text:
The ogres got two of our stagecoaches: this one and one that fell into the marsh just north of here.

I want you to head there and rescue any survivors while we hatch up a plan to deal with these ogres.

passages.title: Stranded at the Marsh
passages.text: Were any of the passengers still alive?

passages.title: Stranded at the Marsh
passages.text: You've done it again, <name>.  You have my thanks.

passages.title: Introductions Are in Order
passages.text:
The Forsaken are right on our heels and now these ogres are trying to flank us, <name>.

They're servants of the ettin Koroth -- the meanest, most destructive force in all of Gilneas.

If we can bait Koroth into charging the Forsaken's forward force, we should be able to cover our retreat and buy some time.

The only way this can work is if we make Koroth furious. It won't be enough to just kill his minions. We need to swipe his most prized possession, a tiger-skinned banner.

passages.title: Introductions Are in Order
passages.text: How did it go, <name>?

passages.title: Introductions Are in Order
passages.text:
You definitely got the ettin angry, <name>.   I heard him myself.

Let's hope this works.

passages.title: Stormglen
passages.text:
Our carriage drivers were told to regroup in the fishing town of Stormglen. Our scouts report there might be shelter and supplies to be found there.

Meet Gwen Armstead there, she'll be in charge of taking care of our people.

passages.title: Stormglen
passages.text:
It's good to see you made it, <name>.  It looks like most everybody did.

We're not doing too bad so far for an emergency evacuation.

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text:
Well, what do you know, <name>? All this time and Stormglen's been left mostly intact.

It's too bad the Forsaken are still working their way inland, but it'll make a fine place to rest our feet for a night or two.

The other half of town is overrun with spiders, so I've asked the villagers to stay away from there.

Perhaps you'd like to lend a hand in clearing the spiders out? I'm certain our injured men and women will sleep more soundly if they know someone's keeping those eight-legged beasts at bay.

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text: You're back, <name>.  Have the spiders been taken care of?

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text: You've done well, <name>.  The spiders are everywhere, however, and I'm afraid we've barely put a dent in their numbers.

passages.title: Pieces of the Past
passages.text:
I found a journal by a man named Bradshaw. Unfortunately it's missing many pages. Especially towards the end.

If you find enough of the pages I might be able to piece together what happened here after the Curse broke out.

Who knows... maybe the people in this town found a way out. Maybe there are still survivors out there.

 Maybe my father is still alive.

passages.title: Pieces of the Past
passages.text: Any luck finding those pages?

passages.title: Pieces of the Past
passages.text: Thank you, <name>.  It will take some time, but I'll try to make sense of what we have.

passages.title: Queen-Sized Troubles
passages.text:
The spiders keep coming in alarming numbers, <name>. You're going to have to go into their lair and kill the broodmother.

We've spotted the giant spider known as Rygna at the edge of the Blackwald in an area covered in thick webs. It'll be dangerous, but we're all counting on you.

passages.title: Queen-Sized Troubles
passages.text: Did you take care of Rygna, <name>?

passages.title: Queen-Sized Troubles
passages.text: Great job, <name>.  We've heard rumors of survivors further in the mountains.  Now we'll be able to send scouts there.

passages.title: Liberation Day
passages.text:
We recently found out that the villagers at Emberstone survived most of the ravages of the Curse.

Unfortunately their village wasn't as fortunate when it came to the Forsaken invasion.

The Forsaken have taken the villagers prisoner and are forcing them to work the nearby mine as slaves.

passages.title: Liberation Day
passages.text: You've done it again, <name>.  The freed villagers are eager to help us against the Forsaken in any way they can.

passages.title: The Blackwald
passages.text:
It took a while, but I think I've put together what happened here. At least partially.

There were survivors of the Curse in this town. They joined others in the mountains, in Tempest's Reach.

Everyone left, except the man who kept the journal, old man Bradshaw. He noticed that the worgen attacks had stopped all of a sudden and decided to venture into the Blackwald.

There is an abandoned mill just northeast of town, it was where Bradshaw lived. See if you can find any clues there.

passages.title: The Blackwald
passages.text:
I've been expecting you, <name>.  Do not be alarmed.

My name is Belrysa.  I am a priestess of the moon... a night elf.

You might not know my people, but the destinies of our two races have been linked since the Curse befell you.

passages.title: Laid to Rest
passages.text:
In our hurried escape for safety, we disturbed the resting homes of our ancestors, <name>. A grave sin, if you'll pardon the pun.

It is tradition that a small memento be buried on top of a Gilnean's graveyard, beneath the shallow earth. The stampede of people fleeing these tunnels has unearthed these mementos and angered the spirits.

Find them and bring them to me. We'll see to it that the dead return to their eternal slumber.

passages.title: Laid to Rest
passages.text: You're back, <name>.

passages.title: Laid to Rest
passages.text: Thank you, <name>.  Let us hope this works.

passages.title: Losing Your Tail
passages.text:
You must have many questions, <name>. And they will be answered in time.

I know why you're here and what you're looking for.

I can't lead you there with the enemy tracking you.

One of Sylvanas's scouts has been following your tracks. You can't lead the Forsaken to the place you seek. Take this talisman and walk along the road just north of here.

Let the ranger lure you to her trap and use the power of the talisman to break free and counterattack.

passages.title: Losing Your Tail
passages.text: Is it done, <name>?

passages.title: Losing Your Tail
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  The scout never had a chance.

passages.title: Tal'doren, the Wild Home
passages.text:
There are others like you, <name>. And they too, were lost and confused.

There is a place where you belong.

Tal'doren, the wild home, was once home to an order of druids who took the shape of wolves.

It is there that you will find the answers you seek. It is also there that you will find someone who can offer guidance. An old friend.

passages.title: Tal'doren, the Wild Home
passages.text:
You're all right, <name>!  I've been waiting for this day for a long time, it truly is great to see you friend.

I've heard of what you've done and I'm thankful... especially for Lorna -- she's all I've left.  I will send for her right away.

passages.title: At Our Doorstep
passages.text:
The night elves have taught us much during this time, <name>. They've taught us who we are and where we come from.

Thanks to them... thanks to this place... we're no longer mere beasts. We have regained free will.

The Forsaken aren't here for our land alone.

They're looking for something we possess. An artifact capable of uncontrollably spreading the Curse to all humanity. We cannot let them find it.

Sylvanas's banshees have come very close. Help my trackers take them out.

passages.title: At Our Doorstep
passages.text: You are as good as I remember, <name>.  It is good to have you back.

passages.title: Preparations
passages.text:
What you know as the Curse began as a heresy among our brethren.

Faced with a losing battle against demonic forces, the Druids of the Pack eschewed the balance they were sworn to and allowed the beast to overtake them.

They were banished to the Emerald Dream where they live in eternal slumber under a tree identical to this one, but not before their curse spread to others.

Today our ceremony will restore balance to your people. Bring me the leaf that grows only in Tal'doren's vicinity.

passages.title: Preparations
passages.text: You've returned, <name>.

passages.title: Preparations
passages.text: These simple leaves grow by Elune's grace.  They will help your mind understand the need for balance and your soul will permanently earn mastery over the beast.

passages.title: Onwards and Upwards
passages.text:
I will do as Darius asked and have our people move through the Blackwald.

You ought to catch up with King Greymane. He and Krennan went into Tempest's Reach after Lord Godfrey confirmed survivors had made their dwelling there.

Follow the road out of Stormglen into the mountains. I asked Krennan to wait for you at the bridge before Tempest's Reach.

passages.title: Onwards and Upwards
passages.text:
<name>!

Genn... they've taken Genn... they've taken... our king!

passages.title: Return to Stormglen
passages.text:
It'll be a long time before our nation comes together again. The old political divisions pale in comparison to what divides us now.

Yet if there was ever a time for us to come together and unite against a common enemy, it is now. And it is you, <name>, who have proven able to bridge the gap between our people.

Return to Stormglen and tell them it is safe to go through the Blackwald on their way to Tempest's Reach. We will take care of any Forsaken who follow them.

passages.title: Return to Stormglen
passages.text: King Greymane gave me a brief rundown of the plan before he set off for the Blackwald.  Doesn't make it sound any less crazy.

passages.title: Slaves to No One
passages.text:
I was one of the few that escaped, <name>. When the Forsaken took over our town and our mine, they treated us with utmost cruelty.

Those of us who were weak and could not endure hard labor were worked to death by the abomination known as Brothogg.

My wife was among his victims, <class>, and I swore that one day her death would be avenged. I am too frail now, but you can deliver justice... for my wife... for Gilneas!

passages.title: Slaves to No One
passages.text: I thank you, <name>.  Our people will no longer suffer under that monstrosity's yolk.

passages.title: Last Meal
passages.text:
I'm not dumb, <name>. I know what's ahead of us.

Our people are going to go through those gates and fight against an enemy that is better trained, has more numbers and better weapons than us.

Even if we succeed, it'll be at a great cost. For most of us, today's meal will be the last.

I cannot fight, but I sure can cook. Bring me meat from the stags that roam this area and I will ensure that the last meal these folks get will be their best.

passages.title: Last Meal
passages.text: Did you get what I needed, <name>?

passages.title: Last Meal
passages.text: I thank you, <name>.  Our men and women will have a last good meal before they set off for battle.

passages.title: Patriarch's Blessing
passages.text:
You've done it, <name>. Even in these times we must honor our dead.

Take these offerings and place them at Aderic's tomb.

Let's hope that's enough to placate the ghosts of our ancestors.

passages.title: Patriarch's Blessing
passages.text: Is it done, <name>?

passages.title: Patriarch's Blessing
passages.text: It's done, <name>.  The dead return to their slumber.

passages.title: Keel Harbor
passages.text:
We might've lost our city, but at least it looks like the dead have forgiven us.

Meet with the rest of the survivors in Keel Harbor.

I'm sure there's plenty to do before we're in the clear. Genn hasn't arrived yet, so I suppose Lord Crowley will be in charge there.

passages.title: Keel Harbor
passages.text: It's good to see you again, <name>.

passages.title: Trading Up
passages.text:
Hobart thinks he's going to feed us on those tiny clucker eggs? Bah! We're going to get some real eggs!

I've already set up some traps on the Raptor Rise up the path to the east. Take this bunch of wild clucker eggs and lay them in the traps. The spiny raptors will go right after the clucker eggs, and then you'll get to trade up to their larger eggs.

Genius!

passages.title: Trading Up
passages.text: How many did you get? I can just taste the massive omelet we're going to cook up now!

passages.title: Trading Up
passages.text:
Nice! Look at the size of those things!

There's no way that Grapplehammer's going to be able to top those!

passages.title: The Biggest Egg Ever
passages.text:
Bamm Megabomb? Who does he think he is? His spiny raptor eggs are no match for what we are about to recover!

As you well know, each Town-In-A-Box is equipped with a micro mechachicken for just such a dietary emergency. Luckily for us, my keen intellect was able to deduce the location that our prodigious, pre-programmed poultry ran off to.

Head north to the Scorched Gully. But beware, its circuit boards are fried and I imagine it's not so micro any longer!

passages.title: The Biggest Egg Ever
passages.text: Just think about the accolades that will rain down upon me... us, when the Biggest Egg Ever is returned!

passages.title: The Biggest Egg Ever
passages.text:
Eureka! My genius saves the day yet again! Take that Bamm Megabomb!

And now, to reap the benefits!

passages.title: Who's Top of the Food Chain Now?
passages.text:
Fine, fine, perhaps the whole egg thing didn't quite pan out. Who's up for some shark meat?

Only one little problem. Well, a big problem, actually. A really BIG problem: The Hammer!

Of course, I have a brilliant idea. Swim out into the Dire Strait to the west and get us some shark parts. Give them to my assistant, Greely. I'm too important to get my hands dirty with the small details.

passages.title: Who's Top of the Food Chain Now?
passages.text: <name>, take it easy on Grapplehammer. He's a genius, but he's got a fragile ego.

passages.title: Who's Top of the Food Chain Now?
passages.text: These will do very nicely! We're going to combine the shark parts and the robotic remains of the Mechachicken into a submersible that should allow you to rid us of that nuisance, The Hammer!

passages.title: Naga Hide
passages.text:
It's oft whispered in dark corners of a material so fine, so exquisite to the touch, that goblins of sophisticated taste will spend any amount of moolah to get their hands on some.

Of course, I'm speaking of naga hide!

<Brett looks around to make sure no one else is listening in.>

I know that you're going to head down there and that it's inevitable that you're going to have to fight those snakes. Hey, they're not going to have a use for their hides anyway. They'll be dead!

passages.title: Naga Hide
passages.text: Well? How many do you have for me? I think that a 95 to 5 split is more than generous.

passages.title: Naga Hide
passages.text: We're going to be filthy rich, I tell you! Well, if we can get off of this island, that is.

passages.title: Irresistible Pool Pony
passages.text:
I've got a plan and you're the only one that I know crazy enough to pull it off!

I need you to take this irresistible pool pony to the Vashj'elan Spawning Pool and inflate it. Then, swim down to their hatchlings with it on. I'll bet anything that the hatchlings can be lured away to follow you.

Bring them back here and we'll proceed with the next phase of the plan.

passages.title: Irresistible Pool Pony
passages.text: That's not enough hatchlings.

passages.title: Irresistible Pool Pony
passages.text: Oh, they're so cute! I wish that we could turn them into little plush toys and sell them for a gazillion macaroons!

passages.title: Town-In-A-Box: Under Attack
passages.text:
<name>, you have to defend us!

I had the eggheads deploy the town's cannon defenses, but it seems like there's an unlimited supply of these Oomlot warriors!

Get your behind into one of those B.C. Eliminators and eliminate the pygmy threat to the town!

passages.title: Town-In-A-Box: Under Attack
passages.text: That's not enough, hon. Can you take care of more of them?

passages.title: Town-In-A-Box: Under Attack
passages.text:
Okay, I think that's good enough for now, but they took a bunch of the townsfolk captive.

We're going to have to take the fight to them!

passages.title: Vengeance or Survival
passages.text:
Tell Greymane that we have trackers on Sylvanas and tell him about the Plague.

The decision will be his. Launch an all out attack against the leader of the Forsaken or try to evacuate our survivors.

passages.title: Vengeance or Survival
passages.text: You present me with the most difficult choice of my life, <name>.

passages.title: The Battle for Gilneas City
passages.text:
The time has come, <name>. We've rallied and armed every available Gilnean.

It is time to meet the enemy head on. Time to settle the score with Sylvanas and her Forsaken dogs once and for all.

Liam is heading the assault from this gate. King Greymane and my father are leading the assault on the other districts.

You have a crucial role to play in this as well. Take this rapier. Use it to inspire our men and women in combat. Speak to Krennan Aranas to take part in the battle for Gilneas City.

passages.title: The Battle for Gilneas City
passages.text: No...

passages.title: The Battle for Gilneas City
passages.text:
We've driven the Forsaken back.  We hold three out of the four districts.

But at what cost...

passages.title: Oomlot Village
passages.text:
The pygmies took most of our people back to their village. Who knows what evil they're up to?

<name>, you have to go up there and free all of the captives before the pygmies work their voodoo on them!

Izzy's already up near Oomlot Village to the southeast. She'll give you the heads-up on what's going down.

Your pygmy helmet looks like it's in bad shape, but it should last long enough for you to get there.

I hope.

passages.title: Oomlot Village
passages.text:
<name>? What are you doing wearing that pygmy helm? Looks like it's about to fall apart.

I'm glad that they sent you up here. I thought for sure they were going to send that jerk, Grapplehammer and his ego-enabling assistant.

passages.title: Free the Captives
passages.text:
They've got a bunch of our people in there. I know that they're doing strange rituals to them. It looks like they're sucking the life force right out of them!

You have to go into the village and free the captives before it's too late!

passages.title: Free the Captives
passages.text:
Great job, but that's not even half of the hostages that they took from town.

Darn it all! They must have taken the rest of the captives to their other villages up in the volcano!

passages.title: Send a Message
passages.text:
The Oomlot leader, Yngwie, is too powerful to be left alive. He's barking nonsense from the raised west side of the village, across the rope bridge.

Go up there and get him before he sends the rest of the village against us.

Piece of cake!

passages.title: Send a Message
passages.text: Nice work, bud! Hope he wasn't too tough.

passages.title: While You're At It
passages.text:
Fine by me if King Greymane wants you to risk your life to rescue a known traitor.

Do me a favor and do something useful while you're out there and kill these cursed fleabags.

passages.title: While You're At It
passages.text: What is it then, <name>?

passages.title: While You're At It
passages.text:
If I hadn't seen you kill a few of the mangy things with my own eyes, I'd think you did not complete the task I asked of you.

It looks like we're hardly putting a dent in their numbers.

passages.title: Three Little Pygmies
passages.text:
Look, I think it's great that we're destroying all of these zombies, even though they're our friends and family. But don't you think we should be taking care of the pygmies that are creating them as well?

At the three Oostan villages, Nord, Sor, and Ost, there are witch doctors: Gaahl, Malmo, and Teloch.

Maybe you could take care of them? I don't want to be turned into a zombie!

passages.title: Three Little Pygmies
passages.text: I gotta tell you, that's a load off of my mind. That is, I won't have to worry about no new zombies coming after my brains!

passages.title: Rockin' Powder
passages.text:
I'll give these pygmies one thing... they sure know how to party! But they're not so clever. I think I've discovered the source of their rockin' powers: Rockin' Powder!

It turns out that this stuff, which turns them into world-class rockers, is also highly explosive. We must have it!

So, while you're in there at Oostan to the east, make sure that you pickup a whole bunch of the stuff. Trust me, you're going to need it for what's coming up!

passages.title: Rockin' Powder
passages.text: Hmm, let me see how much you've got.

passages.title: Rockin' Powder
passages.text:
This will do. In fact, it's more than we need. I devised an ingenious idea for a weapon that the boots will be turned into once you get them to Hobart.

Hand the powder over and I'll load it into the the Super Booster Rocket Boots.

passages.title: Children of a Turtle God
passages.text:
Volcanoth is the turtle god in the cave that these primitives worship.

It's not really a god.

<Hobart rolls his eyes.>

But it is tough enough that I'm going to have to devise a new weapon for you from the one functioning boot we have left.

I think that the age-old motto of "fight fire with fire" applies here. Plus, I like fire!

Let's get some fire glands from Volcanoth's children. That should give me time to modify the rocket boot into something more fitting.

passages.title: Children of a Turtle God
passages.text: No time like the present to be done with the simple task I put before you, <name>. Wouldn't you agree?

passages.title: Children of a Turtle God
passages.text:
Careful with those glands, <name>, careful!

And now to load them into the refashioned shredder boot. I'm certain that you'll be surprised and amazed by my genius invention.

passages.title: Volcanoth!
passages.text:
It took a lot of blood, sweat, and tears, but the Bootzooka, patent-pending, is ready for use!

These no-good pygmies have been feeding our people to their "god", Volcanoth, and they're about to unleash it on our town!

You have to get into the cave and kill that thing before it's too late!

passages.title: Volcanoth!
passages.text:
I managed to get everyone else safely back to town.

Jump in, we gotta get out of here before the volcano blows for good!!!

passages.title: Mine Disposal, the Goblin Way
passages.text:
The paratroopers have mined the beach!

The Warchief asked me if there's anything we can do about that. I told him, 'You bet we can!'. I was thinking maybe you could take this satchel of grenades and detonate the land mines from a safe distance?

It's how we do things, right?!

passages.title: Mine Disposal, the Goblin Way
passages.text:
Boss, do you think you could go back down there and detonate a few more?

Thanks!

passages.title: Mine Disposal, the Goblin Way
passages.text: Score one for the goblins! Stupid dwarves and gnomes.

passages.title: The Pride of Kezan
passages.text:
This is ridiculous! Those gnomes just don't know when to stop!

Goblin pride is on the line here! <name>, you gotta jump into the Pride of Kezan and show them what's what!

Let me know when you're ready!

passages.title: The Pride of Kezan
passages.text: What are you doing back here? Get up there and shoot them down!

passages.title: The Pride of Kezan
passages.text: YES!

passages.title: Let's Ride
passages.text: Bastia will make sure that you get to where you need to go, goblin.

passages.title: Let's Ride
passages.text:
<name>?! Nice kitty.

Look we don't have much time here. You might have noticed that the volcano is blowing?!

passages.title: Kaja'Cola Gives You IDEAS! (TM)
passages.text:
Assistant Greely is clearly bewildered and intimidated. How will she help you to find a way to rescue everyone in this condition?

Maybe if she were to drink one of those Kaja'Cola Zero-One drinks you saw, she'd be able to have a bright idea?

passages.title: Kaja'Cola Gives You IDEAS! (TM)
passages.text: Huh?

passages.title: Kaja'Cola Gives You IDEAS! (TM)
passages.text: <Assistant Greely spots the Kaja'Cola Zero-One in your hand and her eyes seem to come to life.>

passages.title: Throw It On the Ground!
passages.text:
This nightmare will never be over while Blastshadow the Brutemaster still breathes. There are a couple of problems though.

One, being a warlock, he's got a succubus named Delicia Whipsnaps. If you kill Blastshadow quickly, the demon will go back to where it was summoned from.

The second problem, since Blastshadow is a warlock, he has a soulstone that allows him to resurrect. You have to get his soulstone and destroy it so that he'll be dead forever!

passages.title: Throw It On the Ground!
passages.text: The soulstone is the key, <name>!

passages.title: Throw It On the Ground!
passages.text: Your soulstone has expired, Blastshadow!

passages.title: Shredder Shutdown
passages.text:
That no-good Trade Prince Gallywix somehow managed to stow the whole Steamwheedle Sharks footbomb team away on the yacht. I didn't even see any of them!

Now he has them doing his dirty work here at the lumber yard. <name>, you're the <guy/gal> who won the championship for us back home on Kezan. You've got to get rid of them!

passages.title: Shredder Shutdown
passages.text: Looks like you might need to tackle one or two more of those Sharks.

passages.title: Shredder Shutdown
passages.text: I can't say that I was ever much of a footbomb fan, but you're giving me an appreciation for the game!

passages.title: The Ultimate Footbomb Uniform
passages.text:
Look, kid, I'm here to see to it that you've got a fighting chance at the end game. Thrall's going to need your help in the fight against the Trade Prince.

Greely, Hobart, and I have a plan to put together the ultimate footbomb uniform for you so that you can win the game, but I'm going to need some things first.

Lucky for us, this lumber yard is sick with spare shredder parts. Now get out there and give me 110%!

passages.title: The Ultimate Footbomb Uniform
passages.text: Let's see what you have there, <name>.

passages.title: The Ultimate Footbomb Uniform
passages.text:
Yeah, these will do nicely. You did good, kid. I'll see to it that you get the best footbomb uniform ever made.

In the meantime, you've got other bombs to drop on the Trade Prince's lackeys.

passages.title: What Kind of Name is Chip, Anyway?
passages.text:
<Dude/Girl>! You're never going to guess who's out on the oil platform to the north.

<Ace shakes head in disbelief.>

Chip's out there, and he's working for the Trade Prince. That traitor's now working for the other team. But worse, I heard he's got something goin' on with Candy Cane!

I don't know about you, but if he was shmoozin' up to my former definitely-real girlfriend, I'd do something about it.

passages.title: What Kind of Name is Chip, Anyway?
passages.text: There's no two ways about it... he got exactly what he deserved.

passages.title: Release the Valves
passages.text:
We have to stop Trade Prince Gallywix's oil supply and bring his machines to a grinding halt.

We're going to need you to go out to the KTC Oil Platform and release the valves to overload the coolant system. After you do that, head to the platform control panel on the platform and set it to blow.

passages.title: Release the Valves
passages.text: You have not yet released all four of the valves. The coolant to the platform is still functioning within normal operating parameters.

passages.title: Release the Valves
passages.text: All of the lights and indicators on the control panel are going crazy!

passages.title: Good-bye, Sweet Oil
passages.text: There is single big, red button on the platform control console. Clearly if ever there were a button to cause massive explosions, that is it!

passages.title: Good-bye, Sweet Oil
passages.text: I felt the heat from the explosions all the way over here!

passages.title: The Slave Pits
passages.text:
Sassy's over at the Slave Pits. She's there with the orcs getting ready to execute the final play on the Trade Prince.

<name>, take the footbomb uniform up the road to the southwest and find her. I know she's going to want you to lead the charge!

Ack, I'm starting to talk like the coach now!

passages.title: The Slave Pits
passages.text:
I was wondering where you were!

Don't worry, Hobart will get that footbomb uniform converted into the most Ultimate Footbomb Uniform ever!

passages.title: She Loves Me, She Loves Me NOT!
passages.text:
Oh, sweetie! You're never going to guess who's down in the slave pits to the north.

<Sassy shakes her head sadly at you.>

Candy's down there, and she's working for the Trade Prince. She dropped you like a bad habit and now she's working for the other team. but it gets worse. Since you "dealt" with Chip, she's shmoozin' up to the Trade Prince!

I don't know about you, but if she were my absolutely-not-fake girlfriend, I'd rip her fickle heart right out of her chest.

passages.title: She Loves Me, She Loves Me NOT!
passages.text: What did you decide to do, hon?

passages.title: She Loves Me, She Loves Me NOT!
passages.text:
I'm sure she deserved it, <name>. She should never have betrayed you like that.

It gives me the shivers to think that she might have kissed that monster, the Trade Prince!

passages.title: What Kind of Name is Candy, Anyway?
passages.text:
Can you believe that Candy Cane! You know up until you "dealt" with Chip, she was tryin' to start a partner brand with him. Now she's shmoozin' up to the Trade Prince!

I just can't get over the fact that she betrayed you like that with your absolutely-not-fake boyfriend. Maybe you should head down into the Slave Pits and take care of her once and for all?

passages.title: What Kind of Name is Candy, Anyway?
passages.text: Serves her right for stealing your man in the first place.

passages.title: Brothers In Arms
passages.text:
Listen, <name>. For the first time since the civil war I agree with Greymane. Now is the time to put aside our quarrel.

It sure doesn't look like these beasts care much whether you're a rebel or a royal.

Send word back to Greymane. My men will join his.

There's a safehouse not far from here, in Josiah's cellar. My lads stashed some heavy artillery there.

Tell our king that my arsenals are now at his disposal.

passages.title: Brothers In Arms
passages.text:
Rebel arsenals?  In my own city?

What in the bloody hell was Crowley up to?

passages.title: Endgame
passages.text:
We need to get rid of that flying gunship if our people have any chance of escaping.

Here's the plan. Keel Harbor had its share of rebel sympathizers in the old days. I've managed to round up a hefty amount of incendiary explosives from one of our storehouses.

We're going to hit the enemy with a force small enough to fly undetected. The night elf hippogryphs should do the trick.

Tobias will give you the signal when we're ready to go.

passages.title: Endgame
passages.text: The only risks worth taking are the ones that lead to victories worth having.

passages.title: Endgame
passages.text: We did it, <name>.  We've started the evacuation.  If we leave soon we'll leave the Forsaken fleet in the dust.

passages.title: Legends of the Sunken Temple
passages.text:
I will need you to enter the temple first, <name>. I can join you once a path is secure, but I dare not enter blindly. Turned against my kind, I would be a vicious enemy.

You can start by descending the stairs behind me. Then, swim through the flooded depths of the Broken Hall. Once there, follow the passageway to the right to find the Hall of Masks.

Beware of any temple guards. Once you have found the Hall of Masks, I will contact you through the Oathstone.

passages.title: Legends of the Sunken Temple
passages.text: You must not falter, <name>. Your actions will pave the way for me to enter the temple myself.

passages.title: Legends of the Sunken Temple
passages.text:
This is it!

These are the bones of my kin...

passages.title: Step One: The Priestess
passages.text:
My brethren are being butchered here. It's as I thought.

I must ask your help further before I enter, <name>. In the passageway outside this room, the hallway proceeds left and right. To the right, it goes down to the Chamber of Blood. Here the Atal'ai perform their dark rituals.

They have expected and prepared for my kind for years, but not for you. Enter the Chamber of Blood and slay the Priestess Udum'bra. She is one of three foul presences here that must be vanquished before I may enter.

passages.title: Step One: The Priestess
passages.text: You must not falter, <name>. Your actions will pave the way for me to enter the temple myself.

passages.title: Step One: The Priestess
passages.text:
Good riddance. Another source of corruption in this world put to rest.

I thank you for your bravery, <name>.

passages.title: Step Two: The Bloodletter
passages.text:
The trolls here perpetuate the fall of my brethren to the nightmare. They infect and corrupt green dragons with the blood of their foul god, and then harvest the evil that has grown within them. They are being farmed like livestock...

This disgusting savagery cannot continue. Return to where you left the Hall of Masks and take the other corridor toward the Butchery. Gomora the Bloodletter harvests corpses for these foul and evil rituals there. Take his undeserved life from him!

passages.title: Step Three: Prophet
passages.text:
All that yet stands between me and the temple is Prophet Jammal'an himself. He is the leader of the Atal'ai trolls here, a foul manipulator.

Know that you do not face a mere crazed troll, <name>, but an instrument of forces beyond your darkest comprehension. Yet you do not fight alone--my strength and the will of the Green Dragonflight go with you.

Proceed to the Den of the Caller, left through the Hall of Ritual, and then down into the Hall of Bones. At the bottom, you will find Jammal'an.

passages.title: Step Three: Prophet
passages.text:
He has escaped! I should have known it would not be so easy.

The path is clear, <name>. It is time to return.

passages.title: Ethereum Data
passages.text:
Look around you, fleshling. Very close to this transponder should be an Ethereum data cell. Locate that data cell, open it, and retrieve the contents.

Bring it back to this transponder at once!

passages.title: Ethereum Data
passages.text: Have you recovered the data cell?

passages.title: Ethereum Data
passages.text:
<You hold the data cell out so Ameer can read the plans.>

Nothing... Damn them! They're clever but not as clever as Ameer!

What I'm about to ask you to do is quite dangerous. I'll understand if you don't want to continue, fleshling.

passages.title: Potential for Brain Damage = High
passages.text:
They're using relays to transfer information around the staging grounds.

There is only one way for you to see these relays and extract the information they hold. Unfortunately, doing so may cause you irreparable brain damage.

If you're still interested, you'll need to slay Ethereum here at the staging grounds and take their essences. Once you have an essence, drink it down. It will temporarily allow you to see an Ethereum relay, giving you enough time to destroy a relay and extract its information.

passages.title: Potential for Brain Damage = High
passages.text: Have you recovered the relay data?

passages.title: Potential for Brain Damage = High
passages.text:
The Protectorate's reason for existence is now fully realized.

The Ethereum are not here to hunt Dimensius! They are here to become void!

They are manipulating the void energy at this manaforge to bond their own energy into a creature known as a nexus-stalker.

They are undoubtedly using a proto-accelerator to complete the transformation.

passages.title: Recipe for Destruction
passages.text:
Atop Manaforge Ultris lies the tear in the nether that Void Lord Dimensius came through. That tear provides Dimensius with a link to the Void, rendering him immune to physical harm. If we can get a lock on the conduit that Dimensius is using to keep himself phased out of this plane of existence, we can destroy it and then destroy Dimensius.

To do this, we're going to first need you to collect fragments of Dimensius from the void creatures that he sends out to do his dirty work.

passages.title: Recipe for Destruction
passages.text: Have you collected enough fragments?

passages.title: Recipe for Destruction
passages.text: Excellent. With these fragments, we can calibrate a bomb that will destroy the void conduit atop Ultris. With the void conduit destroyed, Dimensius's connection with the void will be severed and he will be left defenseless!

passages.title: The Frozen Flame
passages.text:
It is time we make our move, <name>. I can conjure a portal that will take you directly inside but it will take some time before I can make another and join you.

The Lich King will no doubt sense the magic of your arrival so you will need to move fast to locate Felo'melorn and secure it.

If Lyandra has the blade with her then I fear she may not relinquish it easily. Be prepared for anything, <name>.

passages.title: The Frozen Flame
passages.text:
Felo'melorn... I can barely believe that such great power is locked within a blade as beautiful as this!

With this weapon in your hands, the Legion will surely fall!

passages.title: Before the Storm
passages.text:
<name>! I have been looking all over this strange city for you!

Grand Master Hight has requested all senior monks to return to the Peak of Serenity as soon as possible. That means you too, of course.

I'll bet a week's worth of brew that this has something to do with the assault on the Broken Shore I've heard tales about!

passages.title: Before the Storm
passages.text:
Welcome back to the land of the living, <name>. We nearly lost you in that explosion! Lucky for us that the Wandering Isle happened to be traveling nearby.

The people here have graciously allowed us to reside at the temple. It's not like the Peak of Serenity, but this will make a fine new home.

passages.title: To Speak With Har'koa
passages.text:
The gods have spoken, <name>. We now know what you must do.

You must now go to the Altar of Har'koa to the southeast and speak with the leopard goddess.

passages.title: To Speak With Har'koa
passages.text: Listen closely, little <race>. Time is of the essence.

passages.title: Spirit of Rhunok
passages.text:
My feelings tell me that Rhunok doesn't have much time.

I can tell that the arctic bear god's spirit has already separated from his weakened body. It is his spirit with which you must commune.

His altar lies to the northwest beyond Drak'Mabwa.

passages.title: Spirit of Rhunok
passages.text: I am barely hanging on. You must work quickly or all will be lost.

passages.title: The Ethereum
passages.text:
Directly south of here you will find the Ethereum Staging Grounds. The Ethereum are there, preparing for something... Perhaps an assault on Ultris.

We can't take any chances, though, <class>. Break through their perimeter defenses and take out their training facility.

Once you've destroyed their soldiers and Captain Zovax, locate Ethereum transponder Zeta and use it to establish contact with me to get your next set of orders.

passages.title: The Ethereum
passages.text: Well done, fleshling...

passages.title: The Ethereum
passages.text: We must gather whatever data that they've stored in this area.

passages.title: Delivering the Message
passages.text:
I'm sending one of my demolitionists out to place the disruption device. Just make sure no harm comes to him as he's placing the disruptor.

Keep him protected! He will not fight back if enemies attack him, as he is only a holographic image, but the image can be destroyed!

Return to me once the job is done.

passages.title: Delivering the Message
passages.text: He must succeed!

passages.title: Delivering the Message
passages.text: Thanks to you, their plans are in ruin! Now only one thing remains... Salhadaar.

passages.title: Nexus-King Salhadaar
passages.text:
I have in my possession another disruptor--one capable of destroying the three conduits that surround Salhadaar. Once the conduits are destroyed, Salhadaar's protective force fields will be down. For this act, he will strike at you with a ferocity you have never before witnessed, <name>.

If you are willing to rid the world of Salhadaar, I will give you the disruptor.

passages.title: Nexus-King Salhadaar
passages.text: Is... Is he really dead? Destroyed?

passages.title: Nexus-King Salhadaar
passages.text: It has been a thousand years, maybe more, since Salhadaar began his crusade to exterminate all that would stand in his way. I can hardly believe that this is the last we'll see of him... You have done all of us a great service, <name>, and for that you will be rewarded.

passages.title: Dimensius the All-Devouring
passages.text:
Your brave actions have forced Ameer to react! He has deployed Captain Saeed and the Avengers!

Now all that is left to do is destroy Dimensius.

When you are ready, I will call for Saeed. If he is not currently fighting another battle, he will be awaiting orders from you directly east of here.

Let him know when you are ready to fight and he will put his troops in motion!

I wish you luck, fleshling! We have hunted Dimensius for a thousand years!

passages.title: Dimensius the All-Devouring
passages.text: What of the void lord?

passages.title: Dimensius the All-Devouring
passages.text:
For a thousand years, all we have known is conflict. We have defended our people from the attacks of both void creature and ethereal alike.

Now, one of our most hated enemies lies dead - finally.

I give you the thanks of a hundred million ethereals, fleshling.

passages.title: The Forgotten Tale
passages.text:
The toxins in the murkweed elixir will render you unconscious. So powerful is the effect of the murkweed that even your spirit will be fooled, allowing you to temporarily enter the world of the dead.

Once a spirit, you must speak to the ghostly denizens of the Forgotten Shore. Seek out the cause of their anguish and return to me.

Remember, <name>, these spirits were once Alliance soldiers. Treat them with respect, honor, and dignity.

Now, with elixir in hand, venture south to the Forgotten Shore.

passages.title: The Forgotten Tale
passages.text: I have enough murkweed to make more elixirs, <name>.

passages.title: The Forgotten Tale
passages.text:
<Orik's eyes fill with tears.>

They don't know. None of them know! They think Arthas to be some great hero, when in truth it was Arthas who ordered the ships to be burned. It was Arthas who left us all for dead in this frozen wasteland!

<Orik weeps.>

Not all of the soldiers from the Prince's fleet perished in the freezing winter. I was only a lad when I was given the chance to battle the Scourge... to save our home from certain destruction. I took that chance, <name>.

passages.title: The Truth Shall Set Us Free
passages.text:
Zelig gave this crystal ball to me years ago with specific instruction on its use. For five years, whenever I would feel anger, anxiety, or sorrow over the events that transpired here, I was to focus my thoughts upon the orb.

I now understand why Zelig gave this crystal to me.

Take my crystalline orb to the Forgotten Shore. Find the ruins of my old base on the upper reaches of the beach and place the orb in the center of town. Let the forgotten see the world through my heart and soul.

passages.title: The Truth Shall Set Us Free
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: The Truth Shall Set Us Free
passages.text:
<Orik beams a smile at you.>

You did a good thing this day, <name>. Hundreds of lost souls are now redeemed, thanks to you.

passages.title: Parting Thoughts
passages.text:
You have honored me and honored the memory of hundreds of Alliance veterans, <name>. Zelig was wise in sending you here. Please return to him and give him my thanks. He will be happy to hear of the events that transpired at the Forgotten Shore.

I do not have the gift of foresight like Zelig, but I am certain that great things await you, friend.

Farewell.

passages.title: Parting Thoughts
passages.text:
<Zelig smiles.>

It is I who owe you a debt of gratitude, hero. Orik is like a brother to me. You have changed his life and given renewed hope to countless others.

passages.title: Frostmourne Cavern
passages.text:
They have labeled the cave as Frostmourne Cavern. Why the Scarlet Onslaught is interested in such things is unknown, but by the look of things, the area surrounding the cave is heavily guarded. Nonetheless, we must proceed!

Take this scrying orb and travel north out of town and then northwest toward Scarlet Point. Make your way into the cave and battle your way to the bottom. Once there, use the orb. Return here with what you discover.

passages.title: Frostmourne Cavern
passages.text: Have you searched Frostmourne Cavern?

passages.title: Frostmourne Cavern
passages.text:
Muradin lives? Could it be? I must notify King Bronzebeard at once!

I need to consult the orb. There must be more information - somewhere!

passages.title: But First My Offspring
passages.text:
I am the last of the gods to be subdued, so we must first attempt to free the others. Bound by the magics of my subduers, I am unable to discern their fates.

But first, I would ask that you do me a kindness. Already the Drakkari turn my magic against me. They have transformed my offspring into monstrosities.

Take one of my whiskers. Slay my tortured children and use the magic of it to release them from their nightmare, and bring them back to life.

passages.title: But First My Offspring
passages.text: There are more of my offspring that you must free from their torment!

passages.title: But First My Offspring
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. I will never forget what you have done.

passages.title: My Prophet, My Enemy
passages.text:
My prophet absorbed too much of my power too quickly, and subsequently killed himself. You can see the results at the water-filled crater to the south in Drak'Mabwa.

My former priests have already resurrected him so that he can finish the job. They're channeling my power back into him, and it will not be long now before he reawakens.

You must put an end to him and return with my mojo before it is too late.

passages.title: My Prophet, My Enemy
passages.text: Quickly, <race>, do you have my mojo?

passages.title: My Prophet, My Enemy
passages.text:
You did it.

But now there is one other thing that I need you to do.

passages.title: An End to the Suffering
passages.text:
My body is too far gone now, <name>. It is only a matter of time before a new prophet is elevated and finishes what the other began.

I am going to imbue you with the last of my power. The tormentor inside the altar building carries incense, which will awaken my body and make it vulnerable.

Use the incense and do me the kindness of putting an end to my suffering.

I apologize if I fight back. Even for me, the will to survive is strong.

passages.title: An End to the Suffering
passages.text: If you do not put an end to my suffering soon, <name>, all may be lost.

passages.title: An End to the Suffering
passages.text:
You've done what had to be done and honored me in the process.

I give you my deepest thanks, <name>. I only hope that you and Har'koa will be able to help the others.

passages.title: Rampage
passages.text:
<name>, there is no time left. You must take the key and use it to unlock Akali.

He is being held in the courtyard in front of Gundrak, the capital of Zul'Drak. Akali's chains are secured by four anchor points. You must unlock each of them to set the rhino god free.

Gundrak is teeming with ice trolls. However, I believe that if you're careful, you should be able to slip in without too much danger.

Once you're done, please inform the witch doctor.

passages.title: Rampage
passages.text:
No!

Another god destroyed, its power stolen. And now the prophet of Akali has threatened us directly.

When he comes, he will come for Har'koa. We cannot allow him to take her power too.

We must consult the gods once more, <name>. They will tell us what must be done.

passages.title: The Gods Have Spoken
passages.text:
The gods have spoken and we must heed their wisdom.

Travel north to Zim'Rhuk to destroy guardians there until they yield the unblemished heart. Travel east to the Altar of Quetz'lun and disrupt the altar wardens until you recover their gusty essence.

Deliver both to Har'koa and she will combine them into that which will compel late Akali's prophet to appear.

passages.title: The Gods Have Spoken
passages.text: Do you have that which is required, <name>?

passages.title: The Gods Have Spoken
passages.text:
Your bravery seems boundless, <name>.

Please hand me the heart and the essence, and I will fashion them into that which will compel the prophet to appear before you.

passages.title: Convocation at Zol'Heb
passages.text:
You must take this instrument of convocation--of summoning--to Zol'Heb just south of Gundrak.

Therein you will find a circle of power. Use the convocation to force the prophet of Akali to appear.

My heart goes out to you, <name>. We have been through much together, and you have done all that you can to not only save my life, but those of the other gods the Drakkari have destroyed.

But I fear this time we may not see each other again until the afterlife.

passages.title: Convocation at Zol'Heb
passages.text:
I can only offer you the warmth of my words and the encouragement that comes with them.

Take what time you need to steel and prepare yourself, but I implore you not to take too long or the prophet will surely descend upon us.

passages.title: Convocation at Zol'Heb
passages.text:
You did it! <name>, you are the champion of Zul'Drak!

We will never be able to repay the debt that we owe to you, but the Zandalari have given into my trust a number of objects they believe you might have an interest in.

Please, I want you to have a token of our appreciation, but hurry. I sense another issue of urgency!

passages.title: Monkey Business
passages.text:
We've got major problems with the monkeys in the jungle to the east. They've stolen all of our explosives, and now they're going around throwing them.

Sometimes at us!

I had Fizz Lighter take some of his nitro and put it in these bananas. No monkey can resist a bunch of bananas!

All you have to do is go out there and feed them.

passages.title: Monkey Business
passages.text: Did it work?

passages.title: Monkey Business
passages.text:
They launched up into the air when they ate the bananas?! That is hilarious!

I think I'm going to take a bunch out there and feed them myself!

passages.title: Capturing the Unknown
passages.text:
Heya, <name>, there are strange cave paintings and other artifacts all over the cavern.

Do you think you could use your belt-mounted KTC Snapflash camera to capture images at the designated spots? Also, snap a pic of the altar in the back of the cavern.

I'm sure that Sassy will want the intel.

passages.title: Capturing the Unknown
passages.text:
What are these?

<Sassy examines the pictures while listening to your tale from the Kaja'mite cavern.>

Clearly that pygmy witchdoctor is from some new race never seen before. Maybe we should call them <name>-ians?

They must be the ones that painted all of that stuff in the cavern. I'm not sure that I like what you're describing.

It sounds to me like they're paintings of them and us on an island with an exploding volcano!

passages.title: Orcs Can Write?
passages.text:
Looking through the dead orc's belongings, you find a field journal. Though it is heavily water damaged, the writing is still legible, if barely.

Flipping through the pages, an interesting story unfolds. Good thing you decided to study Orcish.

Like the Trade Prince's yacht, the orcs were fired upon by Alliance warships. You do remember an orc warship that you passed right before the Alliance opened fire. Maybe they were firing on the orcs instead of your ship?

Stupid orcs! They got you sunk!

passages.title: Orcs Can Write?
passages.text: <name>, find anything interesting in the cavern?

passages.title: Orcs Can Write?
passages.text:
Orcs?! They were sunk and stranded too?  And now the Alliance are on the island? Do you think they're going to kill us?

<Sassy looks thoughtful.>

I think it's time for a little sitdown with these orcs.

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy
passages.text:
I hate to ask you to do this, but I guess it's why they pay you the big bucks. Can you deliver that dead orc's field journal to whoever is in charge up at their camp?
