Based on the writing in the book, they should be located at the top of the island, up the incline past the Kaja'mite cavern to the southeast.

Good luck, <name>. I always liked you.

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy
passages.text:
<The orc narrows her eyes at you.>

You must have been on the <race> slave ship that was sunk. What's that you have in your hand?

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy
passages.text:
<The orc makes a move to grab the field journal from you, but then stops herself, exhaling deeply.>

I apologize. It has been a very rough couple of days for all of us.

I am Aggra. All of us here are what remains of the crew of the Draka's Fury.

Perhaps we can work together. We have a common enemy in the Alliance. Their SI:7 assassins are all over this island and they're not going to stop until we're all dead.

passages.title: The Vicious Vale
passages.text:
Our hunter, Kilag Gorefang, and a few scouts, traveled into the vale down the path to the west. They're ...searching for... 'precious cargo'... that we were guarding when the filthy Alliance sunk our ship.

The way is blocked by deadly plants and they have not been able to break through.

<name>, prove your worth as a goblin and a <class>. Journey into the Vicious Vale to find Kilag.

passages.title: The Vicious Vale
passages.text:
<race>, can you fight?

For your sake, I hope so. Otherwise, there may be no breaking through this hell of killer plants.

passages.title: Weed Whacker
passages.text:
<Kilag barely has time to acknowledge you between rifle shots, but his eye does linger a moment on your Goblin All-In-1-der Belt appreciatively.>

Now is the time for creative solutions. Pull something out of that belt and get to work!

<Thinking about the situation for a moment, an idea comes to your mind and it's just crazy enough to work!>

passages.title: Weed Whacker
passages.text:
There are still too many for us to get through.

Have faith in yourself, <name>. Let your true warrior heart shine through.

passages.title: Weed Whacker
passages.text:
I saw it with my own eyes, and still I do not believe it!

You have our thanks and the debt of our lives, little <race>. I hope that soon we can repay you the honor.

May I ask a small favor of you while my scouts and I move on?

passages.title: Forward Movement
passages.text:
Kilag should be in position by now. It is time for you to move forward to the Wild Overlook. The rest of us will pack up here and move out soon.

Just follow the path northwest through the Vicious Vale. Not so vicious any longer thanks to you, eh?

Kilag and his scouts will be keeping themselves hidden just off the path, but the SI:7 assassins are sure to spot them soon, so hurry!

passages.title: Forward Movement
passages.text: Throm-Ka, <name>. We have a problem.

passages.title: Infrared = Infradead
passages.text:
Keep your voice down. The glen north and west of here is crawling with Alliance assassins.

Unfortunately, we haven't been able to spot them. The cowards! They hide and won't fight face-to-face.

You goblins are known for your wondrous goggles. Surely you have a pair that will allow you to see them?

I need you to team up with one of my scouts and kill any of the SI:7 assassins that you spot.

passages.title: Infrared = Infradead
passages.text: You got them all?

passages.title: Infrared = Infradead
passages.text:
Well done, <name>, well done. We'll make an orc of you yet!

Time to move on. We'd better hurry.

passages.title: To the Cliffs
passages.text:
I sent Scout Brax forward along the road to the cliffs overlooking the beach to the west.

I am going to put you onto Bastia. Travel down the path and let Brax know that we are going to take a different route.

We'll see you at the attack on the Alliance beachhead!

passages.title: To the Cliffs
passages.text:
Hello, little <race>. Bastia is fast, no?

We have something very important that needs doing. Can you help us?

passages.title: Get to the Gyrochoppa!
passages.text:
The Alliance have stolen something of vital importance to the Horde. It is being held out on their ships.

At the other end of the beach is a gyrochoppa. Our battlesworn will cover your approach.

Go retrieve the keys to the flying machine from one of their operatives.

Fly out to their flagship, the Vengeance Wake, and retrieve our precious cargo!

passages.title: Get to the Gyrochoppa!
passages.text: Hmm, looks like overly-complicated gnomish engineering with lots of unnecessary instrumentation and safety precautions.

passages.title: Get to the Gyrochoppa!
passages.text:
Hmm, where the heck is the ignition?

It'll be a wonder if it flies without doing something weird, like turning into a chicken or shrinking down to the size of an ant.

Hey look, someone left their loose change in the ashtray! What else is in there?

passages.title: Precious Cargo
passages.text:
They said that their "precious cargo", whatever that is, is being held out on the Alliance ship, the Vengeance Wake.

There's only one thing to do... fly this thing out there and retrieve it!

passages.title: Precious Cargo
passages.text: Perhaps you can help me to get out of this arcane cage?

passages.title: Precious Cargo
passages.text:
If not for you, I would surely be on my way back to Stormwind to be paraded as a trophy and a slave.

The Alliance dogs found me unconscious on the shore and put me in this magical cage. It was keeping me from connecting with the elements.

No longer!

passages.title: Warchief's Revenge
passages.text:
Brothers of Earth and Fire, hear me! Sisters of the Water and Air, heed my call!

Azeroth stands on the brink, its existence near an end! Lend me your power as in times past with my ancient ancestors. Allow me to channel your will through this child of Kezan.

Let us put an end to those who would keep us from healing the world!

passages.title: Warchief's Revenge
passages.text: You have done what few others could have, <name>. Our world owes you a debt larger than you can possibly understand.

passages.title: Help Wanted
passages.text:
Great news! Foreman Dampwick has uncovered a cave full of kaja'mite on the island! What are the odds?

Of course, there's a downside. He took some of the survivors with him to help mine the ore, but none of them have made it out.

Crazy as it sounds, the foreman said that there are monkeys in the cave... with mining picks! They're mining the kaja'mite! How is that even possible?

Can you head southeast to the cavern? The foreman is standing just outside the entrance.

passages.title: Help Wanted
passages.text:
Boss! Er, well, I guess you're not the boss anymore, but still, good to see you!

Can you believe it? We've got a cave full of intelligent killer monkeys mining Kaja'mite!

passages.title: Back to Aggra
passages.text:
Return to the Horde Base Camp and let Aggra know that we still live, <name>.

Tell her that I am moving on to the Wild Overlook and that we will all meet up on the northwest side of the island. I expect to see you there.

We will track down the Alliance and slay them to the last!

passages.title: Back to Aggra
passages.text:
<Aggra gives you the eye as if she doesn't quite believe what you are telling her.>

I am not easily impressed, but if what you are telling me is true, then I have never before heard of such a thing.

You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: Meet Me Up Top
passages.text:
I never thought that I would be a prisoner of the Alliance again. I cannot begin to express my gratitude to you... <name>, is it?

I will meet you up top and from there we will deal with them.

passages.title: Meet Me Up Top
passages.text: My mission is too critical to let these meddlers continue to dog us. It's up to you and I to put an end to this once and for all!

passages.title: Hold the Line
passages.text:
<name>! I'm still not sure if you're alive or dead... human or worgen...

I'm not even sure if I'm really awake. But THIS I am sure of...

We're going to kill a great many of these motherless Forsaken.

passages.title: Hold the Line
passages.text:
Yes, <name>!  Just like old times...

I'm going to have to work hard at not shooting you, but Krennan explained everything to us.

passages.title: The Allens' Storm Cellar
passages.text:
Lord Godfrey is leading the attack near the Forsaken's landing area. See what you can do to help us keep the Forsaken back.

I've been told Godfrey has commandeered the storm cellar in the Allen Farmstead, far to the west. Seek him there.

passages.title: The Allens' Storm Cellar
passages.text: The Forsaken are here in full strength, <name>.  We barely have enough men to hold them back.

passages.title: Two By Sea
passages.text:
The Forsaken catapults are kicking the snot out of us, <name>. And even if we do take care of them, they've two ships with rows of cannons at the ready.

I've a plan to kill two birds with one stone. You're the stone in this plan.

Take out the machinists manning the catapults. After this, use the catapults to launch yourself aboard the Forsaken ships.

If your aim isn't terrible, you should be able to land safely. Once onboard, go below decks and take care of each ship's captain. Good luck, <class>.

passages.title: Two By Sea
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  You might be a bloody beast, but you're our beast.

passages.title: Washed Up
passages.text:
Those Forsaken ships sank way too close to our Fishery. All the survivors are making their way here and, as you can see, we're a bit outnumbered.

Help us hold them back while I finish making repairs to the boats.

passages.title: Washed Up
passages.text: Bloody Forsaken!  Not even the ocean wants them!

passages.title: Washed Up
passages.text: Excellent!  I'm almost done here.

passages.title: Farewell, For Now
passages.text:
Our destinies are forever intertwined. There are events taking place that are reshaping our world and ultimately will destroy it. We must put an end to them before it is too late.

Know that you can always count on me, <brother/sister>! We will meet again on the larger island. May you find peace until then, <name>.

passages.title: Farewell, For Now
passages.text:
Wow, oh wow! Is that who I think it is?

You rescued Thrall, Warchief of the Horde?!!!

<Sassy gives you an appraising look.>

Well, let's see about getting over to that larger island. I sure as heck don't want to swim the strait with all of those sharks down there.

passages.title: Betrayal at Tempest's Reach
passages.text:
King Greymane has been taken prisoner by Lord Godfrey in Tempest's Reach!

He managed to convince two of the eastern lords to go with his plan. The fool seems to think he can strike a deal with the Forsaken by turning Greymane over to them.

Listen carefully, <name>. We need to resolve this with as little bloodshed as possible.

This potion will allow you to sneak in undetected. We need you to assassinate the traitorous lords before this gets out of hand!

passages.title: Betrayal at Tempest's Reach
passages.text: Careful, <name>.

passages.title: Betrayal at Tempest's Reach
passages.text: I wish it could've been avoided, <name>.  Let us ensure this is resolved without further bloodshed.

passages.title: Neither Human Nor Beast
passages.text:
It is time, <name>. This... alchemy that has kept the beast inside you at bay will not last for long.

The first cursed worgen were night elf druids like our new allies. They, however, abandoned the balance that the rest of their kind embraced and allowed the beast to take over their minds.

It is only fitting that their brethren be the ones that deliver us from the Curse. Go, <class>. Drink from the waters of Tal'doren and make peace with yourself.

passages.title: Neither Human Nor Beast
passages.text: It is always good to see you brother.

passages.title: Neither Human Nor Beast
passages.text: It is done then, <name>.  You are one of us now.

passages.title: Take Back What's Ours
passages.text:
Ever since the Forsaken invaded Gilneas, we've tried to keep the location of the Scythe of Elune secret. We moved it at night to one of many safe locations. The Dark Rangers got close, but never found it... until now.

They were last spotted at the Woods' End Cabin, west of here. Blow this horn when you find them and Tobias and his trackers will engage the Dark Rangers.

Only then will it be safe for you to venture inside the cabin and take back the scythe. Hurry, <name>. It must not reach Sylvanas.

passages.title: Take Back What's Ours
passages.text: Do you have the scythe, <name>?

passages.title: Take Back What's Ours
passages.text: I knew we could count on you.  You've done well, <name>.

passages.title: Cluster Cluck
passages.text:
Ridiculous! The greatest goblin mind of all time reduced to food detail? I made the Micro Mechachicken just for this reason and they let it get away!

<Hobart turns a deeper shade of green as his blood pressure rises.>

Do I look like I should be rounding up escaped cluckers? No, my friend, not I! Bamm most definitely, though he's too lazy.

Your station in life has recently taken a turn for the worse. You do it!

Take these remote control fireworks and attach them to the cluckers.

passages.title: Cluster Cluck
passages.text: Not enough cluckers, <name>. We'll all starve.

passages.title: Cluster Cluck
passages.text:
Success! Was there ever any doubt?

Greely, fire up the poultryizer!

passages.title: Push Them Out
passages.text:
The people are free, but the town is still occupied by the Forsaken. They're cut off from their main force, so if we're to drive them out, now's our chance.

Their leader, Executor Cornell, is known for his unbound ruthlessness. Also among them is Valnov the Mad, a so-called scientist who carries out inhuman experiments on villagers too old to work the mines.

Take care of them all.

passages.title: Push Them Out
passages.text: You're back, <name>.

passages.title: Push Them Out
passages.text: We have the people of Emberstone on our side now thanks to you.

passages.title: Flank the Forsaken
passages.text:
I thank you, <name>. We can't rest on our laurels, however.

We found out about a mining town, currently under Forsaken occupation. We sent some of my men, along with Crowley's daughter to the nearby livery stables to begin operations there. Liam should be joining them shortly.

I'll stay here and organize the final push for Gilneas City. Speak to Lord Hewell to secure a horse to get you there.

passages.title: Flank the Forsaken
passages.text: I am glad to have you here, <name>.  We're surrounded by Forsaken on all sides and can use all the help we can get.

passages.title: Knee-Deep
passages.text:
It's time to pack it in, <name>. Most of our people have made it through -- it's your turn now.

Take this torch, you're going to need it. The tunnel is full of nasty, knee-biting critters of the worst kind. Use it to keep them at bay.

Speak to Krennan on the other side.

passages.title: Knee-Deep
passages.text: You're here, <name>.  Most everyone made it through, but now we're stuck here... surrounded by our own... dead!

passages.title: They Have Allies, But So Do We
passages.text:
The night elves made good on their promise. They've brought ships and are ready to offer us sanctuary in their lands.

Unfortunately, the Forsaken's allies have arrived as well.

The orcs are advancing upon us while the Horde gunship prevents the transport ships from taking our people to safety.

The druids are holding the enemy back, but won't last long. Fortunately, the elven ships were carrying siege weapons. Take one of the glaive throwers and meet the enemy head on.

passages.title: They Have Allies, But So Do We
passages.text: You're back!

passages.title: They Have Allies, But So Do We
passages.text: It's almost over, <name>.  Only one obstacle remains between us and survival.

passages.title: A Goblin in Shark's Clothing
passages.text:
Combining the remains of the Mechachicken with these shark parts, we've assembled the greatest fighting submersible of all time: the Mechashark X-Steam!

Hobart and I want you to pilot it, <name>. Go west to the water and activate the Mechashark X-Steam Controller.

You must kill The Hammer if we're to have any hope of exploiting the natural resources of the Dire Strait to their fullest extent. It's for the good of the cartel!

passages.title: A Goblin in Shark's Clothing
passages.text: That monstrously humongous shark is not dead yet! Do I have to do everything myself?

passages.title: A Goblin in Shark's Clothing
passages.text: Excellent work, my boy! The Town-In-A-Box is saved and the Bilgewater Cartel will be profitable once again thanks to my overwhelmingly unbelievable intellect and tinkering know-how.

passages.title: Invasion Imminent!
passages.text:
Your work here is done for now, but there's no rest for the wicked, eh?

You remember Megs Dreadshredder, our old marketing rep? She's taken some others over the hills to the southeast, just past the Raptor Rise. If you follow the path east out of town and follow it south at the fork, you can't miss her.

Apparently there's some trouble or other brewing with the snake-men at the ruins on the shore. Go see if you can't sort it all out, would you?

passages.title: Invasion Imminent!
passages.text: Boss, we gotta problem.

passages.title: Bilgewater Cartel Represent
passages.text:
Looks like the naga down there in the ruins are preparing to invade our Town-In-A-Box. I have lots of dead scouts here as proof.

I don't know about you, but I'm not about to let them try. Let's get the jump on them!

Could you lay the foundation for our new coastal holdings by replacing their banners with our own? That's some prime real estate down there!

passages.title: Bilgewater Cartel Represent
passages.text: There are still some naga banners down there that need to be 'sploded and replaced!

passages.title: Bilgewater Cartel Represent
passages.text:
I wish I could have seen the looks on their scaly faces when you blew up their banners and replaced them with our own.

On second thought, I don't want to be close enough to see their snarls.

passages.title: Surrender or Else!
passages.text:
<name>, you and Ace need to march those naga hatchlings down there and use them as leverage to convince the leader of the naga to surrender to us.

Ace knows where to go on the south side of the ruins... just follow him.

passages.title: Surrender or Else!
passages.text: What's wrong?

passages.title: Surrender or Else!
passages.text:
A faceless of the deep? What's that? That does NOT sound like a naga!

Well, you killed it, whatever it was. It doesn't matter now. We have other fish to fry....

passages.title: Get Back to Town
passages.text:
We were wrong. It wasn't the naga that were preparing to attack... it was the nearby Oomlot tribe.

<name>, you need to get back to the Town-In-A-Box. The pygmies are already attacking!

Here, take this. We bought it off of a pygmy who said it used to belong to some great leader of theirs. Someone whose name translates as Dark Tan Helmet.

It should fool them so that they don't attack you.

passages.title: Get Back to Town
passages.text:
<name>? We're saved!

Who am I kidding? We're all going to die!!!

passages.title: The Hunt For Sylvanas
passages.text:
It's true then? Gilneas has lost her favorite son.

We will mourn when this is all over but not a day sooner.

We will not allow ourselves the luxury of grief while the enemy still breathes Gilnean air.

My father's men are ready to strike while we still have the Banshee Queen's trail. Just say the word if you're ready. Liam deserves swift vengeance.

passages.title: The Hunt For Sylvanas
passages.text: Did you find her, <name>?

passages.title: The Hunt For Sylvanas
passages.text: The Plague?  Something so heinous that not even the orcs condone its use?  I'd say this warrants notifying King Greymane.

passages.title: Slowing the Inevitable
passages.text:
As much as I want to exact swift and brutal revenge... I must honor my son's memory first. He cared for his people first and foremost.

The Undertaker's Pass goes underground below Northgate River. You must prevent the plague from being deployed while we evacuate our men, women and children to Aderic's Repose.

We captured one of the Forsaken's dreaded bombing bats. I want you to fly the infernal beast as best you can and unleash hell upon those who seek to bring the Plague to our people. Hurry!

passages.title: Slowing the Inevitable
passages.text: Is it done, <name>?

passages.title: Slowing the Inevitable
passages.text: You've done well, <name>.  Almost everybody managed to make it through.

passages.title: Oomlot Dealt With
passages.text: <name>, you have to get back to the Town-In-A-Box and warn them about the goblin zombies up in the volcano's caldera!

passages.title: Oomlot Dealt With
passages.text: They turned some of our people into zombies? Tell me something I don't know....

passages.title: Up the Volcano
passages.text:
A whole bunch of our people headed up to the top of the volcano to mount a counter-offensive. There's something horrible brewing up there on the Lost Peak.

They're waiting for you before they make any moves against the pygmies. Those evil little things turned a lot of us into zombies!

<name>, save us!

passages.title: Up the Volcano
passages.text: My star player has arrived!

passages.title: Zombies vs. Super Booster Rocket Boots
passages.text:
Those zombies that got past us are nothing compared to the numbers waiting just through the pass. If we don't deal with them soon, the pygmy witch doctors are going to send all of them against the town, and even the cannons down there won't be able to handle that many!

I brought a couple of shredder boots along. Greely modded them and now they're Super Booster Rocket Boots!

Use the boots to incinerate the zombies in the Oostan villages to the east.

passages.title: Zombies vs. Super Booster Rocket Boots
passages.text: You still have a few <race> zombies to deal with, <name>. Look sharp, superstar!

passages.title: Zombies vs. Super Booster Rocket Boots
passages.text:
You did it! No more zombies to worry about. Let's pause a moment in silence for the stinky departed.

Okay, done.

passages.title: Rocket Boot Boost
passages.text:
You need to get those boots down into the caldera to Hobart Grapplehammer.

Now that they're infused with the leftover rockin' powder, they should have enough thrust to get you all the way there on one shot.

When you're ready, activate the boots. Don't worry, they're automatically set to land you safely.

I think.

passages.title: Rocket Boot Boost
passages.text: Well there you are!

passages.title: Rocket Boot Boost
passages.text:
There's no time to waste, boy!

What's wrong with the actuator on the left boot?!

passages.title: Repel the Paratroopers
passages.text:
The Alliance have caught back up with us at just the wrong moment, my friend. We took care of their ships, but they still have planes that are dropping their vaunted 127th Paratroopers onto the coast below.

It's all that the battlesworn and scouts can do to hold the two ramps against their overwhelming numbers. I'm certain that if you were to aid them, the tide would quickly be turned.

passages.title: Repel the Paratroopers
passages.text: I've not seen a finer display of <class> prowess.

passages.title: The Heads of the SI:7
passages.text:
These orcs were murdered in cold-blood by the Alliance down on the coast. We did nothing to provoke them.

Their deaths should not be in vain, <name>. Will you bring them justice?

<Aggra appears as if she can barely contain her rage.>

There are three SI:7 leaders down there along the beach. Bring me each of their heads.

passages.title: The Heads of the SI:7
passages.text: Has justice been served?

passages.title: The Heads of the SI:7
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. The spirits of the fallen can now be put to rest.

passages.title: The Warchief Wants You
passages.text:
True to his word, Thrall is going to get us going in the right direction to rescue our people. He asked to speak with you.

Good luck, <name>. We're all depending on you.

passages.title: The Warchief Wants You
passages.text:
Once again you have helped us to overcome our mutual enemy, the Alliance.

Now it is time for us to help you.

passages.title: Borrow Bastia
passages.text:
Head back down to the coast and tell Kilag that I'd like for you to borrow Bastia. The panther knows the way to where your friends are being held captive.

Go now. I will see you again before we make our move against the Trade Prince.

passages.title: Borrow Bastia
passages.text:
Of course you can borrow Bastia. That is, if she'll take you.

<Kilag winks.>

passages.title: The Gallywix Labor Mine
passages.text:
We barely escaped with our hides intact!

The Trade Prince has a whole bunch of us enslaved and performing manual labor inside the cavern.

Greely helped the seven of us to get out, but she was recaptured in the process.

<name>, you're the only one crazy enough to walk into an exploding volcano! The assistant will be able to help you free the others.

Hurry! This place is about to blow for good!

passages.title: The Gallywix Labor Mine
passages.text:
<The assistant looks confused.>

Huh... what? Who?

passages.title: Morale Boost
passages.text: You've got to get all the Kaja'Cola Zero-One that you can and make the goblins drink it to boost their morale and free them!

passages.title: Morale Boost
passages.text: Increase their morale, <name>, so that they will run to freedom!

passages.title: Morale Boost
passages.text: I hate the Trade Prince, but you can't argue with the results of his methods. Kaja'Cola Zero-One is a huge improvement over regular old Kaja'Cola at half the calories and twice the ideas!

passages.title: Light at the End of the Tunnel
passages.text:
Okay, we have got to get out of here before she blows for good!

Let's head out the other end of the tunnel on the north side of the mine. We should be able to use one of the mine carts for a quick ride down the side of the volcano.

passages.title: Light at the End of the Tunnel
passages.text: Looks a little rickety....

passages.title: Wild Mine Cart Ride
passages.text: All you have to do is jump in and speak with Assistant Greely when you get to the bottom.

passages.title: Wild Mine Cart Ride
passages.text: As we would say in the Tinker's Union, out of the heat-applied metallic cooking container and into the oxydizing, energetic mixture of reacting gases and solids!

passages.title: The Fastest Way to His Heart
passages.text:
Oh, <man/girl>! You're never going to guess who's out on the oil platform to the north.

<Izzy shakes her head sadly at you.>

Chip's out there, and he's working for the Trade Prince. That cold-hearted snake dropped you like a bad habit and now he's working for the other team. I even heard he's got something goin' on with Candy Cane!

I don't know about you, but if he was my former definitely-real boyfriend, I'd rip his still-beating heart out of his chest.

passages.title: The Fastest Way to His Heart
passages.text: What did you decide? Death or forgiveness?

passages.title: The Fastest Way to His Heart
passages.text:
He got just what he deserved. There, there, don't cry. You'll find someone else that'll treat you right.

Here, let me take that... we wouldn't want people to think that you're crazy.

passages.title: Escape Velocity
passages.text:
We really don't have time to rescue those that are incompetent enough to get themselves captured over and over. Still, since I have some extra rockets leftover, this problem should be a snap.

Take these single-stage booster rockets down into the Slave Pits to the north and put them on the cages.

The cage will lift off into orbit and those idiots will be freed.

passages.title: Escape Velocity
passages.text: You still have have more cages to liberate from their Azerothian bonds.

passages.title: Escape Velocity
passages.text: Oops. Well, what goes up must eventually come down.

passages.title: Final Confrontation
passages.text:
<name>, this is it! Thrall's down at the Gallywix Docks fighting the Trade Prince right now!

You gotta jump into your Ultimate Footbomb Uniform and get over there!

passages.title: Final Confrontation
passages.text: <name>, you have to go deal with the Trade Prince before it's too late!

passages.title: Final Confrontation
passages.text:
You did it! You did it!

We're saved, <name>!

passages.title: Victory!
passages.text:
We just can't thank you enough for all that you've done. Now we can all get off of this island before it kills us!

Thrall is going to want to speak with you first, <name>. I'll rocket you over there.

See you on the ship!

passages.title: Victory!
passages.text: Lok'tar! Victory, <name>!

passages.title: Message for Saurfang
passages.text:
<The Darkspear loyalist opens the package and reads the letter within. As she finishes the note from Thrall, a hint of a fanged smile appears on her face.>

Ya should take dis directly to Saurfang inside Orgrimmar. Be sure ta let him know dat de package be from Thrall.

Take me raptor. Hurry, little one, dere be no time ta waste!

passages.title: Message for Saurfang
passages.text:
What is this, <race>? Your kind are not allowed inside Grommash Hold.

Leave before I have to teach you your place.

passages.title: Message for Saurfang
passages.text:
Thrall had you deliver this?

<The Warchief takes a step back, visibly shaken.>

I understand the meaning of this all too well, <race>.

This smelly thing was caught unattended in the city and seems to recognize you.

I have already put others of your kind to work in Azshara. Take it with you when you leave.

From this day forward, you and your Bilgewater Cartel will serve the Horde!

passages.title: Blessing of the Green Dragonflight
passages.text:
You have done well, <name>. Jammal'an may have escaped our grasp, but his retreat paves the way for me to enter the temple as I desire.

Stay where you are and do not move. I will hasten your return by pulling your spirit to me through the Emerald Dream.

This may cause slight drowsiness.

passages.title: Blessing of the Green Dragonflight
passages.text: You have performed a great service for me and my kind, <name>. Accept this as a symbol of my gratitude, and of your courage.

passages.title: The Prison Rooftop
passages.text:
I don't understand why the king wants to waste time saving his hide, but if you want to risk your life, then be my guest.

Crowley and his men are holed up upstairs, probably plotting against the king as we speak!

passages.title: The Prison Rooftop
passages.text:
Greymane's right.  These beasts do not give a damn about our politics.

Gilneas needs to stand together.

passages.title: Critical Condition
passages.text:
We may have won the first battle, but a critical task still remains.

Dozens of Skyfire pilots were shot down during the initial aerial battle.

Without medical aid, their condition will deteriorate over time, until they finally perish. We are their only hope for survival.

Go into the orchard and revive as many pilots as you can find.

We will leave no one behind.

passages.title: Critical Condition
passages.text: We will remember all the brave Alliance soldiers who fell today. Though they can no longer continue, we carry the fight onward.

passages.title: Critical Condition
passages.text: Good work, <name>. Those soldiers will live and fight another day because of your efforts.

passages.title: The White Pawn
passages.text:
Alright, soldier. I've got a critical mission for you.

Get down to the coastline south of here - in the cove there you'll find a wrecked Alliance vessel. I need you to search it and find out if it was the ship that was carrying Anduin. 

Then, recover the Captain's Log and see if it has any information on where we can find him.

Since the log is from a military ship, it'll be written using a cipher - take it to Nodd Codejack afterwards. He's keeping watch on the wreck from the other end of the cove.

passages.title: The White Pawn
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: The White Pawn
passages.text:
Alright... let me see... using the cipher from when the ship went missing...

<Nodd is clearly doing some calculations in his head.>

Aha!

passages.title: Regroup!
passages.text:
They have an airbase! I have underestimated this Alliance Captain for the last time. So many good warriors lost...

There must have been a few survivors who were able to bail during the crash. We need every able-bodied fighter we can get.

Find as many survivors as you can in the forest below, and I will investigate the wreckage itself. Rally everyone together at the nearby village for a counter-attack.

passages.title: Regroup!
passages.text: Did you find any survivors?

passages.title: Regroup!
passages.text:
These are the only survivors, <name>?

So be it. We will play the hand fate has dealt us.

Numbers be damned. This is where heroes are made.

passages.title: Down Kitty!
passages.text:
I tried to fight one of the jade tigers in the woods but they were too scary. They stare at you and you turn to a jade statue!

Honest truth! Chen's sister's friend Ni heard it from Kai's mom.

I want to be brave like you though. Can you show me how to beat up those jade tigers?

passages.title: Down Kitty!
passages.text: Wow! You are tough!

passages.title: Down Kitty!
passages.text: Wow! You were awesome! You were like *bam* and they were like *aaaaa* and then they were smashed!

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Take No Prisoners
passages.text: The final leg of our journey took us west, to a large hozen village. We set up a small camp in the mountains, outside of their line of sight...

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Take No Prisoners
passages.text: Please, allow me to finish.

passages.title: SI:7 Report: Take No Prisoners
passages.text:
So there you have it. We didn't find the White Pawn, but we came back with intel that could be of even greater importance to the Alliance.

The Horde have allied with the hozen, and are arming them as we speak. They and their monkey army now outnumber us thirty to one.

passages.title: Family Heirlooms
passages.text:
We recently lost a fierce battle against the hozen at Moonwater Retreat.

We evacuated as many of our people as we could, but still, there were many we could not save.

We have no tokens of our lost over which to send our prayers.

If someone could go and retrieve heirlooms from the dead bodies, we could properly lay them to rest, and move on.

It would mean so much to us if you could do this, <name>.

passages.title: Family Heirlooms
passages.text: We still grieve for our fallen brothers.

passages.title: Family Heirlooms
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. You do not know how much this means to the families of the lost.

passages.title: Cryin' My Eyes Out
passages.text:
I coulda taken out da whole lot of 'em, mon.

Shot 'em one by one, den played dead when dey be gettin' close. Fell for it every time, dey did - well almost every time...

One of 'em finally got wise. Called my bluff. Before I knew it, dey was usin' my eyes as marbles.

Ran off with my goods an' left me here ta die, da savages...

Help me, mon. Lemme die wit my dignity intact.

passages.title: Cryin' My Eyes Out
passages.text: You got me goods, mon?

passages.title: Cryin' My Eyes Out
passages.text:
<Zin'Jun sobs...you think.>

Dey done killed Snuff...

What'd 'ol Snuff ever do ta dem?

passages.title: Seein' Red
passages.text:
I was just about ta curl up an' die, mon.

Now, dis!

Snuff an' me go way back. Oh, da memories...

No way I can face Snuff in da afterlife without avengin' his death first, mon!

Dese hooligans be led by one named Konk. We gotta sniff him out an' den snuff him out - for Snuff!

passages.title: Seein' Red
passages.text:
Zin'jun is lost?

This is a dark day indeed, brother. These vermin will pay!

passages.title: Lay of the Land
passages.text:
Curse these furry pests! Kill one, and two more rise in its place...

Nothing has changed, <name>. Orders are orders, no matter how few of us stand and regardless of the odds.

I have plans to make and problems to solve.

I want you to get out there and learn the lay of the land. Don't return until you have something useful to report.

And silence that yammering fool while you're out there!

Dismissed!

passages.title: Lay of the Land
passages.text:
Welcome, traveler.

Please, make yourself comfortable.

passages.title: Scouting Report: Like Jinyu in a Barrel
passages.text:
With our leader turned to jade, our hozen guide disappeared, and a prisoner of war in tow, there was only one thing that Kiryn and I could do:

March into our enemy's territory and deliver some vengeance.

Want to know how it went?

passages.title: Scouting Report: Like Jinyu in a Barrel
passages.text: I'm not quite done yet, <name>.

passages.title: Scouting Report: Like Jinyu in a Barrel
passages.text:
The most important thing we learned was that... not only have the Alliance befriended the jinyu, but they're giving them weapons, and teaching them how to use them.

The Alliance now control a force that outnumbers us thirty-to-one. And we - the HORDE - have befriended monkeys.

passages.title: Acid Rain
passages.text:
Since you've been gone, more and more of these creatures are approaching our camp. They appear to be amassing for a major assault!

We're going to have to take some drastic measures if we hope to see tomorrow.

Here, take my poisoned throwing stars and figure out a way to thin out their numbers.

passages.title: Acid Rain
passages.text: Well, <name>? Do we live to see another day?

passages.title: Acid Rain
passages.text:
Excellent! What a creative solution!

That should hold them off for a while.

passages.title: The Silkwood Road
passages.text:
West of here is the Silkwood Road. It has fallen into shadow as the spiders there have turned to a more evil and gluttonous path.

I would face these villains myself but someone has to defend the noodle shop from... um... dangers and such.

Go, hero, and conquer these beasts! Should you succeed perhaps I shall regale you with some of my epic tales of heroism.

I'll also pay you.

passages.title: The Silkwood Road
passages.text: The silkwood stalkers are not in balance with nature. Predators are one thing but these creatures kill for pleasure. Harmony must be restored.

passages.title: The Silkwood Road
passages.text: Such a noble hero. You remind me of a younger, less good looking version of myself.

passages.title: A Poor Grasp of the Basics
passages.text:
Virmen - they no just eat our food. They trying to start farms of their own. The problem is... well, they ookin' dumb.

You no believe Muno? Last night, they break into tool sheds... steal equipment. When we wake up, we find rakes and wheelbarrows planted in ground.

They was WATERING them. They was trying to GROW WHEELBARROWS.

Please, while you out there, unbury our stuff.

passages.title: A Poor Grasp of the Basics
passages.text: Man, those virmen is dumb.

passages.title: A Poor Grasp of the Basics
passages.text: Thanks, friend. Now maybe a hozen can get some ookin' work done around here.

passages.title: Swallowed Whole
passages.text:
Now, back to your dilemma.

I believe you can help your people build relations with our hozen, as my people have.

The trail behind me will lead you to a body of water the hozen use to gather the fish that feeds them.

Around this time every year, fearsome beasts call those waters home and many hungry hozen are lost to them.

If you were to rescue some of the victims and gather some fish, perhaps you will be regarded more favorably.

passages.title: Swallowed Whole
passages.text: Wikket got slickies... for me!?

passages.title: Swallowed Whole
passages.text:
Wikket save hozen? And bring slickies?

Hmm, maybe wikket not so bad.

Tooki Tooki never liked Dook Ookem anyway...

passages.title: Quill of Stingers
passages.text:
To achieve perfect paint strokes, one must have the right tools. My own have fallen into disrepair, their bristles becoming as unmanageable as hozu hair.

Have you seen the wasps throughout the Arboretum? Their stingers can be fashioned into quills that provide just the right level of sharpness in each line.

Could you gather some for me please?

passages.title: Quill of Stingers
passages.text: Have you been able to acquire some stingers? I would normally ask a monk for help with this but they all seem to be elsewhere at the moment.

passages.title: Quill of Stingers
passages.text: My thanks traveler. These will make a fine set of quills. Here is something for your trouble.

passages.title: The Pearlfin Situation
passages.text:
I've been thinking.

We are cut off from support and a long way from home.

Although these Pearlfin jinyu mistrust our presence, they do not appear to be hostile.

If we could convince them that we are their friends, an alliance between our races could prove extremely valuable.

<name>, you must go speak to the jinyu around the village.

Convince their leaders that we are not to be feared, and that we only wish for peace.

passages.title: The Pearlfin Situation
passages.text: If we can win over the jinyu, they may allow us to stay.

passages.title: The Pearlfin Situation
passages.text:
It sounds like you made quite the good impression.

Well done, <name>!

passages.title: The Elder's Instruments
passages.text:
Oh dear, oh dear... The Elder mustn't find out!

I must have left the Elder's ceremonial instruments behind during the escape.

But... Moonwater Retreat is crawling with hozen by now!

What sort of Pearlkeeper am I, to have lost them so carelessly?

<The old jinyu buries his face into his hands.>

Stranger, could you find it in your heart to help me?

passages.title: The Elder's Instruments
passages.text: The Elder is a Waterspeaker. He speaks to the waters, and they answer.

passages.title: The Elder's Instruments
passages.text:
You found them? Oh thank the spirits of water!

You have saved my tailfin, <name>.

passages.title: Seek Out the Lorewalker
passages.text:
I see that you and your people are desperate to find your Prince Anduin.

I know someone who may be able to help you, a pandaren Lorewalker who knows this land better than anyone. I cannot guarantee what kind of reception you will receive, but he will almost certainly be as curious about you as you are of him!

The Lorewalker lives in the forest to the southwest. Tell him that the Pearlfin have sent you.

passages.title: Seek Out the Lorewalker
passages.text:
You look around the empty house.

It appears you are in the right place, but there is no sign of its inhabitant.

passages.title: Finding Your Center
passages.text:
The dream brew is complete! This time, when you drink it, you must embrace the visions you see from a state of inner focus.

Follow me to my pagoda, and I will teach you how to achieve the inner calm that we pandaren value so much.

Your troubled mind will present you with many distractions, but just remember to stay centered!

passages.title: Finding Your Center
passages.text:
How did you find me?

<Anduin listens to you describe the vision from the Dream Brew.>

Remarkable! That's exactly what happened several days ago. We've been laying low since then.

passages.title: Potency
passages.text:
To make the Dream Brew, we will need several ingredients.

First, to improve its strength, I will need an ingredient from a fearsome creature, the legendary Mist Horror.

It is said that this creature only appears where the fog is deepest.

North and east of here, you will find smaller Mist Creepers roaming the swamps. Kill these creatures until the Mist Horror appears, and then bring me its heart.

passages.title: Potency
passages.text: The mists seem to have a mind of their own, do they not?

passages.title: Potency
passages.text: This is an amazing specimen! I am quite shocked that you have succeeded, actually.

passages.title: Spirits of the Water
passages.text:
Our war against the hozen rages without end, and the future of our tribe is uncertain.

This is why our waterspeaker has decided to seek wisdom from the waters.

Elder Lusshan is waiting. Please deliver the instruments so that they may begin.

passages.title: Spirits of the Water
passages.text: <The Elder's eyes are glazed over. His vision is cast inward, toward the wisdom he has gained.>

passages.title: Spirits of the Water
passages.text:
I saw the vision, <name>. What do you think it means?

I think it is clear that you play some part in it.

passages.title: Sacred Waters
passages.text:
I appreciate you coming all this way to save me, but Ren is gravely injured.

The old pandaren had no reason to help me, yet still he risked his life to save my own.

Before the fever set in, he mentioned that there are healing waters in the cave just down the hill.

It is dangerous, but I will do anything to help my friend. Will you help me retrieve the waters?

passages.title: Sacred Waters
passages.text: Perhaps I could bring some of these healing waters back to Stormwind with me.

passages.title: Sacred Waters
passages.text:
The healing waters should abate Ren's fever for a short while, but alas, I fear it is no permanent cure.

Thank you, <class>. We have granted him a little more time, at least.

passages.title: An Ancient Legend
passages.text:
My father has dedicated his life to studying the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

The Vale is a mythical place, sealed after the Pandaren revolution twelve thousand years ago. We know so little about it!

My father followed a trail of clues to the cave down the hill, seeking a very old poem known as the Song of the Vale, but he is in no condition to retrieve it. It is guarded by some sort of ancestor spirit.

If you are heading that way anyway, would you mind bringing it back to him?

passages.title: An Ancient Legend
passages.text: Did you... find the scroll?

passages.title: An Ancient Legend
passages.text: Oh... it is the poem! Did you... read it? What did you learn about the Vale?

passages.title: A Perfect Match
passages.text:
Elder Lusshan and I agree that the best path forward will be to work together.

We will share with the Pearlfin our superior military knowledge and weaponry.

In return, they will be a powerful ally should we again encounter the Horde.

Take this crate of equipment and weapons. I need you to go around the village and equip the jinyu with weapons befitting their skills.

passages.title: A Perfect Match
passages.text: The jinyu are skilled in different ways. It is up to us to find their strengths.

passages.title: A Perfect Match
passages.text: Good. Let those Horde mongrels show their faces now!

passages.title: Bigger Fish to Fry
passages.text:
I've prepared a team of bright young Pearlfin trainees who need field experience.

Take them northeast, into the Bamboo Wilds, and kill any wildlife that you find.

Don't bring them back until they're fit for battle.

passages.title: Bigger Fish to Fry
passages.text: How are those trainees looking?

passages.title: Bigger Fish to Fry
passages.text:
Your trainees returned recently. I could hardly believe my eyes! They did not look like the same jinyu that you left with.

Excellent work, <class>. Couldn't have done better myself.

passages.title: A Seemingly Endless Nuisance
passages.text:
I apologize for the state of things around here. The virmen - those rabbity creatures, down the hill - have been pushing further and further into my family's farm, and our crops - which are normally bigger, and more delicious, by the way - have been suffering because of it.

I'm no soldier... but you might be! Would you mind pushing some of these virmen off of our land?

passages.title: A Seemingly Endless Nuisance
passages.text: Have you pushed the virmen out yet, <class>? We need to bring in our crops soon, or they'll be lost for sure.

passages.title: A Seemingly Endless Nuisance
passages.text:
<Pang surveys the area around his farm.>

Well, they're not ALL gone yet, but there's less of them. And they aren't holding their ears quite as high anymore.

I'd guess that they're scared of you, <name>.

passages.title: Rampaging Rodents
passages.text:
I went off this morning to watch my papa fight the virmen. When I came back, the farm was full of marmots!

I don't want to kill them, but we need to get rid of them. Hey, I know! We can close the holes!

Fill in their holes with dirt, so they can't come out in our farm anymore.

passages.title: Rampaging Rodents
passages.text: The marmots won't be happy when you try to fill in their holes.

passages.title: Rampaging Rodents
passages.text: Thank you, sir! Now I can get back to my chores.

passages.title: Practically Perfect Produce
passages.text:
Here, <name>. My father will be wanting this.

Thank you, again, for helping with the virmen.

passages.title: Practically Perfect Produce
passages.text: Do I smell turnips?

passages.title: Practically Perfect Produce
passages.text: Ho ho! Now that's what I like to see!

passages.title: The Fabulous Miss Fanny
passages.text:
Most of these vegetables will be sold, but I'd like to keep some for my family. Specifically, my nephew Liang needs some to feed to his pigs.

Unfortunately, the pathway to Liang's farm is currently swarming with Snagtooth virmen. We're going to have to ask Miss Fanny to help us out.

Bring some of the food we've gathered to Miss Fanny, who stands next to my house. Then ask her - NICELY! - to send them down to Liang's ranch.

passages.title: The Fabulous Miss Fanny
passages.text: Not now, neighbor. I need to scrounge up some food for these pigs.

passages.title: The Fabulous Miss Fanny
passages.text:
I understand you're the one who sent the food down from uncle's farm. Thank you.

My pigs are picky eaters, but those turnips and watermelons are some of their favorites.

passages.title: The Meat They'll Eat
passages.text:
I told you earlier, my pigs are picky eaters. They need to eat meat to grow strong, but they don't like mutton, they don't like yak, and I'm not about to feed them any pig meat.

They do, however, eat meat off of the mushan beasts, and they're also quite partial to turtle. Both creatures can be found in abundance to the west.

My skills as a hunter are admittedly quite weak. Can you help out a young rancher and his pigs?

passages.title: The Meat They'll Eat
passages.text:
It hurts my ears to hear their hungry squeals.

Once you've been a pig rancher for a while, you can distinguish hungry squeals from regular squeals.

passages.title: The Meat They'll Eat
passages.text:
<Liang sorts through the meat.>

You're not just a <class>, but you're a butcher, too? You've got an eye for quality pig food, neighbor.

passages.title: A Neighbor's Duty
passages.text:
I'm not the only one having trouble with his stock, it seems. One of Francis' sheep has wandered over to my ranch, for the third time this week. I'm beginning to think he needs help tending to his flock.

You should check up on him, neighbor. And bring this poor little thing with you.

passages.title: A Neighbor's Duty
passages.text: Oh... you have one of my... my lambs?

passages.title: A Neighbor's Duty
passages.text: You really shouldn't have brought the lamb back to me. He... he was safer in that pigsty than he is over here.

passages.title: A Lesson in Bravery
passages.text:
<Master Shang speaks to his shepherd boy.>

Francis, you need to show bravery! You have everything it takes to make a great shepherd, except the courage to face your fears!

<He looks over to you.>

You, stranger. You helped the rest of my family. Francis is like a second son to me.

Show my apprentice what it means to lack fear. Use this rope to lasso and defeat one of the great white hawks above us.

<Shang points to the sky, looks at Francis, and leaves.>

passages.title: A Lesson in Bravery
passages.text: You lack fear. I can sense it in your heart.

passages.title: A Lesson in Bravery
passages.text:
Francis has taken longer than I expected to become an effective shepherd. We all go through these phases... my son Liang was weak once, too. As was I.

But he will learn. It is the Thunderfoot way.

passages.title: Great Minds Drink Alike
passages.text:
Hello again, <name>. What is this, the fourth time we've run into one another already?

Say... my keg is quickly becoming quite empty. I've heard mention of a brewery to the southwest, and that's where we're headed. Care to join us?

passages.title: Great Minds Drink Alike
passages.text:
If yer lookin' fer beer, you came to the right place, neighbor.

Just, ah... excuse the mess. Had me a bit of a problem with virmen the last few days.

passages.title: Getting Permission
passages.text:
My love, Lo, tried to get permission to marry me from the pandriarchs. Though they have passed beyond, their favor would carry a lot of weight.

Thing is, they are spirits, and none of the gifts or tributes we brought impress them. To win their favor they claimed that either Lo or a champion must defeat them in single combat.

Lo is a good man, but not a fighter.

Would you be our champion?

passages.title: Getting Permission
passages.text: Each of the pandriarchs earned their reputation in life and retained them afterward.  I can't even imagine how you will defeat them.

passages.title: Getting Permission
passages.text:
They... they agreed?! Fantastic! Thank you so much! With their blessing we can be the happiest pandaren in all the land!

Please, take this. We meant it to be a tribute for the pandriarchs but they didn't seem interested.

passages.title: In Search of Wisdom
passages.text:
Lorewalker Cho came by and asked for you while you were gone.

He needs your assistance urgently in the town of Dawn's Blossom to the north. For what reason, he did not say.

Speak to Kitemaster Ut-Nam. He would be happy to send you there.

passages.title: In Search of Wisdom
passages.text: Ah! You made it. Fantastic!

passages.title: In Search of Wisdom
passages.text:
Your deeds have sparked a long forgotten memory I have of an ancient prophecy. This deserves investigation.

In order to investigate, I need jade though. I have instructed Toya to gather as much as he can find and give it to you when he is done. Bring it to me and we will see about deciphering the ancient "Emperor's Omen."

While he gathers the jade, feel free to explore. You may find the people of this town are in need of a person of your caliber.

passages.title: All We Can Spare
passages.text:
Alright, I called in every favor I could. Here's what we got.

Cho must be on to something big!

Lemme know when you're ready to go see him - I got a ride all prepared for ya.

passages.title: All We Can Spare
passages.text: Ah, hello again, <name>! You received my message, then?

passages.title: All We Can Spare
passages.text:
I knew Toya would come through for me!

He can get anything, you know.

passages.title: Calamity Jade
passages.text:
You ever seen a shale spider, <class>? Usually harmless, just creepin' around eatin' rocks, but they got a taste for jade like cubs on candy. The boys call 'em "nibblers."

A few days back, we tunneled into a huge nest of these critters. They spilled out into the mines and went crazy, chewed up damn near everything in sight - including some of the boys.

You get in there and clear 'em out, and we got plenty of jade to spare. The quarry is directly west of here.

passages.title: Calamity Jade
passages.text:
Well I'll be... you actually did it!

You lookin' for a more permanent job, buddy? I could use a bruiser like you around full-time!

passages.title: I Have No Jade And I Must Scream
passages.text:
Our whole jade supply line has fallen apart. The mines are a death trap, morale is historically low, and - as if that weren't bad enough - the mason's quarter has been overrun by wood sprites!

Now even the plants are out to ruin me!

You need jade so badly, you can follow the road southwest to the mason's quarter and get it from those glorified chopsticks yourself.

passages.title: I Have No Jade And I Must Scream
passages.text: <Mann looks at you expectantly, eyes wide and nostrils flared.>

passages.title: I Have No Jade And I Must Scream
passages.text:
Catch? They were playin' CATCH with my product?!

I hope you showed those walkin' toothpicks a thing or two.

You know, maybe you ain't a cub after all. I've been lookin' for some muscle to help out with my problem at the quarry.

And judgin' by the size of the Lorewalker's restoration project here, I think you'll need a lot more jade.

passages.title: What's Mined Is Yours
passages.text:
Aw'right, so you need jade, do ya? I'd say we owe you at least that - we got plenty in the quarry, and thanks to yer help we should be back on schedule in no time.

I should probably get back to the wife, so let's you and me take this cart o' the good stuff straight to her.

Now, I ain't never met no <race> t'were too big for me to pull in a wagon. You climb on the back there and let ol' Hao do the legwork.

passages.title: What's Mined Is Yours
passages.text:
Well? Where's Hao?

Don't tell me you couldn't find him...

passages.title: What's Mined Is Yours
passages.text:
You did it! You brought my honey-bear back!

Oh thank you, <name>! Thank you!

passages.title: The Serpent's Heart
passages.text:
You've done great here, kid. Thanks to you, we have quite a bit of extra jade, and I know just the someone who could use it.

My friend Foreman Raike is running the great statue project at the Serpent's Heart.

Bring a shipment of extra jade to him, and tell him his old friend Mann says hello. He'll be eagerly waiting your arrival.

passages.title: The Serpent's Heart
passages.text:
Am I seeing this right? A whole shipment of pure, high quality uncut jade?

Thank goodness. I knew Foreman Mann would come through for us.

Oh and you too. Thanks for bringing it by.

passages.title: The Temple of the Jade Serpent
passages.text:
You've done us a huge favor here, traveler.

Now that we have enough jade to complete the statue, we should send word of our progress to Yu'Lon, the Jade Serpent.

When you arrive, speak to Elder Sage Wind-Yi outside the entrance to the Temple of the Jade Serpent.

If you wish to speed your journey, speak to Kitemaster Shoku. I'm sure he can spare an extra kite for you.

passages.title: The Temple of the Jade Serpent
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Temple of the Jade Serpent
passages.text:
You bring news from the Serpent's Spine?

<The Elder Sage patiently listens to your tale of what occurred at the Jade Mines and at the large jade statue.>

Thank you for coming all this way, stranger. However, I cannot allow you to speak to the Jade Serpent right now.

The ancient one is very busy, and as you can see, is not here at the moment.

passages.title: Instant Messaging
passages.text:
Welcome, wikket! Me Kah Kah - chief of Grookin Hill hozen.

Dook Ookem wanted to be chief, but good wikket grook him good - big gift to Kah Kah.

Hozen has gift for good wikket too. Gift come from great crash. Hozen keep it safe for wikket.

passages.title: Instant Messaging
passages.text:
Impressive work, <name>.

It had not occurred to me that we might somehow befriend these creatures.

With their acceptance, we can now turn our attention to more important matters.

passages.title: Furious Fowl
passages.text:
So these guys like fish, huh? Well how about we finish what you started and make them LOVE us?

I've still got some explosive powder from the wreck, just need something to attract the fish.

Guts is sure to do the trick - never fails. I saw some birds flyin' around south of town.

Well? Whatcha waitin' for?

passages.title: Furious Fowl
passages.text: You didn't touch that stuff with your hands did ya?

passages.title: Furious Fowl
passages.text:
Yeah!

Now that's the stuff. Just you wait and see...

passages.title: Boom Bait
passages.text:
There. I've plastered your bird guts over my explosives.

I call 'em Gut Bombs, patent pending.

Since you made friends with these fellas, how about you do the honors?

Just light the fuse and throw 'em down by the shoreline!

passages.title: Boom Bait
passages.text: I have yet to face a crisis that couldn't be fixed with dynamite.

passages.title: Boom Bait
passages.text:
We've just revolutionized how these cretins.. err, hozen, feed themselves.

They'll never be the same!

passages.title: Taking a Crop
passages.text:
Alright, fine. I DON'T have everything under control here. I spent all morning fighting off virmen. I managed to clear them off of my property, but they got away with some of my crops.

They took them down to the river, to the south. I have no idea what they're doing with them, but it's probably not eating them.

If my father wants his delivery now, I'm going to need some help getting those crops back. Could you help me out?

passages.title: Taking a Crop
passages.text: If my father wants his vegetables, I'm going to need your help.

passages.title: Taking a Crop
passages.text:
Perfect.

<Ang surveys the bruised turnips and the soggy watermelons.>

What were they DOING down there!?

passages.title: Beyond the Horizon
passages.text:
I recognize all you've managed to do here, <class>. My report to the Warchief will include an account of your deeds.

But there's no time to rest!

This land must be charted and prepared for Horde settlement. I've already selected an away team to do just that.

Find them before they grow comfortable here. Inform them of their mission, and try to convince your new friends to send along one of their own to serve as a guide.

You'll be staying here with me. We have preparations to make.

passages.title: Beyond the Horizon
passages.text: Has the away team been dispatched, <name>?

passages.title: Beyond the Horizon
passages.text:
Good work <name>.

The away team you assembled has departed.

I hope Gorrok had the sense to change out of that ragged red shirt. I admire his patriotism, but he's had it on since we left Orgrimmar.

They won't be surprising anyone if he's wearing it...

passages.title: Guerrillas in our Midst
passages.text:
Prince Anduin Wrynn. The very son of our enemy's king! Fortune has smiled on the Horde once again, <name>.

But there's another side of this coin. We'd be naive to think the child was left alone.

Any Alliance scum within sight of this land must be searching desperately for their precious princeling.

You and I are going to scour the area and root out his would-be rescuers.

passages.title: Guerrillas in our Midst
passages.text:
Yes!

By Thrall's bloodied fist, I've missed hunting Alliance!

passages.title: Leaders Among Breeders
passages.text:
Before any kegs are tapped, we have work to do. These virmen are no different than the virmen on the Wandering Isle... a nuisance that breeds as fast as the rabbits they resemble.

Sure, we could kill every last virmen we find, but what's the point in needless bloodshed? Let's just take out their alphas, and they'll slow down with their... reproduction.

passages.title: Leaders Among Breeders
passages.text: The virmen here have strange habits. Stranger names.

passages.title: Leaders Among Breeders
passages.text:
<Chen nods.>

Good work, <name>. You're not bad in combat.

What do you say we team up for the next part?

passages.title: Yellow and Red Make Orange
passages.text:
Uncle Chen says we're going to help this guy out with his virmen problem. Fine by me! I LOVE messing with virmen.

Here's the plan: we're going to paint some turnips orange, and then we'll try to convince the virmen that they're carrots.

This can only end in comedy.

I'll gather turnips. You find something that we can use to make edible orange paint.

passages.title: Yellow and Red Make Orange
passages.text: You have the stuff ready for the paint? I went ahead and gathered some turnips.

passages.title: Yellow and Red Make Orange
passages.text:
Whoah, whoah, WHOAH! You brought back BLOOD? I guess I should have looked around for a half second before I asked you to bring me something red.

Yeesh!

<Li Li turns back to the ingredients, spends a moment crushing the flower petals, and then mixes in some of the blood.>

<She begins to giggle.>

passages.title: Crouching Carrot, Hidden Turnip
passages.text:
Uncle Chen's still got his eye on me, which means I won't be wandering off any time soon. I guess it's up to you to take these turnips... I mean, "carrots"... into the Twisted Warren and deliver them for me.

It should be pretty simple. Just toss the vegetables in front of virmen, then watch their reaction when they find out it's really a turnip!

passages.title: Crouching Carrot, Hidden Turnip
passages.text: Go, torment those virmen, <name>!

passages.title: Crouching Carrot, Hidden Turnip
passages.text: Bah ha hah haaaa! I love messing with virmen.

passages.title: Thieves to the Core
passages.text:
You and that Chen fellow are good people, helpin' out with the virmen like you are. I don't like to ask for favors, but I ain't gonna turn 'em away, either.

While you're out there puttin' the hurt to those rabbit-men, you wouldn't mind keepin' an eye out for some bags o' hops, would ya? I'm pretty sure they lifted 'em last night.

Probably usin' em for pillows, knowin' how they are.

passages.title: Thieves to the Core
passages.text: I done told those virmen to stay off my land.

passages.title: Thieves to the Core
passages.text: Aww, thank ya kindly, sir. You're a real gentleman.

passages.title: Li Li's Day Off
passages.text:
Uncle Chen asked me not to get into any fights while he was away... but that doesn't mean I can't go exploring. Finally, a chance to look around Pandaria without stopping every forty-seven steps for another rest!

You want to come with me? I'll bet there's all kinds of cool places we can visit, not too far away from here.

passages.title: Li Li's Day Off
passages.text: You ready to go out yet?

passages.title: Li Li's Day Off
passages.text:
That was great! You and I should go exploring again sometime.

And it looks like we finished before Uncle Chen got back, too. Perfect.

passages.title: Muddy Water
passages.text:
While you're just hangin' around, I might as well get you involved in my whole beer-makin' "process". Ain't much of a process, really... I just mix all the stuff together and wait.

You probably heard - I like to use the muddy water from the riverbanks, to the south. Would you mind fillin' up this flask with that water and bringin' it back? I'll start gettin' the hops and barley all ready.

passages.title: Muddy Water
passages.text: I knowed you for a friend as soon as I seen you.

passages.title: Muddy Water
passages.text: You done good, <name>. You done good.

passages.title: Broken Dreams
passages.text:
Yes, I found the Stormstout Brewery... although I didn't exactly get the warm reception I expected.

<Chen pours himself a mug of ale.>

Do you want to hear the story?

passages.title: Broken Dreams
passages.text: Maybe I wasn't meant to settle down anyhow.

passages.title: Burning Down the House
passages.text:
Look, <name>!

These Alliance dogs built a camp up on the ridge.

Here, take my grog. Let's make a fire they can see from Stormwind!

For the Horde!

passages.title: Burning Down the House
passages.text:
The Alliance must be purged from this land, <name>!

No half-measures will do!

passages.title: Boom Goes the Doonamite!
passages.text:
It's an emergency!

Looks like you stirred up a hornet's nest killin' all them fish-folk.

They're conductin' a full-on counterattack on Grookin Hill!

I was hopin' to get some R&D time, but we're gunna hafta put my methane-grenade theory to work right away!

Meet me on the east side of the fort, and bring yer throwin' arm!

passages.title: Boom Goes the Doonamite!
passages.text: I think these methane-grenades are gunna impact the environment, if ya know what I mean...

passages.title: Boom Goes the Doonamite!
passages.text: I'd say repelling the attack is an understatement!

passages.title: Evacuation Orders
passages.text:
A few farmers remain in the fields... some perilously close to the crumbling wall. I don't want any farmers pretending to be heroes. We will take care of this mantid swarm, and then they can return to their homes.

My Shado-Pan are too busy defending this town to organize evacuations. You want to prove yourself useful? Get those farmers out of harm's way.

passages.title: Evacuation Orders
passages.text: Once these mantid are slain, we can get to work repairing the wall and restoring the town to its normal state.

passages.title: Evacuation Orders
passages.text:
A few stubborn ranchers want to make my job harder?

<The Watch Commander sighs.>

Fine. I will rob no pandaren of his right to defend his land.

passages.title: The Hidden Master
passages.text:
We should be able to handle the defense of Stoneplow from here on out.

<The Watch Commander motions towards Lin Tenderpaw.>

Lin here is searching for someone she calls "The Hidden Master". I believe I know who she's talking about, and I have a clue for you.

Go north.

passages.title: The Hidden Master
passages.text:
You seek training?

<The pandaren studies your physique for several seconds, without speaking.>

Alright.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Bamboo
passages.text:
We will start with a test: The Trial of Bamboo.

Your friend Lin failed this test.

Follow me, and listen carefully to my instructions.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Bamboo
passages.text: If you cannot pass this test, then there is probably no reason to continue our training.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Bamboo
passages.text:
You show promise, <name>. We will continue.

It is now time for your first round of training.

passages.title: Fog Wards
passages.text:
Trainee.

Several wards surround us, hidden in the woods near my home. They are quite effective at dispersing the mist, but they require constant upkeep.

You will find one to the north, one to the west, and one to the south. Find these wards and light them.

passages.title: Fog Wards
passages.text: See if you can light one of the wards while one of the mist incarnations is nearby.

passages.title: Fog Wards
passages.text: You honor your people, <name>.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Wood
passages.text: You have progressed in your training, I think. Come with me, and we will attempt the Trial of Wood.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Wood
passages.text: I'm prepared, <name>. Are you?

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Wood
passages.text: You have the gift of focus, <name>. Not many of my students make it this far.

passages.title: A Taste For Eggs
passages.text:
I can sense your anxiety, but you are not ready yet. Your training must continue before you perform the final test. As for your task... I need you to fetch me some eggs.

Yes, eggs. The marshland atop the hills to the east is home to a number of birds, all of which are generally peaceful in nature. You should have no trouble gathering enough eggs to last me several weeks.

passages.title: A Taste For Eggs
passages.text: How is your egg hunt going?

passages.title: A Taste For Eggs
passages.text:
Now you know why I don't gather the eggs myself.

Shall we continue your training?

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Stone
passages.text:
You have accomplished much in the short time you have been here, <name>. I would not normally offer this test so soon... but I feel that you're ready.

It is time you attempted the Trial of Stone.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Stone
passages.text:
This test will be trying. You will test the strength of your fists against the strength of stone. Steel yourself, <name>.

Not literally, of course.

Unless you normally wear steel gloves... in which case, you may literally steel yourself.

passages.title: Unyielding Fists: Trial of Stone
passages.text:
<Master Bruised Paw bows before you.>

Stone quivers and breaks beneath your fists. You have the power to move mountains, if you so desire.

There is nothing more I can teach you.

passages.title: Training and Discipline
passages.text:
I told myself that, if I ever made it here to the Hidden Master, I would learn everything I could from him. This is my chance, <name>. I'm not going to let it slip away.

Still, I fear that Stoneplow needs us. I left early, before we were able to push the mantid scouts back. I'd feel better if you would check in with the Watch Commander for me.

Oh, and if you run into the others, maybe you should tell them where the Hidden Master is...

passages.title: Training and Discipline
passages.text:
I'm glad to hear that Lin is well.

Our defenses are holding, for now. The mantid continue to send their scouts over the wall, but they haven't gotten much farther than that.

passages.title: Pages of History
passages.text:
The worst possible thing has happened, <race>.

We. Have. Bookworms.

This is a critical situation. All Bookworms in the library must be eradicated at once to prevent their spread.

We must squash this problem, literally! Please examine the infested books in the library and squash any Bookworms that you find.

passages.title: Pages of History
passages.text: My stomach is too fragile to handle the squashing of bugs. Is it done?

passages.title: Pages of History
passages.text:
Oh, wonderful! I am so relieved that we managed to avert disaster.

No no, don't get too close, please. You still have some squashed bug bits on your shoes.

passages.title: Everything In Its Place
passages.text:
You have helped us more than you can ever imagine, <name>.

I do not know what I would do if our precious scrolls were ever to be lost.

Please return to the Elder Sage Rain-Zhu and tell him that the library is in order.

passages.title: Everything In Its Place
passages.text:
Lorewalker Stonestep is back to work?

Remarkable. You were able to do what the last four priests I sent could not.

I...I think my headache is disappearing.

passages.title: A New Vision
passages.text: Please tell the Elder Sage Rain-Zhu that I will begin my work at once.

passages.title: A New Vision
passages.text: Wonderful! Knowing that the scryer has returned to his meditations has lifted a great burden from my shoulders.

passages.title: Dawn's Blossom
passages.text:
Blood and Thunder! My axe hungers!

We won't return to Orgrimmar until every last Alliance is purged from this land.

I will train these natives myself, if I have to. One way or another, this land will be made ready for Horde settlement.

In the meantime, their chief gave me this to pass on to you - a map and a message in some fancy script.

Do what you must, but be quick about it.

War is brewing...

passages.title: Dawn's Blossom
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>!

Welcome to Dawn's Blossom, a home of my people.

Sadly I must depart. Alas, a Lorewalker's work is never done.

Make yourself at home. Our people could surely make use of one with your talents.

passages.title: Wee Little Shenanigans
passages.text:
So... we bought some cheap grains in bulk. It turned out the grain was infested with sprites.

I HATE sprites. With their wee beady eyes and constant smiling.

I would like to resolve this quietly. Can I buy your services to discreetly eliminate some of these grain thieves?

passages.title: Wee Little Shenanigans
passages.text: Oh good, they didn't turn you into a frog yet. I saw them do that once you know.

passages.title: Wee Little Shenanigans
passages.text: Thank you for your help stranger! Hopefully we can deal with the rest on our own from here.

passages.title: Taste Test
passages.text:
As long as you're here, you might as well help me out. I'm feeling pretty darn unqualified for the task, seeing as I've never drank a drop of beer in my life.

You should try a little sample of each of their grains. Let's see if any of this stuff is sweet enough for Uncle Chen.

passages.title: Taste Test
passages.text: None of this seems to taste sweet enough! What's the deal?

passages.title: Taste Test
passages.text:
Huh. I guess none of that grain is going to work. Uncle Chen is pretty picky.

Maybe the Grainlord knows where we can find something more... special.

passages.title: The Quest for Better Barley
passages.text:
Looking for sweet grain? My father once mentioned a malted cave barley that sounds about right.

If you are willing to brave the peril, there is an ancient cave at the base of the Winds' Edge south of here.

There is even an old lift my father made when he would travel into the jungle.

In the cave is a bush as old as my family. From that bush you can pluck a grain so sweet it will humble your senses.

Just watch out for its guardians.

passages.title: The Quest for Better Barley
passages.text: That jungle sounds spooky.

passages.title: The Quest for Better Barley
passages.text: Now THIS smells like the right stuff!

passages.title: Li Li and the Grain
passages.text:
I'll let you in on my brewing plan, <name>: I'm planning on making an Emperor Stout. Done right, it should be dark, roasty, and high in alcohol.

<A frown appears on Chen's face.>

I just realized... I never told my plans to Li Li. She'll have no idea what type of grain to bring back!

Could you speak with her? I need her to bring back the sweetest malted grains she can find.

passages.title: Li Li and the Grain
passages.text:
<name>? What are you doing here?

So, Uncle Chen wants sweet malts? No problem! Let's get to the taste testing.

passages.title: Doesn't Hold Water
passages.text:
Would you mind checking in on Mudmug? He may need some assistance bringing that water back.

I'm sure he'll appreciate the help of a big, strong <class> like yourself to help him shoulder the load.

passages.title: Doesn't Hold Water
passages.text: <name>! You here to help out? That's mighty swell of you.

passages.title: Gardener Fran and the Watering Can
passages.text:
You want me to just GIVE you some hops? Pfshh! This is the third time today some little <race> like you has come up to me asking for food!

You want food? Then you'd better work!

<She shoves a watering can into your hand.>

Now go water my plants!

passages.title: Gardener Fran and the Watering Can
passages.text: Water my plants you lazy <class>!

passages.title: Gardener Fran and the Watering Can
passages.text:
Hmmph!

Nice farming.

passages.title: The Great Water Hunt
passages.text:
Look at it, <name>: the Gilded Fan. I heared lots of good things about the water they got here. Lots of bad things, too.

No sayin' what kind of water Chen's gonna be needin', so what say we make him a little sampler platter?

Come on, let's get movin'. We'll go scoop up some water together.

passages.title: The Great Water Hunt
passages.text: That Stormstout feller says that he's the best brewer that ever was. Might be true, couldn't tell ya one way or the 'nother as of yet.

passages.title: The Great Water Hunt
passages.text:
Lookee that, neighbor! That is quite the collection of water we got here. With magical water like this, I'm sure that Chen'll make a brew that really shines.

Or possibly a brew that lands someone in the outhouse for a month. I guess we'll just have to wait and see.

passages.title: Weed War
passages.text:
You want some hops? I've got plenty in the shed out back. I'll gladly share some with you... if you'll help me weed my field.

Now "hop" to it! Get it?

passages.title: Weed War
passages.text: You weed like a champion.

passages.title: Seeing Orange
passages.text:
Those virmen... they make me do horrible, horrible, silly things. All involving carrots. I couldn't tell you how many carrots they threw at me.

Let's not waste any more time. Get me out of here!

passages.title: Seeing Orange
passages.text: What's all this fuss about carrots? I don't get it.

passages.title: The Fall of Ga'trul
passages.text:
Alright <lad/lass>. We've taken enough jabs at this warlock army... now it's time to cut off the head.
