Ga'trul's back there, in that big ol' temple ruin. Give him a good what-for, and the Horde will have lost its last stake here in Pandaria.

passages.title: The Fall of Ga'trul
passages.text: What's the matter, <name>? Didn't you find Sully? Did Ga'trul elude you?

passages.title: The Fall of Ga'trul
passages.text:
Sha...

Fighting the Horde on a foreign shore is hard enough.

passages.title: Knocking on the Door
passages.text:
Now, onward to the Stormstout Brewery! It's high time that I was reunited with the rest of the Stormstouts... and what better way to reunite than over a few mugs of ale?

You know where the brewery is, right? Just follow this road to the west. You can't miss it. Of course, you're free to share the road with us - we'll be leaving any moment now.

passages.title: Knocking on the Door
passages.text: The door... it's boarded up?

passages.title: Clear the Way
passages.text:
Are you seeing this? Virmen, hozen, and water sprites... all pouring out of the brewery doors and windows! What the heck is going on in there!?

There is another entrance, on the eastern side of the brewery. I'm going to run over there and try to figure out what's going on. In the meantime, see if you can't get rid of these creatures. There's nothing worse than a drunken hozen.

passages.title: Clear the Way
passages.text: This brewery - it's a disgrace to the Stormstout name! Something needs to be done!

passages.title: Clear the Way
passages.text: I've had just about enough of this brewery. I'm starting to think that you and I should just bust down the wall and clean house.

passages.title: Cleaning House
passages.text:
That's it, <name>. I've had enough of this.

If somebody doesn't do SOMETHING to take care of this brewery, we'll lose it forever. And there's far too much family history - and beer - in there to risk wasting.

So... we're going to break in through the back door. You, Li Li, Mudmug, and me.

It's gonna be a brawl in there.

Let me know when you're ready.

passages.title: Cleaning House
passages.text: Let's do this.

passages.title: Cleaning House
passages.text:
Take a look around - it's a lot calmer outside. All the brewery needed was somebody strong to take care of it.

It's going to take some time to clean this place up, but I don't really mind that so much.

This is, after all... my home.

passages.title: What's Eating Zhu's Watch?
passages.text:
Pandaren always welcome travelers with open arms - and open kegs! But this town full of jerks!

Everyone so busy sulking, they won't talk to Ken-Ken at all!

Can you find someone in town who will talk to us? Maybe normal pandaren just hiding in the houses?

passages.title: What's Eating Zhu's Watch?
passages.text: Something definitely not right! Pandaren supposed to be HAPPY!

passages.title: What's Eating Zhu's Watch?
passages.text: Only one lady-panda who's not crazy? This worse than Ken-Ken thought...

passages.title: Materia Medica
passages.text:
Alright, Ken-Ken pretty sure he knows what wrong with pandaren! Got old, old hozen remedy that do the trick.

Need to mix honey, fish oil, and salt. Ken-Ken saw lots of beehives in the trees around town, and there must be fish left in the dry ponds.

That just leave salt... Mei might know where we can find some.

passages.title: Materia Medica
passages.text: Can't believe Ken-Ken did not think of this sooner. It's the ONE thing that can ruin his day...

passages.title: Materia Medica
passages.text:
Pandaren got a case of the spooky-dooks!

Dooks get scared sometimes, don't wanna come out. Poor, fluffy mopey-dopes must be ready to explode by now!

This just the thing to bring 'em out. That make pandaren happy for sure!

Just like ol' gramma used to say: can't THROW if can't GO!

passages.title: Cheer Up, Yi-Mo
passages.text:
Ever since this storm began, I've just been... tired.

Not physically... no. It's like my very soul is exhausted. Worthless. Hopeless. I imagine it's what one feels when a mate leaves them for someone with a rounder belly, but I've never had a mate so how would I know?

How can I claim to know anything? I'm worthless to everyone but these thunderbirds. At least they'll have a good meal out of me.

<Yi-Mo sighs deeply and continues staring off into the sky. It doesn't look like he's going anywhere.>

passages.title: Cheer Up, Yi-Mo
passages.text:
I can't believe he was actually going to do that... This despair is worse than I had even imagined.

I cannot thank you enough for bringing him back.

passages.title: Why So Serious?
passages.text:
Okay, so that not work. Well... it cheer Ken-Ken up! But pandaren still sad...

We try another old hozen remedy - this time, we go back even further than gramma, way WAY back to ancient times. Hozen still do this sometimes... mostly at parties.

Ken-Ken got woodworking to do - you bring him teeth! Not yours; big ones, like a panther would have!

Oh, and some paint! Mei might know where to find.

passages.title: Why So Serious?
passages.text:
<Ken-Ken is hard at work carving something out of tree bark.>

This gonna be great, you'll see.

passages.title: Why So Serious?
passages.text:
Just in time! All done... look!

<Ken-Ken holds up a carved wooden mask with a ridiculous face.>

Now we put on finishing touches and we gots a guaranteed FUN MACHINE!

passages.title: Apply Directly to the Forehead
passages.text:
Well... THAT was unexpected!

Come to think of it, now Ken-Ken remember why hozen use mask in the first place...

A legend about the Monkey King says he used a mask to cure old pandaren emperor, Shaohao, when he was too sad to lead his people. Then they buried mask--with all his sadness--in the ground.

We should use the mask on more pandaren, but instead of putting sad away in ground, we gonna PUNCH ITS BUTT.

Let's do this, <name>!

passages.title: Apply Directly to the Forehead
passages.text:
This must be the emperor's sad coming back! That is some oooold sad.

Ken-Ken bet pandaren sad get stronger with age, too, like pandaren booze.

passages.title: Apply Directly to the Forehead
passages.text:
We saving pandaren, but the land still sad... Look, rain's not stopping at all!

<Ken-Ken shakes his tiny fists at the sky.>

How many more butts we gotta punch before we fix this town?!

<The sky darkens in response.>

passages.title: Zhu's Despair
passages.text:
Hmm... Is that Yi-Mo kid over there?

<Ken-Ken squints against the increasing torrents of rain.>

It is! He's at the well, and he's not lookin' so good.

Ken-Ken got a bad feeling about this...

passages.title: Zhu's Despair
passages.text:
We did some good work here today, <name>.

Monastery always tell us to leave a place better than we find it.

passages.title: Stoneplow Thirsts
passages.text:
Excuse me... <name>? Did I hear your name correctly?

I've come from Stoneplow, in the west. They sent me to pick up some emergency beer rations, but the Stormstout Brewery is all boarded up!

It looks like your handsome friend there - no, not Mudmug, the other one - has a few casks with him. Could you spare a keg for a town in need?

passages.title: Stoneplow Thirsts
passages.text: Greetings, <class>.

passages.title: Stoneplow Thirsts
passages.text:
Finally! Emmi's come through.

I hope all is well at the Stormstout Brewery. My men don't do well without beer.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text:
Mogu? They seem like the elves, ancient and an over developed sense of entitlement. Everyone of Azeroth must learn, sooner or later, that the Horde is not "visiting" this world. We are here. We are staying.

Teach them this lesson. Quell their numbers in the ruins south and west of here. Break their amassing forces before they decide to attack.

Learn what you can of how these creatures fight, and how they die.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text: You found how many? Sounds like a veritable nest of the vile creatures. If they were more civilized I might consider extending them an invitation to join the Horde.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text: These are more than just a bandit threat. They are an ancient people beginning to rally under a single banner. Mark my words, soon these lands will know war.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text:
The mogu found the Pools of Youth!

Mama Bramblestaff used to tell me old stories about those. During the mogu empire they would use the waters to extend life.

Thing is those stories never ended well for some reason. As if the waters were cursed.

Either way, we should investigate. There is a good chance those waters might help Leza.

It looks like the Pools of Youth are on the northwestern side of the ruins.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text: Leza's pain is immense. Only powers beyond my own can save her and the baby now.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text: At this point I am willing to try anything. This land is claiming my wife and unborn child. I need all the help I can get.

passages.title: Herbal Remedies
passages.text:
Kang's remedy isn't working.

There is something else at work here. A power deep beneath the soil. It is sapping us of hope, hitting us with depression and despair.

Kang tells me this land has lotus plants. I might be able to make a tea that would hopefully lend Leza some strength.

Please, adventurer, search the ruins south and west of here for lotus leaves. I will pay you for your efforts.

passages.title: Herbal Remedies
passages.text:
I've been punched, stabbed, thrown off of a cliff, hit in the face by someone's mace, hit in the face by my own mace, and fell off the elevator at Thunder Bluff on more than one occasion.

None of that pain sounds even half as bad as what Leza is going through. I hope this tea helps...

passages.title: Herbal Remedies
passages.text: Thank you hero. Kor is a brave warrior but he lacks compassion at times. Life must come before death, or there will be none of us left when the fighting is done.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text:
Leza now walks with the ancestors of this strange land. I must look now to the living.

Kor has led a group of our scouts west deeper into the jungle.

I sent a scout of my own to investigate the crane temple. Please, adventurer, seek out my scout, get their report, then meet up with Kor and lend what aid you can to him.

We will join you as quickly as we are able.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text: War. It always comes down to war.

passages.title: Going West
passages.text:
<name>! Well timed!

We were laying an ambush for the Alliance in the ruins west of here when the mogu ambushed us. They are using mage portals to call in reinforcements.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds, on the southern coast where the Krasarang River meets the sea, rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers.

They should be told of what happened here.

If you're headed that way, I have a favor to ask; We often send supplies to the temple, but our last courier has not returned. Please look for signs of him as you travel - where the road forks at the Dojani River, he'd have gone north. When you reach the temple, find Koro Mistwalker.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... And the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Watch, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Barreling Along
passages.text:
No, no, no, don't you worry about pickin' 'em up. I can hold these here barrels.

I may not be the handsomest pandaren, or the smartest, or any fun to be around in the slightest, but I'm stronger than a mushan beast.

I'mma just need you to lead the way.

passages.title: Barreling Along
passages.text: Where's Mudmug?

passages.title: Barreling Along
passages.text: Good! The water's here!

passages.title: For Family
passages.text:
Kor should have caught up by now. He said he was going to secure the Ruins of Korja east of here and meet us to help with the mantid threat.

He may need help against Groundbreaker Brojai. Could you assist him? Kang and I will follow shortly.

passages.title: For Family
passages.text: This land claims so much.

passages.title: For Family
passages.text:
I thank you for avenging my friend, <name>. We did not always see eye to eye, but I will mourn him.

I know he would have wanted you to carry one of his items with you as a token of his memory and gratitude.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
The mantid! They came out of nowhere and smashed our convoy to ruin, scattering our people this way and that.

Now they are preparing to hit Stoneplow.

Please, <class>, destroy some of these beasts before they get sufficient numbers to flank our home.

If my cousin, Ambassador Len, is still alive and at our convoy he should be able to reward you for your help.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text: It has been many thousands of years since mantid were seen on this side of the Great Wall.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <class>! I've never seen anybody stand up to the mantid like that before.

Well, other than the Shado-Pan, of course...

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds, on the southern coast where the Krasarang River meets the sea, rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers.

They should be told of what happened here.

If you're headed that way, I have a favor to ask; We often send supplies to the temple, but our last courier has not returned. Please look for signs of him as you travel - where the road forks at the Dojani River, he'd have gone south. When you reach the temple, find Koro Mistwalker.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... And the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Watch, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Poisoned!
passages.text: The... mogu. Do not trust. Poison. Get sample... sample blades. Bring to Dezco... in Thunder Cleft, west of here.

passages.title: Poisoned!
passages.text: You have news of Chezin?

passages.title: Poisoned!
passages.text:
Chezin is dead? This is very bad news indeed. Kor, Chezin and I have fought dragons, undead, and Alliance on nearly every shore that has a name.

To lose him like this...

Thank you for recovering these weapons. It should teach us much about our new enemy.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text:
Mogu are thugs. They have always been thugs.

Only when they ruled their empires in the old stories did they ever know any kind of magic.

But these mogu are using arcane portals and spells. We need to stop them!

adventurer, look for any artifacts the mogu are using to cast their magics with. I saw a number of their collectors and reclaimers to the west and north that were gathering these items.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Every artifact in our possession is one less weapon in mogu hands.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Well done <name>. You have removed the sword from the child's hands.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text:
So much death. And more to come, if Ambassador Han's stories of the mantid are to be believed.

We must help. We must do our part to save lives.

Travel to Stoneplow. Warn them of the coming mantid attack.

I will join you with what forces I can muster once I have laid Kor's body to rest.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text: Mantid from the south? This is not a good day.

passages.title: The Murksweats
passages.text:
Take a good look. The river nearby is swarming with these snakes. Their venom causes a condition the locals call "the murksweats."

Several refugees were bitten as they fled the temple and have already begun to show symptoms: nausea, vomiting, and intense sweating as the body rejects all fluids, causing dehydration and potentially death.

We are administering anti-venom as quickly as possible, but we'll need more venom glands. Don't bother removing the glands yourself - just bring back the whole head.

passages.title: The Murksweats
passages.text:
<Anduin is focused intently on his hands, swiftly carving venom glands from the snakes.>

Inside the jaw... two inches behind the second set of fangs...

passages.title: The Murksweats
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>. I knew you'd be hardy enough to handle it.

Judging by the sounds coming out of these refugees, I would not wish the murksweats on my worst enemy.

passages.title: Unsafe Passage
passages.text:
As we say at the temple: "Never fight a tiger with a hozen on your back."

We will deal with the sha, but first we must see to the more immediate... nuisance.

<Koro slams the writhing saurok HARD against the stone.>

Groups of refugees from the temple are heading for a camp to the north, but they're being ambushed by saurok. Help me see the next group to the camp and we'll figure out our next move from there.

passages.title: Unsafe Passage
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. We would not have made it without your help.

passages.title: Blinding the Riverblades
passages.text:
"A hooded falcon catches no quarry."

This is one of the first mantras we teach young monks at the temple. It means that even a foe as swift and lethal as a falcon can be neutralized by depriving its senses.

The saurok have scouts all over the region acting as eyes for their raiding parties.

It's time we put their eyes out, don't you think?

passages.title: Blinding the Riverblades
passages.text:
Well done. I only wish I could have accompanied you...

The blood on these hand-wraps is not my own, you know.

passages.title: Sha Can Awe
passages.text:
The sha have the mysterious ability to evoke powerful, often overwhelming, emotional responses in their victims.

As we fled the temple, senior members of the Crane Wing order stayed behind to cover our escape. They are no doubt being subjected to intense emotional trauma, and I fear they are not all strong enough to resist falling into despair.

adventurer, we have to show them there is still hope! Show them that despair CAN be defeated!

passages.title: Sha Can Awe
passages.text: Look for Crane Wing pandaren who are falling to despair and slay sha near them while I support you!

passages.title: Sha Can Awe
passages.text:
Honestly, I'm a little surprised that worked.

Pandaria is proving to be a land where the lines between metaphor and reality are blurred.

passages.title: In the House of the Red Crane
passages.text:
"Broken are the bodies wherein hopeless hearts reside - the blight of despair strikes forth from inside."

This was the last piece of wisdom the Red Crane imparted to me, just hours before the Sha outbreak. It makes sense now...

adventurer, when the Sha attacked, they broke forth from the temple's basement...

All of his teachings - the very Way of the Crane itself... it's all been preparation for facing the Sha of Despair.

The Red Crane has been expecting this conflict for centuries!

passages.title: In the House of the Red Crane
passages.text:
You have vanquished the Sha of Despair. My order can handle the remaining cleanup from here.

It seems the time has finally come to face the consequences of Shaohao's actions.

This conflict has been a long time coming - the arrival of your people was merely a catalyst. Now, your help will be necessary if Pandaria is to survive.

passages.title: The Lost Dynasty
passages.text:
I wonder if I could bother you for another task. My daughter, the good Sentinel Commander Lyalia here, refuses to let me go into the field.

I have spent everyday in that oubliette staring at the ruins to our north, itching to investigate.

If we are where I suspect we are those ruins could contain the key we need to finding the fabled Pools of Youth!

Please, <class>! Go to those ruins and salvage any tablets that still have writing on them.

passages.title: The Lost Dynasty
passages.text:
It is one thing to research the lost dynasties. It is quite another to visit their ancient ruins.

I am giddy as I have not felt in centuries!

passages.title: The Lost Dynasty
passages.text:
Oh! Fabulous! Fabulous!

Your one trip has advanced my research more than ten years of reading dusty tomes and decaying scrolls...

And those "mogu" you saw. I have been doing some research as well as speaking to Kang on the subject.

I suspect now that they were the race of the lost dynasties that my research is derived from.

Of course, that also means that they are the ones who used to control the Pools of Youth.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text:
North! Go north to the Pools of Youth. Get some of the water but be on your guard.

The mogu list this as a "high value" target. Kang Bramblestaff will meet you there if he has not already arrived by your side.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text: Nothing like being mortal to give one a sense of urgency.

passages.title: The Pools of Youth
passages.text:
You... you found the pools! The waters do exist!

Something is wrong though. I feel equal parts shadow and light swirling in this vial.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text:
While you were at the ruins dusting off tablets for my father I lost five scouts to wandering mogu patrols.

These creatures apparently have little interest in peace and are about as trustworthy as the Horde.

They are too numerous and we are too weak, however.

Go to the ruins west of here and cull the mogu numbers. They won't be expecting a <class>.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text:
Kang has been sharing stories with me about these mogu.

Apparently ages ago they ruled as emperors subjugating all free races of Pandaria and the surrounding regions. Now they are little more than hoodlums.

To see these mogu fight though, I suspect they are trying to rekindle some of their older ideals and ambitions.

passages.title: Threat from Dojan
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Another few missions like that and we might have to make you an honorary sentinel.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text:
Mogu do NOT use arcane magics.

They are thugs. They have always been thugs. Only when they ruled their empires in the old stories did they ever know any kind of magic.

But these mogu are using arcane portals and old artifacts. We need to stop them!

adventurer, look for any artifacts the mogu are using to cast their magics with. I saw piles of these items being collected near the Ruins of Korja south of here.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Every artifact in our possession is one less weapon in mogu hands.

passages.title: Re-Reclaim
passages.text: Well done <name>. You have removed the sword from the child's hands.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text:
Help me, adventurer. These poor pandaren are in need of healing, and my powers are weakened.

I did find an old tome in my collection that allowed me to convert the herbs you collected earlier into a healing poultice.

Use this on the injured pandaren and it should get them back on their feet.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text: These mantid are a much bigger threat than I think even the pandaren give them credit for.

passages.title: The Stoneplow Convoy
passages.text:
It has been a long time since I rolled up my sleeves and helped the needy. In my lust for immortality I forgot why I became a priest.

Thank you for reminding me there is good in this world worth fighting for, <name>.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text:
My father gave me his life. Tyrande gave me her trust. My sentinels gave me their allegiance.

It is time I repaid them all.

With Brojai dead we can mop up the remaining mogu. The next threat is the mantid.

Go north to Stoneplow and lend them your help. Tell them I will be bringing what sentinels I can muster to aid in the defense of their city against the mantid.

passages.title: Warn Stoneplow
passages.text: Mantid from the south? This is not a good day.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
The mantid! They came out of nowhere and smashed our convoy to ruin, scattering our people this way and that.

Now they are preparing to hit Stoneplow.

Please, <class>, destroy some of these beasts before they get sufficient numbers to flank our home.

If my cousin, Ambassador Len, is still alive and at our convoy he should be able to reward you for your help.

passages.title: The Mantid
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <class>! I've never seen anybody stand up to the mantid like that before.

Well, other than the Shado-Pan, of course...

passages.title: The Waters of Youth
passages.text:
She is headstrong, my little Lyalia. I should have known she would try to challenge the Lord Reclaimer.

Since her mother died, I forsook much of the time I should have spent with her in search of immortality, insisting that we could live forever, together.

And now my obsession has cost my little Lyalia her life.

Please, adventurer, when she wakes, tell her I love her.

passages.title: The Waters of Youth
passages.text: He... he shouldn't have done that! He shouldn't have paid for my mistake!

passages.title: Call Out Their Leader
passages.text:
Clearly, you are a hero come to aid us.

Slay the Bataari Tribe in the Kun-Lai Pass to the northwest until the Bataari Fire-Warrior is angered enough to appear. Dispatch him.

passages.title: Call Out Their Leader
passages.text: If the war leader of the yaungol is slain, surely our village will be saved and the refugees will be able to return to their farms.

passages.title: Call Out Their Leader
passages.text: We are delivered! I was right about you, <class>.

passages.title: Hit Medicine
passages.text:
Our warriors are fighting to keep the yaungol at bay in the Kun-Lai Pass to the northwest.

Take this liniment. It is a powerful medicine that has been passed down in my family over the generations.

Use the dit da jow to heal the injured warriors if you do not have healing powers of your own to use on them.

passages.title: Hit Medicine
passages.text:
You have my thanks, <name>. You have shown great honor through your actions.

I hope that my family's dit da jow was of some use to you.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers. I suspect they'll know something about what happened here.

The temple is located on the southern coast of the wilds, where the Krasarang River meets the sea.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... So the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Bastion, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
Deep in the wilds rests the Temple of the Red Crane, home of the great Chi-Ji and his most devout followers. I suspect they'll know something about what happened here.

The temple is located on the southern coast of the wilds, where the Krasarang River meets the sea.

passages.title: Into the Wilds
passages.text:
I see... So the sha have seeped out as far as the province already, have they?

Well, I hate to break it to you, but the temple is also overrun with sha. Those of us who haven't been killed or... possessed, or whatever, are fleeing for our very lives.

If you defeated the sha at Zhu's Bastion, I have to implore you to help us deal with them here.

passages.title: Gauging Our Progress
passages.text:
The time for war is at hand, <name>!

We've been training these natives non-stop since you left, and I believe they're as good as they're going to get.

See for yourself. Check in with the others and return with your findings.

We must rely on our enemy being somehow... even less prepared.

passages.title: Gauging Our Progress
passages.text: How is our combat training coming along?

passages.title: Gauging Our Progress
passages.text:
At least they're confident.

That might count for something.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
These hozen are behaving most unnaturally, <name>. Marching in formation? In armor?

This troubles me. We must discuss it at another time, however. I have come to ask for your assistance.

The ancient fresco, where last we spoke, is nearly unveiled. I am certain that it holds ancient wisdom - knowledge that the emperor wanted us to remember.

My meditations alone may not be enough to discern its meaning. Please, take this heirloom to the shrine of my ancestors. I shall require their assistance.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
<Lorewalker Cho shudders, in spite of himself.>

The legends... they're true!

passages.title: Love's Labor
passages.text:
Can I trouble you for another favor?

We're way behind schedule, and this jade shipment is the last we need to finish the great statue.

I've got my hands full, so could you run this ore over to the other foremen?

Historian Dinh, Surveyor Sawa, and Kitemaster Shoku can all be found around the base of the statue. Taskmaster Emi is directing production at the top of the statue.

We're on a deadline, so make sure you do it fast! Time's a wasting!

passages.title: Love's Labor
passages.text: Did you deliver the jade in time?

passages.title: Love's Labor
passages.text: What, done already? You're quite the runner, <class>. You ever thought about making a living out of this?

passages.title: Emergency Response
passages.text:
Your companions have made themselves at home in our land, and brought with them a dangerous conflict.

The full extent of their destruction here we cannot yet know. Already it is... unspeakable.

Nevertheless, to forsake your friends out of spite would be against our way. Any that yet live are doubtlessly wounded and in desperate need of care.

These fireworks were to celebrate the statue's completion. Use them near your companions to signal Mishi, and she will bear them off to safety.

passages.title: Emergency Response
passages.text:
My thoughts will be with your fallen companions, traveler.

May their wounds mend well.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your Admiral Taylor has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house back in Binan Village.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor has Awakened
passages.text:
<name>, is that you? I can't believe we survived the destruction of the Jade Serpent.

Some of us anyway.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your General Nazgrim has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house back in Binan Village.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
Where have you been, <name>? Nevermind. As you can see, we survived the battle at the Jade Serpent.

Unfortunately, so did... they.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your General Nazgrim has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs in the apothecary's house across the way.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
Where have you been, <name>? Nevermind. As you can see, we survived the battle at the Jade Serpent.

Unfortunately, so did... they.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
It would seem that your General Nazgrim has awakened from his injuries. He and his people are upstairs.

He has requested your presence.

passages.title: General Nazgrim has Awakened
passages.text:
Where have you been, <name>? Nevermind. As you can see, we survived the battle at the Jade Serpent.

Unfortunately, so did... they.

passages.title: Westwind Rest
passages.text:
<Admiral Taylor winces in pain.>

Jade Forest was a disaster. 

Anduin's gone. We lost some good people. We didn't stop the Horde from advancing into the continent. 

But I think I've found a way to get the locals on our side. You just helped fight off some of these "yaungol", no?

I hear yaungol sacked Westwind Rest, a local village. We've been told that two groups of survivors have camped out along the road west out of town.

We help them out, maybe they'll consider siding with the Allliance.

passages.title: Westwind Rest
passages.text: I will not rest until our people are returned and this village rebuilt.

passages.title: Westwind Rest
passages.text:
Well... we are alive, and that is better than we could have hoped for without your help.

But, if this is truly to become a base of operations for you, and if we are to join your Alliance, there is one more thing you must do to guarantee our security.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
The yaungol have always been a difficult, proud people, but never this violent or aggressive. 

I do not know what has prompted this change in their behavior, but we don't have time to find out, now. We fear for our lives and livelihoods as long as Ur-Bataar, leader of the Bataari yaungol, lives.

Go, set the banner in his camp ablaze to challenge him, and then defeat him in battle. Only then will we be secure.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
You did it! At the very least, we have justice, and safety, though in the process we have lost so much.

Regardless, it has been decided. We will join the Alliance, and with your help, rebuild this village.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
The yaungol have always been a difficult, proud people, but never this violent or aggressive. 

I do not know what has prompted this change in their behavior, but we don't have time to find out, now. We fear for our lives and livelihoods as long as Ur-Bataar, leader of the Bataari yaungol, lives.

Go, set the banner in his camp ablaze to challenge him, and then defeat him in battle. Only then will we be secure.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text: As long as Ur-Bataar lives, we cannot have peace.

passages.title: Challenge Accepted
passages.text:
You did it! At the very least, we have justice, and safety, though in the process we have lost so much.

Regardless, it has been decided. We will join the Horde, and with your help, rebuild this village.

passages.title: An Unexpected Advantage
passages.text:
Things seem to be goin' our way more and more lately, <name>. I was out doin some explorin' when I came upon this little beauty.

<Sully gestures to the ballista to his right.>

Problem is she's one of a set and the other one is still in pieces. I'd have gotten it together by now if those pesky Grimleers hadn't ambushed me and taken some of the gears and bolts.

Hey, ye seem to be pretty good at handlin' the natives. Ye wouldn't mind goin' and helpin' ol'Sully out would ye?

passages.title: An Unexpected Advantage
passages.text: Did ye find my missing gears and bolts?

passages.title: An Unexpected Advantage
passages.text:
Well these aren't as good as she deserves, but it will have to work.

<Sully pats the dismantled ballista.>

I'll get 'er up and runnin' in no time, just ye watch!

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
I... I escaped from Farmer Chow's, to the southeast of here. It's been taken over by yaungol, but the old man and his wife just won't give it up!

Please, go there and help him out. Maybe if you do, he'll be willing to send some folks back here and help you guys farm up some food for the new town?

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
You're a sight for sore eyes, <class>.

I'll be glad to help you Alliance fellas out. First though, you need to help me get my farm back.

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
I... I escaped from Farmer Chow's, to the southeast of here. It's been taken over by yaungol, but the old man and his wife just won't give it up!

Please, go there and help him... Maybe if you do, he'll be willing to send some folks back here and help you guys farm up some food for the new town?

passages.title: Trouble on the Farmstead
passages.text:
You're a sight for sore eyes, <class>.

I'll be glad to help you Horde fellas out. First though, you need to help me get my farm back.

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text:
Mobility is going to be key to maintaining our foothold in this new land. Problem is, there's no way to maintain mobility without mounts, and... well, we don't have many of those here, now do we?

The local yaks seem to make good mounts. At least, the local pandaren say they do. Why don't you go round some up for us?

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: It's going to take more yaks than that to get this place back into fightin' condition, <name>, yes it is.

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: These yaks will do the trick nicely. Good work, <name>. I'm feeling better about this whole situation already.

passages.title: ... and the Pot, Too!
passages.text:
Sure, I'm willing to help you guys out. But we need to eat, too! I don't even have a pot to cook in! Let alone ingredients to put in it!

Here's a list of the things that I need. Now get!

passages.title: ... and the Pot, Too!
passages.text: Do you have everything from the list?!

passages.title: ... and the Pot, Too!
passages.text: Well there you go. We should be plenty good, now.

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
I know your friends are worried about the animating statues over at Mogujia, but I'll tell you what you should really be worried about.

Where there are animated statues, there are mogu. I don't know if you've seen one before, but if you haven't...

Well, let's just say mogu are bad, bad, news.

While you're dealing with whatever else you're doing, you need to get the mogu behind the trouble!

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text: Did you find him? Is he dead? No? Oh, man. Don't make me worried!

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
Oh, thank goodness! You've saved all of our skins, believe me.

You have no idea how much trouble those guys can stir up.

Err, or, I guess you do, now. Kind of. Almost.

Imagine that, but a lot worse, and for a couple thousand years.

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
I know your friends are worried about the animating statues over at Mogujia, but I'll tell you what you should really be worried about.

Where there are animated statues, there are Mogu. I don't know if you've seen one before, but if you haven't...

Well, let's just say Mogu are bad, bad, news.

While you're dealing with whatever else you're doing, you need to get the Mogu behind the trouble!

passages.title: Mogu?! Oh No-gu!
passages.text:
Oh, thank goodness! You've saved all of our skins, believe me.

You have no idea how much trouble those guys can stir up.

Err, or, I guess you do, now. Kind of. Almost.

Imagine that, but a lot worse, and for a couple thousand years.

passages.title: The Mantidote
passages.text:
<Mei motions towards the battlefield.>

You see those huge mantid commanders out there? They have a strange aura about them. It reminds me of the sadness we saw at Zhu's Watch.

Perhaps... they're under the influence of the sha, too?

I kept Ken-Ken's mask - the one he used to remove the sha from Yi-Mo. I believe that, if we use it on the mantid, we can convince them to turn back.

passages.title: It Does You No Good In The Keg
passages.text:
I been thinkin'.

We got all this beer that Chen brewed, and we got all these people that you've gathered. We should bring the two together.

There's a bunch o' folks out there in the fields, riskin' their lives for Pandaria. You an' I should at least bring 'em a keg or two.

They might raise their mugs in victory. They might enjoy one last drink before gettin' skivvered by a mantid. Either way, I wouldn't want 'em to fight without a good brew in their belly.

passages.title: Students No More
passages.text:
Those five students - the ones who were looking for the Hidden Master - they went up to the front lines, alone. I'd send Shado-Pan to aid them, but I haven't got any left.

There's dangerous creatures up there near the wall. If you find those students, make sure that they haven't fallen to any of them.

passages.title: Students No More
passages.text:
They can't keep fighting like this forever. Those kids are downright heroic, but I don't want them to die as heroes.

It's time to throw in the towel.

passages.title: Retreat!
passages.text:
I'm going to withdraw what few forces I have. We may have to fall back to the Stormstout Brewery, or even Halfhill. That call is Commander Loon Mai's to make.

You go ahead. Deliver word to the Commander. My Shado-Pan will be shortly behind.

passages.title: Retreat!
passages.text:
I see.

Well, we gave it our all. It's time to evacuate, save lives, and reassess our strategy, before these mantid take over the entire valley.

passages.title: The Savior of Stoneplow
passages.text:
That commander speaks hastily. He has the weapon he needs to win this battle. He has YOU.

"But it's too hard," you might say.

You would be wrong. It is not too hard. NOTHING IS TOO HARD.

Go now, <name>. Go, and save Stoneplow!

passages.title: The Savior of Stoneplow
passages.text: All is lost, <name>. Pack up your things. We're headed to Halfhill.

passages.title: The Savior of Stoneplow
passages.text:
I can't believe it! You - a foreign-born <race> - have succeeded where the Shado-Pan have failed. You've succeeded where the WALL has failed.

We may hold this farming village after all.

passages.title: The Gratitude of Stoneplow
passages.text:
One last thing, <name>. Don't worry, it's not another favor. You've killed enough mantid today.

We recently received a shipment of high-quality armor from Kun-Lai Summit. I was planning to keep them for my men... but I can't think of anybody more deserving than you. You'll find them on the second floor of the inn, here in town.

passages.title: The Gratitude of Stoneplow
passages.text: Peering inside, you find...

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text:
Oh, well now, let's have us some fun, <boyo/girly>!

Those Ordo yaungol to the northwest have saved us the trouble o' havin' to make some bombs. They already have them there.

Let's put their explosive barrels to good use and destroy their oil-pumpin' machines, shall we?

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text: Ho ho, that were a fine sight to see. I knew I should have gone up there with ya, <name>!

passages.title: It Does You No Good In The Keg
passages.text:
I been thinkin'.

We got all this beer that Chen brewed, and we got all these people that you've gathered. We should bring the two together.

There's a bunch o' folks out there in the fields, riskin' their lives for Pandaria. You an' I should at least bring 'em a keg or two.

They might raise their mugs in victory. They might enjoy one last drink before gettin' skivvered by a mantid. Either way, I wouldn't want 'em to fight without a good brew in their belly.

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text:
I love blowing stuff up. It's in my blood!

The yaungol to the west at Fire Camp Ordo have a ton of explosive barrels just lying around.

I say we put them to good use and destroy their oil-pumpin' machines while having some fun!

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text: Um, I don't think the job's done yet.

passages.title: Barrels of Fun
passages.text: You can't tell me that wasn't fun, <name>! I knew I should have gone over there with you!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text: <The shield is down. Time to head into the cave and slay the Warbringer of the Ordo yaungol!>

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
You've done it, <name>! I'm in your debt!

Again!

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text: <The shield is down. Time to head into the cave and slay the Warbringer of the Ordo!>

passages.title: The Ordo Warbringer
passages.text:
Once again you've accomplished what no one else could.

Was there any doubt?

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
I can't believe you made it here!

I don't know how much longer I could have stayed hidden in here.

I'm sure that there are others. <class>, we have to rescue them! Then we can go to Shado-Pan Fallback. The master there will know what to do!

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text: There are survivors out there? Surely there are more, <name>?

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
We didn't know that there were any survivors out there.

Thank you for bringing them to safety, <name>.

passages.title: Unmasking the Yaungol
passages.text:
Simply killing Kobai will accomplish nothing, as he is possessed by a particularly powerful and destructive Sha - Malevolent Fury.

You will use the trap I have fashioned from the Blinding Rage Essences you brought. Lure him into the trap, and then steal his mask. Once you put it on, Malevolent Fury will appear and attempt to take control of you.

Defeat him, and we will have made a victory of this tragic situation. You can find him to the north of the retreat, where he taunts us in insane rage.

passages.title: Unmasking the Yaungol
passages.text: Is Malevolent Fury gone?

passages.title: Unmasking the Yaungol
passages.text:
I should feel shame at the loss of the village. I should feel great pride in your success. 

I should feel many things, but must not allow myself to. Until our struggle with the sha is complete, we must maintain total control of our emotions.

passages.title: Tread Lightly
passages.text:
My students tell me the surrounding area is littered with deadly traps, no doubt set by the saurok. Stumbling into one gets you a face full of spikes.

As the saying goes: "The Way is rife with danger - tread lightly, and with scrutiny."

<Koro hands you a long tree branch.>

Here, this is scrutiny.

It should be long enough to set the traps off at a safe distance.

passages.title: Tread Lightly
passages.text: Well, I don't see any spikes in your face. That's a good sign.

passages.title: Tread Lightly
passages.text: Every trap you sprang is a life saved, be it pandaren, beast, or otherwise. Nobody deserves an honorless death like that.

passages.title: Ahead on the Way
passages.text:
Huge maws of despair are spewing out sha from the pagodas on either side of the temple. Meanwhile, your impromptu training in the Way continues.

"She who mends torn umbrella will be more dry than she who strikes at rain."

While I take issue with that particular lesson--sometimes punching the rain can be quite effective--the meaning holds true in this case.

Take out those maws of despair and give my order a chance at reclaiming the temple grounds.

passages.title: Ahead on the Way
passages.text: Koro said there's a pagoda on either side of the temple. Let's find them and wipe out the sha presence in both.

passages.title: Ahead on the Way
passages.text: Koro's metaphors can get a little tiring, but there's always true wisdom behind them.

passages.title: A Line Unbroken
passages.text:
When we regrouped after their initial attack, we numbered three less. You can fight, and we must plan our defense should these cursed yaungol attack again. 

If you would help us, grant our fallen comrades their last rites, and recover their armor. You will find their bodies to the west, near the gate.

And try to keep the birds off them.

passages.title: A Line Unbroken
passages.text: Our comrades, are they at rest?

passages.title: A Line Unbroken
passages.text: Good. I will see to it that the armor is returned to their pupils.

passages.title: To the Wall!
passages.text:
They are attacking again!

<Lin looks to the Ox Gate.>

Archers... on the wall!

I need you to get up there. My wife Suna went to scout the wall with that fool Lao-Chen. Perhaps if he had spent more time preparing defenses and less building that ridiculous ale lift contraption...

It matters not. Get a kite from Len, to the west, and then get up there and find my wife. She'll know what to do next.

passages.title: To the Wall!
passages.text:
Wow, that was quite a bit of kite-flying there. Good job getting up here and not dying.

It's good you're here, too. Lao-chen's got an idea he's working on, but in the meantime we've got yaungol to deal with.

passages.title: Unbelievable!
passages.text:
I simply refuse to believe the guards will not grant us entry to the monastery should we impress upon them the seriousness of the situation.

Friend, go east, to the sentinel in front of the Monastery, and demand admittance. I will come with you.

passages.title: Unbelievable!
passages.text: Unbelievable!

passages.title: Unbelievable!
passages.text: No... this is worse than I could have possibly imagined. The monastery itself has been compromised...

passages.title: Ranger Rescue
passages.text:
I must ask a most important task of you, <name>.

Somewhere among the cages in the Osul camp is my husband, Lin. He is the light of my world.

Please find him and return him to me, and save as many of our fellow Shado-Pan as you can as well.

You should find keys to those cages on the Osul Marauders.

passages.title: Ranger Rescue
passages.text: How did it go?

passages.title: Ranger Rescue
passages.text:
I am truly sorry to hear that Lin did not make it.

Suna is taking the news quite hard. She will forgive me in time.

As for the rest of the Shado-Pan that you saved, well, I am very grateful to see them returned safe and sound.

passages.title: Jung Duk
passages.text:
THIS. IS. WAR.

I will have the heads of everyone who took Lin from me. EVERYONE!

We will begin with the Osul leader, Jung Duk.

Take this Shado-Pan war banner and place it at the center of their camp.

Jung Duk will have no choice but to face you.

Show him no mercy, <name>.

passages.title: Jung Duk
passages.text: Jung Duk's legacy is written in the blood of innocents.

passages.title: Jung Duk
passages.text:
Jung Duk is dead at last.

Hundreds, perhaps thousands, lost their lives due to his violent aggression.

Though they are not here to witness his demise, they owe deep gratitude to your bravery today.

passages.title: Hatred Becomes Us
passages.text:
I should have suspected a sha presence earlier!

We are safe as long as we stand inside the Totem of Harmony's protective wards, but many of our people were not so lucky.

They were trapped outside the camp when the sha's powers manifested, and now they turn upon each other!

Take one of my totems with you. Place the totem near a crazed ally to purify them, but beware.

You may have to face the darkness that gripped them.

passages.title: Hatred Becomes Us
passages.text: Our people are possessed by hatred. We must help them come to their senses!

passages.title: Hatred Becomes Us
passages.text:
Thank you.

The sha preys upon the weak and the vulnerable.

If we are not vigilant, even the strongest of us can succumb to the sha's dark influence.

passages.title: What Lies Beneath
passages.text:
If my suspicions are correct, this place still reels from some lingering darkness.

Whatever happened here... it could not have been the natural course of events.

Even the yaungol are not so brutal as to slaughter their own kind to the point of... this.

I will use the totems that you brought me to perform a cleansing ritual.

I need someone to assist me in the ceremony. Let me know when you are ready.

passages.title: What Lies Beneath
passages.text: I believe that we must drive the taint from this place.

passages.title: What Lies Beneath
passages.text:
We look upon the true face of hatred!

Now it all makes sense. This is the work of the sha.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
Normally, it only takes a few scouts to hold this pass. Most of this territory is in sight of the wall, so archers would devastate any mantid force attempting to push through here. The problem is, most of the archers are occupied with the onslaught at the gate.

Take this flare - it will help you locate the mantid that are sneaking through the eastern pass under our diminished watch. Kill any you find. We can't let them lay a trail that might lead the mantid swarms farther into the steppes.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
The defenders on the wall are stretched thin. The Yaungol are pushing through the gates to Kun-Lai in the north. The mantid are pouring against the gates to the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. I hear that there's been a breach into the Valley of Four Winds in the south too.

We do not have the men to combat all of these threats.

passages.title: Breach in the Defenses
passages.text:
There are more getting through than I thought. I may need to stay here and clean up a while.

You've done more than your part though, <class>. Thank you.

passages.title: The Restless Watch
passages.text:
I'm being told that our scouts have been on duty in Shallowstep Pass for more than 2 days straight, no rest. No wonder mantid are slipping through. Even the most dedicated scouts would slip with those kinds of shifts.

I want you to go out there and deliver orders to the scouts that they are to return to the battlefront immediately for rest and rations. I'll arrange for a new shift to be posted.

passages.title: The Restless Watch
passages.text: This whole battlefront is being worked to the bone. We need more men out here.

passages.title: The Restless Watch
passages.text: Thank you. I'll have the new scouts at their posts shortly.

passages.title: Joining the Fight
passages.text: Lao-Chin's archers will need these arrows down at the bridge. Can you bring them?

passages.title: Joining the Fight
passages.text: Welcome to the mess.

passages.title: Joining the Fight
passages.text:
Taran Zhu told me what became of my camp. I would have stopped it if I could, but the attacks from the bridge have not let up.

Thank you for bringing these arrows - my archers will make good use of them.

passages.title: The Taking of Dusklight Bridge
passages.text:
Let's press these insects back across the bridge and break their spirits!

Follow my lead.

passages.title: The Taking of Dusklight Bridge
passages.text: The mantid aren't likely to return soon after a beating like that... and now Lao-Chin is free to join us in the hunt.

passages.title: Heroes of the Shado-Pan
passages.text: You said that Taran Zhu is in Townlong and was asking for me? Must be something important...

passages.title: Heroes of the Shado-Pan
passages.text: I like that I can always depend on you. You have the spirit of a true Shado-Pan.

passages.title: Do a Barrel Roll!
passages.text:
When I trained as a Brewmaster, I didn't expect to use my knowledge like this...

Did you know beer catches fire when lit? Well, with yaungol oil mixed in, it's downright explosive.

I've mixed the oil in with these kegs. Roll them at the yaungol over by the gate, and ignite them when you get close. 

It'll take a few seconds for the keg to blow, but when it does...

Well, let's just say I wouldn't want to be over there.

Which is why I'll be over here. Mourning the loss of this brew.

passages.title: Do a Barrel Roll!
passages.text: Wha? I was just thinking about my poor, poor beer...

passages.title: Do a Barrel Roll!
passages.text:
Whoo, that was an explosion! Several, in fact.

Sad my beer had to go, but at least we're safe, for now.

passages.title: Where are My Reinforcements?
passages.text:
This has simply gone too far. I cannot ignore our abandonment any longer.

After all that's happened here, and all you've been through in Firebough, we must travel to the monastery.

Whatever they are doing in there can wait! We can take my balloon up the mountain to the Monastery. It's anchored back by the camp, to the northeast.

passages.title: Where are My Reinforcements?
passages.text: Here we are, then.

passages.title: Where are My Reinforcements?
passages.text: Here we are, and now you know why we cannot let our brothers sit idly by.

passages.title: Lao-Chin's Gambit
passages.text:
Alright. Thanks to you, we have the wall under control. Good job. 

I'll stay up here for a little while and make sure no more yaungol get up onto the wall.

You, though, should go back down and see what Lao-Chin has cooked up. I hate to say it, but maybe he had a good idea after all...

passages.title: Lao-Chin's Gambit
passages.text: Ah, hello again. As sad as I am to have to do this, I'm glad I came up with something.

passages.title: Lao-Chin's Gambit
passages.text: Good to see you made it back in one piece. Thanks to your help with the barrels, I've managed to brew up a good surprise for our yaungol friends at the front.

passages.title: Falling Down
passages.text:
It's bad enough trying to hold off the mantid, but now we've got spiders swarming up from the ruins below.

One of my best marksmen caught a blast of webbing around his leg and got pulled straight down!

We think he's alive, but I don't have the manpower to send anyone in after him. We're stretched thin up here, <class>.

If you want to help, use the rope behind me to drop down into the ruins. You're not afraid of heights are you?

How about spiders?

passages.title: Falling Down
passages.text:
The fall wasn't that bad, actually. I've always had a knack for soft landings.

That I landed on a pile of spider corpses probably helped, too.

passages.title: Nope
passages.text:
We're holding, but just barely. Anything you can do to stem the tide of dreadspinners coming up the wall would be a big help.

Feel like tearing open spider eggs one at a time by hand?

I didn't think so. Take one of our dragon guns and light it up down there. I wanna hear those puppies pop.

passages.title: Nope
passages.text: Hey, help me out here!

passages.title: Nope
passages.text: Nice work with that dragon gun. I did what I could down here, but arrows are only so useful against these things.

passages.title: Preserved in Amber
passages.text:
Take... this...

<The dying mantid struggles to outstretch his arm. In his mangled grasp rests a metal fork with two long, thin prongs and an ornately jeweled handle.>

Awaken... the Wind-Reaver...

It is the only way... to end the swarm.

passages.title: Preserved in Amber
passages.text: The Klaxxi... call to me.

passages.title: Wakening Sickness
passages.text:
You will forgive my current state. I have slept for many years.

A Klaxxi'va should have been here to attend my Wakening with kypari sap... but you will have to do.

I sense the buzzing of sapflies to the south. They gorge on the nourishing sap I need. Bring them to me.

passages.title: Wakening Sickness
passages.text: Without nourishment, I will die where I stand.

passages.title: Wakening Sickness
passages.text: This will do.

passages.title: The Klaxxi Council
passages.text:
I must report to the Klaxxi. They would not have woken me unless the situation were dire.

You have not been entirely useless. For that, I will spare your life.

The council may even find a use for you.

passages.title: The Klaxxi Council
passages.text:
This is a sacred meeting place for the Klaxxi.

It would be wise of you to let me do the talking.

passages.title: The Dread Clutches
passages.text:
The imperial clutches have become an abomination! Clutch-Keepers rush the development of new swarmborn, saturating them in this vile "sha" energy before sending them away to the wall.

The Klaxxi wish to stem the tide of swarmborn production in these dread clutches. Put the keepers to death!

passages.title: The Dread Clutches
passages.text: A few less traitors for us to feed to the kunchong when the dust settles.

passages.title: Amber Arms
passages.text:
You! Filth!

You work for me now!

The amber blades of the Shek'zeer Bladesworn are the finest weapons in the empire.

If you are not impaled upon them immediately after leaving here, bring me as many of the blades as you can carry! I want to make sure we have weapons in reserve, should we need them.

passages.title: Amber Arms
passages.text: The bladesworn carry their swords with pride. I want them on my weapon racks!

passages.title: Amber Arms
passages.text: If all goes as planned, the Klaxxi will stop the Empress without your help. Still, it is my role to be prepared.

passages.title: Dead Zone
passages.text:
A Klaxxi'va whispers to the tower. It carries their whisper far; to other towers, to mantid, to paragons. The whisper bounces back, and the Klaxxi hear it.

This way, they see all.

A tower near the palace is quiet. This will not do. It must sing for the Klaxxi.

It is my job to fix the tower, but if you serve the Klaxxi, you should serve me as well. You fix the tower, and I will wait here!

passages.title: In Her Clutch
passages.text:
The crystal sings to the Klaxxi. They sense a paragon in the clutch, east of the tower.

Clutch-keepers are trying to pollute this one. the Klaxxi will not permit this.

Go and find the paragon. Place your hands on his chamber, and the Klaxxi will channel their whispers through you to break him free. Protect him if you can.

passages.title: In Her Clutch
passages.text:
My slumber was interrupted by sudden dreams. Unspeakable nightmares.

Then I awoke.

The Klaxxi have spoken to me. I have my orders. There is much to be done.

passages.title: Amber Is Life
passages.text:
In order for our efforts against the mantid empire to continue, we require more amber.

There is a great deposit of amber underneath the lake to the south, but the area is inhabited by a savage saurok tribe.

I cannot spare anyone else. You must go to the lake and test the tribe's strength. Thin their numbers and eliminate their leader, who is probably hiding in his underground cavern.

Surely this is not too great a task for you?

passages.title: Amber Is Life
passages.text: The amber looks familiar for some reason...

passages.title: Amber Is Life
passages.text:
The whispers seem to be emanating from within this amber.

Could there be another paragon sleeping within?

passages.title: Living Amber
passages.text:
Liquid amber is most efficient for restoring a newly awakened paragon's strength, and is usually provided at a wakening ceremony.

Unfortunately, it seems you did not receive these instructions, so we shall have to improvise.

I can sense a vast quantity of fossilized amber in the lake below us. It will serve, but I am too weak to dig it up myself.

Do this for me, and I will see to it that you are rewarded.

passages.title: Living Amber
passages.text: Do you understand, Wakener? The amber gives life.

passages.title: Living Amber
passages.text: Thank you, Wakener. That is enough for now.

passages.title: Kypari Zar
passages.text:
What is that tree on the hill to the west? Can it be... Kypari Zar?

<Korven the Prime lapses into silence.>

When I returned from my final ravage, before being elevated to a paragon, I was given the honor of planting that very tree.

I see it has grown into a great kypari, but... it seems something is amiss.

There is an old sonar tower at the base of the tree. Take me there, Wakener. I can use the tower to take a closer look.

passages.title: Kypari Zar
passages.text: What has happened to our home? Things feel amiss.

passages.title: Kypari Zar
passages.text: Once, great rivers of amber coursed through this tree's veins. Now, it is but a dried husk.

passages.title: The Root of the Problem
passages.text:
Kypari Zar is dying.

A creature of terrible darkness corrupts it from deep beneath its roots.

The tree cannot be saved, but at least we can lessen its pain.

Look. The vile creature has carved a path to its own lair. We need only follow it down the hill, just behind this tower.

passages.title: The Root of the Problem
passages.text: The swarm knows not of their terrible folly! These precious trees must be protected at all costs!

passages.title: The Root of the Problem
passages.text:
Thank you, Wakener. Kypari Zar can now dream in peace.

However, the beast was merely a vessel for the corruption.

No... the true corruption lies much deeper.

passages.title: A Cry From Darkness
passages.text:
So, you survived the imperial clutches. You are... resilient.

The Klaxxi hear another paragon to the north, among the sha-scorched roots of Kypari Vor.

This one cries out in terror and agony. It cannot be saved.

The Klaxxi want him put down. Go and defeat him or do not return here.

passages.title: A Cry From Darkness
passages.text: The order stands. Slay the fallen paragon.

passages.title: A Cry From Darkness
passages.text:
What?! How did you...

The Deathcaller was a legendary hero. He must not have been fully wakened.

You are fortunate.

passages.title: Sacred Recipe
passages.text:
"When the horror comes a-rising
And the heavens hum with war
Our great vessel of salvation
Must be broken from its core."

The scroll continues on for several stanzas. Perhaps somebody at The Sunset Brewgarden will be able to decipher its cryptic message.

passages.title: Sacred Recipe
passages.text:
Is that some sort of scroll?

Would you mind if I took a look?

passages.title: Sacred Recipe
passages.text:
<Lya reads the entirety of the message.>

This scroll, this... this prophecy...

It's terrifying!

passages.title: Bound With Shade
passages.text:
About that scroll you found...

I keep looking at that line in the second stanza - "bound with wood and shade". The "shade", in particular, intrigues me.

I must admit, I've often considered taking some of the area's residual sha essence and incorporating it into a brew. I suspect that this is the shade which our recipe calls for.

You will find large amalgamations of sha to the southeast of our tree... though you may also be able to harvest some from the local wildlife.

passages.title: Bound With Shade
passages.text:
Beautiful. This will make a fine addition to our brew.

The most dangerous ingredients are quite often the most delicious.

passages.title: I Bring Us Great Shame
passages.text:
I have failed my fellow brewers.

I took some supplies out to the clearing, east of our tree... and I left them there. Now, with the sha corrupting the land, and the mantid on the prowl, it is too dangerous for me to bring them back.

If you would help me look for them, perhaps I could regain some of my lost honor.

passages.title: I Bring Us Great Shame
passages.text: Did you find them? Can it be?

passages.title: I Bring Us Great Shame
passages.text: You have brought me joy, traveler.

passages.title: Rending Daggers
passages.text:
Forget about them, and forget their BREW. We've got real work to do.

The scroll mentions "rending daggers of the great ones". I've got a feeling I know where to find them.

A pair of mantid lieutenants patrol the Horrid March, to the south. Each one carries a ceremonial dagger.

Bring those daggers back here, <name>. We may be on the brink of something big.

passages.title: Rending Daggers
passages.text:
I think I'm starting to understand the next few lines of this prophecy, <name>.

Do you have the daggers yet?

passages.title: Rending Daggers
passages.text:
These daggers, look!

<Lya holds the blades hilt-to-hilt.>

They were built to fit together! But how to join them...?

passages.title: Evie Stormstout
passages.text:
I was too late. She was so small... and I was too late.

She should be given a proper burial. A little warrior like her deserves better than this.

passages.title: Evie Stormstout
passages.text: <Chen is in mourning.>

passages.title: Evie Stormstout
passages.text: <Chen is, for the moment, silent.>

passages.title: The Horror Comes A-Rising
passages.text:
We are protected from the mantid. Such was the agreement made so many millennia ago.

There are forces from which we are not safe, however. The kyparites beneath the ground to the west will haunt us, chase us... even eat us. The mistlurkers eat our kind by the handful.

Help our people, outsider. Defeat our enemies.

passages.title: The Horror Comes A-Rising
passages.text: We hate being eaten.

passages.title: The Horror Comes A-Rising
passages.text:
It is good to have someone of your colossal size in our village.

You have many uses.

passages.title: Fiery Wings
passages.text:
I think that old paper said something about "fiery wings." Those little dragons around here have wings. They're kind of fiery, in a way.

You're quicker than me. Try catching some of those dragons... or at least slapping the powder off of them.

No point in killing a harmless little dragon, if all you want is the sparkle from their wings.

passages.title: Fiery Wings
passages.text: I haven't been able to catch any of those things!

passages.title: Fiery Wings
passages.text:
YEAH!!! FLITTERLING DUST!!!

<Olon throws the powder into the pot.>

This brew is turning out... strange, and pretty smelly. I'm starting to think maybe Lya was right.

passages.title: Great Vessel of Salvation
passages.text:
I know what you and the girl-panda seek. We can perform the rite for you... in time.

First, I require aid. The seeds fall from our great mother-tree. It is our responsibility to collect them, even in dangerous times like these.

Escort my chanters to the motherseeds, that they may bring them back to the collection pit.

passages.title: Great Vessel of Salvation
passages.text: The collection pit is down the hill, just to the west of here.

passages.title: Great Vessel of Salvation
passages.text:
Yes, good. The motherseeds are taken care of.

Now, we may speak of your enchantment.

passages.title: Fires and Fears of Old
passages.text:
We've found the blades, bound them together with wood and shade, and blessed them with an ancient incantation. If I'm not mistaken, it's time to use this thing.

The sprites spoke of an ancient piece of sap within the Amber Hibernal, a mantid cave near their empress' palace. That must be the "Blood of Ancients" that the prophecy spoke of.

Whatever's inside that sap must be important. Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Fires and Fears of Old
passages.text: Make sure to bring that forked blade with you.

passages.title: Fires and Fears of Old
passages.text:
There was a... a mantid inside that amber? I never would have thought that the solution to our war on the mantid would be... another mantid.

There are still many things that I have left to learn, but I do know this: that CERTAINLY wasn't a beer recipe.

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text:
The Klaxxi'va hear another paragon. His cries are weak and lost in darkness. The signal must be strengthened.

There is a tower in Amberglow Hollow that has been silent for many years. It must sing; The Klaxxi demand it!

This time I will go with you. You will help me repair it.

Take the resonating crystal and meet me in Amberglow.

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text: Why are you just standing here?

passages.title: Extending Our Coverage
passages.text:
It is good you showed up when you did.

Perhaps you are not as useless as I thought...

The Klaxxi'va sing to the paragon now. Soon they will know where to send you. For now there are other tasks.

passages.title: Crime and Punishment
passages.text:
The Stinging Trail nurtures young Kypari trees. The empress drains the saplings too early, outsider. They must grow before the amber can be taken.

The Klaxxi'va demand punishment for this crime! It will please them if you rain death on the Ik'thik harvesters.

passages.title: Crime and Punishment
passages.text: The Klaxxi are pleased with our work, outsider. You have proven to be more resourceful than we thought.

passages.title: By the Sea, Nevermore
passages.text:
The Klaxxi'va have spoken to me, outsider. The paragon is hidden in the Briny Muck only, he is not so hidden anymore.

The lizard men surround him. He cannot fall into their scaly hands.

You will find him; you will awaken him. Do not return without him!

If you do this The Klaxxi will be pleased with us.

passages.title: By the Sea, Nevermore
passages.text:
What... what sort of creature are you?

How have you awoken me?

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text:
It is a crime to harvest the young trees, but a much bigger crime to waste the amber.

Young amber is not as strong, but the Klaxxi need it to continue the fight. We will bring them more and they will sing my praises!

Gather the young amber. We will store it until it is aged and can be consumed.

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text: I would go with you to gather amber, but my talents are more useful here.

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text:
Even this raw amber will be of use. We can't afford to be picky in times like these.

The Klaxxi'va will be glad I thought of this. I will tell them you helped!

passages.title: Reunited
passages.text:
You look at me and see I am no great warrior. Why was I chosen to be a Paragon? Not all weapons can be seen, Wakener. One should not judge by appearance alone.

Before I explain further, I need to know that you are trustworthy.

Something precious to me was hidden at the time of my preservation. I am nothing without it.

Defend me as I unearth my greatest weapon, and you will have my trust.

passages.title: Reunited
passages.text: Kovok is just as impressive as the last time I saw him. He will ensure great victories for the Klaxxi.

passages.title: Feed or Be Eaten
passages.text:
After years of working with the Kunchong I developed a theory; raising one from infancy would strengthen the bond and therefore strengthen the sonic connection.

I had just begun training Kovok when I was chosen for encasement. He is still very young and will need diligent training to reach his full potential.

I'm entrusting Kovok to you, but be warned; if any harm comes to him your life is forfeit.

First, you must feed him to gain his trust. The turtles in the area should be suitable for this.

passages.title: Feed or Be Eaten
passages.text: Once the bond is formed a Kunchong will gladly give its life for you.

passages.title: Feed or Be Eaten
passages.text:
Very good! I had half expected Kovok to just eat you. What a pleasant surprise to see you both in one piece,

Perhaps Kunchong raising is in your blood.

passages.title: Concentrated Fear
passages.text:
Amber is power. It brings life.

This... dread amber you brought me has been twisted. It is concentrated fear.

The Vor'thik know this well. Their kypari has been completely engulfed by sha, and they use the dread amber to quicken their own swarmborn.

Bring me the crystals used by the Vor'thik fear-shapers in their rituals. The Klaxxi will study them and decide on a protocol for disposal.

passages.title: Concentrated Fear
passages.text: Do you have the crystals?

passages.title: Concentrated Fear
passages.text: What would happen, I wonder, if you ate one? What would it do to your soft, pink insides?

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text:
adventurer! It is so great to see you healthy, and traveling so far. It would seem that our paths are quite tightly intertwined.

I'm here looking for my family. I am told that several Stormstouts came across the wall to help face the mantid threat. I mean to find them, and join them.

Have you seen anyone named Stormstout come through here? Would you mind helping me ask around?

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text: You are brave to have come across the wall, tauren.

passages.title: Fate of the Stormstouts
passages.text:
<Chen listens intently.>

Big Dan, Han, Evie, and Mama. I understand.

It seems like Dan will be safe here. I will go look for Evie, Han, and Mama Stormstout.

Take care, <name>.

passages.title: A Visit with Lorewalker Cho
passages.text:
Stranger, I may be able to help you find your prince. But first, I would like to know a little more about you and your people.

Come, help me with my chores, and we will chat.

You have the look of a grizzled war veteran, but certainly you have a few minutes to help a bookish Pandaren like myself putter around the house, yes?

passages.title: A Visit with Lorewalker Cho
passages.text: There is nothing like a little manual labor to bring strangers together, don't you think?

passages.title: A Visit with Lorewalker Cho
passages.text:
Despite your many years of combat, you've still got an eye for beauty, <name>. I like that about you!

Now, let's find this missing prince of yours.

passages.title: Kor'thik Aggression
passages.text:
I'm no brewer - just looking at all those heaps of ingredients makes my head spin. Just put the brew in front of me when it's finished, thank you.

No, I'm here to make sure that the brewers don't get cut in half while they're trying to make that perfect brew. It's not an easy job.

The Kor'thik mantid across this basin have been attacking us nightly. If you're already heading over there, why don't you return the favor and attack a few of them?

passages.title: Kor'thik Aggression
passages.text: You've got the makings of a fine brewgarden guard, <race>. Let me know if you ever get tired of the whole "<class>" thing.

passages.title: Skeer the Bloodseeker
passages.text:
Our efforts to secure the shallows before Zan'vess have paid off.

We have spotted another paragon buried in amber, hidden in the waters to the southwest.

Adding another paragon to our numbers is vital. Another champion from ages past could turn the tide in our favor.

I would go immediately, but unfortunately, I am needed here.

Since you are already a Wakener, you can carry out this task in my stead.

passages.title: Skeer the Bloodseeker
passages.text:
The hunger... they said it would be fierce, but I did not expect anything like this.

It is strange to feel so... weak.

passages.title: A Bloody Delight
passages.text:
A warrior is not ready for battle until he tastes the blood of his enemies.

I am still too weak to hunt, so you must go in my stead.

Only the blood from the fiercest predators will do. I can smell their presence in the waters outside this cave!

Bring this to me, and then perhaps you shall see why they call me the Bloodseeker.

passages.title: A Bloody Delight
passages.text: By drinking the blood of your enemies, you acquire their strength.

passages.title: A Bloody Delight
passages.text: Yes, this will do.

passages.title: The Scent of Blood
passages.text:
I'm afraid that I wet my hands with saurok blood while you were away.

I'm sorry, but I could not help myself. Now, watch them attack me.

Pitiful!

Do they think to take vengeance for their fallen? Do they come challenge ME?

I, who have won a hundred wars? I, who stood alone against thousands and still shouted for my enemies to come?

No, these... saurok... will crumple before me like paper before the flame!

I shall show you my might, Wakener. Fight alongside me and see.

Here they come!

passages.title: The Scent of Blood
passages.text: You have succeeded once again. Well done, Wakener.

passages.title: Fresh Pots
passages.text:
We got a load of empty crab pots out there that need fresh bait.

Now, we COULD pull them one at a time and bait them up here in comfort. A nice chair to sit on, maybe a hot cup of tea to keep you warm. Sounds nice, doesn't it?

Never gonna happen.

Head to Lonesome Cove, immediately southeast, and bait those pots with two chunks of fresh sea monarch. By "fresh" I mean killed right there in the water.

Oh, and by "pots" I mean traps. If you wanna be part of the crew, you'd better learn the lingo.

passages.title: Fresh Pots
