passages.text: What's wrong, green? You aren't afraid of the dark, icy sea are you?

passages.title: Fresh Pots
passages.text: Not bad, green, not bad.

passages.title: You Otter Know
passages.text:
You know what happened to the bait in those pots?

Otters. That's what happened.

They prefer fresh clams, but they'll pick our crab traps clean if they're hungry enough.

The otters in Lonesome Cove are protected by law and we run a legitimate operation here. As much as I'd love to chum those little rats and call it a day, we just make sure they aren't hungry enough to raid the crab pots.

Toss 'em a few clams to keep them busy while you're out there.

passages.title: You Otter Know
passages.text: In the words of my old deck boss: "Do what I say, 'cause I said it!"

passages.title: You Otter Know
passages.text: That should keep their little whiskers out of our traps for awhile.

passages.title: Walking Dog
passages.text:
Dog ain't my "pet." He's a member of this crew, and my best friend. Saved my life more than once, you know.

But I'm gettin' too old to walk him anymore, and he still needs his exercise. Take Dog for a trip around the shelf for me, would ya?

He loves to swim through the hot geysers just southeast of the shallows.

He absolutely has to... er... "leave his mark" on the dead whale at the far western edge of the shelf.

Oh, and he'll want to visit our old shipwreck, too. He likes to reminisce.

passages.title: Walking Dog
passages.text: How did it go? I hope he didn't cause too much trouble!

passages.title: On the Crab
passages.text:
I just got word that a string of pots we dropped this morning hit it BIG. We're on the crab!

Problem is, the rips are getting stronger and we lost track of some of the pots. They're just sitting out there, filled with spiky blue GOLD!

I need you back out there. Hook one of these buoys up to any of the full traps you find and send it to the surface for us.

passages.title: On the Crab
passages.text: Nice work out there!

passages.title: Shark Week
passages.text:
Crabbing is our big money-maker, but we send all kinds of goods back around the wall. Oils, plants, even rare minerals - the sea's bounty is rich out here!

Right now the big craze in the markets back home is thresher teeth. Apparently they make great necklaces?

Threshers are all over the Shelf of Mazu to the west. Bring me lots of teeth!

passages.title: Shark Week
passages.text: Having actually seen someone eaten by a thresher, I'm not sure why you'd willingly string their teeth around your neck, but whatever.

passages.title: Shark Week
passages.text: Those are perfect, just put them down over there. I'd rather not touch them myself. Creeps me out.

passages.title: The Mariner's Revenge
passages.text:
I'm not gonna sit in a damn rocking chair while my crew gets devoured by a leviathan!

Come on, let's get to the dock and launch a dinghy. I got a special one set up just for this kind of situation. My own little Mist-Hopper Jr.

We'll give that thing a case of harpoon fever.

passages.title: The Mariner's Revenge
passages.text: Let's go!

passages.title: The Mariner's Revenge
passages.text:
Nice shooting out there!

I knew we could do it. Never met anything that can't be killed with enough harpoons.

passages.title: Welcome to Dawn's Blossom
passages.text:
Cho's off on another one of his adventures, and this one requires a big order of jade. I'm going to have to call in some favors.

How 'bout in the meantime you introduce yourself to some of the locals.

Kai Wanderbrew is a good guy to know, as is Master Windfur. Oh, and say hi to Peiji Goldendraft up at the inn.

Between the three of them, you should get the feel for life in Dawn's Blossom.

passages.title: Welcome to Dawn's Blossom
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Welcome to Dawn's Blossom
passages.text: Good, good, good. You're going to fit right in.

passages.title: Wicked Wikkets
passages.text:
<name> good wikket, they say...

<name> help hozen, they say...

No more grookin' <name>, they say.

That ok. Look out there. Wicked wikkets fallin' like rain, ripe for the grookin'!

Go, join the fun. But remember, Chief Kah Kah gets all the shinies! That's hozen rule number two.

<Jeek Jeek scratches his head.>

Hmm, all hozen rules are number two...

passages.title: Wicked Wikkets
passages.text: Whatcha got, wikket?

passages.title: Wicked Wikkets
passages.text:
Wikket grookin' makin' hozen rich with shinies!

<name> makin' a good second impression. And for hozen, number two is most important!

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text:
Lok'tar, <class>.

We've made progress, but we're going to need mobility if we want to maintain our foothold here in Kun-Lai.

I don't see many worgs, kodo, or the like around here. What I do see are yaks. Our pandaren allies have said they make good mounts, so they'll have to do.

Go round some up and return them here, so we can get our people riding them!

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: The yaks?

passages.title: Round 'Em Up
passages.text: Well done! Well, they're plenty stubborn, I'll say that much. But they should do nicely.

passages.title: The Kunchong Whisperer
passages.text:
To really connect with Kovok you need to challenge him mentally and physically. You must respect his strength and intelligence; only then will he allow you to really train him.

The muckscale tribe may provide an adequate test of his abilities and with you there he shouldn't be in danger.

Additionally, this will allow us to decrease their numbers in the Briny Muck.

passages.title: The Kunchong Whisperer
passages.text:
I am most impressed with your progress, Wakener. Kovok's training is coming along nicely and he seems to be fond of you.

I have no doubt that you are the best choice to assist me in training him.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
I must say, <name>, despite their skirmishes with the hozen, I've never seen the jinyu so militant.

This troubles me. We must discuss it another time, however. I have come to ask for your assistance.

The fresco, where last we spoke, is nearly unveiled. I am certain that it holds ancient wisdom - knowledge that the emperor would have us remember.

My meditations alone may not be enough to discern its meaning. Please, take this heirloom to the shrine of my ancestors. I shall require their assistance.

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text: Yes, <class>?

passages.title: Last Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
<Lorewalker Cho shudders, in spite of himself.>

The legends... they're true!

passages.title: Falling to Pieces
passages.text:
Why would the saurok have amber? More importantly, why would Oracle Hiss'ir be so protective of it?

It is unlikely this came from the heavily guarded Zan'vess, so where did it come from?

Perhaps the Klaxxi will know what to make of it.

passages.title: Falling to Pieces
passages.text: Where did you find this?

passages.title: Falling to Pieces
passages.text:
You were wise to bring this to us. This is a piece of another paragon's encasing amber.

The damage suggests the paragon may be in trouble.

I will speak with the council to decide what should be done next.

passages.title: The Shado-Pan
passages.text:
Our new recruits have spoken in hushed tones about a group of Pandaren they call the "Shado-Pan". They are apparently very strong, and secretive.

That's where you come in. Rumor is they have a base of operations to the southeast, near Firebough Nook. You should travel there as an envoy of the Alliance. Give them any help they require.

passages.title: The Shado-Pan
passages.text: Who are you? Can you fight? If so, we can use your help.

passages.title: A Source of Terrifying Power
passages.text: <The clutch-keepers seem to be using these blinding white crystals as magical foci. Peering inside, you see thick tendrils of black smoke swirling in the center. One of the workers at Klaxxi'vess may know more about this material and why it is so abundant in the wastes.>

passages.title: A Source of Terrifying Power
passages.text:
Do you have any idea what this is? It's amber!

But it is polluted with fear.

I would not expect an outsider like you to understand the consequences of this.

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text:
It is a crime to harvest the young trees, but a much bigger crime to waste the amber.

Young amber is not as strong, but the Klaxxi need it to continue the fight. We will bring them more and they will sing my praises!

Gather the young amber. We will store it until it is aged and can be consumed.

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text: I would go with you to gather amber, but my talents are more useful here.

passages.title: Better With Age
passages.text:
Even this raw amber will be of use. We can't afford to be picky in times like these.

The Klaxxi'va will be glad I thought of this. I will tell them you helped!

passages.title: By the Sea, Nevermore
passages.text:
The Klaxxi'va have spoken to me, outsider. The paragon is hidden in the Briny Muck only, he is not so hidden anymore.

The lizard men surround him. He cannot fall into their scaley hands.

You will find him; you will awaken him. Do not return without him!

If you do this The Klaxxi will be pleased with us.

passages.title: By the Sea, Nevermore
passages.text:
What... what sort of creature are you?

How have you awoken me?

passages.title: Unleash Hell
passages.text:
I will NOT let the Horde gain a foothold on these shores before we do! If you're looking to jump into the fray, I've got a spare gyrocopter for you at the end of the runway. An attack run is already programmed in, all you have to do is concentrate on shooting.

Unleash hell upon these orcs!

passages.title: Unleash Hell
passages.text: What are you waiting for?! Scorch the ground beneath them!

passages.title: Unleash Hell
passages.text: A proper welcome for the Horde to this new land!

passages.title: Touching Ground
passages.text:
Their town is burning and their men are scattered and broken. I need every available man on the ground NOW to finish them off.

Grab one of the parachutes on the edge of the ship and get down there!

passages.title: Touching Ground
passages.text: Move it!

passages.title: Touching Ground
passages.text: 'Bout time you showed up, laddy! Let's do some damage!

passages.title: The Right Tool For The Job
passages.text:
I've scouted the area and found no leads on the prince or Admiral Taylor. We need to neutralize this base quickly and continue our search elsewhere.

Operations here are being led by an orc warlock; Ga'trul. He's barricaded the dock and is trying to escape through a demonic circle.

Put that flaregun to work again and blow those barricades! I'll cover your back and move in when you reach Ga'trul.

passages.title: The Right Tool For The Job
passages.text: We will complete our mission, but right now our priority is that warlock!

passages.title: The Right Tool For The Job
passages.text: We'll catch up with him again. I'm sure of it.

passages.title: Smoke Before Fire
passages.text:
Sully scouted the Horde establishment to the north, and he reports seeing a large pile of explosives, along with a small force of demolishers. That's not to mention the demons that their warlocks have summoned.

Luckily, we came prepared. We've got air support from the Skyfire. We just need to show our pilots where to strike.

<Rell hands you a smoke flare, and gives you a knowing nod.>

passages.title: Smoke Before Fire
passages.text:
What's that you've got, lad? Some kind o' flare?

Shoot, I coulda put together a better flare'n that in half a wink, if Rell had only asked.

passages.title: Smoke Before Fire
passages.text: Me lads up in the sky bring the heat, don't they? Ha ha ha!

passages.title: Unfair Trade
passages.text:
Though we have only just met, we have a common enemy: this group called the "Horde."

Several days ago, their leader made us a trade offer. When we refused, his servants abducted several of our cubs as bargaining chips.

We have called in the Shado-Pan to help, but they are in Kun-Lai Summit, a journey of several days. Can you come to our aid?

passages.title: Unfair Trade
passages.text: Those poor, wee little cubs. Go, help 'em out, <name>. Do what's right.

passages.title: Unfair Trade
passages.text:
Aye, I seen the wee ones, too. Busted a few out on m'way up here.

Ye've done good, lad. Those cubs might have some nasty nightmares, but they'll grow up some day, thanks to you.

passages.title: Onward and Inward
passages.text:
"Sha" energy, hm? Tread carefully, <name> - there's a hidden darkness to this continent.

We'll stay behind to mop up the rest of the Horde, but we need you to continue with the main mission: the rescue of Captain Taylor, and the retrieval of Prince Anduin.

Our aerial scouts think we've found the wreckage of the flagship near Paw'don Village. Go there and report to Admiral Rogers for instructions.

You are welcome to use my gyrocopter.

passages.title: Onward and Inward
passages.text: Excellent work, <class>. I can see why you came so highly recommended.

passages.title: Paint it Red!
passages.text:
They shot out our engines and we floated here - HERE! Right in the firing line of the enemy!

You know what to do, <name>. Get below decks and man those guns!

Show these scum that they're in OUR line of fire!

passages.title: Paint it Red!
passages.text: What are you waiting for?! Get on those guns!

passages.title: Paint it Red!
passages.text:
Superior Horde firepower at its finest!

...and you did okay too I guess.

passages.title: You're Either With Us Or...
passages.text:
The assistance of the nearby village has now become a necessity, adventurer.

We will need to use the village to regroup and tend to our wounded.

Perhaps the villagers will join our cause after seeing the brutality unleashed by the alliance.

You will act as envoy for the Horde. Ensure the cooperation of their leader. Do not disappoint me!

passages.title: You're Either With Us Or...
passages.text:
Your fighting has brought about much destruction for our tiny village!

We have no interest in your war, but we will not turn your injured away.

passages.title: Seeking Zin'jun
passages.text:
Rivett claims to have seen Zin'jun abandon ship with the rest of the survivors. That means he's still out there somewhere.

We can't leave him behind. He could be injured or worse yet, captured!

Go track down Zin'jun and bring him back.

passages.title: Seeking Zin'jun
passages.text:
<Zin'Jun is grievously wounded, but senses that you're friendly.>

Monkey-tings! Everywhere dere be dese monkey-tings!

passages.title: Strongarm Tactics
passages.text:
Scouting reports from the Strongarm Airstrip are in, and I've underlined a few high-priority targets for you.

Two gnomish mechanics have been keeping Alliance gyrocopters in the air. Take out the mechanics, and the gyrocopters' numbers will dwindle.

A dwarven death knight wanders their perimeter. He's an adventurer like yourself - loosely allied and highly dangerous.

Finally, a name I recognize: Corporal Jackson Silver. He's a hero of the Alliance and a deadshot with a crossbow.

Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Strongarm Tactics
passages.text: These aren't your normal kill targets, <name>. Be on guard.

passages.title: Strongarm Tactics
passages.text: Blood and thunder, <name>. Blood and thunder.

passages.title: Choppertunity
passages.text:
I spotted some shoulder-mounted rocket launchers on the way over here.

They mighta been fireworks. I dunno. I'm just going to assume that they were shoulder-mounted rocket launchers until I'm proven wrong.

Point is, in the arms of a skilled <class> like you, they could probably take down a chopper. If you find any lying around, try pointing them at those poorly-built gyrocopters.

passages.title: Choppertunity
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Choppertunity
passages.text: I hope those ding-dongs enjoyed the party you threw for them!

passages.title: Unreliable Allies
passages.text:
We originally welcomed the Alliance as friends. Several of our villagers volunteered to help them build an airstrip. Only recently, however, did it become clear to us that they were building a war base, within shouting distance of our village.

What's worse - I fear that some villagers are being held against their will. If you find them, <class>, let them know that it is time to come home.

passages.title: Unreliable Allies
passages.text:
Although I can't understand why you chose to bring your war to our land, I can clearly see which side is more virtuous.

Thank you for your aid, <race>.

passages.title: Nazgrim's Command
passages.text:
You have a comfortable base of operations, no Alliance around for miles, and a few Horde veterans by your side. It looks like it's time to start painting this continent red.

General Nazgrim should know where to start.

passages.title: Nazgrim's Command
passages.text:
We may have won the battle against the Alliance, but we won't get any further with this many jabbering monkeys on our perimeter.

The hozen are our next target.

passages.title: Domination Point
passages.text:
Now it is time to show this new land the true strength of the Horde.

Return to the beach and light the remaining signal fire. Our fleet is waiting.

passages.title: Domination Point
passages.text: <This fire will signal the full might of the Horde invasion fleet to land on this beach, beginning Garrosh's campaign in Pandaria.>

passages.title: Lion's Landing
passages.text:
For too long the Horde has been allowed to run rampant across Azeroth. I will not see these new lands conquered by some barbaric "warchief."

Are you ready to bring Alliance justice to the shores of Pandaria?

Let us return to the landing site. Use the flare launcher to bring in the fleet proper, and begin Operation: Shieldwall.

passages.title: Lion's Landing
passages.text: <Blue sails are barely visible on the horizon - the full might of the Alliance fleet, awaiting one final signal.>

passages.title: To Mogujia
passages.text:
Throm-ka, <class>. While we were busy defending our foothold here, Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron led a research expedition north into Kun-Lai Summit.

Unfortunately, it seems they have encountered trouble.

Warchief Garrosh Hellscream has already departed to lend his assistance, but he will require additional reinforcements.

Go northward into the mountains of Kun-Lai. Speak to Tak-Tak for transportation.

passages.title: To Mogujia
passages.text: Were you sent from Domination Point?

passages.title: To Mogujia
passages.text: Well met, <class>. We are an archaeological expedition, sent to excavate these ruins. We had no idea that this area was crawling with dangerous mogu.

passages.title: Bloodlines
passages.text:
We managed to fend off the mogu wardens and their dogs, but many of the blood elves from the scouting party were not as lucky.

Many of my people are trapped inside the ruins to the north. We are devising a solution to break them out, but I believe there may be a more straightforward approach.

Go to the ruins and kill the wardens guarding each prisoner. If my intuition is correct, this will free our comrades.

passages.title: Bloodlines
passages.text: These mogu are not to be underestimated.

passages.title: Bloodlines
passages.text: We blood elves have served the Horde faithfully. Lately, I wonder what we have to gain from Garrosh's leadership.

passages.title: To Mogujia
passages.text:
The Explorers' League sent an expedition north some days ago.

We haven't heard from them since, and I'd sleep better at night knowing our folks aren't in some sort of trouble.

Last I heard, Brann Bronzebeard was heading toward Mogujia in the Kun-Lai Summit.

Find him and report back with their status. Fennie over there can give you a ride if you need one.

passages.title: To Mogujia
passages.text: These artifacts must be several thousand years old. Have ye ever seen the like?

passages.title: Bad Blood
passages.text:
The Explorers' League is here to excavate the ruins, and it's my job to protect them.

When we arrived, we found this place crawling with blood elves. Apparently,the Horde are just as interested in the mogu as we are.

This gives quite an opportunity to thin our enemies' numbers, and steal their findings, too.

Slay any blood elves you find in the ruins, and bring back whatever they are digging up.

passages.title: Bad Blood
passages.text: What are those blood elves after?

passages.title: Bad Blood
passages.text: Well done, <class>. I knew that you could get the job done.

passages.title: The Assault on Zeb'tula
passages.text:
Our scouting efforts along the coast have given us valuable intelligence about the island, <class>.

However, we will accomplish nothing if we do not advance forward onto the mainland.

I have assembled a team of our most elite aerial units to begin the attack.

I would like you to join the assault. A champion such as yourself could turn the battle in our favor at the critical moment.

When you are ready to begin the attack, speak to me.

passages.title: The Assault on Zeb'tula
passages.text: We must claim a better strategic position on the island itself.

passages.title: The Assault on Zeb'tula
passages.text:
Yes! You have done it, champion!

We will be as a tide that sweeps over this island, bringing with it a new destiny for our people. And you, hero, are at its forefront.

passages.title: Buried Secrets
passages.text:
I am told that the mogu once possessed hundreds of hidden armories full of earth-shattering weapons.

When a mogu army prepared for war, they struck fear and terror into the hearts of their enemies.

THIS is the knowledge I seek here on Pandaria!

I have sent an expedition to study some ruins to the west, but they work as slowly as dim-witted peons!

Go speak to Fanlyr Silverthorn, their leader. Tell him that I want to see results immediately.

passages.title: Buried Secrets
passages.text: The Warchief sent you? What does he say?

passages.title: The Source of Korune Power
passages.text:
Why hullo there! Have ya ever seen tha like o' these statues? Fascinatin'!

I was scouting up along the ruins earlier, and I spotted somethin' innerestin' up on the highest rise.

I couldn't get close enough, but I think it might be one o' these mogu statues, 'cept it was movin'!

I can't get through all those nasty blood elves, but you look like you could.

Would you mind going up there and bringing me back anything of interest?

passages.title: The Source of Korune Power
passages.text: Did ya find anything up there?

passages.title: The Source of Korune Power
passages.text: Oh my, look at this thing!

passages.title: The Korune
passages.text:
These terracotta wardens are fearsome, but not nearly as horrifying as the creature that we found at the top of the ruins.

Some of our surviving scouts reported seeing some kind of mogu spellweaver on the highest rise to the north.

He practices a type of magic unlike any other we have seen.

We must learn whatever we can from this creature. Slay him, and bring me anything you find.

passages.title: The Korune
passages.text: What did you discover?

passages.title: The Korune
passages.text: Yes, this is remarkable! This is just the kind of artifact that we came here to find!

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text:
It has been two months since the parting of the mists. Alliance scouts, seeking a suitable landing site for the fleet, have engaged Horde forces on a beach in Krasarang Wilds.

Meet with Scout Lynna and help secure the landing site.

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text: You have impeccable timing, <class>. King Wrynn is just about to land, and the full might of our fleet will follow soon after.

passages.title: A King Among Men
passages.text:
There's no time to waste, we need to find Troteman and secure the beach.

We should check on the dwarves, too - the Explorers' League is tough, but they're no army. They should be along the cliff just north of here.

Let us ride, <class>. For our friends. For the Alliance.

passages.title: A King Among Men
passages.text: The Alliance will be a shield, protecting Pandaria from the Horde.

passages.title: A King Among Men
passages.text: I'm satisfied with this site, it's time to bring in our fleet.

passages.title: A Little Patience
passages.text:
King Varian needs decisive adventurers to help him resolve a showdown between Tyrande Whisperwind and a detachment of Horde warriors holed up in the Temple of the Red Crane.

Report to him immediately!

passages.title: A Little Patience
passages.text:
Good to see you again, <name>.

We have a delicate situation on our hands here. We need to plan our next moves carefully.

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text:
It has been two months since the parting of the mists. Horde scouts, seeking a suitable landing site for the fleet, have engaged Alliance forces on a small island off the coast of Krasarang Wilds.

Meet with Scout Rokla and help secure the landing site.

passages.title: Meet the Scout
passages.text: You are just in time. The Warchief is about to land. Once this site passes his inspection, the fleet will follow.

passages.title: The Might of the Warchief
passages.text:
Come, <class>! I want to inspect this island and ensure that my landing team has done their job.

Blood Guard Gro'tash should be somewhere on the northern side of the island looking for a suitable place to build our keep. The goblin survey team will have gone up the eastern coast in search of oil.

Let us crush this pitiful display and claim this land for the Horde!

passages.title: The Might of the Warchief
passages.text: Gorehowl thirsts for Alliance blood.

passages.title: The Might of the Warchief
passages.text: Well done. Our presence here will not be denied!

passages.title: Rise Of An Empire
passages.text:
Warchief Garrosh Hellscream travels north with a squad of his most elite soldiers.

Report to him with news of our continued victory against the Alliance.

Speak to Tak-Tak for transportation.

passages.title: Rise Of An Empire
passages.text: What do you have to report?

passages.title: Voice of the Gods
passages.text:
Too slowly!? We are working as quickly as possible for the Warchief!

We must excavate carefully, catalogue each find, and of course follow safety procedures. He must understand!

Well, we may have something to show him soon. Do you see that stone statue to the west?

We suspect it is an ancient stone storage vessel. Now we just have to find a way to open it.

If you would care to help us with our excavation, please go about it carefully.

passages.title: Voice of the Gods
passages.text: We are quite capable of handling this excavation. I understand the Warchief sent you, but he will get faster results if he leaves us to our work.

passages.title: Voice of the Gods
passages.text: Hmm... very interesting. This tablet will yield many secrets, indeed.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text:
The time has come. Our forces are well-enough entrenched here that we can risk pressing forward, into the Thunder King's lair. Unfortunately, it doesn't look like he'll be opening that gate anytime soon.

I suppose we'll have to make a gate of our own then. Let me know when you're ready, <name>.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text: Let's tear down this wall.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text: With your help, we're one giant step closer to our goal.

passages.title: Decisive Action
passages.text:
Zandalari warships plunder the seas around this island. They ferry in soldiers and war beasts from Zandalar to bolster Lei Shen's army.

If we can capture the palace shipyard, the Thunder King's supply line will be cut off, and your foothold here will be secure.

I have a plan to do just that, and it won't take an entire army.

passages.title: Decisive Action
passages.text:
Excellent work! With that blasted warship out of commission, the bombardments on our forces along the coast will cease.

Taran Zhu has informed me that the Shado-Pan will keep vigil over Stormsea Landing, freeing up Sunreaver resources to press the siege elsewhere. Taoshi will be there. I am sure she will be glad to work with you again.

We are all grateful for your contributions, <name>. Thank you.

passages.title: Someone You Should See
passages.text:
adventurer? It is good fortune I find you.

Chen Stormstout says to give this to you and ask you to meet him at Binan Village of the Kun-Lai Summit.

He found a friend of yours who needs much luck to get healthy.

Chen say speak to Tak-Tak for fast travels.

passages.title: Someone You Should See
passages.text: It is not my place to choose a side in this war. But I am not going to let a troll who has accomplished so much in his day fall by the wayside.

passages.title: Someone You Should See
passages.text: Ah! You received my note. Very good. Vol'jin is near death, and I will need your help healing his wounds.

passages.title: Anduin's Plea
passages.text:
Ah, just the <class> I was looking for. I have received an urgent letter from the young Prince Anduin.

He is playing host to his father, King Wrynn, and several other Alliance dignitaries at the Shrine of Seven Stars in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

According to his most recent correspondence, something bad is happening at the city.

Please go at once and speak with him. I must settle some affairs here at Lion's Landing, but I will join you soon.

Speak to Fennie if you'd like a ride to the Vale.

passages.title: Anduin's Plea
passages.text: Well met, <class>. We have much work to do here.

passages.title: Heart Of The Alliance
passages.text:
I can't believe this has happened, <name>. After all we have been through here on Pandaria, will our people never learn from their past mistakes?

Brann's expedition returned recently from Mogujia, bearing a sample of sha for study.

I had my reservations about this endeavor in the first place, and my worst fears have been realized.

The sha has escaped containment. I do not need to explain the horror of bringing the sha into the heart of the Vale.

We must dispel any sha we can find, and quickly!

passages.title: Heart Of The Alliance
passages.text: We must protect this land, and our people, from the sha's influence.

passages.title: Heart Of The Alliance
passages.text: I see that you and my son have been hard at work. Thank you for taking the initiative to aid our cause here in the Vale.

passages.title: Find Thrall!
passages.text:
<Vol'jin half opens an eye and begins to move his lips as if to speak. Though no sound comes, you decipher two words.>

Find Thrall.

<With an effort, Vol'jin thrusts a hearthstone into your hands and then passes out.>

passages.title: Find Thrall!
passages.text: You have come a long way to see me, <race>. Speak.

passages.title: Find Thrall!
passages.text:
<Thrall stares at the stone you have handed him.>

Vol'jin's hearthstone? My friend, has it come to this?

passages.title: Insertion
passages.text:
<name>! You'll do perfectly.

We know where the Alliance have hidden the Divine Bell. We've already inserted an agent into enemy territory, we just need you to help him execute his mission.

Pack up, <name>. You're headed to Darnassus.

passages.title: Insertion
passages.text:
<name>! So glad Nazgrim selected you.

It's taken a great deal of the Horde's effort to get you here through Jaina's traps. Maintaining our illusion this close to Darnassus is considerably expensive.

Furthermore, the Sunreavers of Dalaran are risking their neutrality by assisting the Horde with this operation.

In other words, we expect only the best from you.

passages.title: The Darnassus Mission
passages.text:
The Divine Bell is in the city. We don't want to cause a scene, we just want the artifact. I need you to find a way in, WITHOUT getting caught. That means no mounts, no flying, no fighting.

I can provide aid. I will magically cloak you, so you may move with stealth. I will also give you a small charm that you may use to return to safety, should you get in trouble.

Now go, <name>. Go, locate the bell, and tag it to be teleported back with you.

passages.title: The Darnassus Mission
passages.text: The bell, <name>!

passages.title: The Darnassus Mission
passages.text:
Well executed, <race>! I knew we could count on you.

Now to get off this wretched tree.

passages.title: Get My Results!
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer. The Warchief has instructed me to dispatch you to Silvermoon.

He grows impatient with the progress of Lor'themar's research and feels they might benefit from your... unique... experiences with the mogu.

Go to Silvermoon and demand that Lor'themar increase the speed of his research.

passages.title: Get My Results!
passages.text:
The Warchief "demands" progress? His impatience is growing more destructive with each command.

As it stands, we could use your expertise.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor
passages.text:
adventurer, King Varian has asked that I send you after his son to Dalaran. He believes you can help negotiate the withdrawal of blood elves there.

These "Sunreavers" claim fealty to the Horde and represent a major threat to the war effort.

Now that our very own Jaina Proudmoore is in charge of the Kirin Tor it should be easy to convince her to remove this Horde threat to her city.

Use the portal here in Lion's Landing to go to the Purple Parlor and lend what aid you can to Prince Anduin.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor
passages.text:
I am glad to see you friend. While I have learned much about diplomacy I think Jaina is too familiar with my tactics.

I could use a friendly hand in resolving this conflict.

passages.title: The First Riddle: Mercy
passages.text:
So, you wake up the Monkey King for a mallet hmmm? Answer first, these riddles three, and then the mallet you shall see.

First riddle!

 "Softly singing a song of pain

 There is a creature tortured and lame.

 Way down south and beyond the wall,

 It hides from its wikket masters' call.

 Seek out the creature sad and somber,

 And free it from its untamed amber."

Bring me the untamed amber.

passages.title: The First Riddle: Mercy
passages.text: Ah, the wise-ish thing returns. Have you my amber?

passages.title: The First Riddle: Mercy
passages.text:
Ah! Amber! Fresh and untamed. Did you kill to get it? But of course.

Though free, the untamed amber is a dangerous thing, and many might die because of it.

Mercy comes in many forms, like spikes and mantid and really ookin' spooky storms.

passages.title: Echoes of Thunder
passages.text:
Ah, <name>, we meet again. I have heard some wondrous news.

High Chieftain Baine Bloodhoof of the tauren has arrived here on Pandaria.

He meets with Warchief Garrosh Hellscream and Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron now, at the Shrine of Two Moons in the Vale of Eternal Blossoms.

He sent me a strange request - to send him a loyal champion of the Horde, capable of combat... and discretion.

I can think of none better to send than you. Speak to Tak-Tak if you seek transport.

passages.title: Echoes of Thunder
passages.text: Well met, <class>. You were sent from Domination Point? Very well. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: The Harmonic Mallet
passages.text:
adventurer! Prince Anduin has somehow slipped his guards again. His control over the light is greatly increasing.

He was last seen heading to Kun-Lai Summit. He gave our mages the slip around the Valley of Emperors.

Can you find him? He insists on searching for what he claims is a counter to the Divine Bell. Perhaps you can talk some sense into him before he seizes control of your mind and has you dance your way back here.

Talk to Fennie for a ride into the mountains.

passages.title: The Harmonic Mallet
passages.text:
I am glad you made it, my friend. I could really use your help with what is to come. My father would prefer I remain in the safe custody of his legion.

But if there is one thing Pandaria has taught me, it is a few people in the right place at the right time can make a bigger difference than the greatest of armies.

passages.title: The Fate of Dalaran
passages.text:
Jaina is refusing to hear me out. Father was hoping I would have some pull with her, but I think she still sees me as a child.

You, on the other hand, are a hero of the Alliance and I know she respects your deeds.

Is there something you can say to her to convince her we need her help?

passages.title: The Fate of Dalaran
passages.text: We are not asking for military forces. But we do need the magical support of Dalaran if we are to stop Garrosh's reckless advances.

passages.title: The Fate of Dalaran
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, hero. I hear the wisdom in Jaina's words.

Let's hope her faith in the Sunreavers is justified.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text:
I have another message for you from High Chieftain Bloodhoof.

It seems you've made quite the impression on him.

He travels with the Warchief's vanguard into Kun-Lai Summit, to the north. They have set up an outpost, Garrosh'ar Advance, just east of One Keg.

You had best not keep him waiting. Speak to Tak-Tak for swift travel.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text: Thank you for coming so quickly.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text: Thank you for coming, <name>.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: The tincture is ready. Now, drink.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: What did you see?

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: What did you see, <class>?

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text:
Glory to the Alliance, <class>. We are making gains against the Horde in the Krasarang Wilds, albeit slowly.

While we hold the front here, we need your help to fight a different battle - one that strikes at our enemy's heart.

Our SI:7 informant, Agent Connelly, has sent word that a Horde vanguard is moving up into the northern reaches of Kun-Lai Summit.

Go without delay. Make contact with Agent Connelly in the field, and find out what is going on.

Speak to Fennie over there for a flight in.

passages.title: The Kun-Lai Expedition
passages.text:
<You do a doubletake when the Pandaren suddenly speaks with Connelly's voice.>

'Bout time, laddie! I've been waitin' fer ya to show up.

These Pandaren are good people but can't mix a martini fer nothin'.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text:
<The radio static crackles, and Agent Connelly continues speaking.>

Now comes the real challenge, <laddie/lassie>. 

Head on over to the center of camp and see what you can overhear.

passages.title: Memory Wine
passages.text: Back so fast, rookie? So what did ye learn?

passages.title: De-Subjugation
passages.text:
The Kor'kron have been trained to be the finest, most loyal soldiers of the Warchief. Their presence here means that Garrosh fears an uprising.

Vol'jin and his people are as much a part of the Horde as any orc.

We must break this occupation and free the trolls. It pains me to say this, but you must eliminate enough of the Kor'kron so that the trolls can retake their city. Then meet me at Darkspear Hold so we might challenge their officer directly.

passages.title: De-Subjugation
passages.text: How did it come to this? It is as if the word "honor" is lost on these orcs.

passages.title: De-Subjugation
passages.text:
The orcs have changed. My Horde has changed. Do I kill my fellow orcs until it is once again "my" Horde? Do I have any right to try force the Horde to be what it once was?

These are troubling times. But for now, I must see to Vol'jin's people.

passages.title: To the Valley!
passages.text:
This sealed communication was sent for you, along with urgent orders to travel to the Valley of Emperors in Kun-Lai Summit.

This looks serious. I'd not delay if I were you.

Speak to Tak-Tak for transportation.

passages.title: To the Valley!
passages.text:
Ah, good. You have come. 

Again, I apologize for the cryptic note - but Garrosh is increasingly distrustful of us. I do not want this operation disturbed by hasty action on his part.

passages.title: A Kor'kron In Our Midst
passages.text:
Garrosh is hell-bent on finding that Divine Bell. I wouldn't be surprised if he tore Kun-Lai Summit apart to find that artifact.

The Warchief's called a gathering at Garrosh'ar Advance, just to our north.

I need to stay here to monitor troop movements, so you'll have to infiltrate their camp and overhear their discussion.

Go to Garrosh'ar Advance and steal some Kor'kron Armor from Reavers, Honor Guards, and Scouts.

Take this radio earpiece. Don't contact me... I'll contact you.

passages.title: A Kor'kron In Our Midst
passages.text: Just as you look at the assembled Kor'kron disguise, your radio earpiece crackles.

passages.title: A Kor'kron In Our Midst
passages.text:
<Agent Connelly's voice comes over the radio.>

Ey, you're good! I knew those Kor'kron wouldn't be a problem fer ya. Couldn't've done much better meself.

passages.title: Legacy of the Korune
passages.text:
I'm not prepared to throw away more of our people fighting against an enemy we don't know or understand. 

See if you can find any clues in the area as to who exactly these "Korune" mogu are. A contingency in case this operation doesn't go as planned.

passages.title: Legacy of the Korune
passages.text: Have you found anything on the mogu?

passages.title: Legacy of the Korune
passages.text:
Good. There's quite a bit to pore through here... 

I will have the Reliquary investigate these. Surely we can use them to discern more of the secrets of these Korune mogu.

passages.title: The Best Around
passages.text:
We're going to need help if we hope to figure out Garrosh's plans for Pandaria.

I have someone specific in mind, but he will not be easy to convince.

Agent Connelly considers himself retired, but one does not simply leave the SI: 7. We've had an undercover agent following his every move for months.

Currently, he is disguising himself as a high roller at Bizmo's Brawlpub. Something about settling an old debt.

Meet with our undercover agent in the Brawler's Guild.

passages.title: The Best Around
passages.text: So you think you are going to talk Connelly out of retirement? Good luck!

passages.title: The Best Around
passages.text:
Following Connelly has been interesting to say the least. The man is a master of disguise!

Talking him into joining you won't be the hard part, <class>. Figuring out which of these lively individuals is him will be next to impossble.

passages.title: To Catch A Spy
passages.text:
Now, I could tell you who Connelly is, but that would be too easy! To catch a spy you have to think like a spy.

You have to pass the test first!

The small things can say a lot about a person. It's all in the details.

I'm going to give you a drink to deliver. I will give you a small detail about something the recipient is wearing. From there it will be up to you.

Be careful who you pick to give drinks to. People here tend to get pretty hostile if you give them the wrong order!

passages.title: To Catch A Spy
passages.text: You learn to look at the details when you barkeep.

passages.title: To Catch A Spy
passages.text: You have a keen eye, <class>! I think you are ready to meet Connelly.

passages.title: He's In Deep
passages.text:
Agent Connelly has managed to infiltrate Garrosh's camp in Kun-Lai! He's been following their every move.

Connelly requested you specifically to assist him in gathering some vital intelligence.

He sent along a disguise for you. Make sure you put it on before approaching the camp! It will no doubt be heavily guarded.

He insists you will know him when you see him. Something about your keen eye for details...

Go talk to Fennie over there for a drop-off.

passages.title: He's In Deep
passages.text:
You've arrived just in time. From the intel I've gathered, Garrosh is hot on the trail of some sort of ancient mogu artifact of power.

If we can figure out what he's after, we can stop him from getting it!

We have to act fast to gather as much information as possible.

passages.title: Bugging Out
passages.text:
I've managed to plant a few bugs around the camp, but there could always be more.

I disguised the bugs to look like statues. They blend in perfectly with the other artifacts lying around.

Your disguise should allow you to move freely around the camp. Just don't go near the dog and don't linger around Garrosh! Nero and Garrosh will see through your disguise.

If you get caught I can't help you. I can't compromise the mission!

passages.title: Bugging Out
passages.text: How'd it go?

passages.title: Bugging Out
passages.text: Well done! Everyone always underestimates the little guys and it is always a grave mistake!

passages.title: Trapping the Leader
passages.text:
It is time to make our move. Go to the Tomb of Shadows, weaken him, and take him captive.

I will stay here in case Garrosh arrives. He must be delayed so that we can take our prize before he destroys it in his anger.

Hurry!

passages.title: Trapping the Leader
passages.text: Move, <name>!

passages.title: Trapping the Leader
passages.text:
We managed to capture our quarry. 

In truth, though, I am not sure what our next move should be. I will contact the leaders of our allies and see if they have ideas - I don't know that our arcane talents are going to pry the secrets of our mogu captive.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text:
Garrosh sent a hundred riders to search the northern coast of Kun-Lai Summit, to seek a mogu crypt matching the one you saw in Shan Kien's memory.

Out of those, one found the resting place of the Divine Bell.

Blademaster Ishi is leading an advance party to secure the bell now.

Go and assist him. Defend that artifact from anyone who might stand in your way!

Speak to Tak-Tak without delay. He can take you there.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text: The Alliance beat us here. How could this happen?

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text:
It's time for our boldest move yet, <name>.

Since you acquired intel on the location of the Divine Bell, we've amassed a top team to excavate the artifact without delay.

Commander Sarannha Skyglaive leads the expedition into the northern-most reaches of Kun-Lai Summit.

Join them at once, and use whatever skills you need to make the endeavor a success.

Good luck, <class>. I don't need to tell you how important this mission is to the Alliance.

Speak to Fennie. She'll get you there quickly.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text: Looks like we're well ahead of the Horde. Not surprising, but we must act swiftly.

passages.title: The Ruins of Korune
passages.text: We blasted the doors open moments ago, <class>. You arrived just in time to join us for the excavation.

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
There's no telling what lies below, so I will lead the initial scouting party myself.

If your report was correct, then the Korune mogu hid the Divine Bell in the rooms below our very feet.

I have a feeling they would not have left such a precious artifact unguarded.

I could use a capable <class> such as yourself to watch my back. Let me know when you're ready.

passages.title: The Divine Bell
passages.text:
Fantastic work, <name>. I could not even imagine the atrocity that Garrosh would commit if this bell were to fall into his hands.

Today, we have secured a safe future for the Alliance. I will see to it that the bell makes it safely to Darnassus.

I will extoll your deeds to the King.

passages.title: He Won't Even Miss It
passages.text:
I've noticed Garrosh and that Reliquary blood elf carrying around some sort of journal.

The journal is never more than a stone's throw away. It must be important!

If you can cause enough of a distraction, you may be able to swipe the journal off the table.

These yaks might just do the trick. Give one of 'em a tap and they'll do the rest.

Just be ready to move fast!

passages.title: He Won't Even Miss It
passages.text: What did you find?

passages.title: He Won't Even Miss It
passages.text:
Phew! That was a close one! I never doubted you for a minute though.

Now let me take a look at that journal...

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text:
Your efforts have culminated in this moment, <class>.

Warchief Garrosh gathers the most elite champions of the Horde in Kun-Lai Summit to witness the ringing of the Divine Bell.

You have more than earned the right to participate.

Go now. The dawn of the new Horde begins today.

Speak to Tak-Tak. He should be able to secure your travel arrangements.

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text: I was wondering when you would arrive, <name>.

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
It is time, <name>. We have traveled a long path to reach this moment.

Today, our Warchief, Garrosh Hellscream, will change the course of our people's history forever.

Today, we witness the birth of Garrosh's Horde!

Do not let anything interfere with the ceremony!

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text: We cannot rely on fate or destiny. We must carve out our own future... the future that WE deserve!

passages.title: Breath of Darkest Shadow
passages.text:
They may have destroyed the Divine Bell, but I have taken the life of the Alliance's prodigal son!

It is nothing less than my own father would have expected of me.

This victory may have come at a high cost, but it is of little consequence.

I will find other ways to destroy my enemies, and bring glory to the Horde!

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text:
Horde forces are amassing in huge numbers at the Emperor's Reach, high up in the mountains of Kun-Lai Summit.

The area is an ancient mogu palace, and certainly a source of untold power.

This can only mean one thing. Garrosh is going to use the Divine Bell, and Anduin... and the Harmonic Mallet... are both missing.

I have no doubt that the fool boy went north by himself.

I don't have time to gather an elite force to detain him. You must go and stop Anduin.

Fennie can take you.

passages.title: The Bell Speaks
passages.text: <name>! Just the <class> I was hoping to see. You couldn't have arrived at a better time.

passages.title: Violence in the Arena
passages.text:
As I suspected, it gets worse up ahead. The Silver Covenant is outright attacking innocent Sunreavers!

This cannot stand. While our prime directive is to rescue Aethas Sunreaver, we must also protect as many blood elves as we can.

I will continue to scout ahead. Fight well, <class>!

passages.title: Violence in the Arena
passages.text:
So much bloodshed! In a place of peace!

Jaina has gone too far this time.

passages.title: A Tactical Assault
passages.text:
If we're to survive up above ground, we're going to need a base of operations.

I'm going to try to take the center of the city. It's risky, but hopefully Jaina and the Silver Covenant won't expect it.

Stay by my side now, <name>.

passages.title: A Tactical Assault
passages.text: Now, let's move quickly.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor's True Colors
passages.text:
Any pretense that the Kirin Tor might have had at being a "neutral" group can officially be discarded. I'm now hearing that Jaina's got Alliance troops stowed away near Antonidas Memorial.

The area's free of Sunreavers, but it still makes my blood boil to see such blatant favoritism from the Kirin Tor.

Go visit the memorial, <name>... and give those Alliance dogs a good kick on your way through.

passages.title: The Kirin Tor's True Colors
passages.text: <Rommath looks displeased.>

passages.title: The Kirin Tor's True Colors
passages.text:
Thank you for that, <name>.

It unsettles me to have to fight directly with the high elves of the Silver Covenant... but I never tire of slaying Alliance.

passages.title: The Remaining Sunreavers
passages.text:
There's still a number of significant Sunreavers who haven't been accounted for. Odds are that they're in the Sunreaver's Sanctuary, caught by surprise.

<Rommath hands you an artifact, clearly made by blood elf hands.>

The place is crawling with Silver Covenant. You'll need to get in, use the Tear to evacuate the VIPs, and then get out.

Stay alive, <name>.

passages.title: The Remaining Sunreavers
passages.text: Be on the lookout for Aethas while you're in there.

passages.title: The Remaining Sunreavers
passages.text: Excellent. They should be waiting for us in Silvermoon when we return.

passages.title: One Last Grasp
passages.text:
We've looked everywhere he's likely to be, except for one place: the Violet Citadel.

Find out if Archmage Aethas is being held within the citadel, <name>. We may get lucky. If not... at least we saved a number of lives today.

passages.title: One Last Grasp
passages.text: Is this... <name>? What's going on here?

passages.title: Darnassus Attacked?
passages.text:
As you know, our night elven allies moved the Divine Bell you retrieved to Darnassus for safekeeping and study. Moments ago, they portaled some Highbourne mages over here to ask for backup. Details are hazy - some sort of stealth attack on the city?

I don't know what to make of it, but Jaina Proudmoore is already on the scene and I suspect they need all the help they can get.

Speak to Seamus Goldenkicks over there for a quick portal to Darnassus. Find Jaina!

passages.title: Darnassus Attacked?
passages.text:
The Bell is gone...

At the scene of the crime, we found traces of arcane magic... I may be able to use my skills to track the thieves.

passages.title: Jaina's Resolution
passages.text:
For too long, I have toiled to mend fences between Alliance and Horde. Time and time again, I've given the Horde the benefit of the doubt - and time and time again, they stab me in the back.

I refuse to be betrayed again! If the Horde intends to use the Kirin Tor as a weapon against the Alliance, then they have no place in Dalaran.

Come with me, <name>.

passages.title: Jaina's Resolution
passages.text: <Jaina looks angry.>

passages.title: Jaina's Resolution
passages.text:
I will instruct you from here on out.

Jaina will be going down into the city to enforce our new rules.

passages.title: Unfair Trade
passages.text:
Most shopkeepers in the Magus Commerce Exchange have sided with the Silver Covenant, but there remain a few holdouts that must be taken care of.

<Vereesa shows you a list of names.>

They will not go easily.

passages.title: Unfair Trade
passages.text:
While I can't say I agree completely with Jaina's methods, I do understand her motives.

Sometimes, you have to fight back.

passages.title: Nowhere to Hide
passages.text:
The Sunreaver's Sanctuary is still crawling with those Horde-loving Sunreavers.

Jaina will have sent the reasonable ones to the Violet Hold. The rest refuse to leave, raising their weapons against us.

Show them the cost of their defiance. They now face the judgment of the Alliance, the Silver Covenant, and the Kirin Tor!

passages.title: Nowhere to Hide
passages.text:
This is a bloody day, <name>, and this is bloody work.

But do not forget what the Sunreavers did to bring this on: They used neutral Kirin Tor resources to aid the Horde in their fight against the Alliance.

Do not hesitate to believe that they would do the same to us, given the chance.

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text:
Compliant Sunreavers will be sent to the Violet Hold. Defiant ones are put to the sword.

NONE are to escape.

The Sunreavers keep their dragonhawk mounts on Krasus' Landing. Take this dust, and use it to render them incapable of flying.

Or kill them. I don't care.

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text: We can't have the Sunreavers escaping and plotting counterattacks against Dalaran. We need to be quick, precise, and thorough.

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text: Now, the Sunreavers have to answer to us. Jail or death - their fate is in their own hands.

passages.title: What Had To Be Done
passages.text:
Thank you for your aid today, <name>. I will be handling the purge from here on out.

Jaina will soon be off to Lion's Landing, to speak with King Varian. She asked for your attendance.

passages.title: What Had To Be Done
passages.text:
I can't fault you for following orders. In fact, I can't really fault Jaina for acting on her own behalf, for once.

But still... we aren't playing a game here. We are dealing with war, with people's lives, with the future of the Alliance itself.

At the very least, we now have the Kirin Tor on our side. Today will be remembered by all as a victory for the Alliance.

passages.title: Stirred, Not Shaken
passages.text:
Alright, I'll tell you how to find Connelly.

Agent Connelly is currently posing as the high roller, Professor Kilt. He spends most of his time in the Boom Room. Rumor has it he's after one of the fighters for some long forgotten betrayal.

Unfortunately, the lounge is by invitation only. Lucky for you I just happen to have an invitation.

Try not to look too obvious when you walk past the bouncers. If you get caught you didn't get this pass from me.

In fact you and I have never met!

passages.title: Stirred, Not Shaken
passages.text:
So the SI: 7 needs a reminder in what the word retirement means?

I suppose they wouldn't be comin' to me if the situation weren't dire.

I'll help, but I'll need a few days to gather some intel.

passages.title: The Silence
passages.text:
D..did we... do it?

<Anduin mumbles the words, even though the effort clearly costs him.>

L..look... in.. my... bag...

Use... flare...

passages.title: The Silence
passages.text:
I hesitate to guess what would have happened if you had not been there with the young Prince, <name>.

Today, you put an end to Garrosh's plans.

You have undoubtedly saved thousands of lives, and most importantly, you brought Anduin back to us.

We are doing everything we can for the boy, but we can only wait and see.

I believe he has the fight in him. I must believe it...

passages.title: Tracking the Thieves
passages.text:
We WILL get to the bottom of this.

<name>, you're coming with me. We'll search every inch of this city if we have to, but we'll find out how they took the bell... and where.

I'm picking up traces of arcane magic here... we need to follow the trail!

passages.title: Tracking the Thieves
passages.text:
I've decided.

Certain members of the Kirin Tor have put their allegiance to the Horde above the order, and I will NOT tolerate it. This is nothing short of a betrayal.

<Jaina's eyes flare with rage.>

Come with me, <name>. We're going to clean up Dalaran.

passages.title: Champions of the Thunder King
passages.text:
This island is riddled with lurking threats from three powerful groups, waiting for the chance to pounce on us. Masters of lightning, ancient and powerful spirits, and primal Zandalari monstrosities.

If you can get your hands on some of the Shan'ze Ritual Stones scattered across the isle, you should be able to beckon these powerful opponents out of hiding and strike out at them.

Find and destroy members of each group to keep them destabilized, and I will make it worth your time.

passages.title: Champions of the Thunder King
passages.text: Against these ancient enemies, there is no rescourse.  We strike first, and they do not strike at all.

passages.title: Champions of the Thunder King
passages.text:
Yours skills as a <class> are unquestionable. You've aided the cause greatly this day. You have my thanks.

And now for that reward I promised you...

passages.title: Champions of the Thunder King
passages.text:
This island is riddled with lurking threats from three powerful groups, waiting for the chance to pounce on us. Masters of lightning, ancient and powerful spirits, and primal Zandalari monstrosities.

If you can get your hands on some of the Shan'ze Ritual Stones scattered across the isle, you should be able to beckon these powerful opponents out of hiding and strike out at them.

Find and destroy members of each group to keep them destabilized, and I will make it worth your time.

passages.title: Champions of the Thunder King
passages.text: Against these ancient enemies, there is no rescourse.  We strike first, and they do not strike at all.

passages.title: Champions of the Thunder King
passages.text:
Yours skills as a <class> are unquestionable. You've aided the cause greatly this day. You have my thanks.

And now for that reward I promised you...

passages.title: The Assault on Shaol'mara
passages.text:
Our scouting efforts along the coast have given us valuable intelligence about the island, <class>.

However, we will accomplish nothing if we do not advance forward onto the mainland.

I have assembled a team of our most elite aerial units to begin the attack.

I would like you to join the assault. A champion such as yourself could turn the battle in our favor at the critical moment.

When you are ready to begin the attack, speak to me.

passages.title: The Assault on Shaol'mara
passages.text: We must claim a better strategic position on the island itself.

passages.title: The Assault on Shaol'mara
passages.text:
Yes! You have done it, champion!

Now, the Thunder King will taste the full force of the Kirin Tor!

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text:
The time has come. Our forces are well-enough entrenched here that we can risk pressing forward, into the Thunder King's lair. Unfortunately, it doesn't look like he'll be opening that gate anytime soon.

I suppose we'll have to make a gate of our own then. Let me know when you're ready, <name>.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text: Let's tear down this wall.

passages.title: Tear Down This Wall!
passages.text: With your help, we're one giant step closer to our goal.

passages.title: A Bold Idea
passages.text:
Zandalari warships plunder the seas around this island. They ferry in soldiers and war beasts from Zandalar to bolster Lei Shen's army.

If we can capture the palace shipyard, the Thunder King's supply line will be cut off, and your foothold here will be secure.

I have a plan to do just that, and it won't take an entire army.

passages.title: A Bold Idea
passages.text:
Well done. That warship won't be raining fire on us again any time soon.

Taran Zhu has informed me that the Shado-Pan will keep vigil over Stormsea Landing, freeing up Kirin Tor resources to press the siege elsewhere. Taoshi will be there. I am sure she will be glad to work with you again.

We are all grateful for your contributions, <name>. Thank you.

passages.title: Thunder Calls
passages.text:
The time to attack the Thunder King has come!

A small group of Sunreavers awaits you near the Shado-Pan Garrison in Townlong Steppes.

Report to Scout Captain Elsia for further instructions.

passages.title: Thunder Calls
passages.text: We must move quickly, <name>! The others have gone ahead of us, but I will brief you in the flight over.

passages.title: Thunder Calls
passages.text:
The time to attack the Thunder King has come!

A small group of Kirin Tor awaits you near the Shado-Pan Garrison in Townlong Steppes.

Report to Vereesa Windrunner for further instructions.

passages.title: Thunder Calls
passages.text: We must move quickly, <name>! The others have gone ahead of us, but I will brief you in the flight over.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text:
There is no time to waste, <name>. Every moment we delay here gives Jaina and the Kirin Tor more of a hold on the Isle.

Lor'themar awaits us. Speak to me when you are ready to depart. I will escort you there myself.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text: This isle holds many secrets my friend.

passages.title: The Storm Gathers
passages.text:
You have arrived just in time, <race>. It is crucial we gain control of these shores before the Kirin Tor.

There is much to explain.

passages.title: Secrets in the Isle of Thunder
passages.text:
I do have one thing I would ask of you, <class>.

We've gotten our hands on a powerful ritual stone that the Shan'ze mogu use to beckon their allies into battle, but we need more than one to perform their rituals.

If you come upon three of these stones, bring them back to me. We can gather our forces and use these stones to beckon some of Lei Shen's most powerful servants directly into our traps.

passages.title: Secrets in the Isle of Thunder
passages.text: Have you found the stones I spoke of?

passages.title: Secrets in the Isle of Thunder
passages.text: Perfect. I will show you how to use these stones, and then you can spring the ambush.

passages.title: Setting the Trap
passages.text:
Take these 3 ritual stones to the location I have marked on your map. There, you will find a Shan'ze ritual object that you can use to beckon one of their powerful allies.

You will need capable friends at your side for this trap to work. Do not go alone, for these will be some of the Thunder King's most powerful servants.

When your enemy shows itself, show no mercy.

passages.title: Setting the Trap
passages.text: Did the ambush succeed?

passages.title: Setting the Trap
passages.text:
Very impressive.

Should you find more stones, you should continue this ruse. It is sure to be quite some time before they catch on to our ploy.

passages.title: The King and the Council
passages.text:
I am glad you are here, <name>. I have been using my dream brew to experience events around the world, but the more I learn, the more confused I become.

For instance, King Wrynn has asked the dwarves of Ironforge for more troops, but they do not all support him.

I will tell you more, but I would also like to hear from your experience firsthand...

passages.title: The King and the Council
passages.text: It is not my place to make stories. I simply tell them.

passages.title: The King and the Council
passages.text:
So, King Wrynn and the Dark Iron dwarves saved the city, and the bitterly divided Council of Three Hammers gained a new unity under the Alliance banner. How interesting!

But what is happening within the Horde?

passages.title: The Warchief and the Darkness
passages.text: I see now how the Alliance king leads his people. But what is the Horde warchief up to? Just below us, a swarm of goblins are burrowing into the sacred vale on his orders. What does he hope to find there? We must find out!

passages.title: The Warchief and the Darkness
passages.text: It is not my place to make stories. I simply tell them.

passages.title: The Warchief and the Darkness
passages.text:
Whaaaat? The remains of an Old God are buried beneath Pandaria? No wonder the land is so haunted!

The warchief's pursuit of those dormant powers are fraying apart the very Horde he leads. His vision is narrow, but very, very dangerous. I must inform the Shado-Pan immediately.

passages.title: Path of the Last Emperor
passages.text:
In his time of uncertainty, the last emperor walked a lonely path up this mountain, until he had at last found his answers.

I am here to walk the same path, and it seems you have questions of your own to be answered. Perhaps you will join me, and we can both be satisfied?

Oh, but I am getting old, and this blizzard is proving too much for my bones. Could you climb ahead and anchor this rope? I can hoist myself along from there.

Together we shall walk the path of the last emperor.

passages.title: Path of the Last Emperor
passages.text:
We made it, <class>! Thank you so much. Please, help yourself to some of my old knick-knacks.

But... I am afraid I have not been completely honest with you...

passages.title: Time Keeper Kairoz
passages.text:
You have found your way to the Timeless Isle, <class>. The bronze dragonflight is keen to investigate the mysteries of this place, but the island is dangerous, and we will need your help.

Midway down this beach, you will find a paved path to the east.

It will lead you to the ancient Celestial Court. You will find Kairoz there, one of the Keepers of Time that we are working with.

Kairoz will answer any questions you might have. Be careful: The way may not be safe.

passages.title: Time Keeper Kairoz
passages.text:
Ah! Well met, <name>!

I was told you would be coming, but had not expected you so soon.

...or has it been a long while? It is difficult to tell, here.

So! Shall we begin?

passages.title: Time Keeper Kairoz
passages.text:
You have found your way to the Timeless Isle, <class>. The bronze dragonflight is keen to investigate the mysteries of this place, but the island is dangerous, and we will need your help.

Midway up this beach, you will find a paved path to the east.

It will lead you to the ancient Celestial Court. You will find Kairoz there, one of the Keepers of Time that we are working with.

Kairoz will answer any questions you might have. Be careful: The way may not be safe.

passages.title: Time Keeper Kairoz
passages.text:
Ah! Well met, <name>!

I was told you would be coming, but had not expected you so soon.

...or has it been a long while? It is difficult to tell, here.

So! Shall we begin?

passages.title: Time In Your Hands
passages.text:
Inhabitants of this strange island barter with a special currency, immune from the fickle fluctuations of time.

You would do well to gather as many of these "timeless coins" as possible! They can be found hidden away in small caches, or gathered from creatures all around the island. Larger, rarer creatures are a better source of coins - you may find it profitable to venture forth as part of a group.

Introduce yourself to Mistweavers Ai and Ku across the Celestial Court, and gather some coins for me.

passages.title: Time In Your Hands
passages.text: You're back already? It feels like we spoke only moments ago.

passages.title: Time In Your Hands
passages.text:
I believe you are getting the feel for this place! Yes, opportunities abound to gather up timeless treasures. Strange events happen all the time here - always keep your eyes open.

Speak to the mistweavers you met to spend your hard-earned currency. Meanwhile, I will continue my research.

Here is a taste of some of the treasures you can find here. More powerful items are available. You'll find that hidden caches in the more dangerous parts of the island can be... extremely rewarding. Good luck.

passages.title: Journey to the Timeless Isle
passages.text:
The bronze dragonflight has discovered a most unusual pandaren phenomenon, <class>. Emerging from the mists, far off the coast of the Jade Forest - an island that was lost in time!

It is a dangerous place, perhaps the most perilous in all of Pandaria. But we are determined to unravel its mysteries.

Here, take this timepiece. A single click will whisk you to the island. Get yourself established, and speak with Watcher Lara. She will guide you to our chief investigator.

passages.title: Journey to the Timeless Isle
passages.text: I see Chronormu has made good on her promise! You are right on time.

passages.title: Journey to the Timeless Isle
passages.text:
The bronze dragonflight has discovered a most unusual pandaren phenomenon, <class>. Emerging from the mists, far off the coast of the Jade Forest - an island that was lost in time!

It is a dangerous place, perhaps the most perilous in all of Pandaria. But we are determined to unravel its mysteries.

Here, take this timepiece. A single click will whisk you to the island. Get yourself established, and speak with Watcher Alundra. She will guide you to our chief investigator.

passages.title: Journey to the Timeless Isle
passages.text: I see Chronormu has made good on her promise! You are right on time.

passages.title: Hints From The Past
passages.text:
There is much to learn of this place, yet it does not yield its secrets willingly.

Something you mentioned the last time that we spoke intrigues me. This Mistweaver Ai, she carries a time-worn journal, if I recall? This may be the answer to many of our questions, or it may simply raise more. I suppose that it all depends on the diligence of the explorer that put pen to paper in this preposterous place.

Obtain a time-worn journal and return to me with it. We shall delve into its mysteries together.

passages.title: Hints From The Past
passages.text: Ah, you have returned. Do you have the journal?

passages.title: Hints From The Past
passages.text:
Ah, you have it! Excellent!

A cursory glance indicates that my presumptions were not far-fetched. Though the pages are worn and waterlogged, most of the entries are still legible. It appears that our friend, explorer Harrington, was quite verbose in cataloguing the creatures and treasures he found on his journey through the island.

Well, are you simply going to stand there? This tome is a veritable trove of mysteries, and we have barely scratched the surface! Adventure awaits!

passages.title: Timeless Treasures
passages.text:
The journal indicates that treasures abound across the island, sometimes temptingly out of reach, and other times hidden in dark caves and hollows. What might have been secreted away here, many generations ago?

And perhaps more importantly, by whom?

Search the island for such treasures, and return to me with your findings. Be warned that all that glitters is not gold, yet the reverse is also true. Sometimes the simple hollowed-out stump is the best hiding place for one's valuables.

passages.title: Timeless Treasures
passages.text: Time flows oddly in this place, I cannot tell if I should be sleeping or eating my mid-day meal.

passages.title: Timeless Treasures
passages.text:
I am happy that you have discovered some riches for your efforts, though we are no closer to unraveling this mystery than before. Take solace in the knowledge that many such bounties are surely scattered throughout the island, eagerly awaiting your exploration skills and combat prowess.

Oh, one last thing, my young adventurer - do not forget to look to the skies now and again.

passages.title: Timeless Nutriment
passages.text:
As you have surmised, the flora and fauna of this island are quite unusual. Not all explanations are mysterious, however. Sometimes, we must listen to the land, to hear the tales of the world around us. Have you considered that the creatures of this island grew to such proportions simply from the nutriment of the land you walk upon?

You will find nutriment in abundance throughout the island: ripe fruits, eggs, meat, flowers, nuts, and even the stones themselves. Eat, and discover the power of the land.

passages.title: Timeless Nutriment
passages.text: Have you enjoyed the abundance of the island?

passages.title: Timeless Nutriment
passages.text: The island gives in abundance, in nutriment and in answers. You only need look around to find what you seek.

passages.title: Wayshrines Of The Celestials
passages.text:
Many years ago, these grounds were a place where my people would come in pilgrimage. Here, they would listen to the words of the celestials, and meditate for many days. In their meditations, they found the fear, anger, despair, doubt, and violence that plagued their spirits.

Before them would be a pathway to enlightenment. For each, the pathway would be different. For all of them, the pathway began with wisdom.

Travel the island, as they did, and discover one of the lost wayshrines of the celestials.

passages.title: Wayshrines Of The Celestials
passages.text: The shrines will not always avail themselves to you. Do not give up, such is the test of patience.

passages.title: Wayshrines Of The Celestials
passages.text: You have experienced the power and wisdom of the Celestials. Let it flow through you now, and remain in your heart for all time.

passages.title: Drive Back The Flame
passages.text:
The pandaren once existed in harmony with the Ordon yaungol. When the island suddenly disappeared, the Ordon faced certain death. In their desperation, the chief shaman called out for aid to the Fire Lords, and was answered.

Ordos was his name. Now, he is a creature of anger and violence. Though his people were saved, he burns endlessly in molten agony.

There is harmony no longer. The Ordon seek to take the Celestial Court, and sacrifice us all to Ordos. Drive them back, and restore balance.

passages.title: Drive Back The Flame
passages.text: The Ordon are not to be trifled with. They have survived on this island under the protections of their ever-burning demigod, Ordos.

passages.title: Drive Back The Flame
passages.text: Your accomplishments are many, and your bravery cannot be questioned. The Ordon have been driven back for the moment, but do not underestimate them. To restore harmony to the isle, we must continue to be vigilant.

passages.title: They Came From the Sea
passages.text:
You're looking for Prince Farondis?

<The ghostly elf narrows her eyes warily.>

I can take you to Farondis... but first things first. These naga attacked suddenly. They take orders from one called Zarrin, in the low hills to the west.

Help me take Zarrin's head, and you'll have my ear.

passages.title: They Came From the Sea
passages.text: <The nightwatcher looks at you expectantly.>

passages.title: They Came From the Sea
passages.text:
<Idri stares at the ugly head.>

Yes, that's him.

passages.title: Under Cover of Darkness
passages.text:
We are off to Stormwind. Tethys will sneak us by water beneath the old barracks under cover of darkness tonight.

The rest will be up to you, Mathias, and myself. We will have to stealth through Stormwind and confront Detheroc at SI:7.

Are you ready to do this, <name>?

passages.title: Under Cover of Darkness
passages.text:
We made it. Now all we have to do is get up there, sneak through my city -- which, mind you, is being watched by everyone -- then reveal and kill a dreadlord inside the headquarters of SI:7, Azeroth's most elite spy organization.

Piece of cake. Ready to save the world, <name>?

passages.title: Round 1, Fight!
passages.text:
All of my gladiators are out of commission!

It's down to you, <name>. Bilgerudder's going to pit his three champions against you.

passages.title: Round 1, Fight!
passages.text: <This is where you expected to find Okuna. Instead, you only found the pack with the weapons.>

passages.title: Maritime Law
passages.text:
Good <sir/madame>, a moment of your time. My fellow salvors and I could not help but notice yon ship that ran aground in the storm last night.

A pity about its crew.

<Mr. Shackles makes empathetic gestures.>

Still, the law's the law. The maritime code is quite clear on the matter. If you find yourself out that way, would you mind terribly checking in on my acquisitions scout, Looper? I would have expected him back for tea some time ago.

passages.title: Maritime Law
passages.text:
Do you know what ship this is? It's the Queen's Reprisal. Queen... as in the Banshee Queen, Sylvanas Windrunner.

If the farmstead weren't sunk under the waves, I'd be heading home to Gilneas right about now.

passages.title: Making the World Safe for Profit
passages.text:
Might I ask a small favor, my friend? These creatures in the tide pools to the east are starting to frighten me. Our efforts to trade with them have been rebuffed at every turn with aggression. This is not good; neither for running a business, nor for profit.

Sadly, I must admit the time for talk has come to an end.

Might you be willing to serve as my representative in dealing with the denizens of Mak'rura and their "queen"?

I can assure you that your efforts will be rewarded commensurately.

passages.title: Making the World Safe for Profit
passages.text: How goes the cleanup?

passages.title: Making the World Safe for Profit
passages.text:
What? A jailer demon you say? Oublion? What a ghastly name.

No wonder we couldn't become trade partners with them. Oh, if only I'd known, there wouldn't have been any need for such slaughter!

Ah well. Live and learn.
