passages.title: The Scythe of Souls
passages.text:
Let's head to the other side of the stand. We will release the demon souls one by one and get the answers that we seek concerning Lord Illidan.

The Scythe of Souls will ensure that we do.

passages.title: The Scythe of Souls
passages.text: We need to compel the demons, <name>.

passages.title: The Scythe of Souls
passages.text:
I wouldn't take what Arev'naal said to heart. The inquisitor demons are masters of misinformation. You don't suspect betrayal within the ranks, do you?

<The Souleater looks thoughtful and grim.>

I fear we won't have all of our answers about Lord Illidan for a while.

passages.title: Picking a Fight
passages.text:
They're coming, <name>!

I will get to work unlocking these fel-magic chains from the cage.

You keep the Legion at bay.

passages.title: Picking a Fight
passages.text:
You have my eternal gratitude, <name>. Let it never be said that I have underestimated the reach and prowess of the Uncrowned.

The easy part's done. Now it's time to do the impossible.

passages.title: The Imposter
passages.text:
Detheroc has SI:7's finest snipers on all of the rooftops. We can't mount up and we can't fly. There are grapple points above so that we can move up the cliff. 

We've also setup hay bales to hide in along the likely routes to SI:7. We just need to stealth in and kill Detheroc.

Once we get up there, we'll separate to increase the chances of at least one of us making it through the city.

Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: The Imposter
passages.text:
You did it! Mathias Shaw is back in charge of SI:7 and you prevented an all-out war between the Alliance and Horde.

The rest of us agree, you've proven yourself an invaluable member of the Council of Shadows and the Uncrowned.

Congratulations, Shadowblade <name>!

passages.title: The Headmistress' Keys
passages.text:
I have a suspicion you are avoiding your studies - but I can see you're anxious to see the Headmistress.

Very well! Headmistress Azuremoon can be found up ahead, though I doubt she will enjoy being interrupted.

passages.title: The Headmistress' Keys
passages.text: Were you able to meet with the headmistress?

passages.title: The Headmistress' Keys
passages.text: She... she gave you her key? My word!

passages.title: The Death of the Eldest
passages.text:
I will do what I can to stabilize him, but I will need your help.

The small amount of energy he has left is coming from the mana pool he rests in.

Follow the whelplings' lead. Dropping ley crystals into the pool gives him a bit of energy - buying him a few more breaths.

They seem to be getting the crystals from inside that cave to the north.

passages.title: The Death of the Eldest
passages.text: Call me a fool. I'd always just thought that grandfather would be with us forever.

passages.title: The Death of the Eldest
passages.text:
Thank you. Your efforts dull his pain.

<She sighs.>

passages.title: You Scratch My Back...
passages.text:
Much better. I knew I could count on you, my friend. Allow me to return the favor.

I know how you can destroy the large mana collector pylons. We shall save your dragon yet!

The pylons only work against ground targets, yet they're defenseless from above. Send your whelplings at them, my friend. The whelplings can fly where we cannot.

Trust me.

passages.title: You Scratch My Back...
passages.text: With the pylons destroyed, Senegos' pool should now be re-energized.

passages.title: On the Brink
passages.text:
This many withered threaten to wipe our brood out completely!

Quickly, <name>! Crack off a ley crystal and heal any wounded drakes you can find out on the battlefield.

I will do what I can to keep these whelplings safe and healthy.

passages.title: On the Brink
passages.text: Hurry, <name>!

passages.title: On the Brink
passages.text:
Well done. I saw the other drakes take to the skies.

And look! You found Emmigosa!

It seems she's taken a shine to you, <name>. I trust you'll keep her safe for now.

passages.title: A Royal Summons
passages.text:
Well met, adventurer. I have come on behalf of King Anduin Wrynn.

My crew is preparing for a special mission, and the king would like you to join us. Please review this official summons and, if you are satisfied, return with me to Stormwind Harbor.

<Rogers hands you a sealed envelope.>

passages.title: A Royal Summons
passages.text: Can we count on you?

passages.title: A Royal Summons
passages.text: Thank you for your cooperation.

passages.title: Assault and Battery
passages.text:
We need to report our position to the Alliance navy ASAP!

I am building a new transponder to send a distress signal, but I need a battery from the Skyfire's communications console.

You'll find the console at the top of the ship - I just hope those undead haven't put their creepy, bony fingers on it yet!

passages.title: Assault and Battery
passages.text: I cannot build a new transponder without that battery!

passages.title: Assault and Battery
passages.text:
NUTS and BOLTS!

Pardon my language.

This thing is almost as dead as the guy you took it from. We need juice, and lots of it. I have an idea...

passages.title: The Lost Legion
passages.text:
The heroic men and women of the 7th Legion stayed at the front of the ship to fight off storm drakes while the crew evacuated.

None of them have returned.

Please find them, adventurer!

passages.title: The Lost Legion
passages.text: <Though his eyes are open, the soldier does not respond to your presence. An electrical field buzzes around him.>

passages.title: Pins and Needles
passages.text:
Hngghh!

Nope, can't stand yet. It's all pins and needles.

Small fries like this are usually no problem for the 7th, but we weren't prepared for their electrical attacks. Before I knew it, I was trapped in some kind of static field. Couldn't move a muscle until you came along.

My comrades were carried deeper into the cave. Get 'em out before they become whelp chow!

passages.title: Signal Boost
passages.text:
The Skyfire's starboard propeller came to rest on the cliffs overlooking our camp - we're gonna use it like a big antenna and push our distress signal so far that even Mekkatorque's alarm clock could pick it up!

Unfortunately, it might attract some unwanted attention.

We're braced for enemy contact down here at the camp - fire up that signal and be ready to defend the antenna!

passages.title: Signal Boost
passages.text:
The distress signal got through. We'll be evacuated to Greywatch immediately.

I'm afraid that, for now, you will have to continue on your mission without us. Once we are settled, I will send out recon patrols to see if we can glean the location of the Aegis.

You must secure the Aegis of Aggramar if we are to drive back the Legion threat!

passages.title: Return to the Grove
passages.text:
Now that my clan is assembled, we shall return to the Grove of Cenarius.

Speak to Malfurion when you arrive. We will find out the cause of Cenarius' illness.

passages.title: Return to the Grove
passages.text: Wonderful. The Archdruids have already assembled.

passages.title: Death to the Witchmother
passages.text:
The numberless years of my life have been dedicated to learning and perfecting the arts of healing and restoration.

Nothing in this world pains me more than taking a life, traveler.

It is with a heavy heart that I must commission the death of Magula, the leader of the harpies that threaten this grove.

May her death save the lives of more noble beings.

passages.title: Death to the Witchmother
passages.text: Has the terrible deed been accomplished, traveler?

passages.title: Death to the Witchmother
passages.text: May peace again fill our sacred grove.

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: Wrath of Azshara
passages.text:
<name>, Warlord Parjesh ran into the magical vortex just ahead. He has returned to an island off the shore to the southeast where Queen Azshara is staging more of her forces.

The queen is beyond angry because we opposed her. Even now, she is summoning up a monstrosity known as her Wrath to exact revenge for our defiance and drown the Broken Isles.

You must defeat the Wrath of Azshara before the queen lets it loose to destroy us all!

passages.title: Eye of Azshara: Wrath of Azshara
passages.text: <The Tidestone of Golganneth stands whole and unprotected.>

passages.title: The Warchief Beckons
passages.text:
Greetings, adventurer. I am here on behalf of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. I should hope you recognize the name.

<Nathanos thrusts a sealed envelope into your hand.>

Read it and follow me.

You can read, can't you?

passages.title: The Warchief Beckons
passages.text: If only she weren't so specific about bringing you to her unharmed...

passages.title: The Warchief Beckons
passages.text: Satisfied?

passages.title: A Grapple a Day
passages.text:
So these trials are what will get us the Aegis, and the next one is on the top of that mountain? That may prove problematic.

The only way I see up the mountain is through that vrykul city, and the gates are shut tight. We should be able to grapple over, though. If you don't have a launcher, I managed to wrangle a spare from one of these vrykul.

I'll scout ahead and see if I can find a good spot to get in.

passages.title: A Grapple a Day
passages.text:
That looks like it'll do the job nicely. 

Let's get in there before we're spotted.

passages.title: No Wings Required
passages.text:
Now that you've got the launcher, we should be able to infiltrate the city. It looks like there's a good spot to grapple onto on the wall just past us. There's a vantage point on top of this ridge.

Once we're in, I'll try to slip past the guards and get a look at the mountain path. I'd appreciate if you could make some distractions for me. If all goes well, I'll meet up with you in the upper city.

Good luck!

passages.title: No Wings Required
passages.text:
You should've seen the look on those vrykuls' faces when you came sailing over their wall! 

I could see that launcher coming in handy in a lot of places. You'd best hold on to it.

passages.title: Return to the Grove
passages.text:
Now that my grove is safe, I can turn my attention to the threat you speak of.

To hear of Cenarius' plight is disturbing indeed. Tell Malfurion that I shall meet him at the Grove.

passages.title: Return to the Grove
passages.text: Wonderful. The Archdruids have already assembled.

passages.title: Return to the Grove
passages.text:
Forgive me, <race>. Archdruid Moonclaw's fall is a terrible blow...

Malfurion must be informed of what has transpired here. Inform him of Thaon's fate and of the return of Xavius.

Make haste, friend. I fear this may be the greatest threat Val'sharah has ever faced.

passages.title: Return to the Grove
passages.text:
Thaon will be dearly missed. We may not have always seen eye to eye, but he was a great druid and a true protector of the vale.

Xavius will pay for his death...

passages.title: Havi's Test
passages.text:
I could sense your power the moment you arrived in this land. You carry great purpose and a heavy task.

Know that the Aegis of Agrammar rests in the high halls of the All-Father. Only if you prove your valor, can you claim it against your foe.

Many trials must you face for this, but first I must know your strength. My stew is incomplete, and my old bones couldn't carry the ingredients up the hill. 

You look like you have a good arm. Will you help an old man finish his stew?

passages.title: Havi's Test
passages.text: Smells good, doesn't it?

passages.title: Havi's Test
passages.text:
Hah, you throw like a shieldmaiden!

What? That's a good thing! 

Try the stew, young champion, and savor the taste of a task well done.

passages.title: A Little Kelp From My Foes
passages.text:
I'm not sure what yer doin' here, but ye have my thanks. If ye want to get any further, though, ye'll need to get past that foul dog, Guarm.

I've tried meself a few times, and I think I have a plan. If we can get some of the seaweed these kvaldir wear, we might be able to trick the mutt. Guarm's mean, ye see, but not too smart.

What do ye say? Think ye can take on a few kvaldir?

passages.title: A Little Kelp From My Foes
passages.text: Do ye have enough for a proper disguise?

passages.title: A Little Kelp From My Foes
passages.text:
Wait... ye killed how many kvaldir? Yer braver than I thought, outsider!

I'm sure Helya will see that neither ye nor I belong here once we get past that dog of hers.

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text:
Well, the bridge option is out. You still got that grapple launcher handy?

It looks like we can get across from the top of that tower over there. First thing's first, though, we'll need to deal with the big ugly sitting out front.

You take point.

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text: Well, we made it this far...

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text: Well, there's no stopping you, is there?

passages.title: The Windrunner's Fate
passages.text:
Finding Sylvanas is our only priority!

We will cover more ground if we split up. I will lead a team into the hills above the enemy's camp while you search the wreckage itself for any signs of the crew.

Once we've cleared the high ground, I will meet you at the far end of the beach.

passages.title: The Windrunner's Fate
passages.text: So, she escaped after all...

passages.title: Wrath of the Blightcaller
passages.text:
The Alliance dogs have bitten off more than they can chew. They have attacked the Banshee Queen, and invoked the wrath of her champion!

Like my bow, my axes, and my hounds, you will be an agent of vengeance. Pile the bodies high, <class>, and know that I am doing the same. When next we meet, I expect to see blood upon your hands.

passages.title: Wrath of the Blightcaller
passages.text: I have no use for soft buffoons! Begone if you haven't the stomach for vengeance!

passages.title: Wrath of the Blightcaller
passages.text: They have only begun to pay for their insolence.

passages.title: A Grim Trophy
passages.text:
It would seem Sylvanas does not wish to be followed - by us or anyone else.

Her will is her own, it is not my place to question. Only to obey.

In the hills nearby, a gryphon master is preparing to take flight, no doubt to pursue our queen from the sky. My rangers are lying in wait - we need only to close our jaws around him.

I will have his head when this is over.

passages.title: A Grim Trophy
passages.text: Do you have his head?

passages.title: A Grim Trophy
passages.text:
Look carefully at this head, <name>. This is what comes to those who stand against the Forsaken.

For now, we should begin our search for the Aegis of Agrammar. I will send some scouts out to discern its location. You should start your search as well. 

What are you waiting for?

passages.title: The Search for the Highlord
passages.text:
Tirion is fading away on that infernal shore... and the Ashbringer with him! We must not waste another moment.

Give the word and we'll set off. We're ready when you are.

passages.title: The Search for the Highlord
passages.text: <Maxwell's eyes seem to struggle to meet your own.>

passages.title: The Search for the Highlord
passages.text: I owe you my life, <name>. We all do.

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text:
I've been doing some nosing around, and it looks like these vrykul are making regular trips up the mountain themselves. They've got some specialized gear for it, so while we're here we should take some.

I'd recommend finding some climbing treads to keep your grip on the slopes, as well as an oiled cloak to keep the rain out. Also, it looks like they carry enchanted lodestones, which seem to keep the lightning at bay. You should probably grab one of those, too.

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text: Did you find everything?

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text: Excellent. These should do well to protect you from the storm.

passages.title: Impalement Insurance
passages.text:
I've got bad news. Those harpoon launchers up on the walls might cause us some problems. 

They can't get at us down here, but once you start climbing that path, they're likely going to try to skewer you.

If you use that grapple launcher, you should be able to get on top of the walls and dismantle them. Watch out for the drakes, though!

passages.title: Impalement Insurance
passages.text:
Hah! I bet they never saw that coming!

Seems like we've got no shortage of obstacles left, though.

passages.title: Above the Winter Moonlight
passages.text:
You should have a good vantage from this tower to grapple over to the mountain path. I can't help you once you're across, but you should be able to take it all the way up to the top. 

I hope you're able to find what you need from the dragons up there. Who knows what the God-King has done to them.

passages.title: Above the Winter Moonlight
passages.text:
You are here for the trial? I'm afraid you might be too late.

This battle with these Felskorn has taken its toll. I am too weak to grant you the power you seek...

But perhaps you may be able to help...

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
In the summit of storms the dragons await. Born of the gods, they will test your will. 

They roost above Hrydshal, where their children serve the Drekirjar. But they are no allies to man or vrykul, and so you must earn their blessing as they see fit.

A friend of yours awaits in Hrydshal, no doubt searching for the answers you now possess. Go to her, and together, you will test your might against the storm!

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
It's good to see you, <name>. Greymane sent me away to scout this village for more information on the Aegis. 

I haven't gleaned much so far, other than that the locals here don't seem so friendly. Of course, when are they ever?

I hope your search fares better.

passages.title: A United Force
passages.text:
The paladins of Azeroth must stand united behind a single leader. With Tirion's passing, you are the one most worthy to wear the mantle of Highlord.

If you agree to accept this duty, inscribe your name into the Libram of Ancient Kings and I will address the masses on your behalf.

The Order of the Silver Hand is reborn, with you as its champion!

passages.title: A United Force
passages.text: Yes, Highlord?

passages.title: A United Force
passages.text:
We've done it, Highlord <name>.

The Order of the Silver Hand is reborn!

passages.title: We Meet at Light's Hope
passages.text:
With you on our side, I know the Legion will fall! But before we march on the Broken Isles, we must put Highlord Tirion to rest.

There is but one place suitable for a paladin of his caliber... Light's Hope Sanctum, a secret bastion of the Light hidden beneath our chapel.

Paladins the world over are on their way to the ceremony. I know Tirion would want you there most of all.

passages.title: We Meet at Light's Hope
passages.text:
It is fitting that you are here.

Time and again, you have fought to save our world. Now, I fear I must ask you to undertake an even greater act of service.

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
In the summit of storms the dragons await. Born of the gods, they will test your will. 

They roost above Hrydshal, where their children serve the Drekirjar. But they are no allies to man or vrykul, and so you must earn their blessing as they see fit.

A friend of yours awaits in Hrydshal, no doubt searching for the answers you now possess. Go to her, and together, you will test your might against the storm!

passages.title: Will of the Thorignir
passages.text:
These vrykul are so boring! Why does Nathanos send me on missions like this? Does he really think the Aegis is here?

I hope you've come to stir up some trouble.

passages.title: A Grapple a Day
passages.text:
So some old magic vrykul is helping us out? I guess that's good, but this trial of yours might be tricky. You see, the only way up that mountain, is through those big walls.

You know, the ones with the mean-looking drakes on them.

I scouted a bit, but couldn't get too far without those drakes trying to make lunch out of poor Duchess. The vrykul have them trained, which can't be good.

I say we sneak in. I managed to snag a few grapple launchers earlier. Grab one and meet me outside the city walls.

passages.title: A Grapple a Day
passages.text: Yes, that should do quite nicely.

passages.title: No Wings Required
passages.text:
That thing looks like it's got the range to get us over the wall. There's a good spot to hook onto right past us - you should be able to spot it from here.

Once you're inside, do me a favor and see if you can distract the guards so I can slip through. I'll see what else I can find out about these vrykul.

passages.title: No Wings Required
passages.text:
Those vrykul were so distracted seeing someone flying through their village, they never noticed me slip by. 

I hope that didn't get you too much unwanted attention.

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text:
When I was scouting this place out, I noticed the vrykul here are no strangers to the treacherous mountain path we're trying to get to. They've got some specialized equipment they're using, and if I were you I'd try to get my hands on some.

You'll want to find some climbing treads to keep your grip and an oiled cloak to keep you dry. They've also got these stones they carry to keep the lightning at bay, so you'll want to pick one of those up as well.

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text: Were you able to get all the gear you needed?

passages.title: To Weather the Storm
passages.text:
Well, the sizing might be a bit big, but I think you can make them work. 

That path doesn't look pleasant, so it'll help to be prepared.

passages.title: Impalement Insurance
passages.text:
It looks like the elements aren't the only thing you'll need to worry about going up that path. Those harpoon launchers on the wall look pretty nasty, and unless we take them out first, they're likely to make short work of anyone trying to scale that path.

They're up on top of the walls, so you'll need to use that grapple launcher to get to them. Just try not to end up drake food!

passages.title: Impalement Insurance
passages.text:
We won't have to worry about those scrap heaps anymore! 

It looks like we've got a hitch in our plan though. That bridge was the only way up.

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text:
Wait, do you still have that grapple launcher? I think you can still get to the path if you can launch from the top of that tower. The gap doesn't seem too bad there.

Of course, we'll have to take out the big guy out front first. He looks tough, but I think we have a chance if we can flank him.

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text: This should be a piece of cake!

passages.title: Another Way
passages.text:
What a fight! 

And here I thought this place would be boring.

passages.title: Above the Winter Moonlight
passages.text:
There, it looks like there's a good spot to launch to right across from here. This path should take you all the way to the top.

According to my intel, your dragons should be up there. Let's just hope that they're still in a state to help you.

passages.title: Above the Winter Moonlight
passages.text:
You are here for the trial? I'm afraid you might be too late.

This battle with these Felskorn has taken its toll. I am too weak to grant you the power you seek...

But perhaps you may be able to help...

passages.title: The Farmsteads
passages.text:
Forgive us, stranger. Mayor Heathrow has been under a lot of stress recently.

I can't blame him: his own daughter, Penelope, has been missing for two days.

In fact, we could use information on several farmsteads to the south: Mayor Heathrow's house, Granny Marl's farm, and the Radcliffes' dock. Can you go check on the situation out there?

Help us, and perhaps the mayor's heart will soften.

passages.title: The Farmsteads
passages.text: How does it look out there?

passages.title: The Farmsteads
passages.text:
I'm sorry for my suspicion earlier. We're all on edge with the recent attacks.

I couldn't be more grateful to you and your friend.

Thanks to you, our situation is under control now. We've got a lot of rebuilding to do, but we'll survive.

passages.title: Answering Aggression
passages.text:
I weep for the Nightborne this day.

<Silgryn gestures out the door.>

Elisande demonstrates the ultimate disdain for her people. So many lives... wasted!

All to relay a message: This is what happens to those who defy her.

<name>, my friend, we must answer her. We must show her that she cannot slay her people without retribution.

Fight back, <name>.

passages.title: Answering Aggression
passages.text: It had to be done.

passages.title: An Urgent Gathering
passages.text:
A critical decision must be made, <name>.

The Legion devastated our forces at the Broken Shore. The mightiest army this world has ever known was reduced to cinders in moments.

We must gather those with the conviction to save our home. Travard of Tyr's Guard and Orik Trueheart have each made plans to do just that, but we must not let them walk alone.

I ask that you seek them out and guide them to Krasus' Landing so that we may make this decision together.

passages.title: An Urgent Gathering
passages.text: Thank you for helping us gather together, <name>. We must stand united.

passages.title: The Rook's Guard
passages.text:
Black Rook Hold is not the same place I knew. Its walls have crumbled, a ghostly echo of its former glory.

If Lord Ravencrest has returned, then surely he will have his former officers at his side.

Kester Farseeker, captain of the guard.

Trelan Shieldbreaker, peerless master of maces.

Starlys Strongbow, who could split arrows while blindfolded.

If we stand any chance of entering the tower itself, they must be eliminated.

passages.title: The Rook's Guard
passages.text: Warriors and fighters came from across kaldorei lands to pledge loyalty to Master Ravencrest. We would have followed him to the ends of the earth.

passages.title: The Rook's Guard
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. May their spirits be at peace.

passages.title: The Runes that Bind
passages.text:
The stone tablet here describes a ritual where a powerful spirit can be broken into weaker pieces by binding them to special runestones. It looks like the Bonespeakers may be using this very ritual to weaken the spirit of Ashildir.

It may be impossible to summon her with her spirit so weakened. The rituals must be stopped.

passages.title: The Runes that Bind
passages.text:
These mystics have gone to great lengths to weaken Ashildir. 

We must hope that her spirit is strong enough for the wakening.

passages.title: Return to the Broken Shore
passages.text:
Fear not, <name>. I'm angry, but I don't chase my own death.

We will fly in and scout the ideal point of attack. The demons are still drunk on their victory, but we will put a swift end to their revelry!

Take my spare mount and we will fly to the Broken Shore. There we will bring honor to our dead.

passages.title: Return to the Broken Shore
passages.text: Welcome to Skyhold, hero. Normally one must die to gain entrance, but times have changed.

passages.title: Secrets of Highmountain
passages.text:
Mayla's father, Ulan, was our last high chieftain. He was slain trying to stop the Underking from seizing the Hammer of Khaz'goroth.

I have watched Mayla all her life and can tell you she has both the courage and the strength to wear the mantle of High Chieftain.

She needs only our help to realize it herself.

Will you meet us at the city entrance along the southern bluff? There is a ritual that might help, but we will need your aid to survive it.

passages.title: Secrets of Highmountain
passages.text: Ah, thank you for coming. Mayla is as stubborn as her father if not more so.

passages.title: The Call of Icecrown
passages.text:
<A powerful presence again touches your thoughts.>

I have ordered your brethren to Icecrown to prepare for the coming conflict, but I have a more important fate in mind for you. You, <name>, will be the hand of our vengeance!

Use the Death Gate to return to Acherus and I shall reveal your role in this.

passages.title: The Call of Icecrown
passages.text: It is time to begin, <name>.

passages.title: The Call of Icecrown
passages.text:
The Lich King made a wise choice in giving you those blades, <name>. You've more then proven yourself worthy of them.

I have to admit though, I'm glad it wasn't me, I'm through with having magical weapons dictate my fate.

passages.title: By Any Means
passages.text:
We need to figure out what rock Varedis is hiding under - the only way we're going to do that is by getting inside this prison.

Do what you must.

passages.title: By Any Means
passages.text: A truly impressive display.

passages.title: By Any Means
passages.text: Suramar is not far from here.

passages.title: Whispers from the Dark
passages.text:
We still have little knowledge of the Horde's activities in the region, but I'm hoping you can help change that.

Lately the woods have been crawling with Sylvanas' agents. The few we have taken out carried orders from her Dark Rangers, who are no doubt in command of her forces here.

While you're on the hunt, keep an eye out for any scouting orders. They may help us pinpoint Sylvanas' objective in the area.

passages.title: Whispers from the Dark
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: Whispers from the Dark
passages.text:
Excellent. The puzzle is finally coming together. 

We may not know why Sylvanas' forces are here, but I think we know where they are.

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
Our course is now clear. We must enter the vault and prevent Sylvanas from obtaining the power to create more Val'kyr. 

The entrance is barred, which is likely what has kept her out so far, but you may have already uncovered the key to this barrier.

You must become the next ascendant.

Complete the rites as depicted on the shields and take down the barrier to the vault. I will send word to Greymane of our findings - he will wish to confront Sylvanas himself.

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
It is good to see you, <name>. 

The assault on Dreadwake's Landing fared poorly, and I had thought our cause lost until Crowley informed me of your success.

Now, let's finish this!

passages.title: Dreadwake's Dilemma
passages.text:
The situation has taken a dire turn, <name>. We were unprepared for Greymane's sudden assault, with only a token force left behind at Dreadwake's Landing, and we are paying the toll.

The beach is now swarming with worgen infiltrators, and if the cannons breach our defenses, they will likely swarm in on us. We're spread too thin here to take the fight to them, but you could change that.

Wipe them out.

passages.title: Dreadwake's Dilemma
passages.text:
It looks like the ravens will feast on worgen flesh today, <class>.

Well done.

passages.title: To Skold-Ashil
passages.text:
Thanks to your initiative, <class>, the situation at Dreadwake's Landing is under control. We have no time to rest on our laurels, however - Sylvanas's mission must still be carried out.

The dark rangers are heading up operations in Skold-Ashil from the tower overlooking the river junction. Seek them out there, and see if you can aid in completing this task.

passages.title: To Skold-Ashil
passages.text:
You seem surprised to find me here? I was surprised as well, to find that my forces were unable to even breach the city of these cursed vrykul! 

The time has come to employ some different tactics, and your arrival couldn't have been more fortuitous.

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
It would seem that the engravings depict a rite of ascension, which allows the shieldmaidens to enter the vault. I believe we can use this to our advantage.

You must become the next ascendant.

Go to the temple and perform the rites. Should you need to wade through the corpses of the shieldmaidens to do so, then so be it. 

Find me when you have completed this task, and we will take the vault for the Horde!

passages.title: Becoming the Ascendant
passages.text:
The hero returns, and with the barrier disabled. I will see that you are commended for this. 

But first, we must claim this vault!

passages.title: The Hunt
passages.text:
This hunt is yours to lead, <name> - a select few Illidari will join you to make sure Varedis meets his end.

The rest of us must stay behind; a small team will have the best chance of making it to his hold undetected.

We will meet you at Krasus' Landing to see you off when you are ready.

passages.title: The Hunt
passages.text:
What of the others? Did they...?

I see. They gave their lives for a worthy cause - the Twinblades will change the tide of this war, mark my words.

passages.title: Nursing the Wounds
passages.text:
I know why Mayla sent you. But as you have seen, the drogbar are not the only threat to Highmountain.

I will not send forces to support until we deal with the minions of High Crawliac.

If you want to help, find my shaman. He was supposed to be dispersing these fires that are ravaging my village.

He was last seen heading for his spirit lodge to the south just before these Cinderwitches descended on us.

passages.title: Nursing the Wounds
passages.text: These harpies are all over the place!

passages.title: Nursing the Wounds
passages.text:
Julan is dead? He was a good shaman and full of life. Not as morbid as some of these spiritwalkers.

I will miss his laughter tonight.

passages.title: Hags of a Feather
passages.text:
The drogbar you freed me from were unusually aggressive. The tribe in the nearby caves seems to be apart from the rest of them, but that didn't stop the Bloodtotem from going on the offensive just in case, capturing some of their number.

That move left the woods exposed to the harpies, however. Your help dealing with these witches would not go unnoticed by Torok. Bring back their feathers as proof of death.

passages.title: Hags of a Feather
passages.text: Your size belies your strength, <name>.

passages.title: Hags of a Feather
passages.text: I could hear them screeching from here. With this victory and the defeat of the Witch of the Wood, Torok will surely be willing to see you.

passages.title: A Gift for Greymane
passages.text:
It looks like the Gilnean infiltrators brought some heavy ordnance to the fight. It's likely they intend to use them on the walls of Dreadwake's Landing.

If these could be rigged to Greymane's ship, it could make for a decisive end to his assault on the outpost.

passages.title: A Gift for Greymane
passages.text: <insert>

passages.title: A Gift for Greymane
passages.text:
By the Dark Lady's favor, you did it! I witnessed the explosion from here - there's no way that Greymane could have survived such destruction! 

You have done a great deed today for the Forsaken. Rest assured, it will be remembered.

passages.title: The Eagle Spirit's Blessing
passages.text:
The spear is linked to a spirit called Ohn'ahra. It has been tradition for us to speak with her and receive her blessing before going after the spear. She may also impart some knowledge.

If you would accompany me to Spiritwatch Point, I will summon the Eagle Spirit and ask for its blessing in the coming fight.

passages.title: The Eagle Spirit's Blessing
passages.text: We've done it!

passages.title: The Eagle Spirit's Blessing
passages.text: We saved the Eagle Spirit and received her blessing. I feel even more confident we will get Talonclaw now!

passages.title: Assaulting the Haglands
passages.text:
Proceed on foot into the Haglands and slay any harpies you find.

Quell their numbers!

We will provide air support and force your prey to the ground where you can deal with them.

Show these witches the fury of your... well... your "you."

passages.title: Assaulting the Haglands
passages.text: It has been many years since we have had to enter the Haglands in force.

passages.title: Assaulting the Haglands
passages.text: Haha! You are covered in the feathers of your enemies.

passages.title: Cave of the Blood Trial
passages.text:
All Bloodtotem and distinguished guests must go through a trial of blood in the cavern beneath this outpost.

I hope it's a good sign that they wish you to participate in this rite of passage. You will need to show proof of your deeds, defeat a Warmonger in single combat, then perform sacrifice at an altar deep in the cavern.

passages.title: Cave of the Blood Trial
passages.text: Are you afraid of the dark?

passages.title: Cave of the Blood Trial
passages.text: They said an outsider would wield the Hammer of Khaz'goroth. I doubt you could even lift it.

passages.title: Cut Out the Heart
passages.text:
This map points out the strategic locations of the Forsaken forces around Greywatch. A marker to the east indicates an apothecary camp where Dread-Riders are being supplied from.

If you were to take out the apothecary in charge of creating this plague, it could stem the invasion and prevent the Dread-Riders from spreading the plague any further.

passages.title: Cut Out the Heart
passages.text:
To think that the Forsaken were brash enough to brew their blight in our own backyard. With the loss of their apothecary, their invasion force is left without teeth. 

You have done well, <name>.

passages.title: Infestation
passages.text:
Those bugs are destroying our crops and attack any of us who get near them.

Would you exterminate some of those vile creatures?

passages.title: Infestation
passages.text: With fewer of those insects out there, I can tend to some of the crops.

passages.title: The Flow of the River
passages.text:
We can leave Farmer Maya in charge of the farmland now that the greatest threat has been reduced.

But we aren't out of hot water just yet, <name>. The fisheries are just as important as our fields, and they are in even greater danger than the farm if what Angler Creel says is true.

passages.title: The Flow of the River
passages.text: I'm glad you arrived when you did. The drogbar are increasing their aggression as we speak.

passages.title: Ahead of the Game
passages.text:
The watcher Yotnar keeps the vault, and he is a fickle one. Challengers come from far and wide seeking the trials, but the watcher chooses not to see.

If you wish to catch his eye, show him you are worth being seen.

Some of these challengers await in camps throughout the Valley of the Sword. Bring their heads to Yotnar, so that he may see them, and you.

passages.title: Ahead of the Game
passages.text: An ironic gift you bring me, challenger.

passages.title: Ahead of the Game
passages.text:
It is a shame to see the first worthy challenger for the Aegis treating the trials with such disrespect. Such hubris cannot win the Aegis, for the gods will surely strike him down for his arrogance.

You, however, seem different. You have shown that you are a worthy challenger. 

I will allow you to begin the trials.

passages.title: A Trial of Valor
passages.text:
To seek the Aegis of Aggramar, a champion must complete three great trials before riding into glorious battle through the Gates of Valor. Here you will find the knowledge of the trials you must seek out, as well as the first challenge you must face.

Above us, adorning the central plateau, you will find the archive for the Trial of Valor. Seek it out, and learn where your path leads.

passages.title: A Trial of Valor
passages.text:
You have learned of the obstacles you must face. 

Do you still wish to continue?

passages.title: A Trial of Will
passages.text:
Upon the highest point of the plateau above, you will find the archive device for the Trial of Will. Seek it out to learn what awaits you in Thorim's Peak. 

Be on your guard, outsider. The one called Skovald has left behind many of his army, and they will no doubt be unfriendly.

passages.title: A Trial of Will
passages.text:
The knowledge you've gained is a powerful tool to use against your foes. 

Do not forget this.

passages.title: A Ring Unbroken
passages.text:
Our defeat at the Broken Shore was decisive. The Burning Legion has a foothold on Azeroth, and the best of our armies are retreating in tatters.

The elders of the Earthen Ring have called an emergency council near the heart of our world - the Maelstrom. <name>, your triumphs throughout Azeroth and Draenor are the stuff of legend. We need you more than ever.

Join me at the Maelstrom. Stormcaller Mylra will be flying there shortly - find her at Krasus' Landing here in Dalaran.

passages.title: A Ring Unbroken
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. You saved me. You saved us all.

I was... outmatched. My relationship with the elements has changed since the events on Draenor. I have some soul-searching to do. <name>, you must carry the Earthen Ring forward without me. You are the leader they need.

passages.title: The Voice of Thunder
passages.text:
The White Tiger has prepared a series of challenges for everyone who wants to possess the weapons of the storm.

Now you know of their power - these are the very artifacts that Ra-den himself wielded during the age of the Titans.

Come! I have led arena teams to victory across three continents. With me in your corner, you cannot lose!

passages.title: The Voice of Thunder
passages.text: We have trained our whole lives for this, <name>. We cannot fail.

passages.title: The Voice of Thunder
passages.text:
You really are the chosen one, <name>. I will gladly lay down my life for you.

Wherever you take the Earthen Ring, I will follow!

passages.title: Lay Them to Rest
passages.text:
I would ask a favor, outsider.

As you step through the graves of ancient heroes, you will no doubt come across spirits of the restless dead, agitated by the Bonespeakers misdeeds. They must be returned to the earth where they are buried, so that they may be judged as well.

Take this bough - it carries with it the essence of the Runewood. Channel its power into a weakened spirit, and it will return to rest.

passages.title: Lay Them to Rest
passages.text:
I see you carry a branch of the Runewood. Then it was you who laid the spirits to rest? 

Though I do not know your purpose, outsider, I appreciate what you have done for our people.

passages.title: Greymane's Gambit
passages.text:
The Skyfire is prepared to make way to Stormheim. Should we become engaged, I will require my best fighters on the front line.

This includes you, <class>.

passages.title: Greymane's Gambit
passages.text:
It seems you were spared the brunt of the explosion. If only Greymane were so lucky...

On your feet! We had better get a move on before the Forsaken are on top of us!

passages.title: The Splintered Fleet
passages.text:
Preparations have been made, and we are ready to set sail.

We must strike out at once. Do not dally, or you will be left behind.

passages.title: The Splintered Fleet
passages.text:
Hey, you're alive! I guess Withers isn't as crazy as I thought.

It's a miracle you escaped the Skyfire alive! The pieces of that thing must be scattered all over these mountains after that explosion!

passages.title: An Unworthy Task
passages.text:
This place is Helheim, the realm of the unworthy dead. Here, the spirits of the dishonorable spend eternity in an endless futile battle, always seeking glory but never able to attain it.

We should not be here.

We must find a way out. I will scout ahead - you should try and release some of these captive spirits here. Perhaps one may have some answers for us.

passages.title: An Unworthy Task
passages.text:
Free at last! 

The kvaldir caught me while I was tryin' to put together a plan to sneak past that foul dog, Guarm, and have had me locked up ever since! 

I thought surely my fate was sealed.

passages.title: Sundered
passages.text:
I imagine the power of your weapon will be what allows us to defeat Geir, but right now you are too weak for the confrontation. We must reclaim the missing pieces of your spirit.

Helya must have scattered them throughout her realm to keep them from you. If you can find them, shine the lantern and they should be set free.

Be careful, though. It is unlikely that Helya left your spirit fragments unguarded.

passages.title: Sundered
passages.text: Have you recovered your power?

passages.title: Sundered
passages.text:
Yes, I can feel your power returned. 

Helya will regret the day she challenged one such as you.

passages.title: Huln's War - The Arrival
passages.text:
Huln Highmountain is the origin of our strength as a tribe. He bested the Legion when last they threatened our survival and unified many disparate tribes.

Live his story, and you will know why his name imbues courage in the cowardly and sows fear in the fearless.

passages.title: Huln's War - The Arrival
passages.text: [In broken Common] Feathered one said you come. Unng Ak not hope for you come. Tauren have thanks.

passages.title: Trail of Echoes
passages.text:
The Nightborne could prove powerful allies against the Legion. We must aid this Thalyssra if we can.

We should be able to find her by tracking her magical echoes, the same way I found her distress call.

I can teleport you near the location where she recorded that message. From there, you must search for ripples in the very fabric of the arcane itself.

My wand should do the trick. Follow the sparks it creates--they should lead you to places where Thalyssra used her magic.

passages.title: Trail of Echoes
passages.text: Who are you?

passages.title: Trail of Echoes
passages.text:
An outlander...

You received my message?

passages.title: Stem the Tide
passages.text:
Skovald has profaned the Gates of Valor with his demonic allies. Among his forces his twisted mystics have conjured portals to ferry his fel allies from their blighted worlds. 

If we wish to stem this tide, these portals must be destroyed. 

I will gather my allies. Take this horn and signal when you have found a portal, and we will strike from the skies!

passages.title: Stem the Tide
passages.text: The portals must be closed if we wish to stop Skovald's forces!

passages.title: Stem the Tide
passages.text:
I do not understand, the portals are closed and yet Skovald's demonic forces still assault the gates! 

We must find where they are coming from!

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Securing the Aegis
passages.text:
The Felskorn may be broken, but the head of the beast yet lives. The God-King will still vie for the Aegis if left unchecked.

You, who have completed trials upon trials, must not let this come to pass. You must claim the Aegis over Skovald's broken bones!

The Halls of Valor await!

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Securing the Aegis
passages.text: With the God-King's defeat, the Aegis of Aggramar is yours to claim.

passages.title: A Heavy Burden
passages.text:
With Ashildir's judgment, your final trial is complete. 

But even Valhallas can wait, for now we must eat! Being dead works up quite an appetite.

Come now, bring some of that fish to roast over the fire. It is far too heavy for me to carry.

passages.title: A Heavy Burden
passages.text:
It is clear that your cooking prowess is only matched by your might in combat. 

Now, on full bellies, we ride to Valhallas!

passages.title: The Story of Huln
passages.text:
You work to unite the tribes. That is no small task. It has only been done once before in the history of this mountain.

Huln Highmountain last united the tribes thousands of years ago to take on the Legion during the War of the Ancients.

passages.title: The Story of Huln
passages.text: The history of this place extends beyond our limited memory.

passages.title: The Story of Huln
passages.text: You have seen only a taste of what Huln Highmountain accomplished during his lifetime. Let us delve deeper into the past...

passages.title: The Hammer in the Deep
passages.text:
<Thrall listens intently.>

You found it! The Doomhammer fell to the Crumbling Depths... But the Legion remains a step ahead of us. If we hurry, we can follow the demon Geth'xun and retrieve the hammer before any more of this realm is corrupted.

Therazane will open a portal directly there. Let's go!

passages.title: The Hammer in the Deep
passages.text: What of the Doomhammer?

passages.title: The Hammer in the Deep
passages.text:
The orcs had a prophecy about the Doomhammer. It was said that a stranger will raise the hammer high, and with it, justice shall reign. Maybe... maybe YOU were meant to be that stranger all along.

Come, <name>. The Earthen Ring needs you. And Azeroth needs us.

passages.title: A Ring Reforged
passages.text:
Speak with Nobundo, and take your place around the circle, <name>. The Earthen Ring will rise again, with you as its leader!

Within these stones stands the legendary Heart of Azeroth, which we can use as a base of operations. Perhaps the power of your artifact can unseal the hidden chambers...

passages.title: A Ring Reforged
passages.text: The Alliance and Horde are in chaos. If we are to save Azeroth, we <class> must bind together!

passages.title: A Ring Reforged
passages.text:
The Earthen Ring rises once more to defend Azeroth. You will be our Farseer, <name>, and we will be your instruments. Only by working together can we preserve our world.

We are yours to command, Farseer.

passages.title: The Dawning Light
passages.text:
It was a miracle that you were able to survive, <name>. It is with great sorrow that I have to say that Grand Master Hight was not so lucky. His spirit now rests with the ancestors.

Now we must look to a new leader for our order, our broken temple. I have spoken with the other masters and we are all of one mind on this.

We all agree that new leader should be you, <name>. You have shown strength, wisdom, courage, and kindness beyond measure.

Walk with us to the temple and we will announce our decision.

passages.title: The Dawning Light
passages.text: Congratulations, Grand Master <name>!

passages.title: Asking a Favor
passages.text:
Caria Felsoul was one of our best... before she answered the Legion's foul call.

She now wields the Aldrachi Warblades - the soul-rending armaments of the ancient race's greatest champion, who fell only to Sargeras himself.

We sent a party to track Caria down, but we have not heard from them in some time. Jace has nearly repaired a Legion communicator so we can make contact - we need only a power source.

Could you ask Khadgar for assistance? Our friends in this world are few.

passages.title: Asking a Favor
passages.text: It's good to see you again. If there's anything I can do to help you take the fight to the Legion, just let me know.

passages.title: An Unexpected Message
passages.text:
Ah, Felo'melorn. I am familiar with this weapon. 

For ages the Council of Tirisfal attempted to recover the blade. Its control over the primal forces of fire would be devastating in the wrong hands. 

As luck would have it, an associate of mine, Archmage Modera has recently uncovered some information on this artifact. This crystal contains a message from her.

I suggest you start your search there. The portal over there will bring you back to the city.

passages.title: An Unexpected Message
passages.text:
<name>, I'm glad you came.

I've found information on just the thing we need to turn this war in our favor.

passages.title: The Path of Atonement
passages.text:
Felo'melorn, the runeblade of the kings of Quel'Thalas. It was said to harness the very essence of flame and after being reforged by Kael'thas could even stand against the legendary Frostmourne.

We thought that the blade was lost with Kael'thas's death but an associate of mine has a lead on where it may be located.

We need every advantage we can get and with Felo'melorn in your hand the Legion surely will tremble!

Ah, our company is here.

passages.title: The Path of Atonement
passages.text:
Our next journey will be to Icecrown, <name>.

There, in the heart of the Scourge, we will find Felo'melorn.

passages.title: Call of the Marksman
passages.text:
Time is of the essence! If Alleria and Thas'dorah are in Legion hands, it is only a matter of time until both are forfeit.

If you are ready, head to the Broken Shore to meet with Ranger-General Windrunner.

She has lent her personal hippogryph to fly you down to the surface.

passages.title: Call of the Marksman
passages.text:
The Farstriders have been interrogating captured demons.

One of the vile creatures claims to know the whereabouts of someone... crucial to our cause.

passages.title: Ulthalesh, the Deadwind Harvester
passages.text:
The book says the Dark Riders were last seen in a place called Manor Mistmantle. If friend can find these riders, then <he/she> can get Ulthalesh!

Calydus will wait here and await your return. Find Ulthalesh, friend!

passages.title: Ulthalesh, the Deadwind Harvester
passages.text: And just why should I help you, <class>?

passages.title: Ulthalesh, the Deadwind Harvester
passages.text:
I am left with little choice. I cannot face another Dark Rider ambush alone, and you are obviously formidable.

I will help you find the weapon you seek, but only if you will allow me to return the others in their possession to their rightful place.

Do we have a deal, <class>?

passages.title: To See the Past
passages.text:
I would like for you to experience firsthand what Huln Highmountain was able to accomplish in a single battle during the War of the Ancients.

To do so, I will need very specific ingredients. They are not too difficult to obtain--you can find all of them near Thunder Totem.

passages.title: To See the Past
passages.text: Earth, air, and water are all magics we have come to know well in our mountain.

passages.title: To See the Past
passages.text: Ah, these will be perfect for what is in store.

passages.title: Following the Curse
passages.text:
Very well. I suppose an introduction is in order. I am Revil Kost, priest of the Light and a seeker of lost artifacts. I've dealt with the Dark Riders before, and have returned to rid this place of them.

The Riders are elusive, but I may have a clue to their whereabouts. In our previous confrontation, I was able to see a glimpse into their past. Granted blessed vision by the Cloak of Purity, I saw the Dark Riders for who they were before.

Come with me to Ariden's camp. I will explain on the way.

passages.title: Following the Curse
passages.text:
It's strange that the Dark Riders haven't followed us here, but I will take whatever boon I can get.

I believe the key to finding the Dark Riders is here somewhere. Let us begin our search.

passages.title: Disturbing the Past
passages.text:
This place is where the merchant, Ariden, set up camp while he was trying to ply his dubious wares to the sorcerer Medivh. It has remained strangely untouched for all this time, which leads me to believe it may still have a connection to its former owner.

Help me search the camp. Let's see if we can find something to lead us to the Dark Riders.

passages.title: Disturbing the Past
passages.text:
Otherwise an ordinary looking journal, this book hums with dark energy as you approach it.

A quick scan of the writing reveals this as the journal of Ariden, and chronicles his time in Deadwind Pass. Toward the end of the journal, the writing begins to change, and the tone becomes noticeably darker. It constantly refers to "the curse" and of the endless desire to possess things of great power.

One such entry catches your eye as you glance through.

passages.title: The Fate of Deadwind
passages.text:
The journal mentions a "stronger pull" for the compass. If the spirits of this place are indeed tied to it, they may serve as the pull we need.

I've come upon several locations in the pass where restless spirits tend to appear. Perhaps if you show the spirits there the compass, they may be able to help point it in the right direction.

You seek these locations out. I'll continue on to Karazhan and see if I can find anything leading to the Dark Riders.

passages.title: The Fate of Deadwind
passages.text:
It looks like it worked, and the compass is pointing toward the river. 

Could it be..?

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text:
There's a sewer grate along the edge of the river leading to catacombs underneath Karazhan. I've never paid it much attention, but it could be where the spirits are directing us.

To think, the Dark Riders may have been under our noses this entire time! Come, let us see where this leads.

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text: Did you find what you seek, <class>?

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text:
Today was a great blow against the Dark Riders, and a victory for the people of Duskwood. 

They are in your debt, as am I.

passages.title: Blade in Twilight
passages.text:
I have been working with Moira Thaurissan to infiltrate the Twilight's Hammer cult. We've learned of an ancient and powerful Old God relic, a blade used at various points in history to wreak havoc.

Moira's double agent informs us a new leader is rising, and plans to cement his ascension using this weapon in an unholy ritual. You must find him, stop the ritual, and seize the artifact.

We will meet in Dalaran afterwards.

passages.title: Blade in Twilight
passages.text: Not too difficult a task, I hope!

passages.title: Blade in Twilight
passages.text:
You have demonstrated no small amount of skill in these sorts of tasks.

That is good, for we will require even more of you if we are to survive this conflict.

passages.title: The Sixth
passages.text:
Greetings, warlock. I speak on behalf of the Council of the Black Harvest.

With the Legion invasion upon us, it is painfully clear that our only hope is to grow stronger. The council plans to tap into the Twisting Nether and call forth more powerful demon allies. The ritual is ready, but we are short one number.

No doubt you have heard of the fate that befell Kanrethad Ebonlocke.

You will be his replacement. Do you accept?

passages.title: The Sixth
passages.text:
You have made the right decision.

Let us hope you live up to your reputation.

passages.title: The New Blood
passages.text:
It is time to begin the ritual, warlock. Be prepared, for the summoning we perform today will be more challenging than any you have known or seen before.

Are you ready?

passages.title: The New Blood
passages.text:
Calydus sorry we not save your friends, but maybe they survive if we hurry.

Jagganoth torture them, yes, but he likes to keep victims alive... mostly.

passages.title: The Heart of the Dreadscar
passages.text:
Friend has the artifact! Now Jagganoth does not stand a chance!

Quickly, you must go back to Dreadscar Rift! You may still be able to save your friends from Jagganoth's vengeance.

If you take the heart of the overlord, his army will be yours to command!

passages.title: The Heart of the Dreadscar
passages.text:
The cruel Jagganoth is defeated!

Friend is the new Overlord of the Dreadscar! 

This place will be friend's new home. With the Dreadscar under your control, you can come and go as you please!

passages.title: The Dead and the Damned
passages.text:
<A powerful mind again touches your thoughts.>

Gorelix the Fleshripper is a monstrous demon. The butcher of a thousand worlds, he has exterminated countless races with his axe, the Maw of the Damned.

A group of Ebon Blade was dispatched to slay him but they have gone missing. You will succeed where they failed.

You will not be alone in this, I've sent Baron Sliver ahead to assist you.

Go, obtain the Maw of the Damned and ensure that Gorelix is no more.

passages.title: The Dead and the Damned
passages.text: It is time to begin, <name>.

passages.title: The Dead and the Damned
passages.text:
That axe makes me feel uneasy, <name>. Its power is undeniable, but its very essence embodies the eternal hunger.

We will use it because we must do whatever it takes to win this war. Still, I'd be careful with that weapon if I were you.

passages.title: Shift Change
passages.text:
This is as good a chance as we are going to get to rescue Verene's daughter.

Here is how this is going to work. 

You are going to wait here for the guard to pass by on their way to their guard shift. Look for something to hide in.

<Silgryn marks a spot on your map.>

You will know the guard by their bright red armor.

Follow closely, but not so closely that you are seen. It may be necessary to kill the guard when you reach your destination.

The child's name is Korine. Good luck.

passages.title: Shift Change
passages.text: W-who are you?

passages.title: Shift Change
passages.text: I-I thought... they were gonna... *sniff*

passages.title: The Delicate Art of Telemancy
passages.text:
I hadn't the time to gather my instruments before fleeing the palace. I came here to salvage some equipment.

This old workshop is actually several rooms connected by teleporter pads.

Elisande's goons are already scouring the place looking for me, but from here I can alter the teleporter network and keep them moving in circles.

You go in. I'll monitor your position and ensure the teleporters work normally for you.

Find these two parts and bring them back!

passages.title: The Delicate Art of Telemancy
passages.text: Salvaging the equipment here is necessary if I am to develop a teleporter network for Thalyssra.

passages.title: The Delicate Art of Telemancy
passages.text: These are in rough shape, but they will suffice.

passages.title: A Foe of the Dark
passages.text:
I cannot believe the Dark Riders found us here. Long have they hunted the scythe to sate their lust for the artifacts of Azeroth. We thought we would be protected within the grove...

And now, Valorn is gone...

You must become the hunter, <name>. Seek the Dark Riders and recover the scythe. We last encountered them near Manor Mistmantle in Duskwood. Start your search there.

And <name>... bring justice to Valorn. The rider must pay.

passages.title: A Foe of the Dark
passages.text:
So I was correct, and the Scythe is your quarry.  Know that in order to retrieve it, we must do what no denizen of Duskwood has ever attempted.

We must hunt the Dark Riders.

I have been tracking them for some time since my encounter with them while hunting down the Wolf Cult.  They are a blight upon these lands, and they hold no right to the artifacts they hoard.

If we wish to recover this artifact, we will need to find their lair. Fortunately, I may just have the clue we need.

passages.title: Fate of the Queen's Reprisal
passages.text: <This is the kind of intelligence that should be shared. Perhaps someone at the Greyfang Enclave on Dalaran will know what to do with it.>

passages.title: Fate of the Queen's Reprisal
passages.text:
<The officer looks down at what you're offering him and his eyes light up.>

Do you know what you have here? You might have just delivered some of the most significant intel of the campaign.

I will see to it personally that this gets into Lord Greymane's hands.

passages.title: Following the Curse
passages.text:
In my previous confrontation with your foe, I was able to see a glimpse into their past. Granted blessed vision by the Cloak of Purity, I saw the Dark Riders for who they once were.

Come, we must go to Ariden's Camp in Deadwind Pass. I can explain its significance along the way.

passages.title: Following the Curse
passages.text:
It's strange that the Dark Riders haven't followed us here, but I will take whatever boon I can get.

I believe the key to finding the Dark Riders is here somewhere. Let us begin our search.

passages.title: Disturbing the Past
passages.text:
This place is where the merchant, Ariden, set up camp while he was trying to ply his dubious wares to the sorcerer Medivh. It has remained strangely untouched for all this time, which leads me to believe it may still have a connection to its former owner.

Help me search the camp. Let's see if we can find something to lead us to the Dark Riders.

passages.title: Disturbing the Past
passages.text:
Dark energy hums from the journal, which appears to be the writings of Ariden, and chronicles his time in Deadwind Pass. One entry in particular stands out:

"The Nightbane have become restless of late, and whispers are abound of the Scythe of Elune having left Darnassus. It must be coming nearer, for the worgen are constantly drawn to it. They will lead me to it.

Those cursed night elves think the weapon is safe in their care. They will soon find how wrong they are"

passages.title: The Tears of Elune
passages.text: The Tear of Elune floats effortlessly, glistening in an ethereal pillar of moonlight.

passages.title: The Tears of Elune
passages.text: <Archmage Khadgar has set aside a space here for the Tears of Elune, as well as the rest of the Pillars of Creation.>

passages.title: The Burden Borne
passages.text:
Your assistance against the Dark Riders has proven a great service to the Light. Though our beliefs may separate us, I know that we share one goal.

You have allowed me to fill my purpose in returning these artifacts to their rightful owners, and for this I am thankful. As for the Scythe of Elune, I can think of no safer place than in your care. 

May it serve you well against the Legion, <name>.

passages.title: The Burden Borne
passages.text:
The Scythe of Elune!

I never thought I would see that weapon used without turning its wielder into a savage beast, but you've brought balance to its primal nature.

Elune has certainly guided your hand, <name>. You've accomplished what no <class> has done before!

passages.title: Apocalypse
passages.text:
<The Lich King's chill voice fills your mind once again>

There is an ancient blade, lost in the echoes of time, that has the power to bring my vengeance upon the Legion. 

It is known as Apocalypse.

I've sensed the blade in the possession of the Dark Riders of Deadwind Pass. Their magic conceals them from my sight but they cannot hide from the scourge! They were last seen by my agents near a place called Manor Mistmantle.

Go there, <name>. Defeat the Dark Riders, and claim the blade!

passages.title: Apocalypse
passages.text: And just why should I help you, <class>?

passages.title: Apocalypse
passages.text:
I am left with little choice. I cannot face another Dark Rider ambush alone, and you are obviously formidable.

I will help you find your artifact, but only if you will allow me to return the others in their possession to their rightful place.

Do we have a deal, <class>?

passages.title: Following the Curse
passages.text:
Very well. I suppose an introduction is in order. I am Revil Kost, priest of the Light and a seeker of lost artifacts. I've dealt with the Dark Riders before, and have returned to rid this place of them.

The Riders are elusive, but I may have a clue to their whereabouts. In our previous confrontation, I was able to see a glimpse into their past. Granted blessed vision by the Cloak of Purity, I saw the Dark Riders for who they were before.

Come with me to Ariden's camp. I will explain on the way.

passages.title: Following the Curse
passages.text:
As much as your company pains me, you are proving to be a powerful ally. 

I believe the key to finding the Dark Riders is here somewhere. It is strange that the riders haven't followed us here, but we should make haste lest they change their mind.

passages.title: Disturbing the Past
passages.text:
This place is where the merchant, Ariden, set up camp while he was trying to ply his dubious wares to the sorcerer Medivh. 

It has remained strangely untouched for all this time, which leads me to believe it may still have a connection to its former owner.

Help me search the camp. Let's see if we can find something to lead us to the Dark Riders.

passages.title: Disturbing the Past
passages.text:
Dark energy hums from the journal, which appears to be the writings of Ariden, and chronicles his time in Deadwind Pass. One entry in particular stands out:

"I hear the whispers. They call me from the wet soil of shallow graves, hearkening me to my legacy. 

"But what legacy? The merchant I once was had no special bloodline...

"Nevertheless, I am drawn to it. The dread blade... the world-ender... Apocalypse."

passages.title: A Grisly Task
passages.text:
Wet soil? Shallow graves?

I think the journal is referring to the gravesites off of the lake near Karazhan. Nobody knows who is buried there, but they may be the key to finding the Dark Riders.

You can... speak to the dead, yes?

passages.title: A Grisly Task
passages.text:
The chill down my spine tells me that you must have met with success.

What did you find?

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text:
The catacombs? I've never heard of such a place. Unless, he means...

There's a sewer grate along the edge of the river leading to a catacombs underneath Karazhan. I've never paid it much attention, but it could lead to the catacombs that the spirit spoke of. 

To think, the Dark Riders may have been under our noses this entire time! Come, let us see where this leads.

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text: Didyou find what you seek, <class>?

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text:
Today was a great blow against the Dark Riders, and a victory for the people of Duskwood. 

They are in your debt, as am I.

passages.title: The Call of Vengeance
passages.text:
I was wrong about you, death knight. Your assistance against the Dark Riders has proven a great service to the Light. Perhaps I should not be so quick to judge.

Nevertheless, you have allowed me to fill my purpose in returning these artifacts to their rightful owners. As for Apocalypse, I can think of no safer place than in your care. 

May it serve you well against the Legion, death knight.

passages.title: The Call of Vengeance
passages.text:
The champion of the Lich King returns, and with a mighty weapon to bear against our demon foes!

May the Burning Legion tremble at the sight of our forces!

passages.title: Special Delivery
passages.text:
Verene's child has gone missing. I can guess what happened, but I need to be sure.

Most guardsmen use couriers to relay delicate information. In this, magic is strictly the province of high ranking officials.

Take this blade. Do not touch the cutting edge. Use it to silently waylay the couriers and collect any correspondence they carry.

With any luck, the missives will tell us exactly where to find the girl.

We guards know everything, after all.

<Silgryn offers you a winning smile.>

passages.title: Special Delivery
passages.text: Were you successful?

passages.title: Special Delivery
passages.text: Fine work. I will read these over.

passages.title: Honoring Success
passages.text:
All has gone as planned. Your new blades are a testament to that.

We will demand a great deal of you in the weeks and months to come, as we must. But we would be remiss if we failed to take a moment to celebrate a job well done.

What do you say?

passages.title: Honoring Success
passages.text: It's kill or be killed.

passages.title: Honoring Success
passages.text: It seems you struck a nerve.

passages.title: Hunter to Hunter
passages.text:
Now that you wield Thas'dorah, it's time to learn more about the night elf who set you on this journey

I suggest returning to the Hunter's Reach shop where you met my courier. Whoever this Emmarel Shadewarden is, it seems she has some part to play in the war against the Legion.

passages.title: Hunter to Hunter
passages.text: There is much to do, noble <class>. But first, I suppose you'll want to learn a little more about who I am and why I have sought you out.

passages.title: On Eagle's Wings
passages.text:
Since ancient times, my order has stood vigil on these Broken Isles, watching for the Legion's return. Only a handful of us remain... but that changes today.

The artifact you hold is more than a weapon. It is a symbol that will unite hunters of all kingdoms and creeds.

I'm sure you have questions. Meet me at the Trueshot Lodge in Highmountain and see with your own eyes what awaits us. Snowfeather and I will make our own way there.

passages.title: On Eagle's Wings
passages.text:
I've observed your skills for some time, <name>. Watched you from a distance.

Wait, that sounds a little creepy. Sorry, my social skills are a tad rusty. Let me start again.

Our order has been on the lookout for hunters who could lead the Unseen Path into a new era. No one is more qualified for that role than you.

passages.title: Oath of Service
passages.text:
Assembled before you are many of our world's greatest archers, rangers, beast masters, and trappers, ready to fight the Legion as one.

It is time to take your first step in becoming a true leader of hunters.

We gather at the fire pit and take our oaths of service before the statue of Ohn'ahra. Touch the statue and kneel before it while I recite the oath, and the Unseen Path will be reborn!

passages.title: Oath of Service
passages.text: Ohn'ahra has blessed our order!

passages.title: Oath of Service
passages.text:
Ohn'ahra has not appeared to us since the order's founding!

This is surely a sign that with you guiding us, the Unseen Path will triumph over the Legion!

passages.title: Tactical Matters
passages.text:
Now that your artifact is ready, it's time to plan your first strike against the Legion.

Speak to Tactician Tinderfell, our expert on such matters.

passages.title: Tactical Matters
passages.text: Hail, Pathfinder! It will be my honor to aid you in the fight against the Legion.

passages.title: The Campaign Begins
passages.text:
The Legion believes we are still reeling from our loss on the Broken Shore.

Let's prove them wrong.

Our scouts have mapped out the Broken Isles, learning everything we can about each region for our imminent assault.

Choose where to strike first, and you will lead the Unseen Path's efforts personally.

passages.title: The Campaign Begins
passages.text: Excellent choice. The campaign against the Legion has begun!

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text:
The catacombs? I've never heard of such a place. Unless, he means...

There's a sewer grate along the edge of the river leading to a catacombs underneath Karazhan. I've never paid it much attention, but it could lead to the catacombs that the spirit spoke of. 

To think, the Dark Riders may have been under our noses this entire time! Come, let us see where this leads.

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text: Did you find what you seek, <class>?

passages.title: The Dark Riders
passages.text:
Though I'll admit I may not have been able to do this alone, I will not forget the transgressions that happened today.

You have what you came for, <class>. I think it is time you were on your way.

passages.title: The Call of Vengeance
passages.text:
Our goals have been met, death knight, and it is time we part ways. I think I will be glad to see the last of you.

Go on, return to your dark masters. We are done here.

passages.title: The Call of Vengeance
passages.text:
The champion of the Lich King returns, and with a mighty weapon to bear against our demon foes!

May the Burning Legion tremble at the sight of our forces!

passages.title: The Emperor's Gift
passages.text:
Ah, Sheilun, the legendary staff wielded by our last emperor. If the Legion were to acquire this weapon, they could unleash untold horrors across the whole of the continent. They must be stopped!

If you want to get to the Terrace as fast as possible, you should hitch a ride directly to the mainland. Tak-Tak, a hozen kite-master, is skulking around west of the temple. Speak to him without delay.

passages.title: The Emperor's Gift
passages.text: The Terrace of Eternal Spring is a very sacred place for mainland Pandaren. I hope you were able to preserve it from corruption. Enough of Pandaria was destroyed when Garrosh Hellscream turned it into a battlefield.

passages.title: The Emperor's Gift
passages.text:
Incredible. The very staff the Emperor used to cloak Pandaria in mists all those ages ago!

Treat that staff well, <name>. It will save your life. And probably the lives of all your friends, as well...

passages.title: Hunter to Hunter
passages.text:
Now that Titanstrike is yours, ye should learn more about the night elf who set us on this journey.

She might well be back at the Hunter's Reach shop where you met her. Whoever this Emmarel Shadewarden is, I'd bet me beard she has some part to play in the war against the Legion!

Thanks again fer the fun, <name>. If ye ever have need of me, just call!

passages.title: Hunter to Hunter
passages.text: There is much to do, noble <class>. But first, I suppose you'll want to learn a little more about who I am and why I have sought you out.

passages.title: Actions on Azeroth
passages.text:
Let me show you the Command Map. Thanks to some draenei construction and naaru magic we now have a window into the Broken Isles! You can devise strategy, send your agents on missions, and choose our first area to operate in.

Take a look and let me know where we are going!

passages.title: Actions on Azeroth
passages.text: An excellent choice! We will do our best to support your efforts on the Broken Isles.

passages.title: Power Grid
passages.text:
This station has fallen into disrepair. The circuit is broken, and to mend it we must recharge the seals in the central chamber.

Both a high potency current and low potency current are needed for each seal. Direct the currents to point at the same seal, then engage the seal.

Me? I shall supervise. You are the help, after all.

passages.title: Power Grid
passages.text: I must admit I am impressed. You may actually be of some use to us.

passages.title: The Dreadlord's Prize
passages.text:
Kathra'natir escaped my grasp, but I know what his next step will be.

He seeks an ancient relic called the Forge of the Guardian, used for centuries by the Council of Tirisfal to infuse their power into the Guardian. The forge was hidden away, its location known only to the Council themselves.

Now the dreadlord has this knowledge.

We must go to the Violet Hold. I only hope we are not too late.

passages.title: The Dreadlord's Prize
passages.text: We must hurry!

passages.title: The Dreadlord's Prize
passages.text:
In times past, the Council of Tirisfal called upon the Tirisgarde, the protectors of Dalaran, to do battle in the Guardian's absence.

It is clear now that the hall of the Tirisgarde must be rebuilt to face this new threat.

I need your help to accomplish this. First of all, you'll need to know how to get to this hall. I will show you.

passages.title: Stolen Knowledge
passages.text:
Morjirn, the head brewer of the Tideskorn clan, has the Storm Brew recipe.

I have never been strong enough to assault his fortress alone, but together with you, I think we can claim retribution for my fallen master. I would like nothing better than to pry the recipe from Morjirn's cold, dead fingers.

While we are there, we will sample his Storm Brew. I'd like to see if his brewing skills are even near my master's.

passages.title: Stolen Knowledge
passages.text: Do you have the recipe?

passages.title: Stolen Knowledge
passages.text:
The last time I saw these notes, I was still a young child.

I understand much of what is written here now.

It won't be easy to acquire everything here, but I believe we can do it, <name>.

passages.title: The Hunter's Gaze
passages.text:
<name>, before you lies your nether crucible - more powerful than any we've crafted before.

The souls of the hundreds of slain demons in Mardum have provided us with enough power to directly observe the Legion on Azeroth.

What we have uncovered so far has been... unsettling. Gaze into the pool and see for yourself.
