Last time we met, <race>, I was in a cage. You risked your life once before for my kin. Are you willing to aid me once again?

The serpents' attack has left many of us wounded. I require mending waters to perform my healing rituals.

I have seen the serpents use this water. Return any that you find to me.

passages.title: Discovery Requires Experimentation
passages.text:
I can sense residues of magic all over you. You will be useful.

I must study how the demon bodies can handle the fel energies in such large quantities. I have plenty of flesh to sample, but there must be something...

Go retrieve some spines from the nearby basilisks so that I may analyze their magical residues. No sense in both of us getting our hands dirty, is there?

passages.title: Discovery Requires Experimentation
passages.text: I hope you brought enough. I will require more energy before my studies are complete.

passages.title: Discovery Requires Experimentation
passages.text: Fel magic is... strange. Almost slippery like an oil, and it burns long and hot. Maybe there's a connection...

passages.title: The Black Tome
passages.text:
I have made a great discovery, <name>.

There is a powerful warlock in the Soul Engine, in possession of a powerful tome. It contains forbidden secrets to summoning the most powerful of demons.

Even the Legion is afraid to call on these fel lords, but now I possess knowledge beyond theirs.

Fetch me the tome and I will never want for magic again.

passages.title: The Black Tome
passages.text: The tome! Do you have it?

passages.title: The Black Tome
passages.text: Yes... Within these pages lies the secret to true mastery of this power.

passages.title: An Ancient Recipe
passages.text:
Suramar is... was... an intellectual's dream.

We studied everything in there, from alchemy and the arts to the very nature of magic itself. How could we be so foolish as to accept them in?

Look at me, lost in the clouds again when there is much to be done. My work requires some fairly difficult ingredients, <race>. Perhaps you would help me procure them?

I am going to need some harpy talons. Crushed into a powder, they will be a potent reagent.

passages.title: An Ancient Recipe
passages.text: Do you have what I require, <race>? We don't have much time to spare.

passages.title: An Ancient Recipe
passages.text: That should be plenty. Talondust loses its potency fairly quickly, so we must make haste.

passages.title: Casual Redistribution
Cling to Hope
passages.text:
Your kindness has inspired me, friend.

I thought I would wander forever among the empty husks of the Withered, but Thalyssra invited me in.

I have chosen to remain here with my people and together we will take back Suramar.

For now I have but one request.

Take this letter to my wife. She should know that I still live, among other things.

Give her the hope that you gave me.

passages.title: Cling to Hope
passages.text: <Noressa eyes you suspiciously.>

passages.title: Cling to Hope
passages.text: Absolon... is alive?

passages.title: In My Sights
passages.text:
I used up all me bullets on a wee invention of mine. I call it: Tha Deployable Bullet Dispenser!

Oh aye. It shoots in-der-scriminantly wit'out all that messy and time-consumin' "aiming" or "thinkin'" that us people-folk are wont ta do.

We had deployed quite a few of 'em east o' here when this swarm of plants came a'thrashin from tha trees.

I didn't 'ave time ta go back an' get me turrets. Would ye mind gettin' them back fer me? Or at least, what's left of 'em?

passages.title: In My Sights
passages.text: Those mean greenies better not've touched me dispensers!

passages.title: In My Sights
passages.text:
Ohhh me poor innocent bullet dispensers! Look what they've done ta yeh.

Well at least they went down shootin', tha's how I'd like ta go.

Ere's tha schematic fer 'em. Deploy 'em near somethun' yeh don't like!

passages.title: Bubble Baubles
passages.text:
Ol' Hobart wanted me ta gather up these shiny, glass trinkets the murlocs carry around, but those bloody buggers ain't willin' to jes' hand 'em over!

I tried the dip-ler-matic approach, but I don't speak murloc, so I just end up shootin' 'em.

Maybe you might have better luck gettin' them baubles.

passages.title: Bubble Baubles
passages.text:
Any luck?

Did yeh try shootin' 'em?

passages.title: Bubble Baubles
passages.text: Well lookie there! You managed to talk 'em outta their trinkets! Ye'll have to teach me their language someday.

passages.title: Keep Yer Powder Dry
passages.text:
So while we've got all tha parts for tha pack again, I'm afraid I'm all outta gunpowder.

This is the worst thing ta ever happen ta me.

But there's hope. Just o'er to tha north are caves filled with crashed ships. Chances are them sea giants crashed one or two ships with cannons. And cannons mean gunpowder, sweet gunpowder.

Search their caves fer sum powder an' bring it on back.

passages.title: Keep Yer Powder Dry
passages.text: Try not ta get it wet, I dunna feel like waitin' fer it ta dry out.

passages.title: Keep Yer Powder Dry
passages.text:
Oh aye, tha's plenty, lad. I made sum adjustments ta tha design fer tha gunpack.

You should probably hold on to 'em, seein as 'ow these inventions of Hobart keep explodin' on me.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Trigger Happy
passages.text:
In order to complete my latest invention, I need a special relic known as the Runestone of Vitality.

Odyn, king of the Halls of Valor is known to use it to breathe life into his constructs.

What I'm asking is no easy task, but I need to take the runestone from Odyn and bring it back to me.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Trigger Happy
passages.text: I'm glad you're the one going up against a god and not me.

passages.title: Halls of Valor: Trigger Happy
passages.text:
Keep your fingers crossed, <name>, and let's hope this works.

Yes! YES! It's alive, ALIVE!

Now I can mass-market these gun parts as toys for children!

passages.title: Fresh Meat
passages.text:
This crater is infested with felfire basilisks.

They may not be the most cunning of creatures, but they are as vile and dangerous as any demon.

However, they may yet prove useful to us. Slay the basilisks, but return to me with chunks of their fel-infused flesh.

I have plans to make use of their freshly carved flesh...

passages.title: Fresh Meat
passages.text: Do you have the Fresh Fel-Flesh I require?

passages.title: Fresh Meat
passages.text:
I see that you have returned with the freshly carved remains of the fel basilisks.

Listen closely, and I will explain the purpose behind retrieving them...

passages.title: Grimwing the Devourer
passages.text:
You have my thanks for rescuing me from captivity, <class>.

However, Azoran is no mere demon. He is a powerful eredar who commands great rank within the Burning Legion.

If you wish to continue with me, I need proof of your strength.

Grimwing the Devourer is the strongest of the felbats and a suitable test of skill. Place the basilisk flesh upon the altar to the north and slay Grimwing when she appears.

Return to me with her head and I will not doubt your ability.

passages.title: Grimwing the Devourer
passages.text: What news do you bring of Grimwing the Devourer?

passages.title: Grimwing the Devourer
passages.text:
Grimwing was a formidable demon... I must say I am impressed with your skill, <name>.

There are many more demons here to kill. It is good to have someone capable at my side.

passages.title: Fel Bent for Leather
passages.text:
Ah, my faithful assistant. I have just the task for you.

As you have seen, fel power permeates living tissue and can easily be coaxed out.

Also, these damned bats are driving me to my wits' end. There is an opportunity to kill two bats with one blade, it seems. Your blade.

Take this crystal. It should rip those hellions from the sky and into your waiting arms.

You may as well bring back their hides, if only to shut up that fellow in the corner for a few moments.

passages.title: Fel Bent for Leather
passages.text: Have you obtained the hides?

passages.title: Fel Bent for Leather
passages.text: I can no longer hear their shrieking. Finally, peace and quiet!

passages.title: Symbols of Power
passages.text:
This demon has information that could lead us to those in charge.

Unfortunately, he is more fearful of his master than he is of us. We need to change his mind about that.

The most powerful Burning Legion soldiers often carry an emblem of their rank and status within the demon army.

Seek out the stronger demons in Felsoul Hold, slay them, and return to me with their emblems.

We will show this wyrmtongue servant who it is he should fear...

passages.title: Symbols of Power
passages.text: Do you have the Legion Emblems?

passages.title: Symbols of Power
passages.text:
I see you have returned with the emblems. Excellent.

Let's see how this wyrmtongue reacts when we show him what we've made of his comrades.

passages.title: Opening the Test Kitchen
passages.text:
I can cook, but I can't really hunt... or even fish, for that matter.

If you bring me ingredients, however, I will use them to research new recipes for you.

We can start with the few fish I managed to scrounge up. You'll find them in the barrel in the back of the kitchen.

passages.title: Opening the Test Kitchen
passages.text: Mackerel may not be extravagant, but it will fill your belly.

passages.title: Opening the Test Kitchen
passages.text:
We've done it! With this technique, we should be able to prepare dried mackerel strips much more efficiently.

I am certain that there is much more we can learn. Keep bringing me ingredients, and I will keep the oven on!

passages.title: King Forgalash's Burden
passages.text:
That sea witch spoke the truth.

I witnessed the Tidemistress confer with King Forgalash on several occasions.

Kill Forgalash and bring the prow from his shoulder to Fjolrik as proof of his demise.

I will meet afterwards in the center of Jandvik. I need to warm myself by its fires.

passages.title: Sigil Reclamation
passages.text:
The smooth square sigil weighs a fair amount more than its appearance would suggest. 

Handling it results in an intense tingling sensation in your palm- this is an object of focused, pure power. 

Such an advantage should not be so easily surrendered to the Nightborne.

passages.title: Sigil Reclamation
passages.text: What is this?

passages.title: Sigil Reclamation
passages.text: You were wise to keep these out of our enemies' hands, <class>. I believe you can be trusted.

passages.title: Shard of Vorgos
passages.text:
According to the wyrmtongue servant, there is a portal that will take you into the Burning Legion command ship. However, the portal is locked to those without the keys.

The first key shard is held by an Ered'ruin known as Vorgos. He resides within the Fel Breach, which is at the end of the Arcway.

Slay Vorgos and place the key shard into its position next to the portal.

passages.title: Shard of Vorgos
passages.text: <The Shard of Vargos pulses in your hand.>

passages.title: Shard of Vorgos
passages.text: <The Shard of Vorgos locks into position next to the portal. Swirling fel energy collects around the shard, filling the room with an ominous, dark presence.>

passages.title: Shard of Kozak
passages.text:
The demon leading the operation in Felsoul Hold is an eredar named Azoran. In order to get to him, we will need to open a portal to the Burning Legion command ship.

Azoran has a demon jailer in his service known as Kozak the Afflictor.

Kozak the Afflictor holds one of the key shards necessary to open a portal to the ship. He can be found in the prison quarters known as the Halls of the Eclipse in the lower portion of Felsoul Hold.

Slay Kozak and place his key shard next to the portal.

passages.title: Shard of Kozak
passages.text: <The Shard of Kozak tugs as if it wants to fly into place.>

passages.title: Shard of Kozak
passages.text: <The Shard of Kozak locks into position next to the portal. You can feel the dark writhing of fel energy surround you as it collects near the portal.>

passages.title: Bad Apples
passages.text:
That fruit over there? That's a pale imitation to what I can grow.

But that accursed Daglir somehow manages to gain the favor of the courts, so we must dine on mediocrity!

We must teach Daglir a lesson for stealing my crop, but we must be discreet.

Outside the shield grows a purple flower called Shadowbloom. Fetch some for me and we'll make sure that he pays dearly for his insolence!

passages.title: Bad Apples
passages.text: I would avoid eating any food until you've washed your hands.

passages.title: Bad Apples
passages.text: Excellent. This will be enough for my purposes.

passages.title: The Key Is Around Here Somewhere...
passages.text:
Well aren't ye a sight fer sore eyes!

It's no use tryin' to bust open this cage, this one needs a key!

Now, I know what yer thinkin', "How is it possible that the Burnin' Legion could capture a dwarf as mighty as ol' Angus here."

Ye can rest easy knowin' I let myself be captured. I'm here to rescue a dear friend o' mine, an' gettin' captured was the only way!

I had the key in me pocket... but it musta' fell out.

It's errm... around here somewhere.

A felhunter ate it a wee while back...

passages.title: The Key Is Around Here Somewhere...
passages.text: Did ye find the key?

passages.title: The Key Is Around Here Somewhere...
passages.text:
Ye found the key! Quickly, see if it fits...

Aye, that's the one! Ye did it!

passages.title: Search and Rescue!
passages.text:
We've got to find Brambley before it's too late!

Ol' Brambley an' I have been fightin' side by side since the Third War. When the Burnin' Legion invaded, we didn't think twice about coming to the Broken Isles.

Fightin' is what we do best!

During the battle ol' Brambley got caught too deep an' got himself captured. Now we've got to rescue him!

Last I saw, the demons were keeping him in a prison cell not far from here... let's go!

passages.title: Search and Rescue!
passages.text: Have you found the key yet?

passages.title: Search and Rescue!
passages.text: It's good to finally be free from this dreadful cage. As thanks, I will keep my word to you and your grotesquely hairy friend.

passages.title: Deciphering Demonology
passages.text:
I found a piece of what appears to be a key to something. I'm certain I can restore it if we can find the other bits.

After that, we need to figure out what it's a key to. An' I think I know how to do that.

I've been studying some of the artifacts I've found, and they seem to be pointing to a hidden chamber. I jes' need some more artifacts to study.

passages.title: Deciphering Demonology
passages.text: How goes the search?

passages.title: Deciphering Demonology
passages.text:
I'm startin' ta think you may be as good an archaeologist as I am. But don't let that go ta yer head, lad.

<Brann lets out a chuckle and begins to study the artifacts you brought him.>

Aye, that's it! I know where the chamber is. And once I've reassembled tha key, we're in business.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Through the Fog
passages.text:
I can't believe that after all that searchin' ye did, it's still missing a chapter!

I'm willin' ta bet that those satyrs got a hand on it and took it somewhere. Probably somewhere dark where no one could find it.

I've heard rumors of a place, the Darkheart Thicket they call it, where the strongest of the satyrs are.

If I had ta guess, I'd say ye need to go there and look around fer it.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Through the Fog
passages.text: A world of nightmares is nowhere where anyone should have ta go to.

passages.title: Darkheart Thicket: Through the Fog
passages.text:
Oh ho! Ye found the missing chapter AND a piece of me titan disc?!

This truly is a day of celebration. I'll let ye have the book, and ye can tell me what 'appened at tha end of it.

passages.title: Tried and True
passages.text:
I have realized through experience that the old methods are usually the best and for good reason. I'm done with alternate means of digging for now, and wish to focus on the right way to do things.

That being said, I believe I've found a new powerful artifact and I'll do literally anything to have it.

I've uncovered a fragment that appears to be a mold for a key. I now simply need the other pieces.

passages.title: Tried and True
passages.text: Have you recovered any of the other pieces yet?

passages.title: Tried and True
passages.text:
Yes, I believe that's all of them.

<Tae'thelan carefully reconstructs the mold.>

And now we just need to forge a new set of keys.

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Misdirected
passages.text:
I've been looking into the history of Huln Highmountain, a legendary warrior from the War of the Ancients whom this very land is named after.

Allegedly some of his personal effects were carried here after his death and have been lost in time.

After some digging around I believe I have discovered the location of one of his artifacts to be in a place called Neltharion's Lair.

I'm no fighter, <name>, but you are. Will you go and recover this artifact for me?

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Misdirected
passages.text: If I've followed the clues correctly, then this could lead to one of Huln's weapons.

passages.title: Neltharion's Lair: Misdirected
passages.text:
This is... not a weapon of Huln's. From the looks of it, I believe this to be the Spear of Rethu, an ancient tauren miner.

I have no interest in this artifact, <name>. You may have it.

passages.title: All That Glitters
passages.text:
Now that the shield is down, the older settlements outside the city have been on my mind.

Did you know that I helped create the filigree on the arcane lamps that are used throughout the city? A simple task, one of my first...

No matter. Nostalgia is the enemy of progress. The lamps are made of material better used in my new works.

Those wretched harpies probably have several decorating their nests. Bring back any you find.

passages.title: All That Glitters
passages.text: Can you imagine, a Lespin original hiding under a pile of leaves? What a waste.

passages.title: All That Glitters
passages.text: Excellent. I shall have these melted down and turned into ingots for my next batch of commissions.

passages.title: Service with a Smile
passages.text:
Oh, simple <race>. Simple, simple <race>.

I did not 'forget' to sweep up those reins from that foolish cakewalk of a knight they call the Lich King. I simply did not bother, as I already received the mighty steed during my raid last week.

<Johnny motions to the horse on his left.>

Since you're here and clearly intrigued by my sweltering greatness, won't you take that superfluous stallion to the assistant resort director in town? My coffers could use a bit of extra lining.

passages.title: Service with a Smile
passages.text: Do not tarry, <class>. The longer you take, the longer until you may dote on me as one of my many admirers.

passages.title: Service with a Smile
passages.text:
<Johnny raises his arm exaggeratedly, glancing at his naked wrist.>

My, my, quite the LETHARGIC adventurer, aren't you? That just might cover my repair bills from the many dungeons I've plundered.

passages.title: Estate Jewelry: A Braggart's Brooch
passages.text:
Amateur merchants worry about losing face from bad products. Masters worry about losing face from bad customers.

Naltethis Springblade has grown too bold for his station, and as such has lost much standing in the eyes of the city's elite.

I sold this man a brooch, a clasp he wears on his cape. I am careful to only sell to those above my station.

My pieces never tarnish, but my name and reputation are much more fragile. Relieve him of my property before he lowers me further.

passages.title: Estate Jewelry: A Braggart's Brooch
passages.text: That oaf will undo years of hard work. It is so much easier to fall than it is to climb...

passages.title: Estate Jewelry: A Braggart's Brooch
passages.text:
Ahh, see! I told you it would not tarnish. Now there's nothing linking me to that fool...

What's that? A plot to weaken his position? Regardless, the damage has been done. Better safe than sorry.

passages.title: Firing Up the Forge
passages.text:
Are you familiar with the Obliterum Forge? It can be used to destroy crafted gear, yielding valuable Obliterum. I'm personally quite curious to see it in action.

One of my many admirers recently gifted me a set of adventuring robes, but I'm afraid they're not quite my style.

Place them inside the forge and see what happens.

passages.title: Firing Up the Forge
passages.text: What are the results, <name>?

passages.title: Firing Up the Forge
passages.text:
Success! While their interior decoration sensibilities may differ significantly from those of Dalaran's architects, the demon hunters do make an efficient forge.

You keep the obliterum, <name>. I have a feeling you'll be needing it eventually.

passages.title: The Taken
Ice and Shadow
passages.text:
We took down one of the Necrodark. Ebonhorn found that it held a shard of ice infused with shadow essence.

Perhaps the villains are using these shards as a kind of talisman. I suggest you deprive them of their trinkets.

I know little of such magics, but it seemed that Ebonhorn had a use for them in mind.

passages.title: Ice and Shadow
passages.text: Did you find more of the shards?

passages.title: Ice and Shadow
passages.text: Perfect timing, <name>. These shards will prove very useful in what I'm about to do.

passages.title: Dazed of the Past
passages.text: Let's begin crafting this mount armor, shall we?

passages.title: Dazed of the Past
passages.text: I'm quite anxious to see how it turns out.

passages.title: Dazed of the Past
passages.text:
Is there anything we can't do? I'm starting to think not!

I'll make sure this barding gets to Mei. You hold on to the pattern and maybe you can make some profit with it.

passages.title: The Arcway: Long Buried Knowledge
passages.text:
Beneath Suramar City is an ancient network of tunnels known as the Arcway.

They were abandoned some time ago as part of the cavern became unstable. Since then, who knows?

Regardless of what is currently down there, I believe you will find something essential to our continued success.

Long ago my people took a thorough survey of the ley lines in and around Suramar. This they would have stored in the library in the Arcway. 

Find this map for me.

passages.title: The Arcway: Long Buried Knowledge
passages.text: Did you find it?

passages.title: The Arcway: Long Buried Knowledge
passages.text: Excellent! I will study this immediately.

passages.title: Sharing the Wealth
passages.text:
Lately there have been a disturbing array of changes involving our most precious resource, Arcwine. 

I imagine Thalyssra has thoroughly educated you about what happens when a Nightborne does not have access to a source of power like Arcwine.

With the presence of the demons came rationing. There are many who do not have enough to sustain themselves.

Bring me as much Arcwine as you can carry. I will see that it gets to the right people.

passages.title: Tracking Down the Scepter
passages.text: The logbook contains the latest information on the Scepter of Sargeras. It appears to have been written by an extremely agitated, excited, or psychotic imp and is barely legible. Take this to Calydus for translation.

passages.title: Leyline Feed: Ley Station Moonfall
passages.text:
<This leyline feed appears to be damaged. The large collector at the top is broken.

The broken piece must be around here somewhere. There are rough scuff marks on the floor that appear to be made by something larger than the creatures inside.

Much, much larger.>

passages.title: Leyline Feed: Ley Station Moonfall
passages.text: <The feed pulses softly.>

passages.title: Leyline Feed: Ley Station Moonfall
passages.text: <As you place the broken piece onto the pillar and begin infusing it with mana, arcane energy begins to repair the break. It slowly begins to turn as the leyline is activated.>

passages.title: Arcane Reavers
passages.text:
Arcane reavers are magical creations of brute strength. They are heavily armored and deliver stunning blows. You, however, can bypass their defenses and avoid their attacks. Your spellcraft is not without many advantages, <name>.

Travel to Dawnstar Spire and blast apart the arcane reavers. From their remains, collect the crystallized fragments of magical energy and return to me. Dawnstar Spire is found to the east, across the lake.

passages.title: Arcane Reavers
passages.text: Didn't get too close to the brutes, I hope?

passages.title: Arcane Reavers
passages.text:
Such a waste, using magic to construct beings of physical strength.  I always thought that's why we allied with the lesser races, after all.

You were good to destroy them so we can use what remains for a more suitable purpose.

passages.title: Beds, Bandages, and Beyond
passages.text:
Welcome to Azure Watch, <class>. Please excuse the disorder you see around you. It's easy to take simple things for granted, like a fully furnished and stocked inn, until you're forced to build one from nothing.

We've managed to salvage this pod for a building, but without the proper furnishings and first aid supplies, the inn is little more than a glorified tent. Nurguni at the Exodar has offered to put together a package to help with our most immediate needs, but I need someone to deliver this list to him.

passages.title: Beds, Bandages, and Beyond
passages.text: Good day, <name>. Are you interested in renting a hippogryph?

passages.title: Beds, Bandages, and Beyond
passages.text:
So you need to go to the Exodar?

That's going to be a bit of a trip, but don't worry, I have a way to get you there very quickly.

passages.title: Delivery for Drazzit
passages.text:
Drazzit will expect to hear something from me soon, but I don't think the site is secure enough for me to leave. If you have time, would you be willing to take some of the salvaged cargo down to him at Mudsprocket?

If you haven't been there yet, it's a small settlement to the southwest of here, beyond the Stonemaul Ruins. You can take the road there from Tabetha's Farm, too. When you get to Mudsprocket, the guy you're looking for is Drazzit Dripvalve.

passages.title: Delivery for Drazzit
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Delivery for Drazzit
passages.text:
<Drazzit accepts the cargo from you.>

I'm so hungry, I could eat a dragon! Thank goodness Moxie finally got some of that cargo down here. We've been reduced to playing dice against the ogre for whatever he's managed to kill on his hunting trips!

passages.title: Amberwind's Journal
passages.text:
If my sources are trustworthy, Lorekeeper Amberwind is overseeing the Alliance investigation of the ruins to the east. I have not yet probed the extent of her abilities: I'm hoping you can give me a full report by engaging her in combat and destroying her.

With a title like 'Lorekeeper,' I'm guessing Amberwind will have a journal on her that'll tell us exactly what those night elves are up to. Fetch that journal for me. No need to run back; use their own scrying stones to contact me remotely.

passages.title: Amberwind's Journal
passages.text:
<Andorel's distorted face appears within the scrying stone.>

<name>, have you made contact? What can you tell me?

passages.title: Amberwind's Journal
passages.text:
Amberwind was making use of an Arcane Construct? Hah! How delightfully inexperienced. It's like watching children play with firearms.

Let's take a look at that journal, <name>. Hold it up to the scrying stone... keep it still ...

passages.title: Arcane De-Construction
passages.text:
Arcane constructs are creatures spawned of pure mana and intellect. In the right hands, a construct allows its user to quickly assimilate vast riches of arcane knowledge. But they're dangerous, <name>. So intelligent! So powerful! So very vulnerable to external tampering...

Let's teach these amateurs a lesson and use their own magic against them. Slay Apprentices and collect their runestones for me. Contact me via the lower scrying stone when you're done.

passages.title: Arcane De-Construction
passages.text:
<Andorel's image is blurry and indistinct. He squints at you and taps against the glass of the scrying stone.>

<name>, is that you? The resolution on this stone is terrible. What kind of hardware are they using?

passages.title: Arcane De-Construction
passages.text:
Good work getting those runestones. To be honest, I only needed one, but the thought of so many night elves slain for such useless baubles fills me with a dark, giddy joy.

Please hold one of those runes up to the scrying stone to let me see. Hmmm. As I suspected, an amateur effort at best.

passages.title: Thunderhorn Totem
passages.text:
There is more work to be done. We must create a new totem to cleanse the Thunderhorn Well.

You must gather the claws of the predators of the Mulgore plains. Hunt prairie stalkers for their stalker claws and flatland cougars for their cougar claws, then return to me.

You will find the prairie stalkers and flatland cougars to the east and west.

passages.title: Thunderhorn Totem
passages.text: <name>, do you have the claws I sent you to gather?  The Thunderhorn Water Well grows more tainted with each passing hour!

passages.title: Thunderhorn Totem
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.  The purity with which these beasts hunt is vital in the creation of the next cleansing totem.

The Thunderhorn Well is a symbol of my own tribe, and to know it is being desecrated by our own kind raises a fury in me I haven't felt for years.

passages.title: Wildmane Totem
passages.text:
There is but one water well left to cleanse, named after the Wildmane clan. For this well to be pure, the land must offer the teeth of a fierce predator, the prairie wolf alpha. Find the alphas to the north, then return to me when your hunt is finished.

Alphas often wander around the base of our mighty city, Thunder Bluff.

passages.title: Wildmane Totem
passages.text: <name>.  Do you have the teeth I asked for?

passages.title: Wildmane Totem
passages.text: Very good, <name>.  I can feel the sacrifice of the land in this offering, and my spirit swells with sadness, and pride.

passages.title: Gather the Intelligence
passages.text:
It's me, <name>, Ortell!

Don't look directly at the outhouse... you'll give away my position.

Everything's going according to plan then? Excellent!

I'm going to need you to obtain some intelligence while you're here. It might not seem like much to get our hands on a map or a letter, but it may mean saving a hundred lives on our side if we can anticipate our enemy's next move.

passages.title: Gather the Intelligence
passages.text: Did you get the documents, <name>?

passages.title: Gather the Intelligence
passages.text:
Excellent job, <name>.  Or should I say: "<name>"damus?

Give me a minute to read these.

passages.title: From the Mouth of Madness
passages.text:
I know of a draught that should jolt these gibbering former slaves back to reality. Gather some stonebloom from the rocks around Gar'gol's hovel, some bitterblossom from the shores of the nearby lake, and a darkflame ember from one of the braziers at the hovel entrance. The draught won't last long, so combine the ingredients at a twilight cauldron by the entrance to the hovel.

One sip of that draught should knock some sense into the brainwashed slaves!

passages.title: From the Mouth of Madness
passages.text: <The cauldron burbles, filled with a disgusting liquid.>

passages.title: From the Mouth of Madness
passages.text:
<You dump out the current contents of the cauldron, instantly killing the surrounding plant life.>

<The draught you brew in its place boils chunky and reeks of rotted cabbage. You turn your head aside and bottle it up.>

passages.title: Nerve Tonic
passages.text:
How am I feelin', you ask?

Well, after bein' yanked from the deck of our ship by a giant sea monster and then left to drown in the sea... not so good!

My nerves are gettin' the best of me, to be honest.

If you could round up some of the supplies that are sure to be floatin' around the nearby wrecks, I could likely whip up somethin' that'll take the edge off...

passages.title: Nerve Tonic
passages.text: Were ya able to grab some supplies, <race>?

passages.title: Nerve Tonic
passages.text:
I trust we both know what's been going on inside these crates...

That's right... ferrrmenntation! Here y'are. My personal secret recipe.

You wouldn't get this from any other guy!

passages.title: Crate of Crab Meat
passages.text:
This crate, labeled 'Crab Meat', seems to have fallen from a recently sunken cargo ship.

Adarrah would surely welcome such a find, considering the ordeal she's had to endure.

passages.title: Crate of Crab Meat
passages.text: What have you got there, <name>?

passages.title: Crate of Crab Meat
passages.text:
Why, <name>! What a surprise!

If anyone ever calls your character into question you be sure to send them my way.

I'll tell anyone who'll listen that in my moment of need, you gave me a case of crabs...

passages.title: A Taste For Tail
passages.text:
It could be days before we're ready to make our way to the surface, and to be honest, I'm already beginning to get hungry.

I hate to be picky, but when it comes to seafood, I'm afraid there are very few things I can stomach.

If you come across any lobster types, I would happily pay you what coin I have with me for their tails.

passages.title: A Taste For Tail
passages.text: Oh, please tell me you were able to find me some food, <class>.

passages.title: A Taste For Tail
passages.text:
Oh, my!

That's some of the biggest, juiciest tail I've ever seen!

passages.title: Seeds of Their Demise
passages.text:
We will decimate the Twilight's Hammer by corrupting and subverting them. 

Seeing that you have no intention of releasing me from my bonds, I require you to collect some reagents for me. My own demonic essence has corrupted the plant life around my shrine here. I need you to harvest some bileberries from the wailing weeds that surround this tower.

My little pets will attempt to harvest YOU in return. Try not to let them agitate one another.

passages.title: Seeds of Their Demise
passages.text:
Has the local flora been giving you a hard time?

<Blackhorn grins disturbingly.>

passages.title: Seeds of Their Demise
passages.text:
Very good. Please crush the berries into a pulpy liquid. That's quite an aroma isn't it?

Now now, don't gag. It's beneath you.

passages.title: The Flameseer's Staff
passages.text:
A powerful artifact known as the Flameseer's Staff was lost during the initial onslaught by the enemy forces. It was an ancient bone staff that granted its wielder power over the elements of fire.

Its fragments litter the area around us. Find them and bring them to Malfurion. Perhaps the artifact's power will still be of use.

passages.title: The Flameseer's Staff
passages.text: Yes, <name>?

passages.title: The Flameseer's Staff
passages.text: Excellent, <name>.  This will be a great weapon against the enemy forces.

passages.title: Durable Seeds
passages.text:
This land has been scourged by fire, but it may yet renew itself.

Some seeds deep in the soil may have withstood the scorching heat here in The Flamewake. These durable plants are the key to this forest's regrowth. Please, collect some of these seedlings for me.

passages.title: Durable Seeds
passages.text: I suspect life still struggles beneath the ash. What were you able to find?

passages.title: Durable Seeds
passages.text:
<The Arch Druid inspects the seedlings.>

These seedlings have survived an apocalypse. Even a handful hold great power. Life always replenishes itself, often stronger than before.

Once the way is clear, we will use these to perform a miracle on this mountain, <name>. You will see.

passages.title: Fresh Bait
passages.text:
I was stunned to discover that Twilight's Hammer had located - and imprisoned - the great turtle ancient Tortolla. As we speak he is chained above the murky waters of the Ashen Lake.

Freeing Tortolla from his bonds will not be easy. But we will take it one step at a time.

Head into the Flamewake and collect for me heaps of core hound entrails. I will explain why later.

And beware of Nemesis the Usurper while you are there! His time will come, but we are not yet prepared.

passages.title: Fresh Bait
passages.text:
Have you collected the innards?

Core hounds are not native to this part of the world, they accompanied Twilight's Hammer from the nether regions of the earth. Do not trouble yourself over their elimination.

passages.title: Fresh Bait
passages.text:
Very good. We will need these to act as bait while they are still warm.

Here is my plan...

passages.title: Cindermaul, the Portal Master
passages.text:
Twilight's Hammer is using these corridors, and others like them, to move supplies from the elemental planes up into Azeroth. In order to seal these passages off, we're going to need to know how they're constructed.

Find for me the Tome of Openings, used by the elementals to open gates between the planes.

Cindermaul the Portal Master should have one. You'll have to kill him. Careful! He's probably got some tricks up his sleeve...

passages.title: Cindermaul, the Portal Master
passages.text: The tome! Have you found it?

passages.title: Cindermaul, the Portal Master
passages.text:
This is the tome we've heard about?

<Jordan hefts the stone slab into his arms and looks it over.>

I see... I guess it's good that I can read some of the elemental script. I'll work on translating this. Meanwhile, there's one final problem to take care of.

passages.title: Can't Start a Fire Without a Spark
passages.text:
Mack's still out of it, and I fear we may lose him if I can't get this fire started. With the wood being soaked, we'll need something special to get it going.

There's an abandoned camp nearby with a barrel of explosives in it. There's no way I can recover it on my own.

Would you mind hauling it back for us? For Mack?

passages.title: Can't Start a Fire Without a Spark
passages.text: Did you get the explosives from the camp, <class>?

passages.title: Can't Start a Fire Without a Spark
passages.text:
Outstanding!

Let's see if this does the trick....

Stand back, <name>!

passages.title: Scrambling for Eggs
passages.text:
There's a pattern to these Wormwing attacks. While groups make a showy assault on the shrine itself, others swoop into the nearby nests and make off with eggs from all the flying creatures of Hyjal.

These animals are under our protection. Before we find out why the Wormwing are doing this, it's up to us to rescue as many eggs as we can from their talons.

passages.title: Scrambling for Eggs
passages.text: <Thisalee is cleaning her nails with a dagger. She looks up at you expectantly.>

passages.title: Scrambling for Eggs
passages.text:
Good, that's a start.

The birds who laid these eggs will never accept them again, so we'll have to raise these birds as orphans in the shrine here. Were Aviana here, she never would've let this travesty happen.

But, on to business...

passages.title: A Gap in Their Armor
passages.text:
Do you see what they're doing here? They're affixing armored plates onto the Dragonkin. A page out of Deathwing's book, I suppose.

Those Twilight Juggernauts look like they'll be invincible once they're complete. There's got to be a way around that armor plating!

Run out there and fetch some of the Twilight armor plates that are waiting to be installed. We'll figure out how to beat this.

passages.title: A Gap in Their Armor
passages.text:
Did you get a hold of some plates? Did you have to kill anyone to get them?

I hope so.

passages.title: A Gap in Their Armor
passages.text:
Look at these things. Ugh, the runes make my eyes hurt. This one here is meant to sear flesh? Seriously? Ouch! Wait a minute...

These plates are designed to be riveted directly into flesh. The pain must be unbearable!

passages.title: Scalding Shrooms
passages.text:
We think that we have a use for the merciless ones that your friend from the cave delivered to us. But I need a preservative for it.

Down below in the Scalding Chasm are some mushrooms with the properties that I need. Bring some back up to me and I'll see what I can do.

passages.title: Scalding Shrooms
passages.text: I heard that you had an unpleasant encounter with putting one of the demons on your head. I can assure you that they are now all quite dead.

passages.title: Scalding Shrooms
passages.text: I will use the mushrooms as a reagent to treat the corpses. We will have one ready for you soon.

passages.title: ... It Will Come
passages.text:
I now imbue you with the energies of the corrupting faceless.

Swim down to my luring totem in the trench to the northeast. Release the energies through it. Bring back the brain of their leader.

Call forth to Ick'thys the Unfathomable... it will come!

passages.title: ... It Will Come
passages.text:
Do you have it, <name>?

With the Unfathomable's brain, we still may yet be able to communicate with L'ghorek, the dying ancient one in front of us.

passages.title: ... It Will Come
passages.text: And now we will see if we can get you into L'ghorek to speak with it before it dies.

passages.title: Runestones of Binding
passages.text:
ON THE OTHER... SIDE OF... MY CHAMBER THERE... ARE... CANDIDATES FOR ASCENSION.

WE WILL NEED... THEIR... RUNESTONES OF BINDING... TO CREATE A... MEANS OF CONTROLLING... A BOUND ELEMENTAL.

passages.title: Runestones of Binding
passages.text: DO... YOU HAVE... ALL THAT IS... REQUIRED?

passages.title: Runestones of Binding
passages.text: WE WILL USE... THESE... RUNESTONES TO ALLOW... YOU TO POSSESS... ONE OF... THE WATER ELEMENTALS.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: The clue to the treasure reads: Good work, matey! Now ye need to head due east. East up the bluffs, east to the road. Look for the ol' chimney ruins near the side of the road. There you'll find an old barrel with your next clue.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: This looks like the right barrel.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: Good work, treasure hunter!

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: Searching through the barrel you discover another piece of parchment. This one reads: Now from this here barrel, face ye North. Straight as the crow flies, keep ye walkin' till you see the empty jug next to the lone windmill on the sea bluffs. If ye poke around that jug, ye just might find what you're lookin' for.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: There's a clue sticking out of the empty jug.

passages.title: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure
passages.text: You're on your way to the jackpot, treasure seeker!

passages.title: Dungar Longdrink
passages.text:
<name>, I gathered into this crate everything Argus asked for. Can you take it to him?

If you've already spoken to Bartlett at Goldshire, then you can take a gryphon back to him. Dungar Longdrink is our gryphon master, over in the trade district.

Speak with Dungar, then get this crate to Argus as fast as you can. We don't want our fighting men and women in Goldshire to go without fresh equipment!

passages.title: Dungar Longdrink
passages.text: Is that sweat on your brow, lad?  You've been running too much.  Next time, take a gryphon!

passages.title: Dungar Longdrink
passages.text: A crate for Goldshire, eh?  People sure are getting lazy. Have you been to Goldshire before?  If so, then it's no problem, my friend.  I have plenty of gryphons trained to fly that route!

passages.title: Explosive Bonding Compound
passages.text:
This guy's the son of the Earthen leader! He almost made it to the temple when he got ambushed by more rock flayers than I can count!

We know that the Earthen Stonefather has the middle fragment of the World Pillar. Maybe if we were to heal his son, the Stonefather would give us the fragment?

My heals won't work on Flint here. But if we were to get some of the quartzite resin off of these monsters, I think I can make an explosive compound that will bond and cauterize his wounds.

passages.title: Explosive Bonding Compound
passages.text: It won't take much resin. Those rock flayers are pretty dangerous though.

passages.title: Explosive Bonding Compound
passages.text:
Good thing that I just happen to be a grand master of all things explosively alchemical.

This won't ignite on its own, though.

passages.title: Without a Captain or Crew
passages.text:
Not sure who you're with, but you don't look like one of... them.

I'm not sure what happened. I slept through supper and woke up to a ship full of dead people and murderers.

Not sure if you want to kill me or not, but I'll spare you the trouble.

<Moody points to a wound in his stomach. His insides are not where they should be.>

I can keep steering the ship for a while longer. You don't die from a gut wound immediately. Just bring me some rope and some rum... no, whiskey.

passages.title: Without a Captain or Crew
passages.text: You have what I asked for?

passages.title: Without a Captain or Crew
passages.text:
All right, help me get tied to the wheel.

<Moody sips from the bottle.>

passages.title: Making Things Crystal Clear
passages.text:
Among the Shuddering Spires are crystals. White, chalky crystals. We can absorb these crystals into our skin. To cleanse us. Purify us.

I do not stride among the stones any longer. I am one with the earth. This carries many boons, but I can no longer retrieve the crystals for myself.

Bring me the crystals that I might be stronger. Carry them away from the flayers. Away from my sons. This honor should be mine.

passages.title: Making Things Crystal Clear
passages.text: Have you done this favor that I asked of you? Did you bring the crystals?

passages.title: Making Things Crystal Clear
passages.text: Ahh... invigorating. Thank you, fleshling.

passages.title: Thunder Stones
passages.text:
To the north lies the Fractured Front. That is where most of the heavy fighting is happening.

Go into Stonehearth proper and grab all of the thunder stones that you can. Our engineers need them for the catapults.

When you have enough, take them to Clay Mudaxle. Don't mind his tongue. He's old and cranky, and should have gone back into the earth thousands of years ago.

passages.title: Thunder Stones
passages.text:
<The older Earthen has cracks where the others do not, clearly ancient.>

What are you supposed to be? Some kind of fleshy mistake? Cursed is what you are!

<Clay spits dust.>

Make yourself useful or get off of my front!

passages.title: Thunder Stones
passages.text:
<Clay grumbles to himself.>

Those'll do. Just put them down over there.

<The Earthen looks you up and down with one eye and then spits dust onto the ground.>

I'm going to have something for you to do in a moment. Maybe.

passages.title: Petrified Delicacies
passages.text:
Petrified bats.

Elementals of that size are picky. You're not likely to find anything better easily.

To the east are basilisks. They petrify stone bats that fly too close and snack on them when they grow hungry. You may find bats scattered around their territory.

I must warn you... if you show that little elemental too much attention, you're unlikely to be rid of it. It can be very... needy.

passages.title: Petrified Delicacies
passages.text: <Pebble starts to look up at you, eyes glowing faintly, growing rounder and larger every moment.>

passages.title: Petrified Delicacies
passages.text: <Pebble leaps upon the pile of petrified bats and rolls around in them, seeming to forget that you exist entirely. Perhaps for the best, if Kor's warnings are to be trusted.>

passages.title: Motes
passages.text:
Some of the rarest crystals form in the most dangerous places. In the Crumbling Depths, you will find painite formations - much better than the gold that your races cherish so much.

As a being of flesh and a being of small stature, you can enter the Crumbling Depths to retrieve motes of painite for me. Would you undergo that danger on my behalf?

passages.title: Motes
passages.text: Painite is one of the most valuable materials to us, particularly due to our inability to reach most of the deposits on our own.

passages.title: Motes
passages.text: Well done, <race>. These will do well.

passages.title: Something that Burns
passages.text:
Alright, we need something that's going to make the compound go, "Boom"!

I'm all out of gun powder, but I think I know what we can use instead... the heart of my fire elemental!

Here, take my fire totem east to the Blood Trail. Just flip the switch on it near any of the lava pools over there and Magmatooth should be summoned. Bring back his heart and we'll be in business.

passages.title: Something that Burns
passages.text: You have the heart yet?

passages.title: Something that Burns
passages.text:
Uh oh. Sounds like he wasn't very happy about the situation. How was I to know? I'm just an initiate after all.

Anyway, I'll worry about Magmatooth later.

passages.title: Field Work
passages.text:
This unfortunate pygmy was in the wrong place at the wrong time.

As you ponder his bad luck, you take notice of the symbols covering his shield - far too elaborate for pygmy scrawl.

Confident that Doctor Jones will find such objects of interest, you set out to find more fragments like this one.

passages.title: Field Work
passages.text: What'dya have there, friend?

passages.title: Field Work
passages.text:
These tablets are covered with titan writings. There's never-before seen information here, <name>!

Missing pieces to an ancient puzzle...

Good work!

passages.title: Mercy for the Bound
passages.text:
It goes without saying that I had no desire to stay here, but there were materials we needed for the ritual... I delayed to secure them, and that is what lead to my capture.

I will return to the circle, but I would be indebted to you if you would finish what I could not. We need hearts from the bound fire elementals that the Twilight's Hammer enslave in the western portion of the encampment.

The elementals are without hope, but in this sacrifice they can extract their revenge.

Find me at camp.

passages.title: Mercy for the Bound
passages.text: Did you recover the hearts?

passages.title: Mercy for the Bound
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. You are quite capable. I'm extremely grateful that you've chosen to aid us.

passages.title: Uncle Carlin
passages.text:
I'm going to play with dolly, but I don't want to play with daddy's sword after all. You'd better keep it.

Even better, can you give it to my uncle Carlin? I'm not sure where he is, but sometimes I hear him crying. It sounds like he's nearby, to the north.

I hope he's not crying for me! <name>, will you find my uncle and tell him I'm alright?

If you find him say I'm waiting for him, and I want to hear the story he used to tell... the one about the rabbits and the berry jam! That story's so funny!

passages.title: Uncle Carlin
passages.text: Any news of my Pammy?

passages.title: Uncle Carlin
passages.text:
You've seen Pamela?  She's alive?

She's dead?  No!  Oh, Pamela!  Why does your spirit still suffer in this world?  Why are you perished, while fortune keeps me alive?  In an instant I would switch places with you and wander dead Darrowshire, a ghost and alone!

Ah, but this news cannot change fate.  Thank you, <name>.  Now my duty, my duty to revenge, burns hot as ever.

Say, what is that sword you have there?

passages.title: A Strange Historian
passages.text:
That sword belonged to Joseph Redpath, Pamela's father - though you probably already knew that. I wish Joseph could again be with his daughter, but it cannot be so. His soul was twisted by the Scourge, and he became a monster.

Pamela's fate is sealed, but perhaps we can change Joseph's fate.

A strange gnome arrived here at this tower not long ago. Her name is Chromie. Take that sword to her. I have a feeling she will be able to help us.

passages.title: A Strange Historian
passages.text: There is something timely about your visit.  You're not from the future, are you?

passages.title: A Strange Historian
passages.text:
What is this?  A warsword?  A butter knife?  I'm useless when it comes to blades.  Let me see...

Ah!  This sword was once in the hand of a great man, but there is much tragedy in that man's past.

Are you here to help him?  It's far too late for him now... but perhaps we can help him in the past!

passages.title: Far from the Nest
passages.text:
Look... I know you have no reason to be fond of me, just as I'm not terribly fond of you, but I need any help I can get.

Our eggs are being stolen by these Twilight invaders. I have no doubt that they want to take them back to Grim Batol to experiment on and pervert. I will NOT let that happen.

If you truly do want to help us, stop them! Recover the eggs. Bring them back to me.

passages.title: Far from the Nest
passages.text: Twilight dragons were born of these disgusting experiments of theirs. The Twilight's Hammer have gone too far. Deathwing has gone too far.

passages.title: Far from the Nest
passages.text:
I don't know if you did this for me or the young inside these eggs, but it doesn't really matter, either way it's clear that you want to be an ally of our flight. I appreciate that.

I cannot forgive the attacks by your allies against my brood, but for now, it seems you have chosen the right side.

passages.title: Be Prepared
passages.text:
Every adventurer worth their salt knows never to step foot in a cave, dungeon, crypt or tomb without an ample supply of rope... right?

You can never have too much of this stuff!

You resolve to scrounging every scrap of it you can find from the skeletons here.

passages.title: Be Prepared
passages.text: What have you found, <name>?

passages.title: Be Prepared
passages.text:
Ahh, rope! Thanks, kid.

Something tells me I'm going to need this.

passages.title: Lessons From the Past
passages.text:
This unfortunate explorer has clearly suffered a bit of bad luck in the recent past.

Prudence dictates that you perform the unenviable task of searching the corpse for clues that might shed light on your surroundings...

passages.title: Lessons From the Past
passages.text: Any news, <name>?

passages.title: Lessons From the Past
passages.text:
Odd...

It looks as if someone used gemstones as lenses.

I should be able to fix them without too much trouble.

passages.title: By the Light of the Stars
passages.text:
Look at this, <name>.

<Harrison holds up the dead scout's goggles.>

I tightened the clamp in the middle and crimped the wires on the edges. They may not be the most comfortable, but they should hold together.

If I've translated your tablets correctly, there's something hidden here - a final piece to our puzzle.

I hope your spectacles hold the key.

Let me know what you find!

passages.title: By the Light of the Stars
passages.text:
So?

Find anything interesting?

passages.title: By the Light of the Stars
passages.text:
Well, kid, it looks like you've done it again.

<Harrison points to an image on the tablets.>

This starlight is exactly what we were missing.

Now we can get to work!

passages.title: The Scepter of Orsis
passages.text:
The chest below unlocks with a loud click as you insert the two stones into the plaque.

Obtain the scepter and bring it back to General Ammantep.

passages.title: The Scepter of Orsis
passages.text: You're back, <name>!

passages.title: The Scepter of Orsis
passages.text: So... this is what Al'Akir wanted all along.

passages.title: Ancient Weapons
passages.text:
Though we aren't formally at war yet, the Neferset do not hesitate to imprison or kill all who trespass upon their territories.

King Phaoris refuses to reciprocate, even when they use our lands to smuggle stolen relics from the tombs of our ancestors.

My scouts report that the Neferset are about to move a major shipment of looted weapons south of here.

I've instructed the laborers you recruited to assist you. Call upon them with this horn when you find the smugglers and recover the weapons.

passages.title: Ancient Weapons
passages.text: You've returned, <name>.  How did the operation go?

passages.title: Ancient Weapons
passages.text:
This is quite timely.  I will distribute these armaments to my best men and to the laborers that you recruited.

I've a feeling they'll show as much courage as my best trained captains.

passages.title: Budd's Plan
passages.text:
I've an idea! Trust me, it's a good one this time!

Get some of those shiny armor pieces the cat-people wear.

This plan cannot fail. Trust me.

passages.title: Budd's Plan
passages.text: Did you get the pieces, <name>?

passages.title: Budd's Plan
passages.text: Excellent.  You'll see, this can't possibly go wrong!

passages.title: The Middle Fragment
passages.text:
I present you with the key to Stonehearth. With it you may unlock the vault to my home and recover the middle fragment of the World Pillar.

Keep the fragment safe, <name>. Make certain to get it to the Temple of Earth in the middle of Deepholm as quickly as possible!

Know that you are always welcome here.

passages.title: The Middle Fragment
passages.text: You've returned. Did you recover the middle fragment?

passages.title: The Middle Fragment
passages.text:
The Middle Fragment of the World Pillar!

Thank you, <name>. I can only imagine what you had to go through to get this to us. I'll see to it that it's placed within the center of the chamber.

passages.title: Idolatry
passages.text:
Zhere is somezhink I need handled, <race>.

My most trusted advisor has run afoul of an ancient curse. A hex zhat has transformed zhe man into a turkey, of all zhings!

I haff studied for days to discover a remedy for his condition, and finally I am ready to conduct zhe ritual.

I vill reqvire several idols from zhe nearby ruins. You are to brink zhem to me at vonce!

Dismissed!

passages.title: Idolatry
passages.text: Haff you brought me zhe idols, <race>?

passages.title: Idolatry
passages.text:
Zhese look to be of sufficient quality.

Vizh zhese, ve are vone shtep closah to zhe cleansink ritual.

passages.title: Angered Spirits
passages.text:
Doctor Venkman vas vone of my greatest researchers, until he had to be put out of my misery.

He did leave me vizh vone of his greatest accomplishments, zhough. Against zhe properly attuned supernatural adversary, zhis veapon vill siphon zhe target's essence.

It is of key importance in zhe ritual I vill be attemptink.

Vhere do you come in, you ask? Simple. You have zhe priviledge of collecting zhe material.

Zhe veapon is calibrated to vork on zhe Furious Specters in zhe temple to zhe east.

passages.title: Angered Spirits
passages.text: Vell, little man? Vere you successful?

passages.title: Angered Spirits
passages.text:
Very goot!

You have earned yourself a place at zhe ritual.

You shall be among zhe first to velcome Gobbles back to his... original form.

passages.title: Kavem the Callous
passages.text:
Kavem was cruel enough before the Neferset signed up with Deathwing. His pleasure in deriving pain now borders on the insane.

It is he who now holds the keys to our shackles.

He dwells in the building next to us, to my right.

Find him and take the key from him. Do not hesitate or show him mercy. He will slit your throat and think nothing of it.

passages.title: Kavem the Callous
passages.text: You're back.  Do you have the key?

passages.title: Kavem the Callous
passages.text: Excellent, <name>.  We will make our way out of here soon enough.

passages.title: Relics of the Sun King
passages.text:
The Seal of the Sun King serves as a defense mechanism for Ramkahen.

When the barrier around Uldum fell, we began to see Wastewander outriders from Tanaris filter into our borders.

They attacked this holy site on their way west and robbed it of the relics which once provided its power.

Recover the relics for us. Without them we are powerless to defend against attacks from the desert.

passages.title: Relics of the Sun King
passages.text: Did you succeed?

passages.title: Relics of the Sun King
passages.text: Thank you.  The rumors I'd heard about you are proving true after all.

passages.title: The Element of Supplies
passages.text:
You'll notice that we're slightly ill prepared for battle.

The tol'vir tribes had never seen any sort of major confrontation for thousands of years.

All the combat protocols that the titans programmed into our ancestors are still there, though. Some are part of our instincts, some get passed on as tradition.

But none of this can compensate for lack of supplies. We need weapons. We need armor.

The best armor is lined with the skin of the riverbed crocolisks nearby. Help us gather some.

passages.title: The Element of Supplies
passages.text: I am glad to see you don't think you're above this sort of task.

passages.title: The Element of Supplies
passages.text: Excellent job, <name>.  You might not think this adds up to much, but this might very well be the difference between life and death to one of our soldiers.

passages.title: Master Trapper
passages.text:
One thing about me that you might not know, <name>...

I come from a long line of trappers. My father taught me, as his taught him, to master the art of trapping creatures in a most merciful manner.

As any master trapper will tell you, the most important ingredient in an effective trap is the bait.

So let's start there.

Fill this bucket with the meat scraps from almost any wild creature in Uldum.

passages.title: Master Trapper
passages.text: Have you got enough to fill my bucket, <name>?

passages.title: Master Trapper
passages.text:
Fine work, my boy!

You'll master this trapping skill in no time.

passages.title: Bleeding the Enemy
passages.text:
I will not lie to you, <name>. We face a tremendous challenge ahead of us.

As you go behind the enemy lines into Neferset City, I want you to bring back the insignia of any Neferset scum you defeat.

It will be a boon to our armies to know that you've dealt a crushing blow to the enemy.

passages.title: Bleeding the Enemy
passages.text: It is good to see you once more, <name>.

passages.title: Bleeding the Enemy
passages.text: Excellent job, <name>.  Our troops will hear of your deeds.

passages.title: Beneath the Surface
passages.text:
Among the other precious gemstones hidden deep out of our reach in the Crumbling Depths, there are enormous ruby crystal clusters. They are infused with terrible energy.

It will not be easy to obtain such a thing, for they are well guarded. But you, you are stubborn and brave. I think this is something you can do.

Within the Crumbling Depths, look to where the tunnels end abruptly in stone. The clusters are found in those passages when they are to be found at all. Should you find one, return to me.

passages.title: Beneath the Surface
passages.text: These crystals are of great value, particularly to Gorsik. I shall have a heavy sway over him if I come into possession of one. I wish this to be so.

passages.title: Beneath the Surface
passages.text: This is exactly what I was seeking. Thank you, <race>.

passages.title: The Secret of Nahom
passages.text:
There is an old story about Nahom. It speaks of how a powerful prophet named Atulhet held off troves of enemies by channeling the power of the sun through this very temple.

Most believe the tale to be just a legend, but that power... would certainly be useful to us now.

The vile Neferset have ransacked Atulhet's tomb. They've taken any artifacts of power and shattered the tablets that encode his memories.

Go to the Tombs of the Precursors to the east and retrieve any fragments that you find.

passages.title: The Secret of Nahom
passages.text: Did you find them, <name>?  Were they salvageable?

passages.title: The Secret of Nahom
passages.text: Excellent.  Let's see if we can find anything of importance.

passages.title: A Long Way from Home
passages.text:
I've a feeling I was able to escape my captors because, frankly, there is nowhere to go.

Stranded on these platforms, they are bound to find me sooner or later. Unless...

It is said that the heart of an elemental noble can grant whoever holds it the characteristics of that element. Which, in the case of air, would be most useful during a downward trip.

Bring me Grand Vizier Ertan's heart so I can use its magic to land safely on the shoreline of Uldum.

passages.title: A Long Way from Home
passages.text: You'd best not suggest I ride with you on... whatever that thing is you flew in on.

passages.title: A Long Way from Home
passages.text: I thank you, <name>.  Even after I had escaped, I did not imagine I'd be able to return home.

passages.title: Twilight Documents
passages.text:
We've tailed one of the Twilight's Hammer operatives here. He goes by the name of Millhouse Manastorm.

We have reason to believe he's carrying important documents.

This is as far as we can safely go, however, without neglecting our duty to defend the Temple of Earth's inner perimeter.

Track down Manastorm and retrieve the documents from him.

passages.title: Twilight Documents
passages.text: These appear to be the right documents.

passages.title: Twilight Documents
passages.text: <You open the documents and look for any noteworthy information.>

passages.title: Relieving the Pain
passages.text:
The Arch Druid has an immense tolerance for pain. I've treated burn victims that spend twenty-two hours a day screaming in pain, and their burns weren't even half as bad as what Hamuul has suffered.

Nevertheless, I can sense that he is in greater discomfort than normal today. Bring me the hearts of the large fire elementals to the southeast. I can use them to prepare a soothing salve for our patient.

passages.title: Relieving the Pain
passages.text: These hearts will give us exactly what Hamuul needs to rest.

passages.title: Relieving the Pain
passages.text:
I must get to work preparing the salve immediately. These reagents lose their efficacy by the minute.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Releasing the Pressure
passages.text:
Having been burned so badly, Arch Druid Hamuul is suffering from edema - swelling of the body's tissues. It takes a great deal of his attendants' effort to keep his swelling down enough for him to breathe.

Normally, to reduce this swelling, we make cuts in his flesh, but he is weak, <name>. I cannot cut him today. I need your help.

Flamewaker scales will aid with the swelling, but you need a lot of them.

passages.title: Releasing the Pressure
passages.text: Do you have the scales? I hesitate to cut the Arch Druid again, but we must relieve the swelling somehow.

passages.title: Releasing the Pressure
passages.text: You are a compassionate <race>. With this many scales, we won't have to cut him again for another day, at least. Perhaps two.

passages.title: Hounds of Shannox
passages.text:
On the Firelands' largest island, our troops have been having trouble against Shannox, the flamewaker hunter. Not only does he have impeccable aim, but he keeps trained hounds that give our troops no end of trouble.

Tholo, in all his wisdom, thinks it would be a good idea to study the biology of these hounds. I, of course, agree with Tholo.

You will find several hounds in the Molten Flow, beneath the Furnace. We will need their ashes to study.

passages.title: Hounds of Shannox
passages.text: Any information we can get will be instrumental in helping our men defeat Shannox.

passages.title: Hounds of Shannox
passages.text:
This ash may seem indistinguishable from any other type of ash you find on this forsaken island, but trust me... you have found the right stuff.

We will have it analyzed immediately.

Return again soon. While I do enjoy spending time with Anren, we also appreciate your company, <name>.

passages.title: Starting Young
passages.text:
Our scouts are bringing back reports of fire hawk hatchlings all over the peak... their eggs must have hatched very recently. Better yet, it seems that they're extremely docile.

I know it may sound a strange and perhaps unsavory request, but if you were able to bring some of those hatchlings back to me, I might be able to train them to aid us in our war efforts.

Are you willing?

passages.title: Starting Young
passages.text:
I can't make up my mind on how to regard these creatures. They act like much like other avians, but they are very obviously native to this fiery place.

I wonder why Ragnaros and his minions have not made attempts to rally them against us...

passages.title: Starting Young
passages.text:
They look to have singed your gloves a bit, but I don't see any damage otherwise. Well done, <class>.

Come by again within the next few days to see how the training has gone.

passages.title: Orchard-Supplied Hardware
passages.text:
They may not be weaponmasters, but many of these farmers can wield a simple hoe or a rake as an extension of their own will.

That mastery coupled with the right motivation could muster a force capable of standing against the mogu.

If you can bring back some tools from the orchard, I'll distribute them to anyone willing to fight.

passages.title: Orchard-Supplied Hardware
passages.text: Were there any tools left?

passages.title: Orchard-Supplied Hardware
passages.text: There are no hunters among us, but we'll fight to protect our loved ones.

passages.title: A Humble Offering
passages.text:
I'm almost ready for the ritual, there's just one more thing we need: An offering.

Relax, I don't mean a sacrifice. Just a bit of food.

There are sure to be mushrooms growing in Tideview Thicket to the northwest that are suitable for this. Please bring some.

passages.title: A Humble Offering
passages.text: Even the dead know hunger.

passages.title: A Humble Offering
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. These mushrooms may not seem like much of an offering, but the sentiment alone will be enough to draw the spirits to us.

Also, they make a pretty fine stir-fry.

passages.title: Egg Collection
passages.text:
Ahhh, I should have known! You have the look of a hungry initiate.

I would gladly help you choose a serpent egg, but the Slitherscale have thoroughly raided the cloud serpent nests.

I'm terribly sorry. I don't know what to tell you.

Unless you're crazy enough to sneak into the saurok camp to the east and retrieve some stolen cloud serpent eggs, I'm afraid I can't help you.

passages.title: Egg Collection
passages.text: The saurok keep the stolen serpent eggs in their camp.

passages.title: Egg Collection
passages.text:
Oh, wonderful!

These eggs look...well...they look a little on the small side. Are you sure you couldn't find any better ones?

Oh well, I suppose with the current situation, we can't be so picky.

passages.title: Disarming the Enemy
passages.text:
If we are to stop the poachers, we need to take more aggressive action.

If we can remove the enemies' primary tools for killing and capturing serpents, we may be able to stop their operation altogether.

I need you to go into their territory on the eastern end of Windward Isle and steal their weapons.

A cat without claws cannot strike.

passages.title: Disarming the Enemy
passages.text: Is it done?

passages.title: Disarming the Enemy
passages.text: We have weakened them, but we cannot celebrate completely. A toothless tiger still has claws.

passages.title: Preservation
passages.text:
Oh no! We must stop them! <name>, is it? The Order needs your help!

Do you know what those horrible Slitherscale saurok are doing?

They have the audacity to steal cloud serpent eggs straight from the matriarch's nests!

While the cloud serpents become ever rarer, those brutes are... are...

<Suchi takes a deep breath.>

...they're eat their eggs for dinner! It's horrible!

Go to Windward Isle to the northeast and recover any unbroken eggs that you can. As students of the Order, it's our duty!

passages.title: Preservation
passages.text: Will those nasty Slitherscale saurok never give up?

passages.title: Preservation
passages.text:
Well done, <name>. As soon as Suchi told me she sent you to recover the stolen eggs, I knew you would accomplish the task.

Our instructors will make sure to return these eggs to a safer place.

passages.title: Tortoise Mastery
passages.text:
Granted, tortoises are not big game but they can be mean game. They also work as the perfect bait for bigger game!

Gotcher found some ol' tablets sayin' that the Torjari Pit is a sacrificin' site. The old empire used ta' feed unruly sorts to the waters as it were.

Well ah mean to see me what's down in that water. Gather up some fresh tortoise shells and meet me at the pit.

Let's see if ol' legends be true.

passages.title: Tortoise Mastery
passages.text: I've always been livin' in me father's shadow. But after today, folks are gonna remember the name of Nesingwary, Jr.!

passages.title: Tortoise Mastery
passages.text: Thank ye. This one aught ta' one up me pop.

passages.title: Mung-Mung's Vote II: Rotten to the Core
passages.text:
Dem virmen's back!

They been biting Mr. Mudclaw's carrots. Ruining his crop. And who is gonna pay? Mung-Mung, that's who!

You go get the chewed up carrots before Mr. Mudclaw sees. They all over the fields to the southwest, and down under the ground in the virmen's tunnels, too.

Otherwise, Mung-Mung in big trouble.

You do this for me?

passages.title: Mung-Mung's Vote II: Rotten to the Core
passages.text: I don't see no chewed up carrots. You don't see no chewed up carrots. Mr. Mudclaw never know, okay?

passages.title: Mung-Mung's Vote II: Rotten to the Core
passages.text: What do you mean, no virmen chewed them up? Teeth marks too small? WHAT? Then who else do this?

passages.title: The Crumbling Hall
passages.text:
An ancient mogu artifact has been uncovered in the Guo-Lai Vault, beyond the Hall of Statues. We've made repeated attempts to retrieve it, but none have been successful.

We cannot let this artifact fall into the hands of the Shao-Tien. I need someone capable to retrieve it, and quickly.

Are you in?

passages.title: The Crumbling Hall
passages.text: Have you recovered the artifact yet?

passages.title: The Crumbling Hall
passages.text:
When everyone else lets me down, you follow through. That's why I like you.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Thousand-Year Dumpling
passages.text:
One of my most popular recipes is the Thousand-Year Dumpling, which is filled with preserved vegetables.

I normally let the vegetables ferment in a hole underneath my house, but when I looked for them this morning, they were gone!

I blame those thieving virmen.

Bring them back, and I'll let you help me cook!

passages.title: The Thousand-Year Dumpling
passages.text: Try not to open any of the jars. If you do open one, you might not want to smell it too closely.

passages.title: The Thousand-Year Dumpling
passages.text: Now, my student, lean in closely. Let me show you the secret of the Thousand-Year Dumpling...

passages.title: Stealing is Bad... Re-Stealing is OK
passages.text:
The hozen, up in the mountains to the west, continue to steal vegetables from my fellow farmers. Being so close to Halfhill, I very rarely suffer hozen attacks, but my friends have not been so lucky.

Seems to me like they steal way more than they can eat. If you can find any intact vegetables up there in those mountains... steal them back!

passages.title: Stealing is Bad... Re-Stealing is OK
passages.text: Have you got them?

passages.title: Stealing is Bad... Re-Stealing is OK
passages.text: Thanks! I'll make sure these are distributed out to my fellow farmers.

passages.title: Fresh Needle Scent
passages.text:
Say, if you really are here to help, I could use me some needles off them sprites in Pranksters' Hollow.

The grummles don't believe in luck they can't smell. They'll pay better for yaks that have that fresh needle scent.

passages.title: Fresh Needle Scent
passages.text: Mmm. Nothing like the fresh scent of needle.

passages.title: Fresh Needle Scent
passages.text: You just earned me a handsome bonus. Getting those needles is a pain in the paw but worth it when we take our yaks to market. Here, for your troubles.

passages.title: Growing the Farm I: A Little Problem
passages.text:
So you need to whack some wily weeds?

No problem, neighbor! Only thing is, I'm running low on weed killer.

I make my own concoction - very potent, totally organic and good for the earth. Plants love it! Well... except for those pesky weeds. They hate the stuff!

If you bring me some Spideroot from the terraces just west of us, I'll make a fresh batch and go down to Yoon's farm myself.

I would gather some myself but... well... I hate spiders. You'll see what I mean.

passages.title: Growing the Farm I: A Little Problem
passages.text: How did the root gathering go?

passages.title: Growing the Farm I: A Little Problem
passages.text:
Well what do we have here? You harvested enough to last me a while.

Many thanks!

passages.title: No Pack Left Behind
passages.text:
The Broketooth hozen south of here killed all of my grummles. What is worse, their packages are undelivered.

Fortune frowns on a grummlepack undelivered.

Please, give my grummles peace on the great trail of beyond and bring their grummlepacks to me.

I will see they are delivered.

passages.title: No Pack Left Behind
passages.text: Grummles are a simple people. We are made to explore and deliver.

passages.title: No Pack Left Behind
passages.text:
You are good fortune for grummles.

When we are back at a proper camp I must buy you the smelliest, luckiest incense I can find.

passages.title: The Broketooth Ravage
passages.text:
They took my luckydo! Their leader hozen here, Mo Mo, stole my rabbitsfoot.

This is most bad fortune for grummles. My rabbitsfoot is a big luckydo for grummles everywhere. If hozen learn how to get luck from my rabbitsfoot then all is lost.

Please can you get it back?

passages.title: The Broketooth Ravage
passages.text: Grummles named for the luckydo that gives the most fortune to specific grummle. It is most important that hozen not steal a grummle's luck.

passages.title: The Broketooth Ravage
passages.text: My luckydo! Oh happy day of good fortune! Many thanks!

passages.title: Oil Stop
passages.text:
When the yaungols came, they began to dig up oil. What is this "oil", I wonder? Perhaps it is thing of much undiscovered luck. This I must know.

Here, take this vial, and fill it with yaungol oil from one of their windmills. I will give you many fortunes if you bring me some.

passages.title: Oil Stop
passages.text: Yaungols are scary. Yaungols with a luckydo like this "oil" are more scary.

passages.title: Oil Stop
passages.text: Happy day! Your reward. May these coins bring you good fortune.

passages.title: Build Your Own Raft
passages.text:
<Jay looks off in the direction of Kea Krak.>

Hmm. They don't seem to be... calming down. We're going to have to try something different.

You'll need a raft. Go grab some wood planks and seaweed, and bring them over to me. I'll put something together for you.

passages.title: Build Your Own Raft
passages.text: You got the stuff? I'll build your raft, I just need materials.

passages.title: Build Your Own Raft
passages.text: <Jay deftly weaves the planks together into a surprisingly seaworthy-looking vessel, then tosses them down into water below.>

passages.title: Gifts of the Great Crane
passages.text:
