The cranes of Krasarang are a gift from Chi-Ji. Even the very feathers they leave behind are a gift for us to appreciate.

We use these feathers to adorn our garments and to fletch arrows. But first... they must be gathered.

passages.title: Gifts of the Great Crane
passages.text: Even the smallest, flimsiest feather is proof enough that Chi-Ji loves us.

passages.title: Gifts of the Great Crane
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

Return to us again soon.

passages.title: It Was Almost Alive
passages.text:
A ritual took place here, and from the looks of it wasn't successful.

Among the abandoned items a book lies open. The text on the pages is foreign to you.

Carrying the whole book may be difficult, but a single page might be enough. If you can get the page to Lorewalker Cho he may be able to tell you what it says.

passages.title: It Was Almost Alive
passages.text: What have you found, <name>?

passages.title: It Was Almost Alive
passages.text:
This text is curious indeed, <name>...

It appears to have been written in the Meng dynasty, but some of the symbols are wrong. I don't think the Mogu wrote this, although it is oddly close.

It will take me some time to translate. Keep moving and see if you can find anything else.

passages.title: A Grummle's Luck
passages.text:
The yaungols stole our luckydos! Mean riders with spears took them from our caravan of brothers coming down the Burlap Trail.

This is very bad fortune. If the yaungol discover the secrets of luckydos all grummles will be in big trouble.

Recover our luckydos from Fire Camp Ruqin north of here and we will pay many fortunes to you.

passages.title: A Grummle's Luck
passages.text: A luckydo is a thing of much good fortune. Yaungol know nothing of how to use luckydos... yet.

passages.title: A Grummle's Luck
passages.text: Hurray! Our Luckydos. Many thanks and fortune to friend of grummles!

passages.title: Natural Antiseptic
passages.text:
The Shado-Pan are rare, elite, and quite expensive to train and replace. We can't afford to have any falling to a poisoned weapon or an infected cut. That's why I need you to get... something.

Let me be blunt. Mushan urine is a great, natural antiseptic. They produce a large amount of it, which is lucky... because we tend to use a lot.

passages.title: Natural Antiseptic
passages.text:
It's messy work, certainly.

Nowhere near as messy as digging graves.

passages.title: Natural Antiseptic
passages.text: Your messy work may have saved a few lives today, <race>.

passages.title: My Father's Crossbow
passages.text:
I came here to visit my dad at the temple. As soon as I got here, I saw the most terrifying thing I've ever seen.

It was a mantid, walking right past me, carrying my father's crossbow.

Something's happened to my dad! We've got to find out what it is... but first, we'll need his crossbow back. I saw him heading west, behind the temple.

passages.title: My Father's Crossbow
passages.text: Did... did you find it?

passages.title: My Father's Crossbow
passages.text:
Yeah, this is dad's.

Let's head on over to the temple. They'll know what...

<Ku-Mo's voice catches.>

...what happened to him.

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text:
I've seen the numbers these invaders have brought with them, this will not be an easy victory. I do know of one thing that may help us gain an advantage.

There is a plant that grows around the village that can be used to make a rather effective explosive liquid. If you can gather enough I can begin brewing the mixture.

The plant you are looking for is appropriately named volatile bloom. Handle it with care, <class>.

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text: Were you able to find a suitable amount of volatile blooms?

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text:
These are perfect! Now, I would go wash your hands a few times <class>.

I would also continue to avoid open flames for a few days...

passages.title: What's Yours Is Mine
passages.text:
The elders want us to mount a defense? We're not monks, <class>; we need weapons if we hope to fight!

Scavenge some arms from those barbarians for me. I should be able to melt them down and make something more suitable for our villagers to fight with.

Bring me as many as you can carry and I'll take care of the rest.

passages.title: What's Yours Is Mine
passages.text: We'll need more than luck to get us through this. I hope you found something I can work with.

passages.title: What's Yours Is Mine
passages.text:
Well, these are better than I had anticipated! I can make four spears for every one of their blades.

Don't you worry, I'll make sure the villagers are armed when the time comes.

passages.title: The Field Armorer
passages.text:
The Shado-Pan fight. As such, their armor often gets cut, scratched, torn, and burned. And it's my job to repair it.

I'm no armorer, but I can repair a broken piece of mail as long as the hole's not too big.

I prefer to use shell fragments from the tortoises that live in the wild fields to the northeast. Get some for me, and I can keep more Shado-Pan armored and alive.

passages.title: The Field Armorer
passages.text: I refuse to let one of our kind fall just because of a broken set of armor.

passages.title: The Field Armorer
passages.text: Excellent. I'll get to repairing the armor tonight, once most everyone's returned.

passages.title: A Proper Poultice
passages.text:
A dry bandage doesn't do much good, other than maybe keeping bugs out of the wound. In some camps, that's the best you can hope for.

Not in my camp, though.

I prefer to make a paste from whatever soothing herbs I can find, and layer that between bandages. The most soothing herbs I've been able to find in the field are the Mao-Willows from the fields in the northeast. If you run into any, bring them back.

passages.title: A Proper Poultice
passages.text: Any luck out there, <name>?

passages.title: A Proper Poultice
passages.text:
These will do.

The Shado-Pan appreciates your work, <name>.

passages.title: Relics of the Swarm
passages.text:
This strange-looking carving is covered in a complex written language that might be mantid in origin.

You notice more relics strewn carelessly among the camps and inside the lake.

Perhaps the Klaxxi would be interested in examining these artifacts.

Who knows? Perhaps it will earn you some favor.

passages.title: Relics of the Swarm
passages.text: What do you have there?

passages.title: Relics of the Swarm
passages.text:
These relics describe the history of Kypari Vos and the nearby amber trees.

I would like to study these.

Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Kunchong Treats
passages.text:
As Kovok grows, he will require equal parts discipline and reward.

I lack no shortage of discipline, but our supply of meat is almost empty.

To the south, you will find turtles roaming north of the Lake of Stars and Kypari Zar.

Hunt them. Kovok likes the taste of their flesh.

passages.title: Kunchong Treats
passages.text: What have you brought for Kovok?

passages.title: Kunchong Treats
passages.text:
Yes, a worthy feast.

Well done.

passages.title: Egg Rescue!
passages.text:
Eggs. Yes, you heard me right. I said eggs, and these aren't for eating.

Have you ever seen a cloud serpent egg?

These rare eggs look like jewels, and were once worth their weight in solid gold.

Shan'ze Dao to the north normally teems with wild cloud serpents, but the mogu and the sprites have their eggs on lock-down.

We need to save as many of these precious eggs as we can.

I'm counting on YOU, <name>.

passages.title: Egg Rescue!
passages.text: Did you find any eggs? The serpents lay their eggs in nests on the beach, but the wood sprites are also known to steal them whenever they can.

passages.title: Egg Rescue!
passages.text:
Gently, gently!

Thank you for recovering these eggs safely, <name>.

I know a few Serpent Riders in the Jade Forest who will take good care of these.

passages.title: Onyx Hearts
passages.text:
The Shan'ze Serpentbinders dominate the minds of wild cloud serpents, but they also create their own dark creatures from stone, metal, blood, and ancient sorcery.

Their creations, the Onyx Stormclaws, guard the island to the northwest.

I wish to study the magic binding these creatures. Bring me their hearts, so that I can better understand what sorcery we are up against.

passages.title: Onyx Hearts
passages.text: The Onyx Stormclaws will never disobey their masters.

passages.title: Onyx Hearts
passages.text: These will do well, <name>. Thank you.

passages.title: Dark Arts
passages.text:
It is said that Shan'ze Dao was once home to a great mogu temple.

There, the Shan'ze studied and practiced the art of subjugating the dead or inanimate.

Much of their knowledge still remains on the island to the northwest, buried among the ruins.

We need to get our hands on their knowledge - both to keep it out of their hands, and to understand the nature of their experiments.

passages.title: Dark Arts
passages.text: Knowledge is powerful. That is why the mogu are so dangerous.

passages.title: Dark Arts
passages.text:
Well done, <name>.

We'll begin deciphering the writing on these tablets at once.

passages.title: Bronze Claws
passages.text:
Among the Shan'ze's fiercest and most loyal creations are their quilen.

These beasts will hunt until they kill their prey, or die in the process.

I need you to not only cull their numbers, but also to retrieve their bronze claws.

Their claws are strong and razor sharp, and we can use them to make weapons and hooks for our cause.

passages.title: Bronze Claws
passages.text: The quilen are fierce, but I see fierceness in your eyes as well.

passages.title: Bronze Claws
passages.text:
These claws will come in handy.

Good work, <class>.

passages.title: Through the Portal
passages.text:
Ah, just the <class> I wanted to see!

We've finally figured out why the portal is not working. We need more arcane powder!

It would take us months to get a shipment sent out to us, but luckily, the mogu on this island carry plenty for their own spells.

They tend to use some older stuff, so we're going to need a lot of it.

passages.title: Through the Portal
passages.text: Did you find the powders?

passages.title: Through the Portal
passages.text:
Excellent! Excellent!

This is just the stuff, <name>.

We'll get to work right away. I have no doubt we'll be done very soon.

passages.title: Sap Tapping
passages.text:
I found a grove of young amber trees to the east, Wakener.

I've placed tapping devices on these trees, but I have been too busy to retrieve the sap.

I need someone to find the extractors. Activate them, then bring me samples of the amber.

passages.title: Sap Tapping
passages.text:
These trees are still young. They are not yet kypari.

Their sap is like water, while the sap of a true kypari tree is like wine.

They must be allowed to grow.

passages.title: Sap Tapping
passages.text:
Ah yes, this is exactly what I needed.

I will examine these samples. We must continue to monitor the health of these young kypari.

passages.title: Putting An Eye Out
passages.text:
Ah! Wakener! You must help me! (You will help me, or else I will help myself to you!)

I need more materials for my experiments, yes yes! (Blood and guts, hearts and brains, tongues and eyes, eyes, eyes!)

To the west, I have seen creatures of mist and fog. They possess such big, round, wonderful globes! Big for seeing, round and unblinking!

Go now, little Wakener. Bring me back a single pristine eye!

passages.title: Putting An Eye Out
passages.text: Ooooh, what wonderful, tasty parts have you brought me?

passages.title: Putting An Eye Out
passages.text: Yes, yes! Wonderful! Oh, so delicious!

passages.title: Profit Mastery: Chasheen
passages.text:
I am totally on to another great scam!

When I was flying overhead I saw a really ancient tigress prowling about.

Do you know how much her blood would go for on the black market? Not to mention if I convince some warlocks it adds extra potency to their summoning spells or something.

If you bring me back some of her blood I will cut you in on the scam. She was prowling about on the far side of the Dojani River from here.

passages.title: Profit Mastery: Chasheen
passages.text: I thought about taking that tiger on myself but to be honest I like living...

passages.title: Profit Mastery: Chasheen
passages.text: Impressive! Can you smell the money? Here's your end.

passages.title: Robbing Robbers of Robbers
passages.text:
Ah, a <class>. I could make good use of your skills.

A convoy was struck just up the road by a band of marauding saurok. These marauders made off with some... merchandise... her ladyship, the Madam Goya, had a mind to sell.

One does not steal from her ladyship.

If you recover these items I will gladly provide you a finders fee.

passages.title: Robbing Robbers of Robbers
passages.text: Saurok are seldom this bold.

passages.title: Robbing Robbers of Robbers
passages.text: Ah, our merchandise. Madam Goya will be pleased. You have the gratitude of her ladyship.

passages.title: Everything I Know About Cooking
passages.text:
I'm so glad you enjoy my food. Are you interested in the recipes? If so, you should learn them properly, from my teachers in Halfhill Market. Everything I know about the kitchen, I learned from them.

Say, if you happen to pass through there, would you deliver this note to Sungshin Ironpaw for me? She was my favorite teacher, and I want her to know that I miss her.

passages.title: Everything I Know About Cooking
passages.text: You have a letter for me?

passages.title: Everything I Know About Cooking
passages.text: My, that's so thoughtful. I love hearing from my old students.

passages.title: The Shoe Is On The Other Foot
passages.text:
I loathe sprites! One time, one of those nasty buggers followed me all day, putting dirt in my tea and bugs in my hair.

I mean, who does that!?

Well, I think it's time for a little payback. Do you know what the sprites up at Windward Isle love more than anything in the world?

Yeah, you guessed it. Shoes!

And we're going to steal them. Won't that make them mad! Hah!

Well, I'm scared to go near sprites, so you'll have to do it, <name>.

passages.title: The Shoe Is On The Other Foot
passages.text: Did you see the looks on their faces? Were they mad?

passages.title: The Shoe Is On The Other Foot
passages.text:
I see you and Ningna have been up to some mischief. Unfortunately, this type of behavior is not condoned by the Order--

Wait, where did you find those shoes? I've been looking for that pair of moleskin riding boots for ages!

Well... I suppose I will let this slide... this time. Hmph.

passages.title: Pooped
passages.text:
<Your serpent catches your gaze and ducks its head bashfully.>

You can tell that someone has gotten out of its pen and had "an accident."

Well, at the rate that the hatchling's been eating, it had to come out the other end... somewhere.

You had better find the serpent's poop and clean it up before the Serpent Masters find out.

passages.title: Pooped
passages.text: <The hatchling watches you innocently.>

passages.title: Pooped
passages.text: The hatchling plays contentedly, oblivious to your efforts. Sigh... sometimes, the life of a serpent trainer is quite thankless.

passages.title: Tiny Treats
passages.text:
As you near, your serpent opens its mouth and begins drooling. It looks quite hungry since you last left it.

From the way it whimpers and slaps its tail, you can tell it is not looking for just any treat, but a special favorite snack.

Your serpent loves to munch on tiny spider eyes, but this delicacy comes only from the Widowspawn spiders in the cave along the coast to the north.

Well, what's a rider to do? Your serpent is waiting.

passages.title: Tiny Treats
passages.text: Your serpent perks up at your return.

passages.title: Tiny Treats
passages.text: Your serpent nudges your hand affectionately, then proceeds to devour the treats!

passages.title: Saving the Serpents
passages.text:
Those Oona hozen have gone too far this time.

Do you know what they are doing with wild cloud serpents? Captured hatchlings are forced to fight one another in the pits, for nothing more than the Oona's amusement.

Savages!

If the young hatchlings learn such aggressive behavior at a young age, they may become violent and corrupted adults. A malicious cloud serpent is not something we want to deal with.

We must save the hatchlings.

passages.title: Saving the Serpents
passages.text:
The Order of the Cloud Serpent has worked for centuries to make the cloud serpents into loyal companions. Our kindness brings out the best in these creatures.

Unfortunately, violence and anger can quickly turn them into destructive monsters.

passages.title: Saving the Serpents
passages.text: Ah yes, these hatchlings look quite tired. They have been through a great ordeal, but thanks to you, they are safe now.

passages.title: Thunderlord for a Day
passages.text:
Pieces of a Thunderlord chain lay on the ground. It is of a very simple design, but effective.

With enough parts, even the most unskilled person could assemble a chain and grapple as effective as those used by the Thunderlord Grapplers.

passages.title: Thunderlord for a Day
passages.text: This shoddy, beaten anvil is used mostly for crafting chains and what little other metal working the Thunderlord require.

passages.title: Thunderlord for a Day
passages.text: With a quick tap of a hammer and a snip of the rings, the Thunderlord Grapple is as good as new.

passages.title: The Inkmasters of the Arboretum
passages.text: I have heard that the Inkmasters at the Arboretum are in need of aid from a scribe of great skill. You should speak with Inkmaster Wei, if you wish to help.

passages.title: Demons Among Us - Horde
passages.text:
If you are reading this, it means I have fallen in battle. As my last request, please deliver this letter to Thalia at Teluuna Observatory.

Dearest Thalia,

You have always been my best friend, ever since we were children growing up in Tuurem.

I have always been too afraid to tell you my feelings, but I cannot leave this world without finally speaking the truth.

Thalia, I love you with all my heart.

I shall wait for you in the next world. I will for eternity for you.

Love,

Thamuun

passages.title: Just the Beginning
passages.text:
I forgive Orgrim. He acted as well all must - we do what our hearts tell us is right.

We should return to your outpost and discuss our next course of action. There is nothing left for us here.

I will ask the human to open a portal for us. We shall speak again there.

passages.title: The Shadow of the Worldbreaker
passages.text:
Looks like we'll soon have another obstacle in our way: that ridiculously large tank that they have pointed at the Dark Portal. The Iron Worldbreaker, I think they call it.

If I had some documentation on how it might work, then I might be able to figure out how to shut it down. Maybe some o' those machinists and laborers have some documentation on how it works?

passages.title: The Shadow of the Worldbreaker
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: The Shadow of the Worldbreaker
passages.text:
Mmm... yes... simple enough.

<The dwarf flips through the pages and no longer seems to notice your presence.>

passages.title: The Gunpowder Plot
passages.text:
Ey, <pal/lady>! We got an issue, here.

Me ol' pal Thaelin's rigged together this here plunger out of spare Blackrock parts - engineerin' whiz that he is - but we're gonna need some gunpowder if we really want ta' do any damage.

passages.title: The Gunpowder Plot
passages.text: Don't go doin' anything inappropriate with that gunpowder, now.

passages.title: The Gunpowder Plot
passages.text: Woo hoo hoo haaaaa!

passages.title: Ameeka, Master Tailor
passages.text:
Ameeka created this book to document and pass down our most cherished crafting techniques to our children. She must have dropped it while traveling. She will be relieved to see her book.

From what I have heard from other villagers, she was last seen on the road to Elodor. Perhaps you can find her there.

passages.title: Ameeka, Master Tailor
passages.text: Hello, traveler! Is there something that I can help you with?

passages.title: Ameeka, Master Tailor
passages.text: Is that my tailoring tome? It is! I'm so glad it is safe! How can I ever repay you?

passages.title: Your First Engineering Work Order
passages.text: Now that the engineering works is complete, we can start producing gearspring parts for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Engineering Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Engineering Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: [UNUSED]Blood of the Annihilan
passages.text:
We must make contact with Lord Illidan's spirit. But to do that, we need something powerful enough to fuel the nether crucible. I know just the thing.

A pit lord named Malinoth has taken over a nearby cave. If we acquire his blood, you can use it to power the crucible. Then, you can make contact with Illidan in the Twisting Nether.

passages.title: Craig's Test Quest Again!
passages.text: An honorable person gives me cloth

passages.title: A Rather Long Walk
passages.text:
I'm concerned for Elder Aldryth. He went out for a walk about ten thousand years ago, and he has not returned.

With these naga attacking, I fear he may be in danger!

If you dare venture out into the fray, do look out for our court elder.

passages.title: A Rather Long Walk
passages.text: Have you seen him?

passages.title: A Rather Long Walk
passages.text:
I can't tell you how relieved I am that Elder Aldryth has returned.

Honestly, life here in the palace hasn't been the same without him. Everything seemed to have... lost its color. Perhaps now we can get back to our normal lives.

passages.title: [UNUSED]Rolling With the Tidestone
passages.text:
Before I forget, <name>: the Tidestone shards. They are yours to protect now.

Bring them back to your dragon. The people of Azsuna stand behind you.

passages.title: Your First Alchemy Work Order
passages.text: Now that the alchemy lab is complete, we can start producing alchemical catalysts for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Alchemy Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Alchemy Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: Your First Leatherworking Work Order
passages.text: Now that the tannery is complete, we can start producing burnished leather for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Leatherworking Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Leatherworking Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]The Ancient One
passages.text:
This place is now the home of what is left of the Blue Dragonflight. Its eldest dragon, Senegos, lies ahead within a pool of ley energy. If any are wise enough to help us find the Pillar of Creation that we seek on Azsuna, it will be him.

Stellagosa went ahead to join her grandfather. She assured me that we are welcome to enter the repose.

Come, <name>, we must hurry. Even from here, I can sense his life force waning. Let us approach him together.

passages.title: The Magister of Mixology
passages.text:
As you must know, I'm a connoisseur of drinks... specifically, arcane-infused spirits. Cocktail mixing is alchemy, and as everyone knows, alchemy is magic.

My latest drink must be more exotic than anything I've conjured before. I already have most of what I need. But there are a couple of items left on the list.

Notice the herons down in the lagoon? As with many of the creatures on Azsuna, the magic coursing through the island permeates them.

Their eggs will do nicely.

passages.title: The Magister of Mixology
passages.text: Are we speaking again because you have my eggs?

passages.title: The Magister of Mixology
passages.text:
Capital! A prodigious start.

I implore you to create this marvelous mixture for yourself. I want to share the delight of alchemical spirits with the world!

You'll need to get more eggs for yourself, though.

passages.title: Presentation is Everything
passages.text:
The eggs will provide the 'oomph' to my drink's character. But there's another element, and this must not be underestimated!

Presentation.

Now, you could go with your standard olive skewered on a toothpick. Maybe a carrot stalk stuck slapdash out of a glass.

But then, you wouldn't be me.

No, my friend. What MY drink needs to sell it visually comes from a one-of-a-kind creature. I'm only going to serve it once and so my drink deserves something unique.

The eyes of Gangamesh are what I need.

passages.title: Presentation is Everything
passages.text: Yes? You have the eyes?

passages.title: Presentation is Everything
passages.text:
I was going to present this to one of the ladies of the court. Doing so might increase my standing in certain social circles.

But, I just can't bring myself to do it. Who better to drink my latest masterpiece than, well... me?

passages.title: Mana Bark
passages.text:
We need bark from the trees if we are going to fix the wood.

Being a mortal, you can walk right in and pick up the mana bark without any trouble, as long as you don't get eaten by something.

Can you get us some mana bark?

passages.title: Essence of the Unbound
passages.text:
I need your help, mortal.

Something has warded the Mana Wood against our kind

That same something is changing the song of the wood. We can hear it.

Enter the wood and gather essence from some of the local wildlife and maybe we can track this thing down.

I will project an image of myself in the wood for when you are done.

passages.title: Rift Rippers
passages.text:
Something is opening rifts to the twisting nether using the ley line energy.

That is never a good thing.

Our kind may not be able to enter the forest, but you can.

Take this gem and look for these unbound rifts. The gem will let you seal these breaches.

I will project an image of myself into the forest when you are done.

passages.title: We Meet at Light's Hope
passages.text:
Thank the Light I found you!

Highlord Fordring has called all paladins to Light's Hope Chapel to discuss our next course of action following the Broken Shore. He sent me to personally make sure you were in attendance.

I will ask Khadgar to direct this portal to Light's Hope for you. We must make haste.

passages.title: Preserving The Lore
passages.text:
<A cool breeze of thought and memory enters your mind as you touch the strangely glowing stone. Within an instant, the purpose of this stone has been made manifest.>

<You realize that what you hold is a Stone of Remembrance; an object imbued with druidic knowledge and lore. The greedy Stoneblood harpies must have stolen these precious artifacts from the druids in Thas'talah. You decide to search for more of these missing stones and return them to the Archdruid of Lore.>

passages.title: Defending The Grove
passages.text:
The harpies have had a presence in Val'Sharah for hundreds of years. They have never been much more than an occasional nuisance; thus we have tolerated their presence here within these woods.

However, something has emboldened them... it feels as though the forest is weakening... they must sense it as well.

The opportunistic harpies have broken the peace and attacked us in a time of weakness.

Help us defend Thas'talah by slaying the invaders.

passages.title: A True Leader Inspires Others
passages.text:
<Lord/Lady> <name>, for all of your mastery over the Light you cannot possibly be everywhere at once. As newly ordained Knights of the Silver Hand it is our duty to carry out your will and defend our world from the darkness.

There is an ancient tome within this sanctum by the armory that can serve as the means to disperse your will - direct our blades and we will carry out your command.

passages.title: Minion! Kill Them!
passages.text:
Per your contract you will help me gather supplies for a perfectly harmless ritual.

I need feathers, and horns. Lots of horns. See those shadowrunners, prowlers and heron over there in the Olivian Veil? They should have lots of both.

Oh! And I need olives. Lots of olives. One for each finger.

Minion! Let's ride!

passages.title: Minion! Kill Them!
passages.text: This land is ripe for the taking. Especially the olives. They are really ripe. And I love ripe olives.

passages.title: Minion! Kill Them!
passages.text: Mmmm. Olives. I love these things. They are the only reason worth to come to this filthy world.

passages.title: Seeds of Remedy
passages.text:
Several of my fellow druids have been gravely wounded. Although my restorative abilities will keep them stabilized, there is still more we can do to aid them.

<Aaelar produces a handful of glowing seeds from his pouch.>

These are efflorescent seeds imbued with the blessing of nature. If I had more of them, I could create a potion that would greatly aid in the recovery of the wounded.

Harvest the efflorescent saplings that grow near the fountain of Delyra and I will prepare the potion.

passages.title: Menacing Sprites
passages.text:
The local sprites are running amok and causing all sorts of problems!

Val'sharah is home to a variety of forest and pond sprites will take any opportunity to spread mischief and chaos. It seems as though an especially wicked group of sprites have descended upon Thas'talah in the wake of the harpy invasion.

They are attacking the local wildlife and bullying the nearby faerie dragons. If you aid the local woodland creatures by taking care of the sprite menace, you will have our thanks.

passages.title: Val'sharah
passages.text: [PH] Go through the portal in Dalaran and meet Malfurion Stormrage in Val'Sharah.

passages.title: Cenarius, Keeper of the Grove
passages.text:
Greetings, hero.

Welcome to Val'sharah. It has been an age since I have set foot in these precious woods. Too long...

Our work here is simple. We must call upon my mentor, Cenarius, and learn where he safeguards the Tears of Elune. With them, you will be one step closer to sealing Sargeras' Tomb and thwarting the Legion.

You have many treacherous tasks in front of you. Consider your visit here a brief respite.

Come, this will not take long.

passages.title: Eyes in the Overlook
passages.text:
Alliance personnel from the Skyfire were spotted parachuting into Blackbeak Overlook.

I was unable to confirm numbers or positions during my flyover, but I did see parachutes tangled in treetops and a LOT of ravenbears on the ground.

If anyone is up there, they must be laying low and keeping an eye on us.

I have posted a rider at the top of the overlook to keep watch while I press forward into Stormheim.

- Liza Cullen, Dread-Rider - 1st Wing

passages.title: [PH] Worg Pelts
passages.text:
You know, it looks awful cold up there. If you plan on surviving your trip through those mountains, you should probably go prepared.

You'll find some worgs roaming the hills around here, and some of them still have their winter coats. Get yourself a few pelts to layer on while you're up there.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
The vrykul around here seem to use scales from these drakes to fashion their armor. 

If you were able to gather enough material from the local drakes, you may be able to make something useful out of it.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text: Oh, what do you have there?

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
Good thinking gathering up these scales. 

It should be simple enough to make a solid piece of armor from them.

passages.title: Halting the Nightmare
passages.text:
The corruption of the vale is the work of satyrs.

The new power they wield is unlike any I've seen... it is dark, seething and terrible.

Nefarious demon totems help spread their taint upon the land.

The Nghtmare totems must be destroyed if we are to hold back the tide of corruption.

passages.title: Rescued From Darkness
passages.text:
Midnight Vale is home to a unique breed of Nightsaber known as the Vale Prowler. For centuries, our clan has lived in harmony with these great feline hunters.

However, even as we speak satyrs are twisting and corrupting the vale into a place of death and nightmare. Even the forest itself lashes out in torment against the living, causing many of the forest creatures to flee the vale.

I fear for the safety of the youngest nightsabers, who may yet be caught in the twisting chaos, unable to escape.

passages.title: Side Effects May Include Mild Undeath
passages.text:
Exposure to this particular "byproduct" is quite nasty.

Rapid cell degeneration quickly reduces the subject to a shambling husk incapable of any reason or thought beyond a violent, throbbing hatred for the warmth of life.

As you might imagine, the local fauna have been affected by the spill. Oh, and most of the crew as well...

Anyway, good luck!

passages.title: Side Effects May Include Mild Undeath
passages.text:
Come now, surely you don't intend to leave them in this state? Have you no compassion?

How about money - you like money, don't you?

passages.title: Side Effects May Include Mild Undeath
passages.text: The R.A.S. is nothing if not humane.

passages.title: The Ashbringer
passages.text:
The blade fell... during the battle... Broken Shore...

<Tirion coughs up blood.>

My time... is short. You must go ahead... into the temple ruins...

You must... retrieve...

...the Ashbringer.

passages.title: Unfortunate Circumstances
passages.text:
The Illidari ask us to trust them, but all I see is failure. Look around... this entire city has been lost!

I tracked down the pit lord Malinoth here and brought what few of my men I had with me to put an end to this depravity. They were not enough.

The brute threw us in this cage and was 'saving us for later.' We need your help, <name>.

passages.title: Let's Make A Deal
passages.text:
Hey there!

You seem like a gullib- er... um... "intelligent" type.

I propose a deal.

I need a minion to be my muscle to help me acquire a few special... "ingredients" for a ritual.

In exchange, I'll give you my former master to do with whatever you demon-slaying types do with demons.

If you are interested, just sign here. In blood, please.

passages.title: Let's Make A Deal
passages.text: Yeah! Yeah! You read the contract? I made it myself. Really good binding clauses in there.

passages.title: Let's Make A Deal
passages.text: At last! A minion of my very own!

passages.title: The Methods of the Nightfallen
passages.text:
I have a theory, <name>.

Have you encountered the nightfallen elves of Azsuna? They descend from the Highborne, and the accomplishments of Highborne smiths are legendary.

These fallen elves do a bit of arcane tinkering, crafting sentries to patrol their camps.

Bring me a memory core from one of their constructs. Who knows what manner of smithlore might lie within!

passages.title: The Methods of the Nightfallen
passages.text: Hopefully we can extract something useful.

passages.title: The Methods of the Nightfallen
passages.text: If my guess is correct, the answer to our welding problem lies within this core.

passages.title: Chicken Scratch
passages.text:
I think I have just the thing to extract the information from this core for you.

<Timofey loads the core into the hopper of a clearly goblin-made machine, then covers his ears.>

You may wish to avert your eyes, blacksmith.

passages.title: Chicken Scratch
passages.text: Highborne! Ancient Highborne! What an amazing find!

passages.title: Chicken Scratch
passages.text: ...is what I would say if we weren't floating directly above the ancestral home of the Highborne. You need this translated or something?

passages.title: Secrets of Leysmithing
passages.text:
I could spend hours poring over the details of this fascinating manuscript!

...is what I would say if this weren't the simplest of tasks for someone of my skill level. It's about something called "Leysmithing". Here.

<The gnome scribbles down a translation on the back of the scroll.>

There it is, word-for-word. Bring me something interesting next time.

passages.title: Secrets of Leysmithing
passages.text: Did you find the engineering shop?

passages.title: Secrets of Leysmithing
passages.text:
I hadn't even thought far enough ahead to realize you'd need this to be translated, too. Good thinking.

See, this is why I keep adventurers like you around the shop.

passages.title: The Highmountain Smiths
passages.text:
I think we've gone as far as we can go with what I know, <name>.

The tauren of Highmountain must have some smiths among their ranks. See if you can find out how to further progress our leysmithing abilities from them.

passages.title: The Highmountain Smiths
passages.text: You, outsider, think yourself worthy of our wisdom?

passages.title: You Are Not Worthy
passages.text:
You wish me to teach you how to strengthen your crafts? We do not simply share the secrets of our trade with outsiders who ask for them.

We do, however, respect craftsmanship and discipline.

Let's see your hammerwork. Our greenhorn trainees use those small anvils over there. Craft your best pair of gauntlets so I may judge your work.

passages.title: You Are Not Worthy
passages.text: I'm waiting, outsider.

passages.title: You Are Not Worthy
passages.text:
The craftsmanship is good, but the quality is feeble at best.

<Barm snaps the gauntlets in half and throws them to floor>

You have proven yourself worthy of my tutelage however.

passages.title: From One Master to Another
passages.text:
Now young one, go back to your master
in Dalaran and continue to practice your swing. We'll always be here if you wish to come back and learn more.

passages.title: From One Master to Another
passages.text: I see, the strength of their work comes from the technique of their hammer strikes. Very interesting...

passages.title: Felsmith Nal'ryssa
passages.text:
Word has been circulating in smithing circles about a pair of Illidari blacksmiths that have been doing exciting work out on the demon-infested front lines of Suramar. I'd follow up myself, but anything described as "demon-infested" is a little too exotic for my tastes.

I just make the armor. I prefer not to wear it.

You, though... you could follow up on this tip. Be on the lookout for Nal'ryssa. From what I hear, she's a hell of a smith.

passages.title: Felsmith Nal'ryssa
passages.text: You here to lend us a hand?

passages.title: Part of the Team
passages.text:
You're a blacksmith?

<The elf looks down at your hammer.>

Still working in leystone, are you? I might be able to help you out.

Alliances out here are hard-won. You've got a pretty face, but that's no guarantee that you aren't working for the demons. I can't afford to trust you yet.

Don't come back until you're caked in demon's blood. Then we'll talk smithing.

passages.title: Part of the Team
passages.text: That'll do.

passages.title: Smith Under Fire
passages.text:
You lack recipes for boots?

What, were you trained by a tauren or something?

Hurry up, then. We probably have a few minutes before the demons attack again. Here's a pattern - show me your work.

passages.title: Smith Under Fire
passages.text: Watch your step out here on the front lines. This isn't your peaceful floating city's blacksmithing shop.

passages.title: Smith Under Fire
passages.text: Not bad, <class>. You know how to swing a hammer.

passages.title: Nal'ryssa's Technique
passages.text:
Listen, <class>. We need smiths like you to carry on the traditions of the Illidari, should we fail in our crusade against the Legion. You are ready to learn.

Bring me materials. Lots of them. When you return, we will have much to discuss.

passages.title: Nal'ryssa's Technique
passages.text: Are you ready to learn?

passages.title: Nal'ryssa's Technique
passages.text: Good. Now let's get to work.

passages.title: The Firmament Stone
passages.text:
When working with felslate and demonsteel, one must use special equipment. Specifically, an anvil hard enough to withstand the energy given off when felslate is hammered.

Urael and I no longer possess such an anvil. But your friends, the Highmountain tauren, do.

Gain access to the Firmament Stone, their sacred anvil, and we can start working with demonsteel again.

passages.title: The Firmament Stone
passages.text:
You have returned, <name>. Have you come for more training?

What? The Firmament Stone?

That's another matter entirely.

passages.title: Tribal Knowledge
passages.text:
First, however, you'll need proper patterns for demonsteel armor. While access to the stone is earned through hard work and perseverance, access to our recipes is limited to the trusted members of our tribe.

Perhaps you should seek another smith if you wish to discuss demonsteel patterns.

passages.title: Tribal Knowledge
passages.text:
I wouldn't expect the tauren to part with their recipes easily. We are not quite as... bull-headed as they are, but even our recipes will come at a price.

Still, you have earned access to the Firmament Stone, and proven the path to another great anvil, should Urael and I need it.

You have earned this recipe, as a token of our thanks.

passages.title: Lord Hal'shara's Tomb
passages.text: The tomb, I've found it.

passages.title: Worthy of the Stone
passages.text:
You have nothing more to prove to me, <name>. Your training is complete.

Only a very small herd of smiths have earned the right to the Firmament Stone. You should speak with Muirn Ironhorn, who maintains vigil over our sacred stone. He will tell you what to do next.

passages.title: Worthy of the Stone
passages.text:
A new face? It's been years...

This is the Firmament Stone. Memorize her curves. Learn her intricacies. If you truly wish to push your smithing skill to the next level, I predict that you will be spending a lot of time at her side.

passages.title: Flower-Pickers and Potion-Quaffers
passages.text:
Now that we know the foxflower flux is safe to use, we can start stocking it. That being said, I don't particularly feel like picking flowers. Do you feel like picking flowers? Didn't think so.

Go talk to the alchemists and herbalists across the way. I'm sure we can set up some sort of work order arrangement.

passages.title: Flower-Pickers and Potion-Quaffers
passages.text: Have you spoken with the alchemists and herbalists yet?

passages.title: Flower-Pickers and Potion-Quaffers
passages.text: Now that that's all taken care of, we can move on to improving our recipes.

passages.title: TRACKING Nightmare 02
Gates of Valhallas
passages.text:
Escaping the grasp of Helya is no small feat. You may prove to be a worthy warrior after all.

Skovald has entered Valhallas; you are running out of time. Legion has corrupted the minds of the Skovald's men. A battalion of unworthy vrykul is attempting to enter the portal to Valhallas.

The giants that protect the gates are fighting a losing battle. There is no end to Legion's onslaught.

Speak with the dragon, Vehdir, inside the gates near the portal. He will aid you on your next task.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
The vrykul around here seem to use scales from these drakes to fashion their armor. 

If you were able to gather enough material from the local drakes, you may be able to make something useful out of it.

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text: What have we here?

passages.title: Built to Scale
passages.text:
Good thinking. If the vrykul can use the drake scales for their armor, why not us? 

It shouldn't be too tough to work this into something serviceable.

passages.title: Black Rook Orders
passages.text:
The letter is written in midnight ink:

"A demon invasion is imminent, but as long as the fires of Black Rook Hold blaze, we shall protect kaldorei lands. Kill any intruders who stand in our way."

- K.R."

Perhaps Jarod Shadowsong will want to see this.

passages.title: Aid For the Wounded
passages.text: [PH] Many of our defenders have been gravely wounded on the battlefield. Take with you this moonstone and use it on our wounded allies on the battlefield. Heal their wounds and renew their courage against the forces of the enemy.

passages.title: Cleansing the Corruption
passages.text:
All along the battlefield, the satyrs have erected dark totems that spread the corruption of the Emerald Nightmare upon the land.

As long as the Nightmare totems remain, we will not be able to hold back the corruption!

If you truly wish to aid us in the fight, destroy the totems that you encounter upon the battlefield.

Our survival depends on it!

passages.title: Nightmare Bombs
passages.text:
[PH] The satyrs have taken to the skies on giant bats. From the air they rain down the corruption of the nightmare upon us.

Disarm the nightmare bombs before they further corrupt the forest.

passages.title: The Demon's Trail
passages.text:
Xavius! How many times must I end that wretched satyr before he stays dead...

We must get to Shaladrassil and find Xavius before it is too late!

My wounds are grave, but they will heal... do not concern yourself with my safety. There is little time... we may already be too late...

passages.title: Our Last Hope
passages.text:
Your jailor, Maiev Shadowsong, stands outside the open door to your cell. The leader of the Wardens has just finished removing your bonds.

In the distance, you can hear sounds of battle. The unmistakable stench of the Burning Legion wafts through the air.

passages.title: Our Last Hope
passages.text:
The Vault has fallen to the Burning Legion.

It pains me to say it, but all is lost, but for one glimmer of hope... YOU. Believe me when I say, I did NOT want to have to do this. However, it would seem I have no choice.

Help me, demon hunter, and I will grant you your freedom.

passages.title: Lost in Retreat
passages.text:
Is this the end?

Our beloved Malfurion. I saw him in the Dreamer's clutches, but Ysera was... changed. Twisted.

Shaladrassil, our mighty world tree, is corrupted beyond recognition.

We were forced to flee our home without our belongings. Some were heirlooms, sacred to us. Return them to me if you can, <class>, I beg you.

passages.title: Lost in Retreat
passages.text: Have you retrieved them?

passages.title: Lost in Retreat
passages.text: It is not much, but it is better than I could have hoped for. You have our gratitude.

passages.title: Breaking Out
passages.text:
We cannot fight our way out of the Vault alone.

Two of your allies, Kayn Sunfury and Altruis the Sufferer, are imprisoned within this room. 

Free them with haste. Their strength will be of great use to us.

passages.title: Breaking Out
passages.text: <The lever seems to control the door.>

passages.title: Breaking Out
passages.text: <Pull the lever.>

passages.title: The Wormtalon Crone
passages.text:
A wicked coven of harpies have overtaken our village.

It was the twisting of the forest that forced us out of our village, but now that the harpies have moved in I fear that we may never be able to return.

The Wormtalon coven are led by a witch called Grelda the Crone. She has made her nest in a cave near our village.

If their leader is defeated, the remaining harpies will surely flee.

Slay Grelda the Crone and we will be forever in your debt, <class>.

passages.title: Malfurion's Cure
passages.text:
The cleansed Mooncaps glow radiantly in your hands as you lift them from the waters of the ancient moonwell.

Mender Onelle will need the Mooncaps in order to make a healing poultice for Malfurion's wounds.

passages.title: Hope Remains
passages.text: The Tear of Elune floats effortlessly, glistening in an ethereal pillar of moonlight.

passages.title: Fel Infusion
passages.text:
So many years of imprisonment has left us weak.

The Vault is overrun with demons. Kill them and gather their souls to regain your strength.

passages.title: Fel Infusion
passages.text: The color has returned to your face, <name>.

passages.title: Rise of the Illidari
passages.text:
Look down there. We are vastly outnumbered.

We will need more allies on our side if we are to escape from here intact. Free the other Illidari imprisoned within the cells of this chamber.

We will need everyone to escape this place alive.

passages.title: Rise of the Illidari
passages.text: Have you freed those you found in the cells?

passages.title: Rise of the Illidari
passages.text: We always knew the Illidari would be called upon to defend this world. It is why we sacrificed everything to become who... WHAT... we are.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED] Kill Feral Dogs
passages.text:
You've done more than enough, <name>. My people and I can clean things up here.

You should return to town and report on our victory.

passages.title: The Warden's Signet
passages.text:
The night elf was carrying a signet engraved with the crest of the Wardens.

The band, made from a silvery, unbreakable metal, has been worn down by time, as if absently twisted and rubbed against its owner's finger.

passages.title: The Warden's Signet
passages.text:
<Jarod gazes at the ring for a long minute before closing his hands around it. He puts the ring in a pocket.>

This is Maiev's ring. She would never part with it.

She must be at Black Rook Hold!

passages.title: The Crusade Calls
passages.text:
((You have just finished the introduction sequence in Dalaran.))

Lord Maxwell Tyrosus of the Argent Crusade sent for you. He mentioned knowing of a weapon we could use against the Legion.

As much as I loathe their ilk, you should go to Krasus' Landing and speak with him. We need every advantage we can muster.

passages.title: Black Rook Hold
passages.text:
Inside the chest, hidden amongst various knickknacks, is a signet engraved with a unique crest.

The band, made from a silvery, unbreakable metal, has been worn down by time, as if absently twisted and rubbed against its owner's finger.

passages.title: Stop Gul'dan!
passages.text:
After his defeat at the Black Temple, we brought Illidan's lifeless body here, to be interred forever within the Vault of the Wardens.

Gul'dan has found his way through our defenses and is trying to steal the Betrayer's corpse.

Even in death, Illidan's body can be used by the Burning Legion. Gul'dan CANNOT succeed.

passages.title: Stop Gul'dan!
passages.text: Excellent. You have absorbed the powers of these brutes. Look how strong you have grown!

passages.title: Into the Foul Creche
passages.text:
One of the demons that I interrogated revealed a particularly juicy bit of information. Apparently, there's an imp mother in the volcano that scribes Legion secrets.

Kor'vas has gone out to find that demon and bring those secrets back for us.

passages.title: Into the Foul Creche
passages.text: <name>. I've found her.

passages.title: Return to the Black Temple
passages.text:
Quickly, <name>, use the Sargerite Keystone.

We must get back to the Black Temple before it is too late!

passages.title: Return to the Black Temple
passages.text:
<As you invoke the power of the Sargerite Keystone, the fel portal is suffused with an otherworldly energy.

It is time to return triumphant to the Black Temple and aid Lord Illidan in repelling the invading forces from Azeroth and Shattrath City.>

passages.title: An End To War
passages.text:
It appears that the great Ancient of War, Ironbranch, has fallen to the Nightmare.

It pains me greatly to ask this of you, but Ironbranch must be put to rest.

In life, he once stood vigil in Shala'nir as a protector of the world tree. In death, my dear friend is no more than a destructive weapon that will be used to cause even more violence.

He must be slain before he does more harm to Val'sharah.

In my heart, I know that he would thank you for this mercy...

passages.title: Hard Lessons
passages.text:
Please understand, stranger, that I am a being of peace. I have discarded any vengeful nature long, long ago.

In my youth, however, many hard lessons were learned through discipline. When applied wisely and properly, discipline can be a great teacher and shaper of character.

It is in the spirit of wisdom and guidance that I would have you teach these harpies a memorable lesson.

passages.title: Before We're Overrun
passages.text:
The doomguard commander and his queen must be dealt with. His eredar are summoning in a huge number of reinforcements.

We need to put an end to him before the Legion overruns our new foothold up in the volcano!

As an added benefit, you can steal his demonic power.

passages.title: Before We're Overrun
passages.text:
Already, the flow of demons from below has slowed to a trickle.

I can sense the doom guard's energy. You have become more powerful.

passages.title: Leystone Deposit Sample
passages.text:
This ore looks like nothing you've seen before.

A mystical sheen moves through the metal in complex, unpredictable patterns. Your trainer in Dalaran would certainly like to see this.

passages.title: Leystone Deposit Sample
passages.text: What's that you've got there, boy?

passages.title: Leystone Deposit Sample
passages.text:
It's so light. So pretty, too! Reminds me of elementium, a bit.

If you see any more ore like this, try and strike it with the grain. You'll waste much less of it.

passages.title: Leystone Seam Sample
passages.text:
This ore has clearly absorbed some of the latent ley energies within the Broken Isles. It is cool to the touch, and reflects light in odd, playful angles.

Your trainer in Dalaran should analyze this.

passages.title: Leystone Seam Sample
passages.text: What've ye brought me now?

passages.title: Leystone Seam Sample
passages.text:
Look at that! She's a lovely one, isn't she?

Treat this type of ore with care, lad. No fat-muscle shoulder swings necessary - just a gentle tap on the right spot and you'll extract much more ore than a beginner.

passages.title: Living Leystone Sample
passages.text:
This is no normal leystone. It is much livelier, shimmering in complex, enthralling patterns. It is easy to stare at.

Your trainer in Dalaran would certainly like to have a look at this.

passages.title: Living Leystone Sample
passages.text: Oh, my...

passages.title: Living Leystone Sample
passages.text:
Now isn't that somethin'? You got this offa one of those rocky creatures down there?

Looks like ye only brought me a bit o' the torso, though. Next time, make sure to get the arms and head too. Lots o' good meat in there.

passages.title: Where Respect is Due
passages.text:
Leystone is a sensitive ore. Our smiths can coax great power out of it, but as miners, we must treat it with respect, or else its power will retreat inward.

<The tauren hands you what appears to be a GLASS mining pick.>

The next time you mine some leystone ore, use this pick. It will break if you strike too hard. THIS is the respect that leystone requires.

passages.title: Where Respect is Due
passages.text: You haven't broken my pick, have you?

passages.title: Where Respect is Due
passages.text:
You've learned much, <name>.

Stay a while. I have a story for you.

passages.title: The Legend of Rethu Ironhorn
passages.text:
A long, long time ago, a tauren by the name of Rethu entered this land. His exploits paved the road that all miners walk.

If you wish to learn more about mining, you must first learn about Rethu.

passages.title: The Legend of Rethu Ironhorn
passages.text: Listen well, <name>.

passages.title: The Legend of Rethu Ironhorn
passages.text: Echoes of Rethu's time in this land still remain, <name>. Be on the lookout for his influence when you are out in the field.

passages.title: Rethu's Journal
passages.text:
Tucked in between a few pieces of rubble, a scrap of paper catches your eye.

Mining carefully, you uncover the tattered remains of an old scroll. The tauren handwriting is archaic, but one word catches your eye:

"Rethu".

passages.title: Rethu's Journal
passages.text: Greetings, miner. What have you here?

passages.title: Rethu's Journal
passages.text:
This... this cannot be! A piece of Rethu's own mining log!

Look here, miner... it details a leystone mining technique he was working on...

passages.title: Rethu's Pick
passages.text:
This seam has been mined before - it bears the telltale diagonal ruts of a miner's pick.

Looking down, that pick now lays on the ground - handle broken, pick-point dulled with use and years.

Carved into the haft is a familiar name:

"Rethu"

passages.title: Rethu's Pick
passages.text: What is that you hold, miner?

passages.title: Rethu's Pick
passages.text:
Rethu's own mining pick...

Well, one of them, anyhow. Stories say he went through them almost weekly.

Still, I've never seen one with my own eyes. Look at the wear on the blade, miner. The angles he used... the strength with which he struck: we could learn much from studying this artifact.

passages.title: Rethu's Horn
passages.text:
The corpse of the rocky beast yielded an unusual treasure: a battered chunk of tauren's horn.

It is clearly very, very old, but something about its color and curve reminds you of Ronos Ironhorn at the Ironhorn Enclave.

passages.title: Rethu's Horn
passages.text: What... what is that, miner?

passages.title: Rethu's Horn
passages.text:
This... this could not be...

This is from a member my tribe, <name>. Where did you find this?

One of the first stories we ever learn about Rethu involves the day he lost his horn in battle. There is no way of knowing if this belonged to him but... but...

passages.title: Rethu's Lesson
passages.text:
You... miner... let me see your pick a moment.

<The tauren spirit eyes your mining equipment.>

You remind me of myself, when I once walked this land. Savor these moments, miner. They cannot last forever.

<With a bow, the spirit disappears.>

passages.title: Rethu's Lesson
passages.text:
You saw a spirit while out mining in the wilds?

No, I do not believe you. One mustn't spend too long out mining, it fatigues the mind. You must be seeing things.

Still, something seems... different about you. You've learned something. Perhaps there's some truth to your tale after all...

passages.title: Rethu's Experience
passages.text:
Miner... you... you know who I am?

I see. That is good. My tribe continues to honor its roots.

If you return to the land of the Ironhorn tribe... let them know that they are looked upon with pride.

passages.title: Rethu's Experience
passages.text:
<The tauren listens as you describe your encounter with the spirit of Rethu Ironhorn.>

I would not normally believe you, but... I can sense truth in your tale. You are a lucky miner.

I am pleased to know that our ancestors look upon us with pride. We have chosen an admirable path.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Rethu's Sacrifice
passages.text:
Miner... speak with me a moment. I haven't much time in this place.

I see you fight for your ore. I believe that is the most noble way to obtain your stone. It gives the land a fighting chance.

Still, one mustn't be callous with their own life. Dig too deep, and the land will overcome you. No stone is worth the price I paid.

But that is a tale for another day...

passages.title: Rethu's Sacrifice
passages.text:
The spirit of Rethu Ironhorn? Tell me everything he said.

He said he... dug too deep? I see. The Earthmother took him.

Thank you for coming to me, miner. This is a tale that the rest of the tribe must hear. We are all the wiser for it.

passages.title: Felslate Deposit Sample
passages.text:
This is one nasty-looking stone.

Your trainer in Dalaran should see this.

passages.title: Felslate Deposit Sample
passages.text: You bring me somethin' new?

passages.title: Felslate Deposit Sample
passages.text:
This is no natural stone, miner. It stinks of demon's blood. Where'd you find this?

Reminds me a bit of old fel iron. Come 'ere, lemme teach you a trick or two on how to properly gather this stuff.

passages.title: Felslate Seam Sample
passages.text:
This ore is remarkably heavy. More disturbingly, it seems to darken and hiss at your touch.

Perhaps your mining trainer in Dalaran has some insights.

passages.title: Felslate Seam Sample
passages.text: Looks like you've been busy down there, miner.

passages.title: Felslate Seam Sample
passages.text: This came out of a cliffside seam? Remember, ye can't mine seams like ye mine deposits. Totally different thing. I'll show ye my trick.

passages.title: Living Felslate Sample
passages.text:
Your miner's instinct is kicking in. Chunks of the infernal's corpse appear to be usable.

Still, there must be a way to extract more ore from the demon's body. Perhaps your mining trainer in Dalaran will know how.

passages.title: Living Felslate Sample
passages.text: What's that?

passages.title: Living Felslate Sample
passages.text:
This came from a blasted infernal? Look out, we've got mister COMBAT miner, here!

Some o' this ore seems to 'ave lost its shine on the trip back, however. Next time, make sure to cut out the sword and spell wounds before ye mine it.

passages.title: A Shred of Your Humanity
passages.text:
To mine for felslate is to seek the very blood of demons. To improve at it, you must become part demon yourself.

Why the dirty look? You said it yourself: you're willing to make sacrifices.

Luckily for you, I'm an expert in this area. I won't put you in any danger, as long as you trust me.

Are you ready?

passages.title: A Shred of Your Humanity
passages.text: Don't waste my time, miner.

passages.title: A Shred of Your Humanity
passages.text:
It is done.

Stretch it out a bit.

You may experience some stray urges to burn worlds and sow chaos for the next week or so. Do your best to resist them.

passages.title: Rin'thissa's Eye
passages.text:
Oddly enveloped within the felslate deposit is a humanoid eye.

It quivers with life. You get the sense that it would blink at you if it had an eyelid.

A mining expert should take a look at this.

passages.title: Rin'thissa's Eye
passages.text: Is... is that...?

passages.title: Rin'thissa's Eye
passages.text:
It is. This eye once belonged to my sister, Rin'thissa.

Poor fool, she cut out her own eye and replaced it with a hunk of ore. That was the tipping point... she's completely fel-maddened now.

Learn from her mistake, <name>.

passages.title: Lyrelle's Right Arm
passages.text:
You blink and rub your eyes, but they do not deceive you. This is a woman's arm, completely enveloped within a felslate seam.

The arm is bloodless, but still twitches. Fel-colored streaks remain where veins once were.

Felsmith Nal'ryssa will certainly want to see this.

passages.title: Lyrelle's Right Arm
passages.text: Lyrelle, no...

passages.title: Lyrelle's Right Arm
passages.text:
This was my sister's. Lyrelle's.

Her fate is clear now. She no longer needed that signet ring... the girl must have traded in her own mining arm for one carved out of felslate itself.

Aren't you glad we only used three small shards?

Take this to heart, <name>: you can lose everything to greed if you don't exercise restraint. Poor Lyrelle paid that price for all of us.

passages.title: Ondri's Still-Beating Heart
passages.text:
What at first looked like another chunk of felslate is, in fact, a humanoid heart, encrusted in rock and filled not with blood but a vile, demonic substance.

It does not appear to belong to the beast you carved it out of... it seems that the infernal was holding it like a keepsake. Luckily your mining pick didn't hit it straight on.

Felsmith Nal'ryssa will want to see this.

passages.title: Ondri's Still-Beating Heart
passages.text: Ondri...

passages.title: Ondri's Still-Beating Heart
passages.text:
My sister Ondri was the first among us to mine, and the first among us to fall. Some Nathrezim dreadlord convinced her to replace her own heart - her heart! - with a chunk of felslate.

I slew the dreadlord myself, but couldn't find the heart. This must be it.

Big sister... I am sorry. Your loss will not be forgotten. We will learn from your missteps.

passages.title: Rin'thissa
passages.text:
My sister Nal'ryssa has her claws in you, doesn't she?

That weakling doesn't know the first thing about mining. She was always too afraid to take the leap. True knowledge comes only from the Great One, the God of Fel and Flame.

You want to truly learn how to mine? Come to Suramar's northwestern corner, and speak my name:

Rin'thissa.

passages.title: Rin'thissa
passages.text:
My sister's soul rests now. I have you to thank for that.

Rin'thissa was always a charmer. You did well to avoid her invitations, and even better to slay her and end her demonic possession. You've learned much since we first met, <name>.

passages.title: Lyrelle
passages.text:
Look at you, miner. Still held back by the limitations of your fragile, decaying flesh.

To truly become one with the demon-tinged rocks of these lands, you must shed your skin and submit to a darker power.

Join us, miner. Bring your feeble body to Felsoul Hold, and speak my name:

Lyrelle.

passages.title: Lyrelle
passages.text:
Poor Lyrelle.

I do not blame you for putting her down, <name>. I thank you. I hope that you would do the same to me, if I were to slip and fall down that same path.

Just... try to learn something from your ordeal. Reflect on your experience. I would hate to see her sacrifice be for nothing.

passages.title: Ondri
passages.text:
You are nothing compared to me. You think yourself hardened, experienced... heroic, even. Hah!

You have no idea what I've been through. The tortures I've endured, the sacrifices I've made. All for the sake of my trade!

Yes, I'm a miner, just like you. Want to learn what I have to teach? Come to the Crimson Thicket in Suramar, and speak my name:

Ondri.

passages.title: Ondri
passages.text: Ondri has always heartless, one way or the other.

passages.title: Ondri
passages.text:
My sister's villainy is finally at an end.

She was always the wisest among us. Sad that she had to go out the way she did. I'm certain there was much she could have taught us.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Sample
passages.text:
This ore. Smells. Horrible. It combines the odor of sulfur with all the worst parts of a rotting corpse.

Someone will probably want it for something.

Maybe your mining trainer in Dalaran will take it off of your hands.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Sample
passages.text: Excuse me, I must have... wait, that smell is coming from YOU?

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Sample
passages.text:
This odiferous morsel ye've brought me... it's infernal brimstone, isn't it?

Amazing.

I've heard tales, but I've never actually SEEN the stuff before.

I've got to study this. In the meantime, here's all I know about this rare, rare ore.

passages.title: Your Will Be Done
passages.text:
Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker has drawn a rough map of what we know of the Broken Isles.

You should speak with him at once - he can best advise you on where we should first strike against the Legion.

passages.title: The Art of Demonsteel
passages.text:
The Firmament Stone is one of the few anvils beneath the sky that can tolerate the hammer strikes necessary to craft demonsteel.

Here, I will show you.

Two parts leystone, one part felslate. No heat, no tempering, just pure strength and finesse.

Try it. I will coach you.

passages.title: The Art of Demonsteel
passages.text:
There you have it... demonsteel.

Welcome to the next level of smithing, <name>.

passages.title: Done with Waiting
passages.text:
Mom got a message and said blood called for blood. She told me to wait here while she went out, but it's been two weeks since then. I'm tired of waiting.

I'll stay home if you go find her. She said she was going to the cliffs far to the south.

passages.title: Fishy Business
passages.text:
Makrura are massing down by the shore, and far too many of them seem to practice water magic.

I think once they've got enough spellcasters, they're planning to summon a massive wave.

passages.title: Die, Fish-People
passages.text:
Makrura are massing down by the shore, and far too many of them seem to practice water magic. I think they're planning to summon a massive wave.

Also, I've come a long way, and I'm out of supplies. I'm so hungry, I could eat almost anything. Even the makrura you kill. Just cut the heads off first.

passages.title: Holy Retribution
passages.text:
I fell in what you now call Tirisfal Glades at the claws of two of Yogg'Saron's most powerful lieutenants... the C'Thraxi. I was able to slay one in my death throes - Az'jtal.

Now, the dark forces deep beneath Azeroth have begun to usher Az'jtal once again into this world. You must go to Tyr's Fall and strike Az'jtal down again before it can fully manifest.

Only once this deed is done may you receive my blessing upon the Ashbringer.

passages.title: A Favor for Mr. Shackle
passages.text:
Throm'ka, <class>. My name is Seska. I represent a... trading company. As you can see, I've fallen victim to these giants and their naga allies.

Three of my associates were also captured while surveying this cove. I'm certain that my employer, Mr. Shackle, would be most grateful if you could procure their release.

passages.title: A Favor for Mr. Shackle
passages.text:
You say your name is <name>? Welcome to our humble den. Seska is very grateful for her freedom.

You haven't perchance seen the rest of my people?

passages.title: A Favor for Mr. Shackle
passages.text:
Excellent, my good sir. I cannot thank you enough for the freedom of my people. Rosh is especially appreciative.

<Gentle Rosh grunts.>

Perhaps you and I can do some more business together.

passages.title: Thieving Thistleleaf
passages.text:
Why the Thistleleaf are collecting the Lunarwing eggs is anyone's guess, but you can be sure it's not to give them a loving home.

Saylanna Riverbreeze will know what to do with these.

passages.title: Thieving Thistleleaf
passages.text: Gather as many eggs as you can and bring them back to me. I will keep them safe.

passages.title: Thieving Thistleleaf
passages.text: Until I can discover what is vexing the Thistleleaf, I'll have to look after the Lunarwing eggs. At least I know they will be safe.

passages.title: Inspiration Strikes
passages.text:
The blood of this creature glows with magical energy. It doesn't SEEM to be poisonous.

Your training in the culinary arts has presented you with some strange ingredients before, but this one is particularly inspiring. Perhaps someone within the Azurewing Repose can suggest a preparation for Leyblood.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Bidding
passages.text:
Uh, are these guys friendlies? I guess it's a good sign they haven't tried to eat Duchess... yet.

Anyway, I have orders. Nathanos caught up with the dark rangers, who were sent forward aboard the Oblivion on a secret mission from Lady Sylvanas herself! Unfortunately the Alliance caught wind of our plan, and now Greymane is attacking the outpost!

We could really use you over there, <name>. Duchess can take you there, just give me the word.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Bidding
passages.text:
Finally someone competent arrives at this sorry excuse for an outpost. 

Our efforts to complete Sylvanas's mission are at a standstill, but now we have even more pressing matters on our hands.

passages.title: The Highmountain Tauren
passages.text:
Ye've brought me a bit of interesting rocks to look at, <name>. I've got a special assignment for ye, if ye're up for it.

I hear stories about these tauren, up in Highmountain, who claim mastery over minin'. I don't know if they're as talented as you or me, but they've been minin' leystone longer.

Pay 'em a visit. See what they have to say.

passages.title: The Highmountain Tauren
passages.text: You are indeed a miner. You have the look of it. There is ore in your blood.

passages.title: Not Dead Yet!
passages.text: They're not dead yet! A little nitro here, a jolt of electricity there... we can bring 'em back! And then, they can pay me! Whaddya say, <name>? Wanna go into business with me?

passages.title: Scouting Report
passages.text:
We were supposed to meet back here, and then sneak back to Gatgetzan. That was hours ago, <name>! The others fanned out across all of Tanaris to gather intel.

Anything you can find will help in the defense of Gadgetzan. Keep your eyes open, <name>!

passages.title: The Felsmiths
passages.text:
Ye have a knack with this felslate, <lad/lass>. Best ship ye off to someone who knows the stuff better than I.

The Illidari have a knack with all things demonic, really, and I've heard about a few miners who've set up shop out near the demons in Suramar.

Pay 'em a visit. See what they have to teach ye.

passages.title: The Felsmiths
passages.text:
You want to mine felslate?

Do you really think you have what it takes?

Are you willing to make sacrifices?

Good.

passages.title: To the Rescue
Secrets of Highmountain
passages.text:
Now that you are familiar with our greatest hero, perhaps you are willing to assist me on a very dangerous endeavor.

To this end I have sent word for one of your allies to join us.

When you are ready, join us in my spirit lodge. It is up the elevators and across the southwestern most bridge.

passages.title: Unused - Wraith Zapper
Unbearable
passages.text:
Not far away, a bear cub looks to be in some distress. Perhaps you should investigate? 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(38938))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(38938))");

passages.title: Assault on Skold-Ashil
passages.text: <insert>

passages.title: Consult the Locals
passages.text:
Whoever wove this fabric CAN'T have intended it only for belts and shoulderpads. There must be some way to sew thread into this material.

Head on down to Azsuna and try to find a tailor. We need to sew if we're going to do any real tailoring.

passages.title: Consult the Locals
passages.text:
My my, look at you! Such an attractive young <class>, and all bedecked in magical finery and weaponry. To what do I owe the pleasure?

Aha! Tailoring! It's your lucky day, er...

I'm sorry, what was your name? <name>?

It's your lucky day, <name>! I happen to be one of the best tailors in Suramar...

passages.title: Runic Catgut
passages.text:
Let me guess... thread troubles? Mm-hm.
I suspected as much. My people weave sumptuous silks, but those silks can be fickle about the types of thread they'll accept.

Shal'dorei silk has a bit of ley energy woven right into it. You need something that's learned to coexist with the ley energies of this land.

I'm talking about owlcats, my good friend! They have what you need. You'll find them amongst the ruins of Llothien.

passages.title: Runic Catgut
passages.text: They are quite remarkable creatures, really. I used to keep one as a pet and mount... but that was a lifetime ago.

passages.title: Runic Catgut
passages.text: Perfect. Marvelous!

passages.title: Hard Times
passages.text:
When I worked at the tailoring guild in Suramar, I would usually work off of a pattern. Something that inspired me.

Unfortunately, I've run into streak of bad luck, and I'm ashamed to say that I no longer have my patterns.

The naga sorceresses in the lagoon to the west, however, have expertly-sewn wristwraps. And the nightfallen to the north wear robes that we can use... if you can pry one from their greedy clutches.

passages.title: Hard Times
passages.text: What've you got in your hands, there?

passages.title: Hard Times
passages.text: You, <name>, are a person of great skill. I send you out for patterns, and you do so without question. Remarkable!

passages.title: The Wayward Tailor
passages.text:
Might I ask a favor, <name>?

As I am recently without a home, shop, family, or friends, I was wondering if you might show me your floating city? I must admit, I am VERY curious about the place. I've also heard good things about their tailoring shop.

I have no way of getting there myself, but certainly such a magical city has SOMEONE who can summon me.

<Lyndras looks at you with hopeful apprehension.>

passages.title: The Wayward Tailor
passages.text: Did you find a tailor yet?

passages.title: The Wayward Tailor
passages.text:
Your friend certainly has an... interesting appearance.

He taught you to sew this silk? Hmm. Maybe we should keep him around for a while.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras?
passages.text:
That's strange. Lyndras was here one moment, and then he ran off the next. He had such a strange look on his face.

Perhaps we should track him down.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras?
passages.text:
Sorry about that, <name>. You caught me snooping around. I suppose my curiosity got the better of me.

Allow me to make it up to you.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras Again?
passages.text:
Oh dear.

He had just promised you that he wouldn't wander off, and then he did it again!

I'm starting to think that this Lyndras character might be a bit too impetuous for my tastes.

Please, go find him, before he gets into any more trouble.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras Again?
passages.text:
My most sincere apologies, <name>. Not only did I make a spectacle of myself, I fear I may have also put the good name of your tailoring shop at risk.

You have every right to be upset with me.

passages.title: Taking Inspiration
passages.text:
I wish I had more patterns to share, but my notebook was lost along with my shop. We'll need to come up with some patterns on our own.

I've been thinking about the leather breeches that the Stormheim vrykul wear. They're certainly much thicker and heavier than anything we could sew, but their embellishing runework is quite impressive.

If I had a few pairs, perhaps I could re-imagine this runework on a more... refined garment.

passages.title: Taking Inspiration
passages.text: I'm looking forward to this.

passages.title: Taking Inspiration
passages.text:
Aha! This will be much simpler than I'd first thought.

<Lyndras takes a moment to jot some instructions down on a scrap of vellum.>

Here, <name>. You should have it.

passages.title: The Right Color
passages.text:
Your assistance, <name>, if you have a moment.

I've been attempting to reproduce a pattern for footwear that I spotted a while back, but I'm having trouble getting the right color for my dye. Our black dye is too dark, our blue dye is too bright, and mixing the two doesn't look right.

The color I'm looking for is more of a squid-ink blue. If, in your travels, you come across any dyes of this color, would you do me the favor of bringing some to me?

passages.title: The Right Color
passages.text: I'm quite close to completing these slippers.

passages.title: The Right Color
passages.text: Marvelous!

passages.title: Where's Lyndras Now?
passages.text:
Lyndras couldn't have gone very far. I mean, we're floating a thousand feet over the sea. 

I heard some commotion across the way this morning near the alchemy shop. I pray that wasn't Lyndras.

Could you please go over there and make sure?

passages.title: The Nightborne Connection
passages.text:
Now that you're able to disguise yourself, you should go to Suramar City and try to find this guild of tailors.

Good luck, <name>, and try not to get caught.
