passages.title: The Nightborne Connection
passages.text:
Ah, a fellow tailor. Pleasure to make your acquaintance, uh... <name>, was it?

I trust you'd like to come into the fold of our guild? Where did you receive your prior training?

passages.title: Proof of Loyalty
passages.text:
<Tytallo listens as you recount what happened with Lyndras.>

I see. You sound almost... sympathetic to the wretch.

The nightfallen are liars and thieves. ALL of them. Lyndras included.

I will not tolerate a student that has any respect or sympathy for those... things. And have you witnessed what they turn into at the depths of their depravity?

If you want to get on my good side, do not return until you are covered in the blood of the withered.

passages.title: Proof of Loyalty
passages.text: If you wish to earn my tutelage, you must first prove that you are on our side.

passages.title: Proof of Loyalty
passages.text:
Hmm.

Very well. We may continue.

passages.title: TRACKING Encounter Botanist
passages.text:
(PH)
Darkgrove has run out of places to hide. Now it is time to finish him off.

If we stop him now, there may be hope for this valley yet.

passages.title: Black Rook Invasion
passages.text:
Once, this area was peaceful and prosperous. Then we saw the first bad omens: strange ailments, spoiled crops, and the like. Now ghosts attack us from that castle across the river, and undead assassins slay our fishers so as to cut off the village's food supply.

We're the last family living this close to the castle, but we daren't retreat: this river is the best route for fishers to bring their hauls in to town. Please, will you take the fight to these undead?

passages.title: Rise to the Occasion
passages.text:
The Lich King made a wise choice in giving you that weapon, <name>.

You've proven your strength and cunning on countless occasions and it is time that you have a position fitting for your accomplishments.

passages.title: REUSE ME
passages.text: asdf

passages.title: A Summons from Saylanna
passages.text:
Sprites have always been mischievous creatures, but lately their mischief has turned to violence.

One of the druids I call friend, Saylanna Riverbreeze, reports that they are assaulting the faerie dragon nesting grounds.

The Lunarwing Shallows lie to the south. You will find Saylanna there.

passages.title: Eye On the Prize
passages.text:
This demon has proved less than useful. I have been using the Scythe of Souls on it, but so far, it has resisted my inquiries. We will see how long that lasts.

I have a different idea...

There is a fresh inquisitor demon ahead. They are horrific fel casters who see through their floating eyes and specialize in dark pacts. If you steal its power, Jace Darkweaver could use some of it in his ritual to spy on the Legion.

Better yet, you will gain its power by ripping it from its smoking corpse.

passages.title: Eye On the Prize
passages.text: <name>. I would salute, but I am in the middle of a ritual.

passages.title: Eye On the Prize
passages.text:
An inquisitor's essence... perfect. Allari was right.

Now to complete my ritual and spy on the Legion's leadership.

passages.title: Assault on Skold-Ashil
passages.text: <insert>

passages.title: Lion Stalkin'
passages.text:
The hills are crawlin' with lions that stalk their prey from afar. These big cats will pounce at anything that catches their eye, including |5<race>. 

While most would fall to such a formidable predator, anyone in my huntin' party would be able to best those beasts.

Prove you've got what it takes by taking down a few of those stalkers.

passages.title: Lion Stalkin'
passages.text: Not a scratch on ya that I can see. I bet those lions never saw ya comin'!

passages.title: Moose Shootin'
passages.text:
Highmountain is home to wildlife that can't be hunted anywhere else in the world. Tell me, <name>, have you ever laid eyes on a moose before? 

The roaming Elderhorn may look like gentle giants, but only a fool would underestimate their strength. 

They should prove to be a good challenge, even for someone as experienced as you.

passages.title: Moose Shootin'
passages.text: Ya can't be huntin' Elderhorn if you're lingerin' around camp.

passages.title: Moose Shootin'
passages.text: You've hunted the Highmountain Elderhorn and lived to tell about it. That's not a feat that most can say they've accomplished. Color me impressed.

passages.title: Demon Destroyer
passages.text:
The demons spreading this corruption must be dealt with. Kill their generals and their plans will unravel.

I have a gift for you. This horn was given to me by Odyn himself, use it to strike down all that stand in your way.

The gods will surely smile upon you if you thwart the advances of Legion.

passages.title: Cleansing the Fountain
passages.text:
The blood from an impaled dreadlord is flowing into a fountain at the base of Valhallas. Following orders given by their "God-King" the vrykul are drinking from the fountain. 

The demon blood is driving the vrykul mad and it's giving them greater power than they deserve.

Take this acorn. Throw it into the fountain. My ravens will take care of the rest.

passages.title: Possessions of Power
passages.text: Echoes of a thousand worlds swirl in the palm of your hand. Its true value lies in the eye of the beholder.

passages.title: The New Chieftain
passages.text:
So you are the one of whom Ebonhorn foretold. I thought you would be taller.

Our High Chieftain Ulan has been slain by the drogbar when they seized the hammer.

His daughter, Mayla Highmountain, has now taken on the burden of High Chieftain.

You can find her on the northern bluff with what few forces we have left to defend this place.

She will have need of you.

passages.title: No Time to Talk
passages.text:
Dargrul has sent his pets to do battle with us.

We need to crush these elementals before their rage swarms into Thunder Totem.

passages.title: No Time to Talk
passages.text: We will all be honorary masons if this keeps up much longer.

passages.title: No Time to Talk
passages.text: It has been a long time since the earth itself has moved against us like this.

passages.title: Wrathshard
passages.text:
The Underking has used the Hammer of Khaz'goroth to render the mountainside into a weapon against us. The hammer is a tool for creation, not a weapon for his amusement!

Even now, his crystal servant, Wrathshard, is driving these elementals out of the mountain down upon my people.

We must hold the bridge against this onslaught.

Enter the cave, find Wrathshard, and send him back to his master in pieces.

passages.title: Wrathshard
passages.text: Dargrul always was a vile creature. I never realized to what extent until he got his hands on that hammer.

passages.title: Wrathshard
passages.text: I suspect this is not the last of Dargrul's assaults. He is still learning the powers of the Hammer like a child with a new toy.

passages.title: Unused
passages.text: You've charged up the gun. Now it's time to use it. Go and confront the ghostly wizard Kiranys Duskwhisper, and drive him out of Bradensbrook.

passages.title: March Forth and Conquer
passages.text:
You should make sure that we do not lose momentum, Highlord. There is still much to be done in Azsuna.

We have a map of the island set up near the front of the sanctum. Meet me there and you can delegate your forces to handle important tasks in the area.

passages.title: Forging the Artifact
passages.text:
We've certainly got our work cut out for us, but not to worry. There's nae weapon in existence that ye can't improve, legendary ones included!

This anvil's only powerful enough to imbue your artifact once before we'll need something better, but that'll have to do fer now.

passages.title: DEPRECATED
passages.text:
The Knights of the Ebon Blade are ready. Place your hand upon the Orb of Command and Acherus will move to its new resting place.

We await your orders, Highlord.

passages.title: The Forge of Odyn
passages.text:
This Forge has been working for longer than your race has existed; we might know a few things. Your weapon is powerful, it will take my personal forge in order to work it.

We can work the artifact to provide various improvements, provided you have enough experience with it. Let's give it a try shall we?

passages.title: The Forge of Odyn
passages.text: Your weapon has untold potential! You will need to get more acquainted with it first and we can work on it some more.

passages.title: Lynore's Fury
passages.text: It appears Eira has a present for you, your first valarjar! You lead 'em, I'll make sure their weapons and armor are ready for war!

passages.title: Peak Urgency
Siege of Crawliac
passages.text: [ph] Defend the bluffs!

passages.title: Moozy's Sojourn
passages.text:
My son! They took him! My wife and I split up to look for him. She went upriver and I went downriver.

Leave me, please, and find Moozy... I might be okay... If you find Moozy, please bring him to my wife upriver.

passages.title: Moozy's Sojourn
passages.text: <Moozy squeals in delight at your presence.>

passages.title: Through the Portal
Missing Shipments
passages.text:
Now that we've gotten to know each other, perhaps you can lend me a hand.

My weekly supply shipment was lost when my longtime courier--you know, old whatsername--was shot out of the sky over the shores of Azsuna. Surely a hardy sort like you could retrieve my lost goods.

passages.title: Missing Shipments
passages.text: I say, I do hope you were able to locate my lost supplies. How are we to build trust between us if you won't do everything I ask?

passages.title: Missing Shipments
passages.text: You found them! I had the utmost faith, of course. What's a few demons or naga to one so dedicated to advancing our craft?

passages.title: There's a Scribe for That
passages.text:
Fine! I admit, even my considerable intellect can't translate the strange tome you discovered. No doubt the water smears made it illegible.

Say, one of those dimwitted scribes down the block owes me a favor. This sort of busywork is just his cup of tea.

passages.title: There's a Scribe for That
passages.text: I don't have time to translate tomes! That's what lesser professions are for.

passages.title: There's a Scribe for That
passages.text: It seems that twerp of a scribe has his uses after all! Let's see what he came up with...

passages.title: Ancient Knowledge
passages.text:
The tome contains a wealth of ancient vrykul recipes! Why, I could be the first alchemist in untold ages to craft one! How fortunate for you, friend <name>, that you are here to bear witness to my greatness!

Awful kind of that Svena person to die and leave her book for us, eh? Silly vrykul...

passages.title: Ancient Knowledge
passages.text:
My poor table!

All the implements we needed to mix the new potions were on that table. Without them, the new recipes are useless!

Finding replacements will be no small task, but I'm confident you're up to it. If you need guidance, I can suggest places to look for the items we need.

Now, off with you!

passages.title: Ley Hunting
passages.text:
The leyflame burner you brought me is useless! This is why I never trust an engineer...

The burner needs to be charged in areas that resonate with ley energy before it can be used to craft our newfound alchemy recipes.

Lucky for us, Azsuna is rich with such power.

passages.title: Ley Hunting
passages.text:
You imbued the burner with ley energy, eh? Let's have a look.

<Deucus examines the leyflame burner.>

Yes, this will do nicely! A crucial step in rebuilding the alchemy table.

passages.title: An Imprecise Burette
passages.text:
Here are your burettes. Should you ever be in the need of anything else, don't hesitate to ask.

<Ms. Xiulan holds up the hair and continues to chuckle to herself.>

passages.title: An Imprecise Burette
passages.text: Oh yes, these are fine. Fine indeed. Unfortunately they need to be calibrated in order to for us to get any accurate readings off of them.

passages.title: Thanks for Flasking
passages.text:
Here is your flask, good as new. A fair trade for those potions.

Be a little more careful with your breakables next time!

passages.title: Thanks for Flasking
passages.text:
Barm did his work, then? I hoped that tauren would come through!

This is a very useful addition to my alchemy table.

passages.title: Forlorn Filter
passages.text:
Next on the list of things to replace are my filters. Now I'm sure you've concluded that an alchemist of my caliber uses only the finest of tools when mixing my potions.

The elves at the Temple of Elune in Val'sharah use Shaldorei silk to craft their robes. Perhaps they'd be willing to part with some for my filters.

passages.title: Forlorn Filter
passages.text: A pile of tattered shaldorei silk lay on the chest.

passages.title: Forlorn Filter
passages.text: This Shaldorei Silk appears to be torn into strips. The elves have apparently been using it as bandages for their fallen warriors.

passages.title: Return the Filter
passages.text:
What was torn has now been mended. I hope you put this Shaldorei silk to good use.

Now, run along.

passages.title: Return the Filter
passages.text: This Shaldorei Silk will make an excellent filter for the alchemy table. Nice work getting that nightborne to help us, <name>!

passages.title: Lining the Crucible
passages.text:
The first step in making this crucible useful is to restore the lining of its interior. That's going to require supplies you'll either gather yourself or obtain through trade with fellow adventurers.

Felwort and yseralline seeds are familiar to herbalists.

Felhide is obtained through skinning.

Blood of Sargeras can be found all over the Broken Isles.

passages.title: Lining the Crucible
passages.text: Restoring the lining of the crucible is no simple task, <name>.

passages.title: Lining the Crucible
passages.text:
It looks like you acquired everything we need. Give me a few moments to apply them to the interior.

<Deucus works on the crucible, restoring its lining.>

Perfect! The crucible is almost ready for use.

Just one more tiny detail...

passages.title: Vault of the Wardens: Bendy Glass Tubes
passages.text:
You find tubing formed from a bendable sort of glass. It appears as though Grimoira was using it to suck out the insides of her victims.

Its magical properties, however, would seem ideal for use on an advanced alchemy table.

passages.title: Vault of the Wardens: Bendy Glass Tubes
passages.text:
What's this you have for me, <name>? Say, these are some wondrous tubes! I bet I know a way to make them even better.

I'll need you to temper these glass tubes in the fire of a dragon's breath under the light of a full moon on the equinox, then travel into the Emerald Dream and--

Oh, hold on. These tubes are perfect just as they are. Nevermind!

Sometimes I get a bit caught up in this whole adventuring business...

passages.title: Going Underground
passages.text:
We're so close to replacing all my equipment, <name>. In order to make flasks again, we need to be able to precisely measure each ingredient.

For that, we need to replace my burette assembly. Unfortunately, burettes aren't easy to come by. We may be able to procure some though through other means by...

<Deucus looks around and beckons you closer.>

Going underground, so to say. As in, the Black Market.

Go see Ms. Xiulan. Mum's the word.

passages.title: Going Underground
passages.text: Well, now that we understand one another let's see what sort of arrangement we can come to.

passages.title: Calibration Experts
passages.text:
It will take the cooperation of several highly skilled sorts to calibrate these burettes for a variety of substances.

Chemist Emmara is an old friend from the Undercity who has helped me with similar endeavors.

Thunder Bluff smells like a barn to me, but Jana Winterhoof is an alchemist with exacting standards.

And while I'd never travel to Booty Bay without a lock on my wallet, Tryks Pourtrue has proven reliable and fair.

passages.title: Calibration Experts
passages.text:
Yes, I'd say these burettes look well-calibrated.

I knew those three would be meticulous. Never underestimate the value of someone who obsesses over tiny details, <name>!

passages.title: Testing the Calibration
passages.text:
Now that you have the burettes calibrated, it's time to test them out! The only way to be sure is by crafting a sufficient quantity of a variety of potions.

Glamorous work? No, but the most important reagent in alchemy is a bit of elbow grease!

passages.title: Testing the Calibration
passages.text: The only way to be sure the burettes are working is to use them!

passages.title: Testing the Calibration
passages.text:
That's quite an armload of potions you made! I think it's safe to say that these burettes are working as intended.

I'll add them to the alchemy table.

passages.title: Channeling Our Efforts
passages.text:
While it's no secret my time is more valuable than... well, anyone's, I fear I must step in and help to replace my decoction conduit.

You will also play a crucial part in this, <name>, as my liaison with the blacksmiths. The thought of getting soot on my robes curls my toes.

Here's a list of what we'll need done. Meanwhile I'll be out gathering the rest of what's needed.

passages.title: Channeling Our Efforts
passages.text:
What's this then?

<Alard takes the list and looks it over. His eyes widen as he reaches the bottom>

I take it you don't fully grasp what it is that you need, do you? If this is truly what's required then we better get started.

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: Rage Fire
passages.text:
Now that we have all the ingredients assembled, we need one last thing.

The fire of my forges burn hot, but not hot enough to work these ingredients into glass. For that, we need more heat. The heat of a dragon, to be exact.

I'm aware of one that has emerged from the Emerald Dream in a corrupted state. Corrupted or not, a dragon's heart burns with enough heat to melt the strongest of materials.

Bring me its heart and you'll have your conduit.

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: Rage Fire
passages.text: I'm getting the mixture ready now. As soon as you return with the heart, I'll begin the construction.

passages.title: The Emerald Nightmare: Rage Fire
passages.text:
<You hand the heart over to Alard. He places it within his forge and it begins to burn white hot.>

Perhaps I should refer to you as Dragonslayer <name> from now on.

Joking aside, I'll begin my forging.

passages.title: Extinguishing the Sentinels
Test - New
Wisp in the Willows
passages.text:
Wisps are the spirits of our night elven brethren who have become one with the forest. But their minds and the way they perceive things are very different than in life.

You should bond with this little one. See through its eyes as it travels to the hidden pools and grows some trees.

passages.title: Wisp in the Willows
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Wisp in the Willows
passages.text: Oh thank you traveler! You have truly helped the forest today.

passages.title: Perrexx the Corruptor
passages.text:
Look around you, <class>. Corruption has befouled my valley. If Malfurion requires my presence to summon Ysera the Awakened, then I will surely aid him, but not until I have purged these demons from my lands.

Perrexx the Corruptor is just ahead. Help me slay this fiend.

Stand by my side, and together we can rout these satyrs and their brethren.

passages.title: Procuring a Prototype
passages.text:
If Addie's going to be a more permanent member of the huntin' party, then she'll need some specialty gear for someone her size.

My munitions expert should have some ideas about what kind of weapon would best suit a gnome.

Stop by his camp and let him know that I'll be needin' a prototype soon.

passages.title: Procuring a Prototype
passages.text:
A gnome hunter, huh? Is that a joke?

Fine, fine. What the boss wants, the boss gets. I'll start working on a prototype as soon as I finish up my latest project.

passages.title: Moonclaw's Wisdom
passages.text:
Our quick action today has stopped this aggression and saved my valley. As you requested, I will join Malfurion in the Grove of Cenarius.

Still, there is much about these satyrs that I wish to tell you. This information would be most valuable to you.

Please meet me in my den before departing.

passages.title: A Mysterious Text
passages.text: You found a water-logged tome near the bones of a massive creature. Written in an unfamiliar language, the book is adorned with runes and alchemical symbols. Perhaps another alchemist would be able to tell you more.

passages.title: A Mysterious Text
passages.text: You found something down in Azsuna, <name>? Do share. It's so rare for something interesting to walk through the door of my quiet little shop.

passages.title: A Mysterious Text
passages.text: Well now, this is intriguing! This book is... well, you see, it's obviously... uh...

passages.title: Bear Huntin'
passages.text:
They say a single hair from the back of a bristlefur bear is sharp enough to cut a dwarf's beard. But if the fur doesn't kill ya, the maul will.

Some lesser hunters have been a meal for those bears. 

Show me you're more than a snack and bring me back a few of those bristlefur pelts.

passages.title: Bear Huntin'
passages.text: Procuring a few Bristlefur Pelts should help sell me on your huntin' skills.

passages.title: Bear Huntin'
passages.text: These pelts are even sharper than I imagined. Well done, <name>.

passages.title: Stories of Battle
passages.text:
The writings carried by the priestess appear to be the first part of an epic poem describing the history of Ashildir, the ancient queen of the Valkyra. 

If Ashildir has a connection to the shieldmaidens here, you may be able to use that to your advantage. 

The answer to her involvement likely lies within the remaining text.

passages.title: Stories of Battle
passages.text: This appears to be the last verse.

passages.title: Stories of Battle
passages.text:
The verses of the poem unfold the tale of Ashildir founding the shieldmaidens and bringing them to Skold-Ashil.

If these shieldmaidens revere the Valkyra queen as this would suggest, your dealings with her in Helheim may prove advantageous.

passages.title: Rating Razik
passages.text:
Hemet is expecting an update on how my munitions research and development is going.

I'm sure you'll be happy to tell my boss that my latest creation worked flawlessly!

You can find him at his camp near the hunters' lodge.

passages.title: Rating Razik
passages.text:
It's good to hear that Razik is makin' some progress on his gadgets.

Maybe if he could design a gun that aims itself, these amateurs infesting the basin would hit their targets for once.

passages.title: Hex-a-Gone
passages.text:
The harpies are relentless in their pursuit to control the basin. They are able to craft bags of foul magic as quickly as we can destroy them.

The Skyhorn cannot gain the upper hand as long as their hexweaver lives. She must be stopped.

passages.title: Hex-a-Gone
passages.text: Hexweaver Akara must be slain if the Skyhorn wish to gain the upper hand.

passages.title: Hex-a-Gone
passages.text: You have done the Skyhorn a great service, <name>.

passages.title: Xavius Event TRACKING
Satyr Line TRACKING
Mending the Filter
passages.text:
Bringing back the cloth in such a manner would not be beneficial to Deucus.

Perhaps there's a tailor here in Val'sharah who'd be willing to mend it for you.

The priestess who helped you earlier may know of such a person.

passages.title: Mending the Filter
passages.text: You dare request such a menial task from me? Surely you must be joking.

passages.title: Deep in the Cavern
passages.text:
We're getting tired of those murlocs. They skitter around the cavern like they own it. They stole some of our most precious relics and got their fishy fins all over them. 

Kill a few of them so they know they don't run things around here.

passages.title: Deep in the Cavern
passages.text: Slippery little critters, aren't they?

passages.title: Deep in the Cavern
passages.text: I could hear their murlurulurls echoing in the cavern. Maybe they'll think twice before taking our stuff next time.

passages.title: Guhruhlruhlruh
passages.text:
The murlocs are usually pretty scared of us, but some bigger one led them into our cavern and they're getting too brave.

Kill their leader. I think its name is something like "Guhruhlruhlruh."

passages.title: Guhruhlruhlruh
passages.text: Can you pronounce murloc names? I never can.

passages.title: Guhruhlruhlruh
passages.text: That ought to send some of the murlocs packing.

passages.title: Vale POI Event TRACKING
Hidden No More
passages.text:
Now that you've uncovered the demons, I can sense them, too. Specifically, I sense a very powerful fel lord deeper in the cave. You need to grab his power while you still can.

If you can deal with their leader, we will take care of the rest of his forces in that cave.

passages.title: Hidden No More
passages.text:
Excellent. You've absorbed that fel lord's power and become more powerful in-turn.

Now, we can fully concentrate on destroying the Legion and their Brood Queen.

passages.title: Vengeance Will Be Mine!
passages.text:
This is why the Legion fears us. We have the ability to turn their secrets against them and in so doing become stronger than they ever can be.

Quickly, <name>, teach us what you have learned.

passages.title: Vengeance Will Be Mine!
passages.text: We await your instruction, <name>.

passages.title: Vengeance Will Be Mine!
passages.text:
I blame myself, <name>. Mannethrel was already struggling. It is a never-ending battle we all must endure... to control the fel energies that we have taken in.

Maybe it would be best if you held off teaching the others for now. We can not afford to lose anyone else.

passages.title: Cry Havoc and Let Slip the Illidari!
passages.text: This is why the Legion fears us. We have the ability to turn their secrets against them and in so doing become stronger than they ever can be.

passages.title: Cry Havoc and Let Slip the Illidari!
passages.text: We await your instruction, <name>.

passages.title: Cry Havoc and Let Slip the Illidari!
passages.text:
I blame myself, <name>. Mannethrel was already struggling. It is a never-ending battle we all must endure... to control the fel energies that we have taken in.

Maybe it would be best if you held off teaching the others for now. We can not afford to lose anyone else.

passages.title: The Forgening
passages.text: Your new weapon is very powerful, but my smiths have mastered crafting over thousands of years. Speak to Master Smith Helgar and see what improvements can be made.

passages.title: The Forgening
passages.text: That artifact is amazing, I can already see the potential we can unlock.

passages.title: The Search for Knowledge
passages.text: While you were out gallivanting, did you notice any lost relics around Azsuna? My sources tell me there are treasures to be found. These rumors merit investigation!

passages.title: The Search for Knowledge
passages.text: A sodden, aged tome lies partially buried in the muck.

passages.title: Moozy's Adventure
passages.text: <Moozy is floating down the river and must be reunited with his mother.>

passages.title: Moozy's Adventure
passages.text: Moozy! Thank the spirits you are okay! Oh thank you for returning him to me. Thank you!

passages.title: A Mysterious Summons
passages.text:
<class>, heed my call. I am aware that you come to Stormheim seeking the Aegis of Aggramar. 

Know that this will be a monumental task.

However, I see promise in you, and thus will guide you through the ancient trials. I must warn you that no mortal has passed even the first of these trials in the recorded history of Stormheim, though countless champions have tried.

If you believe yourself worthy, outsider, seek me outside Aggramar's Vault. Your first test will await you there. 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(39589))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(39589))");
 
 
 
 
 
 const cta = WH.Tools.createWowheadClientCta();
 if (cta) {
 $('.db-page-collection-tracker-cta').append(cta);
 }

passages.title: Blood and Gold
passages.text:
The challengers gathered in the Valley of the Sword have brought with them offerings to the watchers of the vault. 

It might be a good idea to take some of these offerings with you to help in appeasing Yotnar.

passages.title: Blood and Gold
passages.text:
What is this you bring?

You honor me, outsider.

passages.title: Blood and Gold
passages.text:
I appreciate your gifts, outsider. You show great respect to the trials. 

You do well to honor our ways.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras: Sewer Sleuthing
passages.text:
Linzy said that Lyndras escaped down into the sewers of Dalaran. Surely there must be a clue down there as to his whereabouts.

Hopefully he hasn't caused any more commotion amongst the citizens of Dalaran.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras: Downward Spiral
passages.text: Flitz mentioned a manhole near Violet Hold, perhaps that would be the best place to pick up Lyndras' trail.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras: Downward Spiral
passages.text:
The trail ended at Linzy's ley flame burner, lying in pieces upon the ground.

There are too many guards around for this to have gone unnoticed. Perhaps they have some information about Lyndras.

passages.title: Treasures of Deathwing
passages.text:
Neltharion's Vault? Well why didn't that spiritwalker just say so?

When we were jumpin' into the cavern I thought I saw a chamber up high that might have what we are after.

Have a look around this place while I see if I can't find a way up.

passages.title: Calibration Experts
passages.text:
It will take the cooperation of several highly skilled sorts to calibrate these burettes.

Myshalla Streambreeze in Feralas has demonstrated admirable attention to detail.

I loathe Ironforge, but a resident named Krimple Proxmeasure is known for his precision.

And while I'd never travel to Booty Bay without a lock on my wallet, Tryks Pourtrue has proven reliable and fair... mostly.

passages.title: Calibration Experts
passages.text:
Yes, I'd say these burettes look well-calibrated.

I knew those three would be meticulous. Never underestimate the value of someone who obsesses over tiny details, <name>!

passages.title: On Felbat Wings
passages.text:
It is time. We have dealt the Legion's forces a crippling blow from which they will never recover.

Quickly, let us mount up and take the fight to Tyranna's command center.

passages.title: On Felbat Wings
passages.text:
Can you sense her power? It will take all of you combined.

Even so... I better go secure our way out of here.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras: Leyflame Larceny
passages.text:
The guards here must have seen Lyndras come through. The trail of ley dust isn't exactly hard to miss either.

Perhaps one of the guards knows what became of Lyndras.

passages.title: Where's Lyndras: Leyflame Larceny
passages.text:
You looking for that crazed elf? Sorry to say he's been locked up.

We found him hunched in the corner making all sorts of noise and when we approached him, he attacked one of our guards.

We also found him with an item that was reported stolen. We had no choice but to lock him up in Violet Hold.

passages.title: Critter Scatter Shot
passages.text:
The howlers in these hills travel in packs. Three against one isn't a fight I want to pick.

Luckily those wolves are no match for my engineering skills! I just put the finishing touches on the prototype of a device that will help scatter the pack. All I need now is some ammo...

Snatch me some rabbits from the meadow south of here, and I'll let you be the first to try out the hand cannon.

passages.title: Critter Scatter Shot
passages.text: Have you snatched the rabbits yet?

passages.title: Critter Scatter Shot
passages.text: Hrm, these rabbits are a bit bigger than I thought, but we should still be able to stuff a few of them into the hand cannon.

passages.title: The Properties of Leystone
passages.text:
I've never seen anything like this "leystone" ore. It's light, like mithril, but it carries much more of a magical energy... more even than saronite or elementium.

Let's try making something with it. How about a nice pair of gauntlets?

passages.title: The Properties of Leystone
passages.text:
Are you alright? Most of my stock seems to be unharmed by the flames. It's a good thing this wasn't the tailoring shop.

The explosion seemed to happen when I applied the flux.

No flux means no welding. That's a shame. Without the ability to weld, we're limited to crafting belts and bracers.

passages.title: Grand Theft Felbat
passages.text:
You heard what Maiev said. We need to get out of here.

There is an elevator shaft at the far end of these caverns. Let us make our way there.

passages.title: Grand Theft Felbat
passages.text: Kayn and Altruis said you would be coming. Just in time, <name>.

passages.title: Forged in Fire
passages.text:
The fearsome demon, Immolanth, led a Legion army that conquered and eventually ruled a distant nexus world. 

Somehow, the Wardens imprisoned him, then kept him locked up in the chamber to our left. He is contained, but not for long.

The demon's power is a valuable prize to any demon hunter who can defeat him. Whoever can do so will gain power beyond imagining.

I believe that person could be you, <name>.

passages.title: Forged in Fire
passages.text: Yes... just look you... surging with new power and knowledge!

passages.title: Beam Me Up
passages.text:
To the east is an intricate prison chamber designed to contain the beholder, Glazer.

It began malfunctioning shortly after the breach.

You will need to rotate the mirrors in the room to focus an energy beam onto the creature. Otherwise, we cannot break through Glazer's impenetrable shield.

Hurry. Altruis went ahead to assist the others, but we are losing the fight.

passages.title: Beam Me Up
passages.text: I had no doubt you would know what to do.

passages.title: All The Way Up
passages.text:
Kor'vas went ahead to meet up with Kayn and Altruis.

Step onto the elevator when it arrives, and meet them in the Hall of Judgment above.

passages.title: All The Way Up
passages.text:
This is serious. Their core ideals are in direct conflict.

I fear they will take this duel to the death.

passages.title: Harbingers of the Past
passages.text:
<name>, you must stop this argument before the damage is irreparable.

Kayn and Altruis must be reminded of their common bonds.

The Pool of Judgment can reflect memories of the past. Touch it, and draw upon your own recollections. 

Remind them what it meant to fight under Lord Illidan. Remind them why we took the demon hunter's path.

passages.title: Between Us and Freedom
passages.text:
The last of our survivors have fought their way into the final chamber ahead.

Only one obstacle stands between us and the vault's exit - the leader of this demon invasion, Bastillax.

Kill him, take his power, and claim our freedom.

passages.title: Between Us and Freedom
passages.text:
We escaped the Vault, but our work is far from over.

The Legion's assault on this world is just beginning.

If Azeroth is to survive, we may have to work with this... Archmage Khadgar.

passages.title: Illidari, We Are Leaving
passages.text:
The Legion has begun its invasion of our world. Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, brave defenders are answering the call to arms.
 
However, they will ultimately fail without your aid. You Illidari were uniquely trained as weapons against the Legion.

I only ask that you come with me. Further instructions await you on the other side.

passages.title: Illidari, We Are Leaving
passages.text:
If you are ready, I will take you to our destination.

Are you prepared to leave?

passages.title: Illidari, We Are Leaving
passages.text:
The Legion has begun its invasion of our world. Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, brave defenders are answering the call to arms.
 
However, they will ultimately fail without your aid. You Illidari were uniquely trained as weapons against the Legion.

I only ask that you come with me. Further instructions await you on the other side.

passages.title: Illidari, We Are Leaving
passages.text:
If you are ready, I will take you to our destination.

Are you prepared to leave?

passages.title: The Call of War
passages.text:
Today, sorrow grips Stormwind, bastion of the Light. 

King Varian Wrynn has fallen in battle, leaving the crown to his son Anduin.

The leaders of the Alliance have gathered to pay their respects. No doubt they will have need of your unique skills.

You will find the king upon the throne of Stormwind Keep, attended by one of your fellow Illidari. I am needed in Dalaran.

Good luck, adventurer.

passages.title: The Call of War
passages.text:
Dark times have fallen upon Stormwind, <name>.

With King Varian Wrynn slain on the Broken Shore, uncertainty and tension grip the Alliance leaders.

The timing of this tragedy is no accident. The Burning Legion seeks to sow disorder amongst its enemies, weakening its prey from within.

We must act.

passages.title: The Call of War
passages.text:
The Warchief Vol'jin is expecting you.

Enter Grommash Hold straight ahead, and make your introduction.

passages.title: The Path of Huln
passages.text:
The drogbar have a tool of the titans in their possession, and it falls to us to find a way to get around that.

To that end, I recommend we walk the Path of Huln to the place our people first recovered the hammer so many generations ago.

I have asked for the aid of Brann in this endeavor as there are few in the living world more acquainted with titan artifacts.

The road is dangerous, and we could use your aid upon it.

passages.title: Between Us and Freedom
passages.text:
The last of our survivors have fought their way into the final chamber ahead.

Only one obstacle stands between us and the vault's exit - the leader of this demon invasion, Bastillax.

Kill him, take his power, and claim our freedom.

passages.title: Between Us and Freedom
passages.text:
We escaped the Vault, but our work is far from over.

The Legion's assault on this world is just beginning.

If Azeroth is to survive, we may have to work with this... Archmage Khadgar.

passages.title: Legend of Black Rook Hold
passages.text:
<name>, have you heard of Saris Swifthammer?

He was a legendary blacksmith amongst the elves of Black Rook Hold. I wonder if any of his research still exists.

I want you to travel there and see if you can discover anything about Saris, or see if he left anything we can research here at my shop.

passages.title: Legend of Black Rook Hold
passages.text: Thank you again for freeing me, stranger. I see you wish to discuss the art of blacksmithing.

passages.title: Forging New Strength
passages.text:
Even the most nefarious Legion lords fear your presence on the battlefield. Yet they are relentless, fashioning ever more terrible horrors and fiends in hopes of countering your might.

Highlord, we must augment your power to maintain our edge over the enemy.

The altar before you holds within it the essence of the countless heroes of the Light buried in these sacred halls. Place your weapon upon the altar and imbue it with new strength.

passages.title: Forging New Strength
passages.text:
I will continue beseeching the Light to bolster the power of your weapon.

For now, its newfound strength should be more than enough.

passages.title: The Knowledge of Black Rook
passages.text:
You have honored me with your help and now I wish to return those favors to you. On that pedestal there is all my research. Take it with you and learn from it so you may carry on my legacy.

Thank you again, <name>.

passages.title: The Knowledge of Black Rook
passages.text: Were you able to find him?

passages.title: The Knowledge of Black Rook
passages.text: This is... this is amazing! There are techniques in here I'd never imagined trying. Good work, <name>!

passages.title: The Tranquil Forest
passages.text:
Archmage Khadgar sent word about Val'sharah not long ago. It sounds like he has good news.

You should meet him on Krasus' Landing in Dalaran as soon as you are able.

passages.title: The Tranquil Forest
passages.text:
<Archmage Khadgar smiles.>

I rarely get to say this, but I have good news for you, <name>.

passages.title: The Lone Mountain
passages.text:
Our sources tell us that a Highmountain tauren emissary has recently arrived in Dalaran. We don't know his intentions, but his people could be an invaluable contact in the region.

Khadgar is greeting the emissary at Krasus' Landing in Dalaran - you should seek him out.

passages.title: The Lone Mountain
passages.text: Greetings champion. I am Warbrave Oro of the Highmountain tauren. I come on the winds of war to find you.

passages.title: Stormheim
passages.text:
Sky Admiral Rogers has sent word for you to meet her in Dalaran.

She should be waiting for you in the Violet Citadel. It sounded important.

passages.title: Stormheim
passages.text: It's an honor, <name>.

passages.title: Keeping Your Edge
passages.text:
Greetings, Deathlord. The blades you hold, while magnificent, have much untapped potential. As you harvest the souls of your enemies their power will continue to grow.

Grand Master Corvus has studied new techniques that may be of use to you, <my lord/my lady>.

You can find him working the forges on the upper level.

passages.title: Keeping Your Edge
passages.text:
Ah this weapon is amazing! Do you see the souls of the damned dancing along its edge? Oh how they scream for release!

Yes... in their forms I can see how the blade must be shaped.

passages.title: Advanced Runecarving
passages.text:
I've been working for many years to improve the forges. This weapon will be the perfect demonstration of the Soul Forge, their latest design!

We can take your artifact to the forge and shape it to make use of the power it contains, provided you've fed your weapon enough souls first. Let's give it a little try, eh?

passages.title: Advanced Runecarving
passages.text:
Oh yes... that will do nicely!

Return after you've fed your blade another feast of souls and we will make it the most powerful weapon that's ever existed!

passages.title: Shiny, But Deadly
passages.text:
Soulkeeper Uriah and I were transporting demon prisoners to Allari in Azsuna when our caravan was attacked by kobolds.

Those mindless vermin made off with the soul chambers that house our demonic captives.

The crystals may be shiny, but they're also deadly. If they are damaged in any way, the demons trapped within may escape.

Head into the cave nearby and recover the soul chambers before it's too late.

passages.title: Shiny, But Deadly
passages.text: Have you recovered the soul chambers yet?

passages.title: Shiny, But Deadly
passages.text:
Is this all you could find?

While I'm grateful to have these gems in my possession once again, it seems that there are still a few missing. I fear they've been broken, which means the demons within have escaped.

passages.title: Candle to the Grave
passages.text:
These kobolds are taking advantage of the attacks against the Skyhorn tribe. They disturb our graves and steal anything they can get their paws on.

I can do nothing to stop them! Please rid this sacred burial ground of the kobold.

passages.title: Candle to the Grave
passages.text: Some of them seem to be digging less enthusiastically, at the very least.

passages.title: Burn the Candle at Both Ends [NOT USED]
passages.text: You no come in yet! You need yellow candle and green candle before let in to Candleking!

passages.title: Can't Hold a Candle To You
passages.text: Okay guess you can go say hi to Candleking now.

passages.title: Can't Hold a Candle To You
passages.text: Have you found my skull?

passages.title: Can't Hold a Candle To You
passages.text: Thank the spirits! These kobolds do not honor their ancestors in the way we do. I can rest peacefully now.

passages.title: The Soulkeeper's Fate
passages.text:
Soulkeeper Uriah was injured in the kobold attack, but insisted on venturing further into the cave to recover the stolen soul shards. He told me to wait here with our remaining supplies until he returned, but I fear the worst.

Please find Uriah. He is the only one who knows how to trap the demons.

passages.title: The Soulkeeper's Fate
passages.text: Uriah would not want me to waste time with tears. My mourning can wait until the escaped demons are trapped once again.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Theory
passages.text:
I've gone through all the research ye gathered for me and I've come up with a theory. As we know, the ore in this world develops over time, through pressure and environmental changes.

But the Infernal Brimstone ye gave me had its growth accelerated through demonic magic, much like the saronite of Icecrown.

If we're wantin' to test this out, we'll have to get the help of some magic-users.

Take this brimstone back and go see Matthew Rabis. He may know how to breathe life into it.

passages.title: Infernal Brimstone Theory
passages.text: <Sniff sniff> I smell something...fel.

passages.title: The Brimstone's Secret
passages.text:
While you were gathering what I asked of you, I did a little testing on the brimstone. It reacted rather violently when I channeled onto it. Careful casting went into making the creature from whom you took this.

Unless you have a host of demon spell-casters at your disposal, recreating such a creature would be impossible.

That's all I have to tell you. Go now and leave me before my hunger takes over.

passages.title: The Brimstone's Secret
passages.text:
I see. Well that's at least a little helpful.

With that information in mind, I believe we can move forward with our investigation into this resource.

passages.title: Fire!
passages.text: You! Adventurer! Give us a hand! The wagon's caught fire!

passages.title: Fire!
passages.text: Why are you just staring at me with your mouth hanging open! Give us a hand!

passages.title: Fire!
passages.text: That was... unexpected. Fel flames? I'd say this warrants further investigation.

passages.title: Mysterious Dust
passages.text:
Nearly everything in the wagon was obliterated by the fire. All that remains is a small pile of dust.

The cart belonged to Trader Caelen. Perhaps he knows more about what happened.

As for the dust - either the inscription trainers or the alchemy trainers might have some insight.

passages.title: Mysterious Dust
passages.text:
This powder... I think I know what this is. I had theorized its existence, but...

Hey, Vanessa! You'd better come take a look at this.

passages.title: The Council's Approval
passages.text:
Those results certainly were disappointing. Calcination is a tricky process, better reserved for alchemists and blacksmiths. Still, I thought we'd get more than a measly TWO GRAINS of obliterum.

For a more efficient reaction, we'll need a special forge, and to get that...

...we'll need permission from the Council of Six.

passages.title: The Council's Approval
passages.text: I am intrigued...

passages.title: The Council's Approval
passages.text:
I like the way you think, <race>. I've long tried to convince the council that winning this war against the Legion means occasionally stooping to their level.

The Kirin Tor could use more mavericks like you.

passages.title: Friends in Low Places
passages.text:
My contact is one Oxana Demonslay. She has declined invitation to Dalaran proper, preferring to stay in the sewers of the Underbelly.

If there is anybody on this rock that knows how to properly build an Obliterum Forge, it is her.

Oh, and watch your back while you're down there, <name>.

passages.title: Friends in Low Places
passages.text:
The archmage sent you? Hmph.

Was he afraid to come down and visit me personally? Or is he worried that the sewer water might touch the hem of his robe?

passages.title: Cold Hard Coin
passages.text:
I am not interested in gold. Your aboveground currencies have little use down here.

I am, however interested in Sightless Eyes. I will gladly accept some as payment for my services.

passages.title: Cold Hard Coin
passages.text: Sightless Eyes, <name>.

passages.title: Cold Hard Coin
passages.text: <The demon hunter accepts the coins.>

passages.title: The Obliterum Forge
passages.text:
The components of the forge are assembled and, as I understand it, Archmage Karlain has secured a location for us to begin construction: aboveground, near the blacksmith.

Come back and visit sometime, <name>.

passages.title: The Obliterum Forge
passages.text: Let's get a move on, <name>. I am needed at the Violet Citadel.

passages.title: The Obliterum Forge
passages.text:
Look at the horns on that thing. And glowing eyes?

Those demon hunters sure do have a flair for the dramatic, don't they?

passages.title: [PH] Collect Weapons
passages.text: <insert>

passages.title: Curse of the Sea
passages.text:
[PH] <You find a strange glowing orb inside the treasure chest. A commanding voice emits from the orb-- it is Odyn.> 

Very good, <name>, you've found my orb. The souls of vrykul champions are unrightfully being transported to Helheim. These champions deserve a place in Valhallas, not an eternity alongside that witch.

Use this cleansing orb on the cursed vrykul to free them. If the ship reaches the shores of Helheim before the curse is lifted, they will be doomed to serve an eternity as Helya's kvaldir.

passages.title: Stormheim
passages.text:
Nathanos Blightcaller, Champion of the Banshee Queen herself, sent for you in Dalaran.

He should be waiting for you in the Violet Citadel. It sounded urgent.

passages.title: Stormheim
passages.text:
<Nathanos glances over at you, pausing for a moment before acknowledging your presence.>

Yes?

passages.title: Toll for the Soul
passages.text:
[PH] As foretold, you have arrived... Helya is foolish to think I'll let her ferry me into Helheim. Odyn has already smiled upon me, my soul belongs in Valhallas. 

Make no mistake, I am not a prisoner. Before my death Odyn appeared to me in the form of a raven. He praised my battles in life and gave me a quest no vrykul could refuse. The Helerjar arrived... and I let them slay me.

Prisoner-- nay, I am a liberator, sent by Odyn to free the souls of Valarjar.

passages.title: Helping the Hunters
passages.text:
Now, while I continue to fill the rest of our orders, I'd really appreciate it if you would deliver these vellums to Jace Darkweaver down in Azsuna.

He and the other demon hunters have been fighting back the Legion for quite some time and could use this as quickly as possible.

Thanks, <name>!

passages.title: Helping the Hunters
passages.text:
<Jace takes the crate from you and peers inside.>

The vellums! They're finally here.

passages.title: In the Loop
passages.text:
We could use your help down here, <name>. Some of our hunters would benefit greatly from having those vellums applied to their rings right now.

Here take a few. I'll give the rest to one of my other soldiers to hand out.

My hunters probably won't stop to let you apply the enchants, so you'll just have to do your enchanting even if they're in the midst of battle.

passages.title: In the Loop
passages.text: There's no time to waste. We need to get these enchantments out to as many of my hunters as possible.

passages.title: In the Loop
passages.text: That will certainly help us keep these demons at bay for much longer. We're in your debt, <name>.

passages.title: Thunder Struck
passages.text:
I've made contact with a potential source of new enchantments down in Highmountain. The tauren of Thunder Totem command the spirits to imbue items with great power.

Seek out an enchanter named Twaintail and see if he will share his knowledge with us.

Taurens are known for their sharing... right?

passages.title: Thunder Struck
passages.text:
The spirits told me of your coming, outlander. Let us see if you are indeed the hero this land needs.

<The tauren clears his throat.>

Pardon me. I know I come off as a bit dramatic. It's just... well, these things have meaning for me.

passages.title: Fey Enchantments
passages.text:
The new dusts and crystals we've found in these lands are fascinating, as I'm sure you've already surmised. I'm positive we can expand their usefulness to more of our armor.

I'd like you to go back out into the field and talk to a dryad in Val'sharah. Apparently she may be able to clue us into some enchantments for shoulder pieces.

Her name is Nalamya. You'll find her near the Temple of Elune.

passages.title: Fey Enchantments
passages.text:
What is it you want, <race>?

Oh, I see now. You're an enchanter.

I warn you though, if you take my enchantments like those foul elves of Black Rook and use them for evil, you shall feel my wrath one way or another.

passages.title: Led Astray
passages.text:
The night elves are no fools, but the elves of Black Rook follow their commanders with blind loyalty. I've no doubt that the blame for their apathy rests heavily upon their commanders.

I know of two of their leaders, who as we speak continue to command their troops to do nothing against the blight encroaching upon my home.

Go to Black Rook Hold and slay Trelan Shieldbreaker and Starlys Strongbow. Let them be an example for those who can help, but wish to remain cowardly.

passages.title: Led Astray
passages.text: Don't worry about proving what you've done for me. I have my own eyes and ears to tell me of your deeds.

passages.title: Cursed, But Convenient
passages.text:
I need you to return to Azsuna at once, <name>. I've only just heard of an enchantress within the Crumbled Palace who knows of many rare enchantments.

Go to her and see what you can learn at once.

passages.title: Cursed, But Convenient
passages.text:
Ah, a fellow enchanter. Come to earn the marks of my subordinates, have you?

If that's the case, then you may speak with my sentinel and druid. Earn their trust and they'll grant you their marks.

I, however, have a different task for you...

passages.title: An Enchanting Home
passages.text:
The more I learn about the Broken Isles, the more convinced I am that it is a land of wonders!

Ildine and I were just discussing rumors of a dwelling in Stormheim that was once the home to a vrykul enchantress called Tigrid. It is said the site is perfectly preserved, and her enchantments were so potent that they persist to this day!

Investigating the home might uncover valuable knowledge, <name>.

passages.title: An Enchanting Home
passages.text:
So, <race>, you have discovered my home... all that is left of me.

Not even enough to sustain my beloved enchantments...

passages.title: Ringing True
passages.text:
While your presence here would continue to be of value to us, your master in Dalaran has called for you.

I'd like to thank you again for all you've done for us. My hunters have been reminded that they're not alone in this war.

passages.title: Ringing True
passages.text:
<name>, you're back. Excellent work down in Azsuna. Jace gave you high praises for your help with his troops and against the Legion.

Before you go, I wanted to share with you the other new formulas we have for ring enchantments. It would do our side good in this war if you were to share these with your fellow adventurers.

passages.title: Elven Enchantments
passages.text:
You have earned the marks of my most trusted companions. You have also returned my love to me.

I am fortunate to have met you, <name>.

Now return to your master and let him know of what you have learned.

passages.title: Elven Enchantments
passages.text:
<You tell Nalthanis of your time with the cursed elves and the enchantments you learned.>

That's fascinating! You managed, through enchantments, to create a bond with those elves and now they may come to your aid?

Those are some truly powerful enchantments you were gifted, <name>. Don't let them go to waste.

passages.title: The Absent Priestess
passages.text:
After my betrayal, I never thought I could bear to look upon my love again. But thanks to you, <name>, I can at last return.

Go and speak to Enchantress Ilanya. I will let her know that you are worthy of my mark.

passages.title: The Absent Priestess
passages.text:
You have returned my love to me and for that I am forever grateful.

As she is with me now, she shall be at your beck and call should you need her. I grant to you her marks.

passages.title: On Azure Wings
passages.text:
I have some exciting news of my own to report, <name>. Ildine and I had an excursion to Azsuna and made contact with the blue dragons at the Azurewing Repose.

One of the dragons, Kharmeera, is an enchanter who expressed interest in working with you to perfect some of our enchantments.

I understand you were just down there working with the elves, but if you wouldn't mind returning, Kharmeera would enjoy working with you too.

passages.title: On Azure Wings
passages.text: I sense the power of enchantments about you, <name>. Yes, I think I will enjoy working with you!

passages.title: The Card Shark
passages.text:
We have the pigment, but we still require one more ingredient.

Visitors at the Legerdemain Lounge will often play card games, and occasionally their cards are discarded. Go see if you can find some loose cards that players may have gotten rid of between matches.

passages.title: The Card Shark
passages.text: The cards are just for reference, mostly...

passages.title: The Card Shark
passages.text:
And there we have it. Just as good as those witless Darkmoon cretins.

While we owe this success almost exclusively to my genius, I feel you ought to be rewarded for doing the legwork. Here's the recipe for my newest masterpiece.

passages.title: Our New Allies
passages.text:
Have you seen those demon hunters yet? I'm not entirely sold on their allegiance to our cause, but while we have them, we may as well exploit them.

Everybody needs glyphs, you know.

Go see what you can discover about them. Azsuna is as good a place as any to start.

Perhaps my genius has worn off on you and you'll be able to create your own recipes based on what you learn.

passages.title: Our New Allies
passages.text: Are you here to reinforce us, <class>? We could always use your strength.

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text:
You wish to learn what it is to be a demon hunter? That may take some time.

The first thing you can do is fight alongside us. Battle the demons with us and observe how we use their strength against them.

Return to me when you are finished.

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text: Have you seen enough?

passages.title: The Price of Power
passages.text: Some may condemn our methods. We simply do what we must to destroy the Burning Legion.

passages.title: Inscription of the Body
passages.text:
We demon hunters must keep our darkness at bay, lest we succumb to it and become demons ourselves. That is the purpose of marking our skin the way we do.

Up to the north, a demon hunter by the name of Baric Stormrunner is preparing to strengthen his markings. Go to him and learn how we keep our demons at bay.

passages.title: Inscription of the Body
passages.text:
Allari sent you? I am about to start a ritual. I could use you, stranger.

You seem more ally than enemy. In this time, allies are more important than ever.

passages.title: Containing the Demon Within
passages.text:
Now that we have all the essential pieces, let's begin the ritual.

I'll instruct you on how to help me. It is pivotal that you follow my instructions when I give them, or the ritual will fail.

passages.title: Containing the Demon Within
passages.text:
It is done. I fear that if I had waited any longer to improve my wards, the demon in me may have taken over.

Thank you again, <name>.

passages.title: Scribal Knowledge
passages.text:
We do not simply fight the demons, <name>. We observe them.

One of my best demon hunters, Zaria Shadowheart, is currently gathering intel on the demons in Felblaze Ingress.

Go to her. She will teach you what she has learned from the demons invading that region.

passages.title: Scribal Knowledge
passages.text: Allari has sent you to learn from me? In that case, I have much to tell.

passages.title: Runes of Power
passages.text:
Look closely, scribe, and you may learn. As the demons spread out over a region, the more clever ones will inscribe runes upon the ground. The fel taint pervades this entire hillside, but the corruption is darkest around these runes, disallowing anything pure to grow ever again.

Study these runes.

passages.title: Runes of Power
passages.text:
As I'm sure you sensed, these runes hold quite a bit of energy.

Greater knowledge of the Legion is your best weapon against it.

passages.title: Control is Key
passages.text:
We demon hunters ritualistically remove our eyes in order to see the demons more clearly.

Down below, a demon commander walks amongst his troops, unseen by normal eyes. He keeps the chaos in order, as we must keep our chaos in check.

Destroy his warding crystal, then slay him.

passages.title: Control is Key
passages.text:
I commend you, scribe. You would make an excellent demon hunter.

Take this ink as payment for your efforts. I have no need of it.

passages.title: Aethrem Crystal
passages.text:
<Most aethril has a sharp crystalline fiber in the center of the bloom, but this one is particularly well-developed.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Aethrem Crystal
passages.text:
A crystal... inside the flower? That gives me an idea.

I dabbled in jewelcrafting in my younger years. Take a look at this technique...

passages.title: The Burdens of Hunting
passages.text: There is nothing more I have to teach you, scribe. The Illidari stand behind you in the battle against the Legion.

passages.title: The Burdens of Hunting
passages.text:
<Professor Pallin looks over the demon hunter glyphs you've designed.>

Huh! Apparently I don't have to hold your hand as much as I thought.

Look at this glyph you've made right here. If you flip this symbol around, and adjust the stroke width here...

passages.title: Mysterious Messages
passages.text:
The woman at the archaeology shop just dropped off some tablets to be deciphered. Any fool can see they're written in ancient vrykul, but I lent my codex to one of my students, so I'm unable to decipher them here.

His name is Nicholo Swiftfuse, and he is in Stormheim. Let him know that if he fails to decipher them, his apprenticeship shall be terminated.

That is all.

passages.title: Mysterious Messages
passages.text:
Seriously? Pallin wants me to do what now?!

That old bag of wind thinks he's so great, but he's always making me do all his work. It's a surprise I'm not running that shop.

But fine, I'll help you. As long as you help me too.

passages.title: Not So Complex?
passages.text:
Alright, I believe I've finished adding the missing entries into the codex. And we have the machete... err, knife.

All that's left is to make our own tablet and verify my other suspicion about these tablets:

I believe that they're not just simple texts, but a sort of magical device.

passages.title: Not So Complex?
passages.text:
It was a good thing you were here to help me with that.

I surely would have been killed by those spirits!

passages.title: The Ink Flows
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to make a quick delivery for me.

Yes, I've learned by now that such trivial tasks are beneath your skills... but I'm rather busy right now and we both know my time is much more important than yours.

Deliver these contracts to Raethan, the Guard Captain in Dalaran's Underbelly.

passages.title: The Ink Flows
passages.text:
These all seem to be in order.

If you have a moment, scribe, I have a proposition for you that you may be interested in...

passages.title: An Odd Trinket
passages.text:
Wait, <name>, before you leave... did you not notice this?

<Raethan peels a small piece of paper from the bottom of the jewel.>

This wasn't reported stolen. It appears to be a card of some kind. Must be a scribe thing.

Perhaps it may be of some use to you.

passages.title: An Odd Trinket
passages.text: What's that you have there?

passages.title: An Odd Trinket
passages.text:
I... I know this work. My old apprentice, what's-his-name, was trying to prove he could create something as great as I could.

Impressively, he seemed to have succeeded in this one case.

We should learn from what he created and make our own, less putrid version.

passages.title: Roseate Essence
passages.text:
<The pigment milled from this flower is of an exceptionally high quality.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Roseate Essence
passages.text:
How did you get an extract so pure? Show me exactly what you did, step by step.

Fascinating. Do you mind if I write this down, so I can show my other students?

passages.title: Sallow Essence
passages.text:
<The felwort is reduced to a thick, clotted pigment. While all felwort-begotten pigment is somewhat offensive, this batch practically glows with a malevolent energy.>

<Professor Pallin would be interested in seeing this.>

passages.title: Sallow Essence
passages.text:
We've ventured into undiscovered territory, <name>. There isn't anyone out there in ANY academic circles I'm aware of that is milling felwort this effectively.

Well done, student. Or, should I say... well done, junior deputy assistant scribe?

Nah... I still prefer "student".

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Very well, I won't deny it. The Steamy Romance Novel is mine.

I only read it for the penmanship, I assure you! He writes such curvy "B"s... and such ample "D"s!

In fact... you might benefit from a penmanship lesson. The author of these books is one B. Spearshaker. I believe he can be found in the library in Ironforge.

Stop reading, student. You are dismissed. And give me my book back!

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Hello! Ye must be one of me many fans here for an autograph.

Oh, yer here about the romance novels, are ye? I see ye've discovered my little secret.

Ye know, I've grown tired of writing those. I've moved on, ye see. Wrote me last one yesterday.

But perhaps ye'd like to carry on the tradition...?

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
I've lost my passion, scribe. I just can't get into the voice o' the characters anymore.

Take a look at that unfinished book over there on the table. I can't seem to finish it. Maybe ye'll have an easier time with it.

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text: Dang-blasted writer's block!

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
Hmm... yes, ye seem to have gotten the hang of it. I particularly like that line: "Oh, Lord Gravesbane!" That would make a nice catchphrase...

Here, take this list o' story prompts. I certainly don't need them anymore.

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Very well, I won't deny it. The Steamy Romance Novel is mine.

I only read it for the penmanship, I assure you! He writes such curvy "B"s... and such ample "D"s!

In fact... you might benefit from a penmanship lesson. The author of these books is one F. Serbacon. I believe he can be found in the library in Undercity.

Stop reading, student. You are dismissed. And give me my book back!

passages.title: The Plot Thickens
passages.text:
Come for an autograph, have you? Very well, you may present your chest to me.

Oh, you're here about the romance novels? I see you've discovered my little secret.

You know, I've grown tired of writing those. I've moved on, you see. Wrote the last one yesterday.

But perhaps you'd like to carry on the tradition...?

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
I've lost my passion, scribe. I just can't find the voice of my characters anymore.

Take a look at that unfinished book over there on the table. I can't seem to finish it. Maybe you'll have an easier time with it.

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text: Confound this accursed writer's block!

passages.title: The Legacy Passed On
passages.text:
Hmm... yes, you seem to have gotten the hang of it. I particularly like that line: "Oh, Lord Gravesbane!" That would make a nice catchphrase...

Here, take this list of story prompts. I certainly don't need them anymore.

passages.title: An Embarrassing Revelation
passages.text:
This doesn't appear to be an inscription textbook at all... it's more of a steamy romance novel. The pages are just FILLED with tawdry tales of carnality.

Could it have something to do with inscription? Either way, Professor Pallin should be confronted.

passages.title: An Embarrassing Revelation
passages.text:
Get your hands off of... err, I mean... that's not my...

Where did you...

<The professor makes a sputtering sound.>

Someone must be playing a trick on me!

passages.title: Trouble for Okuna
passages.text:
<You open the bottle and find a message inside.>

Help! I need somebody... but not just anybody. I need a champion! I finally escaped the grasp of Prince Oceanus only to be hunted by his father, King Deepbeard.

I was enjoying my freedom and decided to go fishing when that giant attacked. I've been running around these islands trying to avoid that creature ever since... if anyone gets this message, please send help!

passages.title: Kill Azshara
passages.text: xxxxx

passages.title: Meet the Recruits
DEPRECATED
passages.text:
Archmage Khadgar sent word about Val'Sharah not long ago.

His Kirin Tor have opened a gateway between here and Dalaran - you can find it in the alcove behind you if you wish to make use of it, Highlord.

passages.title: Remnants of the Past
passages.text:
<The journal entry appears hastily written.>

I do not know what has become of my village. Ever since the mists engulfed the harbor, my kinsfolk have changed.

Some have grown violent and savage, while others have fallen into madness. Many have ventured into the mists and have yet to return.

In these times, we can usually turn to our leader, Jarl Tarben. Alas, the mists have taken him as well.

I do not know what will become of me. For now, I can only stay at my post and remain vigilant.

passages.title: Remnants of the Past
passages.text:
The mists of this bay rot not only the wood of the ships, but the very souls of its inhabitants.

But it seems you have already discovered this.

passages.title: Keepers of the Hammer
passages.text:
High Chieftain Ulan has requested your presence.

We have learned that the Burning Legion has returned and know that if you are true in your purpose in facing this evil, you will need our aid.

Our people have in our possession a great titan relic: the Hammer of Khaz'goroth.

We intend to lend it to you for this task.

When you are ready, join me at our stronghold of Thunder Totem in Highmountain.

passages.title: Blessing of Cenarius
passages.text:
Cenarius himself has risked much in coming here, if only briefly, to bestow a blessing upon you. He has seen what you are capable of, and has chosen you as champion in this battle.

Speak with him in the grove to the south. 
 See if you've already completed this by typing:

 /run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(39991))
 WH.clickToCopy(document.currentScript.parentNode, "\/run print(C_QuestLog.IsQuestFlaggedCompleted(39991))");

passages.title: Aethril Sample
passages.text:
This herb has clearly been absorbing magical energy from the land. Filaments of ley energy course from root to leaf.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see this.

passages.title: Aethril Sample
passages.text:
From the look of it, I would expect such an herb to be fragile and delicate, but... it's quite sturdy.

Oooh, look at these!

passages.title: Spayed by the Spade
passages.text:
The stem, leaves, and petals are dazzling, to be certain... but look at the pollination filaments, here, and the reproductive organs in the center of the bloom. They contain more energy than the rest of the plant put together.

I suspect that we can more responsibly and efficiently harvest aethril by focusing on these parts.

Still, it looks like this bloom has been damaged. I need undamaged parts if I'm to be sure.

passages.title: Spayed by the Spade
passages.text:
It may seem wrong to remove these most... "intimate" flower parts, but do not fret. They will grow back.

Much like the parts of a troll.

passages.title: Spayed by the Spade
passages.text:
<Your trainer looks over the pistil and stamen, clearly impressed.>

The Earthmother must have been feeling generous when she created the aethril.

Continue to focus on this part of the flower, <name>.

passages.title: Ragged Strips of Silk
passages.text:
Finely made strips of clothing, torn, tattered, and dirty: telltale signs of the withered.

The feral, degenerate outcasts of nightborne society must also be harvesting the aethril... but why?

passages.title: Ragged Strips of Silk
passages.text:
You found withered implements near an aethril bloom?

Hmm... you're the third one today.

passages.title: Desperation Breeds Ingenuity
passages.text:
I believe we may be able to use this clue to our advantage, <name>.

The withered are notoriously thirsty for mana, and will stop at nothing to get it. Perhaps we can study how they use the aethril and use the results to improve our own harvesting methods.

passages.title: Desperation Breeds Ingenuity
passages.text: I am glad you continue to come to my shop, <name>. I am useless with a weapon. We need adventurers like you to solve cases like this.

passages.title: Desperation Breeds Ingenuity
passages.text:
<Your trainer examines the stems, fingering the individual bite marks.>

If you'll pardon my language, they really gnawed the crap out of these things.

Look more closely, though. You can see that they focused on extracting the energy from the stem's central filament...

passages.title: Dreamleaf Sample
passages.text:
The herb is brilliantly green, paper-thin, and somewhat sticky.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see this.

passages.title: Dreamleaf Sample
passages.text:
I know this herb. I've seen it once before, in the Pandaria's Valley of the Four Winds.

This is dreamleaf.

passages.title: An Empathetic Herb
passages.text:
Something is different about this dreamleaf, though. It is less than pure.

I have a theory.

The wilds of Val'sharah have been blighted by a nightmarish curse. Sensitive herbs like this may be susceptible to such a blight.

I need more information before I can draw any conclusions. Find me some healthy samples and some blight-infested samples, and we can continue.

passages.title: An Empathetic Herb
passages.text: Those poor plants...

passages.title: An Empathetic Herb
passages.text:
It is just as I suspected. The infested herb is dying... but this may be turned to our advantage.

Look, herbalist. The dying dreamleaf has swollen with herbaceous extract. While harvesting the healthy dreamleaf is trivial, you can harvest enormous amounts of product from the infested ones.

passages.title: Twisted to Death
passages.text:
The corruption has completely taken this herb.

This blight is a mysterious force whose complexities transcend the teachings of simple herbalism. An expert in such infestation will need to tell you what's really going on here.

passages.title: Twisted to Death
passages.text:
Another plant, fallen...

<The druid attempts to blink back tears, and fails.>

DAMN YOU, NIGHTMARE! DAMN YOUUUUU!!!

passages.title: One Dead Plant is One Too Many
passages.text:
We must exact VENGEANCE for this. While I understand the importance of the balance between the Emerald Dream and the Nightmare, this time it's corruption has gone TOO FAR!

Satyrs. I blame the satyrs for this. Make them pay! Make them pay, and Elune will reward you with her bounty!

passages.title: One Dead Plant is One Too Many
passages.text: Exact your bloody vengeance, <class>. Show them the might of an herbalist.

passages.title: One Dead Plant is One Too Many
passages.text:
I feel the blight subsiding. Good.

Our respite will not last forever, but look... even now, the dreamleaf has succumbed more of its bounty.

passages.title: Choked by Nightmare
passages.text:
Another plant, killed by the blight. This one coiled so hard that it starved itself of sunlight.

You should bring it to Wildcrafter Osme in Lorlathil. He won't be happy.

passages.title: Choked by Nightmare
passages.text:
<Osme looks at the herb.>

<He is silent for a moment.>

NOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!!!!!!

passages.title: Teeny Bite Marks
passages.text:
This herb has been chewed by some of the local wildlife.

What kind of animal would eat foxflower? A bear?

Perhaps your trainer in Dalaran will know.

passages.title: Teeny Bite Marks
passages.text: You're right, <name>. Something has been chewing on this herb.

passages.title: Fjarnskaggl Sample
passages.text:
To one not trained in herbalism, this brambly bush might appear to be entirely useless. Your training, however, reveals this to be a very special plant indeed.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see some more samples of this.

passages.title: Fjarnskaggl Sample
passages.text: What do you have there, herbalist?

passages.title: Fjarnskaggl Sample
passages.text:
What a fantastic find, <name>. This must be the celebrated vrykul herb, fjarnskaggl. I've only read about it in books!

Here, I'll share what I remember with you...

passages.title: Ram's-Horn Trowel
passages.text:
The rune markings along the tool's grip suggest that it was left behind by a vrykul herbalist.

Apparently, the vrykul are also gathering this fjarnskaggl. Your trainer, Kuhuine, mentioned that she had read about this herb in the past.

Perhaps she might be interested in seeing the tools that the vrykul use to harvest it.

passages.title: Ram's-Horn Trowel
passages.text: You found this near a snarl of fjarnskaggl?

passages.title: Vrykul Herblore
passages.text:
<Kuhuine studies the trowel further.>

This is a standard digging tool. There is not much to be learned here, except...

...this DOES suggest that the vrykul are still actively gathering this herb.

The vrykul likely know much more about this herb than we do. All we need to do is find out where their knowledge is stored.

passages.title: Vrykul Herblore
passages.text: Any luck finding those books, <name>?

passages.title: Vrykul Herblore
passages.text:
This book: "Herblore of the Ancients", seems promising, but several pages are ripped out. Shame.

Still, there is much to learn in the others.

<Kuhuine turns to a random page, flips a few pages back and...>

See, look at this technique here!

passages.title: The Missing Page
passages.text:
<The page appears to be ripped out of a larger book. It reads:>

"...the Cairn of the Sea, a place long-known to be beloved by the gods.

He placed his offering of fjarnskaggl at the foot of the cairn, mouthed the words 'Herbs beget herbs', and received the blessing he desired."

This may be related to the books you brought back to your herbalism trainer.

passages.title: The Missing Page
passages.text: What good fortune! This page matches perfectly with the book you retrieved for me. We just need to piece them together, and...

passages.title: Starlight Rosedust
passages.text:
Despite all your training, the rose disintegrated in your hand.

Your herbalism trainer in Dalaran will want to see this.

passages.title: Starlight Rosedust
passages.text:
This herb just disintegrated in your hand?

Fascinating...
