It's all here too! I knew I could count on you! Here, take this reward.

You've earned it!

passages.title: Gobnapped
passages.text:
We never even saw the ambush coming...

The saberon hit us so hard and fast we barely had time to think.

Those overgrown mongrels dragged the others away and left me here for dead...they probably thought I was too close to dying.

I hear they like their meat fresh...
<cough>....well I ain't going down that easy!

Don't worry about me...<cough>...I've been through worse! You're gonna have to go to Sabermaw and get the other merchants out though.

They've probably got 'em all caged up in there...

passages.title: Gobnapped
passages.text:
You got all of the captured traders out of Sabermaw? Fantastic!

Now they owe me and I ain't one to let a debt go uncollected! As for you, take this reward for your trouble!

passages.title: My Precious!
passages.text:
You've got to help me!

I was hiding on the trade wagon that got ambushed just down the road from here. I snuck away before the saberon spotted me...but...but...

THEY STOLE MY MOST PRIZED POSSESSION!

You've got to help me get it back! I watched them drag it into Sabermaw and up that giant hill!

Who knows what those filthy saberon will do to it!

Please, I'm just a kid! You've got to help me out, right?

passages.title: My Precious!
passages.text:
You did a great job, <name>. I couldn't have asked for a better sidekick!

Anyway, now that I've got my treasure back...

I've got to do...

...things and...stuff.

Bye!

passages.title: Tearing Up Talador
passages.text:
Commander, we have a bit of a problem.
We found a location in Talador to set up an outpost but the team that was sent to begin construction have been arguing with each other on what to build. This situation could really put a setback in our plans unless it's dealt with swiftly.

Take a gryphon to Talador and speak with Foreman Eksos before this gets any worse.

passages.title: At Your Command
passages.text:
I'm glad you're here!

Fort Wrynn is nearly complete. We only need to fill this last plot.

Baros provided us with blueprints for two different structures that would fit this space - an Artillery Tower or an Arcane Sanctum.

It's your call, commander. The plans are on the drafting table for your perusal.

passages.title: At Your Command
passages.text: At your command.

passages.title: At Your Command
passages.text: Excellent. This will do nicely.

passages.title: Vignette: Yaga the Scarred
passages.text:
Goren are dangerous, especially in large numbers, and especially when we have a blind, under powered shaman with us.

Fortunately, they have very short lifespans. Unfortunately, they multiply fast and grow faster.

If we are going to do this we need to find the brood mother. Slaying her and her eggs should slow down the onslaught of goren. Check the burrows near the Forge Gates and I will to keep them off of Drek'Thar's scent.

passages.title: The Quarry Quandary
passages.text:
Now that we have the artillery tower built, we're going to need some skilled hands to run it.

I've heard that Ared, one of the best smiths in Shattrath, managed to escape the city's fall. He should be just outside the north wall with the rest of the refugees.

See if you can convince him to work for us.

passages.title: The Quarry Quandary
passages.text: We need to find someone to run this place or we're not going to be producing much of anything.

passages.title: The Quarry Quandary
passages.text:
You are the commander of this fort, yes?

My master wanted to join your fight to reclaim our home but he grew ill and... I'm sorry, he was a great draenei and I will carry on his memory.

Your new building would give me the means to see out my master's vision and honor his passing.

If you would allow me to do this then I would serve you.

passages.title: Tearing Up Talador
passages.text:
Commander, we have a bit of a problem.

We found a location in Talador to set up an outpost but the team that was sent to begin construction have been arguing with each other on what to build. This situation could really put a setback in our plans unless it's dealt with swiftly.

Take a gryphon to Talador and speak with Foreman Eksos before this gets any worse.

passages.title: At Your Command
passages.text:
Commander, the outpost is nearly fully operational.

Gazlowe provided us with two different blueprints to fill this final plot - an Arsenal or an Arcane Sanctum.

Either one would provide us with the additional firepower we need to stop the Iron Horde's advance.

The plans are on the drafting table. It's your call.

passages.title: At Your Command
passages.text: What is your will, commander?

passages.title: At Your Command
passages.text:
Your will be done.

For the Horde!

passages.title: The Quarry Quandary
passages.text:
Now that our arsenal is built we need a skilled smith to operate it.

We recently caught an Iron Horde deserter who claims he used to be one of the Blackrock's best iron workers.

Normally I'd ignore the ravings of a captive, but the weapons we took out of his pack had the finest workmanship I've ever seen.

Commander, I think we should see if he's as good as he claims.

passages.title: The Quarry Quandary
passages.text:
You're the one in charge around here, right? I've heard the guards talk about your exploits and if I wasn't looking at you now I'd swear they were lying.

I've only ever wanted to make the finest blades and put them in the hands of the strongest of fighters. I can tell already that you're exactly the type I want to carry my weapons.

If you can give me a chance I swear you will not be disappointed.

passages.title: REUSE
passages.text:
Teron'gor and his master Gul'dan were here! I tried to stop them... they escaped through the demonic gateway behind me before I could finish them!

I think I can activate the portal open just long enough for you to enter. We have no way of knowing where it leads, but I fear it may end inside Auchindoun!

You have to stop him once and for all!

passages.title: Out of Jovite
passages.text:
Ared and I came this way because we needed a good supply of metal to build his designs and some of the best metal is the jovite that comes from the mine in Kuuro's Claim. In order to supply the artillery tower I'm going to need this metal.

Unfortunately that place was recently overwhelmed by a pack of goren, so you're going to have to fight your way in to get the ore before they manage to devour it.

Nothing that should be too much of a problem for you.

passages.title: Out of Jovite
passages.text: We need to get that ore before those goren eat it all.

passages.title: Out of Jovite
passages.text:
These look pretty good. Ared would have loved to get his hands on these.

<Miall wipes away a tear.>

 I'm sorry, this is making me too emotional, these will do just fine.

passages.title: Iridium Recovery
passages.text:
Ared used to always teach me that the purity of the metal is key. If the metal isn't pure it will crack under stress and be of no use to anyone.

For the artillery tower to function I'll need to make metal as pure as my master would, and for that I need a strong flux.

The dust from crushed iridium geodes would work in a pinch, but we need to find some first. They tend to congregate underground, so check out the mine in Kuuro's Claim nearby.

passages.title: Iridium Recovery
passages.text: I'm going to need a lot of iridium dust to purify the metal to anywhere near my masters standards.

passages.title: Iridium Recovery
passages.text: This won't be as good as some of the stuff we had back at the forge in Shattrath, but it will do.

passages.title: Iridium Recovery
passages.text:
My goods used to be for the very best, now the Iron Horde make copies out of poor metal and give them to everyone.

I'm going to show them what a real smith can do in your arsenal, but first I'm going to need a powerful flux to make the metal as pure as it can get.

The dust from crushed iridium geodes would work in a pinch but we need to find some first. They tend to congregate underground, so check out the mine in Kuuro's Claim nearby.

passages.title: Iridium Recovery
passages.text: I'm going to need a lot of iridium dust to purify the metal to anywhere near my standards.

passages.title: Iridium Recovery
passages.text: This won't be as good as some of the mixes we had back in the Blackrock foundries, but it will do.

passages.title: Out of Jovite
passages.text:
Crafting good equipment requires the best metal and some of the best metal is the jovite that comes from the mine in Kuuro's Claim, just east of here. In order to supply the arsenal I'm going to need this metal.

Unfortunately the place was recently overwhelmed by a pack of goren so you're going to have to fight your way in to get the ore before they manage to devour it.

Nothing that should be too much of a problem for you, <sir/ma'am>.

passages.title: Out of Jovite
passages.text: We need to get that ore before those damned goren eat it all.

passages.title: Out of Jovite
passages.text:
Good size chunks and without a lot of the matrix material on them.

These will do just fine.

passages.title: Going to the Gordunni
passages.text:
We have a good supply of jovite now but there just isn't enough of the material in the mine to keep the artillery tower in stock for long. Down south of here there's a mountain that's just full of the stuff but there's one problem; Ogres!

The Gordunni live on top of that mountain and they have begun trading the jovite to the Iron Horde.

We need to go down there and secure the minerals for ourselves.

I'll pack some supplies and meet you near their fortress down south.

passages.title: Going to the Gordunni
passages.text:
I crafted a few things before we left that we may need: some smoke grenades, a grappling hook, even was able to get Thaelin to throw together a rocket pack.

I'm sure we'll find a use for everything.

passages.title: Finding a Foothold
passages.text:
So, you are the one that has led my children home? I have been waiting for you.

The Iron Horde grows stronger every day.

I have foreseen a great battle, but my visions are clouded. It's as if time is sitting on top of itself. 

One thing is certain, your presence here is of great importance.

passages.title: Finding a Foothold
passages.text: This will have to do.

passages.title: Looking for Lumber
passages.text:
Some of the trees around here look small enough that the workers should be able to down them in no time.

We can leave the hard labor to Shelly's men, but if you'd be willing to mark the trees for them to start with, we should be able to get this operation rolling much faster.

passages.title: Looking for Lumber
passages.text: How goes the lumber hunt?

passages.title: Looking for Lumber
passages.text:
Perfect.

Not only will this lumber do the job, it will look fantastic!

passages.title: Quakefist
passages.text:
I'm getting reports of a giant in the forest.

A few of the Karabor peacekeepers have followed it to a cave. In all honesty I don't think any of our troops are willing to engage the beast.

Maybe you could investigate? I'm sure the peacekeepers would appreciate the help.

passages.title: Quakefist
passages.text: Did you kill the giant in the cave?

passages.title: Quakefist
passages.text:
The base is significantly more secure with that giant dead.

You have made quite an impression on the peacekeepers.

passages.title: Establish Your Garrison
passages.text:
I'm impressed with how quickly you have pulled this group together, commander.

I think it's time we start putting up some walls and establishing a firm perimeter around our base.

passages.title: Establish Your Garrison
passages.text: The garrison is really starting to take shape.

passages.title: Build Your Barracks
passages.text:
I must say, commander, this garrison has really come along.

We have enough materials, all we need now are the blueprints I drafted up and I can begin construction on your barracks.

Hmm... now where did I put those blueprints?

passages.title: Build Your Barracks
passages.text: The troops will sleep a lot better tonight.

passages.title: Build Your Barracks
passages.text: How is the construction of the barracks coming along?

passages.title: The Bounty of Bladespire
passages.text:
The sacking of this fortress is as much your victory as ours. It is only fair you should share in the bounty.

I will have resources set aside as we find them. All you need do is report to your garrison and have them dispatch peons to collect these materials.

passages.title: TEST - Quest Objective Completion Effect Not Firing
[Deprecated] Clearing out the Shadows
A Gronnling Problem
passages.text:
It's gonna be quite a task to build you a fortress if there's gronnlings rampaging around.

I don't think anyone else here can handle taking those big beasts out, so you might need to take care of it yourself.

passages.title: A Gronnling Problem
passages.text: If you can't find gronnlings, you ain't lookin' hard enough.

passages.title: A Gronnling Problem
passages.text: Nasty beasts they got here on Draenor.

passages.title: Obtaining Ogre Offensive Orders
passages.text:
My sister, Mirana, is scouting the upper bluff while I've checked out the lower area. There are two particular ogre mages that do a lot of bossing around in the lower area.

They seem to have some orders or scrolls on them that would help us figure out what's really going on.

Collect that information and meet with my sister on the long stairway up there.

passages.title: Obtaining Ogre Offensive Orders
passages.text: Those orders would be really useful in piecing this whole thing together.

passages.title: Obtaining Ogre Offensive Orders
passages.text: Glad you are here. I almost got killed up there at the top. Oh what are these papers? This is much worse than I imagined!

passages.title: Removing the Paper Trail
passages.text:
This box is filled with writings and diagrams that oddly resemble research into the nullification of magic.

It would be best to ruin these efforts by destroying any research found.

passages.title: Removing the Paper Trail
passages.text: Excellent job thinking on your feet.  The less research these ogres do, the better!

passages.title: The Missing Caravan
passages.text:
I've got a problem and you look like you're just the <race> for the job!

A trade shipment was supposed to arrive yesterday, but it's nowhere to be found. I'm running low on merchandise here and I need somebody to go find out what happened!

If I were to guess, I'd say the saberon are probably involved. Those brutes have been a pain in our side ever since we got here!

Search for the wagon on the road near Sabermaw and hurry! Time is money!

passages.title: The Missing Caravan
passages.text:
<Greezlex lifts his head to look up at you from the ground.>

...No! Don't take me... I... wait...

You aren't a saberon... did Pyxni send you?

passages.title: Kill Goren
Forming the Scroll
passages.text:
We'll need arcane parchment to make the scroll.

The arcane energy everywhere at this nexus froze the ancients in place and settled in their bark.

If we take pieces from the few that haven't been destroyed by the fungal creatures, I can mold them into parchment.

passages.title: Forming the Scroll
passages.text: Yes, these will work great! I can freeze the pulp into a fine parchment.

passages.title: Ravenous Ravens
passages.text:
Do you see that? There is a gigantic raven just past the tree line.

I'm not getting anywhere near that. In fact, I'm not sure any of the men are sufficiently equipped to deal with a threat like that. 

Do you want to handle this one yourself, commander?

Once those ravens are gone we can start sending more troops into the woods. So we will be killing two birds with one stone... or should I say kill five birds with...

<Confused by his own analogy, Baros scratches his head.>

You get the point.

passages.title: Ravenous Ravens
passages.text: Did you kill those ravens?

passages.title: Ravenous Ravens
passages.text: This place is just full of surprises... terrifying surprises.

passages.title: Gathering the Spark
passages.text:
We need arcane energy to complete our scroll. It needs that to coalesce the scroll together.

I have an artifact that can capture energy vortexes in the caldera below, so let's get moving.

passages.title: Gathering the Spark
passages.text: This is why I love magic. It's so... refreshing.

passages.title: Gathering the Spark
passages.text: Perfect! We should have plenty of energy now.

passages.title: <UNUSED>
passages.text:
[PH] Now that we have the armory built we're going to need some skilled hands to run it.
I've heard that the great smith Ared managed to survive Shattraths fall and he should be living nearby in the old quarry. See if you can convince him to work for us.

passages.title: An Audience With The Archmage
passages.text:
I'm pleased to report that your Arcane Sanctum is up and running, commander!

Everything is exactly as the blueprint says... except for this note Baros scrawled on the bottom. "Don't forget to connect the sanctum to the ley line network!"

Commander, I'm a foreman, not a mage. I... have absolutely no idea how to do that.

We've found Archmage Khadgar and some other Kirin Tor not far from here. To the east, near the mountains. Perhaps we should ask them for a hand?

passages.title: An Audience With The Archmage
passages.text:
Ah, so you've built an Arcane Sanctum! Splendid!

Troubles connecting to the ley line network, I take it?

passages.title: An Audience With The Archmage
passages.text:
Your Arcane Sanctum is coming along nicely, commander.

Everything's built to spec... except for one detail Gazlowe scrawled in at the bottom of the blueprint. "Don't forget to connect the sanctum to the ley line network!"

I, uh... I have no idea how to do that.

I'm sorry commander, but magic just isn't my thing. We did spot Archmage Khadgar and some Kirin Tor not far from here. To the east, up near the mountains.

Maybe we should ask them for help?

passages.title: An Audience With The Archmage
passages.text:
Ah, so you've built an Arcane Sanctum! Splendid!

Troubles connecting to the ley line network, I take it?

passages.title: Forming the Scroll
passages.text:
For this plan to work, we'll need infused parchment.

The latent arcane energy at this nexus quickly froze the ancients in place and settled in their bark.

If we rip off strips from the few that haven't been destroyed by the fungal creatures, I can form them into parchment.

passages.title: Forming the Scroll
passages.text: Such clean breaks on each piece! Fantastic.

passages.title: Gathering the Spark
passages.text:
We need to get our hands on arcane energy to complete our scroll. It needs that fiery kick.

I have a device capable of capturing energy in the space below, so let's get moving. The infused creatures shouldn't be an issue for the two of us.

passages.title: Gathering the Spark
passages.text: There's so much untapped power... think of the potential!

passages.title: Gathering the Spark
passages.text: Excellent. This ought to be just what we need.

passages.title: Open the Portal
passages.text: xxxxxx

passages.title: [Deprecated] Doorway to Draenor
passages.text:
I can only maintain a portal from Azeroth for so long.

I'll bring through as many champions as I can, but it will not be easy.

passages.title: Qiana Moonshadow
passages.text:
If we are to win this war we are going to need more than foot soldiers. We need champions.

Qiana Moonshadow's performance in Tanaan and Eventide Landing was quite impressive.

Perhaps you should speak with her about taking on a greater role in the battle against the Iron Horde.

passages.title: Qiana Moonshadow
passages.text:
Luuka is a little shaken up, but he is safe, and that's all that really matters.

Look... commander, I owe you my life. All of us do honestly.

I would be honored to serve as your agent here in Draenor. If you have need of me, you need only say the word.

passages.title: Thunderlord Invasion
passages.text:
Our shadow hunters spotted some of dem Thunderlord gettin' ready to attack us, commanda!

We should be gettin' ready for an invasion!

passages.title: Arakkoa Exodus
passages.text:
I assume you're familiar with the arakkoa, commander? Great, flying birdfolk. Extremely territorial.

Some, however, have withered wings - a disease, maybe. They seem to be outcast from arakkoa society. You find them now and then, squatting in forgotten ruins or peddling trinkets on the roadside.

It seems the Iron Horde has incited the arakkoa by moving into their lands, and the outcasts are fleeing in droves.

We should make contact with these outcasts - they could have valuable information.

passages.title: Arakkoa Exodus
passages.text:
<The arakkoa merchant looks you up and down.>

Well-equipped, aren't we? Azik is betting you are someone of importance to your people.

Come closer, friend. Speak with me for just a moment.

passages.title: The Shadows of Skettis
passages.text:
My people flee our homeland in droves. I sell trinkets to ease the journey.

But I see that you are not interested in trinkets... No, what you seek are answers.

Skettis lies just ahead. Once a great city built by Terokk as a refuge for the unwanted. Now a ruined slum.

An old storyteller lives there - a scrollkeeper named Reshad. Find him and speak these words: "Shadows gather." He will know you are a friend.

Now go. Your presence is bad for business.

passages.title: The Shadows of Skettis
passages.text:
If you're here for some kind of legendary tome of unthinkable power, I'm sorry to disappoint you. I am merely a keeper of history.

I am also very busy at the moment.

passages.title: The Shadows of Skettis
passages.text:
Azik must have seen something in you. I will trust his judgment, for n-

<Reshad is interrupted as a warm gust of wind surges through the hut.>

Oh dear... they've arrived.

passages.title: Hidden in Plain Sight
passages.text:
<Reshad begins hastily stuffing scrolls into his robes.>

I thought I would have more time to prepare! There are powerful relics hidden out there in Skettis - if I leave without them, I may as well have died.

The first is a pair of wingblades being held by an effigy near the front gate. You likely walked right past them on your way in.

Another effigy on the east side of the ruins bears a white mask over its face.

Bring those relics to me, and their secrets shall be yours.

passages.title: Hidden in Plain Sight
passages.text:
Wingblades forged in the name of a sun god to bring freedom and glory to her children.

A mask worn by a great king who would walk among his people in disguise to know their true nature.

passages.title: Hidden in Plain Sight
passages.text: Who would expect to find these treasures draped over straw dolls, left to bake in the sun? Sometimes the best place to hide precious things is in plain sight.

passages.title: Adherents of the Sun God
passages.text:
The arakkoa from Skyreach are all ruled by the Adherents of Rukhmar. They revile those of us who bear the Curse of Sethe, and decree that we must be purged in the name of their sun god.

Soon their gaze will turn to lands beyond Arak.

Challenge their warriors. Buy me time to prepare my escape, and help me set into motion their downfall.

passages.title: Adherents of the Sun God
passages.text:
Skettis will fall today. Neither of us can change that.

We need only to send them a message: we will not die quietly.

passages.title: Adherents of the Sun God
passages.text:
Azik was right to guide you to me. If you were coming to help Skettis, we needed to meet.

And if you were coming to attack us, well, I'd be dead either way, wouldn't I?

<Reshad lets out a cawing laugh and stuffs another scroll into his robes.>

There, that's nearly everything.

passages.title: Orders From On High
passages.text:
The Adherents of Rukhmar are the ruling body atop the spires. Their influence is absolute. Their proclamations taken as the will of Rukhmar Herself.

The herald leading this purge is surely carrying out such orders - likely no more than a list of names and places they plan to erase.

That list would prove invaluable in the days to come. Acquire it for me, and shut that herald up!

passages.title: Orders From On High
passages.text:
<Reshad fastens another scroll to Percy, who squawks meekly in protest.>

Oh, stop whining.

passages.title: Orders From On High
passages.text:
Ah yes, there's my name at the top of the list. And a few Talonpriests from the Shadowglade as well.

They fear the return of Terokk, as they should.

passages.title: The Crone
passages.text:
Do you remember our greeting, adventurer?

"Shadows gather when the raven swallows the day."

It is more than an old verse - it is a call to action. Followers of the old ways are gathering, and I must join them. You are needed, too, I should think

Follow this road down to Crow's Crook. There you will find the home of an old crone. Greet her as you greeted me, and she will guide the way.

You will not see me, but I will be close behind.

passages.title: The Crone
passages.text: You would be wise to turn back, traveler.

passages.title: The Crone
passages.text:
I will point you in the right direction, but I cannot guarantee you'll survive the trip.

Kah-hah haha!

passages.title: The Drudgeboat
passages.text:
[TEMP]<The torn scroll outlines the schedule of several upcoming Frostwolf prisoner arrivals.>

<It appears that they are being shipped in by boat. This could be your method of escape. Khadgar will want to see this.>

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Crushmaul
passages.text:
So you want to fight in the Ring of Trials do you? It's your funeral, bub!

Your first fight is against an exceptionally large and angry ogre named Crushmaul. That's not all though, you'll have to take out his armored boar companion too; Crushmaul never goes into the ring without him!

I hope your affairs are in order, because the last gladiator that fought Crushmaul went home in a body bag...

I'm counting on you! Get your ass inside the arena and speak with my associate Guzrug to start the fight!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Crushmaul
passages.text: What are you waiting for? Get in the ring and start spilling blood!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Crushmaul
passages.text:
Whoa! I couldn't tell if that was Porkchop squealing in there or if you had Crushmaul crying like a little baby!

You've got talent, kid!

Here's your cut of the profit, but why stop there? Together we can make a mountain of gold!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Raketalon
passages.text:
You may have defeated Crushmaul, but the party's over now...you've got another fight!

The Highmaul take gladiatin' seriously; so when they built the Ring of Trials, they searched far and wide for the most brutal creatures they could find!

You're up against a dread raven the ogres are calling Raketalon! I'm telling you, <name>, something about that bird just ain't right...I think it truly enjoys the act of killing!

Raketalon toyed with the last gladiator for hours before eating him.

Try not to die!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Raketalon
passages.text: What are you waiting for? Get in the arena and start spilling blood!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Raketalon
passages.text:
You did it, <name>! Raketalon has actually been defeated!

I'd never have believed it if I hadn't seen it with my very own two eyes. You've got a fire in your belly and dollar signs in your eyes, kid!

Here's your cut of the profit, but don't stop now! You're on a roll!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Hol'yelaa
passages.text:
You won your first two fights, but it's only going to get tougher from here!

Your next fight is against Hol'yelaa, a former rangari who is as crazy as they come.

No, really... Hol'yelaa is bonkers!

Years ago, while on a scouting mission, he single handedly saved his entire rangari unit from a pack of Garn. But something inside of him snapped....

It wasn't long before Hol'yelaa went completely marbles and turned on his own unit!

Alright, the pep talk is over! Get in there and kick some ass!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Hol'yelaa
passages.text: What are you doing standing around? Get in the arena and spill some blood!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Hol'yelaa
passages.text:
Watching you fight in the arena is like witnessing an artist create a masterpiece!

Well, a masterpiece of blood and shattered bones... but hey, everyone's got to be good at something right?

Here's your cut of the profit! That fight was so good I actually thought about giving you a bonus!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Captain Boomspark
passages.text:
You've been making a name for yourself in the arena, <name>!

Don't get too excited though...fame has its consequences! You've been challenged by an up-and-coming gladiator who is looking to make a name for himself, sound familiar?

Your next fight is against Captain Boomspark, a mercenary who came here to fight for the Iron Horde.

The Iron Horde ain't exactly throwing piles of gold around, so now he's here!

He's got a shredder, so watch out for the blades... and the fire too... especially the fire!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Captain Boomspark
passages.text: What are you doing standing around? Get in the arena and spill some blood!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Captain Boomspark
passages.text:
I ain't ever seen anybody dismantle a shredder quite like that before!

You've made me a lot of money, <name>! Only the best gladiators survive this long in the arena; and yet, even with that in mind, there's still something different about you...

It's your eyes...they look as if they've stared death in the face a thousand times and never even blinked.

Take your cut of the profit and rest up, the biggest fight is still ahead!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Roakk the Zealot
passages.text:
The final match is at hand, <name>! You've decimated all of the best challengers! There's nowhere to go from here but the very top...the reigning champion of the Ring of Trials!

The current champ is an arakkoa named Roakk the Zealot. Roakk is a lunatic! He says he's on some divine crusade for the sun or something.

Crazy or not, he's one of the most dangerous fighters I've ever seen and has even fought in the Highmaul Coliseum!

I'm not going to lie, you're probably going to die in there...good luck!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Roakk the Zealot
passages.text:
What are you doing standing around? Don't you hear the crowd screaming?

There's a championship waiting on you!

passages.title: Ring of Trials: Roakk the Zealot
passages.text:
Long live the champ! I knew you could do it!

Could you hear the roar of the crowd in there? It shook the arena like thunder!

This is only the beginning! The Highmaul Coliseum awaits, and as the champion of the Ring of Trials you'll be expected to make an appearance!

passages.title: Gather Lumber
Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
**Eyes Only -- Commander <name>**

With the fall of the rangari base at Telaar, Vindicator Yrel, recommended we establish a new foothold in Nagrand.

I've taken the liberty of dispatching some of our men and supplies. Rangari D'kaan's already reporting that a new outpost is nearly complete. He has indicated that they are ready to receive you.

A gryphon is waiting to catch you up with the latest caravan shipment whenever you're ready, <sir/ma'am>.

-- Bodrick Grey, SI:7

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
They came at us... from... nowhere.

<The lieutenant nearly passes out.>

passages.title: The Might of the Warsong
passages.text:
<The officer is in a great deal of pain. It's clear that he's not long for this world.>

The Warsong. Surprise attack.

Headed... west.

<He takes a moment, before continuing.>

They took the... blueprints....

<These are his last words.>

passages.title: The Might of the Warsong
passages.text:
Commander <name>. It's good to see you. We have much to discuss.

The situation in Nagrand is rapidly deteriorating. We've lost Telaar.

To make matters worse, Grommash has named Garrosh Hellscream the new warlord of the Warsong clan.

passages.title: The Critical Path
passages.text:
The auburn forests of Talador sit at a critical crossroads of this continent, commander. The Iron Horde's fleet is already en route from Gorgrond to Shattrath on the west coast.

Talador will fall if we don't reinforce them. I took the liberty of dispatching Foreman Eksos, who has already begun construction on an outpost for your forces not far from the Iron Horde landing point. He awaits your orders sir.

passages.title: The Critical Path
passages.text: I won't waste any of your time, sir. Let us discuss strategy.

passages.title: Up and Running
passages.text:
The Warsong struck us hard. We lost Telaar, but we have a rare opportunity to strike at the heart of the Warsong.

We need your wisdom and leadership to pull it off, <name>.

First though, we're going to get our survivors out of Telaar. My rangari are ready to strike. We just need to get you to them.

Thaelin has a copter that can get you to them. Unfortunately, his hands are full just trying to keep the infernal thing running.

Help him get it up and running?

passages.title: Up and Running
passages.text: <name>, I can't tell you how great it is to see you.

passages.title: Up and Running
passages.text:
For me? Really you shouldn't have.

Okay, this should do it.

I hope.

passages.title: It's a Matter of Strategy
passages.text:
Da Iron Horde have proved themselves worthy foes.

They managed to get their fleet movin' to Talador from Gorgrond without my spies seein' a thing. Talador be a crossroads for the whole continent. We can't let them have it.

Don't worry boss, we got a plan. Foreman Grobash be settin' up an outpost for our forces as we speak. They be ready for you when you arrive, commander.

passages.title: It's a Matter of Strategy
passages.text: Your will be done. I require your advisement, commander.

passages.title: Operation: Surprise Party
passages.text:
There weren't many survivors of the Warsong attack. The few remaining rangari have gone up to one of the bluffs overlooking Telaar.

The rangari are waiting for you. They're planning a surprise counter-attack.

My copter's taken a beating. The auto-pilot's set to take you up there. I think she's got one last trip in her.

Maybe.

passages.title: Operation: Surprise Party
passages.text:
We've been expecting you, commander.

The situation is grim, but doable with your help.

passages.title: One Step Ahead
passages.text:
Boss, Durotan set off with Draka and Gazlowe to track da Iron Horde's movements along da coast.

Dey waitin' for ya on the cliffs to da northwest.

passages.title: One Step Ahead
passages.text: Ah, <name>. I recognized your scent, friend. We have been waiting for your arrival to begin our task.

passages.title: One Step Ahead
passages.text:
Commander, Vindicator Maraad took Yrel and Thaelin Darkanvil just up to the road from here to track the Iron Horde's forces in the forest.

They are already at work formulating a strategy to stop their operations. They await your arrival on the cliffs to the northwest.

passages.title: As the Smoke Rises
passages.text:
Aruuna burns.

The arakkoa swooped down from their spires and are turning everything to ash. Draenei, talbuk, even orc; they care not for allegiances. They merely want to watch the world burn.

I barely escaped with my life, but my best friend, Barum, stayed behind to find his daughter. The others all say you are a great champion. Please, I beg of you, go to Aruuna and find them.

passages.title: As the Smoke Rises
passages.text: Kalaam sent you? By the Light, I knew I could count on him!

passages.title: Just the Beginning
passages.text:
It... is over.

We should return to your outpost and discuss our next course of action. There are innocent people in danger across all of Talador that need our help.

I will have Khadgar open a portal for us. Let us save our words for now.

passages.title: Delegating on Draenor
passages.text:
There is more work to do on Draenor than we can possibly handle by ourselves. We need to start delegating.

A group of night elves need a champion at Starfall Outpost.

Qiana is a perfect fit for this mission.

passages.title: Delegating on Draenor
passages.text: You can use the Command Table to assign missions to your followers.

passages.title: Delegating on Draenor
passages.text: This is a good start, but we will need more champions to deal with the trials that lay ahead.

passages.title: [Deprecated] Profession Quest
passages.text:
We have cleared out quite a bit of land, commander.

We should continue to fortify the garrison.

Speak with Baros again, he will help you construct your choice of profession buildings.

passages.title: [Deprecated] Invasion Quest
passages.text: xxxxx

passages.title: The Lady of Light
passages.text:
<name>, yes? You are the one in charge here? I am Knight-Lord Dranarus, at your service.

Lady Liadrin has responded to a suspected demon presence near Auchindoun, southwest of here. She has asked specifically for your assistance in ensuring Auchindoun does not fall into Gul'dan's hands.

If you could set forth at your nearest convenience, I am sure the Lady would be most grateful.

passages.title: The Lady of Light
passages.text: We'll have to catch up later. We have bigger problems!

passages.title: A Rediscovered Legend
passages.text:
If your troops are going to learn to fight people you better get people to fight! And they better be good.

Ever hear of Kash'drakor?

He's a big famous Frostwolf orc warrior type that tried to kill us Skulls. He would have won too, if the ogres hadn't snatched him.

To the north is the Stonemaul Arena where they took him and a bunch of other big bad mean fighter gladiators.

If you can find a way to free them, they could be the best trainers you could hope for.

passages.title: A Rediscovered Legend
passages.text:
The Laughing Skull sent you? If they were any other clan I would find that ironic.

I am Kash'drakor, hero of the Frostwolf clan, and champion of the slave pits of Stonemaul.

And yet, despite all these titles, I need your help.

passages.title: Slave Hunters
passages.text:
Anytime a gladiator escapes Stonemaul, they send their hardened slave hunters after us.

I consider myself a capable warrior, years of surviving in an arena have taught me that.

But these slave hunters keep pendants magically tethered to the slaves. With these pendants they can track us down anywhere we go, and kill us in our sleep or when our guard is down.

I have no right to ask this, but can you enter Stonemaul and retrieve these pendants?

passages.title: Slave Hunters
passages.text: Have you the pendants?

passages.title: Slave Hunters
passages.text:
You have shown more honor in this one act than I have seen in many years.

When this is over, I will swear my axe to your forces and pass my knowledge on to your troops.

passages.title: Nazgrel
passages.text:
Escaping Stonemaul was the easy part. The ogre filth that rule the pits still have my son.

For a while they used him as leverage to ensure I would fight in their arenas. But now that I have escaped they will try to train him to replace me.

Please, rescue my son. If they see me they will kill him instantly.

passages.title: Nazgrel
passages.text: This deed will never be forgotten as long as I or my son live. You have my gratitude, hero, and my loyalty.

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text:
Oh, praise the Light, you're here! Exarch Maladaar asked for me to find you.

We need your help. Auchindoun is under attack by demons!

Go to the Burning Front to the southwest as soon as possible! You're one of the few people he trusts to help lead the defense.

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text: I will not allow a single demon to step foot inside Auchindoun. You will help me ensure that does not happen.

passages.title: Krav'ogra
passages.text:
Stonemaul has chieftain, and it has slavemaster. Today, we kill both.

First, Slavemaster Ok'mok. Me fight in arenas since me your size. Me know cruelty. Slavemaster Ok'mok is cruelty.

Want to be true gladiator? Go to Stonemaul Arena, bang challenge gong in center of arena, and face beasts of slavemaster.

Maybe you make Ok'mok so mad he jump down himself to kill you. If he do, kill him instead.

passages.title: Krav'ogra
passages.text: Me watch you from afar. Me like your fighting skills, show much promise.

passages.title: A Rediscovered Legend
passages.text:
This Sparring Arena is a good start, but we will need trainers to help mold your forces into worthy fighters.

There has been a reported spotting of a draenei to the west who matches the description of Akaani.

This is interesting, as we all believed her dead. She was one of the finest warriors the draenei have ever fielded and a master of nearly any weapon forged or found.

Commander, you could not ask for a more skilled trainer. I advise seeking her out, if it is really her...

passages.title: A Rediscovered Legend
passages.text:
You do not have the look of a Stonemaul bounty hunter.

We escaped the clutches of their vile arena but at a heavy cost. We were forced to leave too many allies behind and too many ogres breathing.

We could use a fresh face, one that is unknown to the ogres.

passages.title: Come Together
passages.text:
Your work is done here, <name>. I will stay here for now and help clean up any remaining demons.

You should return to your outpost and let Dranarus know of our success. He can relay that information to Azeroth.

passages.title: Come Together
passages.text: Lady Liadrin was indeed wise in choosing you. I will let Vol'jin know of your victory immediately.

passages.title: Come Together
passages.text:
Gul'dan and his cronies would do well to remember this day. We Auchenai are not to be trifled with.

You should inform Vindicator Icia in your outpost of our success. She can reach out to the scattered refugees and their families.

passages.title: Come Together
passages.text:
I will gather any remaining survivors so we can rebuild what we have lost.

Thank you.

passages.title: Vignette: Jehil the Climber
passages.text:
Goren are dangerous, especially in large numbers, and especially when we have a blind, under powered shaman with us.

Fortunately, they have very short lifespans. Unfortunately, they multiply fast and grow faster.

If we are going to do this we need to find the brood mother. Slaying her and her eggs should slow down the onslaught of goren. Check the burrows near the Forge Gates and I will to keep them off of Drek'Thar's scent.

passages.title: Every Bit Counts
passages.text:
The Jorune Mine, west of here, needs your help!

My good friend Ageilaa sent me to look for help. Exarch Maladaar sent over what vindicators he could spare, but it isn't enough!

Will you go to the mine and help us? We need the crystals from the mine to create more defenses like the crystals you see on the Burning Front.

passages.title: Every Bit Counts
passages.text: Aeun sent you? Help has arrived!

passages.title: Every Bit Counts
passages.text:
Manduil Skycaller was sent on a sensitive mission to Jorune Mine, but he hasn't returned for hours.

I suspect he requires assistance. I will let him brief you on the situation when you find him, but he is likely deep within the mine.

You should report to Ageilaa, a local draenei miner who has agreed to cooperate with us in exchange for helping her regain control of the mine.

passages.title: Every Bit Counts
passages.text: Aeun sent you? Help has arrived!

passages.title: Due Cause to Celebrate
passages.text:
Shall we return to your outpost? It would be a much better - and safer - place to celebrate.

I'll teleport us there.

passages.title: Due Cause to Celebrate
passages.text:
We can finally connect your tower to the ley line network with this crystal.

I also edited your blueprint so you can actually read the thing. Should make building another one much easier.

passages.title: Due Cause to Celebrate
passages.text:
This isn't exactly my idea of the best place to talk.

Shall we return to your outpost? It will be a much better place to celebrate.

I'll teleport us there.

passages.title: Due Cause to Celebrate
passages.text:
With this crystal, we can connect your tower to the ley line network at last!

I also made some modifications to your blueprint that should make it much easier to build another tower in your garrison.

passages.title: Operation: Just Arrowhead
passages.text:
It goes without saying that we'll help you kill any of the Warsong out in the open down there.

You just start the fight, and we'll end it with extreme prejudice.

passages.title: Operation: Just Arrowhead
passages.text:
That bit of justice is sure to have lifted the spirits of my rangari.

Losing Telaar and many of our friends has taken a heavy toll.

Thank you, commander.

passages.title: The Others
passages.text:
There are yet a few survivors. I saw them pile onto Arbiter Khan during the fighting.

More importantly, I can hear little Isel's sobs. She's nearby. I hope her mother is still alive.

Your dwarf friend, Hansel, came in to try to rescue us. He thought he could take the Warsong on his own. I'm afraid I don't know what happened to him.

passages.title: The Others
passages.text:
Khan! No!... he just received his promotion. His whole life ahead of him and now, nothing.

Thank you for getting the others out. Light be... nevermind.

passages.title: ... and My Hammer
passages.text:
When they captured me, the Warsong took my hammer. Will you help me to recover it?

I ask only because it's a holy relic. It should be taken from these orc dogs for no other reason than to return it to Auchindoun.

Perhaps then, a worthy vindicator of the Light will take it up to smite the enemies of the draenei.

passages.title: ... and My Hammer
passages.text: I'm having trouble seeing. I may not have long.

passages.title: ... and My Hammer
passages.text: Thank you for this kindness, <name>. Perhaps I can still salvage some scrap of honor.

passages.title: Operation: Just Arrowhead
passages.text:
It goes without saying that the Warsong in Telaar need to be dealt with. Rangari Ogir and his forces on the overlook will help you kill any of the orcs that are out in the open.

You just start the fight, and they'll end it with extreme prejudice.

passages.title: Operation: Just Arrowhead
passages.text:
That bit of justice is sure to have lifted the spirits of my rangari.

Losing Telaar and many of our friends has taken a heavy toll.

Thank you, commander.

passages.title: Seek Out the Seer
passages.text:
We've been watching you, <name>.

Seer Malune, keeper of memories, has requested an audience with you, adventurer.

She has long foretold the coming of a great hero to destroy the lurking shadow. We believe you are that hero.

Come to Duskfall Island, not far southeast of here, and fulfill your destiny.

passages.title: Seek Out the Seer
passages.text: I am Seer Malune, the great keeper of memories. It is an honor to finally meet you.

passages.title: Durotan Been Askin' For Ya
passages.text: Durotan been askin' for ya, mon.

passages.title: Durotan Been Askin' For Ya
passages.text: You did well against a coordinated Thunderlord attack, <name>.

passages.title: Blood Oath of Na'Shra
passages.text:
You have done me a great service. This blade is as much yours as it is mine.

I offer you this blood oath: I shall serve your cause and lend my knowledge of blades and mining to your forces.

Will you accept it?

passages.title: Blood Oath of Na'Shra
passages.text:
You have done me a great service. This blade is as much yours as it is mine.

I offer you this blood oath: I shall serve your cause and lend my knowledge of blades and mining to your forces.

Will you accept it?

passages.title: Blood Oath of Lokra
passages.text:
You have done me a great service. This blade is as much yours as it is mine.

I offer you this blood oath: I shall serve your cause and lend my knowledge of blades and mining to your forces.

Will you accept it?

passages.title: Blood Oath of Lokra
passages.text:
Commander <name>, Your mastery over the battlefield is astounding. If my people are to survive the coming conflict we will need more of our own people skilled in such warfare.

If you will have me, I would like to join your forces for a time. I wish to learn from you so that I might teach others in my clan.

Will you accept my axe?

passages.title: Thunderlord Invasion!
passages.text:
Sir! Scouts have spotted Thunderlords approaching from the east.

The men are armed and ready. We'll mount defensive positions as soon as you take the field.

passages.title: We Be Needin' Supplies
passages.text:
Commander, our forces are not prepared for frost fightin'. I took da liberty and sent some of our shadow hunters north to establish a supply base. 

Ya might want to be headin' up dere and see what they be up to. Look for a hollow between the Crackling Plains and the Savage Crag.

passages.title: We Be Needin' Supplies
passages.text: Eh dere, boss-mon! Watch ya step. Da ground be cracklin' and breakin' everywhere.

passages.title: Masters of Shadow
passages.text:
The bad orcs tried to catch me, but I snuck away. I'm good at hiding.

All of the bad orcs are bad, but I've remembered the names of the meanest ones, just in case anybody came to save me.

<Luuka takes a deep breath.>

Ungra, Gurran, and... umm... oh! Ankova.

Will you protect me from them?

passages.title: Masters of Shadow
passages.text: How goes your mission?

passages.title: Masters of Shadow
passages.text:
Well done.

Be ready to move. We may have had the element of surprise within this cave, but our advantage is fleeting.

passages.title: Nullin' Void
passages.text:
If I'm reading their spells correctly, it seems that these Shadowmoon orcs are opening portals to bring prisoners here to the slave camps. Brilliant magic, really.

Unfortunately, it is easily nullified.

<Khadgar places a small rune in your hand.>

This rune will deal with their void magic. Activate it near their portals, and they will instantly be nullified.

passages.title: Yrel
passages.text:
Forgive me if I'm a bit flustered - I've never killed anyone before.

My name is Yrel, and I am a student of Karabor.

You say you have an ARMY with you? The Light must truly be watching over me today.

I will follow you, then. Lead the way, <name>.

passages.title: Yrel
passages.text:
Up there - that is Keli'dan the Breaker. No doubt he's been alerted to our presence, and he's attempting to tell his warlord about our little jailbreak.

We have to take him out, <name>.

passages.title: Keli'dan the Breaker
passages.text:
One of Ner'zhul's lieutenants remains, up ahead. The exit to the cave isn't much farther past him.

I will go back and tell Khadgar that the cave is clear. We will rendezvous once you've taken care of Keli'dan!

passages.title: Keli'dan the Breaker
passages.text:
Fine job in the cave, but this is no time to rest.

We have momentum. We must stay in motion.

passages.title: Clear!
passages.text:
You gotta help me fix this robot. I'm friggin' hungry!

I built the Pleasure-Bot 8000 to locate Draenor truffles, and what does it do? It swims to this stupid island and shorts its power fluctuator.

I got it hooked up to these batteries, but it ain't enough juice to jump it.

Be a doll and get me the zapper sacs from the electric eels in the lake, would ya? They oughta be enough.

passages.title: Clear!
passages.text: You got the stuff, buddy?

passages.title: Clear!
passages.text:
Yeah, that's the stuff! You're a good business partner, considering you're a <class> and all.

Now let's just mash these into this port...

passages.title: A Charming Deception
passages.text:
Reshad is more than he appears; a mottled old crow with his beak in a book, certainly, but we need him.

Shadows gather beneath the lonely spire, in Veil Terokk. Reshad must make it there safely.

Along the path you'll find charms primed with illusion spells. You need only touch them to take on Reshad's image.

Adherent assassins are on the prowl for an old outcast with scrolls on his back. They will fall upon you.

Oh, but won't they be surprised when the illusion fades?! Kee-hee-hee!

passages.title: A Charming Deception
passages.text: How very noble of you to act as bait on my behalf. I will not forget this.

passages.title: [PH] Elixir
passages.text:
The final ingredient is a rare flower that grows only in the heart of the Nightmarsh.

This flower feeds only on starlight, and dies when it falls under shadow.

If you can find such a flower, bring it to me. Only its essence will help me gain the clarity I need.

passages.title: Looking For Help
passages.text: We have an accessible fishing spot here, but no bait seems to work! We need to find a local fisherman with some knowledge of the area to help us out. Head southeast and see if you can find anyone on the shoreline.

passages.title: Looking For Help
passages.text: You think I am going to help you?

passages.title: Looking For Help
passages.text: Time to see what you can do.

passages.title: Clear!
passages.text:
Oh, the gnomanity!

The Pleasure-Bot 8000 broke before it could bring me a single Draenor truffle. It swam here and shorted its power fluctuator.

AGAIN!

I have power going to it, but it isn't enough to override the fluctuator.

Could you get me the sacs from the electric eels in the lake? I think that would be just the ticket!

passages.title: Clear!
passages.text: Do you have the eel sacs?

passages.title: Clear!
passages.text:
Those look perfect! By all that is mechanical, this had better work.

Now let's just insert these here...

passages.title: The Den of Skog
passages.text:
So this gronn infestation ain't gonna solve itself. You're gonna have to show them who's boss, Horde style!

With this many gronnlings around there is bound to be a full grown, big mama of a gronn. Find him... it... her... or whatever, and take it out, and the rest of those gronnlings might lose interest in our little operation here.

passages.title: The Den of Skog
passages.text: You find that big gal... or guy... or gronn? Really, I ain't sure what to call them.

passages.title: The Den of Skog
passages.text: Little known fact, old gronn grottos make for great farming soil.

passages.title: Logistical Nightmare
passages.text:
Commander, I am afraid I have... troubling... news.

These saberon followed our encampment from Gorgrond, and have been stealing our supplies, ransacking our ledgers, and slaughtering our peons!

I hate to ask of your time to deal with the matter, but all of our men are stationed guarding the camp from any further raids. We desperately need those supplies so we may enact your will!

passages.title: Logistical Nightmare
passages.text: Commander! Have you had time to locate our supplies and ledgers?

passages.title: Logistical Nightmare
passages.text:
I never doubted you for a moment. You are truly a commander of the people.

Lok'tar ogar!

passages.title: Why Is The Brew Gone?
passages.text:
Commander, we have a bit of a... uh... problem.

This group o' saberon followed us from Gorgrond, and they've been stealin' our footmen's swords an' slaughtering our peasants!

I hate to ask fer your time, but all of yer men are guardin' the camp from any further raids. Plus...

<Quartermaster O'Riley lowers her voice to a whisper.>

They took our beer!

passages.title: Why Is The Brew Gone?
passages.text: Commander! Have ye had a moment to deal with the saberon?

passages.title: Why Is The Brew Gone?
passages.text:
Oh thank goodness, I knew ye would come through!

At your service, as always.

passages.title: Mission Probable
passages.text:
Despite his recent captures, Olin Umberhide seems to be a tauren of some skill in combat. He certainly has learned how to get an enemy's attention.

I have a mission available that might prove ideal for his skill sets.

When you are ready, simply issue the order via the command table in front of me and we will dispatch him immediately.

passages.title: Mission Probable
passages.text: Commander, I have a mission that might suite your new follower quite well.

passages.title: Mission Probable
passages.text: As additional missions come to my attention I will make them available here.

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text:
I was taken captive by the Iron Horde when they raided our caravan en route to Auchindoun.

I escaped, but these spirits won't let me through to join my fellow Sunsworn until someone defeats them in combat!

Please, will you help me defeat them?

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text: I appreciate all of your help, hero.

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. I am truly in your debt.

When I fulfill my duties to Lady Liadrin I will come find you.

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text:
Auchindoun is under attack, stranger, and I intend to help defend it.

The only problem is the only armor I could find was my grandfather's old set, and it isn't nearly enough to defeat the spirits blocking the path toward Auchindoun.

Would you defeat them and let me through the gate with you? I will find a way to repay you!

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text: I will defend Auchindoun with my life. We cannot lose anymore in this war!

passages.title: Gatekeepers of Auchindoun
passages.text: You have my eternal gratitude, hero. I will find a way to repay you someday.

passages.title: Defenstrations
passages.text:
No sooner does power rush to the crystal outside than you hear distant war cries and shouts of alarm. Elodor is being attacked!

If you want your laborers to come home in one piece, you'd best help with the defense of the town. Defeat the invasion and then return to the control console to reset the defenses.

passages.title: Defenstrations
passages.text: The sounds of attack still reverberate from outside, which is alarming, given that the console seems awash with angrily blinking warning indicators.

passages.title: Defenstrations
passages.text:
You saved the town! The controls shut down as you approach, but many of the indicators are still blinking frantically. Something seems wrong.

Hataaru yells out to get your attention outside...

passages.title: The Exarch Council
passages.text:
Good work at the gates! The Shadowmoon orcs have been seeking prisoners for some reason. Their aggression helps our cause.

Come with me. I would like to introduce you to the Exarch Council, "The Hand of the Prophet." I have been trying to convince the Exarchs to support our cause and go on the offensive against the Iron Horde, but they are - as always - too cautious and slow to act.

Come with me, I will introduce you to Exarch Othaar up the hill. Perhaps meeting an Alliance hero can sway the council.

passages.title: The Exarch Council
passages.text:
<Exarch Othaar is a towering, intimidating figure. His eyes bore into you, determining if you are friend or foe.>

So, you are <name>, esteemed <class> of this "Alliance" that has appeared on our shores. On behalf of the Exarch Council, I welcome you to Elodor.

passages.title: Naielle, The Rangari
passages.text:
I am calling the Exarch Council to order to hear your petition. None of us doubt that this "Iron Horde" is a threat, but few can agree on what we should do about it. It is up to you and Vindicator Maraad to gather the Exarchs together.

Exarch Naielle is the leader of the Rangari, the "Eyes of the Prophet." They are our scouts who silently stalk the farthest corners of Draenor. Seek her out in the Rangari Enclave northwest of here.

passages.title: Naielle, The Rangari
passages.text:
<name>! You have only just arrived but already your name is the talk of Elodor.

I will gladly support your cause for the Exarch Council - it has always been my opinion that the draenei need to get out and be proactive in our world instead of hiding behind our walls.

But first, I need your help with something...

passages.title: Hataaru, the Artificer
passages.text:
I will also need you to call upon Exarch Hataaru. I understand you were helping him with our defenses at the gate.

Hataaru is our Chief Artificer - he understands our technology better than any other and has been working tirelessly to recreate the glory of the civilization we left behind.

He has moved to his workstation outside of the Elodor Dig, our crystal mines located just to the Southeast. Look for him at the mine entrance.

passages.title: Hataaru, the Artificer
passages.text:
Ah, <name>! I suspected I would see you again soon.

I am willing to speak on your behalf at the Exarch Council, but an emergency situation has come up...

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
Boss-mon, good to see ya.

Durotan recommended dat we be gettin' a foothold in Nagrand, so I taken the liberty of dispatchin' some of da boys.

Thrall's already reportin' that the outside be nearly complete. He been askin' me to let ya know they be ready for ya.

A windrider be waitin' to catch ya up with the latest caravan shipment whenever you be ready, <sir/ma'am>.

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
They came at us... from... nowhere.

<The stoneguard nearly passes out.>

passages.title: The Might of the Warsong
passages.text:
<The officer is in a great deal of pain. It's clear that he's not long for this world.>

The Warsong. Surprise attack.

Headed into... the Burning Blade....

<He takes a moment, before continuing.>

They took the... blueprints....

<These are his last words.>

passages.title: The Might of the Warsong
passages.text:
Commander <name>. It's good to see you. We have much to discuss.

The situation in Nagrand is rapidly deteriorating. The Warsong clan is on the move.

To make matters worse, Grommash has named Garrosh their new warlord.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text:
I am a humble pilgrim, I swear. Please don't hurt me!

My sister and I were traveling to Auchindoun to pay our respects to my grandmother when we hit an overturned rock and lost control of our caravan. I managed to survive, but my sister...

<Nadur cries.>

Please, you have to help me. I'm desperate. If you could bring me some prowler blood, snapdragon flowers, and a riverhopper eye, I can fashion a potion to bring her back. I just know it....

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: Tuliaa isn't just my sister. She's my best friend.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: Thank you, stranger.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text:
My sister and I were traveling to Auchindoun to pay our respects to my grandmother when we hit an overturned rock and lost control of our caravan. I managed to survive, but my sister...

<Nadur cries.>

Please, I need your help. If you could bring me some prowler blood, snapdragon flowers, and a riverhopper eye, I can fashion a potion to bring her back... I just know I can...

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: I don't know what I would do without Tuliaa... she's not just my sister. She's my best friend.

passages.title: A Pilgrimage Gone Awry
passages.text: Thank you, a thousand times thank you.

passages.title: Echo Hunters
passages.text:
I am no sorcerer, but I've picked up a few spells in my time - enough for me to pass unseen by the naked eye.

Unfortunately, the vampire bats in these woods don't use their eyes. They will hear my shuffling robes and Percy's incessant clucking a mile away.

Clear them away from the path, would you?

passages.title: Echo Hunters
passages.text: Blasted things. Nothing more than flying rats if you ask me!

passages.title: Prune the Podlings
passages.text:
The blood soaked body of Ryan is slumped up against the cave wall. Tiny teeth marks cover his body.

The podlings clearly are a threat to you and your garrison.

It's time to do a little pruning.

passages.title: More Lazy Peons
passages.text:
We have a rare opportunity to strike at the heart of the Warsong. But, we need your wisdom and leadership.

The most important decision will be your choice between building a corral or a tankworks. This choice will setup our approach to the fight against the Warsong.

Thazz'ril will head up our building efforts. Will you give him a hand?

It looks like he's having trouble motivating his peons to work.

passages.title: More Lazy Peons
passages.text: If there's one thing the Horde never seems to be short on, it's lazy peons.

passages.title: More Lazy Peons
passages.text: I knew it was a mistake to bring these guys with me from the Valley of Trials.

passages.title: A Lesson in Mineralogy
passages.text:
<Gazmolf gestures at the large machine nearby.>

I built this machine to break down elementium minerals into base elements. You see, it's not just what's buried within the ground that can be valuable; but also the ground itself!

Take, for example, the earth elementals below us; inside every earth elemental is an earthen core, dense in precious metal!.

Those elementals are going to make us rich! Collect several earthen cores, place them in the Gold-O-Matic 9000, and I'll give you a cut!

passages.title: A Lesson in Mineralogy
passages.text: <The Gold-O-Matic 9000 buzzes and whirrs with the sounds of heavy machinery.>

passages.title: A Lesson in Mineralogy
passages.text:
<The Gold-O-Matic 9000 crunches and grinds through the elemental remains.>

chakk-chackk-chak-chak, chak-a-chak-akk-chk-chk-chk.

passages.title: Gazmolf Futzwangler and the Highmaul Crusade
passages.text:
I'm here in Nagrand recruiting for the Steamwheedle Preservation Society. We're the archaeological branch of the Steamwheedle Cartel.

We're here to collect all of the artifacts, relics, antiquities and oddities that Nagrand has to offer! Currently, we're hiring surveyors, excavators, adventurers... you name it!

If you're interested in getting your hands dirty, talk to Gazmolf Futzwangler over at Stonecrag Gorge. He's the goblin in charge of this expedition!

passages.title: Gazmolf Futzwangler and the Highmaul Crusade
passages.text:
It's good to see that there's still an interest out there in real archaeology!

There's a lot of misconceptions out there about how archaeology is really done, but have no fear! The great and famous Gazmolf Futzwangler is here to educate you.

passages.title: Good Help is Hard to Find
passages.text:
The excavation team is on strike!

Foreman Thazwix and his cronies think they can squeeze the Steamwheedle Preservation Society for some extra dough by refusing to work.

What I need is a scab, a strikebreaker; someone to put some pressure on them by doing the job they refuse to do!

Go down into the gorge, dig up some antiquities for me, and I'll pay you what I would have payed those lazy numbskulls!

passages.title: Good Help is Hard to Find
passages.text: Do you have the Nagrand Antiquities?

passages.title: Good Help is Hard to Find
passages.text:
Great work, <name>!

That bunch of good-for-nothing's came crying when they found out someone else was making their money! I don't think Thazwix, or his cronies, will be much trouble from here on out.

As promised, here's the pay I owe you for a job well done!

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
It's nice to see someone else taking a vested interest in the arcane arts, you know. It's all too rare these days if you ask me!

Unfortunately, I must meet Cordana to handle an important matter, but we're in luck! One of my good friends in the Kirin Tor has agreed to help you connect your arcane sanctum to the ley line network.

He's waiting at my tower. Let's leave immediately and introduce you to one another.

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text: You are <name>, I presume?

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
I am Magister Krelas. Pyromaniac.

Pleasure.

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
It's nice to see someone else taking a vested interest in the arcane arts, you know. It's all too rare these days if you ask me.

Unfortunately, I must meet Cordana to handle an important matter, but we're in luck! One of my good friends in the Kirin Tor has agreed to help you connect your arcane sanctum to the ley line network.

She's waiting at my tower. Let's leave immediately and introduce you to one another.

passages.title: Making Acquaintances
passages.text:
Nice to meet you.

I am Magister Serena. Frost mage extraordinaire!

passages.title: Altar Altercation
They Call Him Lantresor of the Blade
passages.text:
The garrison blueprints were taken to the Burning Blade village when the Warsong sacked your caravan. I can't construct this building without those plans.

There's been talk of a young blademaster who's been exiled from the clan for many years. They call him Lantresor of the Blade.

Our scouts recently saw him return to Hallvalor to challenge the blademaster leadership. Instead, they clapped him in chains.

Maybe he's still alive. Maybe he'll help you recover the blueprints?

passages.title: They Call Him Lantresor of the Blade
passages.text:
Who are you?

Don't you know death by sight, <class>?

passages.title: Fruitful Ventures
passages.text:
Oh no! They must be vegetarians.

What these elekk need is fruit and lots of it. There are cherries all over the place around here under the trees.

You wouldn't mind grabbing me some, would ya?

passages.title: Fruitful Ventures
passages.text:
I heard the worst rumor about how you have to obtain those things.

Something about talbuk first eating them and then 'processing' them, and then... well, I don't want to talk about it.

passages.title: Fruitful Ventures
passages.text: You got them all? I just know this is going to work.

passages.title: Lost Lumberjacks
passages.text:
Shelly and her crew haven't returned from Gloomshade Grove.

It's been days... I hope everything is okay.

passages.title: Lost Lumberjacks
passages.text: This is one of the pack mules Shelly and her crew took to Gloomshade Grove.

passages.title: What We Need
passages.text:
I heard you guys hijacked and wrecked a ship on your way out of Tanaan.

It's like my daddy always said: One man's wreck is another goblin's workshop.

You should head down to the coast west of the garrison and see if you can't find any materials we might salvage. Oh, and uh... should probably watch yourself. I hear there are ogre raiders in the area.

passages.title: What We Need
passages.text: How's the salvage operation comin'?

passages.title: What We Need
passages.text: Hey... now that is some nice salvage. Say what you will about the Iron Horde, but they got some serious raw materials to work with.

passages.title: The Ogron Live?
passages.text:
Commander, our Frostwolf allies reportin' dat the Bladespire ogres have an outpost to our west led by an ogron.

I heard tales of da ogron but never seen one. Dey be brutes, creatures from a time that was best left forgotten. Dey say most were slain during the forming of the original horde. What dey lack in wisdom they make up for in violence, force, and greed.

I counsel dispatchin' dis creature as soon as possible.

passages.title: The Ogron Live?
passages.text: Where the ogron goes, death and pain are sure to follow.

passages.title: The Ogron Live?
passages.text: Well done, boss-mon. The Bladespire ogres been pullin' back their raiding parties. But ya can bet dey be comin' back, and in larger numbers. The threat from their citadel must be dealt with soon.

passages.title: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
Hallvalor is the ancestral home of the Burning Blade clan. Since they're such fast friends, the Warsong have allowed the blademasters to remain in Nagrand.

We are fierce, but we won't win if the Burning Blade attack us. It would be wise to strike first.

passages.title: The Friend of My Enemy
passages.text:
A great victory over the Burning Blade!

This new Warlord Azuka Bladefury sounds formidable. We will have to keep an eye on her and her blademasters.

passages.title: Ishaal's Orb
passages.text:
The Adherents came for me, but I was already hiding. I watched from the shadows as they ransacked my hut.

Then I watched the Shattered Hand orcs arrive and butcher them like dinner fowl. Seems everyone is after us these days.

One of those orc thugs made off with my scrying orb. I will be needing it back if I am to be of any use to Iskar.

passages.title: Ishaal's Orb
passages.text: Have you found the orb?

passages.title: Ishaal's Orb
passages.text:
Hmm... something's not right. She's been tampered with.

Someone else has used my orb to enter the realm of shadows.

passages.title: New Neighbors
passages.text:
The Shattered Hand clan is made up of orcs who can call no other clan home. They are sadistic warriors who maim their bodies, perhaps in a show of solidarity or perhaps because they simply enjoy the pain.

It does not matter. What matters is that they are expanding their territory, butchering anyone in their path.

They must be dealt with.

passages.title: New Neighbors
passages.text: Blood for blood, as it should be.

passages.title: Lunarblossom
passages.text:
How I long to hold Kat'la.

No star or moon can compare to her beauty.

Alas, I am but a simple boar farmer.

If only I could find time to sneak away from this pathetic excuse for a job and pick some lunarblossoms for Kat'la.

I wouldn't dare confess my love to her without a gift.

passages.title: Lunarblossom
passages.text: How can I help you, <class>?

passages.title: Lunarblossom
passages.text: Lunarblossoms! You are too kind! I can't wait to give these to Kat'la.

passages.title: Going to the Gordunni
passages.text:
We have a good supply of jovite in the arsenal now but there just isn't enough of the material in the mine to keep us in stock for long. Down south of here there's a mountain that's just full of the stuff but there's one problem; Ogres!

The Gordunni live on top of that mountain and they have begun trading the jovite to the Iron Horde.

We need to go down there and secure the minerals for ourselves.

I'll pack some supplies and meet you near their fortress down south.

passages.title: Going to the Gordunni
passages.text:
I crafted a few things before we left that we may need: some bombs, a grappling hook, even was able to get one of the goblins to get a spare rocket pack.

I'm sure we'll find a use for everything.

passages.title: Ikky's Egg
passages.text:
<Miraculously, this single egg has eluded the ravagers.

A small tag has been lovingly tied around the base of the egg. It reads "Ikky.">

passages.title: Ikky's Egg
passages.text: <The hatchling springs immediately to flight, then looks at you expectantly and cheeps.>

passages.title: Dropping Bombs
passages.text:
The Gordunni have only a single path to their fortress and it is well-defended from a large attack.

Thankfully they wont be expecting just the two of us to be attempting to break in.

This is a great opportunity to take out their defenses and get some target practice for our artillery gunners back at the arsenal.

Take these smoke grenades and use it to call in an artillery strike on their catapults as we head up.

passages.title: Dropping Bombs
passages.text: Now that we're inside we have much to do.

passages.title: The Den of Skog
passages.text: Olin Umberhide appears to have discovered the parent of the gronnlings and is outmatched by himself. He will be slain without help.

passages.title: We Require More Resources
passages.text:
So what we got here is a good start, but you are looking for something that can support ARMIES!

Truth is, we ain't building anything without the materials to build it, and our supplies from Azeroth are limited.

I got some ideas on how to get you started but you are going to have to keep your eyes open for more materials when out in the field. Lots of useful stuff out there we can change into usable material.

passages.title: Lurking in the Shadows
passages.text:
There are reports of Shadowmoon clan members lurking around the ruins by the shore.

This is a popular spot for young lovers to gaze at the stars and confess their affection for each other.

As you can see we are not a village of warriors.

I will pay you handsomely if you go to the ruins and make sure the Shadowmoon orcs keep their distance.

passages.title: Fish Fight
passages.text: We have an accessible fishing spot here, but no bait seems to work! We need to find a local fisherman with some knowledge of the area to help us out. Think you are up to the task?

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text:
When they clapped me in irons, the Burning Blade instructor, Luhk the Keen-Eyed, took my blade. He's an honorable orc, even if his training techniques are counter-productive.

I want my blade back, <class>. Then, I'll break myself free.

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text: A blademaster without a blade is no blademaster at all.

passages.title: The Blade Itself
passages.text: If you can defeat Luhk, then perhaps there's some hope for you after all.

passages.title: Vignette: Gruuk
passages.text:
Goren are dangerous, especially in large numbers, and especially when we have a blind, under powered shaman with us.

Fortunately, they have very short lifespans. Unfortunately, they multiply fast and grow faster.

If we are going to do this we need to find the brood mother. Slaying her and her eggs should slow down the onslaught of goren. Check the burrows near the Forge Gates and I will to keep them off of Drek'Thar's scent.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text:
To secure the fortress we need to kill Witch Lord Morkurk, but I don't think we should go straight after him.

His three lieutenants - Vorgorsh, Zulmork, and Cromaug - are all powerful mages, and all of them are fiercely loyal to Morkurk.

I suspect that if we engage the Witch Lord that they will rush to his aid. Let's take them out so that cannot happen.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text: We need to make sure those Vizier's are taken care of before we can deal with Morkurk.

passages.title: Punching Through
passages.text:
Now with the viziers gone the whole Gordunni enchantment trade with the Iron Horde will come crashing down!

We can now turn our attention to dealing with Morkurk.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text:
We seem to have arrived at just the right time!

The Gordunni have been enchanting armaments for the Iron Horde and it looks like they haven't picked up the latest shipment.

We could put that gear to far better use! Lets go hunt down their shipping containers. I brought some signal flares that we can use to call in an air pick-up when we've secured the shipment.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text: The goblins said that the flares would surely get their attention. I just hope it doesn't come from the hillside being blown apart.

passages.title: Supply Recovery
passages.text:
Alright, that should be the last one we need. 

Nothing feels as good as knowing you are stronger than your enemy!

passages.title: We Need An Army
passages.text:
So the new warchief decided to send you Warmaster Zog to handle local operations. Zog!

I heard that guy was notorious for organizing the Alliance AND the Horde to face off against the silithid at the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj.

He was a general back then.

Anyway, if you go let him know about the barracks being done I'm sure he'll have some thoughts on how to put it to good use.

You can find Zog up at the town hall.

passages.title: We Need An Army
passages.text: Commander, it is an honor to serve you.

passages.title: Meet Me in the Cavern
passages.text:
It's time, <class>. Time for you to get your blueprints.
