passages.title: The Initiate's Revenge
passages.text:
I... I'm finished. My spirit will be with the Raven Mother soon.

I beg of you, stranger... avenge me! Slay these filthy beasts.

passages.title: The Initiate's Revenge
passages.text:
The lives of all the flock are precious.
I'm glad to know that his murderers have been brought to justice.

Thank you, <name>, you have done us a great honor.

passages.title: The Flock's Revenge
passages.text:
The Bloodmane took several of our initiates when they ambushed our ritual in Ravenskar. They must be taught that the flock will never allow such a deed to go unpunished!

We will kill one of their tribe for each of the flock that has fallen!

head into their accursed home of Bloodmane Valley and slaughter as many of them as you can find.

passages.title: One Step Ahead
passages.text:
Commander, Vindicator Maraad set off with Yrel and Thaelin Darkanvil to track the Iron Horde's movements in the nearby forest.

They await your arrival on a small rise to the southwest.

passages.title: One Step Ahead
passages.text: Ah, Commander <name>. Good to see you. Now our party is complete.

passages.title: Assault on the Broken Precipice
Assault on the Broken Precipice
Assault on the Gorian Proving Grounds
passages.text:
[PH]Commander! You just missed a group of rangari with some disturbing news. The Shadowmoon Orcs have been spotted in the hills above Anguish Fortress. The scouts reported seeing strange rituals and beings of pure darkness. Those orcs must be up there trying to summon more minions from the Void!

If we do not intervene all we have gained in Shadowmoon Valley might be lost!

passages.title: Assault on the Gorian Proving Grounds
passages.text:
[PH]Commander! You just missed a group of rangari with some disturbing news. The Shadowmoon Orcs have been spotted in the hills above Anguish Fortress. The scouts reported seeing strange rituals and beings of pure darkness. Those orcs must be up there trying to summon more minions from the Void!

If we do not intervene all we have gained in Shadowmoon Valley might be lost!

passages.title: They Came From Above
passages.text:
Please, traveler, I need your help.

Aruuna, my home, has been destroyed by the arakkoa. They swooped down from their spires and killed anyone who tried to escape. My family... did not make it out.

 My brother Barum stayed behind to find his daughter amidst the chaos. I beseech you, please, go to Aruuna and find Barum.

He is the only family I have left.

passages.title: They Came From Above
passages.text: Akhan is alive? Light bless us - some good news!

passages.title: Ogre Waygates
passages.text:
Six unique gates exist in Draenor, built by ogre magi in ages past. We've discovered their potency has not diminished over the millennia.

If you can collect enough ogre waystones to activate one of these ancient waygates, we can build a portal from your garrison to that location.

passages.title: Ogre Waygates
passages.text: Did you activate a waygate?

passages.title: Ogre Waygates
passages.text: Your efforts will be well rewarded, <name>.  The ancient waygates now serve you.

passages.title: Pinchwhistle Gearworks
passages.text:
Commander, a goblin courier arrived this morning.

He mentioned that he is from a settlement in the Spires of Arak called the Pinchwhistle Gearworks. They have requested our assistance with some sort of ecological disaster.

If we can earn their trust it'll be worth the effort. Head down there and see what sort of assistance we can provide.

I've already spoken to the flight master and he's set up a special flight to get you out there.

passages.title: Pinchwhistle Gearworks
passages.text:
Hey, you're from that Alliance base right?

Glad you made the trip because we really could use your help!

passages.title: Pinchwhistle Gearworks
passages.text:
Commander, a courier arrived this morning.

He said he's from a goblin settlement in Spires of Arak called the Pinchwhistle Gearworks. They've asked for our assistance with some sort of ecological disaster.

We're spread thin but if we can earn their trust then we might be able to gain a valuable ally.

Head down there and see what sort of assistance we can provide. I've already spoken to the flight master and he's set up a special flight to get you out there.

passages.title: Pinchwhistle Gearworks
passages.text:
Hey, you're from that Horde base right?

Glad you made the trip because we really could use your help!

passages.title: Luring Nat
passages.text:
Now that you are experienced enough with Draenor fishing, we might have a shot at convincing Nat Pagle to join us out here.

If we want Nat to actually come all the way out here, we are going to have to show him real proof of the incredible catches on Draenor. Head out to local waters here in Shadowmoon Valley and see what you can do. All that time you spend honing your skill here in Draenor should pay off now.

passages.title: Luring Nat
passages.text: Find anything worth keeping?

passages.title: Luring Nat
passages.text: This will do nicely... A fish like this would be hard for anyone to deny, especially Nat!

passages.title: Warlords of Draenor: The Dark Portal
passages.text:
<name>, is it? I'm glad you're here. We can use every able-bodied <class> that we can get.

I am assembling a coalition of Azeroth's strongest to step through this Dark Portal and stop the Iron Horde invasion. This may be the only way to save Azeroth.

Will you join us?

passages.title: Warlords of Draenor: The Dark Portal
passages.text: Looks to me like we ended up in the right place.

passages.title: The Great Angler Returns
passages.text:
What's this species, an arcane trout you say? I have never even heard of a fish like this, much less seen one in person!

I have to find more fish like this, it's what I live for! And if the fishing is as good as you say it is, there is just no way I can pass this opportunity up. Take this page from my journal as proof that you found me and I will meet you back at your Garrison.

passages.title: The Great Angler Returns
passages.text: You found Nat? The real Nat Pagle?!

passages.title: The Great Angler Returns
passages.text: We should really catch some big one's when Nat's gets here!

passages.title: Nemesis: Hunter - Hunted
passages.text:
Our enemies surround us, and with each passing day their numbers grow. It is time to make a decisive strike against their armies, champion.

Around me stand effigies of our most hated adversaries. You will be their downfall, <name>. You will become nemesis and they will run in fear at the sight of you.

Now select the target of your rage and burn in effigy that race which you mean to eradicate. Speak to me when you have made your selection.

passages.title: Nemesis: Hunter - Hunted
passages.text:
A last warning: once you have accepted this choice you cannot reverse it or make a new choice until you complete your mission.

If your choice is certain, your aim will be true.

Strike fear in the hearts and minds of the enemy! For the Horde. For Draenor.

passages.title: Besting a Boar
passages.text:
Have you seen the boars they have here? Bigger than I am! Let's get one of them, why not?

You're going to have to head to Gorgrond for that task. Way out in the desolate regions, you'll find the ones we're lookin' for.

passages.title: Besting a Boar
passages.text: That boar has taken to the hay. We'll let it rest up a bit before more training.

passages.title: Wrangling a Wolf
passages.text:
This next one will test you to your very limits, commander. The wolf is the most savage beast in all of Draenor.

The wolves of Nagrand, mounts of the fabled Warsong clan, can rend a man to bits in seconds. They're also faster and more agile than anything you've seen yet.

Here's your lasso. Good luck, and don't get yourself killed!

passages.title: Wrangling a Wolf
passages.text: It almost bit me, but I've got it bedded down and happy. A wolf, in my stables! Who'd have thought?

passages.title: Besting a Boar
passages.text:
The great boars of Gorgrond appear to serve as both a mount and an excellent source of food. Having a few of them in the garrison would not be an unwise idea.

I have created for you another rope, should you wish to ride one down. Be wary of the Iron Horde presence nearby.

passages.title: Besting a Boar
passages.text: The boar has taken to the stables quite quickly. They appear to be nearly domesticated already. It will need some time to rest.

passages.title: Wrangling a Wolf
passages.text:
The wolves of this land have jaws of steel. It is no wonder that the orcs have taken them as their own.

Yet, deep in Nagrand, there are young wolves, ripe for taming. They will present a great challenge to you, as they are more fast and agile than any beast in this land.

Here is your final rope, may luck be with you.

passages.title: Wrangling a Wolf
passages.text: Quite the catch, commander. It will need to rest for some time, but will surely be hungry for combat soon.

passages.title: Arakkoa Exodus
passages.text:
I assume you're familiar with the arakkoa, commander? Great, flying birdfolk. Extremely territorial.

Some, however, have withered wings - a disease, maybe. They seem to be outcast from arakkoa society. You find them now and then, squatting in forgotten ruins or peddling trinkets on the roadside.

It seems the Iron Horde has incited the arakkoa by moving into their lands, and the outcasts are fleeing in droves.

We should make contact with these outcasts - they could have valuable information.

passages.title: Arakkoa Exodus
passages.text:
<The arakkoa merchant looks you up and down.>

Well-equipped, aren't we? Azik is betting you are someone of importance to your people.

Come closer, friend. Speak with me for just a moment.

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
**Eyes Only -- Commander <name>**

Durotan recommended dat we be gettin' a foothold in Nagrand, so I taken the liberty of dispatchin' some of da boys.

Thrall's already reportin' the new outpost be nearly complete. He been askin' me to let ya know they be ready for ya.

A windrider be waitin' to catch ya up with the latest caravan shipment whenever you be ready, <sir/ma'am>.

-- Rokhan

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
They came at us... from... nowhere.

<The stoneguard nearly passes out.>

passages.title: It's a Matter of Strategy
passages.text:
**Eyes Only -- Commander <name>**

The Iron Horde have proved themselves worthy foes.

They managed to get their fleet moving to Talador from Gorgrond without my spies seeing a thing. Talador be a crossroads for the whole continent. We can't let them have it.

Don't worry boss, we got a plan. Foreman Grobash be setting up an outpost for our forces as we speak. They be ready for you when you arrive, commander.

--Rokhan

passages.title: It's a Matter of Strategy
passages.text: Your will be done. I require your advisement, commander.

passages.title: Nemesis: Hunter - Hunted
passages.text:
Our enemies surround us, and with each passing day their numbers grow. It is time to make a decisive strike against their armies, champion.

Around me stand effigies of our most hated adversaries. You will be their downfall, <name>. You will become nemesis and they will run in fear at the sight of you.

Now select the target of your rage and burn in effigy that race which you mean to eradicate. Speak to me when you have made your selection.

passages.title: Nemesis: Hunter - Hunted
passages.text:
A last warning: once you have accepted this choice you cannot reverse it or make a new choice until you complete your mission.

If your choice is certain, your aim will be true.

Strike fear in the hearts and minds of the enemy! Glory to the Alliance! For Draenor!

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Great-Tusk
passages.text:
The first step in training your mount for war will be getting it used to the sights and sounds of combat. If it's not trained properly, it might get spooked and run.

Take this little talbuk out to the plains of Shadowmoon Valley and take on the biggest beast you can find, together. That should raise its confidence!

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Great-Tusk
passages.text: Did you manage to bring down Great-Tusk?

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Great-Tusk
passages.text: That should do it a world of good. We'll let 'er rest for tonight, and take on some bigger targets tomorrow.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Rakkiri
passages.text:
Now that your talbuk has got a taste for combat, let's take it out into an environment it may not be familiar with.

The icy bluffs of Frostfire Ridge should be a good test. Find yourself a big, mean beast out there and take it down with your talbuk.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Rakkiri
passages.text: Oi! That talbuk's performin' admirably. Let's let 'er rest.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Riplash
passages.text:
Now plenty of mounts have been known to run away at the sight of a fierce predator. Way out in the desolate cliffs of Gorgrond, they've got some of the fiercest.

Let's put your talbuk to the test. See if the two of you can't take down the mighty raptor known as Riplash.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Riplash
passages.text: Those were some mighty big claws to tangle with. Your talbuk will need a nap after that one.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Gezz'ran
passages.text:
There's plenty more beasts out in the wild that can make a snack of your favorite mount. One of the most cunning on Draenor is the stalker.

Stalkers can blend into their environments, allowing them to sneak in and steal the eggs of nearby prey. See if you and your talbuk can't overcome this natural defense mechanism. You'll find some mean stalkers out in Talador.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Gezz'ran
passages.text: Ye did it! I'm sure your talbuk's enjoyin' this sort of one-on-one attention. We'll let it rest up a bit.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Bulbapore
passages.text:
Way down south in the Spires of Arak, the land's being overtaken by the mushrooms that grow underwater. The result? Strange fungal creatures sprouting up all over the place.

Taking on a strange creature, like the fungal giant Bulbapore, gives us a great chance to expose your talbuk to predators it's unfamiliar with.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Bulbapore
passages.text: I'll bet that was quite a fight! Great job, let's let it rest for tonight.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text:
Nagrand is home to the mightiest beasts in Draenor, and the ogres of the region have learned to tame them using brutal techniques.

There is one ogre in particular, the Gorian Beast-Lasher, that smells of blood and fear. Go on and see how your talbuk reacts to that.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text: Those poor beasts! I'm glad you two put that ogre out of commission. Check back in tomorrow and we can continue the training.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Darkwing Roc
passages.text:
The windrocs of Nagrand are a smart predator, often swooping down on unwary prey in packs. If your beast doesn't keep an eye on the sky, it's likely to lose both of 'em.

Head on out to Nagrand and take on the fiercest windroc of the bunch, the Darkwing Roc. That'll be a good test for the both of ye.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Darkwing Roc
passages.text: From now on, I'm sure your mount will always remember to keep one eye on the skies. Great job!

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Moth of Wrath
passages.text:
Deep in the forests of Nagrand are some beasts capable of evading almost any predator. The greatest of them all, the Moth of Wrath, is coated with a foul-smelling dust.

If the moth dust is enough to keep wolves at bay, it'll probably be a pretty good test for your talbuk. See if you can't keep it focused and take down that moth.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Moth of Wrath
passages.text: Glad to see you two make it back. It'll need a bit of time to brush that dust off.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Thundercall
passages.text:
The elements can sometimes pose a problem for some beasts. Ever seen a ram in a thunderstorm? They'll hide behind anything larger than themselves. I'm not sure if they think the world is ending or what, but it's not great if you're atop one at the time.

In Nagrand, off on a windswept cliff high above the shore, is a creature made of pure thunderstorms. Hop atop your talbuk and face off against Thundercall, and we'll see if it gets spooked.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Thundercall
passages.text: Well, it's a bit wet, but seems to be in good spirits. I'll get 'er dried off and into bed.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Ironbore
passages.text:
Alright, we've taken on foes in the sky and on land, and even in the rain. What happens when the beasts are below your feet, though? We're about to find out!

The rockworm is a cunning predator, striking at prey from below the sands. Many beasts of Nagrand have grown wary of the rumbling of the earth. Take your talbuk on out to the sandy shores and see if you can't take down one of the elder rockworms: Ironbore.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Ironbore
passages.text: The sand worm's bit the dust? Well done, I'll get this beast bedded down for the night.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text:
The Warsong Clan of Nagrand are some of the best hunters I've ever had the misfortune of meeting. If anyone can pose a real test for your future mount, it's one of their chief beast-killers.

Out in Nagrand, you'll find an orc by the name of Karak. They call him the Great Hunter, and he's taken down more fierce beasts than any other in the clan. Get astride your talbuk and bring him down. In the name of the poor wee beasts!

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text: Hunted the hunter, eh? Your beast doesn't seem any worse for wear, either! I'll brush it down.

passages.text:
That boar's seen it's share of combat out in Gorgrond, so it'll be a bit easier to train. We'll start off in it's home, as you've done with yer other beasties.

See if the two of you can't take down the mighty raptor known as Riplash.

passages.title: Boar Training: The Garn
passages.text:
I've got one last challenge for ye, commander, but if it isn't a doozy.

They call them the garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear a man apart in seconds. Any beast in their right mind would be scared witless at the sight of such a predator.

There's a lone garn that's made it from their usual home in Frostfire, all the way over to Nagrand. Take your boar, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your boar will truly be ready.

passages.title: Boar Training: The Garn
passages.text:
Your rocktusk is now ready to see combat, commander. Here's the reins, you'll need 'em ridin' this bucket of muscle!

Great job with the training!

passages.title: Riverbeast Training: Gezz'ran
passages.text:
This beast's spent quite a few years out in the wilds of Talador, I'd say we start the training there. It's fairly docile, as well. I don't think it will take quite as long to train as the others.

As ye probably know, stalkers can blend into their environments, allowing them to sneak in and steal the eggs of nearby prey. See if you and your riverbeast can't overcome this natural defense mechanism.

passages.title: Riverbeast Training: Gezz'ran
passages.text: Ye did it! I'm sure your riverbeast's enjoyin' this sort of one-on-one attention. We'll let it rest up a bit.

The rockworm is a cunning predator, striking at prey from below the sands. Many beasts of Nagrand have grown wary of the rumbling of the earth. Take your elekk on out to the sandy shores and see if you can't take down one of the elder rockworms: Ironbore.

passages.title: Elekk Training: Ironbore
passages.text: The sand worm's bit the dust? Well done, I'll get this beast bedded down for the night.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text:
The wolves of Draenor are some of the most savage beasts around, but they've also gotten used to the sights and smells of the orcs and ogres that live here. It shouldn't take us much time at all to train this little ball of fur and death.

Let's set it loose against the ogres of the region that yer familiar with. That Gorian Beast-Lasher, the one that smells of blood and fear, go on and see how your wolf reacts to that.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text: Those poor beasts! I'm glad you two put that ogre out of commission. Check back in tomorrow and we can continue the training.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Darkwing Roc
passages.text:
The windrocs of Nagrand are a smart predator, often swooping down on unwary prey in packs. If your beast doesn't keep an eye on the sky, it's likely to lose both of em.'

Head on out to Nagrand and take on the fiercest windroc of the bunch, the Darkwing Roc. That'll be a good test for the both of ye.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Darkwing Roc
passages.text: From now on, I'm sure your mount will always remember to keep one eye on the skies. Great job!

passages.title: Wolf Training: Moth of Wrath
passages.text:
Deep in the forests of Nagrand are some beasts capable of evading almost any predator. The greatest of them all, the Moth of Wrath, is coated with a foul-smelling dust.

If the moth dust is enough to keep wolves at bay, it'll probably be a pretty good test for your wolf. See if you can't keep it focused and take down that moth.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Moth of Wrath
passages.text: Glad to see you two make it back. It'll need a bit of time to brush that dust off.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Thundercall
passages.text:
The elements can sometimes pose a problem for some beasts. Ever seen a ram in a thunderstorm? They'll hide behind anything larger than themselves. I'm not sure if they think the world is ending or what, but it's not great if you're atop one at the time.

In Nagrand, off on a windswept cliff high above the shore, is a creature made of pure thunderstorms. Hop atop your wolf and face off against Thundercall, and we'll see if it gets spooked.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Thundercall
passages.text: Well, it's a bit wet, but seems to be in good spirits. I'll get 'er dried off and into bed.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Ironbore
passages.text:
Alright, we've taken on foes in the sky and on land, and even in the rain. What happens when the beasts are below your feet, though? We're about to find out!

passages.title: Wolf Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text:
The Warsong Clan of Nagrand are some of the best hunters I've ever had the misfortune of meeting. If anyone can pose a real test for your future mount, it's one of their chief beast-killers.

Out in Nagrand, you'll find an orc by the name of Karak. They call him the Great Hunter, and he's taken down more fierce beasts than any other in the clan. Get astride your wolf and bring him down. In the name of the poor wee beasts!

passages.title: Wolf Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text: Hunted the hunter, eh? Your beast doesn't seem any worse for wear, either! I'll brush it down.

passages.title: Boar Training: Riplash
passages.text:
This boar is at home in the rocky plains of Gorgrond, so it will be easier to train. As with other beasts, we will begin the training in the place it calls home.

Test your boar against the great predator Riplash, a raptor known to hunt boars.

passages.title: Boar Training: Riplash
passages.text: A mighty kill. Your beast will need to rest now.

passages.title: Boar Training: Gezz'ran
passages.text:
Many of the creatures of Draenor have grown and thrived in a most hostile environment. One of the most cunning on is the stalker.

Stalkers can blend into their environments, allowing them to sneak in and steal the eggs of nearby prey. See if you and your beast can overcome this natural defense mechanism. You will find a proper predator in Talador.

passages.title: Boar Training: Gezz'ran
passages.text: A savage beast, but you have triumphed. Fine work, I will get your mount some water.

passages.text:

passages.title: Boar Training: Bulbapore
passages.text: You have returned victorious. I will bed your mount down for the night.

passages.title: Boar Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text: Ah, you have hunted the hunter. Many beasts will be pleased tonight.

passages.title: Boar Training: The Garn
passages.text:
The last test for your mount will pit it against one of the great terrors of this land.

The garn. Wolves as black as night, and twice the size of a normal wolf, they can tear an orc apart in mere moments. The beasts here wisely fear them.

There is a lone garn that calls Nagrand its home. Take your boar, mount up, and bring it down. If the two of you survive, your boar will truly be ready.

passages.title: Boar Training: The Garn
passages.text: The garn is defeated, and your boar is now ready to see combat. Here are the reins, may you never part company.

passages.title: Scraps of Iron
passages.text:
At the armory, we can take scraps of Iron Horde armor that you collect and turn them into new gear. It's not the strongest stuff in the world, but it looks good.

Get some Iron Horde scraps and come back my way. I'll set you up with a nice tabard for your troubles.

passages.title: Scraps of Iron
passages.text: Got those scraps?

passages.title: Scraps of Iron
passages.text: Those scraps will do.

passages.title: Unconventional Inventions
passages.text:
We've got a lot goin' on here at the workshop. We're buildin' new inventions all the time, and you can find 'em behind me on the workbench.

Go ahead and grab today's glorious invention. Use it at your own risk.

passages.title: Unconventional Inventions
passages.text: A goblin workshop can get dangerous. Watch out for exploding explosives!

passages.title: Unconventional Inventions
passages.text: Pretty cool invention you have there.

passages.title: The Headhunter's Harvest
passages.text:
Hey der mon, I be ya new headhunter. 
The tavern be a perfect place for adventurers to rest after a long journey. It also be a great place to talk them into joining our cause.

I be havin' a few recruits for ya to look at, if ya find one we can hire then I'll give ya a little somethin' as a finder fee for ya time.

passages.title: The Headhunter's Harvest
passages.text: Ya find a recruit ya like?

passages.title: The Headhunter's Harvest
passages.text:
I'm glad ya be findin' a good hire!

Make sure to check back every week and I'll bring ya me latest recruits.

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: Great-Tusk
passages.text:
The next step in training your mount for war will be getting it used to the sights and sounds of combat. If it is not trained properly, it might become afraid at a very inopportune time.

Though small, take your clefthoof to the plains of Shadowmoon Valley and find the greatest beast you can. It will grow quickly against such a foe.

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: Great-Tusk
passages.text: Your clefthoof appears worn, but happy. You have done well, let it rest for a while.

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: Rakkiri
passages.text:
Your clefthoof is most at home here in Frostfire Ridge, and that is where we will begin the training.

Out on the icy plains, you will find a hunter of blood and death. The winged terror Rakkiri is feared by beasts across this region, and will prove a good first test for your future mount.

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: Rakkiri
passages.text: The clefthoof is in good shape, you are a fine trainer for the beast. It will require some rest.

passages.title: Clefthoof Training: Riplash
passages.text:
Many beasts will cower in fear at the sight of a mighty predator. In the desolate cliffs of Gorgrond lives one of the most fierce. It will prove your next challenge.

Take your beast to the nest of the great Riplash, and see if you cannot emerge victorious.

passages.title: Lost in Transition
passages.text:
<Sir/Ma'am>, the storehouse is fully operational and I've seen to it that your supplies are safely stored away and accounted for.

Unfortunately, during the rest of my audit I found that we are missing a few crates of surplus material - probably misplaced by one of the porters.

If you happen to come across any of the surplus crates while making your rounds, please bring them to me and I'll update our ledger.

passages.title: Lost in Transition
passages.text: Hello commander, what can I do for you?

passages.title: Lost in Transition
passages.text:
Thank you, according to the ledger that appears to be everything we're missing.
Those peons are going to be cleaning the latrines tonight for this!

passages.title: Tricks of the Trade
passages.text:
To pass the time, traders have been known to consume beverages of an inspired nature, if you know what I mean.

Sometimes, they drink a bit too much. Your trader might have stumbled beyond the gates and passed out under a tree. It's been known to happen from time to time.

Luckily, I have a brew that I use to rouse groggy traders. One splash and I find they're more willing to work.

passages.title: Tricks of the Trade
passages.text: Trading isn't always the most exciting enterprise. But I do enjoy it.

passages.title: Tricks of the Trade
passages.text: You have learned one of my tricks of the trade, <name>.

passages.title: Call of the Gladiator
passages.text:
Your merciless rampage has not gone unnoticed, gladiator. So many of your enemies have fallen before your might. It is because of your unrelenting savagery that Imperator Mar'gok himself has requested your presence at the grand Highmaul Coliseum. It is at Highmaul that a battle of epic proportions awaits.

Should you heed the call of the gladiator, present this sigil to my brother, Kharg. He is the arena master residing outside of the Coliseum in Nagrand.

passages.title: Call of the Gladiator
passages.text: A bold decision, gladiator. For most, death is the only thing they find at the Coliseum. Surviving here is more than a test of skill, it is a test of wills. Do you have the fortitude to become a champion?

Try out today's glorious invention on the workbench behind me.

passages.text: Nice invention!

passages.text:
At the Dwarven Bunker, we can take scraps of Iron Horde armor that you collect and turn them into new gear. It's not the strongest stuff in the world, but it looks good.

Get some Iron Horde scraps and come back my way. I'll set you up with a nice tabard for your troubles.

passages.title: Scraps of Iron
passages.text: Got those scraps?

passages.title: Scraps of Iron
passages.text: Those scraps will do.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Great-Tusk
passages.text:
The talbuk is ready for more training, and for this, we will return to its home in Shadowmoon Valley.

One of the great beasts of this land, Great-Tusk, has taken the valley for his own. Pit your beast against him in combat, and if you should survive, it will have greater confidence in its own abilities.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Great-Tusk
passages.text: That was a fine battle to test your talbuk against. It will need to rest before we can continue the training.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Rakkiri
passages.text:
We shall start training the talbuk here, on the icy plains of Frostfire Ridge. We must train it rigorously, or else it may become afraid at the sight of combat, and run.

Find the great blood-sucker, Rakkiri, out on the frozen plains, and bring him down astride your talbuk. That will give it a taste for combat.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Rakkiri
passages.text: Your talbuk is growing quickly, let us let it rest.

Taking on a strange creature, like the fungal giant Bulbapore, will grant you a chance to expose your mount to unfamiliar predators.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Bulbapore
passages.text: You have returned victorious. I will bed your mount down for the night.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text:
Nagrand is home to the mightiest beasts in Draenor, and the ogres of the region have learned to tame them using brutal techniques.

There is one ogre in particular, the Gorian Beast-Lasher, that smells of blood and fear. Go on and see how your beast reacts to that.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text: Those beasts will recover, in time. Let us rest for tonight, you have done well.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Darkwing Roc
passages.text:
The windrocs of Nagrand are a smart predator, often swooping down on unwary prey in packs. If your beast doesn't keep an eye on the sky, it's likely to lose both.

Travel to Nagrand and take on the fiercest windroc of the bunch, the Darkwing Roc. It will be a good test for your mount.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Darkwing Roc
passages.text: From now on, your mount will always remember to keep one eye on the skies.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Moth of Wrath
passages.text:
Deep in the forests of Nagrand are some beasts capable of evading almost any predator. The greatest of them all, the Moth of Wrath, is coated with a foul-smelling dust.

If the moth dust is enough to keep wolves at bay, it will probably be a pretty good test for your talbuk. See if you can keep it focused and defeat the moth.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Moth of Wrath
passages.text: Glad to see you back. I will need some time to brush that dust off of your mount.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Thundercall
passages.text:
The elements can sometimes pose a problem for some beasts. Even the mightiest wolf will often cower at the sound of thunder in the distance.

In Nagrand, off on a windswept cliff high above the shore, is a creature made of pure thunderstorms. Hop atop your beast and face off against Thundercall, and we will see how your mount fares.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Thundercall
passages.text: Your mount is bit wet, but seems to be in good spirits. I will dry it off and put it to rest.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Ironbore
passages.text:
You have defeated foes in the sky and on land, and even in the rain. Next, you face beasts beneath your very feet.

The rockworm is a cunning predator, striking at prey from below the sands. Many beasts of Nagrand have grown wary of the rumbling of the earth. Take your mount on out to the sandy shores test it against the elder worm Ironbore.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Ironbore
passages.text:
You stand strong, though the ground crumbles. Admirable.

Allow your mount to rest for the night.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text:
The Warsong Clan of Nagrand are some of the finest hunters the world of Draenor has ever known. Their beast-killers will aid us in putting this mount to the test.

Out in Nagrand, you will find an orc by the name of Karak, the Great Hunter. He has slain more fierce beasts than any other in the clan. Face him astride your mount, and avenge the slain.

passages.title: Talbuk Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text: Ah, you have hunted the hunter. Many beasts will be pleased tonight.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text:
The wolves of this land are the most savage beasts I have seen, and surely do not fear orc nor ogre.

Bring him to bear against once of the ogres that you are familiar with. The Gorian Beast-Lasher, the one that smells of blood and fear, see how the wolf reacts to him.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Cruel Ogres
passages.text: Those beasts will recover, in time. Let us rest for tonight, you have done well.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Darkwing Roc
passages.text:

passages.text: From now on, your mount will always remember to keep one eye on the skies.

If the moth dust is enough to keep wolves at bay, it will probably be a pretty good test for your wolf. See if you can keep it focused and defeat the moth.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Moth of Wrath
passages.text: Glad to see you back. I will need some time to brush that dust off of your mount.

You stand strong, though the ground crumbles. Admirable.

Allow your mount to rest for the night.

Out in Nagrand, you will find an orc by the name of Karak, the Great Hunter. He has slain more fierce beasts than any other in the clan. Face him astride your mount, and avenge the slain.

passages.title: Wolf Training: Orc Hunters
passages.text: Ah, you have hunted the hunter. Many beasts will be pleased tonight.

passages.title: Rest and Relaxation
passages.text:
Every adventurer should rest when exhaustion sets in - and there is no finer place to get rest and relaxation than at the Lion's Pride Inn!

My best friend, Innkeeper Farley, runs the Lion's Pride. If you tell him I sent you, he may give you the special discounted rates on food and drink.

To find the Lion's Pride Inn, travel south along the road from here -- you can't miss it!

passages.title: Rest and Relaxation
passages.text:
Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold -- that's our motto! Please, take a seat by the fire and rest your weary bones.

Would you like to try a sampling of some of our fine food and drink?

passages.title: The Headhunter's Harvest
passages.text:
The inn provides a perfect place for adventurers to take a rest between their travels. It's also a great place to talk them into joining our cause over a few rounds of drinks.

Go through my selection and let's see if we can obtain a new recruit. I'll give you a little something as a finder's fee for your efforts.

passages.title: The Headhunter's Harvest
passages.text: Find a recruit that you like?

passages.title: The Headhunter's Harvest
passages.text:
Ahh, I'm glad you were able to find a good hire!

I'll get back to looking for more candidates for you. Check back in every week to see my latest selections.

passages.title: The Black Claw
passages.text: Behind me, as ye can probably see, is a giant black claw. We found it while we were out hunting new beasts to tame. The animals seem to be quite afraid of it, perhaps the beast it belonged to used to hunt them.

passages.title: The Black Claw
passages.text:
Like I said, the claw has a strange effect on the mounts we've got here. If ye have it with ye when training a mount-in-training, your mount will be MUCH more vulnerable.

Should ye find the training not rough enough, ye might want to challenge yourself.

I'd have a pretty hefty prize for anyone that could manage that!

passages.title: Teeth of a Predator
passages.text: This necklace dropped off of one of the orc hunters we found while out taming beasts. I've never seen the animals react so strongly to anything!

passages.title: Teeth of a Predator
passages.text:
I've not seen the beasts go so wild in all of my years, as the day we brought this thing back to the stables.

Should ye find the training still not hard enough, take it along with ye. Your mounts-in-training will be even MORE vulnerable.

Be careful! I'd give a prize to anyone that could best every beast with such an artifact, but I don't want to see you wind up dead!

passages.title: The Black Claw
passages.text: You've probably seen this enormous, black claw in our pile of supplies. We found it while we were out hunting new beasts to tame. The animals seem to be quite afraid of it, perhaps the beast it belonged to used to hunt them.

passages.title: The Black Claw
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Black Claw
passages.text:
This claw has a strange effect on the mounts we have. If you have it with you when training a mount-in-training, your mount will be MUCH more vulnerable.

Should you find the training not rough enough, you might want to challenge yourself further by carrying it with you.

I think besting the beasts of Draenor with it would certainly be worthy of a reward.

passages.title: Teeth of a Predator
passages.text: This necklace dropped off of one of the orc hunters we found while out taming beasts. I've never seen the animals react so strongly to anything.

passages.title: Teeth of a Predator
passages.text:
I have not seen the beasts go so mad in all of my years as a sage, as the day we brought this necklace  back to the stables.

Should you find the training still not hard enough, take it along with you. Your mounts-in-training will be even MORE vulnerable.

Be careful! I would gladly reward anyone that could best every beast with such an artifact, but I do not want to see you wind up dead!

passages.title: Unwelcome Memories
passages.text:
The botani in the Everbloom Wilds are doin' some sorta foul magic to create these plant... well... zombies, basically.

I've seen what happens with armies o' mindless slaves. The Lich King...

<Delvar's eyes close.>

No matter. We cannae let this escalate any further. I heard o' a particularly nasty one they've just made... let's kill it and see what makes it tick.

passages.title: Unwelcome Memories
passages.text: No zombies, plant o' otherwise, are goin' ta walk this world if ol' Delvar has anythin' to say about it.

passages.title: Unwelcome Memories
passages.text: I'll be takin' a close look at this... thing. We can't have a repeat o' Northrend.

passages.title: Leorajh's Prayer Beads
passages.text:
When Leorajh became shaman, pridelord gave prayer beads. Beads help Leorajh hear elements.

One day bird-men attacked and took prayer beads. Took them to Skettis.

Master, you help Leorajh get prayer beads back?

passages.title: Leorajh's Prayer Beads
passages.text: Elements don't speak to Leorajh like they used to.

passages.title: Leorajh's Prayer Beads
passages.text: Thank you, master! Elements speak to Leorajh again.

passages.title: Go Fetch
passages.text:
Now THIS is a savage land worthy of my level of heroism!

Oh, hello, I did not see you standing there, staring at me. Perhaps you have noticed that every piece of my armor is an ancient relic, forgotten by time.

As you have properly surmised, an adventurer of my stature does not have time to complete the menial requests I am given daily. I must remain here, yelling aloud to the trade district so that others may witness my heroicness and be inspired.

Today I require a Nightmare Bell, do find one.

passages.title: Go Fetch
passages.text: What do you want?

passages.title: Go Fetch
passages.text: I see you have completed this menial task admirably, almost as if you were intended to experience such a thing. Ah fate, what do you have in store for me next?

passages.title: Sky Dancers
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>, and I thank you for your hospitality.

The Shado-pan have sent several warriors to aid against the Iron Horde, however we can. We are few, though, and they are many.

The arakkoa in the south are both beautiful and deadly. They appear lighter than air, their attacks a deadly dance that flits from opponent to opponent.

The winds are on their side, as the four winds lighten the steps of my own allies. Bring me a sample of their winds, if you are able. It will surely aid us.

passages.title: Sky Dancers
passages.text: Did you find the fifth wind?

passages.title: Sky Dancers
passages.text: I will take this to the Shado-pan right away. Fortune be with you, we will have need of your help again when the winds run quiet.

passages.title: For the Birds
passages.text:
Hi! Have you ever held a peachick hatchling?

<Without warning, Mylune grabs both of your hands and then stuffs a tiny chirping bird in them.>

Isn't it so small and light and downy? Like you're holding a beaky peepy lil' CLOUD! It's so adorable you can't help but hug it and cuddle it and stuff regurgitated food in its teeny-tiny mouth.

<name>, the plantfolk in the Everbloom are turning peachicks into monsters before they can grow into beautiful swans. Or whatever they grow into. Please help them!

passages.title: For the Birds
passages.text:
Have you rescued a peachick? We're all they have, and those awful plant creatures are doing terrible things to them!

<Mylune's voice suddenly drops two octaves and sends a chill up your spine.>

Terrible. Things.

passages.title: For the Birds
passages.text:
<Mylune gently lifts the tiny little bird to her face, nuzzling it. It crawls onto her shoulder and disappears into her nest of green hair. A moment later, a beautiful fan of brightly-colored tailfeathers emerges from the top of her head.>

<Mylune's bright blue eyes grow moist with tears and her mouth goes slack with adoration. You've made the dryad VERY happy.>

passages.title: Cold Steel
passages.text:
Do you know what I want? What everyone who came through that portal wants. Every soldier running from a world that didn't understand us, didn't need us. I want that world to love us as much as we love it.

But we don't really belong there, not anymore. War is part of us, and we can't go back. To everyone back there, we're expendable.

The only thing that makes me feel better now is the feel of a cold iron cannon in my hands, pointed at the enemy.

<Keeshan stares into his mug of ale.>

passages.title: Cold Steel
passages.text: Leave me alone.

passages.title: Cold Steel
passages.text:
Yeah, this will do nicely. I'm going to run out of ammo, but at least I've got something to live for, for a while.

Here, kid, you're gonna need this more than I am.

passages.title: Cro's Revenge
passages.text:
HA! The fruit vendor was so cunning, but I, Cro Threadstrong, am even MORE cunning. I have come back into the past to defeat the ogre army before that fruit vendor can turn them against me!

Bring me the head of a big, strong ogre from the old slag mines, and I will have crushed the fruit vendor before a single apple has even grown!

CAN YOU HEAR ME, FRUIT VENDOR? I WILL HAVE MY VICTORY!

passages.title: Cro's Revenge
passages.text: THE FRUIT VENDOR STANDS NO CHANCE!

passages.title: Cro's Revenge
passages.text:
Revenge has the sweetest taste. Like an apple.

Take this, friend. May all of your fruit be CRUSHED INTO PULP LIKE YOUR ENEMIES.

passages.title: Time-Lost Vikings
passages.text:
Oi, barely made it out of that place!

We came through the portal to help, and the next thing you know, we're prisoners in the Bloodmaul Slag Mine. It was brutal! We were shackled for days, and covered in filth.

And they took my SHIELD!

passages.title: Time-Lost Vikings
passages.text: <Olaf sobs.>

passages.title: Time-Lost Vikings
passages.text: Oi, it's a fair sight dirtier, but that's her! Here, this is for you. You have my thanks.

passages.title: The Cure For Death
passages.text:
Greetings, and my thanks for the warmth of this inn and your hospitality.

As you can see, this malady of death continues to plague me. My studies on Azeroth and in Northrend met with little luck, and all of my leads ran dry.

I have come to Draenor in the hope of finding something, anything, to go on. My first pilgrimage will be to Auchindoun, a house where souls are put at ease.

If you should head there yourself, do let me know if you should happen upon anything of interest.

passages.title: The Cure For Death
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: The Cure For Death
passages.text:
This... may help me. I will need to return to Light's Hope shortly, you have my thanks.

I will not need these supplies any longer, they are yours.

passages.title: The Brass Compass
passages.text:
Greetings, commander. I have come on a mission directly from the captain.

Aboard any vessel on Azeroth that's manned by at least one orc, you'll hear sea shanties sung about a device capable of navigating the broad, rough ocean of Draenor. The orcs used it to keep their heading true in the choppiest of storms.

Perhaps it's just an old sea tale, but this one chance to find that kind of prize has the captain willing to part with some fine treasure.

passages.title: The Brass Compass
passages.text: Did you find the compass?

passages.title: The Brass Compass
passages.text: This might just be what we were looking for. Here's your booty.

passages.title: The Soulcutter
passages.text:
Don't look at me! Who do you think you are?

You and I are on the same side, you know. The necromancers here, we have to kill them. All of them.

Don't you agree?

Of course you do, and you can help me accomplish this goal. Find a Soulsever Blade in that hovel where the necromancers have holed up like rats. It has... special properties... that will aid us against the undead.

passages.title: The Soulcutter
passages.text: Did you find the blade?

passages.title: The Soulcutter
passages.text:
Excellent, most excellent.

I will wear it down quickly, and it cannot be repaired due to its unique nature. Expect to hear from me again.

passages.title: Gloriously Incandescent
passages.text:
I did not come here to fight, I have seen too many die already. I have killed so many with my own hands.

I have come to seek the light, and redemption.

The arakkoa of this land worship the sun as I do. But they are a violent, isolationist, and decadent race, who seem to derive a different message than my own people. This troubles me.

Bring me one of their Sun Crystals. I wish to see this light.

passages.title: Gloriously Incandescent
passages.text: Did you find the crystal?

passages.title: Gloriously Incandescent
passages.text:
The sun, I can see it. It is so bright.

I... wish to be alone. Take this, and my thanks.

passages.title: Aviana's Request
passages.text:
The arakkoa are creatures of the sky, and are thus within the domain of the great Aviana.

I have been sent to procure a feather, that we may parley with them through the language of the winds. We will extend an invitation of peace, and a place on the Great Bough.

Would you aid us in this quest? The feather must come from an arakkoan of nobility. You will find them in the place known as Skyreach.

passages.title: Aviana's Request
passages.text: Did you bring a feather?

passages.title: Aviana's Request
passages.text:
My thanks, <name>. Aviana will be pleased, and we may yet be able to aid you.

Aviana has sought fit to bless you with this, use it well.

passages.title: Cleaving Time
passages.text:
I, Gamon, have come through the dark portal to cleave many orc skulls. Yet my weapon has not kept pace with my rage, and is nicked and dull.

Find me a new weapon - one that is good for removing Hellscream limbs.

passages.title: Cleaving Time
passages.text: What?

passages.title: Cleaving Time
passages.text: I like this blade. It will see me through much removing of limbs. Here, for you, something to remember me by.

passages.title: Family Traditions
passages.text:
He ran off with it! Oh what am I going to do, what am I going to DO?

My son, and my knife, they ran off to Blackrock Spire! Well, the knife didn't run, I suppose. That doesn't matter!

You've got to get it back! Yes, the knife! You've got to get me back my knife!

Go! Now! Stop talking!

passages.title: Family Traditions
passages.text: Where's my knife?

passages.title: Family Traditions
passages.text: You found it! It's safe! I was so worried! Take this, take it!

passages.title: Damsels and Dragons
passages.text:
What ho, squire <name>! Forgive my lips, as they bear gravest news. Dragons have taken up stinking residence within the hallowed halls of Blackrock Spire!

These great wyrms hold a distressed damsel in their scaly graspers. Her name is Zaela, they say. Such a beautiful name!

As my squire, it is your Light-given duty to adventure yourself into this spire and procure evidence of these dragons, lest I waste my heroism on a dragonless quest.

passages.title: Damsels and Dragons
passages.text: Did you find evidence of dragons?

passages.title: Damsels and Dragons
passages.text:
This is dire evidence indeed! I shall head there presently, to slay no less than twenty of the great beasts.

For Doloria!

passages.title: Cenarion Concerns
passages.text:
Ey mon!

De Cenarion Circle sent Zen'kiki out here ta check out dem primals. I woulda been here sooner, but I had a little bit o' trouble gettin' my flight form ta work, mon.

De plants in dis place... I can hear dem talk. Dey be yellin' all the time. Angry an' violent yellin'.

Would ya bring Zen'kiki back a leaf from dis Everbloom place dey be talkin' about? Maybe I can figure out what dey want.

passages.title: Cenarion Concerns
passages.text: Did ya have much luck, mon?

passages.title: Cenarion Concerns
passages.text:
Dis... is no good. Dey want to consume da whole planet. How did dey get so angry? What happened to dem? I'm gonna bring dis back to da Circle, we probably gonna need your help again soon.

One of dem fronds be a bit magical, you hold onto it for a bit.

passages.title: Titanic Evolution
passages.text:
Ah, hello! Do not look so surprised! Did I not also brave the dangers of the Mogu'shan Vaults? I am more sturdy than I look!

I have learned many things of this wonderful place in history already. Did you know that, just like on our world, the titans once came to this place?

At least, that is what I believe! Surely there are signs of the titans' presence here, even now. Should you find one, I would very much like to see it!

passages.title: Titanic Evolution
passages.text: Have you found any signs of the titans here?

passages.title: Titanic Evolution
passages.text:
This is precisely what I was hoping for! I shall begin to study it immediately.

While you were away, I collected these pretty flowers for you!

passages.title: And No Maces!
passages.text:
There are far too many bright-eyed young rogues being sent through this portal and off to war. If I'm going to start up my academy again, some of them have got to survive this little excursion.

While I'm here, I figured I might as well use the opportunity to gather some supplies for my grand opening. You can't start a business without plenty of daggers, after all.

Grab me a crate of weaponry from the Grimrail Depot, there should be plenty lying around. I'll have something nice for you.

passages.title: And No Maces!
passages.text: Did you find me some weapons?

passages.title: And No Maces!
passages.text:
Yes, these will do nicely. My thanks, and here is your reward.

Try not to die, I may need you again.

passages.title: Call of the Talon King
passages.text:
adventurer, you have done much for my people. I wish to thank you on their behalf.

Please visit Veil Terokk when you can.

passages.title: Call of the Talon King
passages.text: Thank you for coming.

passages.title: Leorajh's Prayer Beads
passages.text:
When Leorajh became shaman, pridelord gave prayer beads. Beads help Leorajh hear elements.

One day bird-men attacked and took prayer beads. Took them to Skettis.

Master, you help Leorajh get prayer beads back?

passages.title: Leorajh's Prayer Beads
passages.text: Elements don't speak to Leorajh like they used to.

passages.title: Leorajh's Prayer Beads
passages.text: Thank you, master! Elements speak to Leorajh again.

passages.title: The Critical Path
passages.text:
The auburn forests of Talador sit at a critical crossroads of this continent, commander. The Iron Horde's fleet is already en route from Gorgrond to Shattrath on the west coast.

Talador will fall if we don't reinforce them. I took the liberty of dispatching Foreman Eksos, who has already begun construction on an outpost for your forces not far from the Iron Horde landing point. He awaits your orders sir.

passages.title: The Critical Path
passages.text: I won't waste any of your time, sir. Let us discuss strategy.

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
Commander, good to see you. With the fall of the rangari base at Telaar, Vindicator Yrel, recommended that we establish a new foothold in Nagrand.

I've taken the liberty of dispatching some of our men and supplies. Rangari D'kaan's already reporting that the outpost is nearly complete. He asked me to let you know they are ready for you.

A gryphon is waiting to catch you up with the latest caravan shipment whenever you're ready, <sir/ma'am>.

passages.title: Taking the Fight to Nagrand
passages.text:
They came at us... from... nowhere.

<The lieutenant nearly passes out.>

passages.title: Sanketsu, The Burning Blade
passages.text:
The blade is searing hot to the touch. The jewel on its hilt stares at you, as if daring you to claim it.

Perhaps someone at your garrison would be interested in seeing this weapon.

passages.title: Sanketsu, The Burning Blade
passages.text:
<Lieutenant Thorn handles the weapon, her keen eyes taking note of every line, edge, and scratch. After several moments, she speaks.>

Magnificent.

This blade was honed by a master craftsman, and imbued with ancient magic.

Just imagine if such a powerful weapon were placed in the hands of a skilled warrior...

passages.title: Sanketsu, The Burning Blade
passages.text:
The blade is searing hot to the touch. The jewel on its hilt stares at you, as if daring you to claim it.

Perhaps someone at your garrison would be interested in seeing this weapon.

passages.title: Sanketsu, The Burning Blade
passages.text:
<Warmaster Zog lifts the blade into the air, admiring its balance and heft.>

Never have I seen a weapon such as this. It was clearly made by a master, imbued with ancient magic, and tested in many a battle.

Commander, I will leave the choice to you, but it would be an honor to see this blade placed in service of this garrison.

passages.title: Cymre Brightblade
passages.text: I found some interesting artifacts on a recent dig, and I'd love to put them through their paces to see how they would have performed in their native cultures. Don't suppose you have anything small and furry that can put up a fight?

passages.title: Cymre Brightblade
passages.text: Did you want to pet battle or just talk...

passages.title: Cymre Brightblade
passages.text: Thanks for helping me test out these artifacts.

passages.title: Ashlei
passages.text: I don't really like when my pets fight, but I love making them feel better when they're done.

passages.title: Ashlei
passages.text: Hi.

passages.title: Ashlei
passages.text: That was fun.

passages.title: Rekindling an Old Flame
passages.text:
I am dying, <race>. My flame, it smolders... soon my light will flicker and fade into nothing.

You mustn't allow this. Retrieve for me the Essence of Flame. Allow me to live another day and I will burn every breaker to ash, I swear it.

I will take vengeance for my brothers and sisters.

passages.title: Rekindling an Old Flame
passages.text: Do you have it, <name>? Will you kindle my flame?

passages.title: Rekindling an Old Flame
passages.text: The flames, they burn within me!

passages.title: Gargra
passages.text: Do you wish to offer challenge? My wolves must train to become strong.

passages.title: Gargra
passages.text: My wolves grow restless.

passages.title: Gargra
passages.text: You have helped my pups train, and for that I give thanks.

passages.title: Tarr the Terrible
passages.text: Tarr is the true warlord! Bring your army to fight and I show you.

passages.title: Tarr the Terrible
passages.text: Tarr destroy your face!

passages.title: Tarr the Terrible
passages.text: You lucky this time.

passages.title: Vesharr
passages.text: I had a vision with one who had mastered pets came to challenge me. Has the vision finally come to pass?

passages.title: Vesharr
passages.text: Can you defeat me?

passages.title: Vesharr
passages.text: The feathers have fallen and shown us much.

passages.title: Taralune
passages.text: I strive to teach through non-lethal pet battle. Are you willing to learn?

passages.title: Taralune
passages.text: You have not yet learned enough.

passages.title: Taralune
passages.text: We have learned from each other.  Thank you.

passages.title: Cold Steel Part II
passages.text:
Hey, you.

I wanted to thank you for what you did for me. The feel of that cannon in my hands is all the therapy I'll ever need. But now...

<Keeshan stares off into the distance and grimaces.>...I'm all out of bullets.

Guess I'll just sit here and wait to die.

passages.title: Cold Steel Part II
passages.text: Leave me alone.

passages.title: Cold Steel Part II
passages.text: Ah, that's the stuff. I'm going to run out of ammo, but at least I've got something to live for, for a while.

passages.title: The Search Continues
passages.text:
An old deckhand inspected that device you brought us, and thinks it was quite the forgery. This Iron Horde is trying to copy the mechanism, but they don't quite have the technology.

When you get right down to it, we're not sure how these primitive beasts got a hold of this kind of tool. Wouldn't be half as good of a sea tale if we knew, ha!

We've still got a pile of treasure with your name on it, if you can find us the real compass.

passages.title: The Search Continues
passages.text: Did you find the compass?

passages.title: The Search Continues
passages.text: Let's hope this is the real thing, every time I go through that portal I feel my fur stand on end.

passages.title: Soulcarver Voss
passages.text:
You! You're the one that found me the blade, correct? I have need of your services again.

The blade worked wonderfully, allowing me to sever the tormented undead from this world. Their screams were such beautiful music.

However, the Soulsever Blade cannot be repaired, as it is partially woven with spirit energy that is drawn upon each time a soul is released. I need another, as there are still dark forces at work in this place, raising spirits and turning them.

passages.title: Soulcarver Voss
passages.text: Did you find the blade?

passages.title: Soulcarver Voss
passages.text:
Yes, yes this is perfect. It is time, little souls, to return to the twisting darkness.

<Lilian cackles madly.>

passages.title: Vessel of Virtue
passages.text:
Hello, again, commander. This plague yet vexes me, but I shall remain resolute, with the light as my guide.

The Soulweave Vessel has aided our investigations into the world beyond and the transition from life to death. With more vessels, we may be able to discover the truth behind the bridge between worlds. Perhaps there is a reason why the scourged do not fully make this transition.

Any additional help would be greatly appreciated by the Argent Dawn.

passages.title: Vessel of Virtue
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: Vessel of Virtue
passages.text: Once again, though I will need to return to Light's Hope shortly, you have my most sincere thanks.

passages.title: The Dark Within
passages.text:
The light... has gone out. I know not why.

I am more troubled now than before. I can find little comfort in the everyday. Each day seems darker than the last.

Please, bring me another one of the Sun Crystals. Its light is so warm, so comforting.

passages.title: The Dark Within
passages.text: Did you find the crystal?

passages.title: The Dark Within
passages.text: The warmth comforts me. I thank you.

passages.title: A Plea to the Sky
passages.text:
We have, so far, been unsuccessful in our attempts to contact the arakkoa. Each attempt strips the plumage, and we are left with a feather that is tattered and broken.

Aviana implores you, commander, to find another plume for her. We do not wish to see our brethren become victim of their own violent nature. All beings of the sky have a place with us, in life or beyond.

passages.title: A Plea to the Sky
passages.text: Did you bring a feather?

passages.title: A Plea to the Sky
passages.text:
We will continue to attempt to parlay with the arakkoa.

Aviana's blessing upon you.

passages.title: A Hero's Quest is Never Complete
passages.text:
What ho, squire <name>! Since last we spoke, I have heroically approached the gates of Blackrock Spire and nobly intended to end the toothy reign of its dragons.

Yet, as I neared the place, my mind drifted to thoughts of my Doloria's fair face, and to my own painfully unsatisfied desires.

My sword arm fell limp at my side.

I charge THEE then, squire, to go in my stead and search Upper Blackrock Spire. I must know if the dragons still squirm within its corridors.

passages.title: A Hero's Quest is Never Complete
passages.text: Did you find evidence of dragons?

passages.title: A Hero's Quest is Never Complete
passages.text:
By the light, they breed like great fiery rabbits! I shall head there presently, to slay no less than THIRTY of the great beasts.

For Doloria!

passages.title: An Axe to Grind
passages.text:
I, Gamon, have cleaved many orc skulls. Yet many of the iron horde remain, full of limbs and blood. I will relieve them of these things!

Or I would, if I had an axe. The last one broke in half in the middle of an orc's ribcage.

<Gamon laughs heartily.>

Bring me another, so that I may continue cleaving my way through this land!

passages.title: An Axe to Grind
passages.text: What?

passages.title: An Axe to Grind
passages.text: A mighty blade, but I will wear it out quickly. Orc heads are harder than they look.

passages.title: Mastering the Menagerie
passages.text: I'd like you to do some training. Head out and test your skill against the trainers in Draenor.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Teron'gor
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a fearless group and lead them into the depths of Auchindoun. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and cleanse Auchindoun of Teon'gor's evil presence.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Teron'gor
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. May the souls of Auchindoun remain at peace with the threat of Teron'gor eliminated.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Skylord Tovra
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble an elite group to infiltrate the Grimrail Depot. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and make your way to the Grimrail and put an end to it and Skylord Tovra's air support.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Skylord Tovra
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Eliminating Skylord Tovra's rylak escorts and disrupting the Grimrail will save an innumerable amount of lives.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Skullok, Son of Gruul
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a hardy group to breach the Iron Docks. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and put a stop to the Iron Horde's training facility and their subjugation of Draenor's mightiest, including Skullok, Son of Gruul.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Skullok, Son of Gruul
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Taking down one of Draenor's great giants is regrettable, but letting Skullok, Son of Gruul, remain a tool of the Iron Horde would have led to great distruction.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: High Sage Viryx
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a determined group of adventures and venture into Skyreach. Activate the Challenger's Orb, reach the summit and put an end to High Sage Viryx and her super weapon.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: High Sage Viryx
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. If not for you, all of Draenor may have withered under High Sage Viryx's rule.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Yalnu
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a resolute group of adventures and journey in to The Everbloom. Activate the Challenger's Orb, penetrate the depths of The Everbloom and put a stop to Yalnu and his ambitions.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Yalnu
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Your efforts to stop Yalnu may not only have saved our outpost but all of Azeroth as well.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Warlord Zaela
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a group of stalwart adventures and journey back to Azeroth and Upper Blackrock Spire. Activate the Challenger's Orb, enter the old home of the Blackrock clan and defeat the Ironmarch Vanguard and their new ally, Warlord Zaela.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Warlord Zaela
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Defeating the Ironmarch Vanguard at Upper Blackrockspire is a major blow to the Iron Horde and Azeroth can rest a bit more knowing Warlord Zaela's bid for revenge has been permanently dealt with.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Teron'gor
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a fearless group and lead them into the depths of Auchindoun. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and cleanse Auchindoun of Teon'gor's evil presence.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Teron'gor
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. May the souls of Auchindoun remain at peace with the threat of Teron'gor eliminated.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Gug'rokk
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a formidable group and head into the depths of the Bloodmaul Slag Mines. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and free the miners of Gug'rokk's tyrannical rule.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Gug'rokk
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. The families of the rescued miners will never be able to thank you enough for eliminating Gug'rokk and his slavers.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Skylord Tovra
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble an elite group to infiltrate the Grimrail Depot. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and make your way to the Grimrail and put an end to it and Skylord Tovra's air support.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Skylord Tovra
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Eliminating Skylord Tovra's rylak escorts and disrupting the Grimrail will save an innumerable amount of lives.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Taking down one of Draenor's great giants is regrettable, but letting Skullok, Son of Gruul, remain a tool of the Iron Horde would have led to great distruction.

passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a determined group of adventures and venture into Skyreach. Activate the Challenger's Orb, reach the summit and put an end to High Sage Viryx and her super weapon.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: High Sage Viryx
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. If not for you, all of Draenor may have withered under High Sage Viryx's rule.
