Today, though, their fragrance is muddled with smoke. Please, if you are able, check in on the orchard and see that things are okay. Perhaps my old nose is playing tricks on me.

You'll find the orchard to the southwest, beyond the statue of the Jade Serpent.

passages.title: An Air of Worry
passages.text: If you've come to speak with my fists, take your place in line. Otherwise, I could use your help.

passages.title: The Golden Dream
passages.text:
Ashyo must have experienced what we call the golden dream.

Many of us working here have seen it, too - often after a long day of toiling in the pools. It is said this vision--and the feeling of elation it brings--is a reward to the mind for working the body.

There IS an easier way, though we rarely resort to it anymore: a tea can be brewed using lotus root and dreamleaf, which grows around the shrine on the upper tier.

Bring the dreamleaf to Yan back in town and he can brew the tea for you.

passages.title: The Golden Dream
passages.text: Yes, did you need something?

passages.title: The Golden Dream
passages.text:
Ah... dreamleaf! So you want to see the Golden Dream, do you?

Come to think of it, I haven't seen the Dream in years - not since I was a cub spending long hours playing in the pools. Long before I took up the culinary arts.

Looks like you brought enough dreamleaf for two cups of tea... so why not?

Here's to better days!

passages.title: Kill Mogu Firestarters
passages.text:
As if the attack weren't bad enough, the mogu are setting these ancient orchards ablaze.

I cannot understand what they hope to achieve, but we must stop them. Clear out the orchard so these people have a livelihood to return to.

passages.title: Unbound
passages.text:
Can you see them, adventurer? Farmers from the orchard, tied up and under inspection. Being hauled off in chains.

The mogu value strength above all else. Anyone deemed fit for work will be sent to toil under their cruel whips.

As for the others, well...

Let's not waste any more time.

passages.title: Unbound
passages.text: Those ropes should give with a strong tug.

passages.title: Unbound
passages.text: The pandaren were subjected to mogu rule in ancient times - we'll never let it happen again.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text:
Lok'tar ogar, <race>. I am Nazgrim.

You are hereby ordered to present yourself at Grommash Hold immediately.

All in service to the Horde are to swear an oath of allegiance to their new Warchief.

Do not keep him waiting, <race>.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text: Blood and thunder, orc.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text: Ahh, good. You're here. And not a moment too soon...

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text:
Lok'tar Ogar, old friend. It has been too long since last we spoke.

It is good to see that you emerged safely from the depths of Vashj'ir.

I am stationed here in Grommash Hold.

All in service to the Horde are to swear allegiance to their new Warchief.

You would do well not to keep him waiting, <name>.

passages.title: The Art of War
passages.text: Ahh, good. You're here. And not a moment too soon...

passages.title: Tian Monastery
passages.text:
People come from all over Pandaria to train at the Tian Monastery, just to the north of here. Probably because they never turn anybody down. They'll accept jinyu, hozen... or even a foreign <race> like you!

My childhood friend, Lin, just joined the monastery's order a few weeks ago. If you're interested in learning how our monks train, maybe you should go talk with her!

passages.title: Tian Monastery
passages.text: You've arrived at an exciting time. High Elder Cloudfall has agreed to take on a new class of trainees within the monastery. This could be my big chance to finally learn how to fight!

passages.title: The High Elder
passages.text:
How strange, to have such a foreign-looking <class> visiting our temple. Are you here to study?

You... you look very strong. You wouldn't have any trouble getting accepted into the monastery. You should talk to the High Elder, up on the balcony above.

passages.title: The High Elder
passages.text:
Welcome to Tian Monastery. I see young Lin has helped you understand the role we fill here in our hilltop village.

We are unaccustomed to outsiders. You would do us a great honor to train alongside our younglings. We do not have anything to offer you, <class>... except knowledge, and perhaps an appreciation of what it means to be pandaren.

passages.title: Your Training Starts Now
passages.text:
<Xiao does not look up from his bowl.>

Hey, new <guy/lady>! Glad to see you survived the banquet! Trial One: Complete!

<Xiao eats noisily.>

You'd better speak up with Instructor Xann. He'll be expecting you for your daily exercises.

<He continues eating. You suspect that he is done talking to you.>

passages.title: Your Training Starts Now
passages.text:
First, you drink too much beer... and then you show up to class late? Looks like you've already conformed to pandaren culture.

Let's begin.

passages.title: Groundskeeper Wu
passages.text:
We don't have many rules here, but we do have one particular rule that is worth remembering. If you want to eat...

<Xiao's stomach grumbles audibly.>

...you have to work. Groundskeeper Wu can give you your chores for the day. He's in the market, to the west.

passages.title: Groundskeeper Wu
passages.text:
<Wu addresses you sharply.>

<name>, is it? The High Elder's favored son? Yes, I remember you from the banquet.

Don't expect any special treatment from me, boy. You'll be working just as hard as the greenest pandaren trainee here.

Perhaps harder.

passages.title: Burning Bright
passages.text:
Might I ask a favor of you, trainee <name>?

Before I came to the monastery, I was a stranger to battle. During my time as a trainee, I performed adequately, but I was never placed in any real danger. Now, as a graduate and a wage-earning guard, I am expected to protect this perimeter at all costs.

I can handle greenwood sprites, but the tigers in the western Waxwood are something different altogether. Would you mind taking care of them for me?

passages.title: Burning Bright
passages.text: Please, do not speak of our arrangement with others. My cowardice shames me.

passages.title: Burning Bright
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. A thousand times, thank you.

passages.title: Zhi-Zhi, the Dextrous
passages.text:
Upon the hills to my right, you will find a hozen named Zhi-Zhi. He, too, won enough sparring matches to move up the ranks. I think he will provide you with more of a challenge.

Challenge him, and try to defeat him.

passages.title: Zhi-Zhi, the Dextrous
passages.text: Zhi-Zhi's style is different than that of most pandaren monks. He and his kind tend to have more... energy... than us.

passages.title: Zhi-Zhi, the Dextrous
passages.text: It appears that I must move you up the ranks yet again, <class>.

passages.title: Husshun, the Wizened
passages.text:
The jinyu are long-standing allies of the pandaren, and we welcome any of their kind into our monastery. Husshun, one of their elder shaman, is one of our newest trainees.

His skills as a monk are mediocre at best, but he is still a fierce combatant. He should provide you with the challenge that you deserve.

passages.title: Husshun, the Wizened
passages.text: I do not know why he decided to take the monastic path so late in life. It is not my place to ask. Such questions fall under the responsibility of our Spirit-Sage.

passages.title: Husshun, the Wizened
passages.text:
I must warn you, <class>:

If you continue defeating my best trainees, I will no longer be able to train you. And then you will have no excuse to enjoy the presence of my company.

Think wisely before you quickly dispatch any more of my students.

passages.title: A Test of Endurance
passages.text:
I have taught you everything that I can, <name>. It is time you spoke with Instructor Myang.

The fights that she stages are less traditional than the sparring matches I am used to. Nevertheless, the path of a traveling adventurer like yourself is unpredictable, and a broad knowledge of fighting styles is an admirable trait.

Farewell, <name>, and best of luck on the remainder of your training.

passages.title: A Test of Endurance
passages.text:
Greetings, <name>. You are becoming quite famous among the trainees here. I have already heard your name whispered several times, usually between the puffy and discolored lips one of your sparring partners.

I'm looking forward to working with you.

passages.title: UNUSED
passages.text:
Your training is over, young one. The cycle is complete. Thankfully, this particular cycle ends exactly where it started... with a banquet.

I will meet you over at the banquet grounds. I will likely be dancing on a table.

passages.title: The Lesson of Dry Fur
passages.text:
Through meditation, I intend to find a route to locating Shu. In the meantime, you would benefit from practice and discipline.

Your first task is the task of all trainees entering the pools: cross the balance poles to the west and ring the bell without falling into the pool.

Should you fall, the pool's curse will make it difficult to get on a pole again, so you will need to return to the edge of the pool to start over.

Oh, and beware the cranes.

passages.title: The Lesson of Dry Fur
passages.text: Good. You're a quick study.

passages.title: Stronger Than Reeds
passages.text:
Gather me reeds from the nearby pools.

Do not question why. Do, and then observe the results.

passages.title: Stronger Than Reeds
passages.text: Telling you of my strength means nothing. I must show you.

passages.title: Stronger Than Reeds
passages.text:
Good.

No number of reeds have ever withstood my might.

Step back, and let me dispel your doubts.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Balanced Rock
passages.text:
I require peace to perform my meditation. Practice your arts while I meditate on Shu's location.

Other monks practice balance and combat upon the balance poles in the surrounding pools. Engage them and defeat them.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Balanced Rock
passages.text:
Even now, your skills increase. Your footing becomes more sure. Your blows strike with more force.

Discipline and practice are the keys to reaching our full potential.

passages.title: From Bad to Worse
passages.text:
After their ship crashed, evil creatures swept up from the sea to pick through the wreckage. Our aid may seem but a drop in the pond at the thought of the misfortune they've faced today.

Defeat their tormentors. These people desperately need our help.

passages.title: From Bad to Worse
passages.text: You are a fear to behold upon the battlefield.

passages.title: The Sting of Learning
passages.text:
There are dangers in the pools. The latest and most vicious are the water pincers. A time has come for their numbers to be diminished, and I am no longer up to the task.

If you could clear out some of the water pincers, I would be very appreciative. Beware their numbers... sometimes it's best to lure them from the pool-side rather than wading all the way in.

passages.title: The Sting of Learning
passages.text: The water pincers are strange creatures. They seem to be drawn to still water.

passages.title: The Sun Pearl
passages.text:
Shu, the spirit of water, is eternally young, as are all the spirits of Shen-zin Su. I have been friends with Shu all of my life, but I no longer have it within me to play with him. I am old, and lack the energy.

For all his complexities, Shu is simple to please: he desires friendship. When I returned to play with Shu each season, I would always bring a Sun Pearl as a gift, and then we would play together. You can find a Sun Pearl in the pools to the southeast. Perhaps you can be his new friend.

passages.title: The Sun Pearl
passages.text: The decision to not return to the pools was a hard one. I don't think Shu ever truly understood. He does not know what it is to get older and weaker.

passages.title: The Sun Pearl
passages.text:
Shu's desires are not so different from our own. He does not want to be alone. Unwanted, unloved. He longs to be needed, and to share his life with others.

Knowing that, earning his trust is not terribly difficult. He just wants company.

passages.title: Shu, the Spirit of Water
passages.text: Shu, the spirit of water, is sulking in the deep pool to the north. Cross the rocks and then drop the sun pearl in the center of the pool. He will know what this means.

passages.title: A New Friend
passages.text: He wants you to play with him. Go for it!

passages.title: A New Friend
passages.text: This is your task, <class>. See it through.

passages.title: A New Friend
passages.text:
I have to admit, that looked pretty fun from my angle.

And you seem to have made a new friend.

passages.title: Into the Mists
passages.text:
<Nazgrim fills his lungs with sea air.>

You smell that, <name>? It's the smell of our home, the lands our kind have bled and died to preserve.

And listen... you hear that? It's the sound of peace and safety - a haven we've carved, where our enemies fear to tread.

Remember these things. You won't experience them again anytime soon. We have ourselves a war to win.

Now go get settled, we're shovin' off!

passages.title: Into the Mists
passages.text:
<name>!?

They told me you were dead...

I'm glad to see it wasn't true. There's Alliance to kill!

passages.title: Barrel of Monkies
passages.text: These monkeymen are driving me insane! I was just trying to get some insight into panderan brewing tactics and these hozu things keep drinking the brews before I can properly chemical test them. Can you please go take a few of them out as a lesson to the others? I'll make it worth your while.

passages.title: The Double Hozu Dare
passages.text:
Shin is still missing!

I never... I mean the other kids never should have double hozu dared him to knock on the witch's door. 

We saw a bunch of jade statues south of the Jade Witch's hut. 

Can you come with me and see if any of them are Shin?

passages.title: Monstrosity
passages.text:
It's plain to see that this statue and the surrounding ruins are of ancient origin. Clearly, this land has a deep history, which means it could not have been born of the cataclysm.

And yet these waters have been explored for ages now, with no record of anything here but open sea.

Perhaps if you were to sketch the pieces of this broken statue, you might shed light on the continent's origins.

passages.title: The Sprites' Plight
passages.text:
<Living statues rampage through the woods.

For now, they seem content in pummeling the forest sprites into splinters, but if they continue any further the pandaren will have more than just missing jade to worry about.>

passages.title: Breadcrumb Into Ruins
passages.text:
The spirits released from these statues are being pulled--rather violently--toward the coastal ruins up ahead.

It seems unlikely that they'll be allowed to rest...

passages.title: Break the Cycle
passages.text:
<Mogu conjurers call forth hapless spirits from beyond, forcing them into statues.

It seems that destroying the statues alone will not be enough to break the cycle.>

passages.title: Simulacrumble
passages.text:
<The shattered remains of an ancient mogu statue. This one looks like it never animated before it was broken.

Whatever dark magic the mogu are employing here, it seems to make the brittle statues significantly tougher. Better to destroy them while they are still vacant.

A good old-fashioned kick should do the job.>

passages.title: To Bridge Earth and Sky
passages.text:
We are ready to open the tan-chao and guide all of these spirits back to peace.

If I may, I would have your assistance once more. The mogu will surely sense the ritual taking place and will do everything in their power to halt it. I need only a few moments without interference, and once the path is open it will surge too greatly to be closed.

If you are willing to help one more time, please accompany me to the ritual site.

passages.title: Guess Whose Back
passages.text: <This dragon turtle's massive shell is rock-hard and covered in sharp ridges. One of the locals could almost certainly make use of it.>

passages.title: Guess Whose Back
passages.text:
My MY now look at THIS! What a beautiful shell!

You were wise to bring this to me, my friend. It will make a fantastic serving platter.

Please, take this for your troubles.

passages.title: Rascals
passages.text:
I'll keep trying to find ways to wake this stubborn little guy up, but there is no shortage of trouble on the island it seems. The crops to the south are infested with virmen, rabbit-like thieves and pillagers.

Rascals!

They breed faster than we can kill them! I have the perfect solution for such a situation: kill them faster! With you here, <name>, that shouldn't be a problem.

passages.title: Rascals
passages.text: <name>, that's the way to do it! You show up, and problems start getting solved. That's just one of many reasons why I like you!

passages.title: Stronger Than Wood
passages.text:
Gather me wood planks from construction near the Ki-Han Brewery.

You do not yet know the extent of my strength, so I shall display it to you.

passages.title: Stronger Than Wood
passages.text: Have you done as I've asked?

passages.title: Stronger Than Wood
passages.text:
Good.

My head, it is harder than the densest wood.

Step back, and let me dispel your doubts.

passages.title: Raucous Rousing
passages.text:
You ready for this, <name>? I'm thinking maybe we should have looked for something to cover our ears, but it's a bit late for that now. Just remember that the intense ringing you'll be hearing for the next few hours is the ringing sound of victory!

The honor's all yours, <name>. Ring the gong whenever you're ready!

passages.title: Raucous Rousing
passages.text:
Huh... well... that's definitely the ringing I expected, but I was hoping for a bit more from Wugou. This guy's a deep sleeper, that's for sure.

It's alright, <name>. I've got another idea, and there's not much preparation needed at all - just how I like it.

passages.title: Morning Breeze Village
passages.text:
The fourth and final spirit is Dafeng, the spirit of air. When he is not in the skies, he can be found on the Ridge of Laughing Winds to the west. I've sent both Aysa and Ji to help you find him.

When you are ready, I will summon winds to carry you to the top of the temple. From there, cross the bridges to the west and find Ji in Morning Breeze Village.

passages.title: Morning Breeze Village
passages.text:
<name>, give me a hug! Our parting was not so long this time - I quite prefer it that way!

You've been working with Aysa, have you not? Our disciplines have always kept us apart, so I know little of her. Watching her perform her exercises now, I must confess that she possesses a grace and discipline that is strangely alluring.

There are more pressing thoughts though, aren't there? <name>, let's take care of this monkey problem while we search for Dafeng.

passages.title: Tools of the Enemy
passages.text: The hozen have stolen our brushes and are painting over our scrolls of wisdom with their own wisdoms, if you can call them that. If you're here to help, stop them and bring our brushes back before they can do more harm.

passages.title: Tools of the Enemy
passages.text: I do not wish to disparage the hozen for their aspirations - each race must walk its own path. In this moment, however, they are bringing harm to our bodies and our culture. That is a line that cannot be crossed.

passages.title: Tools of the Enemy
passages.text: I am very thankful, young one. I will soon begin the slow task of documenting all of our wisdoms again, so that the scrolls can be hung for the benefit of all to come.

passages.title: Rewritten Wisdoms
passages.text:
<name>, we must help Elder Shaopai. There are few more deserving of our kindness.

On the way here, you surely noticed the scrolls of wisdom hanging in the grotto to the south. The hozen have defiled many of them, and sadly, they are not recoverable. We will deal with the problem directly - burn the defiled scrolls. Wipe the hozen writings away entirely.

Do not worry for Elder Shaopai. The people shall come together and help him rewrite the wisdoms in time. I shall see to that.

passages.title: Rewritten Wisdoms
passages.text: You're a good man, <name>. You have proven that again and again, and I am glad to stand beside you.

passages.title: The Direct Solution
passages.text:
Alright <name>, this is the second time we've had to deal with ravaging hozen. I think it's time we take care of this problem the Huojin way. No more patience. No more mediation. We go to the source.

We're going into the hozen village to the north and we're punishing those smelly troublemakers. I've been looking forward to a chance to fight by your side again, <name>.

passages.title: The Direct Solution
passages.text: Invigorating! A good fight always makes me feel better!

passages.title: Do No Evil
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to understand that the way of the Huojin is not the way of violence. When fighting is needed, we will not hesitate, but when fighting is not needed, neither do we instigate. However, the direct solution is often cutting the head off the snake, as they say.

The hozen have a leader instigating these attacks. If we remove Ruk-Ruk, we won't have to wipe the hozen out entirely.

I know you are not of the Huojin, but are you with me in what must be done, <name>?

passages.title: Do No Evil
passages.text: <name>, I think you've got a bit of Huojin in you. Stick with me and I'll bring you around, I think.

passages.title: Monkey Advisory Warning
passages.text:
The monkeys have been stealing from the village during their attacks. We should be fine without some of the extra food stores, but the idea of monkeys with fireworks... I'm a little bit concerned. Not to mention, who knows when some fireworks will come in handy?

Help me recover the stolen fireworks from their village, <name>?

passages.title: Monkey Advisory Warning
passages.text: I'm somewhat impressed they hadn't set their village on fire with these things.

passages.title: Monkey Advisory Warning
passages.text: <name>, I'm thinking we should celebrate with these later. What do you think?

passages.title: Stronger Than Stone
passages.text:
Gather me stone blocks from the Ridge of Laughing Winds to the south.

You have seen my strength twice, yet I still spy doubt within your eyes. It will not last.

passages.title: Stronger Than Stone
passages.text: The strength of the body cannot exist without the strength of the mind.

passages.title: Stronger Than Stone
passages.text:
Good.

My head, it is harder than the strongest stone.

Step back, and let me dispel your doubts.

passages.title: Worthy of Passing
passages.text:
The four elemental spirits will help you speak with the land and uncover its plight, but first, I have one small task to ask of you.

Join me, my pupil. Accompany this old pandaren to the western grove.

passages.title: Worthy of Passing
passages.text: I do not have the strength of body or will that I once did. I'm glad there are noble <race> like you to fight on for our people. You've come far, <name>.

passages.title: Unwelcome Nature
passages.text:
You faced forest sprites in the Dawning Valley, but the forest sprites in this grove are a different breed. Crueler and more dangerous.

If you would clear some of these sprites out, the spirits would thank you.

passages.title: Unwelcome Nature
passages.text: The spirits thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Small, But Significant
passages.text:
I am tired, <name>. I must rest.

We have a ritual to perform, but we require some of the charms from this grove. If you wander the grove, you should see them all over hanging from the trees. 

If it does not offend one as young as you, will you permit me to sit and recover my strength while you gather these charms?

passages.title: Small, But Significant
passages.text: Rest feels good. The burdens of life have become a great weight after so many years.

passages.title: Small, But Significant
passages.text: You come through, as you always have. You are truly one of my greatest students. I think you will be something the likes of which the world has never seen.

passages.title: Passing Wisdom
passages.text: This journey shall soon be yours to undertake without me. Stay for a few moments and listen to an old man's words. Let my knowledge serve as a foundation for yours, that you might be greater than I ever was.

passages.title: Passing Wisdom
passages.text: I know, <name>... I know. Such is the way of things.

passages.title: The Suffering of Shen-zin Su
passages.text:
Now is not the time to grieve. The balloon is ready, and Shen-zin Su awaits.

We shall be the first pandaren to speak to Shen-zin Su in hundreds of years. It is a great honor.

passages.title: The Suffering of Shen-zin Su
passages.text: You have undergone a great honor, <class>. Have you come back wiser for it?

passages.title: Bidden to Greatness
passages.text:
It is up to all of you to remove the thorn from the side of Shen-zin Su. Do not let your differences come between you. Trust in each other.

Within the Pei-Wu Forest is a lone hermit. Head directly to his hut. He knows intimately of the dark things that now lurk in the trees.

passages.title: Bidden to Greatness
passages.text:
Evil is rising from the seas and filling the forest. It's not just tigers anymore... something far more sinister lurks in the shadows, waiting to take any <race> unwise enough to stray out alone.

You are not safe here.

passages.title: Evil from the Seas
passages.text: I do not know what this evil is that is infesting the forest, <name>, but I know exactly how to deal with it. So do you, I think.

passages.title: Evil from the Seas
passages.text: You make me proud, <name>. You make all of us proud.

passages.title: None Left Behind
passages.text:
Your friend has been doing everything she can to save my crew. I'm deeply appreciative.

We're still dealing with more than we can handle here: quenching the fires on the wreckage, getting my people out, fighting off these evil sea creatures, and trying to prevent the prisoners from escaping. We're simply in over our heads.

I still have men on the ship that we need to get clear before the wreckage collapses on them. I know this is asking a lot, but can you help?

passages.title: None Left Behind
passages.text: I have no idea who you people are, but fate surely smiled on us this day. Many more would be dead if not for the help of you and your friends. I am in your debt.

passages.title: Stocking Stalks
passages.text:
My men are malnourished, injured, and exhausted, but they are Horde. Every one will fight to their dying breath. As our new ally, we will stand by you when the time comes, but we would stand stronger with weapons.

I have my men out gathering bamboo stalks to fashion into spears. If you can spare the effort, we could use the extra pair of capable hands.

passages.title: Stocking Stalks
passages.text: The Horde does not back down from a fight.

passages.title: Stocking Stalks
passages.text: These are excellent! We'll have them crafted into weapons in no time.

passages.title: Medical Supplies
passages.text: We need supplies to tend to our wounded, but the supply crates containing them were scattered in the crash. If you can bring back any crates you find, I would be very grateful.

passages.title: Medical Supplies
passages.text: Did you find the boxes I spoke of?

passages.title: Medical Supplies
passages.text:
These will do perfectly. I'll get my medics to work immediately.

Thank you.

passages.title: An Ancient Evil
passages.text:
<name>, I was looking for you!

One of the escaping sailors just spotted Aysa in the wreckage of the ship, facing some enormous beast. She might need your help - you should go to her, quickly!

passages.title: An Ancient Evil
passages.text:
<Aysa is clearly exhausted from the fight.>

Your skills in battle... are unquestionable... <class>.

Did you save the escaped prisoners?  ...Where is Ji? Is he okay?

passages.title: The Wanderer
Efficient Excavations
passages.text:
This manual describes outlandish theories on how to most efficiently manage large groups of workers as they engage in massive excavation projects.

After a quick skim of the material, it becomes clear to you that the author of the book is the figure in charge of the over-aggressive pillagers here.

A map on the back cover indicates that the author has a bunker in the southwest region of Uldum.

Perhaps an introduction is in order.

passages.title: Save the Cuddlies
passages.text:
The Fox Grove has become a dangerous place for the local red pandas. 

Sadly due to my actions helping that crazy Brewmaster Shadowpour, the foxes of the grove have developed an inebriation bite. The result is the little red pandas keep getting drunk until they can no longer defend themselves. 

Please! Can you help me?

If you round up some of them I have an aroma about this fire that will help sober them up. That should keep them safe for at least a short while.

passages.title: Lethal Hangovers
passages.text:
I told him not to do it! But "no one stands in the way of Brewmaster Shadowpour".

My master went and contaminated the local water supply trying to "add flavor" to the water. The toxins trickled down here to the Fox Grove where the brew has an irreversible effect on the foxes. 

It warps their minds and sends them into a frenzy. Now they are a permanent danger to any travelers and local wildlife.

Can you help me cull some of their numbers please?

passages.title: Need a Chaser
passages.text:
It appears now that my master managed to poison the entire local water supply with his flavor experiments.

I might have a treatment but need some supplies. In lighter cases my people have found orchids to be a wonderful remedy.

Defeat the orchid chasers in the Orchis Hollow and collect some of the pollinated orchids they carry. We will use them to cleanse the central water source.

passages.title: Drunken Tigers
passages.text:
Orchids may be the cure for my people, but they are an intense opiate for the local tigers. These beasts are often drawn to orchid fields and the intoxicating effects the flowers have on them.

When you add the toxins Shadowpour introduced to the water supply it results in very dangerous and rabid animals. It won't be long before they are threatening the Jade Temple. 

Can you thin some of their numbers please?

passages.title: The New Master
passages.text:
I figured it out! With the toxins you provided I not only recreated Shadowpour's recipe but also fixed the problem he was having that was causing illness.

Do you know what this means? All that flavor and none of the lethal side effects!

Now to deal with the Brewmaster. I've loaded up Chalky with samples. Can you take these to challenge Shadowpour to a tasters' duel?

You'll be subjected to his brews but I will help you cheat by bringing my sobering fire.

passages.title: Aunty Lin Windfur
passages.text:
We will start heading back to town once everyone gets organized. No way is anyone going to mess with me now! I'll boot them in the head! I'm sure I won't be in trouble after this.

Thank you so much for your help. Can you tell Aunty Lin back in Panda Town that we are okay and on our way back? She has tons of old cool stuff she might give you as a reward.

passages.title: Clever Ashyo
passages.text:
I'm not sure where Clever Ashyo got his "Clever" title from. All jinyu are clever, and I wouldn't say that he's any more clever than most of them.

Quite the opposite, actually.

At least he's a capable fighter. He did well enough at Tian Monastery to be selected for our training mission.

If you want to help him look for the Hidden Master, you can find him along the Valley's northern border.

passages.title: Clever Ashyo
passages.text: Where have I seen you before?

passages.title: Lin Tenderpaw
passages.text:
Lin is more talented than she thinks she is. Strong of fist but weak of spirit. With more confidence, she could be better than all of us.

Perhaps she will find the surety she needs on her trip into the west. She's probably on her way to Stoneplow as we speak. Stop and speak to her, if you find yourself on that side of the Valley.

passages.title: Lin Tenderpaw
passages.text:
Oh, it's you!

No, I haven't found the Hidden Master yet. I probably wasted my time coming out here.

<Sigh...>

passages.title: Ken-Ken
passages.text:
So... Ken-Ken. The hozen.

Personally, I'm impressed he's progressed so far in his training. He's got a brain between his ears, which is more than can be said for most of his kind.

He said he was headed east, but, seeing as we're already on the far east side of the valley, I can't imagine he went too far from here. Look for him at Zhu's Watch, in Krasarang Wilds, down the path to the south. See what he's found.

passages.title: Ken-Ken
passages.text:
This place... it... it so SAD!

Ken-Ken never seen a place so sad.

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text:
Kang's pride regularly becomes overconfidence, which often leads him down dangerous paths. His current path is as dangerous as any - he is headed deep into the Krasarang Wilds.

I wouldn't normally ask a favor of a stranger, but... would you make sure that he is well? It would give me relief to know that a brave <race> was looking out for him.

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text: I'm pretty sure this settlement wasn't here a few weeks ago. Where did these people come from?

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text:
Kang's pride regularly becomes overconfidence, which often leads him down dangerous paths. His current path is as dangerous as any - he is headed deep into the Krasarang Wilds.

I wouldn't normally ask a favor of a stranger, but... would you make sure that he is well? It would give me relief to know that a brave <race> was looking out for him.

passages.title: Kang Bramblestaff
passages.text: I'm pretty sure this settlement wasn't here a few weeks ago. Where did these people come from?

passages.title: Steaking a Claim
passages.text:
Since we're already out here, no sense in going back empty-handed, right?

Now, did you know that the porcupines around these parts have just about the rarest, juiciest steak a person has ever tasted?

They're difficult to hunt because of their sharp spikes, but you look like you can handle your own.

Go on and round me up a couple of steaks to take back to camp.

We may be roughing it out in this wilderness, but we can still eat like kings!

passages.title: No Such Thing As A Free Lunch
passages.text:
The fighting's over, but we're not out of trouble yet. Not by a long shot.

Our camp is falling dangerously low on supplies, but our provisioner didn't make it back from the battle.

Some of the troops saw her being dragged into the forest to the north.

Please, would you find her?

passages.title: Fighting the Flames
passages.text:
Those monkeys seem to be more savage than intelligent, but they're smart enough to know that fire is a powerful weapon.

I don't need to explain that if those fires are left unchecked, they'll destroy everything we've built here.

All my men have their hands full, so you'll have to do it. Take this bucket of water and put out those flames!

passages.title: The Dream Brew
passages.text:
The Dream Brew is ready.

Drink it at the Seer's Stone, just to the right of the red pagoda.

Seek, and find.

passages.title: Kill Kher Shan
passages.text:
Kher Shan is one big dooker.

Grooked all my sons! Ick Ick, Nab Nab, Eet Eet, Bitty Bitty, and the others I can't remember.

Wikket wanna help hozen? Go grook Kher Shan!

The dooker's over there.

<Nibi Nibi points to the east.>

passages.title: The Bees' Knees
passages.text:
You really hozen friend, wikket? Let's see, hmm?

Hozen at Grookin' Hill all outta slicky bait. Tigerflies' legs stay twitchy in water - make best bait!

Bo Bo sick from stings. Wikket get bait and take to Grookin.

passages.title: The Bees' Knees
passages.text: Slicky food!

passages.title: The Bees' Knees
passages.text: Woot! Woot! Wikket da Ook Dook!

passages.title: Broken Earthen Figurine
passages.text: This badly broken figurine was discarded by its last owner. However, with the right materials and your skill in jewelcrafting, it could be completely restored.

passages.title: Broken Earthen Figurine
passages.text: This badly broken figurine was discarded by its last owner. However, with the right materials and your skill in jewelcrafting, it could be completely restored.

passages.title: The Scouts Return
passages.text:
Hey, while you were out our scouts came back. And get this, they found some Alliance kid.

You should probably go debrief them.

passages.title: The Scouts Return
passages.text: We may have a problem.

passages.title: The Darkness Around Us
passages.text:
Despite our best efforts, the sha broke the seals around the main temple.

If we cannot hold them back here, their darkness will spread to the rest of the Jade Forest.

We need your help immediately. Kill any sha creatures that you see. They should not be difficult to find.

passages.title: The Darkness Around Us
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Every sha slain is another turn in the tide.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need a weapon suited to your talents. Retrieve a staff from one of the weapon racks below, bring it to me, and show me that you know how to equip it properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need a weapon suited to your talents. Retrieve a crossbow from one of the weapon racks below, bring it to me, and show me that you know how to hold it properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Freshly arrived for your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text:
Today is the day when your fate will be decided. Do you have the strength and cunning to be a <class>? Or are you destined to a life working in the fields?

Each has its place, but I can sense that you aspire to greatness.

Let us begin our training, my newest pupil.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Fresh to your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text:
Today is the day when your fate will be decided. Do you have the intellect and force of will necessary to be a <class>? Or are you destined to a life scribing in the dusty libraries?

Each has its place, but I can sense that you aspire to greatness.

Let us begin our training, my newest pupil.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Fresh to your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text:
Today is the day when your fate will be decided. Do you have the compassion and the keen eye of a <class>? Or are you destined to a life tending to the livestock?

Each has its place, but I can sense that you aspire to greatness.

Let us begin our training, my newest pupil.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Fresh to your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text:
Today is the day when your fate will be decided. Do you have the awareness and wisdom necessary to be a <class>? Or are you destined to a life scribing in the libraries?

Each has its place, but I can sense that you aspire to greatness.

Let us begin our training, my newest pupil.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Fresh to your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text:
Today is the day when your fate will be decided. Do you have the deftness and cunning necessary to be a <class>? Or are you destined to live the life of a humble merchant?

Each has its place, but I can sense that you aspire to greatness.

Let us begin our training, my newest pupil.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Fresh to your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text:
Today is the day when your fate will be decided. Do you have the strength of will to be a <class>? Or are you destined to a life of tending to the shrines?

Each has its place, but I can sense that you aspire to greatness.

Let us begin our training, my newest pupil.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text: Fresh to your training, your first task is simple: Speak to Master Shang Xi.

passages.title: Much to Learn
passages.text:
Today is the day when your fate will be decided. Do you have the strength and hardiness to be a <class>? Or are you destined to a life working the fields?

Each has its place, but I can sense that you aspire to greatness.

Let us begin our training, my newest pupil.

passages.title: Behind the Masks
passages.text:
The sha may seem unstoppable, but this is not true.

Their masks seem to be the source of their power. When a sha and its mask are separated, the creature's essence is banished back to its own realm.

Bring me intact masks, for I wish to study them further. Do be careful. I'm sure the sha will not part with them easily.

passages.title: Behind the Masks
passages.text: Please handle the masks carefully. If you are not careful, they will attempt to consume you.

passages.title: Behind the Masks
passages.text:
I suspect these masks allow the sha to make a physical connection to our world.

I must study them further if we are to banish these creatures forever.

Thank you, <name>. Your aid is greatly appreciated.

passages.title: Saving the Sutras
passages.text:
My adepts had to abandon their studies when the sha invasion began.

Unfortunately, they left their books scattered around the temple grounds. These priceless works of knowledge must be saved!

The sutras can be found near the Training Pit and the Adept's Ring to the northeast.

passages.title: Saving the Sutras
passages.text: How are the sutras? Are they damaged?

passages.title: Saving the Sutras
passages.text: Thank you! What a relief it is to see these texts are safe.

passages.title: Arrows of Fortune
passages.text:
Our war supplies grow low, but especially needed are additional arrows.

Our serpent riders are skilled marksmen, but they can do little without ammunition.

We need someone to brave the battlefields and retrieve any undamaged arrows to refill our stores.

Every arrow you retrieve will be used wisely.

passages.title: Arrows of Fortune
passages.text: Were you able to find any arrows?

passages.title: Arrows of Fortune
passages.text:
These arrows are still in good shape. They will fly straight and true.

Great work, <name>.

passages.title: The Shadow of Doubt
passages.text:
A terrible manifestation of the sha has appeared to the south.

It is trying to destroy an ancient relic, the Bell of a Thousand Whispers.

This bell has never been rung in the temple's history, for it is rumored to be an ancient instrument of power.

Please go and defeat this demon where it stands! We must save this relic!

passages.title: The Shadow of Doubt
passages.text: The bell is said to contain the voices of a thousand fallen temple priests.

passages.title: The Shadow of Doubt
passages.text: You have saved us. From what fate, I dare not imagine.

passages.title: The Search for the Hidden Master
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs.

I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I are trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: The Search for the Hidden Master
passages.text:
Were you listening in? Don't worry, I don't mind. You're welcome to search for the hidden master as well.

Though, if you do find him, I'd appreciate if you came back here and told me where he was.

passages.title: FLAG - Kung Fu Intro
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs. I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: Tears of Pandaria
passages.text:
All of this started with our ponds. In a single day, all of the water retreated down into the earth. When there was no more water in the ponds, it began to fall from the sky.

Despite endless torrents of rain, the ponds do not fill. It's as if the land itself thirsts and cannot be quenched.

Now the ponds birth horrific manifestations of despair. Elementals made of water from the sky and salt from the earth; the tears of Pandaria.

passages.title: Tears of Pandaria
passages.text: I don't know why this is happening, but I can say for certain that those elementals were the start of it all.

passages.title: Tears of Pandaria
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>.

It's time we take back our land from this curse.

passages.title: Search Party
passages.text:
I sent a diplomat to look for allies in the ruins east of here.

My diplomat has not returned and now Kang tells me this jungle is filled with a sinister people known as the mogu.

Chezin is my friend and Leza's brother. To lose a brother would cause her to give in to despair. She already has enough to worry about with her fever.

Could you investigate the ruins east of here and find out what happened?

passages.title: Search Party
passages.text: P... poison. Need... warn... Dezco...

passages.title: Crane Mastery
passages.text:
Thing about hunting birds is you need ammo - and I ain't got any. Thing about hunting with Nesingwary is you need to prove you can keep your tally and bragging rights up.

Can't hunt, can't brag. And I like bragging so this is no good.

Can I hire you to go kill me some carp hunters? You'll find them up and down the river west of here.

passages.title: It's A...
passages.text:
Oh my! This egg is going to hatch at any second!

Well, looks like this little guy is eager to meet you.

Are you ready?

passages.title: It's A...
passages.text: What a proud moment for you!

passages.title: It's A...
passages.text:
Congratulations! It's a beautiful hatchling of your own.

Please take care of it, <name>.

passages.title: They Grow Like Weeds
passages.text:
Ahh, it is you again, <name>.

Instructor Windblade is looking for you. You can find her on the ridge to the east.

She has some news about your cloud serpent.

passages.title: They Grow Like Weeds
passages.text: You are doing well, trainee.

passages.title: They Grow Like Weeds
passages.text:
Congratulations, <name>.

There is great joy in seeing the fruits of your own labor.

passages.title: Flight Training: Full Speed Ahead
passages.text:
The next task will be a little harder.

Are you ready?

passages.title: Flight Training: Full Speed Ahead
passages.text: I hope I do not need to question your dedication.

passages.title: Flight Training: Full Speed Ahead
passages.text: You did better than I expected. Not bad for a new trainee.

passages.title: A Feast for the Senses
passages.text:
I have heard that you know a thing or two about cooking.

As it so happens, serpents love to eat Fish Cakes.

If you use your culinary skills and bring me 5 of these dishes, the cloud serpents around here will be very happy.

passages.title: A Feast for the Senses
passages.text: Were you able to find the necessary ingredients?

passages.title: A Feast for the Senses
passages.text: Oh these do look quite delicious. You are quite the cook!

passages.title: Full Speed Ahead
passages.text:
It is time for our training session.

Follow me around the spires. Let's see if you can keep up while staying mounted.

passages.title: The Easiest Way To A Serpent's Heart
passages.text:
<The hatchling scowls at you.>

Uh-oh, looks like someone is in a bad mood today!

Luckily, you know just the thing that will cheer up the little beast.

Cloud serpents love the taste of tiger meat, but the tender flanks can be... challenging... to acquire.

Luckily, you recall there are some fat, juicy tigers to the northeast, on Windward Isle.

Sure, you might suffer some scratches and a little mauling, but it's all worth it for your serpent, right?

passages.title: The Easiest Way To A Serpent's Heart
passages.text: Looks like the task is done.

passages.title: The Easiest Way To A Serpent's Heart
passages.text: I see you have been hard at work, gathering food for your hungry little serpent. Well done. It may not seem worth it now, but your serpent will know of your efforts, and it will love you for it.

passages.title: Raid Leader Slovan
passages.text:
The raiders are led by a particularly violent saurok known as Slovan. The Crane Temple usually comes to our aid when he attacks but now we find ourselves outmatched and outmaneuvered.

Please, <class>, aid us by destroying this raid leader.

You can find him in his den behind the Krasari Falls.

passages.title: Raid Leader Slovan
passages.text: Slovan has always been a nuisance, but with the Crane Temple's defenses down he has become a true threat.

passages.title: Raid Leader Slovan
passages.text:
You have done us a great service today. On behalf of my people I thank you.

Please, accept this token of our gratitude.

passages.title: Labor for Labor
passages.text:
My wife, Leza, is going into labor but she is very very sick. I need to keep her warm but we've exhausted our supply of dry firewood.

Could you grab some twigs and branches from the nearby trees for me? Time is of the essence!

passages.title: Mushan Mastery
passages.text:
Mushan! Would ya look at the size o' 'em. Old as the dirt they walk on probably. A fine trophy.

If you are lookin' to test your mettle as a big game hunter, start with them.

passages.title: Mushan Mastery
passages.text: They didn't send ya' runin' did they?

passages.title: Mushan Mastery
passages.text:
Well done <name>.

My father travels across the sea to a new continent and all he can seem ta' want to hunt is old borin' wolves.

Me, I like to hunt stuff with meat on its bones.

passages.title: Fox Mastery
passages.text:
So, when I was scouting east of here I saw a collection of foxes. That's what I first learned to hunt when back on the Wandering Isle.

If you want to see the challenge a young pandaren hunter faced when growing up, head east and face off against a bunch of foxes. They tend to be clever and cunning so be on your guard.

passages.title: Fox Mastery
passages.text: I used to go on fox hunts with my father. If he could see me now! Hunting in Pandaria!

passages.title: Fox Mastery
passages.text: Well done! You outfoxed the foxes. I will talk to Mr. Pleeb about getting you another trophy made.

passages.title: Riding the Skies
passages.text:
I can no longer call myself your teacher, <name>.

You have proven yourself worthy of your cloud serpent.

Today, you shall join our ranks. Are you ready?

passages.title: Riding the Skies
passages.text: Today, we become brethren. Congratulations on joining the Order of the Cloud Serpent. Let us ride together!

passages.title: A Helping Hand
passages.text:
I've been pushing and shoving and hammering all morning, but it's hopeless.

These rocks won't budge!

"It will be a breeze," Grandpa said. "Farming's like breathing!" he said. Maybe for him, but not for me!

How am I supposed to succeed at this whole FARMING thing if I can't even clear my farm for planting?

Hey, wait a minute. You look like you've got some muscle on you.

Would you be willing to help me out? Just until I can catch my breath.

passages.title: A Helping Hand
passages.text: I really wasn't cut out for this type of work. I didn't exactly grow up in the country.

passages.title: A Helping Hand
passages.text:
What? You cleared the rocks? That's great news!

Maybe now I can actually start growing something on this farm!

passages.title: The Family Farm
passages.text:
D-did you hear what they said?

It's almost like they don't want me here. Like...I'm not good enough.

Sure I've never run a farm before, but I know how to plant a seed and how to pick a turnip.

<Farmer Yoon's eyes light up.>

You know what? I'm going to show them that I can also become a master farmer!

I'm going to turn this farm into one of the most prosperous in the Valley!

It's too much work for one pandaren, though. Come on! Will you help me?

passages.title: Roll Club: Serpent's Spine
passages.text:
Get to the bottom of the wall in the fastest time possible.

Speak to me when you're ready to roll.

passages.title: Roll Club: Serpent's Spine
passages.text: Ready to roll?

passages.title: Roll Club: Serpent's Spine
passages.text: When they built the wall, I don't think they knew we'd be using it for this.

passages.title: The Thunder Below
passages.text:
Roars have been echoing out from inside the Guo-Lai Halls. The mogu have awakened some ancient beast, and it will not be long before they attempt to release it upon my men.

Find your way to the Hall of the Serpent and slay the beast before it can be unleashed upon us. I would trust no other with such a dangerous and important task.

passages.title: The Thunder Below
passages.text: Have you slain the beast?

passages.title: The Thunder Below
passages.text: You accomplish what I doubt I could even overcome myself. I am humbled by your valor.

passages.title: Cindergut Peppers
passages.text:
A certain few pandaren around here prefer their dishes unbearably spicy. Unfortunately, my access to such peppers is limited.

The Kunzen hozen, in the mountains to the west, often carry cindergut peppers. A few of those and I'll be set for a few days.

Say, could you collect some for me? You might want to wear gloves if you'll be handling them directly.

passages.title: Cindergut Peppers
passages.text: Just put the peppers down on the cutting board, here. I'd prefer not to touch them myself.

passages.title: Cindergut Peppers
passages.text: I don't know how the hozen manage to carry these things on their bodies... let alone eat the things.

passages.title: The Lesser of Two Evils
passages.text:
Like any farming community, we have the occasional virmen troubles.

The most powerful Springtail virmen live high up in the cliffs to the north, and only come down when they run out of veggies to nibble on.

Frankly, I've dealt with virmen before. They're nothing but a pest that must be kept in check, and there's no better way to do that than by killing their warren-mother. Easy as that.

passages.title: The Lesser of Two Evils
passages.text: I've had plenty of experience with virmen in the past. Just show them you're stronger than they are, and they'll back off.

passages.title: The Lesser of Two Evils
passages.text: There, that's done with. Now we shift our focus back to farming, for a change.

passages.title: Stalling the Ravage
passages.text:
The Kunzen hozen, up in the mountains to the west, have been acting up, lighting their fires and shouting their chants. Based on what I've heard and seen around here, that means that a ravage is coming.

There's not much we can do to stop the ravage, but we can at least thin their numbers before they attack.

passages.title: Stalling the Ravage
passages.text: The ravage could come any time now. We have to be prepared.

passages.title: Stalling the Ravage
passages.text:
They'll be attacking, but my farm - and the farms of my friends - should not be in any danger.

Not if we can help it, anyways. Right, <name>?

passages.title: The Kunzen Hunter-Chief
passages.text:
From what I've gathered, the Kunzen hozen have two chiefs. One is harmless - he deals with potions, medicines, and ancient fables. The other one is in charge of the Kunzen's hunters - and the only thing they've been hunting lately is our crops.

The Hunter-Chief is a problem waiting to be solved. I'm sure the local farmers would be grateful if you went up there and, you know, "took care" of him.

passages.title: The Kunzen Hunter-Chief
passages.text: Mm-hmm.

passages.title: The Kunzen Hunter-Chief
passages.text:
No doubt the hozen will have a big ritual tonight, promoting a new Hunter-Chief.

I'm just happy that my fellow farmers can rest easy in the meantime.

passages.title: To the Waterline!
Poisoned!
passages.text: Poison... I... I can feel it... burning. Please, adventurer... grab... grab some of the mogu swords. We need... need poison samples. For an... ant... antidote.

passages.title: Crane Mastery
passages.text:
Thing about hunting birds is you need ammo - and I ain't got any. Thing about hunting with Nesingwary is you need to prove you can keep your tally and bragging rights up.

Can't hunt, can't brag. And I like bragging so this is no good.

Can I hire you to go kill me some carp hunters? You'll find them up and down the river west of here. There are a bunch of them so don't hesitate to hunt while doing other stuff.

passages.title: Crane Mastery
passages.text: Fantastic. Only thing that would make this hunting trip more entertaining is a chair. Here is the reward I promised you.

passages.title: Gryphon, Down
Tanks for Nothing!
Fly, Spy!
Sea Snakes
passages.text:
The rivers here are crawling with venomous aquatic snakes. Several evacuees were bitten as they fled from the temple, and already some are beginning to succumb to the poison.

We are administering anti-venom as quickly as possible, but we'll need more venom glands.

I won't ask you to remove the glands in the field - that would take too long. Just bring back the heads and I'll take care of the rest.

passages.title: Minimum Safe Distance
A Dish for Ella
passages.text:
Oh my, Shrimp Dumplings? My favorite!

Thank you.

passages.title: A Dish for Chee Chee
passages.text: Oh, Valley Stir Fry. Thanks!

passages.title: A Dish for Sho
passages.text: Ah, this is the best gift you could have given me! A warrior needs her strength.

passages.title: A Dish for Farmer Fung
passages.text: How did you know that this is my favorite dish? Thanks.

passages.title: A Dish for Fish
passages.text: Oh boy, this is my favorite! Thanks, <name>!

passages.title: A Dish for Tina
passages.text: Oh this is my favorite dish! Yum!

passages.title: Walking on Sunwalkers
passages.text:
The tauren!

I refuse to let those flea bitten beasts claim the Pools of Youth for the Horde. None of their races have earned the right to immortality. They are by nature a series of short lived mortals who lack the humility and knowledge of how to properly support a long lived society.

They have infiltrators hunting for the pool. Kill those infiltrators before they find it. Their numbers are small so it shouldn't be that hard to cripple their eyes and ears.

passages.title: My Son...
passages.text:
My son - can you find my son?

When the Jinyu attacked, he ran off in the confusion. I don't know if they've done anything with him, or if he's still alive, even.

Nothing else matters if I can't find him. 

I'd ask Mei... but something's wrong with her. She seems too... impulsive since the attack. I just can't trust that she'd bring him back safely.

passages.title: My Son...
passages.text: So horrible... When I saw the killing, I just ran. My father, Mei... are they alive?

passages.title: Repossession
passages.text:
Of course, the first priority is finding my son. But, if we save ourselves only to starve, then what have we accomplished, in the end?

Please, I need you to recover some of the supplies that the Jinyu took from our caravan.

passages.title: Repossession
passages.text: Have you found the supplies?

passages.title: Repossession
passages.text: Thank you... we will eat now, at least.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text:
From the moment I first rose from the river, I knew I was destined to be Waterspeaker.

I was taught many rituals, and have performed all of them, save one.

There was one, an extremely ancient one, that we were told to call upon if our people ever turned against us. 

This must have happened in our people's distant past, because we haven't needed to use it in our village's memory.

I suppose now is the time to do so.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text: That... was not what I expected.

passages.title: The Ritual
passages.text: I see now that this ritual rips whatever was controlling the minds of these creatures from them. I now know what we must do.

passages.title: Comin' Round the Mountain
passages.text:
The mountain pass is very dangerous. You need much luck to survive. Nephew Bentnail will show you the way.

Perhaps today is a lucky day to travel though. Wind blows from the east; this is good sign. Grummles always travel best when east wind blows.

Climb in the cart when you are ready to leave.

passages.title: Comin' Round the Mountain
passages.text: You must be very lucky to survive the pass!

passages.title: Comin' Round the Mountain
passages.text: You've arrived just in time, <class>! I was starting to think I would die up here!

passages.title: The Missing Muskpaw
passages.text:
What the heck are you supposed to be? |5<class>? Never heard of one of them. You here to help or to steal my yaks?

Look, if yer' insistin' on helpin' out, go find my boy. He got himself grabbed by a bunch of sprites and probably doesn't even know we lost the ranch.

They dragged him off to Pranksters' Hollow south east of here. Go rescue him an' I'll see about giving you a reward of some sort.

passages.title: The Missing Muskpaw
passages.text: Thank you for the save, stranger!

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text:
Yaungols! They come through here taking what they want and destroying whatever's left.

I can't have these thugs destroy the last pieces of the Yak Wash here. It's all my boy and I have left.

Head over to our old ranch and dish out some pain on them yaungols. I bet if you kill enough of them they'll think twice before attacking anything in this area.

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text:
Oh, before I forget, I have something I was asked to deliver to you. A letter from one of your companions, I assume.

I was made to understand that your presence was urgently required, so I took the liberty of arranging your passage.

Speak to Ginsa Arroweye just south of here when you're ready. She has a kite waiting.

passages.title: Get Back Here!
passages.text:
Throm-Ka, <name>!

I hope you were able to gather useful information while on your journey through the forest.

Our preperations are almost complete, but your help is needed.

passages.title: Tummy Trouble
passages.text:
I like Farmer Yoon just dandy as a neighbor, but getting my vote is another matter entirely. He does know that my father is the head of the Union, right?

Anyway, I've got bigger problems to worry about. Lotta folks been getting sick from eating bad vegetables.

Since they bought the produce from my market, my reputation is in jeopardy.

Now I've got an idea to cure the stomach rumbles, but it ain't pretty.

If you'd be willing to... um... hurry things along, I just might be indebted to you.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote II: The Real Culprits
passages.text:
What are YOU doing here, citypaw?

Look, I've got my hands full with a break-in at my shed to the west. Some rascals came in the middle of the night and ransacked the place.

I've got missing seeds, broken tools, and eaten inventory to deal with.

I'll just add it to my list of other troubles: a whole wagon of melons stolen, a broken water pump, animals ruining my harvest...

I wish that I could just get to the bottom of all this already!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote II: The Real Culprits
passages.text: Hmmm, I'm sorry to hear that Haohan's up to his neck in trouble. Thank you for bringing me this news. Maybe we can help him out.

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: Knock on Wood
passages.text:
Sure! I know just the wagon that you're talkin' about!

I can fix it right up, but I'll need wood.

There's a whole lot of it down at the bottom of the lake. If you fish it right out - haha, get it? Fish? Oh I just crack myself up sometimes.

Anyway, you bring me here some 'o that wood and then I'll get right to work!

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: Knock on Wood
passages.text: That lake is plum full o' treasures! You just gotta know what to look for.

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: Knock on Wood
passages.text: Aww yeah, this wood'll do jus' fine. You did good, <name>.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote V: Chief Yip-Yip
passages.text:
You ready for the final step of the plan?

The leader of the Kunzen hozen is a brute by the name of Chief Yip-Yip. It's said that he is nearly impervious to pain.

I've injected the melons with a toxic mixture, so don't try eating them!

Once you get his attention, throw these melons onto the ground. Yip-Yip won't be able to resist a sweet striped melon.

When he takes a bite, he'll be temporarily weakened, and you should find yourself an opening to attack.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote V: Chief Yip-Yip
passages.text: The hozen chief is dead? Our plan worked, <name>!

passages.title: A Second Hand
passages.text:
Despite your best efforts, the work is starting to pile up around here.

Perhaps you could ask one of your best friends if they'd like to help out at Sunsong Ranch.

passages.title: A Second Hand
passages.text: It's a sturdy rake.

passages.title: A Second Hand
passages.text: The talismans on the shrine tinkle softly in the wind.

passages.title: FLAG - Weed War Training
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs. I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: FLAG - Pest Problems Training
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs. I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: Blanche's Boomer Brew
passages.text:
Can you smell it in the air? A storm is brewing! And so am I!

Meet me at the hilltop when the storm hits and together we'll whip up a keg of my most famous brew. Can I count on your help?

passages.title: Blanche's Boomer Brew
passages.text:
None too shabby, my <class> friend! We've saved the monastery and still have half a keg left.

Thank you for your help!

passages.title: The Late Mrs. Muskpaw
passages.text:
This well worn trinket has several markings on it confessing love and adoration from the late Mrs. Muskpaw.

Perhaps Lao would like his wife's trinket back.

passages.title: The Late Mrs. Muskpaw
passages.text: Oh, and what have you there.

passages.title: The Late Mrs. Muskpaw
passages.text:
Ya never know how much you can lose until you've lost it. My wife passed a few seasons ago, but I can tell you this is a day when I could use her smile the most.

At least she doesn't have to see what these yaungol did to her beloved ranch.

passages.title: Shocking!
passages.text:
Have you ever had a fresh dojani eel <name>? No?

Well you have not lived then! Head north up to the dojani river and fish up a few for us. Be careful, those eels can zap you if you're not careful!

passages.title: Shocking!
passages.text: Were you able to catch the eels?

passages.title: Shocking!
passages.text: These look like some tasty eels <name>!  I'm sure you will love them!

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text:
For now, the yaungol invaders seem content to steal yaks. Surveying the area, however, you notice they could easily move on the Yak Wash at any moment.

Thinning their numbers may help show the yaungol that this area is protected.

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text: Them yak stealing, ranch smashing, bad breath yaungols gotta learn a thing or two about attacking decent folk.

passages.title: Yakity Yak
passages.text:
Well then, I am mighty grateful for you culling some of those yaungols for us.

Hopefully your little display of authority will be enough to discourage them from coming over here.

passages.title: Wrecking the Wreck
passages.text:
To dislodge the alliance ship, we need to find our engineer. He parted ways with us when we were escaping the wreckage.

You should be able to find him somewhere in the western forest. Tell him Korga sent you and he'll get in line to help.

passages.title: Wrecking the Wreck
passages.text:
Korga sent you, eh? Well, I wouldn't mind doing a number on that ship for my own reasons anyway, but it's going to take some work.

Give me a moment to think...

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text:
We can help you get your ship free, but we'll need more of the explosives we were trying to take back from the Alliance to make it happen.

I ordered the men to grab all the explosives they could before making our escape. If you sift through the wreckage and bodies to our south, there should be some explosive bundles among them, those that didn't already blow up anyway.

Get me enough of them and I think I can put something together for ya.

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text:
You're in one piece. That's a good sign.

Did you get your hands on what I asked for?

passages.title: Handle With Care
passages.text: More than enough. I've got the main control panel constructed. We should be ready very soon!

passages.title: Preying on the Predators
passages.text:
The forest has become far more dangerous ever since Shen-zin Su began shaking. The tigers are agitated and have begun attacking the refugees, and on occasion, me as well.

If these injured and weak survivors are to make it to safety here at the hut, we need to help clear the forest for them.

passages.title: Preying on the Predators
passages.text: Grim work. I've lived in peace with these tigers for as long as I can remember.

passages.title: Preying on the Predators
passages.text: These survivors are in your debt, <class>.

passages.title: Profiting off of the Past
passages.text:
Let me guess, you're here to deal with the mogu statues that are being reanimated. What a coincidence, I'm here to, um... conduct research on the mogu.

I tell you what, if you bring me as many of the mogu relics in there that you can carry, I'll give you a cut. Of the research... funding.

passages.title: Profiting off of the Past
passages.text: Where am I going to be able to put all of the relics?

passages.title: Profiting off of the Past
passages.text:
Wow! I mean, wow! Thank you, <name>!

Now that you've softened them up, I'm thinking that I might head in. Just a few more relics from around the outskirts. Nothing dangerous.

passages.title: A Zandalari Troll?
passages.text:
While you've been destroying the reanimated mogu statues, the unmistakable accent of a Zandalari troll has been taunting you.

It's clear that the threat to Westerly Rest will not end until he's been dealt with.

passages.title: Instant Courage
passages.text:
It is very bad fortune to travel mountain paths without a good guide. We grummles make the best guides, but many have run away. They fear the mountain pass now. Many good grummles disappear up there.

Grummles are good at many things, but are not very brave. Maybe with fire lotus incense you can make them brave. Then they will show you the way.

passages.title: Instant Courage
passages.text: Did you find the hiding guides?

passages.title: Instant Courage
passages.text: Incense works like a charm! Effects will not last long, so you must hurry!

passages.title: The Rabbitsfoot
passages.text:
The Broketooth hozen stole our Rabbitsfoot! He was the grummle with the biggest luckydo.

This is very bad fortune indeed. Please, <race>, we need our Rabbitsfoot back. We need his good fortune back.

Can you search the Broketooth Outpost for him?

passages.title: The Rabbitsfoot
passages.text:
Look what Broketooths and Knucklethumps did to grummle waystation. Hardly a luckydo to be found.

Grummles had a deal with the hozen. We give them food, and they don't ravage. Whenever they think to ravage, Shado-Pan remind them not to ravage.

But all of Shado-Pan are away defending the wall now. And the hozen want more food than the grummles have.

passages.title: Breaking Broketooth
passages.text:
Hozen only ravage when they think their supplies are too few for their number of mouths.

Problem is, hozen always have more mouths than food.

We have very few grummles these days.

It is a hard thing to ask, but can you be a friend to grummles, and destroy some of the Broketooth hozen south of here? It is the only way to prevent them from destroying the landscape.

passages.title: Breaking Broketooth
passages.text: Thank you, <name>! Hopefully that will slow the Broketooth ravage.

passages.title: Lucky Yakshoe
passages.text:
While you were gone, I saw a group of grummles coming down the Burlap Trail. It was led by my Brother Yakshoe.

But then the Knucklethumps attacked. They took my brother and his grummles north.

Please, adventurer! Save my brother. He always has bad fortune and no luck, but he is my brother. Look for him at the alter in front of Fort Silverback.

passages.title: Lucky Yakshoe
passages.text:
Good fortune for me to be saved by a luckydo like you.

And Brother Rabbitsfoot always say I not have good fortune. Bah!

passages.title: Unleash The Yeti!
passages.text:
Your yeti ride gave me an idea. The Ook of Dook has a pet yeti he named Chomp Chomp.

He uses this yeti to scare other hozen in to making him the leader hozen. We need to get rid of that yeti.

Go to Dooker Dome northwest of here and defeat some of the Cagemasters so Chomp Chomp is not tied up as much.

Yakshoe and I will meet you there with lots of incense and a dirty yak.

passages.title: Unleash The Yeti!
passages.text: We found a yak. Did you take out some hozen?

passages.title: Unleash The Yeti!
passages.text: Ready for the yeti?

passages.title: A Zandalari Troll?
passages.text:
While you've been destroying the reanimated mogu statues, the unmistakable accent of a Zandalari troll has been taunting you.

It's clear that the threat to Westerly Rest will not end until he's been dealt with.

passages.title: FLAG - Player Began Finale
passages.text:
Oh, hello. Are you looking for the owner of this place? Then look to the pandaren up at the top of the stairs. I'm just a visitor... like you.

Now if you'll excuse me, my friends and I trying to decide something. We can talk again afterwards.

passages.title: Sudden, Unexpected Crocolisk Aggression
passages.text:
Normally, my day consists of catching fish, and then eating the fish I caught, followed by sleeping. Note that I did not include "fight with a crocolisk" in that list of activities.

You look like a handy <class>. Can you go get rid of some of these crocolisks, so I can get back to my regular routine? The crocolisks normally keep to themselves up at Kea Krak, to the northwest.

passages.title: Sudden, Unexpected Crocolisk Aggression
passages.text: What would make the crocs attack like this?

passages.title: Sudden, Unexpected Crocolisk Aggression
passages.text:
Yesterday, we were fishing happily. Today, the crocs just started... tryin' to eat us.

Strange.

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
Thank the heavenly spirits for you, <class>! I don't know how much longer I could've lasted.

There are other Firebough Nook survivors, I'm sure of it. Will you help rescue them and get us to the safety of Shado-Pan Fallback?

passages.title: Balance Without Violence
passages.text: Some of the fish that the Unga hozen have gathered don't seem do be dead yet. There may still be time to throw them back into the water.

passages.title: Buried Hozen Treasure
passages.text:
The map you hold is crinkled, dirty, and poorly drawn, but you can see a big X on a beach.

Is there buried treasure somewhere on this island?

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
Oh thank you, thank you, thank you. If you hadn't come along...

Wait! There must be other survivors in the Nook like me!

Please, <class>, I beg you. Rescue the rest of my citizens and deliver us safely to Shado-Pan Fallback.

passages.title: Holed Up
passages.text:
Oh, thank you! There's no way I could have made it back on my own.

Come to think of it, there must be others around Firebough Nook that need to be rescued. Shall we go collect them and then head to the safety of Shado-Pan Fallback?

passages.title: Misery
passages.text:
While you are in the water below, you should slay Nahassa, the mortbreath patriarch. He suffers. I can feel his death cries ululating up to the surface of the lagoon.

Find his cave, and put him out of his misery. Not because it will solve Marista's crocolisk problem. Simply out of mercy.

passages.title: Misery
passages.text: Please, <name>. Even the great beasts of this world have a right to die in dignity.

passages.title: Misery
passages.text: Nahassa's fevered suffering has come to an end.

passages.title: Provoking the Trolls
passages.text:
We've managed to push them back this far, but I doubt that we will remain safe for long if we do not deal with them once and for all.

My husband, coward or fool that he is, does not wish to provoke them. I will not be cowed so.

We will do just that. Slay their forward scouts. Perhaps we can provoke - and then defeat - their leader.

passages.title: Destroy the Leaders
passages.text:
And, now they fear you.

Their leaders, a Blademaster and a Mage, lie deeper in the ruins. Kill them.
Make them hurt. For us.

passages.title: Chasing Hope
passages.text:
Chi-Ji is always with us. Even when he is not here in the Cradle, pieces of his spirit run through the forests and beaches of the island, watching us and testing us.

Prove your dexterity in the eyes of Chi-Ji, <name>. Find and catch the spirits of the crane.

passages.title: Chasing Hope
passages.text: Return when you are finished, <name>. Now go!

passages.title: Chasing Hope
passages.text: Chi-Ji smiles on you.

passages.title: Students of Chi-Ji
passages.text:
Our order prides itself on excellence in combat. We hone these combat skills by dueling one another, here on the Cradle of Chi-Ji.

Prove yourself in the eyes of the Red Crane. Venture south, into the center of the island, and duel with your fellow students.

passages.title: Students of Chi-Ji
passages.text: Your trial is not yet complete, <name>.

passages.title: Students of Chi-Ji
passages.text: With every battle - a win or a loss - you improve. You become faster, hardier, cleverer... better.

passages.title: Minh Do-Tan
passages.text:
Your next challenger is another relatively new trainee. His name is Minh Do-Tan, and he has won his last two matches.

He will be waiting for you near the crane statue to the south.

passages.title: Minh Do-Tan
passages.text: Fight hard, <name>.

passages.title: Minh Do-Tan
passages.text: Well done, <name>. You are beginning to make a name for yourself.

passages.title: Julia Bates
passages.text:
We welcome all kinds here within the Cradle, as long as they recognize and subscribe to the ideologies of the Red Crane. One of our new, more exotic trainees comes from the human kingdoms to the northeast. She goes by the rather foreign-sounding name of Julia Bates.

She is your next challenger. You will find her on the island's western shore.

passages.title: Julia Bates
passages.text: Another fight handily won. I anxiously await your next match, <name>.

passages.title: Dextrous Izissha
passages.text:
