passages.text: Cutting down the outgrowth will merely buy us some time. Have you found any suspicious pieces?

passages.title: To Harvest Chaos
passages.text:
<Naralex slowly takes the squirming heart from you, visibly disturbed.>

I've been a fool. The one truth I did not want to accept has been staring me in the face this entire time...this foul thing is proof of that.

You and I have much work to do.

passages.title: Don't Stop Bereavin'
passages.text:
For a moment, I thought my hatred had stilled. My wife laid to rest, a final offering of the blood of her murderers to quell her tortured spirit. I thought perhaps peace would appeal to me.

I was wrong.

I will not rest now until every single filthy, squealing, murderous quilboar lays dead and broken! I cannot kill them fast enough with my own two hands. Go and slay more for me, <race>.

passages.title: Don't Stop Bereavin'
passages.text: Good. Take your reward; this is only a prelude.

passages.title: Concern for Mankrik
passages.text:
I would ask a favor of you, <class>.

A warrior named Mankrik passed through our camp not long ago, on a lonely journey. His wife was killed by the quilboar, long ago, and he still seeks revenge. I cannot forget his eyes...burning with inconsolable hatred, every waking moment.

We did not talk long, but I cannot bear to think of him out there alone. Please, bring this to Mankrik, and tell him it is from me...

passages.title: Concern for Mankrik
passages.text:
<Mankrik snarls.>

What is it!? I'm busy!

passages.title: Concern for Mankrik
passages.text:
Mahka sent you?

<Mankrik's fury quells for a moment.>

It is a small comfort. But nothing can console me until I am done here.

passages.title: Blood of the Barrens
passages.text:
This bright red stone, found clutched in the grasp of a quilboar, has been carefully carved into the likeness of a great boar, with thorny vines sprouting from its back. Its surface is smooth and worn with care.

Did the quilboar make this? If you find others, maybe one of the shaman at Firestone Point could tell you more about them.

passages.title: Blood of the Barrens
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Blood of the Barrens
passages.text:
These are blood shards. They used to be found all over the Barrens.

It's said they were formed from the blood of Agamaggan, the great demigod that the quilboar sprang from. I knew the quilboar prized them, but nobody would think they'd take the time and care to carve them like this one...

There may be more to learn here.

passages.title: The Rise of the Darkspear
passages.text:
Tha Darkspear tribe have long been victims. Outcasts. We found ourselves fleein' our homes time 'n time again... but dis time, it's not fleein' dat drives us here.

Vol'jin has offered us leadership through wisdom, and it has kept us alive dis long. Now dat same wisdom offers portents of a chaotic future for tha Horde unda Garrosh Hellscream.

No, dis time we not fleein'. Dis time, we are fightin' for a home dat will last.

It's time to begin ya trainin', <name>. Speak with Nortet to the east.

passages.title: The Rise of the Darkspear
passages.text:
Anotha newblood, eh?

Ya actually look ta be in shape though. Steady hands. Fierce eyes. I may be able ta turn ya into a real <class>.

Lets not waste anymore time 'den.

passages.title: Mangletooth
passages.text:
I no longer care for honor or glory, <class>. All that matters to me is that the quilboar die, by any means, at anyone's hand.

Mangletooth, the chief of these filthy Razormane, sits in his lair to the northwest, atop a hill. End his life.

I plan to stay here, and pile these bodies until no more vermin run squealing from the Kraul to face me...

passages.title: Mangletooth
passages.text: Is he dead?

passages.title: Mangletooth
passages.text: Good.  Good! They will all die!  Their chieftains, and their women, and their children, and their foul pets!

passages.title: A Troll's Truest Companion
passages.text:
If ya lookin' for something ta do, we need some more raptors moved over to da pens. If ya head over to da island south of here, you can be meetin' with our caretakers and dey can set ya up.

Dey might appreciate a hand too. Got ta be spreadin' da love, ya know?

passages.title: A Troll's Truest Companion
passages.text: Nice ta see new faces 'round here, mon. It's easy ta get ta feelin' isolated since we left Orgrimmar.

passages.title: Mercy for the Lost
passages.text:
The fiend who stole our raptors has been corruptin' dem with some kind of magic. Now dat dey've grown with dis corruption inside of them, I fear dere's little we can be doin' to save dem outside grantin' them da peace of death. Go ta Zalazane's Fall, northwest of here, an' see da task done.

I hope ya can stomach dae work. I don't tink I could bring myself ta do da deed, even knowin' that it be needed.

passages.title: Mercy for the Lost
passages.text:
Thank you, <class>.

It will be takin' brave and determined people like you ta drive da Darkspear up again. I hope dere are more people even half as dedicated to come.

passages.title: Consort of the Sea Witch
passages.text:
I been investigatin' our corrupted Bloodtalons troubles and I think I've found da source. A lone naga. He was holdin' a red orb aloft over our hatchlings and I could see dem... changin'.

I'm certain he tinks his thievery and spellcastin' have gone unnoticed, so ya should be able ta catch him unawares. Kill dis naga and bring me back dat vile orb - you'll be findin' him to da northwest, at Zalazane's Fall.

passages.title: Consort of the Sea Witch
passages.text: Da naga have been our enemies for a long, long time, and our previous encounters with dem have not gone well. It be clear dat dis time will be different. Tings have changed, and you be part of dat change.

passages.title: Consort of the Sea Witch
passages.text:
Well done, <name>! Dis naga has set us back quite some time, but nothin' will be holdin' us down foreva.

It's good ta be havin' ya wit us, <name>. Ya have a fierce heart within ya.

passages.title: Tauren Vengeance
passages.text:
My people are not wrathful by nature, but sometimes a thirst for justice causes us to take up arms in anger.

My old friend Gann Stonespire, on learning of the butchery in Taurajo, flew into a fury. Tribal elders could no longer hold his rage in check.

Now he has all but parted ways with the Horde. He's gone rogue, <name>, and seeks to lash out at the Alliance with a small band of like-minded partisans.

If you, too, seek vengeance, you will find him southeast of here, at the foot of Bael Modan.

passages.title: Tauren Vengeance
passages.text:
<Gann looks you up and down.>

We could use your help, <class>. But this is not a skirmish. We fight here to strike a killing blow... or die trying.

passages.title: Mahka's Plea
passages.text:
I can't put him out of my mind, <name>. Sometimes at night, I can hear his howls of rage and suffering, echoing across the plains. To imagine him out there, alone and in such pain...

Please, I must ask a favor of you. Go to Mankrik, and tell him to come see me.

passages.title: Mahka's Plea
passages.text: I am sorry to ask this of you, but I want him to come here. He needs to leave that place of death...

passages.title: Mahka's Plea
passages.text: Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Intelligence Warfare
passages.text:
I am convinced the Alliance is using spies to scout the field and pass along information. They knew to strike at Taurajo while the hunters were afield. And they countered every one of Gar'dul's moves like he was an open book.

Well <name>, I for one will not be outplayed. Not here. We will win the battle for intelligence.

Even now I hear reports of Alliance operatives slinking around in the shadows, especially here, outside these very walls. Kill them and bring me back something of use.

passages.title: Intelligence Warfare
passages.text: Watch your back, <class>. They could be anywhere.

passages.title: Intelligence Warfare
passages.text:
Hah! The fool didn't destroy these orders.

Let's see what we can learn...

passages.title: The Basics: Hitting Things
passages.text:
Alright, mon. We start with da basics. I need ta know dat you know how ta swing dat weapon you're totin' around.

Go thrash dose tiki targets. Take it slowly. Natural-like. I'll watch ya fighting form and we'll go from dere.

passages.title: The Basics: Hitting Things
passages.text: Strength isn't da end all of defeating ya enemy, and it most certainly isn't tha end all of stayin' alive. Fightin' is about balance. Everytin has its time and place.

passages.title: The Basics: Hitting Things
passages.text:
Not bad, mon. Ya have a natural flow to ya swings - you may have a talent for dis.

Some rough edges ta be sure, but we'll get dose ironed out here and I'll teach ya a few new tings as we go.

passages.title: A Rough Start
passages.text:
Lets put dose skills ta use. I'll start ya off easy, mon.

There be cats killing our boars. Dat food ain't for sharin'. Dose boars are gonna need ta be alive if ya be wanting food tonight.

Dey're all over the island. Bring me some cat pelts.

passages.title: A Rough Start
passages.text: I doubt dey too much of a challenge, mon, but they'll still claw up ya ankles if ya don't stay quick footed.

passages.title: A Rough Start
passages.text: Dese are some fine pelts, boy. We could make some hefty cloaks outta dese.

passages.title: More Than Expected
passages.text:
Ya definitely more den expected, mon. I'm sure dere's more important stuff we can be usin' ya talents on now. Ya don't need ta hang out with da newbloods no more.

Head down to da village to da southeast and make yaself known. Lend a hand here and there and I'm sure ya make yer way up to sometin' more prestigious quick enough.

passages.title: More Than Expected
passages.text: Ya tha new recruit everyone's talkin' about, eh? Welcome ta tha Darkspear.

passages.title: Echoes of Agamaggan
passages.text:
I think the quilboar are being driven by more than just crude desire. Would you help me look into this further?

To the west, scattered among the quilboar's settlements and camps, I've noticed boar skulls. They gleam from a distance, polished smooth...distinct from the remains littered in their waste piles. I think these may be objects of worship.

Bring me several of these to examine, <name>.

passages.title: Echoes of Agamaggan
passages.text: Do you have the skulls?

passages.title: Echoes of Agamaggan
passages.text:
Yes, these are clearly symbols of Agamaggan. But if the quilboar are still devoted to their dead god, what is the source of their vicious agression?  It is said Agamaggan was noble, and even gave his life fighting the Burning Legion...

A moment, <name>. We must confer with the spirits.

passages.title: Dwarf Fortress
passages.text:
I don't know if you noticed on your way in, but this whole fortress is erected around a giant cannon. If we can just find the ammunition magazine, we could blow this place sky-high as easy as kiss-my-hand!

But to figure it out I'm going to need the fortress schematics, and I haven't been able to steal them yet.

Look for the plans on the lowest floor, right down these stairs.

passages.title: Dwarf Fortress
passages.text:
Give me the plans, quickly! Our time grows short.

Mostly because I've been eating my disguise.

passages.title: Dwarf Fortress
passages.text:
Let's see, let's see.

It looks like the artillery shells are prepped here, then loaded into the secure magazine...

<Weezil rubs his hands together.>

<name>, are you ready to blow some stuff up?

passages.title: Carried on the Waves
passages.text:
The Bloodpetals of Un'Goro have a fascinating life cycle.

These trees in front of us bear seeds that fall down into the river when they mature. The river's current then takes the seed north of here, where the seed hatches - almost like an egg - and a newborn Bloodpetal emerges.

I require these seeds for my studies. Take this net, and use it to scoop up the bright orange seeds in the river. You'll have to hunt them down under the water.

passages.title: Carried on the Waves
passages.text: Have you obtained the seeds yet?

passages.title: Carried on the Waves
passages.text: Hmm... yes, these seeds will do nicely.  You have the gratitude of the Cenarion Circle, <name>.

passages.title: Bouquets of Death
passages.text:
You're already familiar with the first phase of the Bloodpetals' life cycle: the waterborne seed. The next phase, however, is not so docile: the pack of juveniles.

When Bloodpetals hatch, they quickly form gangs and travel together, offsetting their weakness with overwhelming numbers. These packs of young lashers normally keep to themselves, but upset one of them and you upset them all.

For our safety and the safety of others, dispose of them. They roam close by, to the west and north.

passages.title: Bouquets of Death
passages.text: Remember the tale of Archimonde, <class>.  The young lashers are much weaker than you, but they can still overrun you with their numbers.

passages.title: Bouquets of Death
passages.text: You return victorious.  Good, good... perhaps the crater will now be a bit safer to those who travel through it.

passages.title: Flowing to the North
passages.text:
Ithis Moonwarden is the night elf druid who indoctrinated me into the Cenarion Circle. He has set up camp north of here, near the cliffs of the crater's easternmost edge. Follow the flow of the Bloodpetal seeds, and I'll wager you'll find him nearby.

My studies are limited only to seeds and other reagents, but he pursues more advanced matters. If you are curious to learn more about Un'Goro's flora, you should speak with him now.

passages.title: Flowing to the North
passages.text:
Ahh... did Garl send you?  How are his studies coming?  I find that he can be a bit slow at times, but he's truly a force to be reckoned with when he takes the form of the bear.

Now, we have more pressing matters to attend to.

passages.title: Blazerunner
passages.text: I'm still a bit concerned about these fire elementals, <name>. One last request: head to the top of Fire Plume Ridge, and kill the one they call Blazerunner. He's the biggest and strongest of all the fire elementals in the crater. With him gone, I'll be able to sleep much better.

passages.title: Blazerunner
passages.text: At last, Blazerunner is dispatched.  Thanks, <name>... he was driving me batty.

passages.title: Peculiar Delicacies
passages.text:
Hey <bub/sweetie>, interested in making an extra dime?

I've got it on good authority that some interested parties are paying BIG money for silithid legs. Yes, you heard me right, silithid legs! Apparently these things are delicious if you cook them right. They're like underground lobsters, and they live just south of here.

Thing is, I'll need a good amount of them to pay for my overhead. Think you could get me 8 dozen or so?

passages.title: Peculiar Delicacies
passages.text: I need a lot of them because I've got to pay for shipping, handling, marketing... oh, and I've got to pay you as well.

passages.title: Peculiar Delicacies
passages.text:
Brilliant!  We're on the cusp of something big here, <name>.  Here's your share of the inevitably huge profits.

Now, on to other matters...

passages.title: Mossy Pile
passages.text:
Here in Marshal's Stand, I can't really do too much profiteering without arousing suspicion from the scientists. There is, however, another place where I might have use of you.

My business associate, Gremix, has a camp northwest of here, on the opposite side of the volcano. He's a savvy business mind, and has a better eye for profit than even I do. I'm sure he could put you to work, if you'd like to make some more coin.

passages.title: Mossy Pile
passages.text: Very well, if Quixxil recommended you, then I suppose you're alright.  In all our years working together, Quixxil's never steered me wrong.

passages.title: Adventures in Archaeology
passages.text:
Hey, you want to try my new diemetradon dogs? No? Raptor risotto? Pterrordax ptacos?

Fine. Oh, I just remembered! I have a friend nearby that might be able to use your assistance. His name is Spark Nilminer, and he's Marshal Expeditions' chief archaeology officer.

He's been sent out to Golakka Hot Springs, to the west. You'll likely find him on the springs' western shore.

passages.title: Adventures in Archaeology
passages.text: Good ol' Nolen.  How is he doing?  Hopefully better than I am...

passages.title: Gormashh the Glutinous
passages.text:
Hey, I know! We've been looking at the wrong tar creatures.

Gremix once told me about a larger-than-normal tar creature that he ran into. It lurks around the tar pit far to the east of here, south of Fungal Rock. I'll bet that the bigger these creatures get, the stickier they get! We'll make some money yet, <name>!

Don't forget the scraper!

passages.title: Gormashh the Glutinous
passages.text: I'm counting on you, <name>.  I'm invested pretty heavily into this "tar as glue" scheme, and it'd be a shame if you came back empty-handed.

passages.title: Gormashh the Glutinous
passages.text:
Yes, this tar is just the stuff...

Hey, wait a minute, my hands... I can't seem to get them apart...

Maybe this wasn't such a good idea. Oh, but wait! Super sticky tar remover! That's where the real money is!

passages.title: Hard to Harvest
passages.text:
The Lakkari Tar Pits, just north of here, conceal a hidden treasure: rare flowers that grow at the bottom of the pits. These tarblossoms, as they're called, are valued for their beauty and their durability. It's been a while since I last harvested tarblossoms, so there should be some new plants growing at the bottom of the pits. Grab some for me?

By the way, good luck swimming in tar. It's nothing like swimming in water.

passages.title: Hard to Harvest
passages.text: Have you obtained the tarblossoms yet?  I don't see them...

passages.title: Hard to Harvest
passages.text: Oh, there they are.  Great work, handsome!  Here's some gold.  You've earned it.

passages.title: Marshal's Refuse
passages.text:
A big part of making money is shamelessness. You have to be willing to profit off of the misfortune of others. It all ends up boiling down to one question: How much do you love money?

When Marshal and his crew abandoned their refuge up to the north, they left behind lots of supplies. This stuff isn't rare, or even particularly valuable, but it's there if you're willing to take it. His camp is up in the cliffs, to the north.

Oh, and be on the lookout for whatever it was that made them leave...

passages.title: Marshal's Refuse
passages.text: Did you find anything good?

passages.title: Marshal's Refuse
passages.text:
It's a bunch of junk, but it's a bunch of FREE junk, and that's all that matters to me.

Well, mostly free.  Here's your share.  Thanks!

passages.title: An Important Lesson
passages.text:
What ho, traveler! You must know that you set foot upon the camp of Maximillian of Northshire! Mayhap you have heard tales sung of my many exploits? I can see from the look in your eye that you have. That glint of recognition plays upon your visage like the White Lady's reflection o'er Stonecairne Lake.

It is clear to me that you seek adventure. As you seem able enough, and thoroughly well-intentioned, I would offer to make you my squire.

passages.title: An Important Lesson
passages.text: Your first quest is a simple one, yet it somehow remains unfinished.  Endure my words and become my squire.

passages.title: An Important Lesson
passages.text: You please me, <name>.  From this day forward, you are no longer a simple beggar, but a squire loyal to Maximillian of Northshire.  Prepare yourself for our first sally, good squire, for together we shall plunge our fists elbow-deep into what they call adventure!

passages.title: The Evil Dragons of Un'Goro Crater
passages.text:
This crater is filled with a malignant breed of dragon. Have you seen them? They wander all about, parading their spiky backs and lizardy faces all around the Crater.

Don't let them fool you, squire, for these dragons are no minions of graceful Alexstrasza. They are clearly vicious, and direly in need of a hero's blade.

I have decided that I will slay no less than 15 of them. As my squire, you must come along. Should we become separated, you may meet me back here at the Hot Springs.

passages.title: The Evil Dragons of Un'Goro Crater
passages.text:
...and that makes 15 of them.

Justice had a name today... and that name was Maximillian of Northshire.  For Doloria!

passages.title: The Spirits of Golakka Hot Springs
passages.text:
A moment of seriousness now, <name>. We have an important quest ahead of us. The treacherous dragons that plague this valley will not cease their mischief until we destroy their repugnant brood mother. Before we even attempt to complete such a task, we must ask the Light for aid.

I have seen the Light manifest itself nearby, in the form of Spirits floating by the shores of Golakka Hot Springs. Come, I must speak with them, and ask them for aid.

passages.title: The Spirits of Golakka Hot Springs
passages.text:
Might I ask you a question?  What act have you committed to make the spirits so angry at you?  I'm impressed that you had the patience to sit so still while they pummeled you so violently.

Now we may proceed.  The teeth and scales of Un'Goro's greatest dragon await us.

passages.title: The Fossil-Finder 3000
passages.text:
One of the things I hate the most about digging is the fact that half the time, all you find is dirt. That's why I've been spending most of my time out here tinkering instead of digging.

Let me show you what I've invented: the Fossil-Finder 3000. I just put the finishing touches on it. If it works properly, it should find the largest fossils in the area. I know, sweet, huh?

Test it out and see if you can find some ridiculously big dinosaur bones.

passages.title: The Fossil-Finder 3000
passages.text: Have you found anything?  Did it work?

passages.title: The Fossil-Finder 3000
passages.text:
What an interesting femur you've brought here, but why's it all sharp and curvy?

...

Wait a minute, that thing's a TALON?  A dinosaur with a talon that size would've been... well, really big, that's for sure.  Is this the only fossil that you found there?

passages.title: Chasing A-Me 01
passages.text:
Unfortunately, something's happened to one of my greatest inventions. You've seen mechanical squirrels, yes? Well, to get closer to the apes of Un'Goro Crater, I created a mechanical ape to blend in with their kind--I call her A-Me 01.

She has been studying the local wildlife at Fungal Rock for several months, but she should have returned by now. I fear the worst for her.

Can you help me find her?

passages.title: Chasing A-Me 01
passages.text: A-Me lies motionless before you.  No power seems to be running through her components.

passages.title: Returning A-Me 01
passages.text:
Greetings. I unit A-Me 01. You... <race>?

A-Me's mission to study the local gorillas was success. A-Me has gathered data and now will bring to Karna.

It time for A-Me to return to Karna. You come with? We embark right away, so make sure you ready first.

passages.title: Claws of White
passages.text:
Stop, <race>. I could use the help of a <class> like you.

Right outside this camp, there are raptors with deadly claws. I've been using the claws for druid rituals, but it doesn't seem to be working. However, I did notice that some of those raptors sometimes have white claws, when most have deathly black ones.

The earth works in strange ways. Maybe you could fetch me some of the white claws, and I'll try one last time?

passages.title: Claws of White
passages.text: Have you gotten any of the claws yet?

passages.title: Claws of White
passages.text:
My mentor says that sometimes you have to take away from nature before you can give back.  These raptors... I feel that they died for good cause.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Crystals of Power
passages.text:
I'm sure you've noticed 'em, <name>. They're everywhere!

What am I talking about? Why, the crystals, of course!

The crystals... They're all over the crater. Most people ignore them, but I have a strange feeling that they hold power within them.

Say, I'm running a little low on the crystals I have here -- think you might be able to collect some more for me? 

You'll find yellow crystals to the northwest, red crystals to the... oh, I'm sure you'll figure it out.

passages.title: Crystals of Power
passages.text: I just know I'm onto something here, <name>!

passages.title: Crystals of Power
passages.text: Now I will continue my experiments! Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Eastern Pylon
passages.text:
High up in the cliffs above me there is a large crystal pylon. Who placed it there, I cannot say, nor can I determine any reason that it would be built in such a strange place.

Maybe you can make more of it than I can. I personally don't care what it does, so you needn't report back to me, but perhaps one of the scholars in Marshal's Stand might be interested in what you discover.

passages.title: The Eastern Pylon
passages.text: You were right to bring this pylon to my attention, <name>.  This is just the sort of thing I've been studying.

passages.title: The Northern Pylon
passages.text:
You've done us a number of favors, <name>... now let Gremix do one for you. The attacks on Marshal's Refuge were terrible, undoubtedly. They came without warning, and took no prisoners. They were lucky that so many of them survived.

A few weeks ago, I came across a crystal pylon in the cliffs to the northeast of here, east of Marshal's Refuge. I think the pylon and the attacks may be related somehow. Maybe you can investigate? I'm sure someone in Marshal's Stand will thank you.

passages.title: The Northern Pylon
passages.text: You think this may be related to the attacks on Marshal's Refuge, <name>?

passages.title: The Western Pylon
passages.text:
Durrin's research touched on one area that intrigues me: a potential link between the titans and the dinosaurs. J.D. Collie back at camp is always talking about titan this and crystal that... maybe she'd be interested.

Before you report to her, you might want to check out the crystal pylon not far from here. It's just up in the cliffs, to the west of here. It's got crystals on it, and it always seemed to me like it might have something to do with the titans.

passages.title: The Western Pylon
passages.text: A pylon in the west?  And a relationship between titans and dinosaurs?  This is a lot to take in, <name>.

passages.title: Roll the Bones
passages.text:
You'd think that being chief digger for Marshal Expeditions means I like digging. There might be worse things to do in this world... but none really leap to mind.

We were supposed to be digging in Terror Run - FANTASTIC name by the way - for dead stegodons and diemetradons. Well, there are plenty of live ones there too! Wil and Hol are still all about studying this death trap, so we need those dinosaur bones. Between you and me though, bringing some from live ones will work out just as well.

passages.title: Roll the Bones
passages.text: Think whatever you want of me, but they're not going to care if the bones they get to research are from ancient stegodons and diemetradons or the ones that almost devoured us wholesale when we were trying to set up our camps.  I'll just be happy if we get out of here alive...

passages.title: Roll the Bones
passages.text:
Excellent, these should do the trick.  And now, if you'll permit me, in case anyone's listening...

THANKS FOR DIGGING ALL OF THESE BONES OUT OF THE GROUND FOR US AND NOT HURTING THE NATIVE BEASTS IN ANY WAY.

Whether you really did or didn't, I don't want to know.  Let's keep it that way, shall we?  Here - maybe this will keep your lips shut on the whole thing.  Anything to get out of here alive, I say!

passages.title: The Fare of Lar'korwi
passages.text:
Once, a long time ago, a brother of mine took some meat from one of Lar'korwi's kills. He didn't know it at the time, but Lar'korwi saw him from the forest. Lar'korwi followed my brother for days, destroying everything he touched. My brother, scared, finally decided to run from the Crater and leave Lar'korwi behind.

Lar'korwi killed him not far from this spot.

If you want to provoke Lar'korwi, find a fresh kill of his and take some of the meat from it.

Start your search to the west.

passages.title: The Fare of Lar'korwi
passages.text: Do not take my words lightly, <name>. If you truly wish to face this creature, then you must be careful... and smart. It will take a great deal of strength and insight to draw out Lar'korwi and defeat him.

passages.title: The Fare of Lar'korwi
passages.text:
This will do nicely, <name>. It seems Lar'korwi eats well these days. Although, I wonder where he found a threshadon in this area. Odd.

Regardless, I will hold onto this until you are ready for your confrontation with the beast. Do not worry for my safety--I am sure you've angered Lar'korwi enough that he will not kill me until after he's tasted your flesh.

passages.title: The Scent of Lar'korwi
passages.text:
I'm actually surprised he has not come for you yet, <name>. But all is well, for I have a final plan that will bring the monster to us.

Being the dominant male gives Lar'korwi rights to breed with any female he chooses--and he chooses many of them. You'll find many ravasaur eggs to the west of here. Get close to them and you should provoke an attack by his mates. The females produce an awful smell from a gland in their heads that allow males to know they are ready to breed. Bring me two of those glands.

passages.title: The Scent of Lar'korwi
passages.text: Be careful, <name>. Getting close to any nest of eggs surely will provoke the mothers... even if you've already secured a gland from one. The mothers can be just as deadly as Lar'korwi himself when they fight to protect their young. But, if you are successful, then we shall have a definitive way of bringing Lar'korwi out from hiding.

passages.title: The Scent of Lar'korwi
passages.text: Ah, fine specimens, <name>. The two pieces you've found should be perfect for baiting Lar'korwi into the open. I cannot wait to see the outcome of your fight with the monster. He is a massive thing with claws as sharp as the finest blades. You will look into his eyes and you will know death.

passages.title: Lost!
passages.text:
You've got to help me, <name>! My friend, Ringo left earlier to explore the volcano to the north of here, and he has been gone way too long. I am really worried about him.

Do you think you could find him? Why don't you take my canteen with you -- if you do find Ringo, I'm sure he'll need it!

passages.title: Lost!
passages.text: Ringo's sack rests on the rock in front of you.

passages.title: Lost!
passages.text: You find what appears to be Ringo's belongings.  If he left these here, he can't have gone far away.  Maybe you should look for him.

passages.title: Super Sticky
passages.text:
I'm always looking for a quick way to earn a gold, <name>. If you help me with my newest idea, I'll let you in on a little of the profit. How does that sound to you?

I thought so!

We're going to be making some glue. Head to the tar pits just north of here, and collect me some tar. Not just any tar, now, you'll need to get it from the beasts that live around the tar pits. As a bonus, if you use my tar scraper on their corpses, you'll keep your hands nice and clean.

passages.title: Super Sticky
passages.text: Tara's done it again -- this super sticky glue will be all the rage!

passages.title: Super Sticky
passages.text: Yeah, this tar is pretty sticky, I guess.  I mean, it's sticky, but it's not "make fistfuls of money" sticky.  I guess I'll have to keep thinking.

passages.title: Williden's Journal
passages.text: You have uncovered a mangled journal. Parts of it remain legible, with a Williden Marshal claiming ownership over the contents therein. If the journal is accurate, then Williden may be found somewhere in the central part of the Crater; according to the journal, he and his companions sought to take a more offensive stance once their refuge was attacked.

passages.title: The Rise of the Darkspear
passages.text:
Tha Darkspear tribe have long been victims. Outcasts. We found ourselves fleein' our homes time 'n time again... but dis time, it's not fleein' dat drives us here.

Vol'jin has offered us leadership through wisdom, and it has kept us alive dis long. Now dat same wisdom offers portents of a chaotic future for tha Horde unda Garrosh Hellscream.

No, dis time we not fleein'. Dis time, we are fightin' for a home dat will last.

It's time to begin ya trainin', <name>. Speak with Soratha to the east.

passages.title: The Rise of the Darkspear
passages.text:
Anotha newblood, eh?

Ya actually have an intense look about ya though. Fiery eyes. You might have the makings of a real <class>.

Lets not waste anymore time 'den.

passages.title: The Basics: Hitting Things
passages.text:
Alright, mon. We start simple. I need ta know dat you know the basics of the arcane arts.

Go thrash dose tiki targets. Take it slowly. Natural-like. I'll watch how you form your casts and we'll go from dere.

passages.title: The Basics: Hitting Things
passages.text:
Not bad, mon. Ya have a natural flow to ya spells - you may have a talent for dis.

Some rough edges ta be sure, but we'll get dose ironed out here and I'll teach ya a few new tings as we go.

passages.title: A Rough Start
passages.text:
Lets put dose skills ta use. I'll start ya off easy, mon.

There be cats killing our boars. Dat food ain't for sharin'. Dose boars are gonna need ta be alive if ya be wanting food tonight.

Dey're all over the island. Bring me some cat pelts.

passages.title: A Rough Start
passages.text: I doubt dey too much of a challenge, mon, but they'll still claw up ya ankles if ya don't stay quick footed.

passages.title: A Rough Start
passages.text: Dese are some fine pelts, boy. We could make some hefty cloaks outta dese.

passages.title: More Than Expected
passages.text:
Ya definitely more den expected, mon. I'm sure dere's more important stuff we can be usin' ya talents on now. Ya don't need ta hang out with da newbloods no more.

Head down to da village to da southeast and make yaself known. Lend a hand here and there and I'm sure ya make yer way up to sometin' more prestigious quick enough.

passages.title: More Than Expected
passages.text: Ya tha new recruit everyone's talkin' about, eh? Welcome ta tha Darkspear.

passages.text:
As ya' start to get da hang of tings, ya gonna figure out how ta do new tricks.

One of da' first ya gonna learn is to keep a steady hand between shots, or else ya gonna find yaself exhausted and not really managin' to kill much.

Go get some more experience 'till ya figure it out, 'den come back and try it out. Let me know when ya tink you have it down.

passages.title: The Arts of a Hunter
passages.text: Good work, mon! Dis stuff come easy to ya.

passages.title: Speak With Spraggle
passages.text:
My good friend Spraggle has been fretting about something for some time now. I'd help her, but as you can see, I'm pretty comfortable right now.

Could you check in with her and see what she needs?

passages.title: Speak With Spraggle
passages.text: What?  Krakle sent you?

passages.title: Winnoa Pineforest
passages.text:
While we've accomplished much here, it would be a tragedy if part of this corruption has escaped our notice. The corridors of the Wailing Cavern stretch throughout the entire Barrens, and if another spot of wild energy has made its way to the surface...

You've done enough for me, though. I would simply ask that you let a fellow druid of mine know of what's happened here. You will find Winnoa Pineforest at Vendetta Point, southwest of here.

passages.title: Winnoa Pineforest
passages.text:
I could feel what occured from here, <class>. It bristled every hair I have.

I'm overjoyed to hear you succeeded in pushing those horrors back, and I'll be sure to scour the area for any stray deviate creatures.

passages.title: No More Mercy
passages.text:
Da naga have committed great atrocities on our people. Da time ta show dem mercy has long passed.

Enter da cave and kill any naga you find dere. Every naga dead dis day is one less naga ta take us unawares later on. I trust ya will be thorough.

passages.title: No More Mercy
passages.text: Well fought, young <race>.

passages.title: Territorial Fetish
passages.text:
Dis is no casual counter-attack. We be fully intendin' ta slaughter every last naga here and do anything we can ta ensure that dey will have no desire ta return.

I want ya ta place dese fetishes on any Spitescale banner ya be findin' inside their cave. It should prove a clear statement of what we think of their presence here. More dan dat, da magic in dese fetishes will be weakenin' any Spitescale dat approach, which should make dem second guess stayin' on our isle.

passages.title: Territorial Fetish
passages.text: Dat should keep dem at bay.

passages.title: The Disturbed Earth
passages.text:
We are here to monitor the scars of the land, and watch for further signs of instability. While we haven't seen any yet, a cataclysmic aftershock could devastate the Barrens even further.

To the northeast, near the chasm, earth elementals rampage out of control. To soothe the earth, these need to occasionally be destroyed, and their essence returned in a ritual. If you help us do this, <class>, I would be happy to reward you.

passages.title: The Disturbed Earth
passages.text: The elements must be carefully balanced, so returning the essence is key.  I hope you've been collecting it...

passages.title: The Disturbed Earth
passages.text: Thank you, friend. It's important we try to calm this earth in every way we can.

passages.title: Our Tribe, Imprisoned
passages.text:
Despite their size, the Bristleback greatly outnumber us. A pack ambush can easily overwhelm even the largest tauren.

Many new initiates have taken up arms to defend our home. Some have given their lives, but others have been captured alive.

Please, find their cages and free them. The battle should keep the quilboar distracted.

passages.title: Our Tribe, Imprisoned
passages.text: Not enough have returned, <name>. Return and free more of our people. Be brave!

passages.title: Our Tribe, Imprisoned
passages.text: Thanks to you, our people are free to fight for our home.

passages.title: Aberrant Flora
passages.text:
Look how strangely the plant life reacts to the bloodpetals in the Roiling Gardens to the north. The trees are enveloped with more flowers and vines than usual. Large, sporous blossoms project themselves from the ground where they once did not.

The land is speaking to us, <race>. The bloodpetals are destroying the balance.

As my final task, I ask you to visit the swarming adult bloodpetals and prune their numbers.

passages.title: Aberrant Flora
passages.text: We cannot move forward until you have put an end to the bloodpetals, <class>.

passages.title: Aberrant Flora
passages.text:
The scent of bloodpetal pollen hangs about your head, <class>.  This is good.

You've earned your reward.

passages.title: Profitable Preservation
passages.text:
You know, the naga are the mutated and prettier versions of the kaldorei, better known as the night elves. Don't ask me... it's a long story.

Suffice to say that I'm sure you could 'procure' an artifact or two while you're down there in the ruins. If you know what I mean?

We have to preserve them in the homes of wealthy collectors everywhere! Right?

passages.title: Last Rites, First Rites
passages.text:
The camp is safe, and the quilboar driven off, all thanks to you, young one. You have my personal thanks for what you have done for my mother, my son, and for all of us.

It is now time to put Greatmother Hawkwind to rest. Lay the final offering at her feet, <name>, and we will say our goodbyes.

passages.title: Last Rites, First Rites
passages.text: Do not be shy, <name>. I am honored to have you lay the final offering.

passages.title: Last Rites, First Rites
passages.text: There is balance in all things. As Greatmother Hawkwind's spirit takes its final journey, you will begin your first.

passages.title: Running the Gauntlet
passages.text:
Look around you, <class>. We've had no luck dislodging the Horde from the hidden trails that overlook this valley. They appear out of nowhere to ambush our supply caravans and then disappear into the hills!

I need you to run the gauntlet to Honor's Stand and let them know the roads still aren't safe. Talk to Mattingly, the supplies officer by the gate.

And kill a few of these brutes along the way!

passages.title: Running the Gauntlet
passages.text: They're ambushing the roads to Stonetalon, too? We just can't get a break here. Where are they coming from, anyways?

passages.title: Is This Stuff Still Good?
passages.text:
You find what appears to be a crate of food, left behind when this camp was abandoned. On the outside of the crate, you can make out a stamp that says "PROPERTY OF MARSHAL EXPEDITIONS".

Perhaps you might find someone who could use this?

passages.title: Is This Stuff Still Good?
passages.text: What have you got there?

passages.title: Is This Stuff Still Good?
passages.text:
Oh... wow... it's some really old food.  Hey Hol'anyee, take a look at this!  This <race> brought us those old rations that we abandoned!

No, not from Marshal's Refuge... from the old base camp!

I'm not sure I want to peek inside.  I'll just give it to Nolen, I guess... he'll know what to do with it.

passages.title: An Abandoned Research Camp
passages.text:
You find what appears to be a piece of research equipment, left behind when this camp was abandoned. Chiseled onto the side of the device are the words "PROPERTY OF MARSHAL EXPADISHUNS".

Perhaps you might find someone who could use this?

passages.title: An Abandoned Research Camp
passages.text: Yes, <name>?

passages.title: An Abandoned Research Camp
passages.text:
Well I'll be... that's Shizzle's old portable dinomometer!  Where did you find this?

I'm surprised it's still functional, even after all these years.  I'll have it delivered to Shizzle promptly.

passages.title: [NOT USED] Lumberjack Slam Placeholder
passages.text:
Placeholder, <name>! This is a placeholder lumberjack quest. You? Grab that lumberjack. And do something ... placeholder-y with him.

You heard me.

passages.title: Going, Going, Guano!
passages.text:
There be more in the Razorfen than just pigs, <bruddah/sistah>. There be bats as well...and if you're goin in there and rilin' up the quilboar anyway, I want ya to bring me back some guano.

Yah, guano. The droppin's. Don't give me that look. It be foul, but powerful, primal stuff for rituals...rituals to keep the earth 'round here strong enough to keep from rippin' apart under all the damn fools warrin' round here.

Just bring Zan'do one pile of guano, yah?

passages.title: Returning a Favor
passages.text:
You know, while you were out doin' your thing, Megs stopped by here. I hadn't seen her in months, but she barely gave me the time of day, just wanted me to tell you she had more business lined up.

She said she was headed over to the Dunemaul Compound to set up shop, something about ogres. Since you're done here, might as well head over...I wouldn't keep a goblin like her waiting.

passages.title: Returning a Favor
passages.text: I've got a great one for you this time, <name>. We're gonna initiate these ogres into the Horde...working directly under us.

passages.title: Seaside Salvage
passages.text:
We've got to get goods moving in this market ASAP if we want to be competitive. I've got an angle for us.

Gadgetzan's under blockade by pirates, but plenty of the goods that get blown off the ships survive intact... they just wash away. Most of them wash up in the shallows just south of town.

Head down there and start salvaging; there's crates full of pure profit just floating around down there.

passages.title: Seaside Salvage
passages.text: Let's see what you've got.

passages.title: Seaside Salvage
passages.text:
Hmm, mostly usable. This is good stuff. I've already got buyers lined up, of course.

Here's your advance for the rest of the work you're gonna do for me and the Bilgewater Cartel...partner.

passages.title: Puddle Stomping
passages.text:
Here's the situation. If we want to establish the Bilgewater Cartel's market presence in Gadgetzan, we'll need to start providing services to the community.

The new coast has been great for business here, but the sea also brought sea giants with it. They're large, foul, and drive real estate values down.

Head to the shallows just south of town and kill as many as you can, and I'll cut you in on some of the deals I'm brokering here.

passages.title: Puddle Stomping
passages.text:
Property values have already gone up since you left. People like seafront views that don't include briny, gnarled giants stomping around.

Here's your cut, <name>.

passages.title: [NOT USED] Build the Fort Placeholder
passages.text: Nice work! For our next placeholder, talk to that dude. Uh, Foreman Franklin. Special stuff will happen.

passages.title: [NOT USED] Protect the Pass Placeholder
passages.text: This here placeholder will be like a shootin' gallery. On Steroids.

passages.title: Tropical Paradise Beckons
passages.text:
Hey, you look like a discriminating adventurer. Are you looking for something different? Something exotic? Something... profitable?

Well shake the sand out of your boots, because I've got a proposition for you. Williden Marshal is looking for competent sellswords such as yourself. He's set up camp at Marshal's Stand, just southeast of the volcano in the center of lush Un'Goro Crater.

Then again, paradise isn't for everyone, <race>. It's up to you. Your tropical oasis awaits.

passages.title: Tropical Paradise Beckons
passages.text:
Hey Hol'anyee, look at the getup on this one!

<Williden turns to face you.>

Ahem.  Our recruiter sent you?  Good.  Let's start out with a bit of honesty: Un'Goro isn't the perfect nirvana that you may have been promised.  You've probably figured that out on the way over here, though.

Shall we get to work?

passages.title: Remember the Light
passages.text:
Magtoor grows weaker by the second, <name>. My remedy is prepared... it must work. It must!

You have done so much for the both of us. I would be honored if you stayed for what may be Magtoor's final moments.

passages.title: Remember the Light
passages.text:
I am moved, <name>. Prophet Velen has been in closely guarded seclusion. He has dared not waste his energy on anything save preparing for the final confrontation he has foretold.

And yet, he came here, in person, to comfort a single dying soul.

I must thank you as well, for helping me make my last effort to comfort my friend. My research will continue... and I hope that Magtoor will continue to watch over me.

passages.title: Report to Aubrey
passages.text:
You there! Fresh off the boat? Welcome to Kalimdor, a land hellbent to kill you or die tryin'.

There's trouble at the hold - as I'm sure you noticed on your way in. Admiral Aubrey needs all hands on deck if we're to make it through this. Consider yourself drafted, <class>!

Follow the road up the hill and you'll find Aubrey in the tower, topside.

passages.title: Report to Aubrey
passages.text:
Hm? What unit are you with, <class>?

No matter, we need all hands. My fleet is in tatters and they've broken into the hold. You armed? That's good enough for me.

passages.title: Gazer Tag
passages.text:
You're going out to hunt hyenas, eh? If you don't mind, I've got an offer myself. I'm in need of eyes from the Glasshide Gazers that lurk to the north. Their eyes contain wonderful crystals, valuable to...collectors.

Now, you may have heard that some sad individuals use these to enhance paramental abilities, but I assure you, my interests are purely academic!

Bring me a good portion of them and I'll pay you well for them. Better than these copper-pinching goblins will, at least!

passages.title: Gazer Tag
passages.text: Do, ah, do you have them?

passages.title: Gazer Tag
passages.text:
Ahh, perfect! Just what I need...full of potent focusing energies...

...ahem! I mean, perfect for my collection! Narain Soothfancy is in no need of artificial enhancement of any kind!

Now take your pay and be off!

passages.title: Cutting Losses
passages.text:
I've spent the last week starin' at this ugly pit trying to think of how to exploit a bunch of dangerous, violent arthropods for profit. Now I'm out of ideas, and starving.

These things are a wash, and I say it's time to start clearing them out. Head down into that pit and start killin' bugs.

passages.title: Cutting Losses
passages.text: This isn't goin' fast enough. There's gotta be a faster way...

passages.title: Chicken of the Desert
passages.text:
I've got an idea, but we're going to need bait.

The other day I saw a rabid blisterpaw hyena wander too close to the edge of the chasm, and one of the silithid comes diving out of nowhere. Nearly swallowed it whole! Horrible sight.

So we're gonna need hyena meat, obviously. Go gather some, make sure it's fresh, and bring it back here. There should be plenty just north of the camp.

passages.title: Chicken of the Desert
passages.text: This is fresh, right? They won't go after anything that's been withering in the sun.

passages.title: Chicken of the Desert
passages.text:
Man, this stuff looks delicious. I'm half tempted to just fry some up myself.

No! We've gotta focus on gettin' out of here.

Maybe just one piece...

passages.title: The Guns of Northwatch
passages.text:
Captain Fisher signaled us from below. The Horde fleet is landing shore parties? We can't let them flank us from the beach.

I've already sent two of my best gunners down there to defend the beach head. Talk to Cannoneer Smythe down on the shore.

You'll have to fight your way through the courtyard to get there. See if you can help the others secure the hold on your way down!

passages.title: The Guns of Northwatch
passages.text: Aubrey sent you? Good! I take it you know your way around a cannon?

passages.title: Run Out the Guns
passages.text: We've got the hardware but not the manpower, <name>. Man one of the carronades on the shore here and take out those incoming boats!

passages.title: Run Out the Guns
passages.text: Sure gets your ears ringing, doesn't it?

passages.title: Run Out the Guns
passages.text:
Ho ho! The beach is ours!

We just might keep a foothold on this miserable dustball of a continent after all.

passages.title: Langridge Shot
passages.text:
<class>! Thank the Light - they've practically driven us back to the docks. The courtyard is overrun!

We're out of canister shot and the orcs are getting ready for an assault up the hill. We need to improvise some scatter-shot, and fast.

Hurry, run into the broken tower here and grab whatever sharp, pointy bits of scrap metal you can lay your hands on. Knives, forks, nails - anything! Load the cannon when you've got an armful!

passages.title: Langridge Shot
passages.text: Paxton has already loaded a charge into the cannon. All it needs is the ammunition you improvised.

passages.title: Langridge Shot
passages.text: The Horde is massing at the base of the hill. Breathlessly, you stuff the debris you collected into the muzzle of the cannon, step back, cover one ear, and tug on the igniter cord...

passages.title: Re-Take the Courtyard
passages.text:
That's one way to clear a hill. Those corpses are impaled with knives and forks!

The Rageroar clan has breached the walls, but we can still turn this fight around. Go down the hill and help our men hold on to the courtyard below...

passages.title: Re-Take the Courtyard
passages.text:
Great work! We've knocked them on their heels, maybe long enough to shore up our defenses.

Provided we find a way to take out their artillery...

passages.title: Back in the Fight
passages.text:
This fight isn't over, <class>. Not by a long shot.

Some of the soldiers in the courtyard still have breath in their lungs. We can save them! I've soaked these rags in an herbal remedy we used to rely on back in Gilneas. The smell is awful but this poultice can practically raise the dead.

Use these bandages on wounded defenders down in the courtyard and we'll see if we can't get them back in the fight.

passages.title: Back in the Fight
passages.text: I hope you have enough bandages. My supply of those herbs was cut off when these brutes sacked my beloved Gilneas.

passages.title: Back in the Fight
passages.text: A steady stream of the walking wounded have come up the hill to see me, <name>. I trust that was your work? Well done!

passages.title: Momentum
passages.text:
We can't just rest on our laurels here, babe. We've got to keep this momentum going! People are talking about us.

Unfortunately, they're also talking about this air-headed gnome, Kelsey, who's apparently been running jobs right alongside us. If we're going to drive her out of what's rightfully a goblin town, we need to seal the deal here.

We're going to take care of Gadgetzan's pirate problem for them, for good. Head south to Lost Rigger Cove, I'll meet you there.

passages.title: Momentum
passages.text: Good thing you're here! I'm gonna need a lot of help if we want to beat these gnomes to the punch.

passages.title: Booty Duty
passages.text:
Let's not be wasteful here, babe. These pirates have tons of valuable nonsense just sitting around, waiting to be fenced. Can you believe they just sit on this stuff?

I mean, why do they even bother taking it if it's just going to sit around? Stolen goods should be sold off and used to buy shiny new things.

Anyway, be a dear and go grab as much of their loot as you can carry while you're out busting heads. Ciao!

passages.title: Booty Duty
passages.text: Let's see what you've got. You're not hiding any for yourself, are you? You'll never find a buyer without me, you know.

passages.title: Booty Duty
passages.text:
Beautiful! And to think these idiots were just sitting on it.

Here's a bit up front, we'll talk about profit-sharing bonuses later.

passages.title: A Great Idea
passages.text:
Now that we've got a good pile of fresh chunks, we just tie it to this rope...and now you're ready to go catch me a silithid.

What? Don't give me that look, it's perfectly safe. Well, mostly safe. Okay, you might die painfully. But it'll be easy! Just throw this meat out there, wait for a bug to pounce on it, and then drag 'em back here by the rope!

Go after one of the swarmers. I haven't seen the other ones go for hyenas before, and you should find plenty of swarmers around the edge of the pit.

passages.title: A Great Idea
passages.text: I don't see any bug with you, pal.

passages.title: A Great Idea
passages.text: Look at the size of it! It's glorious. This ugly sucker's gonna help us bring down the whole hive.

passages.title: Un-Chartered
passages.text:
As I may have mentioned, I'm trying to get these Dunemaul ogres to join the Horde..and work for the Bilgewater Cartel as cheap local labor.

To pull this off, we've gotta pay lip service to the actual initiation process and all that, or I'm going to catch flak later on. So I've gotten this charter drawn up, and slapped the initiation rites onto our own limited time offer labor stipulation contract.

I've got a disguise for you here, so suit up and get all these signatures filled out.

passages.title: Un-Chartered
passages.text: Babe, there's still blank spots on this sheet. Being near ogres isn't rubbing off on your intelligence, I hope.

passages.title: Un-Chartered
passages.text:
Wow, nice work! I'm amazed you even got them to hold a pen without eating it.

You can uh, just throw the suit over there. Away from me. In the fire.

passages.title: Get The Centipaarty Started
passages.text:
Okay, babe. Like I said, the ogres are too dumb to know what signing that charter meant. Now we have to actually get them to come along with us, so we'll be procuring what is apparently beloved local flavor.

Beloved local flavor for drooling idiots, I mean.

Just pop on over to the Noxious Lair to the west, it's that big horrible pit full of dangerous silithid. Kill a bunch of the Centipaar silithid and bring back the pieces so we can hand 'em out, okay? Ciao.

passages.title: Get The Centipaarty Started
passages.text: Have you got enough? These ogres don't look like the type to like small portions.

passages.title: Get The Centipaarty Started
passages.text:
Ugh! This entire camp is like a sampler course of awful smells.

Let's not handle these things any longer than we have to.

passages.title: Fresh out of the Grave
passages.text:
<name>!

Rise, <name>!

Welcome back to the realm of the living. With the blessing and power of the Dark Lady, I have freed you from death's grip.

You are no slave, <name>. You are free to follow whatever path you choose from here. If you choose to serve the Dark Lady Sylvanas, I recommend you speak with Undertaker Mordo. You will find him behind me, in the graveyard.

passages.title: Fresh out of the Grave
passages.text: Hello there.  You must be... <name>?

passages.title: The Wakening
passages.text:
King, peasant, or <class>... I don't care WHAT you were before. I just need somebody with a working tongue.

Being raised from the dead is strenuous. Not everyone copes with it as well as you did. In particular, there are three newly-raised undead who are having trouble coping right now.

I want you to find them and talk to them. It might be that they just need someone that they can relate with.

You'll find them here in the graveyard.

passages.title: The Wakening
passages.text: No dilly-dallying now.  You're among the Forsaken now, and we hold ours to a higher standard.

passages.title: The Wakening
passages.text:
You've done well, <class>.  As you can see, not all of us have resigned to our fates.  I'm glad to see that you're at least willing to work.

Valdred will be a valuable asset to the Forsaken.  As for the other two... there is not much we can do.  We cannot force them to join us.

passages.title: Trail-Worn Scroll
passages.text: Ah, while you were off dealing with the mindless Scourge, this scroll arrived for you. I would think it's some matter of importance as it seems it bears the seal of the hunter trainer Xavier. I would take some time to read it before heading out again.

passages.title: Trail-Worn Scroll
passages.text:
Ah, so you've arrived. Good. I overheard that a few others were able to escape "death" and were heading into town. Perhaps that resilience will pay off in the future also.

You may thank Sylvanas for your freedom... freedom of mind and body. Though you still remain tortured by the plague and its effects, you are now free to come and go as you see fit.

passages.title: Trail-Worn Scroll
passages.text:
I will be here to train you as you grow in experience... find me as often as you like. I charge a minimal fee, but you'll find everything I can teach you to be worthwhile.

Go now and test your skill. Many more things will become known to you as you gain experience, some of which I am unable to discuss with you here. Just know that Sylvanas will need hunters with your type of cunning in the future.

You will be the backbone of our salvation. Do not forget it.

passages.title: Charging into Battle
passages.text:
If you want to become a stronger warrior, you'll need to work on your weapons. You'll find stronger swords and larger shields out on your adventures, that I have no doubt about.

But it isn't just your physical armory that will get stronger - you'll also begin to discover new techniques. Go, get some experience, learn something new, then come back and show me.

passages.title: Charging into Battle
passages.text: You have the makings of a great <class>, <name>.  Go, practice what we've discussed, and return when you are stronger.  Then I may have more to teach you.

passages.title: No Better Than the Zombies
passages.text:
While you were inside that cave, your big friend Darnell came by with some alarming news.

Since the val'kyr arrived, we've seen more and more undead that chose not to join our forces under the banner of the Dark Lady. They've been gathering at a small camp here in the valley, and now they've organized forces.

They plan to attack Deathknell, <class>.

Darnell is just down the road, to the east. Be careful, <name>. While those undead aren't completely brainless, they're still not quite right in the head.

passages.title: No Better Than the Zombies
passages.text:
<name>.  You made it.

You see those tents up there?  That's where we're headed.  The battle's probably already started.

passages.title: Assault on the Rotbrain Encampment
passages.text:
While you were taking care of matters for Executor Arren, I went off on an assignment of my own. Shadow Priest Sarvis asked me to peek in on the Rotbrain camp.

There's a reason why they're called Rotbrains.

Their leader goes by the name of Marshal Redpath, and he's an absolute beast.

Look, <name>... the attack is starting. You're better in combat than I am. Get in there and help out!

When you're done, meet up with Shadow Priest Sarvis in the chapel. Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Assault on the Rotbrain Encampment
passages.text:
Being born again under the power of a val'kyr is a strenuous process.  Many don't survive the shock, turning into zombies or ghouls.

Others retain just enough humanity to seem normal on the outside... but they're sick inside.  We should have slain those rotbrains the day they were raised.

As for you... you're a strong <class>, <name>.  I knew you'd do well.  You'll be headed out of Deathknell soon.

passages.title: Night Web's Hollow
passages.text:
One of our greatest struggles is obtaining the natural resources we need to survive. Gold was scarce in Lordaeron, even in the height of the Alliance's power so many years ago.

There is a gold mine to the west that has been overrun with spiders. We need gold from the mine, but we can't very well get it while the spiders are crawling around in there. I've not much manpower to commit to the task, so we'll just have to do it little by little.

Get up there and see what you can do for us, <name>.

passages.title: Night Web's Hollow
passages.text: Be wary of the spiders' venom, <name>. If you feel a sharp burning, you may want to have it looked at.

passages.title: Night Web's Hollow
passages.text:
Well, it's a start.  It'll take a few weeks or months to fully clean out the infestation.  After that, we'll have to get down there with some torches to burn away the webbing.

You've done your duty well, <name>.

passages.title: Fields of Grief
passages.text:
What have we here? You look like a fledgling <class>. If you hope to prove yourself to the Dark Lady, you need to learn the ways of the Forsaken.

To the west you'll find a farm. Humans infest the land like mold on a rotting corpse. And worse yet, the Scarlet Crusade patrols nearby from their tower. Teach those scum a lesson and steal 10 of their precious pumpkins.

Once you have 10, bring them back to me.

passages.title: Fields of Grief
passages.text: Were you able to gather 10 pumpkins yet, <name>?

passages.title: Fields of Grief
passages.text: You have performed your bidding well, young <class>.  You are proving yourself to be quite an asset to the Dark Lady's army.

passages.title: Reaping the Reapers
passages.text:
Humans are notoriously fickle creatures. The farmers to the west are no exception. Sure, they may be plowing their fields peacefully now, but tomorrow, they may be raising their scythes against us. The Alliance looms close by in Gilneas, and the power of Stormwind looms to the south... any of these could recruit these tillers and use them as a wedge against us.

I want them dead. See to it that it's done.

passages.title: Reaping the Reapers
passages.text: You've the makings of a mighty <class>, <race>.  I heard the cries of those humans from all the way over here.  Perhaps soon we will be rid of this human blight.

passages.title: A Scarlet Letter
passages.text:
Lieutenant Gebler:

How curious that you would decide to take a prisoner... an undead one at that. What were you thinking? Do you think that, just because of the prisoner's former status, that she would be above the edicts of the Scarlet Crusade?

This is most troubling, Gebler. I would remind you that there are penalties for such behavior. I command you to execute the prisoner at once. She is no longer one of us.

passages.title: A Scarlet Letter
passages.text: A letter?  What does it say?

passages.title: A Scarlet Letter
passages.text:
The Scarlet Crusade takes no prisoners.  That they would do so with this young woman... curious.

The powers that you describe are even curiouser.  She passed through the bars of her prison and killed her captor?  Why hadn't she done that in the first place?

passages.title: The Scarlet Palisade
passages.text:
We need someone with "initiative" like yourself to drive the Scarlet Crusade to the grave.

Prove to me you are capable of serving The Dark Lady by travelling west to the tower past the Solliden Farmstead and slaying 10 warriors of the Scarlet Crusade.

passages.title: The Scarlet Palisade
passages.text: Most excellent, <class>.  Your skill in the art of combat is undeniable.

passages.title: The New Forsaken
passages.text:
Speaking frankly, the Forsaken of yesteryear were a sniveling, pathetic group. We huddled together in decrepit old human buildings, hiding from the Scourge, cowering from the Alliance, and groveling at the foot of the Horde.

Look before you now, and see the product of the new Forsaken. We have made our mark here on Azeroth, and that mark will grow. Our dominion will soon blanket the world!

You want my advice? Speak with Magistrate Sevren in Brill, down this road. He runs that town.

passages.title: The New Forsaken
passages.text: Yes, I'm Brill's local magistrate, reporting directly to the Dark Lady.  Impress me, and you may end up meeting the Banshee Queen herself.  Now, onto your first task...

passages.title: The Prodigal Lich
passages.text:
Long ago, the mage Gunther Arcanus, along with Bethor Iceshard and the now-Scourge Necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, were friends and students within the Kirin Tor - a society of mages in Dalaran.

Gunther fell to the Plague, but we thought he either remained dead, or was raised into the ranks of the Lich King. We now know he is free.

We must have him. If you travel east, you will find him on an island in Brightwater Lake. Convince him to join our ranks.

passages.title: Proving Allegiance
passages.text:
Fine. I will continue with this charade, but only because I sense in you a spark of... excellence. But before I believe you I must have proof that you are enemy to the Scourge.

There is an old, bloody altar just off the southern coast of this island. It is used by a powerful Scourge agent, Lillith Nefara.

Take a Candle of Beckoning from this crate here. Light it on the altar and Lillith will awake. Destroy Lillith, and I will believe you are an ally.

passages.title: The Prodigal Lich Returns
passages.text: Take this Nether Gem to my old comrade Bethor, who resides in the Undercity. It will let us communicate ... and I have much to tell him.

passages.title: Dark Lady, Watch Over Us
passages.text: In fact, why don't you speak with Lady Sylvanas herself? The presence of another Kirin Tor-trained mage among our ranks is an occasion worthy of an audience.

passages.title: The Chill of Death
passages.text:
It's so cold, now. The Plague of Undeath crawls through my veins like an icy serpent. The mindless state will be upon me soon. But no doomed destiny will prevent me from serving our Dark Lady. When the call arose I sewed body bags for the fallen soldiers of Sylvanas's mighty army.

Now my hands shake from the chill. If you would bring me five duskbat pelts, I could sew myself a blanket. Help me, <name>, so that I can continue to serve the cause.

passages.title: The Chill of Death
passages.text: Do you have five duskbat pelts yet, <name>?

passages.title: The Chill of Death
passages.text: I appreciate your efforts, <name>.  May Sylvanas recognize your bravery one day. . . .

passages.title: Return to the Magistrate
passages.text: You should return to Magistrate Sevren with the information I gave you. He'll want it as soon as possible, so be swift.

passages.title: Return to the Magistrate
passages.text:
It is troubling to hear of the Scourge slipping past the Bulwark.  Even now, they are ceaseless in their assaults.

But we will not give in.  The Lich King is dead; we will not be taken again!

passages.title: Darkhound Pounding
passages.text:
Lady Sylvanas has called upon the Royal Apothecary Society. She has challenged us to concoct a new plague, a plague deadlier than any ailment on Azeroth. This new disease will bring our enemies - living and dead - to ruin.

My studies show that the blood of beasts might prove to be the key. Here, fill these vials with darkhound blood so I can test my theory.

passages.title: Darkhound Pounding
passages.text: Have you collected the darkhound blood yet, <name>? Time is fleeting!

passages.title: Darkhound Pounding
passages.text: You have done well, <name> and I thank you for your efforts.

passages.title: Garren's Haunt
passages.text:
As you're probably already realizing, the Royal Apothecary Society is a widespread organization. We take our plague-alchemy seriously. It is our belief that the more agents we have performing experiments, the sooner we will realize our objective.

One of our agents performs his work at a small encampment to the north of here. His name is Jerrod, and he could use an apprentice of your... stature.

passages.title: Garren's Haunt
passages.text:
Holland?  He's an amateur.  You don't need a fancy two-story apothecarium to make plague... you need love.  And maybe some good assistants.

Let me show you how plague is REALLY made.

passages.title: Annihilate the Worgen
passages.text:
These worgen must be dealt with, and quickly. Our first priority is to eliminate any which may have infiltrated Brill.

I want you to be on the lookout for any suspicious activity here in Brill, <name>. We know that these worgen can hide in the shadows, so look for any signs you can find... footsteps, kicked-up rocks... anything.

passages.title: Annihilate the Worgen
passages.text: To think, they've been right under our noses!  I'll put my deathguards on alert... this will NOT happen again.

passages.title: Doom Weed
passages.text:
My envoy just delivered me a bushel of gloom weed. Gloom weed! I don't need gloom weed, I need doom weed! You can see the predicament that I'm in, <name>.

I'll make it worth your while to gather what I need. Bring back to me enough doom weed and I'll give you a suitable reward.

It is my understanding that they like to plague the flora near the mass gravesite, to the north of the Brill graveyard. Hurry and be mindful of the gnolls in the area.

passages.title: Doom Weed
passages.text:
<The apothecary mutters to himself.>

They brought me gloom weed?  GLOOM WEED?!

passages.title: Doom Weed
passages.text:
Ah, my doom weed. Excellent!

<Apothecary Jerrod rubs his hands together greedily.>

These will come in quite handy. You've done me, uh, the Lady, a fine service today, <name>. As promised, here is the reward that you deserve.

passages.title: Off the Scales
passages.text:
While you were collecting samples for me, my experiments led me to realize that more reagents will be required for this new disease to spread properly. Poisoning some hapless victim is child's play. Plaguing an entire world proves to be a bit more complicated.

I will need several scales from murlocs in the vicinity. You will find the creatures ambling brainlessly along the coast to the north.

passages.title: Off the Scales
passages.text: <name>, were you able to obtain those scales from the murlocs?

passages.title: Off the Scales
passages.text: The scales are perfect, <name>. Exactly what I needed for this concoction.

passages.title: Holland's Experiment
passages.text:
I am to understand that another one of those foolish Dwarven Mountaineers has just been captured. The deathguard has him stored here in this building, and they've assigned one of their own to persuade him not to escape.

Why don't you go see how the Captured Mountaineer enjoys this special drink I made for him? It contains a subtle hint of what The Dark Lady has planned for the rest of Azeroth.

passages.title: Holland's Experiment
passages.text: Why if I had my trusted rifle you'd be as good as dead, <class>.  Just wait until the Steam Tank Brigade arrives to rescue me!

passages.title: Holland's Experiment
passages.text: Ah, a drink at last.  What matter of ale is this?  I'm sure it's no Rhapsody Malt but I'll take anything to wet the old whistle at this point.

passages.title: Maggot Eye
passages.text:
Maggot Eye is a foul beast, even by gnoll standards. He leads a band of renegade gnolls through the land, tearing up the glades and stealing whatever corpses he can find along the way.

Those are our corpses! We had plans for those!

Maggot Eye resides just up the path from us. Show him no mercy. Mercy is for the weak.

passages.title: Maggot Eye
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Maggot Eye
passages.text: Excellent work!  Now if only I can convince Jerrod to let us move our operation into that shack...

passages.title: Planting the Seed of Fear
passages.text:
It seems that Jerrod has you hunting the murlocs to the north. That's good... we can use their parts for our poisons. I get a little worried sometimes, though...

The Vile Fin spawning grounds are not far off Tirisfal's northern coast, so you'll probably notice several tadpoles among the adults on the shore. If these impressionable young murlocs were to seek revenge against us... that could ruin us. Go chase them, and show them that the Forsaken and the Horde are not to be trifled with.

passages.title: Planting the Seed of Fear
passages.text: Did they run from you, <name>?  Good.  This is better than killing them... if they live to tell the tale, then future generations of murlocs will learn to fear us.

passages.title: Sandscraper
passages.text:
My other assistants are making sure our proud new comrades are put into comfy cages and shipped to where they're needed most. For the Horde. Meanwhile, we've got one last item on our agenda.

Sandscraper, the chief of the Dunemaul Clan, is probably too dumb to even be aware of what we're doing here. But I absolutely loathe unfinished business, babe. He's lurking in the den just over there to the west. Knuckle down, take him out, and we'll be good to sign off on this, 'kay?

passages.title: Sandscraper
passages.text:
And that's a wrap! Nothing left here for us but sand. Good job, babe.

Well, maybe I shouldn't be so hasty. Did you find anything in that ogre den?

passages.title: Scavenged
passages.text:
<You discover a cargo manifest on the body, detailing a long list of sundries urgently needed on the front.>

<A bloody trail in the dirt indicates bodies were dragged south of here, toward the raptor dens.>

<The raptors may have dragged away the supplies, as well. Retrieving those supplies for Corporal Teegan could help salvage this disaster!>

passages.title: Scavenged
passages.text: What? My supply caravan was sacked by those cold-blooded scissor-paw things?

passages.title: Scavenged
passages.text: My supplies! Well, that showed some real initiative, <class>. Those rap-saws or whatever they're called have torn lesser men to ribbons. Thank you!

passages.title: The Family Crypt
passages.text:
The strongest point in the mills is the Agamand Family Crypt. With necromancy, Captain Dargol has raised the ancestors of the Agamands and plans to use them against us.

This cannot pass, and you must stop it. Travel to the Agamand Family Crypt and defeat the raised Agamand ancestors.

passages.title: The Family Crypt
passages.text: Time is not a luxury we have, <name>.  With each passing hour, the Scourge's hold on Tirisfal Glades grows more firm.

passages.title: The Family Crypt
passages.text:
Your actions struck a telling blow against the Scourge.  And your victory will not go unnoticed - not by the Forsaken, nor by our enemies.

Continue the struggle as we all do, <name>, and one day the Forsaken will have the dominion over Azeroth that they are owed!

passages.title: The Mills Overrun
passages.text:
The Scourge are trying to form a base here at the Agamand Mills. If they do, then they can stage further attacks within Tirisfal.

The orders have been given. The Scourge in the Mills must be destroyed.

Collect Notched Ribs from Rattlecage and Cracked Skull Soldiers, and Blackened Skulls from Darkeye Bonecasters.

passages.title: The Mills Overrun
passages.text: Our battles with the Scourge wage on, <name>.  Do your part and throw those cursed, mindless <race> back into the Plaguelands!

passages.title: The Mills Overrun
passages.text: Your efforts are appreciated, <name>.  I will not thank you for doing what is necessary, but I will remember your name.

passages.title: Speak with Sevren
passages.text:
I have destroyed the remains you've given me, <name>. That is, all remains except for these...

Devlin Agamand was weak and sharp-tongued in life, and was among the first to succumb to the plague. He existed as a slave of the Scourge for a long time, longer than most. As such, he may possess knowledge that would be of value to us.

Bring his remains to Magistrate Sevren, and tell him what I've told you. He'll know what to do.

passages.title: Speak with Sevren
passages.text: The fetor of Scourge hangs about you, <name>.  What is it you seek?

passages.title: Speak with Sevren
passages.text:
Devlin Agamand?  Is that him you carry in your sack there?  Ha!

Yes, I know what Coleman wants to try, and I want to try it too.  I hope you're prepared, <name>.

passages.title: Filthy Animals
passages.text:
You probably caught wind of some of them Hecklefang scavengers on the way in - they reek worse than ol' Durty Pete here. Worthless animals! They steal our kills, rummage through our supplies, and worse... they ain't good for eatin'.

Go kill some.

Then kill some more, if you want to.

passages.title: Filthy Animals
passages.text: Ooooo-oooh aye! The best Hecklefangs are the dead ones.

passages.title: At War With The Scarlet Crusade
passages.text:
Though the strength of the Scarlet Crusade wanes, we are still at war. The report Executor Arren sent me indicates Scarlet Crusaders have been raiding from the ruined tower in southeastern Tirisfal near the Balnir Farmstead under the command of Captain Vachon.

Kill 3 of his zealots and 4 of his friars. It should prove to be a devastating blow to the Crusade!

passages.title: At War With The Scarlet Crusade
passages.text: Your actions will slow down the Scarlet Crusade's advancement in Tirisfal quite a bit... hopefully for good.  But other threats loom.

passages.title: To Bigger and Better Things
passages.text:
There isn't much more glory for you here on the Bulwark, <name>. You've done enough already. There may, however, be further adventures waiting in Silverpine Forest.

Speak with my bat man, Timothy Cunningham. He'll give you a ride to Brill, free of charge.

passages.title: To Bigger and Better Things
passages.text: Sure, I'll give you a ride.  If High Executor Derrington asks for it, then technically I have to.

passages.title: Take to the Skies
passages.text:
