passages.text: They're still shooting, but not nearly as much! Yeeeeeeeeeaaaaaaaaaaah!

passages.title: Quiet the Cannons
passages.text:
Now it's time to do something about those darn cannons up on the bluffs to the east!

If you'd be so kind, hop into your boat and cruise on over to the Southsea Holdfast. Up top you'll see a bunch of cannons firing down on us.

Those pirates don't know squat about engineering. It shouldn't be too difficult for you to clog 'em up and make them explode.

passages.title: Quiet the Cannons
passages.text: They're still shooting, but not nearly as much! Yeeeeeeeeeaaaaaaaaaaah!

passages.title: A Little Payback
passages.text:
It's time for a little payback, I think. Can you blame me? After they locked me down in that outhouse and left me to drown?!

I'll make it worth your while if you head up to the Southsea Holdfast on the eastern bluffs and exact my revenge.

passages.title: A Little Payback
passages.text: That'll teach those scurvy dogs! You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: A Little Payback
passages.text:
It's time for a little payback, I think. Can you blame me? After they locked me down in that outhouse and left me to drown?!

I'll make it worth your while if you head up to the Southsea Holdfast on the eastern bluffs and exact my revenge.

passages.title: A Little Payback
passages.text: That'll teach those scurvy dogs! You have my thanks, <name>.

passages.title: Thunderdrome: Grudge Match!
passages.text:
It seems we have a special request! I have here a note from one Megs Dreadshredder, requesting to enter the cage and settle a dispute.

She's asked for you to be her partner, <name>. A fan of your previous victories? Or perhaps you're acquainted outside the ring?

I wouldn't back down now if I were you. This is the grand finale...

passages.title: Thunderdrome: Grudge Match!
passages.text: Stop wasting my time. Enter and fight!

passages.title: Thunderdrome: Grudge Match!
passages.text: Fantastic. I might challenge you to a duel myself someday.

passages.title: Deep Attraction
passages.text:
I've been able to help some of the survivors make it to the cave, but it's starting to get hairy out there. If we didn't have enough problems, some glowing murlocs started creeping up from the nearby crevice to attack the stranded survivors.

The men up there are warriors--they won't go down without a fight--but they're much worse for the wear after that damned shell.

If you have any breath left in your lungs, get up there and take out some of those murlocs. Hellscream's eyes are upon you.

passages.title: Deep Attraction
passages.text: You know what it is to carry yourself with honor, <class>. You do Hellscream proud.

passages.title: Shelled Salvation
passages.text:
A lot of the men haven't made it to the cave yet. It's a safe bet that they're stranded at the vents on the ridge above us.

We found some spiralung shells on the way here. They don't produce much air, but it was enough for us to make the cave.

I need to stay here to count heads and get them back on their feet as they arrive. Do me a favor - go collect those spiralung shells, get them to any of my men that are still up on the ridge, and give them a swift kick in the arse so that they get moving.

passages.title: Shelled Salvation
passages.text: Thank you, <class>. You've proven very useful.

passages.title: Something Edible
passages.text:
Were they trying to starve us all to death?! Not giving prisoners food is just despicable.

We need to get these soldiers fed. The best prospect I spotted on the way here were those giant grouper. Several of those and we shouldn't want for meat for a while.

If you can bring me back some, I'll see to it that it gets cooked and passed out fairly.

passages.title: Something Edible
passages.text: With all the rumbling bellies, it sounds like there's a monster in this cave. It's putting my nerves on edge.

passages.title: Something Edible
passages.text:
Now to hold up my end of the bargain. I'll get this cooked and passed out immediately.

You and I will have to have a talk later. I'm going to need help that these soldiers just can't offer.

passages.title: Commander Jarod Shadowsong
passages.text:
Only once has there been a leader capable of commanding demigods and mortals alike.

His name was Jarod Shadowsong and his ability to lead in battle was such that Cenarius and the other ancients placed themselves under his command.

He disappeared for years and his whereabouts were unknown. Until now.

He is being held captive inside a Twilight camp in Darkwhisper Gorge.

Your job is to infiltrate their ranks and free Jarod. Speak to the one known as Ortell at Darkwhisper Pass to the southeast.

passages.title: Commander Jarod Shadowsong
passages.text:
Hey there.  I'm glad to see they sent someone of your caliber for this operation.

This here's going to call for some subtlety.  We can't risk Commander Shadowsong getting killed.

passages.title: Ain't Too Proud to Beg
passages.text:
Now that you've brought me to safety, I'm afraid I must impose upon your kindness just a bit further.

The captain of our ship, Samir, is still out there. Mack too. I'm sure they made it to the sea floor but beyond that I didn't see what became of them.

I simply couldn't get by in a place like this without their help.

I lost sight of them in a clump of kelp west of where you found me.

Please hurry! They couldn't have gotten far...

passages.title: Ain't Too Proud to Beg
passages.text:
Where would we be without you, <race>!

I don't want to even imagine!

passages.title: Sunken Treasure
passages.text:
The key to the cage is held by Tony Two-Tusk, the pirate admiral, and he's guarded by ogres that you'll never be able to kill!

<Wizzle cries some more and then looks up, an idea forming in his brain.>

I've got it! What do all pirates want more than anything else? No, not grog. Something even better... treasure!

They had a ship full of treasure that was sunk by a giant whale-shark. The treasure is scattered all over down in the Mirage Abyss to the northwest.

Go get it!

passages.title: Sunken Treasure
passages.text: Oh gosh, do you already have all of that sunken treasure?

passages.title: Sunken Treasure
passages.text:
Oh yeah! Look at all that booty.

Wait a minute... bring it closer!

passages.title: Sunken Treasure
passages.text:
The key to the cage is held by Tony Two-Tusk, the pirate admiral, and he's guarded by ogres that you'll never be able to kill!

<Wizzle cries some more and then looks up, an idea forming in his brain.>

I've got it! What do all pirates want more than anything else? No, not grog. Something even better... treasure!

They had a ship full of treasure that was sunk by a giant whale-shark. The treasure is scattered all over down in the Mirage Abyss to the northwest.

Go get it!

passages.title: Sunken Treasure
passages.text: You already have all of that sunken treasure?

passages.title: Sunken Treasure
passages.text:
Oh yeah! Look at all that booty.

Wait a minute... bring it closer!

passages.title: Return from the Firelands
passages.text:
I'll usher out the rest of Goldrinn's followers and seal this portal behind us.

The rest of our forces at Mount Hyjal will want to hear of this victory. Return to Ian Duran and let him know what we've discovered and how we were triumphant!

Simply step through the portal to return to Mount Hyjal.

passages.title: Return from the Firelands
passages.text:
They're moving supplies to Hyjal straight from the elemental planes? That explains so much.

You've made Goldrinn proud by sealing that flamegate, <name>, but there may be more portals to seal. You should check with the other shrines!

passages.title: Two-Tusk Takedown
passages.text:
This treasure's all fake, but it's not like those den whompers are going to know the difference. Stupid ogres!

Here's the plan... you head into the Admiral's Den and spread all of this "treasure" around to any ogres that get in your way. Then all you have to do is confront Tony Two-Tusk.

You'll have the key to the cage in no-time!

passages.title: Two-Tusk Takedown
passages.text: What's going on? You gonna get me out of here?

passages.title: Two-Tusk Takedown
passages.text:
Yeah, yeah, yeah... I'm sure that your little adventure into the cave was very interesting.

How about we talk about it over drinks back on the Speedbarge once you get me out of this cage?

passages.title: Two-Tusk Takedown
passages.text:
This treasure's all fake, but it's not like those den whompers are going to know the difference. Stupid ogres!

Here's the plan... you head into the Admiral's Den and spread all of this "treasure" around to any ogres that get in your way. Then all you have to do is confront Tony Two-Tusk.

You'll have the key to the cage in no-time!

passages.title: Two-Tusk Takedown
passages.text: What's going on? You gonna get me out of here?

passages.title: Two-Tusk Takedown
passages.text:
Yeah, yeah, yeah... I'm sure that your little adventure into the cave was very interesting.

How about we talk about it over drinks back on the Speedbarge once you get me out of this cage?

passages.title: Caught Off-Guard
passages.text:
I can't imagine that our escape from the shell went unnoticed, but either the naga at these ruins were not informed or don't consider us a threat. I do not intend to take such opportunities for granted - we must strike now.

I need you to slip into the lower level of the ruins and take out as many of their patrols as you can. We cannot risk any of those patrols finding out about our occupation of this cave - make sure none escape.

passages.title: Swift Approach
passages.text:
I've taken the liberty of performing some preliminary scouting. The naga may not be aware of out position, but they are not entirely unprepared for intruders.

Beyond their patrols, they have set up magical sentry devices that will warn them of unwelcome guests. Fortunately, they seem to have sacrificed quality for quantity, and there is definitely a window in which the devices can be destroyed before their alarms are answered.

I trust that you can see to this before our other soldiers arrive.

passages.title: An Occupation of Time
A Better Vantage
passages.text:
This cave is our only refuge. There's no place to which we can retreat. There's no help on the way. Whatever happens, this cave must remain safe or we are all sure to die down here.

I have no intention of standing idle. The best way to keep the naga from finding us is to keep them off-balance, but we can't risk them following us back here between strikes. We need a forward post to launch or attacks from.

I'd like you scout the ruins for a suitable base of operation. Something defensible.

passages.title: Upon the Scene of Battle
passages.text:
All around you lie the remnants of a fierce battle. The naga skeletons are no surprise, but the weapons and remains of their apparent opponents are somewhat more unexpected.

Amidst the bones, you spot a strangely prominent piece of metal jutting out from one of the skulls. It's difficult to tell what sort of weapon it might have once been part of, but it stands out sufficiently to prompt you to retrieve it as evidence.

Surely someone back at the cave would be interested in this revelation.

passages.title: A Desperate Plea
passages.text:
The note in this bottle is soaked through, but still legible.

In it, the author claims to have escaped from some sort of undersea naga prison.

He is clearly in fear for his life, and you can't help but wonder if it might be one of your recently abducted shipmates.

At a loss as to how to locate the escapee, you determine to share the find with Erunak.

passages.title: A Desperate Plea
passages.text: If he still lives, I may be able to locate this poor soul.

passages.title: The Darkmist Ruins
passages.text:
I have been beset by visions, <class>. Visions of an icon of great power falling into sinister hands. I see an amulet, held by the ancient elves...sitting forgotten while its surroundings turn to ruins, until it is captured by demons through treachery and malice.

Every night, these sights flow through my dreams. The spirits are warning us. I am too old, and the camp's braves too occupied with guarding us. I must beseech you to follow my visions to the south, to the Darkmist Ruins, and seek out the amulet.

passages.title: The Darkmist Ruins
passages.text: <As you reach towards the pedestal, you find it empty. A chill fills the room, and you hear a faint voice...>

passages.title: Return to Sage Palerunner
passages.text: The soft glow from the pedestal brightens, and you can see a simple chain left behind. This must be the amulet Sage Palerunner sent you here for...

passages.title: Return to Sage Palerunner
passages.text: You've returned. What have you found?

passages.title: Return to Sage Palerunner
passages.text:
I am a fool...I was misled. This is nothing more than a rusted trinket, and my visions have no doubt been fulfilled.

Forgive me, <name>. But should you meet this demoness again, I pray you will triumph over her as you did Verinias.

passages.title: Windshear Mine Cleanup
passages.text:
The Horde has overrun Windshear Mine. I'm not sure what these orcs are hauling out of here or why they're here, but I know that it can't be good. Get in that mine and take out the management. Without goblin overseers, these peons will be even more worthless.

While you're inside, keep your eyes peeled for any other information about the Horde operation in the mines.

Good luck!

passages.title: Windshear Mine Cleanup
passages.text:
Nice job, I could hear their shrill screams from out here. You've turned the whole place on its head!

Did you happen to find any other information about the mining operation?

passages.title: Beyond Durotar
passages.text:
Hmmph... it looks like your services are being requested elsewhere. Ag'tor Bloodfist is looking for recruits to assist the Horde's ventures in Azshara, north of Orgrimmar.

I'm sure you still have work to do here in Durotar, and I understand that they'll shortly be asking for your help in the Barrens. I wouldn't be going anywhere yet if I were you, but if you're itching for some manifest destiny... Azshara awaits.

passages.title: Beyond Durotar
passages.text: Good, you're here.  Welcome to Azshara, the stage for the next act of the Horde's glorious future.  Now get to work.

passages.title: The Ancients are With Us
passages.text:
Nemesis... destroyed.

I feel rejuvenated.
Powerful.
Awakened.

Tell Ysera my strength is hers.

The Twilight's Hammer will fall.

passages.title: The Ancients are With Us
passages.text:
By relieving Tortolla of his final burdens you have acquired for us a formidable ally... and the final piece of the puzzle.

Steel yourself, <name>. The most difficult part of our journey is to begin.

We will bring the fight to their stronghold.

passages.title: Dark Heart
passages.text:
Edana Hatetalon is the queen of the Northspring harpies that reside in the ruins to the west. It is her malicious will that leads the harpies to defend their nests among the ruins of our people.

The harpies can call to her with a horn they carry - blowing it by the Hatetalon stones, in the northern part of the ruins, will summon Edana.

Show no mercy for these foul creatures. Slay her, and bring her dark heart to me.

passages.title: Dark Heart
passages.text: We must not tolerate the infestation of our ancestor's ruins by the harpies.

passages.title: Dark Heart
passages.text: These lands will finally be free of the foulness of the harpies. I cannot thank you enough.

passages.title: Haunted
passages.text:
You think I'm going to just let you go after you killed me like that, mon? No way! I didn't create a piratical mercantile empire out of nothing just to see you bring me down.

You're going to help me get back to life. Find my ex-wife, Ajamon, on the north side of the Holdfast. Just follow your nose. She'll be wherever the stinky brewing cauldron is.

passages.title: Haunted
passages.text: What ya be wantin'? Oh no you don't. I can see ya got Tony's spirit with ya, and I want nothin' to do with it!

passages.title: Free Our Sisters
passages.text:
Yesterday morning I dispatched a squadron of huntresses on a mission into Windshear Crag to obtain information about Horde operations in Stonetalon. Field intelligence reports that they have all been captured, including their squad leader, Huntress Illiona.

Head east into Windshear Crag and slay the Krom'gar infantry that occupy the crag and take from them their keys to unlock the Horde cages holding our sisters.

Do your best to locate Illiona once you've freed the huntresses.

passages.title: Free Our Sisters
passages.text: We don't have much time. To get me out of here you are going to have to take out Warlord Roktrog. He holds the key to this prison.

passages.title: An Offering for Aviana
passages.text:
Although the guardian of all winged creatures is no longer with us in body, I sometimes hear her voice in the whisper of swaying leaves.

<name>, we ask much of you as you set out to preserve this mountain. Before going on, take a moment to reflect.

Take this offering of nectar to Aviana's burial circle, a circle of stones just outside the main door of the shrine. Perhaps some time alone with Aviana's memory will help sharpen your focus.

passages.title: An Offering for Aviana
passages.text: <The spirit fades in and out of your vision, as though here and elsewhere at the same time.>

passages.title: An Offering for Aviana
passages.text:
<A whispered plea rings within your head.>

To be born again, but in darkness...

I have been stolen away.

<The spirit appears frantic, but falls silent as her image fades.>

passages.title: Carcass Collection
passages.text:
These organs be a good start, mon, but we still be needin' lotsa other tings. Normally, we'd be gettin' stuff from family now, but dats only me and my sistah's boy, and Tony ain't worth it!

So, we be substitutin' some stuff. Lotsa carcasses, in fact!

Deep down in the Shimmering Deep, there's tons of dem from when the water came rushin' in. Killed all of dem creatures. Go down there and bring me up some.

passages.title: Carcass Collection
passages.text: Ya gots to get me lotsa those carcasses, mon! We not be rid of his foolish spirit if ya don't!

passages.title: Carcass Collection
passages.text:
Oh, that's disgustin'!

We almost there, mon. Just need ta do one more ting!

passages.title: Futile Pride
passages.text:
This is actually an old orc city... one of the oldest on Azeroth. That is, it was until the ogres pushed us out.

Today's Horde refuses to be pushed over by ogres. My troops and I took the town back by force, and the ogres who once lived here now work as my servants. Now, our real work begins.

You look strong enough, but I'd like to see some proof. Kill one of the ogres that still besiege us, and return to me.

passages.title: Futile Pride
passages.text: Is that ogre blood I smell?  It had better be...

passages.title: Futile Pride
passages.text: Well done, <race>.  You've proven that you can take down an ogre... no small feat.  Now let's see if you can take down an Alliance iron mine...

passages.title: Ogre Combat
passages.text:
I saw your handiwork down there, <race>. How'd you like to hunt some more ogres?

We only enslaved the ones we could catch. Most of the strongest ogres still brood in Dreadmaul Post, plotting our demise. Our guards can handle the scattered ambushers, but we are not yet firmly entrenched, and will buckle quickly under a coordinated attack.

Go south to Dreadmaul Post and send a message, <name>. Slay the strongest before they get any ideas.

passages.title: Ogre Combat
passages.text: You've done well today, <name>.  Not only have you purchased more time before the next ogre attack, but I think you scared some of the captives into working harder.

passages.title: Blood Ritual
passages.text: Our goal is to find the demon hunter, Loramus Thalipedes. Let me know when you are ready to begin the blood ritual, and then stand back.

passages.title: Blood Ritual
passages.text: The ritual is not yet complete.

passages.title: Blood Ritual
passages.text: The blood ritual was a success; I can clearly see where Loramus is right now.  That is, I can see where the pieces of his body lie...

passages.title: Not Just Any Body
passages.text:
Loramus Thalipedes is dead. Well, let me step back... that's an assumption on my part, but I do know that his body lies in three pieces.

<Lynnore ponders for a moment.>

If you bring me the pieces, we still have a recourse. All three pieces are nearby... the Dreadmaul ogres hide them in their caves. In fact, one of them is in that chest, down the ledge behind me...

passages.title: Not Just Any Body
passages.text: Trust me... whatever happened to Loramus, we can fix.  The limits of blood magic are still undefined.

passages.title: Not Just Any Body
passages.text:
I see... yes, we can work with this.

<Lynnore looks at the night elf's head.>

Loramus Thalipedes, demon hunter.  I look forward to meeting you.

passages.title: The Charred Granite of the Dark Portal
passages.text:
Loramus wants us - er, YOU - to gather granite chips from these chunks of rock around the Dark Portal. I don't know what he'd want rocks for, but I have my suspicions, and they're not pleasant ones.

Use this pick and look for small outcroppings of rock along the edge of the portal's blast radius.

passages.title: The Charred Granite of the Dark Portal
passages.text: Keep it down, would ya?

passages.title: The Charred Granite of the Dark Portal
passages.text: I hope this is what he needs.  We probably don't have time for you to return and mine any more.

passages.title: The Vile Blood of Demons
passages.text:
Thalipedes wants demon blood. Personally, the stuff doesn't even seem like blood to me - more like liquid rot - but that's neither here nor there.

Luckily for you, the area around the Dark Portal is crawling with demons. Infernals, felhounds, felguards... they've all got what you need, in copious, pustulent amounts.

passages.title: The Vile Blood of Demons
passages.text: Ugh, what's that smell?  Is that you, or the blood?

passages.title: The Vile Blood of Demons
passages.text:
There's no doubt about it, you found demon blood.

Loramus' requests aside, I'm sure Dar'toon is thankful for your efforts.  They've been struggling to deal with these demon distractions for some time now.

passages.title: Protecting Our Rear
passages.text:
The only reason you see me standing aside Alliance soldiers is because our duty outweighs our enmity... however slightly. We have been charged with protecting the Dark Portal from unauthorized travel, and with the recent cataclysm, we are particularly susceptible to an attack. We've already heard reports of black dragons in the area...

With my men focused on their duty, we need someone to keep the area demons in check. Around the portal you will find three demon lieutenants. Slay them.

passages.title: Protecting Our Rear
passages.text:
Your work is appreciated, soldier.

<The warlord leans in close, and whispers:>

<race>... if you're still interested, I have one more small task for you...

passages.title: Loramus Thalipedes Awaits
passages.text:
The enchantment on these amulets was not complex. Together, their power will grant you access to Razelikh, the amulets' creator.

I am prepared to perform the ritual on you and Loramus. Speak with me when you are both ready.

passages.title: Loramus Thalipedes Awaits
passages.text: Speak with Lynnore, and quickly, friend.  This is but the calm before the storm.

passages.title: Loramus Thalipedes Awaits
passages.text: It would seem that we are prepared to face our demon, <name>.  We have the amulet's blessing, we have the stone knife, and I alone know the demon's true name: Rakh'likh.  Together, this may be enough to defeat the Defiler.

passages.title: Home... Gone... Naga...
passages.text:
<The murloc struggles to speak your language.>

Rockpool... attacked. Naga turn, take village, villagers.

Salt-Flop escape, but others do not. Go south, talk to Chief Neptool. Maybe he survive.

passages.title: Home... Gone... Naga...
passages.text:
<The murloc spirit looks upon you sadly.>

Salt-Flop did not shame himself by running away.  Look behind me, and see for yourself.

The Rockpool had no hope against the naga's attack.

passages.title: Atrocities
passages.text:
<Though his lips do not move, you can feel the murloc chief speaking to you.>

The Bloodwash naga and the Rockpool murloc have lived among one another for as long as we could remember. We have always had our differences, but never provoked one another. Why, then, would they turn on us?

<Neptool looks over his shoulder at his former villagers.>

You see what they do now? They enslave us, sacrifice us, force us to fight one another. I will stop them, <race>... and you will be my weapon.

passages.title: Atrocities
passages.text: You have done well, brave <class>.  I am pleased... but I am not yet satisfied.

passages.title: False Idols
passages.text:
Neptulon the Tidehunter is our god. He was the god of the Bloodwash, too, but they have turned their back on him, it seems. They now choose to worship only Azshara, their naga queen. You will see likenesses of Azshara littered around their settlements, carved out of seastone.

<The murloc spirit eyes your weapon.>

That weapon will do. Send it through their Azsh'ir idols. They need to be reminded that our father Neptulon is the only one who truly rules the seas.

passages.title: False Idols
passages.text:
You make an old murloc proud, <race>.

Thank you, and may the waves ever lap at your feet.

passages.title: Eliminate the Okril'lon
passages.text:
The Horde are a nuisance that we will deal with, but they are proving more difficult than previously expected. You are to put a stop to this.

To the west of Nethergarde, the Okril'lon main forces press on our defenses. They currently hold the Nethergarde Mines, and they mean to move into the supply camps and, eventually, the Keep. Thin their numbers and delay their advance, <name>.

passages.title: Eliminate the Okril'lon
passages.text:
You're an excellent asset to the Alliance and the Kirin Tor, <name>.  Well done.

With time, our forces will retake the mine and press these Horde dogs out of the Blasted Lands.

passages.title: Nethergarde Reigns
passages.text:
Lungertz is a strong leader, but he is proud. He understates the pressure that the Horde is really putting on us. Without our mine... Nethergarde is penniless.

We need to move the Horde forces from the supply camp NOW, and doing so means killing their commander, Captain Metlek. He's not a strong leader, and prefers to bark orders from the back lines, but even so, his death might buy us the victory we need.

passages.title: Nethergarde Reigns
passages.text: Thank you, <name>.  Thanks to your efforts, I am confident that with time, we will take back the Nethergarde Mine.

passages.title: Watcher Mahar Ba
passages.text:
It's time for you to visit the Watcher. He's been in a bit of a mood lately, and I'm not quite sure why.

Head up to the top of the mage tower and check in with him. I don't have any work for you here, but I'm certain that he will.

passages.title: Watcher Mahar Ba
passages.text: My associates were correct to send you to me.  I have a problem which may threaten the sanctity of Nethergarde, and I need someone more capable than most.

passages.title: Fight the Flood
passages.text:
I'm here because Muradin himself knew that this survey needed someone to keep these buffoons on their toes. They're all too scared of the wildlife to do a thing! If I'm to get them off their duffs, I'm going to need some cleanup done.

We've got an elemental problem, first off. The flood did such a number here that the water itself's gone hysterical.

I bet you've never slapped the sense into an entire lake before, but I'm askin' it of you now. Whallop those elementals but good for me.

passages.title: Fight the Flood
passages.text: Roll up your sleeves, $lad:lass;, you're gonna have to do better than standin' around gawking if you want a nod around here.

passages.title: Fight the Flood
passages.text:
Well I'll be. There's someone around here that isn't a disgrace to Magni, bless his poor gravelly heart.

Just for that, you get first crack at the ale, lad. But don't let it get to your bloody head! We've got more gorram work to do, and I won't tolerate you lettin' up early!

passages.title: Sedimentary, My Dear
passages.text:
The destruction of the Stonewrought Dam was no small thing, <lad/lass>. We're here to find out just how bad the damage is. A mighty load of water's rampaged through here, and if it's disturbed the earth too far, we could be in for worse later on.

We can tell a lot from studying the sediment of the flooded area. I need as many soil samples as I can get, so if you could head out there and collect some more, I'd much appreciate it.

passages.title: Sedimentary, My Dear
passages.text: Let's see the sediment, then.

passages.title: Sedimentary, My Dear
passages.text:
Ah, well. The good news is, these will do perfectly. The bad news is I can tell they're the wrong color for topsoil here, even drunk as I am.

That means things aren't looking good for the area, <name>. But we've got more tests to run before we hang up the towel.

passages.title: Thresh Out of Luck
passages.text:
The local wildlife's all messed up from the flood, it seems. This fen used to be full of crocolisks, but I haven't spotted a single one.

What I have spotted are threshadons. Never used to be any here, so the flood must've swept them all right out of Loch Modan.

Lucky for us, because they're tastier than crocolisks, and I'm running low on provisions. Bring me back some threshadon meat for the camp, and I'll gladly pay you for it.

passages.title: Thresh Out of Luck
passages.text: Are they meaty ones? Let's have a look.

passages.title: Thresh Out of Luck
passages.text: Lovely. These'll fry up nice, and the camp'll be spared a week of mushroom biscuits.

passages.title: Fenbush Berries
passages.text:
We're good on provisions, but we're in need of some medicine. Half the camp's fiercely hung over, and a remedy's in order.

Luckily, I know a good folk remedy taught to me by my dear old mum. We just need some local ingredients.

Gather me some fenbush berries, if you would. They keep to where there's water and shade, so look along the shore and near other plants.

passages.title: Fenbush Berries
passages.text: How much've you got?

passages.title: Fenbush Berries
passages.text: These'll do nicely. I'll have the lads back on their feet as soon as I make these somewhat edible.

passages.title: A Dumpy Job
passages.text:
Alright, I need you to help me find my dumpy level.

What's that look for? That's right! I said my dumpy level! It's a piece of significant surveying equipment!

I didn't name the bloody thing, alright? Go look it up! All I did was leave it on a rock long enough for one of those horrible oozes to swallow it up. The place is crawling with 'em, but one of them should still have it inside.

passages.title: A Dumpy Job
passages.text: Did you find the dumpy?

passages.title: A Dumpy Job
passages.text:
Oh good, it's undamaged! Thanks a lot.

You ah, you might want to wipe yourself off a bit there.

passages.title: Drungeld Glowerglare
passages.text:
The Dark Iron clan is up to no good out here. And if that surprises you, you're thicker than the addled blotters over in that tent. Muradin may pay lip service to those sooty cretins back in Ironforge, but out here all bets are off.

We had a raid against the camp last night, and one raid is too many. Their leader's a stout fellow by the name of Glowerglare, and he's hiding in the cave on the south bank of the river.

Bring me Glowerglare's beard as proof he's no longer a threat to us and Ironforge.

passages.title: Drungeld Glowerglare
passages.text: Let's see it, then.

passages.title: Drungeld Glowerglare
passages.text: Good riddance to bad rubbish! I'll burn the foul thing later so it doesn't stink up the camp.

passages.title: Mr. P's Wild Ride
passages.text:
Now Mr. P just needs an angel to help him navigate. Will you be that angel, <mister/miss>? With you helping we can go out into the crag and kill bunches and bunches of Horde! Waddya say? Come on, <mister/miss>! PRETTY PLEASE WITH SUGAR ON TOP?

If we kill enough Horde, Mr. Fallowmere will buy us all ice cream!

passages.title: Mr. P's Wild Ride
passages.text:
<Lord Fallowmere coughs.>

This is awkward...

Good job out there with the robot. You caught me a little off guard. I didn't realize the little girl was so...

<Lord Fallowmere points to his temple and twirls his finger around.>

Special...

Well, whatever gets the job done, right? Am I right?

Probably.

Have some ice cream.

passages.title: Gerenzo the Traitor
passages.text:
<The Gnomecorder comes to life with a loud buzz.>

Come in, <name>! Are you zhere? I have noted on ze map that you are near ze Cragpool Lake vater vheel, is that correct?

It vould appear that ze Venture Co. has holed up at ze vheel. Have a look around vhile you are up zhere. If you happen to zee a traitorous gnome by ze name of Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, put your boot firmly up his keester for me and for Gnomeregan! I vill pay handsomely!

passages.title: Gerenzo the Traitor
passages.text:
<The Gnomecorder buzzes loudly.>

Vonderful! That's von more name I can scratch off of my list!

I vill be in touch.

Xakxak, out!

passages.title: BEWARE OF CRAGJAW!
passages.text:
By order of people not wanting to get themselves devoured whole by a really huge fish, Cragpool Lake is OFF-LIMITS! Someone decided to up and put a huge, dwarf-eating fish in the lake.

It is strongly recommended that you stay out, however, if you are the heroic type and have a few friends around, do us all a favor and kill the damned thing! Maybe I can get some fishing done then, eh?

If you manage to actually do it, meet me back at Windshear Hold for a reward.

-Ol' Irongoat

passages.title: BEWARE OF CRAGJAW!
passages.text: You kill the beast?

passages.title: BEWARE OF CRAGJAW!
passages.text: Well I'll be a monkey's uncle. You actually got the beast, eh? Well, a deal's a deal! Here's your reward!

passages.title: Get Out Of Here, Stalkers
passages.text:
Thelgen Rock's an important site here. We need to use it to study the bedrock formations an' such.

Of course, it can't be that easy, so Thelgen Rock's also full of giant cave stalkers. Big as a dwarf and twice as hungry. Like I said, these fancy-lads are researchers, not warriors, so if I want them to get anything done you're gonna have to help me clear the filthy bugs out.

Kill as many of the blighters as you can and I'll make it worth your while, <name>.

passages.title: Get Out Of Here, Stalkers
passages.text: Good job. I wouldn't be surprised if the horrid things had eggs in there somewhere, but it'll do for now.

passages.title: Down In Thelgen Rock
passages.text:
I'm feeling slightly less wobbly now, so I'm going to start setting up the level for my final measurements here. There's one last thing I need from you.

There's a seismograph set up deep within Thelgen Rock to record any movements in the earth. If things have been continuing to shift since the cataclysm, this'll tell us.

The seismograph's at the very bottom of the cave; find it and bring the record it's created back to me.

passages.title: Down In Thelgen Rock
passages.text: Let's see what we've got, aye?

passages.title: Down In Thelgen Rock
passages.text: Wonderful, lad. This should be all we need. Let's have a look.

passages.title: Incendicite Ore
passages.text:
Thelgen Rock over yonder is something of a natural wonder. It's the only known source of incendicite in the world!

The stuff's rare, highly sought, and ridiculously explosive. Hit it with a steel mining pick and you'll set off a fireworks show that'll put a room full of goblins to shame.

Luckily, I've developed a spark-proof pick for such tasks. I'll loan it to you if you bring me back some incendicite ore, and I'll split you in on the profits, of course.

passages.title: Incendicite Ore
passages.text: Well, you look like you're in one piece.

passages.title: Incendicite Ore
passages.text:
Glorious! Beautiful stuff, this ore.

Good on you for not droppin' your pick. Last person I sent out let the butt end hit the floor, and that part's not sparkproof.

passages.title: The Floodsurge Core
passages.text:
This is all that's left of the huge elemental that attacked you: a frothing orb of water that continues to fight your grip.

Forba might appreciate seeing proof that you helped stop another threat to the camp.

passages.title: The Floodsurge Core
passages.text: Eh? What's that you've got there?

passages.title: The Floodsurge Core
passages.text:
The thing's still got some fight in it! Amazing!

You're a tough one, <name>. It's much appreciated. I'd say a reward is in order before you head out.

Keep doin' your best for Ironforge, you hear? And if you ever see my sister, say hello for me.

passages.title: If the Horde Don't Get You...
passages.text:
<Captain Kosak coughs weakly.>

Was traveling up Webwinder Path, coming from Northwatch Expedition Base Camp in the south. Ambushed. Not by Horde. Spiders. Big, ugly, hairy, nasty spiders.

Fought off dozens, maybe hundreds. Lost count. Overtaken by their queen. She took a chunk right out of me. Barely made it out alive. Might be dying.

More of my men coming. Must provide safe passage. Kill spider queen.

<Captain Kosak passes out.>

passages.title: If the Horde Don't Get You...
passages.text:
<Captain Kosak forces a smile at you.>

Don't worry about me. Should be ok now that big hero killed the spider queen.

Can get reinforcements through safely now.

passages.title: Preparations for the Future
passages.text:
Poisoned travelers are becoming a common occurrence around Windshear Hold. Why just the other day a Northwatch Captain fell prey to the spiders of the Webwinder Hollow. He would have died to the poison had it not been for my anti-venom. Sadly my stock of anti-venom is almost completely depleted.

If you're heading south towards Webwinder Hollow, would you kindly recover Deepmoss venom sacs for me? You should be able to acquire them from Deepmoss spiders.

passages.title: Preparations for the Future
passages.text: Have you recovered the venom sacs I requested?

passages.title: Preparations for the Future
passages.text: This will keep us stocked on anti-venom for the foreseeable future. Thank you, <name>!

passages.title: Properly Inspired
passages.text:
Hello! I've been scrambling, scrambling to prepare for the Admiral's assault. He's got high hopes and high plans to blow all kinds of things sky high! ...or water high? That would do.

Blowing things high takes EXPLOSIVES! I don't have explosives. It's saddening. Very saddening.

I've been properly inspired to improvise though, and the solution has become apparent. The bulbs on the seaweed hanging from the ruins contain a surprisingly volatile gas. Maybe you might gather some for me? Pretty Please?

passages.title: Properly Inspired
passages.text: Tick, tock, tick, tock. Always in such a hurry. No time for innovation. What I wouldn't give for a lab again!

passages.title: Properly Inspired
passages.text:
You are brave indeed! I've seen you battling all manner of murloc, naga, and pointy-toothed fish, but that was nothing! The way you just sling those kelp bulbs under your arm like that is a whole new kind of fearless. BOOM! You could blow up at any second.

You're my kind of <race>.

passages.title: Fallen But Not Forgotten
passages.text:
That was a disaster! Most of our men went down to spears before making it anywhere near the rendezvous.

We're only going to be able to hold this position for so long before the naga overrun us. We need to get out there to the southwest and save as many of the men as we can find - do anything you can.

They won't last long. Please hurry!

passages.title: Fallen But Not Forgotten
passages.text:
Thank you. Truly.

We need to get these men moving as soon as possible. I'll meet you back at the forward post soon, I'm sure.

passages.title: Get Zherin!
passages.text:
If we're going to get those oil drilling rights, we need to know what the Horde is offering. How can we win if we can't do them one better?!

Their negotiator, Trackmaster Zherin, is up there talking with one of their khans right now. Why don't you head up and persuade him to hand over the Horde's proposal?

You don't have to kill him... we're not savages! Just rough him up a bit.

passages.title: Get Zherin!
passages.text: Do you have the Horde's proposal? What are they offering for the drilling rights?

passages.title: Get Zherin!
passages.text:
What?! How'd they get that much gold to offer?

We don't have that kind of money!

passages.title: Get Koalbeard!
passages.text:
If we're going to get those oil drilling rights, we need to know what the Alliance is offering. How can we win if we can't do them one better?!

Their negotiator, Kravel Koalbeard, is up there talking with one of their khans right now. Why don't you head up and persuade him to hand over the Alliance's proposal?

You don't have to kill him... we're not savages! Just rough him up a bit.

passages.title: Get Koalbeard!
passages.text: Do you have the Alliance's proposal? What are they offering for the drilling rights?

passages.title: Get Koalbeard!
passages.text:
What?! How'd they get that much gold to offer?

We don't have that kind of money!

passages.title: Arcane Legacy
passages.text:
The rage of the elements has unearthed a hidden Highborne city in the heart of Stonetalon Mountains.

Directly southwest of here, through Sishir Canyon, you will find the Ruins of Eldre'thar. Within the ruins lie treasures untouched by mortals for ten thousand years!

Take this device and use it on the Highborne ghosts that inhabit the ruins. It will... put their souls to rest and also collect valuable data which I may peruse at a later date.

passages.title: Arcane Legacy
passages.text: I assure you, simpleton, the spirits you captured are at rest. Do not let their protests move you.

passages.title: Capturing Memories
passages.text:
The great cataclysm has unearthed a forgotten Highborne city within Stonetalon Mountains. You must venture southwest to the Ruins of Eldre'thar. Once you are there, search the area for ancient relics. Return the relics to me so that I may study them, <name>.

Go! Lest we keep the arcanist waiting!

passages.title: Capturing Memories
passages.text: Have you recovered the ancient relics?

passages.title: Capturing Memories
passages.text: Wonderful! Arcanist Valdurian will be most pleased.

passages.title: Fool's Gold
passages.text:
We definitely DO NOT have the kind of gold that the Horde is offering. <name>, we have to do something or we're not going to be able to get those drilling rights!

Wait a minute! There was this report from an underwater survey that we did right after the Cataclysm struck. Something about some gold-looking ore that was pushed up from underground. That's it!

Head west to the old stomping grounds of the centaur, Splithoof Crag and Splithoof Hold, and dig some up.

passages.title: Fool's Gold
passages.text: Once you return with enough of that pyrite, we'll give it a once over with a paint brush, pile it all up on a pallet, and send you back up with it to the chieftain.

passages.title: Fool's Gold
passages.text: Genius! Now, where's that gold paint? I know it's around here somewhere.

passages.title: Fool's Gold
passages.text:
We definitely DO NOT have the kind of gold that the Alliance is offering. <name>, we have to do something or we're not going to be able to get those drilling rights!

Wait a minute! There was this report from an underwater survey that we did right after the Cataclysm struck. Something about some gold-looking ore that was pushed up from underground. That's it!

Head west to the old stomping grounds of the centaur, Splithoof Crag and Splithoof Hold, and dig some up.

passages.title: Fool's Gold
passages.text: Once you return with enough of that pyrite, we'll give it a once over with a paint brush, pile it all up on a pallet, and send you back up with it to the chieftain.

passages.title: Fool's Gold
passages.text: Genius! Now, where's that gold paint? I know it's around here somewhere.

passages.title: Onwards to Menethil
passages.text:
This news needs to get to Menethil as soon as possible. I'll send you along on my fastest ram, <name>.

He knows the way, just make sure you're steady in the saddle and hold on tight.

Don't dawdle around the camp. We've got to send word quickly!

passages.title: Onwards to Menethil
passages.text: Welcome to Menethil, stranger. I hope you've got good news or a stiff drink with you.

passages.title: Onwards to Menethil
passages.text:
Let's take a look here.

Oh, this is just lovely. "Significant geological instabilities"? "Threat of sudden, massive topological destabilization"?

Nice to hear that somethin' bad might happen around here. I guess we'll just pick up our flooded town and fly it off somewhere safe!

Bah!

passages.title: Assault on Menethil Keep
passages.text:
We'd barely pulled ourselves together after the flood when the Dark Iron hit the town. My men and I all rushed to defend the townsfolk, but the crazed fools retreated right into the keep itself.

They're holed up good, and we can't destroy the keep. Not with half the town in ruins already.

Take my place, <name>. I'd take the leader on myself if he hadn't dealt me this blow. Enter the keep, slay Horghast, and bring this to an end!

passages.title: Assault on Menethil Keep
passages.text: Is he dead? Is Horghast dead?

passages.title: Assault on Menethil Keep
passages.text:
He's dead! Thank the Makers...

I don't like the looks of them, lad. The Dark Iron I've tussled with were never this crazy. Something's getting to these sods...

passages.title: Return to the Shrine
passages.text:
Aviana's Egg should have arrived safely back at the Shrine. You should go check on it! Choluna should know how to handle this.

I'll finish the last of our business here and catch up with you later.

passages.title: Return to the Shrine
passages.text:
<name>! Is it true you led an assault against a twilight dragon?

You are truly a herald of the ancients!

passages.title: Eminent Domain
passages.text:
It is our destiny to take this oil. Unfortunate that the centaur retreated to here when the sea rushed in.

Unfortunate for them, that is.

They've spit in our faces, <name>. We made them a generous offer and they made the mistake of not accepting. Now we... you, will show them the error of their ways.

Clear the centaur off of the Splithoof Heights. The oil must flow!

passages.title: Eminent Domain
passages.text:
That'll teach them. You've softened the Splithoof up enough that we should be able to govern them now with a minimal guard presence from the Speedbarge.

That is, once we've dealt with their supposed air elemental leader.

passages.title: Eminent Domain
passages.text:
It is our destiny to take this oil. Unfortunate that the centaur retreated to here when the sea rushed in.

Unfortunate for them, that is.

They've spit in our faces, <name>. We made them a generous offer and they made the mistake of not accepting. Now we... you, will show them the error of their ways.

Clear the centaur off of the Splithoof Heights. The oil must flow!

passages.title: Eminent Domain
passages.text:
That'll teach them. You've softened the Splithoof up enough that we should be able to govern them now with a minimal guard presence from the Speedbarge.

That is, once we've dealt with their supposed air elemental leader.

passages.title: Defend the Drill
passages.text:
I'm not leaving here empty-handed! Are you?

I bet you were wondering what's in the giant crate. Well, wait no longer. I want you to take one of our drilling rigs to the oil pools and pump us up some crude.

Of course, you should expect the centaurs to attack. Just defend the drill long enough for us to get a barrel or two out of the ground.

passages.title: Defend the Drill
passages.text: How much oil did you get?

passages.title: Defend the Drill
passages.text:
Oil! Black gold! Tanaris Tea!

We're rich! We just have to clear out the remaining pesky centaur. I'm sure with all the money we're going to make, we can relocate them to some other bluff.

passages.title: Defend the Drill
passages.text:
I'm not leaving here empty-handed! Are you?

I bet you were wondering what's in the giant crate. Well, wait no longer. I want you to take one of our drilling rigs to the oil pools and pump us up some crude.

Of course, you should expect the centaurs to attack. Just defend the drill long enough for us to get a barrel or two out of the ground.

passages.title: Defend the Drill
passages.text:
Oil! Black gold! Tanaris Tea!

We're rich! We just have to clear out the remaining pesky centaur. I'm sure with all the money we're going to make, we can relocate them to some other bluff.

passages.title: When Life Gives You Crabs
passages.text:
There's a lot to do here, <class>, but we need to keep an eye out for the gifts of fate.

When the flood rolled in, right over our houses, it swept a good number of ocean dwellers with it. Menethil Bay's full of crabs now, large and ripe for the picking.

When life gives you crabs, go crab fishing, I say. Bring me back the largest, meatiest claws you can find and I'll pay you.

passages.title: When Life Gives You Crabs
passages.text: Don't bother with the smaller claws, they're more work to shell than the meat's worth.

passages.title: When Life Gives You Crabs
passages.text: A hearty seafood dinner will lift everyone's spirits and help us get the town back in shape again. Thanks for the help, <name>.

passages.title: Reclaiming Goods
passages.text:
Not long ago a merchant vessel, the Blind Princess, was raided by murlocs. Although the ship escaped intact, much of its cargo was dragged overboard by the creatures, including a very valuable statuette of Terenas Menethil. We want that statuette recovered.

Search the coastal murloc hovels for crates, barrels and other evidence of lost cargo. Find the Menethil statuette and return it to me.

passages.title: Reclaiming Goods
passages.text:
This crate is covered with clawed scratches, and the marks of water damage.  Prying it open reveals soggy and rotted straw, as if something of value was stored in the crate.  You search through the straw...

...and find an armload of red-colored bottles.

passages.title: The Search Continues
passages.text:
You thoroughly search this cluster of murloc hovels, and find no trace of the Menethil statuette.

Perhaps one of the two nearby hovels to the north and northeast will have more clues.

passages.title: The Search Continues
passages.text:
This barrel is largely untouched.  Prying it open...

...you are assaulted by the pungent odor of cheese.  It's a little wet, but still tasty!

passages.title: Search More Hovels
passages.text:
This grouping of murloc hovels, after a thorough inspection, reveals nothing.

...but you're certain that the next clue you find will be fruitful.

One of the hovels to the north must have the Menethil statuette!

passages.title: Search More Hovels
passages.text: This barrel is halfway buried amidst the mud and grass ...

passages.title: Return the Statuette
passages.text:
<After pulling the barrel free from the muck and opening it, a silvery figurine is found packed in fine straw. It depicts a young, long-haired paladin with hammer upraised.

This must be the Menethil statuette! You must now return it to Karl Boran in Menethil Harbor.>

passages.title: Return the Statuette
passages.text: Do you have the statuette?

passages.title: Return the Statuette
passages.text:
The captain of the Blind Princess will be relieved to hear this precious cargo has been recovered.  You've well earned this payment for services rendered.

It's good to see dependable folk like you, especially in trying times such as these.

passages.title: They Put the Assass in... Never Mind
passages.text:
Ah, the Explorers' League - such a profound group of morons. Not only do we have tauren ghosts up our butts, the Explorers' League has also managed to open up a backdoor to the primary Horde base in Stonetalon, Krom'gar Fortress.

Now we've got Krom'gar assassins silently executing everyone in the mine.

I need you to head in there and clean house.

I almost forgot to give you these goggles. Put them on immediately. They'll make all the stealthed assassins in the mine plainly visible.

passages.title: They Put the Assass in... Never Mind
passages.text:
<The Gnomecorder buzzes and whirs.>

Hey, this thing on?

<You hear a tapping sound.>

Anybody there?

passages.title: Is This Thing On?
passages.text:
<The Gnomecorder crackles with energy. You can hear Lieutenant Paulson on the other end.>

Stupid gnome junk... Is ANYBODY there? <name>, are you there?

Maybe <he's/she's> dead.

Listen, if you can still hear me, we just got word that a Horde master assassin is in the mines, directing the other assassins. Find her, kill her, report back to me.

Paulson, out.

passages.title: Is This Thing On?
passages.text: Nicely done, <name>! You worked the mines like a pro. Now how about returning my goggles.

passages.title: Leave No Man Behind!
passages.text:
Horde monsters!

<Corporal Wocard spits.>

Look at this place! They've wiped out innocents! Civilians!

Listen, <name>, you've got to help us. Go into the Deep Reaches and look for surviving miners. If any are still alive they're probably scared witless! Check in the nooks and crannies of the mine. Maybe in mine carts! There are bound to be some left alive and in hiding.

passages.title: Leave No Man Behind!
passages.text: Thank the Light! You truly are a righteous instrument of power! The Alliance is lucky to you have, <name>.

passages.title: Spelunking
passages.text:
Hurry, <name>!

Make your way to that cavern at once.

We shall go behind you to ensure that you are not followed.

passages.title: Spelunking
passages.text:
A... a <race>? Here?

I must be mad...

passages.title: Go Blow that Horn
passages.text:
That old, bitter centaur, Skycaller Vrakthris, mentioned a great air spirit that the centaur worship. To secure the Heights, the last step is for us to deal with this thing.

I've seen them blow the giant horn at the top of the hill up there and an air elemental came down. It gave them orders and then dissipated.

Go blow that horn, <name>.

passages.title: Go Blow that Horn
passages.text: It's simple really... you blow the horn, their elemental leader shows up, and you kill it.

passages.title: Go Blow that Horn
passages.text: Well then, let's see them get any kind of magical hocus pocus air support now when we take over!

passages.title: Go Blow that Horn
passages.text:
That old, bitter centaur, Skycaller Vrakthris, mentioned a great air spirit that the centaur worship. To secure the Heights, the last step is for us to deal with this thing.

I've seen them blow the giant horn at the top of the hill up there and an air elemental came down. It gave them orders and then dissipated.

Go blow that horn, <name>.

passages.title: Go Blow that Horn
passages.text: It's simple really... you blow the horn, their elemental leader shows up, and you kill it.

passages.title: Go Blow that Horn
passages.text: Well then, let's see them get any kind of magical hocus pocus air support now when we take over!

passages.title: The Third Fleet
passages.text:
I was once First Mate on the Wave Mistress, ship-of-the-line in the Kul Tiras Third Fleet. The Doomed Fleet. Doomed, for on its last voyage the fleet was attacked by red dragons. Dragons controlled by orcs!

We didn't stand a chance against that dragonfire...and our fleet was burned and sunk off this here coast. I'm the sole survivor of those poor vessels...

...Bring me my mead, <class>. It's down in the cellar of the inn. As far away as I put it from me, I can't go without it in the end.

passages.title: The Third Fleet
passages.text: Oh, I'm so very thirsty!  Won't you buy a drink for this poor, pathetic fool?

passages.title: The Third Fleet
passages.text: Ah!  That hits the spot, and loosens the tongue.  Thanks, mate!

passages.title: Cursed to Roam
passages.text:
<Bolstered, Fitzsimmons continues his tale...>

I am the sole survivor of the ill-fated Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, wrecked off the coast to the north. On one of our ships was hidden a great, and terrible treasure, and the eerie power of it keeps the souls of my brothers trapped within the ships' rotting hulls.

I'm haunted by them day and night. First Mate Snellig calls for me! He's supposed to be dead! Please, <name>, look for him near the shipwrecks and just...tell him to leave me alone!

passages.title: Cursed to Roam
passages.text: Fitzsimmons sent you, didn't he? It's been so long...

passages.title: The Cursed Crew
passages.text:
The sailors of the Third Fleet are damned, forever cursed to wander these shores in agony. Fitzsimmons' anguish is tied to us; so long as we suffer, there can be no rest for him, either.

You must end the suffering of my crewmates' spirits. Purge their ghosts from this plane, and return to me.

passages.title: The Cursed Crew
passages.text: Be thorough in your task, lest the curse take hold of ye as well.

passages.title: The Cursed Crew
passages.text: The cries of anguish have been stifled...but the source of the curse still lurks.

passages.title: Lifting the Curse
passages.text:
To break the curse, there must be a reckoning. Captain Halyndor damned us all to covet a forbidden artifact; the Eye of Paleth. His spirit still covets it, standing guard over the strongbox of his old ship, the Intrepid.

Vanquish the soul of the one who cursed us so, <class>. Defeat the Captain, claim his key, and spirit the Eye of Paleth far from this place.

passages.title: Lifting the Curse
passages.text: This chest is securely locked.

passages.title: Lifting the Curse
passages.text: The key is rusted but it fits the lock neatly.

passages.title: A Mother's Worries
passages.text:
My son Gimlok's the light of my life. It warms my heart to see him playin' with the other children.

I can't help but worry, though. There's sharks not but a few feet away in the bay. If it's deep enough for one to swim its way here...

I can't bear it! Please, you're clearly one <race> that's seen tougher situations than us townsfolk. Would you get rid of those nasty sharks for me? At least a few?

passages.title: A Mother's Worries
passages.text: Oh, bless your heart, to do such a thing for a married woman like me. You're too kind.

passages.title: Armaments for War
passages.text:
I am going to need to put you in harm's way once more, <name>. To the east you will find a mineral rich excavation site that was recently overrun by the Horde. At that site are crates of our weaponry, scattered about all over the place. The Horde has only recently taken over, so it is unlikely that they've found all of our supplies.

Get in there and get our Grimtotem friends some weapons!

passages.title: Armaments for War
passages.text: Have you gathered the armaments of war?

passages.title: Armaments for War
passages.text: This should be enough to supply a hundred Grimtotem! Now to present the weaponry to their chieftain.

passages.title: The Unrelenting Horde
passages.text:
While it is of utmost importance that you secure weapon crates immediately, we need the Unearthed Grounds to the east clear of Horde. If we are to open a supply line for our Grimtotem allies, we're going to need full access to the dig site.

Kill all Horde that you come across at the Unearthed Grounds, <name>. For the glory of the Alliance!

passages.title: The Unrelenting Horde
passages.text: I will call for the infantry to move in and clear up whatever might be left over. If only we had ten-thousand more like you, <name>!

passages.title: Debriefing
passages.text:
This soldier was near death, but I fear we do not have the time to await his full recovery. He has information we desperately need to know.

Be patient with him, but keep him talking until we've learned all that we can.

With luck we might discover just what we're up against...

passages.title: Debriefing
passages.text: Well, it's not encouraging, but it's something...

passages.title: Lo'Gosh is Ready for Battle
passages.text:
Thanks to your efforts, the great wolf ancient once more walks among us.

<class>, I need you to return to the World Tree and let Ysera know that Lo'Gosh is ready to take the fight to the front lines.

You may also speak with her about how to go about unleashing the other ancients.

Lok'tar Ogar, my friend. You have been an inspiration.

passages.title: Goldrinn's Message to Ysera
passages.text:
Goldrinn has been unleashed, and marches by our side! What you've done is nothing short of a miracle.

We must notify Ysera, at the World Tree. The sleeper is coordinating our reclamation of Hyjal, and she'll be delighted to hear that Goldrinn's legendary tenacity is at her disposal.

You may also speak with Ysera about how to unleash the other ancients.

Farewell, <name>. And thank you. You're an inspiration!

passages.title: Hamuul's Message to Ysera
passages.text:
<name>, we have prepared the soil and enlisted the help of the enigmatic turtle ancient.

Please travel to Nordrassil, the World Tree, and notify Ysera that I am prepared to take the next step.

It is important the we awaken all of the ancients we can; speak to Ysera and find out where else on Mount Hyjal you are needed.

passages.title: Return to Aviana
passages.text:
<name>, you've done all you can here. This whole cavern is about to collapse in on itself!

I'll gather up the last of our feathered steeds and ensure that the flamegate is sealed behind me.

You should go on ahead and let Aviana know that this abominable hatchery is no more!

passages.title: Return to Aviana
passages.text:
<Aviana's face is immobile as you tell her about what happened within the hatchery.>

They stole my eggs, <class>. They took them to that foul place. Corrupted them.

My children stolen, tormented, killed in a vat of flame... Yes, we will make Twilight's Hammer pay.

But I confess, part of me wants to fly up and simply watch this whole... world... burn.

passages.title: Aviana's Message to Ysera
passages.text:
For ten thousand years I drifted without form within the Emerald Dream. I awake to a nightmare.

<race>, seek out the dreamer - the dragon aspect you call Ysera - and let her know that I have returned and will aid the Guardians of Hyjal as they crush the Twilight's Hammer.

I will fill their skies with suffering.

passages.title: Free Freewind Post
passages.text:
Alas, it's time for you to leave. How quickly the chicks fall from the nest. Or, something.

Anyway, you've done solid work here, my friend, but Quentin and the night elves have been crying that they urgently need your help with the Grimtotem at Freewind Post to the northwest.

If you ask me, it's a lost cause, but who knows... maybe with your help they'll actually succeed?

passages.title: Free Freewind Post
passages.text: I'm glad that Fizzle finally sent you here. We're helping the tauren to retake Freewind Post and push back the Grimtotem.

passages.title: Firefight
passages.text:
It is... too late for me. Burned to all but the core. I have lived eons ... yet still my end seems sudden.

New life can spring from old. I still have wisdom to pass on. Please... do not let them take me before my work is done.

Keep the tormentors at bay... just a little longer, <class>.

Give me minutes, and I will give you a thousand lifetimes.

passages.title: Firefight
passages.text: Are you there, <class>? My vision is failing... I hear fighting...

passages.title: Firefight
passages.text:
Thank you, <race>.

I am ready now.

All that I am, and all that this forest once was... it is now yours.

passages.title: Tortolla's Revenge
passages.text:
The mountain blooms again! If we act quickly, we can press our advantage.

Our old friend Tortolla, the turtle ancient, is already on the move. At his own pace, of course...

Find Tortolla east of here, at the head of the path leading down into the scorched plains. Our strongholds there fell early in the campaign, but perhaps now we can reclaim them.

passages.title: Tortolla's Revenge
passages.text:
<race>.

I remember you. Savior of my children.

The time has come. For vengeance.

passages.title: Grimtotem Supremacy
passages.text:
Throughout all of Greatwood Vale you will find Grimtotem under attack by the Horde. Hellscream's armies show no mercy and no compassion, killing anything that stands in their way.

But no more! Take the armaments you brought for us and find Grimtotem in battle with the Horde. Give them the weapons of the Alliance and watch as they destroy their Horde assailants! Go, there is much work to do, ally.

passages.title: Grimtotem Supremacy
passages.text: Have you armed the Grimtotem?

passages.title: Grimtotem Supremacy
passages.text: The fight is far from over, <name>. The Horde generals still live...

passages.title: When Archaeology Attacks
passages.text:
Listen, <lad/lass>, any good archaeologists know the risks that come with the job. If you don't unearth an ancient evil or get cursed by wicked spirits at least once in your career, you're not digging up anything worthwhile!

No, the real archaeologists know that a little thing like fossilized bones reanimating into skeletal creatures is no reason to stop working.

I still need those fossil bones. Collect 'em from the fossil monsters roaming around and bring them back to me, and I'll reward you.

passages.title: When Archaeology Attacks
passages.text: Don't be coy about it, now! Bring back a good armful of 'em!

passages.title: When Archaeology Attacks
passages.text:
See? Not bad, eh? Why, I almost wish all my finds decided to dig themselves up for me. It'd make my job a lot easier!

Of course, you made it easier too, <name>. Much obliged.

passages.title: Strike the Earth!
passages.text:
In case you didn't notice, the land here in the Wetlands is pretty messed up. Floods, earthquakes... and on top of it all, even the ground's got a wild hair now.

I never thought we'd be attacked by our own dig site, but sure enough, big chunks of it are now rampaging around trying to flatten any dwarf they see.

You look like a strong, strapping young <race>... mind going down there and slapping some sense into the clods?

passages.title: Strike the Earth!
passages.text: That's showin' em what for! Good on you.

passages.title: Tooling Around
passages.text:
I'm in charge of supplying this dig. It's not that bad, but having to pick up and move out so fast wasn't exactly ideal!

Archaeologists need tools, you know. You can't run around pulling up priceless antiquities with your bare hands. If you're going back to the dig site, can you bring back the tools that got left behind?

passages.title: Tooling Around
passages.text: Are they all here? We left a lot back there.

passages.title: Tooling Around
passages.text:
That's a relief! Maybe we can dig our way out of the hole we're still in, eh?

No, nevermind, just a bad joke.

passages.title: I'll Call Him Bitey
passages.text:
Have you heard some raptors are intelligent enough to be domesticated? It's true! I've seen hunters tame them.

It gets quite lonely out here, you know, even with Wenna to keep me company... a pet's just what I need to brighten my spirits. A little baby raptor would be the best!

If you're out there slaughtering the adults, would you mind bringing me back some mature eggs? You can tell if they're ready to hatch by the wobbling.

passages.title: I'll Call Him Bitey
passages.text: Do you have enough eggs? I can't take my chances with only one. Statistics, you know.

passages.title: I'll Call Him Bitey
passages.text:
Wonderful! These should be ready to hatch within the day...

Now I just need to cobble up a raptor pen before they all hatch nigh-simultaneously. What could go wrong?

passages.title: Gizmos and Gadgets
passages.text:
I've been coming up short on parts recently for my engineering projects, and the other day I finally saw why: the Mosshide gnolls have been making off with them!

I don't have any idea what they could possibly want them for, but I need those gizmos back. They're probably strewn all over the marsh by now, but if you see any, could you gather them and bring them back?

passages.title: Gizmos and Gadgets
passages.text: Did you find them?

passages.title: Gizmos and Gadgets
passages.text: Oh, wonderful! I'll be able to start reassembling these right away. Thank you so much!

passages.title: Crocolisk Hides
passages.text:
I've skinned crocs in the wetlands for years, <class>. Things have changed though.

You see, not to bore you with a sob story, but when the cataclysm flooded Menethil Harbor, our house went with it. My wife and kids don't have a place to stay, and I need to make as much money as I can to get us under a roof again.

I've been skinning crocs 'til I was too tired to move, but I still need more skins to sell. If you bring me some croc hides, I'll pay you a bit for them.

passages.title: Crocolisk Hides
passages.text: Got any croc hides for me?

passages.title: Crocolisk Hides
passages.text: I'm much obliged, <class>. This'll go a ways towards getting my family back on their feet.

passages.title: Hunting Horrorjaw
passages.text:
I've been tempted to go after the big kill... the largest crocolisk out there, Horrorjaw. His hide alone would be enough to get my family out of this hole.

But I'm no fool. One mistake and I could lose a leg, or my life, and then where would my wife and kids be? Still homeless and without a father to care for them.

It's not my proudest moment, but I'll pick my family's safety over pride any day. Please, <class>... hunt Horrorjaw for me. You'll find him in his shady pool to the north, lurking.

passages.title: Hunting Horrorjaw
passages.text: Did you get it? Do you have Horrorjaw's hide?

passages.title: Hunting Horrorjaw
passages.text:
Amazing! You're a true hero, <name>. I'll never forget what you've done for me and my family.

I know it's not much, but please, take this with my blessing.

passages.title: Dinosaur Crisis
passages.text:
We've been getting more and more reports of raptor attacks in the area. I'm seeing to it that this place is safe enough for more settlement to start occuring, so I've put a bounty on the buggers.

A lot have been cleared out already, but the Highland raptors to the north have been growing in number. That won't be true for long, now will it?

Clear out a good deal of Highland raptors, and I'll have a nice reward for you.

passages.title: Dinosaur Crisis
passages.text: Don't be shy with those now. They're dastardly things.

passages.title: Dinosaur Crisis
passages.text: A job well done. Consider this reward not from me, but from Ironforge; the preservation of Khaz Modan is a matter that concerns every dwarf.

passages.title: The Mosshide Job
passages.text:
You seem trustworthy enough to help me out with my real problem, <name>. I was sent here by Ironforge to recover a shipment of gold ingots.

The ingots are part of the Ironforge Royal Treasury, stamped with the royal seal... only an idiot would steal them for profit, far too easy to trace. Oddly enough, this area is full of idiots: Mosshide gnolls.

I don't know how many gnolls you've fought before, but they're foul and brutal beasts, and dangerous. I need you to slay them and recover the missing ingots.

passages.title: The Mosshide Job
passages.text: There should be about eight ingots stolen.

passages.title: The Mosshide Job
passages.text:
Well done! The Ironforge Guard appreciates this, <name>. You've done our city a fine favor.

But something new has come up...

passages.title: Dark Iron Trappers
passages.text:
You may have seen them while you were out, but the Dark Iron clan has been spotted in this area. They're never up to any good, and it looks like they're kidnapping the Mosshide gnolls for some reason.

I don't know what their game is, but we're putting a stop to this before more foul play occurs. Go and stop them.

And if you're worried about fairness, try askin' them politely first and see how far that gets you.

passages.title: Dark Iron Trappers
passages.text: I don't suppose they agreed to come along quietly? Didn't think so.

passages.title: Grimtotem in the Post
passages.text: The journey ahead must begin with you killing the Grimtotem invaders at Freewind Post. If you can't stop them here, we won't be able to move into their territory.

passages.title: Grimtotem in the Post
passages.text:
Grim business, that.<Quentin coughs.>

No pun intended.

passages.title: Grimtotem in the Post
passages.text:
You must do away with the Grimtotem invaders at Freewind Post. They brought it on themselves, the cowards!

We can't take the fight to their territory with our back to them. Please help us take back our home, <class>.

passages.title: Grimtotem in the Post
passages.text:
It's a good start. Normally, I wouldn't wish harm on any of the Earth Mother's creatures.

But attacking us at our most vulnerable moment?! They deserve to die!

passages.title: Save the Sentinel
passages.text:
<Brienna waves a note around with Taur-ahe markings on it.>

Those monsters have captured one of our sentinels! They're threatening to kill her if we don't pull back!

We don't negotiate with cowardly beasts! Please, if you can, rescue her before it's too late, <class>.

passages.title: Save the Sentinel
passages.text: Thank you for freeing her, <name>. Those Grimtotem monsters would have killed her in cold blood.

passages.title: The Brave and the Bold
passages.text:
<Rau dismissively waves a note around with Taur-ahe markings on it.>

Those mongrels have captured one of our braves! They're threatening to kill him if we don't pull back!

We'll never allow those Grimtotem cowards to keep Freewind Post! Please, rescue him before it's too late, <class>.

passages.title: The Brave and the Bold
passages.text: Where's our brave? Is he alive?

passages.title: The Brave and the Bold
passages.text: Thank you for freeing him, <name>. Those Grimtotem would have killed him in cold blood.

passages.title: Horn of the Traitor
passages.text:
Here lies the broken body of the Freewind Post lorekeeper, Montarr. The aged tauren's body is broken, lying in a pool of his own blood.

A trail of droplets leads back to the inn....

passages.title: Horn of the Traitor
passages.text: What's this, <class>?

passages.title: Horn of the Traitor
passages.text:
A traitor amongst the tauren?

I've never heard of such a thing. Clan rivalries and warfare are one thing, but killing your own in cold blood.

<Quentin shakes his head in disbelief.>

passages.title: Horn of the Traitor
passages.text:
Here lies the broken body of the Freewind Post lorekeeper, Montarr. The aged tauren's body is broken, lying in a pool of his own blood.

A trail of droplets leads back to the inn....

passages.title: Horn of the Traitor
passages.text: <name>? What news do you have?

passages.title: Horn of the Traitor
passages.text:
The cliffwatcher was a Grimtotem spy?! No wonder we had no warning!

<Thalia seethes with barely contained rage.>

I don't want that damned thing. Throw it into the water and let the Longhorn name never be spoken again!

passages.title: It's Up There!
passages.text:
Listen, I've been tracking this bomb since you rescued me in Ashenvale. Whatever they're doing with it is going to happen real soon.

At the top of the large oil rig is a control room. Inside that control room you'll find a Krom'gar log book. That log book is the key to where this bomb is heading. Get up there and get the log book! Bring it back here and I'll decipher it for you.

passages.title: It's Up There!
passages.text: Did you recover the log book?

passages.title: It's Up There!
passages.text: OH NO! They plan to "test" the bomb at Thal'darah Grove! That's the school for young druids located in the heart of Battlescar Valley. You've got to return to Barus with this information! Master Thal'darah must be warned!

passages.title: The Lumbering Oaf Problem
passages.text:
Ever seen a hobgoblin? They're another vile goblin creation. Take a goblin, make it even uglier, fatter, bigger and stupider and you have a hobgoblin. Add to all of that a nasty mean streak and we've got a problem.

These lumbering oafs wander the Sludgewerks and Mirkfallon Lake, acting as muscle to the goblins.

Get out there and thin 'em out. Permanently.

passages.title: The Lumbering Oaf Problem
passages.text: Slowly, but surely, we pick away at the Horde's numbers. They won't have a leg to stand on when this war really opens up.

passages.title: Lost Wardens
passages.text:
We held out as long as we could, <class>. But the flames... the heat... We lost the whole town.

Captain Irontree refused to pull back when the flames engulfed us. Our forces are scattered. Maybe some of the others survived? We can mount a counter-attack!

Go into the Scorched Plain and rescue any lost wardens that got separated from the group. Then find Captain Irontree - he's probably taken up a fortified position in the middle of the fighting.

passages.title: Lost Wardens
passages.text: What?

passages.title: Lost Wardens
passages.text:
You've assembled the survivors? Good, good. And the rest of the mountain - healed?

Haha, strike me down! We're on the front lines again!

passages.title: A Hand at the Ranch
passages.text:
Captain Tharran asked me to pass along his thanks for your help and congratulations on a successful mission. He and his men are cleaning up the last of the trolls and tending to the wounded.

He also wanted me to ask you to check out reports about troll raids on the Amberstill Ranch to the north. Ask for Sergeant Flinthammer when you arrive.

passages.title: A Hand at the Ranch
passages.text: So you're the one who's been helping Captain Tharran beat back the Frostmane trolls? I've seen your name in the reports. It's good to finally meet you. You might be just the <class> we need to help secure the ranch.

passages.title: How Disarming
passages.text:
Naga weapons...

As you cast your vision on the naga Holding Pens, you see dozens of similar stacks of tridents positioned strategically.

Destroying their weapons could only hamper whatever wicked designs they are carrying out in this region...

passages.title: How Disarming
passages.text: You're confident that your assault on the naga armaments has made an impact on their effectiveness.

passages.title: What? What? In My Gut...?
passages.text:
Wha...what IS this!?

There's great pain growing... from deep in my bowels.

I think... ugh... they must have poisoned me!

They fed us strangely glowing seaweed that they grow around their stronghold...

I think these cramps will worsen if I don't get more soon...

Please, <race>. Try to find me some!

passages.title: What? What? In My Gut...?
passages.text: Were you able to find me any of their seaweed, <class>?

passages.title: What? What? In My Gut...?
passages.text:
Yes, yes. This is the stuff.

Maybe I can gradually eat less of it and avoid that side-effect.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Pressing the Advantage
passages.text:
It looks like most of the Twilight's Hammer has fallen back to regroup for another assault. Their most dedicated are staying behind to hold the line. This is our chance to whittle away at their leadership.
