Range out along the Scorched Plain and crush the Twilight Field Captains. We'll remove them from the equation!

passages.title: Pressing the Advantage
passages.text: Terrific! Twilight's Hammer will no doubt try to re-take the mountain, but they'll have to do so without the leadership of those fat-for-brains thugs.

passages.title: Desperate Plan
passages.text:
Jorlan and Hexascrub left to find a way to contact help. The trade lanes aren't far, so there might be a chance of success, but I'm wary to let anyone get their hopes up.

In truth, we don't have any other options. We're not likely to last much longer here. The naga will find us eventually, and... well... you saw how many of them there were.

You should go find the two of them on Biel'aran Ridge to the southeast. I'll keep everyone here safe as long as I can.

passages.title: Desperate Plan
passages.text:
Impeccable timing. Like clockwork! Trouble comes. You come. Save the day.  Clockwork!

We've devised our brilliant plan. Gloriously simple, barring the hostility of local life. Simpler yet with a you available!

passages.title: Hostile Waters
passages.text:
Hexascrub came out here with a balloon of some sort that he retrieved from one of our ships. He tried to float it to the top, but those Muckskin Scroungers came out of nowhere and swarmed the thing.

He's got an idea for another balloon, but we need to make sure that the past doesn't repeat itself. I need you to kill off those gill goblins. Or at the very least, enough of them to make them a bit more wary of us.

passages.title: Hostile Waters
passages.text:
Less gill goblins is good!

I'm glad that they're so primitive. I don't think I'd want to be dealing with a race of aquatic tech-freaks right now. Not at all.

passages.title: Unfurling Plan
passages.text:
Survival kits never have any rope. It makes no sense! No sense at all.

I bet those Kvaldir have rope. They're always riding around in boats, tying knots, dressing in nets. Go take some rope from them! I must have it for our plan to work. Absolutely must.

passages.title: Unfurling Plan
passages.text: The rope ties the whole plan together!

passages.title: Unfurling Plan
passages.text:
This is great! I love it. It should work per... ewww! Is this stuff braided with hair?

Doesn't matter. Almost done. This thing will be ready in the twist of a rope.

passages.title: Breakthrough
passages.text:
The fiery army that caused so much devastation up the hill has retreated east of here. Only the Scorchlords remain in action. If we can punch a hole through their lines to regroup with Captain Irontree's forces, the whole offensive may collapse.

<class>, I'm in no shape to continue fighting, but you look like you can do some damage. Slay those Scorchlords and regroup with Captain Irontree!

passages.title: Breakthrough
passages.text: You killed how many? Well, well. Quite a show. I guess my men don't have any more excuses.

passages.title: Hyjal Recycling Program
passages.text:
Reinforcements! I thought we were going to fight this out to the bitter end.

Very few of the Guardians of Hyjal remain, and our supplies are running out. The battlefield around our holdout here must be littered with serviceable arrows.

I know it's beneath your abilities, but can you gather up our spent ammunition? It's the only way we can replenish our supplies!

passages.title: Hyjal Recycling Program
passages.text:
Warden's arrows are crafted of living oak, blessed in the moonwells, and tipped with obsidian arrowheads scrawled with runes invoking the blessings of nature.

They're not cheap.

passages.title: Hyjal Recycling Program
passages.text:
Wonderful! Still sharp. A little blood on the fletching, but they'll fly true.

Thank you, <name>. Our defense of Hyjal can continue.

passages.title: Slave Labor
passages.text:
It will take me some time to break through this barrier and communicate with Nespirah. In the meantime, you can save some of those men that the naga have enslaved in the pits below.

<Duarn produces a length of rope from within his robes.>

This should come in handy.

passages.title: Slave Labor
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>... although I'm afraid I haven't been nearly as productive as you have.

passages.title: The Time for Mercy has Passed
passages.text:
This cavern is an abomination, <name>. And it's filled with horrors from the depths.

I don't want any of these - things - getting through the portal to the outside world. Slay everything!

passages.title: The Time for Mercy has Passed
passages.text:
So it is done.

Knowing that Twilight's Hammer is in league with creatures of malice such as these... it really curdles the blood.

passages.title: Seen Better Days
passages.text:
The world is unraveling around us, <name>. Old enemies seek to destroy us from one end, while ancient forces close in on the other.

<Elder Sareth'na sighs.>

I have seen better days - brighter days, and I long for them...

Across Stonetalon Peak lies the ruins of our old outpost - now overrun with darkness. If you happen to go that way, could you search for my sketch book? It holds many happy memories. I would reward you well for its return.

passages.title: Seen Better Days
passages.text: Have you found my sketch book?

passages.title: Seen Better Days
passages.text: You've found it! Elune bless you, child! Perhaps this book will give me the strength to carry on.

passages.title: Putting Them to Rest
passages.text:
As the Horde were marching upon Stonetalon, I noticed that some of the sentinels had fallen ill. Not long after, they started acting strangely. When the first tentacle burst from the ground the ill sentinels began attacking us. We lost the outpost shortly after...

The sentinels in the peak are now nothing more than shells - husks for something far more sinister. I want you to put the sentinels to rest and retrieve their glaives. Each glaive returned can identify a fallen sister.

passages.title: Putting Them to Rest
passages.text: Recover the sentinel's glaives, <name>. Each glaive is unique to a sentinel.

passages.title: Putting Them to Rest
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Each glaive has the name of the sentinel it belonged to imprinted upon its blade. We can now send word to their families and put their souls to rest.

passages.title: Back to the Depths!
passages.text:
Tendrils are bursting forth from the earth and terrorizing Stonetalon Peak. My sentinels are hardly making a dent in their numbers.

I suspect that there is a force at the heart of Stonetalon Peak that controls the tendrils. Perhaps if we can put a stop to that force, the tendrils will return to the depths from whence they came!

passages.title: Back to the Depths!
passages.text: I'm afraid that the death of Harbinger Aph'lass has not ceased the tendril attacks. You've done all that you can, <name>, and for that I thank you.

passages.title: We Are Not Alone
passages.text:
<Duarn closes his eyes, pauses, and nods.>

Nespirah has just informed me that we are not the only people fighting inside of this shell. A small group of Alliance slaves has escaped and is currently fighting off the naga on the other side of the shell, up on the ledge that overlooks Nespirah's heart.

Go find them, <name>, and see what help they can lend us. With their aid, we may be able to rouse Nespirah from her torpor.

I will remain here, should you need anything.

passages.title: We Are Not Alone
passages.text: <name>... is that you?

passages.title: Call of Duty
passages.text:
Listen up, <race>!

A new landmass has emerged off the coast of Eastern Kingdoms and we are engaged in a critical battle for control of the island!

Victory there will leave Stormwind completely defenseless!

Now is the time to strike!

Report to the docks at once for transport to the battle.

Every warship is engaged, so you'll be boarding a mercenary vessel commissioned by the Warchief himself.

passages.title: Call of Duty
passages.text: Not exactly the battle you had anticipated, I'll wager. But a battle nonetheless, as you shall soon see....

passages.title: Mired in Hatred
passages.text:
The mirebeasts to the west are not my brethren... they are symptoms of the earth's disturbance, a foulness of rot given form.

You would not understand... they take the shape of my kind, infested within with decaying spores, forcing out flourished life in the swamp. They take all and leave only rot. Nothing left, nothing left!

Soothe my mind, <race>. Slay the mirebeasts, cleanse the land, and perhaps my mind will settle.

passages.title: Mired in Hatred
passages.text: They aren't gone... I can still FEEL them...

passages.title: Mired in Hatred
passages.text:
Ahhh... yes. The swamp suffers less now.

More threats, though. More lurk. I can see them!

passages.title: The Threat of Flame
passages.text:
Flame has threatened me for far too long... far too long... but it is no longer the little ones, no longer mere gnats...

The fields burn! The hills and highlands scream, <race>, they scream. The elementals brought here consume all life in their wake.

They cannot stand, they cannot stand. Stop them. STOP THEM! Destroy the bringers of flame...

passages.title: The Threat of Flame
passages.text: Yes... the flames die. There is peace now. Peace for the land.

passages.title: Brood of Seldarria
passages.text:
<The Gnomecorder buzzes.>

Be very careful, <name>. You do not want to rouse that black dragon.

Now, look around you. If this is a nest then there must be black dragon eggs nearby. Search the premises for eggs and destroy any that you see.

Return to me should you find and destroy Seldarria's eggs.

Goldrinn watch over you.

passages.title: Brood of Seldarria
passages.text: A smashing success! Perhaps only a minor victory against the brood of Deathwing, but a victory nonetheless!

passages.title: Hungry Pups
passages.text:
Ah, a new arrival! Good that you're here <lad/lass>! The pups are hungry and we're completely out of food.

Thankfully they love dragon meat, which fortuitously exists in abundance within the Charred Vale, south of here.

Be a good <boy/girl> and fetch me several pounds of black dragon whelp filet.

passages.title: Hungry Pups
passages.text: Hurry, <name>, the pups are hungry!

passages.title: Hungry Pups
passages.text: Excellent. The dogs will be well fed and ready to defend our outpost for weeks!

passages.title: Pay It Forward
passages.text:
You are now able to move about this realm more freely and without fear of drowning.

This is where our work begins.

First, you have many allies nearby who are drowning as we speak. As I saved you, you must save them.

I have enchanted the shell you brought me. Use it to rescue your friends.

Hurry now!

passages.title: Pay It Forward
passages.text:
While you were away, I was able to revive some of the fallen warriors.

We'll need every hand if we are to survive here.

passages.title: For Peat's Sake
passages.text:
The elementals rampaging across Direforge Hill are setting the very land beneath them ablaze. In a marsh such as this, fire can find many places to smoulder through the deep moss and peat.

You must quench the fires before they spread further. Take this flower... blessed by nature's rain, it will let you douse the fires.

The blossom may also prove useful against the elementals themselves.

passages.title: For Peat's Sake
passages.text:
In sparing the land further suffering, you've also helped us soothe the greenwarden.

Many thanks, <name>.

passages.title: Last Stand at Whistling Grove
passages.text:
We might have a chance to beat these flames back thanks to your work in the Inferno.

Still, more wildlife is threatened. Keeper Taldros ran north through the flames, to Whistling Grove.

See if you can help him!

passages.title: Last Stand at Whistling Grove
passages.text: The forest is being devoured!

passages.title: Rest For the Weary
passages.text:
You have done well, <race>, but there is much more to do and I grow weary.

I have expended a great deal of energy sending a distress message to Earthen Ring leadership, pleading for their help.

I must rest if I am to be of further use to us here.

Speak to the leader of the men you've saved and do what you can to help them prepare for battle.

The naga are scouring the waters for us. It is but a matter of time before they return - and they will surely come in even greater force.

passages.title: Rest For the Weary
passages.text:
I hear you, <race>.

I understand the urgency, but these men are in no condition to fight.

passages.title: Buy Us Some Time
passages.text:
Many good warriors have been lost today.

If what the shaman says is true, then we must act swiftly or we will add to their numbers.

The naga are out there, scouring these waters looking for survivors.

We are not yet ready to fight, <race>. You must buy us time to make preparations.

Find the naga that hunt us and delay their efforts.

passages.title: Buy Us Some Time
passages.text: You give those scaly scum something to think about, <race>?

passages.title: Buy Us Some Time
passages.text: Let us hope that your work has bought us the time we need...

passages.title: Traveling on Our Stomachs
passages.text:
I'll need your help if I am to get these orcs ready for battle.

Any worthy leader knows that his warriors travel and fight on their stomachs. No food, no victory.

These warriors are weary from their struggle out there. They need food before they're ready to overcome a naga attack.

Speaking of traveling on stomachs, I saw plenty of crabs out on the sea floor...

passages.title: Traveling on Our Stomachs
passages.text: You got food for the troops, <race>?

passages.title: Traveling on Our Stomachs
passages.text:
Good grub.

Soon we'll be back to fighting strength.

passages.title: We're Here to Do One Thing, Maybe Two...
passages.text:
You're in Hellscream's army now, <name>, and in Hellscream's army we kick butt and take names. Gone are the days of our people starving in the streets of Orgrimmar as we sign treaties with elves. We take what we need now. Kalimdor belongs to the Horde!

The Alliance attempts to stop our expansion every chance they get. Unsatisfied with owning most of the Eastern Kingdoms, those pig-lickers want it all!

Overlord Krom'gar has called for more troops in Stonetalon. Get on the caravan west of here and go!

passages.title: We're Here to Do One Thing, Maybe Two...
passages.text: While you remain in Stonetalon and fight as a Krom'gar soldier you will remain suited up! Am I clear? DO you hear me, grunt? If I see you without Hellscream's beloved tabard I will put my foot so far up your backside that you'll be spitting up laces.

passages.title: Finders, Keepers
passages.text:
I recognize this helm, <race>. You were wise to bring it to me.

The Alliance have a special unit, trained and equipped to explore and fight beneath the sea.

It would seem that they are in this region to do more than just defend against our attack.

There must be more of these down here, and if you can find them it could turn things around for the Vanguard.

passages.title: Finders, Keepers
passages.text: Were you able to locate more of the Alliance gear, <name>?

passages.title: Finders, Keepers
passages.text:
Well done!

Now, more than ever, we are prepared to face the naga!

passages.title: Bring It On!
passages.text:
It is time, <class>.

We are as ready as we ever will be!

I shall address the Vanguard, and then we shall swim into the sea to meet our fate.

passages.title: Bring It On!
passages.text:
No time to address the Vanguard.

Just as well...

passages.title: Sira'kess Slaying
passages.text:
You're the <name> everyone's been talking about? Good to meet ya, love. Let's have a butcher's hook.

Well, enough rabbit, right? Let's get down to it. I need you to swim out northwest to the Sira'kess Front and read and write them snakes something quick.

Nothing fancy. They're looking for a bother, and we'll give 'em a right good one in the ol' boat race.

passages.title: Sira'kess Slaying
passages.text:
Chicken and rice, <name>! That will show those sorry and sad snakes who's the ol' pitch and toss!

Now it's bird lime for that tiddlywink. Finger and thumb or plink plonk?

passages.title: Caught Off-Guard
passages.text:
Our escape from the shell can't have gone unnoticed, but either the naga at these ruins weren't informed or they don't consider us a threat. I don't intend to take the opportunity for granted - we strike now.

I need you to slip into the lower level of the ruins to our west and take out as many of their patrols as you can. We cannot risk any of those patrols finding out about our occupation of this cave - make sure none escape.

passages.title: Caught Off-Guard
passages.text:
Excellent work, <class>.

I will get some patrols out of our own to make sure that no more naga get within sight of this cave. We should have the area secured within the hour.

passages.title: Upon the Scene of Battle
passages.text:
All around you lie the remnants of a fierce battle. The naga skeletons are no surprise, but the weapons and remains of their apparent opponents are somewhat more unexpected.

Amidst the bones, you spot a strangely prominent piece of metal jutting out from one of the skulls. It's difficult to tell what sort of weapon it might have once been part of, but it stands out sufficiently to prompt you to retrieve it as evidence.

Surely someone back at the cave would be interested in this revelation.

passages.title: Upon the Scene of Battle
passages.text: Yes, <class>?

passages.title: Upon the Scene of Battle
passages.text:
A shard of metal?

The remains you describe sound much like the sea vrykul we encountered in Northrend. We'll not be striking any alliances with their sort, no matter the cause. Still, this information may prove useful in the future.

I will think on it further if time permits. Thank you for bringing it to my attention.

passages.title: Properly Inspired
passages.text:
Been all over the place. Blown all kinds of things up. I thought I might have some trouble carrying on the trend, what with the water and all, but it's all just a matter of inspiration.

I found something volatile enough to make bombs out of! There's a bunch of kelp hanging under the terrace to the southwest. Normally kelp stores gas that makes it float - this kelp produces a different kind of heavy gas. It keeps it hanging, but also makes for great explosions.

Gather me some?

passages.title: Properly Inspired
passages.text: Tick, tock, tick, tock. Always in such a hurry. No time for innovation. What I wouldn't give for a lab again!

passages.title: Properly Inspired
passages.text:
You are brave indeed! I've seen you battling all manner of murloc, naga, and pointy-toothed fish, but that was nothing! The way you just sling those kelp bulbs under your arm like that is a whole new kind of fearless. BOOM! You could blow up at any second.

You're my kind of <race>.

passages.title: Fallen But Not Forgotten
passages.text:
That was a disaster! Most of our men went down to spears before making it anywhere near the rendezvous.

We're only going to be able to hold this position for so long before the naga overrun us. We need to get out there to the southwest and save as many of the men as we can find - do anything you can.

They won't last long. Please hurry!

passages.title: Fallen But Not Forgotten
passages.text: These guys aren't in good shape. We may need to retreat sooner than we'd like.

passages.title: Fallen But Not Forgotten
passages.text:
Thank you. Truly.

We need to get these men moving as soon as possible. I'll meet you back at the forward post soon, I'm sure.

passages.title: Desperate Plan
passages.text:
Toldrek and Fiasco left to find a way to contact help. The trade lanes aren't far, so there might be a chance of success, but I'm wary to let anyone get their hopes up.

In truth, we don't have any other options. We're not likely to last much longer here. The naga will find us eventually, and... well... you saw how many of them there were.

You should go find the two of them on Biel'aran Ridge to the southeast. I'll keep everyone here safe as long as I can.

passages.title: Desperate Plan
passages.text:
Look at you, a regular aquatic hero! Trouble comes. You come. Save the day.  You must be proud of yourself!

We've devised our brilliant plan. Gloriously simple, barring the hostility of local life. Simpler yet with a you available!

passages.title: Hostile Waters
passages.text:
Fiasco came out here with a balloon of some sort that he retrieved from one of our ships. He tried to float it to the top, but those Muckskin Scroungers came out of nowhere and swarmed the thing.

He's got an idea for another balloon, but we need to make sure that the past doesn't repeat itself. I need you to kill off those giblins. Or at the very least, enough of them to make them fear us.

passages.title: Hostile Waters
passages.text:
Less gilblins is good.

I'm glad that they're so primitive. I don't think I'd want to be dealing with a race of aquatic tech-freaks right now.

passages.title: Unfurling Plan
passages.text:
Survival kits never have any rope. It makes no sense! Rope and bombs, that's all they should store. The rest of this stuff is just a waste of space.

Except maybe the balloon. That's coming in handy right now.

I bet those Kvaldir have rope. They're always riding around in boats, tying knots, dressing in nets. Go take some rope from them! I must have it for our plan to work. It is non-optional.

passages.title: Unfurling Plan
passages.text: The rope ties the whole plan together!

passages.title: Unfurling Plan
passages.text:
This is great! I love it. It should work per... ewww! Is this stuff braided with hair?

Doesn't matter. Almost done. This thing will be ready in the twist of a rope.

passages.title: Sira'kess Slaying
passages.text:
So, you're the <name> everyone's been talking about? It's good to finally meet you.

Well, enough talk, right? Let's get down to it. I need you to swim out northwest to the Sira'kess Front and kill those naga real quick.

Nothing fancy. They're looking for a fight, and we'll give them one! Well, you will.

passages.title: Sira'kess Slaying
passages.text:
Nice, <name>! That will show those naga who's the boss!

Now it's time for that drink. You want rum or wine?

passages.title: Treasure Reclamation
passages.text:
We've got our reinforcements, but we still need to find a way to pay them. That kind of action doesn't come cheap.

Up on Deepfin Ridge to the northwest, the slimy gilblin have stolen all sorts of treasure. I think that it's time to reclaim some of it for the cause.

passages.title: Treasure Reclamation
passages.text: How much plunder have you managed to reclaim, <name>?

passages.title: Treasure Reclamation
passages.text: That should be enough for now. We know where there's more should the need arise.

passages.title: Treasure Reclamation
passages.text:
Blood and thunder! We have our reinforcements, but they still need to be paid. They won't be cheap.

Up on Deepfin Ridge to the northwest, the slimy gilblin have stolen all sorts of treasure. It's time to reclaim some of it for the Horde.

Hellscream's eyes are upon you, <name>!

passages.title: Treasure Reclamation
passages.text: How much plunder did you get, <name>?

passages.title: Treasure Reclamation
passages.text: That's a lot! And we know where there's more should the need arise.

passages.title: Dealing with the Surge
passages.text:
The elements are in turmoil, <class>. The cataclysm stirred up the long-dormant water spirits of Helm's Bed Lake, just to the south. They're angry, confused, and unwilling to hear my pleas.

I have tried everything I know to calm them, to persuade them to stop lashing out and attacking the sergeant's mountaineers.

It pains me to say this, but no other options remain -- we must kill the elementals.

passages.title: Dealing with the Surge
passages.text: It is never easy to countenance violence against the very elements whose powers I wield, but sometimes there is no other solution. Our duty to the people of Dun Morogh comes first.

passages.title: Those Aren't Masks
passages.text:
<name>, there are these demon squid-things out there that are eating gilblins' heads and then taking them over! That's one way to get slaves.

Think you could swim out northwest onto Deepfin Ridge or into the Sira'kess Front and bring me back some of those Merciless things?

passages.title: Those Aren't Masks
passages.text: How many you got?

passages.title: Those Aren't Masks
passages.text:
Ah, they're ugly, but they mostly look harmless. Smelly though.

Here, let me clean the gilblin stuff out of these. I've got an idea....

passages.title: Those Aren't Masks
passages.text:
<name>, there are demon squids out there that are eating gilblins' heads and then taking them over! They better not come in here!

Think you could swim out northwest onto Deepfin Ridge or into the Sira'kess Front and bring me back some of those Merciless things? Preferably dead, I think.

passages.title: Those Aren't Masks
passages.text: What's that smell?

passages.title: Those Aren't Masks
passages.text:
Ah, they're ugly, but they mostly look harmless. Mostly. They're almost cute in a way.

Here, let me clean the gilblin stuff out of these. I've got an idea....

passages.title: Promontory Point
passages.text: We need to get this information up to Captain Taylor on Promontory Point! He's out there to the northwest with Erunak Stonespeaker and the Earthen Ring.

passages.title: Promontory Point
passages.text:
That's very disturbing news, but I believe our Earthen Ring friends here have a plan.

And now that you're here....

passages.title: Promontory Point
passages.text: <name>, I need you to get this information to Legionnaire Nazgrim on Promontory Point. He's up there to the northwest with Erunak Stonespeaker and those Earthen Ring people.

passages.title: Promontory Point
passages.text:
If it weren't you saying it, I wouldn't believe what that troublesome goblin has to say. This is troubling indeed, but I think our Earthen Ring friends have a few ideas.

And now that you're here....

passages.title: Wings Over Mount Hyjal
passages.text:
<name>, is it true you're going to try to commune with the ancients?

Southwest of here is the Shrine of Aviana, the matron of all flying creatures. It's the home of my favorite instructor, Choluna. I've never encountered one who was so deeply in touch with the spirits of this world. You could learn a lot from her!

The recent attacks have isolated the shrine. But it's easily accessible from the air - look for the second biggest tree on Hyjal. Good luck!

passages.title: Wings Over Mount Hyjal
passages.text:
Oh, you were sent here by Tiala? A wonderful student, she'll do many great things.

Although I sense even greater potential from you.

Please, stay a while in our shrine. There's much to do, but you can't accomplish anything with a troubled mind.

passages.title: We Are Not Alone
passages.text:
<Duarn closes his eyes, pauses, and nods.>

Nespirah has just informed me that we are not the only people fighting inside of this shell. A small group of Horde slaves has escaped and is currently fighting off the naga on the other side of the shell, up on the ledge that overlooks Nespirah's heart.

Go find them, <name>, and see what help they can lend us. With their aid, we may be able to rouse Nespirah from her torpor.

I will remain here, should you need anything.

passages.title: We Are Not Alone
passages.text: <name>... is that you?

passages.title: Get to the Airfield
passages.text:
According to the plans you captured, the Dark Irons are planning a large-scale attack on the Ironforge Airfield! The council has moved most of our forces down into Dun Morogh to deal with the instability brought by the cataclysm, leaving our defenses weakened at the airfield.

We need a way to get you to the airfield quickly. Take the road back west toward Gol'Bolar Quarry and find Mathel Rustwrench. He should have a flying machine you can use. Go!

passages.title: Get to the Airfield
passages.text: Thank goodness you're here, <name>. The airfield's been attacked by the Dark Irons and I don't think we can hold out much longer.

passages.title: Barrier to Entry
passages.text:
Filthy, good-for-nothin' night elves have managed to disarm our entire minefield in Talondeep Pass. Somebody is gonna have to go back up there and re-arm them all! A perfect task for a worthless grunt like you, <name>. Here's to hopin' you don't blow yourself up in the process.

You'll find our "Elf Killers" scattered across Talondeep Pass, directly north of here. Take this wrench and get to work, maggot.

passages.title: Barrier to Entry
passages.text: What do you have to report, grunt?

passages.title: Barrier to Entry
passages.text:
<Saurboz looks you over.>

You have all of your limbs intact. This is a first.

passages.title: Spelunking
passages.text:
Hurry, <name>!

Make your way to that cavern at once.

We shall go behind you to ensure that you are not followed.

passages.title: Spelunking
passages.text:
...<race>? Here?

I must be mad...

passages.title: The Missing Blastgineer
passages.text:
It looks like you might not be completely useless after all. Perhaps you can handle something a little more important.

About two days ago I sent Blastgineer Fuzzwhistle to Windshear Mine. He was supposed to get there, make sure everything was going according to plan with the bomb, and report back. Two days and nothin'...

Head out to the woods south of here and find him. For his sake, he better be dead.

passages.title: The Missing Blastgineer
passages.text:
Blastgineer Fuzzwhistle is definitely dead. It's probably for the best.

It looks like he's holding a note in his hand.

passages.title: Alliance Attack Plans
passages.text:
<You pry the note loose from Fuzzwhistle's hand.>

They're onto us! They know all about the bomb. Planning an attack on Krom'gar Fortress! I think they sent a search party after me. Won't go out like a chump. They'll get a fight.

I think I hear them coming now! Their leader is a high elf huntress named Davinia. She spoke of attack plans. Avenge me by killing her and getting those plans! Her tent is nearby, to the east.

Hellscream's eyes are upon you...

passages.title: Alliance Attack Plans
passages.text: Did you find Fuzzwhistle?

passages.title: Alliance Attack Plans
passages.text:
Damn shame... He was a good goblin.

<Saurboz shakes his fist.>

As for you, <name>, you've done well. These attack plans will help us prepare. I want you to deliver the plans to Overlord Krom'gar personally! There's sure to be a promotion in it for you.

passages.title: Lessons from the Lost Isles
passages.text:
There are great dangers in the woods south of here. They are crawling with Darnassian scouts - assassins sent from Darnassus to kill us. Perhaps we can turn the tables on them, eh?

When I was marooned on the Lost Isles a goblin gave me these infrared heat focals. They allow the wearer to see heat signatures of certain creatures. Take the focals and use them while in the woods to the south. They will allow you to easily spot the scouts. Kill as many of them as you can! For the Horde!

passages.title: Lessons from the Lost Isles
passages.text: Well done, brother! Now they will know that they cannot sneak up on the Horde!

passages.title: Debriefing
passages.text:
This warrior was near death, but I fear we do not have the time to await his full recovery. He has information we desperately need to know.

Be patient with him, but keep him talking until we've learned all that we can.

With luck we might discover just what we're up against...

passages.title: Debriefing
passages.text:
That's it, <race>.

That's all I know...

passages.title: Debriefing
passages.text: Well, it's not encouraging, but it's something...

passages.title: Enemy of the Horde: Marshal Paltrow
passages.text:
My scouts have tracked the cause of this latest fiasco to one man: Marshal Paltrow. He commands the Northwatch forward camp that has established itself in Windshear Valley, west of here. Take him out and you remove a powerful Alliance field commander from the equation.

Paltrow must die, <name>.

passages.title: Enemy of the Horde: Marshal Paltrow
passages.text: Did you find any suspicious documents at Paltrow's camp? Perhaps on his rotting corpse? Any insight into the Alliance's attack patterns would be extremely helpful in the battle for Stonetalon.

passages.title: The Brothers Digsong
passages.text:
Private <name>, at attention! Ve are havink a small problem!

Ve have sent Humphrey and Oskar Digsong out to Underlight Canyon, to the northvest, but they are not comink back. They vere supposed to scout out the area, but ve have lost all contact with them.

Your assignment, Private <name>, is to locate our comrades and, if they live, bring them back to me!

passages.title: The Brothers Digsong
passages.text:
Of course we haven't returned yet!  We've had our fair share of setbacks... not the least of which was the passing of my dear brother Oskar.

<Humphrey sniffles loudly.>

He lost his grip and floated away, the poor lad!  He thought he'd grab some fish to bring back to the captain, but he floated off, and was eaten by one o' those... those great-eels!  Bwaaaah ha ha haaaah!

passages.title: Coldlights Out
passages.text:
Oh yeah! I was supposed to put together a report! I'd almost forgotten!

Looks like mostly harmless wildlife around here... 'cept for those blasted eels... and a few murlocs. Cap'n will be more interested in the murlocs, I think.

Go engage a few of 'em in combat and see what kinda moves they got. From what I've seen, the big ones hunt for fish in the kelp, and the little ones practice some kind o' magic or another... but that's all I know.

passages.title: Coldlights Out
passages.text:
<Humphrey listens as you recount your fights with the Coldlight murlocs.>

Hmm... they sound like regular ol' murlocs... just underwater.  That'll make Cap'n Glovaal happy.

passages.title: First Blood
passages.text:
Be prepared, <name>. You will cast the first blood upon this land for us.

The Syndicate, as they call themselves, are cowardly humans who betray even their own kind. Their isolation will make them easy prey.

Travel north, slay any Syndicate members you find, and claim Northfold Manor in the name of the Forsaken. Bring me the Bloodstone Amulets they wear as proof of your conquest.

passages.title: First Blood
passages.text: I won't be swayed by empty claims. Have you proof of your loyalty?

passages.title: First Blood
passages.text:
This is but a prelude to the slaughter we will visit upon these lands. All will know our name.

You have done well, <name>. Victory for Sylvanas!

passages.title: The Forsaken Trollbane
passages.text:
Let me tell you a story.

Once, there was a foolish troll named Zengu. He was tasked to find the sword Trol'kalar, the legendary blade of the human Trollbane line. He succeeded, and thinking his task done, went to leave Arathi by himself. There he was cut down by the humans, and the sword simply reclaimed.

We will not be so foolish. Our apothecaries have given us the perfect guide to reobtain Trol'kalar: the prince who once held it.

He stands ready to guide you, <name>. Speak with him.

passages.title: The Forsaken Trollbane
passages.text:
Yes... I was once Prince of the fallen kingdom of Stromgarde. I was cut down by the one seeking Trol'kalar.

I rue my foolish life now. I serve...only Sylvanas.

passages.title: Wanted! Marez Cowl
passages.text:
A bounty has been placed on the head of Marez Cowl, a high-level advisor and operative of the Syndicate. She was last seen within the Syndicate controlled territory of Stromgarde.

Bounty may be collected from Captain Nials.

Be warned: Marez is a skilled and cunning warlock, known for her trafficking with demons. Extreme caution is advised when hunting her.

passages.title: Wanted! Marez Cowl
passages.text: Greetings, <class>.  You have a report to make?

passages.title: Wanted! Marez Cowl
passages.text:
You took down Marez Cowl?  Well done, <name>.  Well done indeed!

Marez menaced our Stromgarde defenders, and it is rumored she was an emissary between the Syndicate and some other, darker power.  We are glad to see that she'll no longer ply her powers against us.

passages.title: Mr. D's Wild Ride
passages.text:
Now Mr. D just needs an angel to help him navigate. Will you be that angel, <mister/miss>? With you helping we can go out into the crag and kill bunches and bunches of Alliance! Waddya say? Come on, <mister/miss>! PRETTY PLEASE WITH SUGAR ON TOP?

If we kill enough Alliance Mr. Krom'gar will buy us all ice cream!

passages.title: Mr. D's Wild Ride
passages.text: This is awkward.

passages.title: Mr. D's Wild Ride
passages.text:
<Overlord Krom'gar coughs.>

I am - perhaps for the first time in my life - at a loss for words.

I am really not sure where Clarissa even came from...

passages.title: The Real Threat
passages.text:
Or'Kalar leads the ogres here. He has evaded slaughter for years. His very presence is an affront to the Dark Lady; Mug'thol, traitor to the Forsaken, commands him from afar!

We do not suffer ogres or traitors on Forsaken land. Bring me this ogre's head and I will make sure it's burned properly this time.

passages.title: The Real Threat
passages.text: Speak quickly.

passages.title: The Real Threat
passages.text: This is the fate of all who would stand in our way.

passages.title: Sigil of Arathor
passages.text:
I entrusted the sigil of Arathor to Lieutenant Valorcall, leader of my cavalry. He barely escaped with his life when it was taken.

It is unlikely he will do so again. Valorcall patrols the road between Stromgarde Keep and Refuge Point. Find him, and take the sigil from him once more.

passages.title: Sigil of Arathor
passages.text: Have you the sigil?

passages.title: Sigil of Arathor
passages.text:
Valorcall was loyal to me in life. His death will not be something I bear lightly.

But bear it I must. I am Forsaken. My old existence means nothing.

The sigils are ours; Trol'kalar awaits.

passages.title: Trol'kalar
passages.text:
The last sigil is mine...and with it, the four combine to the Sigil of Trollbane, key to the tomb. We are ready.

Trol'kalar lies sealed with its master's remains, within Trollbane's tomb in the catacombs of Stromgarde. It will be defended heavily...but my presence before you is proof enough that the defenders can be overcome.

Enter the tomb, retrieve Trol'kalar, and bring it here.

passages.title: Trol'kalar
passages.text: Have you Trol'kalar?

passages.title: Trol'kalar
passages.text: Trol'kalar, my father's blade... it seems like it's been an eternity since I saw it.

passages.title: The Princess Trapped
passages.text:
My name is Myzrael. I am a princess of the earth, and my captors, the giants, have trapped me deep beneath the Arathi Highlands. These crystal shards are the only way I can speak with the surface world.

Please help me. Allies of the giants, the Drywhisker kobolds, have a shard like this one in their Drywhisker Gorge, to the east. To power the cluster, you must gather motes of Myzrael from the kobolds and apply them to it.

I beg you, <name>, aid me!

passages.title: The Princess Trapped
passages.text: This cluster of shards looks much like the Shards of Myzrael.  But the same feeling of security does not pulse through them.

passages.title: The Princess Trapped
passages.text:
Ah!  You activated these shards.  Already I feel more myself!

But alas, I am still far from free...

passages.title: What? What? In My Gut...?
passages.text:
Wha...what IS this!?

There's great pain growing... from deep in my bowels.

I think... ugh... they must have poisoned me!

They fed us strangely glowing seaweed that they grow around their stronghold...

I think these cramps will worsen if I don't get more soon...

Please, <race>. Try to find me some!

passages.title: What? What? In My Gut...?
passages.text: Were you able to find me any of their seaweed, <race>?

passages.title: What? What? In My Gut...?
passages.text:
Yes, yes. This is the stuff.

Maybe I can wean off of it and avoid the side-effect.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Breaking the Keystone
passages.text:
Opening the Stones of Binding loosened much of my confinement, but a lock still holds me chained. It is the Keystone you see among this circle of stones. And the key is held by one of my captors, the stone watcher Fozruk.

You must obtain that key, which the stone watchers call the Rod of Order, from Fozruk and use it to open the Keystone.

<name>, you have done so much to aid me. Just a little more...and my gratitude will shake the very foundations of the earth!

passages.title: Breaking the Keystone
passages.text: The Keystone is charged with tremendous geomantic energy.

passages.title: Breaking the Keystone
passages.text: You place the rod in the keystone.  And a shudder is felt beneath you...

passages.title: BEWARE OF CRAGJAW!
passages.text:
By order of Overlord Krom'gar, Cragpool Lake is OFF LIMITS!

The ferocious beast known as Cragjaw has made the lake a death trap. Should you dispatch of Cragjaw, take his huge tooth as a trophy and return it to Spy-Mistress Anara for a reward.

passages.title: BEWARE OF CRAGJAW!
passages.text: What is it that you require?

passages.title: BEWARE OF CRAGJAW!
passages.text: A testament to the might of the Horde!

passages.title: I Got Your Parts Right Here...
passages.text:
Here's the dilemma: I could do one of two things, get killed down here like everyone else or get killed up at Krom'gar Fortress when Krom'gar realizes we've lost the mine. I'm choosing the third option, do nothing. So far, so good.

You need parts? Plenty from the left over junk scattered about in this mine. You just gotta go get 'em.

Good luck! Maybe if you get those parts we might be able to show our faces at Krom'gar Fortress.

passages.title: I Got Your Parts Right Here...
passages.text: How's that part hunt going?

passages.title: I Got Your Parts Right Here...
passages.text: I'll be damned! You managed to get the parts and not die. How are you only a sergeant?

passages.title: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
passages.text:
Dontrag can explain it better than me. Basically, we're stuck between a rock and a hard place. Can't do anything down here due to all of the things that can kill us and can't go back to the base due to all of the things that can kill us - you know?

Perhaps if we worked together we might be able to get this mess sorted out. How about you get started by clearing out some of these elementals that have apparently killed everything in the mine, ok?

passages.title: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
passages.text: Those elementals aren't going to kill themselves, buddy.

passages.title: Between a Rock and a Hard Place
passages.text: Get the parts, kill the elementals and rescue the peons... We get all of that done and we're as good as promoted!

passages.title: And That's Why They Call Them Peons...
passages.text:
These two are USELESS! When they first arrived I thought we were saved. Not so! Instead, Dontrag and Utvoch took one look at the mine and concocted some idiotic plan that involved standing here until... until we all died, I guess. 

You don't look nearly as useless. How about you lend a hand, friend? I've got dozens of peons, scared out of their gourds, hiding in the Deep Reaches. Find them and get them out!

passages.title: And That's Why They Call Them Peons...
passages.text: I knew it! You are a hero! If I have anything to do with it, you'll be promoted to legionnaire!

passages.title: Clearing the Highlands
passages.text:
No threat here will go overlooked. If we are to secure these lands under the Dark Lady's rule, we will tear from them everything living, inch by inch, piece by piece.

To the northeast, not a stone's throw away from this camp is an ogre mound. The Boulderfist ogres that dwell in it must be eradicated, <class>.

They are in the way. Show no mercy or hesitation.

passages.title: Clearing the Highlands
passages.text: Excellent. The march of the Forsaken continues.

passages.title: The Wavespeaker
passages.text:
One of the Earthen Ring, Wavespeaker Valoren, swam down into the Nightmare Depths to the northeast. We haven't heard from her in awhile.

Swim out there and see if you can find her.

passages.title: The Wavespeaker
passages.text: I sure am glad you're here!

passages.title: The Wavespeaker
passages.text:
One of the Earthen Ring, Wavespeaker Valoren, swam down into the Nightmare Depths to the northeast. We haven't heard from her in awhile.

Swim out there and see if you can find her.

passages.title: The Wavespeaker
passages.text: I sure am glad you're here!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Stormer Heart
passages.text:
With voodoo, our troops might have a chance at beating back the Grimtotem assault. With that said, I need several ingredients if I am to invoke black magic.

The first ingredient on my list is a heart from a cliff stormer. The beasts have nearly been hunted to extinction, but a few still exist around these parts. Find one and recover its beating heart!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Stormer Heart
passages.text: I need the cliff stormer heart.

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Stormer Heart
passages.text: Excellent. Once I have everything I need I will mix it all together and unleash the voodoo! Woe unto our enemies!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Ram Horns
passages.text: If I am to invoke voodoo, I will need several special reagents. Bring me horns from the Stonetalon rams of the region, <name>! Without the horns we are done for!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Ram Horns
passages.text: I need the Stonetalon ram horns!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Ram Horns
passages.text: Excellent. Once I have everything I need I will mix it all together and unleash the voodoo! Woe unto our enemies!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Resonite Crystal
passages.text: The final ingredient for the voodoo ritual is a special type of crystal called resonite. It can only be found in the Boulderslide caverns, west of here. Beware the kobolds! They guard the resonite with their lives!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Resonite Crystal
passages.text: I need the resonite crystals!

passages.title: Da Voodoo: Resonite Crystal
passages.text: Finally! Now I will create the charm that will hold the voodoo enchantment!

passages.title: The Queen and Her Court
passages.text:
<Darn grunts.>

Hrmph.

Things falling apart. Darn not happy. Now Darn's mate killed by spiders at Webwinder Hollow. Darn demands vengeance!

Help Darn? Kill Queen Silith and her little spiderlings? For Darn? For Darn's mate!

Webwinder Hollow is northwest of here, up the path. Go!

passages.title: The Queen and Her Court
passages.text: Have you killed Silith for Darn?

passages.title: The Queen and Her Court
passages.text: Darn still not very happy, but Darn will reward you for what you have done.

passages.title: Fight On Their Stomachs
passages.text:
The troops are hungry, <name>. With our supply lines cut off, we're steadily running out of food. I can cook the soldiers a feast if you can get me some ingredients.

Head into the woods west of here and look for Kalimdor eagle nests. Steal the eggs from the nests and bring them back to me.

passages.title: Fight On Their Stomachs
passages.text: I need eggs!

passages.title: Fight On Their Stomachs
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. These eggs should get us through the week.

passages.title: Free Wil'hai
passages.text:
Those tentacle horrors rising from the depths have trapped that poor beast. Please, <name>, can you save it by destroying those things?

Will you free Wil'hai?

Here, take my totem and plant it near the tentacles. The cold it emanates will cause major shrinkage on those monsters and then you'll be able to destroy them.

passages.title: Free Wil'hai
passages.text: Wil'hai is still trapped.

passages.title: Free Wil'hai
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

These nightmarish creatures that rise from below give me pause. I fear that our efforts will be for nothing.

passages.title: Nura Pathfinder
passages.text:
Southern Barrens is under attack by the Alliance. The tauren have sent out a call for help that we simply cannot ignore. All able bodied soldiers of the Horde should assist.

If you wish to help, take the path to the High Road, located in the village. Seek out Nura Pathfinder.

passages.title: Nura Pathfinder
passages.text: The situation is grim, <race>. We need all of the help that we can get!

passages.title: The Turd Problem
passages.text:
We have a little problem...

<Jibbly points to the large turds covering the base.>

We built the Sludgewerks near a wyvern habitat. Now our initial blueprints for the Sludgewerks were drawn up so as not to disturb the wyvern habitat as the beasts are apparently sacred to tauren and orcs. Do you know what's sacred to me? Not getting pooped on, that's what!

Between you, me and the wall, the wyvern must die!

passages.title: The Turd Problem
passages.text: Please help. The guards are getting a little uppity.

passages.title: The Turd Problem
passages.text: I sure hope you didn't miss any. I don't think I can take much more of this!

passages.title: Alina's Reward
passages.text:
The tale of Trol'kalar ends here, then. It will be a weapon to bring death to the living, in the name of the Dark Lady.

Leave me now, <name>. My job is once again to guard the blade. Tell Alina of your victory, I'm sure she will have a reward for you.

passages.title: Alina's Reward
passages.text:
The news of your victory satisfies me, <class>... a rare sensation. The Dark Lady herself has mused that our conquest of Lordaeron may be the only way the Forsaken can find true satisfaction, and pehaps even relief.

But it matters not. Our victory is inevitable. For your loyal service to the Forsaken, I award you in the name of Sylvanas.

passages.title: Hello Lolo
passages.text:
Goutgut get sent scouting. Look at many things. Big adventure!

Goutgut found secret pirate ship. Pirates all scared, run away. But ogre Lolo not run. Lolo make friend with Goutgut!

Goutgut have to leave, but miss Lolo. You go say hello to Lolo for Goutgut.

passages.title: Hello Lolo
passages.text: You friends with Goutgut! Him weird ogre. Smell funny.

passages.title: Hammerfall
passages.text:
You have served us well here, <name>. Now that we've made our mark, the next phase of our conquest will occur over months rather than minutes.

There is much work yet to be done, and I will spare you the tedium of waiting for our fortifications to trickle in. Travel to the east, to Hammerfall. The orcs there will no doubt have use of your aid.

passages.title: Hammerfall
passages.text: Throm'ka, <class>. If your deeds for the undead are as great as you claim, I am honored to help you serve the Horde.

passages.title: Orako
passages.text:
<Captain Verne looks down at his watch.>

Where is that hunter? I sent Orako to Underlight Canyon to prepare a recon report a week ago! Sure, he's a handful, and I didn't mind getting him out of my hair, but I need his report.

Say, what's your name? <name>? Would you be willing to go track him down? It seems strange to send a <class> to find a hunter, but I'm running out of options.

passages.title: Orako
passages.text:
Gah!  These fish are impossible to hit!

<Orako looks at you.>

My wolf got eaten by a fish, and I'm not going back until I find her.

passages.title: Die Fishman Die
passages.text:
A fish ate my wolf, and murlocs look like fish. I'm going to make those murlocs pay!

Head back down to the canyon and kill the fishmen! My wolf will be avenged!

passages.title: Die Fishman Die
passages.text:
I know, murlocs aren't fish.  I thought that killing them would make me feel better, but I still feel sad about my wolf.

<Orako sighs.>

passages.title: Orako's Report
passages.text:
<You remind Orako that he was supposed to send a report back to Captain Verne.>

Right, a report. All that I've seen here is fish. Lots and lots of fish.

<Orako looks over at the sack of fish that you brought for him.>

Bring this back to the captain. This is my report.

passages.title: Orako's Report
passages.text: Where was he?  What happened?

passages.title: Orako's Report
passages.text:
This is his report?!  That idiot...

I suppose we can use the food.  Thanks, <name>.  You've done as well as can be expected.

passages.title: Northfold Manor
passages.text:
We are fighting a war for Stromgarde, and we are losing. The ogres, the Syndicate and we have divided our once great city, and each faction battles the other into a bloody stalemate.

But our forces dwindle while our enemy grows.

Though Southshore has fallen, we must not let any further ground be yielded to our enemies.

Go to the Syndicate base in Northfold Manor and slay them. We must reclaim the land for ourselves before the Horde has a chance to creep further.

passages.title: Northfold Manor
passages.text: Very good, <name>.  The last thing we need with the undead looming is a gang of common thieves distracting us.

passages.title: Proof of Lies
passages.text:
At the heart of Battlescar Valley stands an ancient tree - a tree that has withstood the force of ages and has served as a place of peace and learning for generations. My kin have studied druidism at the grove, alongside the night elves, for as long as I can recall. Now I am to believe that the tree holds within it an Alliance weapon of mass destruction?

Krom'gar is wrong and I will prove it!

I have sent my son, Orthus, to Thal'darah Grove in search of this weapon. Go there now and meet him.

passages.title: Proof of Lies
passages.text: Orthus is dead. He is clutching something in his hand.

passages.title: Is This Justice?
passages.text:
He was a good boy, <name>. Young, loving. He would have never killed any of the young druids. They were his friends! No... Not Orthus.

The General must be called to answer for this crime. I will have justice!

passages.title: Is This Justice?
passages.text: This is justice.

passages.title: Is This Justice?
passages.text:
You saw with your own eyes, <name>. General Grebo attacked us!

Now what will we do? Surely the Warchief will have us all executed for treason.

passages.title: Claim Korthun's End
passages.text:
The Horde has spies in this area? Darkbreak Cove is nearby, and inside lies the Pincer X2! The Horde must not be allowed anywhere nearby!

Someone in Darkbreak Cove will want to hear of this... after you finish slaying some more of these dirty Horde spies.

passages.title: Claim Korthun's End
passages.text: You did well, <name>.  We need to be especially wary of Horde attacks right now.  The Pincer X2 has plenty of firepower at sea, but in the back of this cave, she is exceptionally vulnerable.

passages.title: Guile of the Raptor
passages.text:
The highland fleshstalkers to the south are even fiercer than the others of their kind. They possess not just strength, but true cunning.

When I was trapped by lethargy, even the amulets of strength failed to move me. But Tor'gan used the hearts of the fleshstalkers to imbue me with spirits that conquered my doubt, freeing me.

Our soldiers deserve the guile of the raptor. Collect the fleshstalker hearts for me, <name>.

passages.title: Guile of the Raptor
passages.text: My preparations are made, all I need are the raptor hearts.

passages.title: Guile of the Raptor
passages.text:
As Tor'gan taught me, I transfer the power and the spirit of the raptors into this orb. It will imbue our warriors with the fiery strength and intelligence of the raptor.

The guile of the raptor is yours now as well, <class>. Take it with pride, for the Horde!

passages.title: Just Like Old Times
passages.text:
It's funny. Kin and I have been through so much together, and here we find ourselves back in Arathi, like so many years ago.

We broke up a plot to create a new plague right here, her and I. It doesn't look like the Horde learned their lesson, because they're all over this farm yet again.

Their undead courier is shuffling around as obvious as daylight. If you want to help, find the courier and bring back whatever they're carrying.

passages.title: Just Like Old Times
passages.text:
We appreciate your help in looking for that courier, <name>.

While you were gone, Kin saw an apothecary come out of that same house to the south of here. I'm confident that they're up to no good--I just need proof of it before we go off and do something rash.

Have you had any luck yet?

passages.title: Just Like Old Times
passages.text: Apothecaries yet again. You think they'd get the message. Let's see what it is this time...

passages.title: Quae and Kinelory
passages.text:
The Horde have held Go'shek Farm to the east for a long time; it's never been of much concern compared to the rest of our problems here. But there's been reports of undead activity in the area.

Anything more alarming than shuffling peons over there warrants investigation. This isn't the first time the undead have been up to no good at the farm, so I've sent my best scouts there to check it out. Report to Quae and Kinelory and they'll fill you in.

passages.title: Quae and Kinelory
passages.text:
Refuge Pointe sent you? Good to know they're still there.

We've got some interesting things to check into here, <class>.

passages.title: Quae Trusts You
passages.text:
<Quae begins to go through the folder.>

Expansion...control of territory... these undead aren't cooking up anything new, but they're planning to roll over all of Arathi. We need to disrupt their plans.

I'll keep a lookout from up here. You go with Kin, and get those invasion plans. We're not going to let these walking corpses even know what day it is out here.

And keep her safe, you hear me?

passages.title: Quae Trusts You
passages.text:
The plague took our friends and family, but it was the Forsaken that took Phin. They're just as bad as the Scourge. I'll destroy every one of them with my own hands if I have to.

When you're prepared, come let me know. We'll get started right away.

passages.title: To Be Horde...
passages.text:
Stand by me, <name>, and watch as our mighty weapon destroys our enemies!

Learn what it means to be Horde!

passages.title: To Be Horde...
passages.text: Now do you understand?

passages.title: To Be Horde...
passages.text: Now you truly know what it means to be a member of the Horde, <name>.

passages.title: Kinelory Strikes
passages.text:
All right, <name>. I'm ready if you are.

Shall we?

passages.title: Kinelory Strikes
passages.text: You'd best keep with Kinelory. I trust you, but if something happens to her, I won't be accountable for my actions.

passages.title: Kinelory Strikes
passages.text:
You've done a great service for us, <name>. Thank you.

I hope Kin wasn't too much of a handful down there. She's very friendly, but can be just as deadly when you're her enemy.

passages.title: For Southshore
passages.text:
I've seen Kinelory look way worse after a night in the tavern than she does now. You obviously did a good job protecting her.

Refuge Pointe will want to know of our success. I'm going to stay here with Kin and let her catch her breath. Go on ahead without us.

passages.title: For Southshore
passages.text:
I admit I'm impressed, <class>. It's a small comfort amidst all that's happened here.

You have fought the undead, struck back against the Horde, and honored the memory of the victims of Southshore. On behalf of the kingdom of Stromgarde, I present you with an official commendation, and this reward.

passages.title: The Crazed Dragonmaw
passages.text:
The Dragonmaw orcs nearby are fast becoming a nuisance. Their suicidal attacks on the grove are merely annoying, though they provide my sentinels with some needed practice.

My scouts, however, have seen them rounding up black dragon whelps in nets. The last thing these lands need is a crude revival of dragon-taming. Strike out to the east, <class>, and cut down the whelpstealers; make sure their folly does not come back to haunt us later.

passages.title: The Crazed Dragonmaw
passages.text: The orcs will know better than to press further west now. Well done.

passages.title: Claim Korthun's End
passages.text:
You are seeink spies up above? This is not good... not good at all, comrade.

Return to Korthun's End and destroy them, my friend.

passages.title: Claim Korthun's End
passages.text: You did well, <name>.  We need to be especially wary of Horde attacks right now.  The Pincer X2 has plenty of firepower at sea, but in the back of this cave, she is exceptionally vulnerable.

passages.title: Secure Seabrush
passages.text:
The Alliance has spies in this area? Tenebrous Cavern is nearby, and inside lies the Horde's new submarine, the Verne! The Alliance must not be allowed anywhere nearby!

Someone in the cavern will want to hear of this incursion... after you finish slaying some more of these scheming Alliance spies.

passages.title: Secure Seabrush
passages.text: You did well, <name>.  We need to be especially wary of Alliance attacks right now.  The Verne's got plenty of firepower out at sea, but in the back of this cave, she's far too vulnerable.

passages.title: Secure Seabrush
passages.text:
You saw spies up above? This is not good... I won't have it.

Return to Seabrush and get rid of them before they start trickling into our hideout.

passages.title: Secure Seabrush
passages.text: You did well, <name>.  We need to be especially wary of Alliance attacks right now.  The Verne's got plenty of firepower out at sea, but in the back of this cave, she's far too vulnerable.

passages.title: The Twilight's Hammer Revealed
passages.text:
I and everyone else thought these fools were just Dark Iron up to no good, but these nutters are fullblown cultists!

The Twilight's Hammer wants nothing short of the destruction of the entire world. They've thrown their lot in with Deathwing and Ragnaros, and they've got a history with the Dark Iron.

But it doesn't matter who they are, what matters is they're in Dun Modr and they need to get out! I'll not let any past here. You get in there and crack some skulls!

passages.title: The Twilight's Hammer Revealed
passages.text: I've got to hold the line here, lad. As much as I want to get in there and tear them up, I'm dead set on making sure not a one of the slimy curs escapes!

passages.title: The Twilight's Hammer Revealed
passages.text: Good show, lad, but we've no time to celebrate. Thandol Span's in danger!

passages.title: The Battle of Thandol Span
passages.text:
I've defended the Thandol Span from being destroyed before, against the Dark Iron themselves. And so did my father, and his father before him...

The only Dark Iron that managed to give me the slip ran straight for the bridge. Something's amiss, and I'm betting when we get there we'll be waltzing right into an ugly trap.

I could use your help, <name>, for Ironforge. Are you with me?

passages.title: The Battle of Thandol Span
passages.text: There's no time to waste! Hurry to the Thandol Span!

passages.title: The Battle of Thandol Span
passages.text:
And good riddance!

Thandol Span's safe thanks to you, <name>, and hopefully Calamoth is down for good this time.

passages.title: Unplug L'ghorek
passages.text:
L'ghorek is the ancient that rests upon the shelf across from us. It is being controlled and its life energies slowly consumed by something immense beneath us.

There is a cave known as the Undershell down below L'ghorek. In that cave are three powerful ogre magi that are maintaining a ritual connecting the thing below with the ancient. You must kill these three to disconnect L'ghorek.

passages.title: Unplug L'ghorek
passages.text: Now that you have unplugged L'ghorek, we must attempt to make contact with it. I can sense that the ancient yet lives, but only barely.

passages.title: Fiends from the Netherworld
passages.text:
The ogre magi within the Undershell have summoned protectors for themselves: fleshling fiends from the netherworld.

We cannot risk these aberrations from being later used against our forces. While you are in there, I want you to destroy as many of those things as you can.

passages.title: Fiends from the Netherworld
passages.text: The last thing we needed was a bunch of summoned creatures swarming our forces during the final assault.

passages.title: Fiends from the Netherworld
passages.text:
Those ogre magi inside the Undershell have summoned defenders: fleshling fiends from the netherworld.

I do not want to see these aberrations used against our forces. While you are in there, destroy all of them!

passages.title: Fiends from the Netherworld
passages.text: That's one less thing we need to think about during the final assault.

passages.title: Nothing Left for You Here
passages.text:
There is nothing left for you here, <name>. As for me, I must lay Masha's body to rest. Once I have done that I will go to the bombing site and begin the process of regrowth. Perhaps one day a new grove will bloom - a grove infused with the spirit of my child and the fallen night elf youths.

If you wish to travel to Desolace, I hear word of a blood elf named Furien seeking adventuring partners. Perhaps you should seek him out.

Farewell, friend, I will never forget you.

passages.title: Nothing Left for You Here
passages.text: <Furien groans.>

passages.title: Checking on the Boys
passages.text:
I'm sure you've seen just how bad the damage to the Loch is by now. The damage spreads further than that, I'm afraid; all that water had to go somewhere, and it went down into the Wetlands.

There's a lot of fine dwarves down there trying to help out, and they need supplies. That's why I sent two of my mountaineers ahead with a cask of ale along the path into the Wetlands.

I haven't heard back from them since they set off down the road to Dun Algaz. Would you mind checking up on them?

passages.title: Checking on the Boys
passages.text:
Ah, well met, <class>.

Stormpike sent you? About the keg? Hoo boy...

passages.title: Ascend No More!
passages.text:
TO STOP... THEIR... RITUALS OF ASCENSION... YOU MUST DESTROY... THE ANCIENT CONDUITS.

THEY USE... THE CONDUITS TO... SIPHON... MY ENERGIES AWAY... AND MAKE... ASCENDANTS.

A FIGHT WITH... NEPTULON IS IMMINENT. THE TWILIGHT'S HAMMER... MUST BE DENIED... THESE CREATURES.

passages.title: Ascend No More!
passages.text: THEY SHALL ASCEND... NO MORE!

passages.title: The Trogg Threat
passages.text:
<class>, you may or may not be aware of the trogg threat looming over dwarven lands. With the Ironforge Reserve called up to the Alliance Front, we're left with a fraction of the defense forces needed to keep these lands safe. My regiment is assigned to watch over the town here and we cannot leave our post for fear of invasion.

But we need some pressure put on those damned troggs lurking in the hills. If you're up to the task, wage an assault on the troggs. Bring me back eight trogg stone teeth as proof.

passages.title: The Trogg Threat
passages.text: Do you have eight trogg stone teeth to show me?  If not, there is still work to be done, <name>.

passages.title: The Trogg Threat
passages.text: I am quite impressed, <name>.  You have done the Dwarven race a great favor by defending our lands.  King Magni Bronzebeard himself would be proud!

passages.title: In Defense of the King's Lands
passages.text:
We need to protect the Loch, <name>! With so many of the King's soldiers fighting valiantly on remote battlefields, we've become overwhelmed on the home front. Troggs are tunneling up from every crevice! The trogg infestation poses the largest threat to Ironforge.

We need you, brave adventurer, to venture forth and lay waste to the trogg threat. Slay twelve Stonesplinter troggs and venture back.

passages.title: In Defense of the King's Lands
passages.text: Loch Modan is under siege, <name>!  We need every able-bodied member of the Alliance to aid our cause.  Have you killed those troggs yet?

passages.title: In Defense of the King's Lands
passages.text: Well done, <name>!  You demonstrated uncanny courage on the battlefield.  Our war against the Troggs will be won with efforts such as yours.  You have served King Magni well.

passages.title: Bigger and Uglier
passages.text:
The Mountaineers tell me you are quite brave and capable, <name>. We need a <race> like you around here. The Trogg problem isn't getting any better. The reserves have been called to the front and we're all alone out here. But now that we have a seasoned <class> here, let's see what you can do.

Go out and kill 8 Stonesplinter Shaman and 8 Stonesplinter Bonesnappers. You should find them in and around the caves in the southern mountains.

Let's see if you live up to your reputation, Trogg-Slayer.

passages.title: Bigger and Uglier
passages.text: I knew the second I laid eyes on you, <name>, that you would make Ironforge proud.  You have served our people well. I salute you, <name>.

passages.title: Prisoners
passages.text:
The Twilight cultist dropped this key. Use it to free the Horde prisoners in the cages inside of L'ghorek.

Hurry before the prisoners become sacrifices to whatever lurks below!

passages.title: A Visit With Maybell
passages.text:
You seem like the helpful type, <name>. How about doing an old man a favor?

The last time I was over at the Maclure Vineyards I overheard Maybell crying in her cottage. Would you be so kind as to go check up on her? I'm a little worried.

passages.title: A Visit With Maybell
passages.text: William sent you? Bless his soul. I... I'm ok... It's just... Well...

passages.title: WANTED: James Clark
passages.text:
By decree of the Stormwind Army, a bounty has been placed on the head of James Clark.

Clark is wanted for robbery, burglary, arson, and murder. He is also a suspect in the kidnapping and disappearance of the Brackwell's prized pig, Princess.

James Clark was last seen heading towards Eastvale Logging Camp.

Bring James Clark to justice and report to Marshal Patterson at Eastvale Logging Camp.

passages.title: WANTED: James Clark
passages.text: Turning in a bounty?

passages.title: WANTED: James Clark
passages.text: And justice is served!

passages.title: Twilight Extermination
passages.text:
NOW, TAKE... THE ATTUNED RUNESTONE... AND USE... IT TO POSSESS... ONE OF... THE BOUND TORRENTS... AT... THE CENTRAL TEMPLE. THEY WILL IGNORE... YOU. YOU ARE BENEATH... THEIR NOTICE.

USE... THE ELEMENTAL'S POWERS... TO DESTROY... THE TWILIGHT DEVOTEES... AND... THEIR... FACELESS OVERSEERS.

passages.title: All The King's Men
passages.text:
The Stonewrought Dam may already be broken, <name>, but it holds back more than just water. The whole thing's hanging by a thread. With the land already destabilized, if they blow the remaining part of the dam...

...half of Loch Modan could collapse! The damage would be even more catastrophic. We'll be standing on a giant sinkhole if we don't act fast.

Get to the Stonewrought Dam and stop those Dark Iron Sappers. Make sure none of them get away!

passages.title: Blood Ritual
passages.text:
I suppose you want to know what we're doing. Here's the short version - a version at which I happen to be an expert:

The Shadowsworn cultists wish to summon the demon, Razelikh, back to the Blasted Lands. We cannot allow this to happen. So we're going to summon him ourselves, and then kill him. A task not as simple as it sounds...

Let me know when you are ready to begin the blood ritual, and then stand back.

passages.title: Blood Ritual
passages.text:
The blood ritual was a success; I can clearly see where we are going next.

I'm sorry, I misspoke.  What I meant to say is, I can see where YOU are going next...

passages.title: Not Just Any Body
passages.text:
We need Loramus Thalipedes, the demon hunter. He knows Razelikh's true name, and as you know: if you know the name of the demon, you have power over it. The problem is that Loramus has been killed, and his body torn apart.

If you bring me the pieces, we still have a recourse. All three pieces are in the west... the Dreadmaul ogres hide them in their caves. Move quickly, for much like Grimeo, Loramus also owes me a debt...

passages.title: Not Just Any Body
passages.text: Trust me... whatever happened to Loramus, we can fix.  The limits of blood magic are still undefined.

passages.title: Not Just Any Body
passages.text:
I see... yes, I can work with this.

<Kasim looks at the night elf's head.>

Loramus Thalipedes, demon hunter.  I look forward to our reunion.

passages.title: The Charred Granite of the Dark Portal
passages.text:
Kasim wants you to gather granite chips from these chunks of rock around the Dark Portal. I don't know what he'd want rocks for, but I have my suspicions, and they're not pleasant ones.

Use this pick and look for small outcroppings of rock along the edge of the portal's blast radius.

passages.title: The Charred Granite of the Dark Portal
passages.text: Please, lower your voice.

passages.title: The Charred Granite of the Dark Portal
passages.text: I hope this is what the gnome wanted.

passages.title: The Vile Blood of Demons
passages.text:
Sharim wants demon blood. Speaking personally, the stuff does not even seem like blood to me - more like liquid rot - but that is of no consequence.

Luckily for you, the area around the Dark Portal is crawling with demons. Infernals, felhounds, felguards... they've all got what you need, in copious, pustulent amounts.

passages.title: The Vile Blood of Demons
passages.text: Ugh, what's that smell?  Is that you, or the blood?

passages.title: The Vile Blood of Demons
passages.text:
There is no doubt about it, you have found demon blood.

Kasim's requests aside, I am sure that my Watch Commander is thankful for your efforts.  They have been struggling to deal with these demon distractions for some time now.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text:
Grol... the ogre.

<Kasim laughs.>

It would seem that Grol's body no longer rests with the ogres. His body, along with his amulet of power, is in a wrecked ship off the Shattershore, to the east. His amulet is the last... once combined, the three will give us access to Razelikh, and therein lies our chance to stop his madness.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text: The third amulet, from Razelikh's third lieutenant.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text:
<Kasim clutches the third amulet.>

He was a powerful warrior, this one.  I will keep the amulet until we are ready to proceed.

passages.title: The Final Ritual
passages.text:
The knife is ready. Loramus is present, and he knows what he must do. I must now take the three amulets and use their enchantment to grant you access to Razelikh, the amulets' creator.

I am prepared to perform the ritual on you and Loramus. Speak with me when you are both ready.

passages.title: The Final Ritual
passages.text: Quickly, friend.  This is but the calm before the storm.

passages.title: The Final Ritual
passages.text: It would seem that we are prepared to face our demon, <name>.  We have the amulet's blessing, we have the stone knife, and I alone know the demon's true name: Rakh'likh.  Together, this may be enough to defeat the Defiler.

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text:
Contrary to popular belief, ancient and powerful bloodmages do NOT drink blood. We eat normal food like everybody else - something which can be hard to come by in the recesses of a hostile cultist stronghold.

The ashmane boars in the central valley of the Blasted Lands are, if nothing else, convenient for eating, as their meat does not require any cooking. Would you hunt these boars and help me replenish my ever-dwindling foodstores?

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text: I'm famished!  If you don't hurry, I might actually resort to drinking our reagents.

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text: These are perfect, <name>.  I will eat well for the next several days.

passages.title: Protecting Our Rear
passages.text:
The only reason you see me standing aside Horde soldiers is because our duty outweighs our enmity... however slightly. We have been charged with protecting the Dark Portal from unauthorized travel, and with the recent cataclysm, we are particularly susceptible to an attack. We've already heard reports of black dragons in the area...

With my men focused on their duty, we need someone to keep the area demons in check. Around the portal you will find three demon lieutenants. Slay them.

passages.title: Protecting Our Rear
passages.text: You have not yet killed these demons.  <name>!  Get back to the field!

passages.title: Protecting Our Rear
passages.text:
Your work is appreciated, soldier.

<The commander leans in close, and whispers:>

<race>... if you're still interested, I have one more small task for you...

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text:
<Watch Commander Relthorn Netherwane speaks in hushed tones.>

I have orders from... higher up... that you would be suitable for. I've seen the Horde periodically referring to a stack of papers on that barrel over there. I'd like you to take a look at those papers and find out what it is that they're plotting. My duty and station prevent me from such a questionable task, but a newcomer like you might be able to slip in unnoticed...

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text: Did you get a look at those plans, <name>?

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text:
You're certain nobody saw you?  Good.

<Netherwane listens to your recount of the information you saw.>

Hmph... fairly harmless stuff.  Either the Horde are foolish enough to NOT be planning something against us... or they're hiding their information better than I expected.  Either way, well done, soldier.

passages.title: Surwich
passages.text:
Other than what you've seen, the Portal's been surprisingly quiet. There isn't much more work I can give to you, I'm afraid.

If you're looking for trouble, you might try the Gilnean fishing village to the southwest. Surwich, I think it was.

I know we're supposed to be friends with the Gilneans, but really? Worgen? I had enough trouble getting used to the draenei.

passages.title: Surwich
passages.text: Welcome to Surwich, <race>.  Please, have a look around.

passages.title: Feeling Crabby?
passages.text: Fresh crab legs have always been one of the King's favorite foods. We have had good luck catching fresh crabs in the canals over the past few weeks. Do you think you can lend me a hand and catch a few of them for me? Be sure to catch them alive, they are no good to me dead, the King requires the freshest catch we can muster.

passages.title: Feeling Crabby?
passages.text: You must have fast hands!  I can't believe you caught all those crabs so quickly!

passages.title: Feeling Crabby?
passages.text: These crabs look great!  I will clean these up and make sure that the King hears about your contribution.  Thanks!

passages.title: Supervisor Fizsprocket
passages.text:
According to the documents you salvaged from the caravan, the Venture Co. created many plans to attempt to drive us from our lands here, so that they could have free reign to plunder our lands.

The depths that they would sink to accomplish their goals disgusts and appalls me. I want the mastermind behind their plans killed. His name is Supervisor Fizsprocket, you will find him at the Venture Co. mine east of the ravaged caravan. Bring me his clipboard, we shall see if we find out anything useful.

passages.title: Supervisor Fizsprocket
passages.text: I seethe with anger at the thought of the atrocities the Venture Co. is willing to perpetrate against us in the name of profit.

passages.title: Supervisor Fizsprocket
