passages.title: Apply and Flash Dry
passages.text:
Alright, take this and apply it to his wounds. If the cauterizing effect of the flash dry explosion doesn't crack him wide open, it should completely heal him.

I think.

passages.title: Apply and Flash Dry
passages.text: Don't yap at me. Use the explosive bonding compound on Flint.

passages.title: Apply and Flash Dry
passages.text:
Looks like that did it. He should come to any moment now.

I told you I was a grand master of alchemy!

I've got some extra resin leftover. I can make it into all kinds of explosively wonderful stuff. What do you want?

passages.title: Well, Come to the Jungle
passages.text:
My commander has sent me to scout for potential recruits to assist in the defense of Grom'gol Base Camp in Northern Stranglethorn. Are you familiar with Stranglethorn? It's a long way away... across the Great Sea, on the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms. You fit the build he was looking for... interested in leaving Kalimdor for a while?

If so, then go talk to my cohort Bort in Orgrimmar. He'll help you board the zeppelin.

And tell him I said "Woozle wozzle." He'll know what it means.

passages.title: Well, Come to the Jungle
passages.text:
Hah!  That Cromula cracks me up.

Oh, right, Stranglethorn.  You're really going?

passages.title: The Shell of Shadra
passages.text:
We've one last part to collect, and then we'll have everything we need.

The Shell of Shadra is held by the spider god's last living high priestess, Qiaga the Keeper. She stands atop the Altar of Zul, guarded by other fanatical zealots.

Simple enough, no? Get up the steps of the altar and send her head rolling back down them. Bring the shell to me and we will have Shadra at last.

passages.title: The Shell of Shadra
passages.text: Do you have it?

passages.title: The Shell of Shadra
passages.text: Yes... it's finally time. Shadra will be ours!

passages.title: Shadra the Venom Queen
passages.text: <The ground rumbles as the idol sits on the altar, and the lake below roils! Shadra is emerging!>

passages.title: Shadra the Venom Queen
passages.text:
Excellently done. You have served the Dark Lady well today, <name>.

This virulent blood will supply our armies with all manner of powerful weapons against the disgusting Alliance. We will wipe them from these lands.

For the Horde, of course... and all thanks to you.

passages.title: Meet the High Tinker
passages.text:
I don't know if you'll remember Mekkatorque or not. Nevin tells me that memory loss is pretty common for a Gnomeregan survivor.

Mekkatorque, or more properly, the High Tinker Mekkatorque is the leader of all the gnomes. He has made a habit of meeting with every rescued survivor personally. You should introduce yourself to him. He'll be with his war council beneath the tent in the center of town.

passages.title: Meet the High Tinker
passages.text: It's good to meet you, <name>. You've probably heard others speaking of Operation: Gnomeregan. Let me tell you a bit about what happened and why we left the dwarven city of Ironforge.

passages.title: Meet the High Tinker
passages.text:
I don't know if you'll remember Mekkatorque or not. Nevin tells me that memory loss is pretty common for a Gnomeregan survivor.

Mekkatorque, or more properly, the High Tinker Mekkatorque is the leader of all the gnomes. He has made a habit of meeting with every rescued survivor personally. You should introduce yourself to him. He'll be with his war council beneath the tent in the center of town.

passages.title: Meet the High Tinker
passages.text: It's good to meet you, <name>. You've probably heard others speaking of Operation: Gnomeregan. Let me tell you a bit about what happened and why we left the dwarven city of Ironforge.

passages.title: Meet the High Tinker
passages.text:
I don't know if you'll remember Mekkatorque or not. Nevin tells me that memory loss is pretty common for a Gnomeregan survivor.

Mekkatorque, or more properly, the High Tinker Mekkatorque is the leader of all the gnomes. He has made a habit of meeting with every rescued survivor personally. You should introduce yourself to him. He'll be with his war council beneath the tent in the center of town.

passages.title: Meet the High Tinker
passages.text: It's good to meet you, <name>. You've probably heard others speaking of Operation: Gnomeregan. Let me tell you a bit about what happened and why we left the dwarven city of Ironforge.

passages.title: Revantusk Village
passages.text:
Not all forest trolls are foul nuisances like the Witherbark. North of here in the Hinterlands is Revantusk Village, home to the only forest troll tribe still allied with the Horde.

Even they cannot escape the cruelty of their brethren. The Vilebranch tribe wars with them, distracting them from our battle with the Alliance.

You have fought well here. Speak with Urda if you wish to fly to Revantusk. Their village will have use of your strength.

passages.title: Revantusk Village
passages.text: Welcome to Revantusk, <class>. I hope fighting the Witherbark hasn't exhausted you; the Vilebranch are even worse.

passages.title: The Fall of Jintha'Alor
passages.text:
We've got more to deal with than just dwarves, mon. While I watch the village, my mate Primal Torntusk has gone to lead our warriors against the wicked Vilebranch tribe.

They've killed our brothers, and I was even taken prisoner by them once. No more! This time, the city of Jintha'Alor falls to us.

Go to Jintha'Alor and speak with my mate. She's captured a camp near the entrance to the city.

passages.title: The Fall of Jintha'Alor
passages.text: Welcome, <class>. We're gonna make the Vilebranch regret ever crossin' us.

passages.title: Entrenched
passages.text:
Your intentions appear true.

I will impress upon the other Stone Lords my wary trust.

With this, they should speak to you.

More importantly, they should listen.

Earning their favor may take time. Earning the Stonemother's favor may take more time. Time is a potent offering, so be generous with it.

Among the Shuddering Spires far to the northwest, you shall find Kor the Immovable. He is evenly tempered. His situation lends itself well to seeking outside aid.

Go to him.

passages.title: Entrenched
passages.text:
Diamant says you are to be trusted. Diamant is patient and wise, so I shall allow you to prove yourself.

As it happens, I could use hands that are more... mobile.

passages.title: Intervention
passages.text:
The flayers have gone crazy with hunger. Their digging was once tempered and moderate. Now their hunger cannot be quenched. They grow murderously violent.

The flayers have turned on my sons. They overwhelm them. Kill them. It must stop.

Kill the flayers. They serve no purpose to the earth. Their passing will not be missed. Save my sons. Slaughter any flayers you find.

passages.title: Intervention
passages.text: You've proven useful, <race>.

passages.title: Putting the Pieces Together
passages.text:
<race>. If you act in the service of the Stone Lords, there are those that might aid you.

Watch for the Stonebound. They lie dormant all around the Shuddering Spires. It should not take much prompting to rebind them to service against the flayers.

passages.title: Putting the Pieces Together
passages.text: <Berracite grumbles, and you feel the reverberations gradually roll by under your feet.>

passages.title: Putting the Pieces Together
passages.text: Thank you, <race>.

passages.title: Clingy
passages.text:
<A miniscule elemental seems to have taken a liking to you.>

Caris... carstr... crystal? <Pebble looks up at you expectantly.>

<You did notice a very large crystal formation towards the middle of the Shuddering Spires. Perhaps you should take him there?>

passages.title: Clingy
passages.text: <Pebble looks up at you expectantly.>

passages.title: Clingy
passages.text: <The stones in Pebble's body bounce up and down happily. He seems very appreciative.>

passages.title: So Big, So Round...
passages.text:
<Pebble looks around, excited by something. After a few seconds of confusion, he stops and stares up at you with big, glowy gem eyes.>

Hug-nery... hungry...

<Try as you might, there's no resisting those eyes. Maybe Kor knows what mini-mentals like to eat?>

passages.title: So Big, So Round...
passages.text:
You've made a friend, have you?

Are you certain you want to feed him? He might become attached.

passages.title: Never Again!
passages.text:
<name>, it falls to you to see that this attack by the Burning Legion never comes to pass. You must go and slay their leaders. Without them the demons will be mindless.

You will find Gorgannon in Demon Fall Canyon south beyond Felfire Hill, near Mannoroth's floating, broken spear.

Diathorus the Seeker resides somewhere in the barrow den atop Demon Fall Ridge. To find the ridge, look for a ramp up from Demon Fall Canyon near the Horde's monument to Grom Hellscream.

Bring me their weapons.

passages.title: Never Again!
passages.text: Our night elf scouts report that preparations for the attack are almost complete. Those dreadlords must die soon, <name>!

passages.title: Never Again!
passages.text:
Never again will the Burning Legion threaten Ashenvale! You have delivered us from a fight we very likely would have lost, <class>.

I give you thanks, <name>, and the deepest gratitude of the Hand of Argus. It honors me to have you at our side!

passages.title: Reclaiming Felfire Hill
passages.text:
Little one, to the southwest is an area of Nightsong Woods that has in recent times come to be called Felfire Hill. It is very sad to see the demons crawling over it, spreading their corruption.

Would you do something to help take back the land?

I have a number of seeds that I have been saving for such a purpose. Take them to Felfire Hill and plant them in the fertile dirt mounds.

passages.title: Reclaiming Felfire Hill
passages.text: Good. Though it may take a great deal of your years for the seedlings to grow into ancients, in the fullness of time they will aid us in our fight against all of the enemies of Ashenvale.

passages.title: Never Again!
passages.text:
<name>, you will see to it that this attack by the Burning Legion never comes to pass! Go and slay these dreadlords! Without them the rest of the demons are essentially mindless.

You will find Gorgannon in Demon Fall Canyon south beyond Felfire Hill, near Mannoroth's floating, broken spear.

Diathorus the Seeker resides somewhere in the barrow den atop Demon Fall Ridge.

Return to me with their weapons as proof of your deeds.

passages.title: Never Again!
passages.text: Those dreadlords must die soon, <name>!

passages.title: Never Again!
passages.text:
Never again will the Burning Legion make slaves of the orcs, or any other race of the Horde!

Bravely fought, <class>!  You have the true heart of the Horde beating inside of you!  You give us much honor!

passages.title: A Shameful Waste
passages.text:
Welcome to Forest Song, <class>. Where you see tents, there will one day be buildings, but such ambition requires a steady stream of materials. I cannot bring myself to order our workers to fell any of the ancient trees of this grove, but our neighbors to the west have no such reverence for the forest.

We shall reclaim the tainted wood from Satyrnaar to the west. Take the wood to Gnarl at the Warsong Lumber Camp. He is an Ancient who will purify it for our use.

passages.title: A Shameful Waste
passages.text:
<The ancient creaks as it turns toward you.>

Architect Nemos said that you might be bringing wood salvaged from befouled Satyrnaar.

passages.title: A Shameful Waste
passages.text:
Wood warped by foul demonic magic is of no use to the draenei at Forest Song. Nothing sound can be built with it, but I shall purify it and return it in good time to Architect Nemos and his people for their use.

Some good will come from this tragedy, after all.

passages.title: The Lost Chalice
passages.text:
The area to our west, now called Satyrnaar, was once a prominent shrine built by my people. It housed a priceless relic, the Chalice of Elune, entrusted to the shrine's keepers by the priests of Elune. Pilgrims once traveled to the shrine to experience the healing powers the chalice was rumored to hold.

These stories might be nothing but old wives' tales, but if there is any truth to them, the relic may hold the key to rejuvenating the wounded forest. I must know, <name>.

passages.title: The Lost Chalice
passages.text: Can you feel it, <name>, the touch of corruption upon the wind? If we do nothing, it will continue to advance. That is why I seek the Chalice of Elune. Were you able to find it?

passages.title: The Lost Chalice
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>. There is certainly a latent power here, one that not even constant exposure to the corruption of the satyr can dim.

Do you see how it still shines, after all these years?

passages.title: In Search of Thaelrid
passages.text:
Many rumors circulate these days about the union of the Twilight's Hammer and the naga in Blackfathom Deeps to the west.

My role here is to collect as much information as I can, so we know when and where help is needed.

It has been days now since I sent a scout to check on the activity inside Blackfathom Deeps. Scout Thaelrid has not yet reported back.

My other scouts are preoccupied with pressing matters.

Seek out Thaelrid for me, <name>.

passages.title: The Wicked Revantusk
passages.text:
These Revantusk trolls think they're special for bein' in the Horde. Makes me laugh!

See, the funny part is, it doesn't matter if they're part of the Horde, or some kinda troll empire, or the bloody Burning Legion for that matter. We've fought trolls in these lands for a few centuries now.

In fact, I'll be kind enough to let you lend a hand, <lad/lass>! Grab a weapon and head out to the battlefield and help our boys to the east.

passages.title: The Wicked Revantusk
passages.text: Not bad for a city-dwellin' <race>. Good show, aye!

passages.title: Finding Teronis
passages.text:
A friend of mine from Astranaar, Raene Wolfrunner, asked me to send a scout west to Lake Falathim. Teronis left days ago, just before the Horde attacked.

He was searching for an item he thought could slow the furbolg attacks on our people--a rod created by a now-dead, evil wizard.

Before he left, he mentioned a gem for the rod. Unfortunately, we know that the lake has been invaded by some evil force.

Please, <name>, find my friend.

passages.title: Finding Teronis
passages.text:
Teronis' body lies broken atop the small rise next to the Keeper.

Deep slashes crisscross his corpse.

passages.title: The Ancient Statuettes
passages.text:
I would charge you with a task, <class>.

I was on my boat, skimming over the submerged ruins of Zoram, when naga attacked me, surging from the water and tearing at me with their claws! I fled and the rest, as they say, is history.

I am an archaeologist of sorts, and I am attempting to recover artifacts of the lost city.

Will you head out onto the Zoram Strand to the southwest and recover any ancient statuettes you come across? They are the reason I have braved the dangers of the Zoram Strand.

passages.title: The Ancient Statuettes
passages.text: Have you found many statuettes, <name>?

passages.title: The Ancient Statuettes
passages.text:
That's quite a few that you have found! Thank you, <name>!

The old city of Zoram holds many secrets, and these statuettes may be the key to many of them.

passages.title: Ruuzel
passages.text:
I fear the ancient statuette's secrets will remain forever hidden unless you find the key to their ancient locks.

That key is a ring, the Ring of Zoram. It belonged to the rulers of this city before the waves of the Sundering drowned it.

For years the ring was lost, but the naga have recently found it.

Their leader, Ruuzel, dwells on her isle on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand. Please, <name>, retrieve the ring for me!

passages.title: Ruuzel
passages.text: It is said that the Ring of Zoram is the key to any lock within the city. Do you have it, <name>?

passages.title: Ruuzel
passages.text:
You found the ring! Thank you, <name>.

Please take this as payment, and know that your deeds today will remain forever in my memory.

passages.title: Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger!
passages.text:
Listen, I don't know who you are, but I need your help. My sisters went to take back the Branch of Cenarius from the satyr. They said they'd be back soon, but it's been two whole days!

<name>, you have to find them! They were looking for the ruins of a night elf temple in Xavian to the northwest. I don't know what to think. Look for Anilia, she was leading them on the search.

passages.title: Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger!
passages.text: Judging by the gaping wound in her side, Anilia is on the verge of death.

passages.title: The Branch of Cenarius
passages.text: Anilia puts her hands on your shoulders and draws you close. Gasping, she points towards the arch to the north, before her eyes close and her last wheezing breath leaves her body. "He has taken it... Geltharis..." You know in your heart that Anilia's dying wish is to see the Branch of Cenarius back in dryad hands.

passages.title: The Branch of Cenarius
passages.text: Have you found them? What did Anilia say? Where is she?

passages.title: The Branch of Cenarius
passages.text:
Anilia died? No... that can't be! It was just yesterday that we were running and playing together in the woods.

I guess those days are over...

passages.title: Satyr Slaying!
passages.text:
I can't believe that Anilia is gone... We used to play together in the forests all the time. I almost feel... sad.

I know something that might make me feel better. Please, slay the satyrs that took Anilia from me! Bring me their horns as proof of your actions and you will forever have my gratitude.

passages.title: Satyr Slaying!
passages.text: Please, help me avenge Anilia's death.

passages.title: Satyr Slaying!
passages.text: Thank you, kind <race>. My sister's spirit is gladdened by your efforts.

passages.title: Retaking Mystral Lake
passages.text:
We could easily have held Silverwind Refuge from the Horde had they not taken control of our water elemental defenders on Mystral Lake.

One of their shaman summoned in Tideress, an old and angry water spirit of the forest who befouled our elementals and turned them against us. With the lake and the Horde pressing in on us, we had no choice but to retreat to the spire here.

Go east. Take the lake back so that we will have a chance to retake the refuge some day.

passages.title: Retaking Mystral Lake
passages.text:
Well done, <name>! With the befouled elemental numbers thinned and Tideress put back into the lake, we should be able to launch a counter-offensive on Silverwind Refuge.

Just as soon as we're done with defending the spire....

passages.title: Bathran's Hair
passages.text:
There is a plant that grows in the old ruins of Bathran's Haunt across the road to the east. The plant is called Bathran's Hair and is known to cure ailments of the spirit.

Now the Horde are there harvesting the plant for their own evil schemes.

There is a sick child in Astranaar, and we believe that her illness is more than just physical. I promised my master that I would help seek a cure, but I am no fighter.

Will you go to Bathran's Haunt and gather the plants?

passages.title: Bathran's Hair
passages.text: Have you gathered the Bathran's Hair, <name>?  The child's health grows weaker by the hour....

passages.title: Bathran's Hair
passages.text:
Ah, you have the hair! This is a good first step. There are other ingredients that we will need, but the hair of the fallen Ancient could well be the most important.

I only hope that whatever the Forsaken are devising from the plant will not be turned into a weapon. We simply do not have the numbers to remove them right now, especially with Maestra's Post under attack!

passages.title: Orendil's Cure
passages.text:
<name>, now that it has been bathed in Elune's blessed light, I believe that the concoction will help the afflicted child. Please, take it to Astranaar and give it to the child's parent, Pelturas Whitemoon.

To reach Astranaar, follow the road south and then east. However, if you'd like to get there more swiftly, speak with Sentinel Avana.

passages.title: Orendil's Cure
passages.text: I must apologize, for I have no time to speak. My child, Relara, is deathly ill!

passages.title: Orendil's Cure
passages.text:
This is from Orendil?

His skill with herbs and healing is great! This cure gives me hope, when before I had little....

passages.title: Elune's Tear
passages.text:
I'd hoped Orendil's cure would save Relara, but I fear it only slowed the disease running through her. We must find more powerful medicine! Thankfully, Orendil spoke to me of further remedies should his first one fail.

Elune's Tear is a type of stone that rests in only one place: the remains of Iris Lake, destroyed by the eruption of Thunder Peak, northeast of Astranaar. Orendil said the stone will wash away corruption.

Please, <name>, bring me Elune's Tear and pray it will end my child's sickness!

passages.title: Elune's Tear
passages.text: <name>, did you find the remains of the lake?  Do you have the Tear?

passages.title: Elune's Tear
passages.text:
Oh, you found it! Odd... it looks tarnished somehow. I will place the tear in a stew, and pray that it will cure her.

Thank you! Thank you, <name>!

passages.title: Dryad Delivery
passages.text:
Ah, there you are, <name>. I've pored over the notes Teronis has made and it sounds like your next course of action is to find the other pieces of Dartol's rod.

I would start by heading east along the road to Raynewood Tower.

A dryad there named Shael'dryn is better suited to guide you. Seek her out.

Keep the gem with you--Shael'dryn will need it if she's to help you recreate the rod.

passages.title: Dryad Delivery
passages.text: Hello. How are you?

passages.title: Dryad Delivery
passages.text:
Oh, Raene sent you? It must be serious indeed.

What can I help you with?

passages.title: Playing Possum
passages.text:
The last piece of the rod is held by druids of the claw. I asked their leader, Oso Bramblescar, to give it to me, but he and his guardians nearly killed me! Clearly they too were affected by the Horde's corruption of the Forest Heart.

But, I have an idea for how you can get into Oso's cave and grab the pommel.

Ever since I was a faun, I've been pretty good at playing possum. It works great against bears! I can teach you! Go east to the Shady Nook, and if they try to get you, just use my technique.

passages.title: Playing Possum
passages.text: Did you find the final piece of the rod, <name>? How did my technique work?

passages.title: Playing Possum
passages.text:
You got it? Wonderful for you... and for Raene!

I guess we'll have to see about reassembling it, won't we?

passages.title: Return to Raene
passages.text:
I suggest you find Raene and let her know the rod is finished. I'm sure she'll know what your next course should be.

Be careful... I sense a great deal of power within it for both good and ill. I hope that you and Raene know what you are doing.

Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Return to Raene
passages.text: Yes, <name>? How go your efforts?

passages.title: Return to Raene
passages.text:
You've recreated the rod Teronis had set out to find? That's wonderful to hear.

Shael'dryn has been indispensible in her assistance. Teronis would be proud to see his quest is continuing even after his tragic passing.

<Raene looks over the reconstructed rod with a look of approval and thoughts racing behind her eyes.>

Now it is time for us to make use of its power to eliminate the enemies of Ashenvale!

passages.title: A New Adornment
passages.text:
I'm certain that the long-dead wizard, Dartol, intended to use his rod to subjugate and destroy us just as the night elves and orcs have, but I think now we'll put that thing to an unintended use.

Ran Bloodtooth is the king of all of the Ashenvale furbolg. His tribe, the Bloodtooth, are the most powerful and keep themselves secluded in a camp just to the east.

Kill them all and bring back his skull. Let us see if we can put it to good use.

passages.title: A New Adornment
passages.text: Have you slain Ran yet, my friend? We must have his skull if you're to deliver my people from bondage.

passages.title: A New Adornment
passages.text:
You have done well, my friend.

Now quickly, hand me Ran's skull. While his essence yet taints it, we shall fashion it upon Dartol's Rod giving you the power to influence my brethren and deliver them from evil!

passages.title: To Stonehearth's Aid
passages.text:
The earthen and the stone troggs somehow found their way to Deepholm through Uldum more than fifteen thousand years ago. They've been warring ever since.

If we're to recover the middle fragment of the World Pillar, the Stonefather must be rescued.

Please go to Stonehearth and do everything that you can to aid the Earthen in their war against the stone troggs.

You're our best hope, <name>.

passages.title: To Stonehearth's Aid
passages.text:
The Stonefather's son, Flint, sent you? No time to talk.

We must prevent a second front from opening up on the war!

passages.title: Snapjaws, Lad!
passages.text:
I've got plans to brew up somethin' special for those pesky trolls. Aye, I said for them... a brew they won't ever forget! A brew that'll have them pickin' their tusks out of the hillsides!

I've got a few ingredients steepin' already, but I could use a hand gatherin' more. At the bottom of the Overlook Cliffs to the east, near the shore, is a whole mess o' snapjaws. I need fresh, whole gizzards from them for my blastbrew.

passages.title: Snapjaws, Lad!
passages.text: Got those gizzards?

passages.title: Snapjaws, Lad!
passages.text: Ah, nice an' fresh. I'll get those going while you fetch me some more goods then...

passages.title: 99 Bottles of Booze on the Beach
passages.text:
Now, I know we've got a little battle ragin' and all that, but down at the overlook cliffs are some nice lookin' bottles strewn all over the place. I don't want good drink to fall into the hands o' the Horde!

If you're down that way, collect the bottles for me and bring 'em back here. I'll pay in full for it as if you bottled 'em yourself.

passages.title: 99 Bottles of Booze on the Beach
passages.text: About 12 should do the trick, aye?

passages.title: 99 Bottles of Booze on the Beach
passages.text:
That's the stuff! Wouldn't want any trolls or goblins gettin' pleasure out of these, now would we!

Maybe I can work a bit of this into my next brew...

passages.title: Akiris by the Bundle
passages.text:
It's not easy running a combination 5-star exotic resort/jungle resource salvaging plant! That is, it wouldn't be easy, if I didn't have the organizational skills of a trade prince's personal assistant!

The first trick is multitasking. For example: the naga explorers to our south carry a valuable ocean reed - Akiris reeds. We can sell these reeds to our clients overseas, and we can also stuff our visitors' mattresses with them! Come to think of it, we could probably use some more of that stuff.

passages.title: Akiris by the Bundle
passages.text:
Let's see... we're going to need some shotguns for our nature hikes, rowboats for the oil rig day trip, and...

Oh, you're back already?

passages.title: Akiris by the Bundle
passages.text: Hey hey!  Not bad, not bad at all!  You may have a future in resource acquisition.  Or hotel management.

passages.title: It's You!!
passages.text:
Yes, can I help...

<Sassy's jaw drops to the floor.>

<name>! Is it really you?! Look how big and strong you've gotten! Let me feel that bicep!

Me? I've been trying to make my gold here in the jungle. We're mainly in resource acquisition, but we also do tourism.

I know, genius, right?

Hey, listen. I was thinking... the naga explorers to the south carry Akiris reeds, which we could sell, and use to stuff visitor mattresses. You interested in killing some naga? It'll be just like old times!

passages.title: It's You!!
passages.text:
Let's see... we're going to need some shotguns for our nature hikes, rowboats for the oil rig day trip, and...

Oh, hey Boss <name>.  You're back already?

passages.title: It's You!!
passages.text: I knew you had it in you, boss-man.  You know what they say: You can take the <race> out of the islands, but you can't take the murderous tendencies out of <name>.

passages.title: Prime Slime
passages.text:
Not many dwarves know this, but to get a REAL kick out of my brew I add a wee bit of the oozes around here. Aye, the giant green dwarf-eatin' oozes, those ones.

This brew's gonna have a HUGE kick to it though, so we need a huge slime! There's one lurkin' down in Skulk Rock that's the mother o' them all, absolutely huge...the Direglob, we call it.

If you've got what it takes, head down there and take a chunk out of the Direglob for me!

passages.title: Prime Slime
passages.text: Aye, do ya have it?

passages.title: Prime Slime
passages.text: Look at it! That'll put some oomph into the mix!

passages.title: Skulk Rock Clean-Up
passages.text:
Years ago, there used to be a Horde base deep within Skulk Rock. It's been abandoned since then, but it's still prime territory, worth takin' for our allies!

Problem is, it's full of dwarf-eating slimes and oozes. Those things are slightly less disgustin' than trolls, but they'll still give us a hassle.

With our boys tied up fightin' the Revantusk, I need you to go to Skulk Rock and clear the place out for me.

passages.title: Skulk Rock Clean-Up
passages.text: It's good to see you back... and not missing any limbs, either.

passages.title: Skulk Rock Supplies
passages.text:
I had a cousin in the second war! He used to tell me all about when they led a raid on Skulk Rock. Swept in there and drove the trolls out like rats from a nest. They chased right after 'em all the way to Alterac!

The slimes moved in right quick after that, and there's still cratefuls of old Horde goods sittin' in there. I say we don't let the trolls get it back!

Bring me back a few crates from Skulk Rock to the northwest.

passages.title: Skulk Rock Supplies
passages.text: You got the crates?

passages.title: Skulk Rock Supplies
passages.text:
Looks like it's still good inside! Huh... is that banana bread? Still fresh!

Here, lad, take your share of goods.

passages.title: Down with the Vilebranch
passages.text:
The Revantusk isn't the only tribe of foul trolls we're here to take care of! The Vilebranch have corrupted this land for years from their stronghold of Jintha'Alor.

We're done sittin' by in Aerie Peak twiddlin' our thumbs, if you haven't noticed. Doran Steelwing leads the charge against the Vilebranch from a camp the boys took just to the south. Speak with him and join the fight!

passages.title: Down with the Vilebranch
passages.text: Well met, <name>! We've got a lot of trolls to kill and only so many hands to do it with!

passages.title: Vilebranch Scum
passages.text:
The Vilebranch are a different tribe from the Revantusk, but the difference is academic. Far as we're concerned the only good troll is a dead troll!

But make no mistake, the Vilebranch are just as nasty even without the Horde's chain around their neck. They'll poison this whole land unless we take this stand and get rid of them

You can start with their witchdoctors and headhunters on the lower tier. Let me know when you've killed a fair share of 'em.

passages.title: Vilebranch Scum
passages.text: Aye, we'll have these trolls cleared out yet.

passages.title: Death to the Vilebranch
passages.text:
We're makin' good progress. Keep pressing on, and don't falter!

The Vilebranch berserkers fight like savage animals, whipped into a blood frenzy. Their shadowcasters summon foul spirits from beyond this world! This is why we're getting rid of these depraved creatures, <name>, never forget that.

Head to the middle tier and kill the berserkers and shadowcasters!

passages.title: Death to the Vilebranch
passages.text: It won't be long until we're the only dwarves left breathing on these walls.

passages.title: Stonefather's Boon
passages.text:
With the Stonefather taken prisoner, our forces are demoralized. Normally any one of mine could take five times his number of stone troggs. But now....

I want you to head out into the field surrounding the town. Plant Stonefather Oremantle's banner near my defenders. Grant them his boon and remind them of that for which they fight.

passages.title: Stonefather's Boon
passages.text: Rally more of our troops, <name>.

passages.title: Stonefather's Boon
passages.text:
You have my thanks, <name>. You've made all the difference, and the fate of these cowardly stone trogg ambushers is set in stone.

Now we must get about the business of retaking Stonehearth.

passages.title: We're Surrounded
passages.text:
Our war has been waged for longer than your kind counts time. Let us see if you can make a difference, <race>.

The stone troggs are a mistake of the titans. On your world they have succumbed to the Curse of Flesh. But here, in Deepholm, you see them in their true form.

We're surrounded. Maybe you could go out there and break a few troggs down for us. See what they're really made of?

passages.title: We're Surrounded
passages.text: Are you going to pull your fleshy weight, <race>?

passages.title: We're Surrounded
passages.text:
Not a bad start, though you'll have to destroy more of them than that if you're going to rescue the Stonefather.

A lot more.

passages.title: Nida's Necklace
passages.text:
My friend Nida lost her necklace, and we can't find it. We've been fishing all day right here, and we looked around here already. The only thing I can think of is that it fell into the lake. Our parents don't want us to swim in the lake... my mom says there's some mean things underwater, but you look like you aren't scared of mean things.

Could you find it for her, please?

passages.title: Nida's Necklace
passages.text: Hi.  I miss my necklace.  My daddy got it for me.  Daddy says that there are monsters in the lake.  Did you beat up any monsters?

passages.title: Nida's Necklace
passages.text: Thank you for finding my necklace mister <class>... you are very kind!  My kitty thanks you too - isn't that right Effsee?

passages.title: An Unwelcome Guest
passages.text:
Once again my garden was trampled and pillaged. And I know the brute who is doing it. It's that forsaken boar, the one Marshal Marris has taken to calling Bellygrub.

I won't be able to re-plant the daffodils until next season now. Ruined! All ruined by that one menacing boar. Put an end to that pest! Show me his tusk and I'd be happy to reward you. He seems to spend his time foraging in the field southwest of Lakeshire but occasionally he roams over here and into my garden.

passages.title: An Unwelcome Guest
passages.text: Is Bellygrub still at it or were you able to rid Lakeshire of the pest once and for all?

passages.title: An Unwelcome Guest
passages.text: Finally the menace is laid to rest!  Thank you, <name>, you have done me a great service.  The garden shall be in full bloom this season!

passages.title: We Must Prepare!
passages.text:
More of our citizens go missing every day. We think the gnolls are responsible, but we have no idea where they are taking them! If you are to help us defeat the gnolls and find our people, you must be properly equipped. Unfortunately, we are all out of gnomecorders. Without a gnomecorder, there is no way for us to communicate with you when you are in the field.

Our last good gnomecorder was stolen by marauding murlocs last week. You will have to go to Lake Everstill, east of here, and recover it!

passages.title: We Must Prepare!
passages.text: Have you recovered the gnomecorder?

passages.title: We Must Prepare!
passages.text: Excellent! Let me make a few adjustments here and we should be good to go.

passages.title: Lake Everstill Clean Up
passages.text:
Headed out to Lake Everstill? You'll be happy to know that we currently have a bounty on murlocs. Kill as many as you can and be rewarded! Any murloc will do. All you need to do is kill indiscriminately.

You'll find Lake Everstill directly east of Lakeshire. It's the lake. Has water in it... Any of this ring a bell?

passages.title: Lake Everstill Clean Up
passages.text: Have you killed all the murlocs?

passages.title: Lake Everstill Clean Up
passages.text:
That ought to teach those murlocs a lesson. Hopefully the next time they decide to raid our town they'll think twice.

We both know that won't happen.

passages.title: Tuning the Gnomecorder
passages.text:
The gnomecorder looks to be in working order. I've got you all hooked up, now we just need to tune the gnomecorder for reception.

Head north out of Lakeshire and follow the road up to the graveyard. Once you reach the graveyard I'll attempt to transmit.

passages.title: Tuning the Gnomecorder
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder crackles and pops.>

Can you hear me, <name>? Is this thing on? Ah, yes, I see you there now.

Let's get to work!

passages.title: Like a Fart in the Wind
passages.text:
We were raided last night, or perhaps it was the night before. I'm not really sure when it was as I haven't had a wink of sleep in three days. I'm probably delusional at this point.

Listen, gnolls raided our supply stores and took off with everything! Just like a fart in the wind, they were in and they were OUT! My soldiers saw them running back towards the canyons, northwest of here. Recover our supplies, <class>!

passages.title: Like a Fart in the Wind
passages.text: Did you recover the supplies?

passages.title: Like a Fart in the Wind
passages.text: Thank you, citizen. Without you, we would have starved or worse, been forced to go out and get food for ourselves.

passages.title: Canyon Romp
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder hums.>

The first order of business is a romp through the Redridge Canyons, directly north of Lakeshire. Kill every gnome that you see... woops, did I say gnome? I meant gnoll. Kill every GNOLL that you see and take their collars as proof of deed.

I must warn you, <name>; while you are out there, watch out for ettins. My scouts have reported seeing huge, bloodthirsty ettins roaming the canyons lately. Stay out of their way if you want to remain alive.

Solomon out. I'll be in touch.

passages.title: Canyon Romp
passages.text: Did you recover those collars?

passages.title: Canyon Romp
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder crackles and pops.>

Good work, <name>. I've just been handed some important information. It would appear that our most hated enemy, the Blackrock orcs, have wised up...

I've transferred a few silver over to you for the gnome, erm, gnoll kills.

passages.title: Ongo'longo's Revenge
passages.text:
I've got a plan to pit troll against troll.

The Vilebranch have a big ol' dire troll locked up in a pit with some flimsy-lookin' chains. I've seen those things fight, and there's no way those'll hold if that big brute gets swingin' mad!

I want you to find the dire troll and fight him, <name>. Don't kill him... just smack him around til' he's seein' red, then let him break free and get out of his way! He'll be a big pain for the Vilebranch.

passages.title: Ongo'longo's Revenge
passages.text: Ain't that a hoot! Wish I could've seen it myself.

passages.title: Summit of Fate
passages.text:
You have to go to the summit now, <name>. Our warriors won't go past the final gates. They say it's still as a tomb; not a sound, not a breath, not a hint of motion.

They think it's a trap, but based on what you've brought me, I'm worried it's something even more sinister. Go to the altar, investigate what happened... and bring me back ANY sort of mystical object or dark idol you find! Do you hear me?

passages.title: Summit of Fate
passages.text: What did you find?

passages.title: Summit of Fate
passages.text:
Dead? All of them, around the altar? And you found these spider idols on them...

It's Shadra. The Spider Loa! They're trying to tap her power!

passages.title: Heads Up
passages.text:
Umboda Three-Heads is one o' the biggest trolls you'll see around. He's a savage butcher, takin' heads for his own collection, dwarf and troll alike! It's time he got what he deserved.

Look for the big brute on the lower terraces, and you take his own head right back here!

passages.title: Heads Up
passages.text: Let's see it!

passages.title: Heads Up
passages.text: That's one ugly mug. Maybe he was takin' other heads tryin' to find a prettier one!

passages.title: He Who Controls the Ettins
passages.text:
You've stumbled upon a gnoll document. The gnoll that wrote this propaganda is semi-literate:

BROTHERS OF YOWLER, HEAR DIRTPAW! DIRTPAW GIVEN ORB FROM ORCS! DIRTPAW CONTROL ETTIN THINGS! DIRTPAW CRUSH HUMIES! COME GET DIRTPAW PAW-O-GRAPH IN RETHBAN CAVE. CAVE IS WEST, HIDDEN IN CANYON!

<There's a paw print as the signature.>

<There also appears to be a bite taken out of the scroll.>

You should probably investigate.

passages.title: He Who Controls the Ettins
passages.text: <The orb emanates powerful magic.>

passages.title: He Who Controls the Ettins
passages.text: <The orb hisses as you touch it.>

passages.title: Faces of Evil
passages.text:
The Vilebranch have hung their tiki masks all across the walls of Jintha'Alor. The spirits not gonna be watchin' over them much longer.

Take this torch with ya as ya fight through the Vilebranch, <class>. Set fire to their tiki masks. I'll be watchin' from here as their wards and hexes fade away, an' their heretical dark voodoo goes up in smoke.

passages.title: All That Skitters
passages.text:
There's somethin' I've noticed up there... Jintha'Alor's full of spiders. Small ones about as big as yer hand. Not an unusual sight for the Hinterlands, but somethin's amiss.

To be honest, I don't trust the trolls to keep pets. They're up to somethin'. I need you to bring me some of those spiders. Keep 'em alive if you can, and we'll see what the spirits tell me...

passages.title: All That Skitters
passages.text: Let's see what you've got.

passages.title: All That Skitters
passages.text: By Kurdan's beard... these don't look like any spiders I've seen before. Dark magic's at work here.

passages.title: Venomous Secrets
passages.text:
If the sacrifice has already been made, Shadra's presence is going to start creepin' into this realm. That cave's probably full of her spawn by now.

Don't let them escape, <name>. Slay any of those vile spiders you find!

passages.title: Venomous Secrets
passages.text: Good riddance. May those horrid things never walk these lands again.

passages.title: The Eye of Shadra
passages.text:
Gryphon Master Talonaxe has sent me here to deal with Shadra, the Venom Queen. The conquest of Jintha'Alor isn't enough... the trolls could regroup and summon this creature later, when we're not expecting it.

We'll gather the artifacts first, pull Shadra into this world on our own terms, and put our hammers to that foul creature. I'll need you to help find the artifacts, and put a hurt on the rest of the trolls while you're at it.

We first need the Eye of Shadra, guarded in Agol'watha to the north.

passages.title: The Eye of Shadra
passages.text: Was the tablet right? Did you find the eye?

passages.title: The Eye of Shadra
passages.text: Well done, <name>. We'll be knockin' on this bug's door in no time.

passages.title: The Fang of Shadra
passages.text:
We'll need the Fang of Shadra next.

It's kept in the Creeping Ruins to the east, guarded by Shadra's own spawn. Hideous spiders the size of a dwarf, and twice as strong. Their venom is strong, <name>... don't get careless.

passages.title: The Fang of Shadra
passages.text: Have you got the fang?

passages.title: The Fang of Shadra
passages.text: There it is... only one left, lad.

passages.title: Zanzil's Secret
passages.text:
Years ago, the Gurubashi exiled one of their own from Zul'Gurub: a troll by the name of Zanzil. The reasons why aren't all that clear, but I'd guess it had something to do with his tendency to administer powerful, behavior-altering drugs to anyone he saw. Anyhow, the Gurubashi priests and their blood god have been slain, but Zanzil the Outcast remains...

...as do his powerful, behavior-altering drugs.

I'd like to get my hands on some, <race>. Check the zombies to the southeast.

passages.title: Zanzil's Secret
passages.text:
Excellent... you're not a zombie yet.  That's good.

Oh, umm... nothing.  It's just that... that was a potential risk.  Did I forget to warn you?

passages.title: Zanzil's Secret
passages.text:
<Jasper carefully analyzes the strange compound.>

This mixture is... I don't understand it.  Perhaps we need to run some clinical trials.

passages.title: Shatter Them!
passages.text:
I want you to go out there and I want you to finish them.

Berserkers, Earthrenders, Deathriders... I don't care! I want those stone troggs shattered!

passages.title: Shatter Them!
passages.text: That's a good dent, but it's clear to me that we're going to have to handle this a slightly different way.

passages.title: Hero's Call: The Hinterlands!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Gryphon Master Talonaxe at the aviary in Aerie Peak.

Our new brothers in the Alliance need your help to fend off the aggressive Horde offensive in their beloved homeland. Travel north from the Arathi Highlands, through the dwarven mountain pass and follow the road northwest to Aerie Peak.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: The Hinterlands!
passages.text: Welcome to Aerie Peak, <name>. On behalf of High Thane Falstad, I thank ye for comin' to help us.

passages.title: They've Wised Up...
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder crackles and pops.>

It would appear that the Blackrock orcs have finally wised up. I'm getting reports that they're joining forces with the gnolls and planning an attack. I want details, <name>!

I need you to check out Rethban Caverns, located in the western region of Redridge Canyons. Look for orcs with dark skin. Kill any that you encounter and search their corpses for information.

Solomon, out.

passages.title: They've Wised Up...
passages.text: What have you found out?

passages.title: They've Wised Up...
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder buzzes and whirs.>

Just put the missive in the little compartment and I'll read it. I am fluent in orcish.

<You hear a distraught yell in the background.>

It looks like these orcs are here under the direct command of Yowler. That means Yowler must have the orc invasion plan.

passages.title: Yowler Must Die!
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder hums.>

You need to find Yowler, <name>. He'll be located somewhere in the northern region of Redridge Canyons. Kill that mongrel and search his corpse for the Blackrock invasion plans. Should you succeed, bring the plans to me over at the town hall in Lakeshire.

Solomon, out.

passages.title: Yowler Must Die!
passages.text: Do you have the Blackrock invasion plans?

passages.title: Yowler Must Die!
passages.text:
<Magistrate Solomon takes the plans from you and begins reading.>

Shadowhide army!? Damn those orcs to hell! These invasion plans speak of a massive build up of orcish and gnoll forces in the east. Looks like Gath'Ilzogg, the Blackrock general, is preparing to march his armies across Lakeshire and attack Stormwind directly!

passages.title: A Mangy Threat
passages.text:
We do everything we can to protect our kin and our gryphons. That includes chasin' off predators, whether they be from the forest or from the Horde.

I won't ask you to save us from two-legged monsters just yet. Mangy silvermane prowl the woods to the south where our gryphons range, and they're known to get 'em if they stray too low. Hunt a few of the silvermane and make sure they know our gryphons aren't food.

passages.title: A Mangy Threat
passages.text: Much appreciated, <name>.

passages.title: Out to the Front
passages.text:
We need your help with somethin' more pressin', <name>.

The Horde's been gettin' bolder out here. They've moved in on our territory and started attackin' us outright. The Revantusk forest trolls are attackin' Stormfeather Outpost in broad daylight!

I need you to help out. Talk to Guthrum Thunderfist just outside. He'll put you on a gryphon to Stormfeather Outpost. Kerr Ironsight will fill you in when you get there.

passages.title: Out to the Front
passages.text: Good to see you out here! Let's get to it.

passages.title: Jorgensen
passages.text:
I don't know where Krakauer or Danforth are, but Jorgensen was being held at Render's Camp, northwest of here. I was in the same crap filled cage with him before they relocated me to Alther's Mill.

If we're gonna get him out we'll need the key. A stone cold witch from hell known as Utroka the Keymistress holds on tight to that thing. We'll have to kill her if we're going to get Jorgensen's cage key. She's up north in the valley leading to the Burning Steppes.

Let's go, kid.

passages.title: Jorgensen
passages.text: Messner! Damn, it's good to see a friendly face. Get me out of here!

passages.title: Jorgensen
passages.text: I know where they're holding Krakauer and Danforth. We gotta hurry. They were prepping those two for a sacrifice!

passages.title: Krakauer
passages.text:
Krakauer is up on the chopping block as we speak! The orcs brought in a Gurubashi witch doctor to perform a dark ritual on him. We need to kill that troll to free Krakauer!

Let's go! He's just inside the cave here. Hang a right at the first fork.

passages.title: Krakauer
passages.text: <Krakauer groans.>

passages.title: Krakauer
passages.text:
Wha... Where am I? What happened? Messner? Jorgensen?

OH MY GOSH! We have to get to Danforth! It might already be too late!

passages.title: Return of the Bravo Company
passages.text:
I don't know who you are, <mister/missy>, but you've earned the respect and admiration of the Bravo Company. You've managed to save all our hides and kill a boatload of orcs in the process. Now we return the favor.

Get back to Lakeshire and report to Colonel Troteman. We'll find Johnny and deliver the good news in person. With the Bravo Company back in action, these orcs don't stand a chance.

passages.title: Return of the Bravo Company
passages.text:
<Colonel Troteman salutes.>

Unbelievable work, <name>. You've managed to rescue the entire Bravo Company from the clutches of the Blackrock orcs? With Keeshan's team rescued and Keeshan's belongings returned, there's no way Keeshan could refuse us.

passages.title: Fixer Upper
passages.text:
<Clay sneers at you and makes a sound much like two stones rubbing against each other.>

They've smashed all of our catapults. I've been trying to get this one working, but no luck so far.

Maybe you'd like to make yourself useful. Head out onto the front and grab me any spare parts you come across.

You think you can handle that, flesh bag?

passages.title: Fixer Upper
passages.text: Well? I don't have all day.

passages.title: Fixer Upper
passages.text:
Well then. Maybe you're okay after all.

Alright, alright... don't get all bent out of shape. Just give me a few moments with these parts.

passages.title: A Triumph of Gnomish Ingenuity
passages.text:
We will need all the weapons, inventions, and soldiers we can get in order to defeat Razlo Crushcog and his followers.

Over to the northeast, you'll find Engineer Grindspark, one of a new generation of brilliant gnomish minds. Why, he hasn't had an explosion in over three prototypes!

But enough bragging. Engineer Grindspark is working on a bot that he says will help clean up the toxic airfield. You should introduce yourself to him and see if he needs any help testing it.

passages.title: A Triumph of Gnomish Ingenuity
passages.text: So the high tinker himself has heard of my little project? Splendid! I've almost finished my latest prototype, but maybe you can help me chase down those last few parts.

passages.title: This Ain't My War
passages.text:
They asked me to fight in those wars. I didn't ask them! I did what I had to do to win. So I end up getting captured by those filthy, crap-swilling, maggot orcs and for five long years they used me as a toilet. Finally I break out and head back to my hometown and what do I get? People spitting on me, protesting me, calling me a baby orc killer and all kinds of vile crap!

No, I don't think I'll be helping you. You go back to Troteman and you tell him that this ain't my war.

passages.title: This Ain't My War
passages.text:
<Troteman sighs.>

I'm not giving up on him, <name>, and I'm not giving up on Redridge. We need to boost his spirits... Rouse the slumbering monster within him!

passages.title: Surveying Equipment
passages.text:
Ah, my savior! I've heard that you're on a mission to save Lakeshire... and my bridge. Yep, worked too damned long on that thing to let it get destroyed by an army of marauding orc monsters!

Listen, if you're headed up north towards Render's Camp, would you do me a solid and get me some spyglasses from the Blackrock trackers up there? I could sure use 'em for my new surveying gear.

passages.title: Surveying Equipment
passages.text: Did you recover the spyglasses?

passages.title: Surveying Equipment
passages.text: Fantastic work, <name>! These will come in handy for our next project, the Lakeshire SUPER BRIDGE, meant to traverse the length of Lake Everstill. It should be done in 20 or so years. Give or take a decade or two.

passages.title: Render's Army
passages.text:
Heading up north, eh? How about you wage your own little war against those Blackrock monsters? What do you say, <name>?

Kill any Blackrock orc that you see at Alther's Mill or Render's Camp. Kill until your skin turns red from their blood splatter and then come back to me and I'll pay you handsomely.

It might not stop the Blackrock invasion, but it'll be sure to put a kink in their plans.

passages.title: Render's Army
passages.text: You've probably bought us another day, maybe two. Nice work, <name>.

passages.title: Weapons of War
passages.text:
What I'm about to ask of you isn't going to be easy to accomplish, <name>. Keeshan left everything back there in that orc prison, and I'm not just talking about his soul or his will to live.

If we're going to get Johnny ready for war, we need to recover his prized possessions. The orcs now hold Keeshan's bow and his survival knife.

Head to Alther's Mill, east of here and look for two orc lieutenants, Murdunk and Homurk. They've got Keeshan's gear. Get it back.

I'll be in touch via gnomecorder.

passages.title: Weapons of War
passages.text: Did you terminate Murdunk and Homurk?

passages.title: Weapons of War
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder buzzes with energy.>

Come in, <name>. Do you copy? Troteman here! Great job on getting Keeshan's weapons back! Now there's one final mission you have to run. Are you up to the challenge?

passages.title: His Heart Must Be In It
passages.text:
<The gnomecorder clicks.>

His gear alone won't be enough, <name>. His heart must also be in this battle. To capture that, we need items of sentimental value. The Blackrock orcs of Render's Camp, located in the north, hold two such items that belong to Keeshan.

Get up there and search their coffers for Keeshan's headband and a jade amulet left to him by his wife - who was brutally killed during a Blackrock orc invasion.

Bring them back to me should you succeed.

passages.title: His Heart Must Be In It
passages.text: Did you locate the headband and amulet?

passages.title: His Heart Must Be In It
passages.text: I hope with these items and with his crew all rescued he'll have a change of heart. We can't do this without Keeshan.

passages.title: Adella's Covert Camp
passages.text:
Lady Shandris has already asked for you to assist us further.

Adella has struck out to the east, among the woodpaw gnolls, and established a foothold south of Camp Mojache. You are to report to her if you wish to assist Lady Shandris and the Alliance further.

Don't stray too close to Camp Mojache... the Horde will not hesitate to attack. Keep to the south and look for our banners.

passages.title: Adella's Covert Camp
passages.text: Welcome to Shadebough, <name>. Lady Shandris sent word of you.

passages.title: Steady Hand
passages.text:
Nearby to the north, you will find Terrath the Steady. He has taken upon the task of pulling the stone dragons back into the fold. We find ourselves repeating this trial every few hundred years... the stone dragons are fickle, and bend only to strength.

Terrath is balanced and reasonable, but his goals may not be easily accomplished. Go to him. Appeal to the more balanced side of the Stonemother.

passages.title: Steady Hand
passages.text: Greetings, <race>. I have been told of your coming. If you wish to aid me, then perhaps I can be of aid to you as well.

passages.title: Rocky Upheaval
passages.text:
To the east, on the Crimson Expanse, you will find Gorsik. He embodies the more unstable and violent nature of our kind. He is neither friendly, nor trusting, but his word carries weight.

Proving yourself to Gorsik will go a long way towards proving yourself to the Stonemother.

passages.title: Rocky Upheaval
passages.text:
You are Diamant's chosen.

So small. So fragile.

Do you realize that your actions shall be the basis by which your entire, "Earthen Ring" is judged? You truly think you can stand for so many?

You are a fool. A confident fool. We shall see if you are a capable fool as well.

passages.title: Doomshrooms
passages.text:
The rift to your world has poisoned our home. Corrupted it. Polluted it.

This expanse festers and grows. It becomes difficult to even see the purity of the rock beneath this filth.

If you are here to lend your aid, then go about cleansing this overgrowth. Look for the brightly glowing mushrooms that are growing faster than the others. They are the worst of the offenders.

passages.title: Doomshrooms
passages.text:
You have appealed to Diamant. He is patient. Trusting. Perhaps too much so. You have much to prove if you wish my favor, <race>.

Still, this is a start.

passages.title: Gone Soft
passages.text:
The fungal behemoths that surround us have succumbed to a weakness very similar to that that affects your kind. Their skin has grown soft. They no longer belong with the stone.

Kill them. We do not wish to see this infection spread.

passages.title: Gone Soft
passages.text:
You carry with you a certain degree of potency. I can find some respect for such strength, especially in your kind.

My concerns are not yet abated. Not for the source of the overgrowth, and not for you.

passages.title: Familiar Intruders
passages.text:
Fleshling. Some of your kind skitter among the rocks. Too cowardly to approach, too swift to be crushed.

If you wish my favor, deal with them. I tire of these games.

passages.title: Familiar Intruders
passages.text:
It is good to see you again, brother. I see that your efforts go well. The Stone Lords appear to be showing you some degree of trust.

We've come to help. We might be of some aid in tracking down the source of this sudden growth. I highly suspect your giant friend's aggressions are focused in the wrong direction.

passages.title: Unnatural Causes
passages.text:
This is most definitely magic in origin. Not even druidic. I suspect one among the stone troggs to the north.

Go to Gorsik and point him in their direction. Hopefully this will help earn his favor.

passages.title: Unnatural Causes
passages.text:
The stone troggs? And I am to trust you at your word?

I have no love for the Verlok anyway. Suspicion is more than enough reason to lay waste to them. We shall see if your word is true.

passages.title: Wrath of the Fungalmancer
passages.text:
Their leader hides within his hole ahead. He is the one that has brought the plague upon the crimson expanse.

He must be killed.

One of your Earthen Ring companions is already inside. You should speak with her.

passages.title: Wrath of the Fungalmancer
passages.text:
I cannot fit inside. Our elementals are not up to the task.

You must see this done.

passages.title: Wrath of the Fungalmancer
passages.text:
Well done, <race>.

Gorsik shall hear of your deed. Therazane shall hear of your deed.

You are quite vicious for one so small... and so soft.

passages.title: Shaken and Stirred
passages.text:
I have sent my brothers to assault the Verlok village from below. The Verlok will gather on their rocky ledges, as they always do to avoid our ire. When they do, we shall make the earth itself shake them until they fall at our feet below.

That is where you prove your use. When they fall to the ground amongst my brothers, make sure that they do not rise again.

passages.title: Shaken and Stirred
passages.text: Well done fleshling. Your presence complimented my brothers well.

passages.title: Corruption Destruction
passages.text: If this disgusting growth is truly brought on by the Verlok, then their supplies will be in their village to the north. Bring them to me so that I can verify your claims.

passages.title: Corruption Destruction
passages.text: I await your proof, <race>...

passages.title: Corruption Destruction
passages.text: So your words prove true. You have my gratitude, <race>.

passages.title: In Search of Bravo Company
passages.text:
If you and Keeshan are going to defend Lakeshire, we're going to need to find his old battalion. Last I heard all of 'em - Messner, Jorgensen, Krakauer and Danforth - were captured by the Blackrock orcs. Now I don't know where they could possibly be or if they're even alive, but I'd be a damned fool if I didn't ask you to try and find 'em.

Search Alther's Mill, east of here, for any clues.

passages.title: In Search of Bravo Company
passages.text: Keeshan? You mean JOHNNY'S ALIVE? You bet your sweet behind I'll help, but first you gotta get me out of this damned cage.

passages.title: Breaking Out is Hard to Do
passages.text:
The key to this cage is stored in a pouch over at the worg den, just north of our location. The problem is that the pouch is resting safely atop a tree stump amidst a sea of bloodthirsty man-killing worgs.

You've got one shot to get that key without waking up any of those sleeping worgs. Head to the worg den and find a way into the center. Tread carefully and watch out for the Blackrock worg captain. Get the key and return to me.

If you got a pet, I'd recommend telling it to stay back!

passages.title: Breaking Out is Hard to Do
passages.text: Did you get the cage key?

passages.title: Breaking Out is Hard to Do
passages.text: IT'S PAYBACK TIME!

passages.title: The Wilds of Feralas
passages.text:
You are truly brave to help us protect these lands, hero. If you wish to do more for the wilds, there are others in need of your aid.

The verdant forests of Feralas lie to the south. There, in the shade of the mighty Twin Colossals, you must seek out Konu Runetotem. He has found signs of a disturbing illness.

Follow the road west around the Twin Colossals to find Camp Ataya. Go in peace, <name>, and walk with the Earth Mother.

passages.title: The Wilds of Feralas
passages.text: Peace, friend. I wish we could have met under less troubling circumstances.

passages.title: Battlefront Triage
passages.text:
You seem quick on your feet, <race>. I need someone to go out into the chaos of the front and patch up our injured.

Take my kit. It's simple enough to use.

Heal them before the stone troggs finish them off for good.

passages.title: Battlefront Triage
passages.text: If you ever get tired of your being a <class>, come look me up. You seem very good with those fleshy hands of yours.

passages.title: The Call of Kalimdor
passages.text:
I've been sent by the good people of Theramore to find loyal members of the Alliance who are willing to help Lady Jaina with some problems in Dustwallow.

You weren't really here working for the goblins, were you?

The path back to Dustwallow will take you through Ratchet. Wait on the end of this pier for the next boat. Once you get to Ratchet, speak with Gazlowe. He'll point you in the right direction from there.

Ugh, I think I stepped on a fish! And it flopped!

passages.title: The Call of Kalimdor
passages.text: Yeah?  Whaddya need?

passages.title: Protecting Her Royal Highness Poobah
passages.text:
These vicious jungle cats have been circling me for some time now. I watch them as closely as I can, but they seem to just... disappear into the grass.

How they snarl and hiss!

Don't get me wrong... I still want you to rescue me, but first, clear out some of these cats. I won't need to be rescued if I end up someone's dinner.

passages.title: Protecting Her Royal Highness Poobah
passages.text: Please, my hero, dispose of the stalking panthers!

passages.title: Protecting Her Royal Highness Poobah
passages.text:
It's about time you returned.  I was beginning to worry that I was going to be eaten while you hunted.

A cat eating a princess... wouldn't that be a fancy feast?

passages.title: Negotiations Terminated
passages.text:
Go now, go back to your fleet. Tell them what kind of a monster claims authority over the Dragonmaw.

Our "Warchief" is a traitor to his blood. Since his return from Outland he reeks of demon and leads what remains of our clan to ruin.

Help rid the Dragonmaw of Mor'ghor, and those of us with pure blood will be your allies forever. This I can promise.

passages.title: Negotiations Terminated
passages.text:
The Fel Orcs from Outland have laid claim to the Dragonmaw? Obscene!

If Hellscream knew what was happening here, he'd raze their city to the ground...

passages.title: It's Never Over
passages.text:
Those Blackrock orcs are gonna need an army to handle the Bravo Company and you, <name>. When you're ready to go, meet us at the dock facing Lake Everstill and we'll set off on my riverboat for Camp Everstill on the other side of the lake.

See you there, <name>.

passages.title: It's Never Over
passages.text: It's orc killin' time.

passages.title: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs
passages.text:
Seasoned wolf kabobs are a house favorite! Sure, I can make you some. But first I'll need the supplies.

Bring me five wolf skirt steaks. The dire wolves near the river north of town are good to hunt; I wouldn't stray too far into the woods if I were you.

passages.title: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs
passages.text: Were you able to find five wolf skirt steaks yet?

passages.title: Seasoned Wolf Kabobs
passages.text:
Mmm-mmm! The skirtsteak's the best part. It's not an efficient way to cook, though.

Here, have this recipe. It's a little different, but flank meat's easier to come by when you really need a meal.

passages.title: Dusky Crab Cakes
passages.text:
I'll let you in on a little secret - Dusky "Crab" Cakes are really made from spider meat! I know it's a bit disgusting, but the cakes have a nice, tangy flavor and make great snacks!

If you want to try some still, I'm afraid I'm out of meat. I need some lump meat to whip up a few more cakes.

Venom Web Spiders are a good source - they nest to the north, between the foothills and the river.

passages.title: Dusky Crab Cakes
passages.text: Hail, <name>.  Did you get that lump meat for me?

passages.title: Dusky Crab Cakes
passages.text:
Ah yes, a nice lump you have there!  Let me just get this seasoned with my secret spices (no looking!) and get them to skittering on a skillet for a while...

And, although Dusky Crab Cakes are my specialty and I won't give out the recipe, here's the recipe for a dish that's almost as good.

passages.title: Getting In With the Bloodsail
passages.text:
These plans are... interesting. Firallon, you're smarter than this!

Look, he has all three ships devoted to cannon fire, and only a few men coming in through the tunnel. He can never take Booty Bay with three ships and a dozen footmen. And he knows that.

No, they've got something else planned... and you're going to find out what it is. Speak to Yancey Grillsen, the Bloodsail Recruiter, just to the north of town.

That's right, <name>. You'd better hope that they don't recognize your face.

passages.title: Getting In With the Bloodsail
passages.text: Yarr, ya made a good decision, lad.

passages.title: We Have a Situation
passages.text: One of Clay's catapult teams is broken down on the front. I need you to get some parts from him and get that catapult back in the fight, <name>.

passages.title: The Hermit
passages.text:
I've been told there's signs of activity at Beggar's Haunt. People have reported seeing lights in the tower to the east of town.

Few would be bold enough to stay that close to Deadwind Pass. You're the first to report since I've learned about this; go check it out and make sure whatever's in there is human.

passages.title: The Hermit
passages.text:
Ah, welcome, stranger. I'd offer you something, but there's not much here...

Could I beg you to run some errands for a poor old hermit?

passages.title: Seeing Where Your Loyalties Lie
passages.text:
Thar be just one thing...

Yancey hears things. A few o' me hearties were pretty deep in their cups when they told me about some <race> <class> that came a-rollin' through the Southern Command lookin' for charts and orders. Even ran a couple o' good pirates through, <he/she> did.

Like I said, they were up to their eyeballs in grog, but still... a buccaneer's gotta trust his ears. So I've just got one small task for ye, one sent down from Firallon hisself...

Bring me the head of Fleet Master Seahorn.

passages.title: Seeing Where Your Loyalties Lie
passages.text: Firallon special-ordered this one himself.  Said the tauren's too much of a risk.

passages.title: Seeing Where Your Loyalties Lie
passages.text:
Well blow me down!  Now there's something ya don't see too often.

<Yancey reaches out and shakes your hand.>

Welcome aboard, <name>.  Plunder and booty await ye.

passages.title: Your First Day as a Pirate
passages.text:
Ye may be a slayer of Fleet Masters, but rules is rules and orders is orders. And MY orders say that all new pirates start out as swabbies. It's the rule.

You're to be working for Captain Keelhaul, the commander of the Riptide. It's the westernmost ship in the fleet, which is parked south of the tip o' the cape.

Find him in his captain's chambers, and bring yer papers.

passages.title: Your First Day as a Pirate
passages.text: I trust y'got yer papers, swabbie.  I'd hate t'send ye all the way back to Yancey.

passages.title: Your First Day as a Pirate
passages.text:
Yes... yes... I see... well, everything appears to be in order.

Slayer of the great Seahorn, eh?  That doesn't matter on MY ship.  Only thing you're gonna be slaying is deck stains.  Grab a mop.

passages.title: The Bane of Many A Pirate
passages.text:
Gum disease. It's a real problem, <race>.

I know you're new and all, and probably haven't ever needed your gums cut, but the rest of us pirates have to deal with a little thing called SCURVY. It's why we keep so many limes around here.

Well... we used to keep limes around here. Someone made off with our last shipment, but they can't have gone far - maybe to the nearby islands? Bring them back, and maybe I'll see what I can do to get you promoted from swabbie.

passages.title: The Bane of Many A Pirate
passages.text: I've seen too many good men die to such a preventable disease, <race>.  We need those limes.

passages.title: The Bane of Many A Pirate
passages.text: I'll distribute these right away, <race>.  And I'll see what I can do to put in the good word for you.

passages.title: Cannonball Swim
passages.text:
Help out a fellow swabbie?

Keelhaul asked me to gather up some cannonballs at the bottom of the ocean. Let me tell you why this doesn't work for me.

- One: I have tiny arms. Look at them! Do you really think I can pick up a cannonball, even underwater?

- Two: I have a weak respiratory system. I start to white out after holding my breath for more than ten seconds.

- Three: There are sharks.

You gotta help me, <name>! I've been demoted as far as I can... I don't want to see what comes next!

passages.title: Cannonball Swim
passages.text: I wasn't always a swabbie, you know.

passages.title: Cannonball Swim
passages.text: Thanks, <name>.  I'd been hearing whispers about "Pretty Boy" and a "boo-box".  I don't think I want to go in the boo-box.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Camouflage
passages.text:
We're gonna need some supplies before we take out the Blackrock army and save Redridge. That's where you come in, rookie.

Keeshan put me in charge of getting camouflage together for the Bravo Company field kit. What I need you to do is head south and do a little "gardening." There are two parts to this little adventure that you should know about: (1) Leaves and (2) Fox poop. We need 'em both.

What did you think camo was made of?

Head south and gather what I asked for, <pal/lady>.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Camouflage
passages.text: Leaves and poop - that's what I need.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Camouflage
passages.text: Nice job, rookie. I'm gonna go ahead and put the camo in the box. We should be ready soon.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Chloroform
passages.text:
The first part of this mission is all covert ops, <name>. To that end, we need to be able to incapacitate the enemy without making any sounds. To do that we're going to need chloroform.

The muckdwellers at the bottom of Lake Everstill hold chloroform in their glands. I'm going to need you to go underwater and recover muckdweller glands. Think you can handle it?

Come back to me once you've recovered enough glands.

Where's the lake you ask? Open your eyes, dummy. Directly west.

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Chloroform
passages.text: Did you recover the glands?

passages.title: Bravo Company Field Kit: Chloroform
passages.text: Perfect. Those orcs won't know what hit 'em - literally. I'll need a few minutes to get these in working order and then I'll put them in the Bravo Company field kit.

passages.title: Hunting the Hunters
passages.text:
Just south of here on the Lakeridge Highway are a group of Blackrock orcs that stalk the forests under cover of darkness and ambush the uninitiated. That group is the first line of defense for the Blackrock army. They're scouts, reporting everything they see back to their central command. They need to be taken OUT or our mission here could be compromised.

Head south and kill every Blackrock hunter that you see.

passages.title: Hunting the Hunters
passages.text: Great work, <name>. We need to move quickly before they send for reinforcements.

passages.title: Point of Contact: Brubaker
passages.text:
Before we do a damned thing we need to get a field kit together. You'll help with that, <name>. There's also a matter of scouting. Thankfully for that we got some help from Stormwind. An old war buddy of mine, Brubaker, was sent here by SI:7 to scout around for us. You're to meet him in the field, just south of here.

Meet up with Brubaker and find out what he knows.

passages.title: Point of Contact: Brubaker
passages.text: Brubaker is dead. It looks like the orcs are attempting to send a message with this grisly display. Upon closer examination you notice something in Brubaker's pouch.

passages.title: Starvation Diet
passages.text:
The Creeping Ruin to the east is crawling with fully-grown Shadraspawn spiders. They're large enough to drag off an entire dwarf in the night, and you'll see evidence enough of that when you get there... bodies are cocooned all through the ruins.

They don't keep them alive for long, <name>, but they feed off the bodies for days. It's too late to save the victims, but we can't let those spiders grow fat and thrive. Make sure you get rid of those cocoons.

passages.title: Starvation Diet
passages.text: A grim task for sure, <name>, but it'll keep the spiders left alive from recovering. I thank you.

passages.title: The Night Watch
passages.text:
I'm afraid you're all I've got to help here, <name>. Stormwind's forces are so taxed by greater evils that they can't spare a single footman to protect Darkshire. It's up to me and the rest of the Night Watch to keep our homes safe.

There's more threats here than just wolves, unfortunately. Rotting horrors roam near Blind Mary's Haunt, on the southeast outskirts. If they're not kept in check, they'll be visiting our homes in the night.

Deal with the undead and report back to me for your bounty.

passages.title: The Night Watch
passages.text: I don't have authority to order you around, <name>. But at least think of the citizens here who'll be suffering if those undead are allowed to lurk.

passages.title: The Night Watch
passages.text: Splendid, <name>.  For your service to the people of Darkshire you shall be rewarded.

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
There is a poor, sad spirit, Blind Mary, who haunts an old farm house in the hills south of Darkshire.

Here, take this Spectral Comb and ask Blind Mary to comb her hair. Then bring back the comb and I will glean from it the Ghost Hair I'll need for the thread.

And take care, for dark things now lurk near that house...

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
<Sob> Oh please, don't look at me!  I tore out these eyes with my own hands, but I can still feel your gaze!

I'm hideous!  Hideous!  Please, look away!!

passages.title: Ghost Hair Thread
passages.text:
What is this?  A comb?  It's lovely!  And it glides through my hair as if it weren't the stiff, stringy horror that it is.

Oh, if only I had a mirror...

passages.title: Supplies from Darkshire
passages.text:
Oh, what is a poor old man to do? I need some supplies from Darkshire, but the village is so far away and I am so old and feeble...I would never make the trip.

Can you go to Darkshire and bring me back some ghost hair thread? You can get it from Madame Eva at her home on the Darkshire square.

passages.title: Supplies from Darkshire
passages.text: Ah, ghost hair thread is what you need, is it?  I'm afraid I have none in stock, but I can make some for you...if you can supply the ghost hair.

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text:
NO!!!!!

Take it, take this comb away from me!

I'm a monster, and no one will ever think me lovely again!

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text: I sense that you have seen Blind Mary.  You have my comb...?

passages.title: Return the Comb
passages.text: I can make a spool of ghost hair thread with this, and have a few strands to spare.  Here are some coins for those extra strands.

passages.title: Hard Falls
passages.text:
Stone Dragons bow only to strength. When we have punished them enough, they will bend back to our will.

I have sent many of my strongest giants onto the fields in the west. They will bring the drakes to the ground. You will see to it that they do not take wing again after they fall.

passages.title: Hard Falls
passages.text:
Not just fast it seems. You have some bite in you.

Well done, <class>.

passages.title: Fragile Values
passages.text:
It is now time to draw the Broodmother's attention. To do so, we will need a mallet that the troggs use when making offerings to her.

Seek out the Stone Trogg Beast Tamers that are attempting to tame basilisks in the southern portions of the Pale Roost. You will find a mallet on one of their corpses.

passages.title: Fragile Values
passages.text: Did you find a mallet?

passages.title: Fragile Values
passages.text:
Glorious.
