passages.title: Amongst the Ruins
passages.text:
This is exactly what I need!  A fathom core is an incredible well of information that we will be able to draw much good from.  Whatever the Twilight's Hammer is up to in there - and believe me when I say it is no good - my comrades and I will now uncover.

You've done well here today; the Earthen Ring looks upon you warmly for assisting us.  You've also helped the Horde as a whole, and for that you should be proud.

passages.title: Deep in the Deeps
passages.text:
The Naga and the Twilight's Hammer work together to undo all the progress we've made in this area. What's more, Je'neu tells me that he feels the presence of an Old God lingering far beneath us.

If they wish to witness chaos, we will give them just that.

<name>, cut down their strongest warriors, and we'll see how much they enjoy it.

Search carefully, Blackfathom Deeps is full of underwater passages and side paths in the caves that may hide your targets.

passages.title: Deep in the Deeps
passages.text: I can hear their cries from here! Maybe this will show them how foolish it is to wish for the return of an Old God.

passages.title: The Thunderdrome!
passages.text:
Hey, friend, you interested in excitement? Adventure? Money? Violence?

Well, you'd better like violence, because they just reopened the Thunderdrome in Gadgetzan. It was sad to see it unused for so long, what with the injury lawsuits, and the racketeering charges, and the copyright infringement... But it's back, and just waiting for burly, savage folk like you to enter and throw down with the foulest opponents ever!

Head to Gadgetzan and talk to Dr. Dealwell to sign up. And tell your friends!

passages.title: The Thunderdrome!
passages.text:
Another proud <class>, lured by the promise of fame! Of wealth! Of VIOLENCE!

Yes, welcome, friend. Welcome... to THUNDERDROME!

passages.title: The Thunderdrome!
passages.text:
Hey, friend, you interested in excitement? Adventure? Money? Violence?

Well, you'd better like violence, because they just reopened the Thunderdrome in Gadgetzan. It was sad to see it unused for so long, what with the injury lawsuits, and the racketeering charges, and the copyright infringement... But it's back, and just waiting for burly, savage folk like you to enter and throw down with the foulest opponents ever!

Head to Gadgetzan and talk to Dr. Dealwell to sign up. And tell your friends!

passages.title: The Thunderdrome!
passages.text:
Another proud <class>, lured by the promise of fame! Of wealth! Of VIOLENCE!

Yes, welcome, friend. Welcome... to THUNDERDROME!

passages.title: Blackfathom Deeps
passages.text: Although our position is exposed, we are safe compared to our friends inside Blackfathom Deeps! They stand mere feet away from the most deadly Twilight's Hammer forces in the area. Speak with Sentinel Aluwyn and give them the aid they desperately need!

passages.title: Blackfathom Deeps
passages.text: Thank Elune you're here! We could use all the help we can get.

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy
passages.text:
Cultists...sacrifice...power...

Enemy...awaken...

Old God...imprison...me...

Lord...Kelris...

Bring head...revenge...

ERADICATE!!!

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy
passages.text: Revenge...reward...

passages.title: The Enemy of My Enemy
passages.text:
<The Flaming Eradicator appears to concentrate.>

I spare your life for your help, <race>. Leave now...before I change my...mind.

passages.title: Agamaggan
passages.text:
I sense a being of immense power within these twisted thorns, <name>. The entire area has come alive at its presence.

It must be the Spirit of Agamaggan! He was one of the first and most powerful beings to ever live - the Quilboar worship him fervently.

All the vines you see across the land are a result of his blood; of his sacrifice to save Azeroth in the War of the Ancients.

If there's any being that could steer the Quilboar towards their noble roots, it would be him.

You must seek him out.

passages.title: Going, Going, Guano!
passages.text:
The bats native to Razorfen Kraul produce a very peculiar natural substance. Their guano's stench seems to send the Quilboar into a murderous frenzy - and this place reeks of it!

I need you to find the bat cave, and bring me a suitable sample. If we can reverse the effects and produce an antidote, we may be able to save the Quilboar.

passages.title: Going, Going, Guano!
passages.text: Ah, I see you have returned. Were you able to procure any Kraul Guano?

passages.title: Going, Going, Guano!
passages.text: Well done! This is just what we need, <name>.

passages.title: Willix the Importer
passages.text:
At last, help has arrived!

You have no clue how long I've been held prisoner here. I can't remember the last time I saw the outside of this place.

You see, I am an entrepreneur. Always out for a copper, as they say. I caught wind that pig snouts were selling outrageously high in the market. I figured it would be an easy in, easy out kind of affair. As you can see, I was a bit wrong!

Anyway, if you'd be so kind as to help me get out of here, I'll make it worth your while.

passages.title: Willix the Importer
passages.text: Thanks again, friend! I told you I'd make it worth your while.

passages.title: Agamaggan
passages.text:
I sense a being of immense power within these twisted thorns, <name>. The entire area has come alive at its presence.

It must be the Spirit of Agamaggan! He was one of the first and most powerful beings to ever live - the Quilboar worship him fervently.

All the vines you see across the land are a result of his blood; of his sacrifice to save Azeroth in the War of the Ancients.

If there's any being that could steer the Quilboar towards their noble roots, it would be him.

You must seek him out.

passages.title: Agamaggan
passages.text:
<The Spirit of Agamaggan looks at you. An ancient voice echoes inside your head.>

I've been waiting for you to come here.

passages.title: Take Them Down!
passages.text:
In order to maintain the relative safety in the Southern Barrens, we must put a stop to the current leadership of the Razorfen tribe. Although Charlga Razorflank commands her people through powerful mysticism, her true power is in the strength of the elders around her.

Slay them. Hunt down Bonetusk, the pack leader. Stop Roogug, the overseer of Geomancers. Crush Ramtusk, the quilboar Warlord.

Return to me when the deed is done.

passages.title: Take Them Down!
passages.text: You've done well this day. Agathelos would have taken many lives in its fury.

passages.title: Feeling Thorny
passages.text:
Mankrik's furor over his dead wife raises further concerns, <class>.

The quilboar in Razorfen Kraul are far more ruthless and full of hatred than Mankrik could ever imagine.

You should travel south there and speak with my old friend Auld Stonespire. He works to put an end to their rampage before the land suffers more in its already weak condition.

passages.title: Feeling Thorny
passages.text: Only a veteran like you could brave the dangers lurking here.

passages.title: The Stone Shards
passages.text:
Ancient stones are strewn across this land. The elements flock to them, surrounding them protectively.

These are sites of great power, and the largest is just west of Hammerfall. Not a soul trespasses, but if you go there alone, you can hear whispers from the earth itself.

I have not visited there in a long while... but our grunts have told me the whispers have started again. Would you look for me? Will you see if the stones still speak?

passages.title: The Stone Shards
passages.text:
<The shards pulse softly, and a whisper slowly echoes through your head.>

Help...

passages.title: Myzrael's Tale
passages.text:
As the stone goes quiet, you're left with a vague sense of unease. Something isn't right.

Perhaps you should tell Zaruk of what you've done so far.

passages.title: Myzrael's Tale
passages.text:
I know, <name>. I should not have sent you.

Forgive me... the whispers of the past are sometimes too strong.

passages.title: Scourge First... Alliance Later
passages.text:
Darkmaster Gandling of the Cult of the Damned leads the Scourge offensive here in Andorhal. My old counterpart, Thassarian, leads the Alliance forces. If we're to win Andorhal, we'll have to defeat both, but we will certainly fail if we take on both at once.

I know Thassarian well enough to know that he will focus on the Scourge first. We will do the same.

Take out the weaker, desiccated Scourge to reduce their numbers. The Alliance will have to wait to taste our wrath.

passages.title: Scourge First... Alliance Later
passages.text:
You may not act quickly, but at least you do not fail me.

Very well.  I will have a more important task for you, <name>, when the time is right.

passages.title: War Machines
passages.text:
You fools will never defeat the Scourge with those abominations running around. Koltira blathers on about reducing their numbers, but the Scourge's best weapon here in Andorhal can be found in those lumbering brutes that are throwing my deathguards around like ragdolls.

I won't have it. <name>, enter the battlefield and destroy those monsters.

passages.title: War Machines
passages.text:
With the behemoths out of the way, our victory against the Scourge is inevitable.

Our current chances against the Alliance aren't quite as favorable... but that's no concern of yours.  Not yet, anyhow.

passages.title: Scholomancer
passages.text:
The Scholomance is one of the few Scourge holdouts remaining west of the Thondroril. The headmaster of Scholomance, a cultist by the name of Darkmaster Gandling, has made an appearance on the battlefield.

This will be his final mistake.

You will find Gandling in a square near the southern end of town. I want you to fight and weaken Gandling. I will join you to help finish him off.

passages.title: Scholomancer
passages.text: Excellently done, <name>.  And now, with the leader of the Scourge forces eliminated from Andorhal, we bide our time.

passages.title: Suddenly, Murlocs!
passages.text:
So we've got troggs working for kobolds, and kobolds working for gnolls. The gnolls must've moved in from the Wetlands.

How do I know? Well, they brought friends, because what's left of the Loch is swarming with Bluegill murlocs that were never there before.

Pests are pests, but this coordination is worrying. I need you to talk to Cannary Caskshot. She's one of the best hunters in these parts, and she'll know how to handle murlocs, if you can pull her away from her mug long enough.

passages.title: Suddenly, Murlocs!
passages.text:
Murlocs? Sure, I've hunted murlocs.

And every single stinkin' one of them deserved what they got! You hear me?

passages.title: Smells Like A Plan
passages.text:
Murlocs workin' with gnolls? That's a laugh! Now, just killin' them won't get you anywhere. Too many of the buggers.

But I've got a plan, usin' the old noggin, see. Those murlocs, they have this smell, they get that smell on stuff, and when another murloc smells it, they go all crazy! Makes great bait for 'em.

Anyway, they've got little glands that have that smell in 'em. You go and get me a bunch of those.

passages.title: Smells Like A Plan
passages.text: Now don't you stink all to high hell! I'm assumin' that's because of the murlocs, but it's hard to tell.

passages.title: Smells Like A Plan
passages.text:
Phew! Ain't that a stench.

Now you prepare yourself, because I'm about to wow you with what's left of my mental faculties.

passages.title: A Load of Croc
passages.text:
Now while you're runnin' around doin' whatever the heck it is that you do, would you mind helpin' me out a bit?

See, I usually go out huntin' crocolisks down in the loch, but given certain circumstances, I'd rather sit here right now. Mighty polite of you not to give me grief over it, thanks!

So seein' as how you're such a <gentleman/lady>, why don't you bring me back some crocolisk jaws and I'll give you some mostly-clean money in return.

passages.title: A Load of Croc
passages.text: So did you get those crocolisk things or did I make that up?

passages.title: A Load of Croc
passages.text: Mighty kind of you to help out an ol' fool like me. Here's your reward as promised an' all.

passages.title: Buzz Off
passages.text:
When the Stonewrought Dam burst, it drained near the entire loch. Horrible ecological devastation.

And don't you go thinking it didn't really affect us dwarves! Not only are we plumb out of fish, but there's acres of dead threshadons out there left to rot in the sun. The buzzards are after them, and they're spreading all manner of filth and disease right on the outskirts of town.

I can't ask you to clean it all up, but could you deal with the buzzards? Killin' even just a few will help.

passages.title: Buzz Off
passages.text: Plenty of 'em flappin' around yet, lad.

passages.title: Buzz Off
passages.text: That should help prevent disease and illness from spreading into our remaining water. Many thanks, <name>.

passages.title: Foes Before Hoes
passages.text:
The men who till Felstone Field are no farmers. They're soldiers.

Thassarian's forces needed food, so he sent some of the Alliance north from Andorhal, to tend Felstone Field. The battle for Andorhal may be over, but another battle looms... Forsaken versus human. Killing those soldiers that work at Felstone will give the Dark Lady's forces a decided advantage.

passages.title: Foes Before Hoes
passages.text: Ha ha!  I hope that they come back as zombies.

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text:
How did you get in here?

Oh, it doesn't matter. I'm Murd Doc of the G-Team. We're the best there is, and we're here to retake Gnomeregan!

When nobody else could help him, the High Tinker found and hired us.

But we simply can't do this alone! You're an honorary G-Team Commando now, <name>.

Take this parachute, jump down straight ahead into the Hall of Gears, and kill the Viscous Fallout. After you're done, report to Commando B.E Barechus by the west hallway. You two will get along great, I'm sure.

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text: What're you doing out in the open like that, fool? Get down!

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text: I hope that wasn't too much for you. The mission is far from over!

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text:
That Murd Doc is crazy, <class>. Never, ever, let you find yourself in an aircraft with that gnome.

Stealth usually isn't my thing, and it's certainly not going to be yours. Go down this hallway to the Launch Bay and dispose of the Electrocutioner 6000.

The Electrocutioner is in charge of the aircraft...

...and I hate aircraft. I'm not getting in any sort of aircraft!

Use this parachute to drop down afterwards and speak with Commando Face for your next job.

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text: Woah! How did you see me!?

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text: Took you long enough. Get behind the pillar with me before you blow our cover!

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text:
I'd keep my distance from B.E Barechus and Murd Doc, neither is terribly stable.

You are, though, so let's get you to work! Go down into this tunnel until you get to Tinkers' Court. Hopefully you'll know what to do when you meet Mekgineer Thermaplugg.

Our leader, Commando Hann Ibal waits somewhere in there. He'll reward you handsomely for all your work.

Probably.

passages.title: The G-Team
passages.text:
I'd love for you to come aboard as a full G-Team Commando, but you have other adventures to pursue.

I'm sure we'll meet again, and I hope you'll have considered joining by then. Here's something for your trouble.

passages.title: Home Sweet Gnome
passages.text:
I used t' have quite the home back in Ironforge. That is, I did until I was booted out to make way for the gnomes.

They couldn't stop a bunch of troggs with all them gizmos and machines! An' I have to pay for their weakness?

No, sir. No longer.

Go to Gnomeregan and talk to Commando Murd Doc. Sure, he's a gnome, but his crew, S.A.F.E. I think they call 'em, are going to take Gnomeregan back.

Go! I want my house back!

passages.title: Home Sweet Gnome
passages.text: Never thought I'd see a <race> like you down here. Any particular reason you're risking life and limb?

passages.title: Exploring Gnomeregan
passages.text:
The gnomish capital, Gnomeregan, hasn't been under their control for some time now. I know what it feels like to lose a home.

Please, venture inside Gnomeregan and speak to Commando Murd Doc, a member of S.A.F.E. If there's anything at all that you can do to help them take their home, I urge you to do so. There are dark secrets in those halls.

passages.title: Exploring Gnomeregan
passages.text: Never thought I'd see a <race> like you down here. Any particular reason you're risking life and limb?

passages.title: Moonfire
passages.text:
Druids play an important role in our society, but all too often we are seen as passive dreamers in a world that is changing around us.

The truth is, though, we must actively practice and go out onto the world to develop our connection to nature.

So go, get some more experience. You will begin to feel your connection deepen, learning new skills. Demonstrate the first you learn for me.

passages.title: Moonfire
passages.text: You have mastered the basics of the healing ways quickly, <name>. I have no doubt that your healing skills will often come in handy. Return to me when you need further training.

passages.title: Cleanup on Isle E.
passages.text: The Battle to reclaim the Echo Isles was a costly one. But well worth it, <class>. The great spirit, Bwonsamdi, helped our warriors defeat the foul Zalazane. He protected our warriors with spirits from the island. But some of those spirits fell in battle. Help put those spirits to rest. On the Echo Isles, you will find masks laying about gather them and bring them here.

passages.title: Cleanup on Isle E.
passages.text: Have you gathered the masks, <class>?

passages.title: Cleanup on Isle E.
passages.text: Thanks, <class>.  The spirits can rest now.  As long as we show them respect they will bless us and our new home for a long time.  Spirits be with you, <name>.

passages.title: Gathering Idols
passages.text:
Recently, just before the troggs surfaced within the site, we had uncovered a large number of strange, carved idols. But we didn't have the chance to study them, for soon after their discovery the troggs chased us away from the ruins! And those idols have a strange effect on the troggs. It makes them go berserk!

Bring me 8 idols - I want to study them, and I want them out of trogg hands! You can find the idols on the troggs infesting the site.

passages.title: Gathering Idols
passages.text: Do you have those idols?  We must study them and report our findings to Ironforge!

passages.title: Gathering Idols
passages.text:
You got them!  Nicely done, <name>!

And you don't look too worse for wear, even with those berserk troggs about.  I'm going to keep my eye on you...you show some promise.

passages.title: The Warchief Cometh
passages.text:
You're just in time, <name>nub. It is <name>nub, right?

<Grand Executor Mortuus looks at a sheet of paper.>

Yes, that's what the paperwork says: "<name>nub."

<Grand Executor Mortuus points to your name on the sheet of paper.>

Where was I? Oh yes, you're just in time! The Warchief should be arriving at any moment to meet with our leader and savior, the Dark Lady herself. Just stand by and be at your best behavior. I expect that when this demonstration is over we will all receive commendations!

passages.title: The Warchief Cometh
passages.text: Stand at attention, Zulazanjinub!

passages.title: The Warchief Cometh
passages.text:
Well that was unexpected. I am not one to doubt our Warchief, but...

Nevermind! We have work to do. I'm sure the Dark Lady and the Warchief will get this all worked out.

passages.title: The Binding
passages.text: A noise in the main chamber of the temple draws your attention. You hear a familiar laugh... Lorthuna. She's returned to interrupt the ritual - you must stop her!

passages.title: The Binding
passages.text:
Maruut said when all dis started dat he would gladly give his life ta see our task done. He would be proud of dis success... of dis death.

Da rift be closed on dis side. Deepholm should calm down a bit. It'll be takin' time for Thrall to mend da wound in Azeroth, and we'll be needin' to remain until he finishes.

Thank you for all ya've done. I don't tink we could have been accomplishin' dis so soon without you.

passages.title: Twilight Investigation
passages.text:
The city is still reeling from the seditious acts of the Twilight's Hammer in recent months. They prey on peasant fears and corrupt our most important citizens. We need to find out how deep the conspiracy runs.

I've tasked Major Samuelson of the Stormwind City Guard to head up an investigation. He's right here in the throne room. See if you can assist his efforts.

passages.title: Twilight Investigation
passages.text:
Hmmm, yes? My investigation of the Twilight's Hammer. Of course.

Your assistance will be valuable.

passages.title: The Scarlet Monastery
passages.text:
The same Monastery in Tirisfal Glades that the Scarlet Crusaders now occupy used to be a major training ground for our paladins. Now the Forsaken loom over it from the Undercity and the Crusade prevents us from utilizing it to train the very soldiers we need to deal with the Forsaken!

Look, I don't trust him, but Joseph the Awakened waits inside the graveyard. Go speak with him - although he is a crusader, he says he now rebels against them, providing us with an opportunity to take back what's ours.

passages.title: The Scarlet Monastery
passages.text:
Captain Nials sent you? I haven't seen her in ages! How is she? Did she get my letter?

Oh, you're not here for that. Well then, let's get down to business!

passages.title: Just Close Enough
passages.text:
Make no mistake - there is a ton of stuff to be done here! However, we also need to strike at the Forsaken where it hurts. The Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades is the perfect distance from the Undercity and Brill.

Report to Joseph the Awakened in their Library. He's a rebel crusader that can hopefully help us take the Monastery as our base of operations in that region, and maybe take out Arcanist Doan, one of their most powerful mages, in the process.

passages.title: Just Close Enough
passages.text:
You came here from Southshore, eh? I bet you hunger for revenge against the vile Forsaken that trashed the place. The Scarlet Crusade can help take care of that!

Right after you help me realign their misguided souls, that is.

passages.title: An Old, Crazed Friend
passages.text:
Joseph the Crazed was one of my good friends before he joined the Scarlet Crusade up in the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. I heard that he's in the Armory there trying some ridiculous attempt at taking over Herod's position as Scarlet Champion.

It's a death wish to challenge Herod like that! Go up there and try to talk him out of it.

passages.title: An Old, Crazed Friend
passages.text: You look pretty tough, <class>. There are wrongs to be righted here. Let's get started.

passages.title: Pitting Madness Against Madness
passages.text:
Our renewed forces can handle the situation here for a while without you. I've received reports that Joseph the Insane, a former Scarlet Crusade officer, is in the Scarlet Monastery Cathedral and is taking his band of renegades to strike out against Scarlet Commander Mograine.

This is an excellent opportunity. Go there and help him with his insane task, and maybe we can use the Monastery as an excellent stronghold right at Sylvanas' doorstep!

passages.title: Pitting Madness Against Madness
passages.text:
Wait, you were sent here by THE Shandris Feathermoon? I can barely believe my ears! To know that my cause is supported by her massive army...

Yes, yes, you will be perfect. You're the key to my future!

passages.title: Into the Scarlet Monastery
passages.text:
Oftentimes the best way to ensure our men sustain as few injuries as possible is to cause great harm to our enemies in their very homes and prevent battles from ever occurring!

Travel to the Scarlet Monastery and speak with Dark Ranger Velonara in their graveyard. She is leading a Forsaken assault there and could benefit from a seasoned <class> such as yourself.

passages.title: Into the Scarlet Monastery
passages.text: It looks like Darthalia sent an able <class>, as I requested.

passages.title: The Right Way
passages.text:
My people are not generally fond of the arcane arts that so many other races abuse. Thankfully the wizards within the Scarlet Monastery library are separated from us by considerable land, but their ability to transcend the physical realm concerns me and, ultimately, my tribe's survival.

Travel far to the west to the monastery's library and speak with Dark Ranger Velonara there. Her forces are already poised to strike at Arcanist Doan himself, head magi for the crusade.

passages.title: The Right Way
passages.text:
I'm surprised to see Huntsman Markhor working with me for once. He's usually quite stubborn. He does tend to a strong hatred for magic, though.

I hope you do, too, <class>, because we're going to strip the Scarlet Crusade of theirs.

passages.title: Moving Things Along
passages.text:
I'm waitin' on some very powerful reagents I ordered from the Undercity not long ago. I heard that the shipment is late because the Scarlet Monastery's crusaders are blocking its passage. Da Scarlet Champion, Herod, is likely to blame for dis annoyance.

Please go speak to Dark Ranger Velonara in the Scarlet Monastery's armory, she is goin' to 'take care' of Herod, which means my shipment will arrive safely!

passages.title: Moving Things Along
passages.text:
Yayo'jin is correct, you helping me here will aid her in the Hinterlands as well.

All the more reason to get started immediately.

passages.title: The Gilneas Liberation Front
passages.text:
The battle over this region still rages, <name>nub. Although we soundly beat back the Gilnean defenses and took Gilneas for the Horde, a small group of rebels managed to escape. The "Gilneas Liberation Front" - as they call themselves - make attacks of opportunity against our forces in the field. The rebels have had a few minor victories and now grow brazen in their assaults! The time to strike back is now, <name>nub.

Venture south into the wilds of Silverpine and kill any rebel that you cross.

passages.title: The Gilneas Liberation Front
passages.text: What have you to report, Duridnub?

passages.title: The Gilneas Liberation Front
passages.text:
Vorelocknub has returned! And in one piece!

Defender of Silverpine! Redeemer of the Horde! Vorelocknub, your bravery must be rewarded!

passages.title: Enemies Abroad
passages.text:
Sometimes we must acknowledge the need to protect our allies so that they may protect us. This is one such occasion, <race>.

Travel to the Scarlet Monastery near the Undercity in Tirisfal Glades. Once you arrive, go to the Cathedral and speak with Dark Ranger Velonara. She is leading the final assault against the crusade there, and it would benefit us all greatly to ensure our undead allies secure the monastery before the crusaders have a chance to attack their capital.

passages.title: Enemies Abroad
passages.text: Nazeer is a strong warrior - his hatred for our enemies rivals my own. You are welcome help to my forces.

passages.title: Agony Abounds
passages.text:
You have no doubt heard about the incident that transpired at the Wrath Gate in Northrend, yes? Due to those unfortunate events we are strictly forbidden from using the strain of life-shattering blight that we finally perfected. Now we have rules and regulations and other nonsense!

They've given us some neutered version of the perfected blight and expect us to weaponize it.

If I'm to get this crap functional I'll need several bags full of ferocious doomweed. You'll find it all over Silverpine.

passages.title: Agony Abounds
passages.text: Have you collected the ferocious doomweed I requested?

passages.title: Agony Abounds
passages.text: Agony abounds, friend! The land itself threatens to devour us, and yet we persist. I wonder why that is? With this doomweed and the guts and gore that T'Veen needs, we might have something suitable to send to the Forsaken front.

passages.title: Compendium of the Fallen
passages.text:
Don't fret, I serve no master, <race>. Within these halls lies a book called the Compendium of the Fallen. It holds vast amounts of research that the Scarlet Crusade has done on my kind over the years.

Simply put, I'd like you to retrieve it and bring it back to me. No questions asked.

passages.title: Compendium of the Fallen
passages.text: I don't want to stay in a monastery packed full of undead-hating zealots for much longer. Surely you can understand why. Don't speak to me if you don't have the book with you.

passages.title: Compendium of the Fallen
passages.text: Well done. How about I give you a nice reward for your work, and you don't tell a soul that you saw me here. Deal?

passages.title: Guts and Gore
passages.text:
If we're to get this new blight up and running we'll need clean beast guts. The problem is that clean beast guts are a rare commodity in Silverpine Forest. Most of the beasts here have succumbed to disease and thus only have diseased organs.

Do a sweep of the forested area east of here for worgs and grizzled bears. Kill only the non-diseased variety and rip out their entrails. Bring me all of the clean guts that you can stuff into your backpack!

passages.title: Guts and Gore
passages.text: Remember, I can only use clean beast guts for the new strain of blight we're developing.

passages.title: Guts and Gore
passages.text: Excellent! With these guts and the ferocious doomweed we'll be able to test out our new strain of blight. Now to select a suitable target...

passages.title: Right Under Their Noses
passages.text:
In the right side-room of the accursed cathedral ahead there is a torch on the wall. Move it and a secret door will open. Inside is High Inquisitor Fairbanks. He is now an undead.

I need him taken care of. Kill him in his own room if possible, I'd strongly prefer the crusaders not see him. You know the deal - kill him, and I'll reward you. No other words are necessary between us.

passages.title: Right Under Their Noses
passages.text: <Dominic hands you your reward. No words are spoken.>

passages.title: The Usual Suspects
passages.text:
<Samuelson scratches his chin, absently.>

My investigations reveal, ah, it's likely that there's trouble brewing among the Stormwind dock workers. Shifty lot. Don't trust 'em.

You should go there and shake the place down. Start grilling those longshoremen. That should keep you busy.

Go rout out those Twilight infidels!

passages.title: The Usual Suspects
passages.text:
This doesn't make any sense, <name>.

Why was Samuelson sending us out here on a wild goose chase?

Something doesn't feel right. We should poke around on our own...

passages.title: Iterating Upon Success
passages.text:
The concoction is finally ready, but before I can put my seal of approval on this strain, we'll need to run a field test.

Speak to Bat Handler Maggotbreath, here at High Command, and requisition a bat. The bat will take you to the Dawning Isles, east of here across Lordamere Lake, right into the heart of depravity itself - the Vile Fin murloc dens!

Use the concoction against the murlocs and report the results back to me.

Those results being that you killed them all, as commanded!

passages.title: Iterating Upon Success
passages.text: Have you exterminated the Vile Fin murlocs of the Dawning Isles?

passages.title: Iterating Upon Success
passages.text: Potent enough to exterminate a thousand murlocs! I think I'll put that on the label. You've done well, <name>, and great work around here gets rewarded.

passages.title: Easy Money
passages.text:
Well, hello there!

Whatever brought you, I'm so glad that you're here! My friends will never admit to it, but we could really use a hand.

The ancient region of Uldum has been exposed! Treasures beyond your wildest dreams, free for the taking!

We just need a bit of an escort, what with the bandits and all...

You'll accompany us, won't you?

You're welcome to all the loot you can haul off!

passages.title: Easy Money
passages.text:
Smells like someone else was in this cell recently.

Gross!

passages.title: The Twilight Plot
passages.text:
We came here to investigate rumors of a Titan artifact up at the Masters' Gate to the southwest.

One of those Twilight's Hammer cultists must have the plans for what they're doing up there. You're going to have to get them for us, <name>.

Keep searching the cultists until you find them.

passages.title: The Twilight Plot
passages.text: Those plans are the key to everything.

passages.title: The Twilight Plot
passages.text:
<Mowi takes a look at the plans that you hand to her.>

But... but, this is just gibberish!

What does this even say? What language is that?

passages.title: The Twilight Plot
passages.text:
We came here to investigate rumors of a Titan artifact up at the Masters' Gate to the southwest.

One of those Twilight's Hammer cultists must have the plans for what they're doing up there. You're going to have to get them for us, <name>.

Kill cultists at the Masters' Gate until you find them.

passages.title: The Twilight Plot
passages.text: Those plans are the key to everything.

passages.title: The Twilight Plot
passages.text:
<The examiner takes a look at the plans that you hand to him.>

This is just gibberish!

What does this even say? What language is that?

passages.title: Fly Over
passages.text:
I tried ta fly o'er the terrace an have a look fer myself, but those toastie eatin' pansies kept shootin' at me, an I couldn't get near.

Ya look like ya might be handy with the reins. Why don' ya take yer flyin' beastie up there ta the southwest and see what all the fuss is about?

passages.title: Fly Over
passages.text: What'd ya see? What are those cheese lovers up ta?

passages.title: Fly Over
passages.text: A waygate?! The culties dug up a Titan waygate?

passages.title: Silvermarsh Rendezvous
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>. We know exactly where the meeting location is.

The Upper Silvermarsh is a mercury swamp to the east of here. It's normally only inhabited by elementals and occasional stone troggs, but our scouts have seen some Twilight activity in the region.

Make your way there and let's find a way to eavesdrop on the Forgemaster's meeting.

passages.title: Silvermarsh Rendezvous
passages.text:
This is the place.  Our scouts confirmed the presence of high-ranking Twilight officers nearby as well as potential trogg hunting parties.

Be on the lookout, <name>.

passages.title: Fly Over
passages.text:
I'm quite adept at riding my flying carpet. Unfortunately, when I tried to investigate what the cultists had uncovered up at the Masters' Gate, they nearly shot me down.

You look as if you might be skilled with the flying reins as well. Would you mind flying up there to the southwest to see what they've unearthed?

passages.title: Fly Over
passages.text:
A waygate?! They unearthed a Titan waygate.

This is very interesting and potentially very bad.

passages.title: Too Close for Comfort
passages.text:
I'm happy for Nathaniel: he's spent so long trying to return to Northridge, and now with the Scarlet Crusade out of the way, he can finally move back home. It's just... even for such a seemingly-idyllic setting, it's not really the best place to raise a family.

For example: along this valley's edge, you will find rabid foxes searching for innocent prey. Every once in a while I catch a glimpse of one looking right at me.

Please, <class>, remove some of these foxes. I don't feel safe with them near.

passages.title: Too Close for Comfort
passages.text: I have a family to raise, and I need to do whatever I can to protect them.

passages.title: Too Close for Comfort
passages.text: I feel a bit more relieved, <name>.  Thank you.

passages.title: Hallowed Note
passages.text: Just a moment ago a messenger was looking for you, <name>. I believe she was sent by the priest trainer, Seer Ravenfeather. If this note is from the seer, I would go looking for her immediately.

passages.title: Hallowed Note
passages.text: I am pleased to meet you, <name>.

passages.title: Hallowed Note
passages.text: You have arrived at last. During your training in Camp Narache, I will guide you in the ways of the <class>. You have much to learn and I look forward to counting you among my students.

passages.title: Consecrated Note
passages.text: Just a moment ago a messenger was looking for you, <name>. I believe she was sent by the paladin trainer, Sunwalker Helaku. If this note is from the sunwalker, I recommend going to see him immediately.

passages.title: Consecrated Note
passages.text: I am pleased to meet you, <name>.

passages.title: Consecrated Note
passages.text: We have much to cover. In time, the ways of the sunwalkers will be as plain and natural to you as the shaman's conversations with the elements.

passages.title: The Joy of Boar Hunting
passages.text:
Try to contain your excitement, <name>, for you are in the presence of the greatest boar hunter in Azeroth!

Their cunning intellect, rapid speed, ferocious strength, and resilient hide... yes, boars are the quarry of only the most masterful of hunters. Amateurs need not apply!

Why, I bet you've never even hunted such an exotic beast. I'll bet silver any day that you can't match my record of ten boars killed. Try the ones on the eastern shore of the loch... but don't hurt yourself now, rookie!

passages.title: The Joy of Boar Hunting
passages.text:
You've killed ten already? H...hah! While you were out, I've broken my previous record! To ten... hundred! Yes, ten hundred boars!

A bet is a bet, I suppose... here's your consolation prize, <name>!

passages.title: Extinguishing the Idol
passages.text:
Near the entrance is an idol that functions as a macabre oven for the Quilboar; they...they literally consume their abductees from the Barrens. I can shut down the idol and render it useless, but I need your aid in doing so. My plan: escort me to the idol. Once we arrive, I'll commence the ritual. I'll barely be able to communicate with you, let alone defend myself. Protect me while I shut down the idol.

Are you with me, <race>? Can I count on you to help me end their atrocities?

passages.title: Extinguishing the Idol
passages.text:
Belnistrasz's sudden departure has left behind a burning brazier.  As you stare in to the flame, the image of a great-winged red dragon fills your mind.  A more graveled version of Belnistrasz's voice speaks directly to you.

"Indeed mortals, you are the heroes I had hoped you would be.  Thanks to you the butchery these beasts were perpetrating is a thing of the past.  My faith in your kind has been once more renewed.  Take this as a reward befitting of a hero."

passages.title: Partners in Crime
passages.text:
Although Amnennar is the primary threat here, he is far from the only. You need to slay his lieutenants as well if their hold on the Downs is to be released.

Glutton guards the beginning of the Spiral of Thorns.

Mordesh stands atop The Bone Pile inciting the Scourge into a ravenous frenzy.

Tuten'kash resides underground. In order to bring him out, you must strike the gong in The Caller's Chamber three times.

Good luck, brave hero.

passages.title: Partners in Crime
passages.text: Well done! Without their leaders, the Scourge will pose no significant threat.

passages.title: Thistle While You Work
passages.text:
It's stabthistle season! Stabthistle seeds are responsible for up to 89% of seed-related injuries among hunters.

You'll find Stabthistle seeds mostly in the lower woodland just north of the lodge. They're commonly found at the base of trees, and they will stab and hurt you.

I'd advise you to avoid them, but I actually need someone to help remove them for the sake of safety! Bring me back Stabthistle seeds so we can make sure others don't get hurt.

passages.title: Thistle While You Work
passages.text: Handle them safely, now!

passages.title: Thistle While You Work
passages.text:
I've been informed there's a bear warning active for the woodlands as well! They love those stabthistle seeds.

It's a good thing you gathered those so they don't attract more bears!

passages.title: Defcon: Bobcat
passages.text:
Stop everything! It's come to my attention that there's been bobcat sightings near the lodge. Bobcats!

Now mind you, I've never seen a bobcat, but they're surely dangerous. They're like mountain lions or something. I don't want anyone leaving until the area is secure!

Anyone but you, that is. I'll pay you to help secure the area, <class>. But don't get your face ripped off.

passages.title: Defcon: Bobcat
passages.text:
Okay, yes, I have already been informed that bobcats are much smaller than I was assuming. But that's still pretty dangerous for gnomes!

You've done a good thing for the safety of this lodge, <name>!

passages.title: Hornet Hunting
passages.text:
We're always looking for new game around here. Daryl may like his boars, but the rest of us prefer things more exotic.

Now, I'd never say the Loch draining was a good thing, but it did have a silver lining. The swampy ground's brought in new prey: Hornets!

Giant hornets, mind you. Not many hunters have tussled with massive bugs before. It's rather novel.

If you'd like to give it a try, I'll wager with you. Bring me back some of those nice glossy wings of theirs and I'll pay up.

passages.title: Hornet Hunting
passages.text: How go those wasps?

passages.title: Hornet Hunting
passages.text: Lovely specimens you've got there! Here's my wager, lad.

passages.title: Cure the Scourge
passages.text:
Far more effective than killing swarm after swarm of Scourge is finding a method to prevent living creatures from ever being turned into them. I have an idea for a fine powder that, when inhaled, may stop the entire process.

I need withered tusks off the unliving Quilboar here to make this powder. Bring me an ample amount, and we may be able to stop the Scourge's growth for good.

passages.title: Cure the Scourge
passages.text: Do you have the tusks?

passages.title: Cure the Scourge
passages.text: I have faith that this substance will prevent many future headaches. Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Foxtails By The Handful
passages.text:
We've seen more foxes in the hills lately. Cunning creatures, they are. A good test of a hunter's skills, and a fine profit to boot!

It's their tails, <lad/lass>. Fine and fluffy, they're just as good hung on yer belt to ward off fleas as they are to line the gloves of some fancy noble.

Listen to me prattle on. I'm no goblin; the thrill's in the hunt! But if you bring me back some foxtails, I'll still gladly pay you for 'em. You'll find the foxes just north of the lodge in the lower woodlands.

passages.title: Foxtails By The Handful
passages.text: What've you got for me?

passages.title: Foxtails By The Handful
passages.text: Ahh, you see? Goods of the finest quality. Good work gettin' these.

passages.title: Wing Nut
passages.text:
I'm through with gyrocopters. Sure, they work, but when has that ever been good enough for a real gnome? I want real flight, with WINGS!

I've been studying birds for years now, trying to unlock the final secret to building a machine that flies just like them. That elegant soaring and swooping, the rush of wind over the wings, ahh.

You! You can help me. I need the finest flight feathers you can find. The golden eagles circling near the lodge would be a fine choice...

passages.title: Wing Nut
passages.text: Only the finest feathers will do!

passages.title: Wing Nut
passages.text:
Beautiful. you've got an eye for quality!

Great minds think alike! It's clear you've got an enthusiasm for flight and fowl, so maybe you can help me further...

passages.title: Bird is the Word
passages.text:
I've actually nearly perfected my dream machine: The Skystrider! The world's first flying Mechanostrider! But, well

When I was putting the finishing touches on it in my secret cavern lab, my other creations became, er, jealous. Giving mechanical birds a personality to begin with was probably a bad idea, but that's already done.

I need the Supermechanical Robo-Widget from the original Skystrider if I want to rebuild it! Please, journey into the cave and retrieve it for me!

passages.title: Bird is the Word
passages.text: <The Skystrider sits silent, its chance to fly gone. An obvious hatch on the front is marked "SRW".>

passages.title: He's That Age
passages.text:
I'm not making the Skystrider for me, <name>. Not even for gnomekind. I want my son to be the one to fly it.

I'm old, and my reflexes aren't what they used to be. But my boy Ando could be the best pilot Azeroth's ever seen, if he'd just get over his teenage moodiness!

He sits out by the loch, staring at the sky all day. Something's been bothering him, and yet he refuses to talk to his own father about it. I'm at a loss!

Please, <name>, could you go talk to him? Tell him I need him to pilot the Skystrider!

passages.title: He's That Age
passages.text: I don't care about my father and his silly inventions! It's all just nonsense!

passages.title: Vyrin's Revenge
passages.text:
I don't suppose you'd be interested in a little payback for His Boldness? Daryl does have some skill, it pains me to say.

A year ago, a large bear had been the target of the Farstrider Lodge, but none of the hunters had any luck with him. So, Daryl thought he'd try his hand against him. All he had to show for his effort was that ugly scar over his eye.

Kill the bear, and I'm sure even Daryl would be speechless for once.

The bear, Ol' Sooty, can be found around his lair in the cave to the north.

passages.title: Vyrin's Revenge
passages.text:
Ah, <name>! Back so soon? No doubt you've been at the hunt again? Don't worry if you've had some setbacks, in the long run it will make you better!

...You couldn't get much worse, anyway...

passages.title: Vyrin's Revenge
passages.text:
Er... what's this? A bear's head, by the looks of it.

<He runs a finger along his scar unconsciously.>

Well, that's quite an interesting kill you have yourself there. Couldn't be that bear from back then...

<He trails off then starts to visibly shake.>

Oh, take that away take it away! Get that grisly thing out of here!

passages.title: Missing Parts
passages.text:
<The Sergeant turns his attention to you.>

Look here, if you want to help speed things up around here, get Flintlocke off my back. A whole shipment of siege engine parts was misplaced and now it's scattered all up and down the dock.

Gather up the missing parts and get them to Flintlocke so he can finish construction. He's just across the road from me, waiting.

passages.title: Missing Parts
passages.text:
Eh wot?

My parts. Where are they? You can't build a tank without parts!

If yeh did, it'd be small. An' mostly inner-fectual.

passages.title: Missing Parts
passages.text:
<Flintlocke greedily digs through the machine parts, tossing choice picks over his shoulder.>

Oh aye, 'ere's the stuff.

<He sticks his head all the way into one of the crates.>

But where's me powder? Everything's here but for the powder. I need explosives, man!

You tell the King, no powder, no power. I need me some kersplosions or I ain't leavin' port.

passages.title: Decryption Made Easy
passages.text:
We don't have the tools to decipher these encrypted plans. The Twilight's Hammer do, though.

Would you be a sweetie and take the plans back up there to run them through their one-time decryption engines?

passages.title: Decryption Made Easy
passages.text:
We don't have the tools to decipher these encrypted plans. The Twilight's Hammer do, though.

Would you take the plans back up there and run them through their one-time decryption engines?

passages.title: Fear of Boring
passages.text:
The gyreworms infest the rock, eating away at it until our home will one day collapse. For every one that is killed, twice as many burst forth to follow, but we must carry on the fight. They must be extinguished.

Go to the Crumbling Depths and slaughter any worms that you can find.

passages.title: Fear of Boring
passages.text: Your flesh is well suited for the task. It does not corrode from their attacks as our rockskin does.

passages.title: Fear of Boring
passages.text: You wage a war that we cannot. Thank you for your help.

passages.title: Soft Rock
passages.text: The corruption of the Crimson Expanse has not subsided. Destroy the Fungal Behemoths that shower their filth upon our realm. If they continue to rise, we will continue to destroy them.

passages.title: Soft Rock
passages.text: Once the growth starts, it is near impossible to stomp back into submission. Through persistence our realm will one day be cleansed.

passages.title: Lingering Twilight
passages.text:
Twilight drake riders remain in Deepholm. They are scattered. Defeated. Yet they remain.

Take wing with Aeosera's flight and hunt them down. The stone drakes await you on the ledge to the southeast.

We will destroy every last one of the Twilight. In the Stonemother's name.

passages.title: Desperate Acts
passages.text:
The Cult of the Damned maintains a small camp to the east, Malicia Outpost, which they use for field training outside of the Scholomance. We may have allowed them to proceed unchecked with this training for too long.

If cultists are truly using this plague to inoculate the wildlife, then Malicia Outpost must be where the inoculation is occurring.

Instructor Malicia runs the outpost. Find her, slay her, and find out who she's taking orders from.

passages.title: Desperate Acts
passages.text: You take a look at the paperwork Malicia was carrying...

passages.title: Desperate Acts
passages.text: The orders in Malicia's possession incriminate Darkmaster Gandling of the Scholomance, but they also conceal another important bit of information.

passages.title: The Twilight Overlook
passages.text:
The dragon they're speaking of is Abyssion, <name>. It's not going to be easy to get the fragment off of him.

Meet with Mylra again. She is operating nearby at the Twilight Overlook.

She will tell you what our next move will be.

passages.title: The Twilight Overlook
passages.text: So we're going to have to take on Abyssion to get the fragment?  This operation just got a whole lot more difficult all of a sudden.

passages.title: Looming Threat
passages.text: The Quilboar in Razorfen Downs seem to have allied with the Scourge. This is dark news for us, <class>. We have dire enough problems dealing with these Grimtotem, we won't be able to handle an attack by the Scourge. Venture into Razorfen Downs, east of here, and see if you can find anyone that may be able to help you stop them before they decide to attack here.

passages.title: Looming Threat
passages.text: You seem an able warrior. Perhaps you can help me put an end to the terrible evil here.

passages.title: Looming Threat
passages.text: The Scourge are a direct affront to nature. They have managed to corrupt the Quilboar in Razorfen Downs and now threaten to spread further into Thousand Needles and eventually, I fear, west into Feralas. You must go there and do anything you can to confine them. Perhaps you can find someone in the area to help you? The winds whisper of a powerful presence in the area.

passages.title: Looming Threat
passages.text: You seem an able warrior. Perhaps you can help me put an end to the terrible evil here.

passages.title: Wrath of the Sandfury
passages.text:
De Sandfury are a resilient tribe. Dey have survived sandstorms an' years an' years of other tings long covered by da sands. It would be foolish to assume that the only forces here are da trolls. We been tamin' da scarabs, breedin' da sul'lithuz, an' raisin' our dead to keep on fightin' for all eternity as zombies.

Ruuzlu, da right hand of Chief Ukorz Sandscalp, be plannin' to use dem to retake Tanaris for de Sandfury empire. You best be killin' da trolls in charge of dis if you want to live, mon.

passages.title: Wrath of the Sandfury
passages.text: If dey ain't dead yet, you can't guarantee your own life, <race>.

passages.title: Wrath of the Sandfury
passages.text:
You killed dem? All of dem? And you return alive?

Take what you want off my body, den. It's mostly curse-free, Mazoga promises.

passages.title: Give 'em Hell!
passages.text:
It's the goblins' fault, <race>!

<hic!>

You see, we set off for Silverpine from Bilgewater Harbor, over in Azshara. Huge mistake that was! Never has such a den of inequity and sin existed in our great empire. Those damnable goblins fueled our every vice and set us off to sail with barrels full of ale. 

<hic!>

The shame of it all leaves a mark greater than any scar. Honor must be restored! Kill the Bloodfang worgen that ambushed us. They're scavenging the wreckage to the southwest.

passages.title: Give 'em Hell!
passages.text: Give 'em hell, <race>!

passages.title: Give 'em Hell!
passages.text:
Looks as if you really gave those worgen a beating and, in the process, lifted the "shame haze" they cast over us. Perhaps the sea dogs will quit drinkin' now.

Who am I kidding?

Hah!

passages.title: Fight the Hammer
passages.text:
You've done what I thought was impossible! I'm done moping around here. It's time to gnome up.

I've got to find my father. But you! Don't bother yourself with me any longer. You've got to keep fighting these cultists.

Go talk to Ashlan Stonesmirk to the east. He's trying to stop the Twilight's Hammer, but he has nobody to help him. You're his only hope!

Don't give up, <name>. I won't.

passages.title: Fight the Hammer
passages.text:
You hit the twilight camp at the center of the lake? Not bad, lad!

If you're ready to take the fight right to their doorstep, I've got your chance.

passages.title: Servants of Cho'gall
passages.text:
The Twilight's Hammer started as a clan of the savage Horde. Their leader, Cho'gall, slowly turned his band of ogres into a death cult, welcoming anyone insane enough to wish for the end of all existence. As you can see, there's still plenty of ogres among their ranks; deranged, fanatical, and just as strong as before.

These crude monsters have the gall to come here and spread their filth across our land. The more you kill, the better off Loch Modan will be, <name>.

passages.title: Servants of Cho'gall
passages.text: It may look grim, but we'll win with your help, <name>. They won't keep the dwarves down.

passages.title: Gor'kresh
passages.text:
The ogre left to watch over these crude fools goes by the name of Gor'kresh. He's big enough to boss even these brutes around, and cunning to boot. Never assume an ogre's stupid, that's when they'll get you.

If you take him out, we'll show the Twilight's Hammer that Loch Modan isn't a stepping stone for them. Stand strong against Gor'kresh and drive these fools back into the highlands!

passages.title: Gor'kresh
passages.text: You can do it, <name>.

passages.title: Gor'kresh
passages.text:
You've done it! We may not have stopped the cult dead, but we've shown them we're not easy pickings and given them a welt to prove it.

Take this with my gratitude, and try not to blush if anyone in Thelsamar calls you "hero"!

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Trusting the Traitor
passages.text:
These two are useless. Can I at least count on you to get some work done around here, young adventurer? We've come into contact with Mazoga, a traitor to the Sandfury. He says he can help us find the legendary blade Sul'thraze so we can use it to kick out the Sandfury forever!

We'll probably sell it afterward to the highest bidder, honestly. This place doesn't pay for itself. Go do what he wants...just keep an eye on him. A traitor's a traitor all the same. He's at our camp just east of Zul'Farrak.

passages.title: Supporting the Troops
passages.text:
While it is true that these farmers threaten to overrun us, we still cannot forget about the Alliance's main forces.

Travel west into Andorhal and slay the human soldiers that are fighting with our deathguards. We need all the help we can get.

passages.title: Supporting the Troops
passages.text: You fight well, <name>.  I wish I had your ability... and your bravery.

passages.title: Ashes to Ashes
passages.text:
To the west, deep within Alliance-held Andorhal, you will find their commanders. They do not fight, but call out orders from horseback.

Hunt down and slay these commanders, <name>. The humans won't stand a chance.

passages.title: Ashes to Ashes
passages.text:
Well done.  With them out of the way, I have no more excuses.

Soon, I must battle Thassarian, for honor and for Andorhal.

passages.title: It's Only Poisonous if You Ingest It
passages.text:
Take this cage, <class>. I've placed inside it one of my own mutant bush chickens, with a few slight modifications. Within the butt of this bush chicken is a stick of dynamite laced with gunk from the diseased organs you brought me.

Take the cage out into the surrounding forest and locate the wandering forest ettin. Release the chicken and sit back as my masterwork does its job. The ensuing explosion should be sufficient to kill the ettin or greatly weaken it, allowing you to finish it off.

passages.title: It's Only Poisonous if You Ingest It
passages.text: Have you dealt with the ettin?

passages.title: It's Only Poisonous if You Ingest It
passages.text:
<Apothecary Wormcrud laughs maniacally.>

Was there ever any doubt? An ettin is no match for science!

passages.title: Deeper into Darkness
passages.text:
The Skitterweb matriarch is nearby! You can put an end to the Skitterweb menace by killing her!

Find the brood mother at the end of the cave in the Skittering Dark and destroy her!

passages.title: Deeper into Darkness
passages.text: You killed the Skitterweb matriarch?

passages.title: Deeper into Darkness
passages.text: You rescued our orcs and killed the Skitterweb matriarch? We owe you a great debt of gratitude. You've saved us all from certain execution, <name>. I'm sure we can rouse these drunken idiots now.

passages.title: Skitterweb Menace
passages.text:
Vengeance is all consuming, <name>! Our third ship sank off the coast of the Skittering Dark, northwest of here. The men that made it off that boat were either captured or killed by the Skitterweb spiders of the region. For that, the spiders must die! ALL OF THEM!

Travel to the Skittering Dark and crush those insects!

Be on the lookout for their matriarch. Perhaps if we find her we can end this menace forever!

passages.title: Skitterweb Menace
passages.text: The root of this evil must be found and destroyed! The Skitterweb matriarch must be nearby. No doubt hiding in the nearby cave!

passages.title: Rise, Forsaken
passages.text:
Fenris Isle stands defiantly at the heart of Lordamere Lake - a cruel memory of a time long since passed.

Though no longer infested by gnoll vermin, a new threat has emerged. Human refugees, driven from their holdings in Hillsbrad, have fled to Fenris Isle in hopes of escaping defeat at our hands. A critical error on their part.

You are to take Agatha with you to Fenris Isle and slaughter all humans. She will raise the fallen as Forsaken, bolstering our forces in the process.

Do not fail me, <name>.

passages.title: Rise, Forsaken
passages.text: Victory!

passages.title: Rise, Forsaken
passages.text: I see everything, <name>. Through Agatha all is known to me.

passages.title: No Escape
passages.text:
You must strike at their leaders, <name>. You will find them holed up in the old keep. Battle your way inside and find the holdouts! Turn them for your queen!

None shall escape the mighty grasp of the Forsaken!

passages.title: No Escape
passages.text:
It would seem that Crowley is more formidable than I anticipated. Still, he is a man - flesh and bone - full of secrets. Secrets that I know all about...

You have served me well, <name>. I could use someone of your ability at the Sepulcher. I have a plan to deal with Crowley and his insurgents once and for all. Will you help?

passages.title: Maziel's Revelation
passages.text:
The notes continue Maziel's rambling research into the properties of quicksilver and mercurial oozes.

He appears to have made a major discovery. He mentions hiding his journal in the Lower Silvermarsh to the southwest.

passages.title: Maziel's Revelation
passages.text: Maziel's journal appears to be undamaged by the mercury.

passages.title: Maziel's Ascendancy
passages.text:
Maziel's journal chronicles a ritual of ascendancy that would transfigure his body to one of pure quicksilver.

The ritual would take place in the cave near the Lower Silvermarsh, where Maziel would feed upon the mercurial oozes until achieving full strength.

Perhaps it is not too late to put an end to his madness.

passages.title: Maziel's Ascendancy
passages.text: You've disposed of an enemy before he could grow more powerful.  By eliminating Maziel you've also ensured that his powers will not be used against the Earthen Ring.

passages.title: Shards of the Felvine
passages.text:
The satyr Alzzin the Wildshaper has exerted his corrupt dominion over this part of Eldre'Thalas. The Fruit of Fertility, now corrupted as the Felvine, should be close to Alzzin. It may be the key to purify this ancient place.

When the great satyr falls, capture whatever essence of the Felvine you can. Seal it in this Reliquary of Purity, and bring it to me.

Good luck, and Cenarius' speed.

passages.title: Shards of the Felvine
passages.text: With the Sealed Reliquary of Purity in our possession, it will be possible not only to remove a corrupting threat from the world but also to study it under our judicious watch.  Perhaps we can even devise new means to combat the taint of corruption that ever threatens Azeroth.

passages.title: Shards of the Felvine
passages.text:
You have done well, <class>, and for that I am forever in your debt.  Though the war is far from over, a great battle has been won against those who would bring about our doom.

Please - accept this gold as a token of my enduring gratitude.  If we ever cleanse Dire Maul, know that you will be welcomed here as a hero. Thank you.

passages.title: An Unwelcome Guest
passages.text: You will find that Dire Maul is filled with many nature and arcane elementals. Somehow, a water elemental has found its way into this area. Please gather its essence and take it to me. I am curious as to how one of their kind got here, and what sort of agenda it may have against the natural elements of Eldre'Thalas.

passages.title: An Unwelcome Guest
passages.text: Do you carry the essence, or did the task prove too difficult?

passages.title: An Unwelcome Guest
passages.text: It is very troublesome that a water elemental was here, let alone one that powerful. Take this as my thanks for your efforts. I must examine this essence for any knowledge it may contain.

passages.title: A Villain Unmasked
passages.text:
<You find a complete list of all the Twilight's Hammer cultists in Stormwind.>

<More importantly, you discover a letter from Major Samuelson to his compatriots outlining this entire scheme. The Prince was right: Samuelson is the real villain here, using his connections as commander of the city guard to disguise cult activity.>

<It's time to return to Stormwind Keep and bring Samuelson to justice!>

passages.title: A Villain Unmasked
passages.text: You have evidence incriminating Samuelson? Let's see what he has to say for himself!

passages.title: A Villain Unmasked
passages.text:
Samuelson - corrupted by the Twilight's Hammer? This must have been going on for years. Right here in my very keep!

I am grateful that you and my son were able to get to the bottom of this before my city was brought to harm. I've underestimated how much Anduin has grown - his command of the holy light just saved my life, if not the entire kingdom.

As for you - words alone can't do justice to your heroism this day. Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Pusillin The Thief
passages.text:
Me take quick nap earlier and stupid fast imp take book! Dagg'thol need book to follow orders and Master need book to conquer! Gah!

You <race> help me get book from imp, and I give you shiny something. Go, imp right there to da left! KILL!!!

passages.title: Pusillin The Thief
passages.text: <race> has book?

passages.title: Pusillin The Thief
passages.text: Now you watch Master use book to kill stupid trees and stupid goat men! YAR!

passages.title: Lethtendris's Web
passages.text: Blood Elf Lethtendris has web to catch magic here. She use for herself, but Master want to use for good of whole world! You help get web from stupid elf and not only will Dagg'thol reward you, you see how Master use it way better!

passages.title: Lethtendris's Web
passages.text: <name>, you have stupid elf's web?

passages.title: Lethtendris's Web
passages.text:
This web have lots of magic! Master will be very happy now!

And you make Dagg'thol happy, <race>. Take this so you believe how happy you make Dagg'thol!

passages.title: The Warped Defender
passages.text:
The Ironbark and Warpwood were once the mighty protectors of Eldre'Thalas. Look at how they have fallen! Ultimately, their fate lies at the hands of myself and my fellow Highborne. We were reckless with our power, <race>.

But you, you can right the wrongs here! Venture forth and put Tendris Warpwood to rest. He was the mightiest and last defender of this area, and deserves spiritual release. Be wary, for if you do not dispose of the Ironbark Protectors prior to engaging Tendris, he will call them to assist.

passages.title: The Warped Defender
passages.text: Your work here was noble. Fret not, for Tendris' soul was crying to be put to rest. He is thankful.

passages.title: The Cursed Remains
passages.text:
There are remaining beings here that pose a direct threat to us ever reclaiming this sacred city. Magister Kalendris and Illyana Ravenoak are both extremely dangerous and need to be disposed of as quickly as possible.

Exercise caution, for with there being so few remaining feeding off of Immol'thar's energies, they are likely to be stronger than they first appear.

passages.title: The Cursed Remains
passages.text: Your dedication will make this all that much easier.

passages.title: The Shen'dralar Ancient
passages.text: Some beings here have miraculously managed to remain free of the darkness that runs so rampant. On the second story of the Court of the Highborne rests a Shen'dralar Ancient. Seek it out, it may hold a wealth of wisdom, perhaps even the secret to freeing Eldre'Thalas.

passages.title: The Shen'dralar Ancient
passages.text: Our meeting is no coincidence, <name>.

passages.title: Ando's Call
passages.text:
You've done great work here, <name>. While you were out, that young Ando fellow was here looking for you. Said something about a metal bird.

You might want to go back to the shores of the Loch and see what he wanted.

passages.title: Ando's Call
passages.text: It's working! My father brought it!

passages.title: Brute Strength
passages.text:
Gandling has brought his lieutenant, the Ravenian, with him. This lumbering brute is far more dangerous than any of the other Scourge you will find upon the battlefield... even the abominations.

You will find the Ravenian within a tower near the southern end of town. I recommend caution before fighting him, <name>. He will not be a pushover.

passages.title: Brute Strength
passages.text: Excellently done, <name>.

passages.title: The Gordok Ogre Suit
passages.text:
If you're going to fight the king of the Gordok then you're going to need to get by Captain Kromcrush. Now, you can get by him by killing him, sure. You might actually want to leave him alive.

How, you ask? I think I know! An ogre suit!

I'll make you one if you bring me an Ogre Tannin from upstairs. I'm not going anywhere like this...

passages.title: The Gordok Ogre Suit
passages.text: Just get me that Ogre Tannin, and I'll whip you up an ogre suit that will fool Captain Kromcrush into thinking you're one of his men.

passages.title: The Gordok Ogre Suit
passages.text:
Yeah, this will do the trick.  Just a slip here, and tuck here... heh - this is going to work out just fine!  <A broad smile beams from the chained goblin's face.>

Here you go, you're all set.  Remember- this isn't the most securely fashioned item in the world.  You'll have ten minutes of use before it falls apart, and then you're not going to fool anybody!  Try using it just before you approach him to make sure it lasts as long as you're going to need it.

passages.title: Rush Delivery
passages.text:
Peak Grindstone's team broke down somewhere out there to the west.

Think you can make yourself useful for a change and rush some parts out to them, <race>?

passages.title: Rush Delivery
passages.text: Are those spare parts you have there?

passages.title: Rush Delivery
passages.text: I can't thank you enough, <class>. Now, let's see if we can get this catapult moving again.

passages.title: Saving Warpwood
passages.text:
Just inside the eastern wing of Dire Maul one of the warpwood ancients, Furgus Warpwood, still lives uncorrupted. You must travel there and help him drive out the terrible creatures that have taken it as their own. Taking Dire Maul would be a major step in reclaiming Feralas for our people.

You can find Dire Maul to the southeast of here.

passages.title: Saving Warpwood
passages.text: Have you been in contact with a druid of the talon recently, <class>? I can feel the lingering presence of one.

passages.title: Saving Warpwood
passages.text: Just inside the eastern wing of Dire Maul one of the warpwood ancients, Furgus Warpwood, still lives uncorrupted. You must travel there and help him drive out the terrible creatures that have taken it as their own before they set their sights on Camp Mojache. Perhaps we can even enlist his aid afterward to ensure we maintain our presence in Feralas with enemies on so many sides.

passages.title: Saving Warpwood
passages.text: Your face shows signs of desperate conflict. I honor your presence, brave <class>.

passages.title: The Highborne
passages.text:
Estulan, a powerful and uncorrupt Highborne, has managed to enter the western wing of Dire Maul and has asked for assistance in cleansing it. Regardless of your personal convictions of the Highborne, it is an effort I must support for the good of Feralas. May the wind carry your spirit there with great swiftness.

You will find Dire Maul to the southeast.

passages.title: The Highborne
passages.text: I sensed your coming all the way from Dreamer's Rest. Your assistance would be most welcome.

passages.title: The Highborne
passages.text:
Estulan, a powerful and uncorrupt Highborne, has managed to enter the western wing of Dire Maul and has asked for assistance in cleansing it. Regardless of your personal convictions of his kind, it is an effort I must support for our own good. Please hurry, we need every foothold in Feralas that we can get.

You will find Dire Maul to the west.

passages.title: The Highborne
passages.text: I sensed your coming all the way from Camp Mojache. Your assistance would be most welcome.

passages.title: Eyes in the Sky
passages.text:
The most dire, and most organized, threat to us in Feralas are the Gordok ogres in the northern wing of Dire Maul. I requested a druid of the talon to go there and scout it out. If he still lives, speak with him and he will act as your commander to stop the Gordok before they decide to attack.

That's an order, <class>.

passages.title: Eyes in the Sky
passages.text: Speak softly, <name>. The Gordok may not be intelligent, but they are still dangerous warriors.

passages.title: Ogre in the Field
passages.text:
The most dire, and most organized, threat to us in Feralas are the Gordok ogres in the northern wing of Dire Maul. If we eradicate them and take Dire Maul for the Horde, we will possess a heavily fortified seat of power in this region with numerous artifacts to sweeten the deal. I sent in a small army of Stonemaul Ogres inside earlier - if any have survived, speak with them and finish the job.

That's an order, <class>.

passages.title: Ogre in the Field
passages.text: These ogres no pushovers. I need you help me finish Orhan's task, <race>.

passages.title: Alexi's Gambit
passages.text:
I require your assistance, <class>. Find the undead mage Vectus and the warrior Marduk deep within here. They run the scourge's plagued dragon operation and must be destroyed.

Place this Gambit in the viewing room where they are located. Hopefully, it will react with their forces and utterly destroy them!

Oh, defeating Vectus and Marduk afterward shouldn't be a problem. Right?

passages.title: Alexi's Gambit
passages.text:
You did it!  They are defeated!  And the Gambit... did it work?

Very interesting. You've done well, <name>.

passages.title: Exploding Through
passages.text:
What a find!

Right here... exactly where my notes predicted it would be.

With any luck, inside this chamber will lie clues to the location of the legendary Coffer of the Promise.

That's right, <name>. It's not just a myth. I believe it truly exists.

I'll explain more later. For now, just give me a hand with these explosives.

passages.title: Exploding Through
passages.text:
Shake it off, kid.

Happens to me all the time...

passages.title: The Lich, Ras Frostwhisper
passages.text:
One of Kel'Thuzad's most trusted students oversees the operations in Scholomance. You must confront the lich, Ras Frostwhisper, in his lair. The door to his chamber is adjacent to the viewing room.

Destroy him, <name>. Leave no trace of his existence so that he may never again bring such horrors into our world.

passages.title: The Lich, Ras Frostwhisper
passages.text: Ten thousand souls cry out in unison, <name>! You have struck a mortal blow to the Scourge and their masters.

passages.title: Plagued Hatchlings...For Now
passages.text:
One of the 'projects' underway here is the plagued dragonflight. Thankfully, they're only hatchlings right now, but if we wait much longer they will become one of the scourge's most powerful weapons and a major threat to all of Azeroth, especially my family's land!

Slay ten of their whelps and be sure to take care of Rattlegore as well. He is in the small space beneath where the whelps are housed and prepares supplements to catalyze their growth. Hurry...before they get any bigger!

passages.title: Plagued Hatchlings...For Now
passages.text:
Well done, <name>!  It'll be a long time before they can grow another clutch of dragons.

...At least, I hope it will!

passages.title: Kirtonos the Herald
passages.text:
With blood, Kirtonos may be summoned. It is with blood, then, that Kirtonos must be destroyed.

Within the Chamber of Summoning, you will find a brazier, upon which you shall place a drop of your own blood. Kirtonos will come - he cannot resist. When he appears, unleash the fury and wrath of a thousand innocent deaths upon him.

Should you succeed, you will earn more than just our gratitude.

passages.title: Kirtonos the Herald
passages.text: With the death of Kirtonos, a chapter in the horrible tale of Scholomance comes to a close. You have my deepest, everlasting gratitude for your bravery.

passages.title: School of the Damned
passages.text:
Greetings! As you can see, the Western Plaguelands is very nearly free of the last remnants of the scourge. However, their school of necromancy, Scholomance, still sits full of lost young souls training to become scourge sorcerers! Our work here will be for naught if we do not stop this flow of fresh, not to mention very powerful, necromancers.

Travel southeast to Scholomance and find Weldon Barov. He is the last living member of the Barov line that once owned all these lands and is our current contact.

passages.title: Taelan Fordring's Legacy
passages.text:
Greetings. How do you do? My name is Daria.

I am one of the priests in charge of preserving the peace here in Hearthglen. One of my duties involves maintaining the tower down the trail to the southeast of Hearthglen. This particular tower is of personal importance to the Highlord. It's the place where his son was killed.

With the recent incursion of gnolls, however, maintenance of the tower has grown difficult. Will you help me rid the trail of some of these gnoll vandals, so I can do my duty?

passages.title: Taelan Fordring's Legacy
passages.text: I must admit, <name>... I have been using my mind vision spell to keep tabs on you.  And I must say... the number of gnolls you found on the trail is truly staggering!

passages.title: It's About Time!
passages.text:
Finally! You're here! Get to work!

My men have been sparring with these wooden practice dummies for far too long. Sure, you can learn how to swing a sword by practicing with a dummy, but real combat requires a real combatant.

Hmmm... I had asked for them to send me someone imposing, but I suppose a skinny-armed <race> <class> will have to do.

Now get in there and teach my men how to fight!

passages.title: It's About Time!
passages.text: I'm not paying you to talk to me.  I'm paying you to talk with my soldiers... and then fight with them.

passages.title: It's About Time!
passages.text:
I'm just looking over my paperwork here, and it says that we were expecting a FEMALE <race> <class>.  You're not, umm...

Never mind.  It would appear that you are not the person that I originally hired, but you did a good job.  So I'm going to pay you anyhow.

passages.title: Drudges... <Sigh>
passages.text:
Say, I never caught your name. <name>? Pleased to meet you, <name>.

I've got one more problem that needs fixing, and you have a look about you that just screams "I'm a problem-fixer".

There's a small mine on the northern edge of Hearthglen, where we get most of the ore that the town needs. My drudges who work the mine normally do a decent job.

Unfortunately, it seems that a larger-than-average spider has taken up residence within this cave. Think you can clear things up for me?

passages.title: Drudges... <Sigh>
passages.text: Nice work!  In retrospect, I'm glad that other <race> <class> never showed up... you've proven to be all the help I need.

passages.title: The Battle for Andorhal
passages.text:
Hurry, <name>... there isn't time to waste.

The city of Andorhal is in the middle of a three-way war between the Forsaken, the Alliance, and the Scourge. King Wrynn has rolled the dice and sent a death knight to lead the charge for his cause, but I'm sure he can use all the help he can get. With Arthas dead, now is the time for the Alliance to start to retake Lordaeron.

Speak with the gryphon master, Bibilfaz Featherwhistle, when you are ready, and he will put you on the first flight out there.

passages.title: The Battle for Andorhal
passages.text: It's about time you arrived, <class>.

passages.title: Scourge First... Horde Later
passages.text:
Darkmaster Gandling of the Cult of the Damned leads the Scourge offensive here in Andorhal. My old counterpart, Koltira, leads the Forsaken forces. If we're to win Andorhal, we'll have to defeat both, but we will certainly fail if we take on both at once.

I know Koltira well enough to know that he will focus on the Scourge first. We will do the same.
