Take out the weaker, desiccated Scourge to reduce their numbers. The Forsaken will have to wait to taste our wrath.

passages.title: Scourge First... Horde Later
passages.text:
You may not act quickly, but at least you do not fail me.

Very well.  I will have a more important task for you, <name>, when the time is right.

passages.title: War Machines
passages.text:
Dried-up Scourge... weak. Abominations... strong.

We defeat strong abominations... we win war.

passages.title: War Machines
passages.text:
Abominations... strong.

<name>... stronger.

passages.title: Scholomancer
passages.text:
The Scholomance is one of the few Scourge holdouts remaining west of the Thondroril. The headmaster of Scholomance, a cultist by the name of Darkmaster Gandling, has made an appearance on the battlefield.

This will be his final mistake.

You will find Gandling in a square near the southern end of town. I want you to fight and weaken Gandling. I will join you to help finish him off.

passages.title: Scholomancer
passages.text: Excellently done, <name>.  And now, with the leader of the Scourge forces eliminated from Andorhal, we bide our time.

passages.title: Brute Strength
passages.text:
Gandling has brought his lieutenant, Rattlegore, with him. This clattering horror is far more dangerous than any of the other Scourge you will find upon the battlefield... even the abominations.

You will find Rattlegore within an old town-hall building, near the center of town. I recommend caution before fighting him, <name>. He will not be a pushover.

passages.title: Brute Strength
passages.text: Excellently done, <name>.

passages.title: Go Fletch!
passages.text:
We must always be prepared for battle, <name>. Whether that battle is against the Forsaken in Andorhal, against the Scourge in the east, or against some yet-unknown foe is unknown. What is known, is that we must be ready.

We are low on arrows. I can obtain the shafts and heads, but I still need feathers. The birds that circle to the northwest typically molt this time of year. Would you mind traveling out into the field and gathering some of these feathers for our camp?

passages.title: Go Fletch!
passages.text: It's good to see you back, <name>.

passages.title: Go Fletch!
passages.text:
I will have my fletchers get to work on these.

I'm glad to see you being so useful right away, <name>.  Perhaps later I will have some more exciting tasks for you.

passages.title: Uther's Blessing
passages.text:
These farmers from the south wish to take these farms, but I can't let them enter the plaguelands unprepared. Even with the Scourge gone, danger still looms in the form of the Forsaken. No, we must be ready to fight... and that includes our new visitors.

Before doing anything else, however, I would recommend that you travel to Uther's Tomb, to the east, and place this tribute before his statue to ask for his blessing. Speak with the priest that tends to the tomb when you are finished.

passages.title: Uther's Blessing
passages.text: Uther was a great hero.  It is my honor to serve him, even after he has passed.

passages.title: Uther's Blessing
passages.text: You and the humans at Chillwind Camp wish to re-take Andorhal?  I wish you luck.

passages.title: The Abandoned Crypt
passages.text:
If you truly intend to move forward in this battle for Andorhal... well, perhaps I can help.

To the east lies a large crypt. The bottom level of the crypt was once used for storage of weapons and armor... until the Scourge came. Now that the undead have left, the weapons are free for the taking.

Most of the weapons are probably rusted and rotten by now, but they will serve better than tunics and pitchforks.

passages.title: The Abandoned Crypt
passages.text:
Scattered all over the bottom level of the crypt, you find shattered crates that once held weapons and armor.

It appears that somebody got here before you did.

passages.title: Ambushed!
passages.text:
As you turn around, you see the silhouettes of shambling skeletons on the stairs.

The undead aren't gone from this crypt. They were lying in wait! Furthermore, they appear to be armed with the weapons that you came looking for.

You'll have to escape from the crypt. On your way out, you should gather as many pieces of equipment as you can.

passages.title: Ambushed!
passages.text: What happened at Uther's Tomb, <name>?

passages.title: Ambushed!
passages.text:
Attacked by ghosts?  Strange.  I suppose that crypt wasn't fully healed after all.

You just missed Thurman Grant... you remember, that oaf of a farmer that was here earlier.  He took his men with him and traveled to the nearest farm... against my orders.

passages.title: This Is Our Army
passages.text:
I told Commander Valorfist that we could hold our own, and we intend to. I had a little conversation with the death knight general, Thassarian, on my way over here. We farmers plan to help in our own way.

We will take control of this farm, begin to cultivate the land... and then when the battle for Andorhal commences, we will attack the Forsaken from the rear. They'll never expect it.

First, we need to get rid of these Forsaken outriders. Kill some, then return to me.

passages.title: This Is Our Army
passages.text: My men need your help, <name>.

passages.title: This Is Our Army
passages.text: You fight well, <race>.  My men could stand to learn a few moves from an experienced <class> like you.

passages.title: Naga Reinforcements
passages.text:
They've come slithering up from the ocean depths, <name>. The naga. I think their intent is to reinforce the Bastion of Twilight, probably by heading inland via the Verrall river. We can't let that happen!

Teach them that these shores are ours now, and send them scurrying back to the lightless depths.

Kill the Blackscale naga worming their way through the Obsidian Breakers!

passages.title: Naga Reinforcements
passages.text:
That'll send 'em packing, <name>! Cho'gall won't be able to count on the naga to back him up in this fight. From here on out, it's just us versus the Twilight's Hammer.

...And the Horde.

passages.title: Excising the Taint
passages.text: It looks like a group of the ambushers stayed behind. Make them pay for their insolence! Kill all of the Bloodfang stalkers at Olsen's Farthing. For Sylvanas! For the Horde!

passages.title: Excising the Taint
passages.text: You found the ambushers?

passages.title: Excising the Taint
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's voice invades your thoughts.>

You have avenged the fallen, <name>, but there is more to be done.

passages.title: The Hermit of Witch Hill
passages.text:
The marsh seems to have a strange effect on humans. Some grow mad simply by living here.

Anyone who has ever settled at Swamplight Manor has gone mad in a spectacular way. The latest owner, one "Swamp Eye" Jarl, is already showing signs.

I don't completely understand what's happening there, you'd have my thanks for looking into it.

The manor is at the eastern edge of the swamp. Trek east across Bluefen and past North Point Tower. The manor is in a haunted patch of land called Witch Hill.

passages.title: The Hermit of Witch Hill
passages.text:
Have you come here to spy on me? No?

Perhaps you have an appreciation for fine cuisine, then? Good, you can help!

passages.title: Jarl Needs Eyes
passages.text:
Eye juice is good juice for drinking. Too bad most critters only have two eyes.

But spiders have lots of eyes. Lots and lots. And Darkmist eye juice is tasty. Smooth and salty! Unpopped spider eyes... I taste them already.

Darkmist spiders are west of here, in the Darkmist Cavern. You figure the spiders are named after the cave... or is it the other way around?

passages.title: Jarl Needs Eyes
passages.text: Where are those eyes?

passages.title: Jarl Needs Eyes
passages.text:
You got the eyes!  You got the eyes!  Tasty, tasty spider eyes!

Some eyes... when you stare at them they stare back. Eat those last.  They keep you company... out in the swamp.

Hello, little spider eyes.  Hello!  You taste like chicken.  Gooey, salty chicken!

Mmmh.

passages.title: Cutting the Competition
passages.text:
Look, I'm not about t' play games with ye. The Scarlet Crusade's Crimson Hammersmith was nothin' worth mentionin' before, but now that they're Balnazzar's Risen, the damned dreadlord has taught him t' make all sorts of powerful demonic weaponry.

It's simple. Find their blacksmithing plans and kill the Risen Hammersmith when he comes for 'em, so that we can make sure their army doesn't get their hands on demon armaments. They're powerful enough as it is!

passages.title: Cutting the Competition
passages.text: Are we back on top of the arms race?

passages.title: Cutting the Competition
passages.text: Nicely done, lad! Without them new weapons, they're just as easy t' kill as they were when they were alive!

passages.title: Do the World a Favor
passages.text:
Hyenas, on their best day, are a nuisance.

These foul specimens have a particularly nasty disposition, are riddled with all manner of disease, and are simply a blight on the face of dogdom.

Do the world a favor and rid the deserts of Uldum of this mangy menace.

passages.title: What's Haunting Witch Hill?
passages.text:
I traveled out here to pay Jarl a visit at his new home and it's been a nonstop horror show ever since! There's something seriously wrong here and I can't be the only one who sees it...

Have you seen the ghosts and corpses shambling about Witch Hill? I've a feeling that if anyone knows what happened here, it is them. Seek out these risen husks and risen spirits in the surrounding area, grant them rest through combat, and see what you can learn from them before this evil consumes Jarl!

passages.title: What's Haunting Witch Hill?
passages.text: What have you learned from the spirits haunting this place?

passages.title: What's Haunting Witch Hill?
passages.text:
<Mordant produces a small sheet of paper and a pen, beginning to scribble down notes on your findings.>

From your findings, the spirits in this place must amount to everyone who ever lived on this land, not just the previous occupants.

Something has been corrupting and killing them. Those who follow don't learn the truth until it's too late. We have to put an end to this, <name>!

passages.title: The Witch's Bane
passages.text:
In my years as an herbalist, I've often observed that nature will provide subtle cures to the most vexing of problems. I've read that hedge mages and witch doctors often use the smoke of an herb known as witchbane to draw evil from its hiding places.

If true, this would mean witchbane should be growing near the shallow waters of Witch Hill. You should be able to identify it by its broad leaves and reddish central stalk. Bring me any of the herb you can find, <name>. It may be our only hope.

passages.title: The Witch's Bane
passages.text: Were you able to gather any of the herb? We must work quickly, before whatever evil is behind this infestation consolidates its hold on this area.

passages.title: The Witch's Bane
passages.text:
<Mordant accepts the bunch of herbs from you.>

These match the description exactly! I prepared the torch while you were out. All that remains is to fasten the herbs to the end here.

passages.title: The Great Ezra Grimm
passages.text:
Men as far as Kul Tiras spoke of the legendary Ezra Grimm's premium tobacco. It was a delicacy enjoyed by every single person of importance that visited Stratholme. King Terenas, Uther the Lightbringer, Highlord Fordring...yes, they all enjoyed Grimm's specialty.

Sadly, Ezra stayed in his shop when Stratholme was invaded, swearing on his life that the Scourge would never touch his tobacco. Venture forth and see if even one bit remains here...it is worth its weight in gold, I assure you.

passages.title: The Great Ezra Grimm
passages.text: Did you find any?

passages.title: The Great Ezra Grimm
passages.text:
Truly, you have uncovered the snuff of legends. It is nearly impossible to place a value on this historical tobacco.

Here, have a few coins.

passages.title: Seek and Destroy
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's voice invades your thoughts once more.>

Search the nearby farmhouses for Alliance stragglers. Keep an eye out for any information that could lead us to Crowley and Bloodfang. Seek and destroy all that would stand in your way, <name>!

passages.title: Seek and Destroy
passages.text: What is your status?

passages.title: Seek and Destroy
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's words float in your head.>

This book documents a recent meeting with Ivus Bloodfang. The location mentioned is the Deep Elem Mine. I know of this place. It has only one entrance.

We shall corner and crush them!

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text:
The mistress has put me in charge of this lot. Our primary mission is to get in there, corner the rats, and kill 'em all, including Bloodfang.

You've done us a solid service in gettin' the information, <name>. Join in the glory and help us drive a sword through their miserable skulls!

Let me know when you're ready and I'll call for the charge.

passages.title: Nowhere to Run
passages.text:
WHAT!?

<Sylvanas shrieks.>

CROWLEY!!!!!

Bastards. Those were some of our strongest soldiers. I have underestimated Crowley and Bloodfang for the last time. Clearly they are an enemy the likes of which we have never seen - willing to sacrifice their own to set a trap like this... unheard of in Alliance warfare.

passages.title: On to Something
passages.text:
This is remarkable work you've done! Especially for someone who hasn't taken my courses.

These tablets provide new information on several subjects.

They indicate that these obelisks are part of an enormous ancient mechanism that once kept this whole region masked from the rest of the world.

They also depict how to recharge the mechanism, which is where your Shaft of the Stars comes in...

Get ready, <name>. We have some history to make!

passages.title: On to Something
passages.text: Alright, now let's see what this staff can show us...

passages.title: On to Something
passages.text: Would you get a load of this place!

passages.title: The Battle Resumes!
passages.text:
Word is in from Andorhal, <name>. The battle has resumed.

It has become somewhat well-known among the Alliance forces that you're a hero of the first battle of Andorhal. Thassarian has requested your presence immediately.

passages.title: The Battle Resumes!
passages.text:
Word has it that you helped those farmers arm themselves.  Well, now they've initiated the attack without my order!  They've forced my hand.

The battle has resumed.  This time, we fight the Forsaken... and I fight Koltira, my old brother of the Ebon Blade.

passages.title: Supporting the Troops
passages.text:
I'm no military expert, but this battle looks to be in our favor. Our defenders are equally matched with their deathguards, but the farmers' militia has taken them by surprise from the rear. For the Alliance!

Still, we should all do what we can to make sure that we win. Travel east into Andorhal and slay the Forsaken deathguards that are fighting with our men. The sooner they die, the quicker we can re-take Andorhal!

passages.title: Supporting the Troops
passages.text: For the Alliance!

passages.title: Supporting the Troops
passages.text: You fight well, <name>.  I wish I had your ability... and your bravery.

passages.title: Ashes to Ashes
passages.text:
To the east, deep within Forsaken-held Andorhal, you will find their commanders. They do not fight, but call out orders from horseback.

Hunt down and slay these commanders, <name>. The Forsaken won't stand a chance.

passages.title: Ashes to Ashes
passages.text: You will find them to the east, <name>.  Do not fail me.

passages.title: Ashes to Ashes
passages.text:
Well done.  With them out of the way, I have no more excuses.

Soon, I must battle Koltira, for honor and for Andorhal.

passages.title: Siren's Song
passages.text:
She's still out there... Ophelia, the Siren of the Highlands! Her terrible song will lure you to the depths. I've vowed to stay behind and avenge my fallen crewmates, <class>. If you want to join me, just say the word.

We'll lash ourselves to the mast, we will. We'll shut our eyes. We'll stuff our ears with wax. And when her beautiful illusion drops... we'll strike.

Are you in?

passages.title: Siren's Song
passages.text:
She had me under her spell, <name>. I wouldn't have made it out of there alive if it weren't for you. Thank you!

Maybe the rest of the Alliance fleet can finally anchor here in peace...

passages.title: Val'kyr Incursion
passages.text:
The val'kyr were one of the Scourge's primary weapons. Not only were they skilled in battle, but they could be used to convert corpses into Scourge minions. To think that Sylvanas is stooping to such levels for the sake of the Forsaken...

We need to stop the val'kyr before they wipe us out and turn our army against us. Slay as many as you can find. And bring some of these minutemen with you. If they've survived this long, then they must have some battle skill.

passages.title: Val'kyr Incursion
passages.text:
For every val'kyr you slay, you save dozens of our men... and prevent the Forsaken forces from growing.

Still, they press on.  We may not win this battle after all.

passages.title: Brother Against Brother
passages.text:
Our militia has been nearly wiped out. Only I and these few farmers remain.

Those winged creatures... they took the bodies of our men and... and turned them into walking, undead corpses! With every one of our men they took, they bolstered their own ranks.

It pains me to admit it, but you will need to fight them too, along with the deathguards and val'kyr. As they did in life, they hunt in packs, so take some of my minutemen with you.

passages.title: Brother Against Brother
passages.text: You fought valiantly, but we're getting nowhere.  Every body that falls just fuels their forces.

passages.title: The Maelstrom
passages.text:
Thank the spirits you're here, <name>.

We're not sure how much longer we can maintain the rift in the Maelstrom.

Our most powerful members, led by Thrall, are barely preventing the tear.

Last I heard, our only hope was to go through the breach and attempt to stabilize it from the other side.

I will conjure a portal. Take it and report to Thrall as soon as you can.

passages.title: The Maelstrom
passages.text:
<Thrall's muscles strain as primal energy flows through him.  His eyes shift your way, acknowledging your arrival.>

It is good to see you, <name>.

passages.title: Aradne
passages.text:
Our last hope of victory lies in defeating the val'kyr. You've done well up until now... but you're only one <man/woman> and there are literally dozens of them raining destruction on the battlefield.

One enormous val'kyr sits atop the tower to our south... you can see her from here. Perhaps if we eliminate her, the remaining val'kyr will dissipate.

This is our only hope. Bring some of Grant's men with you. You'll need their protection for this battle.

passages.title: Aradne
passages.text:
I watched your victory from below.  Well-fought, but ultimately, it was for naught.

The val'kyr and the Forsaken press on; soon, they will overtake us.  We have lost Andorhal.

passages.title: The Depravity of the Forsaken
passages.text:
We nearly have this battle won, <name>. I can taste victory. The Forsaken never stood a...

What the hell is that!?

passages.title: The Depravity of the Forsaken
passages.text:
Val'kyr?  Koltira brought val'kyr to this fight?  Has he gone mad?

No, this is not Koltira's work.  This was Sylvanas.

passages.title: Traitors Among Us
passages.text:
It's good to meet you, <class>. I've come to Theramore to help eliminate the problem of the deserters. Not only have some of the men abandoned their posts, but some have filtered back into the town.

These deserter agents are spreading lies and propaganda, hoping to convince others to join their ranks.

They're at virtually every guard post throughout the town and the docks. Find them, expose them, and discredit them. At this point, anything more risks inspiring more sympathy for them.

passages.title: Traitors Among Us
passages.text:
Well done, <name>. I think we managed to catch them off guard. Their agents probably thought themselves safe within the city walls.

Given time, the agitators will return and spread their lies again. We'll use the time you've bought to shut out the deserters further.

passages.title: Discrediting the Deserters
passages.text:
I've altered the leaflets you captured from the deserters' mercenary friends at the docks. Now, anyone who reads them will get an entirely different view of the deserters and their aims.

If we distribute these to enough of the guards, the deserters will be too embarrassed to ever reestablish their presence within our walls.

<Calia hands you a stack of the altered leaflets.>

Why don't you get started while I plan our next move?

passages.title: Discrediting the Deserters
passages.text: I thought I heard laughter coming from the barracks. Did you distribute those leaflets I gave you?

passages.title: Discrediting the Deserters
passages.text:
<Calia chuckles as you describe the guards' reactions to the propaganda.>

Just as I'd hoped! I think it's safe to say any deserter agents who try to infiltrate Theramore will be laughed right out of town!

passages.title: The End of the Deserters
passages.text:
Now that we've eliminated the deserters from Theramore, it's time to complete this operation. My local contacts have reported that the deserters base their operations in a ship moored on a small island to the southeast of the docks.

Arresting their leader, Gavis Greyshield, should cause the others to lose their will to fight. Find him within the ship and convince him to surrender. I wouldn't be surprised if he puts up a bit of a fight for show, but then surrenders when he understands he can't win.

passages.title: The End of the Deserters
passages.text: Have you completed your assault on the deserter base?

passages.title: The End of the Deserters
passages.text:
Gavis' request isn't as outlandish as it might sound. With the proper handling, Lady Jaina can return the deserters to the fold, but that is her decision, of course.

It's been a pleasure working with you, <name>. Without your help, I doubt the operation would've gone so smoothly. When I make my report in Stormwind, it will name you as the <class> who ended the deserter threat.

passages.title: A Disturbing Development
passages.text:
Reports from our scout patrols have recently taken a disturbing turn. They tell of men wearing red Defias bandanas walking the Dreadmurk Shore north of Theramore's walls.

Wreckage in the area suggests they may be survivors of a shipwreck, but our information is limited. Captain Wymor at Sentry Point, a guard tower to the north of the city, is looking for help in following up on the reports.

passages.title: A Disturbing Development
passages.text:
<The captain makes no effort to hide that he's assessing your abilities.>

So you've heard about the recent shipwreck off the coast? Good, I could use some help confirming my suspicions about the survivors. Welcome aboard, <name>.

passages.title: The Hermit of Swamplight Manor
passages.text:
There's a fellow the locals know as "Swamp Eye" Jarl, who lives alone out in the swamp. Sometime ago he "took over" Swamplight Manor after the previous owners disappeared under mysterious circumstances.

I like to send someone to check up on him every once in a while. He kind of reminds me of my grandfather, you know? Some say he's not quite right in the head.

If you're headed northwest on the road out of Theramore, you'll find Swamplight Manor in the Witch Hill area, before the road turns west.

passages.title: The Hermit of Swamplight Manor
passages.text: Get off my lawn... unless, that is, you want to help old "Swamp Eye" with a little bit of cooking. Whad'ya say?

passages.title: This Old Lighthouse
passages.text:
The old lighthouse out to the east hasn't worked for some time, but Babs Fizzletorque has gotten it into her head to get it working again.

I don't know how she plans to do it by herself, but she claims that it'll make the movement of ships and goods into the docks smoother, so I can't really object. Drawing duty on the docks is really nothing to complain about when you could be on the front lines, you know?

passages.title: This Old Lighthouse
passages.text: Good. I can use all the help you can offer. My first priority is to get that lamp re-lit.

passages.title: Is it Real?
passages.text:
Oh, I'm sure you and Babs had a good laugh over the outlandish descriptions and sketches in the book, but have you stopped to consider there might be some truth to the legends?

If you listen closely enough, I bet you can still hear sailors talk about Tethyr, the sea creature the book says lives right here! Of course, if you wanted to know for sure, you could always ask old Nat Pagle.

He's got a small fishing camp on a little island in Tidefury Cove, which is southwest across Dustwallow Bay.

passages.title: Is it Real?
passages.text: So you want to know about sea monsters? Hmm... well, I'll make you a deal, but it's going to involve a lot of alcohol and some embarrassment on your part.

passages.title: Oh, It's Real
passages.text:
Yes, Tethyr is certainly real, and he lives in the waters off Theramore.

Has a thing for bright lights. He's the reason they shut down the lighthouse in the first place, you know...

And if you light it up again, he'll come right back. But no one in their right mind would do that.

So that must be your plan! It's been good sharing a drink with you, but don't blame ol' Nat if Tethyr REALLY turns you into fish bait. If you're going to do this, make sure you consult Major Mills at the Theramore docks.

passages.title: Oh, It's Real
passages.text:
<You recount your experiences with Nat Pagle, carefully omitting the portion about the 'bait test.'>

Well, it sounds like we've got our work cut out for us. I'll make the preparations.

passages.title: Take Down Tethyr!
passages.text:
Sea monster or no, we're not going to risk the safety of our shipping. I've ordered our best marksmen to prepare for a confrontation with this Tethyr. The artillerymen have augmented the dock's defenses with three mortars.

I'm going to order the lighthouse's lamp illuminated. If Tethyr does attack, it will be your job to operate the mortars and take down the beast before it can kill all of the marksmen. I wouldn't stand in one place too long, though. Using the mortars is likely to draw its attention.

passages.title: Take Down Tethyr!
passages.text: Well done, <name>! I'll admit, when I caught my first glimpse of that beast, I had doubts about our ability to defend the docks, but you held together the defenders brilliantly!

passages.title: Retribution
passages.text:
Where Market Row meets Festival Lane, you will encounter The Unforgiven. If you slay the entirety of Crusaders' Square, you will coax out Timmy the Cruel. Both of these former champions committed heinous acts against innocents here in the name of gaining unholy power.

You must destroy both of them and rid Stratholme of their foul presence. Take caution, for they were powerful fighters in life, and their new dark powers will only have made them even more deadly.

passages.title: Retribution
passages.text: Show them no mercy.

passages.title: Retribution
passages.text: You may have this as a suitable reward. I found it nestled in the armor of one of the scourge here.

passages.title: A Summons from Signilda Hardforge
passages.text: Signilda Hardforge has sent word that she wishes to honor you for your mastery of arms and your dedication to the Alliance. Make your way to Stormwind, and speak with her at the Training Hall to the south of Old Town. I do not know what she has planned, but it sounds like she has been impressed with your rapid progress.

passages.title: A Summons from Signilda Hardforge
passages.text: It's good to see that you received my message. I have something important I wish to discuss with you.

passages.title: Hair of the Dog
passages.text:
Thank the Warchief that you're here, <name>. I've made a critical error with the sea dogs and need your help to rectify the situation.

You see, I sent them out against the worgen coming from Fenris Isle stone cold sober. They attacked the beasts and promptly got their butts handed to them. Many of them died, but a few still live, barely clinging on to dear life.

Take this barrel of ale to the Decrepit Fields, east of here, and force it down the throats of fallen sea dogs.

passages.title: Hair of the Dog
passages.text: A-HA! I knew it! Lesson learned, I suppose. We will not fail again. I will be sure to have some ale on hand at the front lines.

passages.title: Lord Aurius Rivendare
passages.text:
This Chapel is the last Light amongst so much darkness. Ras Frostwhisper took his own life in the slaughterhouse, carving his face into a macabre smile in front of the Lich King, who raised him into the Lich that now haunts Scholomance.

The ground where that atrocity occured is now Scourge holy ground, blessed by the Lich King with the very darkest magic. Lord Aurius Rivendare, new ruler of Stratholme, now guards it and continues his master's evil work. Slay him without pause.

passages.title: Lord Aurius Rivendare
passages.text: Don't waste our time. Every second spend chatting away is a second we aren't taking Stratholme back for the Light.

passages.title: Lord Aurius Rivendare
passages.text: Stratholme will become a paragon of all that is good in this world. You have my thanks for your part in this mission.

passages.title: Man Against Abomination
passages.text:
Deep within, you will find Ramstein the Gorger. I cannot bear to tell you the atrocities this monster has commited. Know only this - he deserves to feel the full wrath of countless lost souls, a wrath you will bring upon him.

Have no mercy. Be unwavering in your fury.

passages.title: Man Against Abomination
passages.text: I respect the power you demonstrated in killing Ramstein. With proper rage backing your actions, I think even the Scourge can know fear.

passages.title: SMASH BROODQUEEN
passages.text:
<The following is written in very large print.>

SPIDERS IN NORTH CAVE BAD. POISON OGRES. OGRES GET SICK. BAD!

BIG BIG SPIDER IN CAVE MAKE MORE SPIDERS. MORE SPIDERS BAD!

KILL BIG SPIDER, STOP MORE SPIDERS. KILL BIG SPIDER, GET BIG PRIZE! GOOD!

<A crude drawing accompanies this.>

passages.title: SMASH BROODQUEEN
passages.text:
Are you here about the sign?

I don't want to talk about it unless you've got proof of a kill.

passages.title: SMASH BROODQUEEN
passages.text: By Grom, I'm glad that's over with. If you read that sign you may have some idea how desperate I got after trying to communicate to these lumbering oafs.

passages.title: Weapons for War
passages.text:
The Scourge are adept at forging powerful armaments for their soldiers, making it difficult for our men to kill 'em! There are blacksmithing plans near the Baroness Anastari's ziggurat that their chief swordsmith plans to use for an extremely powerful weapon for Lord Aurius.

We're going to prevent that weapon from being made and stop their regular arms flow with one blow! Go take the plans and kill the Black Guard Swordsmith when he comes to defend 'em, and it'll make our mission much easier.

passages.title: Weapons for War
passages.text: You need to kill their swordsmith! Go!

passages.title: Weapons for War
passages.text: Great! Without a steady flow of their weapons, we'll win through attrition!

passages.title: Reinforcements from Fenris
passages.text:
Those that survived your assault on Fenris managed to drink the blood of the wolf. They turned into ferocious worgen, hell-bent on vengeance. Now they paddle across Lordamere Lake and assault my sea dogs. Many have already been killed. The worgen monsters must be stopped!

Make your way to the Decrepit Fields, east of here, and kill the Hillsbrad worgen that infest the area. Once you've killed them all, make your way to the Horde communication panel, located at the docks. I'll be in touch.

passages.title: Reinforcements from Fenris
passages.text: Report?

passages.title: Reinforcements from Fenris
passages.text:
<Hatchet's communication device crackles.>

Hatchet here, are they all dead?

passages.title: Defias in Dustwallow?
passages.text:
My scouts have reported a shipwreck just off the beach to the northeast. Shipwrecks aren't all that unusual out here, but the reports also indicated the survivors were all wearing red bandanas... the symbol of the Defias!

The reports indicate their leader resides on a large island just off the coast to the northeast of the tower. Kill him and retrieve any documents you find in his possession.

passages.title: Defias in Dustwallow?
passages.text: Were you able to track down their leader?

passages.title: Defias in Dustwallow?
passages.text:
<Captain Wymor accepts the orders from you and reads over them.>

What in the world could 'precious cargo' refer to? The Defias have done some small time smuggling back in Stormwind, but this seems out of their league. The language of these orders suggests a wealthy or noble patron.

passages.title: Renn McGill
passages.text:
From the wording of the orders you recovered, it looks like the first priority of the Defias will be to locate and secure whatever cargo they possessed.

SI:7 has had a salvage diver named Renn McGill working out of Theramore for some time. When he heard about the shipwreck, Renn went north to dive near the islands the Defias now occupy.

If we're to beat the Defias to this cargo, we'll need his help. Look for him in the waters northeast of a small island just north of the island you visited earlier.

passages.title: Renn McGill
passages.text: Well met, <class>. What brings you out here?

passages.title: Renn McGill
passages.text:
<Renn looks over the orders.>

So there was valuable cargo on board! We have to locate it before the Defias recover it. These guys are no divers, but we're going to need some of their gear if you're to help me find the cargo.

passages.title: Secondhand Diving Gear
passages.text:
There's plenty of wreckage strewn across the bottom of the water from here to Alcaz, and the Defias have already got divers out there looking around. With the help of some of their gear, we can get you suited up and ready to join the hunt, but you'll have to do some creative "borrowing" first.

Search this island for a crate of diving gear and something to repair it with. When you've got them, bring them to me and I'll have your gear ready in no time!

passages.title: Secondhand Diving Gear
passages.text: Let's see what you managed to "borrow" from the Defias.

passages.title: Secondhand Diving Gear
passages.text:
Wow, this is in worse shape than I'd thought, and these tools...

Well, I said I'd get this back into working condition for you, so I'd better get to work.

passages.title: Recover the Cargo!
passages.text:
Well, I was able to make enough repairs to this gear to let you dive for awhile, anyway. I wouldn't count on it holding out for a long time, though.

The wreckage of the ship is strewn along the bottom from the east coast of this island out toward Alcaz Island. While that helm holds out, locate pieces of the wreckage on the bottom between this island and Alcaz. Use this salvage kit to search the wreckage for pieces of the cargo. Be careful not to venture too close to Alcaz Island. Those hydra are fierce.

passages.title: Recover the Cargo!
passages.text: Did your search of the wreckage reveal anything about the Defias cargo?

passages.title: Recover the Cargo!
passages.text:
<Renn rifles through the contents of the strongboxes you recovered.>

Good work. Now, let's see if our 'precious cargo' is in here....

passages.title: Jaina Must Know
passages.text:
You must bring news of our findings to Lady Jaina without delay! If the Defias were transporting a prisoner, there's no telling who it might be or if the person is still alive!

One thing is for certain, <name>. The Defias wouldn't go to all this trouble for some petty grudge. Their prisoner must have been someone of importance. Lady Jaina would know better than anyone else what these findings mean. You'll find her at the top of the mage tower at Theramore's center.

passages.title: Jaina Must Know
passages.text: You and Renn have done excellent work in bringing this information to light and reporting it immediately. Now, we must confirm your findings. The implications are too great if we are wrong.

passages.title: Proof of Treachery
passages.text:
Although Onyxia has been exposed and removed from the court, the Defias who carried out her plan must be punished. Carry word to Grand Admiral Jes-Tereth in Stormwind castle that the Defias are the ones who carried out the Varian's kidnapping. I have little doubt that Stormwind's armies will mete out swift and terrible justice to those involved.

I can use my magic to expedite your trip to Stormwind. Just speak to me when you're prepared to go, <name>.

passages.title: Proof of Treachery
passages.text:
So it was the Defias who served as the hands of Onyxia in this plot?

<The admirall's face grows red with anger and her hands clench into fists.>

You and Lady Jaina have done Stormwind a great service this day. The traitors will not live long enough to regret their crimes.

passages.title: Return to Jaina
passages.text:
We must make plans to destroy the remnants of the Defias. Please convey my thanks to Lady Jaina, back in Theramore. She has ever been a loyal friend and steadfast ally.

Go to the Mage Quarter at the western end of the city and speak with Archmage Malin at the foot of the tower there. He will speed your return to Theramore.

passages.title: Return to Jaina
passages.text: I have no doubt that the king meant every word when he told you he plans to destroy the Defias once and for all. He does not make promises lightly, and the enemies of Stormwind should know it.

passages.title: Raptor Captor
passages.text:
The patch of swamp to the northeast is home to a particularly nasty breed of raptors. We've lost more than one unwary soldier to them, but I think we can turn them against our Grimtotem neighbors.

Take this rope and use it to capture Bloodfen raptors or Bloodfen screechers that you've subdued. I wouldn't try to capture one of the beasts until you've weakened them quite a bit in combat. It's going to be quite a struggle.

passages.title: Raptor Captor
passages.text: Did you capture those raptors?

passages.title: Raptor Captor
passages.text: You look a little scratched up, but nothing major. You're certainly in a lot better shape than the Grimtotems will be when our new raptor friends get done with them.

passages.title: The Orc Report
passages.text:
Sifting through the loose dirt, the severed hand of an orc is found. And clutched in the hand is a bone-carved tube. And in the tube is a dirt-stained parchment.

The parchment is written in orcish... and it looks important.

passages.title: The Orc Report
passages.text: Do you have a report to make?

passages.title: The Orc Report
passages.text: Hm... I can't read orcish very well, but this looks like a report... written by an orc spy!

passages.title: Captain Vimes
passages.text:
Captain Vimes should see the orc report you found, <name>. He knows the orcish language better than most. And he should know that there are Horde spies near Theramore!

The captain is in the barracks, on the northeastern side of Theramore Isle.

passages.title: Captain Vimes
passages.text: You have something for me?

passages.title: Captain Vimes
passages.text: A report from an orc spy!  How did you find this?  No matter -- let's see what it says...

passages.title: Mission to Mudsprocket
passages.text:
The Steamwheedle Cartel has recently established a new outpost in the southern part of Dustwallow Marsh. It's called Mudsprocket, if I recall, and it's located on the main road south out of Tabetha's Farm and the Stonemaul Ruins.

This is an excellent opportunity for us to establish new trade contacts and Lady Jaina wants me to send a representative down there to establish contact. Would you be willing to go?

passages.title: Mission to Mudsprocket
passages.text: So Theramore is interested in doing business? Well, that's not an offer I'd turn down. Supplies are pretty scarce here right now, so we need all the business contacts we can get!

passages.title: Inspecting the Ruins
passages.text:
Poor James never recovered from the destruction of the Shady Rest and the murder of his family. The boys and I are doing what we can to find the monsters who did this.

I've sent our best investigator, Inspector Tarem, out to the ruins, but this is too big a job for any one man. If you'd lend Tarem a hand, we'd appreciate it. Light knows, we'd all like to be out there helping.

The main road will lead you to the inn, but take care. Your journey will take you beyond the protection of my soldiers.

passages.title: Inspecting the Ruins
passages.text:
It's good to see that Captain Vimes is finally assigning others to this investigation.

I've used a reflective powder to dust the area. It will reveal suspicious objects and markings, helping you to focus your efforts. Look over anything the dust illuminates.

passages.title: They Call Him Smiling Jim
passages.text:
I can't help it if I feel sorry for ol' Jim there. He wasn't always like that. Ran an inn out in the marsh for a while, wonderful place.

Look, I don't really want to talk about it. Bring it up with Captain Vimes if you really have to. He's stationed on the top floor of Foothold Citadel, the large barracks to the east of Lady Jaina's tower.

passages.title: They Call Him Smiling Jim
passages.text:
James Hyal's his real name. He opened an inn at the edge of the Barrens. Wanted to make a nice place for travelers to stop over...

Might be he was thinking too big, but the inn did do well for a while. Then we lost control of the roads in the marsh, and the ogres took over.

James was too stubborn to give up his dream for safety within our walls, and the Shady Rest Inn was burnt to the ground. We're investigating, but haven't had much luck. If you want to help out, see what you can find in the rubble.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
An iron shield, blackened by the fire that raged through the inn, is affixed to the crumbling chimney, one of the few remaining parts of the structure that once made up the Shady Rest Inn.

The shield can be removed from the brick of the chimney.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Have you found evidence from the site of the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Hm, I'm no expert with the construction of arms and armor. Their use, yes, but not their making.

This shield seems as ordinary as any, excepting the damage from the fire that engulfed the inn.

passages.title: Inspecting the Ruins
passages.text:
If you follow the road south from the village, and then west toward the Barrens, you'll come across the ruins of the Shady Rest Inn.

Theramore has sent an investigator to discover how the inn met its fate. I had a man placed in that inn as a spy and I don't trust in the competence of these humans to uncover what happened.

Whatever you find, don't give a scrap of it to that investigator. We'll handle this ourselves.

passages.title: Inspecting the Ruins
passages.text:
<The inspector regards you with what can only be disdain and distrust.>

Leave this place be, errand boy, or I'll be sure to bring a contingent of guard with me next time to sink the lesson home.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
An iron shield, blackened by the fire that raged through the inn, is affixed to the crumbling chimney, one of the few remaining parts of the structure that once made up the Shady Rest Inn.

The shield can be removed from the brick of the chimney.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: What's that you have there, <name>? Evidence from the remains of the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
I grant that humans have strange decorating tastes, but would they use a plain iron shield to adorn their fireplace? Perhaps this shield was placed there by the ones who burned the inn.

A warning? A threat?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Hmm... I don't see anything out of the ordinary with this shield. We should have Do'gol, the blacksmith, take a look at it, and see if he can tell us more about it, but I wouldn't hold out hope...

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Something for me, <class>?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
This is good shield. Very strong, heavy, good. But Do'gol don't need it. I make shields, not buy them, <name>.

You should know that.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Hmmm, there's writing right here on the rim of the shield, but it's hard to read from all the burned stuff.

I need acid to make it clear. Venom from the darkmist spiders would do good. The spiders have taken over an old mine, the Darkmist Cavern, northwest of the village. Get me some of their sacs and I can clean this up.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Did you get them sacs from the spiders?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
I don't like spiders that are so big I can't sit on them and squish them.

Thanks for getting them, <name>. Now I rip them open and pour them onto the shield...

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Oh, I think I might have dropped too much acid onto the shield. Let me just rub a little...

Hm, kind of hard to read, but it looks like the name Mosarn. Never heard of him. Maybe Krog knows. Krog knows many people.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Mosarn? Sounds familiar... I can't put my finger on it. Maybe it'll come to me later.

It probably isn't important. A shield can come from anywhere and not mean anything...

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Ah, I remember now! Mosarn is a well-respected blacksmith in Thunder Bluff. I knew I had heard his name somewhere, before.

In thanks, the Earthen Ring awarded me with a set of armor crafted by Mosarn. Very good work.

Perhaps he can tell you more about the shield he crafted.

It's not much of a lead, but since we didn't get anything useful out of Reethe, it's all we have.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Hello there, <class>. Something I can help you with?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Yes, you are certainly correct. This is a shield that I made.

I'm afraid there's not much more I can tell you though, <name>. I craft so many different shields and sets of armor, I can't keep track of them all.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
A glint of light on the ground catches your eye from underneath the rubble. Brushing debris and ash caked onto the object reveals the insignia of a gold anchor on white, enameled on the surface: the sign of Theramore.

Underneath the anchor is embossed the name "Lieutenant Paval Reethe".

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text: Have you found any leads on what happened at the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text: Hmm... now this is interesting.

passages.title: Questioning Reethe
passages.text:
It took a long time, but I found Reethe. He hide good for a human.

Ogron worried that he might be crazy after so much time in swamp. You come with me for we go get answers from him.

passages.title: Questioning Reethe
passages.text:
Hmph. It is good that Reethe will no longer be lurking around the swamp, but it is a shame that humans are built so frail that he could not recover from a little arrow wound.

It seems that this thread of the mystery has led nowhere, and we must look elsewhere.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
A glint of light on the ground catches your eye from underneath the rubble. Brushing away debris and ash caked onto the object reveals the insignia of a gold anchor on white enameled on the surface: the sign of Theramore.

Underneath the anchor is embossed the name "Lieutenant Paval Reethe".

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text: Have you found anything of interest at the Shady Rest Inn?

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
It's never good news when a guard's badge is brought to me.

Sometimes it's a man or woman who's fallen in battle, and I'm left to bring the news to the grieving family. Other times we never find out what happened to them. And other times it's even worse than that.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
I don't recognize the name of Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Your best bet would be to check with Adjutant Tesoran. He keeps track of all the records for the Theramore guard, from personnel to their equipment.

He should be able to tell you who this Reethe is with a quick check of his books.

passages.title: Lieutenant Paval Reethe
passages.text:
Hello, <name>. You'd like information about a specific member of the Theramore guard? Reethe, was it?

Just give me a moment to find the right book.

passages.title: Ezul'aan Calls
passages.text:
Ezul'aan, one of the foremost paladins in the realm, has asked to speak with you personally. I do not know what he has planned, but it sounds like he has been impressed with your rapid progress.

You should make your way to Stormwind immediately and meet him at the Training Hall in the Old Town district.

passages.title: Ezul'aan Calls
passages.text: It heartens me to see that my message found you, <name>. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: Dalgrun Calls
passages.text:
Dalgrun Steelpine oversees the training and coordination of hunters in the service of Stormwind. He has asked to speak to you personally. As soon as you are able, travel to Stormwind and meet with Dalgrun at the Training Hall in Old Town.

I have no idea what he has planned, but it sounds like he has been impressed with your rapid progress.

passages.title: Dalgrun Calls
passages.text: Ah, you've arrived. Make yourself at home, <name>. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: Make Contact with SI:7
passages.text:
It seems that the leaders of SI:7 have taken an interest in your progress and your service to the Alliance. Veruca Darkstream, a high ranking member of SI:7, has asked to speak with you. Veruca is awaiting your arrival at the Training Hall in Stormwind.

I'm not sure what she wants with you, but it seemed important.

passages.title: Make Contact with SI:7
passages.text: I hope my message didn't unnerve you, <name>. I have called you here to recognize your accomplishments.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: I have an urgent message for you from Stormwind, <name>. It seems that Speak to Patrice Lancaster has asked to speak with you at the Training Hall in Stormwind's Old Town district. The messenger did not say what the matter concerned, but that you should travel to Stormwind with all haste.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: It heartens me to see that you received my message and responded so quickly.

passages.title: The Temple of the Moon
passages.text: I have an urgent message for you from Darnassus. The message is from the High Priestess of Elune, Tyrande Whisperwind, herself! The messenger did not say what the matter concerned, but that you should travel to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and meet with the high priestess at once.

passages.title: The Temple of the Moon
passages.text: Welcome to the Temple of the Moon, <name>. I am glad that you chose to answer my summons so quickly.

passages.title: An Audience with Mulric
passages.text:
I have an urgent message for you from Stormwind, <name>. It seems Mulric Boldrock has asked to speak with you the next time you're in the city.

The messenger gave no explanation for the shaman's invitation, but you should travel to Stormwind and find Mulric Boldrock at the Training Hall to the south of Old Town as soon as you can.

passages.title: An Audience with Mulric
passages.text: Welcome, <name>. I am glad that you decided to accept my invitation.

passages.title: Frazzle's Request
passages.text:
I just received a message from Stormwind, <name>. One of Stormwind's most renowned mages, Frazzle Frostfingers, has requested that you visit him at the Training Hall in Stormwind. The Training Hall is located in the Old Town district of Stormwind.

I do not know what he has planned, but it sounds like he has been impressed with your rapid progress.

passages.title: Frazzle's Request
passages.text: Welcome to the Wizard's Sanctum, <name>. I have been watching your progress with interest.

passages.title: A Message From Evelyn Thorn
passages.text:
It seems that the elders in our ranks have taken notice of your progress and dedication, <name>. Evelyn Thorn, one of the oldest and most respected members of our circle, has sent word that she wishes to speak with you. You should not take such an invitation lightly. Most only speak with her in the course of their lessons, but if she has asked to see you personally, it must be an important matter.

Hurry back to Stormwind and look for her at the Training Hall to the south of the Old Town district.

passages.title: A Message From Evelyn Thorn
passages.text: I see that my message managed to reach you. Good. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: An Invitation from Moonglade
passages.text:
You just missed the messenger from Moonglade, <name>. He said little, except that he carried an urgent message from Loganaar, one of the honored trainers of the Cenarion Circle. Head to Moonglade as quickly as you can, <name>. The matter sounds important.

Look for Loganaar in the village of Nighthaven.

passages.title: An Invitation from Moonglade
passages.text: I'm glad to see that you have arrived safely in Nighthaven, <name>. I offer you the welcome and the hospitality of the Cenarion Circle.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: I have an urgent message for you from Stormwind, <name>. Patrice Lancaster has asked to meet with you in Stormwind. The message didn't say what the priest trainer wanted to discuss, but you should make your way to Stormwind as quickly as you can. Look for Patrice Lancaster at the Training Hall in the Old Town district of the city.

passages.title: Patrice Lancaster Sends Word
passages.text: I see that you received my message. Excellent!

passages.title: An Audience with Feenix Arcshine
passages.text: I've received an urgent message from Orgrimmar for you, <name>. The renowned mage, Feenix Arcshine, wants you to meet with him in Orgrimmar. I'm not sure what this is about, but if I was you, I would travel to the capital as fast as possible and seek out Feenix Arcshine at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: An Audience with Feenix Arcshine
passages.text: Ah, good. It seems my message did find you.

passages.title: Tamanji's Call
passages.text:
A courier from Orgrimmar just delivered a message for you. I'm to tell you that Tamanji, master of the hunters in Orgrimmar, has asked to meet with you.

Travel quickly to Orgrimmar and present yourself to Tamanji at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Tamanji's Call
passages.text: Good, you're here. Let's get started.

passages.title: The Shattered Hand
passages.text:
A messenger just arrived from Orgrimmar bearing a communication for you. Thega Graveblade, the senior rogue trainer in Orgrimmar, has sent for you. You must head to Orgrimmar immediately and meet with her at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

When Thega Graveblade summons you, the prudent thing to do is obey. Do not keep her waiting, <name>.

passages.title: The Shattered Hand
passages.text: Now that you are here, we can begin.

passages.title: The Riverspeaker Calls
passages.text: News travels upon the winds, young shaman. Your deeds have not gone unnoticed! It seems Hretar Riverspeaker wishes to discuss something with you. Make your way to Orgrimmar as quickly as you can and speak with him at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor. He will be among the others who offer training.

passages.title: The Riverspeaker Calls
passages.text: I see you are both obedient and talented, <name>. Stay that way, and you will go far in the Horde.

passages.title: Gormok Ogrefist
passages.text:
I just received word that you are needed in Orgrimmar, <name>. Gormok Ogrefist, the honored trainer of warriors in the city, has sent for you. It would not be wise to ignore such a summons.

Travel quickly to Orgrimmar and visit The Barracks in the Valley of Honor where Gormok awaits your arrival.

passages.title: Gormok Ogrefist
passages.text: I see you are both obedient and talented, <name>. Stay that way, and you will go far in the Horde.

passages.title: Kazak's Behest
passages.text:
<name>, I have received word that you are needed back in Orgrimmar. Kazak Darkscream, one of the senior warlock trainers, has something important that he wishes to discuss with you. It seems like the kind of thing that cannot wait.

Make your way back to Orgrimmar and speak with him as soon as you can. You will find him at the Training Hall in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Kazak's Behest
passages.text: Ah, you're here at last.

passages.title: A Journey to Moonglade
passages.text:
As you have heard, Moonglade is the home of the Cenarion Circle, the brotherhood of druids. All who dwell there do so in the peace of Cenarius. It is in that spirit that the trainer Loganaar has extended an invitation to visit him in Moonglade.

You will find him in the village of Nighthaven.

passages.title: A Journey to Moonglade
passages.text: Welcome to Moonglade, <name>. I have been looking forward to meeting you.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
I'm sorry I can't be of much help, <name>, but I can refer you to someone who would be. Caz Twosprocket, one of our best blacksmiths, works the forge at the smithy.

Take the shield to him, and see what he can tell you.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Something for me to look at?

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: Hm... interesting piece of iron you have here. Definitely not made by any of the blacksmiths I know over on this side of the sea, and it's certainly not my work.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text:
Ah, I almost missed this... The leather strap on the back must have burned off, but it seems like it was made to fit a large person. I'd guess a tauren, actually.

That's about all I can tell you. Tell Captain Vimes I'm sorry I couldn't be of more help.

passages.title: The Black Shield
passages.text: That's not much information to work on, but we'll have to keep it in mind. Hopefully some of the other pieces of this mystery will fall into place, and paint a more helpful picture of what happened.

passages.title: Daelin's Men
passages.text:
Reddon... Redpath... Ah, here it is! Lieutenant Paval Reethe.

Joined the Theramore guard along with most of the recruits that came across the sea with Lady Proudmoore. Enlisted with the marines of Kul Tiras at the age of sixteen. Distinguished service, promotions...

Listed as missing.

passages.title: Daelin's Men
passages.text:
Missing? That would be Tesoran's kind way of saying traitor.

No doubt he's one of those fools so blindly loyal to Admiral Daelin that he turned traitor.  Isn't that a delicious irony? The deserters accuse us of betraying the Alliance.

passages.title: The Deserters
passages.text:
Reethe? That coward?

We threw him out of camp because he insisted on raiding the supplies of the ogres up at Brackenwall Village. We're not so many in number that we could stand up to those mindless brutes.

He crossed the line one too many times, so we left him to fend for himself.

Now, I helped you out... So, why don't you help us out and forget you bumped into us?

passages.title: The Deserters
passages.text: I will send Lieutenant Caldwell to deal with the deserters at Lost Point. In addition, I will instruct him to find Reethe. The marsh is not so big and trackless that he should be unable to find him.

passages.title: Seek Out Tabetha
passages.text:
The arms you captured in Blackhoof Village have not seen any combat beyond mere training exercises, which means the Grimtotems who destroyed the Shady Rest are still at large.

To the south, in the heart of the Quagmire, lives the witch Tabetha. Though she is a human, she has dealt honorably with us and trained some of our mages.

Ask her for assistance in tracking down the band of Grimtotem responsible for burning the inn. The Alliance must not be allowed to think we were complicit in the attack.

passages.title: Seek Out Tabetha
passages.text:
<Tabetha smiles slightly.>

Krog wishes me to scry for the Grimtotems, eh? Well, I have no need of magic in this case.

It seems we have a mutual enemy. The Grimtotems have built an outpost nearby and are a constant thorn in the side of me and my students.

passages.title: Justice Dispensed
passages.text:
I doubt the Grimtotems will give up their campaign to drive humans from the marsh, though I get the impression you probably don't mind that. At least we have dealt with the perpetrators of the crimes at the Shady Rest Inn.

Go tell your leader that his vengeance has been sated.

passages.title: Justice Dispensed
passages.text:
<Krog listens to your report.>

I'm impressed, <name>. I would've thought that the Grimtotem criminals would've been more difficult to locate. The Alliance are truly incompetent.

In truth, I just sought to answer the death of one of my men, but this situation has been more fortunate than expected. If the Grimtotem choose to retaliate, it will likely be against the Alliance. Perhaps we will soon have the manpower to drive the scum from these shores once and for all.

passages.title: Seek Out Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text:
Avaros Dawnglaive, a senior Blood Knight and advisor to the warchief, requires your presence in Orgrimmar. He has taken an interest in your training, <name>, and it is imperative that you speak with him immediately.

The message I received didn't mention the reason he requested your visit, but you should set out for Orgrimmar right away. Avaros Dawnglaive can be found at The Barracks in the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Seek Out Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text: I've heard much about you, <name>. You have a bright future ahead of you in the Horde.

passages.title: Torn Ground
passages.text:
It won't be takin' much convincin' to turn us against da Twilight - dat's already our goal. We've already come to battle here though, so we may be needin' ya help before we can turn towards dere fortress.

Da Twilight have already brought Iso'rath up from da ground to the south, I'm sure ya noticed. Its tentacles have been burstin' from da ground all around us. We could use a hand beatin' them down if you be willin'.

passages.title: Torn Ground
passages.text: Did ya have any luck with dose tentacles?

passages.title: Torn Ground
passages.text: Tank ya, <class>. A bit of breathin' room helps a lot.

passages.title: Pushing Back
passages.text: Da Twilight's Hammer have destroyed a Dragonmaw town to the south and are performin' dey're summonin' rituals from there. Offer dem no respite to continue wit dey're incantations. Bring tha battle to dem!

passages.title: Pushing Back
passages.text: Revenge is bittersweet, but I'm glad we be havin' someone as powerful as you do see dis done.

passages.title: Unbroken
passages.text:
We are preparing a ritual that may be of use in destroying Iso'rath, the old god bred abomination that the Twilight's Hammer have brought up from the depths. We are delayed though, for one of our strongest was captured during an assault on their encampment.

Earthcaller Yevaa is within the ruins to the south. She is not dead. I am sure of it. Please, rescue her. If any of us is deserving of your aid, it is her.

passages.title: Unbroken
passages.text: Thank the elements that you've come. Did my brothers send you?

passages.title: Simple Solutions
passages.text:
I'm new to this gig. Very new. But ya know what? That gives me perspective!

These shaman buddies of mine have come upon somethin' great, but they're too single minded! They lean on the elements and they forget to make use of the common materials all around them.

In the ruins to the south, I saw those Twilight goons tote in barrels of flammable oil! They used it when they razed the town. I say we use it when we raze them.

passages.title: Simple Solutions
passages.text: I wonder what happens when you douse an elemental with that stuff. Jumbo-super-bonfire-elemental? I'm thinkin' so. We'll have to try.

passages.title: Simple Solutions
passages.text: Now that's what I'm talkin' about! Can you think of all the uses for this stuff? I definitely can't. But I can think of a lot, and I'm liking the possibilities.

passages.title: Meet With Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text:
Avaros Dawnglaive sends word from Orgrimmar -- he wishes to speak with you when you're in the city. I needn't remind you that Avaros is an honored member of our order and his requests should not be ignored.

Next time you are in Orgrimmar, travel to The Barracks in the Valley of Honor and speak with him.

passages.title: Meet With Avaros Dawnglaive
passages.text: I've heard much of your contributions to the Horde, <name>.

passages.title: Of Love and Family
passages.text:
Inside the Scarlet Bastion is a painting of great personal value to Highlord Tirion Fordring. Search for a painting of our twin moons. Chip away at the paint until you uncover the master work, 'Of Love and Family.'

May the Light guide your actions, and please handle the painting with the utmost care.

passages.title: Of Love and Family
passages.text: The painting, <name>. Do you have the painting?

passages.title: Of Love and Family
passages.text: Master Fordring will be glad beyond measure to see this painting again.

passages.title: Talk to Ogron
passages.text:
I know this human, Paval Reethe. Pathetic, even for his kind. He deserted his fellow soldiers and is now hiding out in the woods.

I sent Ogron out to track him down. Some of the others suspect he's been stealing from our supplies. I think I saw Ogron heading off to the southeast.

passages.title: Talk to Ogron
passages.text:
Ogron? Yeah, that me.

Shh. Keep voice down. Crocs hear you.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: Do you feel it, <class>? The elements are uneasy. We members of the Earthen Ring have struggled to find the cause of the unrest. Thus far we have been unsuccessful and now turn to others that may aid us. Speak with Erunak Stonespeaker in Stormwind and see how you might be able to aid us.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: I'm glad you've come, <class>.  These are troublesome times and we could use all the help we can get.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: Do you feel it, <class>? The elements are uneasy. We members of the Earthen Ring have struggled to find the cause of the unrest. Thus far we have been unsuccessful and now turn to others that may aid us. Speak with Earthmender Norsala in Orgrimmar and see what tasks she may have for you.

passages.title: The Elements Cry Out
passages.text: I'm glad you've come, <class>.  These are troublesome times and we could use all the help we can get.

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text:
Alright, these cowards want to fight? Let's see how well they do without any weapons.

I'm sure you must have a torch, or something. Burn their weapon racks.

Burn them all!

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text: Let's see them wage their war now!

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text:
The Grimtotem want to fight? Let us see how well they do without their weapons.

I'm sure you must have something that burns. Set their weapon racks ablaze, my <class> friend.

Let nature take its course.

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text: We shall have to burn more of their weapon racks than that if we are to put a dent in their ability to fight.

passages.title: No Weapons For You!
passages.text: Let us see how well they fight without their weapons.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text:
There's no way around it. If you want to win a battle, you have to spill some blood. In this case... a lot of it.

You know what we have to do.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text: That put a dent in their numbers! Can't say that they didn't deserve it.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text:
There is no alternative: if you intend to win a battle, you must spill the enemy's blood. In this case, unfortunately, a lot of it.

You know what we have to do.

passages.title: Darkcloud Grimtotem
passages.text: While the Earth Mother does not condone such violence, we had no choice. The Grimtotem have ignored Her teachings for too long and are reaping what they have sown.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text:
Sentinel training 101: take out their leaders and your enemy's forces will soon fall apart. We're going to do just that, <class>.

Isha Gloomaxe is the closest of the Grimtotem chiefs. Let's see if we can't take her measure.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text: She was tougher than I thought. We worked well together, but we're going to have to make sure not to underestimate the other Grimtotem chiefs.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text:
Basic brave philosophy dictates that if you kill the leaders of your enemy's forces, they will soon fall into disarray. We are going to do just that, <class>.

Isha Gloomaxe is the closest of the Grimtotem chiefs. We will test her and her axe, and she will be found wanting.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Isha Gloomaxe
passages.text: She was more formidable than her reputation suggested. Although we worked well together, we must make certain not to underestimate the other Grimtotem chiefs.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text:
Elder Stormhoof is a shaman of immense power. Supposedly, he is a direct disciple of Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone, leader of the Grimtotem clan.

We know that he's here and that he's been training their geomancers. We have to kill him, <class>.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text:
That's two of them. Two more to go.

I wonder what he meant about being "chosen"?

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text:
Elder Stormhoof is a shaman chief of immense power. He was taught by Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone, leader of the Grimtotem clan.

We know that he is here and that he has been training their geomancers. We have to kill him, <class>.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Elder Stormhoof
passages.text: That was not pleasant. I wonder what he meant by calling you, "the Chosen"?

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
In shu'halo myth, the Rattle of Bones is connected with the Writ of History and the Drums of War. They are supposed to be powerful tauren artifacts.

We must keep our eyes peeled if we're to find the other two. The writ will most likely look like some kind of pictographic scroll if the stories are to be believed.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text: We'll need the actual writ, not just any tauren scroll hanging.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
I'm fairly certain that's it. This is very intriguing, <name>. What are they doing here? Are they being used as a weapon?

The wind serpent flew northwest to that next bluff. Maybe that's where the drums are?

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
The Rattle of Bones is a part of shu'halo ancient myth. It is always connected with the Writ of History and the Drums of War. They are supposed to be powerful tauren artifacts; gifts from the Earth Mother if the tales are to be believed. I cannot imagine Her being connected with the drums, though.

We must be vigilant if we are to find the other two. The writ will look like a pictographic scroll if memory serves.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text: We will need the actual writ, and not just any scroll hanging.

passages.title: The Writ of History
passages.text:
This is very exciting and also worrisome, <name>. What are these artifacts doing here? Are they being used as a weapons against us by the Grimtotem?

The wind serpent flew northwest to that next bluff. Maybe that's where the drums are?

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
One of the infamous Grimtotem leaders of the Stonetalon Mountains has returned home.

We should take this opportunity to make sure that he doesn't go anywhere else.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text: We need to find and slay Grundig Darkcloud, <name>.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
<The sentinel gives you an appraising look.>

What is it with you? Why do they all seem spooked by you being here?

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
One of the most accomplished Grimtotem leaders of the Stonetalon Mountains has returned home.

We must make the most of this chance and put an end to his campaign of terror once and for all.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: Grundig Darkcloud
passages.text:
<The brave gives you an appraising look.>

There is something special about you, <name>. That much is certain.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Whatever the Grimtotem are doing with these Drums of War, we don't want them to have them.

Don't worry, <name>, we'll figure it all out. But first, we need to gather all of the pieces of the puzzle.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text: The tauren love their drums. I can only imagine the Drums of War will be somehow different from the others.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Surely that was the voice of the Elder Crone!

We must be very careful, <name>. Great danger lies ahead if Magatha Grimtotem has taken notice of you.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Whatever it is that the Grimtotem are doing with the Drums of War, we do not want them to keep them.

Do not worry, <name>, we will figure out what is going on here. But first, we need to gather all of the artifacts.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text: War is not an activity to engage in for those who are faithful to the Earth Mother's teachings.

passages.title: The Drums of War
passages.text:
Surely that was the voice of the Elder Crone!

We must be very careful, <name>. Great danger lies ahead if Magatha Grimtotem has taken notice of you.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
And now the time has come to take out the leader of all of the Darkcloud Pinnacle Grimtotem: Arnak Grimtotem.

It is said that he's the disgraced nephew of Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone and matriarch of the Grimtotem clan. Supposedly, his indiscretions have left him in a state of disfavor with her.

But none of that matters right now. All that matters is that we kill him. For good this time.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text: We have to kill Arnak, <name>, if we are to win the battle for the tauren of Freewind Post.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
For some reason they all think that you've been sent by Magatha Grimtotem. I know it must have something to do with that wind serpent that's been hanging around.

Doesn't matter. Their leader is dead. It's only a matter of time before the tauren of Freewind Post regain their home.

If I were them, I'd push back a little to teach the Grimtotem a lesson, but they probably won't. They're tauren.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
The time has come to deal with the leader of the Darkcloud Pinnacle Grimtotem: Arnak Grimtotem.

He is the disgraced nephew of Magatha Grimtotem, the Elder Crone and matriarch of the Grimtotem clan. His indiscretions have left him in a state of disfavor with her.

None of that matters now. All that matters is that we deal with him. Once and for all.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text: Arnak must fall, <name>, if we are to win the battle against the Grimtotem.

passages.title: Grimtotem Chiefs: The Chief of Chiefs
passages.text:
They all believed that you have been sent by Magatha Grimtotem. There is no arguing that her pet, Arikara, has been lurking about.

<The brave gives you a long look.>

It does not matter. Arnak is dead. It is only a matter of time before we take back Freewind Post.

Perhaps now we will be able to establish a lasting peace with the Grimtotem?

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text:
I am familiar with these artifacts. I believe that they were brought here by Magatha Grimtotem herself. But she's not amongst the Grimtotem on Darkcloud Pinnacle. She disappeared right after she arrived, and no one knows where she is now.

Maybe we can find out.

Take the rattle, the writ, and the drum out to Arikara's Needle. If my guess is correct, the wind serpent will appear again. You'll have to defeat it to gain knowledge of where Magatha is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: Only by subduing Arikara will you discover where Magatha Grimtotem is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: So, she's been taken prisoner by the Twilight's Hammer. I can't say that I feel sorry for her, but she might prove even more dangerous in their hands.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text:
I am familiar with these artifacts. I believe that they were brought here by Magatha Grimtotem herself. But she's not amongst the Grimtotem on Darkcloud Pinnacle. She disappeared right after she arrived, and no one knows where she is now.

Maybe we can find out.

Take the rattle, the writ, and the drum out to Arikara's Needle. If my guess is correct, the wind serpent will appear again. You'll have to defeat it to gain knowledge of where Magatha is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: Only by subduing Arikara will you discover where Magatha Grimtotem is hiding.

passages.title: Invoking the Serpent
passages.text: So, she's been taken prisoner by the Twilight's Hammer. I can't say that I feel sorry for her, but she might prove even more dangerous in their hands.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: Thank you for coming to see me, <name>.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: The spirits knew that you would answer my call, <name>.

passages.title: Losing Ground
passages.text:
I don't know how much longer we can hold out for, <name>. Crowley and Bloodfang's worgen know every hidey hole and safe spot in Gilneas.
