One minute they're standing in front of you and the next minute they're gone! We're gonna lose this war to attacks of opportunity, even though we have a superior military presence.

But momma didn't raise no quitter! Forsaken until the end, my friend.

Head west into the headlands and help our soldiers on the front line. Kill the attacking worgen rebels!

passages.title: Losing Ground
passages.text: Kill the rebels!

passages.title: Losing Ground
passages.text:
If I could still breathe I'd let out a sigh of relief.

Don't get too comfortable, though, <name>, your mission here has just begun.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: There you are, <name>. I was beginning to think my message hadn't found you.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: Welcome, <name>. I'm glad that you accepted my invitation. We have much to discuss.

passages.title: In Time, All Will Be Revealed
passages.text:
The Dark Lady has sent you and Arthura here for a very specific purpose. Before I tell you more, we must make preparations.

Head east into the forest of Gilneas and search near the trees and rocks of the region for a special plant known as wolfsbane. Gather as much of the wolfsbane as you can carry and return to me.

Our mission here goes far beyond the scope of the battlefield, <name>. In time, all will be revealed.

passages.title: In Time, All Will Be Revealed
passages.text: Did you gather the wolfsbane?

passages.title: In Time, All Will Be Revealed
passages.text:
<Belmont takes the wolfsbane from you.>

Good. Now just do as Forward Commander Onslaught commands. Try your best to fit in with the rest of the soldiers. We don't want the Gilneas Liberation Front to get suspicious.

Oh, you didn't know they were watching us? Right now there are five different worgen spies looking down on our position. Just be calm and follow orders. I'll let you know when we are ready to proceed.

passages.title: The F.C.D.
passages.text:
Communications are down with all of our frontline outposts, <name>. As of right now I don't have a damn clue as to the status of our troops in Gilneas. We need to re-establish communications.

I need you to head west into the headlands and find our outpost on the coast. By now the soldiers there are likely all dead, but their F.C.D. might be operational. Grab the device and get back to me.

passages.title: The F.C.D.
passages.text: Recover the F.C.D.

passages.title: The F.C.D.
passages.text: With this device I will be able to communicate with you in the field. Now to check the rest of our frontline outposts.

passages.title: The Zeppelin Crash
passages.text:
Not long ago, a goblin zeppelin crashed to the east. A representative of the Steamwheedle Cartel passed through here a few days ago.

She was looking for information about the zeppelin's cargo and its pilot, Beezil, but none of us really got a good look at the crash. I doubt she'll be able to clean up after the wreck by herself, much less recover whatever cargo the vessel might have carried.

If you have time, you may want to check up on her out at Beezil's Wreck, due east of here, near the mountains.

passages.title: The Zeppelin Crash
passages.text:
So those hermit mages sent you? How can I be sure that I can trust you?

I suppose I can use the help. There's not much here a mage would be interested in, anyway.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Dreadwatch Outpost
passages.text:
I'm not gonna lie to you, <name>. What I'm about to ask you to do is suicide. Chance of failure is about 95%.

All communication from Dreadwatch Outpost has been severed. With the worgen constantly rushing us we have no means by which to get to Dreadwatch to check on our soldiers. I need you to head south to the outpost and check on our soldiers. I'll keep in contact through the Forsaken communication device - F.C.D. - from here on out.

KEEP CLEAR OF THE MAIN ROAD.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Dreadwatch Outpost
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. crackles with static.>

Dreadwatch is lost? This is bad, <name>. Real bad.

If Dreadwatch is compromised it means we've lost Gilneas City.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Rutsak's Guard
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. hums.>

Our next outpost is Rutsak's Guard, located due east of Dreadwatch. Make your way to Rutsak's while avoiding the worgen rushers, <name>. You don't want to deal with those monsters by yourself.

If you make it there in one piece, look for Captain Rutsak.

Just be prepared for the worst.

passages.title: Break in Communications: Rutsak's Guard
passages.text:
Th... Af... After we lost Gilneas City, the port fell.

HU... HUM... HUMANS ARE HERE! Reinforcements from Stormwind! They slaughtered my men. Left me alive to witness their strength. To tell high command... To tell them that the 7th Legion are here...

passages.title: Liquid Gold
passages.text:
As the Scourge swept through Stratholme like a plague, the Knights of the Silver Hand manufactured holy water to use against the invaders. They stored it inside small crates along with other vital supplies, and distributed them throughout the city. Unfortunately, the citizens turned into Scourge reinforcements before the supplies could ever be used!

These supply crates will prove extremely useful to our efforts. Bring me a vial of Stratholme Holy Water, we need to have it replicated in mass quantities.

passages.title: Liquid Gold
passages.text:
Is that the vial of Stratholme Holy Water?

Wait, is that just regular water? Don't play games with ol' Stonebruiser!

passages.title: Liquid Gold
passages.text: Excellent! I think the holy water will prove devastating in large volumes.

passages.title: Argent Reinforcements
passages.text:
The Scourge have some sort of ward in place that's preventing me from opening a portal so that our reinforcements can help us take the city! It's like a neverending screaming inside of my head! Agh!

I'm doing all I can to retain my sanity from that noise with this barrier. My best guess is that the banshees are maintaining the defense. If you could bring me some of their essences, I think I can use them to counteract the ward and get our boys in here!

passages.title: Argent Reinforcements
passages.text: Were you able to obtain the essences? Be careful, they're deadly spellcasters.

passages.title: Argent Reinforcements
passages.text:
Oh my... the banshees are very tortured souls indeed. Merely holding their essence is emotionally painful...

Enough of that for now. I'll get to work on counteracting their magic, then we'll have a portal up and running in no time. Stratholme will be ours soon, I just know it.

passages.title: Vengeance for Our Soldiers
passages.text:
7th Legion... They rushed us in the dead of the night. Their captain barked orders as the submariners slaughtered my men. Then he came to me, put his face in mine, and said something I'll never forget:

"The name's Master Sergeant Pietro Zaren, officer in the 7th Legion. When you see your soldiers being slaughtered in your nightmares - if you even still dream - remember my name and tremble."

Avenge my soldiers! Kill the 7th Legion occupying the Cathedral Quarter of Gilneas City, southwest of here.

passages.title: Vengeance for Our Soldiers
passages.text:
Though we were shamed in battle, the enemy was not victorious. I will not soon forget this, <name>.

If I make it back to Silverpine I will likely retire from the service. War is not in my blood.

passages.title: On Whose Orders?
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. buzzes.>

The 7th Legion are an elite special ops regiment. They've been there, behind the scenes, for almost every major offensive and military engagement the Alliance has ever done. This is bad news. How did they get past our warships? And on whose orders are they here?

We need to get our hands on their orders. This Pietro character will undoubtedly have vital information. Find him at the Cathedral Quarter in Gilneas City and take him out. Search his corpse for clues.

passages.title: On Whose Orders?
passages.text: Status?

passages.title: On Whose Orders?
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. crackles with electricity.>

An Alliance armada is en route? How could this have happened?

<Forward Commander Onslaught cuts out for a moment. You hear worgen howling in the background.>

You've got to hurry, <name>. We're being overrun up here at Forward Command.

passages.title: Gidwin Goldbraids
passages.text:
I love my boys, don't get me wrong. But I TOLD them that I needed FIVE MINUTES to water and brush the horses, and what did they do? They made a stupid bet with each other and ran off! I should have known better... this always happens.

Gidwin's the short one. He headed north, along the river. If you're headed that direction, would you tell him to come back? We've got to get to Light's Hope Chapel, and I'm not against leaving without him.

passages.title: Gidwin Goldbraids
passages.text:
Tarenar?  Is that you?

Whoever you are, would you mind helping me out of this thing?

passages.title: Just Encased
passages.text:
You should have seen me fight! I must have killed six of those beasts, when...

Oh wait, you can count the bodies, can't you? OK, fine. I killed four of them, when the fifth one shot me with this web. To make things even worse... when he blasted me with web juice, my mouth was open!

I can't seem to break these webs, and I doubt you'll be able to, either. No, you'll have to get some of the stomach juice from those undead spider-things. That'll do the trick.

passages.title: Just Encased
passages.text: Oh boy... Fiona is going to be madder than a wet harpy.  You'd better hurry.

passages.title: Just Encased
passages.text:
You're back?!  Thank the Light!

Before you throw that acid on me, I need to ask: Are you the guy who was here before, or are you one of those eight-legged cowards?  I need to know whether or not I should smack you on my way out.

passages.title: Tarenar Sunstrike
passages.text:
As soon as we stopped, they made a bet about "who could kill the most undead in five minutes."

It's been an hour, and I'm still waiting for them to come back.

I saw Tarenar run off to the southeast. Unfortunately, I can't leave the caravan here by itself. If you end up traveling in that direction, could you find him and send him back to me?

passages.title: Tarenar Sunstrike
passages.text: I've found them, <race>.  The Scourge.  How I've longed for this day.

passages.title: What I Do Best
passages.text:
I remember when I was young, I would sneak off into the Ghostlands and just beat up zombies for hours on end. Nobody even PAID me. I just did it.

Now, look in front of you. Those are some serious zombies. I was just about to start beating them up, too. Care to join me?

passages.title: What I Do Best
passages.text:
Five should be good enough.

Yikes, look at the time!  I need to head back to camp.

passages.title: Onward, to Light's Hope Chapel
passages.text:
Now that the boys are back, we can head out. You headed east?

Please, join us! I insist! Yesterday, we were in the Menders' Stead, and I was telling Tarenar, "We have two paladins and a shopkeeper, but you know what we really need? A <class>!"

Don't look at me that way! I'm serious! Come on, hop in the cart.

passages.title: Onward, to Light's Hope Chapel
passages.text:
Hope the ride wasn't too bumpy for you.

Have a look around the tower while the horses rest.  It's no Light's Hope Chapel, but I'm sure you can find some way to keep yourself busy.

passages.title: The Maw of Iso'rath
passages.text:
We are ready to attack the beast. First, we need to destroy it's tentacles, then Yevaa will perform a ritual to summon a powerful fire elemental that we will drop into its maw.

I want you to fly out with our first group attack. Hold steady until an opportunity presents itself, then join the battle with the rest of the shaman in cutting the tentacles down.

Take any one of the gryphons when you're ready to join the assault.

passages.title: The Maw of Iso'rath
passages.text:
The tentacles swept us off of our gryphons as well! They were far more nimble than we anticipated.

No matter. We were prepared for this possibility. I can summon the elemental from here if you can keep me safe.

passages.title: The Worldbreaker
passages.text: There's no time! Deathwing struck before we could form against him. If you do not stop him, the Earthen Ring will end this day!

passages.title: The Worldbreaker
passages.text: You're awake! Thank the elements. I'd almost lost all hope.

passages.title: Nightmare
passages.text:
Iso'rath's brain is revealed! The shaman you've saved should keep you somewhat safe amidst his defenses.

Strike at the brain and destroy Iso'rath!

passages.title: Nightmare
passages.text: You saved many of my closest allies today, <name>. I can only imagine what horrors you witnessed within Iso'rath, but you have the thanks of all of the Earthen Ring.

passages.title: Traveling Companions
passages.text:
While we're waiting here at this tower, we might as well see if anybody else is headed to Light's Hope Chapel. The more, the merrier, I say!

Ask around to see if anybody wants to join us on our trip. I'm sure you can find somebody who's headed to Light's Hope.

passages.title: Traveling Companions
passages.text: Any luck?

passages.title: Traveling Companions
passages.text:
Argus Highbeacon... that old guy on the top of the tower?  Great!

A man his age must have been in the Argent Crusade for a long time.  Maybe he can put in the good word for us at Light's Hope.

passages.title: Little Pamela
passages.text:
The battle for Darrowshire still haunts me, <race>. I wake up in cold sweats, convinced that I'm still there; that it is happening all over again.

I've coped with the loss of my comrades, but the loss of my family members is still cripplingly painful. One of my kin lost during the attack was my young niece, Pamela.

If you are brave enough to enter Darrowshire, will you search for any sign of Pammy? Darrowshire's ruins are due south of here.

passages.title: Little Pamela
passages.text: Hello.  I'm Pamela, what's your name?

passages.title: Pamela's Doll
passages.text:
My auntie Marlene told me to stay here in our house because my father had to go and fight. My father's the bravest man in the whole world!

But I've been here for a long time, and he hasn't come for me. Sometimes bad people come and whisper to me and I want my dad to make them go away, but he's not here!

And sometimes when it gets dark I want to play with my doll but I can't because I left it in town.

Will you find my doll for me?

passages.title: Pamela's Doll
passages.text: Did you find my doll?

passages.title: Pamela's Doll
passages.text: You found it!  You found my doll!  Oh, thank you!

passages.title: Marauders of Darrowshire
passages.text:
I require a rare reagent for the powerful spell I intend to cast: skulls from the scourge who took part in the battle of Darrowshire.

Take this crystal and hunt scourge champions for their skulls. The crystal is enchanted; if a champion took part in the battle, then when you pass the crystal over its skull it will resonate. Bring me those resonating skulls.

Go, <name>. You'll find scourge champions in the Fungal Vale to the north. Go.

passages.title: Marauders of Darrowshire
passages.text: Do you have the skulls?  They are critical for my spell, which will give us the chance to save Darrowshire.  Maybe.

passages.title: Marauders of Darrowshire
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  Are you certain you haven't done this before?

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: I sense a strong power calling to me from the ruins. Can you check again on that southern battle site for me? I'm certain that there's something there.

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: The Wavespeaker was right. There's something here.

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: I sense a strong power calling to me from the ruins. Can you check again on that southern battle site for me? I'm certain that there's something there.

passages.title: The Call of the Blade
passages.text: The Wavespeaker was right. There's something here.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text:
We've defeated the enemy's forces here, <name>. But Hyjal is not the only place where our foes are moving against us.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Naraat the Earthspeaker at the Eastern Earthshrine in Stormwind City for further instructions.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text:
We've defeated the enemy's forces here, <name>. But Hyjal is not the only place where our foes are moving against us.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Farseer Krogar at the Western Earthshrine in Orgrimmar for further instructions.

passages.title: The Battle Is Won, The War Goes On
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: What Tomorrow Brings
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. buzzes.>

Look around the Cathedral Quarter. There should be a telescope nearby that the 7th Legion uses for spying. Find it and use it to scout the harbor. We need to find out how the 7th Legion got past our fleet.

Hurry, <name>. We can't hold these beasts back much longer.

What does tomorrow bring?

passages.title: What Tomorrow Brings
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. crackles with electricity.>

TORPEDOED! We had everything at the water line covered, but nothing below the line. They must have snuck in beneath our defenses and then blown our warships to smithereens.

And now the rest of the Alliance fleet is nearly here...

passages.title: A Man Named Godfrey
passages.text:
Lord Vincent Godfrey spent his life defending the kingdom of Gilneas. When the worgen curse ravaged this land, Godfrey was one of the first Gilneans to take up arms against the beasts. It is said that upon discovering that his king was afflicted by the curse, Godfrey took his own life. He would rather be dead than serve the very creatures that he had defended his home against.

We are going to give him a second chance, <name>. Together we will battle southeast towards Tempest's Reach to collect his corpse.

passages.title: A Man Named Godfrey
passages.text: Lord Vincent Godfrey. The name itself evokes feelings of dread in the hearts of worgen.

passages.title: A Man Named Godfrey
passages.text: Here we are, <name>. He is a little rotted, but no worse for the wear. We must hurry before the Alliance finds us!

passages.title: Bloodfen Feathers
passages.text:
Are you startled by Brogg's presence here, little <race>? Don't worry. Goblins at Mudsprocket are Brogg's friends and you can be, too.

Brogg left Brackenwall Village when new overlord not take revenge against black dragonkin for destroying old home and killing many of Brogg's old friends. Brogg come here to lay friends spirits to rest and avenge them, but Brogg need help preparing. For ritual, Brogg need feathers with strong magic, like ones worn by raptors at Bloodfen Burrow to the west of town.

passages.title: Bloodfen Feathers
passages.text:
<Brogg looks at you hopefully.>

You bring Brogg feathers?

passages.title: Bloodfen Feathers
passages.text:
<Brogg accepts the feathers.>

Brogg pleased with these feathers. Very strong magic. Brogg not know what raptors do to give feathers power, but raptor feathers always best for ritual.

passages.title: Banner of the Stonemaul
passages.text:
When the dragons came and took over Brogg's old home, Stonemaul ogres fled and left everything behind, including clan's banner.

Brogg knows banner was kept deep in Stonemaul ogre mound, but these days it's called Den of Flame. Brogg must have clan banner to get his revenge on dragons who killed his friends.

Brogg's clan's old mound, Den of Flame, is northwest of Mudsprocket and crawling with dragonkin. Banner will be deep inside the cave. Be careful, <name>.

passages.title: Banner of the Stonemaul
passages.text: You bring Stonemaul banner?

passages.title: Banner of the Stonemaul
passages.text: You have Brogg's thanks, <name>. Brogg has big plans for clan banner.

passages.title: The Essence of Enmity
passages.text:
To make the totem Brogg will need for his ritual, he must use the essences of the creatures who killed his friends. The hate and anger of Brogg's enemies will fuel the magic of his vengeance.

Track down Firemane ash tails, scouts, or scalebanes and use Brogg's totem on their corpses. Only when the dragonkin die will they give up their essences.

The creatures you seek swarm over the Den of Flame to the northwest and the Stonemaul Ruins to the north.

passages.title: The Essence of Enmity
passages.text: Do you have the essences? Brogg must have them to avenge his friends!

passages.title: The Essence of Enmity
passages.text: You have Brogg's thanks, <name>. Once Brogg adds their magic to the totem, it will be able to redeem the spirits of Brogg's fallen friends.

passages.title: Spirits of Stonemaul Hold
passages.text:
Brogg has completed the totem that will put the spirits of his friends to rest. When the dragonkin came, they killed all Stonemaul who did not flee. Brogg fled with Overlord Mok'Morokk, hoping to lead a counterattack with other Stonemaul survivors.

The counterattack never came and the spirits of the Stonemaul dead still haunt Brogg and the others. Take this totem north to Stonemaul Ruins and use it near ogre skeletons to draw the spirit to you. Defeat the spirit to give it rest with its bones.

passages.title: Spirits of Stonemaul Hold
passages.text: Brogg must know, have you brought peace to the violent spirits of the Stonemaul?

passages.title: Spirits of Stonemaul Hold
passages.text: Brogg thanks you for your help, although he knows Overlord Mok'Morokk never will. At least surviving Stonemaul can finally focus on problems with the living and leave dead where they belong. Only one thing remains for Brogg to do.

passages.title: Catch a Dragon by the Tail
passages.text:
With the zeppelin crash delaying supplies, we've run out of medicines and bandages.

We're making use of what we can, but between all the insects, the injuries, and the enemies we're encountering here, I can barely keep up! I've found one herb that seems to help heal wounds and dull pain, but it, too, is in short supply.

It's called wyrmtail, and it's abundant in the Dragonmurk and Wyrmbog areas east of town. The plants themselves are made of coiled stalks, and seem to pulsate when you look at them.

passages.title: Catch a Dragon by the Tail
passages.text: Did you find any of the wyrmtail?

passages.title: Catch a Dragon by the Tail
passages.text: Thank you! This will help keep our guys going out in the field until Moxie returns with the rest of the supplies from the zeppelin crash.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
Onyxia's brood has been scattered across the Dragonmurk. It is imperative that no more whelps be permitted to hatch.

Make haste to Wyrmbog in the south of Dustwallow Marsh. Surely, she has made her lair there. Track down the evil dragon's eggs and destroy them.

We will never reclaim Stonemaul Village if the surrounding area remains a breeding ground.

As for Mok'Morokk... I have other plans for the sod.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
You must hurry to the Dragonmurk, <name>. With Onyxia's eggs riddled around the Wyrmbog, we face overwhelming numbers unless something is done quickly.

Destroy her eggs! Don't let the black dragon plague spread across our homeland!

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
Splendid! It will be sometime before Onyxia can produce more eggs.

On behalf of my people, I thank you, <name>.

I have asked much of you so far. Perhaps you can do the Stonemaul Clan one last service.

Mok'Morokk is not fit to lead us. Tharg would make an excellent leader but is hindered by his injuries and age. Drive Mok'Morokk from this place by force. Only then can we appoint a new leader to return us to our proper home in the south.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
Stonemaul Village was invaded by the brood of Onyxia. But why would the daughter of the black dragonlord, Deathwing, descend upon our lands?

This is most troubling. Surely, Onyxia was driven here for a purpose beyond laying siege to a small band of ogres.

Notify Mok'Morokk at once! Action must be taken.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text: Why you tell me 'bout dragons? Me no like dragons. Me like it here. No dragons here.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text: You leave me alone now. Go tell Draz'Zilb we stay here. No black dragon here.

passages.title: The Brood of Onyxia
passages.text:
That lazy coward!

Mok'Morokk displayed strength when Rexxar was our leader. But soon after Rexxar's departure Mok'Morokk fell prey to temptations of power. Rather than lead, he demanded. He does not serve his people but rather expects us to serve him.

Something must be done.

passages.title: A City Under Siege
passages.text:
We will never control the Eastern Plaguelands if we do not control Stratholme. Not only is it a point of incredible strategic importance, it also houses our enemies' leaders - Balnazzar and Lord Aurius Rivendare. Their Risen and Scourge armies threaten to erase all the progress we've made.

The Argent Crusade is well-suited to this task. Travel west through Stratholme's main gate and speak with Packmaster Stonebruiser. He will direct you further.

passages.title: A City Under Siege
passages.text: What a relief it is to see an able-bodied soldier that's on our side! There's plenty for ye to do around here, <race>.

passages.title: Resistance is Futile
passages.text:
<The F.C.D. buzzes.>

This is Commander Lorna Crowley of the Gilneas Liberation Front. If you are hearing this message then you know that the Alliance once again controls Gilneas. Lay down your weapons and surrender. Failure to comply will result in your death.

Our forces have locked on to your position and will arrive shortly. Resistance is futile.

passages.title: Resistance is Futile
passages.text: Surrender? Coward talk...

passages.title: Resistance is Futile
passages.text: No time to bask in the battle glory, <name>. We have a job to do. I have no doubt more of those beasts are on the way.

passages.title: A Grim Connection
passages.text:
I've spoken with Inspector Tarem regarding the evidence you gathered from the ruins of the Shady Rest Inn. He seems certain that the hoofprints and the shield you found there point to the Grimtotem clan of tauren.

With reports of Grimtotem activity on the rise in the marsh, this has to be more than a mere coincidence. I'm sending you to speak with Captain Darill, who is something of an expert on the Grimtotems. Follow the road north out of town to North Point tower. It's the second outpost on the road.

passages.title: A Grim Connection
passages.text: Captain Vimes thinks the Grimtotems are behind the destruction of the Shady Rest Inn? They wouldn't have been first on my list of suspects, but if Captain Vimes sent you here to follow up on a lead, he must have his reasons. Regardless, the Grimtotems have been a thorn in our side for some time and we're always glad to have the extra help.

passages.title: Tabetha's Assistance
passages.text:
I can't spare any men to help search for a second Grimtotem outpost, but I think I know of someone who might be able to help you.

Deep in the Quagmire, to the south, there is a small farmstead owned by Tabetha. She may seem little more than an old hermit, but the truth is that she's a mage and scryer of some renown. Follow the road south to her farm and seek her help in finding the culprits responsible for the massacre at the Shady Rest Inn.

passages.title: Tabetha's Assistance
passages.text: So you want me to scry for Grimtotems, eh? And what will you say when I tell you there's no need?

passages.title: Justice for the Hyals
passages.text:
Although these Grimtotems were simply a nuisance to me, Captain Vimes will want to know of your deeds. Bring him the news that you have tracked down and dealt with those responsible for the burning of the Shady Rest Inn.

It's too late to save Jim Hyal's family, but perhaps the Grimtotems will think twice before attacking anyone connected to Theramore.

passages.title: Justice for the Hyals
passages.text:
<The captain listens to your report intently.>

We have avenged James and his family, but not even that can restore what was destroyed.

passages.title: Tipping the Balance
passages.text:
<Harrison grins.>

That's it, <name>. The pieces we need are hidden in these statues!

They look to be a bit off balance as is. Maybe just a little nudge...

I must say, your field work is coming along nicely. If you applied yourself, you could make a fine archaeologist one day.

passages.title: Tipping the Balance
passages.text: Talk about bringing the house down...

passages.title: Zaeldarr the Outcast
passages.text:
Can you believe that, after all the trouble we have in the Plaguelands... we have to worry about thieves too? And not just normal thieves, troll thieves.

And not just normal troll thieves. Dead troll thieves!

They're led by this big, dead troll named Zaeldarr the Outcast, and they come here at night and steal bodies from our graveyards, then take them back to their evil, dead troll hideout--the Undercroft to the southwest.

Go there and take out Zaeldarr, <name>. I'm sick to death of his mischief!

passages.title: Zaeldarr the Outcast
passages.text: Did you find the hideout, <name>?  Did you take care of Zaeldarr?

passages.title: Zaeldarr the Outcast
passages.text: Great, you got him!  And I hope you taught his gang a lesson too!

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text:
We find ourselves in a much better position against our enemies in Vashj'ir than before you arrived. Don't get me wrong, your aid is still needed here, but perhaps other fronts are in an even more urgent situation.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Farseer Krogar at the Western Earthshrine in Orgrimmar for further instructions.

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text:
We find ourselves in a much better position against our enemies in Vashj'ir than before you arrived. Don't get me wrong, your aid is still needed here, but perhaps other fronts are in an even more urgent situation.

I've been informed that our allies in the Earthen Ring have put out a call for aid in a matter I've been assured is most critical.

Speak to Earthspeaker Naraat at the Eastern Earthshrine in Stormwind City for further instructions.

passages.title: The War Has Many Fronts
passages.text: Your aid is most timely, <name>.

passages.title: The False Warchief
passages.text:
Rend Blackhand was the son of an Orc Warchief. His father was slain by Orgrim Doomhammer, who became the new Warchief over the young orc. Rend now stands as the supposed leader of a false Horde of Blackrock orcs, backed by Nefarian and his army of dragons.

The fool claims that the Horde is also his by birthright, and threatens to take it by force! We cannot allow this to occur in light of his master's influence. Find him in the Upper Spire and bring an end to the false warchief, <class>.

passages.title: The False Warchief
passages.text:
You saw Nefarian when you fought Rend?

<Acride sighs.>

I wish I had accompanied you, then. I could have faced him unaware, outside his lair...but no matter. Nefarian will die by my claw.

You've done well.

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text:
Heya, <name>, Kelsey Steelspark down in Tanaris left a message for you. She says that the gnomes down there in Gadgetzan heard about what you've been doing up here.

Anyway, the Cataclysm hit them hard, too. Not as hard as us, but I'm certain they could use your help.

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text: Greetings and salutations, friend. Welcome to Tanaris!

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text:
Heya, <name>, Megs Dreadshredder down in Tanaris left a message for you. She says that the goblins down there in Gadgetzan heard about what you've been doing up here.

Anyway, the Cataclysm hit them hard, too. Not as hard as us, but I'm certain they could use your help.

Besides, that Megs is a hottie!

passages.title: Tanaris is Calling
passages.text: Well hello there, <class>. Welcome to Tanaris!

passages.title: The Trek Continues
passages.text:
I believe the horses are ready. Argus Highbeacon, the gentleman who works with the Argent Crusade, spoke with me earlier. I understand he will be coming with us... that's great! I'll make room for him.

I know that you are busy, so there's no hurry. Whenever you're ready, hop into the caravan, and we will proceed to the next tower.

passages.title: The Trek Continues
passages.text: Once we get to Light's Shield Tower, the boys can head over to Light's Hope Chapel.  It's close enough that they can walk.

passages.title: The Trek Continues
passages.text: We've enjoyed having you ride with us, <name>.  Hopefully, once Gidwin and Tarenar join the Argent Crusade, we can continue to travel together.

passages.title: Honor and Strength
passages.text:
My name is Vex'tul, and I have watched you fight, <race>. You are strong.

You killed my master, Zaeldarr, but this does not bother me. I value strength over any loyalty that I held for him. I value strength over anything else.

Prove to me one final time your strength, <race>. Do so, and I will lend you MY strength for whatever purpose you may desire.

passages.title: Honor and Strength
passages.text: Honor means nothing.  Strength is everything.

passages.title: Honor and Strength
passages.text:
Yes, you are indeed strong... and I submit to you.

I will join you and your friend, the worgen.  My strength is yours.

passages.title: Boys Will Be Boys
passages.text:
As soon as we arrived here at Light's Shield Tower, those two lunkhead paladins ran off to Light's Hope Chapel. It's still a ways away, but if we're going to follow Argus along his tour of the towers, this is about as close as we're going to get.

Check in on them and make sure they're alright? I know they can handle themselves, but still, it'd make me feel better to know that you were watching over them while I'm stuck here with the caravan.

passages.title: Boys Will Be Boys
passages.text:
I can't believe it.  We're literally FEET away from becoming sworn members of the Argent Crusade.

We'd be in there already if it weren't for Tarenar's dallying.  If he doesn't quit chatting with the locals soon, I'm going to head in there myself.

passages.title: An Opportune Alliance
passages.text:
With your contributions to the food stores, my current assignment is complete.

I will be heading north, to the Plaguewood, next. I understand you may be headed in the same direction.

Do you mind if I join you on the road?

I will head northwest, to Eastwall Tower. If you're interested in teaming up, you can meet up with me there.

passages.title: An Opportune Alliance
passages.text:
You brought us a shaman!  From the Earthen Ring, no less!

I have no idea how we'll fit him in the caravan, but we'll find a way.  Welcome aboard, Rimblat Earthshatter!

passages.title: Smokey and the Bandage
passages.text:
Hey there! Interested in makin' a buck?

I need to get a bandage. Well, actually, I got a friend who needs to get a bandage. Well actually... let's just say it's complicated, but if you go get this bandage, you make money. And so do I. And my friend. Possibly other people.

Stephen Browman used to own the mill to the north, now he's dead. A zombie. The guy at the top wants to have the wrappings from Browman's body.

What's the matter, you don't like money?

passages.title: Smokey and the Bandage
passages.text: You've been fightin' undead.  Did ya find Browman?

passages.title: Smokey and the Bandage
passages.text: Well well well!  Someone who goes and gets things done!  Here's your cut, chief.  I'll be seein' you around.

passages.title: Argent Call: Northdale
passages.text:
Tyrosus has given us our next task: slaying more undead in Northdale. Gidwin is excited to move forward, but I think we should show a little more caution.

Let's meet up with Fiona. She should be at the next tower by now... Eastwall Tower, I think it's called. It's close by, to the northwest of Light's Hope. We can rest there, and plan our attack on Northdale.

passages.title: Argent Call: Northdale
passages.text:
Hello, <name>!  Glad to see you've rejoined the caravan!

Tarenar and Gidwin arrived here before you.  Tarenar's just right there, and Gidwin's... well... he's in a little bit of a mood right now.  I think he's in the tower.

passages.title: Friends on The Other Side
passages.text:
I come with news from Blackrock Spire. We have a new visitor. His name is Acride.

He seeks people of strength, people of intelligence, of dexterity. You ought to go to Blackrock Spire and speak with him.

passages.title: Friends on The Other Side
passages.text:
Hello, what is your business in a place like this?

I'm sorry, who sent you? I'm afraid I've never heard of such a dwarf.

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text:
It is no secret that we aren't fans of the orcs in Blackrock Mountain, but we do carefully watch their every move. Nothing happens in that Mountain without me knowing about it, <class>.

Recently, a different sort of orc came into Blackrock. He resides just inside Blackrock Spire, and I know he's somehow planning to overthrow Nefarian and his whole army of orcs. Normally I wouldn't trust their kind, but we share a common goal for the time being. Find him, he's called Acride.

passages.title: A Potential Ally
passages.text:
Hello, what is your business in a place like this?

So Overseer Oilfist sent you? Listen carefully, we have much to discuss in little time.

passages.title: Blackrock Anomaly
passages.text:
There is an orc inside Blackrock Spire much unlike the others. He speaks with the intelligence and wisdom of one beyond his appeared years, and does not fight against our soldiers like the others do.

You must travel northwest to Blackrock Spire and find this orc, known only to us as Acride. Perhaps he is the key to stopping the orcish army. Perhaps we can stop Nefarian before it is too late...

passages.title: Blackrock Anomaly
passages.text:
Hello, what is your business in a place like this?

So you come at the will of Miss Brightwing, do you? Very interesting indeed.

passages.title: Breaking the Barrier
passages.text:
While Godfrey and I make preparations for our assault upon Gilneas, I want you to lead our attack upon Ambermill, directly east of here.

The former Dalaran magi of Ambermill have erected a magical barrier that somehow cloaks them from vision. They currently reside within some type of pocket dimension, awaiting orders from the Alliance to begin their attack. We must prevent their assault by making a pre-emptive strike. Venture to Ambermill and find information that would grant us access to the mages.

passages.title: Breaking the Barrier
passages.text: Have you found anything yet?

passages.title: Breaking the Barrier
passages.text:
Clever mages. The codex is sealed by a magical ward.

Pity that they weren't clever enough to realize that former archmages of Dalaran are now Forsaken.

passages.title: Unyielding Servitors
passages.text:
The magi of Ambermill have employed foul magic to keep us away. Elemental servitors, created with immunities that we cannot breach, protect their territory.

Venture east to Ambermill and slay the unyielding elemental servitors that guard the town and recover their cores. Bring their cores back to me so that I may devise a method by which we are able to destroy them all!

passages.title: Unyielding Servitors
passages.text: Have you recovered the servitor cores?

passages.title: Unyielding Servitors
passages.text: Well done, <name>. The praise the Banshee Queen lavishes upon you is apparently not unfounded.

passages.title: Relios the Relic Keeper
passages.text:
The Dark Lady is correct in her assertion that I am able to unlock the codex. Unfortunately, I need a signet ring from a Dalaran archmage to do it. My own ring was taken when I died many years ago, but there still might be a way.

While Dalaran has floated away, the outskirts of the city remain. Far to the east lie the ruins of Dalaran. It is there that you will find an archmage known as Relios. "Take" his signet ring and bring it back to me.

You may use the portal behind me to get to the crater.

passages.title: Relios the Relic Keeper
passages.text: Did you recover a Dalaran Archmage's Signet Ring?

passages.title: Relios the Relic Keeper
passages.text:
Perfect. I hope this wasn't too much trouble to come by, <name>. Relios was a pupil of mine back when I was a mortal man thereby making him a competent and formidable adversary. I suppose I could have warned you ahead of time.

Now, let us see the ring.

There we are...

passages.title: Ley Energies
passages.text: The arcane remnant pulses with strange energy. Perhaps you should search for more remnants. Surely Dalar would be interested in such a find.

passages.title: Ley Energies
passages.text: What's that you've got there, <name>?

passages.title: Ley Energies
passages.text: Smart boy! I can most definitely use these arcane remnants in my studies. Indeed, Dalaran was built upon a massive ley line. It's no wonder, then, that such things exist at the crater.

passages.title: Out of the Ziggurat
passages.text:
It is time that I asked a favor of you, <name>.

Far to the north of Eastwall Tower, hidden among the hills, is the Mossflayer capital city of Zul'Mashar. It was here that I was born, and here that I died.

The traitor, Thresh'jin, sits atop Zul'Mashar's ziggurat. It was my every right to be there, but he took the seat from me with treachery and deceit. He is not strong. He is weak.

I will meet you in Zul'Mashar, and we will kill him. Your strength and mine. Together.

passages.title: Out of the Ziggurat
passages.text: I have waited long for this day.

passages.title: Out of the Ziggurat
passages.text: My duty is not over yet.  In many ways, this was the easy step.

passages.title: Practical Vengeance
passages.text:
Under ordinary circumstances I am not a vengeful man. In fact, I am somewhat of a pragmatist. You see, practicality is a paradoxical notion to vengeance. Most revenge ploys are highly impractical.

BUT... in this case - since you're already going to the ruins of Dalaran - you might as well kill every Dalaran affiliated human that you see. The reasons that I want them dead range from hatred to anger to betrayal, but I assure you they are all legitimate gripes. Do this for me and I will pay you handsomely.

passages.title: Practical Vengeance
passages.text: I thought for sure that with the death of a dozen of my most hated enemies I would feel a great burden lifted from my shoulders. Sadly, I do not feel a thing. Perhaps I am a psychopath.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text:
I'm glad you're back! Saving the world or something, I'm sure.

I was dispatched to establish relations with the red dragons in the area, but I'm finding this bunch somewhat less accommodating than the ones at Wyrmrest were. I have, however, been told that you are the type that solves problems.

A problem solver as it were.

Care to take a crack at earning a bit of trust with Lirastrasza at Vermillion Redoubt to the southwest? Anything that might soften her up a bit for me would be lovely.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I believe Lira wanted a word with you.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I'm glad Lira didn't scare you off. I won't say her concerns aren't warranted, but we have a common enemy. She is perhaps a bit overzealous.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text:
Good. You're back. Saving the world again I assume.

I was dispatched to establish relations with the red dragons in the area, but I'm finding this bunch somewhat less accommodating than the ones at Wyrmrest were. I have, however, been told that you are the type that solves problems.

A problem solver as it were.

I need you to gain the trust of Lirastrasza at Vermillion Redoubt to the southwest. Our association with the Dragonmaw has complicated things, but I'm hoping you can ease relations.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I believe Lira wanted a word with you.

passages.title: Warm Welcome
passages.text: I'm glad Lira didn't scare you off. I won't say her concerns aren't warranted, but we have a common enemy. She is perhaps a bit overzealous.

passages.title: Impatience
passages.text:
Damn that dwarf. He's always getting me in trouble with Fiona. Look at her! She won't even TALK to me!

I'm going to stay here and try to mend my friendship with our worgen friend. Would you mind going out and making sure Gidwin is alright? I'm sure he's fine; he knows how to take care of himself. He headed north, and he can't have gone far.

passages.title: Impatience
passages.text: Northdale is home to a few ghosts and banshees.  Nothing ol' Giddy can't handle.

passages.title: Impatience
passages.text:
You didn't see him?  Where could he have gone then?

His... his prayer book?  Why would he leave that behind?

Oh...

By the Light, what have I done?

passages.title: Nobody to Blame but Myself
passages.text:
This is my fault. I... I ignored his warnings, his complaints, everything. I couldn't help myself - I saw those Scourge just beyond the tower, and I... I HAD to go kill them.

Argus says that Gidwin was taken northwest, and that's our only lead, so that's where we'll head.

Northdale and the Argent Crusade be damned! We're getting Gidwin back from those Scourge trash.

passages.title: Nobody to Blame but Myself
passages.text: We have no time, <name>!  We must press on!

passages.title: Nobody to Blame but Myself
passages.text:
Time is wasting, <name>.  Every minute we waste gives the Scourge another chance to kill Gidwin.  If he isn't dead already.

Not that I think he is.  Giddy may be a stick-in-the-mud, but when it comes down to it, he can swing the Light like a champion.

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text: As with any offensive, you first need to soften them up. We've been having a heck of a time getting in there. But someone like you... well, let's just say I have no doubt in my mind that you can get into the Twilight Gate to the southwest and teach the Bloodeye Clan ogres and ettins a thing or two!

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text:
What's the matter? You Alliance boys don't have the stomach to get the job done?

<Kurdran gives you a wink.>

Need me to fly over there and kill them for you?

passages.title: Ogres & Ettins
passages.text: That's the spirit, lad! Today's already shaping up to be a good one.

passages.title: Even Dragons Bleed
passages.text:
I won't be so impolite as to refuse your aid if you're offering it.

We're locked in constant battle with the twilight drakes and dragons to the south. Our strikes have not been entirely without success, but the dragons coming out of Grim Batol have been breathing some kind of corruption upon us that takes time to cleanse.

Velastrasza and Baleflame are attending to our injured brothers. Go and see if you can be of help to them.

passages.title: Even Dragons Bleed
passages.text: Calen has become very trusting. It is not often that strangers are permitted within the redoubt.

passages.title: Life from Death
passages.text:
<race>, I have a task for you.

Take these ruby seeds and plant them at the corpses of any dragonkin that you come across. Twilight or Vermillion, whelping or dragon, it matters not. We need to see that their bodies are returned to the earth so that life can continue to flourish.

In death, there should always be new life. This may be our one consolation during times of war and great tragedy.

passages.title: Life from Death
passages.text: Have you done as I asked?

passages.title: Life from Death
passages.text: In this, we deny Deathwing the destruction that he so passionately seeks. In this, life continues.

passages.title: Encroaching Twilight
passages.text:
Fragile Twilight invaders litter the redoubt. They're pouring in from somewhere to the west.

There can be no mercy offered to them within this hallowed place. Whatever violence grips your moral heart, release it upon them.

passages.title: Encroaching Twilight
passages.text: You have a talent for killing I see. In times like these, that has its place.

passages.title: A Wolf in Bear's Clothing
passages.text:
These worgen take us for fools! One would think that only an idiot would mistake one of their druids in bear form as a real bear. Unfortunately, there are many idiots here at the Forsaken Front. We've already lost a few battalions to organized worgen bear attacks. Yes, it's even more idiotic than it sounds.

Directly east of here, heading towards Hillsbrad, you will find worgen druids roaming the woods, masquerading as bears. Kill them and make our southern supply line safe again.

passages.title: A Wolf in Bear's Clothing
passages.text: I only hope that we don't end up getting beat down by inconspicuous birds, cats and trees next... or seals. Could you imagine it?

passages.title: The Thrill of Discovery
passages.text:
What a find! And somehow it's all remained untouched by plunderers...

Listen, <name>. I need to document this site before we disturb anything. While I do, why don't you have a look around - you know, explore a bit. You've earned it.

Keep your eyes open for anything unusual.

Oh! And please... don't break anything, ok?

passages.title: The Thrill of Discovery
passages.text: Your exploration of the Chamber of the Stars has yielded more questions than answers...

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter I
passages.text:
<Sylvanas hands you the signet ring.>

Take the ring and make your way to Beren's Peril, southeast of here, located in a cave in the hills. Once there, search the cave for the portal to the pocket dimension that conceals the Ambermill magi.

I will communicate with you through your thoughts, <name>. Once you have reached the portal I will give you your marching orders.

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter I
passages.text: <The portal hums.>

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter I
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's voice invades your thoughts.>

Yes, this is it. Now run the ring along the runes of the portal and you should become attuned for transdimensional travel.

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter II
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's words float in your head.>

You are now ready to use the portal. Be warned, <name>, once you step through you will appear in another dimension at Ambermill. There will be a hundred, perhaps a thousand, magi waiting to kill you.

You must persevere and kill all in your path.

passages.title: Transdimensional Warfare: Chapter II
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen's voice invades your thoughts.>

Excellent work, <name>. Now to eject them into our waiting hands!

passages.title: Roots'll Do 'Er
passages.text:
Look here, mate. She's on her last legs! If me bird dies, I'm as good as worthless.

So make yerself useful. Here on the peninsula you can dig up thorny stankroots. Oh the smell will knock you on yer patoot but steeped in water it'll boil up into a right powerful cure-all.

Gather some while I defend me bird. An' hurry! You Alliance wanks don't have a reputation for timely intervention, right?

passages.title: Roots'll Do 'Er
passages.text: Didja get me roots, <class>? Well?

passages.title: Roots'll Do 'Er
passages.text: Oh, that's the stuff all right! Hope ya didn't eat any. Gives you the cramps something awful but it does wonders for birds.

passages.title: Under the Choking Sands
passages.text:
No... it cannot be.

Orsis is all but buried beneath the desert sands.

The enemy will pay for this.

But first we must aid my people. Quick, <name>. We do not have much time before the last of my brethren are buried alive!

passages.title: Under the Choking Sands
passages.text:
I thank you, <name>.  Orsis was punished for not joining the forces of Deathwing.

Prince Nadun has offered my people refuge in his city.  I must go there and tend the survivors.

passages.title: Wretched Hive of Scum and Villainy
passages.text:
<race>... please, I ask your help.

Something's happened to my people. Our commander, Ranger Lord Hawkspear, came upon an item of magical energy, and my friends, my family... they succumbed to its seductive power.

They're corrupted, <race>. All of them.

My Ellaria wouldn't want to live like that, nor would any of my brothers. Please, put them out of their misery. Quel'lithien Lodge is not far; it's just up the hill, to the northwest.

passages.title: Wretched Hive of Scum and Villainy
passages.text: You have no idea how difficult it was for me to pull myself away, <race>.  I nearly ended up one of them.

passages.title: Wretched Hive of Scum and Villainy
passages.text: Do not feel sorry for me.  Those were my friends that you saw at Quel'lithien Lodge, but they were already as good as dead.

passages.title: Blind Fury
passages.text:
Tarenar wasn't joking when he said that he didn't care about judgment and caution. He nearly took off that high elf's head as he ran into the Plaguewood, looking for Gidwin. You should go after him.

The Plaguewood is a big place, <name>. Good luck. I hope to see you <boys/three> come out of the woods in one piece.

passages.title: Blind Fury
passages.text:
I haven't found anything but brainless undead, and plenty of them.  I was just about to kill my way into Stratholme when you arrived.

Did you have any more success?

passages.title: Guardians of Stratholme
passages.text:
Baroness Anastar holds him? Here in the Plaguewood?

The Plaguewood is a big place... but we will find him. We WILL find Gidwin.

Immediately to our east and our west are a pair of necropoli that flank the entrance to Stratholme. Inside them, you will find a pair of death knights - Rivendare's lieutenants. I doubt either would have any use for a paladin hostage, but perhaps they will have some information on his location.

passages.title: Guardians of Stratholme
passages.text: We're getting close.  I only hope it's not too late.

passages.title: Guardians of Stratholme
passages.text: We've got to keep moving!  We're getting so very close!

passages.title: Augustus' Receipt Book
passages.text:
I'm ready for business! What do you want?

Oh wait... I can't open up shop without my receipt book. How am I to keep track of things without my receipt book?

I must have left it in town somewhere. I had a room in the inn... the book must be there.

Bring me my book. Please, bring it to me! Bring me my book and you'll see! I'll set up shop and you'll see that my prices are INSANE!

passages.title: Augustus' Receipt Book
passages.text: Do you have my receipt book?  I can't wait to get back to business!

passages.title: Augustus' Receipt Book
passages.text:
There it is!  And oh my!  I forgot how full it was!

This is a glorious day, <name>!  Stupendous!  Insanely good, I say!

passages.title: Just a Little Touched
passages.text:
I like to check in on Augustus in Terrordale every once in a while, just to make sure he's alright. Some of us undead cope with the plague better than others, I suppose.

Terrordale is west of here. Would you mind checking in on him for me?

passages.title: Just a Little Touched
passages.text: You've come to the right place, mister!  No place better than Terrordale, yes siree, that's right!  The jewel of Lordaeron!

passages.title: Any Portal in a Storm
passages.text:
Our friends in the Earthen Ring have been trying to open portals back to Stormwind, with no luck. But Thordun here tells me he might just have the key.

The crazed water elementals in the nearby Verrall River Delta have been sent into a frenzy. Thordun tells me we can channel their energy into a portal.

I don't understand all this elemental-claptrap, but I understand one thing: killin' elementals and takin' their whirlpool cores. Deliver them to Talaa in the courtyard!

passages.title: Any Portal in a Storm
passages.text: Hello, <class>. Kurdran tells me you've got a solution to getting this portal opened?

passages.title: Any Portal in a Storm
passages.text:
My word, <name>. These elemental energies are so powerful, so chaotic - no wonder the Twilight's Hammer has chosen to build their stronghold here!

I should be able to channel these energies into something more benign and productive though. Let's give it a try...

passages.title: The Perfect Poultice
passages.text:
Are you goin' by way of the Verrall river delta? I've got a tip that'll help your men here... and my bird!

When water elementals carve their way through rock, they create a peculiar kind of muck. It dries hard as stone but carries with it the rejuvenating power of water. You make a cast out of that muck and broken bones knit together like iron.

Bring some of that muck to Talaa, your shaman downstairs. She'll know what to do with it!

passages.title: The Perfect Poultice
passages.text: What is this I keep hearing about the muck of the Verrall River?

passages.title: The Perfect Poultice
passages.text:
Oh... mud. You brought me mud?

Wow - this stuff oozes with power! I see what Thordun was saying, now. I'll distribute this to all of the healers. Our wounded will be on their feet in no time!

passages.title: Cenarion Tenacity
passages.text:
Those druids never give up, I swear. I'd given up on the Plaguelands years ago, but the Cenarion Circle folks keep telling me that the land is not beyond hope.

The most recent visitor was a night elf, on her way to the Fungal Vale, to the north. She told me that these lands will make a full recovery, if we try hard enough. I'm not sure I believe her.

Do you buy this drivel? Maybe you and her should talk. She should still be up there.

passages.title: Cenarion Tenacity
passages.text:
I suppose I had better work on my stealth, if you were able to find me.

Are you interested in helping me heal the Plaguelands?

passages.title: Of No Consequence
passages.text:
Our forces in Pyrewood were recently taken by way of sneak attack. The 7th Legion managed to infiltrate the town with their scouts, ultimately decimating our troops.

The Dark Lady has tasked us with a rescue mission. We are to find survivors and get them out of Pyrewood safely. If any soldiers live they are likely worthless, but we do as the Dark Lady commands.

Let's get this nonsense over with, <name>. Pyrewood is directly southwest of the Forsaken Front.

passages.title: Of No Consequence
passages.text: The sooner we rescue survivors the sooner we can burn down the whole of Pyrewood.

passages.title: Of No Consequence
passages.text: What happened here today is between us. Say a word to anyone and you will find yourself in a corpse pit next to these poor fools.

passages.title: Lessons in Fear
passages.text:
Our enemies are becoming smarter - adapting to our tactics. Recently an attack was made upon Pyrewood Village, southwest of here. Our troops occupying the town were decimated, of course, but what made the attack especially interesting was the racial composition of the attacking force. No humans were used.

<Walden laughs.>

Rightfully, they fear being reanimated as Forsaken.

Let us teach the non-humans a lesson in fear. Together we will show them what happens to corpses that we cannot use.

passages.title: Lessons in Fear
passages.text: Pyrewood Village must be reduced to ashes and our enemies slain!

passages.title: Lessons in Fear
passages.text: I suspect we'll see fewer humans at the Battlefront. The risk for these cowards is too great.

passages.title: The Baroness' Missive
passages.text:
The note is from Baroness Anastari, and it describes a ritual that is about to happen in the Plaguewood's central slaughterhouse - just south of where Tarenar is at. This could be where they're holding Gidwin!

Tarenar will want to know about this... and quickly, before it's too late!

passages.title: The Baroness' Missive
passages.text: What?  Did you find something?

passages.title: The Baroness' Missive
passages.text:
This is it!  If this missive is to be believed, then he's literally right over this hill!

What are we waiting for, <name>?

passages.title: In Defense of the Redoubt
passages.text:
Calen sent word - the Twilight are within the redoubt!

If there will ever be a time when you can earn his favor, this is it!

passages.title: In Defense of the Redoubt
passages.text: I hope you're as tough as your gear suggests. The Twilight's Hammer have made their way within the redoubt somehow and I need someone to hunt them down.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text:
We've managed to infiltrate the Dark Iron Prison!

Well...we may have, anyway.

Kevin Dawson had the...honor...of seeing what was going on over there, and we haven't heard back from him since. You look like the type that doesn't like to die, you should go see if he's ok!

He's supposed to be inside the hall on the south end of the cavern ahead...though something tells me he may not have made it quite that far.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text:
I don't know how I'm still alive. The patrols keep walking past me like I'm not even here.

...Am I dead, <class>?

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text:
This is a little hard to believe, but there are Twilight's Hammer members here in Blackrock Depths! I don't know how many there are crawling throughout this place, but I did hear that their lead interrogator, Gerstahn, is in this hallway.

I don't know what they're here torturing for, but maybe you can find out by confronting Gerstahn?

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: Go! Go! Go!

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: I see...she did not cooperate. Hopefully we can still stop them before something else terrible happens.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text:
Can ye keep a secret? I have a secret tae share with ye if ye can.

Everybody here is CRAZY!!!

There's goblins over there, Dark Irons right over there, and a giant living fire thing right past this gate! An' that's just what I see in this little cave!

And ye! What're ye doin' here!?

Oh, I see. Winky sent ye, did he? Sent ye tae talk t' Prospector Seymour, past this gate and t' the right, did he? Well go! Oralius doesn't even care!

...I'll GET YOU FOR THIS WINKY!!!

<Oralius begins to sob.>

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text:
I would stay away from Oralius. Far, far, far away. He isn't quite right in the head.

Now, let's get onto business!

passages.title: Dark Iron Tacticians
passages.text:
General Angerforge and Golem Lord Argelmach lead the Dark Iron armies and their golems against us. If we are to overcome them, the two must be slain.

Go through this door and unlock The Shadowforge Lock, which separates the East and West Garrisons. Then, follow the stairs and keep to the left at the top until you reach the West Garrison. It is there you will find the General and Golem Lord.

Keep your wits about you, they are both well-seasoned combatants. Find Mayara Brightwing should you succeed.

passages.title: Dark Iron Tacticians
passages.text:
I'm sure you are up to the task I have for you if you've made it this far in one piece.

<Mayara Brightwing lowers her voice to a whisper.>

Between you and me, you may want to enjoy yourself in the Grim Guzzler while you're there. It could be the last drink you ever have.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
Some say that the Grim Guzzler is the secret to the Dark Iron war effort. Their warriors recharge there and emerge thirsty for another innocent soul. I think we can seriously hinder them by causing a bit of chaos here.

I need you to start a fight with three of the bar's infamous patrons. Damage the kegs and Hurley Blackbreath will come running. Steal items off the tables near Plugger Spazzring and he'll fight. As for Ribbly Screwspigot...just talk to the little hothead. Report to Orfus when you're done.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text: Hurry, please. Time is not a luxury we currently have.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
The Dark Irons took our Thunderbrew. I'll never let them live after that. I'd kill 'em all myself if I could!

However, look ahead and you'll see we have slightly more dire matters to attend to at the moment.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text:
Ahead is the creature known only as Ambassador Flamelash. He is the ambassador to the Dark Iron Nation from Ragnaros the Firelord. Beyond that chamber is the Summoners' Tomb, home to the spirits of the seven Dark Iron patriarchs who summoned Ragnaros into our world.

You may not know of the Great Fire, but he will be the end of Azeroth if he is not stopped, and these individuals are directly tied to his hold over the Dark Iron. Slay them, so that this nation may perhaps one day be redeemed.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text: I cannot proceed any further alone, regardless of my combat experience. The Lyceum has proven too difficult for me. If you are here, though...you might be the key to all of this.

passages.title: Patchwork Command
passages.text:
Recent events make it even more apparent that holing up here and making sporadic attacks isn't enough to keep our kind safe, much less retake Grim Batol. We need to be more aggressive, we need to strike into their heart.

I've agreed to send dragons to the aid of your commanders. They were already hatching a plan to strike at Grim Batol, so you should focus your attention there first.

You should be able to find Patch in Dragonmaw Pass, in the canyon below us to the south.

passages.title: Patchwork Command
passages.text:
You got the dragons in the game! Good on you.

We'd already laid out plans for our ambush by the time the dragons contacted us. They're helping by cutting off their retreat.

It's not too late for you to join in on the fun though. We saved some for you.

passages.title: 7th Legion Battle Plans
passages.text:
While destroying Pyrewood will certainly garner us an advantage over the Alliance upon the field of battle, our true purpose here is to leave them crippled.

Southwest of here, near the Greymane Wall, lies the 7th Legion Base Camp. We must search the base camp for battle plans. With the 7th Legion battle plans we will be able to pinpoint all Alliance troop advancement in Silverpine Forest.

passages.title: 7th Legion Battle Plans
passages.text: Search every filthy dwarven corpse.

passages.title: 7th Legion Battle Plans
passages.text:
<Walden flips through the battle plan.>

It looks like the reinforcements from the ships in Gilneas are marching soon. Crowley and Bloodfang have set up an encampment to the southeast for the Gilneas Liberation front.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text:
Da Twilight's Hammer be here for some reason. We don't know why, but Thal'trak be lettin' you in on a lil' secret of ours - da rogue Lexlort waits outside da hall where High Interrogator Gerstahn be so he can kill her if he gets da chance.

She's too smart for dat, though, so you gonna go in an' do it, ya? Go talk to Lexlort and let him know. I'm sure he be ok with it.

passages.title: Into the Prison
passages.text: Get over here. If you blow my cover, I swear to the Warchief I'll kill you where you stand.

passages.title: Sowing Discord
passages.text: The Alliance reinforcements have established a foothold in the southwest region of Silverpine called 7th Legion Base Camp. Our primary goal at the base camp is to sow discord amongst the troops. This is a lightning fast assassination mission to kill their field commander, General Marstone. His death won't stop the Alliance advance, but it will certainly soften their ranks.

passages.title: Sowing Discord
passages.text: Marstone is a decorated field general. He will not go down easy.

passages.title: Sowing Discord
passages.text: The rest of the Alliance fleet will arrive shortly, only to find their base camp decimated. Now for the second and most important part of our battle plan.

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text:
Gerstahn is too heavily guarded and too smart to leave her post, so I'm not going to kill her.

You are.

I'll throw in a little something I picked up off of a guard to make it worth your while.

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: Does it look like I want to be waiting her any longer than is necessary?

passages.title: Twilight?! No!
passages.text: The Twilight's Hammer's presence only complicates our mission here further, but you've done your part for now.  You've earned a reward for your efforts...and some rest. Let's get out of here.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text:
We're fighting a losing battle right now, I'm afraid. The Dark Irons would be difficult to defeat on their own, but their elemental allies have given them new bleeding edge warriors that we simply can't compete with.

I need you to help us infiltrate their domain and kill as many of their vital leaders as possible. Hopefully that will shock their forces and turn the tide in our favor. Report to Razal'blade for further instruction. He's stationed beyond this gate and to the right.

passages.title: Infiltrating Shadowforge City
passages.text: Beyond this door lies the commander of the Dark Iron Army, surrounded by trained soldiers. Are you up for a little killing?

passages.title: The 109th Division
passages.text:
General Angerforge and Golem Lord Argelmach are directly responsible for the horrific slaughter of the 109th Division of the Kargath Expeditionary Force. There were a lot of good trolls and orcs in that division, many of them my close friends.

Well, young <race>, it's time for our fallen brothers to at last have their revenge.

Unlock The Shadowforge Lock, go up the stairs and bear left until you reach the West Garrison. Kill Angerforge and Argelmach, and don't you dare show them any mercy.

passages.title: The 109th Division
passages.text: I'm quite surprised to see you here! You'll be very useful indeed.

passages.title: The 109th Division
passages.text:
Up ahead is the Grim Guzzler. A disgusting bar full of all our enemies, intoxicated and therefore unfit for proper battle.

<Hierophant Theodora Mulvadania grins.>

Ripe for the slaughter.

passages.title: Maliciously Delicious
passages.text:
You know, I've got a problem you might be able to help me out with, here.

See, in addition to the fine pursuit of arms dealing, I'm trying to liven up the entertainment here in Bogpaddle. Apparently there's a bunch of these makrura things in the north waters that don't take kindly to the wild beach parties we've been throwing.

Joke's on them. I'm not gonna be pushed around by giant lobsters; they're my next source of revenue! You bring me some of their tails and we'll turn a problem into profit.

passages.title: Maliciously Delicious
passages.text: You got those tails? Don't be tryin' to push no hacked-up ones on me!

passages.title: Maliciously Delicious
passages.text:
I can see it now: our own famous Bogpaddle Lobster-Poppers! Made fresh from the sea! Oh, it's like this stuff writes itself...

Your help is very much appreciated, my friend. I'll start seeing if I can't cut your people a favorable arrangement, eh?

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
Everyone inside the Grim Guzzler is absolutely hammered and, therefore, easily angered. I think we can seriously hinder the Dark Irons by causing a bit of chaos here.

I need you to start a fight with three of the bar's infamous patrons. Damage the kegs and Hurley Blackbreath will come running. Steal items off the tables near Plugger Spazzring and he'll fight. As for Ribbly Screwspigot...just talk to the little hothead. Report to Thunderheart when you're done.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text: Hurry, please. Time is not a luxury we currently have.

passages.title: The Grim Guzzler
passages.text:
I hear quite the commotion coming from the Grim Guzzler. I see you've been hard at work.

If you'll direct your attention opposite me, you'll notice that we have bigger issues to worry about than toying with drunkards.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text:
Inside this chamber lies Ambassador Flamelash. He is the ambassador to the Dark Iron Nation from Ragnaros the Firelord. Beyond that chamber is the Summoners' Tomb, home to the spirits of the seven Dark Iron patriarchs who summoned Ragnaros into our world.

You may not know of the Great Fire, but he will be the end of Azeroth if he is not stopped, and these individuals are directly tied to his hold over the Dark Iron. Slay them all, and may this unholy union cease.

passages.title: The Dark Iron Pact
passages.text: I cannot proceed any further alone, regardless of my combat experience. The Lyceum has proven too difficult for me. If you are here, though...you might be the key to all of this.

passages.title: The Prophet Hadassi
passages.text:
Prophet Hadassi is the wisest and eldest member of the Orsis tribe.

He has not been accounted for and his well-being is of vital importance.

Go into Orsis and find him. A great day of reckoning will come to the Al'Akir's lackeys if he's been hurt.

passages.title: The Prophet Hadassi
passages.text: Who... who are you?  Sent here... to rescue my people and fight our enemies.

passages.title: The Heart of the Mountain
passages.text:
For years I have sought a certain gem. It is called the Heart of the Mountain and it's the size of your fist! The Dark Iron dwarves have it locked in their vault and, try as I may, they won't let me purchase it.

So I must resort to force.

Fight your way to The Black Vault near the Hall of Crafting, breach its secret safe and gain the Heart. To do that, you must defeat Watchman Doomgrip, and he won't appear until you've opened every relic coffer in the vault!

Good luck.

passages.title: The Heart of the Mountain
passages.text: Do you have the Heart of the Mountain?  To me, its value is without limit.

passages.title: The Heart of the Mountain
passages.text:
You have the heart!  Amazing!  It is even more beautiful than I imagined!

Please, <name>, take this as payment!

passages.title: Crazy Larry
passages.text:
You're gettin' it, <name>. You scratch my back, I scratch yours. Well, more like I scratch the back of your whole army, and just a little harder than the backs of the other side! Was that too complicated?

What I'm sayin' is, that's a lot of backs. So I'm gonna have to ask you to scratch mine a few more times. Whoever stole those landmines may have just hit our boys on the eastern shore.

Head to our camp to the southeast and check on Crazy Larry; he'll fill you in when you get there.

passages.title: Crazy Larry
passages.text:
Silversnap sent you?! I'm DOOMED!

Oh, he sent you to help me! That's different, haha!

passages.title: Kill Gil
passages.text:
Gilblins!

<Larry stares at you silently for a while.>

You never seen a gilblin before? They're crazy! Crazier than me! I just blow stuff up for a living, these guys are WHACKED!

Dunno where they came from, but they're like awful fish goblins! Gills and everything! They wiped out all my men down at the beach, and they took our shipping freighter!

You gotta help! They're just down to the east, go on and get rid of those gilblins!

passages.title: Kill Gil
passages.text: That'll show those fish-faced freaks! Good work!

passages.title: The Prophet's Dying Words
passages.text:
We... are... bound by oath... to protect the scepter of Orsis.

Listen, <class>, I don't have much time... left.

Find the sacred receptacle... in the southern end of the city.

Do not... let it... fall into their... hands...

passages.title: The Prophet's Dying Words
passages.text: Though the chest is locked, there is a plaque bearing interesting hieroglyphs above it.

passages.title: The Sealed Gate
passages.text:
At one end of the Dark Iron Highway stands a massive gate much like the one that protects Shadowforge City on the opposite side. However, we have no idea what's behind it!

All we know is that it's heavily guarded by Anvilrage patrols and the molten giant Bael'gar. You simply must dispose of them and see if you can pry that gate open!

Just imagine what could lie behind it...there could be an entire other half of the city we never knew about! Or nothing! Who knows!

Though, it's probably something...

passages.title: The Sealed Gate
passages.text: Were you able to get past the gate? Or scale it? What's behind it???

passages.title: The Sealed Gate
passages.text:
Darn it! I simply HAVE to know what's behind that gate! This could be the discovery that makes my career, you know!

Hmm....maybe a couple good explosions would do the trick...

passages.title: Jammal'an the Prophet
passages.text:
Jammal'an the Prophet, leader of the Atal'ai and Hakkari trolls, has obtained a small amount of Hakkar the Soulflayer's blood. They are injecting it into the green dragons to use their bodies to produce the massive quantities of blood necessary to summon Hakkar into our world.

We cannot allow this to come to pass. Slaughter Jammal'an and his priests before they get any further in their efforts!

passages.title: Jammal'an the Prophet
passages.text: Were you able to kill Jammal'an? I'll need proof that the deed is done.

passages.title: Jammal'an the Prophet
passages.text: Excellent! I suspect that without Jammal'an's leadership, the trolls will fall to infighting and Hakkar will never set his eyes upon our world.

passages.title: Eranikus
passages.text:
The Hakkar blood the Atal'ai have been injecting into the green dragons has had devastating effects on the dragons themselves. It appears that these dragons, former jailors of the Atal'ai, have been corrupted by its presence in their bodies and have become creatures of Nightmare.

Eranikus, Ysera's primary consort and lead watcher over the temple, was infused with the largest quantities of blood and has become twisted beyond imagination. After Jammal'an is dead, find Eranikus and end him.

passages.title: Eranikus
passages.text: Did you defeat Eranikus?

passages.title: Eranikus
passages.text:
You only defeated Eranikus' Shade? This is most troubling...

Let us hope that his full form does not still exist outside the Temple. Only Ysera herself is stronger than him in our flight.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
We're about to launch the attack upon the Twilight Gate, but there is one last loose end to tie up: Za'brox and Beeble'phod, the disciples of Cho'gall.
