Intelligence has placed them within the Den of the Disciples, a small ogre cave at the southwest corner of the Twilight Gate.

Would you go back in there and kill them?

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text: Is that blood dripping from your pack?

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
<The paladin frowns.>

That's quite a gruesome trophy collection you have there. I would have believed you if you had simply said they were dead. Regardless, thank you for having the foresight to take care of them.

The Twilight Gate will soon be ours. Time to move up to the Twilight Citadel.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
Now, while we're about to launch the attack upon the Twilight Gate, there is one last loose end to tie up: Za'brox and Beeble'phod, the disciples of Cho'gall.

Intelligence has placed them within the Den of the Disciples, a small ogre cave at the southwest corner of the Twilight Gate.

Please head back in and kill them.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text: Is that blood dripping from your pack? I hope that it's not yours.

passages.title: Four Heads are Better than None
passages.text:
<The noble lady grins wickedly.>

That's quite a gruesome trophy collection you have there. I would have believed you if you had simply said they were dead, though I do appreciate the extra effort. Thank you for having the foresight to take care of them.

The Twilight Gate will soon be ours. Time to move up to the Twilight Citadel.

passages.title: The Wrathcaster
passages.text:
One of the more vile members of the Scarlet Crusade, Mataus the Wrathcaster, lurks within the barracks' dungeon. Undeath suits his dark manner.

Were I younger and on the front lines, I'd run him through myself. As things are, I'm left behind to lead our forces from the rear. So I leave the pleasure to you.

passages.title: The Wrathcaster
passages.text: You are well on your way to becoming a true champion of the Light, <name>.  Well done.

passages.title: The Huntsman
passages.text:
We've already lost half a dozen men to a hail of bullets and arrows coming from atop this fortress. I haven't seen the face of the enemy that's firing, but I don't need to. I know the name of the man up there.

Leopold.

That's right, there's only one man up there, picking off my men one-by-one. And from what I can see, there's only one of you.

Sounds like a fair fight to me.

passages.title: The Huntsman
passages.text: If it were up to me, I'd throw him off the edge of the tower.

passages.title: The Huntsman
passages.text: One less thing to worry about.  Nice work up there.

passages.title: The Commander
passages.text:
Scarlet Commander Marjhan is cunning, shrewd, and willing to do anything to win a battle. Before all these things, however, she is loyal.

I have no doubt you'll find her in the barracks' central chamber, fighting under a crimson banner, until she either wins or dies.

Make sure it's the latter.

passages.title: The Commander
passages.text: Good, good.  These barracks are as good as fallen.

passages.title: Like Rats
passages.text:
Well, I'm glad that Eligor and Korfax left some fun for me. It was a battle unto itself to keep them from rushing headlong into the middle of this cathedral.

That's YOUR job, after all.

The cathedral lies ahead of us, the last real bastion of Scarlet power remaining. Within it, Crusader Lord Valdelmar sits atop Tyr's Hand's crumbling pulpit of lies.

There will be no escape; there will be no mercy. The last simpering vestiges of the Scarlet Crusade end here. Slay him.

passages.title: Like Rats
passages.text:
While I can't agree with their methods, I can't argue with their results.  In many ways, the Scarlet were well-intentioned, but their zeal grew too strong, and their hate blinded them to reason.

I only hope that the same doesn't happen to our Brotherhood of Light.

passages.title: In Defense of Quel'Danil
passages.text:
The undead are here! The Forsaken! They've been moving closer and closer, but to launch an all-out attack on us... those horrid abominations!

The young draenei I was charged with have trained with the Highvale elves in combat. They are not defenseless, but they need help!

Please, <name>, assist them! Drive back the Forsaken!

passages.title: In Defense of Quel'Danil
passages.text: Such aberrations in the face of the light... You are brave to face them, <name>.

passages.title: Just a Fancy Cockroach
passages.text:
Evidently, the ancient statues were home to various species of scarab.

Determined to leave this site in the best condition possible, you resolve to ridding the chamber of these pests.

passages.title: Send Word to Phaoris
passages.text:
Hurry, <name>. We must speak to my brother, the king.

He is bent on averting war with Al'Akir and the Neferset. He has foolish hopes that there is a diplomatic solution to this problem.

Maybe once he hears what occurred here he will see reason.

passages.title: Send Word to Phaoris
passages.text: This is just the beginning, <name>.  If Deathwing's minions can bury entire cities, we have little chance of defeating them through conventional means.

passages.title: The Vizier's Vote
passages.text:
Getting Vizier Tanotep to go against my brother's wishes is going to be extremely difficult. His very position is based on enforcing the will of Phaoris.

I've had little luck making the case for open war against Neferset.

Nevertheless you must speak to him. Perhaps he will listen to an outsider's perspective.

You will find the Vizier at the Akhenet Fields on official business.

passages.title: The Vizier's Vote
passages.text:
What manner of creature are you?  You will leave the king's lands before...

Wait!  You are that <name> I've heard so much about.

You must pardon my lack of hospitality.  We have seen all manner of hostile intruders since the barrier around Uldum failed.

passages.title: The High Priest's Vote
passages.text:
High Priest Amet's vote is the only one that is completely outside of our control.

He will vote as his divinations tell him and nothing we do will dissuade him.

I figure that gives us even odds either way.

The only problem we face is that his clairvoyance has failed him ever since the barriers around Uldum fell.

He will not cast a vote unless he regains power over his divinations.

Take the stairs at either side of the Vir'naal Dam and Speak to him to see what you can do to help.

passages.title: The High Priest's Vote
passages.text:
War, you say.

Divinations for war are always difficult.  Some wars must never be fought, even if victory was assured.  Some wars have to be waged even if defeat is certain.

passages.title: The High Commander's Vote
passages.text:
If we're to pass a resolution for war, the high council's vote needs to be unanimous.

I'm certain High Commander Kamses will give us his vote once he hears about what happened at Orsis.

Please speak to him in Ramkahen and make sure that's the case. I must make preparations in case our plan fails.

passages.title: The High Commander's Vote
passages.text:
No need to fill me in on the events in Orsis, <name>.

I've heard about them already.  And about you.  Any enemy of Al'Akir is a friend of mine.

passages.title: Tanotep's Son
passages.text:
I have devoted my life to serving the King. That service is unrivaled in importance by anything... with one exception: my son.

Tahet was captured by Neferset sentries.

They claim my son was trespassing upon their territory. Phaoris is attempting to negotiate his release... but I fear for the worst.

If you were to find Tahet, I would pledge my vote to you.

I do not know where they take the prisoners, but I've seen the guards consult maps to guide them through the thick vegetation.

passages.title: Tanotep's Son
passages.text: This might be the map you're after.

passages.title: Tanotep's Son
passages.text: You've obtained a map of the Vir'Naal river delta.

passages.title: The Blood God Hakkar
passages.text:
Hakkar... The mere mention of The Soulflayer's name will send many running. In the Sanctum of the Fallen God the Atal'ai have recovered a significant portion of his skeleton and seek to restore him to life. Already his children have begun to show up in the area.

Place this egg in that sanctum, and it will force his summoning prematurely. <name>, do not hesitate. Strike once his avatar appears!

passages.title: The Blood God Hakkar
passages.text:
You have successfully stopped Hakkar here, but I fear we are far from done. The Atal'ai transported most of the blood they produced to Zul'Gurub, where the Hakkari work to summon The Blood God there.

<name>, I do not think that this was ever meant to be the place of Hakkar's arrival - it was merely a test to see if the blood was potent enough! Hakkar can only be summoned in Zul'Gurub...and I fear we may be too late to stop the Hakkari with the blood they now have in their possession.

passages.title: Decontamination
passages.text:
You've been down here in Gnomeregan for a long time, <name>, and it's amazing that you've survived and kept your wits so long! We need to get you out.

Before we can send you to the surface to join the rest of the gnomes, you have to go through the decontamination process. Just head into the next room and board the Sanitron 500. It will do the rest! It shouldn't even hurt... much.

When you're all done, check in with Technician Braggle and he'll make sure you get some suitable gear.

passages.title: Decontamination
passages.text: There, now you're fit to head off to the surface and start your new life. The High Tinker will be delighted to hear of your arrival.

passages.title: Dunwalds Don't Die
passages.text:
As I understand it, you're to be looking to bring the Wildhammer clans together with the Alliance for war. Not sure you know what you're gettin' into.

Anyway, if it's battle you're preparin' for, there's definitely one family you want by your side. Head southwest, to the opposite side of the Crucible of Carnage, and there you'll find Clan Dunwald's ruins. They're rightly ravaged, but that's not likely to be stoppin' the Dunwalds. It's just a matter of findin' them.

passages.title: Dunwalds Don't Die
passages.text: If it's Dunwalds you be lookin' for, it's Dunwalds you've found. A couple of'm anyway. I can't find me other brothers for the life of me.

passages.title: While Meeting The Family
passages.text:
Hey there, <lad/lass>. I'm sure Keely's got you worrying about our brothers, but they can take care of themselves. They'll find their way back here one way or another.

Maybe you can do me a favor while you're out meeting the family... Dunwald territory is still infested with Twilight's Hammer and their servants. I'd appreciate it if you could remind them that they're not welcome.

passages.title: While Meeting The Family
passages.text: Now that's what I'm talkin' about lad. My kinda <race>.

passages.title: Sifting Through The Wreckage
passages.text:
The Twilight's Hammer were damn thorough when they sacked our town. Me and me brothers may well be the only ones that held'm back. I gotta be sure though.

As you're siftin' through the ruins, keep an eye out for the bodies of me kinsmen. I wanna know if dere were any survivors... or if it seems like some might have gotten away.

passages.title: Sifting Through The Wreckage
passages.text:
That many dead, eh? Not seemin' likely that anyone outside of me brothers fought through it then. I guess I already expected as much.

Thanks for takin' the time to look for me.

passages.title: Donnelly Dunwald
passages.text:
So you be lookin' to find us, and I be lookin' to find me brothers. It sounds to me like we got some common ground in there abouts.

Donnelly's our eldest, and while his size shows it, his wits might not. He's usually up in the northern ruins - in the hovel. Do ya think you might go lookin' for him for me? It'd be a right comfort if I knew he were safe.

passages.title: Donnelly Dunwald
passages.text:
Hi friend! I don't think I know you... I'm Donnelly Dunwald.

What's your name? I don't think I know you... Do I know you?

passages.title: Eoin Dunwald
passages.text:
Eoin's one of the twins. He's got a penchant for the drink. You'll likely be findin' him over by the old well - the ale stores were in a building there.

Mind making him to pay his worrying sister a visit? Shouldn't take much convincin' if you can get to the ale first.

passages.title: Eoin Dunwald
passages.text: Of all the buildings in all the towns to collapse, why'd it have to be this one?!

passages.title: Cayden Dunwald
passages.text:
Cayden's the other twin. He's got a thirst too, but not for ale. I'm sure he's been havin' a grand time of it since the Twilight came to our doorstep. Gettin' some of that aggression out of his system mayhaps.

I'm thinkin' the best place to go lookin for him is at market row, by the old smithy. He used ta hang out there anyway, but since that place is swarmin' with the most Twilight, he's probably got all the more reason to be callin' it home now.

Bring'm back for me. In one piece would be nice.

passages.title: Cayden Dunwald
passages.text:
Well look at ya, all geared and fancy. Keely send you to keep an eye on old Cayden, eh? Won't be needin' it. I got these louts handled.

Hahah! They chose the wrong dwarf to be ambushin' today! Ahahahahah!

passages.title: Finding Beak
passages.text:
I lost me gryphon. Beak! Where are you Beak?!

Wanna help me find him? I know he's in da hovel. He hasta be.

Beak?! Wheres are ya?

I hope he's okay.

passages.title: Finding Beak
passages.text: Did you find'm?! Please?

passages.title: Finding Beak
passages.text:
You found'm! You found Beak! I like you, new friend!

I'm gonna go show Keely. Keely like Beak too.

passages.title: Anything But Water
passages.text:
Look, buddy. Either you're here to help me find some drink, or you're in the way.

Why don't ya go down to the old storehouse and look downstairs. I had a mighty suspicion that ol' bookkeeper up in there was sneaking sips between pages. I bet he has a keg in his basement!

If ya find anything, come straight back to me! No dallyin'... this is urgent!

passages.title: Anything But Water
passages.text: You stink of sober! Find me some drink!

passages.title: Anything But Water
passages.text:
Donnelly's belly! That's more like it. Good to not be dyin' of the thirst again.

Here, have some. Good ol' Eoin's never so impolite as ta not share!

passages.title: A Steady Supply
passages.text:
Hey bud. Seeing as how you're so friendly and great and all, think you might do a dwarf a favor?

These are Dunwald ruins... there's SURE to be more stock in some of these buildings. If you come upon more ale, bring it my way, will ya? A good dwarf can never have enough!

I'm thinkin' I'll find my way back to Keely, so ya might have to hunt me down, but I'll try'n make it worth it to ya.

passages.title: A Steady Supply
passages.text: Where's me booze?

passages.title: A Steady Supply
passages.text:
Woooooh! That's exactly what my belly needs!

You get me all the nice things.

passages.title: Home Again
passages.text: Ya should find Keely. She'll be eager for word.

passages.title: Home Again
passages.text:
Thank you for bandin' my brothers back together. I know they're tough, but they're even tougher when they're side by side, and there's a lot of Twilight out there.

You're good to put a gal's heart at ease.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
Even I get hunted. I suppose that's what I get for hiding amongst the sheep.

<Mathias studies you for a moment.>

The Twilight's Hammer has taken it up a notch and sent their dark assassins after me. Nice bunch of guys. Dead now. They're made from the souls of the most skilled killers.

Want to do me a favor? Hunt them down. Bring back their soul pendants.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text: How many pendants do you have?

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
I'm not sure what I'm going to do with all of these. I'll probably fence them and donate the proceeds to the Stormwind orphanage.

Now to find someone sick enough to buy such a thing. It'll probably be a goblin. Or, a gnome warlock.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
Even I get hunted, <class>. But that's part of the fun of hiding amongst the sheep.

<Garona studies you for a moment.>

The Twilight's Hammer has taken it up a notch and sent their dark assassins after me. Nice for a group of dead guys. They're made from the souls of only the most skilled killers.

Do me a favor? Hunt them down.

They wear their souls in pendants about their necks. Bring them back to me. Souls optional.

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text: How many pendants do you have?

passages.title: Dark Assassins
passages.text:
What do you think I should do with all of these? Maybe I'll melt them down and have the metal imbued into a new dagger that I can thrust into Cho'gall's chest.

Think there's time for that?

passages.title: Croc-Out
passages.text:
The Stagalbog east of town is swarming with crocolisks. Swarming, you hear me? I've sold every bit of crocolisk you could imagine.

Crocolisk hides, teeth, tails, tongues, eyes, you name it. My point is, they ain't sellin' anymore. There's too many crocs! We're over-supplied and under-demanded.

So since they're of no use to me, and they occasionally eat my guests, I need you to just kill the suckers. Do me the favor, eh? I'll be here negotiatin' things with your people.

passages.title: Croc-Out
passages.text:
All taken care of? Good to hear. Takes a load off my mind.

Now I can focus on proper business for the fine folk of Marshtide and Stonard, weary from the war... and all that junk.

passages.title: Fire the Cannon
passages.text:
My arch-nemesis, Lord Cannon, has foolishly decided to throw his allegiance to the Twilight's Hammer.

In the past, we've coexisted with a shaky truce, but his change of heart leaves me little choice but to put an end to him. Or, I should say, if you want the information that you seek from the dead dwarf, you're going to kill Lord Cannon for me.

Seek him at Cannon's Inferno to the southeast.

passages.title: Fire the Cannon
passages.text:
I am pleased. Lord Cannon was always an unworthy adversary.

Very well, <race>, I will help you gain the information which you seek.

passages.title: Tastes Like Strider
passages.text:
You there! Yes, you! You want a good word put in with the Trade Baron? Give me a hand!

I heard you're the one that got all those makrura tails. They're wonderful, but not enough for proper swamp food. I need drumsticks for my gumbo!

There's plenty of swampstriders just outside town in the Sorrowmurk. I want the biggest drumsticks you can find!

passages.title: Tastes Like Strider
passages.text: Have you got those drumsticks?

passages.title: Tastes Like Strider
passages.text: Ah, good, good! Just what I needed.

passages.title: Pinned Down
passages.text:
My name is Nevin Twistwrench and I'm the commander of the Survivor Assistance Facilitation Expedition, or S.A.F.E.

I don't know how you managed to survive the radiation down here, <name>, but most of the others haven't fared so well. My team is rounding up the survivors, but the radiation-addled leper gnomes are too numerous for us to hold back much longer. They've lost their minds!

If you're still strong enough to wield a weapon or cast a spell, would you help us clear out some of these leper gnomes?

passages.title: Pinned Down
passages.text: Help my men get the way cleared out so we can help the other survivors get out of here!

passages.title: Pinned Down
passages.text: Well done, <name>. My men can take it from here. Let's focus on getting the other survivors out now.

passages.title: See to the Survivors
passages.text:
If we don't do something quick, neither Nevin nor the survivors will make it out of here alive. I'm going to give you my squad's emergency teleport beacon. We still have enough strength and ammunition to fight our way out of here, but those survivors are in no condition to make a run for it.

Use the beacon on survivors to arrange for them to be teleported out of here to the safe area my men have set up. Once you've done that, report back to me and we'll make arrangements to get you out of here.

passages.title: See to the Survivors
passages.text: Nevin's team found a lot of survivors this time, but he's cutting it awful close.

passages.title: See to the Survivors
passages.text:
I know Nevin will be pleased with all the survivors you managed to help. I still can't believe you managed to stay so strong down here in the radiation. You've seen the shape the other survivors are in.

Let's get you to the loading room for decontamination.

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text:
In the Map Chamber there is a door which leads to the legendary Chamber of Khaz'mul. Who knows what secrets could be hidden inside!

What we do know is that it is guarded by Ironaya, a Titanic Watcher of immense size and power. You'll need to defeat her if you intend to unlock the secrets of Uldaman!

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text: Don't worry about the chamber, my boys will check it out! You have more important things to do!

passages.title: It's What's Inside That Counts
passages.text:
The Makers built two Ancient Stone Keepers to help protect Uldaman from would-be invaders and to oversee daily operations while Ironaya and Archaedas slumber. One is still fully operational in Temple Hall, but the one in Echomok Cavern has been corrupted by something.

I fear that one of the Old Gods is responsible for this, and you're going to help me see if that's the case! Topple both of the guardians and bring me their power cores. They'll tell us all we need to know.

passages.title: It's What's Inside That Counts
passages.text:
Where are the cores, lad? By Muradin's Beard, where are the bloody cores?

<Kand takes a deep breath.>

Sorry about that. Have you been able to obtain the cores?

passages.title: It's What's Inside That Counts
passages.text:
This is incredible, <name>. The power coursing through each core...the contrasting powers so close together!

I'll take this to the proper dwarves right away. These cores are extremely important!

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text:
Galgann Firehammer and his band of Dark Irons are in Dig Three guarding a door that we know nothing about! I've had it with their men getting in the way of our work here! The Explorers' League is the only group authorized to handle the artifacts throughout Uldaman!

Go to the dig and dispose of him so that our work can continue undisturbed. I want to know what's behind that door!

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text: Fantastic! Great work! We'll know all that Dig Three has to tell us in no time at all!

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text:
The true goal in Uldaman is to obtain the Discs of Norgannon. The secrets on these discs could change everything about how we view our world. Countless secrets of the Makers are inscribed on them...their value is beyond any material wealth you could possibly imagine.

The problem is that Archaedas, an ancient and powerful creation of the Makers, guards the discs with a venerable army at his disposal. I need you to defeat him and secure the discs for the Explorers' League!

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text: Well done, lad! Now go to the discs and learn all you can!

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text:
In the Map Chamber there is a locked door which I believe leads to the legendary Chamber of Khaz'mul. We do not yet know what artifacts wait inside it.

What we do know is that it is guarded by Ironaya, a Titanic Watcher of immense size and power. You'll need to defeat her if you intend to progress any further into this place.

passages.title: The Chamber of Khaz'mul
passages.text: Reliquary agents are en route to investigate the chamber. You have more important matters to attend to.

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text:
The true goal in Uldaman is to obtain the Discs of Norgannon. These platinum discs could grant our order unbelievable power. Countless secrets of the Makers are inscribed on them...their value is beyond any material wealth you could possibly imagine.

The only problem in obtaining them is that Archaedas, an ancient and powerful creation of the Makers, guards the discs with a venerable army at his disposal. I need you to defeat him and secure the discs for The Reliquary.

passages.title: Archaedas, The Ancient Stone Watcher
passages.text: You are a most reliable agent, <name>. Proceed to the discs and learn all you can. Report back to me immediately after.

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text:
Galgann Firehammer and his band of Dark Irons are in Dig Three guarding a door that we know nothing about! I've had it with their men getting in the way of our work here! The Reliquary is the only group authorized to handle the artifacts throughout Uldaman!

Go to the dig and dispose of him so that our work can continue undisturbed. I want to know what's behind that door!

passages.title: Behind Closed Doors
passages.text: Well done. Dig Three and any secrets beyond that door will soon be ours and ours alone.

passages.title: We Require More Minerals
passages.text:
The Titans built two Ancient Stone Keepers to help protect Uldaman from would-be invaders and to oversee daily operations while Ironaya and Archaedas slumber. One is still fully operational in Temple Hall, but the one in Echomok Cavern has been corrupted by something.

I suspect that one of the Old Gods is responsible for this, and you're going to help me see if that is indeed true. Topple both of the guardians and bring me their power cores. They'll tell us all we need to know.

passages.title: We Require More Minerals
passages.text: Do you have the cores with you, or are you just here to chat? Perhaps we should stop this whole charade and enjoy some snacks and fine wine instead?

passages.title: We Require More Minerals
passages.text:
Both of these cores are still far more potent than most of the cores we use  to power our own protectors, and these are ancient devices!

Thank you, these will prove extremely valuable to our society.

passages.title: Into the Woods
passages.text:
I saw the strangest commotion coming through town the other day. A horse-drawn cart, loaded with crates and chests, a worgen woman at the reins, a blood elf by her side, and a dwarven paladin running behind, yelling some of the most creative obscenities I've heard in quite some time.

They looked like they were headed to Eastern Plaguelands, though I'd imagine they can't be far past the Thondroril River by now. I wonder what they were up to?

passages.title: Into the Woods
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Visitors
passages.text:
My sources at the Menders' Stead have informed me that we will be having some visitors soon. A group of paladins - led by a worgen tradeswoman, of all things - will be arriving here shortly. I look forward to meeting them. Particularly one of them.

Would you mind stopping in and checking in on them? I can't say for sure, but by the time you get there, they should just be crossing the Thondroril River, far to the west.

passages.title: Visitors
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Good Deed Left Undone
passages.text:
G'day, <laddie/lassie>.

The name's Rendel.

Seems ol' Moanah and I got here in the nick of time, eh?

Erunak wasn't kiddin' when he said it was life or death!

So... in our rush ta git over here, we left a little unfinished business off to the east a ways.

A little lady was near death herself. We had no choice but ta leave her by a little air vent when we came here to yer rescue.

How bout yeh git over and help her while there's still time?

passages.title: Good Deed Left Undone
passages.text:
Oh, finally...

I don't know how much longer I can last!

passages.title: An Opened Can of Whoop Gnash
passages.text:
What an accomplishment, felling a mighty sea giant!

The new residents of Smuggler's Hole will feel considerably safer knowing this monster is no longer loitering outside their haven.

passages.title: An Opened Can of Whoop Gnash
passages.text: You took down that Sea Giant, <class>?

passages.title: An Opened Can of Whoop Gnash
passages.text:
It's not much, but it's all I've got down here.

You're more than welcome to it, <class>.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text:
There are three candidates for Ascendancy that we need to eliminate: Dame Alys Finnsson, Master Klem, and Mia the Rose.

I'd like for you to serve as my distraction. When the time is right, I'll step in and finish them off from behind.

Whatever you do, <name>, do not underestimate them. Each got to where they are by being ruthless and very good at what they do.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text:
That takes care of most of their leaders outside of the Bastion of Twilight.

We work well together, <name>.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text:
There are three candidates for Ascendancy that need killing: Dame Alys Finnsson, Master Klem, and Mia the Rose.

I want you to serve as a distraction. When the time is right, I'll step in to finish them off from behind.

Just make sure that whatever you do, you don't underestimate them, <name>. Each of those lunatics got to where they are by being ruthless and very good at what they do.

passages.title: Distract Them for Me
passages.text: That takes care of most of their leaders outside of the Bastion. Not bad work, <name>. Not bad at all.

passages.title: Marshfin Madness
passages.text:
I'm afraid the rest of the Steamwheedle here are gone. All the young ones at the camp to the east were lost when the murlocs came.

Yes, there's always been murlocs on these shores... but not in these numbers. They came in droves from the sea at night, howling and frothing, swarming up onto the land to attack!

We can't have them still running around, now can we? Would you put an old goblin at ease and go beat some of them back into the water?

passages.title: Marshfin Madness
passages.text: I've still got a few tricks up my sleeve, but I'm not going to tussle with murlocs if I don't have to.

passages.title: Marshfin Madness
passages.text:
You have to wonder just what's out there. This is the coast of the Forbidding Sea, with nothing beyond its reaches... but all these fishy folk just stomped right out of it.

What's more, I saw where they've been going...

passages.title: The Warden's Game
passages.text:
You see the statue split into two, then four, then eight identical statues in a square formation.

You hear a voice, not through your ears, but in the back of your mind:

 "A true warden does not face OUTWARD, searching for signs of danger.
 A true warden keeps his gaze INWARD, always focused on protecting his quarry."

Perhaps this is a riddle of some sort?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text:
The Twilight cowards have captured and killed too many red dragons, but one yet lives. Do you remember Lirastrasza? She's shackled nearby and we're going to free her.

But first, we need something sharp enough to cut through her chains.

There's an old ettin named Blindeye the Guardian. He stands watch at the Altar of Ascension to the south.

He has a purely-wrought Elementium axe. I wonder if that's Cho'gall's "ultimate" weapon?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text: Do you have the axe? They're going to kill Lirastrasza soon.

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text:
That thing looks sharp. Sharp enough to the do deed, at least.

But if I'm a judge of weaponry, that's not what Cho'gall's after.

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text:
The Twilight cowards have captured and killed many red dragons, but one's still breathing. Do you remember Lirastrasza? She's chained nearby and we're going to free her.

But first, we need something sharp enough to cut her free.

There's an old ettin named Blindeye the Guardian. He stands watch at the Altar of Ascension to the south.

He has a purely-wrought Elementium axe. I wonder if that's Cho'gall's "ultimate" weapon?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text: Do you have the axe?

passages.title: The Elementium Axe
passages.text: That's a very sharp axe. It'll do the job, but if I'm any judge of weaponry, that's not what Cho'gall's after.

passages.title: Corruption in Maraudon
passages.text:
<name>, I require your assistance immediately! I am Zaetar, son of Cenarius, and I am trapped here after an unfortunate series of events! Before saving me is an option, you must help me clean out the corruption that runs so rampant through Maraudon.

Lord Vyletongue is the satyr ruler of the purple crystal caverns. He is an insidious agent of the Burning Legion and his continued presence can only lead to chaos and death. He can live no longer!

passages.title: Corruption in Maraudon
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>! Eliminating Vyletongue's presence is a key step to freeing me and, ultimately, saving these lands from corruption. Take this as a token of my thanks and an incentive to continue your work here.

passages.title: Servants of Theradras
passages.text:
Princess Theradras, my former mate, has used her enormous power to corrupt the very nature of Maraudon. Even now her creations run rampant here, and I fear that they may soon escape into the open world to sow the seeds of death and destruction.

<name>, venture forth and kill Noxxion and Razorlash. They are two of her most powerful minions and their deaths would cause the callous Princess much deserved grief and suffering of her own. Then, perhaps, you can help free my spirit from her grasp.

passages.title: Servants of Theradras
passages.text: Without her powerful servants, Princess Theradras is significantly more vulnerable. Find her lair, <name>...it is time to strike.

passages.title: Shark Weak
passages.text:
That's one tough shark!

You determine that it's in everyone's best interest to try and distract Budd and hope his attention never returns to Gnaws and this Skeletal Reef.

Perhaps the teeth of the beast will prove captivating enough...

passages.title: Shark Weak
passages.text: Whatcha got there, pal?

passages.title: Shark Weak
passages.text:
What?!

Gnaws ain't dead?!

This kinda takes the quick outta my get rich quick scheme...

Them giant shark teeth are nice and all, but we can't stop 'til that shiney is ours!

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text:
Look at that. Lirastrasza's destroying them!

There are drakes that she's downing that need finishing off, <name>. Wouldn't want the Twilight's healers to get them back up into the air.

Time for a little Coup de Grace.

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text: Our efforts to improve relations with the red dragons has really paid off, <name>.

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text:
Look at that. Lirastrasza's destroying them!

There are still drakes that she's downing that need finishing off, <name>. We don't want the stinking Twilight healers to get them back up into the air.

Time for a little Coup de Grace.

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text: That's all? I think that you can finish off a few more.

passages.title: Coup de Grace
passages.text: Good thing that you and Warlord Krogg made friends with the red dragons.

passages.title: Neferset Prison
passages.text:
Hieroglyphs depicting a chained Tol'vir mark the southeastern corner of the map.

Perhaps Tahet was brought there when he was imprisoned.

passages.title: The Sentinel's Game
passages.text:
As you place the statue in its place, several other stone statues appear in the room. One more ruby-colored statue also appears, in a small enclosure on the far end of the room. You hear a voice:

 "The Sentinel watches.
 The Sentinel protects.
 The Sentinel's vision never falters."

That red statue on the other side of the room looks important. Perhaps you should try to connect the two red statues?

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came
passages.text:
Deathwing made quite a mess when he passed through these parts. If it weren't for me, he'd probably still be here, layin' waste to all the good people of the Badlands.

What, you don't believe me? Fine, let me tell you the whole story.

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came
passages.text: Are you going to listen or not?

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came
passages.text: Some story, huh?  Now you know why Deathwing hasn't come back here since.

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came: The Real Story
passages.text:
Not only was Theldurin's story wrong, it was boring, unimaginitive, and slow.

I'll tell you how things really happened on that day.

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came: The Real Story
passages.text: I'm not done with my story yet.  Sit back down.

passages.title: The Day that Deathwing Came: The Real Story
passages.text: The end!  No moral.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Vashj'ir!
passages.text:
All able-bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Commander Thorak at Bladefist Bay in Durotar.

Now, more than ever, your help is needed in battling our most hated enemy, the Alliance!

To reach Bladefist Bay you must travel south through the main gates of Orgrimmar and enter Durotar. From there, follow the path east to the coast. Thorak will be standing at his post near the docks.

Onward, <brother/sister>! Destiny calls!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Vashj'ir!
passages.text: Lok'tar, brother! You have arrived just in time.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Deepholm!
passages.text:
All able-bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Farseer Krogar at the Western Earthshrine in Orgrimmar.

The Earthen Ring, lead by our former Warchief, Thrall, requires our aid! They report that the elemental plane of Deepholm threatens to overtake our world!

The Western Earthshrine can be found just north of the Valley of Wisdom.

Onward, <brother/sister>! Destiny calls!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Deepholm!
passages.text: Our world is in danger, <name>! We need the help of great heroes, like you, to save it!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Vashj'ir!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Recruiter Burns in Stormwind Harbor.

Recent attacks by the Horde on our trade ships must be met with swift and just force!

Stormwind Harbor can be found in the northwest region of Stormwind City.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance! Fight on, <brother/sister>!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Vashj'ir!
passages.text: All of our war ships are off fighting the Horde. You'll have to take the mercenary ship.

passages.title: Quel'Danil Lodge
passages.text:
I may appear far from home to you, <class>, but quite a few of my people were led here by Ambassador Rualeth. We have settled with the high elves of the Quel'Danil Lodge, to the northwest, to train in the ways of the Light and enjoy the peaceful beauty of this land.

Such peace may be short lived. We have seen the Horde moving further west from here. Could you travel to Quel'Danil and give warning to Anchorite Traska? Her cabin is just north of the main lodge.

passages.title: Quel'Danil Lodge
passages.text:
Yoro sends warning of the Horde? The Highvale have been cautious of an attack for some time now. In fact, we have been--

<Screams and the clash of metal break out to the south.>

By the light... they are here!

passages.title: Once More, With Eeling
passages.text:
Eels are among the creepiest of Azeroth's creatures.

Sure, there are those who pretend that they don't mind them - and others who actually claim to favor them.

They are lying.

Truth be told, no one likes eels. Eels don't even like eels.

Azeroth would be a better place if no one ever had to envision an eel slithering out from the murky depths and biting them.

In the face.

passages.title: The Good Ol' Switcheroo
passages.text:
Look, I'd love to give the order and have my men blast these rebels to bits right now, but I can't because the entire Stockade is under Warden Thelwater's jurisdiction, and he only wants to contain them right now.

Rather than disobey orders, we're going to take care of this in a slightly different manner! We've managed to befriend Mortimer Moloch, who just so happens to be the ruthless rebel leader Randolph Moloch's twin. Kill Randolph, and we'll switch 'em so Mortimer can stop the rebellion peacefully!

passages.title: The Good Ol' Switcheroo
passages.text: We can't make the switch until Randolph is dead!

passages.title: The Good Ol' Switcheroo
passages.text: Yes, Mortimer just faked his own death. He'll probably take on his brother's name and continue on his 'epic schemes'. We'll just have to deal with that when the time comes.

passages.title: By Fire Be Saved!
passages.text:
I'm well-versed in first aid and other forms of healing, and with the help of my Lightwell I've been able to nurse many of our men back to full health. The problem we still have is that it's so cold and damp down here that I'm losing them anyways, despite healing their wounds!

The quakes angered the elements that reside in the prison...when they erupted out of the earth they slaughtered half of the prisoners. If you slay their leader, Lord Overheat, and bring me his core I can use it to warm our men!

passages.title: By Fire Be Saved!
passages.text: Do you have the core? Our men are dying in here!

passages.title: By Fire Be Saved!
passages.text:
Thank goodness! With this fire, our men will live through this ordeal!

Thank you so much, hero.

passages.title: The Pit of Scales
passages.text:
A spot on the southern end of the map was marked with hieroglyphs of crocodiles fighting each other.

That must be where Caimas took Tahet.

Go to the Pit of Scales and find a way to rescue the Vizier's son.

passages.title: The Pit of Scales
passages.text: I thank you for what you've done, <name>.  You can count on my vote when High Council convenes.

passages.title: Baba Bogbrew
passages.text:
Hey, while you were out, the Baron stopped by! He kicked me until money came out!

He always does that though. But this time he asked me to tell you something! He wants you to go south and help out our herbalist, Baba Bogbrew.

She's all the way across the water! But just talk to my girl Daisy outside and she'll send you there the Crazy Larry way!

passages.title: Baba Bogbrew
passages.text:
Ah, it's so nice to have help dropped in.

Modern convenience... I can't get enough of it.

passages.title: The Curse of the Tombs
passages.text:
The Neferset are not the only threat to our sacred tombs.

A gnomish expedition stumbled upon our lands a few weeks ago.

They did not heed our warnings and dug too deep within a cursed vault.

Their entire expedition is now afflicted by a terrible curse that has robbed them of their sanity and taken control of their minds.

They now seek access to the deepest vaults of Uldum and pose a great threat. 

Go to the Sunstone Terrace and put their wretched souls out of their misery.

passages.title: The Curse of the Tombs
passages.text: They couldn't be saved, <name>.  The ancient curse that fell upon them is irrevocable.

passages.title: The Foreman
passages.text:
If we're to find out what's going on down here it looks like we're going to have to fight our way through the entire Deadmines! Glubtok the Foreman will be the first major foe you encounter, a powerful ogre magi. Be careful, he possesses the brute strength of his race backed by his wicked spellcasting!

Take this communicator so that I can keep in touch with you as we continue our investigation. Be careful down there.

passages.title: The Foreman
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Foreman
passages.text:
<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

Nicely done! A clean kill. Now continue on and see what else you can find! We'll crack this case wide open with you on our side, I just know it.

passages.title: The Carpenter
passages.text:
<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

Hello, can you hear me? Excellent!

It looks like Helix is in charge of building an enormous mast. You don't think they're trying to finish the Defias Juggernaut, do you?

You'd better go investigate <name>, and don't be afraid to get your hands dirty! You have clearance to use deadly force if necessary and, let's face it, it's probably going to be necessary.

passages.title: The Carpenter
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Carpenter
passages.text:
<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

Hey, it's Horatio. That was intense! I'm watching your progress on the Stormwind Communicator's Spyatron X3 application.

They sure are using a lot of heavily fortified doors to hide their work. Keep pushing forward and see what you find next. I bet it'll be a huge clue!

passages.title: Artificial Intelligence
passages.text:
<A feminine voice addresses you over the portable terminal.>

Emergency code: 55-729.

Upper cerebral cortex functions in expedition members have been compromised.

Please report to your nearest terminal location, to the southeast of the Sunstone Terrace, for further analysis.

passages.title: Artificial Intelligence
passages.text: <The terminal whirrs as its mechanisms become active.>

passages.title: Artificial Intelligence
passages.text:
Scanning subject...

Cerebral cortex diagnostics indicate the absence of "tomb curse" phenomenon.

Diagnostics did reveal frequent head trauma.  The user would do well to exercise more caution around blunt objects in the future.

passages.title: Fuselight, Ho!
passages.text:
Hey, <race>, listen up. I got a job opportunity that you aren't gonna want to miss out on.

We been sent up here from Fuselight, a new goblin town way down in the Badlands. Lots of money to be had down there, yes <sir/ma'am>. And not nearly so many zombies... or uptight Argent paladin-types.

Nope, it's an untamed wilderness down there, and we're looking for someone like you to help us tame it. Whenever you're ready... we'll be waiting.

passages.title: Fuselight, Ho!
passages.text: Nice landing!

passages.title: First Sample: Wild Eggs
passages.text:
I am experimenting with black dragons. Specifically, I am interested in how they procreate.

My current experiments require plenty of black dragon eggs, which is why I am here in Lethlor Ravine. I'd gather the eggs myself, but I think you'll benefit from helping me out.

You will find them along the edges of the ravine. Beware the guardians that circle above - they do not appreciate stolen eggs.

passages.title: First Sample: Wild Eggs
passages.text: Have you brought the eggs?

passages.title: First Sample: Wild Eggs
passages.text: Thank you for gathering these so quickly, <name>.

passages.title: Second Sample: Whelps
passages.text: I need another favor from you. I need you to obtain the bodies of the black dragon whelplings that fly nearby. Slay them, and bring the corpses to me.

passages.title: Second Sample: Whelps
passages.text: Have you done as I asked?

passages.title: Second Sample: Whelps
passages.text:
This grisly task was necessary, <name>.

All will be revealed to you soon.  For now, know this:

I am no ordinary goblin.

I serve a mistress of unimaginable power, and her motives here are not as dark as they might seem.

passages.title: Rhea Revealed
passages.text:
As I hinted earlier, I am no ordinary goblin. You may have already guessed my true identity.

Allow me to show you my true form. As you have proven yourself trustworthy, I will also share with you the details of my plan.

passages.title: Rhea Revealed
passages.text: You are certainly impatient, <name>.

passages.title: Rhea Revealed
passages.text:
My true name is Rheastrasza, and I am an envoy of Alexstrasza herself, the Aspect of the red dragonflight.

With Deathwing currently occupied with other matters, we are going to find a way to redeem the black dragonflight.

And you are going to help us.

passages.title: Lifting the Veil
passages.text:
The black dragonflight was once noble. They were the earth warders, protecting the very land itself. How ironic that they would become the worst menace the land has known.

I believe that there remains a sliver of hope, however, and so does my mistress. The black dragonflight will live beyond Deathwing's treachery, and will soar as the noble earth warders once again.

I wish to show you something. Close your eyes, and I will reveal to you the final part of my studies.

passages.title: Lifting the Veil
passages.text: You are certainly impatient, <name>.

passages.title: Lifting the Veil
passages.text: We will find a shred of good within these dragons, <name>.  Whether it is in the wild eggs you found, the bodies of the whelplings you slew, or the eggs that we have encouraged Nyxondra to lay... we will find an untainted black dragon.

passages.title: The Venerable Doctor Blam
passages.text:
I made a calculated decision in revealing my identity to you, <name>. I needed you to trust me, but I can no longer stay here in Lethlor Ravine, as my cover has quite clearly been blown.

You may be able to slip away unnoticed, however. Here, take the results of our research, and bring them west. At Agmond's End, you will find a gnome who knows what to do with these samples.

Hurry, <name>! You mustn't loiter here any longer than necessary!

passages.title: The Venerable Doctor Blam
passages.text: Dr. H. Blam, at your service.  How can I be of assistance to you today?

passages.title: The Venerable Doctor Blam
passages.text:
Ooh!  Science stuff!  Let's see what you've got here...

Wild eggs?  Blech.  Useless.  These are never any good.

Ooooh, what's this?  Some sort of... pre-engineered egg?  This looks promising, but I don't want to know what Rhea had to do to get it.

Hmm... yes, some very nice corpses.  Very nice indeed.

Alright, I'll see what I can do.

passages.title: Easily Swayed
passages.text:
The most immediate threat to Fuselight is, without argument, the colony of ogres to the northwest.

Most of our ogre neighbors used to be warrior-types, but it seems that more and more of them are practicing magic. I won't have an army of ogre-magi at my doorstep.

Go take out some of those Dustbelcher ogres. Hopefully they'll get the picture and avoid messing with the might of Fuselight.

passages.title: Easily Swayed
passages.text: I'll feel much better when those ogres are gone.

passages.title: Easily Swayed
passages.text: I wonder where all of these ogre-magi are coming from?  Curious times, indeed.

passages.title: It's Goat Time, Baby
passages.text:
We have a little bit of a goat problem here in Fuselight, in case you haven't noticed. They'll eat anything, and they seem to have taken a liking to the piles of cogs and gears that we tend to leave sitting around.

It's getting really annoying!

You'll find most of the billy goats wandering around the edge of town, near the cliff's edge. Use this device on them to give 'em a little "nudge".

passages.title: It's Goat Time, Baby
passages.text: Well done!  I have no doubt that those goats will be back, but they'll think twice before they nibble my cogs again!

passages.title: Core Access Codes
passages.text:
The expedition's numbers are extremely large, user <name>.

Dealing with them by conventional means would take you an estimated 2,700,136.5 hours.

We can make use of a powerful source of energy held within expedition's crawler vehicle.

We will need the fusion core's access codes to accomplish this.

Mekgineer Twizzleflux has these codes and can be found at the Starwatch Tower to the southeast.

I've uploaded jamming frequencies to a scrambler. Use it to temporarily disable Twizzleflux's defenses.

passages.title: Core Access Codes
passages.text: Did you succeed, <name>?  I estimated your chances of survival at 68.5%.

passages.title: Core Access Codes
passages.text: Excellent job, user <name>.  We must obtain access to the fusion core now.

passages.title: Hacking the Wibson
passages.text:
It is true. New expedition crews have arrived by sea.

My scanners detect that they already have been afflicted by the curse phenomenon.

You must hurry and go aboard the M.A.C. Diver. The access codes will give us control over the fusion core's functions, but there is still a layer of security we must bypass.

User <name>, I must ask you to hack a very sophisticated mainframe known as the "Wibson."

Do not worry I will provide you with further instructions.

passages.title: Hacking the Wibson
passages.text: Greetings, user <name>.

passages.title: Hacking the Wibson
passages.text: I am in control, user <name>.  But I cannot keep the core temperature stable indefinitely.

passages.title: The Machination
passages.text:
<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

He-hello? <name>, are you there? Are you still alive? Hello?

Oh good, you're still there! What in the name of Lordareon are they building? It's some sort of mechanized monstrosity! You have to stop them from completing that...that...thing! 

Throw out the rules, do whatever you have to do to thwart them!

passages.title: The Machination
passages.text:
<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

You're nearing the heart of their domain. There will likely be an extremely fortified door protecting the inner sanctum of the entire Defias operation. See if you can find anything that might pry it open!

I suggest a stealthy method!

passages.title: Mathias Needs You
passages.text:
We've had some good times. I'm really sorry to see you go. But, Mathias says he needs you.

He said it's urgent!

So, you want to grab a drink or something after whatever, <buddy/lady>?

passages.title: Mathias Needs You
passages.text: Good, you're back. We know where Cho'gall's ultimate weapon is located!

passages.title: Garona Needs You
passages.text:
We've had some good times. I'm really sorry to see you go. But, Garona says she needs you.

She said it's urgent!

So, you want to grab a drink or something after whatever, <buddy/lady>?

passages.title: Garona Needs You
passages.text: Good, you're back. It's about time. We know where Cho'gall's ultimate weapon is located!

passages.title: The Hammer of Twilight
passages.text:
While you were in the mine, I was able to figure out where the Hammer of Twilight is being kept. They created it at the Altar of Twilight to the south.

More important than that, the cultists have made a critical error: Cho'gall is personally overseeing its final construction.

Many SI:7 died to bring us this information.

passages.title: The Hammer of Twilight
passages.text: The Hammer of Twilight floats in the middle of the altar, unprotected....

passages.title: The Admiral
passages.text:
<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

I can't believe it...they're almost done rebuilding it! We don't have much time, <name>.

Admiral Ripsnarl, Vanessa's right hand man, is bound to be on board. We'll never get to her if he's still alive to do anything about it. You're going to need to scale the unfinished Juggernaut, find Ripsnarl, and kill him so we can get to Vanessa's private quarters on the top deck.

Be careful, the Admiral bears the worgen curse and would take much pleasure in digging his claws into you!

passages.title: The Admiral
passages.text:
<Bzzzzzzzzzzzzt.>

Your exploits have gained quite the following in the intelligence community, <name>. Many top members of SI:7 have been earnestly watching you infiltrate the Deadmines through their own Stormwind Communicators.

Mathias Shaw himself wants to speak with you! I'll transfer you over momentarily.

passages.title: The Hammer of Twilight
passages.text:
While you were in the mine, I was able to figure out where the Hammer of Twilight is being kept. They created it at the Altar of Twilight to the south.

More important than that, the cultists have made a critical error: Cho'gall is personally overseeing its final construction.

<Garona begins sharpening her blades.>

Many Kor'kron died to bring us this information.

passages.title: The Hammer of Twilight
passages.text: The Hammer of Twilight floats in the middle of the altar, unprotected....

passages.title: The Defias Kingpin
passages.text:
Hello there, <name>. I've heard a great deal about you. Listen closely, you're only going to have one solid shot at this.

The new Defias Kingpin must be inside the hut orchestrating this entire operation. I want you to go inside and take her down, for the sake of the hundreds of innocent people the organization her father started has killed and terrorized.

I'm shocked that she would let you get so close to her domain without fleeing and waiting until more favorable conditions, but it seems we're in luck.

passages.title: The Defias Kingpin
passages.text: You very well may have saved all of Stormwind with your efforts here today, <name>. Vanessa may still be out there, but she is an insignificant threat now that the Juggernaut will be placed under our careful watch. Thank you.

passages.title: Dustwind Dig
passages.text:
I've got an idea, but it's a bit of a long shot. Thankfully, long shots happen to be a specialty of mine.

North of here, the Explorers' League has uncovered a new set of titan ruins beneath the sands. If there's anything older and wiser than dragons, it's titans. Heck, I've heard rumors that the titans CREATED the dragons.

Talk to Lead Prospector Durdin at the camp to the north. He'll have more information than I do about these titans.

What did I tell you? It's a long shot.

passages.title: Dustwind Dig
passages.text:
Titans?  You wanna know about titans?

You came to the right place, lad.  We're on the brink of somethin' big.

passages.title: Ancient Protectors
passages.text: You heard a good amount of rumbling happen in the tomb's central chamber. Those two large statues did look awfully suspicious.

passages.title: Tides of Darkness
passages.text:
The battle's proceeding just the way I wanted it. With their warriors nearly exhausted, I've sent in our cavalry.

What I wasn't expecting was ogres. Our knights are well matched against the brutes, but they're going to need help.

I need you back on the field right away, <name>. Few can bring down an ogre on foot, but I think I can count on you. Don't disappoint me.

passages.title: Tides of Darkness
passages.text: Going toe to toe with ogres is impressive, <name>. I'm glad I've got soldiers like you out here.

passages.title: The Warden's Pawn
passages.text:
Once those Reliquary honks got here, we panicked, and we all just started looting indiscriminately.

A lot of bad archaeology happened that day.

Luckily, Olga happened upon this small jade statue. We thought it to be a key of some sort, but can't figure out what it opens. Maybe you'll have some better luck with it.

passages.title: The Warden's Pawn
passages.text: <The statue clicks into place on the large stone slab.>

passages.title: The Sentinel's Pawn
passages.text:
We very nearly had this statue stolen from us by one of Bloodwatcher's Reliquary stooges. We managed to catch him in the act, and we've retrieved the statue, but it hasn't really paid off.

It appears to be a key of some sort, but I can't find the lock anywhere inside those ruins. You feel like giving it a try?

passages.title: The Sentinel's Pawn
passages.text: <The statue slides into place on the cold marble slab.>

passages.title: Welcome Relief
passages.text:
I've got boys formin' defensive lines on all sides of the town, keepin' back the elementals streaming from the torn ground. They're good lads and they've been holdin' firm, but even the sturdiest dwarf tires eventually.

They're split into shifts: one hour of rest for every hour on the line. Best I can get'm with the men we have.

If you want to be helpin', pick a line and take up a shift. Give some of my boys a welcome breather. Report back in once you've killed several of the elementals.

passages.title: Welcome Relief
passages.text: Don't be dallyin'. These men are pourin' every fiber of their bein' into holding this town, and I'll not see them insulted by the presence of anyone that won't hold their weight.

passages.title: Welcome Relief
passages.text: Good work, boy. Good to have another capable set of hands about.

passages.title: The Only Homes We Have
passages.text:
We've already been pushed back farther than I'd hoped, but I'm not about to give up our homes to these mongrels. They may burn them, pillage them, and spit on the rubbled remains, but we'll still fight to take them back.

That being said, I rather like them not burnt. I have the boys running buckets from the well to try to keep the fire down. If you'd join them, they can help out by tossing you buckets so you don't have to make the runs.

passages.title: The Only Homes We Have
passages.text: As long as we work together, we can overcome anything the Twilight's Hammer might throw at us.

passages.title: The Only Homes We Have
passages.text:
Thanks for your help. Every little bit makes a difference.

We'll keep the water going until we can push the Twilight back.

passages.title: Honorable Bearing
passages.text:
Iain, my second in command, bore the body of one of our fallen heroes to the cathedral to the west. He's the man I've put in charge of reforming a wing of gryphon riders from whatever scattered forces he can find. I would like you to help him.

I should impress upon you the urgency of this task. We will not be able to hold here forever; the Twilight's Hammer or the Dragonmaw orcs will eventually overwhelm us. Putting together an active gryphon wing may be our only hope for surviving these conflicts.

passages.title: Honorable Bearing
passages.text: Greetings, <race>. Sent by Keegan?

passages.title: Clan Mullan
passages.text:
If we're going to pull a full gryphon wing back together, we're going to need to move fast to gather the survivors before they leave or get picked off. I've got a bead on a few groups of riders that stuck together. I'm leavin' to find the Thundermar riders and the Moore riders shortly.

The Mullans were heading up west to the Crucible of Carnage last I saw. Go see if you can convince Duglas Mullan to join up with Keegan - he should owe him a favor or three.

passages.title: Clan Mullan
passages.text:
Iain sent ya?

You don't look like a Firebeard to me. Why exactly should I be listenin' to anything you say?

passages.title: Stubborn as a Doyle
passages.text:
The Doyle riders were last spotted convergin' in the trees to the south, on the border of the Obsidian Forest. They're a stubborn bunch and are likely to take some convincin' if they're going to join up with us.

Your best bet with Keeland Doyle is to tell'm Cailin Longfellow's taken up shelter with us back at the town. Keeland's got a good soft spot for her and she just might be enough to convince him to drag all his boys along.

passages.title: Stubborn as a Doyle
passages.text:
It seems the Doyles suffered the worst of the attacking Twilight drakes.

It's clear that they fought to the end: not a single rider's footprint more than a few yards from his gryphon. It's doubtful there were any survivors.

passages.title: Firebeard Bellows
passages.text:
I also need ya to seek out Mackay and his men on the other side of the Devouring Breach, at the Gorshak War Camp.

The Dragonmaw didn't survive the initial onslaught, and Mackay's lookin' to ransack what he can of their camp to supply our fight. There shouldn't be much convincin' necessary, but they'll likely want a hand wrappin' things up there before they make their way back to Keegan.

Give'm a boot in the arse from ol' Iain if ya have to.

passages.title: Firebeard Bellows
passages.text: Bout that time, eh? Help us wrap things up then.

passages.title: The Fighting Spirit
passages.text:
Keegan wants the Mullans to take wing with'm eh? If there's a dwarf I'd fly for, he'd be it. Still, I don't get why he'd be sendin' an outsider to be recruitin' me - not right polite by my standards.

I'm guessin' ya don't last 20 seconds with any of my boys, at the bar or in the battlefield. Prove me wrong. Take one of'm down in a fight and then I'll think about flyin' with ol' Keegan.

passages.title: The Fighting Spirit
passages.text: Naw, I'll not be fightin' ya. Get in there and challenge one of my boys if you've got a gut on ya at all.

passages.title: The Fighting Spirit
passages.text: That's the stuff! Not half bad. You've got a bit of fight in ya after all.

passages.title: Death Worthy of a Dragonmaw
passages.text:
The Twilight sacked this town, killin' most of the Dragonmaw that lived in it. A few survived though, and they're not right keen on us takin' liberties with their supplies.

Not that that matters much.

Well, I'm not right keen on them attackin' my boys. Kill'm off, chase'm out - I don't care, just get'm gone.

passages.title: Death Worthy of a Dragonmaw
passages.text: That's more like it. Let's finish gatherin' up supplies and get back to Keegan.

passages.title: Personal Request
passages.text:
Shame about the Doyles. It's a fair miracle that as many of us made it out as is though, so can't count it as much of a surprise.

Those louts at Thundermar are cowards. Even after tellin' them it was Keegan askin', they won't set foot outside of their town. I did rope in the Moores though, so that's at least three clans' worth.

Keegan wanted to hear from ya personally when you returned. Go find'm in town.

passages.title: Personal Request
passages.text:
It seems you had some luck bringin' riders back. Well timed too - we just pushed the elementals back, so we should have the arm room to lead an attack right away.

Thank you, <name>. You're a good <race>.

passages.title: Slithering Signs
passages.text:
I settled here well before Bogpaddle was founded, to brew my potions and find some peace and quiet. I know this swamp like the back of my old, gnarly hand.

There's been a change in the wildlife recently. Those winged snakes you may have seen in the stagalbog are wind serpents, and they haven't been seen around here for ages.

They're also prime for ingredients if they're the kind I'm thinking of. Be a dear and gather me some of their hearts, will you?

passages.title: Slithering Signs
passages.text: Don't be squeamish now.

passages.title: Slithering Signs
passages.text:
Let's have a look then...

Mmm, oh dear. That's what I thought these were. They might still be usable, but it's horrid to have such things in my backyard.

passages.title: Orcs and Humans
passages.text:
With war raging across the entire world, the last thing we need is a Horde settlement right in our backyard. Redridge, Duskwood, even Elwynn itself are all a day's march from here.

We've made the first strike, and I don't plan to give the Horde a chance to catch their breath. So consider yourself deployed. Grab a weapon, join the rest of the troops out in the Bloodmire, and start killing orcs.

Report back here after you've done some damage. I want you back alive...and that's an order. Dismissed!

passages.title: Orcs and Humans
passages.text: More black on you than red... that's what I like to see. Looks like you've got what it takes, <name>.

passages.title: Lumbering Oafs
passages.text:
I want victory to be totally assured here. Having more resources isn't enough; we need to make sure the enemy has nothing.

Stonard's forces depend on the lumber gathered from the surrounding woods. The orcish peons that chop the lumber may not be warriors, but they still know nothing but hate for humans.

Show no mercy. I want those peons killed and the supply of lumber to Stonard cut off completely.

passages.title: Lumbering Oafs
passages.text:
We've had strikes on our own lumber line while you've been gone. This should at least put us on equal footing for gathering rates.

Good work, <name>.

passages.title: A Dwarf's Got Needs
passages.text:
I can appreciate a good diggin' as much as any other dwarf, don't get me wrong. It's just that... well, we do so much diggin', and so little drinkin', that sometimes I wonder if I should just hang up me shovel and head back to Ironforge.

But not today. I've got some diggin' in me yet.

Those Dark Iron dwarves at Hammertoe's Digsite - just north of here - make some powerful fine beer, right here in the desert. You think you could pick up a few for me?

passages.title: A Dwarf's Got Needs
passages.text: <Sigrun licks his lips in anticipation.>

passages.title: A Dwarf's Got Needs
passages.text:
<Sigrun instantly downs a dusty mug of shadowstout.>

Wow, this stuff is strong!  I knew they had beer, but I never expected them to have shadowstout!  That's my favorite shadowbeer!

passages.title: The Good Stuff
passages.text:
I've got a little proposition for you, if you're interested.

Those Dark Irons were here before Durdin and his crew arrived. That means that, once these titan ruins opened up, the dark irons were the first ones in there, lootin' all the good stuff. I'll bet they've still got those treasures locked up inside Angor Fortress, northwest of here.

You've more than proven your ability to wallop a dwarf. Head on into that fortress and wallop your way to titan treasure.

I'd go with, but I'm drunk.

passages.title: The Good Stuff
passages.text: Back so soon?

passages.title: The Good Stuff
passages.text:
Now here's some treasure!  I was beginning to worry that these weren't titan ruins at all!

I'll show these to Durdin.  Thanks again, <name>.

passages.title: Survival of the Fattest
passages.text:
We're hard-up for supplies, stranger. With the black dragons raining destruction on what would be our hunting grounds, we have no way to get food.

The ogres to our southwest, however, have exactly what we need. Within their grotto you should find plenty of meat and crafting supplies.

They may put up a fight. Be on your guard.

passages.title: Survival of the Fattest
passages.text: Welcome back.

passages.title: Survival of the Fattest
passages.text: I imagine those ogres weren't too much trouble for you.  Here - some coin for your troubles.

passages.title: Into the Dragon's Mouth
passages.text:
<Dr. Blam stares at the egg in awed silence, blinks a few times, then looks up at you.>

D... did you see that? Incredible! My titan thing idea worked! With your help, of course.

We'll want to get this back to Rhea. She's not at Lethlor Ravine anymore; it sounds like she blew her cover pretty well when she transformed into her true form in front of all those whelps. She's now in the west, staying at an Alliance camp called Dragon's Mouth.

She'll be waiting for you. And for that egg.

passages.title: Into the Dragon's Mouth
passages.text: That's some precious cargo you carry there, <name>.

passages.title: Into the Dragon's Mouth
passages.text:
I'll take that egg out of your hands now.  We need to get this egg incubated... and hidden, quickly.  There are lots of angry dragons looking for this.

It's good to see you again, by the way.

passages.title: The Swift, the Fierce, and the Stout
passages.text:
In my haste to escape from Lethlor Ravine, I forgot to tie up one loose end: Nyxondra. She's free, and she's sounded the alarm among the black dragonflight. Half the flight is here in the western Badlands, combing for this egg.

I'll take care of hiding the egg. You're going to take care of some of the more troublesome dragons. And you'll have help.

Talk to Eric, over on the other side of camp. He and his brothers will be joining you.

passages.title: The Swift, the Fierce, and the Stout
passages.text:
You're the <race> we've been waiting for?  It's about time you got here.  My legs could use a stretch.

Come on boys!  Let's go kill us some black dragons!

passages.title: Eric, the Utility Dwarf
passages.text:
Before we get too crazy what with the dragon-killin', let me tell you a little bit about how I fight.

"The Swift" is what they call me, and here's why: I'll dash straight into your enemies - helmet first, mind you - and stun 'em for a few seconds. I also keep a few potions with me for tight spots.

Why don't we practice fightin' together? Head out into the field, and try out my abilities.

passages.title: Eric, the Utility Dwarf
passages.text: We're not through yet, <name>.

passages.title: Eric, the Utility Dwarf
passages.text:
I'm not what you'd call "very strong" or "battle-hardened", but I get the job done my own way.

Lookin' forward to fightin' with you.  I never fought with a fancy-lookin' <class> before.

passages.title: The Wrath of a Dragonflight
passages.text:
Hello, <name>. It looks like you four have had time to become well-acquainted.

I have my first assignment for you. Kalaran, an ancient black dragon of considerable power, has joined in the hunt for the egg we are protecting. We need to stop him before he gets too close.

You will find him and his minions at the Dustbowl, northeast of Dragon's Mouth. Hunt him down and defeat him. You will likely need the help of your new dwarven allies.

passages.title: The Wrath of a Dragonflight
passages.text: One less dragon to worry about, one step closer to redemption.  Onward, my soldiers!

passages.title: Their Hunt Continues
passages.text:
The black dragonflight means business. It appears that they've taken over a large portion of New Kargath, the large Horde settlement northwest of Dragon's Mouth. Their troops are under the command of General Jirakka and his champion, Moldarr. They must be stopped.

We dragons do not take part in the squabbles between Horde and Alliance, but I do understand the risk you take in entering New Kargath. Please, heroes... be careful.

passages.title: Their Hunt Continues
passages.text: Two more dangerous black dragons have been removed from this egg hunt.  Your greatest task, however, still awaits.

passages.title: The Sorrow and the Fury
passages.text:
My greatest regret is the treatment that we - no, I - gave to Nyxondra. I forced her to lay eggs, then I performed experiments on them. Over, and over, and over again.

Even as a mother myself, I can only imagine her sorrow.

No... I mustn't be weak. Our work is, after all, for the benefit of future generations of black dragons. Her sacrifice was necessary.

She circles the Ruins of Kargath, northwest of New Kargath, insane with fury. Please, heroes... put her out of her misery.

passages.title: The Sorrow and the Fury
passages.text: Just think... Nyxondra may end up being the mother of the new black dragonflight.  In death, she has given a gift to the future generations of Azeroth.

passages.title: The Hidden Clutch
passages.text:
With the major black dragons out of the Badlands, it is now safe to move the egg again. You will find me on a small plateau, north of New Kargath.

Come and find me.

passages.title: The Hidden Clutch
passages.text:
The egg must always be moving.  We are not safe anywhere.

Deathwing, even in his madness, knows all the hidden places in this world.  The egg must not rest.

passages.title: Baelog, the Glass Cannon
passages.text:
Before I start droppin' arrows on those dragons, I'd better introduce myself.

I'm Baelog, the muscle of this group. My sword bites like a crocolisk, and my arrows sing like banshees. I tend to wear down quickly, however, and can't take as much punishment as either of my two brothers.

You give the word, and I'll send an aimed shot right through your target's heart. I can also cheer my brothers on, sending 'em into a battle-fueled frenzy.

Why don't we go try fighting together?

passages.title: Baelog, the Glass Cannon
passages.text: We're not quite ready yet.  A little more practice, then we'll get with the dragon-slaying.

passages.title: Baelog, the Glass Cannon
passages.text: I think you're ready, <name>.  You're getting the hang of this.

passages.title: Olaf, the Big Fella'
passages.text:
You may not have noticed, but I'm pretty big, as far as dwarves go.

I make sure that my two brothers here don't get into too much trouble. They're small, and they don't have a big shield like me. I'm big, and I can handle a few monsters hitting me! Plus, if I'm careful, I can usually get them to hit my shield instead!

I can protect you, too. Come on, let's go practice for a bit. I'll make sure the enemies attack me, and not you.

passages.title: Olaf, the Big Fella'
passages.text: Don't worry, little <race>.  I'll protect you.

passages.title: Olaf, the Big Fella'
passages.text: See?  No need to worry when Olaf is around.  Just let me know, and I'll protect you from the monsters.

passages.title: Stopping the Spread
passages.text:
Slaying the foul creatures that plague the river will not be enough, <name>.

A new generation of these monstrosities already threatens to spawn within our holy waters.

Seek their foul eggs and destroy them.

passages.title: Stopping the Spread
passages.text: I thank you, <name>.  This will make our prophetic visions that much clearer.

passages.title: Trespassers in the Water
passages.text:
Shortly after Uldum's protective barriers fell, the Vir'naal river became afflicted with a terrible corruption.

Whether it was brought here maliciously or accidentally is not of great significance.

The result is the same. As the river becomes clouded so does our ability to peer into what the future holds for us.

Look outside, <class>. These foul creatures were never meant to live in the pristine waters of our river.

Slay them so that the river may grant us visions once again.

passages.title: Trespassers in the Water
passages.text:
Yes, <name>.  I can feel the disruption in the river fading.

Yet, I feel the source of this taint still lingers.

passages.title: Draenethyst Crystals
passages.text:
The lost ones who live in the Fallow Sanctuary look as we look, but they are monsters... driven mad by the rigors of our journey to Azeroth. Once our brethren, they now live in the Fallow Sanctuary to the west, catching or killing any who wander near.

And they have stolen something sacred to us--draenethyst crystals.

We lack the force to enter the Fallow Sanctuary and reclaim our stolen draenethyst from among their huts and campfires, but without those crystals... we too may lose our way.

passages.title: Draenethyst Crystals
passages.text: Do you have the crystals?

passages.title: Draenethyst Crystals
passages.text: Thank you, <name>.  We, are in your debt.

passages.title: Only the Beginning
passages.text:
I miss the days when legions of powerful ogres marched by the Horde's side into battle, the pathetic Alliance cowering at their ferocity. Perhaps those days will return before I am gone to the ancestors.

However, that is not the case now. An ogre magi, Glubtok, has joined forces with the despicable Defias Brotherhood and acts as Foreman over their mining operations. The pathetic fool! End his life for me, and for the spirit and glory of the Horde!

passages.title: Only the Beginning
passages.text:
Do not be alarmed, <name>. I am close to you, waiting in the shadows. You've done well.

You must continue the mission here - I am too valuable to risk my life against petty criminals like these.

passages.title: Reinforcements Denied
passages.text:
Just killing ogres won't be enough. The ogres themselves are being summoned onto the battlefield far too rapidly.

I need you to go far behind the enemy line and seek out their summoners. The orcs are using warlocks to bring their reinforcements in.

Cut down the warlocks, and the portals should close. There aren't many of them; a quick, surgical strike should cripple the enemy.

passages.title: Reinforcements Denied
passages.text: Once again, well done. With a few more pushes the battle will be ours.

passages.title: Traitors!!!
passages.text:
The goblins you'll find working with the Defias are officially traitors to the Bilgewater Cartel, the Shattered Hand, and the Horde itself!
