I haven't yet been initiated into the Shattered Hand, so my loyalties lie strongly with my people. Helix Gearbreaker apparently has no time for such associations, and works on building a mast for the Defias Juggernaut. On behalf of Miss Mayhem and myself, would you kindly 'dispose' of Helix?

passages.title: Traitors!!!
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Traitors!!!
passages.text:
My employers do not take kindly to traitors.

On the flip side, they are renown for their kindness towards the loyal! You deserve to be rewarded!

passages.title: Not Quite There
passages.text:
These prototypes are going to change the face of Horde warfare when I perfect them! The issue I've been having is that their power sources don't allow for complicated combat maneuvers or large frames, both highly desired traits when it comes to fighting Alliance.

The Defias, with some help from goblin traitors like Helix, have almost completed the Foe Reaper 5000, a massive golem that will actually work!

We can't have that going public, can we? I'll lose customers!

passages.title: Not Quite There
passages.text:
Brilliant! Now all I have to do is finish my work, and my Mayhem Reapers will cause...mayhem...on any Horde front!

And there won't be any Defias knockoffs to steal my profits!

passages.title: Good Intentions...Poor Execution
passages.text:
The Defias plan to finish their Juggernaut and use it to lay waste to Stormwind. It is a noble cause any true orc warrior would embrace without a single thought!

Vanessa's fault lies in her execution of their plan. The ship is poorly constructed, the crew practically untrained, and, worst of all, there's a worgen in their midst!

His name is Admiral Ripsnarl, and he must be mercilessly slain in the name of the Warchief. Lok'tar ogar!

passages.title: Good Intentions...Poor Execution
passages.text:
It's a shame that he was both a human and a worgen. Had he been a proud orc warrior I'd have liked to charge into battle alongside such a fierce combatant.

We can speak of ill-fated desires another day. It is time to take what is ours from the enemy.

passages.title: Assault on Stonard
passages.text:
This is it, <name>. We've made our final push into Stonard itself.

I shouldn't have to remind anyone, but I'll say it anyway: We're not orcs, and we're not going to become them out of revenge or spite. Stonard will not be burned to the ground for us to dance on the ashes.

No, I want this done right. I want this surgical. Hold your head high and strike down any orc that picks up a weapon.

passages.title: Assault on Stonard
passages.text: You've followed orders well, <name>. On behalf of the crown, I'm rewarding you for your bravery on the battlefield.

passages.title: The Defias Kingpin
passages.text:
The Shattered Hand has laid mostly quiet for years now.

No more!

You will be the instrument of our rebirth, <name>. Slay the Defias Kingpin and commandeer her ship for the Horde! We will outfit it as a proper orc warship and use it to finally lay waste to Stormwind

Any survivors will spread word of our unstoppable power across all of Azeroth, and all will tremble before our might!

Go now, VanCleef's death will be your greatest triumph yet hero.

passages.title: The Defias Kingpin
passages.text:
COWARD!!! Vanessa VanCleef is a dirty human coward! How dare she flee from battle against the Horde and leave her unworthy subordinate to fight!

<Kagtha composes herself.>

No matter. Her ship is reward enough. The citizens of Stormwind will bear first hand witness to our awe inspiring power using a ship made in part by the very architect of their city!

passages.title: Cutting Supply
passages.text:
We may not be flattening Stonard into dust, but I don't want to have to go in there a second time.

I want you to gather any supplies you see in the town while you're there. Without food, they won't have any fighters after more than a day.

There should be crates scattered all over town.

passages.title: Cutting Supply
passages.text: What's the situation?

passages.title: Cutting Supply
passages.text: Good work, <name>. With this, it's only a matter of time until the orcs are fleeing for the portal or begging for surrender.

passages.title: Orcs and Humans
passages.text:
War rages in the swamp, <name>. Vicious humans have settled north of the city and brought an army to our doorstep.

There is nothing in this swamp for them. Their sole reason for coming here is to attack us, unprovoked. We will not give them the pleasure of victory!

We are undermanned and I need every able orc to take to the battlefield. Go, and slay as many humans as you can.

passages.title: Orcs and Humans
passages.text: I'm pretty sure you still have some slaying to do.

passages.title: Orcs and Humans
passages.text: We will fight to the last orc, <name>. I hope you'll keep yourself alive long enough to properly destroy these trespassers.

passages.title: Lumbering Oafs
passages.text:
We are outnumbered by the Alliance. In their fear they send an army to crush a single settlement. But we will not give!

Without resources, their soldiers will be at a disadvantage. Human peasants busy themselves in the woods outside Marshtide Watch, gathering lumber to rebuild their crumbling walls.

Deny them the wood, and their lives.

passages.title: Lumbering Oafs
passages.text:
No true member of the Horde should find pleasure in killing such terrified weaklings... without challenge, victory has no true thrill.

But your dirty work has helped stave off the Alliance and protect our homes here. Be proud of your work for the Horde.

passages.title: Tides of Darkness
passages.text:
We have suffered many losses, <name>. Dreadmaul Hold has sent ogres from the Blasted Lands as reinforcements, but they can only send so many; the Alliance attacks them as well, even as we speak.

The Alliance has countered our ogres with mounted knights, a strategy that served them well in the Second War. We will need our strongest warriors to turn the tide of battle!

Return to the Bloodmire, <name>, and bring down those knights!

passages.title: Tides of Darkness
passages.text: The ogres are powerful, but without help they will fall to the Alliance riders.

passages.title: Tides of Darkness
passages.text: You are a true champion, <name>, to take the lives of so many on the battlefield. I hope it will be enough to save Stonard.

passages.title: Reinforcements Denied
passages.text:
The Alliance has brought in their mages to summon more reinforcements directly to the battlefield from beyond their fortress. This must be stopped!

Their numbers are few, but a single portal can turn the tide of battle. Attack their mages and shut off those portals!

passages.title: Reinforcements Denied
passages.text: With no link to the outside, the Alliance must rely on what they've brought to the swamp. We shall see if they can handle our home environment.

passages.title: Marking the Fallen
passages.text:
Many warriors have met death to bring us victory, <name>. The fate of a true orc.

I have seen the way the Alliance loots the bodies of our fallen, clutching at our goods like packrats. They will not defile our fallen heroes on this field.

Take these wards with you to the Bloodmire. Place them on the bodies of our fallen warriors. I will be watching, to see how many have fallen, and to honor their sacrifice. Let us hope the spirits give us aid for our respect.

passages.title: Marking the Fallen
passages.text: You honor both the dead and the living with your courage, <name>.

passages.title: We're Under Attack!
passages.text:
The Alliance are at our walls!

Your actions delayed them and weakened their forces, <name>, but in the end we are outnumbered. This is our last stand. Victory or death...

Fight with honor, <name>. They are within the walls as we speak. Drive the human dogs from Stonard, for the Horde!

passages.title: We're Under Attack!
passages.text: There is no time! Go! Fight!

passages.title: We're Under Attack!
passages.text: The Alliance is driven out! Stonard will be safe, thanks to your ferocity. Lok'tar Ogar!

passages.title: Rheastrasza's Gift
passages.text: Wait here. I will retrieve the egg.

passages.title: The Egg Lives On
passages.text:
You were not the only mortal that Rheastrasza confided in.  I too earned the dragon's trust.

I have already moved the real purified egg on to a safer location, away from the Badlands.  It will continue to grow, out of Deathwing's sight.

The red dragonflight is as benevolent as it is powerful.  It was Rheastrasza's final wish that I give this to you.

passages.title: The Lost Ones
passages.text:
When the Dark Portal closed many years ago, regret and fear seized many of us who had come to these lands. In their despair, they cursed the name of the Light, and sank into violence and hatred.

These fallen souls are now the Lost Ones, little more than mindless monsters, attacking all who approach. They grow more corrupt by the day, and as they die off, they have begun to kidnap from the Harborage..

They are beyond help, <name>. Their suffering must end. Will you put them from their misery?

passages.title: The Lost Ones
passages.text: It still pains my heart to have asked you to do this, though I know there is no other way. You have saved those of us still holding on from a terrible menace.

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Bloodeye Bruiser!
passages.text:
I was wondering when you'd show up, <name>! Having a past champion of the Ring of Blood here will be a huge draw! We're gonna be rich, buddy! RICH!

Anyway, this is some old Dragonmaw fighting pit. Didn't take much modification to tune it up to our uses. I put out a few feelers, and got some heavy hitters from all around Azeroth to join in the carnage. Bout time to make some gold!

You know the drill, <name>. When you're ready, let me know and we'll get this show on the road!

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Bloodeye Bruiser!
passages.text:
Well well, if it isn't the once champion of anguish, <name>! I'm seeing good money in the future now that you're here! We're gonna be rollin in the dough, buddy! Filthy RICH!

Anyway, this is some old Dragonmaw fighting pit. Didn't take much modification to tune it up to our uses. I put out a few feelers, and got some heavy hitters from all around Azeroth to join in the carnage. Bout time to make some gold!

You know the drill, <name>. When you're ready, let me know and we'll get this show on the road!

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Bloodeye Bruiser!
passages.text:
I'll tell you what, buddy, this place is a far cry from the rolling plains of Nagrand or the bloodbowl in Zul'Drak, but hey, I go where the gold's at! So welcome to Twi-Hi, pal.

You're new to this pit, so let me set you straight. I'm the fight promoter and this feisty troll next to me is Wodin, my bodyguard. You're the entertainment. When you wanna fight, let me know and I'll set up the match.

If you're ready and got a group of friends with you, we can start! What do you say?

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Bloodeye Bruiser!
passages.text: No payout until the fight's over, man.

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Bloodeye Bruiser!
passages.text: Not bad, friend. You might make some gold out here - if you manage to stay alive.

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Deadly Dragonmaw!
passages.text:
You're going to love this one! The Dragonmaw heard you were entering the arena and they're determined to make sure you don't leave it.

Time for some good ol' <race> on orc action! Let me know when you're ready to do this!

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Deadly Dragonmaw!
passages.text: No love in your heart for orcs I see. You really made a mess of that guy.

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Wayward Wildhammer!
passages.text:
You're going to love this one! The Wildhammer heard you were entering the arena and they're determined to make sure you don't leave it.

Time for some good ol' <race> on dwarf action! Let me know when you're ready to do this!

passages.title: The Crucible of Carnage: The Wayward Wildhammer!
passages.text: No love in your heart for dwarves I see. You really made a mess of that guy.

passages.title: The Dragon and the Temple
passages.text:
These serpents must be from the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. I already had a hint...

Not a few days ago, I had a visitor stop by and ask me to keep an eye out for such things. An elf by the name of Itharius. I'm sure he didn't think I could see through his form... he was a green dragon in disguise, come here to help his fallen brothers no doubt.

He may very well be on to something. Itharius left for the temple itself. Perhaps you'd better go look for him there. Dark things are afoot.

passages.title: The Dragon and the Temple
passages.text:
The goblin sent you? She has a cunning eye, that one.

She speaks the truth. I am here to stem the tide of corruption seeping from this temple. If you would save your people from a wicked fate, <name>, I ask for your assistance.

passages.title: To Marshtide Watch
passages.text:
Regardless of whether you assist me within the temple, your people must be told of what is brewing here.

North of the temple, humans of your mortal Alliance have built what they call Marshtide Watch. They war with the Horde across the swamp, a raging conflict that I foresee only worsening.

It is not my role to interfere in mortal affairs, <name>. I simply ask you bring warning to your people of what lurks within the temple.

passages.title: To Marshtide Watch
passages.text: Trouble within the temple... I wish we could spare forces to deal with it. The war with Stonard is already raging, and we need every man we can get.

passages.title: To Stonard
passages.text:
Regardless of whether you assist me within the temple, your people must be told of what is brewing here.

Southwest of the temple is the Horde town of Stonard. The orcs there wage war with the new human arrivals to the swamp, a raging conflict that I foresee only worsening.

It is not my role to interfere in mortal affairs, <name>. I simply ask you bring warning to your people of what lurks within the temple.

passages.title: To Stonard
passages.text: We have no time to send orcs to the temple, <name>. The humans come, and they are many. Stonard must be defended!

passages.title: Aviana's Legacy
passages.text:
Your expertise is needed elsewhere, <name>.

Just southwest of the World Tree you will find the Shrine of Aviana, home to the Druids of the Talon. Aviana, the matron of all winged creatures, gave her life for this world ten thousand years ago.

I sense her shrine is being threatened, as are the druids who guard it. Seek out Choluna, one of the wisest of the winged druids, deep within the shrine.

passages.title: Aviana's Legacy
passages.text:
Ysera herself sent you to me? Oh! It's a honor to speak with a representative of the aspects.

It's true that our shrine is in jeopardy. The harpies we once sheltered in our boughs have suddenly turned against us.

But please, don't rejoin the fight until you are ready. Our shrine is no mere battleground. Use its peace and power to center yourself.

passages.title: Prayerblossom
passages.text:
I have worked for years to try to cure the affliction of the Broken. The foul energies that corrupted them did more than twist their bodies; it took the comfort of the Light from them. They cannot feel its warmth.

I cannot let Magtoor pass on in darkness, <name>. Before he worsened, I was studying prayerblossom, a flower that grows in the shifting mire. It grows hardy in even the darkest shade. I beg of you, gather these flowers for me, for Magtoor's sake.

passages.title: Prayerblossom
passages.text: Have you brought the prayerblossom?

passages.title: Prayerblossom
passages.text: Prayerblossom has been used by the Broken as a remedy since they settled in this swamp. If it soothes the physical form, it might be used for more powerful healing...

passages.title: Secrets of the Mire
passages.text:
The Shifting Mire takes its name from a unique phenomenon. By some force, the extremely fine silt will collect, and move on its own accord, travelling as if alive.

I originally worried this was some corruptive force, but my studies have shown the opposite; whatever energy invigorates this soil is positive in nature. Perhaps such vibrant life can be imparted onto the Broken to reawaken what they once were.

The silt may not take kindly to being collected, <name>. But please, help gather it.

passages.title: Secrets of the Mire
passages.text: Did you get those samples?

passages.title: Secrets of the Mire
passages.text: It will have to be purified, but this will be most helpful. Thank you.

passages.title: The Morons' League
passages.text:
I need your help in a little project I'm working on, <name>. It falls into a realm I like to call "defensive archaeology".

I like to bury non-magical items in conspicuous places to fool those Alliance idiots into thinking they've found something valuable.

Hmm... Dark Iron dwarves wander Hammertoe's Digsite and Angor Fortress, to the north. Bring their heads back to me. Yes, that's right, their heads.

Once the flesh is stripped, we can use those skulls to interfere with the dwarves' work.

passages.title: The Morons' League
passages.text: <Lidia waits expectantly.>

passages.title: The Morons' League
passages.text: Excellent!  We'll bury these immediately.  Those Explorers' League dimwits will never suspect us!

passages.title: Forcible Acquisition
passages.text:
I've got a little proposition for you, if you're interested.

The Dark Iron dwarves were here long before we arrived. That means that, once these titan ruins opened up, the Dark Irons were the first ones in there, looting all the choice items. I'll bet they've still got those treasures locked up inside Angor Fortress, northwest of here.

I want you to find such a treasure... then steal it.

passages.title: Forcible Acquisition
passages.text: Back so soon?

passages.title: Forcible Acquisition
passages.text:
I knew it!  The High Examiner will be pleased to see this.

Nice work, <race>.

passages.title: Survival of the Fattest
passages.text:
We're hard-up for supplies, stranger. With the black dragons raining destruction on our hunting grounds, we have no way to get food.

The ogres to our south, however, have exactly what we need. Within their grotto you should find plenty of meat and crafting supplies.

They may put up a fight. Be on your guard.

passages.title: Survival of the Fattest
passages.text: Welcome back.

passages.title: Survival of the Fattest
passages.text: I imagine those ogres weren't too much trouble for you.  Here - some coin for your troubles.

passages.title: The Warden's Pawn
passages.text:
One of the few items of worth that we managed to loot from these ruins is this small jade statue.

We believe it to be a key of some sort, but we're unable to determine what it opens. As such, it is useless to me.

Perhaps you'll have some better luck with it.

passages.title: The Warden's Pawn
passages.text: <The statue clicks into place on the large stone slab.>

passages.title: The Sentinel's Pawn
passages.text:
We found this small red statue on the corpse of one of those Explorers' League archaeologists. Sadly, it wasn't us who killed him. The local wildlife had already taken care of that.

The statue is well-crafted, but apparently bereft of magical power. You may use it for whatever means you deem necessary.

passages.title: The Sentinel's Pawn
passages.text: <The statue slides into place on the cold marble slab.>

passages.title: The Warden's Game
passages.text:
You see the statue split into two, then four, then eight identical statues in a square formation.

You hear a voice, not through your ears, but in the back of your mind:

 "A true warden does not face OUTWARD, searching for signs of danger.
 A true warden keeps his gaze INWARD, always focused on protecting his quarry."

Perhaps this is a riddle of some sort?

passages.title: The Sentinel's Game
passages.text:
As you place the statue in its place, several other stone statues appear in the room. One more ruby-colored statue also appears, in a small enclosure on the far end of the room. You hear a voice:

 "The Sentinel watches.
 The Sentinel protects.
 The Sentinel's vision never falters."

That red statue on the other side of the room looks important. Perhaps you should try to connect the two red statues?

passages.title: Ancient Protectors
passages.text: You heard a good amount of rumbling happen in the tomb's central chamber. Those two large statues did look awfully suspicious.

passages.title: New Kargath
passages.text:
<Dr. Blam stares at the egg in awed silence, blinks a few times, then looks up at you.>

D... did you see that? Incredible! My titan thing idea worked! With your help, of course.

We'll want to get these back to Rhea. She's not at Lethlor Ravine anymore; it sounds like she blew her cover when she transformed into her true form in front of all those whelps. She's now in the west, staying at a large Horde establishment dubbed "New Kargath".

She'll be waiting for you. And for that egg.

passages.title: New Kargath
passages.text: That's some precious cargo you carry there, <name>.

passages.title: New Kargath
passages.text:
I'll take that egg out of your hands now.  We need to get this egg incubated... and hidden, quickly.  There are lots of angry dragons looking for this.

It's good to see you again, by the way.

passages.title: The Bad Dogs
passages.text:
In my haste to escape from Lethlor Ravine, I forgot to tie up one loose end: Nyxondra. She's free, and she's sounded the alarm among the black dragonflight. Half the flight is here in the western Badlands, combing for this egg.

I'll take care of hiding the egg. You're going to take care of some of the more troublesome dragons. And you'll have help.

I've paid off a couple of mercenaries to help you. You'll find them inside this inn.

passages.title: The Bad Dogs
passages.text:
You're the <race> we've been waiting for?  It's about time you got here.  My legs could use a stretch.

Come on boys!  Let's go kill us some black dragons!

passages.title: Amakkar, Jack of All Trades
passages.text:
Before we get too crazy with the dragon-killing, let me tell you a little bit about how I fight.

I'm not terribly strong or stalwart like these other two, but I've got a few tricks. At your command I'll stun your enemies to keep 'em held still. I also make sure to keep a few potions around for tight spots.

Why don't we practice fighting together? Head out into the field, and you can see what it's like to fight with a real orc.

passages.title: Amakkar, Jack of All Trades
passages.text: We're not through yet, <name>.

passages.title: Amakkar, Jack of All Trades
passages.text: I'm looking forward to fighting with you.

passages.title: Jurrix the Striker
passages.text:
Oh, you want to talk? Fine.

I'm Jurrix, the only merc here with half a brain. The only one with any bite to my attacks, too. The only reason I keep these meat shields around is to keep myself from getting killed.

Listen, you're the boss of this operation. You give the word, and I'll send a fireball right through your target's heart. If things start getting hectic, I can even warp time a bit so you can fit in a few extra attacks.

Why don't we go try fighting together?

passages.title: Jurrix the Striker
passages.text: We're not quite ready yet.  A little more practice, then we'll get with the dragon-slaying.

passages.title: Jurrix the Striker
passages.text: I think you're ready, <name>.  You're getting the hang of this.

passages.title: Gargal, the Behemoth
passages.text:
You may not have noticed, but I'm pretty big, as far as orcs go.

I make sure that my two pals here don't get into too much trouble. They're small, and they don't have a big shield like me. I'm big, and I can handle a few monsters hitting me! Plus, if I'm careful, I can usually get them to hit my shield instead!

I can protect you, too. Come on, let's go practice for a bit. I'll make sure the enemies attack me, and not you.

passages.title: Gargal, the Behemoth
passages.text: Don't worry, little <race>.  I'll protect you.

passages.title: Gargal, the Behemoth
passages.text: See?  No need to worry when Gargal is around.  Just let me know, and I'll protect you from the monsters.

passages.title: The Wrath of a Dragonflight
passages.text:
Hello, <name>. It looks like you four have had time to become well-acquainted.

I have my first assignment for you. Kalaran, an ancient black dragon of considerable power, has joined in the hunt for the egg we are protecting. We need to stop him before he gets too close.

You will find him and his minions at the Dustbowl, east of New Kargath. Hunt him down and defeat him. You will likely need the help of your new mercenary allies.

passages.title: The Wrath of a Dragonflight
passages.text: One less dragon to worry about, one step closer to redemption.  Onward, my soldiers!

passages.title: Their Hunt Continues
passages.text: The black dragonflight means business. As you've probably already noticed, they've taken over a large portion of New Kargath. These troops are under the command of General Jirakka and his champion, Moldarr. They must be stopped.

passages.title: Their Hunt Continues
passages.text: Two more dangerous black dragons have been removed from this egg hunt.  Your greatest task, however, still awaits.

passages.title: The Sorrow and the Fury
passages.text:
My greatest regret is the treatment that we - no, I - gave to Nyxondra. I forced her to lay eggs, then I performed experiments on them. Over, and over, and over again.

Even as a mother myself, I can only imagine her sorrow.

No... I mustn't be weak. Our work is, after all, for the benefit of future generations of black dragons. Her sacrifice was necessary.

She circles the Ruins of Kargath, northwest of New Kargath, insane with fury. Please, heroes... put her out of her misery.

passages.title: The Sorrow and the Fury
passages.text: Just think... Nyxondra may end up being the mother of the new black dragonflight.  In death, she has given a gift to the future generations of Azeroth.

passages.title: The Hidden Clutch
passages.text:
With the major black dragons out of the Badlands, it is now safe to move the egg again. You will find me on a small plateau, north of New Kargath.

Come and find me.

passages.title: The Hidden Clutch
passages.text:
The egg must always be moving.  We are not safe anywhere.

Deathwing, even in his madness, knows all the hidden places in this world.  The egg must not rest.

passages.title: Rheastrasza's Gift
passages.text: Wait here. I will retrieve the egg.

passages.title: That Gleam in his Eye
passages.text:
If you're looking for Harrison, you just missed him.

He was going on and on about his latest discovery, and how everything was beginning to make sense.

Whatever... he certainly wasn't making sense to me.

I tried to convince him to stay here and just enjoy a few desert sunsets with me, but there's no talking to him when he gets that gleam in his eye.

Perhaps you'd be willing to check in on him?

He was headed to that big monolith, south of here.

passages.title: That Gleam in his Eye
passages.text: It would seem that I'm not the only one interested in these obelisks...

passages.title: I've Got This Guy
passages.text:
Good timing, <name>.

Seems I'm not the only one interested in these obelisks, and these fellas aren't inclined to compare notes...

I think I can handle this guy.

Maybe you could take care of a few of his friends before they make their way over here?

passages.title: I've Got This Guy
passages.text: This guy's tougher than he looks - and he looks tough!

passages.title: I've Got This Guy
passages.text:
That's a relief. Thanks, <name>.

Turns out I've got my hands full here.

passages.title: They Don't Know What They've Got Here
passages.text:
Listen, <name>. I don't have a lot of time to talk here.

These guys are excavating relics from this site and taking pieces of ancient technology that we need!

I need you to check their crates for pieces of an ancient activation device. The officers should have the codes you'll need to open them.

Hurry!

We can't let them load this stuff into their planes!

passages.title: They Don't Know What They've Got Here
passages.text: Have you got the titan activation device, <name>?

passages.title: They Don't Know What They've Got Here
passages.text:
That's it!

Good work, <name>!

passages.title: The Purespring
passages.text:
Magtoor has told me of the shamanism that the Broken practice. The great Nobundo once said that the path of the elements may, in a way, be another way to the Light.

I can only hope there is some truth in this. The elementals that gather near Purespring Cavern to the south are a source of truly pristine water. They can be chaotic and violent, but the pure water harvested from them will be the perfect conduit for the blessing of the Light.

Please, bring me this water, <name>.

passages.title: The Purespring
passages.text: Have the elements given up their source?

passages.title: The Purespring
passages.text: Such clarity... let us hope this will aid poor Magtoor.

passages.title: Ignition
passages.text:
This guy just won't go down!

You're doin' great, kid. Only one thing left to do.

According to my research, there should be a titan statue down below. Use the device to activate it, then break it down.

If my theory is correct, that statue holds the key to reactivating this obelisk.

passages.title: Ignition
passages.text: Time to see if this old mechanism still works...

passages.title: Ignition
passages.text:
According to Harrison's notes, placing the lens upon this dais should re-activate this obelisk.

Exactly what that means remains to be seen...

passages.title: Breath of Mist
passages.text:
The Grell are forest spirits that wander the Misty Valley to the east. Though they resemble imps, I have found no demonic traces among the ones I've studied. They are, as far as I can tell, uncorrupted. 

Those that dwell in the valley move as one with the wind, summoning gusts of breeze at their whim. This pure air may be incorporated into my remedy for poor Magtoor.

Please, <name>, gather the smoky crystals found within the grells' bodies for me. I must exhaust every potential cure.

passages.title: Breath of Mist
passages.text: Do you have the crystals?

passages.title: Breath of Mist
passages.text: I can only hope this will lead to a cure, <name>. Thank you for bringing it to me.

passages.title: Neeka Bloodscar
passages.text:
There is much work to do in recovering from the assault and bracing ourselves for the next one. I will need coordination from all of our scouts.

Neeka Bloodscar is our finest tracker, trained in the harsh Badlands. She has been sent west to Splinterspear Junction to watch for Alliance activity.

Go to Neeka, <name>. Tell her of what has occured in Stonard. Assist her in any way she requires.

passages.title: Neeka Bloodscar
passages.text: I hope the sight of my sniveling amuses you, <name>. It will be the only joy here.

passages.title: Prayerblossom
passages.text:
I have been ruined, <class>. I placed my strength in Helgrum, and now it bleeds from his gaping wounds. Wounds too deep to heal, flesh that refuses to knit.

He murmurs in fear, consumed by fever and pain. I cannot leave his side. Not now. Please, I ask you in shame to gather herbs for me.

The prayerblossom that grows in the swamp is an old remedy for soothing. With enough of it, his pain might be stilled.

passages.title: Prayerblossom
passages.text: Have you brought the prayerblossom?

passages.title: Prayerblossom
passages.text: I will grind these and try to get him to eat. Thank you.

passages.title: Secrets of the Mire
passages.text:
Helgrum's wounds fester in the swamp air. They swell and ooze, filling his final moments with suffering. I must have something to coat them with.

The spirits move through this mire. They inhabit the mud itself, pushing it along in clumps of fine soil that take on lives of their own

The spirits of the cool, pure mud will offer him some comfort. Please, gather it for me, for I cannot abandon his side.

passages.title: Secrets of the Mire
passages.text: Helgrum still breathes. Do you have the mud?

passages.title: Secrets of the Mire
passages.text: At least I can soothe him with my own hands while he still breathes. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Purespring
passages.text:
Helgrum's breathing slows. His time is near.

I need water. Elementals roam the ponds of Purespring Cavern. The water that flows from them is the purest in this swamp.

Even if I could risk leaving Helgrum's side, my axe would shudder in my hand. I must beg you once again to pity me, for his comfort. Bring me the motes of the elementals, that his final drink may be pure and refreshing.

passages.title: The Purespring
passages.text: You've returned.

passages.title: The Purespring
passages.text:
He can only drink so much. The rest might be used for washing his body, after...

<Neeka glares in frustration and shudders, turning her head away.>

passages.title: Last Regrets
passages.text:
If I am reduced to groveling, I may as well ask everything I can. There is one last favor I would ask of you, one more task a shamed orc pleads for.

Helgrum had a prized prey. Duskfang, eater of ogres, the great panther of Misty Valley. He would never allow himself the leisure of stalking it. Though he wanted badly to hunt, our scouting duties were too important.

If he cannot hunt Duskfang in this world, he can hunt the beast in the next. Take up the hunt for him; bring Duskfang's pelt to me.

passages.title: Last Regrets
passages.text: Has Duskfang shown himself?

passages.title: Last Regrets
passages.text:
With Duskfang to shroud his body, he will carry the animal's spirit with him into the afterlife.

Listen to me. An old superstitious fool. I'm so sorry, Helgrum...

passages.title: With Dying Breath
passages.text:
He stirs...

Do not leave, <name>. Please, honor Helgrum with me. You have done so much for him.

passages.title: With Dying Breath
passages.text:
He is gone.

He is right. I must be strong for him...

passages.title: The Titans' Trove
passages.text: As the second defender falls to the ground, a chest appears in the back of the chamber. Could this be what they were protecting?

passages.title: The Titans' Trove
passages.text: You peer into the chest...

passages.title: The Titans' Trove
passages.text: As the second defender falls to the ground, a chest appears in the back of the chamber. Could this be what they were protecting?

passages.title: The Titans' Trove
passages.text: You peer into the chest...

passages.title: The Heart of the Temple
passages.text:
I must confess I have a more personal involvement in this affair. One of the first of the green dragons corrupted here was my brother, Eranikus.

I thought Eranikus gone, lost forever to the darkest rifts of nightmare, but I have heard that his shade has emerged within the temple. I know not whether it is truly him, or an empty, mournful echo.

If you wish to help me further, return to the Hall of Masks and journey through the archway into the true sanctum of the temple. I will find you there.

passages.title: The Heart of the Temple
passages.text: I am pleased to see you once again, <name>. You are truly noble to assist me further.

passages.title: Ruag's Report
passages.text:
Here is Ruag's report, <name>. Let him know his scout is still here.

Do not speak of Helgrum. I will not distract others with news of tragedy.

I have to be strong. We all have to be strong.

passages.title: Ruag's Report
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Ruag's Report
passages.text:
<Ruag reads over the report.>

I see.  Thank you for this information, <name>.

passages.title: Sniffing Them Out
passages.text:
I could smell Godfrey and his companions a mile away from here. They did an exceedingly poor job covering their tracks in flight. It will be the mistake that puts the final nail in their coffins.

One of them is very close, and though the scent has changed slightly in undeath, I'm fairly certain it's Ashbury's. Go inside and tear him to pieces, we'll ensure the Forsaken do not intervene with our task.

passages.title: Sniffing Them Out
passages.text: Kill Ashbury before I lose my patience. You wouldn't like me when I'm angry...

passages.title: Sniffing Them Out
passages.text:
The scent of freshly spilled traitor blood fills my nostrils, and it is absolutely invigorating. However, my bloodlust will not be sated until Godfrey lies on the floor as a lifeless heap.

He thinks an army of mindless corpses can stop the wrath of the Bloodfang? We'll gnaw on their bones for years to come after our work is done!

passages.title: The Harborage
passages.text:
Anchorite Avuun is one of our uncorrupted brethren, what other races know as Draenei. He came to The Harborage to heal us, and try to find a cure. It is he who sent me here to collect these crystals.

He watches over a very sick friend now... and despite sending word to the Exodar itself, he has not found any aid so far. Could you bring these crystals to him, <name>? You may be the only one able to assist him.

passages.title: The Harborage
passages.text: Thank you, <class>. I am afraid it may be too late... but I refuse to give up, even if the Exodar itself does not hear my cries.

passages.title: Onward to the Blasted Lands
passages.text:
We appreciate your assistance here in this swamp, <name>. I would like to inform you that I have received correspondence from Nethergarde Keep.

Enohar Thunderbrew has requested help in investigating the shipwrecks of the Red Reaches, but we have had none willing to make the journey, and I could not leave the Harborage.

Nethergarde Keep sits in the Blasted Lands, south of the Swamp of Sorrows. Do not journey too close to Stonard on your way.

passages.title: Onward to the Blasted Lands
passages.text: Ah, has Avuun sent ye? Good, good...

passages.title: Armored to the Teeth
passages.text:
We've hit an unexpected snag in our assault on the keep, <name>. It seems the servants that tended to Baron Silverlaine and Commander Springvale in life do so now in death as well, and Godfrey has placed them directly between us and him.

Not to worry, we won't let them be anything more than a minor inconvenience. Eliminate Silverlaine and Springvale both and not only will their guards no longer have masters to direct them, it will place us that much closer to our final goal.

passages.title: Armored to the Teeth
passages.text: It is infuriating that we have to kill these ghost soldiers when they are completely outside the main objective, but it must be done. Godfrey is a cunning foe indeed.

passages.title: Armored to the Teeth
passages.text: We're nearly there, <name>. The time is now to charge further ahead and take out Walden!

passages.title: Fighting Tooth and Claw
passages.text:
It appears that Lord Walden has finally taken notice to our presence and has heightened his defenses. It's worthless really... nothing will deter our pack.

The path ahead to him is rife with powerful Scourge minions, but I trust that you will be able to clear the path for the rest of us to follow in. Once we kill Walden, it should be a straight shot to his cowardly leader.

passages.title: Fighting Tooth and Claw
passages.text: We're behind you, <name>.

passages.title: Fighting Tooth and Claw
passages.text:
<Packleader Ivar Bloodfang grins, revealing his razor-sharp teeth.>

It won't be long now before the entire keep is ours, thanks to your valiant efforts.

passages.title: Traitors!
passages.text:
Please, stranger. You must help me.

I came here to investigate the arrival of a powerful ally to the Neferset, only to be betrayed by my closest allies and given up to the enemy.

Go to the terrace above us to the east and find the information I failed to uncover. You'll need to hide from the Neferset. Perhaps you can hide behind one of the large plants on the platform to conceal your presence.

Do this for me and I will help your friends find their way to safety.

passages.title: Traitors!
passages.text: What did you witness, <name>?

passages.title: Traitors!
passages.text:
A djinn!  We must escape as soon as possible.

This unholy alliance of the Neferset with the minions of Deathwing does not bode well for us.

passages.title: Eastern Hospitality
passages.text:
The commander is quite busy now, I'm afraid.

The demands of an operation such as this require much of his attention these days.

While you wait to speak with him, why don't you mingle with some of our guests?

We have invited a variety of Azeroth's most illustrious figures to be present when we unlock the secrets of this region.

I am confident that you will find them most captivating.

passages.title: Eastern Hospitality
passages.text: I trust that you had no troubles fitting in with our guests, hmm?

passages.title: Down to the Scar
passages.text:
The Badlands are home to some unusual people, many of whom have been here for quite a long time.

For example, there were three gentlemen who were staying here in town. I forget their names... the dwarf was Theldurin, I think? Anyhow, they headed south with a pack full of ale a couple of days ago, and haven't been heard from since. I think they were headed to that big scar.

Would you mind checking in on them? I'd like to make sure that they're alright.

passages.title: Down to the Scar
passages.text:
They sent you to check up on us?  Pshh... I've been around this desert longer than any of those chumps.  We're just soaking in some of the scenery and telling stories about old times.

You like telling stories?

passages.title: Devastation
passages.text: The coast is clear. If Rheastrasza or the egg were able to miraculously evade Deathwing's flames, they would probably need your assistance as soon as possible.

passages.title: Devastation
passages.text:
Heroes:

If you are reading this, then my suspicions were correct.  Deathwing has found us.  The egg is destroyed, as am I.

This was, actually, the plan from the beginning.  You see... the egg that Deathwing destroyed was not the egg he sought.

It was mine.

passages.title: The Quaking Fields
passages.text:
Before you can help us here, you're going have to deal with Therazane, the Stone Mother's, forces to the south. The elementals and giants upon the Quaking Fields are being mustered.

They too are after the middle fragment of the World Pillar. They'll attack us amidst our war with the stone troggs and we'll be unable to repel them.

I've sent the arch geomancer ahead. Get to Slate Quicksand and do as he asks.

passages.title: The Quaking Fields
passages.text:
Good, <race>, you're here.

We'll have to act fast if we're to prevent Therazane's forces from attacking.

passages.title: The Axe of Earthly Sundering
passages.text:
The emerald colossi are the greatest of the Stone Mother's creatures. They must be the first to be removed from the field.

I brought Stonefather Oremantle's axe for just this task. Use it to sunder the giants.

That should bring them down to a more manageable size for you to finish off.

passages.title: The Axe of Earthly Sundering
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. Without all of their giants, Therazane's forces will have a harder time taking Stonehearth.

Now, if you please, hand back the axe. I'll keep it safe until you can rescue the Stonefather.

passages.title: Elemental Ore
passages.text:
You're going to have to deal with the leader of Therazane's forces here. However, to get you to him quickly and safely, I'm going to need to perform a ritual.

Go out into the field and collect elemental ore from the ragers. With enough of it, I should be able to make you one with the ground to get you where you need to go.

passages.title: Elemental Ore
passages.text: Have you all that is required?

passages.title: Elemental Ore
passages.text: These should do. I'll just need a moment to prepare the ritual.

passages.title: One With the Ground
passages.text:
The leader of the Stone Mother's forces here is the great earth elemental lord, Avalanchion. Luckily for us, the Twilight's Hammer cultists have decided to invade his lair. They're seeking to bind his elementals to their will.

We will take advantage of the chaos. The earth ritual that I invoke will make you one with the ground. It will take you near to Avalanchion without alerting him to your presence.

It's up to you to finish him.

passages.title: Bring Down the Avalanche
passages.text: Avalanchion stands before you. Slay him to keep Therazane's forces from attacking Stonehearth.

passages.title: Bring Down the Avalanche
passages.text:
You've done what few others could have. Defeating Avalanchion was no small feat.

I'm impressed, <name>. Will you help us with our war against the stone troggs so that we can rescue the Stonefather?

passages.title: Bring Down the Avalanche
passages.text: You have to go back and slay Avalanchion to keep Therazane's forces from attacking Stonehearth!

passages.title: Bring Down the Avalanche
passages.text:
You've done what few others could have. Defeating Avalanchion was no small feat.

I'm impressed, <name>. Will you help us with our war against the stone troggs so that we can rescue the Stonefather?

passages.title: The Desert Fox
passages.text:
Zhere is much to be done in zhis region, <race>.

Ve bozh haf a burning passion for zhe ancient technologies here, do ve not?

Perhaps zhere is a vay for us to vork togezher?

Let us put zhe misunderstandinks of zhe past behind us zhen, hmm?

Now, zhere is an elusive animal in zhe region to zhe east zhat I have been huntink. Brink me zhis creature as a token of your sincerity, hmm?

Zhen maybe I let you in on my operation...

passages.title: The Desert Fox
passages.text: Have you captured zhe Desert Fox, <class>?

passages.title: The Desert Fox
passages.text:
You've done it!

Perhaps I can trust you vizh more serious matters, hmm?

passages.title: Dirty Birds
passages.text:
The sky above the Shriveled Oasis is littered with these nasty vultures.

Like infectious rodents with wings, these creatures serve no great purpose and inflict untold misery.

Rid the skies of this nuisance and leave the region better than you found it.

passages.title: Paint it Black
passages.text:
The ground bleeds, <class>. They tear it open, as one would gouge flesh.

These cultists relish their secrecy but the very elementals they use for their misdeeds can betray them. Seek out Obsidian Stoneslaves northeast of here, among the ruined earth we have named the Black Breach.

Shatter their bodies and find for me a perfect heart of black diamond. I will look into this heart. And I will bare its soul.

passages.title: Paint it Black
passages.text: The heart. A stone heart, of purest black. Have you found one?

passages.title: Paint it Black
passages.text:
<Mallia removes her eyepatch and holds the black diamond before her empty eye socket.>

What have we, what have we - breaches, the breaches number three. Two heads, one wholly given to its master. I see the future. A hammer united. A mountain shattered. Oh - OH!

<Mallia drops the diamond to the floor, covering her face with her hands.>

passages.title: A Vision of Twilight
passages.text:
Cho'gall keeps track of his minions through powerful magical orbs: "The Eyes of Twilight."

In Mount Hyjal, the Guardians of Hyjal managed to find and manipulate one to their own ends. We must do the same. I want one of those orbs, and I want to use it to peer into the very heart of Cho'gall's lair.

Search the Black Breach, across the river to the northeast, and find an Eye of Twilight. Do whatever you need to bring it back to me!

passages.title: A Vision of Twilight
passages.text:
<The Eye sits before you, humming ominously with dark energies.>

<Without warning, the orb rotates, as if to look at you. You sense a malevolent presence, as though the orb is alive.>

passages.title: Gobbles!
passages.text:
At last! Zhe time has come to set my Gobbles free of zhat nasty curse!

Pay attention now, <race>, and stay on guard. Zhere can be no interruptions vhile I perform zhe ritual.

Let me know vhen you haf secured zhe perimeter!

Now, move it!

passages.title: We All Must Sacrifice
passages.text:
<The eye speaks to you, its 'voice' reverberating as if coming from everywhere at once.>

You seek my sight, <race>? My powers come at a price. These disciples of the Twilight have been honoring me with the blood of Wildhammer dwarves from the nearby ruins, but still I thirst. Perhaps you can do better.

Slay my old masters, and my vision is yours. Honor me with the slaughter of the Shaman of the Black. Blood is blood, after all.

passages.title: We All Must Sacrifice
passages.text: I have been watching you, <race>.

passages.title: We All Must Sacrifice
passages.text:
<The Eye glimmers darkly, colors swirling about its dusky surface.>

Ah, the succulent thrill of life extinguished. Do you feel it, <class>? Do you relish it as I do?

No, I see not. You fight to protect the lives of others. Pity.

passages.title: The Explorers
passages.text:
We have a contingent of the Explorers' League in the chamber just to the northwest inside the temple.

They've been making increasing noises about something that the Twilight's Hammer is up to.

<name>, would you be a dear and see what they need?

passages.title: The Explorers
passages.text: Oh gosh! Someone's finally here to help us?

passages.title: The Reliquary
passages.text:
We have a contingent of the Reliquary in the chamber just to the northeast inside the temple.

They've been making increasing noises about something that the Twilight's Hammer is up to.

<name>, would you be a dear and see what they need?

passages.title: The Reliquary
passages.text: Ah, it's about time someone came to speak with us on matters most urgent.

passages.title: The Eyes Have It
passages.text:
Very well then, <race>. You have purchased my services in blood. Take me back to Garona Halforcen.

Oh yes, I already know where you're taking me. Garona's relentless quest for vengeance is no secret. It will be a delight to watch it unfold.

passages.title: The Eyes Have It
passages.text: Did you have any luck within the Black Breach?

passages.title: The Eyes Have It
passages.text:
You found one? I've been searching everywhere. Give it here!

Some of these eyes are won over with riddles or verse. Others require magic. What did this one demand? Ah, it's no matter. What matters is that it's ours.

passages.title: Eye Spy
passages.text:
This terrible thing makes my hair stand on end. Cho'gall uses these to control his minions - now it's time to use it against him.

Let me see... hmm, it's all cloudy. All I can see is you. Why is it showing me you?

<Garona sets the eye out in front of her.>

Look into the eye and tell me what you see. Peer into Cho'gall's lair! What is he doing? Is he heavily guarded? Tell me!

passages.title: Eye Spy
passages.text:
You've gone pale, <class>. What did the Eye show you?

You saw Cho'gall? Wait - Cho'gall saw you? He's watching us? He's watching us right now!?

Damn this stupid dark magic! I'm going to have to infiltrate Cho'gall's stronghold myself.

passages.title: Lunk's Task
passages.text:
Lunk came from the Badlands. Other ogres try to make Lunk fight.

Lunk hate fighting. Lunk want to learn.

Lunk sees machines to the south. Machines made of gears.

Maybe if you ask nicely, machines will give you some gears? Then maybe Lunk can have a gear, and learn about machines too.

passages.title: Lunk's Task
passages.text: You get gears?  How you get them?

passages.title: Lunk's Task
passages.text:
You didn't... KILL the machines to get these, right?.

<Lunk looks upset.>

Right?

passages.title: A Proper Antivenom
passages.text:
Shame that Lunk left. I was beginning to enjoy his company.

Oh well, back to work!

I'm the closest thing that this expedition has to a medical officer, and I'm running low on antivenom. We tend to need a lot of antivenom.

The key to a proper antivenom is ALWAYS to start with the poison itself. The glassweb spiders nearby should be a good place to start. If you kill them, you can probably extract some venom from the sacs within their jaws.

passages.title: A Proper Antivenom
passages.text: Well well, you certainly operate quickly!  You do have the venom, right?

passages.title: A Proper Antivenom
passages.text: This... this is way more than I expected.  This will last us for months!

passages.title: Lunk's Adventure: Spider Rider
passages.text:
Lunk sees you like to kill things. Let Lunk teach you another way.

Lunk always wanted to ride on spider's back. Looks like fun. Spiders move too fast, though. Always slip away.

We work together. You fight spider until it gets weak and tired. Then Lunk jump on spider's back and ride around.

Maybe Lunk even gather some venom for you! No have to kill!

passages.title: The Fewer, the Better
passages.text:
I'm not much of a fighter... I'm more of a mining dwarf. Same goes for Jack and Pris. And Lunk... well, you'd think he'd be a big fighter, but he's the biggest wimp of all of us.

What I'm saying is, it's good that you came here when you did.

It seems likely that we in the Thorium Brotherhood are going to be fighting the other Dark Iron dwarves soon. I'm thinking we should pick off some of their finest before the war starts in earnest. Start with the geologists and watchmen to the south.

passages.title: The Fewer, the Better
passages.text: The fewer of them that remain, the better our prospects are.

passages.title: The Fewer, the Better
passages.text: Thank you.

passages.title: Out of Place
passages.text:
The gorge is an unforgiving place. We don't get a whole lot of fuzzy wildlife wandering around here.

We tried bringing in some wild game, but they haven't fared well at all. There's just no food for them to eat. Now the nearby spiders - which were already dangerous - are getting big and fat on chicken meat.

We'll never get rid of all the spiders, but we can salvage what few chickens remain. Not only will you be feeding the Brotherhood, you'll be saving them a painful death by spider bite.

passages.title: Out of Place
passages.text: Those poor animals.

passages.title: Out of Place
passages.text:
You've got quick hands if you were able to gather this many in such a short time.

Excellent work, <name>.  I'll make sure these ones don't go to waste.

passages.title: A Lumbering Relic
passages.text:
Margol the Rager's an old thunder lizard seen round these parts. Legend has it that he's been here in the gorge since before it was even a gorge. Legend also has it that he ate my brother Barnabas.

I don't care how old he is or what kind of magic he shoots out of his nose. I just want him dead. For Barnabas' sake.

You'll find him wandering the cliffs to the south of here.

passages.title: A Lumbering Relic
passages.text: Bring me the horn, <name>.

passages.title: A Lumbering Relic
passages.text:
Yup, this was Margol's horn alright.  No doubt about it.

Barnabas was a digger, like me.  He never stood a chance in combat against the beast.  I'm glad you were here to set things right.

passages.title: Fury of the Pack
passages.text:
Ah, the sweet scent of victory! My men should be tearing Godfrey to pieces even as we speak. Go up to his domain and collect your share of the spoils - you've earned it!

You'd think that he would have been more difficult to defeat...

passages.title: Fury of the Pack
passages.text: Let's get going.

passages.title: Fury of the Pack
passages.text:
We did it, <name>! At terrible cost... but victory is ours.

This keep could serve well as a home for me and my pack, though we tend to prefer more natural habitats.

It may be best to leave it as a reminder of Godfrey's betrayal and of the Bloodfang warriors that died here in battle.

passages.title: This Land is Our Land
passages.text:
Did you think that a handful of worgen vermin could stop me? Hah!

Shadowfang Keep was part of the Lordaeron kingdom in life, so it is quite fitting that it should belong to the Forsaken in death. Godfrey and his accomplices are minor obstacles at best, and of course we're all happy to take them out for their treachery against the Dark Lady.

Ashbury has positioned himself near the front of the keep, leaving him wide open to attack. Start us out on the right foot, would you?

passages.title: This Land is Our Land
passages.text: Don't test my patience and good will.

passages.title: This Land is Our Land
passages.text: Ah, very well done! They've gotten a hold of powerful allies, but clearly nothing a <class>-champion of the Banshee Queen can't handle!

passages.title: Curse These Fat Fingers
passages.text:
Unfortunately, I can't dish out the beats like I used to, due to this here fat finger problem. Ye see, the climate out here combined with the lack o' air pressure makes me fingers expand. They're like gigantic Thelsamar Blood Sausages, they are...

Ye're gonna have to carry out me orders of business and what have ye.

First on me agenda: Poundin' the livin' daylights out o' the heavy war golems o' the Gorge. Get crackin'.

passages.title: Curse These Fat Fingers
passages.text: Ye're a good lad, ye are. I got ye a lil' present fer yer troubles.

passages.title: The Spiders Have to Go
passages.text:
Normal-size spiders, I can handle.

Giant glassweb spiders make me uncomfortable, but they're far enough away that I don't worry too much.

But lava spiders? <Lolo shudders.> Lava spiders are SCARY. They're enormous spiders. That live in LAVA.

I just got paid for my last week of work, and I'll pay you well to kill those things. You'll find 'em all over Searing Gorge.

passages.title: The Spiders Have to Go
passages.text:
There's no way you coulda killed all the spiders in the gorge, but you definitely made a dent.

Fine, here's what I promised ya.  Don't spend it all in one place.  Unless it's at Thorium Point.

passages.title: Twilight Collars
passages.text:
Have ye seen the ridiculous necklaces those Twilight's Hammer cultists all wear? The gems on those things are bigger than Hansel's fist!

A few hamburger-sized jewels like that, and Burninate over there could really push his blacksmithing business to the next level. Fetch those collars, and he'll make it worth your while.

passages.title: Twilight Collars
passages.text: A ruby-hilted hammer... it has a nice ring to it.

passages.title: Twilight Collars
passages.text:
Hmm... the gems looked... sparklier from afar.  Up close, they look kind of dingy.

Ah well!  A little spit and polish should do the trick, and if not, I can use 'em to practice my disenchanting.

passages.title: Lunk's Adventure: Cranky Little Dwarfs
passages.text:
What you doing? Why you kill?

You need to get things from dwarfs? Ah, Lunk understand. Lunk have a better way.

Listen: you go fight dwarf, but do not kill! Just fight until dwarf get tired. Then Lunk will help dwarf fall asleep. Dwarfs probably just cranky because they don't get sleep.

Come on! Trust Lunk.

passages.title: Lunthistle's Tale
passages.text: Will you assist me, mortal? Hear my tale.

passages.title: Lunthistle's Tale
passages.text: Allow me to finish my story.

passages.title: Lunthistle's Tale
passages.text: I have accepted my fate here in this cage, but the prayer must be found.

passages.title: Prayer to Elune
passages.text:
Will you assist me, mortal? Will you find the prayer to Elune?

As I stated, the prayer was etched onto a golden tablet. I believe they hold it within one of their vile chests, near the entrance to their cave at the bottom of the ridge.

If you do recover my prayer, don't bring it back to me. Instead, take the time to read through it.

Absolution may be asking too much, based on the sins I've committed. But that won't stop me from holding out hope.

passages.title: Plague...Plague Everywhere!
passages.text:
The best part about this plague is that even when it visually fades away, the remaining residue is still quite potent! However, we still have an enormous area to cover before we're done, with plenty of Godfrey's defenses in the way.

It appears that the spirits that served Baron Silverlaine and Commander Springvale in life now guard them in death, and Godfrey is using them to deter us. Show them all the iron will of the Forsaken!

passages.title: Plague...Plague Everywhere!
passages.text: A couple bodiless spirits aren't going to best you, are they?

passages.title: Plague...Plague Everywhere!
passages.text:
Cromush has both a thick skull and a fool's brain, and we'll use that to our advantage. By the time anybody finds out about the plague's true potency, it'll be far too late.

Thank you for keeping quiet during his tirade. I promise you won't regret it.

passages.title: Take it to 'Em!
passages.text:
We was lucky to escape, <class>. I'm not sure I'd feel right if we didn't take care of them ambushers.

Hows about you git back up to Khartut's tomb and give them little buggers what fer!

It's off to the northeast, just inside the entrance to Uldum if'n I recollect correctly.

What're you looking at? I sure ain't in no condition to do it!

passages.title: Take it to 'Em!
passages.text:
Good to see ya, kid.

Would've been even better if you'd have been here to help me take care of these little savages...

passages.title: Ruumbo Demands Justice
passages.text:
You! Wanderer! Bow before the might of Ruumbo, great god of the Timbermaw tribe!

Hear my will! The evil Deadwood tribe lives in the village behind me! They are big jerks!

I mean, they... they sully my name with their wicked misdeeds! They persecute my cherished Timbermaw tribe and hurt them!

I demand you inflict my justice! Defeat the Deadwood and I will give you my... my favor! Yes! The favor of RUUMBO!

passages.title: Ruumbo Demands Justice
passages.text:
It worked!

I mean, uh, YES, the will of Ruumbo has been carried out! You have done well, creature! You may have these shiny coins!

passages.title: Dance for Ruumbo!
passages.text:
You have done well, <race>! Ruumbo is pleased by your bravery, and the delicious honey you have given Ruumbo.

Now, you must... you must dance! Yes!

Dance for Ruumbo! Dance!

passages.title: Dance for Ruumbo!
passages.text:
Those two brats... I should have known! They were smart enough to hush whenever I went to examine the totem.

I'll be sure to find them and drag them back to Timbermaw Hold by the ears! Thank you for looking into it...

passages.title: Orders Are For the Living
passages.text:
Unsurprisingly, we aren't going to listen to Cromush about the plague. However, his brute strength will come in handy for muscling my men through the many foes ahead on the path to Godfrey, the most powerful being his right hand man, Lord Walden.

I'll meet you in Walden's chamber after you finish him off. Then, at long last, we can completely take Shadowfang Keep for the Forsaken!

passages.title: Orders Are For the Living
passages.text: You have your orders, <name>.

passages.title: Orders Are For the Living
passages.text: The time has come! Godfrey will fall!

passages.title: The Corruption of the Jadefire
passages.text:
The cleansing of this forest has been a grueling process. For every success we have achieved, a new challenge has arisen.

The Jadefire satyr have been a constant nuisance. They seek to corrupt the forest just as we seek to cleanse it. Now, we have taken steps to begin eradicating them from Felwood entirely.

Travel to Jadefire Glen to the west and rid the forest of their presence. You'll find the entrance just north of the walls of Deadwood Village; look for their vile banners.

passages.title: The Corruption of the Jadefire
passages.text: Jadefire Glen is our first target in a series of coordinated efforts. The others will be dealt with in time.

passages.title: The Corruption of the Jadefire
passages.text: The Emerald Circle thanks you, <name>. If we all work together here, we can purge these demons from our midst.

passages.title: Sweet, Merciless Revenge
passages.text:
If all goes well you'll just be able to walk right into Godfrey's personal domain and take a reward fitting for such an eager young <class>.

Godfrey is a cunning foe, though, so it may be wise to head up there quickly just in case you're needed. He will pay for what he did to the Dark Lady!

passages.title: Sweet, Merciless Revenge
passages.text: Let's get going.

passages.title: Sweet, Merciless Revenge
passages.text:
For a moment there, I thought all was lost. Even when surrounded by the worgen in Gilneas I had higher hopes!

But you proved me wrong <name>. I will see to it that Sylvanas herself hears of your triumph here today. Don't worry about the mess here, I will gladly see to it myself.

passages.title: The Fate of the Doyles
passages.text: It seems the Doyles already joined their last fight. Iain will want to know of their fate.

passages.title: The Fate of the Doyles
passages.text:
That's a right shame. Stubborn as they were to speak to, they were just as stubborn in a fight. Would have been good to have 'em.

Once this is done, we'll have to send some boys out to bring them back for a proper send off.

passages.title: Do the Imp-Possible
passages.text:
The satyr hide their corrupted moonwell behind an impenetrable barrier of demonic fire. Their forces must have some way of getting through it.

Interrogating the satyr will be useless, but the imps they consort with will be easily swayed. I have a specific one in mind, as well...

In the foothills to the east, a lone imp has been seen wandering, far from the other demons. He should prove easy pickings. Weaken him with combat, and then use this enchanted sack to capture him. Then I'll do the talking...

passages.title: Do the Imp-Possible
passages.text: Do you have an imp for me?

passages.title: Do the Imp-Possible
passages.text:
Imps are creatures of deception. With so many of them spotted at Shadowlurk Ridge, I'm positive something is being hidden there.

Our little friend will tell us exactly how to find it... if he doesn't want to go back in the sack.

passages.title: A Coward's Due
passages.text:
We may be safe here, but there are a lot of Wildhammer who could still use support. Our wing can offer that, but we need to keep bolsterin' our forces if we're going to clear the Twilight completely.

I'm going to have words with Colin Thundermar. Only a coward turns down the callin' of his people, especially in a time this dire.

Go to Thundermar, find Colin and get a real explanation out of'm. I won't be putting up with cowardice in a Wildhammer leader.

passages.title: A Coward's Due
passages.text:
Here here, WOT!? He calls ME a COWARD!?

Just like a Firebeard, all hot air and not a lick of sense. I've been bearing the brunt of a Dragonmaw invasion from the south, much of Thundermar is in ruins, and do any of the other clans stick up to help? NO! Ol' Thundermar is on his own he is, and you'd better believe I'm usin' everything in my arsenal just to stem the tide.

passages.title: Crisis Management
passages.text:
There is a delicate situation that calls for the... objective discretion of an outsider.

You see, an unfortunate incident has upset some of our guests. Rest assured, our top men are sorting out the details.

In the meantime, it would be wonderful if you could calm our more squeamish visitors.

Handle this well, and the furrier is sure to hear of it!

passages.title: Crisis Management
passages.text:
Hmm, still a bit frazzled, are they?

Well, you know what they say. Time heals all wounds.

Except for those of the ambassador, of course...

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Scarlet Monastery Graveyard
passages.text:
The Warchief has requested that any able-bodied adventurer head to the Scarlet Monastery Graveyard, northeast of the Undercity, immediately!

Dark Ranger Velonara has requested more soldiers to help her begin her assault! If you so choose, head to the Scarlet Monastery Graveyard and speak with Dark Ranger Velonara, a clever fighter indeed, to do your part.

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Scarlet Monastery Armory
passages.text:
The Warchief has requested that any able-bodied adventurer head to the Scarlet Monastery Armory, northeast of the Undercity, immediately!

Dark Ranger Velonara has requested more soldiers to help her take out their offensive capabilities! If you so choose, head to the Scarlet Monastery Armory and speak with Dark Ranger Velonara to do your part.

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Scarlet Monastery Graveyard
passages.text:
King Varian Wrynn has requested that any able-bodied adventurer head to the Scarlet Monastery Graveyard, northeast of the Undercity, immediately!

Joseph the Awakened, a former crusader, has requested aid to help him take out the leaders there and reform the crusade! If you so choose, head to the Scarlet Monastery Graveyard and speak with Joseph the Awakened to do your part.

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Scarlet Monastery Armory
passages.text:
King Varian Wrynn has requested that any able-bodied adventurer head to the Scarlet Monastery Armory, northeast of the Undercity, immediately!

Joseph the Crazed has requested help to kill Herod, the Scarlet Champion! If you so choose, head to the Scarlet Monastery Armory and speak with Joseph the Crazed to help him out.

passages.title: Siege!
passages.text:
That Overseer Oilfist couldn't'a picked a worse time to ask me to join a fight. My summit's already under siege!

It's nothin' my guards can't handle, but still, it won't be easy for me to just pick up and send some dwarves into that infernal gorge.

Tell ya what: you take out their marksmen that're holding our fortress under siege, and I'll consider your offer. Ye'll find 'em slinkin' around the flats to the east.

passages.title: Siege!
passages.text:
If nothin' else, you bought us some time, and some room to open up our supply lines through this siege.

Yer a fine <class>.

passages.title: Set Them Ablaze!
passages.text:
I'm not sure if ye've noticed, but my tower's much taller than any o' the other towers here around the Gorge. Some dwarves pride themselves at how deep they can dig, but not me. Sometimes I think I shoulda been born a Wildhammer.

I still don't like the sight o' those other towers, though. Reachin' up like that, ticklin' my tower's feet. Here, take this torch, an' use it on the braziers atop those other towers. They'll be sorry they ever built 'em to begin with.

passages.title: Set Them Ablaze!
passages.text: Looks like ye know how to light things on fire!  An admirable trait in any <race>, for sure.

passages.title: Deceit
passages.text:
What? Why're you still here? Oh, did I promise that I'd help you and the Thorium Brotherhood in yer fight?

I lied.

I just can't spare the men right now. I know I said I'd help, but there's absolutely no way you can convince me to leave Iron Summit right now. Absolutely no way.

passages.title: Deceit
passages.text:
Well well well.  Look who come searching for Lunk this time!

This sounds like case for Lunk's unique brand of no-kill problem-solve.

passages.title: Lunk's Adventure: Rendan's Weakness
passages.text:
Lunk not smart, but Lunk notice things. Today, Lunk notice that Mountain-Dwarf likes to watch people dance.

Lunk like to dance! <name> like to dance! Probably!

Maybe we find some more dwarfs that like to dance. Then we go talk to Mountain-Dwarf, and he will listen to <name>.

passages.title: Lunk's Adventure: Rendan's Weakness
passages.text:
Did I stutter?  I believe I clearly stated that I... won't...

Wow, ye've got some good moves there!  I'm impressed!

passages.title: Blood in the Highlands
passages.text:
You've got some fight in you, <class>. You might do well in the crucible.

What!? You haven't heard of the Crucible of Carnage? That smarmy goblin Gurgthock and his troll sidekick have been plastering us with leaflets ever since he set up shop here in the Highlands. Champions from all over Azeroth fight to the death in there. You should gather up some friends and see how you fare.

The Crucible is just to the southwest. Look for Wodin the Troll-Servant somewhere in the middle of a ring of bones.

passages.title: Blood in the Highlands
passages.text: Hey, you're one big strong heap of <class>. Can you handle the crucible? We got bookies are standing by!

passages.title: Bait and Throttle
passages.text:
You can hold your own on the ground, <name>. I'll give you that.

But we Dragonmaw dominate the skies as well as land. Until you can prove to me you can handle a drake as well as a Dragonmaw, your Horde is nothing to me.

Let's see if you can wrangle one back to Bloodgulch.

First you'll need bait. Go out and kill one of the gryphons that wander the woods west or northeast of here. Make sure it's untamed! Drakes hate the stink of dwarf on their food.

Get the gryphon carcass and you'll know what to do.

passages.title: Bait and Throttle
passages.text: <You gather up the fresh carcass.>

passages.title: Bait and Throttle
passages.text: <You gather up the fresh carcass.>

passages.title: The Greatest Flavor in the World!
passages.text:
Below us is a cave. It's huge! The perfect location for our new refrigerated vault. It's big enough to hold all of our inventory with room to grow.

Unfortunately, when we were almost done equipping all of the pipes, bugs burrowed up out of nowhere and killed all of my employees!

How was I supposed to know?

But it gave me a great idea: silithid-flavored ice cream. We'll make a killing!

All I need now are the ingredients.

passages.title: The Greatest Flavor in the World!
passages.text: You got enough bug goo for the first batch?

passages.title: The Greatest Flavor in the World!
passages.text:
Oh yeah! This is going to be the greatest flavor in the world!

Look out, Tigule and Foror!!!

passages.title: Freezing the Pipes
passages.text:
It's time to break out the I-Scream Cryocannon!

We lifted the tech from the frost cannons on the river boats. If it's one thing that we gnomes are good at, it's miniaturization by way of making everything else that much bigger!

I need you to take the cannon down there into the cave and freeze the pipes we setup in the walls. That'll jumpstart them.

passages.title: Freezing the Pipes
passages.text:
Do you hear that, <name>? That's the sweet hum of the refrigeration kicking in.

We'll be able to store our inventory down there in no time. Thank you!

passages.title: Slavery is Bad
passages.text:
Much like Overseer Maltorius, I'm a rich dwarf. However, I earned my riches through hard work and wise decisions, not through slavery.

OK fine, very little slavery. Hardly any.

Anyhow, the first thing that I see inside these caverns are slavedrivers and taskmasters. I won't stand for this! As you progress through the cavern, kill as many as you can. Report your results to Evonice Sootsmoker, deeper within the Slag Pit.

passages.title: Slavery is Bad
passages.text: You've done good.  I don't like slavery either.

passages.title: Sweet, Horrible Freedom
passages.text:
Of course, we'll want to free as many slaves as we can while we're here. Most of them will likely join forces with us, anxious to fight against their captors.

However, sometimes you will find that slaves are resistant to being freed. It's a strange phenomenon, often called "Durnholde Syndrome".

Either way, you should try to free them. If they resist, treat them as enemies. Report your results to Evonice Sootsmoker, deeper within the Slag Pit.

passages.title: Sweet, Horrible Freedom
passages.text:
Strange how so many slaves cope poorly with freedom.  It's a shame to have to do what we do, but such are the truths of war.

Now, we must move on to more pressing tasks.

passages.title: Kill 'em With Sleep Deprivation
passages.text:
It's a little known fact that dwarves, particularly of the Dark Iron variety, need rest! Lots of rest!

Now I ask you; How can they sleep without pillows? Exactly, <name>, they can't. This is why you must steal their pillows.

Once you've finished your cushion-thievery, talk with Taskmaster Scrange. He's a bit deeper in the cave, working on a covert project with Hansel.

passages.title: Kill 'em With Sleep Deprivation
passages.text:
What?  Pillows?

What?

passages.title: Kill 'em With Sleep Deprivation
passages.text:
I see Evonice is up to her old tricks again.  I guess I'll just... um... hang onto these pillows for a while.

The important part is that you're here.  We're going to need your help.

passages.title: Minions of Calcinder
passages.text:
There is such a thing as digging too deep, <name>. While you'll find the richest mineral veins deep below the surface, you'll also find the most evil creatures.

Like fire elementals.

Calcinder's minions roam the cavern ahead. Every one of them holds a piece of Calcinder's evil within it. Slay as many as you can, and show no remorse.

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Blackrock Depths
passages.text:
King Anduin Wrynn has requested that any able-bodied adventurer head to Blackrock Depths, northwest of Morgan's Vigil, immediately!

The Dark Iron dwarves pose a serious threat to the citizens of Redridge! If you so choose, head to Blackrock Depths and speak with Morgan, who has returned from her extended absence and wishes to enact her vengeance on the Dark Iron nation.

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Blackrock Depths
passages.text:
You look eager to kill a few hundred Dark Irons in justice's name.

Perfect.

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Blackrock Depths
passages.text:
The Warchief has requested that any able-bodied adventurer head to Blackrock Depths, west of Flame Crest, immediately!

The Dark Iron dwarves have already attacked Alliance-held Redridge, and if left unchecked, may soon threaten our few Horde footholds in southern Azeroth.

If you so choose, head to Blackrock Depths and speak with High Executioner Nuzrak, who is reforming the Kargath Expeditionary Force to finish off the Dark Irons once and for all.

passages.title: Adventurers Wanted: Blackrock Depths
passages.text: We've managed to take this small area, but to do anything more we'll need your help.

passages.title: Trouble at Highperch
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, <name>. You should speak with Pao'ka Swiftmountain at Highperch to the southwest.

Perhaps he will know the whereabouts of the Elder Crone?

passages.title: Trouble at Highperch
passages.text:
I know nothing of the Elder Crone, Magatha. What I do know is that the Twilight's Hammer is destroying Highperch.

Will you help me to stop them, <class>?

passages.title: Free the Pridelings
passages.text: The trappers are rounding up all of the young wind riders. <name>, will you go out there and free the pridelings?

passages.title: Free the Pridelings
passages.text: They're precious. One day they'll grow strong, but until then, they must be protected.

passages.title: Release Heartrazor
passages.text: The Twilight's Hammer have the alpha male of Highperch pinned down. You must head east up the ramp and release Heartrazor before the pride loses its patriarch!

passages.title: Release Heartrazor
passages.text: You must free Heartrazor before they cart him off to their evil base!

passages.title: Release Heartrazor
passages.text: The great Heartrazor is a majestic creature. He has told me of his gratitude and fondness for you, <name>.

passages.title: Easy Pickings
passages.text:
The ambush launched smoothly. Most of the guards are dead, but a few are still pinned down with the wagons.

You can see them just to our west, in the canyon below. Get in there and clear them out so we can get this attack on the move.

passages.title: Easy Pickings
