I need ash, <name>. Not just any ash... ash from the greater obsidian elementals that roam the plains to the northwest. The stuff is deep, deep black, which is what we need for our next disguise.

Don't worry, you've already got a disguise. This one is for someone... well, someTHING... else.

passages.title: Blackened Ashes
passages.text: The ashes of the obsidian elementals are particularly dark - exactly what we need for our purposes.

passages.title: Blackened Ashes
passages.text: Yes, these will do.  I will get this packed up for you.

passages.title: Latent Demons of the Land
passages.text:
The lava beds nearby - to the west - play host to flamekin, a brand of fire demon that has long roamed the steppes. Situations are such in the Blackrock army that, if we are careful, we may be able to sneak some of these flamekin behind enemy lines to cause some havoc.

Bring me the bodies of several flamekin. As demons, they are easily resurrected, and then we can use them for our own purposes.

passages.title: Latent Demons of the Land
passages.text: The flamekin are weak, but they travel in packs.  Be cautious.

passages.title: Latent Demons of the Land
passages.text:
To the untrained eye, these will look exactly like imps.

We just need to get them to that untrained eye.  I'll work on preparing them for delivery.

passages.title: A Heap of Delicious Worg
passages.text:
We're going to need fresh meat, which means you're going to be hunting worg. The worg on this side of the steppes should be your target.

<Troteman produces a large blade, which he hands to you.>

Hunt the giant ember worgs. Once you've killed them, use this saw to remove the choicest bits of meat from their bodies. You will find these worgs all over the steppes, but the closest pack rules the land just to our northeast.

passages.title: A Heap of Delicious Worg
passages.text: Any luck out there?

passages.title: A Heap of Delicious Worg
passages.text:
This meat looks good... but I think it needs a little "seasoning".  I'll make sure that gets taken care of.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Blood Tour
passages.text:
My legs are getting a little restless again. You interested in taking a little tour, <name>?

We're going to take a trip around Dreadmaul Rock. I'd like to investigate some of the Blackrock army before we make our move, and I figure we might as well kill some of them while we're on the way.

passages.title: Blood Tour
passages.text:
<Keeshan is covered in blood and sweat.>

That was exactly what I needed.

passages.title: Draconic Vanguard
passages.text:
The Blackrock orcs don't come alone. You've already seen that they've got the Firegut ogres and Smolderthorn trolls on their side. Unfortunately for us, they're also teamed up with the black dragonflight.

The orcs and the dragons have already sent some of their champions to stand guard at rally points, which are marked by a dragon skull on a pike. You and I are going to find these rally points and take out this vanguard before the battle starts.

Ready?

passages.title: Draconic Vanguard
passages.text: Come on, <name>, there's still more of them left.  Our job isn't done.

passages.title: Draconic Vanguard
passages.text:
Your kill count is adding up, <name>.  We're chipping away at them.

And we are going to win.  Redridge will NOT fall to these cowards.

passages.title: A Deal With a Dragon
passages.text:
While we are circling around Dreadmaul Rock, there's one more stop that we need to make.

You remember the hatchlings that you freed from the Whelping Downs? Troteman's been hanging onto them, and we're going to deliver them to someone who will take care of them better than we can. He's staying in Slither Rock, to the northeast of Dreadmaul Rock.

His name is Acride, and he might be the key to victory in the upcoming battle.

passages.title: A Deal With a Dragon
passages.text: You've arrived, <name>.

passages.title: A Deal With a Dragon
passages.text:
Yes, the whelplings.  I will take care of them.

As for the agreement I made with your Colonel Troteman earlier, tell him that I will hold up my end of the bargain.  You will have your dragon for the battle against the orcs.

We hold no particular love for the Redridge Mountains, but we do share your grudge against the Blackrock clan.

passages.title: Glory Amidst Chaos
passages.text:
You and Keeshan are going back to that mountain. There's three orcs who survived the attack, and we won't rest until they're dead.

That's right, I'm talking about the Big Three.

General Thorg'izog crawled back into the Firegut Furnace, and Dragon-Lord Neeralak is cowering in the cave on the mountain's peak. Xi'lun is in the back of the Skull Warren, plotting with his fellow warlocks.

Leave your mark, <name>. Hunt down those sniveling Blackrocks, and teach them the might of Redridge!

passages.title: Glory Amidst Chaos
passages.text:
<Colonel Troteman is beaming.>

Welcome home, boys.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text:
A messenger just asked me to pass along an invitation. It is from the priest trainer, Martin Goodchilde, at The Barracks in Orgrimmar.

He asks that you meet with him at your soonest convenience. The Barracks can be found within the Valley of Honor.

passages.title: Journey to Orgrimmar
passages.text: So you got my message. Good. I have an important task for you.

passages.title: Studies in Lethality
passages.text:
We used a fairly potent strain of blight against the humans of Southshore. As you can see, it worked. The trouble with blight use, though, is that blight tends to stick around after it's served its purpose.

What I need from you is to take this testing kit and get out into the field to get a lethality count from the blight slimes that we've released into the area. Use the lethality analyzer on the blight slimes sweeping the slime pools. Come back to me when you have some solid data.

passages.title: Studies in Lethality
passages.text: Oh my. 250? This thing doesn't go past 250. How are you still standing? You should be a puddle of goo by now. Sylvanas will be most displeased with this information. There might be some things we can do to reduce the lethality levels of the area by a few decades, but that still leaves us out by about a hundred or so years.

passages.title: Green Living
passages.text:
Recycling! It's all the craze these days. The Banshee Queen has decreed that we must conserve if we are to prosper as a people. Everyone must do their part, right? With that said, you will be doing our part for us.

There are likely thousands of blight canister bits and pieces all over Southshore. We can reuse those canisters for more blight bombing goodness. Just head into the ruins here and pick up whatever you can find.

passages.title: Green Living
passages.text: Bring me those canisters!

passages.title: Green Living
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>. You are incredibly resilient to this blight. We'll have to take you in for testing some time.

passages.title: Angry Scrubbing Bubbles
passages.text:
These blight slimes seem to be really angry. They've even got a faint outline of an angry humanoid face in their ectoplasm. You don't think Hinott would be too happy about having non-compliant slimes working the slime pools.

Kill any angry blight slimes that you see and try to get a lock on a breeding pool.

passages.title: Angry Scrubbing Bubbles
passages.text: All signs indicate to a breeding pool being inside the ruined town hall. You'll need to investigate!

passages.title: Trail of Filth
passages.text:
The trail of filth and anger leads into the ruined town hall. Surely there is a slime breeding pool inside the structure. Fight your way inside and deal with whatever angry slime-breeder that you encounter!

Should you succeed Serge Hinott at the Ruins of Southshore will surely want to hear about it.

passages.title: Trail of Filth
passages.text: Perhaps with Chet vanquished, the lethality levels of this place will decrease a tad faster. A job well done, <name>!

passages.title: Helcular's Rod Giveth...
passages.text:
To think, I, a master of necromancy, trained by Kel'Thuzad himself, was reduced to nothing more than a corpse in a grave. Thankfully, my astute apprentice, Thaivand, managed to find a group of heroes to recover this:

<Helcular whips out his rod.>

It is through the power of the rod that I was reborn. The rod giveth and the rod taketh away!

Take it now and use it to empower our dark rangers battling the worgen in the field north of us. Renew their vigor with my rod.

passages.title: Helcular's Rod Giveth...
passages.text: As I said, the rod giveth to our dark rangers and doth taketh away from our enemy!

passages.title: Helcular's Command
passages.text:
Our dark rangers search the fields for worgen terrorists. These worgen have been sent out by their dark masters to hunt and kill us. And though a dark ranger is a formidable combatant, the worgen often attack in packs, which can overwhelm even a dark ranger.

Search the fields around the ruins of Southshore for Bloodfang forsaken hunters. Kill any that you see! For the Forsaken and for Lordaeron!

passages.title: Helcular's Command
passages.text: We should have killed Bloodfang in Silverpine. It's a shame he still lives. It's an even bigger shame that we have as of yet been unable to turn worgen into undead. Surely there is a way...

passages.title: Slap and Cap
passages.text:
Oh for... not again! If you heard the deputy yelling out there, that means we've got a fullblown oil leak on our hands! It's those filthy worgen again!

Listen, it's going to be total chaos out there. Sleep-deprived goblins running around screaming and not knowing what to do. I need you to snap the workers back to their senses.

A good, swift backhand across the face should do it! Once they shake themselves off, they'll get to work capping those gushers!

passages.title: Slap and Cap
passages.text:
It's not working! We're going to have to shut it off at the source.

Go talk to the Deputy outside, he'll walk you through it!

passages.title: The Shredders of Irontree
passages.text:
Disgusting, isn't it? Look at them. Pathetic little things that can't even toil with their own bodies.

They stomp around in their massive metal shredders, carving the forest to splinters. I bet they think they're safe in there, all warm and cozy.

Prove them wrong. Blaze north through the camp and destroy as many shredders as you can. Once you've spilled some blood, we're going to take this place apart for good.

passages.title: The Shredders of Irontree
passages.text: Is the attack complete?

passages.title: The Shredders of Irontree
passages.text: This is but the first strike.

passages.title: Deadwood of the North
passages.text:
There is a camp of Deadwood furbolgs directly to our southwest. Corruption permeates the camp, and I wish to put an end to it before they become a problem.

The Deadwood tribe is evil, but it is the effects of the fel that pollutes their minds. Their hostility is not truly an innate quality, yet they cannot be helped. It saddens me that we must fight our own brethren.

Please, <name> - I ask you to do what must be done. Simply spare me the details; such troublesome images upset me far too much.

passages.title: Deadwood of the North
passages.text:
I sense that you have achieved victory.  Victory... such a hollow word considering what had to be done.  Regardless, you've proven yourself to be worthy of our trust.

It may take some time before the Timbermaw welcome you without hostility within the Hold.  Still, your perseverance will erode any suspicion my brethren may have about you.  So long as you never betray us and raise weapons against us, we will find common ground.

passages.title: Is Your Oil Running?
passages.text:
Last time we had an oil leak this bad, the oil itself tried to get away!

I don't know what does it, maybe all the demon goop floating around here, but when we get a big enough crude leak half of it globs together and tries to run away.

That's profit trying to escape! Go run after those oil sludges and bring back their sweet, precious oil!

passages.title: Is Your Oil Running?
passages.text: That stuff better not still be moving when you bring it back here.

passages.title: Is Your Oil Running?
passages.text: Thank goodness the oil is safe! Well done, <name>.

passages.title: A Bomb Deal
passages.text:
All my workers got driven straight out of the cavern here by those big swamp-lookin' things! Darla's sent me here to pick up the pieces, but have you seen it in there? I ain't goin' in!

There's a ton of explosives left behind that we can't just leave layin' around.

 I'll make you a deal: You run in there and get those explosives gathered up, and I will stay here and not get killed by swamp-things, and if you don't either, I'll pay ya! How's that sound?

passages.title: A Bomb Deal
passages.text: We had a deal, right? Right?

passages.title: A Bomb Deal
passages.text:
Hey, nice! I'll just take those... carefully...

Don't go tellin' the workers I didn't have the guts to go down there myself, you hear? Here's your pay... and a little somethin' extra.

passages.title: Collecting Corruption
passages.text:
Though we druids shun the demonic powers infesting this land, it must still be confronted.

Shatter Scar Vale to the south seethes with corruption. The energies there are so chaotic that they manifest as violent entities, pure fel magic given form to lash out at all life.

I have been keeping a close eye on these chaotic beasts, and studying their strength. I need to make sure they are still weakening with time. Bring me the essences they drop, so I may ensure they are diminishing.

passages.title: Collecting Corruption
passages.text: Be wary with the essence. It is as poisonous as it is powerful.

passages.title: Collecting Corruption
passages.text:
I can tell just from the size of these that the fel taint is healing. Slowly... but significantly.

Thank you, <name>. I will ensure these are properly purged.

passages.title: Fel To Pieces
passages.text:
The infernals that lurk in Shatter Scar Vale are formidable, but not invincible. Much progress has been made in thinning their numbers.

Destroying them is only part of the solution, however. I've found that the stone that infernals are made of still contains large amounts of fel magic even after the infernal's death.

The rubble of slain infernals now litters Shatter Scar Vale, leeching its corruption back into the ground. If you could collect it and bring it to me, I would be grateful.

passages.title: Fel To Pieces
passages.text: Do be sure to pick up after your own kills, as well.

passages.title: Fel To Pieces
passages.text: It's good to see someone who cares about keeping the forest clean. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Megs in Marketing
passages.text:
Boss, while you were down at the mines, Megs Dreadshredder in marketing was asking for you. Something about your "new image" or whatever.

She's right outside the building to the left.

passages.title: Megs in Marketing
passages.text: There he is! I think you're going to like this!

passages.title: Unlimited Potential
passages.text:
Some see the little sand pygmy as nothing more than a pest, a vermin, or worse yet, a vile little demon.

I say they are simply misunderstood!

With the proper care and guidance, these little fellows may just turn out to be a glorious gift of nature.

I would like you to take these cages and use them to capture a few of them for me to work with.

You will need to give them a sound beating before boxing them up, but in the end it will be for their own good.

You'll see!

Go south for pygmies!

passages.title: Unlimited Potential
passages.text:
Splendid!

This is shaping up to be better than I had dared to dream!

passages.title: Camelraderie
passages.text:
Greetings, friend!

You are always most welcome in my humble tent.

Looking for something to do? Sullah has just the thing!

Camels are good to have in hand regardless, but when putting together a performance the likes of my sideshow, they are an absolute must!

Take this harness and use it to subdue a wandering camel.

You may have to, uhh, humble it a bit first... if you know what I mean.

You'll find a desert full of wild camels to the south.

passages.title: Camelraderie
passages.text:
You've done it!

I now have camels to spare. Perhaps one day we shall take our show on the road!

passages.title: Jonesy Sent For You
passages.text:
Listen, <name>, you may want to make your way back to Jonesy when you get a moment.

Chances are, whatever he's got to talk to you about is more pressing than anything I have for you to do.

passages.title: Jonesy Sent For You
passages.text:
Alright, kid.

My research is complete. We're about ready to activate the final obelisk.

passages.title: Kasha Will Fly Again
passages.text:
Kasha will fly again, <name>. She must if we are to claim vengeance! Sadly, Orkus must stay here with Kasha. You must help us. I beg of you!

Listen carefully, quest giver. When I first arrived here I flew around for days to learn the lay of the land. There is a farm east of here that has long since been abandoned and is now overrun by gnolls. On this farm grows a special type of mushroom known as the mudsnout. Go to the stead and gather mudsnout for Kasha. Return here when your pack is full.

passages.title: Kasha Will Fly Again
passages.text: Have you recovered the mudsnout?

passages.title: Kasha Will Fly Again
passages.text: This mushroom is toxic to living things, but provides a restorative boost to the undead. Let us see how Kasha reacts.

passages.title: Terrible Little Creatures
passages.text: Gnolls! These terrible little creatures are a blight upon any land - which is saying a lot when you consider that Hillsbrad is Forsaken territory. Kill as many of the gnolls at the Nethander Stead as you can. For the good of the world!

passages.title: Preemptive Strike
passages.text:
These plans document what appears to be an imminent attack on Southshore. The naga of the Eastern Strand are planning to take over the town now that the Alliance has been pushed out.

Not if you can help it!

Kill all of the naga on the Eastern Strand and report to Helcular at the Ruins of Southshore with the Daggerspine attack plan.

passages.title: Preemptive Strike
passages.text:
HAH! Those naga have some balls on them! To think that they could take Southshore from us in our own territory! Such a preposterous notion.

<Helcular laughs.>

You have done well to thwart their attack - though I do wonder if they could have survived for even a minute in the blight.

passages.title: Take it to the Tree
passages.text:
Those mangy curs think they can just snoop around my site and get away with it? I'll show them...

And what I mean by that is, of course, that YOU will show them. You and the small army of axe-wielding goblin hires I've sent to Talonbranch Glade.

The place will be swarming with worgen by now. Just where we want them. Head to the southeast, join up with the rest of our forces, and let some fur fly.

passages.title: Take it to the Tree
passages.text: Let's hope we put down enough of them to get the message across.

passages.title: Hunting the Damned
passages.text:
The first demons to set foot in this forest were infernals. Long ago, these powerful beings of stone and demonic fire fell from the sky to take this land for the Burning Legion.

The charred craters of Shatter Scar Vale to the south are where these infernals landed, and many still wander there. They are fierce foes, and killing them is both a worthy challenge and a noble cause.

I offer reward for those who join the hunt. Return here afterwards.

passages.title: Hunting the Damned
passages.text:
I thank you for hunting in my stead, <class>.

I've found I must pace myself... finding too much thrill in hunting demons is a dangerous path.

passages.title: Running Their Course
passages.text:
I'd love so much to save every creature in the forest, but as you probably have seen, some are just too far gone.

When we first founded Whisperwind Grove, the woods just to the south were full of beautiful coursers, majestic and gentle creatures. The corruption here hasn't made them violent, but they've wasted away to nearly nothing.

Even if they were cleansed, they would know only pain and suffering. Please, <class>, help put them down for me.

passages.title: Running Their Course
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. They won't spread the corruption any further, and they won't be in pain either.

passages.title: Squirrely Clean
passages.text:
The larger animals are often too far corrupted to save, but you'd be surprised how hardy the little ones are.

Take the squirrels, for example. After washing in corrupted water, they can spread illness far from the original source, but it's slow to affect the squirrels themselves. In fact, a simple washing will result in a clean squirrel and a safer forest!

Here, take this bottle of cleaning mixture. Grab and scrub any squirrel you see in the woods to the south... they'll be thankful for it!

passages.title: Squirrely Clean
passages.text:
Aren't they just adorable?

It's those little victories that keep me going. We'll save this forest one squirrel at a time.

passages.title: Stupid Drizle!
passages.text:
Stupid, stupid Drizle! I told him not to go!

Drizle wanted to steal more honey from Felpaw Village... you know, just west of here? You can see it from the cliff...

Anyway... I told him it was a dumb idea but he went anyway, and then the Deadwood tribe got him, and... and...

Sniff...

I don't know what they're gonna do! Please find him, <Mr./Ms.> <race>! Even if he is a dummy! I don't want Drizle to get eaten!

passages.title: Stupid Drizle!
passages.text: Help! Please help!

passages.title: Stirred the Hornet's Nest
passages.text:
Wow!

It sounds like you really got their attention, <name>. We're never getting in there with them on alert like this.

There must be a way...

It's just a matter of time before Schnottz's men activate the obelisk and I need to research the scrolls you found. I need you to figure this one out without me.

Sullah has connections in these parts. Maybe he has a solution for getting us inside.

passages.title: Stirred the Hornet's Nest
passages.text: You know, I believe I have just the thing!

passages.title: The Chieftain's Key
passages.text:
Sniff... I'm sorry! I didn't mean to get caught! They grabbed me and put this chain on me and left me here! I can't move and my leg fell asleep and I'm hungry!

The chief has the key... Chieftain Bloodmaw, the other ones said. He's in the north end of the camp.

But hurry! Please! Don't leave me alone here!

passages.title: The Chieftain's Key
passages.text: Did you get the key?

passages.title: The Chieftain's Key
passages.text:
Thank you, thank you! I'm getting out of here right away!

And if Ferli sent you here... don't tell her I was crying!

passages.title: Disarming Bears
passages.text:
I would prefer to do as much as we can to protect my people from the Deadwood tribe without slaughtering every last one of them. We've taken steps towards this before, and if you wish to prove yourself to the Timbermaw tribe, I would ask you do this as well.

Look for the piles of weapons kept in Felpaw Village to the southwest. Take as many as you find. If we disarm the Deadwood tribe, we may be able to stop some bloodshed later.

passages.title: Disarming Bears
passages.text: Do you have the weapons?

passages.title: Disarming Bears
passages.text: Thank you, <race>. An action like this will go a long way towards proving yourself as an ally of the Timbermaw.

passages.title: Fire in the Hole!
passages.text:
Land's sakes, pardner! You done shut off those valves but good.

Unfortunately we've had a critical blowout in our gosh-darned central burnoff regulator! Missus Darla's done sent as many workers as she can rustle to go shut it off, but those flames have a mind of their own!

Literally! They're hoppin' up and grabbin' anyone who comes near! So Darla says if you can muster up out of that cave you're in and beat that elemental, she's got a mighty fine prize in store for ya!

passages.title: Fire in the Hole!
passages.text:
Well, my entire operation's nearly been ruined. But you came through in the clinch, <name>.

It could've been worse! I gotta hand it to you.

passages.title: Wisp-napping
passages.text:
Can you believe these worgen here have wisps? The night elves showed them all that druid junk and now they've got their precious little wisps too, giving them all the building material they want without having to harm any precious trees.

If we had those things, we could pull extra wood out of every tree in our site. Free resources, free profit! That's why I've been working on this containment device.

Head to Talonbranch Glade and use it to steal some wisps. Just point and press the button.

passages.title: Wisp-napping
passages.text: Pretty little things, aren't they? I wonder if we can figure out how to make more of them.

passages.title: Back to Business
passages.text:
All this happy friends stuff is great, isn't it? People working together, healing the forest. But what's gonna happen to the forest when it's healed? It's just gonna sit there?

We need this lumber. The Horde needs it. I've got orders here to send as many loyal Horde soldiers--and I'm sure you're loyal--up north to Irontree Clearing.

I've already arranged for the hippogryph master to give you a free ride over there. Talk to Darla Drilldozer when you touch down.

passages.title: Back to Business
passages.text: Fez sent you, hmm? At least he's good for something.

passages.title: Find Fanny
passages.text:
We've started tearing this camp apart, <name>, but there's no sign of Fanny. Maybe you can find her.

We haven't checked the cave just behind me, to the northwest. See if you can find Fanny in the cave!

passages.title: Find Fanny
passages.text:
Fanny is safe! I hear Firebeard was in there with you? Nice to hear he's finally pulling his weight.

Wait, why are you looking at me like that, <name>? Do you know something I don't?

passages.title: Pikwik in Peril
passages.text:
What the heck is going on here? Foreman Pikwik should've shut the valves off by now.

We can cap these leaks all day and if the central valve is off, we're just delaying an enormous explosion.

Listen, if you value money, your life, or either combination of the two, you'd better head south to Irontree Cavern and see if you can find Foreman Pikwik.

passages.title: Pikwik in Peril
passages.text:
It's a disaster down here! The pump's thrown, all my men in there are gone...

You gotta help!

passages.title: The Denmother
passages.text:
Barely a crow's flight to the north, goblins ravage this forest, clearcutting it to fuel the war machines of the Horde and line their own pockets. This one pays enough pleasant words and crafted lies to the druids here for them to turn a blind eye, afraid to disturb the tenuous neutrality here.

The worgen of Talonbranch Glade have had enough. Join us! The hippogryph master can take you directly to our home. Denmother Ulrica will welcome any <race> who wishes to fight.

passages.title: The Denmother
passages.text: Welcome to the home of my pack, <class>. Prepare yourself for war.

passages.title: Wisps of the Woods
passages.text:
I have toiled long here with the Denmother to spread the teachings of Cenarius and the ways of the wild. She has gained much of my trust, and in return, I have been allowed to introduce the spirits of the forest to her students. The company of wisps is a great honor, as well as a useful blessing.

But now the goblins descend on us, and seek to steal the wisps for nefarious use. Please, prevent this blasphemy!

Call the wisps back here from the western woods with this blessed branch, and keep them safe.

passages.title: Wisps of the Woods
passages.text: Have the wisps been saved?

passages.title: Wisps of the Woods
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. Now the Horde will not be able to defile these poor spirits to aid their brutish ways.

passages.title: Into the Clearing
passages.text:
Irontree Clearing must be razed. We can afford no mercy if we want to prevent the goblins from spreading their destruction through the entire forest.

Alton Redding, my most trusted protector, has already led much of the pack around the enemy line to strike while they are distracted here. Seek him out to the west, overlooking Irontree Cavern.

passages.title: Into the Clearing
passages.text: Welcome to the pack, <race>. Let's hope you don't mind getting a bit uncivilized.

passages.title: Oil and Irony
passages.text:
I plan to use the goblin's greed and pollution against them. Any further despoiling of the land they have already carved here will be worth it to stop their further spread.

Deep within Irontree Cavern, just below us, runs many pipes to pump oil through the ground across the entire clearing. These pipes are attached to a master control pump in the very back of the cavern.

Enter the cavern and sabotage the pump. The ensuing havok will give us opportunity for our final strike.

passages.title: Oil and Irony
passages.text: You flip a few switches on the pump and crank a large handle all the way to the right. There's a shuddering rumble in the nearby walls.

passages.title: Borrowed Bombs
passages.text:
The workers in Irontree Cavern below us have been driven out already. Something else has overtaken the cave.

This works in our favor. I spotted at least a few of them dropping explosives as they fled... explosives we'll need for the next part of our plan.

Enter the cave and salvage any abandoned bombs you can find. When you're finished with that and the pump, we'll begin our final assault.

passages.title: Borrowed Bombs
passages.text: Was I right? How many did you find?

passages.title: Borrowed Bombs
passages.text: Perfect. I've had the pack gather explosives from the rest of the camp as well, and with these, we'll have just enough to get things started once the oil is flowing.

passages.title: Bloody Wages
passages.text:
Sad little cowards... look at them flee in panic!

Don't let it fool you, <name>. The second they've regained their wits, those goblins are going to spend every waking moment chopping this forest to bits and sending the pieces to the Horde's war effort.

Don't give them the chance. Kill the workers throughout Irontree Clearing without mercy... show them their greed has a price!

passages.title: Bloody Wages
passages.text: Serves every last one of them right. Let's hope those in charge send the rest of their greedy scavengers somewhere else.

passages.title: Report to the Denmother
passages.text:
With the goblins scattered and their equipment destroyed, they'll either get the message and leave, or be easy pickings if they choose to stay. We've won here.

You've fought as fiercely as any member of the pack, <name>. Return to the Denmother and let her know of our success. I'll be maintaining my watch.

passages.title: Report to the Denmother
passages.text:
Let the goblins and all the Horde know we will not have offers of peace and sanctuary abused... most of all not in our new home.

I am grateful my people have found allies as bold as you, <name>. This reward will represent your bond with our pack. You will always be welcome here.

passages.title: Glop, Son of Glop
passages.text:
Glop had a son. In his grave hubris, he named it Glop. And so the line of fungalmancers continues.

I require you to slay this new fungalmancer. Your shaman ally has already returned, and awaits you at his cave in the southwest of Verlok Stand.

passages.title: Glop, Son of Glop
passages.text: To this day, I do not understand how filthy stone troggs breed so quickly. Perhaps it is better that it is left that way.

passages.title: Glop, Son of Glop
passages.text:
Perhaps one day, we shall slay these stone troggs more swiftly than they can breed, and in so doing, end the line of fungalmancers forever.

In time.

passages.title: The Restless Brood
passages.text:
Aeosera is restless and stubborn. She scoffs at our dominance, and she needs to be reminded of her place.

I still have the mallet you retrieved for me. Return to the western edge of the Pale Roost and strike the resonating crystal.

I will meet you there and lend what aid I can. Put her back in her place, <class>.

passages.title: The Restless Brood
passages.text: And so continues the cycle of the stone drakes. Tumultuous wills in stoic frames.

passages.title: The Restless Brood
passages.text: You are quite skilled at bending the dragon's will, <race>. I would be jealous of your agility, except that it comes with such a fragile frame.

passages.title: The Timbermaw Tribe
passages.text:
The Timbermaw furbolg are the last known tribe of uncorrupted furbolg. They huddle on the edge of these lands, ferociously defending their home of Timbermaw Hold.

Though they are proud creatures, they are in need of much assistance. Should you wish to help, follow the road north from here, and seek them out at the entrance to Timbermaw Hold.

passages.title: The Timbermaw Tribe
passages.text:
The druids of Talonbranch Glade have assisted us before. We are still unused to "friendly" worgen in these woods, but our people are also familiar with the sorrows of curses and corruption...

Sorrows that I hope you can aid us in, <class>.

passages.title: Schnottz So Fast
passages.text:
I'm nearly ready, <name>.

Your scrolls contained enough information to discern their encryption method. Now all that's left is for me to translate the codes.

I need you to scout out the chamber beneath the Obelisk of the Moon. There are likely to be a few of Schnottz's troops down there that escaped your blast.

You take care of them and I'll meet you there when I'm finished.

passages.title: Schnottz So Fast
passages.text:
Alright, <name>.

I think everything is in order. Let's do this!

passages.title: Bad Datas
passages.text:
There should be two titan communication devices in this chamber.

If my translations are correct, one is a death trap and the other will accept the codes and activate the obelisk.

Let's hope I get this right.

Let me know when you're ready.

passages.title: Bad Datas
passages.text:
Okay, <name>.

I think I can do this manually, but I'll need your help.

passages.title: I'll Do It By Hand
passages.text:
Yes, this all looks familiar enough.

Thanks to all the information you gathered for me, I'm sure that I can activate the mechanism. I'll just need some time free from distraction.

As soon as I get started, you can count on that titan construct to try and stop me.

That's where you come in.

I don't need to remind you of what's riding on this. Take down that guardian!

passages.title: I'll Do It By Hand
passages.text: Almost got it...

passages.title: I'll Do It By Hand
passages.text:
That should do it.

Stand back!

passages.title: The Bachelorette
passages.text:
Firebeard? Marry my sister!? I swear the world's gone mad, <name>!

Still, maybe Kurdran is right. A nice normal wedding would ease everyone's mind... and maybe cool off Firebeard a little. It was great to actually work together here against the ogres.

Right then! It's all up to Fanny. Something tells me she won't want to be tied down.

Fly back to Kirthaven and see if she's game. I'll finish up the nasty business with the ogres here.

passages.title: The Bachelorette
passages.text:
<Fanny throws her arms up, exasperated.>

You, Kurdran, Firebeard, and now my brother - everyone's got wedding fever!

Fine, fine, I'll marry Keegan Firebeard. But only 'cuz he's strong and handsome, with a jaw that can cut gravel and an arse like an anvil. Not for any political reasons.

We're going to need your help, though. We got a whole lotta wedding to put together, and not a lot of time to do it.

passages.title: Something Bold
passages.text:
By tradition, Wildhammer brides wear white to show their purity. In addition, they wear a crown of black feathers - to show their CHUTZPAH.

Owl feathers make the boldest statement, and Fanny deserves nothing less. Tawny owls are native to the Highlands. Look for them circling near trees that grow along the cliffs, and take their feathers.

You'll probably want to kill 'em, first.

passages.title: Something Bold
passages.text: Have you Fanny's feathers?

passages.title: Something Bold
passages.text: Ah, you work fast. Bold feathers for a bold woman. Well done!

passages.title: Something Stolen
passages.text:
Everyone's going to want to dress their best for this, and finery is in short supply in the Highlands.

I understand that those goblin wretches off the coast use the finest silk for repairing their zeppelin air envelopes. A waste!

Find a zeppelin flying back and forth between Dragonmaw Port and the Krazzworks, and liberate some silk from the cargo hold in the lower decks.

passages.title: Something Stolen
passages.text: How did the air raid go?

passages.title: Something Stolen
passages.text:
Oh, aye! Kilts for the gents, gowns for the bridesmaids.

Just don't tell the ladies they're wearing clothes fit for a blimp.

passages.title: Something Stewed
passages.text:
Finally, we're going to need a feast. And none of that "finger food" stuff! This crowd wants meat, and lots of it.

Gather up venison from Highland elk and does. Highland worg are good eatin' too - bring back some ribs. We'll show you a feast like you've never had in all the Eastern Kingdoms, friend.

passages.title: Something Stewed
passages.text: What's the food situation, <name>?

passages.title: Something Stewed
passages.text: Lookat that! You're practically bent double under the weight of all that meat. I'd better get my people cooking.

passages.title: Words and Music By...
passages.text:
I've written many an epic tune in my lifetime, <name>, but this upcoming wedding deserves a very special ballad. And fast!

Should I write a love song? A lighthearted ditty? A bawdy drinking song?

I could use some help with the lyrics, if you fancy a go at it.

Talk to me and we'll write a song together!

passages.title: Words and Music By...
passages.text:
Well, it's catchy, that's for sure.

But is it a classic?

passages.title: Burning Vengeance
passages.text:
<name>... is that you? I thought you were dead, with the rest of them!

No, you were always strong, even back then, even in Redridge.

Our fight's not over, <name>. They already attacked our homeland once. I'm here to make sure it doesn't happen again.

If you can still fight like you did back in the day, then join me. You can start by heading south, to the Whelping Downs, and slaying their whelpers and their hatchling black dragons.

It'll be like old times.

passages.title: Burning Vengeance
passages.text:
Glad to have you on my side, <name>.  Bravo Company reunited, right?

Oh, did I mention that Troteman's here, too?

passages.title: Burning Vengeance
passages.text:
I am a Blackrock orc by birth. I spent a large part of my youth inside that mountain.

<Ariok motions towards Blackrock Mountain, to the north.>

But while I share blood with them, I do not share their outlook. And I am seeking an ally to assist me in stopping their upcoming attack.

So prove yourself. Travel south, to the Whelping Downs, and slay their whelpers and the hatchling black dragons. Prove to me that you're ready for this war.

passages.title: Burning Vengeance
passages.text:
I suppose you don't have what it takes.

That's fine.  I can fight this war myself.

passages.title: Burning Vengeance
passages.text:
So you're in, then?

Good.

passages.title: Stocking Up
passages.text:
If we're going to wage war against the Blackrock clan, we're going to need to plan ahead. My father has already put the plan together - now it's time to execute.

I need scorpid stingers... the sharpest ones you can find. Scorpids are all over the steppes, but you can find most of them in the gulch to the west.

Don't worry about what they're for. You'll find out soon enough.

passages.title: Stocking Up
passages.text: Back already?

passages.title: Stocking Up
passages.text:
Those scorpids are easy to underestimate.  You're lucky you didn't end up on the end of one of these barbs.  Or maybe you're just good.

I'll add these to the stockpile.  We're not done yet, <race>.

passages.title: A Future Project
passages.text:
According to my father, we'll need worg hides, and lots of them. It doesn't matter if they're torn, burned, or bloody, but we need plenty of them.

Actually, it's probably better if they're a little beat-up.

You'll find worgs both to the west and to the east of here.

passages.title: A Future Project
passages.text: Let's take a look at those hides.

passages.title: A Future Project
passages.text:
Believe me, <name>... I'm just as anxious to get to the killing as you are.  We've got to keep to the plan.  The armageddon will come soon enough.

I'll keep these hides here.

passages.title: Mud Hunter
passages.text:
Hope you're not afraid of getting dirty. Judging by the looks of you, that won't be a problem.

To the north, at the lava's edge, you'll find piles of dark mud. I need it.

It'd be best if you didn't ask questions, and focused your efforts on following orders, <name>.

passages.title: Mud Hunter
passages.text: You'll want to watch out for those obsidian elementals.  They have a tendency to sneak up on you.

passages.title: Mud Hunter
passages.text:
This is exactly what we need.

Don't worry, <name>... the killing will come soon enough.

passages.title: The Sand, the Cider, and the Orb
passages.text:
My father is waiting for us to the east. Before we head out though, we need to gather some more supplies. This time, you'll be taking it from a warlock by the name of Gorzeeki Wildeyes.

You'll probably find him to the northwest, near the Altar of Storms. Tell him he's going to help us out. We need the sand, the cider, and the orb.

He'll know what it means.

passages.title: The Sand, the Cider, and the Orb
passages.text:
Gah!  Who are you?

Oh, so Ariok sent you?  Good.  Would ya mind sticking around for a while?  It's nothing big... I just need you to kill some warlocks for me.

passages.title: Warlocks Have the Neatest Stuff
passages.text:
Ariok said he needs supplies? I've got plenty of supplies! Problem is, those warlocks have kicked me out of my home, and they're not letting me back in.

<Gorzeeki sizes you up.>

You might be able to get in, though. Head north, and grab some of my slumber sand, my fel slider cider, and a clear glass orb. I'm pretty sure that's what he wants.

Oh, and if you happen to accidentally kill any of those orcs while you're up there, I wouldn't be terribly upset.

passages.title: Warlocks Have the Neatest Stuff
passages.text: Let's see if you managed to get everything.

passages.title: Warlocks Have the Neatest Stuff
passages.text: I hope that's what Ariok was looking for.  It's not doing me much good right now, anyhow.

passages.title: Shadow Boxing
passages.text:
Ner'gosh the Shadow is the leader of those warlocks to our north. He's the jerk that kicked me out of my home once those Blackrock orcs started showing up. Well, they're all jerks, but he's the jerkiest.

If I'm ever going to move back in near the Altar, Ner'gosh has to go.

passages.title: Shadow Boxing
passages.text:
Knowing the way those orcs operate, there'll be another one to take his place soon.  I'll see if I can't sneak back into the altar before that happens.

Thanks, buddy.

passages.title: Into the Black Tooth Hovel
passages.text:
Undercover work is all about swagger. Just act like you're supposed to be there, and you'll be fine.

Your contact inside Black Tooth Hovel will be an orc by the name of Quartermaster Kaoshin. He does NOT know you're a spy, so try and stay cool. Do whatever he asks of you.

<Eitrigg presses a small mechanical object into your palm.>

Place this device in your ear. I will be in touch to give you any special instructions.

Good luck out there, soldier.

passages.title: Into the Black Tooth Hovel
passages.text: Where have you been, grunt?  You're late!  Give me one reason why I shouldn't kill you on the spot!

passages.title: Grunt Work
passages.text:
Bah! You're lucky I'm short-handed today. Otherwise I'd make you my personal whipping <boy/girl> for the week.

The officers and high-ranking soldiers need their boots polished. They've left them out in front of their huts.

I want to see my reflection in those boots, grunt! Get to work!

passages.title: Grunt Work
passages.text: Hmph.  Good work, grunt.

passages.title: General Thorg'izog
passages.text:
Kaoshin turned out to be more helpful than I expected, but we're done with him. It's time you spoke with the General. I think you're ready.

General Thorg'izog is one of the "Big Three" that run the Blackrock forces here in Burning Steppes. He leads from the Blackrock Stronghold to the northwest. Put on your disguise and go speak with him. See if you can earn his trust. I will be in touch, should I need anything further.

passages.title: General Thorg'izog
passages.text: More outsiders?  What do you want?

passages.title: Flame Crest
passages.text:
Our work here in Chiselgrip is done, mostly thanks to you. We'll now be moving on to the northeast, to Flame Crest.

Flame Crest is in the cliffs, past the Ruins of Thaurissan. It should serve as a sufficient base of operations for the final stages of our plan.

Of course, my son Ariok will be joining you on the road. As will I.

passages.title: Flame Crest
passages.text: Oh.  Visitors?

passages.title: Blackened Ashes
passages.text:
I need you to do some more gathering before we can go take out the remainder of the Blackrock army. If we're going to do this, we're going to do it right, and that means being prepared.

I need ash, <name>. Not just any ash... ash from the greater obsidian elementals that roam the plains to the southeast. The stuff is deep, deep black, which is what we need for our next disguise.

Don't worry, you've already got a disguise. This one is for someone... well, someTHING... else.

passages.title: Blackened Ashes
passages.text: The ashes of the obsidian elementals are particularly dark - exactly what we need for our purposes.

passages.title: Blackened Ashes
passages.text: Yes, these will do.  I will get this packed up for you.

passages.title: Latent Demons of the Land
passages.text:
The lava beds nearby - to the south - play host to flamekin, a brand of fire demon that has long roamed the steppes. Situations are such in the Blackrock army that, if we are careful, we may be able to sneak some of these flamekin behind enemy lines to cause some havoc.

Bring me the bodies of several flamekin. As demons, they are easily resurrected, and then we can use them for our own purposes.

passages.title: Latent Demons of the Land
passages.text: The flamekin are weak, but they travel in packs.  Be cautious.

passages.title: Latent Demons of the Land
passages.text:
To the untrained eye, these will look exactly like imps.

We just need to get them to that untrained eye.  I'll work on preparing them for delivery.

passages.title: A Heap of Delicious Worg
passages.text:
We're going to need fresh meat, which means you're going to be hunting worg. The worg on this side of the steppes should be your target.

<Eitrigg produces a large blade, which he hands to you.>

Hunt the giant ember worgs. Once you've killed them, use this saw to remove the choicest bits of meat from their bodies. You will find these worgs all over the steppes, but the closest pack rules the land just to our southeast.

passages.title: A Heap of Delicious Worg
passages.text: Any luck out there?

passages.title: A Heap of Delicious Worg
passages.text:
This meat looks good... but I think it needs a little "seasoning".  I'll make sure that gets taken care of.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Blood Tour
passages.text:
My legs are getting a little restless again. You interested in taking a little tour, <name>?

We're going to take a trip around Dreadmaul Rock. I'd like to investigate some of the Blackrock army before we make our move, and I figure we might as well kill some of them while we're on the way.

passages.title: Blood Tour
passages.text:
<Ariok is covered in blood and sweat.>

That was exactly what I needed.

passages.title: Draconic Vanguard
passages.text:
The Blackrock orcs don't come alone. You've already seen that they've got the Firegut ogres and Smolderthorn trolls on their side. Unfortunately for us, they're also teamed up with the black dragonflight.

The orcs and the dragons have already sent some of their champions to stand guard at rally points, which are marked by a dragon skull on a pike. You and I are going to find these rally points and take out this vanguard before the battle starts.

Ready?

passages.title: Draconic Vanguard
passages.text: Come on, <name>, there's still more of them left.  Our job isn't done.

passages.title: Draconic Vanguard
passages.text:
Your kill count is adding up, <name>.  We're chipping away at them.

And we are going to win.

passages.title: A Deal With a Dragon
passages.text:
While we are circling around Dreadmaul Rock, there's one more stop that we need to make.

You remember the hatchlings that you freed from the Whelping Downs? I've been watching over them, and now we're going to deliver them to someone who will take care of them better than we can. He's staying in Slither Rock, to the northeast of Dreadmaul Rock.

His name is Acride, and he might be the key to victory in the upcoming battle.

passages.title: A Deal With a Dragon
passages.text: You've arrived, <name>.

passages.title: A Deal With a Dragon
passages.text:
Yes, the whelplings.  I will take care of them.

As for the agreement I made with your father earlier, tell him that I will hold up my end of the bargain.  You will have your dragon for the battle against the orcs.

We share your grudge against the Blackrock clan.

passages.title: Glory Amidst Chaos
passages.text:
You and my son are going back to that mountain. There's three orcs who survived the attack, and we won't rest until they're dead.

That's right, I'm talking about the Big Three.

General Thorg'izog crawled back into the Firegut Furnace, and Dragon-Lord Neeralak is cowering in the cave on the mountain's peak. Xi'lun is in the back of the Skull Warren, plotting with his fellow warlocks.

Leave your mark, <name>. Topple these corrupt Blackrock orcs once and for all.

passages.title: Glory Amidst Chaos
passages.text: Good luck, brother.

passages.title: Glory Amidst Chaos
passages.text:
<Eitrigg bows.>

Welcome home, boys.

passages.title: Mystery Goo
passages.text:
The greenish substance inside the cauldron is putrid and viscous. No matter what it is, it doesn't seem to be good.

It would be best to report back to Donova with your findings, along with a sample of the liquid in the cauldron.

passages.title: Mystery Goo
passages.text: I hope you found something, <name>. The Winterfall are becoming increasingly aggressive!

passages.title: Mystery Goo
passages.text: Disturbing news indeed. This stuff's much more like what you'd see in Felwood than in Winterspring...

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Toxic Horrors
passages.text:
I've studied the sample you returned with, and while I can't say for sure, I believe it contains traces of toxic elements. However, the only way to know for sure is to gather some as a comparison.

I believe that the Deadwood furbolg may be gathering these elements from other corrupted creatures in Felwood; in particular, the elementals living in the Irontree Woods, called toxic horrors.

Collect a few samples for me to compare, but be careful -- it's very dangerous there!

passages.title: High Chief Winterfall
passages.text:
The Winterfall furbolg are not a normally aggressive tribe, and this change in their behavior leads me to think that they must be under orders from their chief. We most likely can't undo the damage that has already been done, but if their leader is slain, they may not get any worse.

Head east again, past where you found that cauldron. High Chief Winterfall is here, at the easternmost part of Timbermaw Post.

passages.title: High Chief Winterfall
passages.text: Thank you so much, <name>. I hope to get back to my studies without worry that I will be ambushed. Please accept this as a reward.

passages.title: Words of the High Chief
passages.text:
The Winterfall are no longer a threat to me, but if you still want to find out what was driving the furbolg to create and consume this strange firewater, I think you should seek out Kelek Skykeeper.

He's a druid that once worked to help cleanse Felwood with the Emerald Circle, and has since come here to study the nearby ruins.

You might be able to find him to the east at Lake Kel'theril, where he spends his time recently.

passages.title: Words of the High Chief
passages.text: What is it you carry, <class>?

passages.title: Words of the High Chief
passages.text:
Yes, if you let me examine this for a while, I might be able to translate it for you.

<Kelek flips through the pages.>

When I am able to look over this fully, I will send word to you.

Thank you for sharing this with me, <name>. Very little is known about the Winterfall furbolg.

passages.title: The Ruins of Kel'Theril
passages.text:
At this lake, the Crystal of Zin-Malor was stolen by the Highborne. The crystal was a powerful artifact that bent arcane magic in wild and unpredictable ways... but it could only be held by the worthy, and brought doom upon all others.

The spirits that wander here span generations, each shackled here by Zin-Malor. Some will speak and tell their fates.

Should you wish to learn the fate of Zin-Malor, seek the spirit at the center of the lake...

passages.title: The Ruins of Kel'Theril
passages.text: Pity me, stranger, and all the Highborne, for it was here our folly began... our folly that cursed our children, and our children's children, to this day.

passages.title: Lieutenants of Darkness
passages.text:
The armies of Ramkahen are getting obliterated by Neferset's immortal guardians.

The only way to defeat them is to slay the Dark Pharaoh of Neferset.

Before we make our move, however, we're going to need to take care of his lieutenants.

Go behind the battle-lines and slay Scorpion-Lord Namkhare and High Priest Sekhemet. Only then will we be ready to confront the Dark Pharaoh himself.

passages.title: Lieutenants of Darkness
passages.text: You are a valuable ally, <name>.  We are one step closer to defeating the enemy.

passages.title: Troubled Spirits of Kel'Theril
passages.text:
The highborne spirits are miserable creatures, that's for sure. They are still searching for pieces of the very thing that has cursed them to Kel'Theril forever -- the stolen relic.

If you are that interested, take my pick and go south to the lake, see if you can gather the pieces of it from within the ice.

passages.title: Sullah's Gift
passages.text:
Jonesy tells me you two need to make it up that mountain.

Well, you're not going far with those troopers crawling all over it like ants on a carcass.

Some of my friends were able to confiscate a bit of the enemy's hardware. It should make your journey a bit easier.

Make your way up the ridgeline to the north, and you'll find it waiting for you.

Good luck, you two!

passages.title: Sullah's Gift
passages.text: Glad you could make it, <name>!

passages.title: The Heart of the Matter
passages.text:
The magus has been idle for far too long and an idle magus often leads to poorly thought out schemes. This time I am charged with collecting various beast organs in order to power some type of control rod. I am far too frail to go out hunting beasts - especially yetis!

Perhaps if I were to offer you a reward of some kind you would do it? All I need is for you to head west to the yeti caves and kill yetis. Rip their still beating hearts from their chests and bring them back here.

passages.title: The Heart of the Matter
passages.text: Bring me yeti hearts, <name>.

passages.title: The Heart of the Matter
passages.text: I... um... well... turns out he doesn't need the hearts anymore. Sorry about that! Hope it wasn't too inconvenient! A deal's a deal though, so here is your reward. You can go ahead and keep the yeti hearts. I hear they hold excellent nutritional value - if you're into eating.

passages.title: Yetimus the Yeti Lord
passages.text:
For years the mountain yeti of this region have been allowed free reign. Our complacency in dealing with the yeti menace has resulted in an aberration! Yetimus, lord of all yetis, has grown to a size and strength that our guard simply cannot handle. We fear that should his appetite lead him near Tarren Mill he would devour us all.

Gather a party of suitable adventurers and dispatch the beast. He roams the countryside to the west.

Bring me one of his horns and I will reward you handsomely.

passages.title: Yetimus the Yeti Lord
passages.text: Yetimus must die!

passages.title: Yetimus the Yeti Lord
passages.text:
So it's true, you did kill the beast! The people of Hillsbrad are indebted to you, <name>. You have made the land safer for our citizens.

Take whatever you may desire from our coffers.

passages.title: Salhet's Gambit
passages.text:
Neferset City is too well defended. The mountain next to it, however, is not.

I've spoken to the ranger captain and he's willing to take a handful of his men and secure the strategic mountaintop.

There is one catch, <name>. He agreed, but only if you would spearhead the attack with them.

It must be a small group, else we'll draw the enemy's attention too soon, but trust me... the rangers of Ramkahen are as tough as they come. With you by their side we'll surely succeed.

passages.title: Salhet's Gambit
passages.text: Hail, <name>!

passages.title: Salhet's Gambit
passages.text: You did it, <name>!  Excellent!

passages.title: Humbert's Personal Problems
passages.text:
So this is pretty embarrassing. Where to begin?

Well, you see, Melisara sent me to investigate the yeti menace in the nearby caves, west of here. It was getting late and my armor was weighing heavily on me. I took my gear off and decided to take a stroll. Yes, I, erm, went for a walk. Anyway, when I returned I discovered that my gear had been stolen! It was the yetis. I'm sure of it. They took my pants, sword and helm and ran off into their cave. Get them back for me and I will reward you.

passages.title: Humbert's Personal Problems
passages.text: I'm practically naked here, <name>. Help me out, eh?

passages.title: Humbert's Personal Problems
passages.text: Thank you, <name>! I promise you that this is the last time I take this gear off.

passages.title: Stagwiches
passages.text:
Ever had a stagwich? Me neither. Apparently they're delicious. Now I'm not one for eating, but I am a businessman. If my customers want stagwiches, who am I to argue?

You're probably asking yourself, "What does this have to do with me?" I'll tell you what, <class>, I need stag meat! You get me stag meat from the hill stags of Hillsbrad and I will pay you. Sounds like a pretty good deal, doesn't it?

Get going! Stags are most plentiful to the west.

passages.title: Stagwiches
passages.text: I need stag meat!

passages.title: Stagwiches
passages.text:
That's a hefty load you're carrying. It should keep my customers satisfied for the time being.

Here is your pay, as promised.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Darkshore!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Priestess Dentaria at Lor'danel in Darkshore.

The people of Lor'danel need your aid in caring for the survivors of Auberdine's destruction and securing their town against Twilight's Hammer. Speak to Vesprystus, the hippogryph master at Rut'theran Village outside of Darnassus and he'll arrange a flight to Darkshore.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Darkshore!
passages.text: So, the king has heard our plea? Thank Elune! We can use all the help we can get.

passages.title: Not Fireflies, Flameflies
passages.text:
Most of my fellow residents here at Flame Crest seem to have left at some point. I guess the Burning Steppes weren't INTERESTING enough for them.

Not me, though. I'm always finding new reasons to not leave, and the latest happens to be the flameflies that have been appearing lately.

They appear near lava during the day. By night, you'll find them almost anywhere.

If you wouldn't mind collecting some, I might be able to make it worth your while.

passages.title: Not Fireflies, Flameflies
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: Not Fireflies, Flameflies
passages.text: Nice work!  More pets for Kibler!

passages.title: A Fighting Chance
passages.text:
Blessed be the Light! I need your help!

On my way into Hillsbrad I noticed several families of adorable little deer. As I went out to pet one of the little fawns a ravenous mountain cat leapt out and killed it. I fled to Tarren Mill and swore to solve the plight of the hill fawn. Now, after many days of tinkering, I have created the hill fawn's salvation!

Take my wand into the fields to the west and use it to empower the wee hill fawns. Once empowered they will be able to fend for themselves!

passages.title: A Fighting Chance
passages.text:
WHAT!? No, don't tell me that, <name>! It can't be true! My... I... I would never...

I won't give up, <class>. Just you wait and see. I will save those fawns!

passages.title: Punish the Trespassers
passages.text:
We, priests of Nahom, are guardians of the Tombs of the Precursors.

Ever since the Neferset turned to their new masters, they've turned to great heresies.

They rob the sacred tombs of our forefathers, seeking powerful artifacts and destroying invaluable relics in the process.

Go to the tombs, east of here and punish the tomb-robbers for their transgressions, lest they join their brethren when the Neferset attack on Nahom begins.

passages.title: Punish the Trespassers
passages.text: You're back, <name>.  Is your prowess as great as I've heard?

passages.title: Punish the Trespassers
passages.text:
Perhaps you are as powerful as I've heard afterall.

You have our gratitude.

passages.title: The Cypher of Keset
passages.text:
<Salhet spends some time going over the tablets with the priests around him.>

It's all right here, <name>. Atulhet built a potent weapon into this temple and the only way to access it is with the correct cypher.

It is reportedly hidden in the Keset Pass. We must hope the Neferset looters haven't gotten to it yet. That's where Raider Lord Havat is operating and he's the most ruthless of the lot.

But without reinforcements, this might be our only hope for defending Nahom.

passages.title: The Cypher of Keset
passages.text: Did you retrieve the codex, <name>?

passages.title: The Cypher of Keset
passages.text: It is true then?  It does exist!

passages.title: The Defense of Nahom
passages.text:
The enemy is coming... and in great numbers.

We will get no further reinforcements. Let us hope we can stop the Neferset advance.

If Nahom falls, Ramkahen will follow.

Go outside and speak to one of my sergeants when you're ready. I will help you command the forces we have to the best of my ability.

passages.title: The Defense of Nahom
passages.text: There is no time to waste!

passages.title: The Defense of Nahom
passages.text: We did it, <name>!  We held Nahom.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Tanaris!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Kelsey Steelspark in Gadgetzan.

The Alliance needs your help to win concessions from the local baron and access to the area's priceless resources. You can reach Gadgetzan by traveling south from the Shimmering Deep in Thousand Needles.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Tanaris!
passages.text: We have to persuade the goblins of Gadgetzan to side with us, <class>.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Feralas!
passages.text:
All able bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Konu Runetotem at Camp Ataya in Feralas. Help the Horde secure the great forest against the Alliance and the Grimtotems.

You can reach Camp Ataya by traveling south from Desolace and into Feralas.

Destiny calls!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Feralas!
passages.text: There is much wrong in Feralas. I am glad to have your help.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Feralas!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Telaron Windflight at Dreamer's Rest in Feralas.

The Alliance needs your help to overcome our enemies, the Horde and the Grimtotems. You can reach Dreamer's Rest by traveling south from Desolace into Feralas.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Feralas!
passages.text: Elune has favored us with your arrival, <class>. There is much to do.

passages.title: The Howling Oak
passages.text:
So this is it... our new home. I'm not sure if I'll ever feel like I truly have a home again.

We mustn't be unappreciative of what the night elves have offered us though. Their race is not one to throw out idle welcomes to just anyone. It is a true testament to faith and generosity that they've taken us in.

Gwen and Greymane are in the city proper, at the Howling Oak. You should stop by. Take the portal beneath the tree north of us, then seek out the Howling Oak in the northern portion of the city.

passages.title: The Howling Oak
passages.text:
This oak was grown through the aid of the druids from a seed taken back on Gilneas. It stands for all that we've endured, and all that we've accomplished.

May it serve to remind us that our curse is also our blessing.

passages.title: Legacy of the High Elves
passages.text:
One hundred years ago...

I and a small group of other High Elves traveled here from our homeland, Quel'thalas. We sought the ancient mysteries of Kel'thoril... to find why it was destroyed.

We found fragments in the ice, shards of the crystal. The Archmage we accompanied did not take long to fall under their sway. In our foolishness, we noticed too late.

His spirit wanders in the southeast, among those he drove to madness, still clutching the memory of the precious shard...

passages.title: Legacy of the High Elves
passages.text: Maenius was a powerful mage and an honorable elf.  His spirit did not deserve such an ignoble fate.

passages.title: Legacy of the High Elves
passages.text:
We were shocked before we died. Shocked that one among our noble and austere kind could descend into vicious obsession so quickly. We died as naive fools, the victims of our own blithe assumptions.

The living would know that these events would play out yet again... both here, and among the entire elven race with the fall of Quel'thalas.

passages.title: The Fall of Neferset City
passages.text:
We are ready to strike now, <name>.

If we take down Dark Pharaoh Tekahn, the immortal colossi will fall and our armies will be able to march into Neferset City.

Seek him out and engage him without fear. I will make sure you're not alone when it's time to bring him down.

passages.title: The Fall of Neferset City
passages.text:
It is done.  We have defeated the Neferset inside their own city.

I wish I could say that there is peace for my people at last, but I only foresee more bloodshed.

passages.title: Winterfall Activity
passages.text:
The Timbermaw tend to stay to themselves, <name>. While we do allow safe passage to those we trust, we try to avoid other furbolg tribes if at all possible.

The Winterfall tribe has become increasingly hostile towards us. They seem to be in a state of rage, completely engulfed by their own fear and hatred of anything they do not understand.

The Winterfall carry spirit beads, which have clearly failed to protect them against corruption. Bring me 10 of these beads to show you have thinned their ranks.

passages.title: Winterfall Activity
passages.text: We very much appreciate what you have done for the Timbermaw, <name>.  Your continued efforts will surely earn my tribe's trust and respect.

passages.title: Winterfall Activity
passages.text:
Thank you for what you have done, as saddening as it is.  Accept this as a token of thanks.

I would ask of you to please continue helping us, <name>.  We have very few allies on which to call upon, and without your aid, the threats against my tribe would surely be too much for us to handle alone.

passages.title: Delivery for Donova
passages.text:
Donova Snowden is a kind dwarf who frequents the nearby hot springs. She claims to be studying their magical properties.

She is a kind person and has good relations with our tribe. As the Winterfall have become more and more aggressive, she has begun researching the cause of their corruption.

I must keep my post here, but I have made a basket of refreshments for her. Please take it to her for me and tell her we await her next visit.

passages.title: Delivery for Donova
passages.text: Welcome to the hot springs. What've you got there?

passages.title: Delivery for Donova
passages.text:
Oh, how nice of those dear furbolg. I feel so bad for them, cooped up in that hold, afraid of the world.

But can you blame them? These Winterfall furbolg are turning just as vicious as any in Felwood. I'd like to put a stop to it... if only for the sake of my own research, let alone the dear Timbermaw.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Un'Goro Crater!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Williden Marshal at Marshal's Stand.

The Alliance needs you to provide support to the Marshal Expeditions as they uncover the secrets of Un'Goro Crater's ancient beasts, unique flora, and powerful crystals. You can reach the crater by departing western Tanaris and following the road all the way to Marshal's Stand.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Un'Goro Crater!
passages.text: My team of explorers, researchers, and scientists is the finest in Azeroth, but we need all the help we can get to discover the truth about the crater's history and its denizens.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Silithus!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Windcaller Proudhorn at Cenarion Hold.

Our Cenarion Circle allies require your assistance to fight back against the Twilight's Hammer onslaught. You can reach Silithus by taking the northwestern road out of the Un'Goro Crater.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Silithus!
passages.text: Welcome to Cenarion Hold.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Desolace!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Officer Jankie on the road into Desolace at Tethris Aran.

The brave soldiers of Nijel's Point are beset by demons and the armies of the Horde, and they need your help. To reach Desolace, travel south on the road from the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Desolace!
passages.text: I can get you to Nijel's Point quickly! We need all the reinforcements we can get.

passages.title: The High Council's Decision
passages.text: The High Council is ready to decide on the war with the Neferset tribe.

passages.title: The High Council's Decision
passages.text: Very well, it looks like it's time.  Stay and watch if you so please.

passages.title: Descendants of the Highborne
passages.text:
Not long after my death, the greed of my people would lead to their exile. A continent away, they would become Quel'dorei, the High Elves. In Quel'thalas they would bathe in the power of their Sunwell, and forget their legacy of desire and greed.

These distant descendants returned here, drawn by the hand of fate, doomed to repeat history. Hear their tale now, as I have...

passages.title: Descendants of the Highborne
passages.text:
We were proud and noble. Our faith in the light protected us, and with the Sunwell, we wanted for nothing.

Because of that blindness, we came here to repeat the tragedy of history, as our entire race would in time.

passages.title: Descendants of the High Elves
passages.text:
Long after my death, my people would suffer an even greater mistake. The High Elves relied on the Sunwell and its glory. Never imagining a world without it, we would never make preparations to deal with such a fate.

Later, when the Sunwell fell to the forces of the undead, what was left of my descendants would be lost and helpless... and the path they would take in response would change them forever.

The Sin'dorei, still striving for redemption, would return here as well...

passages.title: Descendants of the High Elves
passages.text:
We were not naive, as our forefathers were. We were suspicious and cunning and ready for betrayal at every turn.

Yet our pride and greed drove us to ruin once more. How many more will be lost to Kel'theril?

passages.title: The Curse of Zin-Malor
passages.text:
You have seen enough. Know that the Crystal of Zin-Malor brings only ruin to all around it.

Leave this place, if you do not wish to join us.

passages.title: The Curse of Zin-Malor
passages.text: The shade! Yes, I saw it too!

passages.title: In Pursuit of Shades
passages.text:
You say it spoke of a master? Of one who holds Zin-Malor?

This is grave news. You must act, <class>! I saw the shade fly off to the south. Take the path to the upper ruins, and you may be able to climb the frozen waterfall after it!

And do not let your guard down... it may be waiting for you.

passages.title: In Pursuit of Shades
passages.text: Did you find the shade? Was anything left to indicate its origin?

passages.title: In Pursuit of Shades
passages.text:
Let me see... faintly written, among the engraved incantations, is the name of its master!

"Umbranse..."

passages.title: Cry of the Banshee
passages.text:
So you are to be our savior? Very well then, I will bond myself with you. Through this bond I will be able to see through your eyes and communicate with you in the field.

According to the plans you brought to us, the Stormpike have enlisted the aid of SI:7 at Sofera's Naze, to the north. SI:7 are comprised solely of humans - humans that we are able to use to our benefit.

Take my mirror and travel north. Engage in combat with the SI:7 and bring them near death. Once they are injured, use the mirror.

passages.title: Cry of the Banshee
passages.text:
<Melisara's voice pervades your thoughts.>

The humans will serve us in life and in death. I will be in contact with you shortly.

passages.title: Cache of Mau'ari
passages.text:
It be hard to describe de E'ko, but all creatures in dese lands have it... beasts, furbolg, even de frost giants. You got to open your mind and know where to look...

Watch me now, an' I show you how to pull out de E'ko.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Felwood!
passages.text:
All able bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Tenell Leafrunner at the Emerald Sanctuary in Felwood. The Cenarion Circle requires your help to wrest Felwood from the control of demons and other corrupt creatures!

To reach the Emerald Sanctuary, travel north from Ashenvale and follow the road until you reach the sanctuary.

Destiny calls!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Felwood!
passages.text: Welcome. My brothers and I are dedicated to the redemption and rejuvenation of this once-sacred forest.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Felwood!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Tenell Leafrunner at the Emerald Sanctuary.

His order requires your help to redeem Felwood from the demonic influences that rule the forest. Head north from Ashenvale and follow the road into Felwood until you reach the Emerald Sanctuary.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Felwood!
passages.text: There is much work to do here. The forest is on the mend, but without our help, it will take generations to restore this once-sacred wood.

passages.title: Hero's Call: Winterspring!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Donova Snowden at Frostfire Hotsprings.

She requires your help to overcome the threat of the Winterfall furbolg. To reach Winterspring, you must travel east from northern Felwood and traverse Timbermaw Hold.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Winterspring!
passages.text: Thank goodness you're here. I've discovered the secret of the fierce Winterfall furbolg.

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Winterspring!
passages.text:
All able-bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Donova Snowden at Frostfire Hot Springs. Her discoveries about the Winterfall furbolg may be the key to dealing with this threat once and for all.

To reach the Frostfire Hot Springs in Winterspring, you must travel east from northern Felwood and traverse Timbermaw Hold.

Destiny calls!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Winterspring!
passages.text: Perhaps you can help me make sense of my discoveries about the source of the Winterfall Furbolgs' strength.

passages.title: Winterfall E'ko
passages.text:
In Winterspring, you will fight misguided creatures known as de Winterfall furbolg. These bear-people be so angry an' ferocious, dey live in a constant frenzy.

Bring me de E'ko of de Winterfall, an' I give you a frenzy so intense, ya legs will let you run like de wind!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Desolace!
passages.text:
All able bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Furien at Tethris Aran in Desolace. The brave Horde warriors of Desolace need your help to beat back the armies of the Alliance and ancient demons.

To reach Tethris Aran, travel south from the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains.

Destiny calls!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Desolace!
passages.text: You... arrived just in... time...

passages.title: Hero's Call: Dustwallow Marsh!
passages.text:
By order of his royal highness, King Anduin Wrynn, all able-bodied citizens of the Alliance are to report to Calia Hastings at Theramore Isle.

You must aid SI:7's Calia Hastings in uncovering the threats to Theramore, both within the city and beyond its walls. You can reach Theramore Isle by taking the boat from Menethil or traveling across the marsh from the Southern Barrens.

For the glory and honor of the Alliance!

passages.title: Hero's Call: Dustwallow Marsh!
passages.text: Deserters from the city guards are spreading discontent in the ranks. We have to get to the bottom of this before it undermines our defenses.

passages.title: Okrilla and the Blasted Lands
passages.text:
I have one final dispatch to deliver to you, <name>. It comes from Dreadmaul Hold, to the south, in the Blasted Lands.

Warmatron Okrilla is waging battle against the Alliance forces of Nethergarde Keep, and she needs the assistance of a stout <class>. You immediately sprung to mind.

Travel south into the Blasted Lands, then head west. Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Okrilla and the Blasted Lands
passages.text: Well, well, well... look what the Ruag dragged in!

passages.title: Warchief's Command: Uldum!
passages.text:
All able-bodied members of the Horde are hereby ordered to report to Adarrah at the Thistleshrub Valley in Tanaris.
