passages.title: The Champion's Call!
passages.text:
Pfft, what happens down here ain't fightin'. It's a couple of guys dancin' around a flag.

You lookin' for some real action, buddy? 'Cause if you are I got the hottest ticket in town.

Ever heard of Gurgthock and Wodin? Goblin and troll who ran the Ring of Blood back in Outland? Well they're here in Northrend and they've started up a whole new fight club over in Zul'Drak. If you're interested go to Zul'Drak, east of Crystalsong. They're at the big arena in the center. Tell 'em Shifty sent ya!

passages.title: The Champion's Call!
passages.text: Shifty sent you, eh?

passages.title: Armor of Darkness
passages.text:
This armor plate is thick and oversized compared to the rest of the golem's defenses. A quick examination of the golem's corpse reveals that this heavier plate seems to have been bolted on as an afterthought or a crude upgrade.

Why would the iron dwarves have added this redundant and mismatched armor to their war golems?

Perhaps Bruor Ironbane would know if he had the chance to examine several of these plates from stormforged war golems.

passages.title: Armor of Darkness
passages.text: What is it you have there?

passages.title: Armor of Darkness
passages.text:
Careful, now. Keep that plate as far away from me as you can. Even being in its presence is enough to inflict pain.

But you're right, <name>, these are gigantic armor plates for a war golem of normal size. What would the stormforged be doing with them? There's only one way to find out.

passages.title: Hit Them Where it Hurts
passages.text:
Bouldercrag's got a good plan to stymie the efforts of the iron dwarves at Narvir's Cradle, and I've got an idea of my own. Work on the iron colossus will come to a halt without any artisans.

Narvir's Cradle is on the south side of the hill sheltering Bouldercrag's Refuge. Go there and slay any stormforged artificers in your path. They may be no different from what we once were, but they build a weapon that threatens us all.

passages.title: Hit Them Where it Hurts
passages.text: There were days when I could never ask someone to do what you did, but my experience with the iron dwarves has extinguished those feelings. We have bought time against the enemy's advance.

passages.title: A New Beginning
passages.text:
It remains uncertain whether or not our people can ever rekindle the affection we once held for Thorim.

May this armor, if nothing else, remind him of the days when we stood together in honor, invincible.

passages.title: A New Beginning
passages.text: How have your efforts fared, <class>?

passages.title: A New Beginning
passages.text:
<As you present Thorim with the reforged suit of armor, he is visibly stricken by its splendor.>

You have done well, <race>, but there remains much to be done.

passages.title: Finish the Shipment
passages.text:
I'm glad you showed up! A shipment of Glowing Ivory Figurines needs to go out to Undermine right now, and I am still short a Chalcedony to complete an eye for the last one.

Bring me one and a Dalaran Jeweler's token will be yours.

passages.title: Finish the Shipment
passages.text: Do you have the Chalcedony yet?

passages.title: Finish the Shipment
passages.text: Here is your Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token as promised.  I have new shipments going out all the time, check by from time to time to see what I need.

passages.title: If There Are Survivors...
passages.text:
Across the Valley of Echoes, west of here, and through the Breach, is the first Scourge encampment in Icecrown known as Scourgeholme. We fought a good fight at Scourgeholme and killed many Scourge, but in the end we were forced to retreat. Many soldiers were left behind - their fate unknown.

If there are survivors, we must attempt a rescue. Directly down this southeastern path is Penumbrius, ally of the bronze dragonflight and caretaker of the proto-brood. Seek him out and ask for his assistance.

passages.title: If There Are Survivors...
passages.text:
<Penumbrius nods.>

My kin will help. Together we will battle the Lich King and his undead legions.

passages.title: Looking for Survivors
passages.text:
Gretchen Fizzlespark wants to use my flying machine to look for survivors from her expedition. Apparently she thinks they're being held prisoner in the village to the north.

The only problem is I don't have a co-pilot. If you're willing to take it on, I'd be more than happy to teach you a move or two.

What do you say, <name>? Deal?

passages.title: Prepare for Glory
passages.text:
This is it then. I'll take care of your bear now, you won't be needing her. The great Drakkensryd will be your next challenge.

Say goodbye to your friends and leave your affairs in order, for you will return victorious... or you won't return at all.

passages.title: Prepare for Glory
passages.text: You've really made it this far.  Never would I have thought you'd progress so quickly among the hyldnir.

passages.title: Lok'lira's Parting Gift
passages.text:
You've been a great ally, <name>. Now comes your true test. You will need skill, courage and a little luck.

<Lok'lira attaches a thin strand of hair to yours.>

You cannot fail now sister. Speak to Gretta the Arbiter. She'll see you on your way.

passages.title: Lok'lira's Parting Gift
passages.text: Are you ready to ride, sister?  There is no coming back.

passages.title: Deemed Worthy
passages.text:
You have succeeded where many have failed, sister. Whether it be by strength and courage or mere luck remains to be seen.

Go back to the village and seek out Astrid Bjornrittar. Tell her of your accomplishments. But be warned. She is not easily impressed.

passages.title: Deemed Worthy
passages.text:
So, sister, you think that completing a few simple chores makes you a heroine?

You shall learn....

passages.title: Sibling Rivalry
passages.text:
Sif? Is it truly you?

No? A <race>? But for a moment....

Enough of this! The visions of my Sif have tormented me for far too long. It is time for me to avenge her, and to bring honor to her memory.

My brother must pay!

passages.title: Sibling Rivalry
passages.text: Hear my words, <race>.

passages.title: Sibling Rivalry
passages.text:
You now know a bit of the history of this land... my land.

I call upon you to assist me in setting these wrongs to right.

passages.title: A Cold Front Approaches
passages.text:
The chill of death stirs in the west, threatening to freeze our hearts and souls to this wasteland and bind us to its dark master. We will stand and we will fight!

The preparations have begun. Report to Siegemaster Fezzik at the front gate for your assignment.

passages.title: A Cold Front Approaches
passages.text: We must be quick or face being overtaken by the Scourge! There's really no time for instructions, <race>. You're just going to have to jump in and hope for the best.

passages.title: The Touch of an Aspect
passages.text:
The dragon-queen, Alexstrasza, possesses magics over all life. In the past, she has used great fire to incinerate undead and rebirth fresh new life in their place. Perhaps her powers might be able to save our Bridenbrad as well.

Alexstrasza makes her home at Wyrmrest Temple in Dragonblight - please go to her and humbly request her aid on my behalf.

passages.title: The Touch of an Aspect
passages.text:
Greetings to you, <race>.

The concern is clear on your face. Please tell me what troubles you.

passages.title: The Will of the Naaru
passages.text:
I appreciate everything that you have done for us, <name>. I have one last errand for you... one last gleaming hope for a paladin who deserves any salvation that we can extend.

Go now to Shattrath and speak to the naaru, A'dal. He has long been a beacon of light and powerful ally to devout paladins. Impart Bridenbrad's story and seek any aid that he might have to offer.

I cannot impress how important it is that you move quickly - I fear our crusader does not have much more time in this world.

passages.title: The Will of the Naaru
passages.text:
<A gentle ringing fills your head as you approach the naaru.>

I know why you have come.

passages.title: The Boon of A'dal
passages.text:
I am pleased that you have come to me, <name>. I know of Crusader Bridenbrad, and of your travels in hope of saving him. Bridenbrad's valor has sparked remarkable selflessness in you, and this is a miracle unto itself.

The Light will take care of its own. I will extend my blessing to Bridenbrad and he shall not endure the corruption of undeath. I shall return you to Dalaran, and you shall return to him. Know that I remain with you.

passages.title: The Boon of A'dal
passages.text:
<As you approach Crusader Bridenbrad, you cannot help but notice that his skin has taken on a pale hue and his breaths are shallow. It is clear that he has little time left.>

You have returned to me, <class>. I must admit... it is good to see you again... your face renews my hope that this land will be free of Arthas's grasp one day soon. I'm proud to have met you...

passages.title: Vaelen Has Returned
passages.text:
I just saw that incompetent fool, Vaelen the Flayed, sneak into the vault building.

Go see to it that he rectifies his mistake and returns my death knights to me!

passages.title: Vaelen Has Returned
passages.text: I think I can guess why you're here, <name>.

passages.title: Have They No Shame?
passages.text:
Archmage Berinand loaned me his research on the Arcanomicron, some sort of map that Malygos is trying to assemble.

I made the mistake of discussing it with a group of Horde adventurers and now it's gone!

It must have been them. Please, recover the book.

passages.title: Have They No Shame?
passages.text: Please, <name>, tell me you've found the book...

passages.title: Have They No Shame?
passages.text:
You found it!? Yes, yes, it's all here.

Please, take this with my gratitude.

passages.title: Have They No Shame?
passages.text:
Archmage Berinand loaned me his research on the Arcanomicron, some sort of map that Malygos is trying to assemble.

I made the mistake of discussing it with a group of Alliance adventurers and now it's gone!

It must have been them. Please, recover the book.

passages.title: Have They No Shame?
passages.text: Please, <name>, tell me you've found the book...

passages.title: Have They No Shame?
passages.text:
You found it!? Yes, yes, it's all here.

Please, take this with my gratitude.

passages.title: Unfinished Business
passages.text:
While it is true that the Prophet of Akali will trouble this world no more, there yet remains work to be done.

The greater part of Akali's blood has empowered another, and it is in him that the true danger lies.

Quickly, <name>, make your way north of Gundrak to Dubra'Jin and speak with Tol'mar. He will be able to direct you further in this cause.

passages.title: Unfinished Business
passages.text: Lissen up, mon. Dere be dangerous work ta be done!

passages.title: Just Checkin'
passages.text:
There have been fearsome sounds echoing from Gundrak. They have been increasing in volume and frequency of late.

My long-time student is currently recording events from her post just west of Gundrak. Perhaps you could find the time to check in on her for me?

passages.title: Just Checkin'
passages.text:
Long-time student? Hah!

If by long-time ya mean my whole life, den I suppose dat be accurate.

To'kini be my cowardly father - too fearful to take up a position so near Gundrak... so he sent me!

passages.title: Blackwatch
passages.text:
The Scourge has a large facility called the Fleshwerks, dedicated to producing abominations and flesh giants. If we can shut it down, we can deprive the Lich King of a large component of his armies.

I've sent Darkrider Arly to the area. She has a small base, Blackwatch, on a ridge overlooking the Fleshwerks and to the west of Corp'rethar. I'm told the Argent Crusade is sending someone to coordinate their efforts there, but the darkrider will know what to do. Find and assist her.

passages.title: Blackwatch
passages.text: Good. We'll need all the help we can get. Olakin here is the Argent Crusade's contribution to our effort. Let's cut the chatter and get down to the business of denying the Scourge their armies of the flesh.

passages.title: Jagged Shards
passages.text:
You pulled this jagged, dark brittle shard from the body of a ghoul. The metal blade lacks a smooth edge, suggesting it was forged by an unskilled hand, or was broken from a larger piece.

You recall seeing similar shards embedded in the bodies of all the ghouls you've encountered at the Fleshwerks, leading you to wonder why their creators bothered to include the metal at all. Perhaps Crusader Olakin Sainrith would have some insight if you brought him the shards from several ghouls.

passages.title: Jagged Shards
passages.text: What is that vile thing?

passages.title: Jagged Shards
passages.text:
<Olakin handles the shards of metal gingerly.>

You saw these on all of the ghouls down there? I've never seen anything like this in all my battles against the Scourge.

passages.title: Discretion is Key
passages.text:
Listen to me, <race>.

It's just been brought to my attention that there's been an incident at the Violet Hold. It would appear that the blues are launching a full scale invasion of Dalaran!

I need you to get to the prison and speak with Warden Alturas at once. He'll give you the details.

That is not all. I need this handled with utmost discretion. We mustn't alarm the citizens of Dalaran if it can possibly be avoided. Do I make myself clear?

Very well. Now, go!

passages.title: Discretion is Key
passages.text:
Not a moment too soon.

Are you prepared to defend Dalaran, <class>?

passages.title: No Mercy for the Merciless
passages.text: Welcome to Wintergrasp, <name>. Your mission is simple. Defeat ten of the Horde's finest. Now, go! Bring victory to the Alliance!

passages.title: No Mercy for the Merciless
passages.text: Glorious! Truly, you are among the champions of the Alliance.

passages.title: Saurfang's Blessing
passages.text:
You are now, and forever will be, a Knight of the Ebon Blade, <name>, but know this: you were once a hero of the Horde.

<Darion stares at you.>

This order must establish allies for itself if it is to survive. You must represent the Knights of the Ebon Blade to the Horde.

On the platform, southeast of me, is a portal to Orgrimmar. Take this letter, given to me on your behalf by Lord Fordring, and deliver it to High Overlord Saurfang. Use the portal.

passages.title: Saurfang's Blessing
passages.text: An interesting turn of events.

passages.title: Saurfang's Blessing
passages.text:
Eitrigg is alive because of this paladin. He would have been executed had Lord Fordring not broken him out of Stratholme.

Tirion Fordring, to have sacrificed everything to save the life of an orc... Indeed, this is a rare event.

Yes. For Tirion Fordring and for Eitrigg! We will accept you as a member of the Horde and your order as allies.

Blood and honor! For the Horde!

passages.title: Battle at Valhalas
passages.text:
I see and hear many things, <name>, and something very important has happened since your defeat of Overthane Balargarde: you are wanted for battle in Valhalas!

You will find the battle pit to the north. Go now with your friends and speak with Geirrvif the val'kyr. The challengers that she will offer you within Valhalas are sure to require their help.

Good luck.

passages.title: Battle at Valhalas
passages.text:
You have bested our finest warriors. Your name is renowned, <name>.

Perhaps you think that this concerns me: it does not. If they can fall to you then they are not worthy and should be nothing but lowly vargul!

But perhaps I can give you and your friends different sport. Valhalas is also a place for combat of all types with many different kinds of foes.

Speak to me again when you and your friends are ready to proceed. We shall see if you are truly worthy.

passages.title: I'm Not Dead Yet!
passages.text:
The Light smiles upon me. I have not yet died in this living nightmare, but the Scourge will kill me and tear my body apart for use in their 'work' here if I cannot escape.

I cannot make it on my own, <class>, but with your help, I may yet live to fight the Scourge again.

Will you help me make my escape before the Scourge's butchers come to finish me off?

passages.title: I'm Not Dead Yet!
passages.text: You have done well. We thought Father Kamaros lost, for certain. Your bravery will serve as an example to all those who oppose the Scourge.

passages.title: Make Them Pay!
passages.text:
The time has come!

Too long have we suffered the company of the self-righteous Alliance! Too long have we stayed our hand from cleansing our world of the weak and the desperate.

Now, we bring an end to our humiliation! Now, we show them the true meaning of fear! Now, we bring honor to the Horde!

Here, at Icecrown, we break the Alliance!

Go, <class>. Hunt them down. Break them. Take their will to live!

passages.title: Make Them Pay!
passages.text:
You have done well, <class>.

Soon, the Alliance shall run from you in fear and the Horde shall honor your name!

passages.title: Opportunity
passages.text:
We recently came upon schematics that indicate a weakness in Icecrown Citadel. An opening in its defenses, both figuratively and literally.

The captured diagrams show an orifice leading several hundred feet into the ground. We're unsure of its purpose, but our scouting has revealed it to be of high importance to the Scourge.

Speak to Sergeant Kregga below Icecrown Citadel, she's leading the attack on the site.

passages.title: Opportunity
passages.text: Just in time, <name>.  Koltira spoke highly of you.  Perhaps you'll be able to push the scales in our favor.

passages.title: Takes One to Know One
passages.text:
While we should never miss an opportunity to strike out against the Alliance, we mustn't forget about the Scourge.

We won't have the numbers here to make a proper assault in the glacier for weeks, but that won't keep us from learning all we can know about their defenses.

I have asked our resident death knight to advise you in this effort. After all, who better knows this enemy than they?

Allow me to introduce Koltira Deathweaver.

passages.title: Takes One to Know One
passages.text:
<Koltira looks you up and down.>

I hope for your sake that you're up to this, <class>.

passages.title: Blow it Up!
passages.text:
This is probably as under-control as this situation is going to get. Let's do this, <name>.

I need someone to light the fuse on those bombs and it looks like you're the one to do it.

passages.title: Blow it Up!
passages.text: These bombs look pretty potent.  They should at least put a dent in the surrounding structure.

passages.title: A Short Fuse
passages.text:
As you light the fuse, you notice that it is consumed by fire far quicker than you would expect.

The bombs are about to go off and your best chance at surviving is to lean towards the pit and hope the fall doesn't kill you.

passages.title: A Short Fuse
passages.text: This pulsing object is covered in a thick layer of ice.  It shimmers strangely beneath the water.

passages.title: A Voice in the Dark
passages.text:
The object is not a crystal at all, but some form of organ, encased in ice.

As you touch it, your hand reels in horrible pain. You feel as if your hand has been cut, yet there is no visible wound.

As you collect your thoughts, you hear a young boy's voice nearby.

"You really shouldn't have done that."

passages.title: A Voice in the Dark
passages.text:
I saw him get rid of it, you know?  He threw it all the way down here.

Said he wouldn't need it anymore.  Said it made him weak.

passages.title: Going After the Core
passages.text:
With Norgannon's Shell in hand, only half of the archive key remains to be found. Luckily, I've had the Explorers' League hard at work chasing down leads about the whereabouts of Norgannon's Core.

Far to the southeast of the Inventor's Library, on the slopes to the north of Dun Niffelem, is a camp bearing my name. The Explorers' League representatives seeking the second half of the key are based there. Bring me the maps and the notes they've made and we should be able to track down the other key half.

passages.title: Going After the Core
passages.text: Have you recovered those notes?

passages.title: Going After the Core
passages.text:
Ruined? What d'you mean, the camp's been ruined?

<Brann clenches his fists in anger.>

Those iron dwarves will pay for this! There's little we can do now, and we have to focus on finishing the key. But once I get into the halls of Ulduar, the irons and their masters will answer for what they've done!

passages.title: The Core's Keeper
passages.text:
Prospector Soren's notes say that Norgannon's Core is in the keeping of a sentinel named Athan, one of Mimir's creations.

Soren says the vault where Athan resides is called "Loken's Bargain" these days.

Loken, eh? The earthen have mentioned him.

The vault is said to be southwest of the ruined Explorers' League camp, with a round entrance on a mountainside overlooking the Valley of Ancient Winters.

Find this Athan and get the core from him, but I wouldn't be surprised if you were in for a fight.

passages.title: The Core's Keeper
passages.text: Was Prospector Soren right? Did you finally find Norgannon's Core?

passages.title: The Core's Keeper
passages.text: This is really it! The key is almost within our grasp. All we need now is a way to combine the shell and the core into a single key. Let's see what Prospector Soren had to say about this...

passages.title: Return to the Surface
passages.text:
You should leave now. You'll find a portal behind me. It'll take you to the surface.

We'll meet again. He'll be looking for you.

It's only a matter of time until he finds you.

passages.title: Return to the Surface
passages.text:
<name>!  We thought you were dead!

We lost a few men in that explosion... but we sure put a hurt on the Scourge.  They're scrambling their forces back to the citadel and leaving big gaps in their defenses.  It's time to push forward.

passages.title: ...All the Help We Can Get.
passages.text:
Desperate times, <class>...

As uncomfortable as it makes me, I'm prepared to accept assistance from anyone - including our resident death knight.

Go to Thassarian and see if he can help us develop tactics against the Scourge that will ensure victory once we are able to mount another offensive.

We have come so far... we must not fail here!

passages.title: ...All the Help We Can Get.
passages.text:
It was wise of Captain Bartlett to send you.

While he frets over your conflict with the Horde, someone must remain exclusively focused on the real mission here - the march on Icecrown Citadel.

Who better to direct your efforts than a former servant of the Lich King?

passages.title: Your Attention, Please
passages.text:
Chief Engineer Boltwrench has proven invaluable in his service aboard the Stormbreaker. Were it not for his ingenuity, we'd be sprinkled across half of the glacier several times over by now.

The thing is, he feels he must share his every miniscule invention or discovery - most of which I don't even understand.

My focus must be squarely on our enemies right now. I cannot afford any distractions.

Please visit him in my stead, <name>. And if you can, assist him. You'll find him belowdecks.

passages.title: Your Attention, Please
passages.text:
Cappy sent you in his place, did he?

Very well, <class>. Roll up those sleeves... time to get to work!

passages.title: Get to Ymirheim!
passages.text:
You need to get down to Ymirheim, that big frost vrykul town in the middle of Icecrown.

Our boy, Blast Thunderbomb, is down there on the west side of town representing the Warsong Offensive in a competition against the Alliance. It's his jumpbot versus theirs in a king of the mountain contest!

Don't let us down, <name>. Goblin engineering pride is on the line! Besides, all the boys here in the hold are counting on you.

That and we've got money riding on it that you can kick those cowards in the pants!

passages.title: Get to Ymirheim!
passages.text: Oh man, am I glad to see you! Did the chief send you down from the Hammer?

passages.title: Get to Ymirheim!
passages.text:
I need you down in Ymirheim, that big frost vrykul town in the middle of Icecrown.

Frazzle Geargrinder is down there on the south side of town representing the Valiance Expedition in a competition against the Horde scum. It's her jumpbot versus theirs in a king of the mountain contest!

Don't let us down, <name>. Gnomish engineering pride is on the line! Besides, all the boys here in the hold are counting on you.

That and we've got money riding on it that you can kick those idiots in the pants!

passages.title: Get to Ymirheim!
passages.text: Did the chief send you down from the Skybreaker? Isn't that thing sweet?!

passages.title: Futility
passages.text:
Do you see now? Sending your men against the prince's armies just swells their numbers.

I don't expect you to understand... you'll probably just end up like the others. You'd best return to whoever sent you. They might be worried.

passages.title: Futility
passages.text:
There you are.  Nice work down in the valley.  The carnage was visible all the way up here.

Are you okay?  You look like you've seen a ghost.

passages.title: Where Dragons Fell
passages.text:
A whole brood of blue dragons fell here. And now, one by one, they're being raised by his servants.

He raised the biggest of them all himself. Bring me some bone dust from the whelps and I'll show you exactly how he did it.

passages.title: Where Dragons Fell
passages.text: Did you get the dust, <name>?

passages.title: Where Dragons Fell
passages.text: Even the mighty wyrms had to heed his call.  How is a simple mortal like you going to resist him?

passages.title: Time for Answers
passages.text:
You have a lot of questions, <name>. You're the only one who can see me because you touched something that once belonged to him... don't you remember?

You don't know what it is? Well I can't just tell you... that would make him really mad. He's not just a prince anymore... he's the king!

Meet me at the Court of Bones, north of Icecrown Citadel and you can see for yourself.

passages.title: Time for Answers
passages.text: There you are.  I started to wonder whether you'd show up.

passages.title: Knowledge is a Terrible Burden
passages.text:
Now you know what you're up against, <name>. An opponent who no longer knows pain... remorse... or humanity. An opponent who will do anything to get what he wants.

The heart was his weakness and now he knows you've found it.

If you're going to go back for it, you'd best bring help. He will not leave it unguarded again.

passages.title: Knowledge is a Terrible Burden
passages.text: Little kid's ghost... Arthas's heart... you'd better slow down... you're making my head spin.

passages.title: Argent Aid
passages.text:
There were rumors about the events you speak of among the death knights. I always expected the story to be more... symbolic.

We must warn others, but we must be discreet. As soon as the Lich King knows we're making our move, he'll move the location of the heart -- we'll never get a chance like this again.

The Horde and the Alliance have been infiltrated by the Cult of the Damned before. The Ebon Blade operates too close to the Scourge.

We have to speak to Tirion Fordring and his Argent Crusade.

passages.title: Argent Aid
passages.text: Heavy words, <name>.  If it were somebody else saying them, I'd be likely to judge them insane.

passages.title: Green Technology
passages.text:
Tezzla is the one you want to meet, yes she is... she mastered a new wavelength, infra-green, and used it to hide herself near the Scourge! Near enough to bomb them!

I'll give you infra-green vision so you can find her hiding above Aldur'thar, the Desolation Gate. Go, go... I know she has work for brave heroes eager to blow up! I mean... eager to blow up the Scourge!

And <name>, the Alliance has stolen our technology and has their own hidden airport nearby. Avoid the dome with the Alliance banners!

passages.title: Green Technology
passages.text: Yes, yes!  You found me!  And just in time!

passages.title: Exploiting an Opening
passages.text:
I've got an interesting assignment for you, <name>. If you're up for a challenge, that is.

We've been tipped off about an opening below Icecrown Citadel. Our engineers have studied the layout and have decided it's a structural weakness.

We've sent some men there along with some "borrowed" saronite bombs. They're under Captain Kendall's command.

With a little help we could deal a huge blow to the forces of the Scourge. What do you say, <name>?

passages.title: Exploiting an Opening
passages.text: Hail, <name>.  Thassarian mentioned you'd be dropping by.  Any friend of Thassarian's is my friend.  Well, any living friend of Thassarian, that is...  He does keep odd company.

passages.title: A Short Fuse
passages.text:
As you light the fuse, you notice that it is consumed by fire far quicker than you would expect.

The bombs are about to go off and your best chance at surviving is to lean towards the pit and hope the fall doesn't kill you.

passages.title: A Short Fuse
passages.text: This pulsing object is covered in a thick layer of ice.  It shimmers strangely beneath the water.

passages.title: A Voice in the Dark
passages.text:
The object is not a crystal at all, but some form of organ, encased in ice.

As you touch it, your hand reels in horrible pain. You feel as if your hand has been cut, yet there is no visible wound.

As you collect your thoughts, you hear a young boy's voice nearby.

"You really shouldn't have done that."

passages.title: A Voice in the Dark
passages.text:
I saw him get rid of it, you know?  He threw it all the way down here.

Said he wouldn't need it anymore.  Said it made him weak.

passages.title: Return to the Surface
passages.text:
You should leave now. You'll find a portal behind me. It'll take you to the surface.

We'll meet again. He'll be looking for you.

It's only a matter of time until he finds you.

passages.title: Return to the Surface
passages.text:
It's you, <name>!  We thought you were a goner.

That explosion of yours put quite a bit of hurt on the Scourge.  Nearly took Captain's Kendall's eyebrows off in the process...

passages.title: Futility
passages.text:
Do you see now? Sending your men against the prince's armies just swells their numbers.

I don't expect you to understand... you'll probably just end up like the others. You'd best return to whoever sent you. They might be worried.

passages.title: Futility
passages.text:
Nice shooting, <name>.  The Scourge never had a chance.

Are you feeling okay?  You look like you've seen a ghost.  Not that it would be an unusual thing around these parts, now that I think about it.

passages.title: Where Dragons Fell
passages.text:
A whole brood of blue dragons fell here. And now, one by one, they're being raised by his servants.

He raised the biggest of them all himself. Bring me some bone dust from the whelps and I'll show you exactly how he did it.

passages.title: Where Dragons Fell
passages.text: Did you get the dust, <name>?

passages.title: Where Dragons Fell
passages.text: Even the mighty wyrms had to heed his call.  How is a simple mortal like you going to resist him?

passages.title: Time for Answers
passages.text:
You have a lot of questions, <name>. You're the only one who can see me because you touched something that once belonged to him... don't you remember?

You don't know what it is? Well I can't just tell you... that would make him really mad. He's not just a prince anymore... he's the king!

Meet me at the Court of Bones, north of Icecrown Citadel and you can see for yourself.

passages.title: Time for Answers
passages.text: There you are.  I started to wonder whether you'd show up.

passages.title: Knowledge is a Terrible Burden
passages.text:
Now you know what you're up against, <name>. An opponent who no longer knows pain... remorse... or humanity. An opponent who will do anything to get what he wants.

The heart was his weakness and now he knows you've found it.

If you're going to go back for it, you'd best bring help. He will not leave it unguarded again.

passages.title: Knowledge is a Terrible Burden
passages.text: Slow down, <name>.  Why don't you start again... from the beginning?

passages.title: Tirion's Help
passages.text:
It's not the first time I've heard that story about Arthas and his heart... always thought it was some made-up tale to impress the rank and file.

We must act on this information immediately. Unfortunately, we must do so in secret.

Arthas's agents are everywhere and if he finds out, our plan is dead in the water.

We need to take this to the Argent Crusade. Every single paladin in that order was hand-picked by Tirion himself. If there's anyone free of cultist infiltration, it's those guys.

passages.title: Tirion's Help
passages.text: Heavy words, <name>.  If it were somebody else saying them, I'd be likely to judge them insane.

passages.title: Xarantaur, the Witness
passages.text:
It seems we're not the only visitors to this area. A courier relayed a message from a tauren named Xarantaur, who said he was visiting a taunka village called Camp Tunka'lo. The note was somewhat cryptic, but it seems this Xarantaur has come to Storm Peaks to learn the history of a taunka legend.

Meet up with him, <name>. See if what he knows can help us in any way. From his description, Camp Tunka'lo is far to the east, beyond the Terrace of the Makers and north of Dun Niffelem.

passages.title: Xarantaur, the Witness
passages.text: So Boktar received my note? That's excellent news. I doubted the taunka longrunner who carried it would reach anyone.

passages.title: The Great Egg Hunt
passages.text:
Noblegarden, celebration of life and spring! I hope you've been enjoying the egg hunt, friend, because I could use the services of a capable individual like you. 

I'm not certain what form of magic was used in the creation of the eggs, and the druids aren't keen on explaining it to me. Perhaps you could collect some shell fragments for me during your egg collection. You can keep the contents of the eggs; all I require is a sufficient sample of the eggs themselves.

passages.title: The Great Egg Hunt
passages.text: Do you have the fragments?

passages.title: The Great Egg Hunt
passages.text: Excellent, excellent, thank you! I may need more of a sample to get truly conclusive results, but you've done well today.

passages.title: The Great Egg Hunt
passages.text:
Noblegarden, celebration of life and spring! I hope you've been enjoying the egg hunt, friend, because I could use the services of a capable individual like you.

I'm not certain what form of magic was used in the creation of the eggs, and the druids aren't keen on explaining it to me. passages.title: Let's Get Out of Here!
passages.text:
The Light smiles upon me. I have not yet died in this living nightmare, but the Scourge will kill me and tear my body apart for use in their 'work' here if I cannot escape.

I cannot make it on my own, <class>, but with your help, I may yet live to fight the Scourge again.

Will you help me make my escape before the Scourge's butchers come to finish me off?

passages.title: Let's Get Out of Here!
passages.text: You have done well. We thought Father Kamaros lost, for certain. Your bravery will serve as an example to all those who oppose the Scourge.

passages.title: Spring Gatherers
passages.text: If you're looking for something to do, I hear there are mages in the settlements near capital cities--Razor Hill, Brill, Bloodhoof Village, and Falconwing Square--who have been recruiting egg hunters for help with some research they're doing. I don't know the particulars, but I'm sure they'd tell you.

passages.title: Spring Gatherers
passages.text: Yes! Yes, I think I have just the task for you...

passages.title: Spring Collectors
passages.text: If you're looking for something to do, I hear there are mages in the settlements near capital cities --Goldshire, Kharanos, Dolanaar, and Azure Watch--who have been recruiting egg hunters for help with some research they're doing. I don't know the particulars, but I'm sure they'd tell you.

passages.title: Spring Collectors
passages.text: Yes! Yes, I think I have just the task for you...

passages.title: Eggs for Dubra'Jin
passages.text:
How ya doin', mon? Thinkin' ya might be helpin' me out? Bah'Kini be needin' lots o' the raptor eggs to be sacrificin' to Dubra'Jin.

How ya thinkin' we not be overrun yet by the Drakkari? Dubra'Jin be lendin' us his aid!

We need ya to gather up the raptor eggs from around the trees outside here in Gundrak. Sometimes the raptors carry 'em to keep 'em warm, too.

passages.title: Eggs for Dubra'Jin
passages.text: Who woulda thought the great Dubra'Jin be wantin' so many eggs? What he gonna do with them anyway?

passages.title: Eggs for Dubra'Jin
passages.text: One, two, three,... hehe, that be a good number o' them, mon! Now we be safe for quite some time!

passages.title: Archivum Data Disc
passages.text:
This platinum disc is surprisingly symmetrical and devoid of any scratches or imperfections. Engraved along its edge, bold runes spell out the word "ARCHIVUM."

There must be a device inside Ulduar capable of reading the disc.

passages.title: Archivum Data Disc
passages.text: The console whirrs with energy as the round receptacle opens.

passages.title: Archivum Data Disc
passages.text: The platinum disc fits perfectly inside the console.  It begins to spin as its contents are scanned by white beams of light.

passages.title: Jack Me Some Lumber
passages.text:
Come closer. No, not too close. Don't want any unnecessary suspicion now, do we?

This coliseum requires more lumber than we've stockpiled and there's no way I'm going to pay to have it shipped in from Grizzly Hills. At the western end of Crystalsong Forest, by the Great Tree, grow a number of young Crystalsong oaks. They'd provide just the kind of planking we need for building and scaffolding. Take this axe, use it to fell the trees and then hew them into planks, but don't let anyone see you!

passages.title: A Chip Off the Ulduar Block
passages.text:
Getting stone for this job has been a nightmare, I tell ya! There are tons of stone available from ruins in safe places, but those holier-than-thou paladins won't go for it. Something about 'priceless artifacts.'

Anyway, whining about that isn't going to get this place built. There are tons of crumbling titan ruins in the Foot Steppes and at the Inventor's Library in Storm Peaks. Take my, uh, 'chisel' with you and see if you can break those huge blocks into useful pieces.

passages.title: A Champion Rises
passages.text:
Congratulations, <name>. You have mastered many kinds of combat and overcome all the challenges you've faced. There can be no doubt that you are ready to compete with the best warriors who have gathered at the tournament, against the champions of the capital cities.

Justicar Mariel Trueheart has asked to speak with you, <name>, and to formally enter you in the champions' grand melee.

passages.title: A Champion Rises
passages.text:
I welcome you as a champion of the tournament, <name>. As a champion, you will be able to compete for the grand championship of the tournament. You may also choose to become a valiant with another Alliance city's delegation and in time, a champion for that city as well.

All champions must have the assistance of a squire, <name>, and you are no exception. Allow me to appoint one of ours to accompany you in battle. He will proudly carry the banner of any city that has named you a champion.

passages.title: Valiant Of Ironforge
passages.text:
Welcome, champion. Word of your combat prowess has already reached my ears. Do you seek to join Ironforge's tournament delegation?

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of Ironforge, your squire will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Ironforge
passages.text: We are proud that you have decided to join us and I know you will shine on the field.

passages.title: Valiant Of The Exodar
passages.text:
Welcome, champion. Word of your deeds has already reached my ears. Do you wish to join the Exodar's tournament delegation?

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of the Exodar, your squire will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of The Exodar
passages.text: It's good to have you on our team, <name>. We will all benefit from training with you.

passages.title: Valiant Of Darnassus
passages.text:
Welcome, champion. I have heard of your accomplishments and we would be honored if you would join the delegation from Darnassus.

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of Darnassus, your squire will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Darnassus
passages.text: The warriors of Darnassus are honored to fight and train beside you.

passages.title: Valiant Of Sen'jin
passages.text:
Greetings, champion. If you are willing, I would welcome you into Sen'jin's tournament delegation.

You will train and rise through the ranks as you have before, but when you are named a champion of Sen'jin, your gruntling will have the option of carrying our banner into battle.

passages.title: Valiant Of Sen'jin
passages.text: I am glad that you have decided to join us and look forward to seeing you in action.

You have earned my respect and the respect of your peers. You defeated all who challenged you and mastered the ways of tournament combat. I have no doubt that you are ready to face down the champions of other cities for the glory of Orgrimmar!
