passages.title: Travel to Moa'ki Harbor
passages.text:
What's that you say, <race>? Anuniaq sent you?

Good, good... there's much to do. We can use all of the help that we can get!

passages.title: Gaining an Audience
passages.text:
<name>, you must travel as swiftly as you can to Wyrmrest Temple and present this letter to the steward, Tariolstrasz.

The temple sits in the center of the Dragonblight. Follow the road east until it ends, and then cross The Dragon Wastes to get to it.

I'm sure that when the steward reads your introduction, he'll see to it that you gain an audience with Queen Alexstrasza. We can only hope that we're not too late.

Thank you for all that you have done on our behalf. Safe journeys!

passages.title: Gaining an Audience
passages.text: Yes, what can I do for you, <race>?

passages.title: Gaining an Audience
passages.text:
A letter of introduction to meet with the queen? Let me see that.

Whatever your business is, I hope that it's important.  The skies are full of attacking blues today!

passages.title: Drak'aguul's Mallet
passages.text:
Corruption....

Even before you delivered these jars, Kraz could sense it. This corruption fills the ancient Drakkari spirits with great angst and prevents them from entering the rest they seek.

Kraz will not lie, <class>. Cleansing this place will require great sacrifice, but we shall speak of that at another time.

There is one among the living here who holds the key to its cleansing. Seek out Drak'aguul and return to Kraz with the mallet he carries.

passages.title: Drak'aguul's Mallet
passages.text: You find the mallet, <name>?

passages.title: Drak'aguul's Mallet
passages.text: You have done well thus far, <name>, but now comes the true test.

passages.title: See You on the Other Side
passages.text:
These Drakkari have met you with nothing but savage hostility. You owe them nothing. Few indeed would carry out the task that Kraz asks of you today.

To cleanse this place and send the spirits to their eternal rest, you must join them in death.

There is one inside the crypt who awaits you - on the other side. He holds the knowledge we seek, <name>.

Use the mallet on the gongs. The spirit of he who corrupts this place will surely deliver you to the spirit world.

Kraz awaits your return.

passages.title: See You on the Other Side
passages.text: Your coming has been foretold, friend. It was good of you to come.

passages.title: Gaining an Audience
passages.text:
<name>, you must travel as swiftly as you can to Wyrmrest Temple and present this letter to the steward, Tariolstrasz.

The temple sits in the center of the Dragonblight. Follow the road east until it ends, and then cross The Dragon Wastes to get to it.

I'm sure that when the steward reads your introduction, he'll see to it that you gain an audience with Queen Alexstrasza. We can only hope that we're not too late.

Thank you for all that you have done on our behalf. Safe journeys!

passages.title: Gaining an Audience
passages.text: Yes, what can I do for you, <race>?

passages.title: Gaining an Audience
passages.text:
A letter of introduction to meet with the queen? Let me see that.

Whatever your business is, I hope that it's important.  The skies are full of attacking blues today!

passages.title: Informing the Queen
passages.text:
<The dragon steward pulls your letter of introduction out of his sleeve.>

Yes... yes, I think that you are ready to see the queen now.

When you are ready, speak to me again and I will see to it that one of these drakes delivers you safely to the top of the temple. You will need to present your letter in person to Queen Alexstrasza.

passages.title: Informing the Queen
passages.text: It is good to finally meet you in person, <name>. I have known you since before you were born.

passages.title: Informing the Queen
passages.text:
You are very courageous to bring us this information. I was beginning to wonder why the blue dragonflight had so boldly initiated an attack upon the temple itself. Now we know that they are using enormous amounts of the very magic they view as such a threat to Azeroth.

<The queen shakes her head in seeming resignation.>

Hypocritical, but so be it. If Malygos will not come to his senses, we have no choice but to take action in response to their assault.

passages.title: Informing the Queen
passages.text:
<The dragon steward pulls your letter of introduction out of his sleeve.>

Yes... yes, I think that you are ready to see the queen now.

When you are ready, speak to me again and I will see to it that one of these drakes delivers you safely to the top of the temple. You will need to present your letter in person to Queen Alexstrasza.

passages.title: Informing the Queen
passages.text: It is good to finally meet you in person, <name>. I have known you since before you were born.

passages.title: Informing the Queen
passages.text:
You are very courageous to bring us this information. I was beginning to wonder why the blue dragonflight had so boldly initiated an attack upon the temple itself. Now we know that they are using enormous amounts of the very magic they view as such a threat to Azeroth.

<The queen shakes her head in seeming resignation.>

Hypocritical, but so be it. If Malygos will not come to his senses, we have no choice but to take action in response to their assault.

passages.title: In Service of Blood
passages.text:
The blood of innocents was once used to sate the thirst of the blade. Alas, such options are no longer available to me.

<Koltira pauses to think.>

We must improvise. South of here, upon the high bluffs, is the tuskarr village of Indu'le. Having been recently overrun by the Blue Dragonflight's chaotic magic, the resident tuskarr of Indu'le have gone mad.

Take this blood gem and use it on a deranged villager. If I cannot take the blood of innocents, I shall have the blood of the meek!

passages.title: In Service of Blood
passages.text: Bring the blood of the meek to me.

passages.title: In Service of Blood
passages.text: A simple task for a simpleton. You have performed within my expectations.

passages.title: In Service of the Unholy
passages.text:
The power of the unholy is coveted among my kind. It makes up the very fiber of our existence, granting death to those that dare make a mockery of it! Thankfully there is a font from which I may draw from in my time of need.

Take this unholy gem and make your way to the Ruby Dragonshrine, east of here. It is there that you will find Duke Vallenhal, death knight of Arthas. Weaken his resolve in battle and unleash the power of the gem upon him. It will finish him off and steal his unholy energy!

passages.title: In Service of the Unholy
passages.text: Fill the gem with the power of the unholy!

passages.title: In Service of the Unholy
passages.text:
<Koltira's eyes widen.>

Impressive. You bested a deathknight of Arthas... Clearly you were not alone... but still...

passages.title: In Service of Frost
passages.text:
The biting cold protects the death knight while repelling his enemies. He that commands the power of frost can incite chaos and destruction!

Take this frost gem and travel far across the open tundra of the Dragonblight until you come upon the Mirror of Dawn, east of Wyrmrest Temple. It is there that you are to battle the legions of ice revenants that dwell upon the lakes surface and take from them the essence of frost. Utilize the power of the gem when they are weak, <name>!

passages.title: In Service of Frost
passages.text: We are all in service of frost here in Northrend.

passages.title: In Service of Frost
passages.text: I can already feel the cold coursing through me, <name>.

passages.title: We Have the Power
passages.text:
We're almost there, but the war golem won't run without power cells. From the information I was able to collect in Dun Argol before we were discovered, both Rune-Smith Durar and Rune-Smith Kathorn each create one power cell.

We'll need one power cell from each of the rune-smiths before our golem will work.

You should be able to find each rune-smith in his workshop on the central level of Dun Argol.

passages.title: We Have the Power
passages.text: Well, did you get those power cells?

passages.title: We Have the Power
passages.text:
<Raegar takes the batteries from you.>

Excellent! We should be all ready to go.

passages.title: The Power to Destroy
passages.text:
While you have done much for me, one task remains.

Beside the world you know exists another world. It is from that world, the world of shadows, that my tormentors assault me. While I am powerless to face my own demons, you could end their reign of terror. You have the strength, I have seen it with my own eyes.

Enter the world of shadows and face the demons that torment me!

Do this and I will translate the tome, as promised.

passages.title: The Power to Destroy
passages.text: The power I hold comes at a great cost, <name>. Many knights, light and dark alike, lost their lives in the final battle at Light's Hope. The prospect of the future looks grim, but at least now I know what I face. The Lich King will never release his grasp and for that alone he must die!

passages.title: Sasha's Hunt
passages.text:
This thing... this curse... that's affecting Silverbrook and Solstice Village... it makes beasts out of people.

My father tried to warn them, but they all listened to the wolfcult instead.

They're too far gone now, it's time to put them down... for their own sake.

passages.title: Sasha's Hunt
passages.text: Have you taken care of the hunters in the village yet, <name>?

passages.title: Sasha's Hunt
passages.text: Killing these monsters won't bring my father back... but that's not the point now, is it?

passages.title: "Let the Fires Come!"
passages.text:
You must help us! The Headless Horseman will attack the village at any moment! Fires will be everywhere! The children aren't safe!

Please, <name>, will you face the fires of the Headless Horseman? When he comes, you must join the fire brigade. Grab a bucket and toss it on the fires, or pass it to a friend who's closer to the blaze. If you put out all the fires then we may yet be saved!

passages.title: "Let the Fires Come!"
passages.text: Oh, thank you!  May the Light bless your good works, kind sir.  The shadow of the Dark Horseman yet looms, but at least, for now, the village is safe from his flames.

passages.title: The Translated Tome
passages.text:
Here it is, <name>. I have translated everything printed upon the pages of the tome. Inside it you will find a list of the names of Cult of the Damned members spanning the entire continent.

Their network of spies and operatives is impressive, to say the least.

Farewell, friend. May the book serve you and your people well.

passages.title: The Translated Tome
passages.text: It's about time! Where have you been?

passages.title: The Translated Tome
passages.text:
<Gort takes the tome from you and begins reading.>

WHAT! This can't be right. I've known some of these orcs for years!

Leave me, <name>. I have much work to do and many traitors to execute.

Take one of these items for your trouble. You've done a great service for the Horde this day.

passages.title: Chill Out, Mon
passages.text:
It be as the prophecies said, mon. A <race> <class> be comin' to set our spirits to rest. We been waitin' for a long time now!

The Drakkari have become a lost people, fierce and savage.

But here we suffer by no fault of our own, mon. This place need cleansin' and only the living can do it.

Speak to me when ya be ready to rejoin your body. Then take the snow from the chest near me here and put my bruddas to sleep.

Take their remnants to your spirit guide. He be knowin' what to do next.

passages.title: Chill Out, Mon
passages.text: Have you completed your task in the crypt, <class>?

passages.title: Chill Out, Mon
passages.text:
You have done well.

Please, sit and listen. There are many things we must discuss.

passages.title: ... Or Maybe We Don't
passages.text:
You'd think the guys making the power cells would've thought to power them up, but no, they've got to make it difficult for us.

Fine, we'll charge those cells the hard way. There's enough power in them to run the golem for a short time, but don't expect it to be any good in combat.

You see the lightning sentries that the irons have posted around the perimeter of Dun Argol? Bring the golem with you, take it close to them, and use the golem to absorb the power as the sentries die.

passages.title: ... Or Maybe We Don't
passages.text: Finally, it's ready. I only hope it holds together long enough to get the job done. If we don't take out the thane leading Dun Argol, Captain Gryan'll be in for a nasty surprise.

passages.title: "Let the Fires Come!"
passages.text:
The Headless Horseman will attack the village at any moment! Fires will be everywhere!

<name>, will you face the fires of the Headless Horseman? When he comes, you must join the fire brigade. Grab a bucket and toss it on the fires, or pass it to a friend who's closer to the blaze. If you put out all the fires then we may yet be saved!

passages.title: "Let the Fires Come!"
passages.text:
The fires are out!  You and your fire brigade were victorious!  Hah!

The Headless Horseman's attack has failed, but until he and his head are destroyed together, he will return.

Until then, however, let's take comfort in the safety you brought our children.  I am honored to have watched your brave work today.

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text:
Ugh! One of those little snobold runts trashed our camp while we were busy with that last dragon. They've been plaguing us whenever we turn our backs... I've had enough!

To the south you'll find the snobolds hiding under the skirts of some of the local magnataur. Go slaughter them.

If the magnataur interfere on behalf of their slaves, kill them as well.

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text: Good riddance.

passages.title: Canyon Chase
passages.text: I can't believe this! Another band of those vermin just tried to take off with more of our supplies. They're scurrying off towards that north canyon, get after them and deal with whoever they're going to!

passages.title: Canyon Chase
passages.text: Chilltusk, eh?  I've heard his name before.  That's some good work, <class>.  Hopefully we can turn our attention back to the dragon menace now.

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text:
Oi, mon! One of dose little snobold runts trashed our camp during da last dragon attack. Dey've been houndin us wheneva we turn our backs and I've had enough. 

To da east you'll find da snobolds hiding under da skirts of some of da local magnataur. Go slaughter dem. If da magnataur interfere on behalf of deir slaves, kill dem as well.

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text: Did ya finish off dose pests?

passages.title: Pest Control
passages.text: Good riddance, mon.

passages.title: Canyon Chase
passages.text: I can't believe dis! Another band of dose vermin just tried ta take off with more of our supplies. Dey're scurrying down da canyon now, get after dem and deal with whoever dey're going to!

passages.title: Canyon Chase
passages.text: Icefist, eh?  I've heard his name before.  Dat's some good work, mon.  Hopefully we Darkspear can turn our attention back to dat dragon menace now.

passages.title: Disturbing Implications
passages.text:
The underside of the horn boasts an emblazoned seal with a hammer and a lightning bolt. Something about the horn seems extremely out of place on a Magnataur.

Take the horn south down the Path of the Titans to Wyrmrest and seek out someone who might be interested in these threatening implications.

passages.title: Disturbing Implications
passages.text: Yes, <race>?

passages.title: Disturbing Implications
passages.text: It is indeed strange for any magnataur to carry an item such as this... and very concerning. I am glad that you have shown this to me.

passages.title: Disturbing Implications
passages.text:
The underside of the horn boasts an emblazoned seal with a hammer and a lightning bolt. Something about the horn seems extremely out of place on a Magnataur. 

Take the horn east across the Dragon Wastes to Wyrmrest and seek out someone who might be interested in these threatening implications.

passages.title: Disturbing Implications
passages.text: Yes, <race>?

passages.title: Disturbing Implications
passages.text: It is indeed strange for any magnataur to carry an item such as this... and very concerning. I am glad that you have shown this to me.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
Such a strange seal to see among magnataur... it suggests an unusual amount of organization.

Magnataur rarely put aside their aggressive natures to cooperate with each other. I suspect they have their eyes set on raiding a large settlement.

I very much doubt that this horn is unique, I need you to prove me wrong. In the canyon northwest of the Azure Dragonshrine you will find Bonesunder. Go challenge him and bring me back any evidence you find that might confirm my concerns.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text: So it is true. They could not have chosen better timing for such an attack... between the Scourge and the blue flight, it is unlikely that anyone else has noticed yet.

passages.title: Mighty Magnataur
passages.text:
Magnataur are hideously violent creatures... this is the main reason we rarely see them come together in any real numbers without killing each other. A powerful leader has stepped up somewhere among them and we need to hunt him down if we are to stop this threat. 

I will start asking around. I need you to disrupt them as much as possible in the meantime.

East of here there are 3 torches erected. Near them, there are 3 dominant Magnataur - put them down to buy us some time to hunt down this leader.

passages.title: Mighty Magnataur
passages.text: Excellent work. No one could tell me who this leader might be, but I was able to uncover the name of someone who will have our answer.

passages.title: Reclusive Runemaster
passages.text:
Dregmar Runebrand is a magnataur runemaster... a rare breed. He's generally solitary, but has been known to associate with the more powerful and influential magnataur in Dragonblight for quite some time. He will know who this new leader is. 

It is unlikely we will gain any aid with the increasing concerns with the Scourge and the blue flight, so I need you to procure the information from Dregmar by any means necessary.

I was told he can be found amongst the cliffs overlooking the Mirror of the Dawn.

passages.title: Reclusive Runemaster
passages.text: Grom'thar the Thunderbringer. Good. Let's end any threat these magnataur might pose here and now.

passages.title: Wanton Warlord
passages.text:
There's no reason to suspect Dregmar's words are anything but true. Whether Grom'thar defeats you or is defeated by you, he can wash his hands of this.

Follow his instructions... take the horn that you brought me earlier, travel to the ring of torches south of the Azure Dragonshrine, and blow it to announce your challenge.

When Grom'thar the Thunderbringer arrives, kill him and bring me his head.

passages.title: Wanton Warlord
passages.text: Did you end this threat for good?

passages.title: Wanton Warlord
passages.text:
You are formidable indeed.

With Grom'thar the Thunderbringer gone, we can leave the remaining Magnataur to fight among themselves and turn our attentions back towards more prominent threats.

Impressive work, <class>.

passages.title: Jin'arrak's End
passages.text:
It is good to see you back among the living. Many who travel the path of the dead do not return to speak of it.

While you were away, a vision appeared to Kraz revealing what remains to be done.

A sacred offering lies somewhere inside the crypt. Take this spirit dust fashioned from the remnants you collected and use it on the offering.

The infused offering will bring an end to the corrupted warlord and will release the many tormented souls.

May the spirits guide your actions, <name>.

passages.title: Jin'arrak's End
passages.text:
It is done.

Your selflessness has brought eternal peace to many souls, ending eons of misery.

May this act lighten your own soul and lessen your burdens, for I see that there are yet many perils you must face.

Farewell, <name>.

passages.title: The Iron Thane and His Anvil
passages.text:
Now that you've charged up your war golem, we're going to put all that energy to good use. Activate the golem inside Dun Argol to take control of it.

Our information about Dun Argol's leader, Iron Thane Furyhammer, suggests his bodyguard protects him from all harm.

That bodyguard is the construct he travels with, called The Anvil. Disable the construct, and his protection will disappear.

The thane stays in the building at the top of Dun Argol and supervises production from the bottom level.

passages.title: The Iron Thane and His Anvil
passages.text:
It worked?

<Raegar clears his throat.>

I mean... of course it worked! This is incredible!

Years from now, Explorers' League initiates will hear the story of how Raegar Breakbrow, <name>, and some hunk o' junk golem defeated the thane of Dun Argol!

passages.title: Blackout
passages.text:
The large hall at the top of Dun Argol houses the power source for the entire area. If you can destroy the power core, it will cripple Dun Argol for some time.

No power means no golems, no sentries, and no more lightning armaments.

When we were sent up here, they told us these explosives were for excavation, but thanks to Iron Thane Furyhammer, the research has been scrapped. We may as well get some use out of them, though. They're the only thing we have on hand capable of destroying the power core.

passages.title: Blackout
passages.text:
<Raegar nods approvingly.>

I can't stand to see explosives go to waste and it'll set our enemies back for sure.

passages.title: Souls at Unrest
passages.text:
<Petrov looks deeply disturbed, breathing heavily and shifting his gaze nervously around the mine.>

My comrades... we must put their souls to rest! I kill them and kill them but.. they just come back!

I've had an idea for a while but I just don't have the heart to do it myself.

Maybe you can do this for me? Take this lantern and use its oil to burn their remains so they never get up again.

I'll answer your questions later. Help my friends first!

passages.title: Souls at Unrest
passages.text: Have you put my friends to rest yet, <name>?

passages.title: Souls at Unrest
passages.text: Rest in peace friends!  Do not worry -- I will tell everyone that we never gave up!

passages.title: Hour of the Worg
passages.text:
It is time, then, <name>. Arugal must be defeated.

Get a couple of people you can trust and head for Bloodmoon Isle. It's just off the coast, east of here.

We'll hit them fast. Take out Arugal's lieutenants -- I'll catch up with you when it's time to take out the monster himself.

passages.title: Hour of the Worg
passages.text:
We got him good, <name>.  But not good enough.

One thing's for sure... we won't be seeing him around these parts any longer.

passages.title: An Intriguing Plan
passages.text:
Prospector Rokar has decided to help us. He's concocted a plan to use the iron dwarves' strength against them.

I must admit, our new 'friend' is more insightful than I'd given him credit for. He's correct in that our numbers are too few for a direct attack.

Travel to Dun Argol, in the snowy regions to the southeast, and capture all the parts of their war golem blueprints from the iron rune-smiths there. Bring the assembled blueprint to Rokar and we'll see if his plan has any merit.

passages.title: An Intriguing Plan
passages.text: Do... do you have those blueprints I asked for?

passages.title: An Intriguing Plan
passages.text:
So Tormak's going to go ahead with the plan? I suppose he wouldn't have sent you if he didn't.

Oh, bother... Now how am I going to figure out how to put this together under all this pressure?

passages.title: The Liquid Fire of Elune
passages.text:
<race> will you assist me?

The Scourge have moved into Icemist to the north. Wherever they go, they spread their taint, and the creatures of the land suffer.

Take this vial, which is filled with the liquid fire of Elune from the moonwell. Please, use the liquid to cleanse the corpses of the blighted wildlife that you find.

passages.title: The Liquid Fire of Elune
passages.text: We have done what we can for the creatures of the land. Now we must take direct action against those that have caused this!

passages.title: Kill the Cultists
passages.text:
The Anub'ar cultists are indirectly responsible for the plaguing of the beasts, and we must put an end to it!

The fumes that emit from the cultists' suits seep into everything they come near, poisoning and corrupting their surroundings.

You must go north to Icemist Village and slay them. Bring back any of their suits that survive your assault and I will see to it that they are properly disposed of.

passages.title: Kill the Cultists
passages.text: The cultists are a blight upon creation!

passages.title: Kill the Cultists
passages.text:
Well done.

I will dispose of these filthy garments by cleansing them in the moonwell and destroying them through the power of the goddess!

passages.title: The Favor of Zangus
passages.text:
An inscription on the back of the favor reads,

"To my favorite pupil,

If you continue to show promise, I will teach you wonders beyond your imaginings.

If you do not, I will have you destroyed!

As ever,

High Cultist Zangus"

No doubt the warden at Stars' Rest will want to see this.

passages.title: The Favor of Zangus
passages.text:
I sense something foul is near.

It is upon your person! What is it, <name>?

passages.title: The Favor of Zangus
passages.text:
So, the leader of the cultists has revealed himself. We have a name.

Vanity and pride will be his downfall!

passages.title: The High Cultist
passages.text:
I have dreamed of Zangus before but without the context that you have discovered, I knew not what it meant. You have brought clarity to the vision that the goddess has bestowed upon me, and now I know that he can be found within the Pit of Narjun to the north.

You know your target, <name>. If there's to be an end to the suffering of the land, the high cultist must die!

passages.title: The High Cultist
passages.text:
With the high cultist destroyed, the rest of his forces can be mopped up and the land and its creatures will recover.

Thank you, <name>. May the goddess illuminate your path.

passages.title: Blackriver Brawl
passages.text:
The Venture Company abandoned operations shortly after we showed up. Clearly they were afraid of what we were going to do to their greedy little hides.

With them gone, their logging camps are up for grabs. Our war machine is a hungry beast... without renewing our supplies we won't make it to Icecrown.

Unfortunately the Alliance seems to have the same idea and we must make sure we're the ones that prevail. Head into the logging camp and help us fight the Alliance scum.

passages.title: Blackriver Brawl
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  Our control over the logging camp might not be complete yet, but thanks to you we're one step closer to smashing these Alliance worms.

passages.title: Of Traitors and Treason
passages.text:
The list I hold must be delivered to High Commander Halford Wyrmbane. He commands the 7th Legion, stationed at Wintergarde Keep on the eastern borders of Dragonblight.

If any of the traitors on this list are stationed at Wintergarde... it could be catastrophic.

Hurry, <name>. Show the document to Palena Silvercloud here at Stars' Rest and explain the nature of your mission. She will put you on her fastest hippogryph to Wintergarde!

passages.title: Of Traitors and Treason
passages.text: Hello, <race>.

passages.title: Of Traitors and Treason
passages.text:
<Palena reads the note.>

You will take my fastest hippogryph, <race>! This information must be delivered to High Commander Wyrmbane at once!

passages.title: Attunement to Dalaran
passages.text:
Welcome, mage.

By now you must be wondering where Dalaran is and how to get there. I will help you.

But before I can teach you how to teleport to our great city, you must attune yourself to the ley lines of Northrend. Otherwise, you risk destroying yourself in the process.

Take this attunement crystal and use it in the pit under the surge needle at the Moonrest Gardens to the west. Then you will be ready to learn the spell.

passages.title: Attunement to Dalaran
passages.text: Very well. If you are ready, then so am I.

passages.title: Attunement to Dalaran
passages.text:
Hello, mage.

By now you must be wondering where Dalaran is and how to get there. I can help you with this if you can survive a simple test.

Before I teach you how to teleport to our great city, you must attune yourself to the ley lines of Northrend. Otherwise, you will destroy yourself in the process!

Take this attunement crystal and use it in the pit under the surge needle at the Moonrest Gardens to the southwest. Then you will be ready to learn what I have to teach.

passages.title: Attunement to Dalaran
passages.text: Very well. If you think you are ready, then let's not waste anymore of my time.

passages.title: High Commander Halford Wyrmbane
passages.text:
<Palena hands the missive back to you.>

Snowstorm will take you to Wintergarde, <name>. I guarantee you that it will be the fastest flight you've ever taken. Go now!

passages.title: High Commander Halford Wyrmbane
passages.text: What have you got there, soldier?

passages.title: High Commander Halford Wyrmbane
passages.text:
<The High Commander reads the missive and then crumples it up.>

Do you know where the people on this list are now? Take a look outside, near the front gate. They're the ones hanging from the arches.

Ghoul bait...

passages.title: Gray Worg Hides
passages.text:
Let me tell you something, mon. When you get put in charge of outfittin' the armies of the Horde, you go through a lot of hides!

Conqueror Krenna, the she-wolf runnin' this place, she gave me a tight deadline. If I don't outfit her whole regiment by week's end she's gonna have me wrestling bears in the pit.

Help me out and I'll pay you top price. I'll be needin' hides from graymist hunters.

You'll find them all around in pockets to the north, hunting stag. Remember, mon. Top price!

passages.title: Gray Worg Hides
passages.text: You get dose hides, mon?

passages.title: Gray Worg Hides
passages.text: You're a life saver, brother.  If you're interested in more work, there's more where that came from.

passages.title: Jun'ik's Coverup
passages.text:
Ah, we have a small problem. Grizzly hides... they be brown, mon!

Think... think!

I got it, mon! Is like this: gray is black an' white all mixed up. You get me some coal an' some flour, I'll grind it all up and dust the hides with it. No one will know the better!

Blacksmiths sell coal for smeltin' an' you can get flour from the provisioner.

passages.title: Jun'ik's Coverup
passages.text: You get the stuff, mon?

passages.title: Jun'ik's Coverup
passages.text: Hope for the best, mon.

passages.title: The Captive Prospectors
passages.text:
Raegar sent a team of prospectors into Dun Argol to search for artifacts and information about the history of the settlement. Raegar's team never expected Dun Argol to be this heavily populated.

They're being held captive while the iron dwarves prepare for war. We haven't the men to charge in after them, and Raegar's too busy fantasizing about defeating the irons to be of much help.

It falls to you, <name>. Any of the irons or their servants could be carrying the keys to the cages holding our men.

passages.title: The Captive Prospectors
passages.text: Did you locate the missing prospectors?

passages.title: The Captive Prospectors
passages.text:
<Mountaineer Kilian listens as you relate what the captive prospectors told you.>

They mentioned Loken and a war against stone giants? You're certain?

So Raegar's instincts were right. We have to find a way to get in there and learn more about their plans.

passages.title: Give it a Name
passages.text:
My, my, how long has it been? How long have we been working on this damned plague? Finally, after an eternity of failure, we are blessed with perfection. This... It doesn't even have a proper name yet! This blight... That's it, BLIGHT! This blight will tear down the very fabric of life!

<Harris hands you a vial.>

Now, find the bat handler, Tobias, and show him the specimen. He'll get you on your way to Venomspite.

passages.title: Give it a Name
passages.text: Highly lethal poisonous gas delivery to Venomspite? Step right up!

passages.title: Give it a Name
passages.text: Uh, yea, you can go ahead and hold on to that vial, friend. I trust you.

passages.title: To Venomspite!
passages.text:
I got a special bat all lined up for you, buddy. Fastest and smoothest ride I've got. He'll take you right to Venomspite - in style.

Just hand that vial over to Chief Plaguebringer Middleton once you land.

passages.title: To Venomspite!
passages.text: You are the delivery boy?

passages.title: To Venomspite!
passages.text: Oh joyous day! And look, just beyond the mountain to the northeast creeps a whole field of Scourge for us to obliterate!

passages.title: Cultivating an Image
passages.text:
Now that we've got the uniform, we've got to get enough information to complete your camouflage.

Raegar brought along this camera to document the team's finds, but I have a different use in mind. I want you to take it with you to Dun Argol and use it to capture the images of iron dwarves.

Of course, your models aren't going to be a cooperative lot, so you may have to, err... subdue them first. Bring back the camera and the images when you're done.

passages.title: Cultivating an Image
passages.text: Did you get those snapshots?

passages.title: Cultivating an Image
passages.text: Good, these should do. Now, to create a kit to pass you off as a convincing iron dwarf.

passages.title: Put on Your Best Face for Loken
passages.text:
Using the images you've captured, I've created everything you need for your overseer disguise kit. You'll make a fine iron dwarf, if I do say so myself.

Take the kit with you to Dun Argol, use it to disguise yourself, then go to the easternmost building on the broad middle tier of the city.

There, you should see a pedestal where the thane and overseers receive their orders from this Loken. Activate it while disguised and learn all you can from the communication.

passages.title: Put on Your Best Face for Loken
passages.text: Did the disguise work?

passages.title: Put on Your Best Face for Loken
passages.text: Could it be that Loken isn't really exaggerating? The titans' stone and iron sons fighting against each other for control of the ancient city of Ulduar. This is madness, <name> and it could destroy our only chance to learn the true history of dwarvenkind!

passages.title: The Forsaken Blight and You: How Not to Die
passages.text:
The details behind the functionality of the blight are hardly important. All you need to know is that it does the job it was designed to do. I have managed to synthesize a strain of the blight that is inert.

<Middleton uncorks a vial and inhales.>

See, my body is still, mostly, intact. Now mix this with a reactive agent and we'd all be turned to shapeless piles of goo.

On the beach south of here you will find pathetic specters of Alliance soldiers past. Slay them and bring me ectoplasmic residue.

passages.title: The Forsaken Blight and You: How Not to Die
passages.text: The residue will be used as the reactive agent to activate the blight!

passages.title: The Forsaken Blight and You: How Not to Die
passages.text:
This will do nicely, <name>. Did those pathetic whelps put up a fight or did they just shower you with ghostly tears of sorrow?

Ah, they get so emotional...

passages.title: Imbeciles Abound!
passages.text:
The shipment from New Agamand was to arrive at Venomspite last week and then be delivered to me after some simple field tests. It is a Horde imperative - the last piece of the "victory puzzle."

<Sintar sighs.>

It is quite disheartening to know that you are surrounded by imbeciles and incompetent boobs!

You must travel to Venomspite, near the eastern border of Dragonblight. Find that buffoon, Middleton, and let him know that I am waiting on the package.

passages.title: Imbeciles Abound!
passages.text: We ran into a little - MINOR - problem. Everyone that tried handling the blight vaporized. We're working on adjusting the formula a tad so it doesn't instantly kill you for looking at it sideways. The good news is that I think I've almost got it!

passages.title: Chug and Chuck!
passages.text:
Hey, you look like you've got a good arm!

We like to keep things lively around camp, and nothing says fun like a good old-fashioned mug toss!

Think you've got the aim to hit S.T.O.U.T.? Just grab a sampler, take a sip, and see if you can land a hit. It's trickier than it looks, but that's half the fun. Step right up and give it a shot!

passages.title: Chug and Chuck!
passages.text: Chug from the mug, then chuck the mug at S.T.O.U.T. I think he can withstand the pounding. I wouldn't have stol.. er... built him if he couldn't!

passages.title: Chug and Chuck!
passages.text:
Wow...  S.T.O.U.T. didn't break... Hmm... Who would have guessed?

I mean, hey, you did it!  Your aim is true, or at least true enough to help guard the camp.  I think you're ready now to take on the Dark Irons if they show up again.

passages.title: We Have the Power
passages.text:
Well, we've got the shell of a golem, but that's not good enough for Tormak. He doesn't realize that these things don't just come together and miraculously start working! We're going to need power cells to animate it.

When I was in Dun Argol, I noticed that Rune-Smith Durar and Rune-Smith Kathorn were the ones who manufactured the cells. We'll need one from each to power our golem.

You should be able to find each rune-smith in his workshop on the central level of Dun Argol.

passages.title: We Have the Power
passages.text: Do you have those power cells?

passages.title: We Have the Power
passages.text:
<Rokar takes the batteries from you.>

These are low, but they'll be enough to start up the golem. He's nowhere near ready for battle, though.

passages.title: ... Or Maybe We Don't
passages.text:
The golem's cells have just enough power to run it at the lowest levels, but it can't power any of its combat systems.

The good news is that the perimeter of Dun Argol is patrolled by lightning sentries. We should be able to use their power to charge up the golem's weapon systems.

Bring the golem with you, take it close to them, it will absorb the power as the sentries die.

passages.title: ... Or Maybe We Don't
passages.text: Did you get that golem charged? Tormak is getting impatient again...

passages.title: ... Or Maybe We Don't
passages.text:
Well, now Tormak can't complain anymore. This baby's as ready as I can make it.

After you tear your way through Dun Argol with it, that overgrown cow'll have to release me.

passages.title: Bringing Down the Iron Thane
passages.text:
Now that the golem is fully charged, it can be used against the leader at Dun Argol.

When I observed Iron Thane Furyhammer, he was always guarded by a personal golem that shielded him from all harm.

That construct, called The Anvil, can be disrupted, causing him to drop the shield. Use your golem's EMP ability to do just that. You'll be able to activate and take control of your golem inside Dun Argol.

The thane is in the main plant at the top and supervises production from the bottom level.

passages.title: Bringing Down the Iron Thane
passages.text: Please tell me it worked...

passages.title: Bringing Down the Iron Thane
passages.text:
So the prospector made good on his promises? Good. I was beginning to wonder if all of this scrounging for bits of metal and stealing building materials would amount to anything.

It's a shame he's of no further use to us.

passages.title: Emerald Dragon Tears
passages.text:
With an inert specimen of the blight compound complete and the activating agent in hand there only remains a need for a suitable shell to house the components.

Southwest of here, on the shores of central Dragonblight, is where you will find the Emerald Dragonshrine. Within the shrine you will find the hardened remnants of a green dragon's tear drop. I don't know the whole story, but apparently they cry a lot right before they die. Go figure.

Go to the Emerald Dragonshrine and gather tears.

passages.title: Emerald Dragon Tears
passages.text: Fortunate it is that we have a location nearby holding a surplus of emerald dragon tears. I would have had to send you to Feralas otherwise.

passages.title: Emerald Dragon Tears
passages.text:
I do believe that the blight is now ready for a field test. Fortuitously, the dread citadel, Naxxramas, is laying siege to Wintergarde Keep. From beneath the very earth that Wintergarde was built upon rise the living dead, eager to do the bidding of Kel'Thuzad.

The Alliance are, of course, outmanned and outgunned. The people laid to rest in the Wintergarde Mausoleum awaken, hungering for flesh!

Perhaps we shall give them a taste of the blight, yes?

passages.title: Cultivating an Image
passages.text:
Now we have to finish the job of making you as repulsive as those iron dwarves.

The best way to do that is to base your disguise on the ugly mugs of real iron dwarves.

When Tormak's hunting party discovered that wayward prospector, they took the camera he carried. Now, I suppose, we'll get the chance to use it.

Take it with you to Dun Argol, kill some iron dwarves, and record their likenesses in this device. Bring it back once you have enough examples.

passages.title: Cultivating an Image
passages.text: Did you get those snapshots?

passages.title: Cultivating an Image
passages.text: These should serve. By Garrosh, these creatures are ugly.

passages.title: Loken's Orders
passages.text:
I've created everything else you'll need for your overseer disguise kit. Try not to retch when you put it on. I took pains to make it as true to reality as possible.

Take the kit with you southeast to Dun Argol, use it to disguise yourself, then go to the easternmost building on the broad middle tier of the city.

There, you should see a pedestal where the thane and overseers receive their orders from this Loken. Activate it while disguised and learn all you can from the communication.

passages.title: Loken's Orders
passages.text:
So he means to foment civil war between the factions of the titans' creation? Why does this titan city of Ulduar mean so much to him? I suppose this is what Kurun and his giants are hoping to prevent.

Well, I doubt we're in a position to keep the giants from fighting each other, but we can find a way to use this to our advantage. I must inform our leaders at once.

passages.title: In the Name of Loken
passages.text:
The iron dwarves stand as one of the fiercest and most coordinated foes in Northrend. Wherever we have traveled, they have battled us with the name of Loken on their lips.

We must learn who this Loken is and what he seeks. The locals may be of help.

To the northeast, at the Redwood Trading Post, a human named Hugh Glass peddles his wares. Further east, at the Ruins of Tethys, you'll find a stone giant named Gavrock. Ask them about this Loken. They've got to know something of use.

passages.title: In the Name of Loken
passages.text: So he is the mastermind behind the iron dwarves? We must find out what he has been ordering the iron dwarves of Dun Argol to do.

passages.title: WANTED: The Scarlet Onslaught
passages.text:
By order of High Executor Wroth all members of the illegal organization known as the Scarlet Onslaught are to be put to death immediately.

No quarter is to be offered, and those proceeding to action upon this decree should be aware that any who are captured by the humans will be left to die, or worse!

In the High Executor's words, "Paint the snow red with their blood!"

passages.title: WANTED: The Scarlet Onslaught
passages.text:
Very well done, <race>. I trust that you were cleverly vicious in your slaying?

Let's see, how much I can offer you from the coffins... er, excuse me, coffers?

passages.title: Blighted Last Rites
passages.text:
Have you read the wanted poster? What is the high executor thinking?!

<Vicky looks around and continues in hushed tones.>

We can't very well have those Scarlet Onslaught idiots being raised by their priests, or worse, rising as the Scourge, now can we?

No, I'm in total agreement with you, we have to do something about the corpses.

I have just the thing. Take this blight that we just created and test it on the prisoner in the cage right here.

No muss, no fuss, no returning enemies.

passages.title: Blighted Last Rites
passages.text:
Did you do it?

Hey, I forgot to tell you that you probably shouldn't let any of that stuff get on you! It's nasty, and you'll never get the stains out, let alone have a hell of a time healing the bubbled-away fleshy bits.

passages.title: Blighted Last Rites
passages.text:
WHAT?! That's impossible! We've perfected the blight. It has a one-hundred percent lethality.

<The apothecary wrings her hands, concern crossing her unliving visage. Clearly frustrated, she continues in an angry tone.>

This is just really odd. Hand me that flask, <class>. I'm not going to be known as the apothecary that ruined everything!

passages.title: Vordrassil's Fall
passages.text:
Long ago, powerful druids planted a tree to the northeast of here.

It was called Vordrassil and it was to be a world tree. It is not known why, but after the tree was fully grown, the druids decided it needed to be destroyed.

Ever since we arrived here, the earth has spoken to me, <name>. Its cries of pain come from the places where Vordrassil's remains fell on the ground.

Corrupting ooze roams those places. Bring me samples of it so we may begin to heal the land.

passages.title: Vordrassil's Fall
passages.text: Have you obtained the samples, <name>?

passages.title: Vordrassil's Fall
passages.text:
This slime is foul with a darkness far more ancient than their worldly forms would indicate.  The land itself has a memory of this evil for as long as it has existed.

We must find out more, <name>.

passages.title: Materiel Plunder
passages.text:
Ah good, new meat. Do you wish to prove yourself, new meat?

The Scarlet Onslaught, the most zealous and racist of the Scarlet Crusade, are in our backyard to the south. If we're going to fight them, we'll need more armor and weapons than I can make in such a short time.

Why don't we take theirs?

More to the point, why don't YOU take theirs?

passages.title: Materiel Plunder
passages.text:
I'll take what armor and weapons you can steal for me, new meat.

Though they'll be of inferior quality to what I can make here, it's better than nothing.

passages.title: Materiel Plunder
passages.text:
You do not smell so fresh now, new meat.

Very well, all of this will do. By what name might I call you, <class>?

passages.title: Let Them Not Rise!
passages.text:
I don't understand it. The blight should have worked!

No sense worrying about it now.

<The apothecary seems relieved for some reason.>

Though it doesn't work on the Onslaught for some strange reason, we still need to keep their priests from raising them.

I have another idea, one that their corpses shouldn't have any protection from.

<name>, take a container of my rats and unleash them upon any Onslaught corpses you come across at New Hearthglen. I starve the vermin, so they should be voracious!

passages.title: Let Them Not Rise!
passages.text:
Oh good! For a moment I thought I was going to have to test the rats out on someone to make sure that they weren't defective.

Progress, finally!

passages.title: Replenishing the Storehouse
passages.text:
G'day, <class>.

The good lieutenant here says that there's been a Horde raid on our storehouse that's left our food supply dangerously low.

No doubt we'll make those cretins pay, but first we need to focus our attention on restocking. My men are doing all they can, but we're going to need every able body to contribute if we're to avert a crisis.

You should have no trouble harvesting venison from the local stag in these parts. Happy hunting!

passages.title: Replenishing the Storehouse
passages.text: How goes the hunt, <race>?

passages.title: Replenishing the Storehouse
passages.text: These are some choice pieces of meat!

passages.title: The Darkness Beneath
passages.text:
Something... dark... happened to the tree Vordrassil. After the druids decided to destroy it, its hollow remains grew roots deep into the ground.

I want you to go to the three locations to the northeast where the tree's trunk shattered and go as far beneath the ground as you can.

Use this orb once you get there to get an imprint of the energy surrounding the area. This might shed some light on what happened to Vordrassil and why it failed to become a world tree.

passages.title: The Darkness Beneath
passages.text:
This orb... it has been tainted by... a purely evil force.

Whatever else I might learn from studying this energy, one thing is certain.  I must destroy this orb as soon as possible.  Its corrupting force is just too strong.

passages.title: Fresh Remounts
passages.text:
Hello. I am Hansel. Pleased to meet you, <sir/ma'am>.

The high executor came to me and said, 'Hansel, I want you to get us new mounts.'

Where does he think dreadsteeds come from? The ground?

<whispering> Actually, they do if you can find a horse graveyard.

But we don't have one of those, so what we need you to do is go south to New Hearthglen, kill the knights, take their riding crops, and steal their warhorses.

Ride the horse back to me here and hand over the reins, if you would.

passages.title: Fresh Remounts
passages.text: I'm sure glad that you came around. I was afraid that I was going to have to go down there and rustle them up myself.

passages.title: Fresh Remounts
passages.text:
Ah, nothing makes me happier than a job well done.

You've done Venomspite a great service in acquiring these horses, <class>.

passages.title: Them or Us!
passages.text:
As if we didn't have enough to concern ourselves with....

With the present food crisis, we find ourselves competing for food with the local worgs. The situation is becoming more dire, and I fear that if we don't address the issue immediately we'll soon find ourselves with nothing to hunt.

Scour the forest, <race>. Kill any graymist you find. Recent reports have sighted a concentration of them on the other side of the river west of here.

passages.title: Them or Us!
passages.text:
Good work, <class>.

This should help ensure that the wildlife in these parts ends up where it should - roasting over our fires.

passages.title: Take Their Rear!
passages.text:
We've all been working hard and it's beginning to pay off, but we're still far from our goal. We need much more meat than we have and it's growing clear that the local stag population won't be enough by itself.

I'm afraid we need you to turn your attention to more dangerous prey - the grizzlies that give this region its name. They're plentiful, and they're well fed from the abundant fish that swim in these streams.

Be safe, <class>!

passages.title: Take Their Rear!
passages.text: The mighty <class> has returned!

passages.title: Take Their Rear!
passages.text:
Outstanding!

Our stores are nearly replenished now. You've done your part, <name>.

passages.title: Eagle Eyes
passages.text:
Well, <name>, we've determined how the Horde was able to locate our hidden stores of food.

It turns out that they were binding their sight to the unsuspecting eagles that soar above the trees here. Using eagle vision, they were able to effectively spy on our every action.

By order of the lieutenant, we've got to hunt down these majestic birds in order to thwart our enemy.

passages.title: Eagle Eyes
passages.text: A somber task, I know. But we can rest easier now knowing the enemy's eyes are no longer upon us.

passages.title: The Failed World Tree
passages.text:
My ancestors once planted a tree in the middle of the Grizzly Hills.

It was called Vordrassil and it was to become a world tree.

For reasons long forgotten, after the tree was fully grown, they decided it needed to be destroyed. Its giant trunk splintered at three locations in the area to the north.

Where the tree touched the ground, foul ooze began to crawl the earth. Bring me slime samples so I can begin my work and the earth can be healed.

passages.title: The Failed World Tree
passages.text: Have you gathered the samples, <name>?

passages.title: The Failed World Tree
passages.text:
The slime is not natural, <name>.  Its very nature is corrupt and... evil.

We must find out more.

passages.title: A Dark Influence
passages.text:
When the tree Vordrassil fell, its hollow remains grew roots deep into the ground.

I want you to go north of here to the three locations where the trunk shattered and go as far beneath the ground as you can. You'll find them west of Grizzlemaw.

Use this orb once you get there to get an imprint of the energy surrounding the area. If we're to heal the land, we must first find out what caused Vordrassil to fail as a world tree all those years ago.

passages.title: A Dark Influence
passages.text:
The energy in the orb is... overpowering...

A dark force has tainted the ground near Vordrassil's remains.  We will need to investigate more.

passages.title: The Forsaken Blight
passages.text:
I have prepared a package that must be delivered to Doctor Sintar Malefious at Agmar's Hammer. The contents of the package include the final blight specimen along with instructions on preparation and samples of the reactive agent.

You will find Agmar's Hammer in western Dragonblight. Just look for the black, jagged metal orc buildings - that will be Agmar's Hammer.

passages.title: The Forsaken Blight
passages.text: About bloody time!

passages.title: The Forsaken Blight
passages.text:
<Doctor Malefious looks through the contents of the package.>

Glorious! Exactly to specifications!

Here is your payment, <name>. Keep what you've seen and done to yourself. This work is all classified - information is given out on a need to know basis.

passages.title: Secrets of the Flamebinders
passages.text:
Even as we attempt to fight off the Horde, the Dragonflayer tribe musters in their village of Voldrune, near the coast to the south.

The most powerful warriors in the village are granted flame-imbued talismans that give them the ability to control powerful, savage proto-drakes. If we can gain control of one of these drakes, perhaps we can use it to neutralize the threat posed by Voldrune.

The Dragonflayer flamebinders create the talismans and imbue them with power. Kill them and take the talismans.

passages.title: Secrets of the Flamebinders
passages.text: Did you collect those talismans?

passages.title: Secrets of the Flamebinders
passages.text: With the talismans in hand, the drake will have no choice but to obey you. I can't wait to see the look on the thane's face when he realizes you've commandeered his proto-drake.

passages.title: Thinning the Ranks
passages.text:
There's a flurry of activity down in Voldrune village to the south. Thane Torvald Eriksson and his huscarls are preparing for war. With most of our men in the field dealing with the Horde's treachery, Amberpine will be vulnerable.

Travel to Voldrune, which is near the southern coast, and show those Dragonflayers we're no soft target.

Slay as many of the huscarls as you can find. Make them think twice about taking advantage of our conflict with the Horde.

passages.title: Thinning the Ranks
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Now, we must follow through and press the advantage.

passages.title: Just Passing Through
passages.text:
We must act quickly, <race>! We can't risk letting those precious seeds become fully digested. They need to come out, NOW.

Forage up some blackroot from the riverbank just west of here and I'll make you a purgative that should get things moving.

Hurry now! And remember, you brought this upon yourself....

passages.title: Just Passing Through
passages.text: Have you found the blackroot?

passages.title: Just Passing Through
passages.text:
These should do just fine...

<Anderhol deftly twists the stalks, collecting their slick fluids in a tiny vial.>

There we go, now it's time to get down to business.

passages.title: Doing Your Duty
passages.text:
Alright, <race>. Here's the juice.

It works immediately, so don't use it until you're safely inside the outhouse.

Now go get me those seeds!

passages.title: Doing Your Duty
passages.text: Got those seeds for me yet, <race>?

passages.title: Doing Your Duty
passages.text:
Well, <name>? Everything come out okay?

Hmm, looks like we caught 'em just in time....

passages.title: A Possible Link
passages.text:
Not long ago we sent an expedition to the east, where it was attacked by crazed furbolgs. One of the survivors described slaying one of them and its body expelling a dark slimy substance.

For thousands of years, the furbolgs in this region have been peaceful. It is possible that there is a link to the furbolgs' behavior and the dark energy we were able to detect earlier.

Bring me samples of the furbolgs' blood. You will find them to the east in the Rage Fang Shrine and the Heart's Blood Shrine.

passages.title: A Possible Link
passages.text: Have you obtained the blood samples, <name>?

passages.title: A Possible Link
passages.text: This blood carries the same taint as the slime you obtained earlier... this does not bode well, <name>.

passages.title: Stealing from the Siegesmiths
passages.text:
I'm tasked with the destruction of the Scarlet Onslaught's ballistae. Unfortunately, the apothecaries and I are at odds on the use of our resources, so I've nothing to destroy them with!

To the northeast are the Carrion Fields. The Scourge siegesmiths there at their forge and meat wagons are demolition masters.

Luckily for us, they also leave their bombs lying about. 

I want you to retrieve them for me, off of the ground or the siegesmiths, I don't care which.

passages.title: Stealing from the Siegesmiths
passages.text:
You'd think that they'd let me make use of the blight spreaders... maybe load them up with something nasty to destroy the ballistae.

But no, they tell me that they're only for special missions.

Whatever!

passages.title: Stealing from the Siegesmiths
passages.text:
<The deathguard rubs his hands together in anticipation.>

Excellent. Their loss is my... our gain!

You didn't have trouble with any of these along the way? Some of them look rather unstable. I may be undead, but I value my existence!

passages.title: The Bear God's Offspring
passages.text:
It is possible that the furbolg of Grizzly Hills have the same taint that plagued Vordrassil. They've been involved in a deadly tribal war recently after years of peaceful coexistence.

The shrines that they guard to the east are home to Ursoc's offspring.

If the corruption has affected the furbolg, it is possible that because of their lineage, Kodian and Orsonn have remained unharmed.

If that's the case, find them and listen to what they have to say.

passages.title: The Bear God's Offspring
passages.text: Ursoc's children are wise.  Their words explain much of what we've seen so far.

passages.title: Bombard the Ballistae
passages.text:
At last, our chance to strike at their siege engines! Don't flub it.

I kid.

A little.

<class>, bombard New Hearthglen's ballistae with these bombs.

We'll show the Royal Apothecary Society how it's done old style. No concoctions required!

passages.title: Bombard the Ballistae
passages.text:
Oh happy day!

By not using the time and resources of the apothecaries to get the job done, I'm sure to attract the attention of the high executor!

Thinking outside the box, that's what I'm all about. Yes, yes, you had a hand in helping too.

Here, if I give you something will you promise to not mention your part in all of this?

passages.title: Need to Know
passages.text:
I need to know what New Hearthglen is up to.

I want you to steal their orders of the day so that I can find that out.

Head south and in their abbey, in their barracks, and on their beach, find those daily plans!

Just in case you're confused, the barracks is the large building right next to the smithy.

passages.title: Need to Know
passages.text:
If you take too long, their daily plans will change, and we may have to start over again.

Don't take too long!

passages.title: Need to Know
passages.text: Well, what are you waiting for, <race>? Hand them over!

passages.title: Naxxramas and the Fall of Wintergarde
passages.text:
Lord Fordragon has led a crushing assault against Arthas at the Wrathgate. In response to this affront, Arthas has sent Naxxramas down upon us. While Kel'Thuzad hides in the floating citadel, his ground commander, Thel'zan, lays siege to Wintergarde Keep. The lower village is already lost and any chance of extracting survivors from the ruins diminishes by the minute.

We must act quickly! Report to Gryphon Commander Urik at the gryphon station at once! He'll get you up to speed.

Leave me!

passages.title: Naxxramas and the Fall of Wintergarde
passages.text:
<Urik points to a gryphon.>

Have you ever ridden one of those? It's simple, friend. Just hop on and tell it where to go.

passages.title: Ursoc, the Bear God
passages.text:
The time has come, <name>. Now we will learn whether our efforts will accomplish what we need or nothing at all.

Take these ashes and seek the furbolg that Kodian told you about, Tur Ragepaw, near Ursoc's Den. You will find the den to the north of Grizzlemaw.

Convince Tur to aid you, for you will need all the help you can get.

Once you've defeated the bear god, use these ashes over his body.

Even if his worldly form is destroyed, his spirit must be saved.

passages.title: Ursoc, the Bear God
passages.text: You've returned.  Did you succeed?

passages.title: Ursoc, the Bear God
passages.text: <The druid looks pale and her eyes stare blankly past you.  She has left a package in anticipation of your return.>

passages.title: Flight of the Wintergarde Defender
passages.text:
With this whistle you can call down a Wintergarde gryphon. Mount the creature and head towards the ruins of Wintergarde Village, now known as the Carrion Fields, southeast of here. Once at the fields, keep your eyes peeled for helpless Wintergarde villagers. When you spot one, fly low and use the gryphon to pick them up. Return the rescued villager here, to the gryphon station.

There are Scourge all over the place so you'll need to keep your wits about you, hero. Good luck!

passages.title: Flight of the Wintergarde Defender
passages.text: Hurry, <name>! You need to save the helpless villagers!

passages.title: Flight of the Wintergarde Defender
passages.text: Outstanding work, <name>! We can get this keep back into working order now with the return of our citizens.

passages.title: Cleansing Drak'Tharon
passages.text:
Drak'Tharon soon be cleansed of them foul undead and restored to her noble purpose. In return for your help, the keep's most valuable treasures be yours, mon!

Once ya be reachin' its top, ya must summon me, and I'll perform the ritual.

Alas, my summonin' will be comin' at a cost. Ya must collect mojo from the survivors.

passages.title: Cleansing Drak'Tharon
passages.text:
We done a great thing, mon! And dis just be da beginning....

Seek me out in Zul'Drak when da time be right.

Dere be a war to be won, mon!

passages.title: The Spy in New Hearthglen
passages.text:
I have a spy within the ranks of the Scarlet Onslaught. I need you to deliver these daily orders to her so that she can plan the next phase of our assault.

She goes by the name of Agent Skully and she's under a magical guise to appear as the Onslaught's cemetery caretaker.

Here, take these orders to her, and then do as she asks. You'll find the graveyard on the side of the abbey.

passages.title: The Spy in New Hearthglen
passages.text:
<The agent eyes you up and down, and then silently motions you over.>

Don't blow my cover, <class>!

passages.title: The Spy in New Hearthglen
passages.text:
You have word from the spy mistress?

<The agent looks around to make sure that no one is watching as she puts down her shovel.>

Let me see those plans.

passages.title: A Means to an End
passages.text:
I received a few barrels of termites from my sister at the Bulwark back home in the last shipment. I think they're going to come in handy for something I have in mind for you.

The lumbermill operations at New Hearthglen are problematic for us, but so far we haven't been able to get anyone in there to take out their foreman.

I think that if you were to unleash these termites on his precious woodworks, he'd be sure to come running.

Ready to take him out, <class>?

passages.title: A Means to an End
passages.text:
I knew my sister wouldn't let us down.

Well done, <name>. The Onslaught's lumbermill will be out of commission for a while, which means no new construction or ballistae.

Thanks for helping me to live up to the family name.

passages.title: Destroy the Sapling
passages.text:
The furbolgs' work must be undone, <name>. The best of intentions do not count for much when the result is tainted by such strong a corruption.

The sapling must be destroyed, for it is the source of this dark influence. Take this torch and use it to set fire to the corrupted sapling and bring me its ashes.

Once cleansed, by fire, I will use what power I can to remove the taint from them. You will need the ashes to purify Ursoc from the evil power that holds sway over him.

passages.title: Destroy the Sapling
passages.text: Have you brought me the ashes, <name>?

passages.title: Destroy the Sapling
passages.text: I can't make any promises, <name>.  But I will try my best to purify these.

passages.title: Vordrassil's Seeds
passages.text:
We must make sure that Vordrassil is never regrown. The furbolg must have harvested its seed.

Go to Grizzlemaw, in central Grizzly Hills, and obtain all the seeds that you can find. I will make sure they're properly destroyed.

passages.title: Vordrassil's Seeds
passages.text: Have you obtained Vordrassil's seeds yet, <name>?

passages.title: Vordrassil's Seeds
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.  I'll take those from you.

The corruptive power of these seeds is dangerous.  I must destroy them right away.

passages.title: Fire Upon the Waters
passages.text:
I have another mission for you.

I was able to repurpose some of the blight to concoct my world-famous burning water. I want you to take it and set the sails of the Sinner's Folly ablaze!

Use it from the dock. Once the sails are on fire, the deckhands will be busy putting them out, and you'll slip belowdecks to 'retrieve' the captain's rutters.

You'll find the ship on Crusader's Landing, below and south of New Hearthglen. Look for the captain's quarters on the first lower deck, behind the stairs.

passages.title: Fire Upon the Waters
passages.text:
Please do NOT tell me that their sails were somehow protected from my burning water!

I'd hate to have to test it out here again.

passages.title: Fire Upon the Waters
passages.text:
Ahhahahahahahahahaha!

Without their rutters, they've got nowhere to run to now.

Looks to me like the end of the Scarlet Onslaught, and just when they were getting started. How sad.

Heh.

passages.title: No Mercy for the Captured
passages.text:
We have more fools for you to kill.

My agents tell me that several of our good citizens have seen fit to fall into the hands of the Scarlet Onslaught.

This will not do.

Go back to New Hearthglen and eliminate Deathguard Schneider, Senior Scrivener Kinnedius, Engineer Burke and Chancellor Amai.

From what I hear, they're spread out throughout the area. No doubt they are being kept in cages awaiting torture.

Speak with them and then kill them!

passages.title: No Mercy for the Captured
passages.text:
What? You were expecting us to have you rescue them?

Now why would we do that when they have a proven track record of getting themselves captured in the first place?

Northrend is a cold place, young <name>. I suggest that you adjust to it.

passages.title: A Possible Link
passages.text:
The furbolgs that live east of here are more aggressive and bestial than the ones we're used to. Our forces have squared off with them more than once, and the survivors always speak of a dark, slimy substance dripping from their corpses.

Their condition could be linked with the contaminants we found on Vordrassil's remains.

Bring me samples of the furbolgs' blood. You will find them in the Rage Fang Shrine and the Heart's Blood Shrine, far to the east.

passages.title: A Possible Link
passages.text: Have you obtained the blood samples, <name>?

passages.title: A Possible Link
passages.text: The corruption present in this blood is identical to that of the slime.  I don't have a good feeling about this.

passages.title: Children of Ursoc
passages.text:
The furbolgs of Grizzly Hills carry with them a corruption of some kind, that is for sure. Tribal war has broken out amongst them after years of peaceful coexistence.

What remains to be seen is whether the bears they worship as gods have also been tainted.

Ursoc's two children, Orsonn and Kodian, dwell in the Heart's Blood Shrine and the Rage Fang Shrine, south and southeast of Grizzlemaw.

See if they will speak to you regarding what has happened here.

passages.title: Children of Ursoc
passages.text: Ursoc's children are wise.  Their words explain much of what we've seen so far.

passages.title: Vordrassil's Sapling
passages.text:
The druids of old seem to have had good reasons for destroying Vordrassil. We cannot let the furbolgs regrow it.

On the other hand, saving Ursoc's spirit hinges on the magic contained by the sapling.

Take this torch and use it to burn the tree. You will find it in the middle of Grizzlemaw, inside Vordrassil's old trunk.

Bring me Vordrassil's ashes. It is my hope that once purified by fire, we may use its magic to cleanse Ursoc's spirit of its dark taint.

passages.title: Vordrassil's Sapling
passages.text: Have you brought me the ashes, <name>?

passages.title: Vordrassil's Sapling
passages.text: Yes!  Vordrassil's magic is still present in these ashes.  There might be hope for Ursoc yet.

passages.title: Ursoc, the Bear God
passages.text:
It is time, <name>. Take these ashes and look for the furbolg that Kodian spoke of. If he went to seek Ursoc, he will be near his den, north of Grizzlemaw.

You will need his help. You won't be able to defeat Ursoc alone.

Once you've defeated Ursoc, use these ashes to purify his spirit. Only then will we know whether our efforts have been in vain or not.

passages.title: Ursoc, the Bear God
passages.text: <The druid looks pale and her eyes stare blankly past you.  She has left a package in anticipation of your return.>

passages.title: Vordrassil's Seeds
passages.text:
We cannot allow Vordrassil to grow again. If the furbolg regrew it once, they can do it again.

Go to Grizzlemaw, in central Grizzly Hills, and obtain Vordrassil's seeds. I will make sure they're properly disposed of.

passages.title: Vordrassil's Seeds
passages.text: Do you have the seeds, <name>?

passages.title: Vordrassil's Seeds
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.  I'll take those from you.

The corruptive power of these seeds is dangerous.  I must destroy them right away.

passages.title: Return to the High Commander
passages.text: Return to High Commander Halford Wyrmbane at once, <name>. Let him know that your mission was a success and that the few remaining villagers that were rescued are back to work.

passages.title: Return to the High Commander
passages.text:
<Halford salutes.>

The townsfolk are all back to work? Already? Outstanding, soldier! We'll get this town built back up and fortified in no time. Before long, reinforcements will be ready to join the fight with Lord Fordragon at the Wrathgate.

I'm getting ahead of myself, of course, as there is much left to do here before we can even think about sending you to the aid of Bolvar.

passages.title: Torture the Torturer
passages.text:
Enough! I want you to put an end to the torture of my people!

The Onslaught's torturer, Alphonse, has been bleeding information out of everyone that gets caught by those fiends! I need to know what they know.

My sources tell me that he has set up shop in the basement of their barracks, which is right next to the smithy.

I'll loan you my personal branding iron to see to it that the job is done right.

Find him and get that information.

passages.title: Torture the Torturer
passages.text:
They knew all of that? And who the hell is this Grand Admiral Westwind that he spoke of?!

<The high executor grumbles to himself about hating surprises.>

Better that we know than have to guess. I hope that you left your... er, my mark.

passages.title: Rescue from Town Square
passages.text:
Just down this path here is Wintergarde's town square. Once a hive of activity for the citizens of Wintergarde, now a warzone, filled with murderous geists hell-bent on vengeance towards the living.

In the buildings surrounding the town square are trapped villagers that must be rescued! I ask much of you, now, <name>, but you are the only soldier I can spare. Free our people. Take this path down into town square and enter those houses. Kill anything that gets in your way! Return to me should you survive.

passages.title: Rescue from Town Square
passages.text:
<Halford says a prayer for the deceased.>

You do the Light's work, <name>.

I fear that our work has only just begun.

passages.title: Without a Prayer
passages.text:
These plans indicate something imminent is being planned.

But first, there's the matter of this strange protection that the Onslaught forces have. If Venomspite is to deal with them once and for all, we must find out who's behind it and eliminate them.

I've noticed that the bishop in the chapel on the far side of New Hearthglen, across from the lumbermill, has stepped up his blessing of the troops. Kill him and steal his prayer book.

Maybe it will give us a clue.

passages.title: Without a Prayer
passages.text: You have the bishop's prayer book? Did you find anything unusual in it?

passages.title: Without a Prayer
passages.text:
A newly scribed blessing at the back of the book you say?

<The agent glances over your shoulder as you flip to the page at the end.>

Damn it all! That's the high abbot's handwriting! I'd stake your life on it.

passages.title: The Thane of Voldrune
passages.text:
Now that you've captured the flame-imbued talismans and weakened Voldrune's defenses, we can strike at its leader, Thane Torvald Eriksson.

The thane's favorite mount is an unruly proto-drake he calls Flamebringer. It is kept bound in chains in the western part of Voldrune, but with the talismans, you should be able to control it long enough to use it against the thane.

Once you have Flamebringer under your control, search the tops of the towers of Voldrune for the thane and show him no mercy.

passages.title: The Thane of Voldrune
passages.text: Have you overcome the thane? We cannot risk leaving him in power.

passages.title: The Thane of Voldrune
passages.text: Good work, <name>. I doubt any of the woodsmen would've wanted to take a crack at the proto-drake, but we couldn't afford to let the Dragonflayers build a base of power in Grizzly Hills. If only the Horde was so easily dealt with...

passages.title: The Flamebinders' Secrets
passages.text:
Even as the Alliance cowards attack our positions, the Dragonflayer vrykul outpost of Voldrune, to the southeast, prepares for war. The vrykul are far from the strongest enemy we face here, but we must eliminate them before they can truly threaten us.

Their most powerful warriors are permitted to ride half-trained proto-drakes into battle. To control the beasts, their flamebinders create powerful talismans. You'll need to slay them and take the talismans if our plan is to work.

passages.title: The Flamebinders' Secrets
passages.text: Did you collect those talismans?

passages.title: The Flamebinders' Secrets
passages.text: With the power of the talismans, the drake has no choice but to obey your commands. The thane's fate is sealed.

passages.title: A Show of Strength
passages.text:
Preparations for war are underway in the vrykul village of Voldrune to the southeast. Voldrune's thane cannot field a large army, but with our forces spread thin, we are still at risk.

We cannot risk giving the thane and his men an opportunity to attack, so we must take the battle to them. If you are truly a <class> of the Horde, you will relish the chance to demonstrate our strength.

Cut down the huscarls and prove to this Dragonflayer clan that the Horde is not to be trifled with!

passages.title: A Show of Strength
passages.text: You have done exactly as I asked. We've got the Dragonflayers on the defensive and it'll soon be time to deal with their leader.

passages.title: The Fate of the Dead
passages.text:
The town square, down this path, is overrun with the undead citizens of Wintergarde! Our own crypt provides a seemingly endless supply of soldiers for the Scourge to throw at us. Take no pity on them, though, <name>. While they were once mortal, capable of compassion and thought, they are now ravaging undead with only one purpose: our destruction.

Venture forth to the town square and deliver the vengeful geists to their maker. Give them peace.

passages.title: The Fate of the Dead
passages.text:
Perhaps now they will rest easy, their spirits free to ascend to the Light.

My thoughts and prayers now turn to Lord Fordragon and our forces at the Wrathgate. We must persevere here, if only to buy them enough time to defeat the Lich King. Wintergarde cannot fall.

passages.title: The Thane of Voldrune
passages.text:
With the flame-imbued talismans, we can finally challenge the thane.

His favorite mount is a ferocious proto-drake called Flamebringer. It is kept bound in chains in the western part of Voldrune, but with the power of the talismans, you should be able to bend it to your will and use it against the thane.

Once you have Flamebringer under your control, search the tops of the towers of Voldrune for the thane and use Flamebringer to destroy him.

passages.title: The Thane of Voldrune
passages.text: Have you overcome the thane?

passages.title: The Thane of Voldrune
passages.text: The few remaining Dragonflayers dare not challenge us after your battle with the thane. Show no mercy to our enemies - that is the way of the Horde.

passages.title: The Perfect Dissemblance
passages.text:
You may wonder how I can maintain this guise; I use a magic mirror that was loaned to me by the spy mistress.

It only has so much power in it, but I think there's enough for the both of us. Here, take it. I want you to use it to impersonate one of the Onslaught raven priests.

Be quick about it... I have no idea how long my glamour will last while you have the mirror.

Realize that you won't immediately be perfectly disguised, so don't count on it being foolproof until I've had a chance to help you.

passages.title: The Perfect Dissemblance
