passages.title: Scourgekabob
passages.text: Whatcha got there, <race>?

passages.title: Scourgekabob
passages.text:
Nothin' better than watchin' them shcourge burn... <hic>.

Wrote a little shong about it. Wanna hear it? Here goes....

passages.title: To Conquest Hold, But Be Careful!
passages.text:
I've received a request for help from our base in the Grizzly Hills. I'm sending you to see Conqueror Krenna.

<The high executor waves a sheaf of parchment in the air as if he could care less what is written on it.>

She's attempting to secure all of the natural resources or somesuch. Just watch your back around her. The word is that she's aggressive even for an orc.

Follow the road east and then southeast. Cross the bridge at the Dragonspine Tributary and go east from the Evergreen Trading Post.

passages.title: To Conquest Hold, But Be Careful!
passages.text:
Who are you?

Tell me why I shouldn't split you in two where you stand!

passages.title: The High Executor Needs You
passages.text:
It's a good thing that I intercepted this request from High Executor Wroth before it got to Overlord Agmar. What is Wroth thinking?

<The sergeant rips up the letter that he's holding.>

<class>, go see what it is that the high executor wants.

Follow the road east and pass through The Dragon Wastes. You'll find a path leading up out of the wastes on the southeast side, and the Forsaken town, Venomspite, will stand before you on the south side of the mountain.

passages.title: The High Executor Needs You
passages.text:
You were sent from Agmar's Hammer? It's about time!

No, the help is not for me. I simply have no one else to spare, but you'll do.

passages.title: Direbrew's Dire Brew
passages.text: Coren Direbrew's corpse clutched this small cask tightly to its gut. This must be his infamous Dire Brew!

passages.title: Direbrew's Dire Brew
passages.text: <name>, your face has a grim set to it.  Do you have dire news?

passages.title: Direbrew's Dire Brew
passages.text: This is the Coren Direbrew's drink?  The brew he wanted more than anything to submit at Brewfest?  Well, officially we can't recognize this submission, but out of respect for a fallen brewer, perhaps I'll have a taste...

passages.title: Direbrew's Dire Brew
passages.text: Coren Direbrew's corpse clutched this small cask tightly to its gut. This must be his infamous Dire Brew!

passages.title: Direbrew's Dire Brew
passages.text: Hey <name>, your face is all smudged!  Have you been to Blackrock Depths?

passages.title: Direbrew's Dire Brew
passages.text:
Ah, so Direbrew finally submitted his brew.  What a pity he had to die to do it...

Oh, well.  Bottoms up, eh?

passages.title: Audience With The Dragon Queen
passages.text:
Our assault against Angrathar has staggered the Scourge, but they remain unrelenting. From overhead they send their frost wyrms to strafe the field of battle, making an advance upon the gate itself impossible. The frost wyrm attacks must be stopped, but before we defile the bones of ancient dragons, we must gain permission from their queen.

Travel southeast to Wyrmrest Temple and seek out Queen Alexstrasza. Tell her what we must do and ask her for guidance.

Go now, <name>!

passages.title: Audience With The Dragon Queen
passages.text:
You have come seeking my council, mortal. This I know, but do you know what it is that you face?

<Alexstrasza points northward.>

North of here are the dying grounds of Galakrond - progenitor of dragonkind. It is from Galakrond that the Titans created the Aspects. Imagine, then, the power of Galakrond. His size alone was greater than all of the Aspects combined! Now attempt to understand what the Scourge do in the Great Dragonblight.

Frost wyrms, mortal, should be the least of your concerns.

passages.title: Audience With The Dragon Queen
passages.text:
Though I know you hunger to destroy the Scourge that stand before us at the Wrath Gate, we must first deal with the threat that looms overhead. Until the strafing assaults of the frost wyrms are halted, we cannot move forward.

But before we assault the dying grounds of dragons, we must first be granted permission. Venture now to the hallowed halls of dragonkind: Wyrmrest Temple. Once there, seek out Queen Alexstrasza.

Ride now, <name>! Southeast, to Wyrmrest!

passages.title: Audience With The Dragon Queen
passages.text:
You have come seeking my council, mortal. This I know, but do you know what it is that you face?

<Alexstrasza points northward.>

North of here are the dying grounds of Galakrond - progenitor of dragonkind. It is from Galakrond that the Titans created the Aspects. Imagine, then, the power of Galakrond. His size alone was greater than all of the Aspects combined! Now attempt to understand what the Scourge do in the Great Dragonblight.

Frost wyrms, mortal, should be the least of your concerns.

passages.title: On Ruby Wings
passages.text:
Use this beacon to signal a Wyrmrest vanquisher. Climb upon its back and fly north to Galakrond's Rest. Once there, command the dragon to destroy the Scourge scavengers that work to unearth Galakrond. Once the area has been cleansed, fly to the Wicked Coil, overlooking Galakrond's Rest, to destroy Grand Necrolord Antiok and recover the scythe that he uses to control the wyrms.

Do this and return to Queen Alexstrasza for a hero's reward!

<name>, beware the rotting storm giants that wander the area!

passages.title: On Ruby Wings
passages.text: Destroy the Scourge at Galakrond's Rest before it is too late!

passages.title: On Ruby Wings
passages.text: I knew that you would return, <name>. You have served the Wyrmrest Accord and saved your people from certain death. Let it be known to all and let it be recorded for posterity!

passages.title: Return To Angrathar
passages.text:
With Antiok slain and the scythe in our possession, the frost wyrm assaults upon your forces at Angrathar will halt. The wyrms that remain in the Dragonblight will be hunted and destroyed, their bones returning to the earth.

The time to make your final stand is now, <name>. Return to Fordragon Hold and notify Highlord Fordragon.

passages.title: Return To Angrathar
passages.text: Know this: all that you have done has led to this moment. Without your efforts, we would have been finished! Now, stand guard as I take to the field and end this!

passages.title: Return To Angrathar
passages.text:
With Antiok slain and the scythe in our possession, the frost wyrm assaults upon your forces at Angrathar will halt. The wyrms that remain in the Dragonblight will be hunted and destroyed, their bones returning to the earth.

The time to make your final stand is now, <name>. Return to the Kor'kron Vanguard and notify Saurfang the Younger.

passages.title: Return To Angrathar
passages.text:
My father was right about you, <name>. Everything that he said has come to pass - only one final duty remains unfulfilled. I will now lead the Kor'kron to the front line. The time to end this war is at hand. The Lich King's tyranny ends today!

Take my post now, <name>, and stand guard over our forces.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: High Standards
passages.text:
Listen, <class>. This is the Argent Crusade. Our men will fight to the end and never complain no matter what the conditions.

That said, we've taken some heavy casualties in this campaign and we've been hitting it hard with little or no sleep for months. That all takes a toll on morale, whether we admit it or not.

It may not seem like much, but seeing our standard raised over the battlefield is of considerable comfort to a soldier. Take these banners and raise them at the pedestals in Drak'Sotra.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: High Standards
passages.text:
Good work, friend.

Amazing what a little of one's colors do for a battleground.

You'll want to head on over to Captain Rupert next. He's stationed at the wall, just northeast of here.

passages.title: Defend the Stand
passages.text:
Despite our substantial successes in the lower third of Zul'Drak, we must still face the onslaught of the Scourge. Such is the way in this frigid hell.

The attacks are unrelenting, yet my men need rest. If you are willing, we could use your aid in reinforcing them.

Below in the courtyard you'll find no end to the fighting. Dispatch the Scourge there with all the zeal you can muster, <class>.

passages.title: Defend the Stand
passages.text: Your assistance in this matter is greatly appreciated. Were it not for your efforts, we would have difficulty in holding the unliving back from our steps.

passages.title: Argent Crusade, We Are Leaving!
passages.text:
<The sergeant quickly reads through the orders you've handed him, a frown coming over his face.>

Look, <lad/lass>, I'd love to just up and leave, but take a look out there. All of my people are fighting.

Tell you what, you've come this far, you think you're up to doing me a small favor? Head out there and round up my soldiers?

Tell 'em that the sergeant orders them to report back immediately. Lend them a hand if you will.

passages.title: Argent Crusade, We Are Leaving!
passages.text:
Alright then. We'll collect up the rest and head back to the stand.

It's a shame that we have to leave so soon. Doesn't quite feel like the job's done here, and quite frankly, I get the feeling that prophet in front of the altar is going to be big trouble!

passages.title: New Orders for Sergeant Stackhammer
passages.text:
<class>, you're here to help, right? I've got new orders for our forces that are currently deployed at the Drakkari altar to the north.

You can't miss it. Just head straight up the avenue. Sergeant Stackhammer shouldn't be hard to find.

passages.title: New Orders for Sergeant Stackhammer
passages.text: What's this all about?

passages.title: New Orders for Sergeant Stackhammer
passages.text:
<The dwarf sergeant warily eyes the orders in your hand.>

Are those new orders for me, mister?

passages.title: Trouble at the Altar of Sseratus
passages.text:
There's trouble at the altar of the snake god.

The presence of the Scourge has weakened the land, <race>. This in turn has weakened the wild gods.

We know that the Drakkari are taking advantage of this to do evil things to the gods.

I need you to be my eyes and ears. The Altar of Sseratus is at the end of the avenue to the north. Sneak around the back and get a look inside of the main altar building.

Whatever you do, avoid the prophet at all costs!

passages.title: Trouble at the Altar of Sseratus
passages.text:
Dead?

<The hexxer's spirit is visibly lowered at the news you bring.>

They've killed Sseratus and drunk deeply of his mojo; the prophet especially!

We must figure out a way to put an end to him before he drinks too much more!

passages.title: Mopping Up
passages.text:
I couldn't help but overhear what you were talking to the sergeant about. That doesn't change the fact that we still have a job to do here.

While you're out there, do you think you could help us to put some of those followers of Sseratus out of their misery?

passages.title: Mopping Up
passages.text: Thanks, <class>. I'd have hated to leave without accomplishing what we came out here for in the first place.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Intestinal Fortitude
passages.text:
Finally, the patrol arrives!

Here's the situation, <race>. We've lost many of our finest soldiers in this campaign and have had to call upon our recruits to fill in the gaps.

We've just fought one of our fiercest battles and many of the recruits were simply not prepared to face this enemy. There are more fights ahead, and I need them ready to follow orders.

If there's one thing I can't stomach, it's cowardice. Perhaps you can help them find the courage to continue.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Intestinal Fortitude
passages.text:
Well done, <class>. And not a moment too soon. I've received word that a counter-attack is imminent.

You should be on your way. The next post is to the northeast, near the coliseum. Captain Grondel should be waiting for you there.

passages.title: Precious Elemental Fluids
passages.text:
<The hexxer examines the decanter of mojo.>

I have an idea for how to deal with the prophet of Sseratus. But first, we're going to need some things.

The Drak'Sotra Fields are directly to the south. Because of the stresses on the land from the Scourge and the deaths of gods, the wall between worlds has weakened and the elementals are flooding in.

We need the precious fluids of their lords. If you combine three links from the elementals a tether will be made, and one of their lords can be summoned.

passages.title: Precious Elemental Fluids
passages.text: Do you have the precious fluids?

passages.title: Precious Elemental Fluids
passages.text:
Excellent. When combined with the mojo, these fluids will dilute the effectiveness of the mojo without completely eliminating it.

Now, one more thing.

passages.title: The Hills Have Us
passages.text:
While we focus to hold our ground at Wintergarde and deal with the unfolding events of the Wrathgate, battalions from as far away as Westfall battle their way through the dense foliage and inhospitable denizens of Grizzly Hills. All in hopes of finding an alternate route into Icecrown.

Lieutenant Dumont, stationed at Amberpine Lodge, has enlisted the aid of able bodied citizens willing to risk life and limb in the uncharted wilds. Will you rise to meet this challenge?

passages.title: The Hills Have Us
passages.text:
You were almost shot down, eh? Savage monsters - those Horde.

Payback will come for what they've done. You can count on at least that much, <class>.

Now, it's time to put you to work.

passages.title: Leave No One Behind
passages.text:
Ahh, good. They sent someone.

Listen, <race>. We need a hand here. Our forces were pushed back and we've lost Drak'Sotra to the Scourge. Where they came from is anyone's guess....

The point is, we need every man we can get here, and some of our best have yet to return from battle.

I need you to enter the ruins now that the fighting has died down and find our wounded, patch them up, and bring them here to me.

Scour Drak'Sotra! They couldn't have gone far.

passages.title: Leave No One Behind
passages.text: Have you rescued our veterans, <name>?

passages.title: Leave No One Behind
passages.text:
Saved them all, did you? Outstanding!

Maybe you'd consider sticking around the post here? We could sure use someone like you....

passages.title: Nice Hat...
passages.text:
My hat? Yes, it's an unusual style, I know, from far away... few tailors here know how to make them.

When I was young and hot-blooded, I wore it as a standing challenge. Many came seeking to defeat me and win it for themselves... but no one ever did.

Ah, but those days are long past. I'm an old man, now: I drink, I fish, but I no longer duel.

passages.title: Nice Hat...
passages.text: I was unbeatable, in those days... proud, and rightly so. No challenger ever won this fine hat...

passages.title: Nice Hat...
passages.text:
My... my hat! So... it WAS you. I'd thought so. The old scars ached when you drew near, but... so young! You've not changed at all!

Well... so now you know my secret. I WAS beaten... once. Here: take this hat, in return for mine. You've more than earned it.

passages.title: Nice Hat...
passages.text:
My hat? Yes, it's an unusual style, I know, from far away... few tailors here know how to make them.

When I was young and hot-blooded, I wore it as a standing challenge. Many came seeking to defeat me and win it for themselves... but no one ever did.

Ah, but those days are long past. I'm an old man, now: I drink, I fish, but I no longer duel.

passages.title: Nice Hat...
passages.text: I was unbeatable, in those days... proud, and rightly so. No challenger ever won this fine hat...

passages.title: Nice Hat...
passages.text:
My... my hat! But... how did you...?

Well... no matter. So, now you know my secret. I WAS beaten... once. Here: take this hat, in return for mine. You've earned it.

passages.title: Too Much of a Good Thing
passages.text:
There. I've modified the mojo. Now when the prophet drinks it, not only will he lose some of his power, his mind will also be addled by the effects of the fungus.

At least that's the theory.

As for how to get him to drink it, might I suggest you simply throw it at him? No doubt he'll catch and drink it given the arrogance that he's displayed at the altar.

Unless you can kill him, <class>, your Argent Crusade is about to come to a terrible end.

passages.title: Too Much of a Good Thing
passages.text:
Amazing! You've saved your people and the rest of Northrend from his madness.

Unfortunately there's more of this insanity occurring up in the higher tiers of Zul'Drak.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Whatdya Want, a Medal?
passages.text:
Look at me, <race>. Do I look like I have time fer fillin' out reports?

It be all I can do to keep this post free o' the bloody Scourge, and they want me to mess with paperwork!

<sigh> No sense in complainin'. I need to get the commander some kinda kill count from the last skirmish.

You wanna be helpful? Go and get me all the medals you can find from the dead trolls around here. That'll hafta be close enough.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Whatdya Want, a Medal?
passages.text: You get those medals for me, <race>?

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Whatdya Want, a Medal?
passages.text:
Well, now!

Ya saved me a fair bit o' work there lad. I'm grateful. I'll be sure ta make mention of ya in me report.

Off with yeh now. Finklestein'll likely be waitin fer ya a bit west o' here.

passages.title: Where in the World is Hemet Nesingwary?
passages.text:
When I heard that the legendary Hemet Nesingwary was setting sail for the Sholazar Basin, I offered to help fund his expedition. We know little of Sholazar, but it's said to be a lush paradise in the midst of this frozen continent.

Hemet has agreed to send back samples of exotic plants, reagents, and crystals. There hasn't been any word from him. Monte Muzzleshot was supposed to be bringing them supplies, but he hasn't returned, either. If you'll look into it, I'll send you in my flying machine.

passages.title: Where in the World is Hemet Nesingwary?
passages.text: Aye, Hemet's here. He's at the camp, just go northwest toward the river and you'll soon see it. And for the love of the Light, lad, have him send someone to cut me down!

passages.title: Need an Engine, Take an Engine
passages.text:
She's ruined... ruined! I told that captain to be careful with such a precious cargo, but would she listen to me? No!

When the ship ran aground, it damaged my flying machine, the Spirit of Gnomeregan. Now, we're left without any means to send our reports!

There is a chance, though, that the Venture Company's antics may work in our favor. They shot down another flying machine right about where Monte parachuted into the swamp to the east. Go there and retrieve the engine. It may be our only hope.

passages.title: Need an Engine, Take an Engine
passages.text: Well, were you able to get the engine? I just know that archmage who funded the expedition is getting nervous.

passages.title: Need an Engine, Take an Engine
passages.text: There... just set it down there. Be careful! If you ruin this one, we're in big trouble. Now, let's see what I can do.

passages.title: Venture Co. Misadventure
passages.text:
Ever since we arrived, the Venture Company has hampered our efforts to secure our campsite and survey the area. Normally, we wouldn't care what they were up to, but they've started antagonizing our scouts and shooting down supply flights.

We can't allow this insult to stand. Hemet Nesingwary's expedition came here to hunt, and hunt it shall.

Go to Swindlegrin's Dig, on the far side of the crystal pillar to the northeast, and kill any Venture Company employee you see!

passages.title: Venture Co. Misadventure
passages.text: That should hamper their operations, but I worry that the foreman will try to bring in more workers. We have to complete the job while we can.

passages.title: Wipe That Grin Off His Face
passages.text:
We must send Foreman Swindlegrin packing if we're going to shut down his mine permanently, but be careful. His bodyguard, Meatpie, is a large, mean ogre, and isn't likely to let you see the foreman without a fight.

The two probably occupy a platform that would let them look out over the entire Venture Company operation at Swindlegrin's Dig.

Remember, the dig is on the far side of the Suntouched Pillar to the northeast. Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Wipe That Grin Off His Face
passages.text: What a relief to hear that the Venture Company will trouble us no more. You have my thanks, and that of Hemet for dealing with this problem. A game hunter cannot, in good conscience, lift her weapon against another person.

passages.title: Gluttonous Lurkers
passages.text:
My master, Finklestein, is in the shrine at Heb'Valok to the northwest preparing a truth serum, and he needs basilisk crystals. Heb'Valok is on the west side of the road leading north before the Altar of Sseratus.

There are basilisks to the east at Drak'Agal.

If you grab the Zul'Drak rats and throw them at the basilisk, they will become gorged and docile after eating five. Then you'll be able to take their crystals.

Killing the basilisk won't do you any good. That'd just break its crystals!

passages.title: Gluttonous Lurkers
passages.text:
What's all this?

By any chance have you seen my no-good apprentice, Pestlepot?

I sent him on an errand quite some time ago and he has yet to return!

passages.title: Gluttonous Lurkers
passages.text:
Oh, most excellent! Thank you. The crystals appear to be in fine condition!

I have no doubt that Pestlepot put you up to doing his chores for him. Nevertheless, your assistance in this matter is greatly appreciated!

passages.title: Playing Along
passages.text:
My kill! You take my kill!

<Gekgek taunts you with his spear.>

You dumb, <race>. Now you owe Gekgek! You be Frenzyheart slave. You slay many more beasts for Frenzyheart.

You go Frenzyheart Hill to northeast - you tell High-Shaman Rakjak you the new slave.

Go, <race>! Go or I taunt you a second time!

<Gekgek waves his spear around menacingly.>

passages.title: Playing Along
passages.text:
You the new slave?

Good. We running out.

passages.title: The Ape Hunter's Slave
passages.text:
You think you so great hunter, eh? You no Frenzyheart, you not know of hunt.

Goregek is great ape hunter. He slay so many ape you can't count on claws.

You go with Goregek and hunt hardknuckles to east. You the slave, <race>. You do what Goregek tell you.

passages.title: The Ape Hunter's Slave
passages.text: Goregek show silly <race> slave how it done.

passages.title: Tormenting the Softknuckles
passages.text:
Slave thing!

Rakjak want me to babysit you while I kill hardknuckles. I feeling generous today, so I let you kill some too, but don't get in Goregek's way!

Rakjak not know yet, but Goregek has eye on big bad hardknuckle mama. We go to Hardknuckle Clearing to east and poke softknuckles with poker and she sure to come yelling!

<Goregek rubs his hands together gleefully.>

passages.title: Tormenting the Softknuckles
passages.text:
Goregek take you to kill big mom of hardknuckles, eh? You lucky!

Dumb softknuckles squeal good!

<Rakjak squeals loudly and breaks out laughing.>

passages.title: The Underground Menace
passages.text:
Lion killer, chicken chaser, new Frenzyheart slave...

I know you no want to stay slave, so I tell you what to do. Show you better than the other Frenzyheart hunters and then Rakjak respect you.

Under sands of south river there a beast that kills wasp, apes, and even wolvar. He called Serfex. You bring claw of Serfex to Rakjak and maybe he release you from slaveness.

Hope Dajik teaching you good so Serfex be easy stuff.

passages.title: The Underground Menace
passages.text: I not ask for you, <race>. What you want?

passages.title: The Underground Menace
passages.text:
You kill Serfex? I bet you follow mighty wolvar that kill Serfex and take claw.

My claw now.

passages.title: Flown the Coop!
passages.text:
Dumb Goregek stumble into chicken house and let all the chickens go!

They all around hill - go get chickens back!

<Elder Harkek shoos you away.>

passages.title: Flown the Coop!
passages.text: You catch chickens?

passages.title: Flown the Coop!
passages.text:
Good! I was worried about foodstuffs. I already pretty hungry.

Thank you, <race>.

passages.title: The Wasp Hunter's Apprentice
passages.text:
Rakjak not dumb. Maybe you good at killing things. Maybe Frenzyheart can make you into real hunter.

Dajik hunts giant wasp things better than all wolvar. Go with Dajik to Sapphire Hive to southeast or to river in south and learn the hunt.

passages.title: The Wasp Hunter's Apprentice
passages.text:
We kill many many wasps.

Rakjak don't think they run out.

passages.title: The Sapphire Queen
passages.text:
Bristlepine can be dangerous, but most stay far away from wolvar. Wasps on other hand not fear the Frenzyheart... they even kill some of our hunters.

I know Rakjak want wasp queen dead, but no wolvar want to go into her hive. You go kill wasp queen in Sapphire Hive to southeast and get stinger for Rakjak. Me bet Rakjak like that.

passages.title: The Sapphire Queen
passages.text: You smell like wasp things.

passages.title: The Sapphire Queen
passages.text:
You killed queen wasp! You stronger than Rakjak thought.

Maybe wasps go away now and stop attacking Frenzyheart hunters.

passages.title: Mischief in the Making
passages.text:
You good hunter, but Frenzyheart can make you stronger. Harkek think maybe you ready for something more important.

Before Rakjak send you on important mission, you need gather things for Rakjak. All along river to south are blue crystals. Rakjak need lots of blue crystals.

You go get crystals now.

passages.title: Mischief in the Making
passages.text: Almost ready for long journey. Gekgek come back with crocolisk just moment ago.

passages.title: Mischief in the Making
passages.text: Good <race>! Okay, all ready.

passages.title: A Rough Ride
passages.text:
Zepik is best hunter of the Frenzyheart. Zepik hunts big-tongues... ugly things near swamps that try to steal all stuff they can find.

Zepik going on long trek to break big-tongue shrine and try to scare them away. We no want big-tongues in this land anymore.

There a crocolisk chained on northeast side of hill, next to tree - go with Zepik and do what Zepik tell you.

passages.title: A Rough Ride
passages.text: They tell Zepik you good hunter for not being Frenzyheart.

passages.title: A Rough Ride
passages.text:
We here! Must work fast.

Watch out for big-tongues.

passages.title: Lightning Definitely Strikes Twice
passages.text:
Okay, the crystal things...

The big-tongues use the crystals to power their rain shrines. Zepik not know quite how it works, but Zepik does know that if they use wrong crystals, the clouds and the rain go crazy!

Zepik tried to sneak in at one of their other rain shrines, but it not go so well. It sure to go much better with two!

Take crystals, place at big stone pillar shrine thing, then smash them to release power. Zepik not sure what will happen, so might want to step back after.

passages.title: Lightning Definitely Strikes Twice
passages.text: Zepik think this go much better with partner. You strong for not Frenzyheart.

passages.title: Lightning Definitely Strikes Twice
passages.text:
It work so good!

You see lightning smash that oracle guy? So good!

<Zepik rubs his hands together and chuckles maniacally.>

passages.title: The Mist Isn't Listening
passages.text:
Gorillas and wasps are boring! Big-tongues the only thing fun to hunt.

While we mess up rain shrine, we kill lots of mist big-tongues. That sure to make them not want to come back to village thing.

<Zepik nods to himself confidently.>

passages.title: The Mist Isn't Listening
passages.text:
I stab those big-tongues good.

You did okay I guess.

No, I just kidding! You good hunter. I glad to hunt with you.

passages.title: Hoofing It
passages.text:
Okay, we done! Time to go back. No crocolisk to ride this time though.

If we go east and stay near ridge, it should lead all the way back near hill.

Need to be careful not to go far below ridge though or we might go right into big-tongue tree village thing. Zepik not think they like us right now.

passages.title: Hoofing It
passages.text:
Blown up by lightning?

<Rakjak breaks out laughing for a moment.>

You good hunter. Rakjak like you. Maybe one day you can be honorary Frenzyheart!

Only maybe though!

passages.title: Troll Patrol: The Alchemist's Apprentice
passages.text:
Ahh, you must be the promised patrol. Your timing couldn't be better. I have urgent need of an extra pair of hands.

We have a Drakkari prisoner who's been sent here to undergo questioning. Before the interrogation begins, I require assistance in the creation of a truth serum.

Creating a truth serum is tricky business, demanding keen instincts, perfect timing, and improvisation at every step.

Let me know when you're ready, <race>. And remember, timing is everything!

passages.title: Troll Patrol: The Alchemist's Apprentice
passages.text: You see, <name>, there is far more to true alchemy than mixing a few ingredients....

passages.title: Troll Patrol: The Alchemist's Apprentice
passages.text:
You've done it!

The intelligence gathered from that troll will undoubtedly be of great value. I'll be certain to make mention of your efforts in my report to the commander.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Bones of Nozronn
passages.text:
Bones of Nozronn, Oracle Soo-rahm sends <name> to you!

We have prepared incense for you. Light it and place it near Nozronn's head and you will hear his voice.

<Confused, you tell Soo-rahm that you haven't even told him your question.>

True, we not know, but mighty Nozronn does. Do not doubt. Nozronn will answer your heart's question.

Go. Nozronn not wait long.

passages.title: The Bones of Nozronn
passages.text: Well, have you consulted the native oracle?

passages.title: The Bones of Nozronn
passages.text:
<Hemet listens as you describe what you learned.>

Way to go, lad. No dead rhino tells Hemet Nesingwary where and what he can hunt. We'll show that heap o' bones.

passages.title: The Cleansing Of Jintha'kalar
passages.text:
We wrested this ancient Drakkari temple from a swarm of invading Scourge. Not more than one-hundred paces from where we stand is the ruined city of Jintha'kalar. Scourge necromancers run amok, turning the living Drakkari trolls that remain into servants of the Lich King.

All are now lost to the Light. All must be purged.

<Valus looks upon you sternly.>

All.

passages.title: The Cleansing Of Jintha'kalar
passages.text: Leave nothing for the Lich King to resurrect!

passages.title: The Cleansing Of Jintha'kalar
passages.text:
As you can see, the Scourge war machine presses onward, yet the armies of the Horde and the Alliance remain divided, making for easy prey. It is for this reason that we must remain united.

<Valus is lost in contemplation for a moment.>

The Argent Crusade has use for a man like you. Perhaps you would be interested in joining our cause? To battle and die at the side of the Ashbringer?

passages.title: Reclamation
passages.text:
It is time, <name>. The Etymidian is one of the most destructive forces ever created by the titans and I am loathe to unleash him in my lands.

There is little choice, however. Our enemies have forced my hand and the fury of the titans will cleanse all.

passages.title: Reclamation
passages.text:
I am grateful for your help, <name>.  It is my duty to watch over these lands and all life that dwells on them.

Thanks to you, that life will continue to thrive while the forces of death wage in the bordering regions.

Your actions will not be forgotten.

passages.title: The Activation Rune
passages.text:
This colossal being appears to be inactive. You notice an empty rune-shaped slot on its chest.

Perhaps you might be able to find the missing rune inside the nearby overlook.

passages.title: The Activation Rune
passages.text: <The rune-shaped slot on The Etymidian's chest appears to glow with faint power.>

passages.title: The Activation Rune
passages.text:
<You hear the rumbling sound of stone grinding as The Etymidian's limbs come to life.>

I am needed somewhere?

passages.title: The Etymidian
passages.text:
It is time, <name>. The Waygate has been activated for the first time in seven centuries. Use it to travel to where our final hope lies.

Let us put an end to those who would seek to bring the taint of undeath to this pristine land. Let us unleash the Etymidian.

passages.title: The Etymidian
passages.text: <As you read the engravings on this stone colossus, you realize that this is the weapon that Freya spoke of.  This is the Etymidian.>

passages.title: Dreadsaber Mastery: Stalking the Prey
passages.text:
I have heard that the natives tell stories of a large dreadsaber they call Shango. I haven't seen any evidence of this Shango's existence, but my injuries have kept me from venturing outside the camp.

If you fancy yourself something of a tracker, you might be able to find out the truth about Shango. Debaar said she saw some large tracks on her last outing. Go north from the camp toward Bittertide Lake, and search its southern shore for the prints.

passages.title: Dreadsaber Mastery: Stalking the Prey
passages.text:
<Buck listens as you recount your findings.>

I think you may have found the proof we need for this Shango. And I think I have an idea as to where we can find him.

passages.title: Death to the Necromagi
passages.text:
When the trolls brought down Kolramas, it crashed next to us to the southeast. Unfortunately the crash did not destroy all of the Scourge within.

Now they're raising our men from the dead and using them against us!

This will not be allowed to continue. You will see to it that their necromagi are slaughtered! Do we understand each other?

passages.title: Death to the Necromagi
passages.text:
It's not enough!

<The sergeant's voice cracks as he mourns the corruption of his fallen comrades.>

We must do more to show respect for the memories of those men!

passages.title: Skimmer Spinnerets
passages.text:
Why do I always get the tough tasks to tackle?

The Scourge at Kolramas have plague sprayers that are getting dangerously close. You don't want to know what's going to happen if they start heading this way!

I've got an idea for how we might bring them down, but first we're going to need something... something from their own creatures.

The Hath'ar skimmers can spin a very strong web that we can put to good use. Bring back some of their spinnerets.

passages.title: Skimmer Spinnerets
passages.text: Those spinnerets have to be intact if I'm going to be able to put them together into a device that you can use.

passages.title: Skimmer Spinnerets
passages.text:
Those'll do!

Now we're going to need some raw parts so that I can put the launching device together for you.

passages.title: Malas the Corrupter
passages.text:
<name>, head back down there!

You'll find the leader of Kolramas, Malas the Corrupter, gloating from atop the crashed necropolis.

Kill him and bring me his head!

passages.title: Malas the Corrupter
passages.text: I look forward to mounting his head on a pike. Let's see him come back from that!

passages.title: Malas the Corrupter
passages.text:
You're the hero of the hour, <name>.

You deserve our deepest respect, and something more I think.

passages.title: A Tangled Skein
passages.text:
There! One tangled skein thrower ready and waiting for you to take those plague sprayers down.

You just aim and let loose. The webbing should foul up their hover spells long enough to cause them to crash to the ground just like Kolramas.

Kind of poetic. I like that!

passages.title: A Tangled Skein
passages.text:
Yay! You're the best, <name>!

I wasn't looking forward to being sprayed with Scourge stuff, that's for sure! I guess it's going to be hard for those stupid nerubians to spread their evil now!

How about I give you a little something for saving my skin?

passages.title: Rhino Mastery: The Kill
passages.text:
Now that we know where to find Farunn, all that remains is the battle against the great beast. Are you ready to take on this rhino, <name>? For all the spirit's blustering, I'm certain it was telling the truth about the beast's strength.

When you're ready to face him, head north past the Suntouched Pillar and look for Farunn on the northeast shore of the Bittertide Lake. It may even venture near the Glimmering Pillar. Bring back its horn to commemorate your kill.

passages.title: Rhino Mastery: The Kill
passages.text: Did you kill the beast?

passages.title: Rhino Mastery: The Kill
passages.text:
<Hemet examines the horn.>

An astounding trophy from an amazing animal! <name>, I've been hearing rumors of even bigger, more ferocious game in the northern reaches of the basin and I'd like you to help us track it down.

passages.title: Lab Work
passages.text:
I assume by your interruption that you wish to be numbered among those I am considering for apprenticeship.

A worthy aspiration...

Should I someday choose to accept your petition, I must be confident that you can find your way around my laboratory. I have many ingredients here; some plentiful, and others in short supply.

Take your time, <class>. Find a muddy mire maggot, a withered batwing, an amberseed, and some chilled serpent mucus.

Succeed, and I'll know to take your request seriously.

passages.title: Lab Work
passages.text: Have you become accustomed to my laboratory, <class>?

passages.title: Lab Work
passages.text:
Yes, yes, that's a good start.

Should I call upon you to help me with an actual recipe, you'll need to locate ingredients in a timely manner.

Keep that in mind, <class>.

Farewell.

passages.title: Dreadsaber Mastery: Ready to Pounce
passages.text:
Shango awaits, <name>. If you have succeeded in your tracking, he will not know that you stalk him, and you will need the advantage.

He is supposed to be bigger, stronger, and more ferocious than the other dreadsabers of the basin. Travel north, to the western shore of Bittertide Lake and near the falls that feed it, do battle with Shango. If you succeed, return with his pelt.

passages.title: Dreadsaber Mastery: Ready to Pounce
passages.text: Have you taken on Shango?

passages.title: Dreadsaber Mastery: Ready to Pounce
passages.text: What an exquisite pelt from such a noble animal! It heartens me to see that the rumors about Shango were indeed true, <name>. Your pursuit of the creature has been flawless. You are a true huntsman.

passages.title: Powering the Waygate - The Makers' Perch
passages.text:
It is time then. Let us activate the waygate.

You will find the first switch inside the Makers' Perch in the western edge of the basin.

Beware, <name>. The titans used the perch to watch over their creations. Many of their stone servants still guard the place.

passages.title: Powering the Waygate - The Makers' Perch
passages.text: You're back, little one.  I was beginning to worry about your well-being.

passages.title: Powering the Waygate - The Makers' Perch
passages.text: We're halfway there, <name>.  One more switch needs to be activated before we can retrieve the Etymidian.

passages.title: An Issue of Trust
passages.text:
This should never have happened. The forces of undeath storm the very cradle of life!

If you're not here to destroy the minions of the Lich King, then leave at once. Do not incur my wrath by distracting me from my duties.

passages.title: An Issue of Trust
passages.text: Do not waste my time, mortal.  The titans' creations must be defended!

passages.title: An Issue of Trust
passages.text: Very well, <race>.  I am satisfied that you're not one of the Lich King's minions... perhaps there is something you can do for us after all.

passages.title: The Drakkari Do Not Need Water Elementals!
passages.text:
Intelligence reports that ever since those water elementals appeared in the Drak'Sotra Fields, a number of Drakkari shaman have come down from the upper tiers of Zul'Drak to take control of them.

I cannot stress enough, <sir/ma'am>, how dangerous that could prove. We do not want them to have water elementals at their disposal.

The commander has ordered that these Drakkari water binders are to be put to the sword. Head south when you're ready.

passages.title: The Drakkari Do Not Need Water Elementals!
passages.text:
Excellent work, sir!

I'll see to it that the commander is apprised of your mission results.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Something for the Pain
passages.text:
Gritty as my men are, they're still mortal.

Wounds and pain diminish their ability to perform their missions. No amount of training changes that simple fact of life.

Thankfully, one of our alchemists has developed a recipe for a salve that binds to our bandages and greatly reduces the pain our soldiers experience.

The salve requires a special poppy these trolls cultivate just west of here. Go to Drak'Sotra Fields and harvest some of them to keep our stockpiles from running out.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Something for the Pain
passages.text: Have you collected the water-poppies, <name>?

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Something for the Pain
passages.text:
Fine specimens, <name>.

On behalf of my soldiers, I thank you for your efforts today.

Captain Rupert is likely the next stop on your patrol. He's stationed at the wall just east of here.

passages.title: The Blessing of Zim'Abwa
passages.text:
I am heartened to see the zeal with which your Argent Crusade is dealing with the Scourge, <race>. I would like to help with your efforts.

The Drakkari trolls of this once-great city used to make regular offerings to their gods, but now neglect them, or worse.

If you were to make offerings to the gods, they would show their appreciation in return.

Zim'Abwa's statue is just to the southwest. Zim'Abwa would gladly accept your offerings of Drakkari artifacts as a sign that you are protecting Zul'Drak.

passages.title: The Blessing of Zim'Abwa
passages.text: <Zim'Abwa stares inscrutably to the north and the south.>

passages.title: The Blessing of Zim'Abwa
passages.text: <If Zim'Abwa could move his face, Zim'Abwa would make a vicious grin.>

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Done to Death
passages.text:
Trust me, <race>. I know....

The smell of burnt flesh has become sickening to even me, a Forsaken. Nevertheless, it is our solemn duty to ensure that our brethren never walk with the Scourge.

Pour this oil on the corpses of our fallen to ensure that we never face them on the battlefield as enemies.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Done to Death
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

It's not the most glorious job on the battlefield, but it must be done. I'll make note of your service in my report.

Captain Grondel is likely waiting for you to the northeast, just outside the amphitheater.

passages.title: Crocolisk Mastery: The Ambush
passages.text:
The largest crocolisk in the basin, known around here as "Bushwhacker" for his ambush prowess, likes to sun himself in the shallow waters of River's Heart. It's the large lake at the basin's center, and is to the east of our camp.

I want you to take the camouflage I've prepared and hide on the western beach of River's Heart and ambush Bushwhacker when he shows himself. Bring back his mighty jaws if you are able to overcome him.

passages.title: Crocolisk Mastery: The Ambush
passages.text: Did our plan work?

passages.title: Crocolisk Mastery: The Ambush
passages.text:
<Debaar listens as you describe the failure of the disguise.>

What do you mean, our plan didn't work as intended?

Well, you did manage to get the kill, to your credit. Look at the size of this jaw! Hemet will be proud of our efforts. This crocolisk was truly a monster.

passages.title: Fortunate Misunderstandings
passages.text:
I sorry! I not mean to get you in trouble!

<The injured oracle stares at you blankly for a long while.>

You save me! We thank you. We going to go back to village now. You come too... you can stay with us! Puppy-men kind of mean anyway.

Let me know when you ready to go, okay?

passages.title: Fortunate Misunderstandings
passages.text: Who you? You stink of puppy-men.

passages.title: Fortunate Misunderstandings
passages.text: You help us? You welcome then, dryskin.

passages.title: Make the Bad Snake Go Away
passages.text:
We were here long before the puppy-men came. This is very sacred place - we will not leave.

You seem like maybe you good, but we have Lafoo stay with you just in case. You understand we think.

There snakes thing that keeps trying to eat our hatchlings. Go with Lafoo and make them stop, okay? Especially big one near waterfall to northeast.

passages.title: Make the Bad Snake Go Away
passages.text:
Snake gone?

Good <race>. We thank you.

passages.title: Gods like Shiny Things
passages.text:
Soo-say said we go with you. You be nice, okay?

Ooh, ooh! We know! We can make Soo-say happy if we bring back more offerings for shrine! We not need to go far, there's always stuffs to dig up around village... just look for sparkles in dirt!

Let's go! Let's go! More offerings for shrine!

passages.title: Gods like Shiny Things
passages.text: Hello dryskin. You get along with Lafoo good?

passages.title: Gods like Shiny Things
passages.text:
Shinies for the Great Rain Stone! Good! Good!

We offer these right away. Lafoo thought of this, yes? He a very smart Rainspeaker.

passages.title: Making Peace
passages.text:
We have great idea. You were friends with puppy-men, they maybe listen to you.

We want you to go give offering to Shaman Vekjik. He southwest where river turns into waterfall. Tell puppy-man we no want fight. Tell him we play nice.

You good <race>. We trust you do this right.

passages.title: Making Peace
passages.text: Puppy-men play nice now?

passages.title: Making Peace
passages.text:
So mean! We only be nice and they only be mean.

They keep messing with great stones... maybe they not know great stones are sacred.

passages.title: Back So Soon?
passages.text:
<High-Oracle Soo-say stares at your forehead for a while before speaking.>

Soo-gan ask for help. We think they might have been attacked by puppy-men again.

We sending you and Jaloot to help... follow west river up to Mistwhisper Refuge. Do what Soo-gan says... hit the puppy-men on the nose if they being mean, they don't like that.

<High-Oracle Soo-say goes back to staring at your forehead as you leave.>

passages.title: Back So Soon?
passages.text:
We think we seen you before. You visit Mistwhisper village sometime already?

Soo-say said you good. Soo-say smart, so we trust you too.

<Mistcaller Soo-gan offers an awkwardly large smile.>

passages.title: The Lost Mistwhisper Treasure
passages.text:
So some puppy-men come and smash blue crystals at Great Mist Stone! Lots of rain and lightning and badness... blue is wrong crystal for Great Mist Stone! Dumb puppy-men.

After lightning, puppy-men stole big treasure we found in the sea-lake. We need treasure back to give to Great Mist Stone! Mist Stone is angry after what the puppy-men did!

One who took it named Tarter... no, Tiktak... no, no... Tartek. That it, Tartek! He went to the camp thing to north. Go get treasure back!

passages.title: The Lost Mistwhisper Treasure
passages.text: Dumb puppy-thieves.

passages.title: The Lost Mistwhisper Treasure
passages.text:
You did it! You strong and nice! Good friend of Mistwhispers!

<Mistcaller Soo-gan lets loose a big toothy grin.>

passages.title: Forced Hand
passages.text:
We try to be nice to puppy-men ever since they came, but they nothing but mean.

We okay with them being dumb - they not do much harm. Now they mess with sacred shrines though. Sacred shrines not for messing with. The Great Stones are here from all the way back when the Great Ones made us.

We wouldn't know what to do if the Great Mist Stone were hurt. Go to their camp to north... make puppy-men stop and not come back!

passages.title: Forced Hand
passages.text: You squash good. Thank you for help.

passages.title: The Angry Gorloc
passages.text:
I not think you be back in time to go out again, but I wrong. I sending Moodle to nearby Mosswalker friends to bop silly Mosswalkers for not coming see shrine. Their village is east, up ridge, northeast of broken pillar.

You go with Moodle! He extra smart Rainspeaker... you listen to him good-like.

passages.title: The Angry Gorloc
passages.text:
Soo-say fumbles a bit, but he's not dumb. I do think he's been far too forgiving though... the puppy-men are not going to stop or leave us alone. The only way to stop them is to kill them... there is no "peace."

<Moodle puffs up his chest and points to himself.>

That I am good at.

passages.title: The Angry Gorloc
passages.text:
Before you say anything, do not assume me as foolish as most of the Oracles you've met. I've been into the world a bit, I've learned your language, and I'm not easily duped.

I knew the Mosswalkers were dead before we ever came, though I didn't know that the undead were behind it.

They are not supposed to be able to enter this land... the destruction of the Lifeblood Pillar must have allowed them in somehow. We must see to it that they leave.

passages.title: Lifeblood of the Mosswalker Shrine
passages.text:
I've always suspected that the pillars have been the main reason for our weather and seclusion from the undead... this confirms it a bit.

Not terribly long ago, there was a sound of a great explosion when the Lifeblood Pillar fell. The weather changed for the mosswalkers almost immediately... it began to snow, something we never see.

They were able to stop the snow by bringing more lifeblood crystals to the Great Moss Stone. Perhaps if we can do the same, it will help ward off the undead as well.

passages.title: Lifeblood of the Mosswalker Shrine
passages.text: The Mosswalkers were good people... they did not deserve this.

passages.title: Lifeblood of the Mosswalker Shrine
passages.text: We might be too late for the shards to make a difference, but our options are somewhat limited.

passages.title: The Mosswalker Savior
passages.text:
There's some small chance that the Mosswalkers are not all dead yet... and at the very least, they deserve to not be butchered like this.

Let's find some revenge for this slaughter and see if there are any to be saved in the process.

passages.title: The Mosswalker Savior
passages.text: I wish I had known how key the pillars and the stones were much earlier... perhaps I could have prevented this.

passages.title: The Mosswalker Savior
passages.text: I'm very glad there were some to be saved... with luck, they'll make it back to Rainspeaker Canopy safely.

passages.title: A Hero's Burden
passages.text:
Perhaps the crystals will ward off the undead gradually, but there is one more thing that must be done.

We need to find the leader of these undead and kill him to ensure there's no one to push the wretches back upon us. If my suspicions are correct, he will be somewhere inside the fallen pillar... the Sundered Shard.

The corpses being dragged there would suggest as much anyway.

I'll place the shards and bring the news to Soo-say... I'll leave the rest up to you.

passages.title: A Hero's Burden
passages.text: <The phylactery rests ominously on the ground next to Artruis' dead form.>

passages.title: A Hero's Burden
passages.text:
<Inside Artruis's Phylactery you see what seems like an endless void... and you think you hear screaming in the distance from somewhere inside.>

<As you're about to leave, you see an object floating in the void, just barely in reach.>

passages.title: Crashed Sprayer
passages.text:
I know that one of those plague sprayers crashed somewhere within Drak'Sotra to the west of us.

Why don't you see if you can find it. I can use the parts from the sprayer to create the device that's going to bring those things down!

passages.title: Crashed Sprayer
passages.text: Do you have the parts? Huh? Do you?

passages.title: Crashed Sprayer
passages.text:
<The specialist steps back a bit when presented with the parts.>

Ew, those things are totally gross!

Okay, okay, hand them over and I'll see what I can do. I probably should have had you take them to a priest first for purification.

passages.title: Pure Evil
passages.text:
We know that Kolramas, the crashed necropolis to the southeast, was carrying a large amount of an ore known as saronite when the trolls shot it down.

My scouts tell me that much of the saronite is strewn about within the innards of that thing.

Eitrigg and his friends back at The Argent Stand want a bunch of the stuff so that they can study it.

I want you to head in there and see if you can collect enough for them.

passages.title: Pure Evil
passages.text:
Yes, <class>?

Please tell me that you have the saronite that we requested Captain Rupert to acquire?

passages.title: Pure Evil
passages.text:
Can you not feel the pure evil of the stuff?

We must use the expertise and magics at our disposal, combined with the power of the Holy Light, to pierce the veil of iniquity surrounding this tainted ore. We must determine its origins.

Quickly, hand the saronite to me!

passages.title: Troll Patrol
passages.text:
Unsheathe that weapon, <race>. It's time to go on patrol!

I've got four posts under my command and it's crucial to our success that they remain in our control. I'm ordering you to visit each of them and offer your assistance.

You can begin with Captain Brandon southeast of here. He'll direct you to the next post when he's finished with you.

Report back to me once you've assisted each of my men. And remember, you'll be more richly rewarded for returning to me quickly - so double-time it!

Dismissed!

passages.title: Troll Patrol
passages.text: Well, <name>, at least you've made it back in one piece. I suppose that's worth something....

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Can You Dig It?
passages.text:
One of our troops came across an old treasure map during our last offensive. If what it shows is true, then there are priceless troll artifacts nearby.

My soldiers have their hands full, pressed between the Drakkari and the Scourge. I need you to follow up on this intelligence.

Take this shovel and use it at the loose dirt mounds to the southwest. Return to me after a diligent search has been conducted.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Can You Dig It?
passages.text:
Thank you for looking into this for me, <name>. I'll make mention of your service in my report.

You'll likely want to visit Captain Rupert next. He's stationed at the wall due east of here.

passages.title: Kick, What Kick?
passages.text:
So you think you can shoot?

Well, let's give it a try. Here, we'll start you out with something nice and gentle. Don't worry, it's got no kick to it at all. Remember, don't point that gun at anything you don't intend to fire at.

Now, when you're ready, just take aim at that apple on top o' old Lucky Wilhelm's head and let 'er fly!

passages.title: Kick, What Kick?
passages.text: Satisfied with the results?

passages.title: Kick, What Kick?
passages.text: You're not a bad shot, but you'll get better with practice. How would you like to make a little wager?

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Throwing Down
passages.text:
Clever...

Just when it seemed we were getting things under control, they tunneled right underneath us and secured the shrine!

Now we're caught between two nethurbian armies and our predicament is worsening by the minute.

As our first course of action, we must stop them from reinforcing. Their tunnels must be sealed.

Take these grenades and throw them down their craters to the northwest.

passages.title: Troll Patrol: Throwing Down
passages.text:
We're not out of the woods by any means, but your efforts have helped to slow the enemy down.

Captain Grondel up in Drak'Agal will likely have need of you.

Farewell, <name>.

passages.title: The Great Hunter's Challenge
passages.text:
So y'have something of a hunter's instinct. You're not a bad shot, and Hemet hasn't driven you out, so he must be planning on including you in the hunt.

How'd you like to have a bit of a competition, just me and you?

Hemet and the others will ask you to help in their hunting. Along the way, you and I will count up the kills we contribute to their goals. Now, this isn't something you can win in the blink of an eye, and you'll find yourself killing many different kinds of creatures. Good luck!

passages.title: The Great Hunter's Challenge
passages.text:
So, you've come to concede already?

<Drostan's jaw drops as you tell him you've already made all your kills.>

No way! How in Azeroth did you do that? I just made my 58th. So close!

But fair's fair. I underestimated you, <name>, but you've earned this victory fair and square.

passages.title: Pa'Troll
passages.text:
Welcome to The Argent Stand, scrub. I am Commander Kunz, but you - you can call me... Commander.

Don't think you're going to just cruise through my region, picking which missions you're going to participate in, answering to no one.

Here, you report to me and you follow my orders to the letter. Understood?!

First, you're going to get familiar with my men and the region we're charged with clearing.

Report to each of them and do as they ask. Return to me when your patrol is done.

passages.title: Pa'Troll
passages.text:
It's about time you got your carcass back here! Thought we'd lost ya to the Scourge - not that it would've been a great loss....

If you're going to continue to serve the Crusade, you'd best make a more impressive showing.

Take note, <race>! Your future patrols will be rewarded based on your timeliness.

Dismissed.

passages.title: Something for the Pain
passages.text:
Gritty as my men are, they're still mortal.

Wounds and pain diminish their ability to perform their missions. No amount of training changes that simple fact of life.

Thankfully, one of our alchemists has developed a recipe for a salve that binds to our bandages and greatly reduces the pain our soldiers experience.

The salve requires a special poppy these trolls cultivate just west of here. Go to Drak'Sotra Fields and harvest some of them to keep our stockpiles from running out.

passages.title: Something for the Pain
passages.text: Have you collected the water-poppies, <name>?

passages.title: Something for the Pain
passages.text:
Fine specimens, <name>.

On behalf of my soldiers, I thank you for your efforts today.

Captain Rupert is likely the next stop on your patrol. He's stationed at the wall just east of here.

passages.title: Throwing Down
passages.text:
Clever...

Just when it seemed we were getting things under control, they tunneled right underneath us and secured the shrine!

Now we're caught between two Nerubian armies and our predicament is worsening by the minute.

As our first course of action, we must stop them from reinforcing. Their tunnels must be sealed.

Take these grenades and throw them down their craters to the northwest.

passages.title: Throwing Down
passages.text: Have you sealed the nerubian tunnels, <name>?

passages.title: Throwing Down
passages.text:
We're not out of the woods by any means, but your efforts have helped to slow the enemy down.

Captain Grondel up in Drak'Agal will likely have need of you.

Farewell, <name>.

passages.title: Creature Comforts
passages.text:
Well, it ain't glamorous, but it needs doin'.

My troops have been fightin' their hearts out while knee-deep in stagnant water for days on end. That just can't be good fer ya.

What they need is a nice fire to dry 'em out and lighten their spirits.

This part of the city's soaked, but the dead roots of these thornwood trees have a way of resistin' the moisture.

Round us up some fuel for burnin' and we'll be mighty grateful.

passages.title: Creature Comforts
passages.text: Ya got the wood fer a fire, <race>?

passages.title: Creature Comforts
passages.text:
Mighty kind of ya, <name>. Mighty kind indeed.

Now you'll be findin' ol' Finklestein due west o' here, just over the rise.

passages.title: Cocooned!
passages.text:
Now that the tunnels have been sealed, our next concern is recovering those who have fallen to the enemy.

With any luck, several of our soldiers are still alive and relatively well inside the nerubian cocoons.

Free them, <class>, while you still can!

passages.title: Cocooned!
passages.text:
These nerubians have taken a heavy toll, <class>.

Nevertheless, I am grateful for your efforts.

passages.title: Stocking the Shelves
passages.text:
Listen, <class>. I realize that it's a lot to ask....

Fresh spider ichor is somewhat hard to come by, even in these heavily infested regions. But Finklestein said he'd settle for no less than a vat of it, and that he needs it soon.

I'll keep my men out in the field collecting reagents, but if the alchemist's order is going to be filled in time, they'll require some assistance.

As you roam the fields of Zul'Drak, keep your eyes peeled for trapdoor crawlers and bring me all of the ichor you can find.

passages.title: Stocking the Shelves
passages.text: Have you collected the reagents I need, <class>?

passages.title: Stocking the Shelves
passages.text:
These look to be excellent samples, <name>.

Thank you for your assistance.

passages.title: Clipping Their Wings
passages.text:
Ever since Finklestein's arrival, I've been relegated to collecting various ingredients for his experiments and recipes.

I'll follow my orders as I've vowed to do, but I'm a seasoned veteran. I've taken part in dozens of conflicts. I'd much rather be on the front lines, having a more direct impact on the Crusade's outcome here.

Help me, <race>. Collect some bat wings for me so that I might get back to the real action sooner.

passages.title: Clipping Their Wings
passages.text: Have you finished collecting those bat wings for Finklestein?

passages.title: Clipping Their Wings
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>.

I thank you for your assistance.

passages.title: Returned Sevenfold
passages.text:
The agents of the Lich King have foolishly trespassed upon these lands where the power of life rules supreme. All harm they inflict will be returned to them sevenfold.

The monster directly responsible for corrupting the land is known as Thalgran Blightbringer; you will find him just to the north of here. Take this ward and use it to reflect the power of death upon him. Show the Scourge that the power of life prevails above all.

passages.title: Returned Sevenfold
passages.text: Is it done, <name>?

passages.title: Returned Sevenfold
passages.text:
You continue to prove yourself, <name>.  Perhaps I was too quick to judge you.

I had assumed you were here with the poachers who were recently stranded in my lands, but perhaps you're ready to put that behind you.

passages.title: Powering the Waygate - The Makers' Overlook
passages.text:
We cannot stop now, <race>. You've triggered the first switch, but one remains.

The titans constructed a second vantage point where they oversaw their creations. You'll find it to the east, high in the mountains.

Pull the activation switch theta inside the overlook and the waygate will open.

passages.title: Powering the Waygate - The Makers' Overlook
passages.text: The waygate is active, <name>.  It is time!

passages.title: Post-partum Aggression
passages.text:
Broodmother Slivina's likely to be a snarling ball of teeth, spikes, and talons. You've gone and stolen her children away and no mother takes kindly to that.

'Tis true they hatched from eggs, but she loves the little beasts no less than your mother loves you.

She'll be desperate and fierce in equal measures, everything Hemet loves in a target. You and he, along with that mammoth, should be a match for her.

She's on her perch at the northern edge of the Savage Thicket and hungers for revenge.

passages.title: Post-partum Aggression
passages.text: Well, you're alive. How did you fare?

passages.title: Post-partum Aggression
passages.text: Well, I had a whole speech prepared, but the old man himself has some words he wants to say to you.

passages.title: The Blessing of Zim'Torga
passages.text:
Hexxer Ubungo probably told you about making offerings to the gods of Zul'Drak. Zim'Abwa is not the only god that stands forgotten by the Drakkari.

We have taken refuge within the presence of Zim'Torga, the Mother of Prosperity. As with Zim'Abwa, if you were to give offerings of the Drakkari to her, she is sure to give you her blessing.

passages.title: The Blessing of Zim'Torga
passages.text: <You can feel the eyes of the Mother of Prosperity upon you. She is wondering what a <race> such as yourself is doing standing before her.>

passages.title: The Blessing of Zim'Torga
passages.text:
<Zim'Torga's thoughts pervade your own. She senses the offerings you are about give to her and is pleased.>

<She conveys that you will be appropriately rewarded.>

passages.title: Exterminate the Intruders
passages.text:
I am an embodiment of but one aspect of Freya, daughter of the titans. I am the Lifewarden -- I was left here to protect this land against the threat of the Scourge.

I never anticipated the Lich King would send willing living servants to do his work.

I could easily crush these cultists myself, but I am all that stands between the undead armies and the rest of the basin. Go, <name>. Deliver my wrath to these insolent trespassers.

passages.title: Exterminate the Intruders
passages.text: You speak the truth.  The intruders at the camp were dealt with... but I'm afraid it might have been too late.

passages.title: The Emblazoned Runeblade
passages.text:
The single most important piece of equipment to a death knight is the runeblade. It is through the runeblade that a death knight commands the powers of frost, blood and the unholy. The runeblade also acts as a vessel to store the death knight's runic power.

The time has come to create your first runeblade. Search the weapon racks on this floor and locate a battle-worn sword. Once found, take the sword to a nearby runeforge and use it to create a runeblade.

passages.title: The Emblazoned Runeblade
passages.text: The runeblade is an extension of your being. A <class> cannot battle without a runeblade.

passages.title: The Emblazoned Runeblade
passages.text: Well done, <name>. You have successfully created your first runebladed weapon. With it you will sow the seeds of chaos and destruction! In your wake will be a bloodied field of battle, littered with the corpses of all that would dare oppose the Scourge.

passages.title: The Lifewarden's Wrath
passages.text:
We were not quick enough, <name>. The cultist scum have arrived at the Glimmering Pillar and are making preparations to destroy it, I can sense them.

We don't have much time. Blow upon this horn atop the Glimmering Pillar to channel my power through the crystal.

We shall show this scum to not trifle with the titans' creations.

passages.title: The Lifewarden's Wrath
passages.text: Have you taken care of the cultists, <name>?

passages.title: The Lifewarden's Wrath
passages.text:
Impressive.  I wasn't expecting a mere mortal to prove as worthy an ally as you.

I fear our efforts have not been sufficient, however.  The Scourge shows no signs of stopping.

passages.title: The Leaders at Jin'Alai
passages.text:
You thinkin' what Ahunae thinkin', mon?

Some of the Drakkari trolls have gathered at the Pools of Jin'Alai to the southwest. We be needin' to draw out their leaders, and Ahunae knows just how you be doin' it, too!

Go in there and kill those trolls. When you kill enough, their leaders show up.

When they show up next to their totems, you make sure to be gettin' the treasure of Kutube'sa, Gawanil, and Chulo the Mad, mon.

passages.title: The Leaders at Jin'Alai
passages.text: The <class> must be back talkin' to Ahunae because the <class> has all that treasure.

passages.title: The Leaders at Jin'Alai
passages.text:
The scalper thinkin' that you be his kind of <race>!

What's these candybars doin' in here? What we do with this, mon?

Ahunae say that you can have them back!

passages.title: It Could Be Anywhere!
passages.text:
When I found out that Miss Boulian was helping Nesingwary with his expedition, I signed up as a deckhand immediately. You see, I'd been meaning to marry her for months!

I had it all planned out. I was going to propose the very night of the shipwreck... but now the ring is gone. I've searched everywhere!

I know it might sound crazy, but I know the engagement ring is in the Basin. If some Venture Company didn't steal it, maybe a wild creature ate it. But it's here somewhere... I just know it!

passages.title: It Could Be Anywhere!
passages.text: The ring, <name>!  Please... tell me you've found it!

passages.title: It Could Be Anywhere!
passages.text:
You did it!  You actually found it!

I don't know... I don't know how to thank you!

passages.title: Breaking Through Jin'Alai
passages.text:
I have been trying to commune with the gods. However, the medicine men at the Pools of Jin'Alai are performing rituals that are interfering with my attempts.

It is imperative that we break through their obtrusion. If you were to head southwest into the pools area, I am certain that you would come across the cauldrons they are using for their magic.

Disturb each of the cauldrons to bring down their ritual that is blocking me.

passages.title: Breaking Through Jin'Alai
passages.text:
Yes, I can already feel the difference. Thank you.

Let us see if we can make contact with the gods now.

passages.title: You Can Run, But You Can't Hide
passages.text:
Once the Scourge have a target in their sights, they'll stop at nothing to acquire it.

You're doomed to a mindless existence as a walking corpse....

<Stefan's face twists into a cruel grin.>

... unless we can use their desires against them.

I'll explain later. I have complex magic to prepare which requires certain material components.

Travel due east of here to the Reliquary of Agony. Slay abominations and gather the ghoul drool you'll find there then return to me with their remnants.

passages.title: You Can Run, But You Can't Hide
passages.text: Have you brought me the components I asked for, <name>?

passages.title: You Can Run, But You Can't Hide
passages.text:
<Stefan sifts through the foul components.>

Well, it's far from perfect, but it'll have to do. Now brace yourself, <class>. This is where it gets good....

passages.title: Kickin' Nass and Takin' Manes
passages.text:
Before you meet Nass, there's something you should know.

He got a toxic dose of blight back in the day, and now he's deaf, blind, and mostly numb.

It's not all bad, though. He's virtually immune to the stuff now, which makes him perfect for certain tasks - like the one I'm about to give you.

There are many freshly scourged trolls nearby and we need to study the blight's effect on them. Take Nass, and this boot. When you've slain a troll, give him a good kick and he'll know to take a hair sample.

passages.title: Kickin' Nass and Takin' Manes
passages.text:
You know, you remind me an awful lot of my Nass.

Maybe it's just the nose...

passages.title: Some Make Lemonade, Some Make Liquor
passages.text:
Life's tossed me a cartload of lemons this time! When the ship ran aground, the kegs carrying my best brew burst! All we have now are a few bottles of rum, and it won't sustain a thirsty expedition!

We need to get some booze cooking, and fast!!

The trees in the Wildgrowth Mangal, to the east, seem laden with fruit, but it's too high for me to reach. Look for good, strong vines, see if you can use it to shake some of that fruit out of the trees. Bring me whatever you can find.

passages.title: Some Make Lemonade, Some Make Liquor
passages.text: Did you have luck winning any of that fruit from those darn tall and stingy trees?

passages.title: Some Make Lemonade, Some Make Liquor
passages.text: Well, that's a better assortment than I would've expected from this place. Now, for the important question: can we distill it into anything drinkable? We'd better get started.

passages.title: Near Miss
passages.text:
It was either wisdom or luck that prevented you from wearing this choker, <race>.

Either way, your acquiring it was no random occurance. You've been targeted by someone, or something....

Take your choker to Bloodrose, here. Let her demonstrate the fate that nearly befell you.

passages.title: Near Miss
passages.text: Yes, <race>?

passages.title: Near Miss
passages.text:
Now you've observed the fate that was meant to befall you.

As I mentioned before, this was no coincidence. The creation of such a device is very involved, and the required resources would not be squandered on a random target.

The simple truth of the matter is this; You're wanted by the Scourge....

passages.title: Close Call
passages.text:
It was either wisdom or luck that prevented you from wearing this choker, <race>.

Either way, your acquiring it was no random occurence. You've been targeted by someone, or something....

Take your choker to Bloodrose, here. Let her demonstrate the fate that nearly befell you.

passages.title: Close Call
passages.text: Yes, <race>?

passages.title: Close Call
passages.text:
Now you've observed the fate that was meant to befall you.

As I mentioned before, this was no random act. The creation of such a device is very involved. You've somehow caught the attention of the Scourge leadership.

The question is not how, why, or even who... but what will we do about it?

passages.title: The Frozen Earth
passages.text:
We captured these elementals from nearby, and I have plenty of defenders now. But, it takes a great deal of power to make them strong enough to stand up to our enemies.

The frozen earth at Drak'Mabwa to the northwest have what I need to maintain our defenses. I'll need more of their essence if I'm to keep this up.

passages.title: The Frozen Earth
passages.text: I hope that you've returned with enough. The attacks from the Pools of Jin'Alai have become more desperate after what you did to them.

passages.title: The Frozen Earth
passages.text: Thank you, <class>. Those essences should be enough to fuel my casting for quite some time.

passages.title: Death Comes From On High
passages.text:
Towering above this platform is the eye of Acherus. From it you will call forth a probe that you will then use to analyze Scarlet Crusade fortifications at New Avalon. The eye has a host of powers that should make the acquisition of this data simple.

Use the eye's siphon to analyze the forge, town hall, hold, and chapel. The eye's control mechanisms are located on either side of this platform. Waste no more time, <name>.

The Scourge will have this place. The Lich King commands it!

passages.title: Death Comes From On High
passages.text: Our assault upon the Scarlet Crusade will become legend.

passages.title: Death Comes From On High
passages.text:
They prepare for battle - as expected - but there is something else. I sense an old enemy. An enemy that I destroyed long ago...

It matters not. We will send the full might of the Scourge against them before they have a chance to evacuate their homes and put in place their defenses.

passages.title: Silver Lining
passages.text:
Once the Scourge have a target in their sights, they'll stop at nothing to acquire it.

You're doomed to a mindless existence as a walking corpse....

<Stefan's face twists into a cruel grin.>

... unless we can use their desires against them.

I'll explain later. I have complex magic to prepare which requires certain material components.

Travel due east of here to the land beneath the Reliquary of Agony. Slay the ghouls and abominations you'll find there and return to me with their remnants.

passages.title: Silver Lining
passages.text: Have you brought the components I asked for, <name>?

passages.title: Silver Lining
passages.text:
<Stefan sifts through the foul components.>

Well, it's far from perfect, but it'll have to do.

Now brace yourself, <class>. This is where it gets good....

passages.title: Still At It
passages.text:
Now that we've got the raw materials, I've had my assistant ready the still. He'll oversee the process, but I want you to help keep everything under control. You might be tempted to think that we just throw everything into the still and let it sit, but you're wrong.

Ingredients and heat need to be added at certain times, and the pressure regulated at others. You'll have no more than 10 seconds to react to a situation. Speak with "Tipsy" McManus when you're ready to start distilling.

passages.title: Still At It
passages.text: Well, how did it turn out?

passages.title: Still At It
passages.text:
<Grimbooze gives the cask a shake.>

There's something in here, but the million gold question is, can you drink it? Don't you go anywhere; you'll be responsible for overseeing the sampling of the product, too.

passages.title: The Taste Test
passages.text:
And now for the moment of truth!

<Grimbooze chuckles.>

I've always wanted to say that. Normally, I'd debut a new drink at a banquet, but we can't have one in the middle of the jungle.

Instead, just take samples to a few trusted friends and return with their comments. Let's see, we'll definitely want Hemet Nesingwary's opinion, and Hadrius Harlowe's, too. They're here in camp. You'll want to head over to Lakeside Landing, near the center of the Basin and offer Tamara Wobblesprocket a taste.

passages.title: The Taste Test
passages.text:
Two out of three drinkers agree, eh? Not bad for a first try. Not bad at all. I suppose I'll have to whip up something else for Tamara by way of apology.

Now... what should we call this creation?

passages.title: Dressing Down
passages.text:
There... I've created a disguise that should make you indistinguishable from the Scourge.

You'll be free to walk among them as long as the disguise holds. Only the blightguards will be able to see through my illusion. Watch out for them!

Another thing you must know is that the disguise is unstable and may drop unexpectedly, so stay alert.

Let's test it out. Use the choker and visit the Scourge merchant just east of here. Return to me with a bottle of bitter plasma.

passages.title: Dressing Down
passages.text:
Well, <name>?

Did you purchase that flask?

passages.title: Dressing Down
passages.text:
So? How are you enjoying scourge life?

Believe me, it's not all it's cracked up to be....

passages.title: Suit Up!
passages.text:
There... I've created a disguise that should make you indistinguishable from the Scourge.

You'll be free to walk among them as long as the disguise holds. Only the blightguards will be able to see through my illusion. Watch out for them!

Another thing you must know is that the disguise is unstable and may drop unexpectedly, so stay alert.

Let's test it out. Use the choker and visit the Scourge vendor just east of here. Return to me with a bottle of bitter plasma.

passages.title: Suit Up!
passages.text:
Well, <name>?

Did you purchase that flask?

passages.title: Suit Up!
passages.text:
So? How are you enjoying Scourge life?

Believe me, it's not all it's cracked up to be....

passages.title: Feedin' Da Goolz
passages.text:
Git o'er heer, gool! Yeh, I talkin' to yoo.

It feedin' time now. Gotta git da grub ta all da gools!

Speshal grub dis time! Bowels an' brainz bowl... num, num, num.

Jus drop da bowl nexta da gool. Gud way ta make frenz.

Yoo got goolfrenz? Ha, ha, hah!

passages.title: Feedin' Da Goolz
passages.text: Num num!
