Perhaps you do have the heart of a warrior.

Time will tell...

passages.title: The Admiral Revealed
passages.text:
When High General Abbendis was confronted at New Hearthglen, the grand admiral protected himself within an impenetrable sphere of magic before making his escape.

I am particularly adept at nullifying magic.

Take this to use against him inside The Hidden Hollow when he puts the sphere up. I wish that I could be there to see the look on his face when you do it.

Deal with him.

passages.title: The Admiral Revealed
passages.text:
MAL'GANIS?!!

<The lord-commander laughs with abandon.>

The fools were taken in by the demons yet again and now they are destroyed!

I trust that my favorite <class> will stick around long enough to help us finish off the rest of them? Perhaps one of these would convince you?

passages.title: On Brann's Trail
passages.text:
After the discovery of Brann's journal in Grizzly Hills, we've only had one other communication from Brann. A mysterious note found its way to Explorers' League headquarters in Ironforge, with no indication of where it came from. All it said was that we're to meet Brann at his camp and help him with his search.

From what I can tell, the camp should be located northeast of here, across the Bor's Breath River and at the foot of some ruins from the Path of the Titans.

passages.title: On Brann's Trail
passages.text: Did you find Brann's camp?

passages.title: On Brann's Trail
passages.text:
<Archaeologist Andorin looks at you expectantly.>

You were supposed to come back with Brann, not a piece of paper. What's going on here?

passages.title: Sniffing Out the Perpetrator
passages.text:
The tone of Brann's note suggests he meant to bury something with the note, maybe a pack of some kind. You're sure this was all you found?

Okay, I'm going to have you take one of these frosthounds with you. The frostborn use them for tracking. Bring it to the destroyed camp and let it get Brann's scent.

It should at least lead you to the location of those missing possessions, and if we're lucky, Brann himself.

passages.title: Sniffing Out the Perpetrator
passages.text: You... you're not a member of the Explorers' League, at least not one I remember. But, if you recovered the communicator, they must've sent you. Good, that's almost what I was hoping for.

passages.title: WANTED: Ragemane's Flipper
passages.text:
Posted by Chief Rageclaw:

Chief Rageclaw trusty lion seal, Ragemane, bite hand that feed him. Rageclaw say Ragemane no more good because of bad Drakuru trolls. Chief Rageclaw very sad to ask that Ragemane be killeded and Ragemane flipper be returned to chief as proof.

You find Ragemane to southeast, at Rageclaw Lake.

Chief Rageclaw sorry for bad writing. First time use one of these things; plus, Chief Rageclaw is wolvar, not person.

passages.title: WANTED: Ragemane's Flipper
passages.text: Poor Ragemane. He was gift from brother-in-law.

passages.title: WANTED: Ragemane's Flipper
passages.text:
<Chief Rageclaw cries.>

Had Ragemane since pup. Sad day for Rageclaw. First troll attack Rageclaw, then troll make Ragemane bad. Rageclaw never trade with troll again!

passages.title: Pieces to the Puzzle
passages.text:
Thank the Light that someone got my message. Now that I'm safe from the iron dwarves, I need to ask your help with something. I've got a lead on Norgannon's keystone, which guards access to Ulduar's archives, but the Titans divided it into two pieces and secreted them away.

One of the pieces, the keystone's shell, is held within the Inventor's Library on the northern coast, south of Ulduar itself. The first thing you'll need to do is retrieve the fragments of an access disk from the library's guardians.

passages.title: Pieces to the Puzzle
passages.text: Did you complete the disk?

passages.title: Pieces to the Puzzle
passages.text: Wonderful! Now that we have the disk, you must use it to open the Inventor's vault!

passages.title: This Just In: Fire Still Hot!
passages.text:
Trolls attack Rageclaw Den and kick Rageclaw out! It get worse. Trolls now burning village! This very bad. Chief make top Rageclaw shaman, Moky, do study on fire. Results very surprising! Fire still hot and can burn things.

Will you help Rageclaw and put fire out? Moky has special Rageclaw fire extinguisher for you. Use special fire extinguisher to put out fire at Rageclaw Den to southeast. Sometimes take many sprays to douse fire, but extinguisher always have water! Rageclaw magic strong!

passages.title: This Just In: Fire Still Hot!
passages.text: It strange because I know you put fire out, but fire still burning. Maybe this thing not so good after all, eh? Still, Moky pay you for what you do! Hopefully troll burn too!

passages.title: Data Mining
passages.text:
That disk you assembled... it's blank! That crafty Mimir must've hidden the information somewhere else. Look around the Inventor's Library; do you see any databanks there?

That might be what you need to do with the disk. Try using it near some of those databanks. Perhaps it's set to retrieve and store information from them. After you've tried your hand at that, contact me again and let me know what you've found. Meanwhile, I'll be trying to track down the other half of the archive key.

passages.title: Data Mining
passages.text: Did you try using the disk? What did you find?

passages.title: Data Mining
passages.text:
<Brann looks at the disk as you hold it up.>

I can't tell if there's anything stored there or not! You have to tell me what happened.

<You describe the data retrieval process.>

So it worked? At least we can count on Mimir to be systematic. Can't say that for the rest of these Keepers from what I've been hearing...

passages.title: Trolls Is Gone Crazy!
passages.text:
Drakuru... You know who this troll is? I think bad troll are controlled by the Drakuru troll. They call themself Drakuru trolls - that how I know. Now you see why I am chief of Rageclaw. Smartest of all wolvar!

But that not why I talk to you now. Bad troll come and kick Rageclaw out of den. Rageclaw that no run away held as prisoner in village. You go to Rageclaw Den, southeast, and free captured Rageclaw. Kill troll for lock opener. You maybe kill many troll for many lock opener.

passages.title: Trolls Is Gone Crazy!
passages.text:
Rageclaw thank you, <name>. Though Rageclaw Den probably lost forever and troll-Rageclaw friendship also lost forever... and also now I think of it, Ragemane lost forever too. Also brother-in-law. He gone. Hrm, have you seen Chief's mate? I think she gone too.

Maybe you go now. Chief a little depressed.

passages.title: When All Else Fails
passages.text:
So... so I don't think we're going to be getting a good foothold in those mountains.

Trust me, I'm not one to give up easily... but between freezing engines, nasty vrykul women, territorial dragon want-to-bes and the half a dozen other nasties settled in the area, this just ain't happening.

Don't let that dissuade you though! Just because we can't get a foothold doesn't mean we won't get you there... one-way trips are pretty simple when you get down to it.

<Ricket nods at some nearby rockets.>

passages.title: When All Else Fails
passages.text:
Ow! That looked painful. It was a pretty grand entrance though, lad!

Welcome to Frosthold! Are ya here to help us find a path into Icecrown?

passages.title: Offering Thanks
passages.text:
Ah! Thanks for coming up here, <lad/lass>.

Judging by your wide eyes and shivering hands, I'd venture a guess that you're somewhat new. Sounds like it would be good for you to meet our gracious hosts then!

We've got some extra medical supplies... to be honest, we weren't expecting to have such a comfortable setup. Go ahead and give this crate to Glorthal over there, and lend them a hand if you would too. We don't want them to think we're ungrateful for how welcoming they've been.

passages.title: Offering Thanks
passages.text: Hello.

passages.title: Offering Thanks
passages.text:
Medical supplies? Thank you! Not exactly sure what to do with them to be honest, but I'm sure they'll be useful.

It's good to meet you... there's such a colorful variety among your peoples. We're not used to having visitors up this way very often - it's good to have some fresh company.

passages.title: Missing Scouts
passages.text:
There is something that I could use a hand with now that I have you.

We have a few scouts that are extremely late in returning. The peaks are harsh... but these boys know what they're doing.

Head to the east... along the Bor's Breath valley and near Bor's Fall... they should be out that direction. If you find any sign of one of them, bring me back news immediately. We have a few enemies in the area - if any of them are getting a bit uppity, the more warning the better.

passages.title: Missing Scouts
passages.text:
When a scout doesn't come back for this long... that's about the expected result. The harpies then?

King Stormheart has us train hard year round... he's turned us into amazing fighters. At times like this, I understand why it's necessary. He's the wisest and strongest leader I've yet seen among our people... don't let his peachy skin fool ya.

passages.title: Loyal Companions
passages.text:
Fresh blood! Good to meet ya! I've got some work if you've got some time.

Off to the east are the Foot Steppes... pretty hard land, but there's quite a group of rhino that graze there. Our birds have a taste for that rhino meat, but it's always a bit dangerous for them to go hunting with all of the proto-drakes that nest around there.

If you're keen, head over that way and get some rhino meat, bring it back to the peaks above here, and then use it to feed some of the eagles that nest there.

passages.title: Loyal Companions
passages.text: These birds have been loyal to us for a long time... we get on pretty well.

passages.title: Loyal Companions
passages.text: Thank you, kindly... and I'm sure they're quite appreciative too. They make powerful allies; you'll be well off being on this side of their graces.

passages.title: Stemming the Aggressors
passages.text:
Damn harpies. We've beat that bunch into submission more times than I can remember... and they stay quiet for a time after each bout. This time, I'd thought that maybe it sunk in.

Apparently not.

Their memory may be a bit short, but if their numbers are thinned enough, they'll keep to themselves. Head into the valleys in the north and east and clear out a fair chunk of them for me, will ya?

passages.title: Stemming the Aggressors
passages.text: It's dirty work, I know, but we appreciate it. Now what was the name the scout mentioned... Sirana?

passages.title: Baby Stealers
passages.text:
A few weeks ago, if you looked up, you'd see dozens of those beautiful eagles soaring the skies. Now, only a few if any. They've taken to staying with their nests nearly all the time now because the harpies have been stealing their eggs.

The harpies have grown a taste for eagle flesh, it seems... the sick wretches are caring for the eggs long enough to feast on the hatchlings. Go into the valleys to the north or the east and find the eggs... bring them back here, and I'll take them back to the nests.

passages.title: Baby Stealers
passages.text: We'll get this harpy problem taken care of... the eagles will be free to soar the skies again soon.

passages.title: Baby Stealers
passages.text:
Good stuff, lad. You're making fast friends.

If you stop back by soon, I'm sure we can find one that will let you ride... they should know that you're trustworthy now.

passages.title: Sirana Iceshriek
passages.text:
This Sirana Iceshriek sounds like the one that's spurring the harpies to be more aggressive. If we kill her, I suspect their attacks won't last long afterwards.

One of our stormriders claims to have spotted her circling the peak directly northwest of here. Go find the wench and put her down. Let's see this done.

passages.title: Sirana Iceshriek
passages.text:
It's done then. Thank you.

I've spoken with Fjorlin - he said that his men will take charge of keeping the harpies down a bit. As long as we don't let up again, they won't find the courage to think they can attack our people.

I know this wasn't the most tasteful work - take this as a token of my appreciation.

passages.title: Pushed Too Far
passages.text:
You were there with Loken, weren't you? The iron dwarves captured Veranus, the brood mother of the proto-drakes. The drakes don't seem even a little bit happy about the situation... they've gotten very aggressive.

They've pushed into stormcrest territory and the eagles have taken to an all out fight with them. It's time to return the favor. We're riding to the Foot Steppes and slaughtering them there.

King Stormheart left this hammer to me - make good use and see to it that I get it back.

passages.title: Pushed Too Far
passages.text: This is completely out of control.

passages.title: Pushed Too Far
passages.text: I don't see the drakes being dissuaded so easily. Stop back by tomorrow if you think you can spare more time to help.

passages.title: Ancient Relics
passages.text:
Why hello thar!

Before you be headin' off to do your grand questin' and adventure, might I beg a wee favor of ya, <lad/lass>?

These mountains be packed full'a precious relics and baubles... this place be a dream come true for tha league. I'd be much obliged if ya could bring any such treasures you stumble upon back ta me. You can even share in me ale for tha trouble! Trust me <lad/lass>, that's a rich deal!

passages.title: Ancient Relics
passages.text: Did ya find some o' dem relics for me?

passages.title: Ancient Relics
passages.text:
Beaut! Yer a good one you are.

Tilt one back wi' me! Let us celebrae' this glorious find!

passages.title: Fervor of the Frostborn
passages.text:
I be more than willing ta lend my shelter and home ta travelers in need, but I'm nae too keen ta force my people inte yer affairs.

I'll tell ye what... my people are warriors, straight and true. On the day a frostborn becomes a man, he has ta prove himself in battle. He has ta show us that he'll not let size hold'm back.

Show me yer as strong and fierce as one of my men, and I'll have them lend ye an ear or a blade. Speak ta Fjorlin over by the cliff to the south there and he'll put ye ta the test.

passages.title: Fervor of the Frostborn
passages.text: Ha! Grand tale lad... perhaps ye have a bit of frostborn blood in ye, eh? Yer not just talk anyway, and that's what I needed to hear.

passages.title: Unwelcome Guests
passages.text:
Our scouts have spotted iron dwarves in the valley north of here. I overheard King Stormheart sending you to visit Drom and I'm admittedly a bit worried about'm.

If you find any iron dwarves when you head down there, put'm down hard and fast for me, eh? I dun think they know exactly where we are or how to get here just yet, and I'd prefer to keep it that way.

passages.title: Unwelcome Guests
passages.text:
Grim news, lad. Those iron dwarves seem to be increasing in numbers... we've been seeing them all over the mountains. I smell war coming.

Thank you for dealing with this bunch... a little more time bought.

passages.title: The Lonesome Watcher
passages.text:
I never found the core... but I've often spoken to the keeper Creteus, and his omissions give him away. You'll find Creteus over the mountains to the east, in the Foot Steppes, keeping watch on the Engine of the Makers. The core might well be in there, but you'll need to win Creteus's favor.

The iron dwarves were here looking for something... it might well be the core. They took my ring. Find their leader, get the ring back, and show it to Creteus so that he knows I sent you.

passages.title: The Lonesome Watcher
passages.text:
Hello, <race>.

I am pleased that you have opted to utilize your tongue over your blade when making my acquaintance. I have found that a more and more rare quality among your kind of late.

passages.title: The Lonesome Watcher
passages.text:
Drom's ring? I am to assume Drom is not well if he did not introduce you directly. I am sorry to hear of that. Drom is a noble dwarf, if an inquisitive one.

On what business have you come then?

passages.title: The Hidden Relic
passages.text:
During your absence, I was privileged enough to parley with the dwarf Brann Bronzebeard. This dwarf indicated his purpose for seeking the keystone, and I am satisfied that it is for satisfactory intent... I believe this dwarf may be the entity for which the keystone was created.

Norgannon's Core is located in the Frigid Tomb to the southeast. Its guardians are ancient beings of ice, and they will not welcome your presence. Best these guardians and retrieve the keystone with my blessing, <race>.

passages.title: The Hidden Relic
passages.text: <As the chest opens, air rushes out into the chamber, carrying with it the musty smell of something that has been here for countless years. Norgannon's Core rests in the bottom of the chest, undisturbed by the ages.>

passages.title: The Master Explorer
passages.text:
Combining the keystone will require Norgannon's Binding - a device located in the Engine of the Makers, the large pit beside us. Brann should be down there with the other half of the keystone now. I have instructed him on the use of the device. He awaits your presence.

I will do what I can to keep the iron dwarves occupied, but I do not have confidence that I will hold them for long. King Stormheart is returning to the defense of Frosthold with some of his men shortly. Please hurry, <race>.

passages.title: The Master Explorer
passages.text: Hey there, lad! Good to meet ya in person. Did you find it?

passages.title: The Master Explorer
passages.text:
You're brilliant, lad! Brilliant! This will be a glorious day indeed.

Quickly, hand me the core before those iron dwarves make their way down here.

passages.title: Ancient Relics
passages.text:
Welcome to the peaks.

I have a simple request before you head off on whatever grand jaunt you have planned. There are relics and treasures of ancient Ulduar scattered through these mountains. Most are likely in possession of the various sentient races.

Return any that you find to me, and I will reward you in kind. Perhaps I'll even let you partake on my many potent ales.

passages.title: Ancient Relics
passages.text: Were you able to find the relics of which I spoke?

passages.title: Ancient Relics
passages.text: These will do nicely! I am much obliged. Perhaps a drink for your troubles?

passages.title: Orders From Drakuru
passages.text:
Minions be hearin' da call of your masta! Da Lich King be givin' Drakuru full control of da armies of da Scourge in Zul'Drak. We be commanded ta kill everyting.

EVERYTING MUST DIE!

We be processin' all da corpses in da Dead Fields and sendin' em up ta Prince Navarius' crew in Zeramas for Scourgin'! Notin' goes ta waste on Drakuru's watch!

Soon we be drinkin' da blood of da prophets ta become stronger dan eva before! Zul'Drak and Gundrak gonna fall to da Scourge!

passages.title: Orders From Drakuru
passages.text: Drakuru, eh? I've heard the name before...

passages.title: Orders From Drakuru
passages.text:
If this is the same Drakuru from Drak'Tharon Keep we are going to need... outside assistance.

Death knights of Acherus are stationed nearby, undoubtedly following the same trail of Scourge destruction that lead the Argent Crusade here. As half of our army is tied up at the Argent Stand, battling crazed Drakkari trolls, we will have to join forces with the Knights of the Ebon Blade.

<Lantinga mutters under his breath.>

I was hoping I'd never have to see those scoundrels again after Light's Hope...

passages.title: The Ebon Watch
passages.text:
West of here, across the ruined roads and structures, is the death knight encampment of Ebon Watch.

<Crusader Lord Lantinga rolls up Drakuru's orders.>

Take these orders and deliver them to Stefan Vadu. He is the death knight in command at Ebon Watch. Let him know that the Argent Crusade will deal with Prince Navarius. They'll have to handle Drakuru.

Be careful, <name>. The way to Ebon Watch is teeming with Scourge.

passages.title: The Ebon Watch
passages.text: What have you got there, <race>?

passages.title: The Ebon Watch
passages.text:
<Stefan reads the missive, then crumples it up and tosses it into the fire.>

Old news. The Argent Crusade is - once again - late to the party. We've been tracking Drakuru since Grizzly Hills. He is slated for eradication.

passages.title: The Drakkensryd
passages.text:
This is it. You've passed all the tests of the Hyldsmeet... all but one. You've risen among our sisters' best and fiercest.

The final test is at hand. The Drakkensryd - the true test of a Hyldnir's worth and warrior spirit. It'll be you, your riding drake, a chained harpoon and a score of your sisters vying for dominance.

Show no quarter. None will be expected.

passages.title: The Drakkensryd
passages.text: Sif... is that you?

passages.title: It's All Fun and Games
passages.text:
The Knights of the Ebon Blade want to take the Scourge base known as The Shadow Vault to the northwest. I have a contact in their group who has asked for help.

The first step is to blind the Lich King. He's using a device known as The Ocular to watch the area, which floats above the vault's spires.

Our dwarves have created something for you to use against it. After the 'eye' has been destroyed, find Baron Sliver on the vault grounds. He's pretending to still be under the Lich King's will.

passages.title: It's All Fun and Games
passages.text:
The Ocular still stands! Thassarian was a fool to trust you.

Whoever you are, don't return again until it is destroyed. My position here must not be compromised!

passages.title: It's All Fun and Games
passages.text:
Perhaps now we can really get something done. Don't be fooled though, the Lich King can still 'see' through his Scourge minions.

That's why you're here.

passages.title: SCRAP-E
passages.text:
This card allows the user to access the control panel of the scrapbot designated SCRAP-E, in order to perform maintenance and reprogram the bot's directives.

SCRAP-E appears to be assigned to the interior of the building at The Inventor's Library. The card displays a list of the bot's broken components and failing systems. With the proper parts, the bot can be restored to working condition.

passages.title: SCRAP-E
passages.text: <You open SCRAP-E's access panel.>

passages.title: SCRAP-E
passages.text: <You begin performing the repairs indicated by the access card. When the repairs are complete, you close the access panel and throw the power switch.>

passages.title: The Prototype Console
passages.text:
Designation SCRAP-E.

Directive: Maintain consoles and databases of Inventor's Library in Keeper Mimir's absences.

Time since last maintenance cycle: 489 days.

Status of schematic data: unknown.

Current tasks: Repair prototype console.

passages.title: The Prototype Console
passages.text: You examine the display on the repaired prototype console. At least one of Mimir's schematics seems to have survived the long period between maintenance cycles. From the diagrams and instructions displayed in the schematic's file, you could easily construct the mechagnome shown.

passages.title: I Have an Idea, But First...
passages.text:
When I was in the - ahem - employ of the Lich King, we would often use a device known as a sovereign rod to keep some of the more intelligent Scourge in line.

I require that you assist me in the construction of a new one.

Luckily for you, all of the necessary components are at hand: a cultist rod, an abomination hook, a geist rope, and a handful of Scourge essences.

This should not be difficult, <class>.

passages.title: I Have an Idea, But First...
passages.text: When you've managed to acquire that which I have asked of you, I will fashion the device, with a few modifications for our purposes, and we'll be on with our business.

passages.title: I Have an Idea, But First...
passages.text:
Quickly, hand them to me and stay out of sight!

The rod, the hook, and the rope are all very self-evident in their usage when combined. I just need to infuse the result with the essences and we'll be ready to proceed.

It's all very mundane in its composition, but extraordinary in its application!

passages.title: It's All Fun and Games
passages.text:
The Knights of the Ebon Blade want to take the Scourge base known as The Shadow Vault to the northwest. I have a contact in their group who has asked for help.

The first step is to blind the Lich King. He's using a device known as The Ocular to watch the area, which floats above the vault's spires.

Our goblins have created something for you to use against it. After the 'eye' has been destroyed, find Baron Sliver on the vault grounds. He's pretending to still be under the Lich King's will.

passages.title: It's All Fun and Games
passages.text:
Perhaps now we can really get something done. Don't be fooled though, the Lich King can still 'see' through his Scourge minions.

That's why you're here.

passages.title: Free Your Mind
passages.text:
Vile, Lady Nightswood, and The Leaper would make excellent weapons in the fight against the Lich King if they can be broken from his will. That is what the Sovereign Rod is for.

You'll find them on the ledges to the east and west of the vault, as well as on the mid-tier of the vault above us. The rod is to be used upon the corpses of the three.

Fly now. We will have them as our own!

passages.title: Free Your Mind
passages.text: You have NOT turned them yet. Do not insult my intelligence, <class>!

passages.title: Free Your Mind
passages.text:
We will put those three to good use once we finally take the vault.

Speaking of which....

passages.title: Crusader Forward Camp
passages.text:
Crusader Dargath, Crusader MacKellar, Engineer Reed and the twins, Gerk and Burr, were sent to the Dead Fields to establish a battle front days ago. As of my last correspondence with them, they had successfully established a camp on the border of the Dead Fields, northwest of here.

In light of this newfound information about Drakuru and Prince Navarius I think it would be prudent to send someone to the Crusader Forward Camp post-haste.

Pack up your belongings, <name>. You must leave at once!

passages.title: Crusader Forward Camp
passages.text:
Everything was fine until the Scourge attacked. They took off with Dargath, Gerk and Burr and they also destroyed our ride. Guess who led that attack?

<MacKellar nods.>

Navarius...

Seems this whole area is some type of factory for Scourge. We're in the middle of a damned undead mine field!

passages.title: The Missing Bronzebeard
passages.text:
Before we left, I received the file Scout Vor'takh compiled on this Brann Bronzebeard. There can be no doubt that Brann was headed for the Storm Peaks from his journal entries and findings in Grizzly Hills. Before we crashed, I caught sight of a campsite south of here, across the Foot Steppes, and overlooking the frozen Bor's Breath River.

If Brann isn't there, search the camp and its environs for any clues as to where that blasted dwarf might've gone. Bring back anything you find.

passages.title: The Missing Bronzebeard
passages.text: Did you have any luck finding Bronzebeard's camp?

passages.title: The Missing Bronzebeard
passages.text: Of course, with our luck, I probably could've predicted this. Well, we're not going to let him get away that easily. Let's see what that note says.

passages.title: If He Cannot Be Turned
passages.text:
Death knights, such as General Lightsbane, are held on too tight of a leash to be able to be turned from the Lich King's will except under the most extraordinary circumstances.

The general keeps himself within the vault overseeing the creation of new weapons. Disturb one of his weapon racks at the northern forge and I assure you, he will come. I'll send Vile, Lady Nightswood, and The Leaper in to help you.

If we are to finally own The Shadow Vault, General Lightsbane must fall!

passages.title: If He Cannot Be Turned
passages.text: General Lightsbane and his forces are defeated? The Shadow Vault is taken?

passages.title: If He Cannot Be Turned
passages.text:
Death knights, such as General Lightsbane, are held on too tight of a leash to be able to be turned from the Lich King's will except under the most extraordinary circumstances.

The general keeps himself within the vault overseeing the creation of new weapons. Disturb one of his weapon racks at the northern forge and I assure you, he will come. I'll send Vile, Lady Nightswood, and The Leaper in to help you.

If we are to finally own The Shadow Vault, General Lightsbane must fall!

passages.title: If He Cannot Be Turned
passages.text: General Lightsbane and his forces are defeated? The Shadow Vault is taken?

passages.title: Making a Harness
passages.text:
So you want to ride? Well, if you've made it this far someone must think you've got a shot at the Hyldsmeet.

First things first; we'll have to make you a harness.

In the cliffs to the south, you'll find scattered groups of yeti. Their hides are tough and just the right thickness. Bring me some and we'll get you started on the path of the bear-rider.

passages.title: Making a Harness
passages.text: Did you find the hides yet?  You'll find yeti in the hills below.

passages.title: Making a Harness
passages.text: These will do nicely.  I'll have the harness ready for you in no time.

passages.title: Making Something Out Of Nothing
passages.text:
Prince Navarius must be stopped. We can't let the Scourge continue to use this area as a zombie factory. If we can get the tank operational we might stand a chance. What I need right now are spare parts.

Northwest of here is an area called Thrym's End. The Scourge armies are using the area as a base of sorts. Spread out across the base is the wreckage from their arrival. Bits and pieces of Scourge scrap metal litter the landscape. Get that stuff to me and I'll try and put it to good use.

passages.title: Making Something Out Of Nothing
passages.text: I really don't know if this plan will work, <name>. Just bring me the scrap metal and I'll do what I can.

passages.title: Making Something Out Of Nothing
passages.text: What is this junk! Ah, damn it all! It's useless. Scourge metal isn't gonna do the trick. What are we going to do?

passages.title: In Search Of Answers
passages.text:
These poor creatures are the only survivors.

According to their chief, the Drakkari trolls and Rageclaw wolvar have been allies for thousands of years. They've been living here, alongside the trolls, for generations, completely unaware of the ever changing world around them. To the Rageclaw, a troll is a troll, so the troll attack upon their den took them by surprise.

We need some answers, <name>. Scour their village - southeast of here - for clues as to who or what is in charge of these attacks.

passages.title: In Search Of Answers
passages.text: There is a scroll floating in the air above the strange altar. This must be what Crusader Lord Lantinga is looking for!

passages.title: That's What Friends Are For...
passages.text:
We were attacked by Prince Navarius and at least a dozen Scourge. I told Dargath and the twins to stay inside the tank, but they wouldn't listen. Dargath looked me in the eyes and said, "If somebody doesn't get out of this tank, they'll kill us all." He then made Reed cut the engine and charged. Most heroic thing I've ever seen.

I heard the Prince barking orders to the monsters. Sounded like he was taking them to Thrym's End, northwest of here. We have to rescue our friends. Will you go look for them?

passages.title: That's What Friends Are For...
passages.text: It was a great sacrifice that those three made and it won't soon be forgotten. Their passing will not be in vain. We will be victorious!

passages.title: Discipline
passages.text:
Let's start you off with something straightforward. The male vrykul that work the mines for us do so against their will... purely out of fear of our blades.

Once in a while, one of them will lose their motivation. Find any uncooperative vrykul and put them in their place.

Take this disciplining rod. You'll want to inflict pain, not death. Well, most of the time anyway.

passages.title: Discipline
passages.text: Is it done?  I hope you didn't slay too many of the mongrels.  We need the manpower.

passages.title: Discipline
passages.text: Not bad for a new overseer.  I've another task for you if you're feeling brave today.

passages.title: The Nose Knows
passages.text:
In order to track down Brann, we're going to need a creature with a keen sense of smell and a good tracking ability. There weren't any hounds on the zeppelin, but I think I have a substitute.

After the crash, I sent Khaliisi down the east face of the mountain to start hunting for food. Her cat, Frostbite, excels at tracking prey in the snow. Tell her that she'll have to part with her companion for a while, at least. She can hunt on her own, but we have no other way of catching up to Brann Bronzebeard.

passages.title: The Nose Knows
passages.text: So Boktar has volunteered Frostbite for an errand, eh? Well, this had better be important. He knows better than to try to separate a hunter from her pet!

passages.title: Sniffing Out the Perpetrator
passages.text:
Boktar can have his way this time, but I'll expect him to make it up to me. Don't look at me like that. Boktar may be in command, but no one tells a hunter what to do.

'Put that beast away,' he says. 'Make it stop growling.'

All of a sudden he changes his mind when it suits him. Next time he complains, Frostbite'll just nip him a bit. Don't worry, she'll do an admirable job tracking your prey. After she locates her target, you're on your own to deal with iron dwarves, or Brann, or whatever you find.

passages.title: Sniffing Out the Perpetrator
passages.text:
<An image of a dwarf appears as you activate the communicator. It can only be Brann Bronzebeard.>

<From the look on his face, Brann seems shocked to see you and begins gesturing furiously.>

passages.title: A Great Storm Approaches
passages.text:
You are not like the others, little one. You do not reek of the ancient death. Perhaps you can be trusted.

I am Gymer, king of the storm giants. I was lured here by my brother, Thiassi, now an undead servant of the Lich King. By the time I realized that his cry for help was a trap, it was too late. I am now a prisoner of the Scourge and I fear that soon I will suffer the same fate as many of the other storm giants.

Find a way to release me from this cage and I will aid you to the best of my ability.

passages.title: A Great Storm Approaches
passages.text:
A... A storm giant? I don't know about this, <name>. That sounds risky. On the other hand, I don't think we have too many other options.

If I do this you have to promise me that you will get your giant friend to help us deal with Navarius and his cronies.

passages.title: Gymer's Salvation
passages.text:
Now you say that he's locked up in a 100 foot tall cage, eh?

If my calculations are correct, we should be able to at least weaken the hinges on the cage, giving the giant enough leeway to break out.

If this is going to work I'm going to need some plasticizers and stabilizers.

Banshee essence should do nicely for the plasticizer. You can get that from the banshees in the Dead Fields, northeast of us. The stabilizer can be found on the earthragers to the southwest, near Ebon Watch.

Get a move on!

passages.title: Gymer's Salvation
passages.text: Without the plasticizers and stabilizers I'll never be able to make the explosives necessary to break your friend out of jail.

passages.title: Gymer's Salvation
passages.text: Thankfully we weren't in short supply of explosives. Putting together the jumbo seaforium charge should be no problem with the materials you brought me.

passages.title: Mending Fences
passages.text:
If I hope to wrest control of the Temple of the Makers from my brother, I must make amends with my old allies.

Perhaps by eliminating a common enemy, we may at least take a step towards renewing my friendship with the frost giants.

Fjorn has besieged Dun Niffelem with giants of iron. You must defeat him at Fjorn's Anvil, far to the east of here, and weaken his forces sufficiently for the Sons of Hodir to emerge victorious.

Take this charm, <name>. Use it to summon my earthen to your aid.

passages.title: Mending Fences
passages.text:
So, it is done then.

Let us hope it is enough.

passages.title: Our Only Hope
passages.text:
What I'm about to give you is called seaforium. It is a highly volatile explosive with some unique properties. Due to its malleable nature, you will be able to fill in the hinges and cracks of the cage for maximum damage.

Return to your friend and use the jumbo seaforium charge to set him free.

Let's hope he honors the bargain. He's our only hope.

passages.title: Our Only Hope
passages.text: I am a giant of my word, little one.

passages.title: Our Only Hope
passages.text:
FREEDOM!

Do not be afraid, little one. Gymer is an honorable giant. Like you and your people, I too wish to see the Scourge driven away from this land and the Lich King destroyed. I will help you, as promised, to the best of my ability.

passages.title: Speaking with the Wind's Voice
passages.text:
I suppose we shouldn't have expected to find Brann so easily, not with our luck. If we can make sense of what Brann is saying, you can persuade him to give up his location.

The power of the wind is strong in these mountains, and it may prove a great boon to us. A knowledgeable shaman can hear the sound of all the world's tongues on the wind.

To the northwest, on the Snowdrift Plains, you will find beings made of wind, the stormriders. Capture their voices and bring them to me.

passages.title: Speaking with the Wind's Voice
passages.text: Have you brought the wind's voices?

passages.title: Speaking with the Wind's Voice
passages.text: You should be able to communicate with the dwarf now. Ask Boktar what he requires of you. There is little time to lose.

passages.title: Gem Perfection
passages.text: It has the cold of the Icewyrm's breath up here does it not? Not only do I lack customers for my crafting skills, but I also lack stock of gems to sell! If you can bring me several uncut gems to replenish my stocks, I can teach you the skill of gem perfection. This will allow you to sometimes cut a perfect gem with increased bonuses when cutting a uncommon quality gem from Northrend.

passages.title: The Storm King's Vengeance
passages.text:
My people have been decimated by the Lich King. The Scourge now use the corpses of storm giants to create mindless flesh giants, or worse, stitched together aberrations like Thrym.

I will stop at nothing to see them all driven from this world. We will work together to destroy the Scourge that threaten Zul'Drak.

We will kill them all: Navarius, Algar and Thrym!

When you are ready, let me know and we will begin our destructive journey.

passages.title: The Storm King's Vengeance
passages.text:
Unbelievable! This will be a story for the ages, <name>! One man rode upon the head of the king of storm giants and decimated an entire Scourge army!

And I was there to see it all happen...

passages.title: Catching up with Brann
passages.text:
What are you waiting for? The language barrier has been broken, thanks to Moteha. Contact Brann Bronzebeard and find out anything you can about where he's hiding and what he's chasing after.

Maybe we can still salvage something from this disaster.

passages.title: Catching up with Brann
passages.text:
<Boktar listens as you describe your conversation with Brann.>

There's truth to the dwarf's words. Vor'takh's plan is not the way of the Horde. If Brann Bronzebeard knows of a way to stop these iron dwarves and their patron, it serves us to help him.

passages.title: The Refiner's Fire
passages.text:
Beneath its porous exterior, this hunk of metal gleams with a mysterious quality.

You feel it would only be prudent to burn off the slag at Fjorn's Anvil.

As you ponder where in this frozen waste you might find something hot enough for the job, a fire revenant crosses your path...

passages.title: The Refiner's Fire
passages.text: The surface of the anvil is scalding, in sharp contrast with the wintry air.

passages.title: The Refiner's Fire
passages.text:
You place the metal on the anvil and immediately upon adding the sparks they work the ore furiously.

When at last they burn out, you are left with a large piece of metal that gleams with a light of its own.

passages.title: Forging an Alliance
passages.text:
<Thorim, for the first time since your meeting him, smiles.>

This is all beginning to have the smell of fate's hand, <race>.

Your discovery is what remains of my armor, long ago cast off in a fit of grief and left to the elements. Only the sons of Hodir are capable of its reforging, for they are its original creators.

Perhaps you've done enough to soften their hatred of me. Seek out their king, Jokkum, if he still breathes.

Find your way into his good graces and plead for his assistance.

passages.title: Forging an Alliance
passages.text:
It would seem that I have refined my technique considerably. That, or the legends surrounding this anvil are true.

This suit of armor is superior to the last, and took less material to create.

With the excess, I was able to fashion you a little something as payment for your assistance.

passages.title: Aberrations
passages.text:
The Lich King sent emissaries to us on three different occasions. All three were promptly dismembered.

Our sisters in Valkyrion were not as dedicated to our traditions and accepted the Scourge's advances. Now instead of capturing their drakes from the wild, they raise them from the blight and filth that the Scourge wallow in.

Take the frost oil that the Valkyrion Hyldnir carry on them and use it to freeze any blighted eggs you find. Rumors speak of a fetid pool of blight where the eggs are kept.

passages.title: Aberrations
passages.text: You have our thanks, sister.  We cannot allow our valiant traditions to be corrupted.

passages.title: Norgannon's Shell
passages.text:
Charging inventor's disk.

Disk charging completed.

Preparing emergency protocol gamma.

Emergency protocol loaded. Please use the charged disk to activate the guardian of Norgannon's shell, Archivist Mechaton. The archivist will release the shell once your identity has been verified.

Please have a pleasant millennium.

passages.title: Norgannon's Shell
passages.text: Did you find Norgannon's shell?

passages.title: Norgannon's Shell
passages.text: That's it! That's the first half of Norgannon's keystone. Well done, <name>. I've had Archaeologist Andorin on the lookout for clues to the shell's whereabouts for a long time. He's never going to believe me when I tell him it was an intrepid <race> who found it instead.

passages.title: Rare Earth
passages.text:
It seems so long ago that these hammers pounded and hewed stone instead of iron. Our expulsion from Ulduar saw the weakest of us dead and the strongest of our craftsmen reborn as warriors.

As the irons beat us back, even the strongest find themselves failing.

We can do little for the wounded, save when we have a stock of enchanted earth. We used to mine it from the deposits on the sheer cliff face to the northwest, but the constant battle has prevented us from replenishing our stock. Would you help?

passages.title: Rare Earth
passages.text: Were you able to find any of the earth?

passages.title: Rare Earth
passages.text: This will allow us to patch up more of the fallen. Thank you, <name>, on behalf of all who defend the refuge.

passages.title: Fighting Back
passages.text:
The refuge's defenders have done their best to blunt the iron dwarves' attacks, but we keep losing ground inch by inch. My men are hardy, but not tireless. Without reinforcements, it's only a matter of time until we will be overrun.

Would you lend your skills to the refuge's defense? It would greatly improve the morale of the defenders and give them -- and me -- hope of mounting a counterattack.

Kill any of the stormforged or their creations you encounter outside the refuge.

passages.title: Fighting Back
passages.text: You've given the defenders something to cheer about. Seeing the enemy fall by your hand has reinvigorated them and bolstered their courage.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Yggdras!
passages.text:
I'll tell you what, buddy, this place is a far cry from the rolling plains of Nagrand. These trolls are dirtier than ogres; but hey, I go where the gold's at! So welcome to Zul'Drak, pal.

You're new to this racket, so let me set you straight. I'm the fight promoter and this feisty troll next to me is Wodin, my bodyguard. You're the entertainment. When you wanna fight, let me know and I'll set up the match.

If you're ready and got a group of friends with you, we can start! What do you say?

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Yggdras!
passages.text: No payout until the fight's over, man.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Yggdras!
passages.text: Not bad, friend. You might make some gold out here - if you manage to stay alive.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Magnataur!
passages.text:
This next match is a doozy, buddy! Apparently some magnataur from the Dragonblight wants a piece of the action. You ever fought one of those before? All I can tell you is to aim high!

We'll get this party started when you give me the word.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Magnataur!
passages.text: No payout until the fight's over, man.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Magnataur!
passages.text: Wow! When I first saw Stinkbeard, I thought you were done for! Nice work!

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: From Beyond!
passages.text:
I'm not gonna lie to you, pal. You might be overmatched here. This next one is a being from the elemental planes! I don't even know what's gonna show up in that arena!

If you think you're up to it, get in there and give 'em hell!

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: From Beyond!
passages.text: Unbelievable! I thought this whole place was going to explode when it first appeared! You really dominated that round!

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Tuskarrmageddon!
passages.text:
This next one's fightin' from a dark place, kid. The kind of dark that can only happen when you've been on the flip-side. He's hungry and willing to do whatever it takes to win. Watch yourself! I've heard he wrestles yetis for exercise!

We'll start when you're ready.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Tuskarrmageddon!
passages.text: I was worried for a while there, <name>. When he busted out the seals and penguins... Well, I didn't know what to think to be honest. It looked pretty damn ridiculous.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Korrak the Bloodrager!
passages.text:
You're not gonna believe this, pal. Your next fight is against Korrak the Bloodrager! Looks like the Drakkari trolls are pulling a power play! And let me tell you, buddy, he's been sippin' the animal god juice. He's good and ready to pound you into the ground.

Are you ready?

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Korrak the Bloodrager!
passages.text: No payout until the fight's over, man.

passages.title: The Amphitheater of Anguish: Korrak the Bloodrager!
passages.text: Damn, I remember Korrak from way back in my younger days when I used to work for the Frostwolf Clan. He would never shut up! I think you just did the world a great service, <name>.

passages.title: Relief for the Fallen
passages.text:
The refuge's defenders fight bravely, but they cannot keep up with the iron onslaught.

With the earth you collected, I can make bandages to help heal the wounds of some of the fallen. The more defenders we can patch up, the longer we'll last out there.

Take these poultices and use them to heal the wounds of the fallen defenders outside the refuge. Get as many back into the battle as possible, <name>. Every casualty is one too many.

passages.title: Relief for the Fallen
passages.text: The warriors that you've healed will aid us in holding the line even longer. If we are to truly be free of the iron threat, we must find a way to strike at them behind the lines.

passages.title: Honor Challenge
passages.text:
The first step we're going to take is at a place in Jotunheim called the Savage Ledge. It's just over the mountains to the west.

On the ledge the vrykul warriors are always sparring, being instructed in the finer arts of battle by their thane's men.

I want you to take this flag and issue a challenge to a number of them. Let's demoralize them with the 'mere' skills of a <race>, shall we?

<The duke grins, his rotting teeth flashing in the dim light of the vault.>

passages.title: Honor Challenge
passages.text:
Already I'm hearing reports of the prowess you displayed on the Savage Ledge. Excellent, <name>... excellent!

And now I think it's time to issue a decree to the thane of those vrykul that you so easily defeated.

passages.title: Off With Their Black Wings
passages.text:
Traitors. We Hyldnir have little love for them.

The dwellers of Valkyrion have gone unpunished for far too long. While we remained loyal to Thorim, they became the Lich King's lapdogs!

They call the ones who receive his gift val'kyr. They fly on feathered wings, like the harpies they are.

You will find Valkyrion far to the northwest, beyond the Temple of Storms. Slay these winged she-wolves, sister. Slay them and I will reward you with one of my most prized possessions.

passages.title: Off With Their Black Wings
passages.text: The val'kyr are nothing but the Lich King's lapdogs.  They will be put down like the scum they are.  They've made their choice, now they have to live with the consequences.

passages.title: Shadow Vault Decree
passages.text:
Thane Ufrang the Mighty sits within his hall overlooking the Savage Ledge. I've studied him. The thane is a patient vrykul, with a head for strategy and warfare. He's also shown a penchant for biding his time and not wanting to overplay his hand in the ongoing battle.

I need him dead!

I've written a decree. Stand before the thane and read it aloud.

<The duke arches his eyebrow in amusement.>

It should... unnerve him at the least.

passages.title: Shadow Vault Decree
passages.text:
<Duke Lankral nods his approval at your report of success.>

We face a foe that dwarfs us, not only in stature, but also numerically. If we are to win the battle for Icecrown, we must outthink them!

With Ufrang dead, that gives us an advantage in Jotunheim. Let us see if we can capitalize on it.

passages.title: The Champion of Anguish
passages.text:
This is the end, my friend! Your last opponent is going to be your greatest challenge. He's a vrykul champion from the steppes of Icecrown and he's out for blood! Defeat him and you'll be crowned the champion of the Amphitheater of Anguish! This fight is going to make us both rich!

Let me know when you're ready and we'll start.

passages.title: The Champion of Anguish
passages.text: No payout until the fight's over, man.

passages.title: The Champion of Anguish
passages.text: You did it, <name>! That was the most exciting fight yet! What are you going to do with your winnings? Me? I'm going to Dalaran and blowing it all in the Underbelly. Lot of hot action going on down there!

passages.title: Get the Key
passages.text:
<class>, the key to my shackles is hanging around the neck of Instructor Hroegar outside.

Perhaps you could retrieve it by separating his head from his shoulders?

passages.title: Get the Key
passages.text: Do you have it?

passages.title: Get the Key
passages.text: Thank you, <race>. Just hand me the key, I'll take care of it myself.

passages.title: Gem Perfection
passages.text: My skills are going to waste in this wretched place. I spent many years learning to cut gems into their perfect form and have nothing to work on! You look like the type who may be able to find me some gems and if you do I can teach you the skill of gem perfection. This will allow you to sometimes cut a perfect gem with increased bonuses when cutting a uncommon quality gem from Northrend.

passages.title: Valkyrion Must Burn
passages.text:
The crate is filled with incendiary harpoons. You recall seeing harpoon guns and dry stacks of hay outside.

Perhaps Iva will appreciate the extra effort and reward you appropriately.

passages.title: Valkyrion Must Burn
passages.text: Now that is what I call dedication!  Those traitors might have a new master now, but they'll never forget their sisters' parting gift.

passages.title: Eliminate the Competition
passages.text:
Mrrfrmrfrrmrrr...

<The Leaper clears his throat.>

Sorry about that. It can sometimes be hard to understand what I'm saying. You know how it is.

I wanted to make sure that if you find yourself at the Savage Ledge, over the mountains to the west, that you make sure to eliminate the competition there.

Specifically, I'd like you to challenge to duels and humiliate Sigrid Iceborn, Efrem the Faithful, Onu'zun, and Tinky Wickwhistle in front of the vrykul.

passages.title: Eliminate the Competition
passages.text: That was important, <name>. By driving them off, you're keeping them from interfering with whatever we need you to do over there.

passages.title: A Spark of Hope
passages.text:
Clearly, this is more than an ordinary hunk of metal.

Unlike any ore you're familiar with, it is hard but not brittle, far lighter than it looks, and glows even when cool.

Looking closer, you can make out one of Thorim's runes shining beneath the surface....

passages.title: A Spark of Hope
passages.text: What have you there, little one?

passages.title: A Spark of Hope
passages.text: You notice Thorim's stern countenance brighten with recognition as you present the ore.

passages.title: Slaves of the Stormforged
passages.text:
To the southwest, on the western side of the Snowdrift Plains, the iron dwarves have dug a mine into the hillside. There, they use captive mechagnomes, servants of Keeper Mimir, to mine ore.

I don't know where these mechagnomes came from, nor what they would do with their freedom, but perhaps we can win their help.

Go to the Frozen Mine, <name>, and set these creatures free from their bondage. Ask if they would fight alongside us against iron dwarf tyranny.

passages.title: Slaves of the Stormforged
passages.text: Have you freed the slaves of the stormforged?

passages.title: Slaves of the Stormforged
passages.text: I had hoped that more of the captives would choose to join us, but I do not blame them. Willing allies are few and far between, and we are thankful that you have lent your blade to our cause.

passages.title: Shipment: Blood Jade Amulet
passages.text: A wealthy shipping concern has requested a collection of Blood Jade Amulets to sell at Undermine. If you can bring me one, I can reward you with a Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token.

passages.title: Shipment: Blood Jade Amulet
passages.text: Do you have a Blood Jade Amulet for my Undermine shipment?

passages.title: Shipment: Blood Jade Amulet
passages.text: Here is your Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token as promised.  Come back tomorrow and I am sure I will have another item I need from you!

passages.title: Shipment: Glowing Ivory Figurine
passages.text: A wealthy shipping concern has requested a collection of Glowing Ivory Figurines to sell at Undermine. If you can bring me one, I can reward you with a Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token.

passages.title: Shipment: Glowing Ivory Figurine
passages.text: Do you have a Glowing Ivory Figurine for my Undermine shipment?

passages.title: Shipment: Glowing Ivory Figurine
passages.text: Here is your Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token as promised.  Come back tomorrow and I am sure I will have another item I need from you!

passages.title: Shipment: Wicked Sun Brooch
passages.text: A wealthy shipping concern has requested a collection of Wicked Sun Brooches to sell at Undermine. If you can bring me one, I can reward you with a Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token.

passages.title: Shipment: Wicked Sun Brooch
passages.text: Do you have a Wicked Sun Brooch for my Undermine shipment?

passages.title: Shipment: Wicked Sun Brooch
passages.text: Here is your Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token as promised.  Come back tomorrow and I am sure I will have another item I need from you!

passages.title: Shipment: Intricate Bone Figurine
passages.text: A wealthy shipping concern has requested a collection of Intricate Bone Figurines to sell at Undermine. If you can bring me one, I can reward you with a Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token.

passages.title: Shipment: Intricate Bone Figurine
passages.text: Do you have an Intricate Bone Figurine for my Undermine shipment?

passages.title: Shipment: Intricate Bone Figurine
passages.text: Here is your Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token as promised.  Come back tomorrow and I am sure I will have another item I need from you!

passages.title: Shipment: Bright Armor Relic
passages.text: A wealthy shipping concern has requested a collection of Bright Armor Relics to sell at Undermine. If you can bring me one, I can reward you with a Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token.

passages.title: Shipment: Bright Armor Relic
passages.text: Do you have a Bright Armor Relic for my Undermine shipment?

passages.title: Shipment: Bright Armor Relic
passages.text: Here is your Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token as promised.  Come back tomorrow and I am sure I will have another item I need from you!

passages.title: Shipment: Shifting Sun Curio
passages.text: A wealthy shipping concern has requested a collection of Shifting Sun Curios to sell at Undermine. If you can bring me one, I can reward you with a Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token.

passages.title: Shipment: Shifting Sun Curio
passages.text: Do you have a Shifting Sun Curio for my Undermine shipment?

passages.title: Shipment: Shifting Sun Curio
passages.text: Here is your Dalaran Jewelcrafter's Token as promised.  Come back tomorrow and I am sure I will have another item I need from you!

passages.title: The Gifts of Loken
passages.text:
The one who commands the stormforged iron dwarves is called Runeseer Valduran. Although I have never seen them, it is said that his master, Keeper Loken, who took over Ulduar, has given Valduran powerful titan artifacts.

It could explain the strength and ferocity my men see in the stormforged warriors.

Valduran's base, Nidavelir, lies to the southwest, across the Snowdrift Plains. Go there, <name>, and neutralize his power. Destroy these gifts of Loken's and help us to sap the strength of his followers.

passages.title: The Gifts of Loken
passages.text:
<Bouldercrag nods grimly.>

You've weakened the stormforged considerably, but they'll keep fighting. Their casualties matter nothing to them, while our defenders continue to fall. Even if it costs them a hundred or a thousand iron corpses, they'll keep fighting until we've been pounded to gravel.

passages.title: You Can't Miss Him
passages.text:
<Jokkum listens patiently to your request, then ponders it carefully before responding.>

So it is you we have to thank for Fjorn's demise?

While it's true that you have aided us in our time of need, there is still much that must be done to repair our relations with Thorim.

For now, I shall allow Njormeld to reforge the armor we gifted to the Stormlord so many ages ago. Consider it payment for your assistance against Fjorn.

Njormeld was sent to recover Fjorn's anvil. You should find him there.

passages.title: You Can't Miss Him
passages.text:
Reforging Thorim's armor? It can be done.

First though, there's the matter of the anvil...

passages.title: Battling the Elements
passages.text:
Snorri was once the pride of our nation. A mighty warrior, many an enemy fell to his club.

We honor him, though he's no longer what he once was. Age has taken its toll, dulling his senses and sapping his strength. Still, he remains as proud as ever, never missing an opportunity to join a battle.

Speaking of battle, we're cooling Fjorn's anvil so it can be taken home. The remaining fire revenants are putting up some resistance. Help Snorri relive his glory days, <race>. Guide him against this enemy.

passages.title: Battling the Elements
passages.text: Were you able to lead Snorri to another victory, <class>?

passages.title: Battling the Elements
passages.text:
An honorable performance, <race>. I shall inform the king of your assistance.

The anvil is nearly cool enough. I shall see you in Dun Niffelem soon.

passages.title: Yulda's Folly
passages.text:
The witch that started it all, Yulda the Stormspeaker came to our very village. She dared to insult our noble traditions and spouted the Lich King's venomous promises of power.

She ought to have left with a sword through her, but her magic was strong and she managed to escape.

Seek her in Valkyrion inside the largest dwelling and show her that we are not to be trifled with.

passages.title: Yulda's Folly
passages.text: Yulda had it coming.  No one gets away with insulting the Hyldsmeet.  Not even one of our own.

passages.title: Is That Your Goblin?
passages.text:
I trust that's the green little one you've been looking for. If I were you I'd step in before that Hyldnir splits him in half.

You've arrived in the middle of the Hyldsmeet, so all challenges must be accepted by participants. There's nothing to stop you from taking your green friend's place.

passages.title: Is That Your Goblin?
passages.text: You're back.

passages.title: Is That Your Goblin?
passages.text: Well done, young one.  It looks like our deal has been satisfied on both our ends.

passages.title: Taking on All Challengers
passages.text:
Let's get you started. The good news is that by defeating Agnetta, you've earned yourself a spot in the next round of matches.

The bad news is that all your opponents will also have defeated someone in the first round. Do not expect pushovers.

passages.title: Taking on All Challengers
passages.text: You've done it, <name>.  You've bested some of the fiercest fighters the Hyldnir race has to offer.

passages.title: The Brothers Bronzebeard
passages.text:
That does it! We finally have the keystone... It's beautiful! I've been around the world more than once, but this thing's got me all jittery with excitement again. I suppose now's not the time to stop and admire though, we need to get the heck out of here.

Hop on my flying machine and help keep us covered from those iron dwarves on the way out!

passages.title: The Brothers Bronzebeard
passages.text: My pardons, lad! I got all caught up in tha moment and I neglected ye entirely.

passages.title: The Brothers Bronzebeard
passages.text: King Stormheart sends his most sincere thanks for reuniting him with his brothers. It seems he's off to settle a score now - perhaps you'll meet with him again on Arthas's doorstep.

passages.title: In Memoriam
passages.text:
Surely Thorim has told you of the tragedy that divides us.

It was in Thunderfall, northeast of here, that these events unfolded. The frozen fossils there are a reminder of that dark day, as are the spirits that haunt that place.

If my people are to forgive Thorim, something must take the place of those images. A memorial must be constructed to bring our hearts peace.

Go there, <race>. Collect the fragments of Hodir's Horn that was shattered that day.

passages.title: In Memoriam
passages.text: Have you found the pieces of Hodir's Horn?

passages.title: In Memoriam
passages.text:
Another good deed you have done on Thorim's behalf, <class>.

This will help to soften the hearts of my people towards him.

passages.title: A Monument to the Fallen
passages.text:
Bring these fragments to Njormeld. He will use the pieces of that sacred relic in the construction of a mighty monument.

May it soothe the pains and heal the scars my people have borne these many years.

May its presence help to bring about a new age that sees us once again in glorious battle at Thorim's side.

Go now, <class>. Njormeld awaits you.

passages.title: A Monument to the Fallen
passages.text: You have brought the fragments of Hodir's Horn, <race>?

passages.title: A Monument to the Fallen
passages.text:
<Njormeld's eyes become noticeably moist as he pours the contents of the bag onto the anvil.>

The Horn of Hodir....

This was a sacred gift to our people from Hodir himself, <race>. It is a relic of great importance to us.

When you next return to our stronghold you shall see the fruits of your labor.

Farewell.

passages.title: Hodir's Call
passages.text:
You have done a great service to the giants of Dun Niffelem. Without your aid, this monument would not exist.

As you silently ponder its significance, feelings begin to flood your heart. The feelings fill your mind with thoughts and images... as well as a sense of urgency.

The sensations fade and leave you with a knowledge of what you must do. The restless spirits at Thunderfall must be put to rest.

As you set off, you find that your hands have been filled with an ethereal horn.

passages.title: Hodir's Call
passages.text: You are filled with a sense of peace and contentment knowing that the once tormented souls of Thunderfall are now resting peacefully.

passages.title: Facing the Storm
passages.text:
Like Bouldercrag, I once served the keepers as a craftsman in Ulduar, but with Loken's betrayal, I turned my hammer toward our new foes.

When we could spare the men, I led raids on Nidavelir to relieve the pressure on our defenders, but our lines are near collapse.

You've proven yourself a capable combatant and a staunch ally. Perhaps you'd be willing to take up our banner and take the fight to Nidavelir, the iron dwarf stronghold to the southwest, across the Snowdrift Plains.

passages.title: Facing the Storm
passages.text: There may be hope for victory, <name>. We have never been able to sustain an attack on the stormforged, but with your efforts, Valduran may yet fall!

passages.title: The Armor's Secrets
passages.text:
The presence of that armor plate is disorienting, but we need to find out all we can from it. It could be part of one of Valduran's schemes.

He's dedicated an extraordinary amount of effort to mining, refining, smithing, and testing this metal.

To the east, along the northern mountain face, is a building called Mimir's Workshop. It hasn't been used in quite some time, but if we're lucky, some of its attendants are still functional. Take your armor plate there and learn what you can from it.

passages.title: The Armor's Secrets
passages.text: What did you learn?

passages.title: The Armor's Secrets
passages.text:
<Bruor listens as you describe what you learned in the workshop.>

So Valduran's master has given him this sinister metal to construct a giant weapon? That must be what he intends to use for the final strike against us! We need to stop him before he's able to complete it and unleash this weapon.

passages.title: Hot and Cold
passages.text:
As you stare at the anvil you relive your recent accomplishments, particularly those which brought this artifact to rest here.

It suddenly occurs to you that more remains to be done. To the east, smoldering scraps clutter the landscape--shrapnel from the battle fought there.

If they could be cooled and gathered somehow, the frost giants would have an abundant supply of metal and the region would be cleared of these remnants of war.

passages.title: Hot and Cold
passages.text: A luminous blue glow surrounds the anvil.

passages.title: Hot and Cold
passages.text: You feel a sense of accomplishment as you realize that your efforts continue to strengthen the renewed bonds between Thorim and the Sons of Hodir.

passages.title: Ebon Blade Prisoners
passages.text:
Now that I'm back, I'm certain that the baron will want me to recover my men. I can see that we're barely hanging on here. The Lich King's forces are about to break through and we won't be able to hold without my captured death knights.

Can you assist me once more, <name>?

Go back to Jotunheim and let them out of those cages. Break the damn locks, I don't care what you have to do. The vrykul likely have the keys.

Just get my men free!

passages.title: Ebon Blade Prisoners
passages.text: Thank you, <class>. With the death knights that you freed, we'll be able to hold the line... for now.

passages.title: The Last of Her Kind
passages.text:
For as long as I can remember, we've obtained our best bears from the Hibernal Cave to the east.

Those times might finally be gone. The cave has been overrun by ravenous jormungar and the wild bears are all but extinct.

If you were to find a surviving matriarch, however, I would guarantee you that she would fight better than any of these bears born in captivity.

Take this harness to the Hibernal Cave and rescue a surviving matriarch. Good luck finding one.

passages.title: The Last of Her Kind
passages.text: I'm impressed.  I never thought I would see an icemaw matriarch again.  Especially not one this size.

passages.title: Valduran the Stormborn
passages.text:
We have no choice, <name>. What you learned in Mimir's Workshop means that we must act before Valduran can complete and unleash his new weapon.

Even now, the refuge's defenders fight to buy us time to deal with Valduran the Stormborn.

You must go to Nidavelir, across the Snowdrift Plains to the southwest, and then find and face Valduran. But you will not be alone. Bring this war horn with you and sound it as you prepare to face the leader of our enemies. Bruor and I will aid you in this battle.

passages.title: Valduran the Stormborn
passages.text: At last, Valduran is dead, and the stormforged are weakened, but if his boasting is true, we must continue fighting the stormforged in his absence. This weapon they're building could be the end of us.

passages.title: Forging a Head
passages.text:
Greetings, <race>.

I have a task that King Jokkum felt you would be suited for, assuming you still strive to gain favor with our people.

I have developed plans for another artifact, one that will grant Hodir's blessing of protection to our stronghold. I have nearly all that I require for its construction. All that remains to collect are the very eyes of our fallen enemies.

Take this tool, and gather the eyes from the iron giant corpses that litter our fields.

passages.title: Forging a Head
passages.text: Have you collected the final components I seek, <race>?

passages.title: Forging a Head
passages.text:
It is nearly done.

With this artifact in place, Dun Niffelem shall be warned of impending dangers before they are upon us.

passages.title: Fate of the Titans
passages.text:
Norgannon's Core is not at this location. I am not sure why you seek it, <race>, and I am equally unsure if you truly know the purpose of that which you seek.

I would like you to aid me before I consider extending my assistance. I have recently encountered knowledge of the watcher, Thorim. His seat of power is contested, and his fate remains to be seen. This troubles me, for I do not know of the other watchers. Utilize this databank to examine their temples to the northeast and return the knowledge to me.

passages.title: Fate of the Titans
passages.text: Have you returned with the knowledge that I seek, <race>?

passages.title: Fate of the Titans
passages.text:
The news you bear forth is grave indeed. I do not know the fate of the remaining watchers, but their absence spells dark times for all of the lands of Azeroth.

I shall examine the knowledge contained in the databank that you have returned and attempt to fully assess the situation. I believe I am in possession of knowledge that you deem more pertinent at this moment however, so I shall allow you to partake in said wisdom first.

passages.title: Placing Hodir's Helm
passages.text:
The helm is forged.

Your efforts have not gone unnoticed, small one. Though there remains much to do, we sons of Hodir are grateful for your accomplishments.

In return, I offer you the opportunity to present Hodir's helm to our king and our brethren.

Fly to the sparkling tip of the small ice spike in front of me and read to our people from this tablet.

Enjoy the privilege, <class>. Never before has an outsider been given such an honor!

passages.title: Placing Hodir's Helm
passages.text: Have you placed Hodir's Helm, <race>?

passages.title: Placing Hodir's Helm
passages.text:
<Njormeld gazes up at Hodir's Helm, visibly moved.>

That will do, little <race>.

That will do....

passages.title: Destroy the Forges!
passages.text:
In my folly, I'd thought Valduran's project at Narvir's Cradle, a large construction area to the south, no more than a grotesque monument to "Keeper" Loken's cruelty.

Now we know the truth, that it was meant to be used as a weapon against us and our allies. We must not allow this iron colossus to reach completion, <name>, for it will mean the end of the refuge.

Go to Narvir's Cradle, find the lightning forges the stormforged artisans use, and sabotage them.

passages.title: Destroy the Forges!
passages.text: Excellent work! Oh, it won't stop the iron dwarves, but it'll take them valuable time to rebuild those forges. I daresay we've gained the advantage.

passages.title: The Slithering Darkness
passages.text:
The vile jormungar have taken over most of the Hibernal Cavern. They are despicable beings... children of Loken, Thorim's scumsucker of a brother.

As Thorim's servants we owe it to ourselves to kill these scum where we find them. You'll find the cavern just east of here, outside the village.

passages.title: The Slithering Darkness
passages.text: The jormungar are vile creatures.  You did well in destroying them.

passages.title: Crush Dem Vrykuls!
passages.text:
Dem vrykuls at the Jotunheim needs to be crushed!

<name> crush dems good!

passages.title: Crush Dem Vrykuls!
passages.text: <name> is my bestest little <race>!

passages.title: A Colossal Threat
passages.text:
You've done an excellent job of delaying the work on the iron colossus, but I fear we've only made the stormforged more determined to complete the weapon.

Even now, they're bringing in new laborers and the overseers push them to the limit. We may not be able to keep them from bringing the colossus online, after all. Return to Narvir's Cradle, to the south and find the documents detailing the colossus' offensive and defensive abilities. They should be near the tents and forges on the bottom level.

passages.title: A Colossal Threat
passages.text: Did you find the documents we're looking for?

passages.title: A Colossal Threat
passages.text:
<Bouldercrag begins to look over the documents, his eyes wide.>

I had no idea the irons were capable of this! Our men will have no chance against this behemoth if it's completed. Fortunately, it looks like they're still lacking a key part.

passages.title: Spy Hunter
passages.text:
The rapport you've developed with the inhabitants of Dun Niffelem has yielded some unexpected discoveries.

For example, you somehow find yourself able to understand the denmother's guttural growls and sharp quips--at least you think you do.

It would seem that she senses danger outside the stronghold and wants you to do something about it.

With her forepaw, she removes the chain from around her neck and lets it drop at your feet. As you pick it up you notice an aged fang attached to it...

passages.title: Spy Hunter
passages.text: The frostworg denmother looks at you curiously.

passages.title: Spy Hunter
passages.text: As you slide the chain back around the denmother's neck she licks your face approvingly.

passages.title: Leave Our Mark
passages.text:
We must attack the vrykul of Jotunheim on many levels. Brute force, of course, is good, but I prefer a more cerebral approach.

I want you to demoralize them.

My men here have forged a number of banners for you. I would like for you to take and plant them near the corpses of fallen vrykul.

Let the banners serve as a constant reminder to them that they face a more immediate threat than the wrath of the Lich King.

passages.title: Leave Our Mark
passages.text:
Well done, <name>. Let them see the desecrated corpses of their fallen comrades and think twice about striking at us!

If you come back tomorrow, I will make certain to have more banners prepared for you.

passages.title: The Warm-Up
passages.text:
You've been very fortunate, sister. This is a matriarch the likes of which hasn't been seen in years.

A good bear won't do you much good without the skill to ride it.

I'm going to have you practice some moves on Kirgaraak. He's the largest yeti we've ever managed to capture so be careful. Don't be afraid to walk away if he gives you a beating... there's a reason why we keep him chained.

passages.title: The Warm-Up
passages.text: How did it go with the yeti?

passages.title: The Warm-Up
passages.text:
Not bad.  I was hoping Kirgaraak would snap your neck so I could keep your bear.

Just joking, sister.  Well... half-joking.  That's a really nice bear you've got.

passages.title: Into the Pit
passages.text:
Besting a tethered opponent is one thing. Fighting other bear riders on equal footing is another.

Head into the Pit of the Fang and use what you've learned to defeat your opponents. Good luck, sister.

Glory awaits, should you succeed.

passages.title: Into the Pit
passages.text:
You really did it!  You made it out with your health.  Wish we could say the same for your bear.

It's going to take a while for her to recover.  Fortunately you won't need her for a while.

passages.title: The Heart of the Storm
passages.text:
According to the documents you captured at Narvir's Cradle, the iron colossus is complete except for one key component -- the Heart of the Storm.

Without it, the iron colossus' weapons would be much weaker than the design predicts. If we can deny Overseer Narvir the heart, we could defeat the colossus!

Notes on the documents you found say that the heart is in Uldis, a titan facility far to the south. Its entrance is on the south side of a tall mountain overlooking the Bor's Breath River.

passages.title: The Heart of the Storm
passages.text: With the heart in the hands of Narvir, the colossus will achieve its full power! We'll have no choice but to fight it.

passages.title: The Bone Witch
passages.text:
You remember Lady Nightswood, don't you? She certainly remembers you. She's the forlorn and very angry banshee that you 'saved' when you also broke Vile and myself out from under the Lich King's dominion.

The lady has gone into Jotunheim and possessed their bone witch. She intends to wreak havoc upon the vrykul from within.

She has asked that you seek her out. You'll find her in the cave on the south side of Njorndar Village to the southwest within Jotunheim.

passages.title: The Bone Witch
passages.text:
<name>, you came.

Already I have heard of your activities on the Savage Ledge. This is good. I am glad that you seem willing to help with undermining the vrykul here at Jotunheim.

You and I are going to have a great deal of fun with them!

passages.title: Emergency Measures
passages.text:
The cold in these mountains is brutal. We have a day or two before we burn up all the wood from the wreckage.

We spotted worgs inside a cave directly east of here. I need you to find the cave and obtain some furs. It might not sound like much, but it might be the difference between freezing to death and living another day.
