<Malynea puts aside the scroll dismissively, but her face is furrowed with concern.>

passages.title: Runaway Shredder!
passages.text:
I've been trying to impress our new Horde allies with our legendary goblin efficiency, but in hindsight automating the shredders was a bad idea. Now they're mindless killing machines, rampaging over the countryside. Don't get me wrong - that kind of thing has its place - but for the time being I need a brave <class> to help me get these things under control.

It's easy. Automated shredders, like all machines, must first be beaten into submission. Afterwards, seize the controls and I'll radio you instructions.

passages.title: Runaway Shredder!
passages.text:
<Labor Captain Grabbit's voice crackles over the radio.>

Hey <name>! Are you reading this?

Piloting that sucker is easy. Push the pedals for your pedal controls and, ah, move the levers for your lever controls. Got it?

passages.title: The Captain's Logs
passages.text:
Now that you've got that thing under control, let's gather up the lumber I was supposed to be collecting. Otherwise these orcs are going to build a catapult out of ME!

Fresh lumber should be stockpiled all around the area. Use the shredder to collect all you can.

passages.title: The Captain's Logs
passages.text: How's the wood processing going? You should see what that thing does to broccoli!

passages.title: The Captain's Logs
passages.text: Great! You've loaded the shredder to capacity. You're getting pretty handy with that thing...

passages.title: Up a Tree
passages.text:
Hold still a second, I'm going to bring your main buzzsaw controls online.

Night elven snipers from Talrendis have been hiding in the trees, taking potshots at my workers. I want you to take care of those snipers... by first taking care of those trees. Look for Azshara saplings east of the main gates. Your shredder will know what to do. Chop to it!

passages.title: Up a Tree
passages.text: Great work, <name>! That's how we took care of business back on Kezan.

passages.title: Rescue at Sea
passages.text:
The Kvaldir have set up camp at Hrothgar's Landing, the small island to the North. We sent Captain Aerthas Firehawk to the area, but they ran into a Kvaldir Raiding party heading to the Tournament Grounds! The Firehawk is now under attack by the raiders and is vastly outnumbered. Get out there and show those Kvaldir why attacking the Sunreavers is a poor plan indeed. 

The Firehawk is between Hrothgar's Landing to the north and the Tournament Grounds, on the western side of The Sea Reaver's Run.

passages.title: Rescue at Sea
passages.text: Have you defended The Firehawk?

passages.title: Rescue at Sea
passages.text: Great job, Champion.  The fight continues, but now the Kvaldir know that we do not tolerate such attacks.

passages.title: Taking Care of Business
passages.text:
With all of the troubles down in the Kaja'mine, Foreman Dampwick's been going crazy trying to find you. He said something about some 'defiant trolls'.

The kaja'mite that our trolls are mining is critical ingredient in Kaja'Cola. That bubbly stuff is making us a fortune, and it's going to get you a promotion to Trade <Prince/Princess>!

But first, we have to get production flowing again. You'll find the foreman to the east. Here, give him this as an incentive to get his act together.

passages.title: Taking Care of Business
passages.text:
Um... everything's going great. Yeah.

What's that?

passages.title: Taking Care of Business
passages.text: A gift from Sassy? I hope it's a bonus!

passages.title: Stop The Aggressors
passages.text:
The Kvaldir, fearsome vrykul raiders, have disrupted our shipments and murdered the tuskarr inhabitants of an island to the north, renaming it Hrothgar's Landing. If they are allowed to get a foothold there, there is no doubt that we will be their next target.

The crusade's forces have their hands full dealing with the Scourge, and we must defend the tournament grounds. Fly north from the grounds until you reach the island and take on the Kvaldir before they can destroy anything else.

passages.title: Stop The Aggressors
passages.text: Your actions have shown that we Sunreavers are far better allies to the Argent Crusade than the Silver Covenant and it is we who will be triumphant.

passages.title: Gormok Wants His Snobolds
passages.text:
Two of my men have already been killed trying to confine the magnataur called Gormok the Impaler, yet the creature still rages. It howls for hours about being without its favorite snobold.

If the Argent Crusade didn't wish to use this monster in the coliseum, I'd slay it myself. Perhaps it's time to bring the beast its playthings. Take this net and travel to Garm's Bane in southeast Storm Peaks. It's just northeast of K3. Capture some of those snobolds and pray to the Light you've found the right one.

passages.title: Gormok Wants His Snobolds
passages.text: Have you managed to round up those snobolds yet? Gormok's anger shows no signs of lessening.

passages.title: Gormok Wants His Snobolds
passages.text: The sooner we get these stinking things out of my sight and into their cage, the faster my mood will improve. I wish the Argent Crusade had given the Silver Covenant the care of this creature. They're going to have to get their hands dirty when the battle for Icecrown Citadel starts and I have a feeling they'll prove fragile and fussy allies.

passages.title: You've Really Done It This Time, Kul
passages.text:
Crusader Kul has gone and gotten himself into trouble again, only this time he's not alone. When he saw the cultists making camp at Deathspeaker's Watch, west of the tourney grounds, Kul gathered the aspirants for an attack.

They were easily captured, and now Kul languishes in a cage on the platform in the camp. I am sure that the cult will sacrifice the prisoners unless we can rescue them. Any of those cultists could carry keys to the black cages. Find the keys and free Kul and the captive aspirants.

passages.title: You've Really Done It This Time, Kul
passages.text: Kul will live to embarrass himself again. That's far from the first time someone's had to save Kul from himself. With examples like him, it's no wonder most of the aspirants are taking up the habits of the Silver Covenant.

passages.title: A Leg Up
passages.text:
The Argent Crusade dispatched a fast ship carrying tallstrider meat and other supplies for us here at the tournament grounds, but it never arrived. Scouts reported seeing it attacked by the Kvaldir, fearsome vrykul raiders who roam the seas.

They've slain the crew and taken the cargo to an island called Hrothgar's Landing. If you look to the north, you can see it shrouded in the mist. Would you help us in recovering the stolen supplies? Without those tallstrider legs, we'll soon be out of food.

passages.title: A Leg Up
passages.text: Were you able to recover any of the missing supplies?

passages.title: A Leg Up
passages.text: These look a little worse for wear, but they're still edible. The crusaders will be glad to hear that we've had some success. Maybe we can give the half-eaten ones to the Silver Covenant. That would make my day.

passages.title: The Light's Mercy
passages.text:
I've been listening to Confessor Paletress speak, and I must tell you, her words have made me think. We fight beside the crusaders, but we can learn from them, too.

Off the north coast is Hrothgar's Landing, where the seagoing Kvaldir have overrun an old tuskarr settlement and slain the villagers. Take this book and read the rites for the dead near the corpses of the villagers. It will allow their spirits to escape the mists engulfing the island and find peace.

passages.title: The Light's Mercy
passages.text: Have you seen to the spirits of the slain Tualiq villagers?

passages.title: The Light's Mercy
passages.text:
<Girana accepts the prayer book from you.>

Thank you. We don't always see eye-to-eye with the crusaders, but I've learned a lot from Confessor Paletress in my time here.

passages.title: What Do You Feed a Yeti, Anyway?
passages.text:
The crusaders have captured a yeti that they're calling Icehowl. He's to be a participant in the coliseum battles and we've been asked to help with his training and upkeep.

The crusaders weren't fond of my suggestion that we feed some Silver Covenant members to the beast. The creature prefers shark meat, so I want you to fly down to the Crimson Dawn, floating in the strait to the north. Get some fresh chum from one of the buckets on the boat, then spread it in the water to attract sharks.

passages.title: What Do You Feed a Yeti, Anyway?
passages.text: I hope you have something to feed Icehowl, otherwise I really will start bringing Silver Covenant members down to his cage.

passages.title: What Do You Feed a Yeti, Anyway?
passages.text: I'm glad we've gotten that done. It's not the most glorious task in the world, but when we partnered with the Argent Crusade, we promised to do all they asked of us without complaint. Of course, the same cannot be said of the Silver Covenant.

passages.title: Defend the Gates!
passages.text:
Egah - what's going on?

<Screams, shouts, and the roar of combat fills the radio.>

<name>! Get back here right away. Hurry back to the gates - we're under attack!

Help us fend off the invaders. I'm arming your grenade launcher!!

passages.title: Rescue at Sea
passages.text:
Champion, Captain Wavecrest and her ship were sent north to disrupt the Kvaldir in Hrothgar's Landing when they were intercepted by a Kvaldir raiding party headed to the Tournament Grounds. Unfortunately, the Kvaldir far outnumber the crew on board and are slowly taking over the ship.

We need you to go north to The Wavecrest in The Sea Reaver's Run, between the Tournament Grounds and Hrothgar's Landing and help the crew fend off the attack. You should see the ship on the east side of the pass.

passages.title: Rescue at Sea
passages.text: Have you helped fend off the Kvaldir attack?

passages.title: Rescue at Sea
passages.text: It seems things are worse than we initially thought.  You still made a valiant effort and saved many of The Wavecrest's crew's lives.

passages.title: Life of the Party
passages.text:
Oh wow, baby! Everyone is here! Who cares about some stupid dragon?

We setup the party around the pool. Sounds like they're having a great time already. You are going to look so fine!

Why don't you head over to the pool and keep everyone entertained? I'll join you in a moment... I just have to grab my stuff.

passages.title: Life of the Party
passages.text:
Very nicely done, ma'am. The party appears to have been a smashing success!

Er... what's that?

passages.title: Arborcide
passages.text:
How's that shredder holding up? I think I can bring your emergency power supplies online - that'll recharge you when you're wounded.

Listen, these night elves are being strengthened by an ancient of war who's taken root just west of the gates. He's a big, giant tree. You know what to do! Take him out!

You were made for this!!

passages.title: Arborcide
passages.text:
You did it, <name>! The invaders have pulled back. And they told me I was crazy for installing a grenade launcher on a woodchipper...

Great work with the Shredder. With an impressive showing like that right here on the Warchief's doorstep, the Horde can't doubt what goblin technology can do for them. I owe you a big thanks!

passages.title: Report to Horzak
passages.text:
You've done a bangup job getting our lumber operations in order. But word on the wire is that we're falling under our stone quota. You'd think if we could move mountains, we could gather up a few rocks...

Well, that's not my problem, but maybe you can make it yours. Report to Horzak Zignibble up ahead at the Orgrimmar Rocketway Exchange. See if you can't help him straighten out his operations. Just follow the road northeast and find him in the rocketway tower.

passages.title: Report to Horzak
passages.text: You're here to help? Excellent! Here, sign this indemnity waiver. And here, this noncompete clause. Let's get you started!

passages.title: Call to Arms: Isle of Conquest
passages.text:
As we get closer to victory in Icecrown, it's become more apparent that our armies are going to have to deal with the Horde before they can deal with the Lich King.

The elite guard known as the Kor'kron has been deployed to block our advance in the Isle of Conquest. The isle is of vital strategic importance, <name>. See to it that our lads prevail!

passages.title: Call to Arms: Isle of Conquest
passages.text:
Victory in Northrend will be ours soon... but not until we obtain a foothold in Icecrown to transport and supply our forces.

The Isle of Conquest is an ideal location. It is easily defensible and rich in resources. The Alliance have reached the same conclusion and have sent the Seventh Legion to wrest control of it from our forces.

Go, <name>, and ensure that the Horde prevails at any cost!

passages.title: Stone Cold
passages.text:
Workers act like it's their job to complain. If it isn't the backbreaking labor, the long hours, or the low pay, it's being turned to stone by basilisks. It's always something!

But I'm thinking maybe this whole workers-to-stone business could be a big moneymaker for me. What if those guys are now high-quality stone? My whiny employees could be worth more to me as luxury building materials than a source of labor! Grab a stonified mountainfoot miner and haul him or her back to me.

passages.title: Stone Cold
passages.text: Get to the strip mine, <name>, and get me a sample of one of my former workers!

passages.title: Stone Cold
passages.text:
Well well, let's take a look at what we got here...

<Horzak examines the shattered remains of the poor petrified miner.>

Bah! Crumbly! Useless. Wouldn't even make a good countertop. My miners may be mediocre workers, but they make lousy bricks.

<Sigh>. Well, I suppose we should re-fleshify these guys so I can get some return on my investment.

passages.title: The Grateful Dead
passages.text:
It's good to visit with friends and family again, though I may have overdone it... I've already eaten everything they made for me!

Might I trouble you for some more of that delicious Bread of the Dead? I'd be most grateful...

Chapman there sells the recipe, I think.

passages.title: The Grateful Dead
passages.text: You don't have any Bread of the Dead, do you?

passages.title: The Grateful Dead
passages.text:
Ah, more delicious Bread of the Dead, thank you!

Please, take this in return... a little something fun for the holiday.

Might I trouble you for some more of that delicious Bread of the Dead? I'd be most grateful...

Chapman there sells the recipe, I think.

passages.title: The Grateful Dead
passages.text:
It's good to visit with friends and family again, though I may have overdone it... I've already eaten everything they made for me!

Might I trouble you for some more of that delicious Bread of the Dead? I'd be most grateful...

Chapman there sells the recipe, I think.

passages.title: The Grateful Dead
passages.text: You don't have any Bread of the Dead, do you?

passages.title: The Grateful Dead
passages.text:
Ah, more delicious Bread of the Dead, thank you!

Please, take this in return... a little something fun for the holiday.

Chapman there sells the recipe, I think.

passages.title: Call to Arms: Arathi Basin
passages.text:
The reality of fighting on multiple fronts, <lad/lass>, is that we cannot spread our forces too thin or we risk losing it all!

Critical troop deployments are necessary on a day by day basis. Today it is the battle of Arathi Basin that demands immediate reinforcements.

Return to me with news of victory, <name>. We cannot allow the Horde scum to secure the resources that are rightfully ours!

passages.title: Call to Arms: Eye of the Storm
passages.text:
The fight against the Horde knows no boundaries, <name>. Even in Outland, territorial disputes and old hatreds are enough to tip the scales in favor of war.

Go into the Eye of the Storm and make sure the Alliance prevails in Outland just like it has in Azeroth.

passages.title: Call to Arms: Warsong Gulch
passages.text:
The Silverwing Sentinels fight to protect the forest in Warsong Gulch. We aid them, not because we're tree-lovers, but because the forest forms a natural protective barrier for Alliance territory.

Their need is greater today than it's ever been. We need to deploy reinforcements right away unless we want to see Ashenvale annexed to the Barrens!

passages.title: Call to Arms: Arathi Basin
passages.text:
Arathi Basin is on the verge of being lost to Alliance forces. We must send reinforcements at this very moment or all our efforts will have been in vain.

Do not delay, <class>, go to Arathi Basin and crush the enemy. Victory to the Horde!

passages.title: Call to Arms: Eye of the Storm
passages.text:
We will fight and crush the enemy wherever we find them. Azeroth, Outland, the place makes no difference.

We cannot allow the Alliance to establish superiority in the Eye of the Storm. Take the battle to them today... tomorrow it might be too late!

passages.title: Call to Arms: Warsong Gulch
passages.text:
The Alliance is an insidious enemy, <name>. They claim to defend the Ashenvale forests to justify their acts of aggression against our territories in the Barrens.

Today we have an opportunity to drive the enemy from our lands once and for all. Go to Warsong Gulch and take back what is rightfully ours!

passages.title: My Time Has Passed
passages.text:
<Weakly, Furien beckons you near and struggles to speak.>

Careless... I was shot down by Alliance fire...

You must... inform my sister.

Take my mount, <race>... he'll bring you to her...

<Furien expires.>

passages.title: My Time Has Passed
passages.text:
What!?

Furien!! My brother is no more?

They must pay! All of them!

passages.title: Translation
passages.text:
It is true that Furien dedicated his last days to a special research project. What that was, he would not share with me.

Fortunately, I was able to recover his journal, but it's written in a code that I cannot decipher.

Perhaps there is a clue to its translation in the region to the east where he spent his time.

Take the journal, <class>, and speak with Narimar when you are ready to investigate this mystery.

passages.title: Translation
passages.text: Comparing the characters on the ancient tablet to those in Furien's journal, it is clear that there is a distinct correlation.

passages.title: The Perfect Prism
passages.text:
There's got to be a way to reverse the basilisks' stonification. Those irritating night elf saboteurs who have been lurking around my mine must know something we don't. They seem to be immune to the gaze of the beast!

I want you to find out their secret, <name>. Pick off a few of the Talrendis saboteurs skulking about in the rear of the strip mine and get a sample of whatever charm or ding-dong they're wearing to give them immunity. Radio me from the main forge building once you're successful.

passages.title: The Perfect Prism
passages.text: <Strange goblin speakers hiss and crackle.>

passages.title: The Perfect Prism
passages.text:
<Zignibble's voice squawks over the speakers.>

Is that you, <name>? Still alive? You aren't trashing my explosive stockpiles are you?

Hmmm... you say you found a clear crystal pendant. That makes sense. A perfect prism would refract the gaze of the basilisk. Maybe we can use this to our advantage. Time to drop some science!

passages.title: Furien's Footsteps
passages.text:
You can decipher bits and pieces of the text, but it will require extensive study before Furien's work becomes coherent.

For now, as you look off to the northeast, you think you can make out some of the ruins depicted in the journal.

From what you can tell, these ruins seem to have been of some significance to Furien's research.

passages.title: Furien's Footsteps
passages.text:
It is clear to you now that these ruins are those that Furien recorded in his journal.

After examining the engravings upon the ruins themselves, you feel that you are able to decipher more of Furien's writings.

passages.title: Refleshification
passages.text:
<The nearby radio calls out to you.>

Hey <name>, you got that gun? Good! Don't point it directly at your eye.

Aim that baby at my stonified workers and the refracted light should reverse the petrification process. Or it will melt them. Whatever. Return my workers to a state of profitability! And if the refleshification process makes them crazy-go-nuts, they should be killed for insurance purposes. Horzak OUT!

passages.title: Refleshification
passages.text: Hey look, all your limbs are intact.

passages.title: Refleshification
passages.text: Ah, good. Now we can get these slackers back to work. You've earned a cut of the profits though - minus the usual company fees. Take your pick!

passages.title: All Becoming Clearer
passages.text:
Something has changed... perhaps a side-effect of Elune's cleansing ritual.

While it's by no means perfect yet, your understanding of the ancient language in the journal has vastly improved.

The ruins in the northern mountains of Sargeron appear to be the main focus of Furien's enthusiasm. Something there, he felt, would aid him in driving the Alliance from this region.

You close the journal determined to find this ruin and discover its secrets.

passages.title: All Becoming Clearer
passages.text: This appears to be the ruin depicted in Furien's Journal.

passages.title: All Becoming Clearer
passages.text:
It is clear to you now why you were guided here.

You recognize this ancient runestone from Furien's final journal entry:

"The ancients revered the gems created by this mystical object, claiming that they were gifts from the goddess herself. It was believed that they were weapons capable of delivering them from any enemy."

passages.title: Firestarter
passages.text:
You are now able to understand the script in which the journal was written.

Along the runestone, it is explained that the monument's gemstones were imbued with the power to summon a firestorm.

The storm could grow to be a mighty weapon either through sustained worship of Elune, or charged by spiritual energies of the fallen.

Looking down upon the newly revealed ghosts of Elune's disciples, you reason that you have neither the time, nor the inclination to worship the goddess of your enemy....

passages.title: Firestarter
passages.text:
It is done! Furien's exhaustive research was not in vain.

The raging Vortex is ready to be unleashed upon your enemies at last!

passages.title: A Quota to Meet
passages.text:
Mountainfoot iron is a brittle alloy, but with the right bribes it meets goblin safety standards. Zignibble here is having trouble on the production end of things, but that doesn't change any of my deadlines. I've got a quota to fill!

Head down into the Mountainfoot Strip Mine and gather up any ingots of Mountainfoot iron you find. There should be piles of it smelted and ready for shipment.

passages.title: A Quota to Meet
passages.text: Did you get my shipment together?

passages.title: A Quota to Meet
passages.text: Well done! When it comes to iron, always pick quantity over quality.

passages.title: Rider on the Storm
passages.text:
You cannot help but to feel a twinge of pride, having unlocked this long lost secret of the ancient worshippers of Elune.

You now possess the power to inflict great damage upon your enemy.

As it was Furien's tireless work that made this possible, it only seems right that the weapon should be unleashed upon those who took his life.

The Alliance scum at Nijel's Point shall pay for their offenses against the Horde!

passages.title: Rider on the Storm
passages.text:
Very impressive, <class>.

You completed Furien's work and rained vengeance down upon his killers.

You have brought peace to my brother's soul, and to my mind. Please accept this gift for your diligence.

passages.title: Proof of Demise: The Black Knight
passages.text:
My counterpart, Archmage Timear, has asked me to warn you of something dire. Soon, you will be participating in the Trial of the Champions at the Argent Coliseum in Icecrown. You must beware of interference from one known only as the Black Knight.

Bring me a fragment of his soul that the Kirin Tor will know he is dealt with. I am told that failing to do so will be your own undoing.

passages.title: A Thousand Stories in the Sand
passages.text:
The ruins around Lake Mennar, to our east, have a tale to tell. The lesser races - like those clumsy dwarves - would go after the truth with picks and shovels. <Malynea wrinkles her nose.> We'll be using more elegant methods.

My scrying magic is somewhat rusty, but with the right trinket I should be able to peer through the shrouds of time. The bones of my forefathers have long since rotted away but some of their personal treasures may remain - bring me some.

passages.title: A Thousand Stories in the Sand
passages.text: Have you gotten your hands dirty for me?

passages.title: A Thousand Stories in the Sand
passages.text:
<Malynea furrows her brow and begins sifting through the artifacts you brought her.>

So the spirits of the dead still haunt those old stones, hm? Well <name>, as it happens, I'm counting on their help. Let's see what the dead have to say...

passages.title: Survey the Lakeshore
passages.text:
All these cruddy ancient ruins have to be bulldozed if we're ever to see Azshara's full potential. Look on my map here - you see Lake Mennar, to the East? I'll tell you what I see: a future rocket fuel depot!

But we need an accurate lay of the land before we can clearcut, bulldoze, landfill, and pave over that lake. All of my surveyors have been spooked off by the oogly-boogleys haunting that area. Escort one of my Jr. grade surveyors to the area and take readings from the equipment that's been set up.

passages.title: Survey the Lakeshore
passages.text: No buncha dead elves can put a stop to progress. Not on my watch!

passages.title: Survey the Lakeshore
passages.text: Beautiful work! Now that we know the area better, we can tear this lake a new one.

passages.title: Gunk in the Trunk
passages.text:
Those ancient ruins have survived ten thousand years of wind and weather, so I brought out my biggest and bestest bulldozer to flatten 'em. I call her "Margene."

But my dozer's been letting me down lately, <name>. The moment I drove her into those haunted woods, her engine seized up with a spine-chilling howl. Now my engineers tell me something's clogging her valves. Go over there and inspect Margene's engine compartment, and bring me back a sample of whatever gunk has her stalled.

passages.title: Gunk in the Trunk
passages.text: Margene is one heck of a machine, isn't she?

passages.title: Gunk in the Trunk
passages.text:
Busted ball bearings! Look at this stuff - ugh, SMELL this stuff - my poor, poor dozer!

<name>, I consider myself a goop expert and this here goop ain't natural. It's supernatural. This is ghost goop. We're going to need more than a mechanic...

passages.title: Ten Pounds of Flesh
passages.text:
According to Furien's Journal, this ancient brazier was placed here for the performing of sacrifices.

As far as you can make out from the entry, a blessing is bestowed upon the being who places the flesh of Elune's enemies on the brazier's burning embers.

Looking around, you determine that the satyrs who now possess this region would likely qualify.

passages.title: Ten Pounds of Flesh
passages.text: The brazier silently awaits an offering.

passages.title: Ten Pounds of Flesh
passages.text: The divine brazier indiscriminately endows you with a blessing.

passages.title: Memories of the Dead
passages.text:
The runes on this ring you found are still legible: it was given to "Kalytha" when she was granted admission to the Academy. With the right spell or two, this personal trinket of hers is the gateway to her soul.

Take the ring back to Lake Mennar. Kalytha's spirit should now be visible to you on the shore of the lake. Touch her and the ring will allow you to see the world as she sees it, forever reliving her final hours. Probe her mind, <name>! Speak to the others and learn the secrets of Lake Mennar...

passages.title: Memories of the Dead
passages.text: You reel as the spirit's vision fades, relieved to once again feel the earth beneath your feet and the comforting rhythm of your own quickened heart.

passages.title: To the Hilt!
passages.text:
You immediately recognize this statue from a sketch in Furien's Journal.

Though the words associated with the entry elude you, the sketch seems self-explanatory. After battle, the enemies' weapons were to be cast upon the basin in exchange for a divine gift of some sort.

As you ponder this ritual, the glint of steel catches your eye from a nearby weapon rack....

passages.title: To the Hilt!
passages.text: The statue stands expectantly.

passages.title: To the Hilt!
passages.text:
With the ritual completed, you are awarded a divine gift.

You can't help but wonder what Elune would think of someone such as you receiving one of her boons.

passages.title: You'll Know It When You See It
passages.text:
With his dying breath, Kohor mentioned the summoning of a demon that could threaten the entire region.

He may have been bluffing, but that's not a chance worth taking.

This cannot wait for the Horde's invasion of Desolace to take shape. You must scour Thunder Axe Fortress for clues and bring an end to this potential threat.

passages.title: You'll Know It When You See It
passages.text: The Burning Blade must not be allowed to succeed with their plan!

passages.title: You'll Know It When You See It
passages.text:
It is most fortunate that you took the time to search for this.

No one would have expected the Burning Blade to be in possession of something so powerful!

passages.title: Putting Their Heads Together
passages.text:
So it's true....

The parchment you discovered in Thunder Axe Fortress details a powerful summoning ritual. One stronger than the Burning Blade have ever been known to possess.

Clearly, this rite must be stopped at all costs!

Perhaps if this demon were summoned forth prematurely the crisis could be averted.

passages.title: Putting Their Heads Together
passages.text:
You diverted what would have been a serious crisis, <class>.

If that summoning was delayed just a bit longer, the demon would have become far too powerful for our small forces here to contend with.

Please accept this gift as our thanks for your service.

passages.title: It's a Town-In-A-Box
passages.text:
The trade prince had an entire town-in-a-box in the ship's hold! I managed to recover it while you were out saving all of our skins.

Do you want to do the honors? All you have to do is climb to the top of that huge pile of explosives and push the plunger, and whamo kablamo, instant town!

passages.title: It's a Town-In-A-Box
passages.text:
<cough, cough!>

Hey! Where's the dock?! Someone stole the dock and the oil refinery from our town-in-a-box!

Who would do such a thing?

Where's the Trade Prince?

passages.title: Early Adoption
passages.text:
As the region becomes more lush, the creatures of the desert are being forced into increasingly confined spaces.

A particularly distressing result is the impending extinction of the local swoops. Predators feast on the birds and their eggs when they take nest.

I have acquired some swoop eggs from Tanaris and coated them with an irresistible pheromone. Place one in each nest you find, then protect it until a swoop comes to carry it off.

You will be doing a service to the balance of this land.

passages.title: Early Adoption
passages.text:
You have done well, <class>.

This land is in your debt.

passages.title: Shear Will
passages.text:
I'd be amazing! At archmagery. Amazing! He won't even talk to me because I don't have a stupid robe and hat. Pffft.

The most amazing archmage this land has ever seen can't just have any robe and hat. I need to show him that I'm something special, and I know just how to do it.

Go out there and kill some of those hippogryph things. Bring me back a TON of feathers.

You heard me! A whole bunch of feathers! Go go, I'll have the robe ready for them by the time you get back.

passages.title: Shear Will
passages.text: My robes looking pretty good. Did you bring those feathers?

passages.title: Shear Will
passages.text: Ha ha! Perfect! Let me toss this together really fast. The Archmage is sure to be taken in by my style!

passages.title: Fletch Me Some Plumage!
passages.text:
Say, <class>, while you're out there exploring the desert wastes, do me a favor?

Keep an eye out for Dread Swoops. Their oily feathers make for the best fletching, and to the right buyer they can fetch a handsome price.

Lucky for you, I know all of the right buyers!

passages.title: Fletch Me Some Plumage!
passages.text: How is the search for swoops coming?

passages.title: Fletch Me Some Plumage!
passages.text:
Well now, that's quite a load of feathers, <class>.

They'll make for a good pillow 'til I get 'em to market!

passages.title: Slitherblade Slaughter
passages.text:
Time and again, the naga have proven to be enemies to the balance of nature. I have no qualms with the spilling of their blood.

Your best efforts though, would barely put a dent in their forces here. Where one falls, two seem to rise in their place.

I have a plan, <class>. Your objective is not merely to take the lives of the enemy, but to gather components necessary for the next stage of our investigation....

passages.title: Slitherblade Slaughter
passages.text: Have you collected the components I require?

passages.title: Slitherblade Slaughter
passages.text: You have done well, <class>. But I'm afraid that your work here is just beginning.

passages.title: Mortar the Point
passages.text:
The Naga started making a move on the peninsula here after we finished building this rocketway terminal. But there's no problem in this world that can't be solved with gratuitous firepower! That's what my daddy used to say. Before the accident.

I'm running short on supplies, though. Do me a favor and collect the mortar shells I left stockpiled in the Secret Lab just west of here. Keep me supplied and I'll let you call in the artillery strikes!

passages.title: Mortar the Point
passages.text: I hope you have more ammo for me. I've got nothing to shoot off over here but my mouth!

passages.title: Mortar the Point
passages.text:
Sweet! Beautiful! Brilliant! Who loves you?

With my mortars re-supplied, I can help you as you assault the Naga east of here. Use these markers to call in an artillery strike anywhere on the cliffs, and I'll splatter the whole area with fiery hurt. Oh delicious, merciless, random destruction! I hope you're well-armored...

passages.title: Wetter Than Wet
passages.text:
Neptulon's minions have arrived here and are doing all they can to thwart us. Clearly, they've discovered our motives.

This only confirms my suspicion that what we seek is indeed somewhere in these ruins!

These water elementals are no match for our forces! Take this trident and use it to destroy the worthless servants of the Tidehunter.

When we find what we seek here, Neptulon himself shall fear for his life!

passages.title: Wetter Than Wet
passages.text: Tell me, minnow. Have you done as I asked?

passages.title: Wetter Than Wet
passages.text:
The enemy's ranks are thinning, little minnow.

Perhaps you are worthy of assisting in our search....

passages.title: Charge
passages.text:
You're alive, <name>! That must mean I did something right.

It's a shame our lessons were cut off a little short. But, as you go and learn on your own, you'll start to discover new techniques.

Go get some more experience, learn something new, and then try it out against the bloodfang worgen to our west.

passages.title: Charge
passages.text: Excellent work!

passages.title: Deep Impact
passages.text:
Queen Azshara seeks entrance into the plane of water, for what I do not know.

She believes that the ancients held the keys to finding its location.

I have personally been charged with scouring the ruins in this region, and none shall rest until we discover the secrets we seek!

Submerged just to the north are a concentration of ruins. Use this staff to search through the rubble.

Return to me only when you have located that which we seek!

passages.title: Deep Impact
passages.text: Could it be....?

passages.title: Deep Impact
passages.text:
Yes! You've found it!

Neptulon's engravings... there can be no mistake!

passages.title: Report to Twocrush
passages.text:
A magical barrier pulses around you, chilling your bones. You feel secure behind this enchanted wall.

Torg Twocrush will want to know what you've discovered here!

passages.title: Report to Twocrush
passages.text:
An energy barrier, you say? This explains a great deal! I've seen firsthand how Naga leaders have been able to turn aside the blades of some of my best warriors.

Now we know the source of their power, <name>. Let's finish this!

passages.title: Eviscerate
passages.text:
Good to see you alive!

No, of course I don't have that gold I owe you. Now's not really the time to bring that up is it?

Listen, maybe I can show you the ropes, save your skin with all the carnage going on. 

As you learn how to fight, you'll start to learn new things. Go get some more experience, and then when you figure out something new, try it on the Bloodfang Worgen. I'll be watching

passages.title: Eviscerate
passages.text:
Don't get ahead of yourself now.  Just remember who taught you everything you know.

And now let's see if we can get out of this city with our skins attached.

passages.title: Corruption
passages.text:
It is true then! You live!

I never got a chance to share my greatest discovery with you. After I began my training, and began to become accomplished, I heard the voice Balcephoth of the felshadows in my head... he taught me the forbidden secrets of...

Corruption!

Go now, gain some more experience, maybe you'll learn a new spell, too. You can go use it against the Bloodfang Worgen to our west.

passages.title: Corruption
passages.text: Yes!  You can feel the power, can't you?

passages.title: Steady Shot
passages.text:
So I've got good news and bad news.

The bad news is that there are more worgen in the woods than in here... so we really have no safe place to go to.

The good news is that you're starting to get the hang of this. As you get more experience, you'll start to learn how to do new things.

Once you learn your first new ability, try your hand at it against the bloodfang worgen to our west.

passages.title: Steady Shot
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  These <race> will regret ever setting foot in our lands.

passages.title: Learning the Word
passages.text:
You have much to learn, <name>. And I've much to teach you.

These are perilous times, however, and I fear that you may need to learn much on your own

Have no fear, <brother/sister>. The Light will guide us through this.

Go, get more experience, and learn a new skill. Use it against the bloodfang worgen nearby.

passages.title: Learning the Word
passages.text: You are blessed, <name>.  The Light shines upon you, even in these dark times.

passages.title: Mystery Solved
passages.text:
Your efforts have paid off. The great risks you have taken have proven worthwhile.

You have discovered the object of the nagas' desire and their reason for overrunning the coast of Desolace.

As for the engravings you've discovered, your duty is clear...

passages.title: Mystery Solved
passages.text: What have you learned, <class>?

passages.title: Mystery Solved
passages.text:
The vision was true!

You have singlehandedly succeeded where others have failed.

The Circle will have no choice but to pay attention to these findings.

passages.title: Watch Your Step
passages.text:
This is somewhat simple and somewhat not simple. All the way up there are Energy Conduits. Rather like this one right here one might say! Indeed, I do say.

Now for you. You must use my jump pads to ascend the pinnacle, and you must touch all of the conduits you see along the way. When you get to me at the top, you should be all juicy with energy, because really that's the only way to be.

And be sure to keep moving or you're likely to be sent for quite a trip!

passages.title: Watch Your Step
passages.text:
No no no, you've got it all wrong. You were supposed to gather Energy from the Conduits before you came up here, remember?

One more time, with style!

passages.title: Watch Your Step
passages.text:
It is in this moment that most of my apprentices wonder if there was a logical purpose to storing the energy for my portal in those conduits so that it has to be collected in such a fashion.

Of course there's a purpose! I wish to study your behavior... your strategies, your mistakes, your frustrations, your triumphs. Those are the entire point of these trials.

Now, more. More trials! Doesn't that sound exciting?! Of course it does.

passages.title: Pro-liberation
passages.text:
I knew these guys would be trouble as soon as we started building this tower. Scoffing our bribes. Stealing our workers.

Labor isn't cheap with all the construction in Azshara. I need those men back!

passages.title: Pro-liberation
passages.text: There's no way I'm paying them for time in captivity. Greedy little punks.

passages.title: Pro-liberation
passages.text:
Thanks there, pal. Here's your commission.

If you'll excuse me, I've gotta get these slackers back to work.

passages.title: Xylem's Asylum
passages.text:
Quite marvelous of you! A pleasure to observe. Much to study.

Off you go now, retire to my tower. Joanna will get you situated. I shall open a portal for you.

passages.title: Xylem's Asylum
passages.text:
Welcome! You seem to have survived the trials relatively unscathed. Good for you, love.

You look to have come with a purpose in mind as well. A question. Your thoughts are very loud, it's hard for me to not hear them.

Go ahead then, hon. Ask away.

passages.title: The Trial of Fire
passages.text:
The Trial of Fire... oooh... sounds intimidating, doesn't it? No? Hm. Well I kind of thought so. Firsts are first, you touch the fire crystal and the portal to the trial opens.

To beat this trial, you have to hop around in the fire runes without getting hit by the fire. If you stay unflamed long enough, you win!

There are little signs to help you - fire hopping to its new rune, fizzles when a rune goes cold. You can figure that stuff out if you want. Or just guess! That's what most people do.

passages.title: The Trial of Fire
passages.text: Um, no. You're not done. Get back in there and get toasty!

passages.title: The Trial of Fire
passages.text: Woo! Good for you! That trial really put a fire under your bottom.

passages.title: Official Assessment
passages.text:
You have accomplished much in your efforts against the naga, <name>. But I fear it is not nearly enough....

This is my official assessment of the naga presence.

I'm confident that my peers in the wildlands will take the necessary action.

Bring this to Karnum at the glade in the center of the Cenarion Wildlands to the southeast. He will know what to do.

Thank you, <name>. And farewell.

passages.title: Official Assessment
passages.text:
<Karnum opens and reads Korrah's Report.>

This is alarming news, indeeed, <race> - something we have no shortage of here.

I shall call a council regarding the issue. You will be summoned if you are needed.

passages.title: When Science Attacks
passages.text:
Did you see the explosions on the way in? The Secret Lab is engulfed in flames! Again! If we don't stamp out those flames we're going to hit critical temperatacity and resonate into a meltdown cascade.

Here, I'm entrusting you with a canister of experimental hypercooled pressurized liquigel: The most volatile fire retardant known to science! (Keep that canister away from open flame.) Put out the fires and hose down my interns, then contact me via the squawkbox in central control.

passages.title: When Science Attacks
passages.text:
<Greely's squeaky voice peels through a set of speakers.>

Rocketway to Secret Lab! Rocketway to Secret Lab! Come in, Secret Lab...

passages.title: When Science Attacks
passages.text: Nice work, <name>! Now, we need to decouple the reaction core matrix from the fuel sumps, or that whole place is gonna blow itself to Outland...

passages.title: Segmentation Fault: Core Dumped
passages.text:
Once we flush the central reactor, I need you to return the core to me. It's 100% refined azsharite crystal, which is both powerful and dangerous. And lovely. Oh precious azsharite, the shaper of worlds to come!

The giant lever to your left will dump the core and send it to me via the rail system. The core will be superheated, so you'll need to periodically douse it with the Fireliminator on the way here... don't let it reach critical temperature!

passages.title: Segmentation Fault: Core Dumped
passages.text: Don't worry about the residual effects of all those burning chemicals in the lab. Hair grows back!

passages.title: Segmentation Fault: Core Dumped
passages.text:
Whew, the sample is secure. And it's still steaming! Thank you, <name>.

Azsharite is a complex mystery wrapped in a velvety enigma of danger. Grapplehammer insists that we learn more about this strange substance.

passages.title: Taking Part
passages.text:
What a glorious time we live in!

The former wastelands of Desolace are blooming, bursting with life. Imagine, <class>, if all of Azeroth's wastelands awoke in such a fashion! Perhaps someday...

It's true that there are weighty issues at hand here, but why not take a moment to appreciate the wondrous miracle we are witnessing?

In fact, why not take part in it? Here are some Cenarion Seeds. Use them at the more fertile spots of the wildlands.

Perfect medicine for lifting a weary soul!

passages.title: Taking Part
passages.text: The rejuvenation is so invigorating! Don't you think?

passages.title: An Introduction Is In Order
passages.text:
I have heard of your exploits here in Desolace, <name>. We are in your debt.

I'm afraid I must involve you in yet another crisis, one more pressing than the rest.

The landscape is not all that has changed here of late. Old conflicts have made way for new, more dire ones. I should allow our guest to explain further....

Khan Leh'prah is among the last of the Kolkar tribe that once possessed all of eastern Desolace. We found him near death on our borders. Listen to his words.

passages.title: An Introduction Is In Order
passages.text: Be not afraid, <race>. I mean you no harm.

passages.title: Delicate Negotiations
passages.text:
There is but one way to win the trust and loyalty of the Magram.

It must be beaten out of them.

They have suffered many losses in their war against my clan. They now possess an unfamiliar land, where they struggle just to feed themselves.

Now is the time to strike.

Speak to me when you are ready, then ride in and plant my spear in the Fatherstone. If we can kill enough of them, their Khan will submit to our will.

passages.title: Delicate Negotiations
passages.text: What do you want?

passages.title: Delicate Negotiations
passages.text: Why is it that you meddle in centaur affairs, <race>?

passages.title: Full of Hot Water
passages.text: Ergll indicated that you should be able to use the Engorged Azshara Sea Sponge to summon a "jumbo" elemental near the Tower of Eldara to the northeast.

passages.title: Full of Hot Water
passages.text: You're back!

passages.title: Full of Hot Water
passages.text: Convenient, no? Who needs hot springs anyway. This is perfect.

passages.title: Not So Fast!
passages.text:
<The Khan of the Gelkis clan stares at you with an empty gaze as you detail the demon threat and Leh'prah's visions.>

It matters not to me what becomes of this land now. I have failed my clan and my forefathers....

There is but one thing left in this world that might bring my old soul hope, and she's likely dead as well.

My precious daughter, Kherrah, was taken from me by the Maraudine clan. If you can bring her back to me alive, I shall consider your proposal.

passages.title: Not So Fast!
passages.text: As you slaughter their enemy, the Gelkis clan cannot help but to acknowledge your prowess.

passages.title: Blubbergut
passages.text:
Ahoy, mon!

You think you be able ta do something for da village here?

Most whales we can handle fine, but there be a special whale out there that be too big for our spears.

Blubbergut been gettin' bigger an' bigger - eatin' up the fish we use to live on!

Get out there and find the thing, then make him pay for his gluttony!

passages.title: Blubbergut
passages.text:
Oy, mon! Ya did it!

We soon be havin' fish to eat, thanks be to you.

passages.title: Chipping In
passages.text:
As you have no doubt noticed by now, the recent changes to the land have had many side-effects. Some of these are beneficial, while others pose serious problems.

Just south of the village the local lobstrok are emerging from the sea and choking off the road to the village.

Please, <class>, go and thin the numbers of this pest.

passages.title: Chipping In
passages.text: Has our lobstrok problem been dealt with, <class>?

passages.title: Chipping In
passages.text: On behalf of us all at Shadowprey Village, I thank you, <race>.

passages.title: Dressed to Impress
passages.text:
Every man's got to learn his own lessons I suppose.

Here, take my wizard hat. I have no doubt that he'll take you on as an apprentice if you look the role... you just might have to jump through some hoops first. Tiny flaming hoops, suspended over spikes, with spinning blades on the other side.

You should be able to find an image of Xylem on top of that hill to the northeast.

passages.title: Dressed to Impress
passages.text: Hello.

passages.title: Dressed to Impress
passages.text:
Well look at you, aren't you just a marvel of modern Magery! Quite a fancy hat, I must say.

Apprentices. Apprentici? I do think that I might have quite a few already, but I suppose one can never have too many appren..tici.

passages.title: Infernal Encroachment
passages.text:
The demons are on the move, <race>!

If nothing is done, we'll be overrun in a matter of weeks. I've just returned from Mannoroc Coven, where the infernals there are falling from the sky!

We need to at least buy ourselves some time. Get down there and pick up where I left off!

passages.title: Infernal Encroachment
passages.text:
Well done, <race>!

The danger persists, but you have bought us some time.

passages.title: Maurin's Concoction
passages.text:
<Maurin carefully seals his concoction into the hollow kodo horns.>

Here you are, <class>.

Bring these to Karnum. It's up to him how he wants to use them on the naga. 

I'll be watching to gauge the effectiveness of my formula!

passages.title: Maurin's Concoction
passages.text: I hate to use such unnatural measures, but I fear we simply have no choice....

passages.title: Jugkar's Undoing
passages.text:
You recognize this as the essence of a summoned demon.

Dangerous and rarely understood energies weave in and out of its surface.

As you gaze upon it, a vision fills your mind - an image of yourself controlling demonic minions. A rush of excitement flows through you as you imagine wielding such power.

Looking at your surroundings, you wonder how this treasure might be used against this demonic enemy....

passages.title: Jugkar's Undoing
passages.text:
You should be proud of how you manipulated the enemy's power and used it against them.

You've dealt the demons of Mannoroc a severe blow....

passages.title: Cleansing Our Crevasse
passages.text:
As you of course know, <name>, the naga remain a serious threat to the region. The time has come for us to drive them back into the sea!

When you are ready, Grimfeather will take you to the crevasse where they are preparing a violent assault. Once there, use Maurin's Concoction to teach them a lesson they shall not soon forget.

passages.title: Cleansing Our Crevasse
passages.text: Have you dealt with the naga in our crevasse, <name>?

passages.title: Cleansing Our Crevasse
passages.text:
Your deeds continue to impress me, <name>.

Please accept this gift on behalf of the Cenarion Circle.

passages.title: The Crimson Courier
passages.text:
We cannot attack the Scarlet Crusade's command directly; they are too well defended. But there's more than one way to skin a cat. They'll be nothing without their main force.

The Deathstalkers have been collecting data on the activity of the Crusade outside of Stratholme. Each day, a report is sent from their central command to Tyr's Hand. This report is the key, <race>! Find the Crimson Courier and recover that report. Bring it to Nathanos.

passages.title: The Crimson Courier
passages.text: Succeed now and you will have almost earned my respect, <class>.

passages.title: The Crimson Courier
passages.text:
<Nathanos laughs.>

Excellent! Finally! An opportunity to destroy the Scarlet Oracle!

passages.title: [DEPRECATED] Battle of Hillsbrad
passages.text:
Because you fought with such valor and perseverance in the Battle of Hillsbrad, I have written this commendation, extolling your heroics in combat for the high command to recognize.

Take this sealed commendation to Bragor Bloodfist in the Undercity. Go with pride, <class>.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED] Battle of Hillsbrad
passages.text: Why aren't you out on the battlefield, <class>?

passages.title: [DEPRECATED] Battle of Hillsbrad
passages.text:
So you're the <class> who tore through the Alliance forces in the Hillsbrad Foothills? I've heard your name already. Word travels fast.

The Horde can use someone like you if you keep this up, <name>.

We need to keep our eyes on all threats around us, but with that king leading them, the humans will continue to be a problem. You've confirmed that there's strength enough in the Horde to end that threat in time.

passages.title: An Unholy Alliance
passages.text:
Supposedly this Malcin is outside Razorfen Downs. There's no question - he has to die.

My contacts in Orgrimmar tell me their scouts have found signs of the Plague down there. The quilboar are showing signs of being plagued, too; they're much more powerful. Whatever the Scourge are doing down there needs to end. Now.

Find this Malcin and kill him. Report back here when he's dead.

passages.title: An Unholy Alliance
passages.text:
Did you find the Ambassador, <name>? Did you kill him?

I will not have the Scourge gain a foothold in Kalimdor. We've fought too hard to allow them easy access to our cities.

At least their crone still numbers among the living. She might be stupid enough to allow the Scourge in her home, but she must have sense enough to know she'd lose everything if she took the 'power' they offer.

passages.title: An Unholy Alliance
passages.text:
Good work, <class>!

You've done the Horde proud by stopping the Scourge from setting down roots on our soil. An act like that deserves a reward, and the Forsaken have enough lying around that I'm sure they can spare a few things.

We may not know everything they've done in the Downs, but we'll find out. They can't slink around in the dark forever.

passages.title: Elune's Gifts
passages.text:
Simply intolerable!

Satyrs of all things, desecrating our sacred lands...

Their days are numbered, <race>. I can assure you of that. As soon as we have the numbers, I shall lead a charge that will rid this land of the wicked creatures.

For now, though, perhaps you could put my mind at ease?

Travel just east of here to Sargeron and scour the ruins. Find the relics of Elune and ensure that they are in good condition.

I'll pay you well for this favor.

passages.title: Elune's Gifts
passages.text:
The relics are intact! Well, indeed, that is something.

You have put my mind at ease, <race>. Please accept this as my gift to you.

passages.title: Into The Scarlet Monastery
passages.text:
One of my duties while I'm stationed here is to help the Forsaken take care of their borders, and that, <class>, is exactly what you're going to do for me.

I might live and breathe, but the Scarlet Crusade will cut down my people as quickly as they will one of the undead. They're a problem here, a big one, and you're going to do something about it.

Go to the Monastery and slay High Inquisitor Whitemane and her lieutenants.

passages.title: Into The Scarlet Monastery
passages.text: I'm sure Sylvanas will be glad to have that problem taken care of, <name>. The task I gave you wasn't easy, but here you stand, victorious. That commands respect, and what you've done won't be forgotten.

passages.title: The Power to Destroy...
passages.text:
Listen up, <class>.

You may not know this, but Orgrimmar's got a problem. Deep in Ragefire Chasm, a sect of the Shadow Council called the Searing Blade performs their sinister work. They're mainly orcs, and I can't trust sensitive information in the hands of the grunts there. That's where you come in.

They should have two books in their possession. I want them kept out of the hands of the Searing Blade and the Forsaken alike. Bring them to me directly.

passages.title: The Power to Destroy...
passages.text: Did you secure the books? They need to be kept out of the wrong hands.

passages.title: The Power to Destroy...
passages.text:
Good, <class>. You've done well. I'll keep these safe from prying eyes; the last thing we need is a strong Shadow Council rising up again.

Check back with me in the future; there's always something that needs doing around here, apparently, and I might need another able body.

passages.title: To the Hilt!
passages.text:
The handmaiden of Elune! It's even more glorious than the stories tell.

The legends surrounding this relic come to your mind as you draw near it:

In ancient time, after battle, the enemies' weapons were to be cast upon the basin in exchange for a divine gift of some sort.

As you ponder this ritual, the glint of steel catches your eye from a nearby weapon rack....

passages.title: To the Hilt!
passages.text: The statue stands expectantly.

passages.title: To the Hilt!
passages.text:
With the ritual completed, you are awarded a divine gift.

You can't help but to feel a great sense of honor as you receive one of Elune's boons.

passages.title: Nothing a Couple of Melons Won't Fix
passages.text:
The markings on the Sargeron ruins, combined with what you've gleaned from Furien's text make one thing clear:

There is something special about the old fountain in the Sanctuary of Elune.

It would seem that one could expect special power from washing their face in the fountain. First, of course, there would need to be something in the ancient fountain with which to wash.

Pondering this problem, you spot a melonfruit at the base of a nearby tree....

passages.title: Nothing a Couple of Melons Won't Fix
passages.text:
After filling it with liquid from the melons, you proceed to wash your eyes from the ancient font.

Upon opening your eyes, you are able to see the spirits of ancient elves, still faithfully carrying out rituals to their goddess.

You ponder the significance of this revelation and determine to study Furien's research for more clues....

passages.title: Putting Their Heads Together
passages.text:
So it's true....

The parchment you discovered in Thunder Axe Fortress details a powerful summoning ritual. One stronger than the Burning Blade have ever been known to possess.

Clearly, this rite must be stopped at all costs!

Perhaps if this demon were summoned forth prematurely the crisis could be averted.

passages.title: Putting Their Heads Together
passages.text:
You diverted what would have been a serious crisis, <class>.

If that summoning was delayed just a bit longer, the demon would have become far too powerful for our small forces here to contend with.

Please accept this gift as our thanks for your service.

passages.title: A Gigantic Snack
passages.text:
While you're here running around the cliffs, perhaps you can help me with another line of investigation. The giants who walk these cliffs have been here since these mountains formed. Maybe they know where the Azsharite comes from? It's in our best interest to befriend these giants and find out.

Gather up a gigantic meal for me as a peace offering! Kill the mistwing cliffdwellers that have been such a nuisance to our studies and collect their carcasses for me.

passages.title: A Gigantic Snack
passages.text: I probably should've warned you that mistwing chimaeras can shoot lightning.

passages.title: A Gigantic Snack
passages.text: Phew! The stench! Well, hopefully that massive heap of carcasses smells more appetizing to a giant.

passages.title: Jugkar's Undoing
passages.text:
You recognize this as the essence of a summoned demon.

Dangerous and rarely understood energies weave in and out of its surface.

As you gaze upon it, a vision fills your mind - an image of yourself controlling demonic minions. A rush of excitement flows through you as you imagine wielding such power.

Looking at your surroundings, you wonder how this treasure might be used against this demonic enemy....

passages.title: Jugkar's Undoing
passages.text:
You should be proud of how you manipulated the enemy's power and used it against them.

You've dealt the demons of Mannoroc a severe blow....

passages.title: Befriending Giants
passages.text:
A cursory study of the azsharite you brought me reveals that it's not biological in nature, nor is it naturally formed. There's another creature in Azshara with similar properties: the cliff giants that lumber around these cliffs.

One of the giants seems willing to help our research along. Take the meat you collected to Gormungan, the giant standing just west of here. Befriend him, then grill him - find out if he knows the secret of azsharite!

passages.title: Befriending Giants
passages.text: What did you discover? You look pale, <class>!

passages.title: Befriending Giants
passages.text:
Speak slower - what are you saying? Am I hearing you right? Those formations of azsharite are actually where the giants have - oh my. Groady!! Let's not tell Dr. Grapplehammer, he's made this stuff his life's work.

Well, at least now we know where azsharite comes from, and why it's so rare. We've got to figure out a way to speed up, uh, "production!"

passages.title: Cleansing Our Crevasse
passages.text:
I recognize this foul creation. It's a terrible disease that kills almost instantly, and in a most violent manner. Loathe as I am to employ such devices, I fear we have no choice here.

As you of course know, the naga remain a serious threat to the region. The time has come for us to drive them back into the sea!

When you are ready, Grimfeather will take you to the crevasse where they are preparing a violent assault.

Use the concoction on the naga and their allies to make Desolace safe!

passages.title: Cleansing Our Crevasse
passages.text: Have you dealt with the naga in our crevasse, <name>?

passages.title: Cleansing Our Crevasse
passages.text:
Your deeds continue to impress me, <name>.

Please accept this gift on behalf of the Cenarion Circle.

passages.title: The Terrible Tinkers of the Ruined Reaches
passages.text:
Scoundrels! Infidels! Ever since I started my operation here in Azshara the Gadgetspring family has hampered my studies and sabotaged my research. And now a mob of middling, second-rate tinkers have rallied to their aid! I have pressing business to attend to: see to it that those gnomes are finished for good.

Head to the Ruined Reaches on the coast, south of my Secret Lab, and start rolling some of their disproportionately enormous heads for me.

passages.title: The Terrible Tinkers of the Ruined Reaches
passages.text: I trust you've dug a significant number of tiny graves along the coast, yes?

passages.title: The Terrible Tinkers of the Ruined Reaches
passages.text: Oh - marvelous. Tell me more. And that precocious young Gadgetspring? Dead as well? Ah, wonderful. My work here is important but at times I do miss the carnage of demolishing my enemies on a more personal level. Here, perhaps you can make use of some of my discarded equipment.

passages.title: Azsharite Experiment Number One
passages.text:
Well, I can think of one surefire way to send a giant running to the bathroom, but you're not going to like it. What we need is a ... massive ... laxative. Oh hey! Would you believe the gnomes have something of the sort? That can't be a coincidence. I wonder what they're trying to push through over there?

Our intelligence reports that the laxative was delivered to Gadgetspring's tower, down on the shoreline south of the Secret Lab. Retrieve that laxative and feed it to Gormungan!

passages.title: Azsharite Experiment Number One
passages.text: Once you have the laxative, try to feed it to Gormungan. And maybe give him a magazine or something. Do it for science!

passages.title: Azsharite Experiment Number One
passages.text:
So it was a no-go? Literally? Well, Grapplehammer won't take no for an answer. We'll have to try something else.

Maybe I'll have my interns smuggle this laxative into the night elf encampment. That'll be good for a laugh, at least.

passages.title: Azsharite Experiment Number Two
passages.text:
Okay, new plan. We'll SCARE it out of 'em! In my experience most large creatures are terrified of tiny ones - like rats. Hmm. This place is crawling with rats, but how do we coax them over to the giant?

Hey! You don't mind having your cellular matrix broken down and reassembled do you? It's only painful while it's happening. I can shrink you down to rat-sized and you can ride one of these brutes over there like a horse. It's so crazy it's got to work! Speak with me when you're ready for shrinkage...

passages.title: Azsharite Experiment Number Two
passages.text: Hey <name>, you look shaken up. Did you scare the giant into going to the bathroom? Or yourself?

passages.title: Azsharite Experiment Number Two
passages.text: So scaring him didn't work, either? Double-nertz! I'll have to break the news to Grapplehammer: Azsharite's going to remain the rarest substance on the planet. We'll have to use it sparingly.

passages.title: Wasn't It Obvious?
passages.text:
Azuregos! Yes, of course. Troubled old dragon, but lovely heart. I don't think all the years of vagabonds assaulting him have done him much good. He's a mite strange these days.

Not long ago, when returning yet again to our local Spirit Healer, Anara, I couldn't help but notice that her and Azuregos seemed to be hitting it off. I imagine he's still keeping her company.

The portal behind me is probably the quickest way to reach her. It might sting a little though.

passages.title: Wasn't It Obvious?
passages.text: Azuregos! At last you've found him!

passages.title: Turning the Tables
passages.text:
Azuregos and Kalecgos are due to meet up at the Northern Rocketway Terminus. You should meet with them there to make sure that Kalecgos doesn't require any additional help.

Should you prefer to not be dead, Anara will likely be able to help.

passages.title: Turning the Tables
passages.text:
Great to see you again! Thank you for finding Azuregos and sending him to me.

I do feel I owe you an apology - I may have undersold how difficult it would be to accomplish the task I gave you. You performed quite admirably, <name>.

passages.title: Into the Fray!
passages.text:
For untold generations, the centaur clans have fought against one another, but no more.

Because of your deeds, we stand here together fighting a common foe. We shall win our ancestral lands back from these demons, or we shall die as brothers.

What of you, <name>?

You have earned the right to fight alongside us. I have a group of my best centaurs for you to lead into battle.

Will you take up the spear?

passages.title: Into the Fray!
passages.text:
Well done, <name>!

Let us finish this!

passages.title: Death to Agogridon
passages.text:
Our goal is within sight, <name>!

We can break the will of this demon army by bringing down the one who leads them. If we can succeed, Desolace will be ours!

When you are ready, lead a group of centaurs through the pass to the south, into Shadowbreak Ravine. Find where Agogridon hides!

I will gather the other khans and meet you there to face him in battle.

passages.title: Death to Agogridon
passages.text:
Agogridon is no more.

The demons shall never again take hold in our lands!

passages.title: Nine's Plan
passages.text:
My benefactors used their diminutive intellect to construct an interplanetary transport. As designed, this so-called "Rocket" is a death trap. But I suspect a simple re-engineering of the fuel catalyst semifold would render a stable mixture, providing a breathable oxygen byproduct. To implement such changes, I require the original engineering plans.

Locate the Laboratory Archives and ring the doorbell to gain entry. The plans will be held by the lab director himself, presuming he still lives.

passages.title: Nine's Plan
passages.text: I suspect the archives are close, <name>. Locate those plans!

passages.title: Nine's Plan
passages.text:
<The raptor snatches the paperwork in her prehensile claws and holds the schematics up to her face, clucking her pointed teeth dismissively.>

These are like the scrawling of children. Common sense precludes the routing of control hydraulics so near to the secondary stage burners! Still, this is salvageable.

Do you know how to refactor fuel matrixes for pressure variations at a fixed acceleration? No? Very well, perhaps you can do something else for me while I reconfigure the rocket...

passages.title: The Deathstalkers
passages.text:
The Syndicate? I would never have suspected. It seems the lords of Alterac have fallen far in the years since their betrayal.

Hawkins will be pleased to learn of this, and as you were so instrumental in this discovery, it would be fitting if you were the one to deliver it to him.

Ah, and how could I forget?

Welcome to the Deathstalkers.

passages.title: Raptor Raptor Rocket
passages.text:
Shortly after my intellect was augmented, I bred with Subject Four in order to create a unique race of cognitively superior raptors. Subsequently, Subject Four neither called nor wrote: I have determined to disembowel him upon our next encounter.

Nonetheless, there are enough raptor children imprisoned in this lab to provide adequate genetic stock for repopulating my race. Please release them from their cages and carry them to the rocket.

passages.title: Raptor Raptor Rocket
passages.text: My beautiful children may attempt to bite you upon release, but at their stage of physical development, it is unlikely that their attacks will be fatal.

passages.title: Raptor Raptor Rocket
passages.text: Wonderful! Exemplary work, <name>! As you have no doubt surmised, my objective with regard to this rocket is to utilize it as a sort of astral cradle, an ark if you will, allowing my newly-forged race to slip the surly bonds of this ravaged planet and colonize a world to our own liking. You have been instrumental to our cause. Please accept this currency as I will be minting my own monetary units upon arrival. Farewell, <name>!

passages.title: Dozercism
passages.text:
...what we need is a priest!

Fortunately I have a small budget set aside for the blessing of machinery. Take this flare gun and head over to Margene, my poor sweet busted bulldozer. Fire off the signal and one of our finest airborne priests should airdrop in to get a handle on the situation. Come back when my bulldozer is taken care of!

passages.title: Dozercism
passages.text: How is Margene doin'? Running like her sweet self again?

passages.title: Dozercism
passages.text:
What? ...What?

Margene! Oh my sweet Margene!!

passages.title: Need More Science
passages.text:
<Clubnik wipes away a tear, then juts his chin out with determination.>

Never again, <name>! No bulldozer deserves the fate of my Margene. We're going to need some industrial ghostproofing. This is a job for our top scientists, and I know just the woman for the job! Look for Assistant Greely at the Southern Rocketway Terminus. She's the administrator for Azshara's world-famous Secret Lab, and she owes me a favor.

passages.title: Need More Science
passages.text:
What is Clubnik talking about? Haunted construction equipment? Does it look like I have time for ghost stories?

I've got a laboratory in the middle of a meltdown, fires burning, animals mutated, and worst of all - projects falling behind schedule. Help!

passages.title: Hacking the Construct
passages.text: Now we will hack their arcane construct and use it to wreak havoc. Have you done this type of magic before, <name>? No? Hah! That makes my plan all the more delicious. Nearby you should see a formidable arcane construct they've summoned. Thanks to the runestones you gathered, we know how to communicate with it. Talk to the construct and say "Al'teth la c'tolgar." Got that? Repeat it? Close enough. Report back to me and let me know what happens!

passages.title: Hacking the Construct
passages.text: Haha! Hah - HA! Night elf "mages" fleeing their own arcane creation. Your actions have made my month, <name>. That's why we blood elves don't use arcane constructs anymore - they've been outlawed for, oh, 1500 years. It's amusing to me to watch our foes repeat the mistakes of the past. "Mages." Indeed.

passages.title: The Blackmaw Scar
passages.text:
The Blackmaw furbolg that live in this area have broken rank with their Timbermaw brethren as we began to aggressively settle Azshara. They've gone wild, <class>, and harass our forces at every turn. Worse, we have seen them engaging the night elves from Talrendis on friendly terms. We cannot allow the two to ally!

Just southwest of here you will find a great scar across the earth where my scouts report night elven activity. Slay them and gather any intelligence you find.

passages.title: The Blackmaw Scar
passages.text: The Blackmaw are ferocious. Were they ever to organize, they would prove to be an immense disruption to our work here.

passages.title: The Blackmaw Scar
passages.text:
I see... This definitely looks like a working draft of some sort of treaty. That's a worst-case scenario for us, <name>: Night elves coordinating attacks with entrenched furbolg allies.

My initial instinct - a full-out frontal assault - would only drive them into the arms of the Alliance. We will have to take a different approach...

passages.title: Diplomacy by Another Means
passages.text:
In order to infiltrate and disrupt the Blackmaw negotiations, we'll need to know where they're happening. In Blackmaw Hold to the southwest, I suspect you'll find night elven ambassadors milling around, making preparations.

<Haggrum spits on the ground.>

Kill them at your leisure, and search the area for important documents. Oh, and grab a set of their ambassador's robes, we'll need them.

passages.title: Diplomacy by Another Means
passages.text: Do you have the robes? Andorel here has been whipping up some magic for us to use.

passages.title: Diplomacy by Another Means
passages.text: Excellent work! Let me see those documents. Hmm. Now we know exactly when and where the final negotiations will happen. Don't worry if those robes don't fit you - I've got it all worked out.

passages.title: The Blackmaw Doublecross
passages.text:
Andorel here has crafted a little bit of magic for me. Come, stand next to my fire, and steep yourself in the fumes from the tea. Drape the robes around you and you'll take on the appearance of a night elven ambassador to the Blackmaw.

Don your disguise and speak to Andorel here in camp. He'll teleport you to the heart of Blackmaw hold, where the negotiations are to take place. Speak with Chieftain Ungarl and sabotage the treaty. Then, kill as many Blackmaw as you can on the way back!

passages.title: The Blackmaw Doublecross
passages.text: If our ruse pays off, <name>, we will forever drive a wedge between the Alliance and the Blackmaw.

passages.title: The Blackmaw Doublecross
passages.text:
Victory! The Blackmaw won't know who to trust anymore.

With that delicate bit of business complete, I can orchestrate a full-on assault against those beasts without worrying about them siding with the Alliance.

You do good work, <name>. Perhaps we should place you in the Horde diplomatic corps? Hah-har!

passages.title: Rites of the Earthmother
passages.text:
For you to continue with the Rites of the Earthmother you must pass two more tests. It is time for you to broaden your experience, <name>.

Travel to Bloodhoof Village and seek out the Ahmo Thunderhorn. There you may continue your journey and earn the acceptance of the elders of Thunder Bluff.

Take this totem to Ahmo. He will recognize my carvings and help you on your path.

Follow the road out of Camp Narache and travel with haste. Do not stray or you will lose your way.

passages.title: Sharing the Land
passages.text:
<name>, there are many conflicts that wound this land. It is my hope that you will not bear witness to as many of them as our elders have. Yet there is one that I would ask you to seek. It will give you some sense of how terrible, if left unchecked, even a small threat can be to the land.

Palemane gnolls have settled to the south of Bloodhoof and in a cave to the west. They disrespect our attempts to communicate with them, and they slay the wildlife of Mulgore unbridled.

Words are no longer the answer.

passages.title: Sharing the Land
passages.text: If the Palemanes had respected the land and its inhabitants more, this conflict would have never occurred.

passages.title: Sharing the Land
passages.text: <name>, it is good you've taken the task seriously. Respect of the land and its creatures is important. Death and life are a circle... a necessity. One cannot exist without the other. Take time to ponder this and do well to never forget it.

passages.title: Rites of the Earthmother
passages.text:
You have passed the Rites of the Earthmother and earned your place in Thunder Bluff.

But in order to maintain the spot that you strived so hard to achieve, you must continue to prove your worth to your people.

We are hunters, <name>. Down below in Mulgore there is a mighty kodo named Arra'chea. Show me your skills in the ways of tracking and hunting by bringing me the Horn of Arra'chea.

passages.title: Garrosh's Autograph
passages.text:
They say that Garrosh Hellscream is one of the greatest heroes in the Horde! When I grow up, I want to be a hero of the Horde too!

Do you know Garrosh, <name>? Could you do me a favor, please? Could you get his autograph for me? I dunno how to ask him, and he probably wouldn't listen to someone like me... but you! You're an adventurer, like him! I bet he'd give you his autograph easy!

Please?

passages.title: The Battered Hilt
passages.text:
This battered old sword hilt has seen better days. Before the hilt was snapped from the blade, it must've been a magnificent example of the blacksmith's art.

The graceful symbols and exotic gemstones decorating the hilt suggest that the weapon may have belonged to a powerful person. Surely, the Silver Covenant members would be interested in hearing about the recovery of such an artifact. Seek out their representative at Quel'Delar's Rest, south of the Argent Tournament Grounds.

passages.title: The Battered Hilt
passages.text: What is it that you have there?

passages.title: The Battered Hilt
passages.text:
<Caladis takes the hilt from you and slowly turns it over in his hands.>
