<name>, we can't let that happen. If Azshara defeats the Tidehunter and takes his power for herself, I'm not sure any number of us could ever hope to oppose her on the seas.

The first step is clear at least - we need to hunt down the fiend that destroyed our ships. The navy was confident enough to bring in a new fleet, perhaps they have a plan.

passages.title: Her Lady's Hand
passages.text:
Battlemaiden!

Find my Honor Guard upon the field of battle and relieve them of their foes. I need them to return to guard the priestesses immediately!

I will hold the entrance. Be swift!

passages.title: Her Lady's Hand
passages.text: I dispatched my Honor Guard when the fighting broke out. They are better equipped to deal with the chaos of this kind of battle, and I am hardly in need of their aid.

passages.title: Her Lady's Hand
passages.text:
Well done, Battlemaiden.

I will attend to the eastern bridge. I need you to attend to the temple itself. The ritual must not be interrupted.

passages.title: The Fires of Mount Hyjal
passages.text:
Do you see it, <name>? From the ridge southwest of here... plumes of black smoke curling into the sky.

Mount Hyjal is burning.

If the fires have raced this far up the mountain, surely they threaten the Grove of Aessina and all of our forces there. Can you investigate?

Speak with Laina Nightsky near the Grove of Aessina. Last I heard, she was fighting off the assault.

passages.title: The Fires of Mount Hyjal
passages.text:
Can this wait, <class>? The battle is not going well.

Oh, you're here to help. I hope you don't mind a little heat...

passages.title: To the Fathom-Lord's Call
passages.text:
Fathom-Lord Zin'jatar has sent word that the Kvaldir leader has shown himself. I would like you to make your way to him at the far end of the terrace above us, on the middle level of the ruins: Nar'shola Terrace.

Kill any Kvaldir that stand in your path on that terrace. We want the echoes of this defeat to ring in their minds so that they will dare not return to threaten our purpose here.

Your devotion does not go unnoticed, my battlemaiden. Go knowing that you have my blessing.

passages.title: To the Fathom-Lord's Call
passages.text: It is good of you to join me, Battlemaiden. The echoes of your combat graced your approach. It was a beautiful sound to behold.

passages.title: Bombs Away: Windshear Mine!
passages.text:
Ve have discovered ze vhereabouts of ze gigantic goblin bomb zat you discovered at Silvervind Refuge.

You remember Boog? Ze gnome you rescued from ze orcish vagon of agony? Vell, he and Minx have tracked ze bomb down to Windshear Mine. Go zhere immediately, <name>! Zey'll be expecting you.

passages.title: Bombs Away: Windshear Mine!
passages.text:
Good to see you again, <name>. Thanks for the rescue in Ashenvale. Damn shame about all the gnomes we lost.

You ready to get down to business?

passages.title: The Flow of Muisek
passages.text:
I've done all I can for you. Muisek stronger than the hippogryph just isn't within my power to work with yet, so I won't make you deal with the disaster that could bring.

But while you've been busy, I've fully readied the hippogryph muisek. Take it to my master, Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Camp Mojache. He can create powerful weapons with it, and hopefully he'll be impressed by what I've done.

passages.title: The Flow of Muisek
passages.text: I sense something familiar in your presence...

passages.title: The Flow of Muisek
passages.text: Well done indeed... I'd expect nothing less from my own daughter. She'll make a fine witch doctor someday.

passages.title: Don't Look Them in the Eyes
passages.text:
Keep your head down, <name>. No need to draw unwanted attention.

Looks like the orcs are piling that balloon up with some type of ore from the mine. Get in there and take the ore from the orcs. Bring me back whatever you manage to grab and I'll ship it off to the professor for examination.

Before you go, a word of advice: you can avoid the Krom'gar pretty easily in there as (1) they're dumb as dirt and (2) they can't see anything if they're carrying ore. Of course, you need to kill them to get their ore.

passages.title: Don't Look Them in the Eyes
passages.text: Get me those ore samples!

passages.title: Don't Look Them in the Eyes
passages.text: Not too much trouble, I hope. With these samples we should be able to figure out what they plan to do with the ore and the big bomb.

passages.title: The Twilight Egg
passages.text:
The egg is unlike any that you've seen before. Its translucent shell appears to bend the light around it.

Accompanying it, you find a note describing the arrival of a fertile broodmother at the Ascendant's Rise.

Perhaps you should show this to Aronus.

passages.title: The Twilight Egg
passages.text: You were right to come to me with this, <name>.  This represents a great threat to us if we do not act swiftly and boldly.

passages.title: Illegible Orc Letter
passages.text:
You've discovered a parchment with an impressive looking Horde seal imprinted upon its page. Unfortunately, the rest of the document is completely illegible as it is in orcish.

Take the letter to Boog. He might know what to do with it!

passages.title: Illegible Orc Letter
passages.text: What have you got there?

passages.title: Illegible Orc Letter
passages.text:
<Boog takes the letter from you and begins to examine it.>

Interesting.

<Boog smells the parchment.>

Hrm... Troubling...

<Boog folds the paper in half and looks at you.>

Can't understand a damn thing written here - if that is writing. Could just be toilet paper. Sure smells like it.

passages.title: Minx'll Fix It
passages.text:
The good news is that Minx is fluent in orcish and she's nearby. Head back into the mine and find her. She's probably deeper inside, standing around being useless.

Don't forget the parchment!

passages.title: Minx'll Fix It
passages.text: What have you got there?

passages.title: Minx'll Fix It
passages.text:
<Minx takes the letter from you and begins to read it.>

Uh oh...

<Minx smells the parchment.>

Disgusting!

<Minx folds the paper in half and looks at you.>

The good news is that this isn't toilet paper. The bad news is that the ink on this paper is a mixture of kodo poop and blood. That's not the worst of it, though...

passages.title: Orders from High Command
passages.text:
The letter is actually an order from Horde high command. Someone named Overlord Krom'gar has issued a "strip job" on this mine in order to obtain something called azure iron flake. Presumably this flake is obtained from breaking down the ore.

It gets worse. They plan to mix the azure flake with the explosives sitting inside the huge bomb outside and blow up Windshear Hold.

We don't have a moment to lose, <name>! Take this translated copy of the letter and return to Boog! He'll know what to do next.

passages.title: Orders from High Command
passages.text: Well? What's it say?

passages.title: Orders from High Command
passages.text:
<Beads of sweat roll down Boog's overly large forehead as he reads the translated letter.>

This is bad. Really, really bad. You have to warn Lord Fallowmere at Windshear Hold.

What in the... It's MOVING! The goblin balloon is taking off! We're too late!

passages.title: Oh, the Insanity!
passages.text:
So, I've been thinkin'...

If someone's out-of-their-mind-guano-crazy, do they know it?

Case in point, I coulda swore that I'd collected a barrel of gunpowder from the cannonballs around here, but it's nowhere ta be found.

I distinctly remember lifting the cannonballs from them Gilblins just west of here.

Maybe they're right... maybe I really have lost it.

passages.title: Oh, the Insanity!
passages.text:
You want nuthin' to do with me, <race>.

I'm a touch... screwy.

passages.title: Oh, the Insanity!
passages.text:
My gunpowder!

You found it! I'm not crazy after all!

passages.title: Commandeer That Balloon!
passages.text:
We don't have a moment to lose, <name>. You're going to have to commandeer that hot air balloon and stop it!

How? I have no idea! We don't have time to argue details! Grab onto that rope ladder and climb up! Just start banging on stuff once you're inside!

If you somehow manage to stop the balloon and survive, report to Lord Fallowmere at Windshear Hold in the west.

Good luck, we're all counting on you. Now if you'll excuse me I'm going to RUN FOR MY LIFE!

passages.title: Commandeer That Balloon!
passages.text: Amazing story, lad. I'd have never believed you had I not seen it with my own eyes. You did enough damage to that balloon to make those fiends pull back! Alas, the threat is far from over. We have only delayed the attack. There is much work to do if we are to stop the Horde from destroying Stonetalon!

passages.title: The Wormwing Problem
passages.text:
Skylord Omnuron has been too gentle with the Wormwing harpies. He allows them to share a perch on this mountain just because they're creatures of the air. Well <class>, not all creatures of the air are created equal.

When the attacks on Hyjal began, the Wormwing went into a frenzy. They're up there right now, assaulting a sacred shrine they once claimed to revere.

I'm not troubled. Now we have a reason to drive them from Hyjal, don't we?

passages.title: The Wormwing Problem
passages.text:
<Thisalee nods, contentedly, her eyes sparkling.>

Feels great to be off the leash, doesn't it?

passages.title: Dah, Nunt... Dah, Nunt...
passages.text:
So, seein' as ya been so kind to me, I'm inclined to let you in on a special secret.

I've found the biggest shiney of all, no more than 50 steps from where we're standin'!

Only one thing stands between you, me, and great fortune - and his name is Gnaws.

Don't fret now - I've got a plan.

Gnaws loves his grubs, so I've loaded one up with that gunpowder so as to make like a trap of sorts, ya see?

Just set it floatin' up in the reef. Once the shark is dead, we're rich!

passages.title: Dah, Nunt... Dah, Nunt...
passages.text: Well? Is Gnaws dead, <race>?

passages.title: Dah, Nunt... Dah, Nunt...
passages.text:
Amazing!

You watch the great white beast swim off into the depths and wonder to yourself if anything could ever take him down...

passages.title: Built to Last
passages.text:
My lady, I have a request from the High Priestess that I am to pass along to you. Many of the city's defenses remain from long before it sunk beneath the waves, and some of them are but a trivial task to reactivate, were it not for the countless Kvaldir that stand in our way.

We are told you are to be fighting on Nar'shola Terrace above us. You would do my lady a great service if you would but touch some of the devices as you pass. Your noble blood should prove more than sufficient to reactivate them.

passages.title: Built to Last
passages.text:
The Nar'shola Wards are performing perfectly. I will inform the Mistress of the Tides of your aid immediately.

Thank you for your assistance, my lady.

passages.title: Not Soon Forgotten
passages.text:
The Kvaldir leader has shown his rotting, ugly face but a short swim from here, down this hall to our west. We kill him now and the Kvaldir occupation of our once beloved city shall be ended.

Beware Battlemaiden, for he is no weakling. He has many Kvaldir at his command. Some Sira'kess Sea Witches have been dispatched to weaken him during your attack, but they will be interrupted if you let any of his Kvaldir attack them.

Show no mercy, Battlemaiden.

passages.title: Not Soon Forgotten
passages.text:
<The Kvaldir General crumples to the ground, defeated.>

<With this, the ruins of Vashj'ir have been claimed for Lady Naz'jar. Her ultimate goals remain uncertain, but it is clear that the naga came here with purpose.>

<If only you could continue, you are sure that the answers to defeating the naga lie within this vision, but the Wavespeaker's magics are waning, and you are losing your connection with the Battlemaiden.>

passages.title: With a Little Help...
passages.text:
Fine, I be helpin' ya. He not gettin' outa payin' me alimony that easy! 'Sides, there be the baby he had with me sistah ta take care of!

First thing we needin' is the innards of his closest friends. That'd be his cap'ns.

Go down there an' pay the three of them a visit.

passages.title: With a Little Help...
passages.text: A fresh heart, lungs, an liver be what we needin'. The ones from his cap'ns will have ta do though they all be likely picked.

passages.title: With a Little Help...
passages.text:
<Ajamon makes a face at the state of the organs.>

They's gonna have ta do. It not be like he had many friends. Ain't that right, Two-Tusk?

passages.title: A Prayer and a Wing
passages.text:
A winged visage? Could it be...?

<name>, there's no time to waste. You may have been speaking to Aviana herself, trying to return to us.

I'll need something from Aviana's past to reach out to her. High atop the ridge overlooking this shrine, you'll find a series of huge nests belonging to Blaithe, an ancient bird of prey that was once her consort. For ten thousand years he's been mad with grief.

Go to one of his roosts, and use this call to summon him. Kill Blaithe and bring me one of his feathers.

passages.title: A Prayer and a Wing
passages.text: Don't trouble yourself over Blaithe's condition. Grief robbed that creature of a soul epochs ago. He was but a shell of his former self, a beast of pure rage.

passages.title: A Prayer and a Wing
passages.text:
That was nasty work, <name>, but it had to be done.

And if Aviana is truly to be resurrected, then perhaps your actions have enabled Blaithe to someday come back as well?

Now let's see if we can contact our long lost guardian...

passages.title: A Plea From Beyond
passages.text:
<You can't make sense of the spirit's urgent plea, but maybe Choluna can decipher what's going on here.>

<Speak with Choluna back inside the shrine!>

passages.title: A Plea From Beyond
passages.text: Slow down, <class>! You look as though you've seen a ghost...

passages.title: Culling the Wendigos
passages.text:
The wendigos in the Grizzled Den to the southwest of town have long been a thorn in our side. They're never quite strong enough to threaten Kharanos directly, yet they prey on travelers, mountaineer patrols, and supply convoys.

I'm going to be withdrawing my observers from the Grizzled Den because I need them on the troll front. Would you help my men finish culling the wendigo population? Without strength of numbers, they won't be able to attack us.

passages.title: Culling the Wendigos
passages.text: Now that you've dealt with the wendigos, we should be able to focus our efforts on the Frostmane trolls to the east.

passages.title: Pilfered Supplies
passages.text: With the Frostmanes making trouble to our east, the wendigos have sensed our weakness and grown bolder in their raids. Only one of the four most recent supply wagons has made it here safely. The wendigos made off with the rest, stashing it in the Grizzled Den, a cave southwest of town. If you're willing to go down there and recover the stolen supplies, you would have the gratitude of all the townspeople and the mountaineers defending Kharanos.

passages.title: Pilfered Supplies
passages.text: Did you find any of the missing supplies?

passages.title: Pilfered Supplies
passages.text: Well done, <name>. The mountaineers will be glad to hear that half-rations are at an end. They'll need all their strength to continue fighting the Frostmanes.

passages.title: Rumble in the Lumber... Mill
passages.text:
Prepare yourself, <name>! The Warlord comes! Kill him and take his key. Use the key to release me.

Should we make it out of here, report the following to Lord Fallowmere at Windshear Hold:

The Horde has aborted their plans to destroy Windshear Hold due to the efforts of one of our heroes. They now plan to move the bomb to Battlescar Valley and drop it on our armies battling the Horde at that location.

They must be stopped!

passages.title: Rumble in the Lumber... Mill
passages.text:
A hero thwarted their plans to destroy Windshear Hold, eh? That hero was you, <name>. You are the pride of the Alliance!

It seems that you have bought us a little bit of time. I must plan for the battle that lies ahead of us. Seek out the other inhabitants of Windshear Hold and lend them your assistance. I will call for you when I am ready to initiate our defensive strategy.

passages.title: DUN-dun-DUN-dun-DUN-dun
passages.text:
If ol' Gnaws had heels he'd be on 'em right now.

Fortunately for you, I think like a shark.

Gnaws is mad as all get out and we're gunna use that to our advantage.

Here, I found this chain while out treasure-huntin'. Use it to tie off to that harpoon gun.

When Gnaws sees ya he'll be consumed with rage - that's when we strike!

You try to finish him off and I'll sneak in there and grab the shiney.

Hurry, <class>, before he grows them teeth back!

passages.title: DUN-dun-DUN-dun-DUN-dun
passages.text: This really ain't as bad as it looks...

passages.title: Thinning the Horde
passages.text:
The Horde's numbers swell as reinforcements from Ashenvale and Azshara arrive. There is no diplomacy to be had with the beasts. This is Hellscream's Horde and Hellscream's Horde wants our blood! We will not sit idly by and allow them to take our land and kill our people. We must act!

We must thin the Horde! Consider it your daily responsibility.

Venture forth into Stonetalon Mountains and slay as many of the Horde as you are able. Let them know that the Alliance will not surrender!

passages.title: Thinning the Horde
passages.text:
Good. Their blood is on Hellscream's hands. Send enough of them back to Orgrimmar in a body bag and the populace of the Horde might react.

<Lord Fallowmere laughs.>

Who am I kidding? They're monsters!

passages.title: Just Ask Alice
passages.text:
Mr. P is sick, <mister/miss>. Won't you help him? All you have to do is find his hat and batteries and he'll be all better. I'd go get them myself, but I can't leave Mr. P alone!

His hat was stolen by the meanies in the Venture Co. over at the water wheel and his batteries are hidden around Windshear Crag. You'll just have to look real hard for those!

Would you kindly bring Mr. P's stuff back so he can teach those baddies in the Horde a lesson?

passages.title: Just Ask Alice
passages.text: Mr. P is so sad. We need to make him happy!

passages.title: Just Ask Alice
passages.text:
<Alice claps excitedly.>

Mr. P you're gonna be ok! Hooray!

<Alice expertly places all of the parts you collected into Big Papa.>

Oh, Mr. P! I knew it!

passages.title: Heartstrike
passages.text:
We don't have any hope of taking the Nethergarde Mines from the Alliance... at least not yet. Nethergarde is well-defended, and their supply routes are established and strong. Our goal, then, is to damage their economy. We can't take the mine by force, but with surgical strikes we can drastically reduce the mine's efficiency.

I have men creating a distraction outside the mines. Head east, sneak into the mines, and speak with Rofilian Dane for your assignment.

passages.title: Heartstrike
passages.text: Finally... another operative shows up.  I hope you're loosened up... it's time to tango, partner.

passages.title: It's All Mine
passages.text:
All over this cavern you'll find unguarded piles of ore, just waiting to be tampered with. Our first choice would be to steal the ore, obviously, but that requires mine carts, protection, and labor... three things we just don't have. So instead, we're just going to ruin this little mining party with a little bit of highly corrosive solvent.

Take this bottle - CAREFULLY - and pour it onto those heaps of ore. 'Cause if we can't have this ore, then neither can they.

passages.title: It's All Mine
passages.text: I wouldn't store that solvent where I store my potions, if I were you.

passages.title: It's All Mine
passages.text: There's nothing quite like a big fat kick in the wallet, is there, you Alliance lunkheads?!

passages.title: Pick Your Fate
passages.text:
It costs the Alliance approximately fifty gold to train a miner, two hundred to train an engineer, and three hundred to train a foreman. Every Alliance goon that we kill isn't just a military victory... it's a financial one.

Now get down there and destroy their workers!

passages.title: Pick Your Fate
passages.text: Excellent work, friend.  I like the way you do business.

passages.title: Into the Mountain
passages.text:
The next phase of operations takes place deeper within the mine. Speak with Tak'arili for your next assignment. Just follow the mine cart rails to the southeast, and follow the curve around. You'll see him at the entrance to the mine's upper chamber.

It's been a pleasure doing business with you, <name>.

passages.title: Into the Mountain
passages.text:
Good, you here already.  Stick around for a bit, little <race>.  We gonna mess with the Alliance.

I love my job, mon.

passages.title: That's Not Us
passages.text:
First things first... it looks like we got ourselves a problem. These miners down the pathway to the right have been runnin' around like a chickens without they heads on. My best guess is that they dug too deep and found somethin' nasty... a demon, an elemental, or some kind o' tentacley beast.

Tak'arili don't like surprises. Find out what the problem is and take care of it, then we get ourselves back on track.

passages.title: That's Not Us
passages.text:
So it was a demon?  Those miners never seen a demon before?  We're in the Blasted Lands, mon!  Demons are everywhere!

<Tak'arili sighs.>

Ah well... let's get on to da good stuff, shall we?

passages.title: Some People Just Need Killing
passages.text:
The tunnel ahead, headin' west, will take you straight to Chief Prospector Hondo's office. He's the big cheese around here, and Tak'arili's heard tell that he's a darn fine miner. That's why he's gotta die.

There's just one problem: the pathway is completely FILLED with those pesky Nethergarde flunkies. That's why you gotta disguise yourself. Hop inside this box here, and sneak down the pathway. Hopefully you won't draw too much suspicion on your way to da killin'.

passages.title: Some People Just Need Killing
passages.text: Hondo ain't gonna know what hit him.

passages.title: Some People Just Need Killing
passages.text: Nice work, mon!  Without Hondo, these guys are helpless.  Dis mine'll be ours soon enough!

passages.title: Mission Complete
passages.text: We be done here, mon. Only thing left to do is send a report to Okrilla. You doin' anything right now?

passages.title: Mission Complete
passages.text: You've returned, <name>?

passages.title: Mission Complete
passages.text:
<Okrilla glances over the report.>

Impressive, <name>.  I wouldn't have hidden in that box, but otherwise, you have performed bravely and admirably.  The battle we won today may not win us any immediate spoils, but the damage you've done to the Alliance will last for a long time.

passages.title: The Dreadmaul Furnace
passages.text:
I meant what I said, <race>. You helped me, now I'll pass on what I know.

A demon hunter recently came through here, but only briefly. He was headed south, speaking of demons. Normally I'd have slain the night elf on sight, but he didn't seem to be Alliance scum, and anybody who kills demons is useful to me for the time being.

You should check in with Lynnore and Drazial, a pair of blood mages I sent down that way. They've camped in the back of an ogre cave.

passages.title: The Dreadmaul Furnace
passages.text:
Okrilla sent you?  Okrilla the killa'?

<Lynnore listens to your tale.>

Loramus was his name?  I'm sorry to say that we have not seen your demon hunter... but we have ways of finding him.

passages.title: Attune the Bloodstone
passages.text:
I admit, we haven't picked the most... convenient of spots to perform our studies, especially for passing adventurers who wish to enter and leave at will. Our agreement with the ogres is tenuous, and I'm afraid we can't convince them not to attack you when you draw near.

However, I can allow you to attune yourself to our bloodstone teleporters. Simply place your hands on the stone to my right, and you will be teleported outside of the cave. Then use the stone outside to teleport back!

passages.title: Attune the Bloodstone
passages.text: The attunement process is simple, but will certainly come in handy down the line.

passages.title: Attune the Bloodstone
passages.text: Excellent.  Now that that's out of the way...

passages.title: The First Step
passages.text:
To perform the ritual you've requested - and perhaps some more rituals in the near future - we're going to need blood. The Blasted Lands are filled with every type of reagent we might need for our blood magic... it's just a matter of the correct combination.

<Lynnore quickly confers with Drazial for a moment.>

Basilisks and hyenas, even amounts. And we're going to need plenty of it. Head east, to the center of the Blasted Lands. And don't forget... you can use that teleporter!

passages.title: The First Step
passages.text: Ogre blood only takes you so far.  Do you have it?

passages.title: The First Step
passages.text:
<Lynnore eyes the blood hungrily.>

More than enough, and still warm!  Now, let's get this ritual started, shall we?

passages.title: The Altar of Storms
passages.text:
Up on the bluffs above our comfy cave is a powerful altar. A powerful DEMONIC altar, guarded by cultists, but powerful nonetheless. If you can reach it, you can use it to bring Loramus back to us.

The altar will likely resist your efforts, so you'll have to protect Loramus' body while the ritual completes. Bring the demon hunter back to me afterwards.

passages.title: The Altar of Storms
passages.text: You... you fool!  What have you done?

passages.title: Time is Short
passages.text:
I was hunting a demon named Razelikh, when his ogre lieutenant Grol assaulted me. I was caught unaware, and I died... but so did Grol.

Razelikh plans to return to the Blasted Lands and overwhelm the lands with his demons. Even now, he is preparing to summon his legions to eliminate us.

<The demon hunter quickly draws a rune in the air, then hands it to you.>

Deliver this to Wazzik at the Dark Portal, to the southeast. He will guide you. Quickly! We haven't much time!

passages.title: Time is Short
passages.text: Do I know you, good <race>?

passages.title: Time is Short
passages.text:
What?  LORAMUS?!

Oh blast, keep it down, would ya?  If my boss gets word that I worked for Loramus, do you know how quickly I'd be on my rear end?!

<Wazzik takes the rune from you, presses it to his chest, closes his eyes, and nods.>

Well, you weren't lying.  Let's get to work.

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text:
Contrary to popular belief, blood elf bloodmages do NOT drink blood. We eat normal food like everybody else - something which can be hard to come by in the recesses of an ogre stronghold.

The ashmane boars in the central valley of the Blasted Lands are, if nothing else, convenient for eating, as their meat does not require any cooking. Would you hunt these boars and help us replenish our foodstores?

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text: I'm famished!  If you don't hurry, I might actually resort to drinking our reagents.

passages.title: A Bloodmage's Gotta Eat Too
passages.text: These are perfect, <name>.  Lynnore and I will eat well for the next several days.

passages.title: Enhancing the Stone
passages.text:
<Wazzik finishes packing the materials up in a neatly-wrapped package.>

That's all that Loramus asked of us. When you see him, make sure you let him know how much of a help I was. I fear he will not see my hand in this.

passages.title: Enhancing the Stone
passages.text: <class>... you return...

passages.title: Enhancing the Stone
passages.text:
This is sufficient.  If you see Wazzik again, you may tell him that he performed satisfactorily.  I will get the bloodmages to work on fashioning the stone knife of sealing.  There is no need for questions now.  All will be revealed in time.

While they work, I have another task for you to complete.  Actually, make that three tasks.

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text:
<Warlord Dar'toon speaks in hushed tones.>

I have orders from... higher up... that you would be suitable for. I've seen the Alliance periodically referring to a stack of papers on that barrel over there. I'd like you to take a look at those papers and find out what it is that they're plotting. My duty and station prevent me from such a questionable task, but a newcomer like you might be able to slip in unnoticed...

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text: Did you get a look at those plans, <name>?

passages.title: Watching Our Back
passages.text:
You're certain nobody saw you?  Good.

<Dar'toon listens to your recount of the information you saw.>

Hmph... fairly harmless stuff.  Either the Alliance are foolish enough to NOT be planning something against us... or they're hiding their information better than I expected.  Either way, well done, soldier.

passages.title: The Sunveil Excursion
passages.text:
Oh, right, I received a notification from someone a few days ago. The Reliquary, was it? They're looking for someone to... do something...

<The Warlord rifles through some papers.>

Ah, here it is! Yes, Rohan Sunveil of The Reliquary is seeking able-bodied adventurers to assist with an archaeological expedition to the south.

Here, take this with you. Why don't you go speak with that elf?

passages.title: The Sunveil Excursion
passages.text: Welcome, traveler.  Thank you for responding to my summons.

passages.title: The Amulet of Allistarj
passages.text:
When my master helped me to take my eyes out, he gave me the gift of sight... a sight much greater than yours, or even of these blood-craving elves. My sight allows me to see objects of demonic power, such as the Amulet of Allistarj.

Allistarj himself is dead, but he locked his amulet up in a trove inside the Serpent's Coil, to the east. Along with the other amulets, this relic will give us access to Razelikh's perch.

passages.title: The Amulet of Allistarj
passages.text: Allistarj left a piece of himself in that amulet.  Even now, I can sense his evil.

passages.title: The Amulet of Allistarj
passages.text:
<Lynnore examines the amulet.>

He was an archmage, I can feel it.  I will hold the amulet for you while you collect the rest.

passages.title: The Amulet of Sevine
passages.text:
Sevine's amulet is in the hands of a murloc, far to the east, on a shelf that overlooks the Shattershore. How it ended up in that murloc's possession, I cannot say, but I can state with certainty that you will find it there.

I feel a stronger connection with Sevine than with the rest of Razelikh's servants... possibly because she built the Altar of Storms, upon which you resurrected me. Bring her Amulet to Lynnore, along with the rest.

passages.title: The Amulet of Sevine
passages.text: Sevine's amulet... along with the others, we can reach the Rise of the Defiler.

passages.title: The Amulet of Sevine
passages.text:
<Lynnore hefts the amulet.>

A warlock... and a powerful one at that.  I will hold onto this until the time is right.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text:
Grol... the ogre who tore me apart.

<Loramus laughs.>

It would seem that Grol's body has changed hands several times since we died together, but it no longer rests with the ogres. His body, along with his amulet of power, is in a wrecked ship off the Shattershore, to the east. His amulet is the last... once combined, the three will give us access to Razelikh, and therein lies our chance to stop his madness.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text: The third amulet, from Razelikh's third lieutenant.

passages.title: The Amulet of Grol
passages.text:
<Lynnore clutches the third amulet.>

He was a powerful warrior, this one.  I will keep the amulet until Loramus is ready to proceed.

passages.title: You Are Rakh'likh, Demon
passages.text:
Hero, listen well.

First, we must travel to the Deathly Usher, who waits at the northern foot of the Rise of the Defiler, to our northeast. The usher will take us to the top of the rise. Once there, I need you to help me defeat Razelikh, for I fear that I am not strong enough to defeat him alone.

Most importantly, I need you to hold the stone knife, and do not use it until I tell you to. The knife will trap Razelikh's soul within its new, eternal prison.

If we succeed, speak with Wazzik.

passages.title: You Are Rakh'likh, Demon
passages.text:
I see.  So this was Loramus' plan all along.

I suspected correctly, but I suppose I refused to believe it.  And now, his final instruction for me makes much more sense:

He asked me to let you choose from one of these.

passages.title: The Mad Magus
passages.text:
There's only one ting left dat we can do. Ya gotta slay someone with the big mojo in Tony's presence.

No, not me!

Ol' Magus Tirth went crazy when he tried ta stop the waters rushin' in at the Cataclysm. Now he be hauntin' the area just south of the Holdfast.

Take dis soul stick an' use it on his corpse, mon. Then bring Tony back an' we be gettin' him back in his body.

Ya can use me spirit portal ta get down there an' back.

passages.title: The Mad Magus
passages.text: Ya gotta use the stick on Tirth's corpse if ya gonna help, <name>.

passages.title: The Mad Magus
passages.text: Now we gonna bring Tony Two-Tusk back ta life. You both ready, mon?

passages.title: Neptool's Revenge
passages.text:
No number of naga deaths will bring back the Rockpool tribe, but any amount of revenge will help the spirits of my people rest more easily.

Many of the more powerful Bloodwash have set up a fortress in the caverns to the northwest. Slay them, in the name of the Rockpool. The remaining Bloodwash have erected gladiatorial pools and Azsh'ir altars on our beach, where they pit my people against one another and worship their false god. Slay them, in the name of the Tidehunter.

passages.title: Neptool's Revenge
passages.text: The last Rockpool may be taken hostage today and killed tomorrow, landwalker... but they will pass into the underworld knowing that a brave <race> avenged their death.  Thank you.

passages.title: The Future of the Rockpool
passages.text:
The Rockpool tadpoles left upon this crate appear tired, scared, and nearly dried out. They need to be taken to the water, and quickly.

Perhaps if you can drag this crate across the beach and into the Forbidden Sea, far off the coast of the Red Reaches, then they will have a chance of escaping, and the Rockpool murlocs may live on...

passages.title: Our Fallen Friends
passages.text:
Based on what you're telling me, it sounds like there aren't many survivors... just restless spirits. The least we can do is give them their rest.

<Enohar takes a long draw off of a mug of black ale.>

Head back to the Shattershore and vanquish the worgen ghosts that still remain. Doing so should release their spirit from this world and allow them to pass into the next.

passages.title: Our Fallen Friends
passages.text:
<Enohar takes a sip off of a freshly-refilled mug.>

Aye, you've done well, lad.  You do the Alliance proud.

passages.title: Curtail the Darktail
passages.text:
The other thing that concerns me about those shipwrecks is all the vultures that they've attracted. Knowing how those birds operate, they've already picked the bones clean, but still... we can't allow them to further desecrate the bodies of our friends.

Before I brewed, I hunted. Here, take this bow, and more importantly, these arrows. They've been laced with a little concoction that should give those bonepickers a surprise.

passages.title: Curtail the Darktail
passages.text:
It's a tragedy, what happened on the Shattershore.  They weren't even soldiers... just people looking for a new home.

I think we've done all we can, <name>.

passages.title: Minor Distractions
passages.text:
Nethergarde has stood steadfast for years against the demon onslaught that plagues this land. Our watch is never-ending, our vigilance unfaltering, and our courage bottomless.

We have held these lands since the portal opened, but now these Horde insects have the insolence to stand in our way!? We have protected THEM as well as we have protected ourselves!

<Lungertz looks you over.>

Let's see if you've got a hand for combat. Slay one of the Horde's Okril'lon scouts that nibble at our perimeter.

passages.title: Minor Distractions
passages.text: Hmm... not bad.  You're quicker than many of my men.  Stick around, <name>... I may have use of you yet.

passages.title: Remove Their Arms
passages.text:
Say there... <name>, is it? I've got a proposition for you which involves explosions. Interested?

I couldn't help but overhear your conversation with the quartermaster. You see... I've been working on an explosive device. It's not very effective against other creatures, but devastating against artillery. If you're heading back into the field to visit those orcs, find some enemy supplies and give this thing a try. Who knows... maybe they like explosions too.

passages.title: Remove Their Arms
passages.text: Ahh, the sound of things going boom makes my heart pitter-pat.  You've made this gnome's day, <name>.

passages.title: A Closer Look
passages.text:
We've seen countless ships sail past the shore to the southeast, but most pass by inconspicuously. Several days ago, however, a powerful storm carried several of the ships to shore and left them wrecked.

I'd bet a pint of Nethergarde Bitter that they were Horde ships if I didn't love Nethergarde Bitter so much. I can pay you gold, though, if you'll go check out those ships and report back.

passages.title: A Closer Look
passages.text: What news from the Shattershore, <name>?

passages.title: A Closer Look
passages.text:
You saw worgen?  That's bad.

Worgen ghosts?  That's even worse.

Those weren't Horde ships... they were Gilnean.  And they must have been headed down to Surwich, at the bottom of the Tainted Forest.  That makes a lot more sense.

We've got to try to help them, <name>!  The worgen are our allies!

passages.title: Cultists at our Doorstep
passages.text:
You may have already run into some of the Shadowsworn cultists that dwell in the caves just to the southwest of Nethergarde. They do not impress an immediate danger upon our fortress, but I fear that they are planning something more dreadful than you can imagine.

The low-ranking members carry spell foci that might hold an answer. Bring some back to me intact, if you can wrench them from the cultists' hands.

passages.title: Cultists at our Doorstep
passages.text: The cultists will not part easily with their foci.  Slay them quickly before they suspect our intent.

passages.title: Cultists at our Doorstep
passages.text: Ably done, <name>.  Now we see if my suspicions are correct.

passages.title: The Demons and the Druid
passages.text:
The Reliquary is focused on the acquisition and preservation of magical artifacts. Our particular excursion is focused on the demonic artifacts that are hidden in what used to be the Tainted Scar.

A worgen druid has taken residence in the scar and is coaxing a forest to grow. He seems to be failing, however, as the area is still infested with demons.

Anyhow, his forest stands in the way of our excursion, as do these demons. Slay the tainted ones, then return to me so we might deal with the druid.

passages.title: The Demons and the Druid
passages.text: The forest is not yet cleared of the taint, <name>.  Do as I say, and then we may proceed with our mission.

passages.title: The Demons and the Druid
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

I should be a bit more up-front with you.  The demons were a nuisance, but they are not the real problem.  That worgen druid is our problem.

passages.title: How Best to Proceed
passages.text:
Your demon-slaying down there bought our scouts enough time to get a good look at that druid. My intelligence tells me that his name is Marl Wormthorn... a rogue Gilnean druid of substantial power. He resides in Maldraz, the large, twisted tree at the center of the forest, and is protected from harm by some strange force. Whether that force is of demonic or natural sources, we have yet to determine.

Speak with Elijah. He may have some more information for you.

passages.title: How Best to Proceed
passages.text:
Rohan's sending YOU to slay his druid?  Very well.

You should know: Marl Wormthorn is as much demon as he is druid.  Even a druid of his power doesn't have a chance against the demonic energies that run so deeply through this land.  That does not, however, make him any less of an obstacle.

passages.title: Demoniac Vessel
passages.text:
We need a way to get Wormthorn's attention. Something to break him out of his trance. Something that's guaranteed to work.

The few types of wildlife that managed to make a foothold in the Tainted Forest are, without a doubt, affected by the land's latent energies. Your task is to collect their body parts and find a way to combine them into a vessel. If Wormthorn's trance is druidic, or even if it is demonic, a large enough vessel of tainted animal flesh should be able to break it.

passages.title: Demoniac Vessel
passages.text: Dawnflight's plan is a good one.  Do you have the vessel, <name>?

passages.title: Demoniac Vessel
passages.text: Brilliantly done, <name>.  We have what we need to break the worgen's trance.

passages.title: The Downfall of Marl Wormthorn
passages.text:
Wormthorn's unnatural forest threatens our excursion's progress. His trees' roots break our picks, his moss grows over our excavation sites, and his animals attack my men. When it comes to digging, I'll take a demon-infested wasteland over a forest any day.

Take the demoniac vessel and use it on Marl Wormthorn to pull him from his trance. Return to me when he is no more.

passages.title: The Downfall of Marl Wormthorn
passages.text: I haven't time for this, <name>.  You came here for a reason, and it wasn't to chat.  Get back to work.

passages.title: The Downfall of Marl Wormthorn
passages.text:
Hopefully, with this druid out of the picture, we can get back to our digging.  The world is full of powerful artifacts, <name>.  You just need to be willing to do what it takes to get to them.

Feel free to take one of these.  The Reliquary is always happy to share some of its trove with fellow members of the Horde.

passages.title: Frostmane Aggression
passages.text:
The cataclysm has thrown the balance of power in Dun Morogh into question, <name>. Without warning, a wave of troggs emerged from the caves near Gnomeregan and overran the Frostmane trolls. The trolls have been migrating east ever since.

There has always been a Frostmane presence up on Shimmer Ridge, to the northwest, but with the migration, the trolls now surround us. We can't allow the trolls to use this position to their advantage. While my men hold the line in the east, strike against Shimmer Ridge.

passages.title: Frostmane Aggression
passages.text: We should be able to focus our efforts on the rest of the trolls to the east, but there's still the matter of the wendigos in the Grizzled Den.

passages.title: A Bird in Hand
passages.text:
It's time to get to the bottom of this. We need to interrogate the matron of these beasts, Marion Wormwing. We'll capture her alive. Here's the plan:

The harpies communicate across the ridge using a series of signal fires. If we extinguish one, Marion is sure to come investigate.

You fight her as a distraction while I sneak up behind and grab her. I'll leave the questioning to you. Let's get her, <name>!

passages.title: A Bird in Hand
passages.text: Marion used to visit the shrine here. Skylord Omnuron tried to give the harpies the benefit of the doubt, but I never trusted her.

passages.title: A Bird in Hand
passages.text:
So the Harpies are tools of some sort of dragon - "Sethria."

But what are the dragons doing to those eggs? And what's this 'special' egg that Sethria wanted so badly?

This is beyond me, <name>. I've given a report to Skylord Omnuron - he'll know what to do next.

passages.title: A Bone to Pick
passages.text:
We did it!

Gnaws is down, and I have our shiney!

That's good news.

Darn shiney is cursed treasure - makes everyone who touches it a skeleton.

That's bad news.

These cursed pirates say the Gilblin King has the secret to remove the hex.

That's good news.

I can't step foot outside the reef or I'll be cursed forever.

That's bad news.

passages.title: A Bone to Pick
passages.text:
So, <race>...

You gunna remove this curse, or what?

passages.title: A Bone to Pick
passages.text:
This is it?

How is this gunna remove - wait a minute...

passages.title: Fact-Finding Mission
passages.text:
The dragon Sethria must be stopped. We know that her roost is south of here, along the southern cliffs of Hyjal, but beyond that we know little else.

I have sent Thisalee on a fact-finding mission to Sethria's Roost. She specifically requested your help - evidently you made quite an impression with the young druid.

Meet Thisalee just beyond the tunnel leading to Sethria's Roost. And remember, this is a fact-finding mission - don't do anything crazy!

passages.title: Fact-Finding Mission
passages.text:
Ah, <name>! I was hoping to see you out here.

What, Omnuron calls this a 'fact-finding mission?' Bah! Facts are best found on corpses.

Let's do some damage.

passages.title: Decisions, Decisions
passages.text:
This is no magic solution to my curse! It's just a hammer!

I may be crazy, but I'm not stupid.

There's NO WAY I'm gunna use this to break my shiney - not after all I've gone through to get it.

<Budd pauses in thought for a moment.>

But that means I'm stuck down here for eternity...

I had just learned to sail, you know.

Ohhh... I can't decide.

Here, you take the hammer and I'll just set the shiney down and look the other way.

passages.title: Decisions, Decisions
passages.text: Oh, what might have been...

passages.title: Negotiations
passages.text:
<name>, great job defending the Speedbarge! I've got something else that I need you to help out with.

I've sent Crazzle Sprysprocket and Kravel Koalbeard northeast to negotiate with the centaur survivors. Their Splithoof Heights is dripping with oil!

I figure those smelly half horses won't know what they've got and we'll get the rights to pump up that black gold for a song, but I'd feel better if you took charge of the talks.

What do you say?

passages.title: Negotiations
passages.text:
<Crazzle gets a gleam in his eye.>

I've got Kravel Koalbeard up there talking to one of their chiefs, but now that you're here, we'll have the rights to pump up their oil in no time!

passages.title: Negotiations
passages.text:
<name>, great job defending the Speedbarge! I've got something else that I need you to help out with.

I've sent Riznek and Trackmaster Zherin northeast to negotiate with the centaur survivors. Their Splithoof Heights is dripping with oil!

I figure those smelly half horses won't know what they've got and we'll get the rights to pump up that black gold for a song, but I'd feel better if you took charge of the talks.

What do you say?

passages.title: Negotiations
passages.text:
<Riznek gets a gleam in his eye.>

I've got Trackmaster Zherin up there talking to one of their chiefs, but now that you're here, we'll have the rights to pump up their oil in no time!

passages.title: Sethria's Brood
passages.text:
First order of business is to thin the herd here. This place crawls.

Let's start slaughtering these dragonkin and worry about why they're here later.

passages.title: Sethria's Brood
passages.text:
You're good at this.

I like you.

passages.title: Looking Forward
passages.text:
The Admiral used the information you gathered for him to make a forward post under the terrace to our west. He's been preparing there for some kind of attack against the naga.

You should go to him immediately and inform him of the scope of what you've witnessed. Our force is small, and I fear for our soldiers if we charge in too recklessly.

Take my sea horse. It knows the way.

passages.title: Looking Forward
passages.text:
Good to see you again, <class>. I almost thought we'd lost you to the Wavespeaker's fool errand.

Did anything come of it?

passages.title: Clear Goals
passages.text:
I see. The news you bring is grim, but I was not entirely unprepared for such possibilities. Without any effective scouting of naga numbers, I knew our plan was risky, but that's why we established this forward post.

Let me put it to you plainly, <class>. If we do not keep the naga off-balance, they will bring the fight to us. We do not have the structures or the men to mount a defense, so that is not an option.

We need more time. Can you thin their numbers to the south?

passages.title: Clear Goals
passages.text: More naga are amassing to the south than reported too it seems. We shall have to move quickly then.

passages.title: Not Entirely Unprepared
passages.text:
I overheard your conversation with the Admiral. I know what we're doing sounds insane, but we really don't have much choice. There are people back at that cave that are depending on us.

I've stationed lookouts on various ledges in the immediate area. They're burning ammo fast on the scattered naga scouts. Can you bring them more crossbow bolts to buy us some extra time?

passages.title: Not Entirely Unprepared
passages.text: You are perhaps the most dependable person I've ever met. I wish I could have more men half as thorough as you.

passages.title: Curious Distraction
passages.text:
Hah! Did you see the Admiral giving me dirty looks and decide to throw some sympathy my way? I've pretty much lost hope of making him understand that these ruins offers us some opportunity to salvage some usefulness out of this whole mess.

I'd actually hoped that you might turn up again - you seem like the only one I can rely on. I've seen a few tablets like this one spread about the nearby ruins and I put together a rubbing kit for transcribing them. Up to the task?

passages.title: Swift Action
passages.text:
We have everything we need to begin the attack.

If your claims were correct, you would do well to make sure you cling tight to your mount as we make the attack. Anyone who gets caught in the open water isn't likely to out-swim a naga.

Kill as many as you can as we make the attack run and we'll rendezvous on the broken ledge of the terrace above once we've expended our explosives. Hopefully by that point there will be few enough that we can finish them off the old-fashioned way.

passages.title: Swift Action
passages.text: Speak to Enginner Hexascrub to secure a mount for the assault.

passages.title: Swift Action
passages.text:
You did great up there! You devastated their ranks, but there were far more than we accounted for, and most of our men went down out there in the masses of naga.

We'll need to hold this position as long as possible to buy them time. Hopefully some of them will still make it to the rendezvous.

passages.title: Gauging Success
passages.text:
Vicious louts... they did a lot of damage with those spears.

<The admiral winces slightly as he clutches a wound on his side.>

We'll hold here as long as we can for all the men to make it. I need someone to scout their numbers to see how much damage we did.

One of the biggest groups of them was around the corner on the northwest portion of this round terrace, and the other was a bit farther to the north in the small tunnel, also on this middle level of the ruins.

Up for some scouting?

passages.title: Gauging Success
passages.text:
Still so many? They must want something very important here to come in such numbers.

I will be honest with you, <name>, because you deserve at least that: I don't know how much hope there is. We will retreat shortly, but we won't be able to defend ourselves when they strike back. We don't have anywhere to run... we're running out of options.

I'm sorry, I should keep such thoughts to myself. Do me a favor and don't mention any of that to the men. I'll figure something out.

passages.title: Visions of the Past: The Slaughter of Biel'aran Ridge
passages.text:
Look, I know this is asking a lot during a time like this, but I need you to tear yourself away from this defeat for a moment.

I will tend to these soldiers - you need to find the location of that battle with the Kvaldir General to the west that you told me about. You should be able to glimpse more of the Battlemaiden's experiences from there. I have a strong feeling that the key to defeating these naga will lie with that Battlemaiden.

Please hurry - I will do everything I can to buy you time.

passages.title: Visions of the Past: The Slaughter of Biel'aran Ridge
passages.text:
You're finished! Just in time. I don't think we could have held them much longer.

An artifact? Could this be something we can use against the naga? I suppose that would require finding it.

We may have to attend to more pressing matters first, until an opportunity to pursue this further presents itself.

passages.title: Visions of the Past: The Invasion of Vashj'ir
passages.text:
The shard you recovered looks to be of naga origin. I had hoped to find a strong focal object like this for a spell I've been working on that would allow us to glimpse into the recent past.

I've enchanted the blade, but you'll have to take it to a place where we know its owner was. I want you to travel back to the site where you found it and use the blade.

Perhaps we can uncover more behind what the naga are doing here. Or even better, maybe we'll uncover a weakness that will give us a better chance.

passages.title: Visions of the Past: The Invasion of Vashj'ir
passages.text:
A Battlemaiden? I never heard of such a thing.

The way you explain it, it sounds like the naga forces are far greater in scope than the Admiral could possibly have realized. We might be able to learn more through the blade if we can find other locations where this Battlemaiden was present, but the information you gave me makes me fear for the admiral and his soldiers. We must warn them.

passages.title: Disassembly
passages.text:
We have to stop these juggernauts before they're completely encased in armor. Right now they're vulnerable, but only if we pry aside the plates and hack at the marred flesh beneath.

Take my shiv, and jam it between the plates of armored juggernauts to deprive them of their armor.

Once they break from their trance, you're in for a tough fight - keep prying loose that armor and stop those juggernauts!

passages.title: Disassembly
passages.text:
Oh good.

You're still alive.

passages.title: Disassembly
passages.text:
That was some fancy bladework, <name>!

There's one less threat for us to worry about in Hyjal.

passages.title: The Ancient Brazier
passages.text:
What do we have here? A <race>? Come to steal our land with your honeyed tongue and promises?

You do not fool me. I have lived a long time, and I know what dealing with your kind means. But the khans do not listen to their elders like they used to.

Since you are here, I will put you to use. When the waters rushed in, the great water spirit, Aquarian, doused the Ancient Brazier deep inside of Splithoof Hold.

Use this brand to reignite the brazier. Aquarian is sure to come. Bring me the Sacred Flame.

passages.title: The Ancient Brazier
passages.text: You have the Sacred Flame? Do not speak to me unless you do, <race>!

passages.title: The Ancient Brazier
passages.text:
You did this favor to ingratiate yourself with me, but I will not sing your praises.

I know what is to come. Where the sea failed, the great air spirit will strike you and your people down for your many transgressions against the elements.

Begone from my sight!

passages.title: The Codex of Shadows
passages.text:
<This elaborate book contains hundreds of vellum pages bound within a slate cover. It's written in many languages, most unfamiliar. Carefully inked illustrations depict sorcerers or even entire buildings vanishing into curtains of shadow.>

<Many illustrations depict magical artifices like those you see around camp. You suspect the dragon Sethria is trying to keep something hidden. Thisalee will want to hear about this!>

passages.title: The Codex of Shadows
passages.text:
They're doing what?

They're cloaking something? Of course - so our aerial scouts can't see anything with our eagle-eyes!

passages.title: Egg Hunt
passages.text:
Skylord Omnuron wants us to find Aviana's Egg, and I can almost guarantee you it's cloaked by one of Sethria's shadow devices.

Search around the camp for shadow cloak generators and shut those things down until you find the egg.

Once you've unveiled it, I'll call out to the other druids. Defend that egg until we can carry it off to safety.

Go get that egg, <name>!

passages.title: Egg Hunt
passages.text:
We did it, <name>! Aviana's Egg should soon be tucked safely in the boughs of her shrine.

Do you think this means she'll really return to us?

passages.title: Tell 'Em Koko Sent You
passages.text:
Northwatch could really use a powerful <race> like you. We're taking a beating in the Southern Barrens and need your help! Are you interested in lending the Alliance a hand?

The bomb? Yea, it's a problem, but Stonetalon isn't exactly prime real estate. This place was a dump before the Horde sunk their claws into it!

I'll leave the choice in your hands. If you want to help us out in the Barrens, take my horse, Blue Steel. He's grazing at the crossroads south of here. He'll get you past the orc blockade.

passages.title: Tell 'Em Koko Sent You
passages.text:
Kosak sent you, eh? Surprising. I thought for sure that he'd be dead by now.

Well if you made it past the blockade then you definitely have something that we can use.

Now, do you have any news of the Horde? What are they doing? Where are they going? Tell me everything.

passages.title: Bombs Away: Mirkfallon Post!
passages.text:
Scout Commander Barus, stationed at Mirkfallon Post, to the northwest, has spotted the Horde bomb. The Krom'gar hot air balloon, with bomb attached, is currently at the new goblin fueling station at Mirkfallon Lake. This might be the opportunity we need to take that thing out once and for all.

Gather your things, <name>, and move out! Scout Commander Barus awaits your arrival at Mirkfallon Post.

And <name>, your tenacity is a testament to the strength and fortitude of the Alliance!

Glory be unto you!

passages.title: Bombs Away: Mirkfallon Post!
passages.text: I'm assuming you saw the Krom'gar hot air balloon on your way here. If not, get your eyes checked. It's hovering directly over the oil platform.

passages.title: Fallowmere Beckons
passages.text: You're still here? What are you waiting for, a personal engraved invitation? Lord Fallowmere beckons, fool! Go to him now!

passages.title: Fallowmere Beckons
passages.text: Good to see you again, <name>. I have some news from Mirkfallon Lake.

passages.title: Keg Run
passages.text:
Alright. We need to get this ale to where it's going right away!

Ironforge has sent out an expedition of surveyors to check the damage done to the wetlands when the dam burst. Forba Slabchisel's the one leading it...and believe me, you don't want to get on her bad side!

Showing up with an armful of ale will help with that. Go and take this ahead to her, and she might even ask you to stick around for some work.

passages.title: Keg Run
passages.text: Aye? What've you got for me there?

passages.title: Keg Run
passages.text:
Hah! Nice to see those addlebrained mountaineers knew to hand the ale off to a real man to get the job done.

Welcome to my survey. If you're of the mind to help Ironforge by takin' over the intended jobs of some useless, lazy sods that call themselves dwarves, you're in the right place!

passages.title: Sethria's Demise
passages.text:
While you've been raiding Sethria's nest, messages have been flying back and forth between here and the shrine. Skylord Omnuron was at first reluctant, but I've persuaded my fellow druids to risk a direct assault on Sethria herself.

Everyone agreed to my plan... provided YOU spearhead the attack.

Take this signal rocket and engage Sethria on the far ridge. When she reveals her true colors and shifts to her dragon form, fire the rocket and backup will arrive to help you!

passages.title: Sethria's Demise
passages.text: If a minor dragon like Sethria can cause us so many problems, I hate to see what else Twilight's Hammer has in store...

passages.title: Sethria's Demise
passages.text:
Sethria is slain! I knew it was worth the risk.

I'll stay here to look for survivors, but I imagine they'll want to see you back at the shrine.

passages.title: Fake Gold for Black Gold
passages.text:
Now that the "gold" is ready, I want you to take it up to Khan Ablinh. He'll be so overwhelmed, I bet he'll offer to help us setup the drilling rigs. We could use the horsepower.

Haha, get it? Horsepower?

passages.title: Fake Gold for Black Gold
passages.text: What's this? That is a lot of gold you have there.

passages.title: Fake Gold for Black Gold
passages.text: Just put it down on the ground, <race>.

passages.title: Fake Gold for Black Gold
passages.text:
Now that the "gold" is ready, I want you to take it up to Khan Blizh. He'll be so overwhelmed, I bet he'll offer to help us setup the drilling rigs. We could use the horsepower.

Haha, get it? Horsepower?

passages.title: Fake Gold for Black Gold
passages.text: What's this? That is a lot of gold you have there.

passages.title: Fake Gold for Black Gold
passages.text: Just put it down on the ground, <race>.

passages.title: Hammering It Out
passages.text:
The rift that was here left behind this strange device, but why?

Someone in a capital city may have more information.

passages.title: Hammering It Out
passages.text: What's this then?  Another device?

passages.title: Hammering It Out
passages.text:
Not another one! <name>, these devices have been springing up all around Azeroth. We know that they can instigate elemental disturbances in the area, including causing tears in the elemental planes.

The devices stink of Twilight's Hammer.  The engravings covering the surface and the captured elemental essence implicate Cho'gall and his minions are behind this.

If you find more of these, bring them to me or one of my associates. We need to learn more about what's behind this attack.

passages.title: Back to Crazzle
passages.text:
I am NOT stupid!

Go back to your master and tell him that there will be NO deal! That is, if you can survive to make it back to him.

passages.title: Back to Crazzle
passages.text: THEY WHAT?!

passages.title: Back to Riznek
passages.text:
I am NOT stupid!

Go back to your master and tell him that there will be NO deal! That is, if you can survive to make it back to him.

passages.title: Back to Riznek
passages.text: THEY WHAT?!

passages.title: Pushing Forward
passages.text:
Most of the mountaineers and steam tanks in Dun Morogh are battling along the Frostmane Front, which is approaching us from the southeast. We can barely hold the trolls back, let alone advance into their village and take on their leader.

They've blocked our path of approach with mysterious totems that choke mountaineers who come in range, leaving the victims helpless against their enemies. This stone is inscribed with a rune of fire; it should be able to destroy the totems and free our mountaineers.

passages.title: Pushing Forward
passages.text: Was the rune able to destroy the totems? Were we too late?

passages.title: Pushing Forward
passages.text: Finally, some good news from the Frostmane Front. I'll have the mountaineers press their attack immediately. Now, we must signal our gnomish allies at Steelgrill to start their advance.

passages.title: The Deep Reaches
passages.text:
The purpose of this base was to establish a foothold in Stonetalon for Theramore and to open up a supply line to the night elves. The Horde, unfortunately, has given us one hell of a fight. Hellscream's armies are mighty and unrelenting. I haven't seen this type of ferocity from the Horde since the second war.

Now it would appear that the mine the Explorers' League dug out is being used by the Horde to "backdoor" us. We need to seal that thing off!

passages.title: The Deep Reaches
passages.text: Seal it off? That's gonna take some work, friend.

passages.title: Undersea Sanctuary
passages.text:
I believe I've located the author of your note, friend.

It would seem that he is in desperate need of attention if he is to survive.

I shall attune one of my scrying orbs, that you might see him for yourself.

passages.title: Undersea Sanctuary
passages.text: Have you familiarized yourself with the cavern's location, <name>?

passages.title: Undersea Sanctuary
passages.text:
We must make haste!

As you can surely see, his time is not long.

passages.title: Claws from the Deep
passages.text:
Murlocs are crawling out from the deep waters and building their villages on the coastline. They are harassing our fishers and merchants and must be stopped.

One of these murlocs, Gobbler, skulks with other bluegill murlocs and harries merchants along the road, always then retreating to the safety of the nearby murloc hovels. Our merchants are in jeopardy, and we will pay to secure them.

Gobbler prowls the river inlet north of here. Find him, slay his kin, and bring me his head.

passages.title: Claws from the Deep
passages.text: Our merchants will not be safe until we are rid of Gobbler and those murlocs.

passages.title: Claws from the Deep
passages.text:
Ah, well done <name>.

Accept this as payment for fulfillment of your contract with the Merchant Marines.

passages.title: An Ancient Reborn
passages.text:
I'm convinced that YOU are the herald of Aviana, <name>. It was you who first saw her and rescued her essence from the claws of a dragon.

Yes, I believe Aviana is to be reborn into our world. And you shall have the honor of ushering her over the threshold.

Take this incense and burn it before Aviana's egg in the room just above me.

The ancient awaits, <name>. Our deliverance is here!

passages.title: An Ancient Reborn
passages.text:
I ... live.

Those that tried to corrupt me and kidnap my children will soon feel the rake of my talons, <class>. Believe it.

Continue to push forward across Hyjal. I will collect myself and assemble with the other Ancients.

passages.title: The Hatchery Must Burn
passages.text:
<name>! Choluna spoke true: the goddess has returned! A miracle in our midst.

While you were able to kill the twilight dragon Sethria, we have not yet located all of the eggs that the harpies had delivered to her. Thisalee and I have tracked them to a great hatchery constructed within the Firelands. It is not of this realm, so Aviana cannot accompany you.

Fly south and enter the flamegate in the center of the valley. Farden Talonshrike has been sent ahead and will be waiting for you within.

passages.title: The Hatchery Must Burn
passages.text:
So it's true - Aviana has returned, with you as her herald.

There's much to be done here. We are deep in the heart of the Firelands. Sethria smuggled stolen eggs from Mount Hyjal here to hatch her own hideous creations - birds of prey, trained for war.

I hope you're ready to fight back!

passages.title: Shuttin Her Down
passages.text:
To bring this mine down you're gonna need to blow up her support beams. I can provide you with the explosives you'll need, but you're gonna have to trudge through Krom'gar assassins to get to all of the beams.

The good news, if any exists, is that we always mark our support beams with a big 'X.' Look for the markers and plant this dynamite near 'em. Once you've planted all the dynamite come on back up here and I'll activate the explosives.

Kaboom!

passages.title: Shuttin Her Down
passages.text: Here goes nothin'!

passages.title: The Eye of Paleth
passages.text:
Opening the chest reveals a blackened orb, pulsing with an eerie light. This must be the foul Eye of Paleth that damned these sailors' souls.

Such corruption should be purged. Perhaps a priest in Menethil Harbor could help you.

passages.title: The Eye of Paleth
passages.text: How can I help you, lad?

passages.title: The Eye of Paleth
passages.text:
The Eye of Paleth? You say Fitzsimmons sent you out?

By the light...not again. Fitzsimmons is dead, lad. You've not the first to come to me like this, either.

passages.title: A Special Kind of Job
passages.text: You've done an admirable job down here, <name>. Force Commander Valen has taken notice and requested that you see him immediately. He's got a special mission lined up for you - one that'll hopefully put a cold stop on the Horde's incursion into Stonetalon.

passages.title: A Special Kind of Job
passages.text: I knew that you'd be a special snowflake when I first set my eyes upon you, <name>. So special, in fact, that I'd trust no one else here with what I'm about to ask of you.

passages.title: Deliver the Goods
passages.text: Alright, <name>, I need you to get this oil back to Fizzle on the Speedbarge, and let him know the good news!

passages.title: Deliver the Goods
passages.text: What's this? Is that oil?!

passages.title: Deliver the Goods
passages.text:
It is oil! You're really proving yourself to be invaluable, <name>!

Too bad I'm going to have to send you off now.

passages.title: Deliver the Goods
passages.text: Alright, <name>, I need you to get this oil back to Pozzik on the Speedbarge, and let him know the good news!

passages.title: Deliver the Goods
passages.text: Hello again, friend. Is that oil?!

passages.title: Deliver the Goods
passages.text:
It is oil! You're the best, <name>!

Too bad I'm going to have to send you off now.

passages.title: The Last Living Lorekeeper
passages.text:
You have awakened the ancients, <name>, but the wilderness spirit Aessina remains silent. With her help, we can turn the tide of this attack and undo the damage Twilight's Hammer has done.

There may be one who can help us. The oldest of the trees, Nordu, stood in the center of what is now the Flamewake for thousands of years. His wisdom is as old as this mountain. If that old tree still lives, perhaps he can awaken Aessina... seek him out.

passages.title: The Last Living Lorekeeper
passages.text: I ... have not yet ... perished.

passages.title: Death by Proxy
passages.text:
Can you hear them fighting down below, <name>? It would appear that the Grimtotem tauren are no longer in the good graces of the Horde. I don't know what happened, but we can turn this to our advantage.

I will arrange a meeting with an ambassador from the Grimtotem. What I need you to do is put together a peaceful offering.

<Force Commander Valen points to Cookie.>

Talk to "Cookie," <name>. He's already been briefed on what we need to do.

passages.title: Death by Proxy
passages.text:
The name be "Cookie," lad: greatest cook 'cross Azeroth. Now the Commander's told me what we be needin' to do. To gain audience with the Grimtotem chief we're gonna have to cook up the finest of tauren cuisine.

Ye get me the ingredients and I'll put together an offerin' no tauren could refuse. Not even a grim tauren or whatever them things be.

passages.title: Free Freewind Post
passages.text:
Well, it looks like it's time for us to part ways, at least for a while. To the northwest, the tauren of Freewind Post are in desperate need of your assistance in pushing back the Grimtotem clan!

You know, you've been such a great help around here, I bet you're going to be their <hero/heroine> in no-time!

passages.title: Free Freewind Post
passages.text: I am honored that you have come to help, <class>. It was kind of Pozzik to send you.

passages.title: A Proper Peace Offerin'
passages.text:
To make the perfect peace offerin', I be needing the following ingredients:

Kalimdor eagle eggs, obtained from Kalimdor eagle nests. They be scattered about the forest to the west.

Ram haunches! You'll find ram haunches on Stonetalon rams.

The last ingredient be a little tougher to come by, but we be needin' it to make the ramlette. Head southwest to Boulderslide Canyon and find the kobold caves. Kill the kobolds and take their special cheese.

Bring it all back and I'll cook up a masterpiece!

passages.title: A Proper Peace Offerin'
passages.text: This ramlette ain't gonna make itself!

passages.title: A Proper Peace Offerin'
passages.text: Stand back, <name>, there's about to be a flavor explosion and I wouldn't want ya gettin' hurt.

passages.title: Help from Steelgrill's Depot
passages.text:
With your help, we've managed to push toward Frostmane Retreat. Our forces will soon be in position to dwindle down the Frostmane trolls' reserves, leaving their village open to attack.

That's where the Gnomeregan covert ops team comes in. Their technicians have figured out a way to deploy operatives behind enemy lines without alerting the Frostmanes to our presence. Head to Steelgrill's Depot, just northeast of town, and speak with Delber Cranktoggle. He'll tell you more about it.

passages.title: Help from Steelgrill's Depot
passages.text: Ah, you must be the <race> that Captain Tharran said he'd be sending. I've already used the deploy-a-tron to get most of the covert ops team into position at Frostmane Retreat. They're just waiting on your arrival.

passages.title: The Ultrasafe Personnel Launcher
passages.text:
The cataclysm has brought our enemies closer to home, so the chief of Gnomeregan covert operations asked me to build a device to dispatch personnel quickly and quietly to any corner of Dun Morogh.

Behold, the ultrasafe personnel launcher!

With a jolt of electricity and the benefit of a VLD parachute system, uh, that's 'very late deployment' for you laymen, this baby'll get you to the front in no time. Just hop aboard and prepare for flight! Slamp Wobblecog will be waiting for you in the drop zone.

passages.title: The Ultrasafe Personnel Launcher
passages.text: Don't worry, the feeling of being zapped won't stay with you for more than a few minutes. All in all, it's not a bad way to get where you're going. That parachute system needs some work, though. Very late deployment, indeed. Sometimes, too late. Anyway, we have a mission to carry out.

passages.title: Eliminate the Resistance
passages.text:
The Frostmane chieftain died in the initial trogg onslaught, but they've been led by a well-respected warrior ever since. Battok the Berserker was the one who organized the Frostmane retreat, the construction of the new village, and the strikes against Kharanos and the mountaineers.

If we remove Battok, the Frostmanes' organization should crumble, leaving the mountaineers free to pick off the survivors. Battok will be in the village, just east of here.

passages.title: Eliminate the Resistance
passages.text: Excellent job, <name>. With Battok dead, I'll send the signal to Captain Tharran. This should be the end of the Frostmane threat.

passages.title: Strike From Above
passages.text:
Delber's technicians have been up day and night helping us prepare for this strike. Aside from building and tuning the personnel launcher, his men have prepared the covert operations air wing for a strike on Frostmane Retreat. They'll be waiting for a signal to begin their strikes.

Take this flare with you, and set it off near the cluster of buildings at the northern end of the village, and the buildings at the southern end of the village. The flying machines will make a quick strike at each site.

passages.title: Strike From Above
passages.text: Both you and the air wing performed admirably. There's no way that the Frostmanes will remain here now. All that remains is to begin mopping up the survivors.

passages.title: Sating the Savage Beast
passages.text:
You heard the commander, <name>. Deliver me perfect offerin' to the Grimtotem ambassador! Him and his crew be waitin' for you at the bottom of the southeastern path.

This is sure to put us in the good graces of their chieftain!

passages.title: Sating the Savage Beast
passages.text:
<Ton Window sniffs at the air and raises his left hand.>

You have brought something for us?

passages.title: Sating the Savage Beast
passages.text:
<Ton and his bodyguards scarf down the meaty offering.>

This... this is the greatest thing I have ever tasted. You may prove to be a valuable ally, but before the Grimtotem agree to work with the Alliance, you must agree to our terms. I will now give to you those terms as told to me by my leader. Take them back to your commander and see if he accepts.

passages.title: Terms of Service
passages.text:
Grimtotem need weapons! The Horde, empowered by their Warchief and with the help of their new goblin allies, have amassed powerful weaponry. Our armaments are simply no match for their firepower. Supply the Grimtotem with strong weapons and we will work together to destroy the Horde!

These are our demands! Supply the Grimtotem and we will fight for the Alliance!

passages.title: Terms of Service
passages.text: Well???

passages.title: Terms of Service
passages.text:
Weapons, eh?

<Force Commander Valen sighs.>

I'm about to make an executive decision here, <name>. Let's hope this pays off, else King Wrynn will have my head!

passages.title: Grundig Darkcloud, Chieftain of the Grimtotem
passages.text:
The Grimtotem chieftain awaits your arrival, <name>. Take the weapon crates with you and head to Grimtotem Post, south of here.

Good luck, <name>. Should anything happen to you I will personally notify your next of kin and let King Wrynn know what you have done for the Alliance.

passages.title: Grundig Darkcloud, Chieftain of the Grimtotem
passages.text: Do you have the weapons?

passages.title: Grundig Darkcloud, Chieftain of the Grimtotem
passages.text:
These are fine weapons! Powerful steel! My warriors will be unstoppable armed with such weaponry. Magatha smiles down upon you, <name>.

There is but one thing I ask of you, perhaps two.

passages.title: Downfall
passages.text:
By the time that we received word that Hellscream had sent another mag'har orc to oversee the Horde troops in southern Stonetalon, it was too late. Camp Aparaje was burned to the ground and all Grimtotem in the area incinerated.

Now the Horde have four of their most fearsome generals commanding the battle for Greatwood Vale, including the mag'har, General Glubgok.

You must travel to the ruins of Camp Aparaje, south of here, and kill the generals. We stop the Horde NOW! Return to me with their mark!

passages.title: Downfall
passages.text: Are the generals dead?

passages.title: Downfall
passages.text:
<Grundig crushes the insignia in his massive fist.>

Yes, ally, you have done it! It will take Hellscream weeks to recover from this blow. Southern Stonetalon belongs to the Grimtotem... and the Alliance, of course.

passages.title: Dances with Grimtotem
passages.text: Return now to your leader and tell him all that you have done for the Grimtotem. Tell him that the Alliance may pass freely across our borders.

passages.title: Dances with Grimtotem
passages.text: Outstanding work, <name>! Now our forces only need to worry about the Horde as they enter Stonetalon.

passages.title: All's Clear
passages.text:
Pack up your gear, <name>, it's time to join up with the rest of the Northwatch forces in Southern Barrens. Your first mission in Southern Barrens should be fairly straightforward.
