I've one more favor to ask, fleshling.

There is a basilisk, much larger and much older than the rest. Though we normally fear nothing from their kind, this one has become so potent as to petrify some of my sons. This shall not be abided.

Find Gorgonite to the east and slay him. He has lived much longer than necessary.

passages.title: Rock Bottom
passages.text:
Thank you, <race>. You've done all that I can ask of you. I shall impart my favor for you to the Stonemother.

May the stone beneath your feet hold you steady during your quest for the World Pillar.

passages.title: A Head Full of Wind
passages.text:
I'm no druid, but some of these mushrooms do not look to be naturally occurring. I know that our Stone Lord friend over there is eager to blame this on exposure to Azeroth, but I suspect more domestic causes.

I saw some clouds of red mist to the northeast, near the water's edge. They seemed to be spurring new growth in their wake. Take one of my wind-devils with you and get me a sample from those clouds. You may have to stay close to the ground to spot them.

passages.title: A Head Full of Wind
passages.text: You let the mist touch your skin? I hope there weren't any adverse affects.

passages.title: A Furious Catch
passages.text:
Are you up for a challenge, <name>? Good, I was hoping you would be. The Southfury River flows just west of Orgrimmar and your challenge can be found within its mighty flow.

We are looking for a giant furious pike. This esteemed fish used to be prevalent in these areas but ever since the floods hit, the big ones have been much harder to find. Head out to the river and let's see just how good of an angler you really are.

passages.title: A Furious Catch
passages.text: Were you able to catch a giant pike?

passages.title: A Furious Catch
passages.text: <name>, you got one!  It's a rare day that I get to see such a strong, beautiful fish.

passages.title: The Holy Water of Clarity
passages.text:
Hey, listen. You don't look like any old tourist, and I'm in a bit of a pickle. My cousin up north sent me this weird artifact, and I need your help to... ah... identify it.

To start out, I'm going to need you to obtain The Holy Water of Clarity. Rumor has it that whoever drinks from this spring is given a vision of clarity.

Sounds pretty promising, doesn't it?

Obtain it from the Nek'mani Wellspring at the peak of the naga camp. Good luck!

passages.title: The Holy Water of Clarity
passages.text:
<Flem's ears perk up as you approach.>

The Holy Water of Clarity?  Is it here!?

passages.title: The Holy Water of Clarity
passages.text:
<The goblin downs the water in one gulp.>

Ahh... do you know how hard it is to get fresh water in Stranglethorn?  It's no wonder that the nagas guard their shrine so ferociously!

Oh, right... that artifact.  Clarity...

I've got it!

passages.title: Diffractory Chromascope
passages.text:
To properly identify this artifact, I will need tools for analysis. A diffractory chromascope should suffice, I think.

I already have the mithril casing, which surprisingly, is the hardest part to find. We simply need two other pieces: a ruby and a sapphire.

There's pirates nearby, just to our south, and a bit farther to the east. Pirates love treasure... why don't you see if you can find some gems for me?

passages.title: Diffractory Chromascope
passages.text:
<Flem's eyes sparkle.>

Are those gems I see?

passages.title: Diffractory Chromascope
passages.text:
<Flem weighs the gems in his hands and nods in approval.>

Yes, these will do.  Now to perform the analysis...

<The goblin clacks the gems together for a while, then looks up at you.>

Oh, you're still here?  You don't think I'm a fraud or something, do you?

passages.title: Scaring Shaky
passages.text:
If there's one thing I can't stand, it's people who don't pay their gambling debts! And there are a lot of people who owe me. Think you can help me collect?

First, there's "Shaky" Phillipe down by the docks. He owes me plenty after last week's game and I want my due! But to get it, we'll have to scare him.

Go out of town and hunt elder mistvale gorillas. Find a nice selection of giblets, then take them to Shaky. Don't let on that they're from an animal; let him think the worst.

passages.title: Scaring Shaky
passages.text: Hey!  I don't like the look you're giving me, mister.

passages.title: Scaring Shaky
passages.text:
Ack!  Where'd you get these?  No, don't tell me. I don't want to know!

Who sent you?  Sea Wolf?

passages.title: Return to MacKinley
passages.text:
Here, take this pouch and give it to Sea Wolf. And tell him I meant to pay him back! I swear!!

I just got a little drunk and lost my way, and...you know how things are. He'll understand - you don't have to get rough!

passages.title: Return to MacKinley
passages.text: Here here, <name>.  Did you get Shaky's payment?

passages.title: Return to MacKinley
passages.text:
Heh heh, well done!  And when you showed Shaky those giblets, how hard did he shake?

Hah!  He's so easy to read, when I play cards with him I can't help but win!

Thanks for your help, <name>.  Now it's your turn to get paid...

passages.title: Kill-Collect
passages.text:
There's three phases to debt collecting: asking nicely, asking forcefully, and something I like to call "Phase Three".

Unfortunately, collecting during Phase Three is something that this old dog can't do any more. That's why I employ so many cronies, stooges, mooks, goons, and noble adventurers like yourself!

Juntz Fitztittle, Ephram Moonfall, and Maury Wilkins are hiding out on the eastern coast. You should have no problem visiting them all in one trip... and bringing back their valuables.

passages.title: Kill-Collect
passages.text: <name>, did you find those debtors?

passages.title: Kill-Collect
passages.text:
Great!  I can get a good price for these, especially for what's inside Maury's foot!  Thanks much, <name>!

I hope those three learned their lesson: don't bet something you can't afford to lose.

And maybe it's too late for them, but...they should be careful of who they gamble with.

passages.title: Stranglethorn Fever
passages.text:
Sick...so...very s-s-sick... have contracted Stranglethorn Fever....

...technically... CAPE of Stranglethorn Fever....

...deadly v-v-virus....

...only cure... is... is... to eat the heart of M-m-m-m-mokk the Savage... elusive white beast....

...Witch Doctor Unbagwa... only one who can s-s-summon....

...seek Unbagwa in hidden cave on southern cape....

...hurry... dying... dying....

passages.title: Stranglethorn Fever
passages.text:
....mother?

...so cold...

...heading into the Twisting Nether...h-h-h-hold me mother....

passages.title: Stranglethorn Fever
passages.text:
...feel strength returning....

Where might I be?  Booty Bay?  Oh my!  I had the strangest dream...

...the weakness has not completely left me....

passages.title: The Captain's Chest
passages.text:
I used to sail a ship from here all the way to Ratchet, in Kalimdor. I was a successful captain with a sterling reputation.

Until...

Those cursed sea giants ruined me! They smashed my ship, killed my crew, and set me on a lifeboat to Booty Bay. I will not rest until their corpses pepper the ocean floor!

One of the giants, Gorlash, stole my captain's chest. I hear Gorlash wanders the coast east of here. Find him and get back my chest! Do that, and you'll have earned a captain's gratitude.

passages.title: The Captain's Chest
passages.text: Ahoy, <name>!  Did you find Gorlash?  That chest was my favorite, and it has a hidden compartment that held my greatest treasures!

passages.title: The Captain's Chest
passages.text:
You found it!  What a glorious day for ol' Hecklebury, this is.  Getting back my chest cools some of the fire in me.

But my revenge isn't complete...

passages.title: A Giant's Feast
passages.text:
The next giant on my list is called Negolash. I remember vividly how he leapt from the seafoam and plucked poor Poop-Deck Paul from the crow's nest.

Swallowed him in one gulp, he did. And snapped my mizzenmast in two on the way down.

No man on my crew deserves such a heinous death. So we're going to use Negolash's appetite against him. Kelsey Yance should be able to sell you some meat, and Whiskey Slim has enough booze to knock out... well, a sea giant. You'll find both of them in town.

passages.title: A Giant's Feast
passages.text: We're going to need a lot of food, <name>.  Quantity over quality is the goal here.

passages.title: A Giant's Feast
passages.text:
This wasn't expensive, was it?  Well, here's some pieces of eight to reimburse you.

Now let's get onto this revenge, shall we?

passages.title: Mok'rash the Cleaver
passages.text:
Mok'rash the Cleaver is the last of the lot. And the largest, by my memory. Taller than a wave in a windstorm, with a beard like a kelp forest and a hammer like an oak tree.

He taunts me from Janeiro's Point, the island right off the end of this very pier. It's because of him that I'm still trapped here, living this lamentable landlubber's life.

If you can swim, then head out to Janeiro's Point and slay Mok'rash.

Take care, <name>. Mok'rash will not lay down as easily as his brothers.

passages.title: Mok'rash the Cleaver
passages.text: I've been waiting for this moment, <name>.

passages.title: Mok'rash the Cleaver
passages.text:
Mok'rash... Negolash... Gorlash... they're all gone.

I suppose I have no excuses now.  I can return to the high seas and a life of pillage and booty!  And it's all thanks to you.

Now I just need to get myself a ship...

passages.title: A Dish Best Served Huge
passages.text:
Take this food, and put it in our old lifeboat, southeast of here along the coast. When Negolash smells all that food, he'll come running!

And when he does, there will be a stouthearted <class> ready to knock his corpse back into the briny deep.

passages.title: A Dish Best Served Huge
passages.text: Is it done, <race>?

passages.title: A Dish Best Served Huge
passages.text:
I can't believe my fortune, <name>!  Meeting you has turned my luck to the better, make no mistake there!

If I ever get a new ship and you're looking to sail the seas, you would be my honored guest.

passages.title: Message in a Bottle
passages.text:
Inside the bottle you find a note which reads, in fairly good handwriting:

<To any that can aid me->

<Please, my need for help is dire. A great beast holds me captive on an island in the South Seas.>

<The stars at night are foreign to me and obscured by the jungle trees, but on the clearest days I see shoreline to the northwest, and what seem to be large sailing ships to the southwest.>

<I beg of you, my would-be savior, please help me.>

passages.title: Message in a Bottle
passages.text: Have you come to free me?

passages.title: Grubby Little Paws
passages.text:
I understand that you're anxious to rescue me, but the time is not yet right. First I'm going to need some of my things.

The gorillas and the monkeys on the other side of the island have taken most of my possessions. I'll need my tiara, my scepter, my slippers, and my diary before I'm ready to leave.

What? Stop looking at me like I'm some sort of insane person. You don't know what it's like being a princess.

passages.title: Grubby Little Paws
passages.text: I shudder to think what Mukla plans to do with me.

passages.title: Grubby Little Paws
passages.text:
<Poobah surveys her belongings.>

Looks like it's all here.  Alright, I think I'm ready to be rescued now.

passages.title: Mukla's Demise
passages.text:
<name>, I now put my faith in you to help free me. The great Skymane King Mukla is my captor. He commands the beasts of this island, and they keep me here against my will with the aid of this chain. If you can slay him and find the key to this shackle, I shall be indebted to you greatly.

I often hear him to the southeast side of the island, but please be careful: he is not to be trifled with.

passages.title: Mukla's Demise
passages.text: I thank my ancestors someone has come to aid me. Do you have the key that will free me?

passages.title: Mukla's Demise
passages.text: <name>, you have saved me from a great dishonor. If it was within my power, I would offer you a place among my tribe. But for now, all I can only offer you is this token for the courage and nobility you have shown.

passages.title: They Drew First Blood
passages.text:
Take this bundle of Keeshan's possessions and head back to the Lakeshire inn basement. Bravo Company is already there, talking to Keeshan. Remind him of who drew first blood, <name>. Lakeshire needs Keeshan. The Alliance needs Keeshan.

Dismissed, soldier!

passages.title: They Drew First Blood
passages.text: You again?

passages.title: They Drew First Blood
passages.text:
<Keeshan takes the bundle from you and opens it.>

My bow... and knife! Where did you...

Jade's amulet... My darling Jade.

<Keeshan picks up his red headband.>

We got orcs to kill.

passages.title: The Bloodsail Buccaneers
passages.text:
You sure seem eager to work, matey. Not sure why some land-loving <race> <class> is offering help to the Blackwater Raiders, but I'm not going to turn you away.

We've made Booty Bay our happy home away from the high seas, but word has it that the Bloodsail have some new plan cooked up. All me boys are too busy hitting the grog and looking for ladies! What I need is a scout.

Check the cove just north of Booty Bay along the Savage Coast and see what you find.

passages.title: The Bloodsail Buccaneers
passages.text: On top of the barrel, you discover a map with some hastily written text on it, along with some coins.

passages.title: Bloodsail Treachery
passages.text:
The map shows Booty Bay with a red "X" drawn precisely at the spot at which you are standing.

The scribbled text reads:

"Set up your command post here, and bide your time. The Fleet Master will send out word when it's time to make your move."

"I'm placing Lieutenant Bruce in charge here. This time will be different. This time we take Booty Bay once and for all."

The map is held in place with a dagger, placed right through the location of Booty Bay.

passages.title: Bloodsail Treachery
passages.text: Sure, I remember you, <class>.  Back from scouting I see....

passages.title: The Baron Must Be Told
passages.text:
Shiver me timbers! So the Bloodsail Buccaneers are planning some sort of attack on Booty Bay? Why, the nerve of those scoundrels. Booty Bay will always be run by the Blackwater Raiders!

This is bigger than I thought. Report what you have learned to Baron Revilgaz at once! You'll find him here in Booty Bay.

passages.title: The Baron Must Be Told
passages.text:
Bloodsail Buccaneers attacking Booty Bay?  This isn't the first time that those blaggards have tried something.  Booty Bay is impenetrable!

Sounds like they might be changing their strategies up, though.  Wouldn't put it past Firallon to try something crazy.  Very well, let's see what else they're up to.

passages.title: Details of the Attack
passages.text:
I want to know details, <name>. Our supremacy over the Bloodsail is due largely in part to our stronghold here in Booty Bay, but intelligence also plays a critical role.

The Bloodsail maintain a few meager camps to the south which they call their "Southern Command." Well, you're going to raid their excuse for a southern command, find their plans, and slaughter their men. Return with whatever information you can find.

passages.title: Details of the Attack
passages.text: Ahoy, <name>.  What word do you bring of the Bloodsail encampment to the south?

passages.title: Details of the Attack
passages.text:
Perfect, <name>.  Now that we know their plan, it's just a matter of time.

And to think the fools have dropped anchor just off the cape....

passages.title: Up to Snuff
passages.text:
Ah, the sea life. I ain't gonna say it's the good life, but it's my life.

When I get into port I like to find me a good bottle of grog and some high quality snuff. Nasty habits but what's a pirate without his vices, right?

So you can imagine how heartbroken I was to find out the herbalist here in town has gone and sold out of the stuff. Says his shipment got hijacked by those damned Bloodsail Raiders.

I bet a fearless <class> like you could convince 'em to share the goods, eh?

passages.title: Up to Snuff
passages.text: Any luck finding the goods, matey?

passages.title: Up to Snuff
passages.text: Good show, <name>!  And just before I need to ship out too!  Can't thank you enough, old friend.

passages.title: Keep An Eye Out
passages.text:
Avast! Who goes there?

Argh, I am but useless without me special enchanted eye. Bad enough to have lost me eyes in battle in the first place! But by some stroke o' luck we docked in Menethil and a traveling wizard enchanted a special glass eye that let me see again.

Last night I ended up gettin' jumped by some Bloodsail Buccaneers on me way out. Took me eye, they did! Seems those blokes have found their way to Booty Bay.

Help an old sea dog out by gettin' me eye back?

passages.title: Keep An Eye Out
passages.text:
Ahoy, me bucko!  Might not be able to see but I can smell ye from halfway across port.

Could really use me eye back.  Captain's going to keelhaul me when he finds out me peeper is in the hands of them dirty Bloodsail Buccaneers.

What good is a lookout who can't see?  The crow's nest used to be me home...without me deadlights I'd be lucky to scrub the bilge.

passages.title: Keep An Eye Out
passages.text:
Shiver me timbers and timber me shivers!  Ye found me beautiful eye!  Let's see if she still fits.

<Kshhh-thunk>

<name> ho!  Blimey, I can see!!

passages.title: An Old Sea Dog
passages.text:
This old, weathered coin was found on the body of the pirate "Good-Boy" Bruce. Its front side bears the image of a large, unfamiliar pirate ship; on its back side, the term "Brashtide Crew".

Someone who has been in the piracy business for some time might know what this coin is, or what it means.

passages.title: An Old Sea Dog
passages.text: What's that you've got there, <race>?  Let me see it.

passages.title: An Old Sea Dog
passages.text:
That coin!  Where did you get it?

Bruce... yes, I see.  He was one of the Blackwater Raiders once.  One of us, before Greymane closed the Gilneas ports and held his crew captive.

I know that what happened in Gilneas changed the people there, but I never expected them to change their loyalties.  Especially not Bruce.

If you wouldn't mind, could I keep the coin?  I'll pay its worth in gold.

passages.title: Wolves at Our Heels
passages.text:
The dire wolves are the most common threat to the townsfolk here. They lurk in the forests on all sides of us, though most are along the north bank of the river.

These aren't the runt dogs you see in Elwynn, or wherever you come from. They're big as a man and twice as vicious.

If you wish to assist the people of Darkshire, hunt the dire wolves so our streets can be safer.

passages.title: Wolves at Our Heels
passages.text: Don't go thinking that was too easy. Far greater dangers lurk deeper in the woods.

passages.title: You Say You Want a Revolution
passages.text:
If what you say is true, <name>, then we have friends within the Dragonmaw Clan. We can support an insurgency from within their ranks and avoid a lot of bloodshed on both sides.

I can help, but the most dangerous part is up to you.

My Axebite Warriors will launch an offensive on the shores. During the confusion, I need you to slip behind the lines and speak with your revolutionary contact, Zaela.

We'll arm the Dragonmaw and overthrow their fel masters!

passages.title: You Say You Want a Revolution
passages.text:
<name>, what are your people doing? Are you attacking the Dragonmaw or are you here to rid us of Mor'ghor's corruption?

Ah, I see now. I like the way you think. Warchief Mor'ghor won't even know what hit him.

Let's do this!

passages.title: Insurrection
passages.text:
The weapons the Horde has supplied us with will be more than enough. The four of us should split up and arm as many Dragonmaw workers and merchants as we can.

Don't underestimate us, <name>. You'll find even our tradesmen are ferocious in battle.

Let's do as much damage as possible. Arm a squad of Dragonmaw and lay waste to the fel enforcers and warlocks that have intimidated my people for so long. Then meet back here to launch our final strike!

passages.title: Insurrection
passages.text:
Revolution, at last!

The Dragonmaw are finally undoing the shackles of the filth who have held us back!

passages.title: Insurrection
passages.text:
We've lost a lot of good orcs, but the fight is going our way, <name>.

Mor'ghor's regime is collapsing. All that remains is to destroy the beast himself.

passages.title: Death to Mor'ghor
passages.text:
The time has come. Mor'ghor dies today.

Be warned, <class>. Demon blood courses through his wretched veins, and he channels unnatural power. He will be destroyed, yes. But it will not be an easy fight.

You remember where Mor'ghor resides, at the top of the camp. I will meet you there. Finish him!

Be sure to recruit 3 Dragonmaw followers if you are short - you will need our help.

passages.title: Death to Mor'ghor
passages.text:
Well done, <name>! You have done the Horde proud in my absence.

The Dragonmaw have joined us, with Zaela as their new leader. Blood was shed, but casualties were low, and we have their complete loyalty.

Our Horde grows stronger!

passages.title: Troggzor the Earthinator
passages.text:
You have to put an end to this now!

Go back northwest onto the front and kill their battle leader, Troggzor the Earthinator. Bring me his cudgel as proof.

passages.title: Troggzor the Earthinator
passages.text: Is he dead? Do you have the cudgel?

passages.title: Troggzor the Earthinator
passages.text:
<Gravel solemnly nods his head.>

Finally, we can move forward and rescue the Stonefather.

passages.title: Death From Below
passages.text:
This is bad. It seems the Daggerspines are amassing for an attack.

Naga are known for their ruthlessness in battle. They will keep attacking until I am dead.

I don't value my own life above that of my crew members, but you must help to defend me. The crew will not be able to make it back to Booty Bay without my knowledge of the seas.

The naga will be coming from the sea. I need you to remain up here with me to fend off the attack. Man the cannon and drive them back.

Are you ready, <name>?

passages.title: Death From Below
passages.text:
We survived the attack!

We could not have done it without you, <name>.

We'll be heading out as soon as the tide rises. If you weren't such a promising hero I'd offer you a place on my crew. But I can tell you have bigger fish to fry.

Even if you are a puny <race>....

passages.title: Close Escort
passages.text:
Alright, I think I've got it working again. You've got to get the catapult to the stone trogg town, Needlerock Slag, just to the north of the front.

The driver will go with you. I'll head back and let Gravel know.

There's no doubt that the stone troggs will try to stop you. You just keep them off of the catapult. It packs a big punch.

Let me know when you're ready, <name>.

passages.title: Close Escort
passages.text:
<The catapult chief gives you an appraising look.>

Word of your prowess has spread ahead of you, <race>. Let's see if you can help us keep these fungal horrors off of the front.

passages.title: Swabbing Duty
passages.text:
I want the surface of the Riptide t'shine like a star ruby, Swabbie <name>. I keep a tight ship around here, and it's swabbies like you that make it happen!

Well, what're y'waitin' for, y'cockle-brained bilgerat? Head updecks and start swabbin'!

passages.title: Swabbing Duty
passages.text: I heard the most furious mopping sounds from down here, mate.  That's EXACTLY what your Captain likes to hear.

passages.title: Unspeakable Atrocities
passages.text:
<You unfold the note and begin reading.>

Keeshan, if you're reading this note, I'm dead. Likely that my position was compromised.

Orcs are committing unspeakable atrocities against their prisoners. Yes, prisoners, Keeshan. They've got cages full of P.O.W's. If you're gonna blow up this valley, you'll need to free the prisoners first.

Tell my wife I love her and to take out the damned trash.

-Brubaker

PS - They've got black dragons.

Take Brubaker's report back to Keeshan.

passages.title: Unspeakable Atrocities
passages.text: They got Brubaker?

passages.title: Unspeakable Atrocities
passages.text:
<Keeshan reads the report.>

DAMN IT! This just got complicated. We've got prisoners of war to rescue before we can blow up the valley. Not to mention the orcs have black dragons on their side.

Are you ready, <name>?

passages.title: Can't Make An Omelette Without...
passages.text:
The Vilebranch broodguards to the northeast tend the eggs of Shadra's brood. Even if we kill the Vilebranch, those eggs will still sit there, waiting to hatch and release those horrible creatures further into the wilds.

We need to take care of this properly. Tear any eggs you see out of the egg sacks and bring them to me. Don't try to destroy them on your own; you might let the little ones out.

When you get them back here, I'll see that they're properly disposed of!

passages.title: Can't Make An Omelette Without...
passages.text: Do you have the eggs?

passages.title: Can't Make An Omelette Without...
passages.text: I'll see these are burnt to ash right away, and scattered to the winds for good measure.

passages.title: Preserving the Barrens
passages.text:
For years, the Barrens have been the heart of the Horde presence on Kalimdor, a vital link between the orcs of Durotar and the tauren settlements in Mulgore.

In the chaos of the cataclysm, floods, earthquakes, and even a quilboar invasion threaten to separate us from this vital grassland.

You look ready for a challenge. Report to Kargal Battlescar at Far Watch Post and ensure the route to the Barrens remains clear! Head west from nearby Razor Hill and cross the Southfury River to find him.

passages.title: Preserving the Barrens
passages.text:
A fresh recruit from Orgrimmar is it?

<Kargal sizes you up.>

I'll take what I can get. Keeping the roads open has been a nightmare.

passages.title: Attracting Attention
passages.text:
Swabbie <name>! This is a sad day fer ol' Cap'n Keelhaul. Today I lose m'best swabbie.

A letter's come in from Fleet Master Firallon. Apparently he's heard about the excellent swabbin' y'been doin', and he wants t'take ye aboard the Crimson Veil as his Jack o' Swords and third mate. She's moored just next t'the Riptide.

Piracy career-wise, this's a big step fer ye, Swabbie <name>. I recommend y'take his offer.

Dismissed!

passages.title: Attracting Attention
passages.text:
So ye be the one that did ol' Seahorn?  Yancey sent word, but I wanted to make sure he hadn't been telling his tall tales again.

I'll make it brief.  Ye did well on Keelhaul's crew, but I expect ye to do even better on mine.  I've got an entire fleet to attend to, so you'll be helpin' to run the day-to-day of me ship.

Welcome aboard the Crimson Veil, sailor.

passages.title: Prisoners of War
passages.text:
The Bravo Company field kit is ready, <name>. I'm gonna equip you with it and you're gonna enter Render's Valley, southeast of here, and free our P.O.W.s. I'm sending Jorgensen with you to watch your back.

Now the prisoners are being held on the northeast side of the valley in a large cage, but the key to the cage is in a cave on the south side of the valley. You'll have to steal the key, create a distraction, and free the citizens.

Good luck, <name>! I'll be in touch through the field kit.

passages.title: Prisoners of War
passages.text:
<The radio on the Bravo Company field kit crackles.>

Looks like the P.O.W.s are free. Time to initiate Operation: End All.

passages.title: Ol' Blasty
passages.text:
We've got some work to do. How much experience have you got with cannons? Hmm... really? Well, how about with ancient, fallin'-apart pirate cannons?

We've got a few cannons updecks that work the old-fashioned way: you load one cannonball in at a time, aim, lock it into place, and fire. Works well if you're tryin' to hit the side of a three-sailer... not so well for rowboats and the like.

Why don't you head upstairs and lob a few shots at Smilin' Timmy Sticks?

passages.title: Ol' Blasty
passages.text: You look a little green, <name>.  You feelin' alright?

passages.title: Ol' Blasty
passages.text: I like the cut of your gib, <name>.

passages.title: Our Mortal Enemies
passages.text:
Hey, new <guy/girl>, take a look at this.

<The dwarf flips up his eyepatch to reveal a living, functional eyeball.>

I don't wear this patch because of any lost eye. I wear it because this OTHER eye is so strong, the normal one was just weighin' it down.

This eye's good for seein' all kinds of things, like those masked hooligans that follow us around. Fleet Master says that they've been spotted over on Jaguero Isle. Once you get there, fire this flare gun, and I'll help you spot 'em.

passages.title: Our Mortal Enemies
passages.text: Excellent work, <name>.  The eternal battle wages on, but we've tipped the scales in favor of the pirates today.  Firallon will be happy to hear the news.

passages.title: Drive-By Piracy
passages.text:
Now that you know how to handle our cannons, it's time to hit some real targets!

The Venture Company has found gold to the north of here... a rare type they call "Black Gold". More like a Black Spot if you ask me.

We're going to take that gold, but first, we need to get rid of those Venture Company goons. I've got an oarsman who will take you out there. Head off the ship down the gangplank and speak with him on the islet's northern shore.

passages.title: Drive-By Piracy
passages.text: Those goblins will learn the fury of the Bloodsail!

passages.title: Drive-By Piracy
passages.text:
Ahahaha!  Blasted 'em clear off their rigging!  I'll drink to that!

You've got a bright future, kid.

passages.title: The Damsel's Luck
passages.text:
I know ye just arrived here on the Crimson Veil, but I need to send ye off on another task. The Damsel's Luck is the third ship in me fleet, moored over to the east. Her skipper - Captain Stillwater - is no longer with us.

Damn those masked hoodlums!

Anyhow, Ironpatch told me about yer heroics at sea, and I be runnin' low on quality brigands. I think yer more than capable for this new duty.

Congratulations, matey. Ye be the new captain of the Damsel's Luck.

passages.title: The Damsel's Luck
passages.text:
You see a set of plans unrolled on the table.  They explain everything!

These are the details of the impending attack on Booty Bay.  Battle formations, plans of attack, and something about a group called the "Brashtide Crew".

passages.title: To Win a War, You Gotta Become War
passages.text:
<The Bravo Company radio beeps.>

Do you understand yet, <name>? Do you now see what we gotta do to win a war against these monsters? YOU GOTTA BECOME WAR! NO MERCY!

With the P.O.W.s freed you're clear to plant the seaforium. Carefully make your way into each of the structures out there and plant a charge.

Plant a seaforium charge at the Blackrock munitions hut and the Blackrock tower. Once you're done meet up with me and the rest of Bravo Company at Shalewind Canyon, east of Render's Valley.

passages.title: To Win a War, You Gotta Become War
passages.text: And now, we blow the whole damned thing up.

passages.title: Deliver the Thread
passages.text: Here is your thread, <name>. It has a thousand uses, from binding evil spirits to sewing life into inanimate objects.

passages.title: Deliver the Thread
passages.text: I need to string the ghost hair thread along my door and my windows to keep out unwanted spirits.  Did you get it for me?

passages.title: Deliver the Thread
passages.text:
Delightful!  This will do splendidly...

Here, good <name>, take this as payment for your honorable deed.

passages.title: Don't. Stop. Moving.
passages.text:
When Deathwing came, the Stone Dragons flocked to him. In his absence, they are again without purpose. They swarm and feed upon our kin.

I have bound dozens of Opalescent Guardians, but am unable to lead them from the safety of cover. I need someone more swift, as I suspect you might be.

Lead them by ground towards Therazane's Throne to the east. Surely, some will not make it, but as long as you keep moving, you should be able to bring several to join our forces there.

passages.title: Don't. Stop. Moving.
passages.text: Did they make it, <class>?

passages.title: Don't. Stop. Moving.
passages.text: Well done. Of my main strengths, speed is not one.

passages.title: Resonating Blow
passages.text:
On the western edge of the Pale Roost, you will find a resonating crystal. Strike it with the mallet and the broodmother will come.

Be ready for battle. I will be there to aid you, but she will not be easily overcome.

passages.title: Resonating Blow
passages.text:
Impressive, fleshling. You are far more capable than I initially assumed.

I will extend that sentiment to the Stonemother as well.

passages.title: The Brashtide Crew
passages.text:
The charts mention a group called the Brashtide Crew. This name is new to you, though you've heard about a few other newcomers to the Buccaneers.

Maybe it's time you paid them a visit and found out what they know.

passages.title: The Brashtide Crew
passages.text:
The Brashtide Crew aren't just pirates... they're worgen pirates!  And they're joining in on the attack!

Revilgaz is definitely going to want to know about this.

passages.title: Sinking From Within
passages.text:
The attack on Booty Bay is looming. You'll have to return to Booty Bay quickly and inform the Baron.

First, however, it might be a good idea to sabotage some of the pirates' supplies while you're still in their favor. The pirates keep most of their supplies belowdecks, spread out across the entire fleet.

passages.title: Sinking From Within
passages.text: You've set the pirates back several days' work.  Hopefully this will delay their attack.

passages.title: Call of Booty
passages.text:
You feel like you've done just about enough damage, and you know the Bloodsail's battle plans. You've done everything that Baron Revilgaz has asked of you.

It's time to hang up the pirate hat and return to Booty Bay. The battle looms near.

passages.title: Call of Booty
passages.text:
The Brashtide!?  I thought they were dead and gone YEARS ago!

<Revilgaz listens intently as you relay the information you gathered.>

No, that absolutely makes sense.  And it's not good news either.  The Brashtide are formidable foes, and if their numbers are anywhere near what they were before they disappeared, we're in for a nasty battle.

passages.title: Juice Delivery
passages.text:
Here's your Zombie Juice...

...and be careful with this stuff. It's strong enough to raise the dead!

passages.title: Juice Delivery
passages.text: I need that Zombie Juice to keep me warm on these cold, dark nights.  Did you get it for me?

passages.title: Juice Delivery
passages.text:
A thousand thanks, <name>.  You warm an old man's heart with your foolish-...I mean...with your kindness!

Here you are, friend.  Take this as a token of my gratitude.

passages.title: Doublerum
passages.text:
<Baron Revilgaz sighs.> Even with all my suspicions about Firallon's plot, we aren't prepared for a full two-front attack between the Bloodsail and the Brashtide. It's going to take a small miracle to hold Booty Bay today.

I've got a barrel of Doublerum in my chambers. Take the stairs down three flights, and check the first door on your right. You can ignore the warnings on the barrel... those should be the least of your worries.

passages.title: Doublerum
passages.text: This must be the doublerum.  You pour a glass for Revilgaz, then consider pouring one for yourself...

passages.title: A Shambling Threat
passages.text:
Dustwallow is Horde territory, <name>. The humans may have their little island and their precious sand bar, but the marsh belongs to us.

In time, we will surely win this stalemate with the humans. For now, we must master our own territory. The withervine bog beasts to the north rise from the marsh itself to attack any living thing that approaches. If we own this marsh, we must not let our own land fight back against us!

Slay the bog beasts, if you wish to serve the Horde. You will be rewarded.

passages.title: A Shambling Threat
passages.text: Well done, <name>. We'll be able to focus on greater threats here now.

passages.title: Classy Glass
passages.text:
Now there is just one more item needed to complete this device. Cog's blueprint calls for a lens of some sort. The only lens I know of that would be large enough will be very difficult to acquire.

There is an ogre by the name of Zzarc'Vul who resides in the mound in southern Duskwood. If you can, bring to me his monocle and I will use that as our lens!

passages.title: Classy Glass
passages.text: Were you able to convince Zzarc'Vul to lend us his monocle for our experiment?

passages.title: Classy Glass
passages.text: At last!  The stargazing device is complete!  Thank you, <name>.  Now I can continue my research. . .

passages.title: Bones That Walk
passages.text:
There's even fouler undead left to deal with, <name>.

Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, further south of town, is a place you don't want to be caught in at night. The bones that rise from the ground there are cunning enough to remember how to swing an axe or cast a spell.

I shouldn't need to explain how dangerous that makes them. Proceed with caution, but remember the people of Darkshire that will suffer if you falter.

passages.title: Bones That Walk
passages.text: The people of Darkshire thank you, <name>.  You have proven yourself to be a great ally of The Night Watch.

passages.title: Reinforcements From Theramore
passages.text:
Hawthorne dead... my own son murdered... the situation in the Barrens is out of control, <name>.

I'm going to take charge of Fort Triumph and try to lock things down. To do that, I'm going to need reinforcements. Reinforcements that were promised from Theramore weeks ago!

Travel to Theramore in Dustwallow Marsh and give Captain Garran Vimes an earful. What good is that blasted road through the swamp if the men and materiel aren't rolling in?

passages.title: Reinforcements From Theramore
passages.text:
What now, soldier?

Reinforcements? For the Barrens? We've been bleeding supplies and men there for months!

Does someone need to remind Twinbraid of the attack on Northwatch? Our losses at Honor's Stand? What happened to the men I sent to Fort Triumph? We've nothing to spare!

Listen <name>, if you want to help out our cause, you'll focus your efforts here in Dustwallow. Between the deserters and the Horde encroachment... we could use a hand.

passages.title: Vile and Tainted
passages.text:
Your previous accomplishments have convinced me that you are ready to take on the toughest worgen infesting the woods.

Of the worgen that have made their new home here, the Vile Fangs and the Tainted Ones have proven the most dangerous. They've settled down near some of the caves and in the mine to the south.

From far away you can even see the light from their bonfires...

passages.title: Vile and Tainted
passages.text: Intimidating beasts aren't they? But have no fear, <name>, those who stand for the Light will never fall!

passages.title: Vile and Tainted
passages.text: <name>, to be honest with you, I did not believe that you would get this far, but you are clearly a <class> to be reckoned with. In fact, if you wish to formally join Master Carevin's struggle, I will gladly write for you a letter of recommendation.

passages.title: Prepare for Takeoff
passages.text:
I've got an idea, but it's going to involve some footwork on your part. As a goblin cartel, the Blackwater Raiders have a lot of explosives on hand. In fact, I know for a fact that our old friend Narkk keeps a case in the back of his shop, in the Old Port Authority.

Go grab them and bring them here, if they haven't already exploded.

passages.title: Prepare for Takeoff
passages.text: You're still alive?

passages.title: Prepare for Takeoff
passages.text: You brought them!  I'm beginning to think the tide is turning in our favor, <name>.

passages.title: The Final Voyage of the Brashtide
passages.text:
We'll never survive this attack with all these worgen pirates pouring into the harbor from the north. Luckily, it looks like they're not armed with cannons, so if we can get you out of the harbor, you can attack from the skies.

Kebok, the Horde flight master's assistant, is right around the corner. Talk to him and let him know that you're going to need his bravest wind rider.

Bring a couple armloads of handbombs with you. You'll need all of them to stop those attack boats!

passages.title: The Final Voyage of the Brashtide
passages.text: We're still overwhelmed, matey.  Get back out there and protect my town!

passages.title: The Final Voyage of the Brashtide
passages.text:
I hope those mongrels know how to doggy paddle!

Actually, I take that back.

passages.title: Flight to Brackenwall
passages.text:
Listen, I got no special love for the Horde... but then again, I got no real hate for you guys either.

Your gold is as good as anyone else's.

That two-headed ogre and his pet fish left some gold for your travel costs. I believe the person you're looking for in Dustwallow goes by the name of Krog. And the best way to get there is to talk to our flight master, Bragok. He'll fly you there, if you want. The flight's free, thanks to your friend.

passages.title: Flight to Brackenwall
passages.text: Lok'tar, <race>.  Welcome to Brackenwall.

passages.title: Flight to Theramore
passages.text:
Listen, I got no special love for the Alliance... but then again, I got no real hate for you guys either.

Your gold is as good as anyone else's. Sometimes better.

Jeyne left some gold for your travel costs. I believe the person you're looking for in Dustwallow goes by the name of Calia Hastings. And the best way to get there is to talk to our flight master, Bragok. He'll fly you there, if you want. The flight's free, thanks to your friend.

passages.title: Flight to Theramore
passages.text: Welcome to Theramore.

passages.title: Bloodsail's End
passages.text:
We've nearly won the day, largely thanks to you. One task remains, however... kill Fleet Master Firallon.

It looks like most of Firallon's crew is already dead, but I know that old sea dog well enough to know that he's not done yet. No, he's cooped up tight in his cabin, ready to go down with his ship.

Speak with Kebok again to get a wind rider. I'll try to hold off the cannonfire while you're on board.

passages.title: Bloodsail's End
passages.text:
<name>!  You're awake!  We found you bobbing in the harbor, shortly after the remaining attackers had turned tail.  We were worried about you for a while there...

I've been meaning to thank you, <name>.  Not only did you provide us with the intelligence to prepare for this attack, but you helped fight off the Bloodsail AND the Brashtide.  Your name will always be remembered here in Booty Bay.

We here in Booty Bay pride ourselves on our booty.  Care to take first pick?

passages.title: AHHHHHHHHHHHH! AHHHHHHHHH!!!
passages.text:
I'm here to help you and Bravo Company end this mess. You're to get in the Bravo Company siege tank and clear a path to Keeshan's Post on the other side of the valley, north of here.

This is a high alert situation soldier as the Blackrock orcs are now aware of your location and sending a large force to meet you head on. Terminate them all with extreme prejudice.

I'll see you on the other side. May the Light have mercy on your soul.

passages.title: AHHHHHHHHHHHH! AHHHHHHHHH!!!
passages.text: We're ready for the final assault.

passages.title: AHHHHHHHHHHHH! AHHHHHHHHH!!!
passages.text: The only thing left to deal with now are the orcs holding out at Stonewatch Keep.

passages.title: Lost In The Deeps
passages.text:
Pebble has gotten himself lost again, somewhere deep in the Crumbling Depths.

He's fortunate that his size makes him unworthy of the effort for those gyreworms, but it's only a matter of time before he stumbles too close to one and gets eaten. Whatever he's so intent on down there is certainly not worth it.

He seems to like you. Please, go and find him and bring him out of those tunnels to safer playing grounds.

passages.title: Lost In The Deeps
passages.text: Pebble is much smarter than he lets on, but he is spoiled. I fear one day he may suffer for it.

passages.title: Lost In The Deeps
passages.text:
You've done well. Now that these are rocklings are free to learn our ways, they will grow tall and strong.

One day, we will extinguish the gyreworm infestation from our realm, and these rocklings shall no longer be plagued in their youth.

passages.title: Darkblaze, Brood of the Worldbreaker
passages.text: As Troteman cuts out, the world around you grows eerily silent. In the distance you see a full grown black dragon!

passages.title: Darkblaze, Brood of the Worldbreaker
passages.text:
<A single tear rolls down Troteman's left cheek.>

They died in defense of the Alliance. In defense of our kingdom! Heroes, all of them, and they will be laid to rest as such.

passages.title: A Curse We Cannot Lift
passages.text:
What we do here is not a cure. The transformation cannot be removed once inflicted. But the mind...

The mind can be restored, through alchemy, if enough is left intact. This worgen you've encountered sounds like he's fighting to stay aware, <name>. We've got to find him again.

If he's fled the Yorgen Stead, search the Addle Stead to the south; he may be lurking in one of the buildings.

Inject him with this ampule to tranquilize him. You'll need to be quite close.

passages.title: A Curse We Cannot Lift
passages.text:
You've got him!

No time to lose, then. We'll prepare to administer the serum right away.

JITTERS! Get ready!

passages.title: You Can Take the Murloc Out of the Ocean...
passages.text:
I need something to cut into the raw, elemental power of these bracers... something strong and abrasive, but still of the sea.

The Murkgill murlocs have moved inland from the sea, but they still carry vials of sea salt on them. What they use it for, I can't be sure, but it will serve for our studies. You can find the Murkgill in the glade south of the Rebel Camp and east of Bal'lal ruins.

passages.title: You Can Take the Murloc Out of the Ocean...
passages.text: The salt?

passages.title: You Can Take the Murloc Out of the Ocean...
passages.text: We have what we need.  Are you ready to activate the Altar of Naias, <name>?

passages.title: The Altar of Naias
passages.text:
The salt you brought was sufficient to activate the bracers' innate enchantments. I have taken these enchantments and combined them into a summoning token... a gift, if you will.

Return to the Isle of Naias, and place the gift on Naias' altar. Call me again once you have Naias' heart.

passages.title: The Altar of Naias
passages.text: I eagerly await the results.

passages.title: The Altar of Naias
passages.text:
My colleagues within the Kirin Tor will be happy to learn that the heart is ours.

Thank you for your assistance, <name>.  I couldn't have done it without you.

passages.title: The Source of the Madness
passages.text:
After reducing the basilisk blood out of the elixir, I've uncovered an unusual precipitate. It appears to be a blue crystal of some sort...

<Brother Nimetz consults his notes.>

It's not a singing blue crystal... not a pulsing blue shard...

<He flips forward a few pages.>

... not a piece of the Mind's Eye. Nope, this isn't something we've seen before in Stranglethorn. If anyone has any more of this substance, I want it. Check the high-ranking Kurzen troops, in the back of their cave.

passages.title: The Source of the Madness
passages.text: Make sure you handle that stuff carefully, <name>.  We don't know what it is.

passages.title: The Source of the Madness
passages.text:
<Brother Nimetz opens up a pouch and lets you place the crystal inside.>

I knew they'd have some more of this substance.  I'm going to send this to my contacts at Fort Livingston, to the south.  Hopefully they'll have some more luck with it.

Thank you for everything, <name>.

passages.title: The Fate of Kurzen
passages.text:
Hello, <class>.

We are soldiers of Stormwind, and rebels from Kurzen's Compound, a large outpost that you'll find just to the southeast of here. We were under the command of Colonel Kurzen, until he and those close to him started to descend into madness...

We rebelled, set up camp here, and stood against Kurzen. Now, my sources are telling me Kurzen has disappeared. I trust my source, but it would help to hear from a third party. Please, head into the compound and find some documentation of his fate.

passages.title: The Fate of Kurzen
passages.text: What were you able to find, <name>?

passages.title: The Fate of Kurzen
passages.text: They KILLED him?  And all this time, I thought he had them underneath an iron bootheel...

passages.title: Spared from Madness
passages.text:
Kurzen's death is a relief, but what's more interesting, and perhaps more immediate, is the sign of some potential allies within the compound.

I don't care what it says on that prison record, I know EXACTLY why those 3 were locked up: refusal to follow orders. They must have been spared from the madness, much like my fellow rebels here, and incarcerated for speaking up.

Find them, <name>. Find them, and send them back here.

passages.title: Spared from Madness
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.  It looks like my suspicions were correct... the three prisoners seem to have escaped the affliction that gripped Kurzen and the rest of his men.

Before you arrived, Emerine teleported them over to Stormwind to get cleaned up after their ordeal.  They promised to return soon.

passages.title: Stopping Kurzen's Legacy
passages.text:
Now that our allies have been evacuated, it's time to run a final raid on Kurzen's Compound. They will never be weaker than they are right now, and with your help, we may be able to weaken them beyond repair.

Those four names that were listed in the Officers' Dossier - Anders, Gaulus, Miranda, and Esquivel - will be the highest-ranking personnel remaining. Look for them in that cave in the back of their compound. Removing all four will be devastating to Kurzen's forces.

Go with honor, <name>.

passages.title: Stopping Kurzen's Legacy
passages.text: Remove the heads, <name>.  I know you can do it.  My men will clean up the remainder of their forces after you are done.

passages.title: Stopping Kurzen's Legacy
passages.text:
Marvelously executed, <name>.  My men and I can handle the rest.

With Kurzen out of the picture, we may be able to continue our original expedition here in Stranglethorn, which was... ahh...

No matter.  Please, feel free to peruse our armor stores.  You may find something that fits you well.

passages.title: Just Hatched
passages.text:
While looking through this soldier's possessions, you look down to see a newborn raptor hatchling looking back up at you. Was it following this Kurzen militiaman the whole time?

You can see it studying you, learning your features and following your movements.

The lashtail hatchling has formed a bond with you.

Perhaps someone back at the Rebel Camp will know what to do with a raptor hatchling.

passages.title: Just Hatched
passages.text:
Yes, the little one seems to have taken a liking to you.  You're lucky... at this age, the raptors are calm, peaceful, and easily trained.  Keep her, <name>... she may come in handy.

In fact...

passages.title: I Think She's Hungry
passages.text:
It looks like your young raptor is hungry. If you're looking to keep her, why don't you find something for her to eat? The lashtail often attack the basilisks of Stranglethorn, which can be found to the east, beyond Kurzen's Compound.

She probably isn't strong enough to hunt on her own yet, but I'm sure she will eat freshly killed basilisk meat.

passages.title: I Think She's Hungry
passages.text:
She looks bigger already!  You can see, these raptors grow quickly.  You are lucky to have found such a strong companion.

Keep her by your side as long as you can, <name>.  I'm sure she will prove to be an asset in the future.

passages.title: Sacred to the Bloodscalp
passages.text:
Ahh... these must be names of their totemic creatures - the animals that they attribute to the spirits. Let's see... Mahamba as water, Tsul'Kalu as earth, Pogeyan as... air? Fire? I can't make this part out.

I'd like some more information on these spirits of theirs. The Bloodscalp have a camp close to here, in the Tkashi ruins. Maybe you can find some details there.

passages.title: Sacred to the Bloodscalp
passages.text: It's likely that these totemic creatures are based on some of the fantastic creatures that roam this jungle.

passages.title: Sacred to the Bloodscalp
passages.text:
First you save me from the madman's jail cell, and now you bring me some keys to understanding trollish shamanism.

This is turning out to be a pretty good week!

Thank you again, <name>.  I will see to it that you have the support of the Wildhammer clan as you continue on your journeys.

passages.title: Deep Roots
passages.text:
On a somewhat unrelated note, I've been putting together a collection of troll stories and legends for a... personal project. I was just thinking you might be able to help me find some of them.

The Bloodscalps at the Bal'lal ruins, on the coast to the southwest, maintain a large tablet documenting some of their stories. Of course, I'll reimburse you if you're able to bring any of these stories back to me.

passages.title: Deep Roots
passages.text: Did you make it down to Bal'lal Ruins yet?  Did you find the tablet?

passages.title: Deep Roots
passages.text:
To be honest, I'm sending this information home to Stormwind, for my wife and son.  They love to hear about what I've been doing out here in the jungle, and I only get to visit so often.  Every little bit helps.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Favored Skull
passages.text:
Your pet raptor seems to have found a new toy: a skull, from a nearby troll skull pile.

What sets this skull apart from the rest is beyond you, but for some reason, she won't put it down.

Osborn Obnoticus, the gnome you saved from Kurzen's Compound, is an expert in troll history and physiology. Maybe he'll have some idea what makes this one so special.

passages.title: Favored Skull
passages.text:
What do we have here?  A young raptor, and her pet <race>.  Hah!

More importantly, what is that skull you have there?  This was no ordinary troll.  He was big...

... and strong, too.  You know, I've been meaning to try my hand at some troll magic.  How hard could it be?  Let's use this strong fellow as a test subject, shall we?

passages.title: A Physical Specimen
passages.text:
The soul is ready, but the body is not. For a skull as well-formed, as marvelous, as beautiful as this... we will need a suitable body.

The chief of the Bloodscalps, Gan'zulah, won his throne with brute force. If he still lives, you'll find him in Zul'Kunda, to the west.

Taking his body won't be easy, but nothing a sturdy <class> like yourself couldn't handle. Bring it back here when you're done.

passages.title: A Physical Specimen
passages.text: Gan'zulah was a brute and a tyrant.  I've got a feeling that this troll will be different.  This troll magic is easier than I thought it would be!

passages.title: A Physical Specimen
passages.text: You have done well, <race>.  We have a head, a body, and some juju-voodoo-mojo nonsense.  Now, just a little shock of electricity to get things started, and...

passages.title: Bloodlord Mandokir
passages.text:
<race>. You just resurrected your worst nightmare. You didn't think I was a friend, did you, <race>? Ah, ha ha haaaa!

You've served your purpose. I've returned to the realm of the living, and it's all thanks to you. So, instead of killing you, I'm going to make you a deal instead.

Give me that raptor.

You must already know that she's no normal raptor, and I need a replacement for Ohgan. Do it, or both you and the gnome will taste my rage.

passages.title: Bloodlord Mandokir
passages.text: All I ask is the raptor, <race>.  Give it to me, and the gnome lives.

passages.title: Bloodlord Mandokir
passages.text:
I'm glad to see you've come to your senses.

Come and visit us in Zul'Gurub sometime, <race>.  I'll be watching...

passages.title: Priestess Thaalia
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. I know you didn't have to save my life.

The return of Bloodlord Mandokir is ill news. He was killed inside Zul'Gurub several years ago, and we thought we had seen the last of him and his kind. The trolls of Zul'Gurub were attempting to perform a hideous, horrible ritual. If Mandokir is alive, then it stands to reason that he is not the only one.

The explorers at Fort Livingston, far to the south, may know more. Speak with their priestess.

passages.title: Priestess Thaalia
passages.text:
Mandokir is alive, yes.

You are responsible, yes.

You may be able to stop him still, yes.

passages.title: Population Con-Troll
passages.text:
I understand you may be headed to Zul'Kunda soon. While you are there, I have a small task for you.

The trolls are outgrowing Stranglethorn. The Bloodscalp in the West, the Skullsplitters in the East... they pour out of their ruins and into the jungle, disrupting the natural balance of the region. It is time we restored that balance.

Zul'Kunda is the Bloodscalp capital. Inside you will find the most high-ranking Bloodscalps. Reduce their numbers, then return to me.

passages.title: Population Con-Troll
passages.text: Balance is restored - for now.  We may call on you again in the future, <name>.

passages.title: Audience with the Stonemother
passages.text: Stay where you are, champion. I have not yet decided what to do with you or your Earthen Ring.

passages.title: Audience with the Stonemother
passages.text: Ya've done well, brotha. Da Stonemother be listenin' and da World Pillar is not far from our reach.

passages.title: Flight to Auberdine
passages.text:
From Rut'theran, there are two methods of travel to Auberdine: by ferry and by hippogryph. Both are quick and reliable, but if you have not yet flown to Auberdine by hippogryph, then I suggest you do.

It is sound advice to speak with the hippogryph master in every town that has one. Once you speak to the master, you can then fly there from other towns.

Here is Nessa's collection. Speak with me again when you are ready to fly to Auberdine and deliver Nessa's collection to Laird.

passages.title: Venture Company Mining
passages.text:
If I'm going to repair this pot, I'm going to need reagents. And to get them, you're going to have to do an eensy little bit of killing. I hope you don't mind.

Those dastardly Venture Company geologists have been collecting some tumbled crystals that will suffice for what I need. You'll find them around their Base Camp, on the other side of Lake Nazferiti, to the east.

I don't care what you have to do to get them.

passages.title: Venture Company Mining
passages.text: Do you have those crystals?

passages.title: Venture Company Mining
passages.text:
These will work fine.  Just a moment please.

<Krazek thrusts the stones into the cooking pot and wiggles them around a bit.>

All fixed!

passages.title: Return to Corporal Kaleb
passages.text:
So, this pot is fixed. I even added an extra steam whistle, and look! There's a new chopper at the bottom that'll cut through leg bones!

Yes yes, Krazek's Crock Pot is a 100% cook pleaser! I'm sure its owner will be satisfied.

passages.title: Return to Corporal Kaleb
passages.text: Hello, <name>.  Did the goblin Krazek fix my pot??

passages.title: Return to Corporal Kaleb
passages.text:
It's fixed!  This is great, now I can get dinner started!  Thanks so much, <name>.

I hope Krazek didn't give you too much trouble.

passages.title: Big Game, Big Bait
passages.text:
We're only going to get one shot at capturing Abyssion, <name>. Let's make it count.

We'll test out the trap on the biggest of the stone dragons in the Alabaster Shelf.

To lure the stone matriarch, we're going to need to gather sufficient bait.

Take this knife and carve 5 sides of basilisk meat. That ought to be enough even for her appetite.

passages.title: Big Game, Big Bait
passages.text: Did you obtain the meat?

passages.title: Big Game, Big Bait
passages.text: That should be enough to lure the beast, <name>.

passages.title: Raging River Ride
passages.text:
Enjoy your cut of the loot, <name>!

I hate to share, but business is business. And that double-dealer Nozzlepot is guaranteed a 10% cut of this treasure. Can you deliver this to him at his outpost in the north?

He's got a little research station upstream, along the river. If you travel just northeast of town here, Horton Hornblower can give you a free ride on one of his riverboats. Tell him I sent ya!

passages.title: Raging River Ride
passages.text: Welcome, <class>. Fresh off the boat from Ratchet? Any news?

passages.title: Raging River Ride
passages.text:
<Nozzlepot snatches the bag of gems from you.>

Gazlowe calls this 10%? You tell him I'm going to weigh these!

I suppose he expects me to pay you a delivery fee, as well? Fine, fine. Have some spoils!

passages.title: Mystic Masters
passages.text:
The Needlerock mystics have taken control of the fungal giants that have sprouted in their chasm, down below. Now they seek to control our war constructs.

Go north into Needlerock Slag and do something about it! Isn't that what you're here for?

passages.title: Mystic Masters
passages.text:
A few less stone troggs is always a good thing. Glad to see that you're a decent <class> after all.

We'll soon know the exact location where they're keeping my father captive. Hope you survive until then.

passages.title: Testing the Trap
passages.text:
You must set the trap for the matriarch now.

Go to the western end of the Alabaster Shelf and place the trapped basilisk meat in the center of the feeding grounds.

passages.title: Testing the Trap
passages.text: Well done, <name>.  Here's to hoping the trap performs as well when we try it on Abyssion.

passages.title: Mind Vision
passages.text:
To know Mandokir, you must see Mandokir.

To see Mandokir, you must use eyes of raptor.

You have formed bond with raptor: Ohgan'aka: daughter of Ohgan.

To strengthen bond, we need feathers.

You will go northeast, and you will find the feathers, yes.

passages.title: Mind Vision
passages.text: Raptor named Ohgan'aka, still your friend.

passages.title: Mind Vision
passages.text:
You bring feathers, yes.

You can follow directions, yes.

passages.title: See Raptor
passages.text:
We have the feathers, yes.

We have the <class>, yes.

Speak with Priestess when you are ready.

passages.title: See Raptor
passages.text:
Your vision not Ohgan'aka's, no.

You are not ready.

passages.title: See Raptor
passages.text:
What did Priestess tell you?

The raptor is daughter of Ohgan, heir to Mandokir's seat.

Hah!

passages.title: Be Raptor
passages.text:
Mind Control, very powerful, yes.

With luck, you can help Ohgan'aka escape from Zul'Gurub.

Then, Ohgan'aka becomes <name>'aka again!

Speak to Priestess, yes, and help <name>'aka escape.

passages.title: Be Raptor
passages.text:
What a shame, yes.

This is what the spirits wanted, yes.

Maybe when you are stronger, you will go into Zul'Gurub and take back your <name>'aka from Mandokir, yes.

For now, Priestess give you this.

passages.title: Ghaliri
passages.text:
Priestess is not very good at speaking Common, no.

Maybe you go speak with Ghaliri, in front of that tent.

Tell him about what you've seen inside Zul'Gurub, yes.

passages.title: Ghaliri
passages.text:
<You explain to Ghaliri what has happened up to this point.>

It would seem that Jin'do has survived, and he is rallying his brothers to once again summon Hakkar into this world.  It was good of you to come to speak with me.

There is not much we can do now but to wait, and watch.  Jin'do is weak, and prime for striking, but I must wait for word from Rastakhan before issuing orders.  Until then, you and your raptor will have to wait.

passages.title: Nighttime in the Jungle
passages.text:
Nighttime in Stranglethorn is a beautiful thing. The skies fill with stars, and the moon casts its rays right between those leaves, right there. I could stare at these skies all night.

Unfortunately, the trolls that walk the ruins of Zul'Mamwe are interfering with my astronomy. They burn braziers, day and night, which rob me of the darkness I need.

Please, <name>... travel east into Zul'Mamwe and put them out.

passages.title: Nighttime in the Jungle
passages.text: I can see the difference already.  I can't wait until later tonight, when I get to perform my observations again!

passages.title: The Mind's Eye
passages.text:
One of the Vale's many treasures lies nearby, on OUR side of the giant whirlpool. The Mind's Eye is held by an ogre mage, in the Mosh'Ogg ogre mound just to the northeast. His name is Mai'Zoth. From what I understand, he is vicious, and his magic is strong.

And if he has the Mind's Eye, then his magic will be stronger still.

Thus far I've been unable to get near enough to take it from him. Will you give it a try?

passages.title: The Mind's Eye
passages.text: Do you have the Eye?

passages.title: The Mind's Eye
passages.text:
You retrieved the eye!  Your might is the stuff of legends, <name>!

And to think my brother and sister said we wouldn't find anything of worth here in the Vale.  Hah!  And I'm just getting started!

passages.title: The Mosh'Ogg Bounty
passages.text:
There's been some activity up north, at the rebel camp. I just heard from a soldier named Nimetz that some <race> <class> up there found the key to what's been driving them so crazy. That wasn't you, was it?

Anyhow, he sent a sample to me, and it looks just like the rocks I've been seeing over at the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, to the northeast.

I've heard that the ogres are guarding a chest up in some ruins behind their mound. I suspect it may be related. Care to fetch it for me?

passages.title: The Mosh'Ogg Bounty
passages.text: Why is it that the OGRES always find the priceless artifacts?

passages.title: The Mosh'Ogg Bounty
passages.text:
<Wulfred peers into the box.>

This... this is not like what I expected.  I had thought it would be a... a...

<His eyes glaze over.>

Ahem!  I'm sorry.  I'm not sure what came over me.  I'll be sending this south, to the Explorers' League Digsite in the Cape.  Maybe they'll know what to do with it...

passages.title: The Mosh'Ogg Bounty
passages.text:
There's been some activity up north, at the rebel camp. I just heard from a soldier named Nimetz that a <race> <class> up there found the key to what's been driving them so crazy. That wasn't you, was it?

Anyhow, he sent a sample to me, and it looks just like the rocks I've been seeing over at the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, to the northeast.

I've heard that the ogres are guarding a chest up in some ruins behind their mound. I suspect it may be related. Care to fetch it for me?

passages.title: The Mosh'Ogg Bounty
passages.text: Why is it that the OGRES always find the priceless artifacts?

passages.text:
<Wulfred peers into the box.>

This... this is not like what I expected.  I had thought it would be a... a...

<His eyes glaze over.>

Ahem!  I'm sorry.  I'm not sure what came over me.  I'll be sending this south, to the Explorers' League Digsite in the Cape.  Maybe they'll know what to do with it...

passages.title: Mor'Ladim
passages.text:
From what my scouts tell me, Mor'Ladim wanders throughout Duskwood, following a strange and meandering path through the cemetery. We buried him out past the house on the hill, you know where that is?

There isn't anything I can do to help you, but I wish you good luck.

passages.title: Mor'Ladim
passages.text: I don't blame you if you're having trouble with him, <name>. Some of our strongest Watchers have been lost to Mor'Ladim.

passages.title: Mor'Ladim
passages.text:
You killed him? That's no small accomplishment, <name>! On behalf of the people of Darkshire and the Night Watch, I thank you.

Ah... there is one small matter, however...

passages.title: A Daughter's Love
passages.text:
Here, take this and lay it on his grave. Maybe... somehow, he'll know that I'm okay, and that none of us hold him responsible for what happened.

<There are tears in her eyes now, as she slides a ring from her right hand, and presses it into your hands.>

And... thank you, <name>.

passages.title: A Daughter's Love
passages.text: Leave me be...

passages.title: A Daughter's Love
passages.text:
<A ghostly voice sounds on the wind...>

This is...? Sarah? Could it be she's still alive? The weight is removed from my shoulders...

<name>. Take my sword, Archeus. As my soul is put to rest, I have no more need for it. It was forged to do good, and though I have proved myself unworthy to hold it, perhaps you will carry on the Light through it.

Lys, my love...

passages.title: Saurfang Will be Pleased
passages.text:
The portal is ready!

It's not powerful enough to transport an army, but we can maintain the connection long enough to allow important individuals to pass back and forth.

Saurfang will want to know about our progress here. Walk through the portal to Orgrimmar, then deliver the news him.

passages.title: Saurfang Will be Pleased
passages.text:
<class>, you've returned from Dragonmaw. The portal is functioning then? Good.

Before you return to your work there, we've got some dirty business to clean up right here in Orgrimmar...

passages.title: Recruitment
passages.text:
We've been shipping in dead bodies from Silverpine, Hillsbrad... hell, anywhere we can get them from. We can't, however, afford to ignore the bodies which are sitting right on our front doorstep.

The last vestiges of the Scarlet Crusade roam here in Tirisfal Glades. While we've managed to push them from Deathknell, several of their bodies litter the buildings to the north and the east.

Go find them... and bring that Darnell fellow with you. He looks strong enough to carry a few corpses.

passages.title: Recruitment
passages.text: Have you managed to scavenge up some corpses?

passages.title: Recruitment
passages.text:
Great work <name>.  I knew you weren't useless.

Here, take one of these.  We deathguards have piles of these things just sitting around.

passages.title: Scourge on our Perimeter
passages.text:
If you're going to be an asset to the Forsaken, you need to learn how to fight. And there's no better target than the Scourge minions that continue to pester us.

The wretched ghouls and Rattlecage skeletons that roam the north and to the east are former troopers of the fallen Scourge. They should prove to be an even match for a fledgling <class> like you.

Do not tarry - when you are done, speak to me again.

passages.title: Scourge on our Perimeter
passages.text: Those who dally in this task might as well end up wandering about aimlessly like our fallen brothers and sisters in the village.  Let's hope you will fare better than them, yes?

passages.title: Scourge on our Perimeter
passages.text:
You're growing in strength, <name>.  I've seen your type before.  You will be moving out of Deathknell and on to greater things before long.  Just make sure you don't lose sight of where you started.

You have much to accomplish, <class>.

passages.title: Flight to Razor Hill
passages.text: When you're ready to take the wind rider down to Razor Hill, simply speak with me again. When you get there, waste no time in finding Gar'Thok. He's the one responsible for preparing reports on recent Alliance activity in Durotar.

passages.title: Flight to Razor Hill
passages.text: Eitrigg sent you? The warchief must be getting anxious to read my reports. I'd've sent them long ago, but each day we discover more about the Alliance's plans for invading Durotar.

passages.title: To the Cape!
passages.text:
The Explorers' League is growing, <name>. Not only have they taken in worgen like me, but they have expanded their range in search of artifacts. One of our best, Bronwyn Hewstrike, has set up a camp in the south, where he believes an item of titan origin may be hidden.

Bronwyn asked me to perform some duties here in the north, one of which was to identify potential recruits. You seem to be made of the right stuff. Talk to Robert Rhodes, the flight master, and he'll send you down there. Bronwyn's treat.

passages.title: To the Cape!
passages.text: Wulfred has a good eye.  I think you'll do just fine here at my camp.

passages.title: Return to Eitrigg
passages.text:
Since you've already spoken to Doras, you'll be able to hire a wind rider to take you right back to Orgrimmar. Each time you arrive in a new town, be sure to speak with the town's flight master. After that, you'll be able to use the flight master's services to travel quickly.

Speak to me again when you're ready to purchase a return flight to Orgrimmar. Bring those reports to Eitrigg in the Valley of Strength once you've landed.

passages.title: Return to Eitrigg
passages.text: Did you bring those reports?

passages.title: Return to Eitrigg
passages.text:
<Eitrigg examines the reports.>

The Alliance has grown bolder than we'd thought! I'll talk to the warchief about sending reinforcements right away. Thank you for getting these reports to me so quickly. I hope this coin is enough to cover your travel expenses.

passages.title: Maywiki
passages.text:
<Linzi looks troubled.>

You know, there's a troll hiding behind that pile of boxes. She must be awfully sad, if she doesn't want to come out and talk to anyone.

<Linzi places some of the Akiris reeds in a kerchief and ties it together.>

Here, give these to her. They're very soft, and that maybe they will make her feel a little more comfortable back there.

passages.title: Maywiki
passages.text: Care to explain yourself, <class>?

passages.title: Maywiki
passages.text:
<The troll looks into the package.>

You have my thanks.  You may tell your young dwarven friend that I am not sad.  I am waiting.  For you.

I have identified you as the most promising <race> here in this strange town.  I have a task for you, if you would be willing to take it.

passages.title: Backdoor Dealings
passages.text:
Zanzil the Outcast, an exile from the Gurubashi tribe, is my quarry. Recently, I have heard tales from my brothers in the north about his planned reentry into society, starting with the emissary he sent to the Skullsplitters. This is not good news.

I want you to peer into Zanzil's current plans. Take this incense, and place it in front of the bat totem in the Ruins of Jubuwal, to the north. Hir'eek will guide you from there.

passages.title: Backdoor Dealings
passages.text: You have not done as I asked, <race>.  Perhaps I was wrong to have selected you for this task...

passages.title: Backdoor Dealings
passages.text:
It is as I suspected.  Zanzil is too haughty to interfere with the squabbles between the Bloodscalps and the Skullsplitters.  No, he is playing a part in a grander scheme... Jin'do the Hexxer is using him to help bring Hakkar back to Zul'Gurub.

It's good that we found this out now, because it offers us a simple solution.

passages.title: Eliminate the Outcast
passages.text:
You are to kill Zanzil. You rode on Hir'eek's wings and saw through Hir'eek's eyes; you know where Zanzil hides within the Ruins of Aboraz. Travel there and kill him.

Oh, and <race>: if we become separated, you should use this fetish. It only works within Stranglethorn, but it will transport you back here to me should you need to return swiftly.

Good luck, <race>. Zanzil is no ordinary opponent.

passages.title: Through the Troll Hole
passages.text:
It looks like Zanzil's portal into Zul'Gurub is still open. Zul'Gurub is a dangerous place, but Maywiki entrusted this task to you.

The portal lies in wait in front of you.

passages.title: High Priestess Jeklik
passages.text:
Ahead of you looms a ramp up to one of the city's many terraces. The bat-shaped totems ahead of you indicate that this is the domain of High Priestess Jeklik, a follower of Hir'eek.

Jeklik was one of the Hakkar-worshipping priests that Zanzil was planning to resurrect. Perhaps if you hurry, you can stop the resurrection!

passages.title: Plunging Into Zul'Gurub
passages.text: Zanzil the Outcast has once again escaped through one of his portals. Follow him!

passages.title: High Priest Venoxis
passages.text: Venoxis was the second of the two priests that Zanzil planned to bring back from the dead. You have already succeeded in destroying the body of High Priestess Jeklik... Venoxis must be the next.

passages.title: High Priest Venoxis
passages.text:
I ask you to slay Zanzil the Outcast, a lowly, hermetic exile of the Gurubashi, and what do you do?  You dash headfirst into the Gurubashi capital and eliminate one of their High Priests!  Very nearly two!  Only one word suffices to explain such a rash and foolhardy endeavor:

Heroism.

Jin'do the Hexxer still walks within Zul'Gurub's walls, but he lost one of his legs when you crushed Jeklik.  Today's battle is ours.

passages.title: Recipe for Disaster
passages.text:
Did you see that explosion I made? I must have flown 10 inches off the ground!

I've just got to get Zanzil's recipe so I can find out why it did that. One of Zanzil's flunkies at the Ruins of Aboraz must have it on him. Head east, to the coast of the Cape, and snatch it for me!

passages.title: Recipe for Disaster
passages.text:
Did he use shimmerweed?  I'm guessing he used shimmerweed.

No wait... amberseeds!  It's gotta be amberseeds.

passages.title: Recipe for Disaster
passages.text:
This is fascinating!  Just think of all the applications!

Thanks again, <name>.  Remember, if you ever need anything mixed for you... and I mean ANYTHING... you can always ask The Flask.

passages.title: Perfectly Pure
passages.text:
This humour won't serve on its own. Too thick. WAY too thick.

The nagas to our west maintain a shrine that dispenses the only clean water this side of Duskwood. For most potions, I'll use river water, but Bronwyn demands accuracy!

Obtain it from the Nek'mani Wellspring at the peak of the naga camp. Good luck!

passages.title: Perfectly Pure
passages.text: <Dask looks eagerly at your pack as you approach.>

passages.title: Perfectly Pure
passages.text:
Do you know how hard it is to get fresh water in Stranglethorn?  It's no wonder that the nagas guard their shrine so ferociously!

Alright, let's get this mix started!

passages.title: If They're Just Going to Leave Them Lying Around...
passages.text:
Father says that a responsible merchant is always keeping an eye out for good deals. I've been trying to look for deals everywhere I go, and I think I've just found one!

The naga to the west have dozens of statues that they place on the ground where they live. They couldn't possibly need all of them... so I was thinking that we'd take some for ourselves!

Free statues! That's a good deal, right?

passages.title: If They're Just Going to Leave Them Lying Around...
passages.text: Let's see 'em!

passages.title: If They're Just Going to Leave Them Lying Around...
passages.text:
These statues are beautiful...

Wow, I had no idea the naga were so talented.  Thanks, <name>!

passages.title: Airwyn Bantamflax
passages.text:
