passages.text: Shame that these half-formed things are too brittle and warped to be used for some weapons of our own. But it's thanks to you that we had the chance to get them out before they set. I'm not about to complain.

passages.title: Playing Dirty
passages.text:
Have you seen the huge lumbering ettins roaming the forests? Cursed things came from Gilneas. Now they wander the land searching for their next juicy meal. We've managed to subjugate and utilize some of them to haul our wagons, but the others... well, they must be killed!

Unfortunately, we can't spare any soldiers to do the job. That's where you come in, <class>!

I have a plan, but it's going to require some materials. Head out into the forests around this base and collect diseased beast organs.

passages.title: Playing Dirty
passages.text: We are Forsaken! This is how we do it, <class>.

passages.title: Playing Dirty
passages.text: Excellent! Now to prepare the "meal."

passages.title: The Battle Resumes!
passages.text:
Word is in from Andorhal, <name>. The battle has resumed.

It has become somewhat well-known among the Forsaken that you are a hero of the first battle of Andorhal. Koltira has requested your presence immediately.

passages.title: The Battle Resumes!
passages.text: Thassarian and the humans made their move.  I thought I had an agreement with Thassarian... but I suppose this will do.

passages.title: The Farmers' Militia
passages.text:
The battle started when they attacked us from the rear. I let my guard down, and a group of poorly-armed farmers and militiamen swung into our flank from the Writhing Haunt.

They may be weak, but unchecked, they threaten to overwhelm us with their numbers.

Lindsay's pet abominations can handle the melee combat. You take this collar, stay in the rear, and use it to release my ebon gargoyle upon these farmers.

passages.title: The Farmers' Militia
passages.text: Merely a dent in their numbers... but the sight of their fellow men falling from the skies surely weakened their resolve.

passages.title: Lindsay Ravensun, Revealed
passages.text:
I was informed that that worthless woman, Lindsay Ravensun, would be here to support me in this battle, but so far, she's done nothing but brood within the basement of the greathall behind me. All the better, I suppose. She was a bit of a distraction.

Still, I cannot and will not stand for insubordination. Find her, and bring her to me.

passages.title: Lindsay Ravensun, Revealed
passages.text:
You won't be taking me anywhere, <name>.

While Koltira prances about with his playmate, Thassarian, I plan to win this battle.  Then I'll make Koltira suffer for his weakness.

Don't believe me?  Fine, I'll let you in on a little secret...

passages.title: Ace in the Hole
passages.text:
You have no idea how difficult it was to stay disguised while I watched Koltira let this war slip away from us. Even now, those infernal farmers threaten to overwhelm us. All because he refused to slay a friend.

Take my val'kyr again, <name>. With her by your side, kill these farmers, convert them to Forsaken, and mobilize them. Then take a group of them into Alliance-held western Andorhal and hunt down this death knight, Thassarian.

We will win this war yet.

passages.title: Ace in the Hole
passages.text: This skeleton... what could it mean?

passages.title: Ace in the Hole
passages.text:
This is the body of Lurid, Thassarian's trusted knight.  With Thassarian nowhere to be found, it would seem that the Alliance forces have withdrawn.

The Forsaken have won the battle for Andorhal.

passages.title: Andorhal, Once and For All
passages.text: Sylvanas will want to know about Thassarian's departure from Andorhal. You resolve to return to the Forsaken-held side of town.

passages.title: Andorhal, Once and For All
passages.text:
See?  All it took was a little help from the val'kyr.  These creatures are turning to be much more helpful than I had first thought.

Now, on to other matters.

passages.title: Charge!
passages.text:
Good. You are off to a bright start. This road will be long, and as you become more accomplished, you will begin to discover that you can do things you could never have imagined before.

Go, get more experience, and learn a new technique. Once you have, demonstrate it on one of the training dummies.

passages.title: Charge!
passages.text: I think you've mastered the basics of the charge, <name>. Don't forget to return when you need more training.

passages.title: Cataclysm in the Catacombs
passages.text:
Don't worry about me, <class>. I've uncovered the Twilight's Hammer plot. They've been stealing and stockpiling explosives coming into Stormwind harbor. Somehow, they've gotten access to the catacombs underneath the Cathedral of Light. I've heard talk of someone called "The Black Bishop."

There's no time to warn the guard, <name>! You've got just minutes to get into the catacombs and disarm that bomb. Go! Now! Or THOUSANDS of PEOPLE will DIE!

passages.title: Cataclysm in the Catacombs
passages.text:
<3 ... 2 ... 1 ...>

<You wet your fingers and snuff out the fuse. The cathedral is saved!>

Underneath the powder kegs you find a heap of notes and papers. Apparently the cultists were trying to destroy the evidence behind them.>

passages.title: Lost in the Darkness
passages.text:
Some would say that we are lucky to be alive. Those people would be idiots. At least had we died we would not have had to face the Warchief's wrath. Alas, what's done is done! Now we must attempt to regain our lost honor.

The third ship in our fleet sank off the coast of the Skittering Dark, northwest of here. Those that made it to shore quickly found themselves swarmed by the giant spiders of the area and encased in webbing.

If there are survivors we must free them! Go, <name>! To the Skittering Dark!

passages.title: Lost in the Darkness
passages.text: Lok'tar, <name>! Once the ale wears off my orcs will be ready!

passages.title: Orcs are in Order
passages.text:
<Admiral Hatchet hands you an envelope sealed with the mark of the Horde.>

This is your commendation letter. It's the least I could do for you given the circumstances.

Return to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner with the letter and inform her of our status. Let her know that we will be ready to march on her command.

Goodbye, <name>. You are an excellent soldier.

Northeast, <lad/ma'am>. To Forsaken High Command!

passages.title: Orcs are in Order
passages.text: And the orcs?

passages.title: Orcs are in Order
passages.text:
<Sylvanas raises an eyebrow.>

So the orcs are in order?

<Sylvanas reads the commendation letter.>

Recovered their supplies? Killed a dozen worgen? Toppled an ettin? Freed their soldiers and destroyed the Skitterweb matriarch?

I say this rarely, <name>, but I am impressed. Perhaps your ability matches your aspirations. We shall see, for now you will be tested!

passages.title: Lordaeron
passages.text: Ride with me to the Sepulcher, <name>. There are many things I wish to discuss with you. It is imperative that you understand the history of Lordaeron and the plight of the Forsaken.

passages.title: Lordaeron
passages.text: Do you now understand the importance of our mission here? Crowley and his Alliance dogs must be stopped!

passages.title: Twilight Research
passages.text:
The book you found appears to detail some form of research carried out by a member of the Twilight's Hammer.

It deals with the oozes in some way, but there are multiple pages missing.

Perhaps if you found additional notes you might be able to make sense of it.

passages.title: Twilight Research
passages.text: <You scroll through the notes, trying to put them in order.>

passages.title: Twilight Research
passages.text:
The notes deal with High Cultist Maziel's research on the elemental properties of quicksilver.

His obsession with the subject borders on the insane.

passages.title: Alzzin the Wildshaper
passages.text:
The monster responsible for the ruin you see before you is called Alzzin the Wildshaper. To reach him, however, you will need to also slay Zevrim Thornhoof, the satyr who currently holds the still noble ancient Old Ironbark in his grasp.

Once Ironbark is free, he will help you make an entrance into Alzzin's domain. Enter and slay him without mercy, for there is no other way.

passages.title: Alzzin the Wildshaper
passages.text: Time is running short, <race>. I trust you will not fail.

passages.title: Alzzin the Wildshaper
passages.text: Ah, very well done indeed. You've made an old spirit very happy this day. You deserve proper thanks for the risks you've taken.

passages.title: The Madness Within
passages.text: This madness must come to an end. The age of the immortals has long since passed. Destroy the guardians surrounding the five pylons to lower the force field. When this is done, destroy Immol'thar. With the Prince's power greatly reduced from the demon's demise, attack and end him as well. Lay the spirits of this city to rest, adventurer, and make the Prince pay for his wrongdoings.

passages.title: The Madness Within
passages.text: Be wary, adventurer. The Prince is... persuasive.

passages.title: The Madness Within
passages.text: We thank you, hero.

passages.title: The Treasure of the Shen'dralar
passages.text: In the library, Athenaeum, you will find an ancient chest hidden beneath the stairway. Take from it that which you desire.

passages.title: The Treasure of the Shen'dralar
passages.text: You open the chest to find...

passages.title: The Winds of Loch Modan
passages.text:
Father finished the Skystrider. It's amazing! Once we get the bugs worked out, I'm going to use it to fight for justice, just like you.

I know you've got to move on, and help other people, being a hero and all, but how about a ride? I'm about to take the Skystrider on its first flight, and I'll be honored if you join me. I'll drop you off at Algaz Station.

What do you say?

passages.title: The Winds of Loch Modan
passages.text:
What in blazes WAS that? A flying mechanostrider?

You know what, I don't want to know. I'm just going to pretend that didn't happen, and we'll be all nice and businesslike.

passages.title: Deepholm, Realm of Earth
passages.text:
I knew you'd heed our call, <name>. When Deathwing was first defeated by the other dragon aspects, he retreated to Deepholm, the realm of earth.

Deathwing's return to our world left a rift open between Azeroth and Deepholm.

If we don't mend the breach, this land will be torn asunder.

We're doing our best to contain the damage on this side of the rift. Aggra will take you through the rift so you can help repair the damage from the other side.

Get on her wyvern when you're ready.

passages.title: Deepholm, Realm of Earth
passages.text:
You've arrived just in time, <name>.  All our resources are tied up keeping the rift stable.

We need someone like you to help us recover the fragments of the World Pillar.

passages.title: Unfinished Gordok Business
passages.text:
Now you da king, so maybe you get prized Gordok artifact back from Guard Mol'dar! Da king before you never listened, just like all da other kings since da old timey Gordok king!

Artifact is called da Gauntlet of Gordok Might. Old timey stories say only da one true king da Gordok can get it back. You find it and it will become mighty gauntlet you wear forever! Yar, I show you!

passages.title: Unfinished Gordok Business
passages.text:
Wow... you ARE da true king! Old king never even ask about da gauntlet!

Look - this mark on da gauntlet an old old OLD timey magic mark, older than da Gordok they say.  Well, I learn one thing as little ogre - how to make mark come to life and give power back to gauntlet!

I do it for you, king!  Here, take da gauntlet and rule FOREVER!

passages.title: King of the Gordok
passages.text:
In Gordok society, their king is simply their strongest warrior. If anyone, ogre or otherwise, kills the current king, they are automatically hailed as the new one.

The new king receives tribute from any living guards, Stomper Kreeg, and Captain Kromcrush. Find and kill King Gordok while killing as few of their other leaders as possible, and not only will your reward be great, you will be able to use your power as king to halt the Gordok invasion without conflict!

passages.title: King of the Gordok
passages.text: I have faith that you will be able to complete the task set out before you.

passages.title: King of the Gordok
passages.text: Yes! I can see that you were indeed successful. You have received your tribute, the Gordok advance will exist no longer, and the Gordok are blissfully ignorant! This is a true winner's scenario, <name>.

passages.title: King of the Gordok
passages.text:
You kill Gordok leader, you new ogre king. If you king, then ogre leaders like Kromcrush and Kreeg that survive pay you big tribute and you stop Gordok invasion. If you do that, then me very happy ogre and we take Dire Maul FOR DA HORDE!!!

Go, little <race>! Kill ugly Gordok ogre king and maybe dis be new Stonemaul Hold! Yar!

passages.title: King of the Gordok
passages.text: You new Gordok king?

passages.title: King of the Gordok
passages.text: Little <race> did it! Now Horde more powerful than ever! YAR!

passages.title: Elemental Energy
passages.text:
It's taking every ounce of our power to keep this realm stable in the absence of the World Pillar.

As shaman we can tap directly into the energies of the elementals that inhabit Deepholm and use them to heal the damage that the rift is causing.

Take this totem and place it on the ground outside. Any energized geodes or lodestone elementals destroyed in its proximity will fill it with the energy we require.

passages.title: Elemental Energy
passages.text: Thank you, <name>.  We need all the power we can muster to keep Deepholm stable.

passages.title: Hobart Needs You
passages.text: Heya, boss, Hobart Grapplehammer's wants to speak with you. He says it's a matter of some urgency.

passages.title: Hobart Needs You
passages.text: There you are, my boy. I have something very important for you to do!

passages.title: Barov Family Fortune
passages.text:
Within Scholomance lays the Barov family fortune. Alexi and I are the last two Barovs in existence.

However, I am the only living Barov, so our family's vast empire belongs to me! Find me the deeds to Caer Darrow, Brill, Tarren Mill, and Southshore and I will repay you generously. The Barov estate will be reborn at long last!

passages.title: Barov Family Fortune
passages.text: Bow your head in my presence, <race>. I am a noble, after all, and you are a copperless peasant.

passages.title: Barov Family Fortune
passages.text: Excellent work, <race>. Alexi deserves nothing for his foolishness.

passages.title: The Reckoning
passages.text:
Your performance was admirable, soldier. You make the Forsaken proud, which is more than I can say for our general, Koltira Deathweaver.

I intend to have a word with that death knight. He has shamed himself and his cause.

passages.title: The Reckoning
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: The Reckoning
passages.text:
I have nothing against the Knights of the Ebon Blade, but Koltira needs to be reminded who he works for now.  His loyalty must lie with the Horde.

Or, more specifically, the Forsaken.

I wouldn't plan on seeing Koltira anytime soon.  Now that I have him... you can rest assured that any bonds he may have had with that Alliance scum will be thoroughly broken.

passages.title: Doctor Theolen Krastinov, the Butcher
passages.text:
Doctor Theolen Krastinov is responsible for the deaths of thousands. His nickname, The Butcher, is well earned for the atrocities he takes joy in executing. He must be punished, justice must be meted out.

Find him and exact upon him the agony he has inflicted upon countless innocents, including me and my husband. Once he is destroyed, burn our remains. Turn them to ashes, <name>. Release our grieving souls.

passages.title: Doctor Theolen Krastinov, the Butcher
passages.text: I can feel my spirit healing, <name>. You have done my husband and I a great service.

passages.title: School's Out Forever
passages.text:
Darkmaster Gandling serves as headmaster of Scholomance, and is therefore responsible for countless deaths at the hands of his students. For that he must be punished.

He will not come out easily. Lure him out by slaying his six professors whose rooms connect to the Headmaster's Study. Be wary, for when the last falls he will come, and he will come infuriated with vast magic backing his assault. Don't let him make it out of here alive.

passages.title: School's Out Forever
passages.text: Without a headmaster, the school will descend into chaos. It will not put forth any more of its vile 'students' into the field. Thank you.

passages.title: Unusual Behavior... Even For Gnolls
passages.text:
Allow me to concentrate for a moment.

<You feel Daria's mind vision travel elsewhere, then it returns to you.>

Further down the trail, south of Taelan's Tower, the gnolls have carved out a small meeting area to the east of the main road. Something is happening there... I'm not certain what. We should investigate. I will look for anything out of the ordinary... you just protect yourself.

passages.title: Unusual Behavior... Even For Gnolls
passages.text:
Gnolls and necromancy... what a surprise!  And I thought that, here in the Western Plaguelands, we had put these dark days behind us.

<You sense Daria's eyes focusing on something on the ground.>

Wait... what is THAT?

passages.title: The Good People of Hearthglen
passages.text:
See those reagents over there? And these supplies right here? Those belong to the Argent Crusade.

Gnolls are known for thievery, but as far as I know, Hearthglen hasn't had any incursions since the Redpine came. Very suspicious.

I know a few helpful folks within Hearthglen: Morris Vant, Outfitter Mendelev, Bree Ironstock, and High Cleric Alphus. All can be trusted, and are well-connected. Question them, to find out if they know anything about these lost supplies.

passages.title: The Good People of Hearthglen
passages.text:
Did you notice, <name>?  Many names were mentioned, but one name was mentioned far more than the others.

Bisp.

passages.title: Bagging Bisp
passages.text:
Magus Bisp is one of Hearthglen's most preeminent arcanists. To imagine that he would be interacting with gnolls... and dabbling in necromancy? Unthinkable.

You'll find him atop the tower near Hearthglen's main gate. Hopefully he'll have an explanation for all of this. If not, well... I wouldn't go to the top of that tower unprepared, <name>.

passages.title: Bagging Bisp
passages.text: I suppose that we can take his aggression as an admission of guilt.  You alright, <name>?

passages.title: Turning Yourself In
passages.text:
So... you killed a member of the Argent Crusade, inside of Hearthglen. Usually that's not smiled upon, even in self-defense.

I recommend you come back to Mardenholde Keep, and turn yourself in to Highlord Fordring. Hopefully he will hear you out, and will be sympathetic with your situation. I hope I haven't gotten you in any trouble.

passages.title: Turning Yourself In
passages.text:
I'm already aware of your actions, <name>.  I welcome you into my town, give you my blessing, and what do you do?

You slay the traitor that we've been hunting down for weeks.  Well done.  Your heroism is budding much earlier than even I had anticipated.

passages.title: The Endless Flow
passages.text:
Araj the Summoner is bolstering the Scourge defenses with simple skeletons... an army of weaklings that will overwhelm you before it overpowers you. He has assembled animi within Andorhal's northern towers that spew these skeletons out at an alarming rate. But I've got the solution!

<Lang passes you a handful of grenades.>

Their function is simple. Throwing these grenades at a bone animus... or, for that matter, a mob of skeletons... will reduce them to splinters.

passages.title: The Endless Flow
passages.text: I know what those devices sound like when they've blown up... and I haven't heard that sound yet.  Get back out there, <name>.

passages.title: The Endless Flow
passages.text: These grenades are all explosives, nothing more.  I may not be a goblin engineer... but I still understand the value of being able to just explode things every once in a while.

passages.title: Araj the Summoner
passages.text:
With the animus destroyed, the next logical step is to take out Araj himself, and to take a shard of his phylactery. You've probably already seen him, lurking at the fountain in the center of town.

Take my grenades with you. They won't do anything to Araj, but if he decides to summon any of those skeletons, you can use them to blow them away. Again.

passages.title: Araj the Summoner
passages.text: Araj is a formidable opponent.  Be prepared.

passages.title: Araj the Summoner
passages.text: Araj dead... this is good.  That gnome has done his part in winning this war.  As have you, <name>.

passages.title: Victory, For Now
passages.text:
The Alliance are victorious, and our forces are still strong. Military strategy dictates that we attack the Forsaken now, while they are recovering and unaware. I made a deal, however...

We will wait. We attack Koltira and his troops when the time is right. In the meantime, speak with Ginny Goodwin and take a flight to the Chillwind Camp, to our south. Commander Ashlam Valorfist will give you your next assignment.

You will hear from me when you are needed again in Andorhal.

passages.title: Victory, For Now
passages.text: Word arrived shortly before you did, <name>.  With the Scourge ejected from Andorhal, we are one step closer to retaking Lordaeron.

passages.title: A Mighty Hunger
passages.text:
I hail from Westfall, far to the south... as do these men that travel with me. We are farmers, and nothing more.

I had been told that Lordaeron had been healed, and that it was ready for tilling. However, this "Commander" now tells me that it's too dangerous to proceed. He says that there's a war going on, and that the plaguelands still aren't healed.

Before anything else, I need to get some food in my men's stomachs. Anything will do. Bear seems to be plentiful.

passages.title: A Mighty Hunger
passages.text: We've traveled a long way.  Anything you can spare would be appreciated.

passages.title: A Mighty Hunger
passages.text: You hunt like a true <class>.  Even if we can't set up our homesteads... at least we can still eat.

passages.title: Those That Couldn't Let Go
passages.text:
Sorrow Hill, up the road to the northeast, was one of the first places that the Argent Crusaders and Cenarion Circle were able to heal. The area is now freed of the Scourge.

However, there are still many specters of the past that, for some reason, have not passed on into the next world. They may be mourning, they may have unfinished business... or they may just be lost.

Take my thurible and use it to douse them with holy incense. One way or another, we will help them move onto the next plane.

passages.title: Those That Couldn't Let Go
passages.text: Hopefully most of them passed on peacefully.  I thank you, <name>.

passages.title: The Writhing Haunt
passages.text:
The farmers traveled to the Writhing Haunt, an old farm to the northeast, across the river. Someone needs to keep an eye on them.

Bring them those rusty weapons and armor you found. We can't have them fighting with pitchforks.

passages.title: The Writhing Haunt
passages.text: Did Valorfist send you?  He doesn't know when to let up, does he?

passages.title: The Writhing Haunt
passages.text:
Well, now that you're here, we'll gladly take that armor off your hands.

You can keep the weapons, though.  These men wouldn't know which end to hold.

passages.title: Combat Training
passages.text:
In fact, you might still be able to help train some of my men. You probably noticed the abomination outside. We initially tried to fight him, but he didn't fight back. He seems to want to help out on the farm.

Take a group of four settlers and challenge this abomination to combat. He seems to be pretty tough, but with one of him and five of you, I think you'll have a chance at beating him.

passages.title: Combat Training
passages.text: If we're going to help out in this battle for Andorhal, we need to learn how to fight.

passages.title: Combat Training
passages.text:
We can handle things from here.  I thank you for your help, <name>.

I assume that when we next meet, it will be in battle.  Take care of yourself until then.  We'll need all the help we can get.

passages.title: The Menders' Stead
passages.text:
These men and women here at Chillwind Camp have noble goals, but their ultimate purpose is war. I would like to offer you an opportunity to pursue more peaceful goals.

At the Menders' Stead, beyond war-torn Andorhal to the north, the Argent Crusade has joined forces with the Cenarion Circle. Together, we work on healing this land from the plague that used to reign here.

Are you interested in joining our cause, <class>?

passages.title: The Menders' Stead
passages.text: Welcome, <class>.  As you can see, our camp is a joint expedition between Argent Crusade members and Cenarion Circle druids, but we welcome all who wish to help heal the land.

passages.title: A Strange Disc
passages.text:
The etching around the surface of this object indicates that it is of ancient origins, and yet no signs of wear can be detected.

A hole on its edge, full of splintered wood, indicates that it is meant to be put atop a wooden staff of some sort.

Before showing this to Doctor Jones, you should find the other piece.

passages.title: A Strange Disc
passages.text: Yes, <name>?

passages.title: A Strange Disc
passages.text:
<Doctor Jones puts on his spectacles.>

Let's have a look at this. Shall we?

passages.title: Salvage Operation
passages.text:
Between the Horde and the naga, our fleet has been decimated. We can't do anything to bring back the men who gave their lives to the sea, but sink me if I allow all of our supplies to be lost forever.

Swim out to the Obsidian Breakers southwest of Highbank and retrieve our supplies from the wrecks and the ocean floor.

passages.title: Salvage Operation
passages.text: How much were you able to recover?

passages.title: Salvage Operation
passages.text:
Look at all this! You were able to recover more than I thought. We can outfit a whole squad of marines with this stuff.

We have the gear. If we only had some way to bolster our numbers here in the Highlands...

passages.title: Honor the Dead
passages.text:
A convoy of veteran troopers and Forsaken catapults were ambushed earlier today while attempting to cross Olsen's Farthing, directly south of here. It was a total loss: all troopers were killed and all catapults destroyed.

Bloodfang's pack was responsible for the ambush, though likely they have all fled back into the hills, preparing their next cowardly strike. Their day will come, but for now I want you to go to Olsen's Farthing and honor our fallen.

Recover their Forsaken insignias.

passages.title: Honor the Dead
passages.text: Have you recovered the insignias?

passages.title: Honor the Dead
passages.text: I will see to it that these insignias are returned to the Undercity at once. The registrar will place their names in our records so that their sacrifice may never be forgotten.

passages.title: Marsh Frog Legs
passages.text:
I like cooking. Good swamp cooking. Fried green frog legs and the like.

And I'm all out of legs. The manor is overrun with frogs, though. Giant marsh frogs. Think you could bring me some of those legs? Nothin' to it, really. Just bop 'em on the head and bring me the legs.

Then I'll make a stew and stew it up and suck it down and give you some too.

Do you like stew?

passages.title: Marsh Frog Legs
passages.text: Spice.  We could all use some spice in our life.  You agree?

passages.title: Marsh Frog Legs
passages.text: Ah, that's the spice!  Now here's some swampy good stew.

passages.title: Jarl Needs a Blade
passages.text:
I have cutting to do. I can't tell you what I'm going to cut, but... I need myself a blade. A certain blade...

Some people call it a sword. I call it a swing blade.

You help me? Those fish-men, you know, murlocs or whatever they're called.... There's one they call Razorspine, carries a big sword, lives north of here near the beach. That's the sword I need!

But don't sleep on this. What I'm cutting won't keep forever...

passages.title: Jarl Needs a Blade
passages.text: You have my blade??

passages.title: Jarl Needs a Blade
passages.text:
That's a good blade.  It has a good swing.  It's a good swing blade.  Thank you.  Thank you, thank you, thank you!!!  Now I want to try it....  

Later.  I'll try it later.  But like I was saying... thanks.

passages.title: Cleansing Witch Hill
passages.text:
The torch is ready. Plant it at the end of the dock and be prepared to face whatever comes forth.

I have no idea what the torch's smoke may reveal... if anything emerges at all. I must say, I have my doubts about this kind of folk magic, but we haven't time for anything else. For your sake and Jarl's, I wish you luck.

passages.title: Cleansing Witch Hill
passages.text: Is it over?

passages.title: Cleansing Witch Hill
passages.text:
It worked?

<Mordant clears his throat.>

I mean... it worked! Jarl and I are in your debt, <name>. Now the only remaining problem is my friend's taste in furniture, and I'm afraid that won't be solved as easily.

passages.title: Hungry as an Ogre!
passages.text:
You meet some people out here sometime. Nice people. Met an ogre once. Ogres get hungry just like me.

I'll never forget what he said. He said "Mud big ogre. Me hungry. Go bash fishy. Bring Mud food. You feed Mud or Mud eat you."

So I got him those fish and he ate 'em up. That's when I started too. The heads are the best part, all soggy-like.

Don't crush those heads now. It makes them sad. Sad heads aren't good eating. Get me happy heads and I'll eat them and be happy too.

passages.title: Hungry as an Ogre!
passages.text: Jarl's hungry. Just like that ogre.

passages.title: Hungry as an Ogre!
passages.text:
Wonder what it's like to be an ogre. Big people have to eat more.

Ogres must be even hungrier than me. That doesn't sound very fun.

passages.title: Cornered and Crushed!
passages.text:
<The Banshee Queen speaks through your mind.>

We must act quickly, <name>. They mustn't be given the chance to flee. I am dispatching a squadron of my most powerful troopers to the Deep Elem Mine. I'm also sending the Horseman with them to ensure that nothing goes wrong. Meet him at the Deep Elem Mine, east of Olsen's Farthing, and CRUSH those rats.

passages.title: Cornered and Crushed!
passages.text: I 'spose we're to corner them first then crush, eh?

passages.title: Alas, Andorhal
passages.text:
Head south, to Chillwind Camp. Tell Commander Ashlam Valorfist everything that happened here.

Me? I'm going west, into Tirisfal.

My battle's not over yet. I've got an appointment with that harpy that calls herself a Banshee Queen... and I'm finding out what she did to Koltira.

passages.title: Alas, Andorhal
passages.text:
Lost?  No... next, they'll be coming for Chillwind, I suppose.  This was a major strategic blow to the Alliance's plans for Lordaeron.

Very well.  I will report the results of this battle to King Wrynn.  I don't expect him to be happy.

passages.title: The Dreadlord Balnazzar
passages.text:
With the fall of the Scarlet Crusade, their disguised demon leader, Balnazzar, released the possessed body of Grand Crusader Dathrohan and went on a rampage, killing every remaining crusader here. He then used his necromantic power to raise them all as vile undead slaves.

Balnazzar refers to his new army as the Risen. We cannot let him grow this army - they are extremely powerful and, unlike Arthas' Scourge, Balnazzar will not hold his forces back. Kill him while we still have a chance, <class>.

passages.title: The Dreadlord Balnazzar
passages.text: The Light commands you.

passages.title: The Dreadlord Balnazzar
passages.text: It's good we stopped Balnazzar now. Before long, his army would have overtaken all of Stratholme, giving him a powerful center for his new unholy empire.

passages.title: Propaganda War
passages.text:
The deserter agents were doing far more than just chatting up the guards. We've found a number of leaflets the deserters somehow managed to smuggle in on a ship in the docks.

The ship used to transport the leaflets is still in Theramore, at the farthest dock. If you can sneak aboard and capture the rest of their propaganda documents, their agents will lose their most powerful tool. Be careful! The ship is manned by seasoned privateers and the cargo is probably being kept in the captain's quarters.

passages.title: Propaganda War
passages.text: Did you manage to find and capture the remaining propaganda leaflets?

passages.title: Propaganda War
passages.text:
<The SI:7 agent nods in approval.>

Excellent. All that remains is to discredit the deserters so that they'll never gain a foothold in Theramore again, and I have just the plan to do it.

passages.title: Thresher Oil
passages.text:
The old log in the lighthouse indicates that the lamp was fueled with oil from the threshers that live along the coast here.

<Babs wrinkles her nose at the mention of such outdated technology.>

I suppose it's a practical, if inelegant solution. The log says that the oil taken from the youngest murk threshers works the best, and those live right underneath the docks of Theramore.

If you're up for it, would you help resupply the lighthouse with fuel?

passages.title: Thresher Oil
passages.text: Were you able to get any of that thresher oil?

passages.title: Thresher Oil
passages.text: Well, I have my doubts, but this is the only solution available right now. Once we have it up and running, I'm sure there will be time to look at other ways to fuel the lamp.

passages.title: Dastardly Denizens of the Deep
passages.text:
You know, it's amazing what you can find in that old lighthouse. After I lit the lamp, I noticed this book in one of the old trunks up there.

<Babs holds up the book and reads the title dramatically.>

"Dastardly Denizens of the Deep!"

Why, I think I might swoon if I ever saw one of these! I'm sure it's good for a laugh or two, but I simply don't have time for reading right now.

You know who might enjoy it, though... that fishmonger on the docks, "Dirty" Michael Crowe. He collects old books.

passages.title: Dastardly Denizens of the Deep
passages.text: What'll it be today? The snook is quite good.

passages.title: Dastardly Denizens of the Deep
passages.text: Well, now, that was thoughtful o' Babs to send that over. I don't know if you've leafed through it or not, but there's a lot of truth to the tales in that book. Sailors didn't just make it all up, you know.

passages.title: Nat's Bargain
passages.text:
So you found a copy of Dastardly Denizens of the Deep, did you? Well, I can tell you from experience, it's all true. I've even seen a few of 'em with my own eyes.

But you want to know about Tethyr. I said I'd make you a deal, so here's what I want you to do. I'm working on a new line of baits, but I haven't tested this one yet.

Just take this paste -- yeah, it smells a little foul -- smear it on yourself, and swim into the deep part of Tidefury Cove to the southwest. Let me know how it works!

passages.title: Nat's Bargain
passages.text: Remember, the deal is "don't come back until something bites you."

passages.title: Nat's Bargain
passages.text:
Not bad at all, but you know, I think I'd get a bath in as soon as possible, if I was you.

Now, about your sea monster...

Help yourself to a brew or two in the meantime.

passages.title: The Waters Run Red...
passages.text:
<The communication console hums.>

Those worgen you killed were the scouting party. There are hundreds more incoming! Looks like Crowley and Bloodfang made the blood offering to every human in Lordaeron.

Get in one of those Horde cannons and send them all back to their makers. Let the waters of Lordamere Lake run red with their blood!

passages.title: The Waters Run Red...
passages.text: Though you killed a large number of the newly turned worgen, many more are sure to appear. Still, their assault will have softened. Well done, <name>!

passages.title: The Menders' Stead
passages.text: I can handle training from here. If you're looking for something else to do, I recommend heading up the road to the northwest. The Cenarion druids and Argent Crusade have a small camp set up there, at Dalson's old farm. Maybe they can keep you busy until we need your help again.

passages.title: The Menders' Stead
passages.text: Welcome, <class>.  As you can see, our camp is a joint expedition between Argent Crusade members and Cenarion Circle druids, but we welcome all who wish to help heal the land.

passages.title: Survey Alcaz Island
passages.text:
It looks like Renn's hunch about Alcaz Island was right. We need to survey that island, but it would take a whole brigade of troops to fight our way in there.

Theramore's defenses can't weather such a hit, so I've arranged with Cassa Crimsonwing, the apprentice to Theramore's gryphon master, to allow you to use one of her beasts to survey Alcaz from the air.

Alcaz Island holds the key to the mystery of the Defias' involvement in this kidnapping.

passages.title: Survey Alcaz Island
passages.text:
<Lady Jaina listens intently as you report the results of your aerial survey.>

A rune circle, dragonkin? The Defias have allied themselves with HER? The traitor?

<Lady Jaina composes herself and prepares to explain.>

passages.title: Unleash the Raptors
passages.text:
Now that we've got our raptors, our next move is to "encourage" them to attack the Grimtotems at Blackhoof Village to the northwest.

I've got a leftover haunch of... well, it doesn't really matter what it is. It'll be your bait. Set it down on the ground in Blackhoof Village near the windmill in the center of the settlement. The raptors should take care of the rest, if their training took.

passages.title: Unleash the Raptors
passages.text:
<The sergeant doesn't bother to hide his grin.>

Good. That ought to forestall a raid or two.

passages.title: The Lost Report
passages.text:
Sifting through the loose dirt, the severed hand of an orc is found. And clutched in the hand is a bone-carved tube. And in the tube is a dirt-stained parchment.

The parchment is a report made by an orc who spent weeks spying on the city of Theramore.

After scanning the parchment, it is clear that it must be brought to the orc spymaster in Brackenwall Village.

passages.title: The Lost Report
passages.text: You have something for me?

passages.title: The Lost Report
passages.text:
Good work, <name>.  Our agent, Marg Nighteye, was stationed outside Theramore.  He was charged to spy on the city.  

This is his latest report, and it may be his last -- from your testimony, I fear that Marg met his end in the swamp...

passages.title: Prisoners of the Grimtotems
passages.text:
We're doing all we can to keep the Grimtotem raiders at bay, but they keep launching assaults on the tower. Even worse, they've managed to discover and capture the patrols the captain sends out to gather information and safeguard the road.

I suspect the captives are being held in Blackhoof Village, to the northwest. Knowing the Grimtotems, the defenders of the village probably carry the keys to the prisoners' cages with them. I don't care what you have to do, <class>, just bring back my men alive.

passages.title: Prisoners of the Grimtotems
passages.text:
The freed captives have already begun returning from Blackhoof Village. The information the captain is receiving from the prisoners will give us an advantage in our next battle against the Grimtotems.

You have my thanks and that of the men.

passages.title: Suspicious Hoofprints
passages.text: Rows of hoofprints lead away from the still-smoking skeleton of the Shady Rest Inn. There are at least a few visible impressions, with more rows of prints almost imperceptible in the soft mud of the marsh.

passages.title: Suspicious Hoofprints
passages.text:
Hoofprints... It could have been the quilboar, I suppose. Or maybe even the centaur. Their presence in the Barrens is not insignificant, and I would not think it a stretch to commit such an act.

Did I tell you? It wasn't just that the inn was burned down... The owner's woman and pup were killed. Bad business, that.

Nonetheless, I will send Kagoro to find where the tracks lead.

passages.title: Suspicious Hoofprints
passages.text: Rows of hoofprints lead away from the still-smoking skeleton of the Shady Rest Inn. There are at least a few visible impressions, with more rows of prints almost imperceptible in the soft mud of the marsh.

passages.title: Suspicious Hoofprints
passages.text:
Hoofprints, eh? It is true that there is an extraordinary amount of centaur activity in the lands near the Dustwallow Marsh. In brief excursions into the Barrens, we found their camps and holdings dotting the area.

I'll send out Falgran Hastil, one of our trackers, to see if he can find where the tracks lead.

passages.title: Together Again
passages.text:
We saw to it that the sentinel was healed and re-equipped. I already sent her back into the field.

Head back up and go to Darkcloud Pinnacle. She'll meet you there.

passages.title: Together Again
passages.text: Good to see you again, <name>. Let us put the fear of the Goddess into the Grimtotem.

passages.title: Together Again
passages.text:
We saw to it that the brave was healed and re-equipped. I already sent him back into the field.

Head back up and go to Darkcloud Pinnacle. He'll meet you there.

passages.title: Together Again
passages.text: I am honored by your presence, <name>. Let us put the fear of the Earth Mother into the Grimtotem.

passages.title: The Deserters
passages.text:
It has been a struggle maintaining a presence in the marsh, but through strength of our resolve, we have been able to maintain several defensive watchtowers throughout the area.

The latest information and scouting reports I have received indicate that a group of deserters has squatted in our abandoned tower at Lost Point, southeast of the inn.

The local lieutenant seems to be Balos Jacken. See if you can get some information out of him.

Be warned, <name>. He may be a tough nut to crack.

passages.title: The Deserters
passages.text: Did Vimes send you? Couldn't do his dirty work himself, could he...

passages.title: To Forsaken Forward Command
passages.text:
The time has come to destroy Crowley, Bloodfang and every dog at their command. To do this, though, will require cunning and planning the likes of which they would never dare dream!

As one of my most trusted soldiers, <name>, I need you to go to Forsaken Forward Command, located in Gilneas, and report to Deathstalker Commander Belmont. I have sent Belmont ahead with my plans. He awaits your arrival.

Arthura will escort you to Forward Command. Tell me when you are ready and I will send you on your way.

passages.title: To Forsaken Forward Command
passages.text:
Well if it isn't Seamannub!

I hope you're ready for battle, because that's all you'll find in this hellhole. We're at the heart of contested territory and these worgen mongrels won't give an inch!

passages.title: Peace at Last
passages.text:
I wish we had a way of letting James Hyal's wife and son know that we have brought their murderers to justice.

<Captain Vimes produces a small wreath decorated with flowers.>

There are some who say that their spirits will know, even if we cannot reach them. It's not much, but I'd like you to lay this wreath at the Hyal family monument. It's one of the stones in the graveyard just north of Theramore's gates.

passages.title: Peace at Last
passages.text:
<Captain Vimes smiles slightly as you relate the events you witnessed at the Hyal family grave.>

It's good to know that they understand. You didn't tell them about James, did you?

I'll deliver his wife's message to him, but I doubt he'll understand.

passages.title: Return to Krog
passages.text:
I hope I've been helpful to you and I'm sorry I can't offer more information. My apprentices and I produce such a large volume of arms and armor that it's almost impossible to recall details about any individual piece.

Not only do we outfit the braves defending tauren lands, but the Grimtotems have a particular fondness for my work. A seasoned warrior knows good work when he sees it.

passages.title: Return to Krog
passages.text: He actually said that the Grimtotems are his biggest customers? Mosarn gave us more help than he knows. With this much pointing toward the Grimtotems, I think we just found our first suspects.

passages.title: The Grimtotem Plot
passages.text:
With the activities of the Grimtotems in Thousand Needles brought to light, many tauren now regard them with suspicion. We've seen high-ranking Grimtotems engage in murder and kidnapping to advance their interests and I fear we may become their next target.

Blackhoof Village, to the northeast, near Bluefen, is a large new Grimtotem settlement. Their leaders, the elders, will all have orders from Thunder Bluff. See if you can capture the orders and piece them together to learn the Grimtotems' plans.

passages.title: The Grimtotem Plot
passages.text: Were you able to find any trace of the orders?

passages.title: The Grimtotem Plot
passages.text:
<Krog reads over the battle plan.>

There's no doubt in my mind that the Grimtotems are moving against the humans. What I don't understand is what their intentions are toward us. We knew nothing of these plans and we lost a good man because of it. I don't trust that we're not next on their list.

passages.title: More than Coincidence
passages.text:
We've gleaned as much as we can from the ruins of the inn. I'm concerned about where the investigation will lead us from here, but we must know the truth.

Between the hoofprints and the shield with Mosarn's mark, I'm led to believe that the Grimtotems may have been involved. They've recently established a settlement in the swamp, Blackhoof Village to the northeast. Travel to Blackhoof Village and search for more arms of Mosarn's manufacture.

passages.title: More than Coincidence
passages.text: What did your search of Blackhoof Village reveal?

passages.title: More than Coincidence
passages.text:
<Krog inspects the weapons and armor you've brought from Blackhoof Village.>

This is unmistakably the work of Mosarn. Questioning him further may draw too much attention, but we have a bit more freedom in dealing with the Grimtotems.

passages.title: Raze Direhorn Post!
passages.text:
There's no scrying necessary to see the trouble my new "neighbors" are creating. And if this is the band that burnt down the Shady Rest Inn, as you claim, there's no reason to tolerate their presence any longer.

Take this torch and raze their camp to the ground! You'll find Direhorn just to the north of my farm, near the road. You can't miss it, really, as the Grimtotems have done a splendid job of announcing their presence with those totems they favor.

passages.title: Raze Direhorn Post!
passages.text: Have you put that torch to good use?

passages.title: Raze Direhorn Post!
passages.text:
The Grimtotems should have no trouble understanding our latest message.

As for you, your contact at Brackenwall Village will want to know of your success. If I know him, he'll appreciate the taste of vengeance.

passages.title: The Grimtotem Plot
passages.text:
With the activities of the Grimtotems in Thousand Needles brought to light, many tauren now regard them with suspicion. We've seen high-ranking Grimtotems engage in murder and kidnapping to advance their interests and I fear we may become their next target.

Blackhoof Village, to the northeast, near Bluefen, is a large new Grimtotem settlement. Their leaders, the elders, will all have orders from Thunder Bluff. See if you can capture the orders and piece them together to learn the Grimtotems' plans.

passages.title: The Rattle of Bones
passages.text:
A tauren rattle lays here, exuding supernatural power. Its keepers slain, the artifact is undefended.

Perhaps the sentinel will have some insight into its significance?

passages.title: The Rattle of Bones
passages.text: That's the fabled Rattle of Bones, <name>!

passages.title: The Rattle of Bones
passages.text:
It's true then! What is it doing here, though? And if it's here, that must mean that the writ and the drums are also nearby!

Maybe there's some link between it and the wind serpent that just appeared? I think that I've an idea what that creature is as well.

passages.title: The Rattle of Bones
passages.text:
A tauren rattle lays here, exuding supernatural power. Its keepers slain, the artifact is undefended.

Surely the brave will have some insight into its significance?

passages.title: The Rattle of Bones
passages.text: The fabled Rattle of Bones, <name>!

passages.title: The Rattle of Bones
passages.text:
It is true then! What is it doing here, though? And if it is here, that must mean that the writ and the drums are also nearby!

Perhaps there is some link between it and the wind serpent that just appeared? I think that I have an idea what that creature is as well.

passages.title: Korok the Colossus
passages.text:
The monstrosity has fallen, granting a brief reprieve to the Forsaken soldiers on the front lines.

Take Korok's second head and return it to Forward Commander Onslaught at Forsaken Forward Command.

passages.title: Korok the Colossus
passages.text: Korok is dead?

passages.title: Korok the Colossus
passages.text: That towering behemoth has killed hundreds of Forsaken soldiers. You've done a great thing, <name>.

passages.title: The Grimtotem Weapon
passages.text:
During the last Grimtotem attack, I was wounded, but not before I managed to capture a curious totem our enemies were using against us.

It seemed to be emitting raw bolts of energy during the battle, but in all my experiments, I haven't managed to figure out how it works. I'll loan the totem to you if you agree to help me test it.

The watery areas surrounding the farm are home to pesky mottled drywallow crocolisks and drywallow daggermaws. Try fighting the crocolisks near the totem.

passages.title: The Grimtotem Weapon
passages.text: Have you had any luck testing the totem?

passages.title: The Grimtotem Weapon
passages.text:
<The apprentice listens as you describe your experiment.>

A haze and some lightning? That's it? There's got to be more to the totem than just that! The Grimtotems aren't likely to bring something like this to the battlefield unless it has some kind of utility.

passages.title: A Fitting Weapon
passages.text:
From your earliest days, <name>, your trainers identified you as a natural talent. Your rapid progress and dedication have made you an example.

In recognition of your service, King Wrynn has commissioned the royal armorer to forge a special weapon.

Legend has it that the cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest is home to a variety of materials that you will need. Travel there and find the lost Silverlaine family sword, a supply of moonsteel ingots, and sinew from ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: A Fitting Weapon
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: A Fitting Weapon
passages.text: Ander told me to expect you. It's quite an honor to be crafting a weapon for you, <name>. With these materials, it will be a fine blade indeed.

passages.title: Our Boys on the Shore
passages.text:
The situation here in the Highlands changes by the minute. Our objective is to storm the Bastion of Twilight, but I can't even secure a landing zone on the shore without the blasted Horde creating trouble.

While I scrape together the remains of the fleet, I need men on the shore securing the beach head.

Report to Lieutenant Emry on the shore and help his marines to beat back the Horde!

passages.title: Our Boys on the Shore
passages.text:
Keep your head down 'fore you lose it, <class>!

This is MY beach.

The Horde WANTS my beach.

They will NOT have my beach.

Is the beach situation clear?

passages.title: The Reagent Thief
passages.text:
If there's one thing you can count on Apprentice Morlann to do, it's whine about reagents.

Normally, I just ignore him, and it never works. This time, I'm going to try something different.

Maybe if I replace the missing reagents before he notices, he'll leave me alone. The most common reagent we both use is marsh venom, which comes from the darkfang creepers and noxious shredders in the marsh north of the farm. If you bring me the venom, I'll replace it before Morlann notices it's gone.

passages.title: The Reagent Thief
passages.text: Did you get that venom? Morlann's going to discover that it's gone any moment now...

passages.title: The Reagent Thief
passages.text:
<Apprentice Garion inspects the venom.>

This is absolutely perfect! He'll never know the difference.

passages.title: Direhorn Raiders
passages.text:
The Grimtotems up at Direhorn Post, just to the north, are getting bolder by the day. At night, you can often hear them chanting about their deeds in battle against people who've tried to settle here.

They're determined to drive us from Tabetha's farm even though she's trained generations of apprentices here. We've defended the farm as best we can, but Apprentice Garion was wounded in the last attack.

Go to Direhorn Post and kill any Grimtotem you can find! The attacks must stop.

passages.title: Direhorn Raiders
passages.text: Have you made any progress in stopping the Grimtotem attacks?

passages.title: Direhorn Raiders
passages.text:
<Apprentice Morlann nods.>

Good. Can't say I'll miss the company, if you can call it that. You'd think at least in the middle of the swamp you'd get some privacy, you know?

passages.title: Scouting the Shore
passages.text:
It's them or us, <class>. Only one of us can command this beach.

North of here you'll see a small hill with a commanding view of the shoreline. Whoever controls that hill will have the upper hand up and down the shore!

I need to know what the current situation is. Scout the beach head control point, marked by that enormous flag, and return to me.

You don't have to try to capture it, unless you're spoiling for a fight...

passages.title: Scouting the Shore
passages.text: That's the lay of the land, soldier. If you're having trouble fighting here on the coast, you might consider pitching in and helping us take and hold that hill.

passages.title: The Hand of the Light
passages.text:
I have been watching your progress, <name>, and I can only conclude that the Light shines brightly upon you. You are becoming an exemplary <class>.

To honor your dedication, King Wrynn has commissioned the royal armorer to forge a special weapon.

The materials to make your weapon are unique, and only found in the cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Travel there and recover the holy symbol of Commander Springvale, a supply of moonsteel ingots, and sinew from the ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: The Hand of the Light
passages.text: Do you have the materials for your weapon?

passages.title: The Hand of the Light
passages.text: Lord Grayson has told me much about you and your dedication to the Light and the Alliance. It will be a great honor to craft a hammer for you, <name>.

passages.title: A Well-Earned Reward
passages.text:
I am not the only one impressed by your progress <name>. Your mastery of bow and pet and your dedication to the Alliance have reached the ears of King Wrynn.

In recognition of your service, the king has commissioned the royal bowyer to craft a special weapon.

The cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest is home to the unique materials needed for your weapon. Travel there and obtain the scope from Lord Godfrey's gun, a supply of moontouched wood, and sinew from the ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: A Well-Earned Reward
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: A Well-Earned Reward
passages.text: Who knew that cursed old keep hid such valuable items? I'll be honored to craft them into a fine weapon for you.

passages.title: Corrosion Prevention
passages.text:
Just look at this area! It's swarming with oozes. If I don't find some way to keep them under control, they'll corrode the wreckage and the zeppelin's cargo!

I can't go back empty-handed, <class>! Help me dissolve these oozes before they've digested everything!

This device, when powered, will concentrate energy on the slimes, causing them to explode. The zeppelin's fragmented power core should power the device. The one near the main crash works all the time, but the others flicker on and off.

passages.title: Corrosion Prevention
passages.text: Did you make any progress against those oozes?

passages.title: Corrosion Prevention
passages.text:
Well, it does look a little cleaner out there...

I suppose it's time to get down to the business of salvaging this wreckage.

passages.title: Secure the Cargo!
passages.text:
This zeppelin was carrying six months' worth of supplies to us at Mudsprocket! Sure, they've been able to barter for some of what they need, but they won't hold out forever.

I've been sent out here to recover what I can of the cargo, but the wreckage is scattered all over the marsh in this area. I'm sure a lot of the cargo didn't survive the crash, but are you willing to help me recover what we can?

passages.title: Secure the Cargo!
passages.text:
<Moxie looks frantic with worry.>

Did the cargo survive? Did you find any of it?

passages.title: Secure the Cargo!
passages.text: Wow! You certainly found a lot more than I expected would be out there. I'm not sure how much Drazzit thought we were going to find out here, but he's going to have to be happy with this for now.

passages.title: A Royal Reward
passages.text:
SI:7 has been watching your progress with interest. You service to the Alliance is well-known and tales of your deeds have reached the king's ears.

In recognition of your service, King Wrynn has commissioned the royal armorer to forge a special weapon.

The cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest is home to the exotic materials for your weapon. Travel there and recover Commander Springvale's sharpening stone, a supply of moonsteel ingots, and sinew from the ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: A Royal Reward
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: A Royal Reward
passages.text: It was quite an honor to receive the commission for your weapon, <name>. When Tony mentioned using so many exotic materials, I had my doubts, but it seems you managed to find them all. This will be a fine reward for all you've done for the Alliance.

passages.title: Blessings of the Elements
passages.text:
Your talent has attracted much attention in shamanic circles, <name>. Word of your mastery of the elements and dedication to the Alliance has even reached the palace.

In recognition of your service, King Wrynn has commissioned the royal armorer to forge a special weapon.

The materials for your weapon can only be found in Silverpine Forest's cursed Shadowfang Keep. Travel there and retrieve Lord Walden's talisman, the Book of Lost Souls, and the essence of the ghosts haunting the castle.

passages.title: Blessings of the Elements
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: Blessings of the Elements
passages.text: I have rarely had the chance to work with such exotic materials, but even I can sense the power residing within them. I will have the honor of crafting an incredible weapon for you, <name>. The farseer did not underestimate your abilities when she told me about you.

passages.title: Mastering the Arcane
passages.text:
You have proven yourself a brilliant student and a dedicated servant of the Alliance. Word of your accomplishments has even reached the ears of the king.

In recognition of your service, King Wrynn has commissioned the royal enchanter to create a special weapon.

The materials required for your staff are found only in Silverpine Forest's cursed Shadowfang Keep. Travel there and find a lost heirloom of the Silverlaine family, a supply of moontouched wood, and the essence of the ghosts haunting the keep.

passages.title: Mastering the Arcane
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: Mastering the Arcane
passages.text: Ah, I have been expecting you, <name>. Maginor Dumas has spoken highly of you and the royal commission only confirms his words. It is an honor to be able to craft a staff for you.

passages.title: A Boon for the Powerful
passages.text:
The king is finally beginning to take note of our power and our value to the Alliance, thanks to your deeds. Perhaps they are beginning to accept our kind.

King Wrynn has commissioned the royal enchanter to create a powerful weapon in recognition of your achievements.

The materials you will need come from Silverpine Forest's Shadowfang Keep. Travel there and obtain the tenebrous orb held by Lord Godfrey, the Book of Lost Souls, and the essence of the ghosts haunting the castle.

passages.title: A Boon for the Powerful
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: A Boon for the Powerful
passages.text: I won't ask what you had to do to come by such rare and powerful materials, but I'm glad to have the chance to work with them. Your weapon will be magnificent!

passages.title: The Circle's Future
passages.text:
The Cenarion Circle is pleased with your progress, <name>. You are a credit to all druids and we look to you and your peers as the future of of our brotherhood.

The circle has decided to honor you with the creation of unique staff.

The rare and powerful materials needed for your staff can only be found in Shadowfang Keep inside Silverpine Forest. Travel there and retrieve Lord Walden's collection of elixirs, a supply of moontouched wood, and sinew from the ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: The Circle's Future
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your staff?

passages.title: The Circle's Future
passages.text: Ah, you must be the <class> Loganaar was talking about. It is a pleasure to finally meet you. Loganaar and other members of the circle speak highly of you. It will be an honor to make a weapon for such a <class>.

passages.title: The Captive Bride
passages.text:
Of course! Lakota Windsong! Why didn't I think of this before?

Arnak kidnapped Lakota years ago and tried to force her into being his bride. She managed to escape, but in the chaos of the recent attack on Freewind Post, he took her again.

She has to be around here somewhere. She's become quite the mystic in recent years. I'm guessing she'll know what to do with these tauren artifacts.

passages.title: The Captive Bride
passages.text:
It is embarrassing to have been kidnapped by Arnak again. I heard the fighting outside. Did you kill him?

<The shaman looks sad for just a moment.>

I am happy to be free once more. Now, how can I help you, <race>?

passages.title: The Captive Bride
passages.text:
Lakota Windsong! Why did I not think of this before?

Arnak kidnapped Lakota years ago and tried to force her to be his bride. With help, she was able to escape, but in the chaos of the recent attack on Freewind Post, he took her again.

She must be near. She has become quite the shaman in recent years. I am sure that she will understand the significance of the rattle, the writ, and the drums.

passages.title: The Captive Bride
passages.text:
It is embarrassing to have been kidnapped by Arnak again. I heard the fighting outside. Did you kill him?

<The shaman looks sad for just a moment.>

I am happy to be free once more. Now, how can I help you, <class>?

passages.title: Favored of the Light
passages.text:
The Light truly shines in you and your dedication to the Alliance, <name>. You serve as an example to your fellow priests and comrades in arms.

In recognition of your deeds, King Wrynn has commissioned the royal enchanter to create a special staff.

The materials for such a weapon can only be found in the cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Travel there and find the lost holy symbol of Commander Springvale, a supply of moontouched wood, and ghostly essence from the spirits haunting the keep.

passages.title: Favored of the Light
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: Favored of the Light
passages.text:
I can't believe you managed to get all those materials. I wouldn't think of venturing into Shadowfang Keep! The stories about that place are horrific.

Enough of that, though. This is a time to recognize your achievements, not prattle on about my silly fears.

passages.title: Favored of Elune
passages.text:
You are a true servant of Elune, an example to our people, and stalwart servant of the Alliance. The Temple of the Moon and the court of Stormwind wish to honor your achievements.

We have commissioned the royal enchanter to create a staff for you.

The materials for your staff can only be found in the cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Travel there and find the lost holy symbol of Commander Springvale, a supply of moontouched wood, and ghostly essence from the spirits haunting the keep.

passages.title: Favored of Elune
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: Favored of Elune
passages.text:
I can't believe you managed to get all those materials. I wouldn't think of venturing into Shadowfang Keep! The stories about that place are horrific.

Enough of that, though. This is a time to recognize your achievements, not prattle on about my silly fears.

passages.title: A Budding Young Surgeon
passages.text:
You have shown yourself to be a capable priest and a credit to the people of Gnomeregan. The high tinker and the king of Stormwind wish to honor your contribution to the Alliance.

They have commissioned the royal enchanter to create a special staff.

The materials for such a weapon can only be found in the cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Travel there and find the lost holy symbol of Commander Springvale, a supply of moontouched wood, and ghostly essence from the spirits haunting the keep.

passages.title: A Budding Young Surgeon
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: A Budding Young Surgeon
passages.text:
I can't believe you managed to get all those materials. I wouldn't think of venturing into Shadowfang Keep! The stories about that place are horrific.

Enough of that, though. This is a time to recognize your achievements, not prattle on about my silly fears.

passages.title: A Fitting Weapon
passages.text:
From your earliest days, your trainers always knew you would make your mark on the Horde. You have fought bravely and given our enemies reason to fear.

As a reward for your dedication, the warchief has commissioned his personal smith to forge a special weapon.

The cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest is the only place to get the materials you'll need. Travel there and find the lost Silverlaine family sword, a supply of moonsteel ingots, and sinew from the ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: A Fitting Weapon
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: A Fitting Weapon
passages.text: Grezz Ragefist told me to expect you. Those materials will make a fine sword. Always use it for the glory of the Horde.

passages.title: Landgrab
passages.text:
The Horde's Axebite Marines are all up in my precious, precious beach.

<The Lieutenant points north, along the shore.>

Kill them.

passages.title: Landgrab
passages.text:
Dead? By the dozen?

It's a start, <class>. It's a start.

passages.title: Greasing the Wheel
passages.text:
Sorry about that. I was pretty sure you were one of those spider-beasts, doing a bad <race> impression.

How do you do? Gidwin Goldbraids, at your service. I'm in a bit of a hurry back to my caravan, but I was wondering if you might do me one last favor? My pal Fiona runs a small shop, and she could probably use some of these herbs that grow along the river shore.

I'm thinking if we give her some nice herbs, she'll be MUCH less likely to murder me. That's the plan, anyway.

passages.title: Greasing the Wheel
passages.text: Giddy's got you mixed up in all of this now?

passages.title: Greasing the Wheel
passages.text:
I'll tear that pint-size paladin to shreds before he... wait a minute are those Banshee's Bells?  You brought these for me?

Oh, Gidwin asked you to get them for me!  That sweet little guy.  Alright.  He's off the hook for now.

passages.title: A Gift For Fiona
passages.text:
My traveling companion, Fiona, runs a small vendor's shop out of her caravan. She and I, along with our friend Gidwin, are all on our way to Light's Hope Chapel. I'm sure you can join us, if you like... though Fiona might be a little mad at me.

Fiona always forgets why she's mad if you give her a gift. Kill some of the plaguehounds north of here, then bring their blood to Fiona at the caravan, down by the river. She'll love it. We'll talk again there.

passages.title: A Gift For Fiona
passages.text:
I should have guessed it.  Tarenar made you get me a gift?  That thoughtless idiot!

Umm... what was the gift, anyhow?

passages.title: A Gift For Fiona
passages.text:
Why, this is exactly what I needed!  Fine, I'll forgive Tarenar for running off.

<name>, you're welcome to join us anytime.

passages.title: The Maw of Madness
passages.text:
I can't believe it, <name>. Me own son - me own flesh and blood! Throwing his lot in with those fiends from the Twilight's Hammer. Did you see what he became when he tried to destroy the wedding? Oh ... why? Why?

It's that beast, <name>. The enormous mouth emerging from the earth to our west. "The Maw of Madness!" My son said it spoke to him, but I thought it was just nightmares.

The Earthen Ring is trying to destroy it. Go to Earthcaller Torunscar, west of here, and see how you can help!

passages.title: The Maw of Madness
passages.text: Welcome, brotha. You've chosen a harsh time to be joinin' us, but that is to our fortune. We could use ya help.

passages.title: The Weeping Wound
passages.text:
A beast, <name>! I saw a beast. A great maw, an even greater hungering. They can't possibly know what they unleashed.

It is here. Its terrible shapeless body is erupting right into the Highlands.

I saw you in my vision, <name>. You struggle with the Earthen Ring to contain the beast. You will face the darkness.

Go now, before the beast grows in power. Speak to Earthcaller Torunscar at the Circle of the Elements, northwest of here atop the ridge beyond the ruined Drakgor Encampment. Hurry!

passages.title: The Weeping Wound
passages.text: Welcome, brotha. You've chosen a harsh time to be joinin' us, but that is to our fortune. We could use ya help.

passages.title: Devoured
passages.text:
We knew this was a possibility, but we had no idea how the beast would defend itself. Iso'rath's body is reacting quickly to our threat.

I can complete the summoning from here, but only if you can hold back Iso'rath's defenses. Keep them busy! We will survive this!

passages.title: Devoured
passages.text:
I've brought you back from the brink of death, hero!

Deathwing is upon us! We need your help.

passages.title: The Terrors of Iso'rath
passages.text:
We need you! You were stuck in some kind of nightmare. So are many of the other shaman.

It doesn't matter... our plan is falling apart. Some of our shaman are channeling protective auras that should combat the digestive juices and keep you alive, but we need you to rescue the other shaman from the tentacles. We won't be able to defeat Iso'rath without them!

Don't stay out in the stomach without the other shaman for too long or you'll be digested alive!

passages.title: The Terrors of Iso'rath
passages.text: The battle is not over. The shaman within Iso'rath need you!

passages.title: The Terrors of Iso'rath
passages.text: United with the Earthen Ring, we can survive the horrors of Iso'rath. Now it is time to turn our vengeance upon him!

passages.title: Rough Roads
passages.text:
The Argent Crusade built these towers to be points of light in the darkness of the Plaguelands. I walk the paths between these towers, protecting and maintaining them.

The roads have been dangerous lately. Plagued wildlife runs rampant, and bats swoop down upon unsuspecting travelers. It would make the next leg of my journey much easier if you could clear some of this wildlife out of the way for me.

passages.title: Rough Roads
passages.text: Of course a young <race> like you would have no trouble taking care of a few wild animals.  With the roads clear, my journey to the next tower will be much easier.

passages.title: Villains of Darrowshire
passages.text:
The Annals of Darrowshire tells of the villains of that battle. It tells how the ghoul lord Horgus the Ravager was destroyed by Alliance forces during the battle. He was slain among the foothills north of here, and his skull remains there.

Marduk the Black was never defeated, but his fabled sword now rusts, ownerless. It can be found near the road to our southeast.

Retrieve these items, <name>. I know not why, but I am certain their fate lies with you.

passages.title: Villains of Darrowshire
passages.text: Did you find the skull and the sword, <name>?

passages.title: Villains of Darrowshire
passages.text: You found them!  Well done, <name>!  These relics hold within them the memories of the Scourge forces at Darrowshire.  We will need these if we are to save your Joseph Redpath.

passages.title: Heroes of Darrowshire
passages.text:
The heroes of Darrowshire held relics of their own, and inside of those relics lie more precious memories.

First, speak with Carlin and obtain the Extended Annals of Darrowshire. Within the tome lies the narrative that will drive our excursion through time.

Then, you will need to head west to the Marris Stead. The former owner of the Marris farmhouse collected relics from the battle of Darrowshire - for what reason, I am not certain.

Gather these relics, and return to me.

passages.title: Heroes of Darrowshire
passages.text: Do you have the relics, <name>?

passages.title: Heroes of Darrowshire
passages.text:
You have the relics?  Good.  I will get to work on resolving any temporal discontinuities.

Don't worry... that's not something you have to worry about.  You just gather the reagents.

passages.title: The Battle of Darrowshire
passages.text:
Now, <name>, you will take part in battle of Darrowshire, and you will save Joseph Redpath.

Place this relic bundle in the Darrowshire town square, and the spirits of Darrowshire will rise. Join their battle and assure that these two things come to pass: Davil must survive beyond the death of Horgus, and Redpath must survive to be corrupted, then defeated.

After defeating the corrupted Redpath, his spirit will be saved. Speak with him, then return to his daughter Pamela.

passages.title: The Battle of Darrowshire
passages.text: I think I heard ghosts outside.  They whisper scary things to me...

passages.title: The Battle of Darrowshire
passages.text:
The fighting is over!  I heard my daddy whisper to me.  He scared away all the ghosts and he says he's coming home!  I'm so happy!

He also said I should welcome you if came to our house, so I made some tea!

I hope you like lots of sugar!

passages.title: Hidden Treasures
passages.text:
Daddy told me to give you this key. He said it opens a chest out back behind the house.

He also wanted me to thank you. Did you do a favor for him? Did you tell him you found my doll?

Well here's the key. And thank you <name>. Thank you! You're a very nice <man/lady>!

passages.title: Hidden Treasures
passages.text: This chest is old and covered in grime.

passages.title: Hidden Treasures
passages.text: The key fits the lock, and the chest opens...

passages.title: I'm Not Supposed to Tell You This
passages.text:
My daddy always kept two swords: one for fighting with men, and one for hunting the animals. I wasn't supposed to touch his swords, but I knew where he hid them.

One day, he told my mommy that he was going to fight a "lone hunter" in the hills to the east, but he brought his animal sword with him! When he came back, he didn't have his sword with him.

When daddy comes back, he'll be so happy when I give him his animal sword! Will you go and find it?

passages.title: I'm Not Supposed to Tell You This
passages.text: Daddy loved his animal sword.  He seemed sad when he didn't have it anymore.

passages.title: I'm Not Supposed to Tell You This
passages.text: That's my daddy's sword!  How did you find it?  Did you find the bad hunter?

passages.title: A Marksman's Weapon
passages.text:
You have picked up the ways of the hunter quickly, <name>. Your skills have made you a credit to the Horde and an example to the younglings.

As a reward for your progress and hard work, the warchief has commissioned his personal bowyer to create a unique weapon.

The cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest is the only place to get the materials we'll need. Travel there and retrieve the scope from Lord Godfrey's gun, a supply of moontouched wood, and sinew from the ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: A Marksman's Weapon
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: A Marksman's Weapon
passages.text: I'm honored that the warchief chose me to craft a weapon for you, <name>. With such exotic materials, it will be a very fine bow.

passages.title: Blade of the Shattered Hand
passages.text:
Many members of the Shattered Hand do not survive their training, <name>. Not only have you survived, but you will soon become a feared blade of the Horde.

As a reward for your progress, the warchief has commissioned his personal smith to forge a weapon.

The cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest is the only place to get the materials you'll need. Travel there and recover Commander Springvale's sharpening stone, a supply of moonsteel ingots, and sinew from the ghouls and geists infesting the keep.

passages.title: Blade of the Shattered Hand
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: Blade of the Shattered Hand
passages.text: Gordul told me that you would be bringing a variety of unusual materials, but I didn't expect anything like this. Moonsteel is said to be very rare and there's only one place I know to get it. You have risked much for this weapon, <name>, and I'll see to it that you receive a fitting reward.

passages.title: Hretar's Task
passages.text:
The elements and spirits speak to you with clear voices, <name>. You have become a powerful shaman and an example to others wishing to serve the Horde.

Word has even reached the warchief, and he has commissioned his personal smith to forge a special weapon for you.

The cursed Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest is the only place to get the materials you'll need. Travel there and obtain Lord Walden's talisman, the Book of Lost Souls, and essence from the ghosts haunting the keep.

passages.title: Hretar's Task
passages.text: Did you bring the materials I'll need for your weapon?

passages.title: Hretar's Task
