passages.text:
Ya done it?! Dey be no more?

Here ya go, mon. Take dis gift for bringin' justice to da frozen wastes.

passages.title: Gal'darah Must Pay
passages.text:
Da mighty Akali has been slain, <race>.

My role in life be to record, not fight. But dis cannot stand! Gal'darah and his followers must pay!

Avenge Akali's death, mon. It be da right thing ta do.

passages.title: Gal'darah Must Pay
passages.text:
Ya really did it?

You surpassed my expectations, mon. Take dis gift for bringin' justice to da frozen wastes.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
At first glance, it be lookin' like da same old story here - trolls tappin' into forbidden powah by destroyin' da very beings dey should be worshippin'.

If what I learned be true, den dey have a special golem - one like nuthin' created before!

Bring me back a piece from dat golem ta study.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text: You get me a piece of dat golem, mon?

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
Ahh, yeah mon! Dat be what I'm lookin' for.

Here ya go - take somethin' nice for your troubles.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
Dis whole mess coulda been avoided if da Drakkari had worshipped da gods instead of destroyin' dem.

I heard dat dey have a special golem - one imbued with forbidden powah.

Bring me back a piece from dat golem so we can learn from our bruddas and sistahs.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text: You find da golem? I'm sure it's in there somewhere.

passages.title: One of a Kind
passages.text:
Amazin'! Dis be like nothing I've ever seer before.

Good work, mon.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
Gundrak looks doomed. You know dis to be true.

If you be havin' the courage, search for history tablets to see what brought the Drakkari Empire to such an end.

Perhaps one day we be bringin' dem back to der former glory.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text: You find da Drakkari history tablets, mon?

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
You be havin' my thanks, mon.

These will be very useful to us, I'm sure of it.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
Da land of da ice trolls is a shadow of its former glory.

If you be havin' the courage, search for history tablets to see what brought the Drakkari Empire to such an end.

Perhaps one day we be givin' dis land back to a new line of frost trolls.

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text: You find da Drakkari history tablets, mon?

passages.title: For Posterity
passages.text:
We trolls been subject to da splittin' of empires for longer than some races been existin'.

We always regrow from da ruins.

passages.title: To Catch a Thief
passages.text:
Just beyond this cave lies Ravenholdt Manor. You need to get inside without being seen!

<Mostrasz places an enchantment on you.>

There - now I'll be able to keep an eye on you and communicate as you venture into the compound. Now sneak into that manor, locate the egg, and don't get caught...

passages.title: To Catch a Thief
passages.text:
So, you will join with me?

Good. Very good.

passages.title: The Forlorn Watcher
passages.text:
I would gladly give my life for the Makers or their creations.

However, since Loken's betrayal it seems all of Ulduar has turned on the world. One in particular, the Maiden of Grief, seems to reel in agony at her new orders.

Please lay her to rest and bring me one of her tears.

passages.title: The Forlorn Watcher
passages.text: I wish there were another way, but it seems death is the maiden's only salvation now.

passages.title: The Forlorn Watcher
passages.text:
<Kaldir stares into the crystal in silence for a moment.>

No being has ever felt such sincere sorrow as the Maiden of Grief has.

Let us remember her spirit as we continue our efforts against Loken.

passages.title: Corrupt Constructs
passages.text:
The iron dwarves are busy at work carving out massive stone constructs that I fear will soon be used as powerful weapons.

You must defeat their overseer, Krystallus, and the dark rune giants already walking the halls before it is too late!

passages.title: Corrupt Constructs
passages.text:
Well done, <race>.

Every weapon we can take away from Loken is a great boon to our own war effort.

passages.title: Champion of the Tournament
passages.text:
With this tournament we grow ever closer to our final confrontation with the Lich King.

<name>, fight with valor and honor. Every fighter here has gathered for the common good.

Together, we will stop Arthas!

passages.title: Champion of the King
passages.text:
With this tournament we grow ever closer to our final confrontation with the Lich King.

<name>, you are to represent the Alliance in this grand arena.

Prove yourself against Azeroth's finest. Go forward with honor.

passages.title: Diametrically Opposed
passages.text:
I shall speak plainly to you, little <race>. My people have not been the same since our ties with Thorim were severed.

Volkhan will not rest until either he, or we, are no more. We only want peace, but it seems we have no choice but war.

passages.title: Diametrically Opposed
passages.text:
Volkhan shall haunt the dreams of my people no more.

Continue your efforts, little <race>. In time, I am certain my people will grow to forgive Thorim.

passages.title: Whatever it Takes!
passages.text:
One way or another, Loken shall fall.

The honor and glory of his defeat shall be yours.

Return to me with his lying tongue, and earn my unending gratitude.

passages.title: Whatever it Takes!
passages.text: Has justice been brought to Loken?

passages.title: Whatever it Takes!
passages.text:
That vile worm is dead?

You have turned out to be a great boon to my people, little <race>.

Please accept this gift in return for your loyal friendship.

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text:
Loken's forces prepare for war. What they are not ready for is to be attacked themselves.

Now is the moment to strike. Take out General Bjarngrim and his army, lest they mount an offensive on all life on Azeroth!

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text: Have you vanquished their forces?

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text: Though few outside of us shall ever know it, you have certainly saved the world on this day.

passages.title: Stormherald Eljrrin
passages.text:
I have sent an emissary to the Halls of Lightning to take the battle to Loken.

He undoubtedly needs assistance, given the strength of Loken's armies. Lend him any aid you can so that we may finally stop the traitor.

passages.title: Stormherald Eljrrin
passages.text: Our time to act is short. Loken prepares for war.

passages.title: DEPRECATED: Shadow Hunter Urko'jin
passages.text:
We need to fill the remaining slots in the new blockade fleet before the night elves can reestablish their spy network in the city.

The Darkspears have yet to contribute much to the war effort, but if we can convince Shadow Hunter Urko'jin to add his forces to the fleet, that will change.

Problem is, Urko'jin won't go to war without the blessing of the spirits. Pay a visit to Darkspear Hold in the Echo Isles, retrieve the totem of seafaring, and deliver it to Urko'jin in the Valley of Spirits.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve a spellblade and a hand fan from one of the weapon racks below, bring it to me, and show me that you know how to hold it properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve a mace and a book of prayers from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve a pair of daggers from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve an axe and a shield from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: First, you will need weapons suited to your talents. Retrieve an axe and a shield from one of the weapon racks below, bring them to me, and show me that you know how to hold them properly.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text: Picking up your first weapon is also a symbolic gesture. Every <class> that leaves these training grounds must be ready to take up arms in defense of their fellow <race>.

passages.title: The Lesson of the Iron Bough
passages.text:
A fine weapon. It should suit your needs well.

Now let's put it to use.

passages.title: Mothallus!
passages.text:
The esteemed Journeyman Chu would appear to have created a monster. It is silken death with wings.

Mothallus.

You have already faced its brood. Now we ask that you help us face the creature itself.

Please, <class>, venture into the pit and rifle the bait. This will bring the beast to you.

Our mothfighters will assist you as you need, though silk tends to stick to them more than most so you may need to help them, should they become overwhelmed.

passages.title: Mothallus!
passages.text: Have you vanquished the beast?

passages.title: Mothallus!
passages.text:
We are pursuing perfection in our art and in ourselves. Along the way many mistakes will be made.

I'm sure by tomorrow this field will be swimming with more mistakes. Still, we thank you for your help.

passages.title: The Moth Rebellion
passages.text:
Oh... oh good! A <class>! Could you help me?

I created a strain of vile monsters during my experiments to improve silk output.

The result was a full-scale moth rebellion. Can you use your <class>iness and destroy some of these mutants?

passages.title: The Moth Rebellion
passages.text:
Master Goh keeps telling me I need to relax and that failure is part of learning. But this is a dangerous failure.

The kind that might get people killed.

passages.title: The Moth Rebellion
passages.text: It seems like there's not QUITE as many corrupted moths out there. At the very least, you've bought me some more time before I get in big, big trouble.

passages.title: Hidden Power
passages.text:
Our temple defenders have battled relentlessly for hours. No doubt they grow tired.

I will give you mantras to deliver to our fighters.

Do not be fooled by these pieces of paper. These ancient scriptures hold words of untold power.

passages.title: Hidden Power
passages.text: Words hold great power. Use them wisely.

passages.title: Hidden Power
passages.text:
The sha's numbers are unending, and our numbers few. But we are not daunted by difficult odds.

Thank you for doing your part to protect our home, <race>.

passages.title: Flames of the Void
passages.text:
Do you see the violent black and white flames erupting all around the temple?

The greater our doubt, the stronger they rage. Unchecked, they will devour the entire temple.

We have but one hope.

Take flight on one of our war serpents. Fly it near the pure springs of water, and then douse the fires with water from the pools.

passages.title: Flames of the Void
passages.text: These fires burn unlike anything in our world.

passages.title: Flames of the Void
passages.text: You have done much to help curb the fires. Thank you for your efforts.

passages.title: Where Silk Comes From
passages.text:
Would you like to be a Silkmaster for a day?

The first thing you'll need are fresh mulberry leaves. You can find them in our grove of mulberry bushes to the northwest.

Next you will need to feed them to a hungry silkworm in our feeding pit to the west.

And finally you should get some raw silk from our processing hut on the south side of our farm.

Have fun!

passages.title: Where Silk Comes From
passages.text: Have you found all of the items? Did you pay close attention to our process?

passages.title: Where Silk Comes From
passages.text: Superb specimens. I will see to it they find their way to the right place. Please enjoy this free sample.

passages.title: Securing the Province
passages.text:
With our grip on the province loosening, saurok from the wilds have already moved in to the cave just north of town.

Most of our hunters are face-down in their own tears, so the saurok just walk in here like they own the place and grab whatever they want!

I want to send a message that Zhu's Watch is not to be crossed.

Will you be my messenger?

passages.title: Securing the Province
passages.text: Thank you, <name>. That should teach those savages to know their boundaries.

passages.title: Borderlands
passages.text:
Bonfires are surprisingly effective at discouraging beasts from wandering out of the wilds. We have three along the border to the southwest which we normally keep lit at all times.

Nobody's been there for days, though, and the fires must be out by now. It's only a matter of time before the wilds creep back in and overtake the land we have kept safe for centuries.

Please, re-ignite the bonfires. They are critical in keeping the province safe, and they are memorials to the founders of our way of life.

passages.title: Borderlands
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

Zhu Province serves as a corridor from the upper tier of the valley down to the sea.

Keeping the province safe requires daily efforts to maintain a border against the savage Krasarang Wilds.

passages.title: Into the Brewery
passages.text:
We need to find out what's going on inside that brewery, <name>!

We may have cleared out some of the bigger pests, but I'm certain there's plenty more where they came from. Gather up a few of your friends, and meet me inside!

passages.title: Into the Brewery
passages.text:
You came! Great!

I'm looking forward to fighting by your side again, <name>.

passages.title: Assassinate Creed
passages.text:
The city has been in chaos for days now. Hiram Creed, disguised as a Gilnean, has infected the lot of those dogs with his own draconic blood. Even the Forsaken are having trouble routing him out.

Only a surgical assassination can end this!

The bridge behind me is relatively unguarded. Slip in through merchant's square and head south - you'll find Creed in the middle of the military district.

I'll keep an eye on you and pull you out if there's any trouble.

...There WILL be trouble!

passages.title: Assassinate Creed
passages.text: Hiram Creed. Among the black dragons, he is known as "Creetharus."

passages.title: Assassinate Creed
passages.text:
Creed is finished. The Gilneans who followed his lead are on their own now - assuming his corrupted draconic blood works its way out of their system without killing them.

Either way they're no longer a concern of ours.

passages.title: Murozond
passages.text:
If we are to destroy Deathwing, we will need the power of the Dragon Soul. To obtain the Dragon Soul, I would have to take you back to the Sundering, ten thousand years in the past... but that time passage is blocked to me.

The creature that blocks us from accessing this time passage is named Murozond. He must be slain, here, in this twisted future, before we can continue our plot to unmake Deathwing.

This is why you were brought here, <name>.

passages.title: Murozond
passages.text:
This is a future of Azeroth, yes... but not an inevitable one.

This future is what my fellow aspects are trying to avoid.

passages.title: Murozond
passages.text: Murozond is no more. The timeways are open to me once again.

passages.title: Archival Purposes
passages.text:
From what I understand, you intend to avoid this future. If this is true, then we must archive data from this timestrand before it is lost to us.

We believe that the most interesting and valuable elements of this future are the powerful "echoes" that roam the dragonshrines.

Take this vessel with you as you silence these echoes. A portion of their energies will be archived within the bronze dragonflight's depository.

passages.title: Archival Purposes
passages.text:
Nozdormu is acting with haste. This is something that Nozdormu does not usually do.

Normally I would be more thorough with my archival. However, given the circumstances, we are forced to pick and choose what we record... and to employ the help of mercenaries like you.

passages.title: Archival Purposes
passages.text:
<Alurmi collects the vessel from you.>

I will handle these from here. Of course, they must be properly labeled, documented, and stored.

passages.title: The Path to the Dragon Soul
passages.text:
I cannot simply fly up and grab the Dragon Soul. The old gods protect it.

To make matters worse, their shield is strengthened by the swirling, arcane energies that emanate from the Well of Eternity, and those energies are being focused by the great demon Mannoroth.

Distract Mannoroth, and the link between the Dragon Soul and the Well will be broken. Without the Well's power, the old gods' ward will be weakened, and the Dragon Soul will be vulnerable.

And then I will take it.

passages.title: The Path to the Dragon Soul
passages.text: What?

passages.title: The Path to the Dragon Soul
passages.text:
Thank you for your help, stranger.

You fight well. I hope to fight with you again in the future.

passages.title: To Wyrmrest!
passages.text:
The Dragon Soul... a weapon with enough power to defeat Deathwing. Thanks to you, it is now safely in our hands.

Come! The aspects await us. We must bring the Dragon Soul to Wyrmrest Temple, in the center of Dragonblight.

passages.title: To Wyrmrest!
passages.text: Come, <name>. We do not have much further to travel.

passages.title: To Wyrmrest!
passages.text:
I owe my life to you, heroes.

Now that we hold the Dragon Soul safely within Wyrmrest, it may be that all of Azeroth owes their lives to you.

passages.title: Documenting the Timeways
passages.text:
You... <name>, was it? You assisted with our archival in the past. Well, technically it was the future, but I believe you understand. Time is highly relative.

I require more information for our archive. While you and Nozdormu don't intend to overwrite this timestrand, as you did in the End Time, we can still benefit from more data.

I require information on Captain Varo'then, one of Azshara's pretty little handmaidens, and... hmm... oh, how about that big felguard, just down those stairs?

passages.title: Documenting the Timeways
passages.text: We rarely enjoy the opportunity to employ a brave <class> like you. Our archive grows more thorough, thanks to your efforts.

passages.title: The Twilight Prophet
passages.text:
The missive reads as follows:

"The Hour of Twilight is upon us. The world-shaman Thrall approaches Wyrmrest with the Dragon Soul in hand, feebly whimpering one final threat to destroy our glorious master."

"Stop Thrall, and we win our war. I will be watching you from nearby."

 ~ The Twilight Prophet

passages.title: The Twilight Prophet
passages.text: I have my suspicions about this Twilight Prophet.

passages.title: The Twilight Prophet
passages.text:
It is truly as we foresaw: Benedictus was the Twilight Prophet. And now he is no more.

We dealt a mighty bow to the Twilight's Hammer today. Let us hope that it was a deathblow.

passages.title: The Deed is Done
passages.text:
Prince Wrathion will be pleased to hear that you've succeeded. You should report back to him at Ravenholdt Manor.

The Prince has been known to be extremely generous to those who help him.

passages.title: The Deed is Done
passages.text:
That's wonderful news, <name>. Creed was not the most powerful of the remaining black dragons, but his manipulation of the Gilneans was truly diabolical.

I've prepared a reward for you. These blades may not look like much at present, but in the right hands they may yet awaken.

Perhaps in YOUR hands...

passages.title: Cluster Clutch
passages.text:
The daggers I have given you are lifeless shells. They can do great things, once they are given a means to contain the power I have in mind.

I need for you to acquire Shadowy Gems for me. The facets of these unusual stones are like windows into the infinite. They are often used by minions of the Twilight's Hammer to control the most powerful of elementals.

A great battle is raging around Wyrmrest Temple. Collect Elementium Gem Clusters from Deathwing's minions and bring the gems to me.

passages.title: Cluster Clutch
passages.text:
How many gems have you collected?

Are my father's minions as twisted as he?

passages.title: Cluster Clutch
passages.text:
Ah, do you see how they shimmer? Many fine gems sparkle in the light, but only these seem to sparkle with darkness.

I'll perform an enchantment on these while you are on your next mission.

Are you ready?

passages.title: Our Man in Karazhan
passages.text:
Your next target is the Black Dragon Nalice, who is engaged in some sort of arcane debauchery beneath the ruined tower of Karazhan.

Your primary mission is to destroy her, but if you can bring me back a vial of her blood, I'll be able to use it to augment the power of the daggers I've given you.

Your accomplice Zazzo has already been dispatched to the scene and awaits you there. He'll have more details.

passages.title: Our Man in Karazhan
passages.text:
Madness. Insanity!

I don't know what Nalice is up to down there, but the entire basement radiates with diabolical arcane energy. She's got an entire cult worshipping her as a goddess.

If we're going to take her out, we have to do it soon. I hope you're ready for this!

passages.title: Blood of the Betrayer
passages.text:
I've pinpointed Nalice to the Master's Cellar, an extended basement you'll find in the ruins up ahead.

Dragon cultists are everywhere, and Nalice has set up some strange arcane storage devices throughout the area. Perhaps you can use those to your advantage?

Sneak past the cultists, obliterate Nalice, and grab a vial of her blood for Wrathion.

I'll keep my eyes on you and pull you out if you get into any trouble. But I'm NOT coming in there with you!

passages.title: Blood of the Betrayer
passages.text: Nalice. Dead?

passages.title: Blood of the Betrayer
passages.text:
You did it? She's dead? Unbelievable! You're some kind of miracle-worker!

Here, let me see that blood. I can preserve its energies in an arcane matrix for your trip back...

passages.title: A Score to Settle
passages.text:
Utgarde's forces are organizing under the advisory of Prince Keleseth, a san'layn ambassador of the Scourge.

We cannot allow the vrykul to benefit from his counsel any further. Silence him.

passages.title: A Score to Settle
passages.text: Is it done, <name>?

passages.title: A Score to Settle
passages.text:
Revenge feels good.  To think that this is but a taste of what's to come.

Arthas will get what he deserves soon enough.

passages.title: Victory in the Depths
passages.text:
<Zazzo performs an enchantment on the vial of blood, then quickly hands it back to you, as though it's toxic.>

Done! You'll want to get this back to Wrathion as soon as possible, along with those two daggers of yours.

I don't know what he plans to do with this stuff. Between you and me, sometimes that little dragon kid creeps me out. Good luck!

passages.title: Victory in the Depths
passages.text: Ah, you've returned! I no longer sense Nalice's presence. Is she dead? Or has she somehow eluded us both?

passages.title: Victory in the Depths
passages.text:
You are, indeed, a master of your craft. Nalice is dead, and it is time you are rewarded for your efforts.

<Wrathion takes the vial from you, his face a mask of equal parts reverence and revulsion. He drops the gems you collected one-by-one into the blood, muttering an incantation.>

<Without warning he pours the blood over the blades of the daggers, and the steel seems to writhe and twist as though alive. When the smoke clears, the daggers have altered their shape.>

passages.title: Sharpening Your Fangs
passages.text:
Do you understand why I have you assassinate the dragons, yet spare the mortals? It isn't their fault. They must seek out their own destiny, free from the meddling of my kind.

We are nearing the end of our mission, and it is time for you to seek out your own destiny as well. I can continue to augment your weapons, but collecting shadowy gems won't be enough. My work will require entire clusters. Gather them from my father's minions...

passages.title: Sharpening Your Fangs
passages.text:
How many clusters have you acquired?

The tenacity of your race continues to inspire me!

passages.title: Sharpening Your Fangs
passages.text:
You have done it! No doubt you placed yourself and your allies in great peril to acquire these. Your sacrifices will be rewarded in time. I will use these as the foundation of a powerful enchantment for you.

But we will need one additional catalyst. Are you ready for your final and most dangerous mission, <class>?

passages.title: Cleansing Drak'Tharon
passages.text:
'Ey, mon, you be here! Dis is good, mon!

Drak'Tharon soon be cleansed of them foul undead and restored to her noble purpose. In return for your help, the keep's most valuable treasures be yours, mon!

Once ya be reachin' its top, ya must summon me, and I'll perform the ritual.

Alas, my summonin' will be comin' at a cost. Ya must collect mojo from the survivors.

passages.title: Cleansing Drak'Tharon
passages.text:
We done a great thing, mon! And dis just be da beginning....

Seek me out in Zul'Drak when da time be right.

Dere be a war to be won, mon!

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text:
Two words: Tiger Blood!

This is gonna sell better than saronite back on the black market. Especially once I finish spreading a rumor about how it makes you all buff and stuff.

Thing is, I ran out of ammo. Can you round up a few vials of tiger blood for me? I'll cut you in on the scam.

passages.title: Wild Things
passages.text:
Welcome to the Order of the Cloud Serpent, <race>. I can see from the spark in your eye that you wish to join the Order.

Let me get a good look at you.

<Elder Anli gently holds your head and gazes at your face.>

Hmm. I see honesty and earnestness in your heart. You have journeyed far to come here, but I am afraid you must go yet further.

Your path into the Order begins now.

Speak to Instructor Tong at Windward Isle to the northeast to take the first step.

passages.title: Wild Things
passages.text:
Thank goodness, they finally sent someone!

Things have gotten out of control!

passages.title: Beating the Odds
passages.text:
At first, the Slitherscale were too frightened to approach the wild serpents.

Then, I caught them snatching the eggs under the cover of night.

Now, they are slaughtering adults and hatchlings alike!

If we do not do something, these gentle creatures will be completely wiped out. Then there won't even be an Order of the Cloud Serpent to join!

Go and slay these vile Slitherscales, and then we will talk.

passages.title: Beating the Odds
passages.text: The Order rarely meddles with the natural balance on this island, but it is too important to save the serpents.

passages.title: Beating the Odds
passages.text:
Thank you, <race>.

I tried to stop the Slitherscale where I could, but I was no match for their numbers.

Your work today will help preserve an entire generation of cloud serpents.

passages.title: Empty Nests
passages.text:
When the attacks began, the young hatchlings scattered in terror.

They are roaming around the island, lost and scared.

If you want to help, take this rope and leash the lost little ones. Take them back to their nests. Return them home.

passages.title: Empty Nests
passages.text: Did you return the hatchlings to their nests?

passages.title: Empty Nests
passages.text:
Don't worry. The hatchlings will be safe inside their nests.

I can't thank you enough for arriving when you did.

passages.title: Choosing the One
passages.text:
I have examined each egg, <name>. Out of the lot that you brought me, I have chosen the three eggs with the most promise.

You may choose only one egg to take with you. Are you ready to make your final selection?

passages.title: Choosing the One
passages.text:
You may choose only one egg to take with you.

Choose carefully. There is no going back.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Excellent, just excellent! I will return the other eggs to their nests, undisturbed.

In the meantime, deliver your egg to Instructor Skythorn at The Arboretum.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text: The wild cloud serpents live in a delicate balance with nature. Their rare eggs are quite vulnerable to enemies.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Ah yes, Elder Anli mentioned that a new student had joined our ranks. I see you have already chosen your cloud serpent egg.

I will instruct you on its care. Let me see it for a moment.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Excellent, just excellent! I will return the other eggs to their nests, undisturbed.

In the meantime, deliver your egg to Instructor Skythorn at The Arboretum.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text: The wild cloud serpents live in a delicate balance with nature. Their rare eggs are quite vulnerable to enemies.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Ah yes, Elder Anli mentioned that a new student had joined our ranks. I see you have already chosen your cloud serpent egg.

I will instruct you on its care. Let me see it for a moment.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Excellent, just excellent! I will return the other eggs to their nests, undisturbed.

In the meantime, deliver your egg to Instructor Skythorn at The Arboretum.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text: The wild cloud serpents live in a delicate balance with nature. Their rare eggs are quite vulnerable to enemies.

passages.title: The Rider's Journey
passages.text:
Ah yes, Elder Anli mentioned that a new student had joined our ranks. I see you have already chosen your cloud serpent egg.

I will instruct you on its care. Let me see it for a moment.

passages.title: Flight Training: Ring Round-Up
passages.text:
Now that your serpent is fully grown, you are ready to begin flight training.

As with all novices, you must start at the beginning.

Your first task is simple. Fly through 6 of the cloud rings between the spires to the east.

passages.title: Flight Training: Ring Round-Up
passages.text: How did your first flight go?

passages.title: Flight Training: Ring Round-Up
passages.text:
What have you learned from this lesson?

Speed. It's all about speed.

passages.title: Snack Time
passages.text:
Cloud serpents love to eat, and one of their favorite treats is the sugar minnow.

These fish can be found in salt or fresh water anywhere in Pandaria. I trust you have some skill in fishing, and your own fishing pole to catch them?

Bring me a fresh catch and I'm sure the hungry beasts around here will be very grateful.

passages.title: Snack Time
passages.text: Did you find a good place to fish?

passages.title: Snack Time
passages.text: Oh wonderful! These fish will do nicely.

passages.title: Fragments of the Past
passages.text:
The Order of the Cloud Serpent's history stretches back thousands of years, and although we have tried to preserve the old ways, there are ancient techniques that have been lost over time.

You can help us recover some of this knowledge by searching Pandaria's dig sites for clues to our past.

Use your archaeology skill to survey around Pandaria and bring me whatever you find.

passages.title: Fragments of the Past
passages.text: How did the excavation go?

passages.title: Fragments of the Past
passages.text: Amazing, <name>. These relics are invaluable to our studies. We will learn much from these fragments.

passages.title: Just a Flesh Wound
passages.text:
Many of the baby hatchlings at Windward Isle have been injured as a result of all the fighting.

I have been told that you may be able to help them, with your access to powerful bandages.

Please go northeast and use some of the best bandages you can acquire to save the injured hatchlings.

passages.title: Just a Flesh Wound
passages.text: Wonderful! It is a good thing you are trained in the arts of first aid.

passages.title: Sweet as Honey
passages.text:
<The hatchling scampers about, then whines and whimpers.>

From the cloud serpent's behavior, you have a hunch that it wants a sweet treat.

The fragrant trees in The Arboretum are home to many honey hives.

It will be a simple matter to collect combs from the nearby honeykeepers.

passages.title: Sweet as Honey
passages.text: <The hatchling spins around in glee as you return.>

passages.title: Sweet as Honey
passages.text:
The hatchling leaps for your hand. It winds its long, serpentine tail around you and begins to lick the honey from your fingers.

That tickles!

passages.title: Catch!
passages.text:
<The hatchling looks up at you with a bored, listless expression.>

You have a feeling the serpent is tired of being cooped up all day.

 How about playing a little game of catch?

passages.title: Catch!
passages.text: <The serpent watches you curiously.>

passages.title: Catch!
passages.text: Oh my, I see you and your serpent are having a great time! Well done, <name>. Playtime will greatly increase your serpent's mental and physical acuities.

passages.title: The Sky Race
passages.text:
The time for the great race is upon us!

Traverse the course among the spires and pass through the checkered flags on each of the 10 balloon checkpoints.

Make sure to pass underneath the finish line when you are done.

The competition will be fierce, but I wish you luck. Speak to me when you are ready to begin.

passages.title: The Sky Race
passages.text:
Wonderful! How does it feel to finish the Sky Race?

You must be eager to collect your prize!

passages.title: Restoring the Balance
passages.text:
The situation at the islands remains dire, <name>.

The Slitherscale saurok have not responded to our attempts at peace, so only one option remains.

In order to protect the wild cloud serpents, we must rid the island of their presence. Only then can the cloud serpents be left to live in peace.

passages.title: Restoring the Balance
passages.text: The poachers will wipe out the cloud serpents completely if they are not stopped.

passages.title: Restoring the Balance
passages.text: If the poachers will not listen to diplomacy, then they will surely listen to our blades. Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Feeding Time
passages.text:
<The serpent darts forward and bites your fingers.>

Ouch! It seems, without a doubt, that the little beast is hungry. You recall that some meaty-looking turtles can be found on the wild cloud serpent island to the northeast.

Perhaps some turtle meat will fill the hatchling's voracious appetite.

passages.title: Feeding Time
passages.text: <The serpent looks at you with hungry eyes.>

passages.title: Feeding Time
passages.text: You are learning well, young trainer. Saltback meat is tough, but loaded with the nutrients that a young hatchling needs to grow.

passages.title: Emptier Nests
passages.text:
Oh, thank goodness, another cloud serpent trainer!

I just received word that the wild hatchlings at Windward Isle to the northeast are in serious trouble!

While the adults fight those terrible saurok, who is watching the cute little babies? No one, that's who!

WE HAVE TO SAVE THEM!

I'm sending every trainer I can find to go and help. If you aren't too busy, can you make sure the hatchlings are safely delivered back to their mothers' nests?

passages.title: Emptier Nests
passages.text: I see you have been taking good care of the young hatchlings out there. Well done.

passages.title: Thieving Raiders
passages.text:
Saurok!

These vile creatures are obsessed with killing and stealing. They attacked our settlement without provocation or warning.

Please, <class>, can you aid us?

Help us recover our lost possessions from these Riverblade raiders that march along the river and we will gladly reward you.

passages.title: Thieving Raiders
passages.text: I think they even stole my holy spittoon.

passages.title: Thieving Raiders
passages.text:
Not many would stop to help a village in need... especially so deep in the wilds.

You are a champion to our people, <name>.

passages.title: Stalker Mastery
passages.text:
Tigers! No matter what land I go to I hear about these big fanged beasts. And yet I haven't had a chance to hunt any of them.

Let's go hunt some tigers. I'll go east, you go west. I think I saw some near Dustback Gorge. I'm sure there are tons near those mushan.

passages.title: Stalker Mastery
passages.text: What's your count up to?

passages.title: Stalker Mastery
passages.text: Wow! You really racked up a count. I'll chat with Mr. Pleeb about getting the best one converted to a trophy for you.

passages.title: Mushan Mastery: Darkhide
passages.text:
My boy here is a talented hunter... in training. Let's show him an old 'Nessy style hunt shall we?

I saw a mighty big mushan east of here with a hide dark as night. It looked like it had taken down a number of hunters in its day.

If you want a big game hunt, go try an' take it on.

passages.title: Mushan Mastery: Darkhide
passages.text: Puttin' the "big" into "Big Game Hunter."

passages.title: Mushan Mastery: Darkhide
passages.text: Now that's a proper trophy right there.

passages.title: Parental Mastery
passages.text:
If them tablets were correct, all ay got ta do is a small dance ritual and the big thing o' the deep will be summoned.

When it comes out, we'll get 'em and show me pop we are both true big game hunters like him.

passages.title: Parental Mastery
passages.text: Now that is how ya big game hunt.

passages.title: Parental Mastery
passages.text: You saved me son! I canno' ever thank ye enough. Please! Take this fer your efforts.

passages.title: Flight Training: In Due Course
passages.text:
Now that you have learned the basics of the race, you should go learn the course.

Explore the spires and collect a race flag from each of the checkpoints.

Fly through each checkered flag to collect it.

passages.title: Flight Training: In Due Course
passages.text: Do you have what it takes to compete... and win?

passages.title: Flight Training: In Due Course
passages.text: Well done. If you hadn't been capable of finding the checkpoints, I fear you would never have done well in the Sky Race.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Flame
passages.text:
This is one of the challenges I put upon my warriors to keep them strong and fast. Let's see how you fare.

Survive the ring for 60 seconds without getting pushed out or killed. Stay on your toes.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Flame
passages.text: The constant danger in the ring prepares us for life or death fighting we have to endure outside the wall.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Flame
passages.text: Not bad, <class>. Not bad at all.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Blades
passages.text:
This is one of the challenges I put upon my warriors to keep them strong and fast. Let's see how you fare.

Survive the ring for 60 seconds without getting pushed out or killed. Stay on your toes.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Blades
passages.text: The constant danger in the ring prepares us for life or death fighting we have to endure outside the wall.

passages.title: Survival Ring: Blades
passages.text: Not bad, <class>. Not bad at all.

passages.title: Mantid Under Fire
passages.text:
The mantid are attacking again, and we're a bit short-handed up on the wall. In hopes that you'd help, I saved one of the more fun posts for you: the hot oil!

It's a bit more violent and a bit less scandalous than it sounds.

It's simple really. Get up on the wall, find one of the oil stations, and dump it on any of the mantid pouring up against the wall. It's very effective.

passages.title: Mantid Under Fire
passages.text: The hard part is the cleanup. Fortunately, you're not responsible for that.

passages.title: Mantid Under Fire
passages.text: You've done devastating damage to the mantid forces. The wall defenders should be able to get things under control.

passages.title: Learn and Grow II: Tilling and Planting
passages.text:
Okay, now we've got our seeds, it's time to plant them.

First, we have to prepare the soil! You gotta till the soil and break it up to make a nice bed for our little sprouts.

Till those two plots of soil over there, then plant the seeds in them.

passages.title: Learn and Grow II: Tilling and Planting
passages.text:
Well, go ahead - bust that soil up and plant the seeds!

You aren't giving up already are you? I need your help!

passages.title: Learn and Grow II: Tilling and Planting
passages.text:
Nicely done.

Notice how those seeds sprouted immediately? That's part of what makes this valley so ideal for farming - something about the soil here just makes veggies grow like crazy!

The work's not done yet, though.

passages.title: Learn and Grow III: Tending Crops
passages.text:
My grandfather used to say "Yoonie, a cabbage is like a woman: ignore her and she'll turn rotten. Pamper her and she'll grow big and plump and you can put a ribbon on her and take her to market to show her off to your frie-" look, he was from a different time, okay?

The point is, now that our cabbages have sprouted, they need attention! Today they look a little dry, so you should water them.

Here's the old watering can grandpa left. It will always be near the field if you need it.

passages.title: Learn and Grow III: Tending Crops
passages.text:
Come to think of it, grandpa said a lot of really offensive things.

Maybe I should avoid quoting him from now on...

passages.title: Learn and Grow III: Tending Crops
passages.text:
Great, the cabbages are tended and looking good!

Today they were thirsty, but you never know what they might need. Pay close attention to your crops and tend them accordingly.

I got all kinds of advice from my grandpa, so if you're ever unsure of how to take care of something, feel free to ask!

Just make sure it's strictly related to farming...

passages.title: Learn and Grow IV: Harvesting
passages.text:
It's time for our hard work to pay off! Normally we'd have to wait a day before the crops are ready to harvest.

Fortunately, those seeds Greenfield gave us were specially designed to grow FAST. The yield won't be worth much, but they're good for stepping new farmers through the process.

Our cabbages should be ready to harvest. I'll let you do the honors, of course!

passages.title: Learn and Grow IV: Harvesting
passages.text:
Look at those... err, what do they say around here? Oh yeah, b'yoots!

Look at those b'yoots!

I think I'm getting the hang of this farmer thing.

passages.title: Learn and Grow IV: Harvesting
passages.text:
Well, those are the basics!

Till the soil, plant the seeds, tend to any threats, then wait for the results!

Today was easy, but stay on your toes: my grandfather told me all kinds of crazy stories about farming at Sunsong Ranch.

Farming ain't all giant turnips and roses, you know.

passages.title: Learn and Grow V: Halfhill Market
passages.text:
All right friend, all of that farming was just for practice!

Are you ready to try the real thing?

There's a lady by the name of Gina Mudclaw who runs the Halfhill Market, which is across the street to the south.

I heard she's looking to buy some vegetables. Since it's your first time meeting her, you shouldn't go empty-handed.

Why don't you look around the ranch and see if there are any items hiding around?

Might be that we'll find a good gift to take to our new neighbor!

passages.title: Learn and Grow V: Halfhill Market
passages.text: Hey, haven't seen your face around here before! What's your name?

passages.title: Learn and Grow V: Halfhill Market
passages.text:
Oh my, a marsh lily!

How did you know that these are my favorite? I just might take a liking to you, stranger.

Thank you!

passages.title: Mung-Mung's Vote I: A Hozen's Problem
passages.text:
I've been thinkin' about how to get into the Tiller's good graces, <name>.

Now, the Tiller's Union accepts new farmers each year, and there are five members on the voting council.

We already got Gina's vote, but we'll have to prove ourselves to the other four members of their board.

Why don't you go over and say hello to Mung-Mung? He works with Mr. Mudclaw out on the Mudclaw's farm to the northwest.

passages.title: Mung-Mung's Vote I: A Hozen's Problem
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Growing the Farm I: The Weeds
passages.text:
Hey <name>, I've been thinkin' recently about expanding my farm.

See that plot there that's just covered in weeds? If we can get rid of those weeds, we could use that land for planting.

I heard there's a farmer by the name of Gai Lan who knows a thing or two about weed whackin'.

His farm is just out west. Go talk to him and see if he'd be willing to help us.

passages.title: Growing the Farm I: The Weeds
passages.text:
Oh yeah, Farmer Yoon. I've seen him around town.

Seems like a nice enough fella.

passages.title: Bloodied Skies
passages.text:
We have cannons set up on the top of the towers flanking the main gate. They are our best method to clear the skies when the flying mantid try to pass over the wall, like they are now.

Looks like you're on, <name>.

passages.title: Bloodied Skies
passages.text: You've got good aim, <class>. I'll remember that the next time the fliers come.

passages.title: Watery Woes
passages.text:
I love fishing. I'd be enjoying myself much more, however, if I had my bait and my lures. They were thrown away in a... a misunderstanding with my wife, Rin.

<Gladecaster Lang sighs.>

Should I let a whole day of fishing be ruined, just because of a little domestic squabble? No! All I need is bugs and feathers, after all, and this glade is filled with those two things.

Care to help a fisherman out?

passages.title: Watery Woes
passages.text: I refuse to not fish. Fishing's who I am!

passages.title: Watery Woes
passages.text:
Finally, someone who understands me. Fishing is what it's all about, right?

Maybe I should leave New Cifera... just pack up my things and join the Anglers, down in the south. Of course, I couldn't leave my family behind...

But still... a pandaren can dream, right?

passages.title: A Crocolisk Tale
passages.text:
How could this crocolisk have grown so large?

Certainly, rumors exist of very old crocolisks that have grown to enormous sizes... but this female can't be more than a dozen years old.

Perhaps someone in New Cifera can shed some light on the subject.

passages.title: A Crocolisk Tale
passages.text: What's that you've got there?

passages.title: A Crocolisk Tale
passages.text:
This tail came from a crocolisk? Funny, we don't get many crocs this far upstream.

Have you seen some of the enormous fruits and vegetables that our farmers can grow? Your crocolisk grew so large for the same reason - there's something in the water.

What it is, we're not quite sure... but we count it among our blessings. Humongous vegetables are great. The odd giant crocolisk every now and again is really just a side effect.

passages.title: The Battle Ring
passages.text:
We have some fresh trainees that are far from being a danger to you, but in numbers, they may prove enough of a challenge. And if not, they could use the lesson in humility.

Step into the battle ring when you're ready. Don't go easy on them.

passages.title: The Battle Ring
passages.text: Step into the ring. Show them how a real <class> fights.

passages.title: The Battle Ring
passages.text: Very impressive. It seems they have much learning to do. I'll see to that.

passages.title: Water, Water Everywhere
passages.text:
How'd you like to make yourself useful?

The season's been awful dry lately. I need someone to water the crops out in the Heartland. Here's the thing: I need you to water ALL of the crops.

I keep a few kites with Wing Nga, the flightmaster across the way. Grab one of those kites, then throw water on any areas that look dry and dusty.

passages.title: Water, Water Everywhere
passages.text: Just come back when you're done. And don't break any of my kites.

passages.title: Water, Water Everywhere
passages.text: Hmph! I knew you were a good waterer when I first saw you. You've got good watering arms.

passages.title: Chasing the Chicken
passages.text:
Say, you there! <name>, was it? I've got a problem, and I need someone with better legs than mine to help me solve it.

My prize-winning chicken has flown the coop! Now she's out in the open, mingling with the other hens, wild birds, and... <gulp> ill-intentioned roosters.

My farm is west of here, south of the Skyrange. Could you find her, and bring her back to me?

passages.title: Chasing the Chicken
passages.text: I swear, she's never done this before.

passages.title: Chasing the Chicken
passages.text:
You found her! You've got an eye for fowl, kid.

I'll hold onto her for now. Don't worry, I'll make sure she's punished later.

passages.title: Pest Problems
passages.text:
One of my farmhands, Wika-Wika, has been tilling the soil in my westernmost field. I understand he's had some problems with pests.

He's got plenty of pesticide to spray the bugs that eat my crops, but I'm afraid he has no way to deal with the marmots.

Would you lend him a hand? With rampant hozen and virmen attacks, I can't afford to lose crops to simple pests.

passages.title: Pest Problems
passages.text: Well, good. That that's taken care of. Neatly done, <race>.

passages.title: Weed War II
passages.text:
Ssshhay... d'you know that guy over on the farm, with the... the *hic*... the weed problem? Gai Lan, I think his name was. I love that guy, man.

Anywayshh, he said that if I *hic* sent an adventurer over to go pick his weeds, he'd get me some ale.

It's jusht a few weeds, not too many, probably.

*hic*

passages.title: Weed War II
passages.text: Thanks, mishter *hic* <name>.

passages.title: Money Matters
passages.text:
I love working in the market, although there's one aspect of this job I really dislike: collecting debts.

While most pandaren debts are simply due to laziness, there are a few unsavory characters around town who simply don't want to pay, and there's some who are just too poor.

A few people here in town owe me money. Could you go talk to them, and remind them about what they owe?

passages.title: Money Matters
passages.text: You know, it's kind of nice having a thug... er, I mean, <class>... like you around.

passages.title: Money Matters
passages.text: I'm glad that nasty business is over with. Nobody gave you any trouble, did they?

passages.title: They Don't Even Wear Them
passages.text:
A few weeks ago, a group of those jumpy little Springtail virmen broke into my lockbox and stole several handfuls of my jewelry. I've since found a few pieces, but they still have most of my collection.

If you're headed up to the Springtail Crag, in the cliffs to the north, you should keep an eye out for them. I'd love to get my jewelry back.

passages.title: They Don't Even Wear Them
passages.text: Can you believe how irresponsible and juvenile those virmen are? Don't they know how much that jewelry COST?

passages.title: They Don't Even Wear Them
passages.text:
Oh, <name>! I'd kiss you right here and now if you weren't... well, if you weren't covered in virmen dust.

Thanks, though!

passages.title: Not in Chee-Chee's Backyard
passages.text:
Not all hozen are the same. Chee-Chee's tribe was forest hozen... came from Jade Forest. Pretty easy to get along with.

The Kunzen invaders... they come from mountains, far to the north. Not nearly as nice as Chee-Chee.

They come into our green land, take our things, leave big mess behind.

Chee-Chee wants to kill them. You like to help?

passages.title: Not in Chee-Chee's Backyard
passages.text: Great! Chee-Chee knew you could do it!

passages.title: Where It Counts
passages.text:
I've been watching those Kunzen hozen, and I've noticed a consistent pattern. Whenever they're getting ready to attack, they participate in strange, barbaric rituals around their totem.

If we can disrupt this ritual, not only will we put off any impending attacks, we can deal a huge blow to their morale! So get in there, rough them up, and make as much of a mess as possible!

passages.title: Where It Counts
passages.text: What are you waiting for? Get up there and have some fun!

passages.title: Where It Counts
passages.text: Hah! They'll be cleaning that mess up for days.

passages.title: The Kunzen Legend-Chief
passages.text:
I've heard people talk about the hozen like they're just some tribe of barely-functional idiots... but that's not true! They have brains, too - they just don't all like to use them that much.

I've heard that the Kunzen tribe has two chiefs - one in charge of fighting, and one in charge of stories, lore, and history.

What I wouldn't give to see what kind of stories they tell...

passages.title: The Kunzen Legend-Chief
passages.text: I'll bet hozen legends aren't that much different than our own.

passages.title: The Kunzen Legend-Chief
passages.text:
Wow! Look at this! It's...

<Fish flips through the pages, and her face sours.>

Oh, I think that's a dirty picture. But the rest of this is very interesting! I just love learning how other creatures think. Thanks, <name>!

passages.title: You Have to Burn the Ropes
passages.text:
I, umm... well...

Oh, never mind. It was a stupid idea.

It's just that, I was thinking that maybe we can stop the Kunzen hozen from attacking us without having to, you know... KILL anything. I noticed a few ropes on the side of the mountain. I think they're using them to climb down to our farms and...

No, forget it. It was a silly idea anyways.

passages.title: You Have to Burn the Ropes
passages.text:
<Ella's face lights up.>

You did it? For me? Oh, thank you, thank you, thank you, thank you!

passages.title: The Truffle Shuffle
passages.text:
I like to bake with truffles... when I can find them. They only grow up on the Skyrange, and in very, very scarce amounts.

They're a fantastic ingredient, but we can't risk over-farming them. That's why we need to replace what we've taken. Bring me a handful of adult truffles, and plant some of these spores in their place.

passages.title: The Truffle Shuffle
passages.text: We won't need many truffles. They're for flavor only, really.

passages.title: The Truffle Shuffle
passages.text:
These will do nicely.

Now, <name>... stand closer. Let me show you a thing or two about baking...

passages.title: The Mile-High Grub
passages.text:
Have you ever tried Mushan Tail Stew? Chances are, if you have, that it was stringy and tasteless. You see, there's a trick to making the perfect Mushan Tail Stew: you need to cook it at high elevation.

I've already gathered the ingredients. Take this pot up to the Kunzen Village, up in the mountains to the west, and prepare the stew over their bonfire.

passages.title: The Mile-High Grub
passages.text:
I used to make daily trips into the mountains, just to practice making this stew.

I was younger, then.

passages.title: The Mile-High Grub
passages.text: This is fantastic! You are quite the aspiring cook, <race>.

passages.title: Simian Sabotage
passages.text:
The hozen steal from us, and we keep stealing our stuff back. It has to stop sometime.

<Farmer Yoon hands you a barrel of fireworks.>

Find some of our stolen supplies in their mountain camp to the west, and place these fireworks beside them. Hopefully, if they see the explosions, they'll think our supplies are defective and stop stealing altogether.

It's worth a shot, right?

passages.title: Simian Sabotage
passages.text: Good luck up there, <name>.

passages.title: Simian Sabotage
passages.text: Hopefully they're put off from stealing any more of our supplies. I know I personally wouldn't want to drink any explosive beer, or use an explosive rake.

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text:
Two words: Tiger Blood!

This is gonna sell better than saronite back on the black market. Especially once I finish spreading a rumor about how it makes you all buff and stuff.

And this jungle is just full of tigers. Can you round up a few vials of tiger blood for me? I'll cut you in on the scam.

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text: I like hunting with Nesingwary and all but he's in it for the hunting. I'm in it for the profit, and he doesn't pay us.

passages.title: Profit Mastery
passages.text: Great! This stuff is gonna make me a mint back in Kalimdor. Here's your cut.

passages.title: The Blastmaster
A Dish for Gina
passages.text: Bringing food to me on the busiest market day? What a sweetheart you are!

passages.title: A Dish for Old Hillpaw
passages.text:
I haven't had this dish since my wife died. Somehow, she must have sent you to me.

Thank you, <race>.

passages.title: A Dish for Haohan
passages.text: Charbroiled Tiger Steak for me? How did you know this was my favorite dish?

passages.title: A Dish for Jogu
passages.text: Nothing like a delicious cold brew, and some Sauteed Carrots to wash it down.

passages.title: Enraged Vengeance
passages.text:
<The Swordmistress does not look well. There's a darkness to her eyes uncharacteristic of the pandaren.>

I don't think I've ever been as... as furious as now. What betrayal!

I fought them off when they attacked, killed a few here, but Merchant Shi is too much of a coward to let me go and finish the job!

You, do it for me. Kill them. Kill them all.

passages.title: Enraged Vengeance
passages.text: It is satisfying to hear that our enemies are dead. Perhaps you can use one of my bodyguard's weapons.

passages.title: A Gift For Tina
passages.text:
That Tina Mudclaw is in the Halfhill Market today, visiting her sister. She's really nice, but she's really hard to get gifts for!

There's a little jewel that can be found in the cliffs to the north. It's called a chrysoberyl, and it changes color when you hold it. I'll bet she doesn't have one of THOSE!

Look inside the virmen caves. I bet you'll find one really fast.

passages.title: A Gift For Tina
passages.text: Hey there, <name>! Nice to see you again.

passages.title: A Gift For Tina
passages.text:
<Tina holds the gem in her hands, and watches it change from a pale blue to a bright red.>

A chrysoberyl? That's so sweet! Was this Andi's idea?

Of course I already have several... but this one is beautiful, too. I'll add it to the collection.

passages.title: A Gift For Chee Chee
passages.text:
That crazy Chee Chee is actually pretty neat. Mah always said that hozen were nothing but trouble, but... I guess he's just a better hozen then the rest of them.

We should do something nice for him! Those mountain hozen in the west make some really fancy stir fry, and keep bowls of it inside their little hozen houses.

I bet Chee Chee would love some!

passages.title: A Gift For Chee Chee
passages.text: Mmm?

passages.title: A Gift For Chee Chee
passages.text:
For me? Me, Chee Chee?

This brings Chee Chee back to when Chee Chee was little wikkin' baby. Chee Chee's mama used to make it just like this.

passages.title: A Gift For Sho
passages.text:
Sho - that girl who lives up in the mountains - is in town today. I saw her walking toward the Halfhill Market.

Such a long walk... she must be hungry! And I think I know just the thing that she'll like.

The hozen up on the Skyrange cook a soup out of fish and apples. It sounds gross, I know... but it's awesome. You'll find it near their big, scary totem.

passages.title: A Gift For Sho
passages.text: Oh! Hello, <name>.

passages.title: A Gift For Sho
passages.text:
I was famished! How'd you know? Who told you?

Andi, huh? That kid's gonna grow up to be a real heartbreaker someday...

passages.title: A Gift For Fish
passages.text:
That Fish Fellreed is kind of weird. First of all, her name's Fish. That's weird.

Once you talk to her, though, she's really a nice lady. Did you know that she's an animal lover?

I've got an idea! The Kunzen hozen, in the mountains to the west, make little animal statues and put them in their huts to scare off bad guys. I bet Fish would LOVE something weird like that!

passages.title: A Gift For Fish
passages.text: Hey, <name>! What's up?

passages.title: A Gift For Fish
passages.text:
Aww, look at him! He's ADORABLE! With his fuzzy little tail, and his...

<She composes herself.>

I mean, ah... thanks, dude. It's pretty cool.

passages.title: A Gift For Ella
passages.text:
That poor Ella. She's so shy! I saw her standing in the Halfhill Market, looking really hungry, but afraid to talk to any of the chefs.

We should bring her some food! And not any boring food - something special.

The Kunzen hozen make spicy shrimp dumplings from ingredients they've stolen from our farms. I don't like spicy food, but Ella might!

passages.title: A Gift For Ella
passages.text: Oh, umm... hi.

passages.title: A Gift For Ella
passages.text:
You didn't have to do this! I didn't need any... any...

<Ella eyes the dumplings, and her mouth begins to water.>

Well, maybe I was a little hungry. Thanks, <name>. And give my thanks to Andi, as well.

passages.title: A Gift For Fung
passages.text:
Farmer Fung is pretty mean, and just a little scary. Mah always said that he was one of the best farmers in the valley, though.

I think I know the perfect gift for a mean, kind of scary guy like him.

There's some big plainshawks that circle the hills to the west of here. You should get one, find a big piece of meat, and then ask Kol Ironpaw to grill it up!

passages.title: A Gift For Fung
passages.text: Harrumph!

passages.title: A Gift For Fung
passages.text:
Hey! Where'd you get that? I thought they were out of plainshawk!

Andi asked you to get this for me? Huh. Maybe I underestimated that kid.

passages.title: A Gift For Old Hillpaw
passages.text:
Old Hillpaw has about a million chickens on his farm... but that's not what he REALLY loves.

I saw. He collects blue feathers.

I don't realy know where to get a blue feather around here, but I do know where to find some blue pearls!

Check the oysters in Cattail Lake to the northwest. I'm sure a blue pearl will look nice with his feather collection!

passages.title: A Gift For Old Hillpaw
passages.text: <name>! You startled me.

passages.title: A Gift For Old Hillpaw
passages.text:
Well would you look at that! I'll have to keep this somewhere that the chickens can't get to.

Did Andi tell you to get this for me? Funny kid, that one.

passages.title: A Gift For Haohan
passages.text:
Haohan Mudclaw is the big boss of the Tillers union and the richest guy in the Valley! He's been nice to let me stay here, so I want to do something nice for him.

He likes expensive stuff, like ruby shards, but I don't have a lot of money, so I need to get him something else.

I know! I've seen a great big fish in Cattail Lake! We should get one of its teeth as a gift!

passages.title: A Gift For Haohan
passages.text: Need something, <class>?

passages.title: A Gift For Haohan
passages.text:
Well, would you look at that! You don't see a tooth like THAT everyday.

You been hunting sharks, <class>?

Thank you, <name>. And send my thanks to Andi, as well.

passages.title: A Gift For Jogu
passages.text:
Sometimes I feel sad for Jogu. He's the only jinyu around, and I don't think he has any friends. Other than his smelly bottle, of course.

You know what? I've got an idea. Farmer Yoon has a basket of craneberries inside his house, and a few apples as well. I'm sure you could bring them to the stillmaster in the Halfhill Market and get him to brew something special for Jogu.

passages.title: A Gift For Jogu
passages.text: Hmm?

passages.title: A Gift For Jogu
passages.text:
<Jogu takes a long swig from the hooch.>

That'sh it! I've got a new favorite drink. An' it'sh this one!

You know what, <name>? You're alright. I mean it, man!

passages.title: A Gift For Gina
passages.text:
Have you seen Gina Mudclaw, the market girl? She has it all - looks, brains, and nice big tummy. Could you deliver a gift for me?

I wanted to pick some orchids that grow on top of the big hills to the west, but I can't climb that high. Could you pick a few and bring them to Gina?

Oh, and when you see her... tell her I said "hi".

passages.title: A Gift For Gina
passages.text: Hey there!

passages.title: A Gift For Gina
passages.text:
These are beautiful! Did you get these for me?

Ahh... so they're from Andi, are they? I think I know somebody who's getting a kiss on the forehead later this afternoon...

passages.title: At the Yak Wash
passages.text:
Look, my father is crazy. I love him, but he's crazy.

These yaungol managed to completely obliterate our ranch and scattered our yaks every which way.

If I know my father though, he's going to try to go head to head with the yaungol to get the yaks back.

Can you help us round up some of the yaks so my father doesn't do anything stupid?

Just ride them over to the Yak Wash so we can clean them up and sell them to the grummles.

passages.title: At the Yak Wash
passages.text:
The grummles always insist they have better luck with cleaned yaks.

As long as they pay more I'm not going to argue. We need the gold. Now more than ever.

passages.title: At the Yak Wash
passages.text: Well done, stranger! Hopefully we'll be able to cash these in and recoup some of the damages the yaungol inflicted.

passages.title: Back in Yak
passages.text:
I wasn't lying about your reward. Here, take these washed yaks to the grummle caravan master Eightcoins.

You can find him at the Grummle Bazaar west of here. He'll credit us and give you a delivery fee.

He may be short, but he is our biggest customer.

Return to me if you lose the yaks. More often than not they just come right back here anyway. Once they've been cleaned that is.

passages.title: Back in Yak
passages.text: And what have we here?

passages.title: Back in Yak
passages.text: Ah! I can smell the luck from here. The Muskpaws always have good yaks for sale.

passages.title: The Waterspeaker's Staff
passages.text:
There is great dissent in Inkgill, <race>. Elder Shai Hu drank the sha-corrupted waters of the mere, and forced the others to do the same. When I protested, Orachi of the town guard confiscated my ritual staff and banished me.

Now, I am not only an exile, I am unable to speak with the waters that once gave me guidance!

I am not a fighter. But if you are, perhaps you can recover my staff from Orachi? He is in town to our north.

passages.title: The Waterspeaker's Staff
passages.text: Have you found the staff?

passages.title: The Waterspeaker's Staff
passages.text: Good. Now we have some hope of redeeming this situation.

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote I: Yak Attack
passages.text:
The next voting member on the Tiller's council is Farmer Fung, and it's easy to see why.

That man's vegetables are the biggest in the valley! I only hope that someday I can grow pumpkins as big as his.

If we hope to join the Tillers, he would be the next person to convince.

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote I: Yak Attack
passages.text: Oh? You're with that new farmer in town, aren't you?

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote II: On the Loose
passages.text:
You want my vote for Farmer Yoon? Ha! You're joking, right?

Listen, I'm not going to vote for some citypaw with no lick a' knowledge about farming the earth.

It would be an embarrassment to farm alongside you or that Yoon shmuck.

Now let me deal with my own problems. Some devil let my prize yaks loose, and now they're running wild northwest of Halfhill.

If I could just get my yaks back, then maybe I'd be able to sleep at night.

passages.title: Farmer Fung's Vote II: On the Loose
passages.text:
<Farmer Fung stares at you with his jaw on the floor.>

I... I can't believe... YOU recovered all of my prized shagskins!

Do you... do you know what this means to me?

My family's only been good at two things - raising enormous vegetables and raising yaks.

The shagskins you see are the result of generations of work.

You have saved my family's legacy, <name>.

passages.title: Nana's Vote I: Nana's Secret Recipe
passages.text:
The next vote we'll need is from Nana Mudclaw. She's Haohan's grandmother, and she's been a Tiller longer than you and I have been alive!

She's still working at the Tillers building in Halfhill. Why don't you pay her a visit?

passages.title: Nana's Vote I: Nana's Secret Recipe
passages.text: Yes, Nana Mudclaw... that is me. I may be old, dear, but I haven't lost my memory. Old Man Whitewhiskers, on the other hand, is another story.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote I: Bungalow Break-In
passages.text:
This is going to be tough, <name>.

The last vote we need comes from Haohan Mudclaw, the head of the Tillers Union.

I know he wasn't too keen on us to start, but we've learned so much about farming, I'm sure he'll have a change of heart!

Go speak to him. You can be very convincing, right?

passages.title: Haohan's Vote I: Bungalow Break-In
passages.text: What do you want?

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: The Broken Wagon
passages.text:
Hey <name>. I've been looking at that wagon every day, day in and day out, since the day I moved in. Quite an eyesore, don't you think?

I heard in town that Fish Fellreed is quite handy with tools. She might be able to fix it up, and then we could turn that patch of land into a plot for farming.

Why don't you talk to her and see if she'd be willing to do the job?

passages.title: Growing the Farm II: The Broken Wagon
passages.text: You need my help fer somethin'? You came to the right gal!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote III: Pure Poison
passages.text:
All right, <name>. This is our big chance!

Mr. Mudclaw's farm is in big trouble. Those mountain hozen are coming down at night, wrecking his crops and eating his hard-earned harvest.

We've got to get rid of them for good, and I know just how to do it.

Back in the day, my grandpa showed me how to mix a wounding poison to deal with the pests on the farm.

The virmen warrens to the north hold the key ingredients for my mixture.

Don't look so worried, <name>! I'm pretty sure this is going to work.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote III: Pure Poison
passages.text: The hozen are going to get a big surprise!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote III: Pure Poison
passages.text:
You got the ingredients? Good work!

Now I just need to make the concoction.

passages.title: Lost and Lonely
passages.text:
The starving, mangy dog whines piteously and attempts a brief wag of its tail.

It looks like it could use a good meal right about now.

passages.title: Lost and Lonely
passages.text: A light comes into the dog's eyes. It seems to recognize you.

passages.title: Lost and Lonely
passages.text:
The dog perks its ears up at the sight of the juicy steak.

As soon as you throw it down, the dog starts eating ravenously.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote IV: Melons For Felons
passages.text:
All right, now I happen to know that those mountain hozen love a delicious, sweet melon.

Mr. Haohan's last harvest of melons got stolen, so we're going to have to grow some of our own.

Once we have our harvest, we'll use them to lure the nasty hozen's leader out of its cave!

passages.title: Haohan's Vote IV: Melons For Felons
passages.text: Let's make sure we grow some good melons, <name>. Those crafty hozen only like the sweetest melons.

passages.title: Haohan's Vote IV: Melons For Felons
passages.text:
Wow, <name>! Those are some big melons. Those are hard to grow, and I should know because I've tried! 

I don't know how I would run this place without you, <name>.

passages.title: Growing the Farm III: The Mossy Boulder
passages.text:
Now that we're officially members of the Tillers Union, Mr. Mudclaw said he'd be happy to help us upturn this big ole' rock in the middle of our field.

Once we clear away that stone, I've got something special planned.

Run down and give him a holler to let him know that we're ready.

passages.title: Growing the Farm III: The Mossy Boulder
passages.text: Yoon needs a neighbor to lend a hand, eh? Well I'll be plenty happy to oblige.

passages.title: Learn and Grow I: Seeds
passages.text:
Well, first things first! I'm going to need lots of help 'round here.

If we're going to be partners, you've got to learn how to harvest crops, and if you wanna harvest crops you gotta plant seeds!

Now it's my understanding that a mister, uh... Grainfell? No, that wasn't it... Greedfill? That doesn't sound right...

Greenfield! That's his name! He's the man to see for seeds.

Greenfield's got a stall over at Halfhill Market, directly southeast of here - go see him and pick up some vegetable seeds.

passages.title: Learn and Grow I: Seeds
passages.text:
How'd it go, partner? Did you get those seeds from Groanfur?

Err... Greenfield?

passages.title: Learn and Grow I: Seeds
passages.text:
He waved at me! And he gave you the first pack of seeds for free?

Well, what a nice guy!

You're doing a great job so far. Here's a little... seed money. Hah!

passages.title: What Lurks Below
passages.text:
Legend tells of a great beast in the forest to the north. My son is missing and I fear he may have wandered too near its lair....

Head northwest to Krasari Falls and look for a mysterious whirlpool - this is the key to revealing what is hidden there. Kill the wretched beast and recover any clues to my son's whereabouts.

passages.title: What Lurks Below
passages.text: What news of my son?

passages.title: What Lurks Below
passages.text:
My son's ring?  What does this mean?

<Rassan appears thoughtful.>

The situation is grim, but not without hope.  My son is careless with his belongings, so perhaps he simply threw it into the pool?  Thank you for your help <name>, I will not soon forget this great favor you have done for me.

passages.title: Jagged Abalone
passages.text:
Pandaren have been harvesting jagged abalone in this area for generations. Now it's time for you to learn the ritual.

The abalone can be found just northeast of here in narsong trench. Be careful, we have noticed increased shark activity in that area recently.

passages.title: Jagged Abalone
passages.text: Did you see any sharks down there?

passages.title: Jagged Abalone
passages.text: Oh!  Looks like you found plenty of abalone out there.  Great job <name>!

passages.title: Fishing for a Bruising
passages.text:
The riverblade saurok clan is attacking one of our local fishing expeditions! They need help right away!

Thin those saurok out and help that expedition return safely!

passages.title: Fishing for a Bruising
passages.text: The expedition is safe.  Thank you <name>.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Burlap Waystation
passages.text:
Bad fortune for grummles today. Hozen have begun to ravage! They attack our supply line to the Serpent's Spine.

Can you help? We are not fighters. We are grummles. Good fortune to those who help grummles.

Go with a group of grummles to the Burlap Waystation. Keep them safe. Make sure at least one grummle survives.

Grummles shall reward. Grummles always reward.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Burlap Waystation
passages.text: Good fortune to friends of grummles.

passages.title: The Burlap Trail: To Burlap Waystation
passages.text: Many thanks and fortune to you, friend of grummles. But the journey to the Serpent's Spine is not safe yet.

passages.title: Who Knew Fish Liked Eggs?
passages.text:
Great cranes have been nesting in this area for generations. The Narsong Spires provide a sheltered area to rear their young.

Their pristine eggs are revered as bait for catching the silver goby. Retrieve a crane egg and see if you can catch a goby!

passages.title: Who Knew Fish Liked Eggs?
passages.text: Did you catch a silver goby?

passages.title: Who Knew Fish Liked Eggs?
passages.text: The elusive silver goby!  You truly are becoming an angler <name>!

passages.title: A Monkey Idol
passages.text:
Before, grummles keep hozen from ravaging by bribing with food.

But now the Broketooth hozen south of here have their big magic idols. The Ook of Dook has trained them to use their idols to get power from sacrifices.

They are using them to kill grummles!

You must destroy these idols!

For every idol, there is a chief. Kill the chief and throw corpse on their altar.

passages.title: A Monkey Idol
passages.text: Hozen are learning that it is most bad fortune to get sacrificed on one's own altar.

passages.title: A Monkey Idol
passages.text:
A confident hozen is a dangerous hozen.

Thank you for your help, friend of grummles.

passages.title: Thumping Knucklethump
passages.text:
The Knucklethump hozen have new chief, the Ook of Dook.

He sees fear in the west, anger in the south, hatred in the north, and yaungols in the east.

And so he sets his hozen to ravage, gathering food and supplies for coming famine.

They are many Knucklethumps and dangerous.

Please, Luckydo, can you defeat their fighters?

passages.title: Thumping Knucklethump
passages.text: It is sad so many hozen must die.

passages.title: Thumping Knucklethump
passages.text: You are a true luckydo.

passages.title: Hozen Love Their Keys
passages.text:
The hozen have a yeti! They call it Old Poot Poot and keep it at the back of their cave.

Hozen are normally scared of yeti, but now they feed it grummles.

They have a Hunter Chief, Cho Cho the Wicked. Can you see if he has a key on him to the yeti shackles?

Bad fortune for hozen if a yeti is loose in their fort.

passages.title: Hozen Love Their Keys
passages.text: A luckydo would be wise to never travel near a yeti on a dirty yak.

passages.title: Hozen Love Their Keys
passages.text: Oh wow that looked like one wild ride!

passages.title: The Snackrifice
passages.text:
They took my grummles! Hozen don't eat grummles, but yeti do. And the Knucklethumps have a yeti.

Please rescue my grummles. Cut them down or let them out of cages. Rescue them any way you can.

Many fortunes and rewards if you do this.

passages.title: The Snackrifice
passages.text:
Today is a day of many good and bad fortunes. Bad fortune that hozen stole my grummles. Good fortune that my <race> saves my grummles. Bad fortune that so many hozen must die to learn lesson. Good fortune that humans are luckydos and know how to fight.

Grummles are not fighters. We carry, we explore, and we are content.

passages.title: Grummle! Grummle! Grummle!
passages.text:
Now that grummles are rescued, we need to rescue our supplies.

The Ook of Dook is only chief because he has supplies.

Go to the Dooker Dome area north west of here. Take some grummles with you. Keep them safe and get them near supply crates.

Grummles know what to do from there.

Rabbitsfoot and I will meet you there.

passages.title: Grummle! Grummle! Grummle!
passages.text: Grummles are good at carrying things.

passages.title: Grummle! Grummle! Grummle!
passages.text: Now that hozen king is going to learn why it is bad fortune to cheat grummles.

passages.title: The Leader Hozen
passages.text:
