I've got some customers lined up that wanna collect some good old fashioned ears. But not any old ears. They only want the absolute waxiest ears money can buy! 

Guess they think they're lucky or something'.

Anyways, I need you to go get 'em for me. I don't want to hurt any animals, so you'll need to get 'em from the Alliance over at Lion's Landing.

Have fun - and remember, only bring me the waxiest!

passages.title: Good Luck, Have Fun
passages.text: Ears, <name>, I wanna see some ears!

passages.title: Good Luck, Have Fun
passages.text: Good and waxy, just like they asked for. Here's your share.

passages.title: We Require More Minerals!
passages.text:
Gnomes are excavating a stone quarry to the northeast.

They're building stuff with it!

<Zazzix rolls his eyes.>

They're too stupid to realize it's special mogu stone for creating animated statues. 

WE can mix with a little Goblin magic juice to make some real big explosions!

But the stuff is heavy. They've got some of their stupid bomb-bots there for excavating the stone. Blow 'em up near slabs and you'll get chunks small enough to carry. 

Or, just kill 'em and take it. Whatever works.

passages.title: We Require More Minerals!
passages.text: You got some stone? I wanna blow stuff up!

passages.title: We Require More Minerals!
passages.text:
Ha! YES! You got me some! I'm gonna make the best bomb EVER!

Man I love bombs! Love making them, love blowin' em up...

... and yeah, that IS how I got this eyepatch. What's it to ya?

passages.title: Sentry Wards
passages.text:
We've spotted heavy air support over their base, in the form of way too many dwarves on way too many griffons. Means we can't get any vision of the area from above.

A troll... friend of mine gave us a set of Sentry Wards, which we can use to spy on their base and get a vantage point on what's going on in there.

Bad news, friend - you're going to be the one going in there.

passages.title: Sentry Wards
passages.text: Good work, <name>. I've already been getting some useful information that should help make our next offensive even more devastating.

passages.title: Hard Counter
passages.text:
We've managed to get some Demolishers on the beach, but the stupid dwarves are also out there with their stupid mortar tubes, preventing the Demolishers from pushing forward and assaulting the keep itself!

Get out there, kill some dwarves, and blow up some mortar tubes.

passages.title: Hard Counter
passages.text:
Oh heck yeah! That'll show 'em that NOBODY blows stuff up like goblins blow stuff up!

Oh, and you did good work too.

passages.title: Runnin' On Empty
passages.text:
I've never seen this quality of oil! Problem is the oil needed a little extra refinin'.

I heard of this system where you use ocean water to speed up the process. I don't have time to waste down here, so I just threw the barrels into the bay.

Pretty good idea, I know. Problem is, I'm not sure how to pull it out of the bay...

Maybe someone of your expertise could help me out.

passages.title: Runnin' On Empty
passages.text: So he found a use for the bay after all? Waste not, want not I guess!

passages.title: Runnin' On Empty
passages.text: Oh, yuck! Why are these barrels wet?! Oh nevermind! At least you got here before they made me work. I can't think of anything more horrible!

passages.title: Stacked!
passages.text:
We just filled an order this morning. How could they possibly need more already?!

My team has been workin' double-time to get these trees chopped and processed.

Problem is we have an infestation of Lion's Landing troops down here. I already risked my neck once today, I'm not goin' back out there!

Goob will go with you and help you fill this order. He's not the brightest, but he can do the heavy liftin'.

passages.title: Stacked!
passages.text: Did you get that order filled?

passages.title: Stacked!
passages.text: It's about time you showed up with this lumber order! I was just about to come down there and get it myself.

passages.title: Don't Lose Your Head
passages.text:
My probes have detected three very dangerous targets in the courtyard of Domination Keep.

They have an ogre emissary, a Kor'kron officer, and an insane goblin bomb maker.

My siege-o-matics are not ready for one on one combat so it is up to you to eliminate the targets.

Good luck! Report back to me on the Skyfire when done.

passages.title: Don't Lose Your Head
passages.text: Great work! Sorry to put good soldiers in harms way but my Auto-Demolish-o-Tronic Mk 2 isn't functional yet.

passages.title: Resource Gathering
passages.text:
Oh, the poor peasants...

They are cowards, yes, of course. But they don't know how to fight, and they go out to collect lumber for our efforts... the Horde targets them... It's just awful all around!

But, we need that lumber if we're going to hold out. Go out and collect any they've dropped.

passages.title: Resource Gathering
passages.text: Did you gather the lumber yet?

passages.title: Resource Gathering
passages.text: Good work! With this, we'll be able to finish reinforcing the structure of the keep, which will help keep people safe. You've saved lives today!

passages.title: Tower Defense
passages.text:
The gnomes are running our quarry operation to the northwest. The stone there is especially tough - the gnomes tell me the mogu used it to fashion their constructs. 

I don't know. What I do know is that we use that stone to build our towers, and the Horde has dispatched the Bilgewater goblins to steal it from us.

Get out there and get some back. By the way - collateral damage may break up the stone slabs there. If so, pick that up, too.

passages.title: Tower Defense
passages.text: You brought us the stone yet?

passages.title: Tower Defense
passages.text: Alright! We'll get that stone mortared into the cracks in our walls faster than a Dwarf downs a pint.

passages.title: Siege Damage
passages.text:
The Horde got the bright idea to send Bilgewater goblins to attack our quarry.

They've been packing heavy explosives - heavy explosives that will react with the ammunition in their demolishers.

Kill the Bilgewater goblins until you find an explosive, plant it on one of the demolishers... and BOOM! Siege ended.

passages.title: Siege Damage
passages.text: We need you to take out those demolishers, soldier!

passages.title: Siege Damage
passages.text: You really showed them who owns this beach, <name>. Good work!

passages.title: Burn Out!
passages.text:
Those goblins are gettin' out of hand! First they level the forest and set up that abomination of a rig. Then, they start dumpin' their oil barrels into the bay!

We got to put a stop to this madness! At the very least we need ta set them back.

We need to take out their fuel supply! Maybe you'll even get to kill a few goblins in the process!

passages.title: Burn Out!
passages.text:
Wish I could've been there to watch their fuel burn! Probably put on quite the show.

You've done well, <name>!

passages.title: Necessary Breaks
passages.text:
It goes against me nature to break things on purpose, but in this case it's necessary.

That rig the goblins are usin' is held together by a wish an' some bubblegum. We need to exploit the situation a little more.

We have some saboteurs down there already, but we can use someone of your expertise to hurry the job along.

Get down there an' start breakin' and stealin' some valves!

passages.title: It's Only Right
passages.text:
This is barbaric warfare, <class>! We've lost so many trying to keep the Bilgewater operation from spreading any further.

Those fallen soldiers fought honorably and deserved to be given their last rights. At the very least we need to be able to notify their next of kin.

Perhaps you can collect their identification tags so we can honor them in some small way.

passages.title: It's Only Right
passages.text: Even warfare should have some courtesies.

passages.title: It's Only Right
passages.text: You have done these soldiers a great service, <name>. The only thing left to do is make sure they did not die in vain.

passages.title: Beastmaster's Hunt: The Crane
passages.text:
Along with the snare, you get some advice on crane hunting:

The greatest cranes of the Krasarang Wilds are not tempted by simple things like food. You will need to play on the creatures' emotions if you wish to draw them from their hiding places in the jungle.

Cranes abound on both the Cradle of Chi-ji and the Narsong Spires, both of which can be found east of here. Pluck those cranes' quills, then place them in a visible spot near the Crane Temple. Your quarry will come running to you.

passages.title: Beastmaster's Hunt: The Crane
passages.text: This is the spot, near the Crane Temple.

passages.title: Beastmaster's Hunt: The Crane
passages.text: You place the feathers in the dirt, then look off in the direction of the temple...

passages.title: Beastmaster's Hunt: The Crane
passages.text:
Along with the snare, you get some advice on crane hunting:

The greatest cranes of the Krasarang Wilds don't care about simple things like food. You need to play on the creatures' emotions if you want to draw them out of the jungle.

There's plenty of cranes on the Cradle of Chi-ji and on the Narsong Spires, both to the west of here. Pluck some of those cranes' quills, then put them in a visible spot near the Crane Temple. Your quarry will come running to you.

passages.title: Beastmaster's Hunt: The Crane
passages.text: This is the spot, near the Crane Temple.

passages.title: Beastmaster's Hunt: The Crane
passages.text: You place the feathers in the dirt, then look off in the direction of the temple...

passages.title: Ancient's Fall
passages.text: The crane has fallen.

passages.title: End of an Elder
passages.text: The tiger has fallen.

passages.title: A Colossal Victory
passages.text: The crab has fallen.

passages.title: A Colossal Victory
passages.text: Well fought, <name>.

passages.title: Ancient's Fall
passages.text: The crane has fallen.

passages.title: End of an Elder
passages.text: The tiger has fallen.

passages.title: A Colossal Victory
passages.text: The crab has fallen.

passages.title: A Colossal Victory
passages.text: Well fought, <name>.

passages.title: One Magical, Flying Kingdom's Trash...
passages.text:
Before we enter into a business relationship, I am required by the terms of my rehabilitation program to inform you that I am a recovering potion addict.

There, now that THAT's out of the way, let's talk portals!

You see, the big portals in the cities - the ones running all day and night - leak tons of magical energy. It crystallizes around the edges and is generally regarded as trash.

But I noticed during my, uh... hiatus in the sewers of Dalaran, that these shards still had power.

Interested?

passages.title: One Magical, Flying Kingdom's Trash...
passages.text:
I knew you would be!

Here's the catch - the shards, in their current state, are unstable. But the soil in this valley is renowned for its magical properties! I am sure if you were to "plant" the shard, a very interesting reaction would take place.

It could stabilize, leaving you with a functioning portal! Or... it might tear open a magical rift that spits out transdimensional horrors!

My gut tells me it will be a little of both, but there's only one way to know for sure.

Here, take a sample!

passages.title: Krasarang Steampot
passages.text:
The Boss-Lady desires crabs!

Why are you looking at me like that? It's not uncommon for a classy person, such as her loveliness, to want crab for dinner. What did you think I meant?

There are some big crabs wandering around on Bilgewater Beach that should be suitable for her refined palate.

Bring Sezik the best crab meat you can find!

passages.title: Krasarang Steampot
passages.text: Boss-Lady wants a steampot does she? Well, maybe she should come down here and make it herself!

passages.title: Krasarang Steampot
passages.text:
This meat is disgusting! It's going to take every spice I have to cover that smell up.

Only the best for the Boss-Lady!

<Sezik grins and winks at you.>

passages.title: Grave Circumstances
passages.text:
The Court of Bones crawls with mogu forces. Endlessly do they perform their rituals of lightning and thunder.

If our mission to take this island is to succeed, then we cannot allow them to hold such a strategic position.

They must be eliminated.

passages.title: Grave Circumstances
passages.text: The mogu are powerful, but with cunning and tenacity, we can defeat them.

passages.title: Grave Circumstances
passages.text: Excellent. You have dealt the mogu a blow that they shall not easily forget.

passages.title: This Just Won't Do
passages.text:
The Zandalari here are very powerful, <class>. They should not be underestimated. We cannot afford to ignore them as a threat simply because they do not wield swords.

More arrive every day, and with them centuries of magic knowledge. This threat must be dealt with, and quickly.

Aid us in clearing this area, <class>. Perhaps we can even learn something from them in the process.

passages.title: This Just Won't Do
passages.text: Magic can be a great ally or your worst enemy. Let's not leave it to chance.

passages.title: This Just Won't Do
passages.text:
It's impressive how easily you were able to cut them down.

Perhaps, it's you they should not underestimate. Thank you for your assistance, <class>.

passages.title: Maximum Capacitor
passages.text:
The mines north of here are being used to extract Ghost Iron ore and energize it with lightning energy.

We need to destroy the drills they use to extract the ore. They are impervious to normal attack, but can be overloaded using the proper methods.

Oh - and while you're there, take out whoever is running the operation.

passages.title: Save Our Scouts!
passages.text:
The heavy mogu presence in the mines let us know it was a place of great importance - but we needed to gather more information on their activities there, so we sent agents into the mines to spy on them.

Unfortunately, many were captured, and we've found that some are being tortured in the mines. You have to go rescue them - nobody deserves what they are going through...

And, when you finish, kill whoever captured them. No mercy, adventurer!

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text:
So Jaina and the Kirin Tor think they can push us out again? I will not stand by and allow them to repeat the events of Dalaran!

This time we fight back! This time we do the pushing...

Go to Violet Rise and slay any Kirin Tor agent you find.

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text:
So, Violet Rise runs red with the blood of our enemies? Well done, <name>.

This will be an ongoing battle I fear. We must continue to show our strength here.

passages.title: Bilgewater Infiltrators
passages.text:
There is nothing more unnerving than walking along, minding your own business, and hearing someone following you. I swear I hear it all over the place down here! We're being watched!

I have a feeling the entire beach is just crawling with spies!

I made some improvements to our infrared goggle tech to put an end to the sabotogery. That's right sabotogery! Now I just need you to try 'em out! Feel free to dispose of any spies you happen to catch.

passages.title: Bilgewater Infiltrators
passages.text:
Very nice, <name>! I knew it! I knew there were Alliance sneaking around down there!

No one messes with a Bilgewater rig and gets away with it!

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
We assault the mogu at the Court of Bones, but I fear we merely send them fodder for their abominable rituals.

The mogu do not merely kill their prisoners - they steal their souls and imbue them in machinations of stone, or reforge the fallen into ghostly tools of war.

Horde or Alliance, it matters not. We cannot allow the mogu to bolster their numbers.

Go into the crypts. Free any prisoners that are still living.

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. You have lightened my heart of a heavy burden through your heroic actions.

I will remember your efforts on this day.

passages.title: Storming the Beach
passages.text:
Our lumber supply is being jeopardized by constant attacks from Lion's Landing.

We've been able to keep the attackers at bay, but it's time to really show 'em some muscle!

Head down to the coast and start splitting some skulls!

passages.title: Storming the Beach
passages.text: Excellent work down there, <name>! That should keep 'em outta our hair for awhile!

passages.title: WANTED: Chief Engineer Cogwrench
passages.text:
Wanted for crimes against the Bilgewater Operation!

Chief Engineer Cogwrench was last seen building what appeared to be a giant spider tank on the edge of Bilgewater Beach.

Extreme caution should be used when approaching.

A large reward has been posted for Cogwrench's destruction.

passages.title: WANTED: Chief Engineer Cogwrench
passages.text: Excellent work, <class>! This brings us one step closer to pushing them out of Pandaria!

passages.title: WANTED: Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson
passages.text:
Wanted for crimes against the Domination Point forces!

Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson is responsible for leading several ground assaults against the Bilgewater lumber operation.

Last spotted occupying an island south of Quickchop's Lumber Farm.

passages.title: WANTED: Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson
passages.text: Do not return without his blood on your hands!

passages.title: WANTED: Lieutenant Ethan Jacobson
passages.text: It's a good day when another Lion's Landing leader falls, <class>! Good work!

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text:
The Reliquary is having a field day out here, literally!

Every day, the researchers find more relics to study and catalog.

Recently, one of our adventurers found this scroll at the Court of Bones.

I believe that this incantation can be used to call beyond the grave. And if my Mogu is up to date, I'd say you should use it in the last room in the Hall of the Exalted.

Would you be willing to test out my theory?

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text: Ah yes, you've just confirmed my theory! Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text:
The creatures the Zandalari ride don't start out so big, nor do they start out the vicious and loyal creatures they become.

If you can frighten some of the hatchling skyscreamers away from the beach, perhaps they will have a chance at a real life.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text: You have returned, <race>. It is my hope that these young skyscreamers have the lives they deserve without dealing with the harsh treatment of the trolls.

passages.title: Very Disarming
passages.text:
Look around you, <class>. What do you see? I see an opportunity.

The casters here work to imbue the Zandalari weapons with powerful magic. As if a sharp blade isn't enough to cut even the strongest foe down to size.

In my scouting I've noticed the weapons are not very well guarded. This is where you come in...

If we can steal a few of these weapons we may be able to use them. At the very least they are out of enemy hands.

passages.title: Very Disarming
passages.text: So? What did you find?

passages.title: Very Disarming
passages.text:
Excellent work, <class>!

These weapons are terrifying on their own, nevermind the magic they are infused with.

passages.title: Knowledge Is Power
passages.text:
The Zandalari here practice a different kind of magic. We must understand it before we can defeat it, <class>.

Their control over the arcane and shadow is impressive. I wish to learn how they have achieved what so many others have not.

I believe their ritual artifacts may hold the answers I seek. Bring me a sampling of the artifacts you find, and I will ensure you are rewarded properly.

passages.title: Knowledge Is Power
passages.text: Did you find the artifacts?

passages.title: Knowledge Is Power
passages.text: These will do nicely, <class>. Excellent work.

passages.title: Flash! Aaaaaahhhh!
passages.text:
The gnomes have brought their flying contraptions. I want my skies CLEAR!

Get up there on whatever mount you have with you and destroy those paltry devices.

You may use this grog I "acquired" from our goblin allies. It would be better served blasting down gyrocopters than in the gullet of those little green fiends.

passages.title: Flash! Aaaaaahhhh!
passages.text: Hellscream's eyes are upon you.

passages.title: Flash! Aaaaaahhhh!
passages.text: Ha! Simple mechanical toys are no match for a well aimed bottle of grog.

passages.title: Bug Off!
passages.text:
This cave is crawlin' with nasty shale spiders! How's a girl supposed to get any work done with them gobbling up the miners AND the ore?!

This seemed like a good opportunity to use my newest invention, Bug Off. See, all you have to do is spray this stuff all over the shale spiders. They hate it and it doesn't seem to have many long term side-effects for the miners!

What could possibly go wrong?

Take this handy sprayer and get to work!

passages.title: Bug Off!
passages.text: Shale spiders. Why did it have to be shale spiders?!

passages.title: Bug Off!
passages.text: Now that's what I like to hear! I bet those spiders will think twice before messing with a Bilgewater operation again!

passages.title: Universal Remote-Explode
passages.text:
The Mecha-Pounders are really making things difficult down here, but I think I may have the solution!

I made this universal remote for myself, but it looks like I hit a specific frequency that has an useful result!

Apparently this frequency weakens their armor!

Use the remote to take them down a few notches then punch 'em in the face!

passages.title: Universal Remote-Explode
passages.text: How'd the remote work for ya?

passages.title: Universal Remote-Explode
passages.text:
Good work, <name>! I saw the fireworks from here!

Who knew being a genius was this easy? I don't even have to try anymore.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
I have three magisters entrenched in Ihgaluk Crag, monitoring the saurok and - where they can - turning them against the mogu. I need you to find them and see if they need any supplies or assistance.

They will be concealed from view. Look for shimmering columns of light within the saurok village.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
<The archmage listens carefully to your report.>

I understand. Thank you for your aid, <class>.

passages.title: Captive Audience
passages.text:
The Kirin Tor have gone too far! Now they hold our fellow Sunreavers as war prisoners!

There will be no discussion of prisoner exchange. We will handle this ourselves.

Go to Violet Rise and free as many prisoners as you can. Do not get captured yourself. We cannot afford to lose you too.

passages.title: Captive Audience
passages.text:
Those you have rescued today would no doubt thank you, if they had the strength.

Our task here will be ongoing. I refuse to leave anyone behind!

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text:
Jaina possesses several very powerful magic artifacts. These items travel with her at all times, and are never far from her grasp. I have an interest in one of these items.

A tome, filled with knowledge, passed from one archmage to another. I have only ever seen glimpses of it.

Now that we fight on opposite sides I see no issue in removing the tome from her possession.

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text: Do you have it? Do you have the book?!

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text: I have desired this book for many years, <race>. It's power is too immense to describe. You have done me a great service.

passages.title: Charged Moganite
passages.text:
We have been dispatching spies into the Kirin Tor base of operations on a daily basis. Some had orders to recover charged moganite from the enemy and bring it here.

They have not returned, and I can confirm they have left the Kirin Tor base.

Search the jungle between here and there and find any of the charged moganite that might have been lost in transit. Bring it to me and we will put it to good use.

passages.title: Charged Moganite
passages.text: Well done, champion. This artifact will be put to better use in our hands than in the hands of the Kirin Tor.

passages.title: Tactical Mana Bombs
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer, just the <race> I was looking for. I have received another batch of tactical mana bombs that I need planted in key positions across Violet Rise to the southeast.

Here, take these. I do not trust our standard soldiers with such firepower. Oh... and don't shake them, whatever you do.

Plant one of the Kirin Tor ships, another one near their supplies, and the last on the construct they are building.

passages.title: Tactical Mana Bombs
passages.text:
I am sure the use of even these smaller mana bombs has Jaina squirming with rage. Serves her right.

Dalaran was my home before her grandparents were born. What right did she have to expel me from my home?

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The Skumblade threaten our people, but responding with all-out slaughter would be an overreaction.

A more reasonable response to their threat would be to slay some of their tribal leaders. There will be less bloodshed, and they will still respect our perimeter.

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The saurok value strength above all else. They only respond to strength.

Peace with the saurok will require some amount of bloodshed. The question is, how much?

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
I know the true price of bloodshed. I know the cost of war.

It would be simpler to blindly massacre our attackers until they yield. But is it right?

passages.title: Surgical Death
passages.text:
The Zandalari train skyscreamers to become ferocious beasts in the skies. The spiritbinders require endless sacrifices - of our people - to be brought to them. And, the jaguar warriors venture ever closer toward the heart of our camp.

Find them in Za'Tual and remove the threat.

passages.title: Surgical Death
passages.text: I shall continue my unrest until the threat is subdued, but your aid brings us closer to that goal. I thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Metalocalypse
passages.text:
You've made a good start, but now it's time to really make a dent in their operations.

Take out Metal Lord Mono-Han, of the mines.

passages.title: Fleshcrafter's End
passages.text:
The mogu responsible for the torture of the agents, Fleshcrafter Goju, stands outside the mine.

Killing him would be the only justice for what he's done to your agents.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text:
The raptors and compies of the Zandalari represent a substantial threat to our forces here. They are superb hunting beasts that can track prey over great distances and are often lethal to encounter when caught unawares.

I need you to head into the Beast Pens and cull their numbers. We need to make sure to slay them before they are fully trained.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text: Say what you will about the Zandalari but none can contest their ability to turn even the most repellant of creatures into a trained weapon.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text: We lost three good soldiers when we first arrived on this island. Killed in their sleep by compies that had snuck into their tent. Some nights I still hear the screams.

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text:
The forge lies ahead of you, and with it the heart of the mogu's weaponsmithing ability.

And beyond that, the mogu gatekeeper, who holds the key to unlocking the gate to the next part of the city.

It's time to move out!

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Good work. What you did today brings us one step closer to our ultimate goal.

passages.title: Treasures of the Thunder King
passages.text:
My scouts have returned with word that more of the treasures from Lei Shen's tomb are being brought up into the citadel. We have access to a secret sewer entrance, but a door bars us from intercepting the shipment. If we're going to succeed in this raid, we will need a key that only the most trusted of Lei Shen's forces carry.

If you get your hands on such a key, bring it to me.

You can keep whatever spoils you steal from our raid. I simply want to see that this shipment never makes it to Lei Shen.

passages.title: Treasures of the Thunder King
passages.text:
We must disrupt Lei Shen in any way we can. Anything to hinder the rise of his power. Anything to hinder his armies from being bolstered.

If that means highway robbery, I can live with that.

passages.title: Treasures of the Thunder King
passages.text:
Not entirely unsuccessful. Still, we'll do better next time.

Thanks for providing us with that key. The raid would not have gone off without you.

passages.title: Direhorn or Devilsaur
passages.text:
We have an opportunity to disrupt the Zandalari war machine as well as have a little fun in the process.

Within these beast pens, a devilsaur and a direhorn are being outfitted with armor, their minds being enslaved to the Zandalari charms.

Go into the camp and disrupt one of these binding rituals. It doesn't matter which one. Just kill those who are trying to bind the creature. This should let the fully armored beast run mad through the Zandalari camp. Then sit back and watch the hilarity ensue.

passages.title: Direhorn or Devilsaur
passages.text: So... did you decide the devilsaur or the direhorn?

passages.title: Direhorn or Devilsaur
passages.text:
Few things in this world and beyond are more entertaining than watching a rampaging ancient beast tearing through an enemy's settlement.

If times were not so dire I would consider selling tickets to such an event.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text:
The Zandalari use a series of fetishes and charms to maintain their control over their menagerie of beasts.

Two can play at that game.

I want you to find some of these fetishes and try them out on the various beasts in the Beast Pens.

Take careful note of how each beast responds to each fetish. Then report your results to me.

Maybe this will give us the edge we need against the Zandalari.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text: I heard screaming? Was that your efforts perhaps?

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text: Very interesting results. I am sure there is a mage somewhere that cares about the specifics. I, on the other hand, am just glad to hear the sound of trolls being assaulted by their own beasts.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text:
This is not a glamorous job. Let me put it to you bluntly.

The Skumblade saurok pile all of their filth into a pool in the middle of their village. This filth is so concentrated and so rancid that it has congealed into moving, animate matter.

The saurok can keep their filth-pool, but once it starts spreading outside of the village, I'd say it's time to intervene.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text: Jobs like this make me glad that I left most of my nose in the tomb.

passages.title: Disarming Irony
passages.text:
Well, it would seem the Lady Proudmoore has decided to use our own weaponry against us. Our perimeter wards reported several spies slipping through our defenses carrying tactical mana bombs.

I would enjoy the irony if these bombs were less dangerous.

Search for these bombs and disarm them. Our wards reported one near the horde ships to the north, one on a bridge to the main isle, and one near our scrying crystals on the eastern side of the Promontory.

passages.title: Disarming Irony
passages.text: Good work. The real irony is had these been normal bombs we would have had a much harder time detecting them. Some gnomish devilry could have spelled the end of our operation here.

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text:
To think, we were once on the same side! The Sunreavers' treachery caught us all off guard. Never again!

They have shown their true natures to us. Siding with Garrosh and his madness has marked them all for death.

Kill any agent of the Sunreavers that you find. We will show them no mercy here.

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text: How many have been slain?

passages.title: Old Enemies
passages.text: You have put a good dent in the Sunreaver forces here. Like vermin, there will always be more. We must be at the ready at all times.

passages.title: Desconstruction
passages.text:
The Kirin Tor constructs are primitive at best. Nevertheless, they pose a threat.

Go to Violet Rise and dismantle Jaina's pitiful war machines. Show the Kirin Tor how easily they can be defeated!

This will be a message the Kirin Tor cannot easily ignore.

passages.title: Desconstruction
passages.text:
So the constructs have fallen? Good!

We will remind Jaina and the Kirin Tor at every turn that the Sunreavers are not to be taken lightly.

passages.title: Infiltrating the Black Temple
passages.text:
It's clear that Jubeka's soulstone has lead you here to the Black Temple. 

The question remains... why?

The only remaining option is to head inside and figure out why they were here.

passages.title: Infiltrating the Black Temple
passages.text: You have done more for this world than you can know, <class>. It is... something of a shame Kanrethad met this end. A shame, but inevitable.

passages.title: Ogudei's Lieutenants
passages.text:
There are two extremely powerful mogu spirits that the Alliance unearthed in their ineptitude.

These are choice targets for us, <class>. If you kill them and collect each of their essences, we could make great progress on decoding the history of this strange ruin.

passages.title: Ogudei's Lieutenants
passages.text: The essence isn't going to make itself, <race>.

passages.title: Ogudei's Lieutenants
passages.text: What treasures! With any luck, the spirits will return and we will be able to sample their essence further.

passages.title: It Is A Mystery
passages.text:
We have detected several... anomalies in these mines, of an arcane or spiritual nature. They are disrupting our attempts to discern the nature of the magic used in the spirit binding rituals here.

They are quite elusive, but we've managed to isolate the arcane signature of one of these anomalies, and one of our mages has enchanted this bauble with its signature.

Take the bauble. It will begin to glow more brightly as you approach the anomaly. Once you reach it, you can use the bauble to draw it out.

passages.title: It Is A Mystery
passages.text: We are still dealing with that anomaly! Hurry!

passages.title: It Is A Mystery
passages.text: Ahh, yes. I received word from one of our researchers that they are no longer troubled by that anomaly. Well done.

passages.title: Pandaren Spirit Tamer
passages.text: Legend tells of legendary pandaren spirits that roam the lands of Pandaria. Find them and defeat them in a pet battle.

passages.title: Pandaren Spirit Tamer
passages.text: I can't belive you took out those spirits!

passages.title: Dis-Assembly Required
passages.text:
Those shredders are becoming a problem down there, <class>.

We've sent in the Mecha-Pounders, but it just isn't enough. They're getting damaged faster than we can repair 'em!

I happened upon this strange remote while scouting. With a little bit of re-configurin' I think we can use it.

Try usin' it on the Jungle Shredders. Hopefully it will destroy them and then you can bring me the scrap metal.

passages.title: Dis-Assembly Required
passages.text: So what did that remote do?

passages.title: Dis-Assembly Required
passages.text: Goblin construction leaves somethin' to be desired, but it'll have to do. Good work, <name>!

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text:
You know, there is a way we can improve your S.E.L.F.I.E. cam, if you're interested. With the right focusing lens, I could add all kinds of features to that thing.

I've heard that way out on old Yojamba Isle in Stranglethorn Vale, the mother of all basilisks has been seen. Her hide is dotted with gems that'd make the perfect lens, if I could get my hands on them.

She's not going to go down easy, though. You might want to bring some friends along.

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: That crystal spine matriarch has the gems we need to upgrade your lens, any luck with that?

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: Count me surprised to hear from you again, you must be tougher than I thought. You've earned my respect, kid, here's your lens upgrade kit. Now get out there and take some S.E.L.F.I.E.S!

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text:
Hi again! Oh, I forgot to tell you! I've devised a foolproof way to improve your S.E.L.F.I.E. cam! 

In fact, with just the right gemstones, I can make a lens that would allow us to do all sorts of things!

Some fellow explorers have told me about a large basilisk out on Yojamba Isle in Stranglethorn Vale. Her hide is dotted with tons of high-quality crystals! What a perfect coincidence!

She sounds pretty tough, though! You should bring some friends!

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: Hey, stay out of my shot! Oh, it's you! Did you take down that basilisk yet?

passages.title: Crystal Clarity
passages.text: I knew from the moment we met that you were an adventurer, just like me! Here's your lens upgrade kit, now get out there and take some S.E.L.F.I.E.S!

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text:
You look like you've got a discerning eye for the visual arts, want to try your hand at photography?

I can make you one of these S.E.L.F.I.E. cameras, I just need a few parts.

For the strap, grab me a Russet Belt from one of the armor merchants around here.

I've got a shipment of extra housings waiting by the back entrance to the city, grab me one when you're over there.

Oh, and a Standard Scope, most any engineer can make you one of those.

Now get out there, kid. Fame awaits!

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text: You got those parts for me, or what? I'm busy here!

passages.title: Light Camera Action
passages.text: You're all set, kid. You've got a face the camera will love, now get out there and get shooting!

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Without warning Wrathion slices his thumb and presses it against your forehead. His blood burns to the touch, but rapidly disappears into your skin.>

There! My eye is upon you, <class>. I am watching.

The Pandaren, like the Alliance, value the concept of "Valor." There are many ways to prove yourself valorous on this continent, from daily tasks to the defeat of heroic enemies within their lair. I will let you choose your own course.

Prove your bravery to me, <name>!

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Wrathion nods slowly.>

Yes, <name>. I saw your deeds, and I was most impressed.

You are truly an instrument of change.

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Without warning Wrathion slices his thumb and presses it against your forehead. His blood burns to the touch, but rapidly disappears into your skin.>

There! My eye is upon you, <class>. I am watching.

The Pandaren, like the Horde, value the concept of "Valor." There are many ways to prove yourself valorous on this continent, from daily tasks to the defeat of heroic enemies within their lair. I will let you choose your own course.

Prove your bravery to me, <name>!

passages.title: A Test of Valor
passages.text:
<Wrathion nods slowly.>

Yes, <name>. I saw your deeds, and I was most impressed.

You are truly an instrument of change.

passages.title: Bolstering the Defenses
passages.text:
This island is a dangerous place, <name>. We have to worry about attacks from the Zandalari, mogu, saurok, and worst of all the Sunreavers.

I had perimeter wards placed on the outskirts of our camp for additional protection. In their current state they will only injure an attacker, but I'm done with warnings!

With your help we can super-charge the wards into a more deadly defense system.

passages.title: Bolstering the Defenses
passages.text:
Excellent work, <name>. Those perimeter wards should keep out all manner of filth.

With Violet Rise protected we can focus on more pressing matters.

passages.title: They All Fall Down
passages.text:
The Zandalari do not tolerate weakness in their ranks, <class>.

Those that are deemed weak are often sacrificed in barbaric ceremonies. The victims' spirits are captured and entombed within the sentries you see guarding the grounds.

I wish to study their essence. For this I will need your help.

Take this resonance crystal and siphon the spirits from the sentry corpses.

 Do not allow them to escape!

passages.title: They All Fall Down
passages.text: Have you completed your task, <class>?

passages.title: They All Fall Down
passages.text: Excellent work, <class>! This will aid my studies greatly, as well as advance our cause here.

passages.title: Power Play
passages.text:
The Zandalari have found a way to infuse items of great power with the essence of their loa. These items are often passed from one generation to another, each recipient adding to the item's power.

Two such items exist here. To be specific, two masks, worn by two brothers.

Spiritbinder Tu'chek and Arcanital Ra'kul must be stopped and their masks destroyed.

Kill them and return their masks to me. I will make sure the masks are disposed of.

passages.title: Power Play
passages.text: Do you have the masks?

passages.title: Power Play
passages.text: Getting these masks was no easy task, <class>. I am grateful for your service.

passages.title: The Crumbled Chamberlain
passages.text:
You there! Assist me.

In life I was the Royal Chamberlain for his majesty, the Thunder King. For my dedication, I was condemned to this stone form, forever forced to watch over a portion of his wealth.

Someone has desecrated my glorious body and sent pieces of it across the island. The thought of spending an eternity as nothing more than a head depresses me.

Search the island, recover these pieces and I shall grant you one of his majesty's treasures.

passages.title: The Crumbled Chamberlain
passages.text: I require ALL of my pieces. If so much as a pebble is missing, I shall consider forfeiting our agreement.

passages.title: The Crumbled Chamberlain
passages.text: Ah! To feel whole again! You have my gratitude, servant. Take this stone and use it wisely. Should you encounter his majesty the Thunder King in your travels, do not tell him where you received it, or you will be standing in a statue next to me for the remainder of eternity.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
In the Court of Bones, the Thunder King's sorcerers perform dark rituals.

To bolster their numbers, the Shan'ze soulrippers are imbuing ancient stone statues with stolen spirits from the living.

After these stone conquerors are brought to life, they will be formidable opponents on the battlefield.

We must stop their ritual before these statues can be revived.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text: It is a mystery how the mogu can imbue life into inanimate stone, but with enough study, we, too, may one day be able to understand that power.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
A good defense is just as effective as a strong offense. One less enemy to worry about.

Well done.

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
We assault the mogu at the Court of Bones, but I fear we merely send them fodder for their abominable rituals.

The mogu do not merely kill their prisoners - they steal their souls and imbue them in machinations of stone, or reforge the fallen into ghostly tools of war.

Alliance or Horde, it matters not. We cannot allow the mogu to bolster their numbers.

Go into the crypts. Free any prisoners that are still living.

passages.title: Soul Surrender
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>. You have lightened my heart of a heavy burden through your heroic actions.

I will remember your efforts on this day.

passages.title: Grave Circumstances
passages.text:
The Court of Bones crawls with mogu forces. Endlessly do they perform their rituals of lightning and thunder.

If our mission to take this island is to succeed, then we cannot allow them to hold such a strategic position.

They must be eliminated.

passages.title: Grave Circumstances
passages.text: Excellent. You have dealt the mogu a blow that they shall not easily forget.

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text:
Every day, we uncover additional relics from the Court of Bones.

Recently, we discovered this scroll amongst the gravestones in one of the deepest crypts.

I believe that this incantation can be used to call beyond the grave. And if my Mogu is up to date, I'd say you should use it in the last room in the Hall of the Exalted.

Would you be willing to test out my theory?

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text: How did it go?

passages.title: Into the Crypts
passages.text: Ah yes, you've just confirmed my theory! Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
In the Court of Bones, the Thunder King's sorcerers perform dark rituals.

To bolster their numbers, the Shan'ze soulrippers are imbuing ancient stone statues with stolen spirits from the living.

After these stone conquerors are brought to life, they will be formidable opponents on the battlefield.

We must stop their ritual before these statues can be revived.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text: It is a mystery how the mogu can imbue life into inanimate stone, but with enough study, we, too, may one day be able to understand that power.

passages.title: The Conquest of Stone
passages.text:
A good defense is just as effective as a strong offense. One less enemy to worry about.

Well done.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
I have three magisters entrenched in Ihgaluk Crag, monitoring the saurok and - where they can - turning them against the mogu. I need you to find them and see if they need any supplies or assistance.

They will be concealed from view. Look for shimmering columns of light within the saurok village.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text: Good luck, <name>.

passages.title: Manipulating the Saurok
passages.text:
<The archmage listens carefully to your report.>

I understand. Thank you for your aid, <class>.

passages.title: De-Constructed
passages.text:
Saurok consistently test our borders, and our constructs usually fend them off. Some constructs, however, have been defeated and dragged back to Ihgaluk Crag.

I want those constructs back. No slithering lizard will steal Silver Covenant property under my watch.

passages.title: De-Constructed
passages.text:
Hmph... saurok.

<Modera spits.>

passages.title: De-Constructed
passages.text:
That's more like it.

Thank you, <class>.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text:
It pains me to think of the torture the poor skyscreamers must endure as the trolls train them to become implements of war.

The hatchlings are quite fearful, and will fly away if you even get close them. Please, frighten some away before the Zandalari corrupt them.

passages.title: Preventing a Future Threat
passages.text: Welcome back, <race>. The hatchlings you frightened will live a better life without their captors.

passages.title: Surgical Strike
passages.text:
Zandalari spiritbinders perform sacrifices to their gods, the beastcallers bend innocent skyscreamers to their will, and the jaguar warriors venture closer to us by the day.

Dispose of these threats in Za'Tual, <race>, and watch the might of the trolls weaken.

passages.title: Surgical Strike
passages.text: With a few of their more threatening kin slain, perhaps the Zandalari will show reluctance next time they decide to trifle with us.

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The Skumblade threaten our people, but responding with all-out slaughter would be an overreaction.

A more reasonable response to their threat would be to slay some of their tribal leaders. There will be less bloodshed, and they will still respect our perimeter.

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
The saurok value strength above all else. They only respond to strength.

Peace with the saurok will require some amount of bloodshed. The question is, how much?

passages.title: The Residents of Ihgaluk
passages.text:
I know the true price of bloodshed. I know the cost of war.

It would be simpler to blindly massacre our attackers until they yield. But is it right?

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text:
This is not a glamorous job. Let me put it to you bluntly.

The Skumblade saurok pile all of their filth into a pool in the middle of their village. This filth is so concentrated and so rancid that it has congealed into moving, animate matter.

The saurok can keep their filth-pool, but once it starts spreading outside of the village, I'd say it's time to intervene.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text: Sorry in advance about the smell.

passages.title: Just Some Light Clean-Up Work
passages.text: Well done, <name>. Looking at you, I'm suddenly quite proud of Dalaran's state-of-the-art plumbing system.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text:
The raptors and saurid of the Zandalari represent a substantial threat to our forces here. They are superb hunting beasts that can track prey over great distances and are often lethal to encounter when caught unawares.

I need you to head into the Beast Pens and cull their numbers. We need to make sure to slay them before they are fully trained.

passages.title: Compy Stomp
passages.text: We lost three good soldiers when we first arrived on this island. Killed in their sleep by compies that had snuck into their tent. Some nights I still hear the screams.

passages.title: Direhorn vs Devilsaur
passages.text:
We have an opportunity to disrupt the Zandalari war machine as well as have a little fun in the process.

Within these beast pens, a devilsaur and a direhorn are being outfitted with armor, their minds being enslaved to the Zandalari charms.

Go into the camp and disrupt one of these binding rituals. It doesn't matter which one. Just kill those who are trying to bind the creature. This should let the fully armored beast run mad through the Zandalari camp. Then sit back and watch the hilarity ensue.

passages.title: Direhorn vs Devilsaur
passages.text: So... did you decide the devilsaur or the direhorn?

passages.title: Direhorn vs Devilsaur
passages.text:
Few things in this world and beyond are more entertaining than watching a rampaging ancient beast tearing through an enemy's settlement.

If times were not so dire I would consider selling tickets to such an event.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text:
The Zandalari use a series of fetishes and charms to maintain their control over their menagerie of beasts.

Two can play at that game.

I want you to find some of these fetishes and try them out on the various beasts in the Beast Pens.

Take careful note of how each beast responds to each fetish. Then report your results to me.

Maybe this will give us the edge we need against the Zandalari.

passages.title: Dino Might
passages.text: Very interesting results. I am sure there is a mage somewhere that cares about the specifics. I, on the other hand, am just glad to hear the sound of trolls being assaulted by their own beasts.

passages.title: Centuries in Sentries
passages.text:
Sacrifices are common place in Zandalari society. There is however one oddity among these barbaric rituals; volunteers. They treat it as a great honor!

The weak still seek to contribute, even if that means giving their lives to be bound to the sentries you see walking around. Locked away in service to their people.

Take this resonating crystal. Once destroyed, drain the sentry of its Zandalari inhabitant. Return the crystal to me when your task is complete.

passages.title: Centuries in Sentries
passages.text: How many spirits have you captured?

passages.title: Centuries in Sentries
passages.text:
This is very interesting, <class>. The crystal hums with the rage of its captive inhabitants. Even after the passage of time their devotion has not decreased.

I will need to study this further.

passages.title: The More You Know
passages.text:
This whole area is littered with Zandalari artifacts. I would be lying if I said studying them didn't interest me. I am fascinated by the significance of these objects to their rituals.

The more we understand our enemies, the better prepared we are to defeat them.

If I am to study them, I will need to see them up close. Bring me as many artifacts as you can find.

passages.title: The More You Know
passages.text: What have you brought me, <class>?

passages.title: The More You Know
passages.text: These are excellent finds! Studying them will take time, but there is much to be gained in understanding the Zandalari.

passages.title: Out of Enemy Hands
passages.text:
Magic is a frightening opponent when wielded by an experienced caster. A blade however, is terrifying in even the most inexperienced hands.

The Zandalari have some impressive weapons, made even more deadly by the magic they are enhanced with. We should relieve them of this advantage.

Steal as many of the weapons as you can find.

passages.title: Out of Enemy Hands
passages.text: What did you find out there? Anything that can be of use?

passages.title: Out of Enemy Hands
passages.text: Excellent work, <class>! These weapons are impressive. Now we have a few less things to worry about in the field of battle.

passages.title: All In the Family
passages.text:
Conqueror's Terrace is watched over by two brothers; Spiritbinder Tu'chek and Arcanital Rak'ul. They are powerful magic users and should not be underestimated.

Their power seems to stem from the ornate masks they wear; relics passed down from one generation to the next. Each owner imbuing it with their own magic before passing it on.

We must deal with the brothers and destroy their masks before they fall into the wrong hands.

passages.title: All In the Family
passages.text: Where are the masks?

passages.title: All In the Family
passages.text:
It's a shame really that these masks must be destroyed. I would have liked to study this ancient magic, but it is better that they be destroyed than become the tools of the Horde.

Good work, <class>.

passages.title: Even Giants Fall
passages.text:
The Zandalari worship the loa; animal spirits they often call to their aid. They may be trying to bind these spirits into a huge golem. The outcome would be disastrous.

I've sent ahead a scout to gather more information, but I think this task may require your expertise.

Stop that ritual at all costs!

passages.title: Even Giants Fall
passages.text: It's fortunate that you were able to intervene, <class>. Who knows what damage that golem would have caused had he not been stopped.

passages.title: Keep It Secret
passages.text:
The Zandalari here are a threat to our campaign, <class>.

Their use of magic is an abomination. They mix the power of arcane with the darkness of shadow with little care to consequence.

We cannot afford for them to find their full strength here or for the Horde to learn of their twisted magic.

Their numbers must be thinned. I will leave this task to you.

passages.title: Keep It Secret
passages.text: Well done, <class>. The more Zandalari we destroy, the less chance their magic will fall into Horde hands.

passages.title: Maximum Capacitor
passages.text:
The mines north of here are critical to the mogu supply line. They are using giant lightning enchanted drills to extract the ore.

If you can disrupt the drills, they'll be destroyed, greatly slowing their ability to make weapons.

Oh, also, kill whoever is in charge, will you?

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text:
The forge lies ahead of you, and with it the heart of the mogu's weaponsmithing ability.

And beyond that, the mogu gatekeeper, who holds the key to unlocking the gate to the next part of the city.

It's time to move out!

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Good work. What you did today brings us one step closer to our ultimate goal.

passages.title: On Her Magic-ey Secret Service
passages.text:
Under orders from Jaina herself, some of our agents attempted to sneak past mogu lines to find out what was going on in the mines.

They were captured, and are being subjected to who-knows-what kind of awful tortures.

You must free them and kill whoever captured them. We don't leave anyone behind!

passages.title: Life Blood
passages.text:
Scouts unearthed this strange construct hidden within the Lightning Vein Mine. A secret weapon of the Thunder King no doubt.

Perhaps, there is a chance we can use this discovery to our benefit. If we can re-animate it, we can study it. More importantly, we can discover its weakness.

Go to the Throne of Thunder and use this crystal to capture whatever essence animates these constructs.

Return to me when the task is complete.

passages.title: Life Blood
passages.text: Were you successful in our endeavor?

passages.title: Life Blood
passages.text:
Excellent work, <class>. This is a dark magic indeed. We have much to learn here if we are to succeed.

Now, we have only to hope that we can reanimate this creature.

passages.title: Securing A Future
passages.text:
It is rumored that the Thunder King's power comes directly from a hidden source within his palace.

Even when he is defeated a new tyrant, Garrosh perhaps, could still use this magic to a terrible end.

That is unless we make the first move!

Take my staff into the Pinnacle of Storms. Once Lei Shen has been defeated place my staff in the center of his dais.

We will drain the rest of his power and make sure it stays in our hands.

passages.title: Securing A Future
passages.text: We will be unstoppable once Lei Shen's power has been fused with my staff.

passages.title: Securing A Future
passages.text:
You have just secured our advantage, <name>. Your work here will be remembered.

Garrosh will be made to pay for his actions!

passages.title: Subtle Encouragement
passages.text:
The saurok are vile, but we share an enemy: the mogu. And I'd rather send saurok to kill mogu than send my own men.

We've been collecting mogu weaponry. Bury these polearms into the skulls of the saurok. Feed our enemies' rivalry, and you may save Horde lives.

passages.title: Subtle Encouragement
passages.text: As much as it pains me to say it: try not to kill them all. We need some alive if we want to turn them against the mogu.

passages.title: Subtle Encouragement
passages.text: Masterfully done, <class>.

passages.title: Subtle Encouragement
passages.text:
The saurok are vile, but we share an enemy: the mogu. And I'd rather send saurok to kill mogu than send my own men.

We've been collecting mogu weaponry. Bury these polearms into the skulls of the saurok. Feed our enemies' rivalry, and you may save Alliance lives.

passages.title: Subtle Encouragement
passages.text: Masterfully done, <class>.

passages.title: Extended Shore Leave
passages.text:
The Zandalari have already begun repairing that warship, but we can keep it crippled with minimal effort.

Simply relieve the new captain of his post, and steal the ship's damage report from that workshop just outside the vault.

No captain. No repairs. No warship.

passages.title: Extended Shore Leave
passages.text: Each passing hour brings us closer to breaking the Thunder King.

passages.title: Extended Shore Leave
passages.text:
Casualties are down significantly with that warship out of commission, and we continue to press the siege on Lei Shen.

Fantastic work out there today, hero.

Please, take this - you have earned it.

passages.title: Raiding the Vault
passages.text:
The Swollen Vault is a repository for some of Lei Shen's nastiest weaponry and most prized trinkets - not surprisingly, these are often one and the same.

One artifact in particular, an amulet known as the Choker of Storms, could help us to understand his apparent mastery over lightning.

Break into the vault and slay the hoard-keeper. Take his key and use it to recover the amulet from a cache at the back of the vault.

passages.title: Raiding the Vault
passages.text: The Thunder King's strength is legendary. We need every advantage we can get if we want to defeat him.

passages.title: Raiding the Vault
passages.text:
What's this? A necklace? What are you trying to- ahh, I see... A relic from the Thunder King's vault! Fascinating... Powerful, too.

The Kirin Tor will keep it safe. In return, please accept this.

passages.title: Lightning Steel
passages.text: Your trained eyes can see that this metal ingot has some very strange properties. Perhaps there are clues to its nature somewhere around here?

passages.title: Lightning Steel
passages.text: While the language is incomprehensible, the diagrams in this book yield their knowledge to your skilled blacksmith's eye. It is clear that, by manipulating the properties of ghost iron, you can create a material of great power, perhaps powerful enough to recreate and increase the power of weapons long lost to the mists of time.

passages.title: Charged Moganite
passages.text:
We have been dispatching spies into the Sunreaver base of operations on a daily basis. Some had orders to recover charged moganite from the enemy and bring it here.

They have not returned, and I can confirm they have left the Sunreaver base.

Search the jungle between here and there and find any of the charged moganite that might have been lost in transit. Bring it to me and we will put it to good use.

passages.title: Charged Moganite
passages.text: Well done, champion. This artifact will be put to better use in our hands than in the hands of the Sunreavers.

passages.title: Tactical Mana Bombs
passages.text:
Ah, adventurer, just the <race> I was looking for. I have received another batch of tactical mana bombs that I need planted in key positions across Dawnseeker Promontory to the northwest.

Here, take these. It is time to give the Sunreavers a taste of their own medicine.

Plant one on the Sunreaver ships, another one on their scrying crystals, and the last on the bridge that connects to their forward base.

passages.title: Tactical Mana Bombs
passages.text: It pains me to resort to such weaponry, but the Sunreavers must be taught the price of their actions.

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text:
Grand Magister Rommath has something in his possession that I want.

He brought a very powerful tome with him. It would be better for our cause if it were no longer in Sunreaver hands.

Locate Rommath's book of incantations and bring it to me.

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text: Did you find the tome?

passages.title: Spellbound
passages.text: Ah yes! This is it. You've done well, <race>.

passages.title: Breaking Down the Defenses
passages.text:
Even the strongest defense can still have a weakness, <class>. We just need to find the weakness in the Sunreaver's defense and then exploit it as much as possible.

Scouts have reported the use of perimeter wards around Dawnseeker Promontory. They're powerful, but not deadly.

Disabling them would allow us to keep closer watch on their activities.

passages.title: Breaking Down the Defenses
passages.text: Excellent work, <race>! I was able to get a few of my scouts behind their lines before the perimeter wards were repaired.

passages.title: Enough with the Bombs!
passages.text:
The Sunreavers have planted tactical mana bombs around our camp. These must be dismantled before they are detonated.

Look for them in areas of high importance such as our supplies. Make sure you find and disable them all. We cannot afford to lose any ground here.

passages.title: Enough with the Bombs!
passages.text: I'm grateful for your efforts here, <name>. We would have lost so much had you not disarmed those bombs in time.

passages.title: Captive Audience
passages.text:
The Sunreavers will stoop to even the lowest levels to get what they want, <name>.

I received reports earlier that several Kirin Tor have gone missing. I suspect the Sunreavers may have something to do with this.

Hopefully they have not been harmed, or my wrath will be swift and terrible. I trust you to bring them back in one piece, but please hurry.

passages.title: Captive Audience
passages.text: You have saved many today, <name>. I cannot imagine the horror of being frozen and helpless among so many enemies.

passages.title: Overpowered
passages.text:
The Sunreaver forces have grown more powerful recently. I suspect magic to be at play here, but I can't be certain.

I think it would be wise to investigate their camp to see if you can find the source of this extra power.

Once you find it, use this crystal to overload and destroy it.

passages.title: Overpowered
passages.text:
So they've constructed objects that infuse their forces with additional power? This will have to be watched closely.

Thank you for your efforts today.

passages.title: Deconstruction
passages.text:
Scouts are reporting a large number of constructs patrolling outside of Dawnseeker Promontory.

If left unchecked they will pose a considerable threat should the Sunreavers mount an attack.

The only answer is a preemptive strike. We'll destroy them before they can attack us!

passages.title: Deconstruction
passages.text: Good work, <class>. As long as we keep the construct numbers in check, we will ensure our success here.

passages.title: Work Order: Dominance Offensive II
passages.text:
Once your red blossom leeks are ready to be picked, you'll need only to package them for pick-up.

Just think; your red blossom leeks will be a part of your faction's efforts in Pandaria!

passages.title: Work Order: Dominance Offensive II
passages.text: The crate sits empty awaiting your crops.

passages.title: Work Order: Dominance Offensive II
passages.text: Throw the Red Blossom Leeks into the crate! A Dominance Offensive representative will be along shortly for pick-up.

passages.title: Work Order: Operation: Shieldwall II
passages.text:
Once your witchberries are ready to be picked, you'll need only to package them for pick-up.

Just think; your witchberries will be a part of your faction's efforts in Pandaria!

passages.title: Work Order: Operation: Shieldwall II
passages.text: The crate sits empty awaiting your crops.

passages.title: Work Order: Operation: Shieldwall II
passages.text: Throw the Witchberries into the crate! An Operation: Shieldwall representative will be along shortly for pick-up.

passages.title: Work Order: Golden Lotus II
passages.text:
Well, hopefully these crops will be suitable!

Once your white turnips are ready to be picked, you'll need only to package them for pick-up.

passages.title: Work Order: Golden Lotus II
passages.text: The crate sits empty awaiting your crops.

passages.title: Work Order: Golden Lotus II
passages.text: Throw the White Turnips into the crate! A Golden Lotus representative will be along shortly for pick-up.

passages.title: Work Order: Shado-Pan II
passages.text:
Well, your work is done for the day! Now to wait for the harvest tomorrow.

Once your green cabbages are ready to be picked, you'll need only to package them for pick-up.

Only the finest cabbage will do for the Shado-Pan!

passages.title: Work Order: Shado-Pan II
passages.text: The crate sits empty awaiting your crops.

passages.title: Work Order: Shado-Pan II
passages.text: Gently place the Green Cabbages into the crate! A Shado-Pan representative will be along shortly for pick-up.

passages.title: Work Order: The August Celestials II
passages.text:
Once your striped melons are ready to be picked, you'll need only to package them for pick-up.

A trainee from the Cradle of Chi-Ji will be along shortly to collect their order.

passages.title: Work Order: The August Celestials II
passages.text: The crate sits empty awaiting your crops.

passages.title: Work Order: The August Celestials II
passages.text: Throw the Striped Melons into the crate! Now the August Celestials' order is ready to go!

passages.title: Work Order: The Klaxxi II
passages.text:
Once your mogu pumpkins are ready to be picked, you'll need only to package them for pick-up.

I wouldn't dilly-dally if I were you. The Klaxxi aren't known for their patience!

passages.title: Work Order: The Klaxxi II
passages.text: The crate sits empty awaiting your crops.

passages.title: Work Order: The Klaxxi II
passages.text: Throw the Mogu Pumpkins into the crate! A Klaxxi representative will be along shortly for pick-up.

passages.title: Extended Shore Leave
passages.text:
The Zandalari have already begun repairing that warship, but we can keep it crippled with minimal effort.

Simply relieve the new captain of his post, and steal the ship's damage report from that workshop just outside the vault.

No captain. No repairs. No warship.

passages.title: Extended Shore Leave
passages.text: Lei Shen will fall to our onslaught, and my people will find glory in his ruin.

passages.title: Extended Shore Leave
passages.text:
This so-called "Thunder King" is surrounded and cut off from his allies. No tyrant is strong enough to stand alone.

Your efforts have not gone unnoticed. Take this, with my thanks.

passages.title: Raiding the Vault
passages.text:
The Swollen Vault is a repository for some of Lei Shen's nastiest weaponry and most prized trinkets - not surprisingly, these are often one and the same.

One artifact in particular, an amulet known as the Choker of Storms, could help us to understand his apparent mastery over lightning.

Break into the vault and slay the hoard-keeper. Take his key and use it to recover the amulet from a cache at the back of the vault.

passages.title: Raiding the Vault
passages.text: You have good news, I hope.

passages.title: Raiding the Vault
passages.text:
Ah, I know a powerful artifact when I see one. You were wise to bring this here. I will see that Aethas examines it right away - perhaps we can put it to work in our favor.

In the meantime, take this in trade.

passages.title: So You Want to Be a Blacksmith...
passages.text: While it is best to learn the properties of simpler metals and work your way up, it is possible to learn how to become a good blacksmith through mastering the various applications of ghost iron for common household objects. If you wish to take this path towards becoming a zen master blacksmith, I can teach you. Whichever way you choose, you will have my respect if you can show me that you can make a ghostly skeleton key.

passages.title: So You Want to Be a Blacksmith...
passages.text: How are your studies coming along?

passages.title: So You Want to Be a Blacksmith...
passages.text: Well done. You are ready to become a zen master blacksmith.

passages.title: No Fishing Pole Necessary!
passages.text:
You don't even need to equip a fishing pole in Pandaria!

The waters are TEEMING with fish. You'll catch one pretty much every time, as long as you are paying attention. Give it a go!

passages.title: No Fishing Pole Necessary!
passages.text: Catch 5 Golden Carp. Try it without a fishing pole!

passages.title: No Fishing Pole Necessary!
passages.text: Let me see...  Yes, these are nice. Good job! Here, have some more.

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text:
There's more you must do. 

Kill Itoka, master of the forge, and find a codex fragment from Fleshcrafter Hoku, gatekeeper of the Thunder King.

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Good work. What you did today brings us one step closer to our ultimate goal.

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text:
There's more you must do. 

Kill Itoka, master of the forge, and find a codex fragment from Fleshcrafter Hoku, gatekeeper of the Thunder King.

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Well?

passages.title: Forge Ahead!
passages.text: Good work. What you did today brings us one step closer to our ultimate goal.

passages.title: So You Want to Be a Blacksmith...
passages.text: While it is best to learn the properties of simpler metals and work your way up, it is possible to learn how to become a good blacksmith through mastering the various applications of ghost iron for common household objects. If you wish to take this path towards becoming a zen master blacksmith, I can teach you. Whichever way you choose, you will have my respect if you can show me that you can make a ghostly skeleton key.

passages.title: So You Want to Be a Blacksmith...
passages.text: How are your studies coming along?

passages.title: So You Want to Be a Blacksmith...
passages.text: Well done. You are ready to become a zen master blacksmith.

passages.title: Leave Nothing Behind!
passages.text:
The Thunderlord clan has become a thorn in my side I will no longer tolerate.

Go east and leave none alive! Burn their supplies! Leave them nothing to cling to.

Converge on the Savage Crag to the east when it is done.

passages.title: Leave Nothing Behind!
passages.text: Hrmph. The burning smell of Thunderlord. This pleases me, <class>.

passages.title: To the Garrison
passages.text:
My father is avenged. The sons of the Iron Wolf are all slain.

Go to the garrison your people are constructing in the south. There, herald my return to my laggard brother.

The time has come for the "chieftain" to be reminded of what it means to be a Frostwolf.

passages.title: To the Garrison
passages.text:
Ga'nar is coming. Good. We need his forces if we are to press the advantage.

I can only hope his bloodlust has quelled enough for him to listen to reason.

passages.title: END OF PROTOTYPE! [Return to Durotan at Ogre Citadel]
passages.text:
Ah! The weapons of my father, Garad. Too long this beast has coveted them as trophies, memories of slaying our beloved chieftain. I thank you Outsider. Your help today has proven most useful indeed.

Now I must bring these artifacts before my brother. The time has come for he and I to have a proper discussion about leadership.

passages.title: A Little Field Work
passages.text:
My dream brew can only tell me so much. Its visions are scattered in time and space. But it is clear that a showdown is brewing at the Horde capital of Orgrimmar.

You should go there, and see these events for yourself!

In my dream brew I see two brave Alliance spies alone in Durotar. I see "Amber" and "Sully"...

Perhaps you remember them? I think they need your help!

You'll find Amber and Sully in Kalimdor, near Skull Rock, at a place called the Dranosh'ar Blockade.

passages.title: A Little Field Work
passages.text:
<name>! I cannot tell you how relieved I am to have some backup!

King Wrynn himself sent us to gather intel on Garrosh's activities and Orgrimmar's defenses, but... things are looking grim.

We need your help.

passages.title: Gathering Intelligence
passages.text:
Garrosh continues building up his forces in Orgrimmar - this place is like a fortress!

King Wrynn won't want to risk an assault until we have as much information as possible.

Use Project C4T to navigate through the Blockade. Try to gather as much information as you can. Look for any high priority documents and any weakness we can take advantage of. Keep your ears open and your head down!

passages.title: Gathering Intelligence
passages.text: Did you find us anything useful?

passages.title: Gathering Intelligence
passages.text:
Let's see... the warchief is moving tons of supplies through the Barrens... And what's this about the Darkspear? The trolls are in open rebellion?! Garrosh certainly has his hands full.

I think I know how we can use this intel. It's a crazy idea, but it just might work...

passages.title: Grandpa Grumplefloot
passages.text:
The challenge card I have for you today belongs to a grummle by the adorable name of Grandpa Grumplefloot. While the grummles aren't particularly well-known for their combat skills, they are remarkably lucky little creatures.

Perhaps it's their... what do they call them... their luckydos?

passages.title: Grandpa Grumplefloot
passages.text:
Great fighting out there! Even if he was just a little guy.

You've earned every bit of this.

passages.title: The Bear and the Lady Fair
passages.text:
The challenge card you've earned belongs to an unusual pair of characters. I'm not quite sure any further description would do them justice.

Maybe you should just purchase the challenge card and see for yourself.

passages.title: The Bear and the Lady Fair
passages.text: You sailed through the air so... so... majestically! Well done!

passages.title: Master Boom Boom
passages.text:
You have earned a card belonging to a bomb-throwing hozen named Master Boom Boom.

While hozen are naturally attracted to the destructive power of explosives, they seldom learn how to use them properly without blowing themselves up in the process. Master Boom Boom is the exception.

Good luck!

passages.title: Master Boom Boom
passages.text:
I'm not sure how to feel. I wanted you to win, but then again... I also kinda wanted to see you explode.

No hard feelings! I just like seeing explosions.

passages.title: Razorgrin
passages.text:
The challenge card you've earned today belongs to one of the most deadly creatures in the South Seas: Razorgrin. One bite from those teeth of his, and you're nothing but an unrecognizable pile of skin, blood, and entrails.

Have fun!

passages.title: Razorgrin
passages.text:
Congratulations!

Also, how embarrassing would it have been if you got eaten by a beached shark?

passages.title: Splat
passages.text:
You may already be familiar with Blat, one of our Rank 2 challengers here in the Brawler's Guild. The challenge card you've earned belongs to Splat, its older, nastier sister.

Try not to get yourself killed, <name>. And if you do, at least make it entertaining for the rest of us!

passages.title: Splat
passages.text: You left quite a mess behind you, but you did it. Well done, <race>!

passages.title: Mecha-Bruce
passages.text:
Everybody knows Bruce. Everybody loves Bruce! And eventually, everybody kills Bruce.

An orcish hunter with a knack for engineering thought that this was a shame, so he's found his own crocolisk and geared him up a bit.

The challenge card you've earned grants you the right to fight Mecha-Bruce. It's bound to be a bloodbath. The question is... will you be the chomper, or the chompee?

passages.title: Mecha-Bruce
passages.text:
Aww... poor Mecha-Bruce.

I'll give you your reward. But I don't have to be happy about it.

passages.title: Dippy and Doopy
passages.text:
Brawler's Guild vets will remember Dippy, the penguin. Dippy's not the most accomplished challenger in the Brawler's Guild, but he's no pushover, either!

Actually, come to think of it, he IS kind of a pushover...

Anyway! The card you've earned gives you the right to challenge Dippy alongside his older, huger brother, Doopy. They may both be pushovers, but that doesn't mean that one or both of them won't eventually murder you.

passages.title: Dippy and Doopy
passages.text: I never thought I'd say this, but successfully beating up a couple penguins is the sign of a true, tried-and-tested brawler. You've earned your reward.

passages.title: Blingtron 3000
passages.text:
The Blingtron line didn't really pick up until the 4000 series hit the vendor shelves. Few remember the Blingtron 3000, but it was a real engineering marvel in its own right!

The challenge card you've unlocked gives you the ability to fight Blingtron 3000 right here, in the Brawler's Guild.

Lucky you!
