passages.title: Friend of the Exarchs
passages.text:
An excellent choice! We'll send your pick directly to your garrison to help with any missions you encounter.

Now, about those supplies you requested...

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text:
This was a betrayal from within. There's no other explanation for it. None of the Exarchs trust each other now - especially me. But Othaar and Akama can damn their laws. We've got to rout out the traitor and the only way to do it is to speak to the corpse!

Join me just outside the Altar of Sha'tar atop the eastern cliffs. Soulbinder Nyami and I will perform an exorcism to save Hataaru's immortal soul... and maybe learn who did this to him.

Do you trust me, <name>?

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text: Exarch Hataaru didn't deserve to die that way. Not like this.

passages.title: Speaker for the Dead
passages.text:
One of the five Exarchs is dead. Another is a traitor. Dark times.

We will end this here and now. Can I count on you for one final task?

passages.title: The Sting
passages.text:
The exarchs seem to trust you, <class>. Are you venturing into the Umbrafen?

The Sporebats in this area are usually docile, but something's got them all riled up. When they attack, their stingers wrap around exposed limbs. I've seen them tear through reinforced leather like it was paper. How do they work, I wonder?

Could you bring me a pristine sporebat stinger? I'd love to study it.

passages.title: The Sting
passages.text: Most draenei avoid the Umbrafen, but we rangari seem drawn to the most dangerous places - that's where you really learn how the world works.

passages.title: The Sting
passages.text:
Would you look at that - the entire tentacle is barbed. Uggh. No wonder the wounds they inflict tend to get infected. We could learn something from this. I wonder if rangari explorers should start equipping themselves with whips?

Thank you, <name>. This Alliance that you come from must be quite the collection of heroes!

passages.title: Warning the Exarchs
passages.text:
You set the book ablaze, but not before noting its contents. The demonic tome was dedicated to enchanting weapons with fel energy. It looked as though the goal was to ensnare the victim's soul.

The Exarchs must be warned that traitors are among them! The Council should be meeting now just up the hill to the east.

passages.title: Warning the Exarchs
passages.text:
Dead! Exarch Hataaru is dead! His body was discovered moments ago, stabbed in the back. The weapon that killed him was fel in origin. Tell me everything you know.

<Maladaar nods as you describe what you found.>

Yes. The traitors wanted to capture Hataaru's soul. Someone wants something he knows, dead or alive... We must act at once.

passages.title: The Traitor's True Name
passages.text:
We must give the traitor no place to hide. I have a focusing lens that will illuminate cloaked fel energy. If it were placed on a high point, it could act like a beacon, lighting up anyone in town who reeks of the fel taint.

There is a prayer circle atop the Exarch's Rise to the north that will serve our purpose. Plant the focusing lens, <name>. If you reveal anything, deal with it. Then meet me below.

passages.title: The Traitor's True Name
passages.text: What happened up there?

passages.title: The Traitor's True Name
passages.text:
<The Exarch listens to your tale, his face contorting into concern, grief, and finally anger.>

So Othaar has lost his way. "Socrethar" he calls himself now. At last we have our answer. I fear my capture at the hands of the Iron Horde was his doing. There may be other traitors amongst us - I must hurry back to Auchindoun and make sure we are safe.

In the meantime, I believe the Exarchs owe you a decision...

passages.title: Send Them Running
passages.text:
Your scouts have located the saberon's alpha male just outside our gates!

Commander, I believe that dispatching this target will send any of these remaining vermin running back to their caves.

I do not wish to ask more of you, but you are the only one capable of this task, <sir/ma'am>.

passages.title: Send Them Running
passages.text: Is the alpha male dispatched?

passages.title: Send Them Running
passages.text: For <name>! For the Horde!

passages.title: Not In Your House
passages.text:
<Sir/Madame>, we have located the saberon's alpha male just outside our gates!

We believe that slaying him will send any remaining saberon running with their tails between their legs, but the beast is positively massive!

I do not wish to call upon you once more, but you are the only one capable of this task.

passages.title: Not In Your House
passages.text: Victory! For the Alliance!

passages.title: What We Got
passages.text:
Every fortress needs three things.

One: peons! Find Skaggit and have him get our peons back to work.

Two: building materials. I had the peons set up a cache for you where they will store resources they create while you are away. You should check it out.

And three: raw experienced muscle! Constructing buildings in a garrison can take some time but I think we can speed up your first building by hiring Skaggit's recently promoted Senior Peon II. Find him and tell him I sent ya.

passages.title: What We Got
passages.text: If buildin' a stronghold were easy, everybody'd be doin' it.

passages.title: What We Got
passages.text: Yeah, that's the stuff. Lumber, stone, peons, more peons. It's like we are building you a stronghold or something.

passages.title: Last of the Talonpriests
passages.text:
Talonpriests live among us in secret, guarding the rites of the Talon King's return.

The Adherent proclamation you acquired in Skettis revealed two of them living in the Shadowglade to the north. Orcs have moved into the region, and the Adherent's beam weapon left Veil Akraz a smoking crater.

As you can see, my people are beset by enemies on all sides.

Talonpriest Ishaal survived and is in hiding. Drink this elixir near his hut to peer into the shadows and make contact with him.

passages.title: Last of the Talonpriests
passages.text:
Hm, not what I was expecting when I heard that Iskar was sending help.

No matter. You'll have to do.

passages.title: Behind the Veil
passages.text:
Soon after the orcs swept in, Veil Akraz was laid to waste by a beam of light from Skyreach.

<Ishaal's eyes glass over as he peers into his orb.>

It seems they missed their true target. Zellek is still there, hiding in the realm of shadow.

And... someone else as well. The orc assassin who used my orb.

Take this. Drink it in Veil Akraz and find Zellek.

Oh, and be careful. It's a little more potent than the last one. You'll see...

passages.title: Behind the Veil
passages.text:
Well, you are not stabbing me yet.

That is a good sign.

passages.title: Forbidden Love
passages.text:
My son, Kral'za, is beyond stubborn. 

After we split from the Shadowmoon Clan he refused to let go of his relationship with a young Shadowmoon orc.

I forbid him to see her anymore. He ran off earlier today and has not returned. 

I don't trust Dol'mak. Like the other Shadowmoon orcs she continues to dabble in the void.

passages.title: Forbidden Love
passages.text: Aka'Magosh, <class>. I knew that void witch was no good.

passages.title: To Even the Odds
passages.text: [TEMP] The Shattered Hand orcs are using their prisoners as living training dummies. Let's even the odds and give them some weapons.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
The blade is not the only important item a blademaster carries.

Once he has passed his final tests in the Masters' Caverns, the blademaster is given the honor of wearing the Burning Blade's banner.

When my petition to reclaim my rightful place with the clan fell upon deaf and craven ears, I was stripped of that honor.

No doubt, my banner has been stored away somewhere in Hallvalor. They'll give it to some other aspiring blademaster if they don't burn it first.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text: Do you have my banner?

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
I don't expect you to understand the importance of what you've done.

Perhaps one day you will.

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text:
The Gordunni were given copies of my blades as a gift from the Iron Horde. But what do they use them for? Toothpicks!

Sure the blades are low grade copies but it's still MY design and I can't stand to think of them in those ogre hands for a moment longer!

<Sir/Ma'am>, While we are in here can you do me a favor and get those blades out of their hands!

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Were you able to get all of my blades back?

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Thank you, commander. With this another stain on my honor has been removed.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
The time has come to challenge the Burning Blade masters.

Go to the back of the cavern. There you will find the challenge ring and the masters watching over it from above.

Pull the blade from the middle of the ring to issue your challenge. My clan values honor above all else and will respect your claim to trial by combat.

As reward, you will be allowed to walk away with your blueprints and your life. Or, you will be dead.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text: Do you have the garrison blueprints, commander?

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
The garrison blueprints. Outstanding.

There's only one thing left to do.

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Witch Lord Morkurk is the leader of the Gordunni. He's the one that set up the Iron Horde trade and, even worse, my former boss gave him one of my best maces!

We got to get my mace back! I mean... we need to kill him to secure the jovite for your arsenal!

Morkurk is an accomplished mage so you better be prepared. Here, take the rocket pack and use it if you need to dodge an attack quickly or something.

Also, if you happen to find my mace I'd like to get it back.

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text: Do you have my mace?

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Fine work commander! Your combat skills are clearly second to none. I am honored to be your armorer!

Let's get back to the outpost so we can take stock of our new inventory. I saved a few flares to call us in a ride back.

passages.title: Loola's Lost Love
passages.text:
Oh it was horrible.

My husband and I were fishing in the marsh, I fell asleep and when I woke up he had been turned into a toad!

I'm sure it was one of those Shadowmoon orcs I hear so much about.

He jumped into the muddy waters before I could catch him.

Will you help me find my lost love, <class>?

passages.title: Loola's Lost Love
passages.text: Hmm... I'm sure one of these toads is my husband.

passages.title: Earth, Wind and Fire...and Water
passages.text:
The Elemental Plateau has become unstable, and so the cycle of rebirth must begin.

It is a natural part of our life cycle that impurities are accumulated in the elemental body over time.

When enough contamination has taken place, an elemental will become unstable and in some cases volatile.

A necessary part of rebirth is pure, living essence which can be found atop the Elemental Plateau, as well as in the body of an elemental spirit.

Return to me with the essence and we shall begin the rebirth.

passages.title: Earth, Wind and Fire...and Water
passages.text: Bring to me the living essences of the elements, that I may plant the seeds of rebirth.

passages.title: Earth, Wind and Fire...and Water
passages.text:
You have done well.

Although the Elemental Plateau is no longer stable, the cycle of rebirth will soon take place and the elements will be born anew.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text:
It's time to fight fire with fire.

We have Morkurk cornered. His protections gone. Use the scroll once you engage Morkurk...

...and enjoy the fireworks.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text: Ogres. It's always ogres.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text:
That's what we were after.

Let's get out of here!

passages.title: A Choice to Make
passages.text:
We're ready to start building. All that we need is for you to make a choice.

The blueprints are on the drafting table. Take a look.

Then, let me know if we're going to construct a corral or a tankworks.

passages.title: A Choice to Make
passages.text:
This is a momentous occasion, commander. Thazz'ril and his peons will get to work right away.

You'll see; this decision is going to be critical in our efforts against the Warsong.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text:
We have Morkurk cornered. He's all ours now. Use the scroll once you engage Morkurk...

...and enjoy the blizzard of your forces raining down on his head.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text: It's all come down to this moment.

passages.title: The Final Step
passages.text: Looks like Morkurk was no match for the two of us, huh?

passages.title: The Blessing of Samedi
passages.text:
Three of mah shadow huntas come here wit' me. De Warsong kill dem.

We need ta help dey souls move on. Jus' in case ya find dem first, use dis on dere bodies.

It send dere souls ta Samedi, Loa of de Grave.

passages.title: The Blessing of Samedi
passages.text:
Dey movin' onta a betta place. Samedi be sendin' dem on all dey missions now.

Dank ya, <name>.

passages.title: Shields Down!
passages.text:
De time has come, commanda. Packleader Kargora an' de Arkonite Shield no longa protected.

We need ta kill her an' destroy de shield crystal.

passages.title: Shields Down!
passages.text:
I'm sorry to hear about Kajassa's shadow hunters, but we couldn't afford to let the Warsong have Telaar.

With the death of Kargora and her pack, we're one step closer to the invasion of the Warsong's home, Grommashar.

One step close to justice.

passages.title: Cult of the Ravenspeakers
passages.text:
These outcasts are not the only cursed arakkoa holding their ground in Arak.

A curious cult has formed in worship of Ka'alu, my consort and the keeper of my brood. They are considered to be quite... odd.

Regardless, the outcasts will need their help. Without the wings of the ravens, Iskar can never take his fight to the spires.

Take this feather and place it in the offering basket south of here. The so-called "Ravenspeakers" will surely take notice.

passages.title: Cult of the Ravenspeakers
passages.text:
Ah, you come to learn the truth of things.

We will need to test your dedication first, yes!

passages.title: Polishing the Iron Throne
passages.text:
These stinking Blackrock cowards think they're humiliating me.

They're just making me angrier.

Overseer Gotrigg, in the hut over there, carries my shackle key. If I'm going to get out of there, I'm going to need that key. Then... vengeance can begin.

passages.title: Polishing the Iron Throne
passages.text: You'll have to pry that key out of his cold, ugly hand.

passages.title: Polishing the Iron Throne
passages.text:
<Ga'nar works his neck out of the shackle.>

Much better.

passages.title: The Debt We Share
passages.text:
These mortal shells that we call bodies are not ours to keep. The body is a gift of earth that must one day be returned from whence it came.

The time has come for this body to return to the elements.

Know that you have lifted the weight from an old heart, <name>. As I pass on from this realm, I do so without regret. I have fought on behalf of my people and my land, I have served the elements, and I have loved.

It would honor me if you would stay during these final moments, <class>.

passages.title: The Debt We Share
passages.text: When I face my ancestors in the realm of spirits I will do so without shame or fear, for I have lived an honorable life.

passages.title: The Debt We Share
passages.text:
Gar'rok was a loyal keeper and a true friend. He will be missed, but so is the cycle of life on this world.

In time we will call a new keeper of the elements, and he will serve us as Gar'rok did before him.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
The blade is not the only important item a blademaster carries.

Once he has passed his final tests in the Masters' Caverns, the blademaster is given the honor of wearing the Burning Blade's banner.

When my petition to reclaim my rightful place with the clan fell upon deaf and craven ears, I was stripped of that honor.

No doubt, my banner has been stored away somewhere in Hallvalor. They'll give it to some other aspiring blademaster if they don't burn it first.

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text: Do you have my banner?

passages.title: Not Without My Honor
passages.text:
I don't expect you to understand the importance of what you've done.

Perhaps one day you will.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
The time has come to challenge the Burning Blade masters.

Go to the back of the cavern. There you will find the challenge ring and the masters watching over it from above.

Pull the blade from the middle of the ring to issue your challenge. My clan values honor above all else and will respect your claim to trial by combat.

As reward, you will be allowed to walk away with your life. Or, you will be dead.

passages.title: Challenge of the Masters
passages.text:
A great victory over the Burning Blade!

This new Warlord Azuka Bladefury sounds formidable. We'll have to keep an eye on her and her blademasters.

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text:
The Gordunni have plagued the people of Shattrath ever since the city was founded. Over time they amassed quite a hoard of weapons they captured from our defenders in raids.

Getting these weapons in the hands of our soldiers would be practical and I personally would like to get them out of the hands of the ogres.

While we are in here can you do me a favor and gather up any of those weapons you come across.

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Were you able to find any weapons?

passages.title: Prized Repossessions
passages.text: Thank you, commander. With this a great dishonor on the legacy of Shattrath has been removed.

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Witch Lord Morkurk is the leader of the Gordunni. We need to kill him to secure the jovite for use in our artillery tower.

Morkurk is an accomplished mage so you better be prepared. Here, take the rocket pack and use it if you need to avoid any of his deadly magic.

Archenon poros!

passages.title: The Lord of the Gordunni
passages.text:
Fine work commander! Your combat skills are clearly second to none. I am honored to be your armorer!

Let's get back to the outpost so we can take stock of our new inventory. I saved a few flares to call us in a ride back.

passages.title: To the... Rescue?
passages.text:
The Parchment of Dust reads: "Put the featherless against one another so that our claws remain unsullied!" How wise the high Ravenspeaker is to foresee this day.

There is a great beast on the hillside to the west by the name of Stonescale. It has abducted one of the flock and despite our many attempts we have been unable to defeat it. 

Go, prove yourself by slaying the beast and rescuing Tillik! Fulfill your destiny in the name of the Raven Mother!

passages.title: To the... Rescue?
passages.text: Tillik's disappearance caused great sadness to the Flock.

passages.title: To the... Rescue?
passages.text:
Tillik! Dear friend I'm so glad you have returned! All of the acolytes missed your witty banter after the evening chants.

<Iktis looks back towards you.>

Yes, now your great test is done. You have fulfilled the requirements of The Parchment of Dust!

passages.title: Talon Watch
passages.text:
By now you must be wondering about all of this curse business. What could distort a majestic arakkoa into... well, into this?

<Reshad drags a crooked hand through the mottled feathers about his face.>

A raven is prepped and waiting to fly you to Talon Watch. There shall your eyes be opened to the origin of this curse.

Present the Eye of Anzu to Talon Guard Kurekk. He will guide you from there.

passages.title: Talon Watch
passages.text: Reshad sent an outsider here? You must be very important... or very dangerous.

passages.title: Talon Watch
passages.text:
<Kurekk gazes at the orb.>

Is that... what I think it is?

We must get this to the Talon Altar.

passages.title: Ritual Severance
passages.text:
I could not defeat this curse, and long ago resigned myself to rest in darkness.

But the Sethekk are performing dark rituals to draw me back, slowly binding me to Sethe's will. Should they succeed, Sethe would have me draw a dark cloak across the horizon, and bathe the world in his blood.

Disrupt their rituals, so that I may return with my own free will. Then, together, we shall bring an end to Sethe's return.

passages.title: Ritual Severance
passages.text:
Ah... I feel their grasp slipping.

Thank you, mortal.

passages.title: Servants of a Dead God
passages.text:
Even in death, Sethe exerts influence. The Sethekk cult was born of this influence: led by a false king in service of the dead god.

Silence their prophets, for they seek a future of black seas and blighted skies.

Defeat their chosen champions, for they have pledged themselves to a lie.

passages.title: Servants of a Dead God
passages.text:
Weapons and zealotry do not make one strong.

They turned to Sethe because they were too weak to face death.

passages.title: Prepare for Battle
passages.text:
There's nowhere to hide up here. We need to keep moving, and to do that, we need to pass right through the heart of the Iron Horde.

It's time to turn this unarmed group of prisoners into an army.

passages.title: Prepare for Battle
passages.text: These prisoners are no less brave than you or I, <name>. Give them a weapon and an ounce of hope and they will fight like the storm.

passages.title: Prepare for Battle
passages.text:
Great work, <name>.

Don't put away your weapon yet - now's when the REAL work begins.

passages.title: Prepare for Battle
passages.text:
There's nowhere to hide up here. We need to keep moving, and to do that, we need to pass right through the heart of the Iron Horde.

It's time to turn this unarmed group of prisoners into an army.

passages.title: Prepare for Battle
passages.text: These prisoners are no less brave than you or I, <name>. Give them a weapon and an ounce of hope and they will fight like the storm.

passages.title: Prepare for Battle
passages.text:
Great work, <name>.

Don't put away your weapon yet - now's when the REAL work begins.

passages.title: Golmash Hellscream
passages.text:
Those who die in brutal combat often enter the spirit world in unrest. So it was with Golmash, father of Grommash Hellscream.

Crushed within the jaws of a hulking gronn, Golmash still found the strength to bury his axe Gorehowl deep into the eye of the monster. When they fell, it was the gronn who died first.

Such is the heroic death that every Warsong dreams of, yet few attain. But Golmash's mighty spirit lingers restlessly, stirring the other spirits into unrest.

Put his mighty soul to rest, <name>.

passages.title: Golmash Hellscream
passages.text: Have you brought peace to the spirit of Golmash Hellscream?

passages.title: Golmash Hellscream
passages.text:
Golmash was a mighty warrior in life.

Few orcs have been as honored by their clans and feared by their enemies as the great Giantslayer... the father of the Hellscream name. With the mighty spirit of Golmash Hellscream finally put to rest, the ancestral grounds may once again be a place of peace and reverence.

You have our thanks, <name>.

passages.title: On the Mend
passages.text:
Nisha will heal.

This ordeal has taken a toll on her. She needs water and rest.

I will bring her to my camp and make her comfortable.

Will you meet us there with some fresh water?

passages.title: On the Mend
passages.text: <Nisha raises her head.>

passages.title: On the Mend
passages.text: <Nisha laps up the water.>

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text:
The dead ones were the strong ones it seems. The weak ones wander about killing invaders to this marsh.

It feels... wrong... to kill them, but they are worthless and get in our way. Kill these shambling fools so we can move further into the marsh easily.

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text: Have you taken care of those walking corpses?

passages.title: Clearing the Way
passages.text: You take too long. Something calls to us deeper in there. Whatever it is, I will have its skull or die trying.

passages.title: Into Anguish
passages.text:
Rulkan's gift to you, the Fragment of Anguish, will allow you to pass into the fortress unhindered. Go up these stairs to the doorway, then use the fragment to enter the compound.

Once you are inside, you will find three altars powering the magical barrier around their stronghold.

Destroy these runes, and Yrel and I will be able to join you in finding Ner'zhul.

passages.title: Into Anguish
passages.text:
<You hear Prophet Velen's voice in your mind.>

Good work, <name>! The barriers are down. We are on our way.

passages.title: Bad at Breaking
passages.text:
Screams and growls echo from the canyon below - even more than usual.

I don't dare leave Nisha here alone yet.

Will you investigate those noises, <name>?

passages.title: Bad at Breaking
passages.text: They are enslaving gronn? This is an even bigger problem than it might seem.

passages.title: What the Bony Xuk?
passages.text:
Good to see your bones are still intact, <name>. Xuk's too.

When you set off into the heart of the canyon, Xuk came to offer my services. Xuk not letting you take all of the skulls!

Xuk will share with you powerful spirit magics my clan has passed down for many generations. While Xuk make preparations, you must gather the reagents.

First, we'll need crystals from husks of goren corpses. You can find their bodies in the canyon.

passages.title: What the Bony Xuk?
passages.text: Laughing Skull have some dirty tricks behind our masks.

passages.title: What the Bony Xuk?
passages.text: Yes... we don't need their bones, but we do need their crystals.

passages.title: Heart of the Fen
passages.text:
If only the trees here weren't screaming at me I could concentrate better. Never mind, they are only trees.

This spot is used up but now I can feel a much stronger presence deeper in the marsh. I will go there now and take what is rightfully mine!

Then I will share it... with everyone...

passages.title: Heart of the Fen
passages.text:
Grulkor was crazy to think he could harness the power of those mushrooms, but then, most Laughing Skull are crazy.

Still, not a complete waste of time.

passages.title: Rescue Rangari
passages.text:
Many of our rangari have not been accounted for. It would seem the followers of Iyu have taken captives.

We will continue to search the area for survivors.

In the meantime, follow the Wildwood Wash west toward Highpass and look for any signs of our rangari comrades.

Our people are stout and capable survivors. You may find more than you expect. Have them stay near the road and we will follow as soon as this... dwarf creature... has fixed his mechanical vessel.

passages.title: Rescue Rangari
passages.text: It is no small thing for us to welcome so many strangers into our camps. Gorgrond is not the sort of place that breeds trust easily.

passages.title: Rescue Rangari
passages.text:
The rangari are stout survivalists. I knew they would not go down without a fight.

Thank you, <name>, for your help in this. You have done us a great honor.

passages.title: The Pride of Lok-rath
passages.text:
You think the Warsong are so easily defeated?

<There's a rasping sound, like rope on metal.>

I'm already tired of you Alliance, and you've just invaded my homeland.

<The sound becomes more pronounced as Uruk Foecleaver looks you straight in the eye.>

There will be no surrender. The Warsong bow to no one!

passages.title: The Pride of Lok-rath
passages.text: Unfortunate, but I'm glad you made it out of that trap alive.

passages.title: Fire Ammonite
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Frostfire Ridge for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Fire Ammonite
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Fire Ammonite
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: If They Won't Surrender...
passages.text:
This is the backbone of the army we intend to send against Garrosh Hellscream and Grommashar.

If they won't surrender, we have no choice but to eliminate the Warsong.

passages.title: If They Won't Surrender...
passages.text: Regrettable, but I understand the pride of the Warsong. I would never surrender.

passages.title: Shut 'er Down
passages.text:
Burrowing native creatures known as "goren" have tunneled into our crystal mines. Judging from our experience at the gates, I suspect my own experimental resonance crystal is whipping the native wildlife into a frenzy.

Enter the Elodor Dig to the north and disable the malfunctioning resonance crystal!

Be careful - my earthworkers report that the mine is crawling with those beasts.

passages.title: Shut 'er Down
passages.text:
Excellent. I will send in some peacekeepers to quell any remaining problems.

Exarch Naielle may be right - perhaps I am too aggressive in adapting our technology to this world. Still, I will never quit. Our civilization must move forward!

passages.title: Jawless Skulker
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Gorgrond for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Jawless Skulker
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Jawless Skulker
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Fat Sleeper
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Nagrand for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Fat Sleeper
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Fat Sleeper
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Blind Lake Sturgeon
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Shadowmoon Valley for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Blind Lake Sturgeon
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Blind Lake Sturgeon
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Blackwater Whiptail
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Talador for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Blackwater Whiptail
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Blackwater Whiptail
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Abyssal Gulper Eel
passages.text: We need to stock the garrison pond with local fish. I need you to search the waters in Spires of Arak for fish that we can stock up with. Once you have the fish, you will need to slice them up and look for eggs inside.

passages.title: Abyssal Gulper Eel
passages.text: Anything biting?

passages.title: Abyssal Gulper Eel
passages.text: These will do nicely, <name>!  Thank you!

passages.title: Defungination
passages.text:
Have you seen the fungus out there in the water? It's growing faster than a baby ravasaur from Un'goro, and if we don't get it under control, the Gearworks is gonna be ruined like our last village.

Uncle Krixel used to tell me to burn away the red fungus because that's what makes it grow so fast.

You could help us out by taking a flame blaster and clearing out some of those spores down in the shallows.

passages.title: Defungination
passages.text: Hey good job out there! I couldn't have done it any better myself.

passages.title: Silence the Call
passages.text:
The Warsong clan, in their lust for dominance, have turned to the darkness of the void for power. Dark shamanism is a loathsome, dangerous practice that abuses the elemental gift I have bestowed upon them.

There is one among the Warsong that calls out the loudest to the void, an elder shaman named Kuhlrath. Slay him and the rest of his dark shaman.

I will not allow the Warsong to abuse the elements and desecrate tradition.

passages.title: Silence the Call
passages.text: Have you put an end to the Warsong ritualists?

passages.title: Silence the Call
passages.text: The gift of shamanism is not one to be taken lightly. When the gift is abused, the elements will rise up in indignation and smite the shaman.

passages.title: The Shadow of the Void
passages.text:
The moment has come to take on the void lord. Invalidus grows more powerful by the minute, so you must move with haste if you are to defeat the monster.

At each of the Warsong ritual locations there is a void crystal; these crystals are used to channel the energy of the void from within the Twisting Nether.

Disturb the crystal, and Invalidus will sense your presence below.

Be ready, as soon as the crystal is disturbed, Invalidus will waste no time hunting you down.

passages.title: The Shadow of the Void
passages.text: Have you defeated Invalidus?

passages.title: The Shadow of the Void
passages.text: With Invalidus destroyed and the Warsong rituals halted, the threat of the Twisting Nether has subsided.

passages.title: The Right Parts for the Job
passages.text:
Uncle Krixel's a tough one but he won't be going anywhere on foot with his leg broken.

He has a flying machine he brought from Azeroth that can fly us out of here. Problem is, the engine's busted.

I'll need some parts to fix the thing. My car's wasted but those broken shredders just outside of town should have what we need. We don't have time to break them down by hand so just use this rocket launcher and blow 'em apart. Anything that survives the blast should be strong enough to use on the engine.

passages.title: The Right Parts for the Job
passages.text: Got any parts for me?

passages.title: The Right Parts for the Job
passages.text:
Great work <name>!

Give me some time and I'll have this thing ready to roll out!

passages.title: The Pride of Lok-rath
passages.text:
You think the Warsong are so easily defeated?

<There's a rasping sound, like rope on metal.>

I'm already tired of you Horde, and you've just invaded my homeland.

<The sound becomes more pronounced as Uruk Foecleaver looks you straight in the eye.>

There will be no surrender. The Warsong bow to no one!

passages.title: The Pride of Lok-rath
passages.text: Unfortunate, but you made it out of the trap alive and Lok-rath is dealt with.

passages.title: If They Won't Surrender...
passages.text:
This is the backbone of the army we intend to send against Garrosh Hellscream and Grommashar.

If they won't surrender, we have no choice but to eliminate the Warsong.

passages.title: If They Won't Surrender...
passages.text: Regrettable, but I understand the pride of the Warsong. I would never surrender.

passages.title: Avenge and Reclaim
passages.text: I will avenge my master and retrieve her life's work. Honor demands it. My heart yearns for it. If I die trying, so be it. The murderer will pay.

passages.title: Avenge and Reclaim
passages.text: The murderer will pay.

passages.title: Avenge and Reclaim
passages.text: My heart is furious with you for stealing my kill, but my mind knows that I did not have the strength to avenge my master myself. I will forgive you, if you allow me to pay my debt of honor.

passages.title: Book of Alchemical Secrets
passages.text: The writing in the leather-bound tome is undecipherable, except for the inscription inside the cover: "For my daughter, Ang'kra."

passages.title: Fair Warning
passages.text:
The ogron here are far from brilliant, but they are more intelligent than the gronn. They're large, and even stronger than they look.

Their leader, Borogahn, is especially formidable. Despite several fights, I have not yet managed to kill him.

Heed my words, friend. Take caution as you explore their lair.

Nisha is ready to move. Ask her to take you to the mouth of the cave, and I'm sure she would be happy to.

passages.title: Fair Warning
passages.text: Most people cannot handle ogron in single combat.

passages.title: Chains of Iron
passages.text:
The artifact we seek is within our grasp.

Be prepared for a fight. If they truly have learned how to control gronn, this may be more difficult than I anticipated.

I will join you in this battle as soon as you arrive.

passages.title: Chains of Iron
passages.text: The artifact is yours, and is well earned.

passages.title: Chains of Iron
passages.text: Good work, <name>. We can use this artifact against the Iron Horde when the time is right.

passages.title: Obliterating Ogres
passages.text:
We got more of those magic tossing ogres here which is never a good thing.

These new ogres are especially bossy and have increased work being done here.

Do you know what stops ogres from working hard? Dying.

Kill some ogres here and get this camp back to its normal boring self.

passages.title: Obliterating Ogres
passages.text: Great! They are pretty scared now. Its hard to do research when you are afraid of being stabbed in the back at any time!

passages.title: Reglakk's Research
passages.text:
Okay so these orders say Reglakk is in charge of something called Breaker research, which makes super powerful ogres. I don't know about you but that sounds bad.

I'm pretty hurt, do you think you can go up there alone and make Reglakk rethink his research?

passages.title: Reglakk's Research
passages.text:
We stopped him for the time being, but I think we'll have to come up with a more permanent solution. No doubt he's back in Highmaul plotting new versions of Breakers.

I think a visit to ogre capital is far overdue.

passages.title: And Justice for Thrall
passages.text:
The time has come, commander. You've dealt with all of the Warsong's allies and holdings.

Our troops are massing at the gates of Grommashar. The rangari have reliable intel that Garrosh is holed up inside the Warsong fortress.

All of our efforts have led to this moment. Let's take out Garrosh.

passages.title: And Justice for Thrall
passages.text:
It's over. The Warsong are broken. Garrosh Hellscream is finally dead.

Somehow, I sense it's only a matter of time before Grommash seeks vengeance.

passages.title: And Justice for Thrall
passages.text:
The time has come, commander. You've dealt with all of the Warsong's allies and holdings.

Our troops are massing at the gates of Grommashar. The shadow hunters have reliable intel that Garrosh is holed up inside the Warsong fortress.

All of our efforts have led to this moment. Let's put an end to this once and for all.

passages.title: And Justice for Thrall
passages.text:
It's over. The Warsong are broken. Garrosh Hellscream is finally dead.

It's just a matter of time before Grommash seeks vengeance.

passages.title: Your Second Blacksmithing Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Blacksmithing Work Order
passages.text: We look forward to serving you again.

passages.title: Keeping it Together
passages.text:
So much work to do... I don't even know where to start.

Making sure this garrison is operational is not an easy task.

Shelly still hasn't reported back to me, my assistant Brightstone and her crew are who knows where, ugh... I'm so caught up I haven't even had time to check our cache for resources.

If I were a mage, do you think I could use mirror images to do all of this at once?

passages.title: Keeping it Together
passages.text: Can we speak a little later, Sir? I don't really have time to talk at the moment.

passages.title: Keeping it Together
passages.text:
You did what? You are a life saver, commander.

With those tasks out of the way my job will be much easier.

passages.title: Infiltrating the Sargerei
passages.text:
One of my men has already infiltrated the Sargerei's ranks, but I need you to help him.

In order to protect his cover, you will need to disguise yourself as one of the enemy.

Kill Sargerei until you collect a cowl, robe, and slippers to create a disguise.

After donning the disguise, introduce yourself to Soulbinder Zamaya as a new student, then tell Anchorite Laanda that 'the rain falls on Shadowmoon.'

The secret phrase will identify yourself as an ally.

passages.title: Infiltrating the Sargerei
passages.text: Yes, initiate?

passages.title: Infiltrating the Sargerei
passages.text:
Welcome, my friend. I have managed to earn a bit of favor with the Sargerei, but they still guard their secrets closely.

Only the strongest will be accepted in the ranks of the Sargerei.

Soulpriest Zamaya is the leader of our operations here. To secure our objectives, you must first win her trust.

passages.title: Pesky Podlings
passages.text:
Ah, initiate. Are you ready for your first task?

The woods to the south are filled with pesky podlings. The filthy things dig up our farms, steal supplies, and prey on unwitting trainees.

They are disgusting, horrible creatures which need to be eliminated.

<Zamaya gives you a skeptical look.>

I will require their spears as proof that you finished this task.

passages.title: Pesky Podlings
passages.text: Those filthy creatures don't deserve to live.

passages.title: Pesky Podlings
passages.text: I expect no less from an initiate.

passages.title: An Ancient Threat
passages.text:
To the northwest, an Ancient has settled into a forest glade.

I need someone to take care of this nuisance.

This should be a simple matter, even for an initiate like you.

passages.title: An Ancient Threat
passages.text: Not bad.

passages.title: Weapons Of Our Enemies
passages.text:
We are doing well, initiate. We are close to gaining access to the council's chambers.

Meanwhile, our subterfuge will continue. Atop the hill to the northeast, you will find the Sargerei training grounds.

For months they have been hammering, forging, and crafting the finest weapons to equip into battle.

We can undo their work in only moments, <name>.

Steal their weapons. Let us see if they can still strike, then.

passages.title: Bushwhacker
passages.text:
We are continuing the search for Thaelin's people, but these botani, they are a larger threat than we ever realized.

To infest their victims... monstrous.

Please, commander, if you find yourself in Evermorn Springs to our west, slay as many of those creatures as you can.

Stop them from committing such acts of horror. Bring them to justice.

passages.title: Bushwhacker
passages.text: Well done, commander. At every turn you seem to demonstrate an efficiency with war that even our most seasoned exarchs might fight to be challenging.

passages.title: The Life Spring
passages.text:
So we came here cause we needed a weapon we saw the botani using.

Hansel grabbed the artifact an' Scorchbrow an' I were supposed to grab the special water the thing runs on.

We didn't know that water so full of life forms an elemental.

If ya mosey up to the cauldron at the base of that fancy lookin' ancient artifact in Evermorn Springs, you'll be findin' this beast. If ya can kill it and get its water, we can use it when we get the rest of the artifact.

passages.title: The Life Spring
passages.text: Now I see why some become Rangari. This is exciting.

passages.title: The Life Spring
passages.text: You are carrying something of great power on you. I could feel it as you approached.

passages.title: Preventing the Worst
passages.text:
Have you seen all the fungus on the buildings in Pinchwhistle Point? It's only a matter of time 'til it releases enough spores to infest the whole coastline!

The remaining infected that are in Pinchwhistle Point will be too far gone for us to save later on, so let's do the right thing and put them out of their misery and prevent an even worse outbreak.

I made some firebombs that will burn the fungus down, but I'll need you to place them while I set up the detonator.

Are you up for it?

passages.title: Preventing the Worst
passages.text: I'm almost done here. Have you placed all those firebombs yet?

passages.title: Preventing the Worst
passages.text:
Good work!

Ok I need to just finish setting up the ignition mechanism and we'll be all set.

passages.title: The Razorbloom
passages.text:
Kaalya thinks she picked up a trail. Seems a bunch of dwarves went north to Razorbloom by the signs.

Problem is that place is filled with plant people. I ain't much use against plant people.

Are you willing to investigate?

passages.title: The Razorbloom
passages.text: The plant people fattened up my friends with fruit an' honey an' mead. Seems they were fattenin' them up for sure.

passages.title: Pearing It Up
passages.text:
While you do Zamaya's work to earn her favor, we will secretly be sabotaging the Sargerei operation.

In the forests to the northwest, the podlings have gathered stolen pears from the farms. The little pests go crazy for the stuff.

The pears also happen to be a main food source for the Sargerei, so naturally, we're going to destroy the harvest.

That should take care of the podlings AND the draenei at the same time.

passages.title: Pearing It Up
passages.text: Excellent! I admit I love the taste of those pears as well, but it is a small price to pay to destroy our enemy.

passages.title: Down the Goren Hole
passages.text:
These beasts came at us so fast we didn't have time to mount a proper defense. They went right for the metal and chewed through any wall we had.

If we don't kill some of them soon they'll bring the whole fortress down on us.

passages.title: Down the Goren Hole
passages.text: All in a day's work, eh Commander?

passages.title: Down the Goren Hole
passages.text: You give me blackrock orcs, troggs, er evil leper gnomes an' we'd be fine. But these acid munchin' beasts are the end of us.

passages.title: Iyu
passages.text:
Did ya hear that?

Sounds like that genesaur wants its 'will' back. I told ya this place is nuthin' but bad luck.

I'll git that shot ya gave me loaded properly and see if I can't weaken that thing up. You better get up there and deal with it though...

passages.title: Iyu
passages.text: How goes your search?

passages.title: Iyu
passages.text: That was a challenge.

passages.title: A Harsh Reminder
passages.text:
Welcome to the front lines, outsider, where the wastelands and the jungle collide.

When their forces forget about the ferocity of the Laughing Skull, this is where we come to make them remember.

By fierce and merciless destruction we survive. This is the way of Gorgrond.

Join in! Let us see if you can withstand the brutality of our land.

passages.title: A Harsh Reminder
passages.text: I like killing things. And bones.

passages.title: Hardly Working
passages.text:
Those who were not incinerated at Veil Akraz are forced to help the Adherents excavate the very weapons aimed at their heads.

Anyone trying to escape is vaporized by the overseer's Apexis turret.

With these effigies, they won't know anyone has left! Place one near an enslaved worker and observe as it creates a perfect copy. It even cloaks the subject in shadow, so they can slip away safely!

passages.title: Hardly Working
passages.text: Deception is the ultimate power. Remember this, <name>.

passages.title: The Ritual of Binding
passages.text:
The time has come for you to undertake the Ritual of Binding, <name>.

This ancient, shamanic rite has been practiced since long before I was born. To be chosen is a great honor.

Many shaman see vivid elemental visions during the rite; experiencing this world through the very elemental bonds that hold it together.

When you are ready, speak with Kalandrios to begin the rite.

passages.title: The Ritual of Binding
passages.text: Tell me of your vision, <name>. What did the elements reveal?

passages.title: The Ritual of Binding
passages.text:
<Farseer Drek'Thar listens closely as you speak of your vision.>

I see... these are truly dark days. Cho'gall has invaded the heart of Oshu'gun, draining the naaru of its life. He seeks to destroy the naaru, birthing a dark, void god in its place.

Cho'gall must be stopped. Come, we must travel to the sacred mountain before it is too late.

passages.title: Hot Seat
passages.text:
<Apexis constructs are about to emerge from their ancient chambers on a warpath. The arakkoa are sure to send more sol-shapers to support them.

The interface and the turret hum in soft resonance.>

passages.title: Hot Seat
passages.text:
Ahh, well done. Even with my condition, I could sense the carnage from here.

It must have been quite a show, kah-hah-haww.

passages.title: The Dark Heart of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
We are not far from the inner chamber, <name>. The truth behind the evil here awaits us.

I can project my spirit into the chamber to guide you, but it will be up to you to defeat the evil that lays within.

May the wind of Kalandrios guide your arm, the wisdom of Aborius enlighten your faculties, and the flame of Incineratus burn your enemies.

May the memory of Gordawg be your shield.

passages.title: The Dark Heart of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
You have done well, <name>.

By defeating the void god Decimatus, the destruction of this great valley has been avoided. The threat of the pale has subsided for now as well.

The loss of Gordawg will be felt throughout Nagrand, but someday a new earthen fury will take seat upon the Throne of Elements and balance will be restored.

passages.title: The Ritual of Binding
passages.text:
It is time for you to undergo the Ritual of Binding, <name>. I will wait here as you speak with Kalandrios to begin the rite.

During the ritual, you will experience the vision of the elements. Return to me when the ritual is complete, and we will speak more.

passages.title: The Ritual of Binding
passages.text: Speak to me of your vision, <name>. What mysteries did you behold?

passages.title: The Ritual of Binding
passages.text:
<Vindicator Nobundo listens closely as you speak of your vision.>

These are grave images of which you speak, <name>! If Cho'gall continues bleeding the naaru of its Light, K'ure will die and in the naaru's place a void god will emerge. Void gods are terrible creatures that live only to destroy!

We must travel to Oshu'gun immediately and put a stop to the threat of Cho'gall!

passages.title: That Pounding Sound
passages.text:
Commander. The rangari and I were just discussing the merits of various 'hunting' approaches.

I assured her that the SI:7 are well-equipped to deal with any situation, even ones out in the wild.

She seems to think that we don't know what we're doing when it comes to bringing down game in 'her land.'

We're not going to let her get away with saying that, right? Let's take down some clefthoof.

passages.title: That Pounding Sound
passages.text: It's unbelievable how arrogant these rangari can be.

passages.title: That Pounding Sound
passages.text:
Twelve pairs, huh? That's pretty good, commander.

Um, no, I think that's about how many I managed to bag. Yeah... about a dozen pairs of ears. Yep....

passages.title: A Parting Favor
passages.text:
I don't know what happened. My crew and I must have been the first to fall.

My wife, the innkeeper, is in the same stupor you found me in. I can feel it... and there are others with her.

Please, give the townsfolk peace and show their essences to my wife. That should bring her back from that cold abyss.

passages.title: A Parting Favor
passages.text: Everything is so hazy... what happened? Who are you?

passages.title: A Parting Favor
passages.text: We're... dead?

passages.title: Shocking Assistance
passages.text:
It's been a struggle to support the family since my wife died, and I got too ambitious when I got a contract for shockscales.

Alas, there is no way I will hunt enough eels to fulfill it in time now.

passages.title: Shocking Assistance
passages.text: Thank you so much for finding my father.

passages.title: Shocking Assistance
passages.text:
You did this for my family? After you saved our father? Thank you, <name>.

You wished to know about Draenor alchemy? I will do my best to share my knowledge with you.

passages.title: A Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text:
I... I remember now. Watch Commander Branson told us to stay in the inn... he said we would be safe here.

Then...

Then that THING broke through and slaughtered everyone!

The last thing I remember seeing was it descending into the larder.

passages.title: A Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text: Is the creature dead?

passages.title: A Piece of the Puzzle
passages.text: I will convince the others of our fate. There's no denying it anymore.

passages.title: King of the Breezestriders
passages.text:
Let me guess, you found it in a talbuk's flank?

<Laara seems lost in thought for a moment.>

That arrow was intended for Tall Buck, king of the Breezestriders. Another talbuk - the one you killed - jumped in the way as I was taking my shot.

I suggest you go after the king. When I was hunting him, he seemed fond of the pond at Lonely Falls to the south.

passages.title: King of the Breezestriders
passages.text: How goes the hunt for Tall Buck?

passages.title: King of the Breezestriders
passages.text:
Well done, <name>. You succeeded where I did not.

Perhaps you outsiders aren't such bad hunters after all.

passages.title: That Pounding Sound
passages.text:
Commander. The frostwolf and I were just discussing the merits of various 'hunting' approaches.

I assured her that the shadow hunters are well-equipped to deal with any situation, even ones out in the wild.

She seems to think that we don't know what we're doing when it comes to bringing down game in 'her land.'

We're not going to let her get away with saying that, right? Let's take down some clefthoof.

passages.title: That Pounding Sound
passages.text: It's unbelievable how arrogant these frostwolves can be.

passages.title: That Pounding Sound
passages.text:
Twelve pairs, huh? That's pretty good, commander.

Um, no, I think that's about how many I managed to bag. Yeah... about a dozen pairs of ears. Yep....

passages.title: King of the Breezestriders
passages.text:
Let me guess, you found it in a talbuk's flank?

<Ogka seems lost in thought for a moment.>

That axe was intended for Tall Buck, king of the Breezestriders. Another talbuk - the one you killed - jumped in the way as I was taking my shot.

I suggest you go after the king. When I was hunting him, he seemed fond of the pond at Lonely Falls to the south.

passages.title: King of the Breezestriders
passages.text: How goes the hunt for Tall Buck?

passages.title: King of the Breezestriders
passages.text:
Well done, <name>. You succeeded where I did not.

Perhaps you outsiders aren't such bad hunters after all.

passages.title: The Dark Heart of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
Amongst the timeworn wreckage of the Genedar is the entrance to the vessel's inner chamber. The void energy appears to be most concentrated in that place.

You must enter the inner chamber and face whatever evil lurks within. I fear whatever fate may have befallen the great naaru K'ure in that place, but regardless the evil there must be purged.

May the Light be with you, <name>.

passages.title: The Dark Heart of Oshu'gun
passages.text:
The fate of K'ure could not have been prevented.

Cho'gall accelerated the naaru's transition into a void god in hopes of bringing destruction upon Draenor. Cho'gall must be dealt with, but for now let us honor the memory of the great naaru K'ure.

K'ure was truly the savior of my people, a friend to the virtuous, and a teacher of prophets.

May the great naaru ever live within our hearts.

passages.title: Mossy Fate
passages.text:
Your wolf queen will not let me out of her sight.

The children of the magnaron may have destroyed my village but it was the children of the genesaur who took my people.

The botani and their minions drag our people to the Razorbloom, and if we see them again, it is not as they were in life.

You have already helped the Skulls, so I ask your help again.

Enter the Razorbloom and search for my people that were recently taken.

Perhaps they may even be alive.

passages.title: Mossy Fate
passages.text:
Dead? All dead? Dead and mulched and forgotten. No Chag with his missing nose or Meka with her love for chewing faces.

And Torg, my beloved Torg. A son we had together. A son that is still missing.

The botani will pay for this. They will burn for this.

passages.title: Bushwhacker
passages.text:
Kaz is using us, I am sure of it. She is a Laughing Skull and must NOT be trusted.

For now, I am willing to play along until we can learn more. 

Kaz is going to ask for you to travel to Evermorn Springs. When there, I recommend you slay any botani you encounter.

Culling the numbers of these horrific casters will hopefully save future orcs from such a infested fate.

I will stay with Kaz and keep a close eye on her.

passages.title: Bushwhacker
passages.text:
I had thought the Laughing Skull were planning something. Now I think I am beginning to understand.

They match savagery with savagery.

passages.title: The Life Spring
passages.text:
It sounds like these... "dwarves"... you found managed to steal a powerful botani artifact.

But the fools didn't know they need a special water to power it.

To the north is a well along the Evermorn Rise.

There you will find a guardian, a creature of water we have named Utrophis.

Slay it and take its essence and you will be one step closer to claiming the power of the botani and their genesaur.

passages.title: The Life Spring
passages.text: For years the Laughing Skull would not touch the sacred waters. We feared the wrath of the botani. We should have set them to burn long ago.

passages.title: The Life Spring
passages.text:
The Waters of Utrophis. I have never held or smelled or tasted it before. But I have heard many stories, many legends.

I was expecting something more grand.

passages.title: Attack of the Iron Horde
passages.text:
We received reports of the Dark Portal turning red right before the attack. They call themselves the Iron Horde, yet they seem to have no affiliation with the Horde we know.

Their army is extremely well equipped, and their numbers appear to be unending.

They have already taken Nethergarde Keep. Our troops on the frontlines could use your help, <class>.

passages.title: Attack of the Iron Horde
passages.text: Good form, champion. I'm sure your presence on the field was inspiring for our troops.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor
passages.text:
Admiral Taylor had figured out who was behind all this. He told us to save who we could... he wanted to handle matters himself.

We never heard from him again, but we have our orders.

Please... please find him. He went towards the farm.

passages.title: Admiral Taylor
passages.text:
From one commander to another... thank you.

We've been through a lot together, haven't we, <name>? Vashj'ir... the Jade Forest... Lion's Landing...

I am truly honored that I could end my journey by your side.

passages.title: Lunatic Lieutenants
passages.text:
It is time we learned more about our new enemy.

Our scouts have identified a number of the Iron Horde's lieutenants. Their attack is too organized to be run by tribal knowledge alone. Surely their lieutenants have access to secret battleplans. 

You are the only soldier I can trust with this mission, <name>.

passages.title: Lunatic Lieutenants
passages.text: Were you able to gain access to any battleplans?

passages.title: Lunatic Lieutenants
passages.text: Let's take a look at these battleplans.

passages.title: Toothsmash the Annihilator
passages.text:
If the battleplans you brought back are true, the Dreadmaul ogres are as much to blame for this devastation as the Iron Horde. It's time we send those ogres a message.

It looks like the Iron Horde's main contact is a large ogre in Dreadmaul named Toothsmash. Killing him will put a dent in their battleplans.

passages.title: Toothsmash the Annihilator
passages.text: Toothsmash is dead? Good, I'm sure it will take the Iron Horde a while to find another ogre smart enough to help them with their efforts.

passages.title: Growing Wood
passages.text:
I found this dwarf, Thuldren, runnin' out of Tangleheart like his boots were on fire.

Says his mole machine showed up here and he barely made it out alive. And another called Frenna might still be inside.

One useful thing he told me is that the creatures in there have sap that can be used to grow things real fast.

By the way, I'm gonna go lookin' for Thuldren's mole machine. Find me in Tangleheart when you're done.

passages.title: Growing Wood
passages.text: Don't be such a sap. Get it?!

passages.title: Growing Wood
passages.text: You got it! You should be able to use this mole machine one way back to your outpost.

passages.title: Down the Goren Hole
passages.text:
Dwarves are dumb. Don't they know that if you dig a deep hole you are going to have goren attack?

If you are going to go into that iron fort you better kill a bunch of goren otherwise they are going to chew the walls enough to cause a cave-in.

I would do it myself but I'm still stuffed from all that fruit the botani made me eat.

passages.title: Down the Goren Hole
passages.text: Goren like to chew things. I HATE THAT!

passages.title: Down the Goren Hole
passages.text: Goren, goren, gone!

passages.title: Iyu
passages.text:
There is a genesaur here!

It wants its artifact back.

Kaz and Draka are fighting it now on the surface but they need you. Draka said I could fire the big gun. So I will stay here and do that.

passages.title: Iyu
passages.text: Was the shaman being truthful?

passages.title: Iyu
passages.text: It was an honor to fight by your side today, commander.

passages.title: [Deprecated]
passages.text:
We wouldn't have survived Tanaan without you. Many draenei and Alliance alike owe a great debt to you.

King Wrynn personally requested that I place you in charge of our operations here in Draenor, and after seeing you in action, I'm inclined to agree.

This is your garrison to found. Plant the banner and we'll begin construction immediately, commander.

passages.title: Trust No One
passages.text:
Nothing is the same since I returned. There is always whispering - everywhere, whispering. Maraad cannot see it, but there are even traces of fel energy here in Elodor. We have been infiltrated!

I must attend to the Exarch Council, but I need you to investigate. Follow the traces of fel energy that I will illuminate. If there are truly traitors in our midst, they will have to have some sort of hideout. Find it! I will wait for you with the other Exarchs.

passages.title: Trust No One
passages.text: A flesh-bound book lies on an unholy altar. Your skin crawls. Maladaar was right!

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text:
Commander, Yrel and Maraad have a tactical suggestion.

They recommend a small expedition group be sent into the savage wastelands of Gorgrond far to the north.

Reports from their rangari suggest that land may hold ancient secrets or primal knowledge that we might use to exploit weaknesses in the Iron Horde that our enemy would not expect.

If you wish to go I will have a gryphon prepared for you at once.

passages.title: The Secrets of Gorgrond
passages.text: Welcome to Gorgrond, Commander. We only just arrived ourselves.

passages.title: Control is King
passages.text:
Apexis technology is fascinating, isn't it? Machines powered by solar energy. Energy which itself has been imbued with magic!

Simply brilliant!

Ah, but there's always a catch. And I think you may have found it.

Bring the interface device back to Veil Terokk, will you? I'll be along shortly with the Apexis cores.

If my theory is right, we may be able to turn the Adherents' own weapon against them!

passages.title: Control is King
passages.text: Did you bring the device?

passages.title: Control is King
passages.text: It will take some time, but this may be the key to our victory.

passages.title: Mercy for the Living
passages.text:
You can see that the dead were the lucky ones. Those that live wander about attacking anything not infected with these vile spores.

I cannot bring myself to slay them, but if you could bring mercy to those poor people I would be very grateful.

passages.title: Mercy for the Living
passages.text: Perhaps we shouldn't have wasted time on them, this place... drains me. Still it was a good deed you have done.

passages.title: Growing Wood
passages.text:
We got the lumber mill good an' built, but we be needin' more wood!

The Rangari tol' me there's botani usin' some kinda sap to grow ancients fast as you like.

Get yer hands on some o' that sap and I betcha I can put it work.

What? Oh, Glyza here? Found 'er crashed here and she knows a thing or two about lumberjackin'. I'll take her back to the outpost later.

I'll meet ya inside Tangleheart if I can find it.

passages.title: Growing Wood
passages.text: Glyza is good with tools.

passages.title: Growing Wood
passages.text: Sap? Who called me a sap?! Oh...

passages.title: Heart of the Fen
passages.text:
The pounding in my head is almost unbearable but I must see this through. With all the spore samples I've taken I know where to go and what to do.

I will find the source and spread... no! Destroy it! I will do what needs to be done!

passages.title: Heart of the Fen
passages.text: That is terrible news. I will warn off all scouts from venturing to the Crimson Fen from now on.  Thank you and I am glad you were not affected by the spores...

passages.title: A Harsh Reminder
passages.text:
Welcome to the front lines, commander, where the wastelands and the jungle collide.

The battle below rages on, but I believe one side is beginning to overwhelm the other. This cannot be allowed to happen.

The gronnlings are gaining an upper hand and must be stopped before they pose a threat to Highpass.

I will get closer to the battle while you thin their ranks. Meet me within Affliction Ridge when you are done.

passages.title: A Harsh Reminder
passages.text: You have a true talent for combat.

passages.title: Chains of Iron
passages.text:
The artifact we seek is within our grasp.

Be prepared for a fight. If they truly have learned how to control gronn, this may be more difficult than I anticipated.

I will join you in this battle as soon as you arrive.

passages.title: Chains of Iron
passages.text: We have the artifact, and with it we will make the Iron Horde pay.

passages.title: Chains of Iron
passages.text: Yes... Think of the orcs that will fall before us with this power...

passages.title: The Talon King
passages.text:
<As Reshad begins reciting a tale of Terokk's glory days, your eyes fall to the twin swords at the effigy's belt.

They had seemed so plain in Skettis, but now they thrum with power, as if reacting to the scrollkeeper's words.>

passages.title: The Talon King
passages.text:
That was but one of many such tales.

No arakkoa living or dead has ever compared to the Talon King.

passages.title: Attack of the Iron Horde
passages.text:
We received reports of the Dark Portal turning red right before the attack. They call themselves the Iron Horde.

Their army is extremely well equipped, and their numbers appear to be unending.

They have already taken Okril'lon Hold and Nethergarde Keep. Our troops on the frontlines could use your help, <class>.

passages.title: Attack of the Iron Horde
passages.text: Aka'Magosh, champion. I'm sure your presence on the field was inspiring for the troops.

passages.title: Taking a Trip to the Top of the Tank
passages.text:
We cannot risk the reactivation of the Dark Portal. Now is the time for the deathblow.

Thaelin should have figured out how to get that tank working by now. Take him with you, and turn that tank against the Dark Portal itself. We will follow behind you.

passages.title: Taking a Trip to the Top of the Tank
passages.text: This... I can work with this.

passages.title: Lunatic Lieutenants
passages.text:
It is time we learned more about our new enemy.

Our scouts have identified a number of the Iron Horde's lieutenants. Their attack is too organized to be run by tribal knowledge alone. Surely their lieutenants have access to secret battleplans. 

You are the only soldier I can trust with this mission, <name>.

passages.title: Lunatic Lieutenants
passages.text: Were you able to gain access to any battleplans?

passages.title: Lunatic Lieutenants
passages.text: Let's take a look at these battleplans.

passages.title: Toothsmash the Annihilator
passages.text:
If the battleplans you brought back are true, the Dreadmaul ogres are as much to blame for this devastation as the Iron Horde. It's time we send those ogres a message.

It looks like the Iron Horde's main contact is a large ogre in Dreadmaul named Toothsmash. Killing him will put a dent in their battleplans.

passages.title: Toothsmash the Annihilator
passages.text: Toothsmash is dead? Good, I'm sure it will take the Iron Horde a while to find another ogre smart enough to help them with their efforts.

passages.title: Bronze Victory
passages.text: With every victory, or claim here grows more strong.

passages.title: Silver Victory
passages.text: Without each battle, or sovereignty here grows, Commander.

passages.title: Gold Victory
passages.text: Our foes cringe, Commander. Hah! They'll lick their wounds for days before even dreaming of another fight.

passages.title: The Ebon Hunter
passages.text:
The laser should be good to go once we get it set up, there's just one more thing I need.

There's a spore walker that hunts on the delta just southeast from here. It has an apparatus on its face that can fire a powerful laser - way more powerful than what we have hooked up.

I want it.

We'll be mining faster than you can imagine once we get that bad boy hooked up!

passages.title: The Ebon Hunter
passages.text: I should probably have mentioned that the laser is pretty... potent.

passages.title: The Ebon Hunter
passages.text: Perfection. Let's get it hooked up!

passages.title: Wake of the Genesaur
passages.text:
One moment we see a great metal beast rolling into our camp, the next a genesaur follows it and sends a wave of pure chaotic life at us.

The manifestations left behind by the genesaur must be culled so we have time to salvage what we can before leaving.

If you are here to help, then start killing as many of the violent plants that are assailing us as possible.

passages.title: Wake of the Genesaur
passages.text: This has not been a good day.

passages.title: Wake of the Genesaur
passages.text: A good start. The growth from a genesaur is pure chaos and must be culled whenever possible.

passages.title: The Ebon Hunter
passages.text:
We're ready to set up the laser, but we're going to need more firepower to cut through this stuff.

The Ebon Hunter stalks the delta just southeast from here. It has an apparatus on its face that can fire a laser way stronger than what we have hooked up.

We need that.

You should go get it while we set up the laser.

passages.title: The Ebon Hunter
passages.text: By the way, that laser is very dangerous. Be careful!

passages.title: The Ebon Hunter
passages.text: Alright, let's put this thing to use!

passages.title: Terokk's Fall
passages.text:
<Once again, Reshad's voice envelops you.>

Terokk was a powerful and respected king, beloved by his people.

His sages, however, were not so loyal. Hungry for control of Skyreach, they conspired against him.

passages.title: Terokk's Fall
passages.text: Since that day, the sages have remained in power in Skyreach, now calling themselves the Adherents of Rukhmar and claiming to be the heralds of Her will.

passages.title: The Avatar of Terokk
passages.text:
My long sleep was disturbed by dreams of the past. I cut down my old enemies again. I watched my daughter die again.

You were there. I felt your presence in these dreams. And your past was revealed to me as well.

Someone has woven our fates together. My people are yours to protect, and your enemies are mine to destroy.

The Shattered Hand are rallied in Bladefist Hold. Left to their own, they would claim this land for the Iron Horde.

Take my power, and together we shall break them.

passages.title: The Avatar of Terokk
passages.text: Take what you have earned, <name>.

passages.title: The Avatar of Terokk
passages.text:
The Shattered Hand is in shambles and the Avatar of Terokk now walks among us.

When I promised you power back in Skettis, did you expect that it would come without any strings attached? Ha!

passages.title: Supply Drop
passages.text:
Your laborers below have finished with the harvest and are ready to cart supplies back to your garrison. Don't worry about the safety of your caravan this time; I will dispatch a rangari detail to shadow them from the woods and protect them.

The Exarchs will always watch over you.

Your supplies should be waiting for you when you return to your garrison. Good luck with your campaign, <name>!

passages.title: Supply Drop
passages.text:
Commander! Zipfizzle arrived with your laborers in tow just moments ago. We've got a huge surplus of food, now, and promises of more where that came from.

Apparently the draenei threw in some other resources as well. Very good work, sir. What should we build next?

passages.title: Azeroth's Last Stand
passages.text:
Countless times you have battled against impossible odds and unspeakable evil - and returned the victor. Now, once more, you have answered the call of duty, prepared to risk your life to save the world that you love - our world.

You are Azeroth's last hope, <name>.

While the challenges that stand before us are daunting, there is no other that I would trust to lead this mission.

The enemy at the front may have the information we need to win this war. Seek and destroy!

Go now, <name>! For Azeroth!

passages.title: The Power of Poison
passages.text:
G.V.? We need a name and a location. Not damned initials.

<Velonara pulls out a small vial.>

This is my last vial of wracking poison. We use it to extract information from prisoners. It is... potent.

Coat your weapon with it and head into the Shattered Hand camp just ahead. Engage them as normal and demand answers - the poison will take care of the rest. I've had enough of these orcs.

passages.title: The Power of Poison
passages.text: This Gardul Venomshiv is as good as dead.

passages.title: The Power of Poison
passages.text:
G.V.? We need a full name. A location!

I have an idea fer how we can find those out.

<Hulda pulls out a small vial.>

This is my last vial o' wracking poison. We use it when we need tae extract information from prisoners.

Coat yer weapon wi' it and head into the Shattered Hand camp just ahead. Engage them as normal and demand answers - the poison will take care o' the rest.

passages.title: The Power of Poison
passages.text: Gardul Venomshiv, eh? He's good as dead.

passages.title: Preservation Capitalization
passages.text:
I'm looking for precious artifacts. The kind of artifacts that can help solve some of the greatest mysteries of Draenor, and make the Steamwheedle Preservation Society a ton of moolah. And ladies love the moolah, know what I'm sayin?

So, get me the artifacts, I'll get the ladies, and you get... wait, what are you looking for again?

passages.title: Preservation Capitalization
passages.text: What do you find? Anything worth selling? Err.. preserving.

passages.title: Preservation Capitalization
passages.text:
Nice! What did you get?

A necklace, not bad.. another necklace, good. A giant rock in the shape of an ogre head?

<Greblin seems puzzled, he glances up at you.>

Seriously? This is a rock in the shape of an idiot. Whatever, the necklaces look good.

Not a bad find overall.

passages.title: Khadgar's Task
passages.text:
This world poses many dangers to our own. Chief among them is the Iron Horde - your garrison and the full might of your army is directed at this foe. But for myself I have a different target in mind.

Gul'dan.

Here, make yourself comfortable. Have some mana strudel. I will share my plan as I create your ring...

passages.title: Khadgar's Task
passages.text:
Your ring is finished. This is but the first step - with more time together we'll be able to create a ring of legendary power. But first things first!

Gul'dan could be hiding anywhere, but if we can locate any of his lieutenants I think I know a way to flush him out. Let's begin by gathering the magical reagents I'll need.

passages.title: Legacy of the Sorcerer Kings
passages.text:
For over a thousand years, the ogre sorcerer kings maintained an iron grip over their empire using a variety of artifacts. Trusted lieutenants were given magical gems that allowed them to enforce the emperor's will out in the field. These "Abrogator Stones" still maintain their power even today, and can be found scattered throughout the Highmaul complex. Sometimes in clusters.

Collect $1oa of these Abrogator Stones for me!

passages.title: Legacy of the Sorcerer Kings
passages.text: Do you have the stones? I never thought I'd turn to ogres for magical might, but those ancient Sorcerer Kings knew a thing or two about raw arcane energy that would keep Kirin-Tor scholars busy for ages.

passages.title: Legacy of the Sorcerer Kings
passages.text:
<Khadgar holds some of the stones up to the light, allowing narrow filaments of arcane energy to spiral from stone to stone.>

I don't think I'll ever underestimate ogres again, <name>. One or two intelligent ones can mold the others into a formidable army.

passages.title: Power Unleashed
passages.text:
You've more than earned a reward, commander. I'll wrap things up here and meet you back at my tower - you can use my portal as a shortcut.

Speak to me when you arrive and I will use Kairoz's power with the crystals you gathered earlier to upgrade your ring!

passages.title: Power Unleashed
passages.text: Do you slay a lot of dragons? You handled that like a professional.

passages.title: Power Unleashed
passages.text:
How are you feeling? Can I get you a drink?

I wish I could say that things will get easier from here, but we're just getting started. I must ask you to storm the very heart of the ogre empire... Are you ready?

passages.title: Touch of the Kirin-Tor
passages.text:
<Khadgar's breathing is labored and his face is drained of color, but his eyes still flash with energy.>

You saved me, <name>. Once again I underestimated Gul'dan, and it nearly cost me everything.

Come, help me up. While Jaina is here, the two of us can work together to upgrade your ring. You've earned it! Let me know when you're ready.

passages.title: Touch of the Kirin-Tor
passages.text:
How are you feeling?

That ring of yours is now one of the most powerful artifacts on this world. Which is good. Because we're about to strike right at the heart of the enemy...

passages.title: Heart of the Fury
passages.text:
