passages.title: The Dark Lady's Concern
passages.text: I assure you, commander, the Dark Lady has the Horde's best interests at heart. We must stop these botani immediately.

passages.title: The Dark Lady's Concern
passages.text: Thank you, commander. The Dark Lady will appreciate this greatly.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
There are others that harness the shadows to do their bidding. You know of them, commander... the Shadowmoon orcs.

They have begun to master their craft... they call to the shadows beyond this realm...

I desire their power. They have one who possesses a staff of particular interest... we should claim it as our own.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text: Taking out our enemies and gaining great power in one motion... my people have a saying for this: Killing two orcs with one stone.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
Yes... yes... this will do nicely. We can use this to do great things.

Thank you, commander.

passages.title: Ogre Ancestry
passages.text:
Lunk no like fight, want to learn. You help Lunk learn?

Find Lunk ancestors. Lunk have many question. Where Lunk come from? Why Lunk Lunk?

Lunk stay here. Small ogres mean, big ogres meaner.

passages.title: Ogre Ancestry
passages.text: How can Lunk Lunk if Lunk not know what Lunk is?

passages.title: Ogre Ancestry
passages.text:
Lunk know you kill many ogre for this, and Lunk very upset about this, but Lunk also still grateful.

Wait, dis not Lunk family club...

passages.title: Budd's Gambit
passages.text:
Listen, I don't know how I got here, but I have it on good authority that there is an entire island made of shiny things and it's just off of the coast a ways.

All we have to do is hop in the water and swim out there, then we can load up our pockets and swim back! I'm just going to rest up and do some stretching before heading out.

Don't try and stop me!

passages.title: Budd's Gambit
passages.text: What?

passages.title: Budd's Gambit
passages.text:
Oh... this is... well that's very shiny isn't it? I think... I'll just sit here for a while.

<Budd smiles contentedly.>

passages.title: Oralius' Adventure
passages.text:
Me n' Winky, off on adventures again! This is the life, I tell ye. No burning air to breathe, an' plenty of ogres to kill!

<Oralius rubs his belly.>

We did leave a bit of a mess back there in the Blackrock Spire, though. A whole mess of these iron-plated orcs and some proto-dragons marched right on up from the south and took it over.

Ol' Winky, he couldn't take the guilt. Went on back by himself he did, to stop them!

Or... to JOIN them! Winky, ye two-timing son of an orc. Ye've got to stop him!

passages.title: Oralius' Adventure
passages.text: Did ye stop him?

passages.title: Oralius' Adventure
passages.text:
Good thinkin'. Winky always loved these flameflies. If we gather enough of them, maybe we can convince hiim to come back!

Maybe, er, you should hold onto this for a while, eh?

passages.title: The Void-Gate
passages.text:
My 'master' is an idiot, but you look like you've got some smarts in that oddly-shaped head.

Listen up, the Twisting Nether is a chaotic abyss, and things work differently there. I've felt some disturbances, and they don't bode well for any of us.

Yes, there are things happening here, in Draenor, that are causing ripples in the nether. No, don't try to wrap your head around how that works, you'll only hurt yourself.

It's simple: bring me a Void-Gate Key, and maybe I can stop the bad things.

passages.title: The Void-Gate
passages.text: You do know that any time you waste talking to me brings us closer to doom, right?

passages.title: The Void-Gate
passages.text:
Perfect, here's a prize for your efforts.

I've got to head out and save everyone now. Again.

passages.title: Feeling A Bit Morose
passages.text:
So many years of waking up as a spirit, reanimated by some unseen force time and again, has left one with certain desires - the comforting, velvet blackness of death being chief amongst them.

One will, however, settle for the lesser prize of a solution capable of removing the scuff marks that the commander's wonderful compatriots left behind in the dining hall in their woefully short stay in Karazhan, whereupon they barely had enough time to irreparably damage the priceless furniture.

passages.title: Feeling A Bit Morose
passages.text: Was the commander successful?

passages.title: Feeling A Bit Morose
passages.text:
One is eternally in your debt for what is, one is certain, an entirely selfless act on the part of the commander.

Though more barrels were likely available, one will staunchly make do with the single barrel provided, comforted in the knowledge that the commander must deal with the great pressing issues of this land, and does not have time to clean up the mud that that so dutifully follows the commander's heroic allies.

passages.title: Shadowy Secrets
passages.text:
Though the Lich King has been defeated, we are no closer to unlocking the secrets of the Frozen Throne than we were when jousting pointlessly at the Argent Tournament. Bolvar remains resigned to his fate.

Perhaps there is something here, though, that can aid us. Ner'zhul was not always the Lich King, you know. Once, he was a mere orc dabbling in dark powers beyond his comprehension.

Find whatever you can of his early studies, and we may have our answers.

passages.title: Shadowy Secrets
passages.text: Did you find any of Ner'zhul's notes?

passages.title: Shadowy Secrets
passages.text:
You have my thanks. I will bring this back to the Ebon Hold immediately.

Take this, I... acquired it... from one of the Shadowmoon.

passages.title: The Huntresses
passages.text:
I do not wish to come out of the shadows, but I mean you no harm. My purpose here is my own secret to keep, I simply needed a warm place to bed down for the night.

I can see that you are not the type to be easily swayed into leaving. Very well, perhaps you can aid me in my search.

I am looking for someone, it is not important who. All you need to know is that I will reward you for any sign of high elven weaponry that you should come across.

passages.title: The Huntresses
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: The Huntresses
passages.text:
This is... it can't be.

I must be off, here is your reward. I do not part with it lightly...

passages.title: For The Children!
passages.text:
Wait, wait! Don't attack me! I've changed!

Really, I've turned over a new leaf, I promise. I haven't said "DOOOOOOM!" in months! All I care about now is saving the poor little orphans of Azeroth, whose parents have been taken by this tragic war.

That's why I'm here! Why, with just a single Miniature Iron Star, I could provide clean water and power for all of the orphans of Azeroth! And no one could stop me!

So, what do you think, sweetcheeks? Want to help ol' Milhouse save the orphans?

passages.title: For The Children!
passages.text: Did you find the Iron Star?

passages.title: For The Children!
passages.text:
You know, you're quite handy, and awfully powerful. Why don't I just follow you for a while?

Look out Draenor, DOOOOOOOOM is coming!

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text:
Before I was shipped off to Gorgrond, I was stationed at the Broken Precipice in Nagrand, maintaining order over the unruly dredges. Vizier Dar'gud refused to let me take my favorite sword; he told me "I wouldn't need it where I was going."

I want it back, commander, and we are powerful enough together to take it from Dar'gud's bloody corpse.

It would mean a great deal to me. An ogre without his sword isn't an ogre at all.

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text: I want my sword more than I can tell you, commander.

passages.title: An Ogre Without His Sword...
passages.text:
Yes... this is it.

Commander, I will cleave your foes like never before now that I have my sword.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
There are others that harness the shadows to do their bidding. You know of them, commander... the Shadowmoon orcs.

They have begun to master their craft... they call to the shadows beyond this realm...

I desire their power. They have one who possesses a staff of particular interest... we should claim it as our own.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text: Taking out our enemies and gaining great power in one motion... my people have a saying for this: Killing two orcs with one stone.

passages.title: Scrying Hard or Hardly Scrying
passages.text:
Yes... yes... this will do nicely. We can use this to do great things.

Thank you, commander.

passages.title: Put a Bird on It
passages.text:
<name>! Have you met the peachick you saved the other day?

<Mylune holds up a peachick hatchling, then trills and twitters at it. She gestures to you, says your name, then continues chirping animatedly to the little bird. The two ignore you and engage in a lengthy bird-conversation, long enough to make you feel awkward. Finally the dryad turns her attention back to you.>

Did you hear that? More peachicks are still trapped in the Everbloom! If you don't save them... well, you heard what will happen!

passages.title: Put a Bird on It
passages.text: <Mylune stamps her hooves impatiently.>

passages.title: Put a Bird on It
passages.text:
Oh, thank you <name>! You've made a lot of wee baby birds very happy.

You're my favorite <race>!

passages.title: A Fruitful Proposition
passages.text:
The head of just ONE ogre won't be enough to stop the fruit vendor. No, the fruit vendor is wise, they would not put all of their fruit into one basket.

Bring me the head of ANOTHER ogre! Ha! Then what will the fruit vendor do? Cry onto their bananas as they rot and fall to the ground.

DESPAIR, FRUIT VENDOR. SO DELICIOUS!

passages.title: A Fruitful Proposition
passages.text: THE FRUIT VENDOR STANDS NO CHANCE!

passages.title: A Fruitful Proposition
passages.text: We are one step closer to crushing the fruit vendor's grapes into muddy wine.

passages.title: Like A Dwarf In A Mine
passages.text:
Baelog and Eric swear there's got to be treasure at the bottom of the mine. Why? Because it's a mine! An' we sure do love rocks that sparkle.

On our last trip, we were beaten back by huge ogres. Baelog held up the rear, swingin' his sword, while Eric rushed on ahead to try and find a quick exit.

Wouldn't you know, in all that excitement, I done lost my shield AGAIN?

<Olaf looks at you imploringly.>

passages.title: Like A Dwarf In A Mine
passages.text: <Olaf sobs.>

passages.title: Like A Dwarf In A Mine
passages.text: By the light, that's her! You've done it again, an' I can't thank you enough! We'll try to be more careful next time.

passages.title: Bloody Expensive
passages.text:
Welcome back, commander. The commander is obviously in a great hurry, and certainly the thought of removing their coat or boots or not dripping all over the floor are much too far beyond consideration.

The commander remembers the acidic solution, yes? Quite effective it was, though one barrel was not enough to remove ALL of the blood stains from the portraits, or the tapestries, or the ceiling.

Surely this must have been the most heroic and viscous battle in recent history.

passages.title: Bloody Expensive
passages.text: Was the commander successful?

passages.title: Bloody Expensive
passages.text: Again, though more barrels were likely available, one will staunchly make do with the single barrel provided, comforted in the knowledge that the commander must deal with the great pressing issues of this land, and does not have time to clean up the mud that that so dutifully follows the commander's heroic allies.

passages.title: Like Father, Like Son
passages.text:
He's done it again! My son took my knife and yelled something about a 'chromatic hide,' then ran off for the Spire! What would he even do with something like that, wear it around like a cape?

If it's not too much to ask, would you keep an eye out for the knife? You know, next time you're around Upper Blackrock Spire. Which, hopefully, is soon. VERY soon.

passages.title: Like Father, Like Son
passages.text: Where's my knife?

passages.title: Like Father, Like Son
passages.text: You've saved it! A little nicked, but that can be fixed. Thanks!

passages.title: Secrets of Soulbinding
passages.text:
We have reviewed Ner'zhul's notes, which you brought to us previously. Though we are closer to understanding how these warlocks have learned to bind souls and control the undead, the picture is incomplete.

We will need more pages if we are to see the whole picture. I do not want to experiment with partial information and create an abomination. There are enough of those in Northrend as it is.

passages.title: Secrets of Soulbinding
passages.text: Did you find any of Ner'zhul's notes?

passages.title: Secrets of Soulbinding
passages.text: We are greatful for your aid. I shall retire shortly.

passages.title: Fate of the Fallen
passages.text:
I feel that I can trust you, perhaps. You have, at least, not spoken of my secret to anyone, and for that I thank you.

I have need of your aid again, and in return, I will share some of my own information. I am here, you see, to find an elf by the name of Alleria. She was lost years ago, on Draenor. It is my faint hope that the twisting nether brought her here.

I do not know if such a thing is even possible, but do keep an eye out for any signs of high elves as you travel.

passages.title: Fate of the Fallen
passages.text: Did you find anything?

passages.title: Fate of the Fallen
passages.text:
Another one? How curious.

I may not be much closer to finding her, but these arrows bring some comfort to me, at least.

passages.title: The Leaf-Reader
passages.text:
Good ta see you again, mon!

De Cenarion Circle sent Zen'kiki out here ta find some more of dem plants. We not likin' what we be seein' here.

If ya find any more of dem leaves, bring one on back. Dey can see right through Zen'kiki's tree disguise, even when he plant himself in da ground!

And dat make it harder to run!

passages.title: The Leaf-Reader
passages.text: Did ya have much luck, mon?

passages.title: The Leaf-Reader
passages.text: Thanks, mon. I'm gonna bring this back to the Circle, just as soon as I can figure out how ta fly in da savage winds of dis place.

passages.title: Lessons of the Past
passages.text:
I have returned! You must have known that a world so rich in history could not keep me away for long!

<Lorewalker Cho chuckles, holding his enormous belly.>

I have perhaps been taking part in too many celebratory feasts, now that the Vale has been cleansed. There is so much to celebrate in Pandaria!

Should you find any future evidence of titanic influence on the native species, I will be here, heartily enjoying the roast clefthoof.

passages.title: Lessons of the Past
passages.text: Have you found any signs of the titans here?

passages.title: Lessons of the Past
passages.text: Another excellent find from our most illustrious hero! I will immediately begin transcribing your heroic deeds!

passages.title: Learning Is Painful
passages.text:
The academy is up and running, in a secret location of course. Maybe it doesn't exist at all?

By the by, I appear to be running quite dry on sharp, pointy instruments of education.

<Lonika winks at you several times before nudging you sharply in the ribs with her dagger.>

passages.title: Learning Is Painful
passages.text: Did you find me some weapons?

passages.title: Learning Is Painful
passages.text: Once again, you have proven yourself invaluable. Perhaps you would like a teaching job?

passages.title: Flamefly Trap
passages.text:
Ol' Winky still hasn't come back! Now I'm gettin' worried.

Do me a favor and get another one of those flameflies from Upper Blackrock Spire. If we get enough of em,' Winky's sure to see the glimmer and come heading on back.

An then we'll have him right where we want him!

passages.title: Flamefly Trap
passages.text: Did ye get another fly?

passages.title: Flamefly Trap
passages.text: Oi, that's a bright fly! Thank ye, we'll just keep on tryin' until that two-timing ol' Winky comes on home.

passages.title: Whispers in the Darkness
passages.text:
If you don't mind, I'm trying VERY hard to prevent all of our worlds from collapsing into the void, AGAIN.

Oh, right, you helped me last time, didn't you? Well, you've got great timing. I'm in need of another Gate-Key.

Well? Go on! The infinite horrors of the abyss aren't just going to wait until you've had a nap! Having that many tentacles makes them really antsy.

passages.title: Whispers in the Darkness
passages.text: You do know that any time you waste talking to me brings us closer to doom, right?

passages.title: Whispers in the Darkness
passages.text:
Perfect, here's a prize for your efforts.

I've got to head out and save everyone now. Again.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Gug'rokk
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a formidable group and head into the depths of the Bloodmaul Slag Mines. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and free the miners of Gug'rokk's tyrannical rule.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Gug'rokk
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. The families of the rescued miners will never be able to thank you enough for eliminating Gug'rokk and his slavers.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a resolute group of warriors and venture into the Shadowmoon Burial Grounds. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and put a stop to Ner'zhul's communion with the void before he takes all of Draenor with him.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Putting an end to Ner'zhul and his deathly rituals will allow many to sleep better at night.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a resolute group of warriors and venture into the Shadowmoon Burial Grounds. Activate the Challenger's Orb, and put a stop to Ner'zhul's communion with the void before he takes all of Draenor with him.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Ner'zhul
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Putting an end to Ner'zhul and his deathly rituals will allow many to sleep better at night.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Warlord Zaela
passages.text:
<name>, I need you to assemble a group of stalwart adventures and journey back to Azeroth and Upper Blackrock Spire. Activate the Challenger's Orb, enter the old home of the Blackrock clan and defeat the Ironmarch Vanguard and their new ally, Warlord Zaela.

Return to me when you've completed this challenge and I shall reward you handsomely.

passages.title: A Worthy Challenge: Warlord Zaela
passages.text: <name>, you've done a great service. Defeating the Ironmarch Vanguard at Upper Blackrockspire is a major blow to the Iron Horde and Azeroth can rest a bit more knowing Warlord Zaela's bid for revenge has been permanently dealt with.

passages.title: The Bloodshed Never Ends
passages.text:
You are insatiable, gladiator! Let none doubt your voracious appetite for destruction and death!

Imperator Mar'gok will be very pleased to see you battling upon the arena floor of the Coliseum once more!

As before, I will accept nothing less than 100 lives!

Kill or be killed, gladiator!

passages.title: The Bloodshed Never Ends
passages.text: To the victor go the spoils! All hail <name>!

passages.title: Bronze Victory
passages.text: With every victory, or claim here grows more strong.

passages.title: Gold Victory
passages.text: A complete victory! Draenor denizens will mewl for weeks as they lick their wounds, in whatever dark places they live.

passages.title: The Prophet's Final Message
passages.text:
This unassuming iridescent crystal contains some of the final thoughts of Great Prophet Velen, created sometime in the hours before he confronted Ner'zhul.

Deliver the crystal to Prophet Velen's Memorial beneath the Coliseum of Light near Karabor to hear his final message.

passages.title: The Prophet's Final Message
passages.text: The arcanum hums in your hand as you get close to the memorial.

passages.title: The Prophet's Final Message
passages.text: The shrine has dozens of niches where the Prophet's followers have placed their own memory crystals, mourning the great leader's sacrifice. You slide the crystal into an empty socket and the memorial comes to life...

passages.title: Fungal Bundle
passages.text: The umbraspore giant you killed seemed immune to the volatile spores in the area. Perhaps the odd growths you found all over its body contribute to its immunity. You grab a big, disgusting fungal lump in order to give it to the rangari for study.

passages.title: Fungal Bundle
passages.text: What did you find, <class>?

passages.title: Fungal Bundle
passages.text:
Oh - you were attacked by an Umbraspore Giant? They're very dangerous - you were brave to face one down!

This growth you found doesn't seem to be part of the giant. It's almost like another organism living in symbiosis. We'll have to study this more closely and see what benefit it conveys to the host.

Thank you, <name>. Outstanding work!

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text:
Greetings commander.

Word of your exploits has made its way back to Trial Master Rotun, and he has humbly requested to see your prowess in person. Fighting in his proving grounds would be an excellent way to spread your reputation to the farthest reaches of the Alliance, and beyond.

If you're interested in proving yourself, talk to me to enter Trial Master Rotun's Proving Grounds.

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text: Have you completed your challenge?

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text:
Congratulations, commander. You have survived Rotun's trial and proven yourself powerful indeed. 

Here, take this weapon, that you may further dominate your foes in battle!

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text:
Hail commander.

Word of your exploits has made its way back to Trial Master Rotun, and he has requested to see your prowess in person. Fighting in his proving grounds would be an excellent way to spread your reputation to the farthest reaches of the Horde, and beyond.

If you're interested in proving yourself, talk to me to enter Trial Master Rotun's Proving Grounds.

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text: Have you completed your challenge?

passages.title: Proving Grounds
passages.text:
Congratulations, commander. You have survived the trial of Trial Master Rotun and proven yourself powerful indeed. 

Here, take this weapon that you may futher dominate your foes in battle!

passages.title: Thirst Unending
passages.text:
If there is only one lesson you deign to remember from your time on Sunstrider Isle, let it be this - control your thirst for magic. It is a thirst unending, <name> - what you absorb must be controlled and released via Arcane Torrent. Failure is to become one of the Wretched... hopelessly addicted and insane.

Seek out a mana wyrm and unleash your Arcane Torrent upon it. Learn to master your power. When you have sufficiently released an Arcane Torrent, return to me.

passages.title: Thirst Unending
passages.text:
It is not an option or a choice... you must quench your magical thirst.  To fail in this is to fail as a <race>.  Those who thought they could control their needs without tutoring now find themselves as one of the Wretched.

You do NOT want to end up as an insane addict.  Believe me.

passages.title: Thirst Unending
passages.text:
You've done well today, <name>.  Your willingness to learn shows that you may very well rise above the unyielding cravings you must endure as a <race>.

Rest not on your laurels, young one, but instead seek to master what you have learned.  Only through diligence will we as a race survive.

Take this - it may be of some use to you.  Go now, and bring glory once more to our people.

passages.title: A Fistful of Slivers
passages.text:
It's a shame that we've lost control of many of the creatures here on the island. This was once a tranquil place of study and research. Now it's all we can do to keep from being attacked by our own creations!

I'm going to offer you a chance to receive a magical boon in exchange for some collecting work on your part. Bring me a stack of arcane slivers that are found on the mana-using creatures of Sunstrider Isle, and I will cast a spell on you that should aid your adventures on the isle.

passages.title: A Fistful of Slivers
passages.text:
Many of the creatures here on the isle were at one point bound into non-aggression and complacency by our magical skills.  When the Scourge destroyed the Sunwell, our hold over these creatures shattered.  Arcane slivers are the remnants of the control we once had, and as such might be usable in fashioning a new device to aid us in regaining their control.

Better still, perhaps the slivers could be used to see what malaise the isle truly suffers under...

passages.title: A Fistful of Slivers
passages.text:
Splendid - these will do nicely.  I've been doing quite a bit of thinking on the current malaise Sunstrider Isle suffers under.  One possible course of action I had pondered was to collect these arcane slivers from the beasts on the isle.  In doing so, they could be experimented on; this would provide a potential source of culpability.

Anyway, I will tend to the research.  Allow me to place this incantation on you.  I believe you'll make good use of it!

passages.title: Solanian's Belongings
passages.text:
With all the chaos happening here at the Sunspire, I haven't had a chance to collect my belongings I've left outside at various places on the isle. I must maintain my vigil over the Sunwell here, so I'll ask you to collect them in my stead.

I need my scrying orb, my scroll of Scourge magic, and my journal. Use this satchel for some extra space, as my things are rather bulky. Return them to me and I'll give you a little something - you know, for the effort; you can keep the satchel as well!

passages.title: The Shrine of Dath'Remar
passages.text:
Day after day I stand here, watching, waiting. I've been accused of dwelling too much on our past, while my eyes look to the horizon. But it is my firm belief that each visitor to this island should honor those who have sacrificed all so that they may continue to do so.

Dath'Remar Sunstrider was our first king. He led us here from Kalimdor through the Maelstrom.

Seek out his shrine to the west and do not return to me until you have read the plaque upon it in his honor.

passages.title: The Shrine of Dath'Remar
passages.text:
Ah, <name> - thank you for sharing your experience at the Shrine of Dath'Remar.  First off, you should be commended for your sense of duty and respect - it will serve you well not only here, but in all of Azeroth as well.

As for the odd sensation, it is no doubt a contributing part of the taint that has befallen Sunstrider Isle.  We shall keep an eye on it; thank you for alerting us to it!

passages.title: Solanian's Belongings
passages.text:
With all the chaos happening here at the Sunspire, I haven't had a chance to collect my belongings I've left outside at various places on the isle. I must maintain my vigil over the Sunwell here, so I'll ask you to collect them in my stead.

I need my scrying orb, my scroll of Scourge magic, and my journal. Use this satchel for some extra space, as my things are rather bulky. Return them to me and I'll give you a little something - you know, for the effort; you can keep the satchel as well!

passages.title: Solanian's Belongings
passages.text: Have you had a chance to find my belongings?  Once we reassert our dominance over Sunstrider Isle, I will need them in my work.  For now though, I must maintain my watch over the Sunwell... or what remains of it.

passages.title: Solanian's Belongings
passages.text:
Well done - I knew you'd be perfect for the task.  Once it's safe to make use of our outdoor facilities on the isle, I'll be putting these things to good use.

Like I mentioned, please feel free to keep the satchel.  Also, you may find this piece of armor to be useful.  Consider it ample compensation for a simple task performed dutifully!

passages.title: Inoculation
passages.text:
Zhanaa needs our help to salvage parts from the Exodar. Taerix prepared an inoculum that can be given to the Nestlewood owlkin that live in the area of a lot of the salvage.

Just get close to the unaffected ones and use the crystal on them. Unfortunately, you'll have to kill the others. You'll find the owlkin at Nestlewood Thicket and Nestlewood Hills to the southeast.

passages.title: Inoculation
passages.text: The more we can do to clear up Nestlewood, the faster Zhanaa can get back to work.

passages.title: Inoculation
passages.text:
With many of the owlkin now inoculated, we can focus on getting out of here and not have to worry about wiping out the owlkin population in the area.

Here, choose from these.  You've done good work, and you deserve to be rewarded!

passages.title: Spare Parts
passages.text:
We managed to recover a damaged holographic emitter from the crash. If we repair it, we'll have a chance to find other survivors outside of Ammen Vale.

There were devices from the ship that could be salvaged for spare parts in the area, but the local owlkin carried them off before we could get to them. 

<name>, you must go south to Nestlewood Thicket and Hills to find the spare parts.

passages.title: Spare Parts
passages.text: When we have those spare parts, I know that we'll get this emitter repaired. With any luck there will be someone else out there left to talk to.

passages.title: Spare Parts
passages.text:
Let me take a look at those.

Yes, I think that these will do nicely; good job, <name>. The emitter is rather complex so it may take some time to finish the repairs. I'll let you know when it's ready.

In the meantime, you might see if Vindicator Aldar has anything he could use you for.

passages.title: Lazy Peons
passages.text:
Cursed peons! They work hard gathering lumber from the trees of the valley, but they're always taking naps! I need someone to help keep the peons in line.

You look like the right <race> for my task. Here, you take this blackjack and use it on any lazy peons you find sleeping on the job. A good smack will get them right back to work! Return the blackjack when you're done.

Look for them underneath the trees in the valley. Lousy slacking peons...

passages.title: Lazy Peons
passages.text:
No good lazy...

 Eh?  Do you have my blackjack?  Did you catch any peons sleeping on the job?!

passages.title: Lazy Peons
passages.text: Good, good.  Maybe they'll think twice before slacking next time!  Thanks for the help!

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Heap of Apexis Crystals
passages.text: Of course you agree.

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Mountain of Apexis Crystals
passages.text: Of course you agree.

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Piles of Gold
passages.text: A simple exchange with complex results.  That's the art of doing business.

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Immense Fortune of Gold
passages.text: A simple exchange with complex results.  That's the art of doing business.

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Stockpiled Garrison Resources
passages.text: Feeling safe, stranger?

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Tremendous Garrison Resources
passages.text: Feeling safe, stranger?

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Extended Honor
passages.text: A bloody price to pay just to play with luck.  Let's hope it was worth it.

passages.title: Sealing Fate: Monumental Honor
passages.text: A bloody price to pay just to play with luck.  Let's hope it was worth it.

passages.title: Assault on the Gorian Proving Grounds
passages.text:
The ogres at the Gorian Proving Grounds are rousing champions to turn against our forces in Nagrand.

A decisive assault on their training grounds should prevent them from mustering the forces they need to stand against us, and will help remind them that we are not an enemy they want to make.

passages.title: Assault on the Gorian Proving Grounds
passages.text:
The ogres at the Gorian Proving Grounds be rousin' champions to turn against our forces in Nagrand.

A decisive assault on their training grounds should prevent dem from musterin' the forces dey be needin' to stand against us, and will help remind them that we are not an enemy they want to be makin'.

passages.title: The Frostwolves Stand Ready
passages.text:
Though we have lost much this day, the Frostwolves stand ready to uphold our pact with your people.

To honor this agreement, some of my clan have asked to join your ranks and fight alongside your forces.

Our numbers are strained so I ask that you chose only one.

Speak with me when you have made your decision.

passages.title: The Frostwolves Stand Ready
passages.text: Have you decided which orc to take with you?

passages.title: The Frostwolves Stand Ready
passages.text:
Excellent choice. I will be sad to see them leave, but I know they will help strengthen our combined packs in the coming conflicts.

I will see that they make their way to your garrison as soon as they have said farewell to their loved ones.

They should be ready the next time you need to send followers on a mission.

passages.title: Your First Enchanting Work Order
passages.text: Now that the enchanter's study is complete, we can start producing draenic dust for you. When you have the ingredients, please speak with my assistant to start the first work order.

passages.title: Your First Enchanting Work Order
passages.text: Yes?

passages.title: Your First Enchanting Work Order
passages.text:
Let me unpack that for you.

I should let you know - while we managed to expedite this one, future work orders will take longer.

passages.title: Your Second Alchemy Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Blacksmithing Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Enchanting Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Engineering Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Engineering Work Order
passages.text: We look forward to serving you again.

passages.title: Your Second Inscription Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Jewelcrafting Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Leatherworking Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Tailoring Work Order
passages.text: Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Your Second Inscription Work Order
passages.text: It normally takes us a day to complete one work order. Place another work order with my assistant. Once it is complete, we will leave it out here for you to collect.

passages.title: Slagworks: Heart of the Mountain
passages.text:
Blackrock orcs fight like no other clan. They rely on arms and armor forged in the heart of their unnatural crucibles.

Deep within the Foundry of the Blackrock clan is a furnace powered by a primal force known as the Heart of the Mountain. Destroy it, and deprive our foe of the arms they rely on.

Travel to Blackrock Foundry and defeat the Heart of the Mountain.

passages.title: Slagworks: Heart of the Mountain
passages.text: Well done, commander. With da Heart of da Mountain defeated, you have crippled the ability of da Blackrock clan to use their most powerful furnace.

passages.title: Slagworks: Heart of the Mountain
passages.text:
Blackrock warriors use weapons forged in cursed fire by the breath of a creature o' pure flame: The Heart o' the Mountain. Let's disarm 'em, <boy/lass>! Destroy that infernal creature, and the Blackrock won't have enough heat to fuel their Blast Furnace.

Travel to Blackrock Foundry and defeat the Heart o' the Mountain.

passages.title: Slagworks: Heart of the Mountain
passages.text: Well done, commander! With the Heart of the Mountain defeated, the Blackrock will have nothing to wield but sticks and stones.

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text:
You ever heard of the Ring of Blood, commander?

It's pretty simple. Big ogre named Mogor loves watching people fight for their lives against savage beasts. Ambitious goblin called Gurgthock arranges the fights and rakes in the profits.

Anwyays, Gurgthock and I are long time buddies and he's arranged a special exhibition match just for you! Pretty sweet, right? Just whisper into his ear "I seek the seeker."

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text: Word is already spreading of your epic fight, commander. This may improve relations with the ogres in the future.

passages.title: Death to Tremor!
passages.text:
Your outpost in Gorgrond has a serious saberon problem, commander, and we can't really afford to keep sending more troops to help 'em out. So I have an idea.

There's an enormous worm beast on the west coast of Gorgrond called Tremor, better known as the devourer of lobstroks. If you took that thing down and brought the, well, pile of partially digested lobstrok meat back here, we can cook it here, ship it back there, use it to calm the saberon for a good long time!

passages.title: Death to Tremor!
passages.text:
Orders commander?

And what is that awful smell?!

passages.title: Death to Tremor!
passages.text: Excellent. This meat ought to keep those pesky saberon busy.

passages.title: Death to Hivelord Ik'rix!
passages.text:
We've got a radical new idea to try using ice ravager carapaces in our tempering process for armor and weapons. It's the sort of trailblazing work we strive for, commander!

Only problem is, ravagers apparently aren't keen on our guys and gals taking their carapaces off of them. There's this particular ravager at the Southwind Cliffs in Frostfire Ridge called Hivelord Ik'rix - if you could take him down we wouldn't need more for weeks!

passages.title: Death to Hivelord Ik'rix!
passages.text: Yes, commander?

passages.title: Death to Hivelord Ik'rix!
passages.text: Thank you, commander. We will get to work on this right away!

passages.title: Bloodmaul Slag Mines
passages.text:
The Bloodmaul ogres are brutal slavers, commander. Innocents from across Draenor are dragged deep into the volcanic slag mines in Frostfire Ridge to dredge up cart after cart of gems and ore, never to return.

We suspect that they have turned their focus to unearthing an ancient relic of immense power for their sorcerer-king.

The ogre Gug'rokk rules over the slag mines with an iron fist. Take him down and the mines will fall as well.

passages.title: Bloodmaul Slag Mines
passages.text: We can't allow da slag mines to operate. Gug'rokk has cracked his last whip against da bloody backs of the innocent.

passages.title: Bloodmaul Slag Mines
passages.text:
Da Bloodmaul be finished, and with dem Imperator Mar'gok's chances of acquirin' da relic within da slag mines.

Ds be a good day, mon.

passages.title: Shadowmoon Burial Grounds
passages.text:
Ner'zhul was once a noble orc - he was the wise chieftain and elder shaman of the Shadowmoon clan. In his desperate bid to join the Iron Horde he has spat on all he once stood for and twisted his ancestors' spirits to tap into dark, forbidden power... all to please Hellscream.

The Shadowmoon has fallen, commander. Enter their ancestral burial grounds and put an end to Ner'zhul's madness before he pulls all of Draenor into the engulfing maw of the void.

passages.title: Shadowmoon Burial Grounds
passages.text: I already be feelin' da relief of da ancestral spirits of Draenor with Ner'zhul's fall. You have deprived Grommash of a powerful weapon, commander.

passages.title: Upper Blackrock Spire
passages.text:
Hellscream's Ironmarch vanguard managed to reach Blackrock Mountain and has allied with Warlord Zaela of the Dragonmaw clan. Even now the Iron Horde readies to invade Azeroth while Zaela prepares a doomsday weapon in the heart of the mountain to ensure nothing stands in their way.

You must put a stop to Zaela once and for all, commander. She has been a thorn in our side for too long.

passages.title: Upper Blackrock Spire
passages.text: With Warlord Zaela's fall we can be focusin' our efforts on Draenor and da heart of da Iron Horde. They have nowhere to hide now.

passages.title: Upper Blackrock Spire
passages.text:
Hellscream's Ironmarch vanguard managed to reach Blackrock Mountain and has allied with Warlord Zaela o' the Dragonmaw clan. Even now the Iron Horde readies to invade Azeroth while Zaela prepares a doomsday weapon in the heart o' the mountain to ensure nothing stands in their way.

You must put a stop to Zaela once and for all, commander. She's been a thorn in our side for too long.

passages.title: Upper Blackrock Spire
passages.text: With Warlord Zaela out of the picture we can focus our efforts on Draenor and the heart of the Iron Horde. They have nowhere to hide now.

passages.title: Shadowmoon Burial Grounds
passages.text:
Ner'zhul wasn't always evil - once he was the wise chieftain and elder shaman o' the Shadowmoon clan. In his desperate bid to join the Iron Horde he's forsaken all he once stood for and twisted his ancestors' spirits to tap into dark, forbidden power... all to please Hellscream.

Enter their ancestral burial grounds and put an end to Ner'zhul's madness before he pulls all o' Draenor into the engulfing maw o' the void.

passages.title: Shadowmoon Burial Grounds
passages.text: I'm no shaman--far from it--but even I can feel the relief of the ancestral spirits of Draenor with Ner'zhul's fall. You have deprived Grommash of a powerful weapon, commander.

passages.title: Bloodmaul Slag Mines
passages.text:
The Bloodmaul ogres are brutal slavers, commander. Innocents from across Draenor are dragged deep into the volcanic slag mines in Frostfire Ridge to dredge up cart after cart o' gems and ore, never to return.

We suspect that they have turned their focus to unearthin' an ancient relic o' immense power for their sorcerer-king.

The ogre Gug'rokk rules over the slag mines with an iron fist. Take him down and the mines will fall as well.

passages.title: Bloodmaul Slag Mines
passages.text:
The Bloodmaul are finished, and with them Imperator Mar'gok's chances of acquiring the relic within the slag mines.

This is as fine a day as I've seen in some time.

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text:
Da goblin Gurgthock be requestin' your presence at the Ring of Blood in Nagrand, boss-mon.

It seems that Mogor, da lord of da ring, be holdin' an exhibition match der and he want you to fight his newest acquisition.

I think it be safe, commander. I heard of dis goblin's work before. If you be ready, whisper to him "I seek da seeker."

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text: Word already be spreadin' about your exploits. If da ogres did not fear your strength yet, dey should now.

passages.title: Death to Tremor!
passages.text:
Da Gorgrond outpost be havin' troubles with saberon, and we can't afford ta throw troops at the problem any longer. Don't worry, I be havin' an idea.

There be an enormous worm beast on the west coast of Gorgrond called Tremor, da devourer of lobstroks. If you killed da beast and brought da pile of lobstrok meat back here, we can cook it 'ere, send it to da outpost, and use it to calm da saberon for good!

passages.title: Death to Tremor!
passages.text:
Ey, commander.

What be that awful smell?

passages.title: Death to Tremor!
passages.text: Dis be exactly what we need, commander. I'll send it to da chefs right away.

passages.title: Death to Hivelord Ik'rix!
passages.text:
We been tryin' out a new way to temper weapons with ice ravager carapaces. Der icy hides are perfect for da process.

Hivelord Ik'rix in da Southwind Cliffs nearby is rumored to be da largest ravager we ever seen - if you could bring its carapace back, we'd be able to make all sorts of things!

passages.title: Death to Hivelord Ik'rix!
passages.text: Ey, boss-mon. What can I do for you today?

passages.title: Death to Hivelord Ik'rix!
passages.text: Excellent. Dis be exactly what we lookin' for!

passages.title: Welcome to the Darkmoon Races
passages.text:
So this is your first race, eh? Don't worry - it's easier than it looks. Let me break it down for you...

Run through that big banner there. That starts everything. Then, follow the smaller banners until you see a big, blue Post. Hit that, then return here.

You're scored on your time, so finish as fast as you can! And watch out for those electrified tripwires. They'll slow you down if you run through them. Good luck!

passages.title: Welcome to the Darkmoon Races
passages.text: Hurry! Hit the blue post!

passages.title: Welcome to the Darkmoon Races
passages.text:
You made it! This is just a practice race so your time doesn't matter... other than bragging rights.

Time to try the real race!

passages.title: An Inside Job
passages.text:
If Garona's intelligence is correct, Gul'dan will be inside this Iron Horde compound. With Garona's help, slip inside, gather any info you find, and learn what Gul'dan intends to do.

The guards are on high alert. Garona can "liquidate" individual guards for you, but she must not be seen! You will have to choose your targets carefully and pick your way through the bastion undetected. Don't let anyone sound the alarm.

If things get too hot, I'll teleport you to safety. At least... I'll try.

passages.title: An Inside Job
passages.text:
Don't give up. I know you can do this.

<Despite his words, Khadgar doesn't seem so sure.>

passages.title: An Inside Job
passages.text:
Well done, both of you!

Gul'dan is even more slippery than I imagined. He's been building up his power base behind the scenes, and now that we've weakened his foes, he's moved in to take control of what remains of the Iron Horde.

We need to plan our next move.

passages.title: Light Be With You
passages.text:
You've done everything I've asked, <name>. I believe we can apply one final enchantment to your ring. But... we must be cautious. Last time I augmented your ring I killed you. (Sorry.) It will take a divine act to empower you further.

Fortunately, you've made some powerful allies during your time here. Travel to the Temple of Karabor, where Yrel is waiting for you. With the blessing of a Naaru your ring will become as powerful and unique as - well, as you yourself. Go to Karabor. You've earned it.

passages.title: Light Be With You
passages.text:
You have earned this, <class>. You've traveled the length and breadth of my world. You've surmounted unimaginable odds and stood toe-to-toe against ancient beasts, dark magics, and terrifying machines. Time and again you've inspired my people with your patience and bravery.

Thank you, <name>.

passages.title: Draenor's Blessing
passages.text:
You've done everything I've asked, <name>. I believe we can apply one final enchantment to your ring. But... we must be cautious. Last time I augmented your ring I killed you. (Sorry.) It will take an act of ancient magic to empower you further.

Fortunately, you've made some powerful allies during your time here. Seek out Farseer Drek'Thar at the Throne of Elements in Nagrand. There you can receive the blessing of the elements and safely unlock your ring's final form. Go, hero! Claim your reward!

passages.title: Draenor's Blessing
passages.text: More than any other you embody the might of the Horde, champion.

passages.title: Draenor's Blessing
passages.text:
You have earned this, <class>. You've traveled the length and breadth of this savage world. You've surmounted unimaginable odds and stood toe-to-toe against ancient beasts, dark magics, and terrifying machines. Time and again you've surprised me with your patience and bravery.

Thank you, <name>. I am proud to call you my friend.

passages.title: The Final Assault
passages.text:
Our campaign in Draenor has taken an unexpected turn. With Gul'dan assuming power over the Iron Horde, history is poised to repeat itself - our world is in more peril than ever.

It's time to bring the full might of your garrison to bear against Tanaan Jungle. Build a shipyard for your garrison! I will meet you at your new shipyard and we will discuss our next move from there.

passages.title: The Final Assault
passages.text:
We meet again.

Now that you have a shipyard, let's talk about next steps...

passages.title: Treasure Contract: Amulet of Rukhmar
passages.text:
It seems the Adherents of Rukhmar have stumbled upon some information leading to an ancient amulet, said to possess the power of their god and bestow it upon the wearer. We should make sure they don't find it.

Head to Skettis and find what they have learned. Hopefully we can find it before they get to it.

passages.title: Treasure Contract: Explosive Discoveries
passages.text:
In Shadowmoon Valley there is a cave said to possess an ancient tome that may contain secrets that can help our cause against the Iron Horde. The cave, however, is protected by an ancient barrier composed of arcane energy.

There is a goblin in Darktide Roost, said to know how to take down any barrier. Persuade him to give up his secrets and bring back the book.

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: The First Ingredient
passages.text:
You will need three ingredients to make Megacharge's special "Arcane Bunker Buster," which should be able to take down the barrier. The first ingredient, some precision blasting powder, should be available nearby. The book reads:

"To make one, you'll first need to acquire some high grade, precision blasting powder. Here in Blackfuse Company, it's pretty easy to come by, since they use it for all of the cannons."

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: The Second Ingredient
passages.text:
With the blasting powder acquired, you now must find a suitable detonator. A note attached to the entry in the cookbook hints to where one might be found:

"Reminder: Order more high-voltage detonators. The last shipment was lost off of the Shadowmoon coast near the demon-inhabited cliffs. Maybe we should send a diving team to salvage."

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text:
The components have been gathered and the "Arcane Bunker Buster" is assembled. Hopefully, this should pack enough punch to take out the barrier.

There's only one way to find out...

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text: Dr. Jones asked me to take this book from you, but I'm not sure I want to touch it.

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text:
I'll make sure this gets to Dr. Jones. 

To be honest, I'm eager to get it off my hands.

passages.title: Assault on Ironhold Harbor
passages.text:
The Iron Horde continue to bring in reinforcements from all over Draenor to reinforce their position at Hellfire Citadel. If we don't cut off the flow of supplies then we risk losing control of our plans in Tanaan.

A strategic attack to the supply lines at Ironhold Harbor is just the thing to keep the Iron Horde on the defensive and maintain our momentum.

passages.title: Assault on Ironhold Harbor
passages.text:
Welcome back, commander. Our scouts just returned with word of your success.

Well done!

passages.title: The Real Race
passages.text:
Ok, Darkmoon Racer, let's see what you got!

The real race has four legs: get to the blue post, then green, then red, then back here. 

Your time matters, so do it fast!

passages.title: The Real Race
passages.text: You haven't hit all the markers. Hurry!

passages.title: The Real Race
passages.text: Good job, and nice time!

passages.title: The Real Big Race
passages.text:
Here's the big one! Good luck out there!

This race has four legs: get to the purple post, then green, then red, then back here. 

Your time matters, so do it fast!

passages.title: The Real Big Race
passages.text: You haven't hit all the markers. Hurry!

passages.title: The Real Big Race
passages.text: Good job, and nice time!

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Broken Spear
passages.text:
Looking through Argoram's journal, it becomes apparent that claiming this relic will be far more complicated than simply finding the pieces of the spear.

However, that would be the best place to start...

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Fire
passages.text:
The weapon has been assembled, but it lacks the power that made it a legend. In order to restore it, you must receive three blessings: one of fire, one of frost, and one of beasts.

The first blessing mentioned in the journal is that of fire. The journal reads:

"He describes an ancient monolith, perched upon the edge of a precipice extending from the cliff where the searing magma falls into the sea. I believe the location he speaks of is just overlooking Tor'goroth's Tooth."

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Frost
passages.text:
The weapon has been imbued with the Blessing of Fire, drawing power from the Molten Shamanstone. The Frozen Shamanstone should impart the next blessing. Argoram mentions its location in his journal:

"As I was maneuvering away from the great boulders hurled at me by the ogron brutes, I glanced what looked like another monolith atop the tallest of the snow-capped towers in Bloodmaul. Perhaps this is the Frozen Shamanstone, which is thought to grant the Blessing of Frost"

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Beasts
passages.text:
Gronnsbane now pulses with energies of fire and frost. All that remains to restore the full power of the weapon is to receive the Blessing of the Beast. Argoram believed this could be accomplished by bloodying the weapon against one of the ancient black rylaks of Stonefury Cliffs. His journal reads:

"High in the Stonefury Cliffs, I have seen an altar where the ogres have left offerings to these ancient beasts. Perhaps I could use it to lure one of them"

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Beasts
passages.text: Have you returned with the Thunderlords' relic?

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Beasts
passages.text:
Who would've thought that such a normal looking spear would be able to take down a full-sized Gronn? 

I'm sure Dr. Jones will appreciate this in his collection.

passages.title: Uncovering the Artifact Fragments
passages.text: The Artifact Fragments seem to come from any creature we've found in the outskirts of Ashran. Go out and kill any you find and bring at least five to Ecilam the Mage near the campfire in Stormshield Stronghold.

passages.title: Assault on Ironhold Harbor
passages.text:
The Iron Horde continues to bring in reinforcements from all over Draenor to reinforce their position at Hellfire Citadel. If we don't cut off the flow of supplies then we risk losing control of our plans in Tanaan.

A strategic attack to the supply lines at Ironhold Harbor is just the thing to keep the Iron Horde on the defensive and maintain our momentum.

passages.title: Assault on Ironhold Harbor
passages.text:
Word of your success has already been passed on by our scouts. 

Lok'tar!

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text:
Gurgthock stopped by from the Ring of Blood and said that Mogor wants his Blood Champion to participate in a special exhibition match. That's you, commander!

Just whisper "I seek the seeker." into Gurgthock's ear and he'll get things going for ya!

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text: Word is already spreading of your epic fight, commander. This may improve relations with the ogres in the future.

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text:
Da goblin Gurgthock stopped by and be sayin' that Mogor wants his Blood Champion to fight in an exhibition match against something terrible he's dug up. Dat be you, boss.

If you be ready, whisper to Gurgthock "I seek da seeker." He take care of da rest.

passages.title: Death to Nullifier Darkoor!
passages.text: Word already be spreadin' about your exploits. If da ogres did not fear your strength yet, dey should now.

passages.title: Bringing the Bass
passages.text:
You know what would boost morale around here?

Bass. Beats. Music!

Everyone loves a party! You go out and get me some hardware, and I'll make a system that will shatter Draenor itself.

passages.title: Bringing the Bass
passages.text: Collect a Bass Blaster, Laz-Tron Disc Reader, Phonic Amplifier, S.P.R.K. Capacitor, and a Cord of Ancient Wood.

passages.title: Bringing the Bass
passages.text: What great shape this stuff is in. Yeah, honest! I think I can work with this junk. Give me just a minute here...

passages.title: Assault on the Temple of Sha'naar
passages.text:
Up in the hills of Tanaan Jungle, the Sargerei have converted a once-sacred temple into a den of demonic summoning.

We must attack them now, before their rituals complete. The longer we delay, the stronger our enemy grows.

passages.title: Assault on the Temple of Sha'naar
passages.text: How goes the attack, sir?

passages.title: Assault on the Temple of Sha'naar
passages.text:
Welcome back, commander. Our scouts just returned with word of your success.

Well done!

passages.title: Treasure Contract: The Artificer
passages.text:
I have heard of a draenei artificer by the name of Maatun that was seeking to restore an old draenei crystal, possibly of naaru origin. He called the crystal the Dream of Argus. 

The draenei went missing after seeking out help from the Shadowmoon orcs back before they allied themselves with the Iron Horde. One of your scouts recently spotted a draenei matching the description of Maatun near the entrance of the Pillars of Fate. Go there and see what you can dig up.

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The First Fragment
passages.text:
In his quest to restore the Dream of Argus, Maatun enlisted the help of three orcs. These same orcs betrayed him and took the crystal shards before they could be combined. If you find these orcs, they may still have them.

The first target shouldn't be far. The journal reads:

"I was told she spent most of her time in the crystal cave to the north of the encampment. There she studied the native crystals for ways to improve their potential abilities."

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Second Fragment
passages.text:
The second orc that Matuun mentioned was a master runecarver and sorcerer. He should be located somewhere in the main camp. The journal reads:

"She mentioned that the orc could normally found in one of the runemaster's huts in the southern part of the camp. They could be identified by the standing stones surrounding the structure, as well as the floating runestones above."

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Final Fragment
passages.text:
The last orc to be found was a hermit who kept away from the bulk of the Shadowmoon orcs at the Pillars of Fate camp, but was often seen in the high hills above. The journal reads:

"It is said, however, that he can often be seen among the graves upon the high hill, overlooking the camp below. There he would commune with the dead ancestors, whom it is said he preferred over his living brethren."

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Crystal Reborn
passages.text: With the shards recovered, it is now possible to restore the Dream of Argus. You must seek out the device that Maatun mentions in his journal, which is said to be in a cave overlooking Anguish Fortress.

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Crystal Reborn
passages.text: Were you able to restore the draenei crystal?

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Crystal Reborn
passages.text:
This is incredible! I would never be able to tell that this crystal was once broken! 

I'm sure Dr. Jones will be pleased to see this, as well as the draenei if the stories behind it are true.

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text:
The components have been gathered and the "Arcane Bunker Buster" is assembled. Hopefully, this should pack enough punch to take out the barrier.

There's only one way to find out...

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text:
I can sense a bad voodoo comin from ya, mon. 

Dat be da book I'm feelin?

passages.title: Dark Grimoire: Breaching the Barrier
passages.text:
Dis book be a bad ting, mon. I'm glad we got it before it came into da wrong hands. 

I'll get it ta Jones for ya.

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Beasts
passages.text:
Gronnsbane now pulses with energies of fire and frost. All that remains to restore the full power of the weapon is to receive the Blessing of the Beast. Argoram believed this could be accomplished by bloodying the weapon against one of the ancient black rylaks of Stonefury Cliffs. His journal reads:

"High in the Stonefury Cliffs, I have seen an altar where the ogres have left offerings to these ancient beasts. Perhaps I could use it to lure one of them"

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Beasts
passages.text: You bring da spear from da Thunderlords?

passages.title: Gronnsbane: The Blessing of Beasts
passages.text:
Jones will be happy when he sees dis. 

Here's da payment he promised.

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Crystal Reborn
passages.text: With the shards recovered, it is now possible to restore the Dream of Argus. You must seek out the device that Maatun mentions in his journal, which is said to be in a cave overlooking Anguish Fortress.

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Crystal Reborn
passages.text: You get da crystal put back togetha?

passages.title: Dream of Argus: The Crystal Reborn
passages.text:
Astoundin, mon! I'd a never been able ta tell dis was eva broken. 

Here's da reward dat Jones left, I'll get dis to im.

passages.title: The Road of Glory
passages.text: The Horde intends to force us out of Ashran, <name>. We can't let them succeed. March into the Road of Glory and thin their ranks by at least five.

passages.title: [DEPRECATED]Assault on the Temple of Sha'naar
passages.text:
The Sargerei council continues to work in secret with the warlock, Gul'dan. Up in the hills of Tanaan Jungle, they have converted a once-sacred temple into a den of demonic summoning.

We must attack them now, before their rituals complete. The longer we delay, the stronger their forces become.

passages.title: Bleeding the Bleeding Hollow
passages.text:
The Bleeding Hollow provide significant reinforcement to the Iron Horde in Tanaan. From their home in Zeth'Gol they relentlessly pursue our scouts, disrupt our operations, and gather more power for Gul'dan's magic.

We should consider a direct raid on Zeth'Gol to make them pull back their forces across the valley. This should give us some breathing room... for a time.

passages.title: Bleeding the Bleeding Hollow
passages.text: Have you completed the raid, general?

passages.title: Bleeding the Bleeding Hollow
passages.text: I already have reports of Bleeding Hollow hunters falling back to Zeth'Gol. This will give us a good edge in the battles to come.

passages.title: Bleeding the Bleeding Hollow
passages.text:
The Bleeding Hollow provide significant reinforcement to the Iron Horde in Tanaan. From their home in Zeth'Gol they relentlessly pursue our scouts, disrupt our operations, and gather more power for Gul'dan's magic.

We should consider a direct raid on Zeth'Gol to make them pull back their forces across the valley. This should give us some breathing room... for a time.

passages.title: Bleeding the Bleeding Hollow
passages.text: Have you completed the raid yet, general?

passages.title: Bleeding the Bleeding Hollow
passages.text:
Well done, commander! The Bleeding Hollow are sending their best warriors back to Zeth'Gol to defend it.

This should give us an advantage, albeit temporarily.

passages.title: Battle At The Iron Front
passages.text:
General, our troops are currently engaged in a conjoined assault at the Iron Front. The fight has been raging for some time now, and casualties are high.

Report to the Iron Front and lend your strength to the war effort. I have no doubt that your presence on the battlefield will inspire the soldiers to victory!

passages.title: Battle At The Iron Front
passages.text:
I'm already hearing reports from The Iron Front that the tide of the battle has turned.

Soon, The Iron Horde will have nowhere to run!

passages.title: Battle At The Iron Front
passages.text:
The war against the Iron horde rages on.

Not far from here at The Iron Front, our warriors are engaged in mortal combat with the enemy. They fight tenaciously and with great fury, but the losses have been severe.

Go to The Iron Front and show the enemy that we will not falter in this war.

Show them that we fight as wolves!

passages.title: Battle At The Iron Front
passages.text: Thanks to your aid, we have gained a foothold at The Iron Front. Soon, Gul'dan and the Iron Horde will have nowhere else to run.

passages.title: Scrap Meltdown
passages.text: We've had a breakthrough in melting down the scraps you've been collecting! If you can get me a small pile of 'em, we can get your troops something a bit more useful.

passages.title: Scrap Meltdown
passages.text: Do you have the scraps I've asked for?

passages.title: Scrap Meltdown
passages.text: Here ya are, commander. We've got to let the forges cool for a while, but we should be ready to process more scraps tomorrow.

passages.title: Scrap Meltdown
passages.text: We've figured out how to make those scraps in to something a bit more useful to your troops. Bring me a pile of them and I'll have our smiths process it for you.

passages.title: Scrap Meltdown
passages.text: Do you have the scraps I've asked for?

passages.title: Scrap Meltdown
passages.text: Very good, commander. This should prove useful to your troops.

passages.title: Challiane Vineyards
passages.text:
Please, outsider, help me.

My recipe for Nightrose wine was to be the toast of Queen Azshara herself. But before I could make it, the vile vintners took it from me and locked me away.

Please, recover my recipe so that I might bring it to Lady Challiane and earn the queen's favor.

passages.title: Challiane Vineyards
passages.text: Have you found the pieces of the recipe?

passages.title: Challiane Vineyards
passages.text:
Thank you, outsider! Thank you very much.

You have done more for me than my own people ever have.

Lady Challiane would never take the word of a lowly cellarman over her vintners.

Now I can use this recipe to earn her favor, and then the favor of our beloved queen Azshara...

passages.title: Dark Ascension
passages.text:
You skim through the pages of the tome, most of them filled with notes on the nature of shadow and illusion. On the last pages you discover a journal:

I continue to search for a cure to the curse of Sethe. If Terokk was restored I would not be in this situation. Damn Reshad!

I was contacted by an orc that identified himself as Gul'dan. He has a cure for the curse! I must travel to Tanaan to search for the location of this "cipher" of his.

Take this information to Reshad.

passages.title: Dark Ascension
passages.text: I wish it had not come to this...

passages.title: Dark Ascension
passages.text:
Thank you, <name>.

This was no easy task and I am grateful once again for your assistance. Iskar's madness must be stopped.

I trust that when the time comes you will be ready.

passages.title: This IS In My Contract.
passages.text:
To perform my ritual I need to use a special cave I have prepared at Gloombound Barrow.

Meet me there and I will "give" you your reward. Hee hee.

passages.title: This IS In My Contract.
passages.text: Great deal right? You got to kill a demon, your fancy weapon got more fancy, and I get to be the master now. Everybody wins!

passages.title: A Bit of Ore
passages.text: It's been a pleasure trading with you.

passages.title: Assault on the Ruins of Kra'nak
passages.text:
The Shadow Council have recruited the Sethekk and other power hungry Arakkoa to their service. Our allies in the Order of the Awakened have tracked them to a ruin in the west of Tanaan where the Shadow Council is instructing them in the use of fel magic.

We must strike at them before they can master their diabolic powers.

passages.title: Assault on the Ruins of Kra'nak
passages.text:
Welcome back, commander. Our scouts just returned with word of your success.

Well done!

passages.title: Assault on the Ruins of Kra'nak
passages.text:
The Shadow Council have recruited the Sethekk and other power hungry Arakkoa to their service. Our allies in the Order of the Awakened have tracked them to a ruin in the west of Tanaan where the Shadow Council is instructing them in the use of fel magic.

We must strike at them before they can master their diabolic powers.

passages.title: Assault on the Ruins of Kra'nak
passages.text: How goes the attack, sir?

passages.title: Assault on the Ruins of Kra'nak
passages.text:
Welcome back, General. Our scouts just returned with word of your success.

Well done!

passages.title: Hook, Line, and... Sink Him!
passages.text:
I can build you a shipyard. And not some wasteful piece of over-engineering like this place.

But I'm going to need my blueprints. My work was confiscated when Gul'dan turned this harbor over to Admiral Knar.

<Roark spits.>

Gul'dan's green poison courses through Knar's veins. He's calling the shots from on high. We'll need to grapple up there to take him out.

passages.title: Hook, Line, and... Sink Him!
passages.text: I will rebuild.

passages.title: Hook, Line, and... Sink Him!
passages.text:
<Solog Roark takes in the view of his harbor one final time.>

We built it all for nothing, <class>. Gul'dan will claim whatever your troops do not destroy.

Next time, I will build something that will last.

passages.title: We Need a Shipwright
passages.text:
The Iron Horde - or whatever Gul'dan is turning them into - has fallen back and fortified the entrance to Tanaan. A direct assault will take a heavy toll.

However, the sea lanes are open. If we attack by both land and sea, Gul'dan's Horde will have no quarter. <name>, it's time to build a shipyard!

We'll need to source local resources. Travel to the Iron Docks, where a small Alliance reclamation force is already waiting. Gather what equipment you can, and find us a shipwright capable of building a fleet!

passages.title: We Need a Shipwright
passages.text:
Commander! I was told to expect you. The situation here is chaos.

My Rangari have had this place under surveillance since your original assault. It's come back to life in recent weeks as the remnants of the Iron Horde flee to Tanaan under Gul'dan's orders.

My scouts have learned something that might interest you...

passages.title: The Eye of Kilrogg
passages.text:
If you wish to know what Kilrogg and his new master intend, you will need his eye. After the ritual all chieftains place their eye under the protection of the ghosts of the Bleeding Hollow in the next chamber.

Go and locate the Eye of Kilrogg in the vault. The other chieftains will not stand with us, and will fight you for it.

Then place it on the ritual mark nearby to get your answers.

passages.title: The Eye of Kilrogg
passages.text: What have you learned?

passages.title: The Eye of Kilrogg
passages.text: Bah. Kilrogg not here. Only omens and warnings. That is your path <name>, mine is to destroy Kilrogg...

passages.title: Raw Beast Hides
passages.text: It's been a pleasure trading with you.

passages.title: Some Dust
passages.text: It's been a pleasure trading with you.

passages.title: Sumptuous Fur
passages.text: It's been a pleasure trading with you.

passages.title: Herbs Galore
passages.text: It's been a pleasure trading with you.

passages.title: Critters of Draenor
passages.text: I love collecting pets, and I've picked up a few unusual pets here in Draenor. What would you say to a battle? If you can defeat my humble team, I think we'll both learn a few new tricks.

passages.title: Critters of Draenor
passages.text: Are we going to battle or what?

passages.title: Critters of Draenor
passages.text: Not bad.  Not bad at all.  Stop by the next time I'm in the neighborhood, and I might have some new pets to check out.

passages.title: Critters of Draenor
passages.text: I love collecting pets, and I've picked up a few unusual pets here in Draenor. What would you say to a battle? If you can defeat my humble team, I think we'll both learn a few new tricks.

passages.title: Critters of Draenor
passages.text: Are we going to battle or what?

passages.title: Critters of Draenor
passages.text: Not bad.  Not bad at all.  Stop by the next time I'm in the neighborhood, and I might have some new pets to check out.

passages.title: DEPRECATED
Masters of Disguise
passages.text:
<You scan over Knockwhistle's report.>

"My chute caught a piece of shrapnel. Made a rough landing in a ravenbear nest. Luckily, a bunch of eggs broke my fall.

Lost sight of Illandris and Shwayder. Both are masters of disguise, and I am confident they can remain undetected.

Will continue to monitor the enemy's activity. Just need to clean all the yolk off my cloaking device. Hope the mother's not around...

passages.title: Masters of Disguise
passages.text: We cannot speak freely - the Alliance have eyes and ears in the hills.

passages.title: Masters of Disguise
passages.text: Finally, I can get back to the action!

passages.title: Numismatics
passages.text:
I hate to be too cynical, but I don't think we're gonna find Nolan in one piece. Or in a lot of pieces.

Nolan was a nut for finding rare coins. He's been from one end of the world to the other finding them, and now he's gone and gotten himself killed looking for more mint condition Draenei coins. Tell you what - let me show you what these coins look like, you bring me a few more of them and I'll set up an exhibit in his honor.

passages.title: Numismatics
passages.text: How's the coin hunt going?

passages.title: Numismatics
passages.text: These are in great condition. Nolan would be green with envy.

passages.title: Numismatics
passages.text:
I told him this was a fool's errand. Of course he would get himself killed over a handful of coins! Oh well, there are always new lovers to find.

You'll have to do in the mean time. And you are quite easy on the eyes, aren't you? Be a dear and find me more coins that look like this one? I need them for... research.

passages.title: Numismatics
passages.text: Well? Do you have the coins I asked you to find?

passages.title: Numismatics
passages.text:
Excellent work. I knew you'd be useful, sugarplum.

There's something very unusual about these coins...

passages.title: Bringing the Bass
passages.text:
It's a bit quiet around here, in between the invasions and all.

You're in luck though, Commander! I can fix that, and boost morale among your troops all at the same time.

All you need to do is bring me a few items from around Draenor, and I'll fill your garrison with music. I'll even throw in a few music rolls from my own collection to get you started!

What do you say?

passages.title: Bringing the Bass
passages.text: Collect a Bass Blaster, Laz-Tron Disc Reader, Phonic Amplifier, S.P.R.K. Capacitor, and a Cord of Ancient Wood.

passages.title: Bringing the Bass
passages.text: This is the best Draenor has to offer? Lucky for you I went to engineering school. One Tune-O-Tron 5000 coming up!

passages.title: Pump it Up
passages.text:
The Black Rose was a seafaring laboratory for the Royal Apothecary Society. Naturally, we had some volatile... "byproducts" onboard.

Regrettably, one such substance was released during our skirmish with the Alliance gunship. As you can see, it is taking quite a toll on the coast.

The R.A.S. must remedy this situation before we press further inland.

Please take a containment unit and fill it with waste - for us to dispose of properly at a later time, of course.

passages.title: Pump it Up
passages.text: There's still room in that containment unit.

passages.title: Pump it Up
passages.text:
Wonderful, just put that down anywhere. Careful not to spill it!

<The apothecary snickers.>

passages.title: Completionism
passages.text: Interesting - the coins you've brought back from your Garrison are slightly different than the ones Nolan collected in Outland. Y'see here, the markings along the edge? Very interesting stuff! This requires some more study an' that means more coins! Bring them to me and I'll see if I can scrounge up something for your trouble.

passages.title: Completionism
passages.text: Aye? Y'got them coins yet?

passages.title: Completionism
passages.text: Y'know, I think we might be on to somethin' big here.

passages.title: Completionism
passages.text:
This is intolerable! The coins you brought me do not match the rest of the coins I already have! You aren't counterfeiting these are you? No? Hrumph. In that case I'm sorry we fought, dearie.

There's only one thing to do, buttercup: we need to complete the new set you've discovered. Bring me more misprinted coins!

passages.title: Completionism
passages.text: I certainly hope these coins can complete this set so I can se-- er, so I can treasure them forever.

passages.title: Completionism
passages.text:
That wasn't so hard now was it, peaches?

<Estelle holds the coins you brought up the the light and practically purrs.>

Yes yes, these are so very strange...

passages.title: A Curious Oddity
passages.text:
I've been looking at some of the other coins in circulation plus the ones you've brought back. Some o' these are misprints... others are just plain wrong. Look 'ere. This one's got two heads. And the second one is smiling at me, where it wasn't before.

There's a bigger mystery in play here and these misprints are the key to figuring it out. I'm gonna need even more.

passages.title: A Curious Oddity
passages.text: We're on the verge of a breakthrough here.

passages.title: A Curious Oddity
passages.text: Good, good! I've got some awful suspicious suspicions about these here suspicious coins.

passages.title: A Curious Oddity
passages.text:
Well sweet pea, I have good news and bad news for you. The good news is that you brought me enough coins to complete this new misprint set! The bad news is that not a single one of them has matched the original partial set.

See here - this coin has two heads. And the face on the reverse is grinning at me, where he was looking so dour only an hour ago. This one squints when I shine a light on it. Such a mystery! I must have more!

passages.title: A Curious Oddity
passages.text: Has anyone told you today that you're beautiful? You are.

passages.title: A Curious Oddity
passages.text: Honeybiscuit, when this is all over, you and I may be remembered as stumbling on a great paranormal discovery. Or I will at least.
