passages.title: Fortify the Runestones: Blood Knights
passages.text: Your deeds honor us, <name>. You have fought well this day.

passages.title: Fortify the Runestones: Farstriders
passages.text:
The Magisters placed a handful of runestones across Eversong, each one charged with arcane magic that wards off the Lightbloom.

As you might guess, the runestones require a huge amount of power to function. The Magisters feed them with latent arcana, but that kind of power draws a lot of attention. Bad attention.

As Farstriders, it's our duty to defend Eversong from those kinds of threats--especially when the Haven is looking at us. Go recharge the runestones and fight off whatever tries to stop you.

passages.title: Fortify the Runestones: Farstriders
passages.text: We need to keep those runestones safe.

passages.title: Fortify the Runestones: Farstriders
passages.text: Nice work. You know how to see a mission through smoothly. I have a few ranger recruits who could learn a thing or two from you.

passages.title: Cowardly Cheery Bombs
passages.text:
Goblins love bombs, I get that. But does EVERYTHING have to blow up?

Do me a favor: In the next Dastardly Duos match you enter, find a cheery bomb inside one of the wooden tree and planter props.

After you find the bomb, but before it "blows up"... smack it for me. Don't worry, they're cowards.

passages.title: Cowardly Cheery Bombs
passages.text: Those cheery bombs are asking for it, <name>. Find one in a Dastardly Duos match and smack it!

passages.title: Cowardly Cheery Bombs
passages.text: Way to go, <name>. You have to show those bombs who's boss, you know?

passages.title: Borrowing Corruption
passages.text:
Adventurer, I have made an amazing discovery. 

Analyzing the memories from the time I have discovered that I might be able to recreate the corruption effects that have been wielded in the past. Albeit in a much more controlled way. 

I will need you gather some black blood residue from defeating the bosses of the Corrupted or Lost areas of the map and a few more of the displaced corrupted mementos.

passages.title: Borrowing Corruption
passages.text: Were you successful?

passages.title: Borrowing Corruption
passages.text:
Yes, by combining this residue with the displaced corrupted mementos I can... yeah just like so... and then with a bit of my bronze magic... there. Done.

Now that I have a working knowledge I can also make more if you bring me additional displaced corrupted mementos. I will see if I can refine the process anymore. Check back with me later.

passages.title: Enhancing Corruption
passages.text:
Welcome back adventurer. I have made a new discovery but I need to test it out. 

Hidden in the Lost areas of the Horrific Visions I believe is a rare black blood coagulate. This might be the key to increasing the power of the corruption effects... in a safe way. 

If you can go into these areas and find this item and also bring me back more displaced corrupted mementos I should be able to increase the potency of the corruption effects.

passages.title: Enhancing Corruption
passages.text: Were you successful?

passages.title: Enhancing Corruption
passages.text:
Ok, this is promising... the coagulate catalyzes slower so the increased corruption is more contained... yes, this allows a higher yield of corrupted material without any negative side effects.

Alas, I cannot keep it stable for long. These effects will not last. I am sorry adventurer but we should take advantage of the effects while we can. 

Again, if you bring me additional displaced corrupted mementos I can make you more of these greater corruptions.

passages.title: That's Not Yours
passages.text:
The rutaani in the Blossoming Terrace are crafty. They've trained their petalwings to search and grab anything shiny that rolls down from the Den.

And, I suspect, sometimes they grab things that haven't naturally fallen.

So we want to get those things back. That's where you come in.

Go into the terrace, and don't hesitate to use force to send a message. That's a language we all understand.

passages.title: That's Not Yours
passages.text: Have you found those missing things?

passages.title: That's Not Yours
passages.text:
You found quite a few things. Including...

... Wait, that's mine. I thought I'd lost that.

<Seila mutters foul words about thieving birds.>

passages.title: Overcharged Console
passages.text:
With the shards ye found, we can use the console tae restore the titan discs and use them to access powerful boons. 

Use the console's disc repair feature to create a titan disc, then use that disc to select a starting node in the overcharge console's interface.

passages.title: Overcharged Console
passages.text: Did it work?

passages.title: Overcharged Console
passages.text:
My remote console shows that there was a change. The overcharged console is funnelin' excess energy to a new node. This should grant ye that node's power when venturin' intae other areas where the titan constructs have emerged.

We'll use the titan force's own energy against 'em!

passages.title: Pesky Pests
passages.text:
Nearby creatures are suffering an infection of Light, and are being drawn to the Sunbath. Our guests find it disturbing. That is a problem, when one is trying to enjoy a tranquil escape from the world.

I confess, having one run into your leg while you are swimming can be unnerving.

Please, dissuade the invading sungrubs from joining us, and take to the sky to chase off those persistent butterflies.

passages.title: Pesky Pests
passages.text: Are the insects giving you trouble?

passages.title: Pesky Pests
passages.text:
That wasn't so bad, was it? 

Val does get a bit dramatic, but you performed wonderfully.

passages.title: Lost in Light
passages.text:
It seems some of our more adventurous guests have not returned from their hike. Val said he saw a rutaani skulking about earlier, but I was certain he was just trying to add some drama to our day.

The Lightbloom infiltrated the Sanctum to the north and has been spilling residual issues our way.

Our guests are here to escape the troubles of the world... This all could become a bit too real for them.

If you'll take care of that situation, I'll make sure Val keeps the guests distracted.

passages.title: Lost in Light
passages.text: Did they make it back?

passages.title: Lost in Light
passages.text:
Tormenting our guests was a step too far.

She encroached on the sunbath and has paid the price for her actions.

Thank you, new friend of the Solaar family!

passages.title: Ultra Prime Deluxe Turbo-Boost: Powerhouse Challenges
passages.text:
<Undermine has a problem. Here's what we need. An established group, or just a bunch a ya really, ready to help out our pals in Undermine. Help clear out the worst of the competition, and we'll make it worth your time.

Complete the task, and collect a special reward from Consultant Wrexxle outside of the the Dornogal Treasury. Limited time offer. Some restrictions will apply.>

passages.title: Ultra Prime Deluxe Turbo-Boost: Powerhouse Challenges
passages.text: Yous looks out for us, and we return the favor. Right?

passages.title: Ultra Prime Deluxe Turbo-Boost: Powerhouse Challenges
passages.text:
Thanks, pal. Undermine is a mess right now. We'll take all the help we can get.

And hey, a deal's a deal. Here's what we owe.

We call this the jackpot reward for first time help. Check back again for more work!

passages.title: A Path Not Yet Chosen
passages.text:
I'm trying to figure out what career path to follow, but I keep second-guessing myself. The Farstriders, the Blood Knights, the Magisters... they all seem so incredible that I can't decide.

I was hoping if I spoke to each and earned a recommendation, I might finally understand where I'm meant to be. Would you help me?

passages.title: A Path Not Yet Chosen
passages.text: I really hope I find where I belong...

passages.title: A Path Not Yet Chosen
passages.text:
Wow... I can't believe I actually got all three recommendations. They all said such kind things, but now I feel even more torn than before!

Do you think... perhaps you could help me choose?

passages.title: How to Train Your Protege
passages.text:
I did everything they asked--the trials, the lessons--and they all said I did well... but I still don't know where I truly belong.

Each path felt right in its own way, and now my heart feels pulled in three directions.

Please... could you help me decide?

passages.title: How to Train Your Protege
passages.text:
Ah... so the boy has chosen at last. He has heart--too much perhaps.

Yes. This will be recorded and honored. You've done more than deliver a message--you've helped shape a life. Thank you.

passages.title: Secret Ingredients
passages.text:
Our gregarious guests have partaken so much from our stores that we are running dangerously low of our special Solaarian sintalia.

The rich taste of belanise, with its intoxicating scent, contrasts perfectly with the sharp tartness of the local berries. Carefully prepared then soaked in our special blend of spirits, then served--it's to die for!

Just between us, if the berries are not handled just right, the infusion can be quite deadly. Otherwise... delicious, invigorating, purifying, glorious!

passages.title: Secret Ingredients
passages.text: Are you gathering carefully?

passages.title: Secret Ingredients
passages.text:
Magic! Perfection! You could not be more skilled if I had wished you into existence.

That is an interesting thought. Could I have?

passages.title: Harvest of Darkness
passages.text:
You... make yourself useful.

As a master of terrible beasts, it is my job to mold these hatchlings into dreaded beasts. I pit them against each other and they grow ever more violent.

But the elves here insist that I will yield better results with just a bit of... tender loving care. Let us put this to the test.

This runt is Fidoficus. You will show him tenderness and affection, and then we will see how ferocious he becomes.

Collect some delicious dietary treats for him and return to me.

passages.title: Harvest of Darkness
passages.text: These ingredients will make for a highly nutritious and equally delectable meal.

passages.title: Harvest of Darkness
passages.text:
Fidoficus will be renowned for his ferocity.

I can see the violence growing in him.

One day, he will be a worthy pet for a domanaar such as myself.

passages.title: Little Monsters
passages.text:
When I sent a request for aid from Har'alnor, I did not expect them to send me an outsider. No matter.

The denizens of Fungara Village have gone quiet. Normally, I would be thrilled: they're horribly screechy. But the way they are shambling about... it is like they have forgotten that they yet live.

<Ghikal shudders.>

I tried to get close, but they attacked me on sight.

I will need samples of their flesh. Go and bring them to me, so I can see what has happened here.

passages.title: Little Monsters
passages.text: I do not know what is going on, but to err on the side of caution... do not let them bite you, hrm? Whatever plagues them may be infectious.

passages.title: Little Monsters
passages.text:
Goddess forfend. This is not fungarian flesh at all.

What ARE they?

passages.title: You Are Legend
passages.text:
Whatever these things are, they're not fungarians. Not anymore. 

Har'alnor has enough to worry about with the Lightbloom as it is. It cannot afford to be trapped between its forces and these... things.

Do what must be done. Destroy as many of them as you can.

passages.title: You Are Legend
passages.text: Do not feel regret. These things are not alive anymore. Not in any way that matters.

passages.title: You Are Legend
passages.text: You are quite the accomplished slayer of aberrations. Perhaps you should consider a vocation in monster-hunting.

passages.title: Decayed Land
passages.text:
As far as I can tell, these fungarians are all already dead. Something is animating their corpses from within, like puppets attached to unseen vines.

This fungal matter that's infesting them must be coming from somewhere... and judging from the size of the ones further north, we'll find plenty of it there. Find it, get rid of it, but for Aln'hara's sake don't breathe it in.

passages.title: Decayed Land
passages.text:
We've culled the worst of the growths to the north... but there are smaller ones already beginning to sprout. Where are they coming from?

There must be a source, and we'll have to find it if we mean to solve this thing.

passages.title: Belly of the Beast
passages.text:
I normally raise my beasts on a diet of raw, bloody carcasses and souls ripped asunder by the Void.

But we shall try your mortal ways.

I hear you... cook? And that makes the treat better?

Do this. Then, take him on a walk around the Howling Ridge. Even I know exercise is good for digestion.

Only the most ferocious of creatures is worthy of serving me. I hope neither you nor Fido disappoint me.

passages.title: Belly of the Beast
passages.text: He is still small, but one day, he will grow to be a terrible foe.

passages.title: Belly of the Beast
passages.text:
Is the beast's savagery growing?

I'm sure I will begin to hear of his violence from those around the Howling Ridge.

passages.title: Reticent Evil
passages.text:
I do not understand. We've searched high and low, north and south. Everywhere we go, we find animated corpses and small fruiting fungus, but where is the central body? Where is--

Oh, goddess. Of course.

The water, <class>. Check the water.

passages.title: Reticent Evil
passages.text:
It is done, then.

You did well to survive untainted. The wilds are a dangerous place, and survival is never a guarantee.

Now go. I must remain and ensure that these abominations cannot spread any further.

passages.title: Mighty and Superior
passages.text:
The beast is fed and exercised. Imagine, mortal... one day his maw will grow to fit you inside it a thousand times over. 

Now, we will test his potential for true violence. 

There is a beast that has laid claim to a den south of the Howling Ridge. 

Fidoficus trusts you now. Go with him and bear witness to his might.

passages.title: Mighty and Superior
passages.text: Fidoficus has grown fearsome, and perhaps you have claim to some of his growth.

passages.title: Mighty and Superior
passages.text:
Fidoficus will grow so terribly large, that it is he who will be walking you. 

Only then will he be worthy of joining me as my attack behemoth.

passages.title: Far from the Hinterlands
passages.text:
As a Torntusk of de Revantusk tribe, I am cautious of Witherbark because of our history with dem in de Hinterlands. My family moved here because of dem.

The Witherbark here in Zul'Aman seem to respect us, but de Witherbark I remember in de Hinterlands killed and backstabbed their allies for power.

They worshipped de spider loa, Shadra.

When de Hinterlands's Witherbark temple Shadra'Alor fell, de Witherbark must have fled somewhere. Look around for evidence of Hinterlands Witherbark and of Shadra.

passages.title: Far from the Hinterlands
passages.text:
All de places dey mentioned are right next door to Shadra'Alor! Dey probably worshipped Shadra.

We can't trust dem. Dey are like de venoms dey use. Dey will poison de rest of de tribe against de Revatusk--against us all!

passages.title: The Eye of the Loa
passages.text:
I lost friends to venoms made from Shadra's spiders in de Hinterlands. I gotta know if Shadra's lurkin' around here, twistin' de minds of these Witherbark. No Revantusk will be safe in Zul'Aman with Shadra-worshippin' Witherbark around!

Maybe I seem paranoid, but I have my reasons. And you have Halazzi's ear. You could ask him to reveal to you any hidden spiders, yes? I know those long ears can hear dem skitterin'!

There is a shrine behind me. Stand in front of it and see if he'll grant you a boon.

passages.title: The Eye of the Loa
passages.text: Did Halazzi help you? He can hear anything, but he also can see what's hidden in shadow.

passages.title: The Eye of the Loa
passages.text:
De spiders fled? I thought dey would put up more of a fight. And you said dey were small? Hm.

Well, it doesn't matter. Halazzi has set us on this hunt now. We need to see it through.

passages.title: Maisara Caverns: Deep in Maisara
passages.text:
Shadra has asked dat we recover de third piece of Mixer Jamanga's ritual, de Shell of Shadra. With it, maybe we can bring her back.

She recognized both de Witherbark and Revantusk as her allies. I felt her approval upon all of us. I believe this is de right choice.

Halazzi set us on dis path, and we each got our roles to see it through. Gather your allies and go into Maisara Caverns! I would expect one of their leaders to hold de shell. Kill dem and take it back.

passages.title: Maisara Caverns: Deep in Maisara
passages.text: I think dat Shadra will honor her word.

passages.title: Maisara Caverns: Deep in Maisara
passages.text: I can't imagine dat was easy. Halazzi must have blessed your hunt.

passages.title: Eco-Dome Al'dani
passages.text:
We have received word from Ve'nari that the Wastelanders continue to stand in the way of progress on K'aresh. They threaten the most promising eco-dome.

The restoration directive of K'aresh must not be interrupted.

Put an end to these inefficiencies.

passages.title: Eco-Dome Al'dani
passages.text: Have you put an end to their efforts?

passages.title: Eco-Dome Al'dani
passages.text:
This is a promising beginning to our new relationship with K'aresh.

Good work, outlander.

passages.title: Manaforge Omega: A Walking Shadow
passages.text:
Hero, can you hear me? There's a translocator the Shadowguard uses to send cargo to their reserves that can carry you directly to their post beneath the Manaforge. An ambush they'll never see coming!

There is of course, a catch. We do not have clearance to use their supply lines... so we need you to procure some for us. Take down the highest-ranking member of the Shadowguard you can find, return with identification, and we'll forge you a one-way ticket to the front lines.

passages.title: Manaforge Omega: A Walking Shadow
passages.text: That certainly qualifies as high-ranking, <name>! After I work my magic, that translocator is as good as ours. Next stop, enemy territory!

passages.title: Manaforge Omega: A Walking Shadow
passages.text:
Hero, can you hear me? There's a translocator the Shadowguard uses to send cargo to their reserves that can carry you directly to their post beneath the Manaforge. An ambush they'll never see coming!

There is of course, a catch. We do not have clearance to use their supply lines... so we need you to procure some for us. Take down the highest-ranking member of the Shadowguard you can find, return with identification, and we'll forge you a one-way ticket to the front lines.

passages.title: Manaforge Omega: A Walking Shadow
passages.text: That certainly qualifies as high-ranking, <name>! After I work my magic, that translocator is as good as ours. Next stop, enemy territory!

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines
passages.text: My friend, we've finished working on some new tools to ensure you'll do some real damage to the Shadowguard. Come by and let's sort it out together.

passages.title: Behind Enemy Lines
passages.text: My friend! Thanks to our informants inside the Manaforge, we've uncovered some technology that can help you bring it down. This translocator has been calibrated to project your soul back here for a few moments, allowing you to access whatever you may need--but be warned. The pull of Omega's energy fields are strong, and will rip your essence back to your body's position in short order. I'm told it's... quite painful. Still, any advantage is a good advantage. Make haste!

passages.title: Head Hunting: Loom'ithar
passages.text: Our intelligence describes a colossal beast within the Manaforge, responsible for producing the fabric that gives the Shadowguard their very form. Take it down and we'll hinder their ability to produce reinforcements. Oh, and Ba'choso says to bring some of the silk back with you - he may be able to fashion it into something useful.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Loom'ithar
passages.text: Have you procured a sample?

passages.title: Head Hunting: Loom'ithar
passages.text: Its quality is unlike anything I've ever seen! I'll get to work right away. Now, let's discuss your payment.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Forgeweaver Araz
passages.text: My friend, I hope your assault is going well. It's time for you to dispatch the Forgeweaver; using his mastery of technomancy he oversees both the Manaforge's production pipelines... as well as the ritual to return Dimensius to this plane. His workshop will be further in and heavily guarded, but cutting him down should stop their plans of resurrection for good.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Forgeweaver Araz
passages.text: Does the Forgeweaver yet live?

passages.title: Head Hunting: Forgeweaver Araz
passages.text: <name>... I should have seen that coming. His devotion to Dimensius knew no bounds, and he certainly had contingencies in place to make sure the ritual would be completed. We'll have to attack from another angle. We found some debris from his inner sanctum that made its way here - if you have the skill, we can teach you how to use it for your own ends.

passages.title: Head Hunting: The Soul Hunters
passages.text: Careful in the wastes, my friend. Scouts report that a trio of Demon Hunters are training south of the Manaforge - with one of them exhibiting power like we've never seen. You can avoid their path if you wish, but ignoring them could open you up to being flanked should they decide to engage. I recommend taking them out if you can, as well as providing us some samples of their newfound strength.

passages.title: Head Hunting: The Soul Hunters
passages.text: Soul energy like I've never seen it. While we cannot return them to the way they were, I believe you can use these runes to empower yourself even *through* death. Take them with you, and use them wisely.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Horrors of the Forge
passages.text: By now no doubt you've seen some of the Manaforge's Elite coming to Salhadaar's aid. I'm sending you a list of names now - focus on these targets, and you may uncover spoils to aid your assault.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Horrors of the Forge
passages.text: Have you eliminated your targets?

passages.title: Head Hunting: Horrors of the Forge
passages.text: Nicely done, champion. The resources they were hoarding will find a much better home with your companions.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Nexus-King Salhadaar
passages.text: The hour of Salhadaar's demise is upon us. While he may posture upon his Voidwing, he grows desperate at the feet of the All-Devouring. The army he commands is not enough for your might - strike him down.

passages.title: Head Hunting: Nexus-King Salhadaar
passages.text: Though not the end he deserved, we will celebrate his defeat nonetheless. See Zo'ropo to trade for a well-deserved reward. You have my eternal gratitude for deposing him.

passages.title: One Will Not Rise
passages.text:
Now's our best shot! We end de sacrifices here! Stoppin' de dark energy has weakened her hold.

Then, you can be de one to bring back her head.

Uh, and <name>--no tellin' de chief about me callin' him Big VunVun. He'll be turnin' me into a frog if he hears dat again.

passages.title: Drain You
passages.text:
Do you... see...? They follow... They plead... for help...

<The voidwalker strains and shudders as it tries to communicate.>

Too weak... too starving...

<It feebly hands you a shard of dark matter.>

This... will feed me... then together... we find the missing elves...

passages.title: Drain You
passages.text:
I am better now... stable, but a fatigue still clings to me.

If we're to find your scouts, I will need your help.

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text:
My Shadowtrade Mercenaries will fight for Stormarion Cores, no questions asked, but they do get hungry also!

Food is quite scarce here, so we need supplies!

Take a mercenary out with you and find some food for them to eat. I'll make it worth your while!

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: Is that mercenary well fed?

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: When it comes to mercenaries, nothing keeps them loyal like a full stomach... and gold.

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text:
My Shadowtrade Mercenaries will fight for Stormarion Cores, no questions asked, but they do get hungry also!

Food is quite scarce here, so we need supplies!

Take a mercenary out with you and find some food for them to eat. I'll make it worth your while!

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: Is that mercenary well fed?

passages.title: What's For Lunch?
passages.text: When it comes to mercenaries, nothing keeps them loyal like a full stomach... and gold.

passages.title: Hitting the Hammer
passages.text:
The Twilight Hammer is dirtying up the ruins of Zeb'tala. Clean up the area and bring back some of their personal tokens. One never knows what curiosities may appeal to those vying for relevancy.

Those mindless cultists may stomp around and act tough, but you will make quick work of them.

passages.title: Hitting the Hammer
passages.text: Have you found anything useful?

passages.title: Hitting the Hammer
passages.text:
You have successfully blunted those Twilight tools. Whether or not we will have any takers for this odd assortment of tokens is yet to be determined.

There is, however, no accounting for taste.

passages.title: Hold the Watch
passages.text:
There is still a lot of friction on the border with Zul'Aman, but we must hold the watch on all fronts.

Check in with Bloodguard Nelric at the Thalassian Pass. It is rumored to be one of the most uneventful posts. I am certain he would appreciate a reprieve, if only for a few moments.

Stay alert, adventurer!

passages.title: Hold the Watch
passages.text:
An uneventful watch is more rewarding than an empty conversation.

The Blood Knights appreciate your service.

passages.title: Naga Blades
passages.text:
It seems the locals currently find great appeal in naga blades--the brinier the better. On our southwestern shore, you will find the Daggerspine naga.

They have these grungy, barnacle-encrusted scimitars that would perfectly fit the bill.

Go grab a few of those. They could have value in some of our upcoming discussions.

passages.title: Naga Blades
passages.text: Were you able to procure some blades?

passages.title: Naga Blades
passages.text:
Excellent work! These will do nicely.

Between us, my personal preference leans toward the colorful seashells. Maybe that is because my sword is more than an adornment.

passages.title: Sunfire to the Blade
passages.text:
I guess there is one benefit to being part of the courtly intrigue: one does hear things. We have this concoction of sunfire infused with the holy energy of the Blood Knights, courtesy of the court alchemists.

Take this down to the Sanctum of the Moon and test it on the Twilight intruders. I look forward to hearing the results in detail.

passages.title: Sunfire to the Blade
passages.text: How did it go?

passages.title: Sunfire to the Blade
passages.text: Anar'anel belore! You love to hear it. This news is sure to warm a few hearts for our cause.

passages.title: That's Our Wood
passages.text:
It seems the lure of the lightwood continues to be a problem.

We may as well take advantage of the trolls' hard work! Collect what they have harvested. We can make use of it.

What we do not use for weapons, we can hand over to the carvers. The nobles will clamor over lightwood decor.

passages.title: That's Our Wood
passages.text: Did you gather the lightwood?

passages.title: That's Our Wood
passages.text:
Your task is done. These will prove useful.

Do not let on that the Blood Knights got first pick.

passages.title: Lightbloom Dimmed
passages.text:
All of this small talk makes my ears twitch. I would be so much more useful doing field work. For now, you get to do the fun part.

The creatures within the Lightbloom are getting a bit dense. I need you to get out there and lower the volume.

I am sure you'll run into many options while you are out there. Take a whack at a few for me.

passages.title: Lightbloom Dimmed
passages.text:
You have performed well. Silvermoon appreciates your service.

I would have happily swapped places with you, but we all have our assignments.

passages.title: Less Lawless
passages.text:
The Tideborne are always running just over the legal line. They are an annoyance at best, but will push boundaries when given too much rope.

The ones in Sunsail Anchorage made the mistake of ripping off some nobles not too long ago. Maybe go smack them around a bit--remind them to respect their betters.

passages.title: Less Lawless
passages.text: Have you taught the Tideborne a lesson?

passages.title: Less Lawless
passages.text:
Ah, that must have been such fun! My bar may be lower today, after the engrossing discourse on the harvesting cycle of the basic peacebloom.

Apologies. Know your service is appreciated.

passages.title: Taxing the Tideborne
passages.text:
Have you ever noticed, that sometimes there is benefit in letting someone think they are getting away with something? The Tideborne will continue to smuggle in plain sight, feeling clever at the taxes they're avoiding paying to Silvermoon.

This does add up, though, over time. When you have a moment, please head down to the harbor and relieve them of some of their back taxes.

passages.title: Taxing the Tideborne
passages.text: Is it still stealing when stolen from thieves?

passages.title: Taxing the Tideborne
passages.text:
One must appreciate the special jingle of a heavy sack of purloined coins.

Excellent work, my friend.

passages.title: Chop It Down
passages.text:
We received word there's a creature from Lightbloom Ath'Ran making trouble on the western coast. It has caused a bit of drama.

Head over and resolve the issue.

passages.title: Chop It Down
passages.text: Is the issue resolved?

passages.title: Chop It Down
passages.text: Good work. I'm sure that will make for some excellent kindling.

passages.title: Lovely Plumage
passages.text:
The beautiful members of the Silvermoon Court do so love their colorful embellishments.

For this, we can stock up while doing a good deed! Head over to Thuron's Livery and pick up some of the brightly colored feathers shed from the hawkstriders in training.

Vaelith gets clean up service and we get the lovely plumage.

passages.title: Lovely Plumage
passages.text: Did you find loads of feathers?

passages.title: Lovely Plumage
passages.text:
You are so good at this!

One of these days, we should pile these feathers up and let everyone jump in them. I think you would be surprised how many proper lords and ladies would gleefully participate.

For now, we will explore feathery accents.

passages.title: Sungrub Silk
passages.text:
Oh, adventurer, have you ever visited the Solaarian Sunbath? If not, it's highly recommended.

The sungrubs that wander nearby have a precious silk from which amazing fabric can be made. Solwin Brightstitch is reputed to be masterful in this, with his sartorial magic.

The raw materials are often sought out to have him create unique and personalized goods from scratch. Bring us some of that lovely silk. It will provide a soft cushion when faced with harder discussions.

passages.title: Sungrub Silk
passages.text: Oh, did you get all of the silk?

passages.title: Sungrub Silk
passages.text:
Perfect! I have to confess, it will be hard to give some of this up.

I must remember, I have a job to do here. It can't all be fun and games.

Your work is appreciated.

passages.title: Windrunner Memorabilia
passages.text:
The nobles do so love the unusual. Take a look around Windrunner Village. There are sure to be some interesting mementos still tucked away there.

I will find an advantageous home for the pieces you bring back.

passages.title: Windrunner Memorabilia
passages.text: Did you find anything interesting?

passages.title: Windrunner Memorabilia
passages.text:
I asked for unusual and you delivered! A couple of these seem a bit... suspect.

I'm sure it will be fine. What could go wrong with items of mysterious origin?

passages.title: Put a Little Snap in Their Step
passages.text:
Those naga are, as ever, being a beachfront nuisance. Do they not understand that is a prime location?

We may not be able to reliably drive them off, but a little mischief would not be untoward.

I found this tune that drives the snapdragons mad. They will just attack whoever is nearby. Take this and give it a shot!

passages.title: Put a Little Snap in Their Step
passages.text: Are the naga adequately harassed?

passages.title: Put a Little Snap in Their Step
passages.text:
I feel bad for the snapdragons, but I can't help but laugh at the look of surprise on their face when their little buddies pounce on them.

Thank you for making the day a little more entertaining.

passages.title: Potted Lashers
passages.text:
It seems some of the nobles are botany-curious where the Lightbloom is concerned. They seek the exotic to adorn their windowsills and lurk in the dangerous section of their greenhouses.

That's where you come in, adventurer!

Go harvest those small and pernicious plants. Their bulbs will be the best for planting.

passages.title: Potted Lashers
passages.text: Any problems with the harvest?

passages.title: Potted Lashers
passages.text:
The results of sharing these with the Silvermoon elite could range from passably amusing to disastrous.

Either way, I look forward to seeing the results of their gardening efforts.

passages.title: Brightwing Conservation
passages.text:
The conservators at Brightwing Estate have a mischievous young dragonhawk named Cerul that likes to run away whenever their backs are turned. He doesn't go far, but it has become a game for him to get them to chase him.

Take this delicious treat with you and use it to lure him back home.

passages.title: Brightwing Conservation
passages.text:
It makes everyone happy to have all the creatures home at Brightwing. Having a peaceful place to enjoy the coast is a benefit to all.

Thank you for letting Cerul enjoy a little play time!

passages.title: Ghostland Peppers
passages.text:
The delicate blue ghostland peppers may not look like much, but they have a mean burn. Many nobles won't admit it, but they are quite popular in the noble games of "Truth or Challenge."

Please procure a few for me. I like to watch them sweat.

passages.title: Ghostland Peppers
passages.text: How goes the harvest?

passages.title: Ghostland Peppers
passages.text:
Joy! These will bring much excitement, and some chagrin, to the court.

Many thanks! Oh, and <name>... be sure to cleanse your hands before you rub your eyes--or worse. I learned that the hard way.

passages.title: Sunset to Sea
passages.text:
Naga have set up camp on the Sunset Strand. The sunset slugs that called it home are distraught and seem unsure what to do. This little tune will remind them of their home.

Go inspire them to seek the freedom of the open sea.

passages.title: Sunset to Sea
passages.text:
Best of luck to our little nudibranchian friends! Yes, I made that word up, but is it not accurate?

Thank you for helping them seek out more pleasant waters.

passages.title: A Little Errand
passages.text:
When conversations get tense, it can be challenging to keep words flowing in a productive way. At times like these, I find a little social lubrication is in order.

Swing over to Goldenmist Village and pick up a cask of Vintner's Golden. It's proven to have a euphoric side effect that can be quite helpful.

passages.title: A Little Errand
passages.text: Did you find the cask?

passages.title: A Little Errand
passages.text: Perfect! This is just what the court ordered.

passages.title: Where Has the Wine Gone?
passages.text:
I entrusted one of my apprentices with the delivery of several cases of particularly expensive wine. He was to bring them here from my private storage, but he has not yet arrived.

I should hate to ask you to retrieve him, but I cannot stress enough how expensive those bottles are.

Please see if you can locate him and my delivery. He should have been traveling from the north to arrive here.

passages.title: Where Has the Wine Gone?
passages.text: I dearly hope my apprentice has a colorful excuse for his tardiness.

passages.title: Where Has the Wine Gone?
passages.text:
The wine attacked you both, you say? Ah yes, I suppose the mana in that particular vintage is prone to sedimentation.

I am pleased most of it was recoverable.

passages.title: Diminutive Demand
passages.text:
Keeping preciously small animals as pets is a popular pastime among the nobility. The more unconventional the animal, often obtained through magic, the more of a conversation piece it is.

I have enchanted this wand with the appropriate shrinking spell. Use it on some of the colorful toads out near the ponds and bring them back here. The nobles will find them delightful.

Naturally, the toads may not take kindly to the enchantment. But I trust you can handle that, should it occur.

passages.title: Diminutive Demand
passages.text: Fear not. The enchantment is quite permanent.

passages.title: Diminutive Demand
passages.text:
Oh, they are positively precious, are they not?

I imagine we will see quite a few miniscule toads in handbags this coming season.

passages.title: Pyrepetal Purposes
passages.text:
Lord Saltheril, that old lynx, has put me in a bit of a bind.

He has requested a grand fireworks display to accompany tonight's dinner service, but we are dreadfully low on pyrepetal dust. It is an herb native to Eversong, highly flammable and quite dazzling when set aflame by pyromancy.

Could you help us replenish our stores? We mostly harvest it from the woods near Scintilas Falls.

passages.title: Pyrepetal Purposes
passages.text: Do be careful to keep the pyrepetals away from open flame.

passages.title: Pyrepetal Purposes
passages.text: Wonderful. This quantity should be sufficient for a lovely round of fireworks.

passages.title: What Horrible Magic
passages.text:
Have you seen the encampments the naga have been constructing along our coast? Dreadful business.

Not only do they menace our ships and disrupt our trade routes, but they might pose a real threat to Eversong's inland settlements if allowed to continue operations unchecked.

Their arcanists are particularly dangerous. Dispose of them and our guests will be in your debt.

passages.title: What Horrible Magic
passages.text: I trust this task is within your skill set.

passages.title: What Horrible Magic
passages.text: Marvelous. I am certain our guests would have preferred to see the battle themselves, but tales of your heroism will do nicely.

passages.title: Fit for a Magister
passages.text:
Battle prowess and magical skill are important, of course, but one cannot deny the power of appearances. A well-dressed army instills far more faith than one bedecked in rags.

Fortunately, a fine set of robes can be both flattering and functional. The mana silk produced at the North Sanctum can be woven into robes that deepen and intensify our magical reserves.

Be a dear and gather some for us, would you? My wardrobe could use a seasonal refreshment.

passages.title: Fit for a Magister
passages.text: Do be careful around the mana wyrms. I understand they can be aggressive after harvesting.

passages.title: Fit for a Magister
passages.text:
Mana silk has a beautiful sheen, does it not?

The Magisters will be looking spectacular throughout the soiree.

passages.title: Power Clean
passages.text:
The festivities have been wonderfully entertaining, which means the nobles have been leaving a bit of a mess around the estate. Lord Saltheril's servants have been keeping up with the cleaning, but the Magisters could lend a hand.

Enchanting a few brooms to sweep the pavilion should be an easy but impressive feat.

I was informed that an arcanist was employing the same tactic over at Farstrider Hold. Go retrieve some of his brooms and I will have them re-enchanted here.

passages.title: Power Clean
passages.text: Technically any broom would do, but the magic is easier to weave if the object has already been primed to receive the enchantment.

passages.title: Power Clean
passages.text: We will have the estate shining in no time.

passages.title: Turbo-Boost: Trade Must Flow
passages.text:
<The Trust is under pressure from the cartels to keep markets open. We seek associates capable of removing certain... obstacles. Cartel So has been authorized to distribute substantial riches if you are successful.

Complete the task, and collect a special reward from Fixer So'kir outside of the Dornogal Treasury. Parties shall remain unbound by any implied oaths arising in the course of trade. Uniform Broker Code standard terms apply.>

passages.title: Turbo-Boost: Trade Must Flow
passages.text:
The Trust thanks you for your assistance, <name>. 

As promised, here is your reward. 

To celebrate the success of our new partnership, we are including a small performance bonus. Please return later for more work!

passages.title: Simply Magical
passages.text:
Who... Who are you? Who sent you? Lilaju?

De cultists massacred our village. I stayed behind to make sure everyone got out.

But de cultists captured me and now dey say dey got somethin' extra special for Idago. I'd rather not find out what.

Dis magic holdin' me here is amateur work. De spells to release de bindings are sure to be in de magical tomes de cultists brought here.

Find de tomes and rip some pages out. Then we can piece together de right words to release me.

passages.title: Simply Magical
passages.text: Appreciate ya, <name>. For freeing me and for keeping an eye on dis one here.

passages.title: Simply Magical
passages.text: De girl's foolishness aside, I owe you my life.

passages.title: Bronze Simulacrum
passages.text: <Erus will be delighted to scrap this for you for a heaping sum of bronze.>

passages.title: Bronze Simulacrum
passages.text: You have something for Erus?

passages.title: Bronze Simulacrum
passages.text: YES! Erus will scrap!

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text:
Well <class>, it's your lucky day. I just happen to have an extremely genuine Brawler's Guild Invitation right here in my stockpile.

That said I'll need a moment to process the paperwork. That requires my complete concentration without your prying eyes on me. So do please give me a moment.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text:
Here's your extremely genuine Brawler's Guild Invitation.

Please note all sales are final.

There will be no refunds, or receipts.

passages.title: Questionable Qualifications
passages.text: Some of the lines look a little crooked.

passages.title: Ta'readon's Mount Voucher
passages.text: This token bears the seal of Overseer Ta'readon in Oribos. They would be interested in seeing this.

passages.title: Ta'readon's Mount Voucher
passages.text: I see you have served our merchants admirably. Accept one of our finest steeds as a reward.

passages.title: Purging the Vaults
passages.text: Send their souls howling back to Ula'tek.

passages.title: Prey: Anguish from Beyond
passages.text: After you...

passages.title: Bounty of the Cursed
passages.text: What have you found?

passages.title: Bounty of the Cursed
passages.text: We'll use de Soulcoilers' own works to purge dem.

passages.title: Decisive Incursions
passages.text: Now dat was a battle worthy of de old songs! I can see why Zul'jarra likes you.

passages.title: From Whence it Came
passages.text: Can you feel it? De violence just waitin' to spill over?

passages.title: Turn Back the Surge
passages.text: We must survive.

passages.title: Spoils of the Vaults
passages.text: Careful not to fall in de rivers of venom.

passages.title: Counter-Curse Bounty
passages.text: Careful not to fall in de rivers of venom.

passages.title: Shoulder to Shoulder
passages.text: Dis is a war, <name>. No one should fight alone.

passages.title: The Grimoire of the First Necrolyte
passages.text:
This ancient tome appears to be the spellbook of Sataiel, the first necrolyte.

Within its pages of curses and cantrips, you discover instructions for a ritual that Sataiel was concocting to empower Ulthalesh, the Deadwind Harvester. She calls this ritual, "The Rite of the Executioner."

The site was chosen and prepared, but Sataiel met her unfortunate end before she could proceed. Perhaps you can pick up where she left off?

First, you'll need some skulls.

passages.title: The Grimoire of the First Necrolyte
passages.text: There's just enough room on the altar for the bounty of skulls you've collected.

passages.title: The Grimoire of the First Necrolyte
passages.text:
The altar is coated with hundreds of years of dust, but the candles somehow still glow in the distance.

This must be the site for the ritual.

passages.title: Pledge of Loyalty
passages.text:
The eagle appears to have a message for you:

To: <name>

I hope this message finds you well.

Word of Ohn'ahra's omen has traveled fast. There are many who wish to pledge their loyalty to the Unseen Path's new leader.

Return to me at Trueshot Lodge, and we can discuss this further.

 -Altar Keeper Biehn

passages.title: Pledge of Loyalty
passages.text: I see you received my message.

passages.title: Needs of the Many
passages.text:
You've seen that the Legion is everywhere. Even with the Illidari as your allies, we are at a great disadvantage.

We need an edge against the Legion... something to send them back to the Nether.

We have heard that Dalaran will be the focal point of our campaign. I suggest you go there. You must do anything necessary to become stronger. ANYTHING.

I have seen Kirin Tor mages near Grommash Hold. They can send you to Dalaran.

Go. Take revenge upon the Legion!

passages.title: Protect the Home Front
passages.text:
The Legion hasn't just invaded this city. Their evil is spreading across Azeroth, threatening the far corners of our world.

We must seek them out and stop them, everywhere their darkness touches.

We've dispatched scouts around the world to watch for Legion activity. As invasions arise, we'll mark the locations on your map.

Make them suffer, <name>!

passages.title: Protect the Home Front
passages.text: Find them! Stop them! Suffer well!

passages.title: Protect the Home Front
passages.text:
You've done it! You've broken an invasion!

If only that had ended our campaign. But the Legion will never relent until they are destroyed... or have destroyed us.

Don't let up! Fight off more of these wretched invasions, <name>. The wyrmtongue we're holding captive here will reward your efforts.

passages.title: Supply Dropped
passages.text:
These supplies for the Earthen Ring have not been processed yet. It looks like someone has been rummaging through them and looting whatever can be carried. You have reasons to suspect the Grimtotem tribe, on account of the fact that one of their champions is nearby, visibly pilfering your stuff.

Challenge the Grimtotem to secure your resources!

passages.title: Supply Dropped
passages.text: <The Grimtotem Champion snorts derisively at you.>

passages.title: Supply Dropped
passages.text:
Very well, I yield - I yield!

Curse you, <class>, and that weapon of yours. Without it the Grimtotem would've been victorious.

Take your lousy supplies. But we will be back!

passages.title: Trading for Dreams
passages.text:
From the look of you, I take it you're an alchemist, yes?

I'd be willing to trade my services with you for a price that I deem is fair.

I have been away from Suramar for some time now. I long for an Ysera's Dream Draught. To concoct it, you'll need some dreamleaf as well as the leaves of a Dreamer's Tear.

One grows not to far from here in the clearing of some ruins. Take my flask, make this drink for me, and I'll do as you ask.

passages.title: Trading for Dreams
passages.text: <Leyweaver Erenyi seems lost in thought.>

passages.title: Trading for Dreams
passages.text:
You've crafted this rather well. I'm slightly impressed.

Now let me see that silk of yours...

passages.title: Welcome to Legion!
Illidari Allies
passages.text:
At first I was unsure whether it was wise to allow the Illidari inside the city. But they may have just saved all our lives.

I gave the demon hunters leave to establish a temporary camp in the Mage Quarter. I'd like you to be my personal envoy to them. Thank the Illidari for their assistance and see how they can aid our cause.

Just... keep your eyes open. They have harnessed a terrible power, and we must be ready should they be consumed by the darkness within.

passages.title: Illidari Allies
passages.text:
I see by the blood spatters that Jace revealed the demons to you. I trust the young king is safe.

We have more work ahead of us, <class>. Much more.
